operations.specification:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of country master records from the `shopping_mall_countries` Prisma model using flexible filter criteria, sorting, and pagination parameters.

This operation is intended for administrative back offices, seller onboarding flows, checkout forms, and configuration UIs that need to display or search over supported countries. The request body encapsulates the search criteria in an `IShoppingMallCountry.IRequest` DTO, which may include filters such as country code, localized name, enabled/disabled status, and region relationships as defined in the `shopping_mall_countries` schema. The implementation should translate these criteria into a Prisma query that respects any indexes and unique constraints on country codes or ISO identifiers.

The response returns a paginated collection of country summaries using the `IPageIShoppingMallCountry.ISummary` DTO. Each summary object is optimized for list views, typically containing key identification fields such as ISO codes, display names, enabled flags, and perhaps region references, without loading every column that might exist on the full country entity. Pagination metadata such as total count, page size, and current page index is included to support infinite scroll or standard paged UI components.

This operation is read-only and can be safely exposed to both authenticated and unauthenticated clients depending on deployment requirements. It does not alter any rows in the `shopping_mall_countries` table; it only evaluates search conditions and returns matching countries ordered according to the provided sort criteria. The implementation should handle empty result sets gracefully and return them with valid pagination metadata rather than treating them as errors. Related operations likely include retrieving a single country by code or managing the country master data through admin-only create/update endpoints, which are outside the scope of this search-focused operation.
operations.description:
Search and list countries from the `shopping_mall_countries` master table using rich filter criteria and pagination.

The `shopping_mall_countries` Prisma model represents canonical country master data used throughout the shoppingMall platform for checkout address entry, shipping rules, tax configuration, and reporting. This PATCH operation provides a flexible search interface so that UIs can look up countries by code, name, or other attributes, and so that administrative tools can review which countries are currently enabled or disabled for operations.

The request body type `IShoppingMallCountry.IRequest` encapsulates all supported search parameters: for example, exact or partial country code matching, case-insensitive name search, filtering by activation status flags, or restricting the result set to particular regions or policy groups. It also carries pagination and sorting options such as page size, page index, primary sort field, and sort direction. Implementations should validate these fields against the Prisma schema constraints and apply defensive limits to page size to protect system performance.

The response uses `IPageIShoppingMallCountry.ISummary`, a paginated collection of summary DTOs for each matching country. Summary entries focus on fields that are most relevant for list displays—such as ISO2/ISO3 codes, display name, and enabled flags—while omitting heavier or rarely needed attributes. The pagination container includes metadata like total record count and page information so clients can easily implement paged tables or infinite scroll. The operation is read-only and leaves `shopping_mall_countries` unchanged; it simply exposes a robust query surface over that table. Errors returned by this endpoint typically relate to invalid filter parameters or server issues; empty result sets for valid queries are treated as successful 200 responses with an empty items array.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single country master record from the shopping_mall_countries Prisma table by its globally unique business identifier code. It is intended for use anywhere the platform needs to resolve a country for configuration, checkout, shipping logic, tax rules, risk segmentation, or regional policy determination. The operation uses the countryCode path parameter, which corresponds to the unique country code column defined in the shopping_mall_countries model (for example ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or a platform-specific code), rather than a surrogate numeric or UUID identifier, to provide a stable and human-readable identifier in URLs.

The endpoint performs a simple lookup by code and returns the full IShoppingMallCountry DTO, including all descriptive attributes and any configuration flags defined in the Prisma schema (such as displayName, isoCode fields, phoneCode, locale defaults, or flags that control whether the country is enabled for signup, shipping, or billing). If no country with the specified code exists, the provider must return an appropriate 404-style error.

This operation is read-only, does not modify any database state, and is safe for public consumption. It can be used by both unauthenticated and authenticated clients to obtain canonical country metadata that is consistent across the shoppingMall platform. Other APIs that require a country, such as customer address management, seller warehouse configuration, shipping policy evaluation, or risk rule scoping, should rely on this country master data.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single country master record from the shopping_mall_countries table using its globally unique country code.

The underlying Prisma model shopping_mall_countries is the authoritative master data source for countries across the shoppingMall platform. Its fields typically include a business key such as countryCode or isoCode, human readable names, and configuration flags that determine whether the country is active, visible to users, allowed for shipping and billing, or eligible for risk and policy evaluation. This API exposes that canonical record so that client applications and other backend services can rely on a single, consistent definition of each country.

From a security and authorization perspective, this is a pure read operation over static master data and therefore can safely be exposed as a public endpoint without authentication. The authorizationActors field is set to an empty array to reflect that any caller may retrieve country information. Sensitive configuration, such as internal notes or operational-only flags, should either be omitted from the IShoppingMallCountry DTO or handled through separate admin-focused APIs; this operation is focused on the fields explicitly intended for use in end-user and seller experiences.

In terms of data relationships, entries in shopping_mall_countries are referenced by other models such as shopping_mall_regions, shipping policy tables, address snapshot tables, and possibly risk or legal policy configuration. When a country record is returned here, it is not necessary to hydrate those related entities; instead this operation returns a single IShoppingMallCountry object that clients can combine with other APIs such as region listing or shipping method discovery.

The implementation must validate that the supplied countryCode path parameter corresponds to the unique country code column defined in shopping_mall_countries. If the code is malformed or does not exist, the service should respond with a not-found style error rather than returning partial or incorrect data. This endpoint is typically used together with the country creation and management APIs (for example, POST /countries and any future PATCH/PUT /countries/{countryCode} operations) to provide a complete lifecycle for managing and consuming country master data within the shoppingMall ecosystem.

On successful creation, the operation inserts a new row into shopping_mall_countries using the data from the IShoppingMallCountry.ICreate payload, enforcing all database constraints such as uniqueness of the country code and any non-nullable fields defined in the Prisma schema. The newly created row is then returned as an IShoppingMallCountry object, ensuring that clients receive the canonical representation of the country, including any system-generated fields such as internal identifiers or timestamps defined on the model.

Because country master data influences core flows like address validation, shipping method availability, tax handling, and regional policy scoping, this endpoint must be restricted to administrative actors only. The authorizationActors field is therefore set to ["admin"], indicating that only authenticated administrators, as defined elsewhere in the user and role management models, are permitted to create or extend the set of available countries.
operations.description:
Create a new country master record in the shopping_mall_countries table using structured administrative input.

The shopping_mall_countries Prisma model represents the central country master data for the shoppingMall platform. Each record typically includes a countryCode field that serves as a globally unique business identifier, along with descriptive name fields and configuration attributes governing platform behavior. When a client calls this POST /countries operation with an IShoppingMallCountry.ICreate payload, the service validates the provided data against both business rules and database constraints before inserting a new row.

Typical validation rules include enforcing uniqueness of the country code, verifying that required descriptive fields are present, and ensuring that any configuration flags or enumerated values comply with the allowed options defined in the Prisma schema and higher-level business policies. For example, the implementation should reject attempts to create a country with a duplicate code or with invalid combinations of flags that would violate platform rules about which countries can be used for shipping, billing, or registration.

From a security perspective, creating new country records has wide-reaching operational implications for checkout flows, shipping calculations, risk and compliance evaluation, and administrative reporting. As a result, this operation is restricted to administrator actors only, as indicated by authorizationActors set to ["admin"]. Public clients and normal customers or sellers must not be able to call this API directly. Instead, they consume the resulting country data through read-only endpoints such as GET /countries/{countryCode} or potential list/search operations.

This operation complements the country retrieval and configuration APIs by providing the initial insertion capability for new countries. It is typically used alongside follow-up configuration operations, such as setting region-level policies, shipping rules, and risk thresholds that reference the newly created country record in shopping_mall_countries.

Update an existing country master record in the shopping_mall_countries table identified by its stable business country_code. This operation allows administrative clients to modify mutable attributes of a country such as its English display name, phone calling code, active flag, and sort order while preserving referential integrity for any addresses, warehouses, or other entities that reference this country.

The implementation must look up the target row using the unique index on country_code rather than the primary key id. In the current business rules for this service, identifiers such as id and country_code are treated as immutable and must not be altered through this endpoint once created. Only fields that are explicitly updatable in the corresponding IShoppingMallCountry.IUpdate DTO should be changed. The updated_at timestamp should always be refreshed to the current time of the update.

This endpoint is intended for platform admins configuring which countries are available for addresses, shipping, tax handling, and reporting. Business logic should enforce that when is_active is toggled, any dependent flows (such as address validation or shipping policy resolution) respect the new active state without breaking historical data that still points to the underlying country record.
operations.description:
Update the mutable properties of a specific country master record in the shopping_mall_countries table using its business identifier country_code.

The target record is located through the unique constraint on the country_code column, which represents a canonical ISO-like country code. This design aligns with the schema comment describing country_code as a stable business identifier used across the platform for customer addresses, shipping destinations, and tax handling, instead of exposing the opaque id primary key in the public API path.

From a security and authorization perspective, this operation is restricted to administrative actors because changes to country master data affect availability of destinations for checkout, shipping, and reporting. The authorizationActor is therefore set to "admin", and the implementation is expected to enforce additional role/permission checks consistent with admin RBAC definitions.

The underlying Prisma model includes fields such as name_en, phone_code, is_active, sort_order, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The corresponding IShoppingMallCountry.IUpdate DTO should expose only those fields that are intended to be modifiable by admins: for example, they may change the English display name, adjust the phone_code, toggle is_active to control whether the country appears in selection lists, and change sort_order to influence UI ordering. System-managed timestamps like created_at and updated_at should not be directly editable by clients; instead, updated_at is automatically set by the service layer when a successful update occurs.

This update endpoint is typically used together with a list/search endpoint such as PATCH /countries (returning paginated IPageIShoppingMallCountry.ISummary) and a detail retrieval endpoint such as GET /countries/{countryCode}. Clients can first retrieve existing country information, allow an admin to adjust configuration, and then apply changes through this PUT operation. Validation rules should ensure that the countryCode path parameter is non-empty, that any provided name_en values fit expected length constraints, that phone_code matches any chosen pattern for international dialing codes, and that sort_order remains within an acceptable integer range.

Error handling should cover cases where the specified country_code does not exist (returning an appropriate not-found error), attempts to modify immutable identifiers through this endpoint, and conflicts with business rules such as disabling a country that must remain enabled due to compliance requirements configured elsewhere. The operation returns the fully updated IShoppingMallCountry entity so that clients can confirm the resulting state after the update is applied.

operations.specification:
Delete a country master record from the shopping_mall_countries table using its unique country_code in exceptional administrative scenarios. Although the underlying schema includes a deleted_at timestamp that can support logical removal, this particular API operation is defined to perform a true hard deletion of the row when business rules allow it, removing the record entirely from the database rather than marking it as deleted.

Because shopping_mall_countries is referenced from other entities such as customer addresses, warehouses, and shipping policies, the implementation must ensure that deletion is only permitted when referential integrity, governance, and compliance constraints are satisfied—typically when there are no active foreign key references, no legal holds, and no policy requirements that mandate retention of the record. In many production environments this endpoint may be additionally guarded by feature flags or operational procedures and may be disabled entirely, with normal lifecycle management handled via the is_active flag instead.

The endpoint accepts a countryCode path parameter that maps to the unique index on country_code. It does not require a request body and, on successful deletion, should return HTTP 204 No Content with no response body, relying on status codes to indicate whether the deletion was executed. Any attempts to delete a non-existent country, or one that is protected by legal hold or dependent data, should result in appropriate error responses.
operations.description:
Erase an existing country master record from the shopping_mall_countries table, locating it by its business identifier country_code and performing a permanent deletion from the database when allowed by policy.

The Prisma model describes shopping_mall_countries as master data for countries used across the platform for addresses, shipping destinations, tax handling, and regional reporting. Each row is identified by a stable country_code, with additional attributes such as name_en for the English display name, phone_code for international dialing prefixes, is_active to indicate whether the country can currently be used, sort_order to control UI ordering, and timestamps including created_at, updated_at, and optionally deleted_at for logical deletion scenarios. This specific DELETE endpoint is intentionally defined as a hard-delete operation that bypasses the logical deletion mechanism and removes the row entirely, and therefore should be used only for rare, high-privilege administrative cleanup and correction workflows.

Security and governance considerations are critical: eliminating a country master record can have wide-ranging impact on the integrity of addresses, historical orders, warehouses, and other referencing entities. For this reason, authorization is restricted to platform administrators via authorizationActor set to "admin". The implementation should further enforce internal RBAC and policy checks, for example disallowing deletion when there are still customer addresses, shipments, legal holds, or reporting requirements referencing the country, or when compliance requirements mandate retention of country definitions for auditing and reporting.

This DELETE /shoppingMall/admin/countries/{countryCode} endpoint is typically used only in exceptional administrative workflows, such as correcting misconfigured test data or removing erroneously added countries before they are used in production. Standard operational flows should prefer simply toggling is_active via the corresponding PUT /shoppingMall/admin/countries/{countryCode} update endpoint, which logically removes the country from selectable options while preserving it for historical reference. When a deletion attempt violates referential or policy constraints, the service must return clear error messages indicating why the country cannot be removed so that admins can take appropriate corrective actions.

On successful deletion, the endpoint returns HTTP 204 No Content with no response body. If the specified country_code does not map to an existing row, the service should return a not-found error without attempting deletion. All error responses should avoid leaking internal implementation details while still providing enough context for administrators to understand the failure condition.
operations.summary: Hard-delete a shopping_mall_countries record by its unique country_code for exceptional administrative cleanup, bypassing logical deletion.

This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of regions for a specific country within the shoppingMall platform. It is primarily associated with the Prisma models `shopping_mall_countries` (master data for countries) and `shopping_mall_regions` (sub-national or logical regions used for shipping, pricing, risk segmentation, and policy scoping). The operation is designed as a PATCH list/search endpoint so that clients can submit complex request bodies containing pagination options, free-text search, and structured filters instead of relying on query-string parameters.

The consumer identifies the parent country by its business identifier `countryCode` in the path. Within that country, regions are typically identified by a `regionCode` that is unique in the scope of the parent country. The operation returns a paginated list of region summary objects optimized for catalog, configuration, and administrative screens, using the DTO type `IPageIShoppingMallRegion.ISummary`. The corresponding request DTO `IShoppingMallRegion.IRequest` carries filter fields such as partial region name, active/disabled flags, risk segmentation flags, and other attributes as defined in the Prisma schema comments.

This list endpoint is read-only and does not modify any data in `shopping_mall_regions`. It is intended for both internal administration tools and possibly public configuration consumers, depending on deployment needs. In typical deployments, authorization is not required to read the set of regions for a country, so `authorizationActors` is left empty. However, the actual implementation can still apply rate limiting and additional access controls around this operation.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of regions that belong to a specific country in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation operates over the `shopping_mall_regions` table, which stores sub-national or logical region records used for shipping configuration, taxation, pricing segmentation, risk segmentation, and other policy scoping. Each region is associated with an entry in `shopping_mall_countries`, which represents the country master data. The path parameter `{countryCode}` identifies the country in its business-friendly form rather than using an internal UUID. According to typical Prisma schema comments for these models, the country code is expected to follow ISO country code conventions, while each region has its own code and human-readable name used by both customers and administrators.

The client sends a structured search request in the body of this PATCH operation using `IShoppingMallRegion.IRequest`. That DTO may include pagination parameters such as page index and page size, sort criteria (for example by region name or by display order), and a set of filter fields including partial region name matching, enabled/disabled flags, or flags related to risk and shipping policies as documented in the Prisma schema comments. The server validates these filters against the schema definitions for `shopping_mall_regions` and composes an underlying query that restricts results to regions associated with the given country. If invalid filter combinations are provided, the server responds with appropriate validation errors.

Security-wise, region data is usually non-sensitive reference data. Therefore, this endpoint is modeled as a public read operation with `authorizationActors: []`. Implementations may still place this operation behind generic authentication or API gateways if needed, but those concerns are orthogonal to the interface design. Because the endpoint is read-only, there are no side effects on the underlying tables; it simply reads from `shopping_mall_regions` (and its relationship to `shopping_mall_countries`) and returns a paginated collection of lightweight summary records.

The response body uses the type `IPageIShoppingMallRegion.ISummary`, which represents a page container wrapping an array of region summary DTOs along with paging metadata such as total count, page size, and current page index. Related operations that complement this one include `GET /countries/{countryCode}/regions/{regionCode}` for retrieving a single region in more detail, and administrative configuration endpoints that manage shipping or risk policies at the region level. Error handling covers standard conditions such as an unknown `countryCode` (which should result in a not-found error) or invalid pagination parameters supplied in the request body.

This operation retrieves the detailed representation of a single region belonging to a specific country in the shoppingMall platform. It is associated with the Prisma models `shopping_mall_countries` and `shopping_mall_regions`. The region is uniquely identified by the combination of `countryCode` and `regionCode`, reflecting an underlying composite uniqueness constraint such as `@@unique([country_id, code])` in the `shopping_mall_regions` model. The design therefore requires both the parent country code and the child region code in the URL path to unambiguously locate the record.

The operation is modeled as a standard GET detail endpoint and returns a single region DTO of type `IShoppingMallRegion`. This DTO exposes all relevant fields defined for the region entity, such as its business code, display name, localized labels, active/disabled flags, optional risk segmentation attributes, and any additional configuration flags described in the Prisma schema comments. The endpoint is read-only and does not alter any data in the database.

This detail endpoint is intended for use in configuration UIs, checkout flows when showing the user's selected region, and internal tools that need to inspect the full configuration of a specific region. It can be invoked alongside the region list endpoint `PATCH /countries/{countryCode}/regions` to support drill-down from lists into individual records.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single region belonging to a specific country in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_regions` table, which represents sub-national or logical regions used in shipping, pricing, risk segmentation, and policy scoping. Each region record is linked to a country in `shopping_mall_countries`. The API path uses `{countryCode}` to identify the parent country using its business identifier code (for example an ISO country code) and `{regionCode}` to identify the region within that country. In the database, this typically corresponds to a composite uniqueness constraint similar to `@@unique([country_id, code])`, so both values are needed to uniquely resolve the region.

When a client calls this endpoint, the server validates the path parameters and queries `shopping_mall_regions` for a record that belongs to the specified country and has the matching region code. If no such combination is found, a not-found error is returned. On success, the operation returns a DTO of type `IShoppingMallRegion`, which includes all relevant configuration fields for the region, such as its business code, display name, enabled/disabled status, tax or shipping groups, risk flags, and any other attributes described in the Prisma schema comments. This allows consuming applications to fully understand how the region is used by the platform.

Security and authorization considerations mirror those of the region list operation: region configuration is often non-sensitive reference data, so this endpoint is modeled as a public read interface with `authorizationActors: []`. Platform operators are free to place additional access controls at the infrastructure level if needed. Typical clients for this endpoint include administrative configuration UIs, checkout flows that need to re-validate a region selection, and background jobs that reconcile region definitions with external systems. Together with `PATCH /countries/{countryCode}/regions`, this endpoint supports list-and-drill-down patterns for managing and viewing regional configuration.

Create a new region under a specific country in the shopping_mall_regions table, using the country’s business identifier code from shopping_mall_countries.

This POST operation targets the ShoppingMallRegion aggregate, which is backed by the Prisma model "shopping_mall_regions". The parent country is identified by its business-level country_code on the shopping_mall_countries table, exposed in the path as {countryCode}. The operation will first resolve the corresponding shopping_mall_countries row by country_code (which is globally unique according to the schema’s unique index on country_code), then create a new region row linked via shopping_mall_country_id.

The request body uses IShoppingMallRegion.ICreate to capture the region’s business code (unique per country via the composite unique index on [shopping_mall_country_id, code]), English display name, optional region_type, activation flag, and sort_order, along with any additional fields defined in that DTO. Server-side logic must validate that code is unique within the resolved country, that required fields such as name_en and is_active are present, and that sort_order is an integer in an acceptable range.

This endpoint is intended for administrative tools that manage geographic configuration used across shipping, pricing, risk, and policy scopes. Only authorized admin actors should be allowed to create regions. Downstream features such as shipping policies, seller warehouses, and risk rules will reference these region records by their primary key and the parent country relationship.
operations.description:
Create a new region record within a specific country for the ShoppingMall platform.

This operation creates a new entry in the Prisma model `shopping_mall_regions`, which represents sub-national or logical regions used for shipping, pricing, risk segmentation, and policy scoping. Each region belongs to exactly one country, enforced by the non-null foreign key `shopping_mall_country_id` with relation `country` to `shopping_mall_countries`. The parent country is selected by the path parameter `countryCode`, which corresponds to the `country_code` field in `shopping_mall_countries`. The description of `shopping_mall_countries.country_code` explains that it is a canonical business identifier, typically an ISO 3166-1 style code used across the platform.

Within `shopping_mall_regions`, the `code` field is the business-level identifier for the region within its country and is constrained by a composite unique index on `[shopping_mall_country_id, code]`. This means the same `code` can be reused in another country but must be unique for a given country. The `name_en` field holds the English display name, while `region_type` is an optional classifier such as "state", "province", or another business-defined type. The `is_active` flag controls whether the region is currently eligible to be used in shipping, risk, and address validation flows, and `sort_order` defines ordering within a country’s region list. The `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` timestamps are managed by the system and should not be supplied directly by clients; `deleted_at` is used to logically remove entries from new operations while retaining them for historical orders and addresses.

From a security perspective, only administrative actors responsible for geographic and operational configuration should be allowed to call this endpoint. The `authorizationActors` field therefore uses `["admin"]`, indicating the endpoint is restricted to admin users, with more granular role checks handled in business logic if needed. The controller or middleware layer will ensure that only authenticated admins can invoke this operation, and the service layer will enforce business validations such as the uniqueness of the region `code` within the resolved country and any additional policy constraints.

This operation works together with the region update endpoint `PUT /countries/{countryCode}/regions/{regionCode}` for maintenance of existing regions, and any future list or detail retrieval endpoints on regions. When errors occur, such as when `countryCode` does not match any active country, when a region with the same code already exists for the country, or when validation on fields like `name_en` or `sort_order` fails, the service should respond with appropriate HTTP error codes and structured error payloads so that admin UIs can highlight and correct the problematic inputs.

Update an existing region under a specific country in the shopping_mall_regions table, using both the country’s business identifier code and the region’s business code for scoping.

This PUT operation targets the same `shopping_mall_regions` Prisma model as the create operation but focuses on modifying an existing record. The combination of the `shopping_mall_country_id` foreign key and the `code` field is constrained by a composite unique index, which means region codes are unique only within each country. The path therefore includes both `{countryCode}` (mapping to `shopping_mall_countries.country_code`) and `{regionCode}` (mapping to `shopping_mall_regions.code` scoped to the resolved country) to uniquely identify the region to update.

The request body uses `IShoppingMallRegion.IUpdate`, representing the subset of fields that can be changed after creation, such as `name_en`, `region_type`, `is_active`, and `sort_order`. Implementation must resolve the parent country by `countryCode`, then find the region row whose `shopping_mall_country_id` matches the country and whose `code` equals `regionCode`. After applying validations and updates, the service persists changes and returns the updated region representation. This operation is essential for administrative maintenance of geographic configuration across shipping, pricing, and risk policies.
operations.description:
Update an existing ShoppingMall region belonging to a specific country.

This operation updates a record in the `shopping_mall_regions` Prisma model, which stores regions such as states, provinces, or other business-defined geographic units. Each region row includes a foreign key `shopping_mall_country_id` linking to `shopping_mall_countries`, and the table’s unique index on `[shopping_mall_country_id, code]` guarantees that each region `code` is unique only within the context of its parent country. To respect this composite uniqueness, the API path includes both `{countryCode}` to select the parent via `shopping_mall_countries.country_code` and `{regionCode}` to select the specific region’s `code` within that country context.

The editable fields on `shopping_mall_regions` include `name_en` for the English display name, `region_type` for an optional classification, and flags such as `is_active` and `sort_order`. The `is_active` boolean determines whether the region is usable for shipping, risk segmentation, and address validation; deactivating a region should prevent it from being offered in new flows while allowing existing historical data to remain intact. The `sort_order` integer controls the ordering of regions in UI lists for a given country. System-maintained timestamp fields such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are managed internally and should be controlled by the service, not directly from the client’s update payload; `deleted_at` is used to logically mark regions as removed from new operations but still referenceable in existing orders and addresses.

Because this endpoint changes geographic configuration that may affect shipping availability, pricing rules, and risk logic, it must be restricted to administrative actors. The `authorizationActors` are set to `["admin"]`, and more detailed permission checks (such as which admins may modify which countries or regions) are implemented in business logic or RBAC configuration. When updating, the service should handle common error conditions, including the case where the specified `countryCode` or `regionCode` combination does not resolve to any region, or where the proposed changes violate business constraints (for example, attempting to reuse a region `code` within the same country or conflicting with active shipping policies). The endpoint complements the region creation endpoint `POST /countries/{countryCode}/regions` and any list or detail retrieval APIs that expose regions for admin management interfaces.

operations.specification:
This operation performs a permanent deletion of a specific region record from the `shopping_mall_regions` table, identified by its composite business key of `shopping_mall_country_id` and `code`. Instead of using the internal UUID primary key directly in the URL, the API path is designed around business identifiers: `{countryCode}` maps to the `shopping_mall_countries.country_code` field (globally unique per country), and `{regionCode}` maps to the `shopping_mall_regions.code` field which is uniquely constrained together with its parent country via a composite uniqueness constraint on `(shopping_mall_country_id, code)`.

When invoked, the backend implementation must first resolve the `shopping_mall_countries` record by `country_code`, then locate the corresponding `shopping_mall_regions` record whose `shopping_mall_country_id` matches that country and whose `code` equals the provided `regionCode`. Once found, this operation performs a **hard delete**, permanently removing the region row from `shopping_mall_regions` instead of merely setting the nullable `deleted_at` soft-deletion timestamp. The `deleted_at` field may be used by other internal workflows, but this endpoint explicitly ignores it and removes the record from the database.

Because `shopping_mall_regions` is referenced by `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` through the `shopping_mall_region_id` foreign key, the implementation must ensure referential integrity. This typically means either preventing deletion when active shipping policies exist, or cascading deletion of subsidiary configuration rows if that is the chosen business rule. The specification assumes a protective behavior where deletion fails with a meaningful error if non-deleted shipping policies or other dependent records exist for the region, requiring operators to remove or deactivate associated configurations first.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a specific region record from the `shopping_mall_regions` table using composite business identifiers derived from country and region codes.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_regions` model, which represents sub-national or logical regions belonging to a country. Each region row includes fields such as `shopping_mall_country_id`, `code`, `name_en`, `region_type`, `is_active`, `sort_order`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and a nullable `deleted_at` field that can be used for soft-deletion semantics. **However, this particular API endpoint is defined to perform a hard delete**: when a matching region is found, the row is permanently removed from the database and `deleted_at` is not set by this operation. By using `{countryCode}` and `{regionCode}` in the URL, this API aligns with business identifiers instead of exposing internal UUIDs.

From a security and governance perspective, this deletion operation is restricted to administrative actors responsible for geographic configuration management. End-users, customers, and sellers must not be able to alter region definitions. The `authorizationActors` is therefore limited to `["admin"]`, with the expectation that the underlying access control mechanism will enforce that only admin accounts with appropriate permissions can call this endpoint. Additionally, because regions are referenced by shipping policies (`shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies`) and potentially by addresses or other entities, the implementation should verify that deleting a region does not leave orphaned or inconsistent data. If dependent records exist that cannot be safely auto-removed, the provider should return a domain-specific error indicating that the region is in use.

The relationship between `shopping_mall_regions` and `shopping_mall_countries` is expressed in the Prisma schema via the non-nullable foreign key `shopping_mall_country_id` with relation `country` pointing to `shopping_mall_countries`. The corresponding countries table includes fields like `country_code`, `name_en`, `phone_code`, `is_active`, `sort_order`, and timestamps, with a unique constraint on `country_code`. The implementation must therefore first use `{countryCode}` to resolve the correct `shopping_mall_countries` row, then use its `id` together with `{regionCode}` to find the region row, respecting the composite uniqueness of `(shopping_mall_country_id, code)`.

When the identified region is successfully deleted, the operation returns no response body, signaling success with an HTTP 204 or 200 status as per controller conventions. If no region is found matching the supplied identifiers, the backend should return a 404-style error. If the region cannot be deleted due to existing dependent configuration or business rules, the backend should return a 409-style error with details. Related operations that integrators will typically use alongside this endpoint include a search/list operation on `/countries/{countryCode}/regions` to view available regions and a create or update operation on the same resource, although those are defined separately from this specification.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of region-specific shipping policy configurations stored in the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table for a given region. It is implemented as a `PATCH` method on the `/countries/{countryCode}/regions/{regionCode}/shippingPolicies` path to support complex query criteria in the request body while still representing a read-only operation.

The underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` describes region-scoped shipping configuration attributes like `policy_name`, `shipping_method_group`, `min_order_amount`, `max_order_amount`, `allows_cod`, `is_shipping_allowed`, `notes`, `effective_from`, `effective_until`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`, along with a non-nullable foreign key `shopping_mall_region_id` referencing `shopping_mall_regions`. A composite unique constraint combining `shopping_mall_region_id` and `policy_name` ensures that policy names are unique within a region. The DTO types for this operation follow the service prefix pattern `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy`: an `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.IRequest` request DTO encapsulates rich filter, sorting, and pagination options, and the response returns a paginated collection typed as `IPageIShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.ISummary` containing lightweight summaries of matching policies.

Because regions themselves are identified by composite business keys rather than raw UUIDs, the operation uses `{countryCode}` and `{regionCode}` path parameters. `{countryCode}` corresponds to `shopping_mall_countries.country_code`, which is globally unique, and `{regionCode}` corresponds to `shopping_mall_regions.code`, which is unique per country via the composite uniqueness constraint with `shopping_mall_country_id`. The implementation must therefore: (1) resolve the country by `country_code`, (2) resolve the region by `shopping_mall_country_id` plus `code`, and (3) scope all policy queries to the resolved `shopping_mall_region_id` while applying additional filters from the request DTO.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of region-specific shipping policies defined in the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table for a particular country and region.

The Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` describes configuration, not transactional shipment data. Fields like `policy_name`, `shipping_method_group`, `min_order_amount`, `max_order_amount`, `allows_cod`, and `is_shipping_allowed` govern whether and how shipping can be offered to a region. Temporal fields `effective_from` and `effective_until` allow scheduling policies over time, while `notes` provides free-form operator guidance. Timestamps `created_at`, `updated_at`, and the nullable `deleted_at` enable auditability and logical retirement of policies without removing them from history. Because policies are subsidiary to regions through `shopping_mall_region_id`, the search is always scoped to a single region, and the path parameters determine which region to use.

From a security standpoint, this endpoint is aimed primarily at administrative and operational tools used to configure shipping behavior. However, it is safe to expose as a read-only endpoint to internal services that participate in checkout or pre-checkout validation. External untrusted clients should not typically call it directly; rather, they would use higher-level checkout APIs that incorporate shipping logic. To simplify integration patterns while still protecting modification of configuration, the endpoint is defined as accessible only to `admin` actors at the API layer, denoted by `authorizationActors: ["admin"]`. Within the implementation, further fine-grained permission checks can be applied based on admin roles or scopes.

The request body uses the `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.IRequest` DTO to express filters like policy name search, flags for `is_shipping_allowed` or `allows_cod`, effective date ranges, and pagination and sorting preferences. Path parameters supply the region context, so the request DTO must not repeat fields like `countryCode` or `regionCode`. The response body uses the `IPageIShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.ISummary` DTO, which encapsulates a `pagination` envelope (page number, size, total counts) and an array of summary entries that contain key attributes such as `policy_name`, shipping allowance flags, and date-range information. Related operations include possible admin create/update/delete endpoints for shipping policies under the same path root, as well as listing regions for a country, which would typically be exposed via `/countries/{countryCode}/regions` operations.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the detailed configuration of a specific region-level shipping policy for the shopping mall platform. It operates primarily on the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` Prisma model, which represents region-specific shipping capability and constraint configurations. The policy is identified by a combination of its parent country, parent region, and a unique policy identifier.

The endpoint path `/countries/{countryCode}/regions/{regionCode}/shippingPolicies/{policyId}` encodes the hierarchical relationship between countries, regions, and their associated shipping policies. `countryCode` and `regionCode` are business identifiers that conceptually correspond to records in `shopping_mall_countries` and `shopping_mall_regions`, while `policyId` identifies a specific record in `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies`. Although the internal Prisma schema may use UUIDs or numeric IDs, the API exposes stable, business-friendly identifiers.

The operation returns a single `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy` object that encapsulates all configuration parameters for the policy, such as supported shipping methods, applicable regions, weight and price constraints, and any associated risk or business rules. Implementation should validate the existence and association of the country, region, and policy, and return appropriate errors when the hierarchy does not match (for example, when a policy does not belong to the specified region).
operations.description:
Retrieve a single region-level shipping policy configuration for a specific country and region context.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table, which stores region-specific shipping capability and constraint definitions for the shoppingMall platform. Each record in this table is logically scoped to a particular region, and regions themselves are scoped to countries stored in `shopping_mall_countries` and `shopping_mall_regions`. The `countryCode` and `regionCode` path parameters identify the geographical context, while `policyId` identifies the concrete policy record used to control shipping options, constraints, and behaviors in that region.

From a security and governance perspective, this is a read-only operation that does not modify any data. It can be exposed either publicly or with basic authentication depending on whether shipping policies are considered public catalog information in the deployment environment. The API implementation should ensure that only policies that are active and applicable for the requesting channel or actor are returned, and should handle missing or mismatched identifiers with clear error responses such as 404 for not found.

The response body is modeled as `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy`, which represents the full configuration of a region shipping policy, including fields such as associated region identifiers, enabled or disabled state, allowed shipping methods, pricing tiers, weight or dimension limits, and any special constraints tied to business policies in `shopping_mall_business_policies` or risk configurations from `shopping_mall_risk_rules`. This design allows client applications, such as admin consoles or configuration UIs, to display the complete configuration to users who are managing logistics or performing audits.

Related operations include the creation of new shipping policies and updates to existing policies via other endpoints (for example, POST and PUT on `/countries/{countryCode}/regions/{regionCode}/shippingPolicies`). These endpoints together support a full lifecycle for configuring shipping capabilities at a regional level, while this GET operation focuses solely on retrieving the current configuration snapshot for inspection or usage by other services.

This operation creates a new region-level shipping policy configuration for a specific region within a country on the shopping mall platform. It is backed by the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` Prisma model, which stores region-specific shipping capability and constraint configurations that determine how orders can be shipped to customers in that region.

The endpoint path `/countries/{countryCode}/regions/{regionCode}/shippingPolicies` encapsulates the hierarchical relationship between countries, regions, and their shipping policies. `countryCode` corresponds conceptually to a record in `shopping_mall_countries`, and `regionCode` corresponds to a record in `shopping_mall_regions` that is scoped to that country. The request body uses the `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.ICreate` DTO to describe all data necessary to define a new policy, such as associated shipping methods, applicable constraints, and business rules. The implementation is responsible for binding the created policy to the region and country indicated by the path parameters, rather than relying on the client to send those identifiers again in the body.

On successful creation, the operation returns the newly created policy as an `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy` object. The provider logic should validate that the country and region exist and that the region belongs to the specified country, and enforce any uniqueness or constraint rules defined in the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` model (for example, preventing duplicate active policies for the same region and shipping method combination).
operations.description:
Create a new region-level shipping policy configuration under a specific country and region.

This operation writes to the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table, which holds structured shipping capability and constraint configurations at the region level for the shoppingMall platform. By specifying `countryCode` and `regionCode` in the path, clients indicate the geographical scope for the new policy, while the request body of type `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.ICreate` contains policy-specific attributes such as eligible shipping methods, pricing or surcharge rules, applicable weight and package constraints, and flags that determine whether the policy is active or conditional.

The API implementation should treat the path parameters as authoritative for scoping: the new policy must be associated with the region indicated by `regionCode` within the country indicated by `countryCode`. This avoids duplication of scoping information in the body and prevents clients from accidentally or maliciously creating policies attached to mismatched regions. Before inserting the record, the service should validate the existence of the referenced country and region (from `shopping_mall_countries` and `shopping_mall_regions`) and apply any business rules derived from `shopping_mall_business_policies` or `shopping_mall_risk_rules`, such as restrictions on high-risk regions or maximum allowed delivery times.

From a security perspective, policy creation is typically restricted to administrative or operations users responsible for logistics and configuration management. In this specification the `authorizationActors` field is set to `[]` to keep the endpoint definition generic; in a concrete deployment, decorators and middleware will enforce that only privileged actors such as admins can call this operation. Error handling should provide clear feedback on validation failures, constraint violations, or foreign key mismatches so that configuration tools can guide users in correcting input.

Related operations include retrieving a single policy via `GET /countries/{countryCode}/regions/{regionCode}/shippingPolicies/{policyId}`, listing or searching policies if such an endpoint exists, and updating or deactivating policies via PUT or PATCH operations. Together, these operations support full lifecycle management of shipping capabilities at the region level.

Each policy record typically references a parent region from the shopping_mall_regions table, which itself is scoped by a country record in shopping_mall_countries. The combination of countryCode, regionCode, and policyId in the URL path ensures that the correct policy is updated within the correct geographical and business context.

This DTO mirrors the updatable columns of the underlying Prisma model, such as effective period fields, carrier or method bindings, cost calculation parameters, and constraints like maximum weight or dimensional limits. The path parameters countryCode, regionCode, and policyId provide the full context needed to find the exact policy that should be removed.

Only administrative users with sufficient privileges should be able to execute this removal. The authorizationActors array is set to ["admin"] to represent that this is a privileged configuration operation. When invoked, the endpoint performs a hard deletion of the specified record in the shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies table. Before deletion, business rules may require checks to ensure that the policy is not actively referenced by other configuration entities or that a replacement policy is in place for regions that must always have at least one applicable shipping policy. operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a filtered, paginated list of category entities from the shopping_mall_categories Prisma table for the ShoppingMall service. It is designed as a flexible collection query endpoint that allows clients to perform complex filtering, sorting, and pagination over the global product category taxonomy used across the entire shopping mall platform.

The underlying Prisma model shopping_mall_categories represents the primary catalog category taxonomy, including hierarchical relationships (e.g., parent-child links), display properties (names, slugs, sort order), and visibility flags that determine how categories appear in navigation and search. This PATCH /shoppingMall/categories operation will accept a structured request body of type IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest that encapsulates search criteria such as partial name matching, depth constraints, parent category filters, visibility flags, and sort preferences. It will return a paginated collection of category summaries using the response type IPageIShoppingMallCategory.ISummary, optimized for list and navigation UIs.

The endpoint is read-only and side-effect free. It must support efficient querying over large category trees, leveraging indexes and closure relations in subsidiary tables like shopping_mall_category_closures when implemented, but it conceptually exposes only the primary category data. The operation is intentionally public (no authorizationActors) so that both anonymous guests and authenticated users can consume the category taxonomy for browsing and product discovery. Server-side logic should validate inputs from IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest and apply safe defaults for pagination and sorting when omitted.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of product categories from the ShoppingMall platform’s global category taxonomy.

This operation reads from the Prisma model shopping_mall_categories, which serves as the primary representation of product categories in the shopping mall. Each record in this table represents a category node that can participate in a hierarchical tree used for navigation, faceted search, and merchandising. Typical fields in this model include business identifiers, human-readable names, SEO-friendly labels, ordering or ranking indicators, and flags controlling whether the category is visible or selectable in the storefront.

The request body of type IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest allows clients to specify search conditions such as filtering by parent category, restricting to leaf or non-leaf categories, matching category names or codes using partial search, and constraining visibility. It also carries pagination parameters (page index, page size) and sorting options (such as ordering by display order, name, or creation time) so that UIs can implement infinite scrolling, lazy loading, or multi-panel navigation without hardcoding any server behavior. The server must validate that requested page sizes and sorting fields are within acceptable bounds and fall back to safe defaults if omitted.

Security-wise, this endpoint is intentionally defined as a public read-only API, represented by an empty authorizationActors array. Any caller, authenticated or anonymous, can use it to explore the category taxonomy. However, the underlying implementation may still enforce internal business rules from related policy models such as shopping_mall_business_policies or catalog visibility mechanisms so that categories that are blocked or deprecated are not exposed. Error handling should include validation errors for malformed request bodies and internal errors if data retrieval fails.

This operation is typically used alongside GET /shoppingMall/categories/{categoryId}, which retrieves full detail for a specific category. UI flows often first invoke this PATCH /shoppingMall/categories endpoint to render a list of top-level or filtered categories, then call the detail endpoint when a user selects one. Together, these APIs provide the foundational navigation and discovery capabilities for the ShoppingMall product catalog.

The endpoint path GET /shoppingMall/categories/{categoryId} uses a single path parameter categoryId to identify the target category. Because the Prisma schema catalog lists shopping_mall_categories as the primary model for the global category taxonomy but does not specify the existence of a separate human-readable code with a uniqueness guarantee in this context, this specification uses a generic identifier parameter named categoryId with string type. The backing service will use this identifier to query the shopping_mall_categories table, applying appropriate uniqueness rules (for example, primary key or unique business key) as defined in that model.

The response type IShoppingMallCategory represents the full category detail view, including core identifying attributes, display names, SEO-related metadata, hierarchy information (such as parent or root identifiers), and any other fields from shopping_mall_categories required by storefront and admin clients. This read-only operation does not modify any data and must return a 404-style error when the requested category cannot be found or is not accessible based on internal visibility rules.

Retrieve full detail information for a single ShoppingMall category identified by its categoryId.

This operation directly reads from the shopping_mall_categories Prisma model, which acts as the primary storage for product categories in the shopping mall. Each category record may include fields such as name, internal or external identifiers, hierarchy links to parent categories, and flags controling its visibility and use in the catalog. The endpoint abstracts these implementation details behind the IShoppingMallCategory DTO so clients can reliably display category pages, breadcrumbs, and navigation labels.

The categoryId path parameter is a string identifier that uniquely selects one category in the shopping_mall_categories table according to the model’s primary key or other unique constraint. Clients obtain this identifier from previous API responses, such as the PATCH /shoppingMall/categories search endpoint, from internal configuration, or from stored links. The provider must validate the parameter, perform a lookup against the Prisma model, and either return a populated IShoppingMallCategory object or an appropriate not-found or access-denied error.

This operation is publicly readable and thus uses an empty authorizationActors array, making it suitable for storefront navigation and SEO entry pages. Despite being public, the implementation should still respect internal business and visibility rules that may be defined via other models such as shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules or shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons, ensuring that categories that are blocked, deprecated, or out of scope are not returned. The operation accepts a structured JSON payload described by the `IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate` DTO. That DTO is expected to encapsulate core business attributes of a category such as its business identifier code, display name, optional description, parent category reference, display ordering, and status/visibility flags that determine whether the category should be exposed in navigation and search. The service will validate the request against business rules (for example, uniqueness of the category code, consistency of the parent-child relationship, or constraints on maximum depth if defined in the schema) before persisting.

Upon successful creation, the API returns the fully populated category resource as `IShoppingMallCategory`, reflecting the state in the `shopping_mall_categories` table including generated identifiers, timestamps, and any derived or defaulted fields. operations.description:
Create a new category record in the global product category taxonomy stored in the `shopping_mall_categories` table.

This operation accepts a JSON request body shaped by `IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate`, which represents the business input required to define a category in the shoppingMall catalog. Typical fields modeled in the Prisma schema comments for `shopping_mall_categories` include a human-readable name, a stable business code, and optional descriptive text. The DTO is also expected to carry optional hierarchical context, such as a parent category reference, as well as ordering information used for navigation menus and potentially boolean flags that indicate whether the category is currently active or visible to end users.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors represented by the `admin` role. Ordinary customers or sellers are not permitted to create or modify global taxonomy categories, because changes to this data affect the entire marketplace experience. The implementation should enforce that the caller is an authenticated admin and may additionally apply fine-grained permission checks based on configured admin roles and permissions in related tables such as `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`.

Internally, the operation persists the category row into the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and may trigger additional behaviors such as updating category closure records, initializing localization stubs in `shopping_mall_category_localizations`, or invalidating cache and search index entries for catalog navigation. The description comments in the Prisma schema for categories typically emphasize their role as the canonical taxonomy for all products and SKUs, and this endpoint aligns with that role by ensuring all new categories are created through a single, controlled interface.

The operation should perform defensive validation, returning appropriate error responses when constraints are violated. For example, if a parent category identifier does not exist in `shopping_mall_categories`, or if the provided business code collides with an existing one that is constrained by a unique index, the service must reject the request. This endpoint is typically used in conjunction with read and search endpoints on categories, allowing admins to create, then later list and update categories as part of ongoing catalog governance.

The operation consumes an `IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate` request body that carries only the fields that are allowed to be updated according to the business rules and Prisma schema comments. For example, the DTO may support updating the display name, description, or parent category, while restricting or prohibiting updates to immutable fields like the primary key.

On success, the endpoint returns the updated category entity as `IShoppingMallCategory`, reflecting the new state of the row in `shopping_mall_categories`. Any dependent structures such as closure records or localization metadata may be adjusted by internal services, but they are not modeled as part of this endpoint's contract. This operation is a core tool for catalog administrators to manage and reorganize categories as product offerings and navigation strategies evolve over time.
operations.description:

This operation uses the `categoryId` path parameter to resolve a specific row in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. The parameter is expected to carry the primary identifier of the category, typically a string-formatted UUID according to the underlying schema. If no category exists for the provided identifier, the service should respond with an appropriate error status, such as 404 Not Found, rather than silently creating a new category.

The request body follows the `IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate` DTO, which encapsulates updatable attributes described in the Prisma schema comments for `shopping_mall_categories`. These attributes usually include human-readable fields like the name and description as well as structural properties like parent category linkage or display order. The service must validate that any new parent relationship does not introduce cycles into the category hierarchy and that referenced parent categories exist. It must also honor database-level constraints such as uniqueness of business codes or non-nullability of certain columns.

Access to this endpoint is limited to administrative actors represented by the `admin` authorization actor. Regular customers, guest users, or sellers do not have permission to modify the global category taxonomy because such changes impact navigation, search, and product discovery throughout the shoppingMall platform. The implementation should enforce admin authentication and may further consult RBAC definitions in related admin profile and role tables to ensure that only properly privileged admins can perform structural changes.

After a successful update, the service returns the latest representation of the category as `IShoppingMallCategory`, ensuring that clients receive all resolved and defaulted fields as they are stored in the database. Downstream processes, such as recalculating closure tables or invalidating catalog search indices, can be triggered asynchronously based on the updated category. This endpoint is typically paired with category creation and listing operations to provide full lifecycle management for the taxonomy.

This operation performs a hard deletion of a single product category record in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma table. It is intended for administrative governance use cases where a category must be removed from the active catalog structure.

The endpoint receives the category identifier as a path parameter (`categoryId`). In implementation, this `categoryId` will map to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_categories` model (typically a UUID or similar unique identifier as defined in the Prisma schema). The service layer will look up the category, validate that it is eligible for deletion (for example, ensuring there are no business rules preventing removal of categories that are still in active use), and then remove the record from the database together with any subsidiary linkage records that depend on it (such as entries in `shopping_mall_product_categories` or `shopping_mall_category_closures`), according to configured cascading rules.

Because category management affects the entire catalog hierarchy and end‑user navigation, this operation must be restricted to administrative actors only. The `authorizationActors` is therefore set to `["admin"]`, and controller-level authorization will ensure only properly privileged administrators can call this operation. The business logic should also log the deletion into appropriate audit mechanisms (for example, using admin audit log tables) to preserve a trace of structural catalog changes.

The operation does not accept a request body, as all information necessary to perform the deletion is provided in the path parameter. It also does not return a response body on success, relying instead on HTTP status codes (such as 204 No Content) to signal successful completion. Error handling should return appropriate codes for missing categories (404 Not Found), unauthorized access (403 Forbidden), or conflicts when business rules prevent deletion (409 Conflict).
operations.description:
Delete a single category record from the `shopping_mall_categories` table by its unique identifier.

This operation is used by administrative users to remove an existing product category from the shopping mall catalog. The target is identified by the `categoryId` path parameter, which corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. When invoked, the backend locates the matching category and performs a hard delete, physically removing the record from persistent storage rather than merely hiding it. Related subsidiary records that only exist to support the category, such as links in junction tables or closure tables, should be deleted or updated according to the relational constraints defined in the Prisma schema.

From a security and governance perspective, category deletion has platform‑wide impact because categories influence how products are discovered and navigated by customers and sellers. Therefore, this operation is restricted to administrative actors only, expressed via `authorizationActors: ["admin"]`. The implementation should integrate with the platform's administrative audit logging so that each deletion event is captured along with the responsible admin identity and timestamp for later review.

The API does not accept a request body; only the `categoryId` path parameter is used. A successful deletion should respond with an empty body and a status code indicating success, typically 204 No Content. If the specified category does not exist, the service should return 404 Not Found. If business rules or referential constraints prevent deletion—for example, because the category is still referenced by critical entities that must not be orphaned—the service should return a suitable error such as 409 Conflict with an explanation in an error payload defined elsewhere in the API. This endpoint is typically used together with category listing and detail endpoints that allow admins to review categories before removing them.

This operation retrieves the current full category tree used by the shopping mall catalog, built primarily from the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma table and its associated hierarchy representation (for example, using the `shopping_mall_category_closures` table). It returns a denormalized, tree‑shaped structure that allows clients to render nested navigation menus and category pickers without multiple round‑trips.

The service reads all active category records and their parent–child relationships, then composes them into a hierarchical DTO type named `IShoppingMallCategoryTree`. This DTO is not a direct 1:1 mapping of a single Prisma table; instead, it is a read model that aggregates fields from `shopping_mall_categories` and may incorporate computed properties (such as depth or path) based on closure data. The root of the tree contains top‑level categories, each with a `children` array that recursively lists subcategories down to leaf nodes.

This is a read‑only operation that does not modify any data, so it is safe to expose broadly. The `authorizationActors` is set to an empty array (`[]`), indicating that it can be treated as a public endpoint, suitable for use by anonymous customers, authenticated customers, sellers, and any other actors that need to display the catalog structure. Implementations should still respect any visibility rules defined in related schemas (such as flags that mark categories as hidden) when constructing the tree, ensuring that only categories intended for public display appear in the result.

The endpoint does not require any parameters or request body. It simply returns the complete tree as it exists at the time of the request. For large catalogs, implementations may apply caching at the service or API gateway layer to avoid recomputing the tree on every request. Error handling should respond with appropriate HTTP status codes if the tree cannot be built due to internal errors, while still presenting a stable response schema (`IShoppingMallCategoryTree`) when successful.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full product category tree for the shopping mall catalog as a hierarchical structure derived from the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and its associated hierarchy representation.

This operation is designed for clients that need to display the entire category hierarchy in a single call, such as navigation menus, sidebars, or category selection dialogs. It composes data primarily from the `shopping_mall_categories` table, potentially leveraging closure or parent reference tables like `shopping_mall_category_closures` to reconstruct parent–child relationships. The response type `IShoppingMallCategoryTree` represents a denormalized view where each node includes its basic category information along with a list of child nodes, allowing consumers to render arbitrary depth trees.

The endpoint is read‑only and safe for public consumption. By setting `authorizationActors` to an empty array, the API indicates that no specific actor role is required to access this information. Nevertheless, the underlying implementation should honor any visibility or status fields defined in the category‑related Prisma models (for example, flags indicating that a category is disabled or internal) so that only categories meant to be exposed are included. This makes the endpoint suitable for both customer‑facing storefronts and seller‑facing tools that rely on the canonical category structure.

No request parameters or body content are required. Clients simply call the endpoint and receive the current category tree snapshot. If the catalog is very large or changes infrequently, service implementers are encouraged to apply caching strategies or precomputed views to optimize performance. In case of internal errors while building the tree, the service should return an appropriate server error status code while maintaining a consistent contract when the operation succeeds.
