operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the immediate child categories for a given parent category within the shopping_mall_categories Prisma model. It is designed to power catalog navigation UIs where, given a selected category, the client needs to show all direct children in the taxonomy so users can drill down step by step.

The underlying data primarily comes from the shopping_mall_categories table, which represents the global product category taxonomy. In typical schemas, each category row includes a unique identifier, business code, display name, and possibly a parent reference that indicates the tree structure. If a closure table such as shopping_mall_category_closures exists, the implementation would use it to efficiently find only those categories whose parent matches the given categoryId, but the API contract itself is expressed in terms of the logical parent–child relationship defined by shopping_mall_categories.

The response returns a collection of category summary objects optimized for navigation rather than fully detailed administrative editing. Each summary contains the core fields that a storefront or seller portal needs for rendering menus and category pickers. Pagination is not applied here because the number of child categories for a single parent is typically small and suitable for loading in a single request.

This endpoint is read-only and does not modify any category data. Authorization is kept open (public) so that both anonymous shoppers and authenticated users can discover categories. Business rules such as hiding blocked or unpublished categories will be enforced in the implementation based on flags defined in shopping_mall_categories and related visibility tables, but those rules are transparent to the caller; the caller simply receives the list of children that are currently visible.
operations.description:
Retrieve all immediate child categories of a given parent category from the shopping_mall_categories taxonomy.

This operation is centered on the shopping_mall_categories Prisma model, which stores the hierarchical category structure for the shoppingMall platform. Each category row typically has an identifier and meta fields such as display names, slugs, and flags that indicate visibility or availability. The given categoryId path parameter identifies the parent category whose direct children will be returned. The implementation locates the target parent in shopping_mall_categories and then queries for all categories that are directly beneath it in the hierarchy. If a closure or adjacency structure exists, the query filters to relationships that represent exactly one-level depth below the specified parent.

The endpoint is designed for storefront navigation scenarios such as expanding a menu tree, rendering category browse pages, or allowing sellers to select a subcategory for product placement. Only categories that are currently active and allowed to be shown in the catalog will be included in the result set, based on business flags stored in shopping_mall_categories or associated visibility tables like shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules. Hidden, deprecated, or blocked categories will be omitted so that clients never need to implement additional filtering logic.

Security-wise, this operation is intentionally public and does not require authentication because category browsing is a fundamental capability for both guest users and signed-in customers or sellers. However, the implementation can still apply actor-aware visibility rules (for example, categories only visible to certain seller tiers) by inspecting the authenticated principal when present. Since the endpoint is read-only, it does not alter any records in shopping_mall_categories or related tables, and it can be heavily cached for performance.

Error handling includes returning a not-found error when the specified categoryId does not correspond to any record in shopping_mall_categories that is accessible under current policies. If the parent exists but has no children, the operation will succeed and simply return an empty list. Clients are encouraged to call this endpoint together with higher-level category listing APIs (such as root-category listing) to build complete navigation trees.
operations.summary: List immediate child categories for a parent category from shopping_mall_categories.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent category in the shopping_mall_categories taxonomy whose immediate child categories should be retrieved.

responseBody.description: Array of category summaries representing the immediate children of the specified parent category.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full chain of ancestor categories for a given category within the shopping_mall_categories Prisma model, enabling clients to construct breadcrumb trails and understand where a specific category sits inside the global taxonomy.

The underlying data comes from shopping_mall_categories, which defines each category and its relationship to parent categories. In many schemas, a closure table such as shopping_mall_category_closures records all ancestor–descendant pairs along with their depths. The implementation can leverage such a table to efficiently fetch all ancestors of the specified categoryId, ordered from the root category down to the immediate parent. Regardless of the physical implementation, the API contract presents a simple ordered list of ancestor category summaries derived from shopping_mall_categories.

The response returns an ordered array of category summary objects representing each ancestor in the hierarchy. This is particularly useful for building SEO-friendly breadcrumbs, contextual navigation headers, and admin tools that need to show the full path to a category. The endpoint is read-only, does not alter any category data, and is safe to cache.

Authorization is public so that both anonymous and authenticated users can obtain the hierarchy context needed for navigation. Internally, the implementation will honor visibility flags in shopping_mall_categories and any related visibility control tables, omitting ancestors that should not be exposed while preserving a consistent path for the visible portion of the tree.
operations.description:
Retrieve all ancestor categories of a given category, ordered from the highest-level root down to the category’s immediate parent, based on the shopping_mall_categories taxonomy.

This operation focuses on the shopping_mall_categories Prisma model and the logical tree it defines. The categoryId path parameter identifies the target category. Using either a parent pointer in shopping_mall_categories or a dedicated closure table such as shopping_mall_category_closures, the implementation discovers every ancestor category that leads from the taxonomy root to the specified category. The results are sorted so that the first element is the root category, followed by each intermediate category, ending with the immediate parent of the target.

The primary use cases include constructing breadcrumb UI components, generating navigation aids on product listing and detail pages, and enabling admins and sellers to see the full path of a category when managing catalog assignments. Each ancestor is returned as a summary representation backed by fields from shopping_mall_categories, such as display name and any codes or slugs required for building URLs or internal links.

From a security perspective, the endpoint is intentionally accessible without authentication because breadcrumb and hierarchy information is typically public. Nevertheless, the implementation will apply business rules that may hide certain categories based on configuration, using columns in shopping_mall_categories or related visibility configuration tables. Ancestors that are blocked or not intended to be visible can be excluded to avoid leaking internal classification structures.

Error handling behavior includes returning a not-found error when the specified categoryId does not match any record in shopping_mall_categories that the caller is allowed to see. When a category exists but has no ancestors (for example, it is a root category), the endpoint successfully returns an empty array. Clients commonly invoke this operation alongside category detail retrieval so that both the category’s own data and its hierarchical context can be displayed together.
operations.summary: Get ordered ancestor categories for a category from shopping_mall_categories.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the category in shopping_mall_categories whose ancestor chain should be retrieved.

responseBody.description: Ordered list of ancestor category summaries from the root down to the immediate parent of the specified category.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: The target category must exist in shopping_mall_categories before its ancestor chain can be retrieved. Creating a category via this admin endpoint ensures a valid categoryId for ancestor lookup.

operations.specification:
Retrieve all descendant categories for a given category from the shopping_mall_categories table using the precomputed hierarchy stored in shopping_mall_category_closures.

This operation exposes a read-only view over the category taxonomy, allowing clients to obtain the full subtree rooted at a specific category identified by its UUID primary key id. It leverages the closure table shopping_mall_category_closures, where each row links an ancestor_category_id to a descendant_category_id along with a depth value, to efficiently fetch all descendants at any depth.

The endpoint is intended primarily for navigation, faceted search, and administrative tooling that needs to render category trees or compute affected scopes when business rules change. It does not modify any data. The response returns a collection of categories represented by the DTO type IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary, which is a summary view derived from the shopping_mall_categories model and may include key fields such as id, slug, name_en, status, sort_order, and is_leaf.

This operation must respect the deleted_at and status fields on shopping_mall_categories. Only categories that are not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null) and that are in a lifecycle state that should be visible (typically status = "active"; hidden or deprecated categories may be excluded based on business rules implemented in the service layer) are included in the results. The closure rows in shopping_mall_category_closures are assumed to be maintained by other write operations on the category tree and are not mutated here.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full list of descendant categories for a specific category based on the precomputed hierarchy stored in shopping_mall_category_closures.

The underlying shopping_mall_categories model represents the global product category taxonomy for the shoppingMall platform. Each category has an id primary key and optional parent_id that forms a tree structure, along with fields such as slug, name_en, description_en, status, sort_order, is_leaf, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The description explicitly states that categories support lifecycle states such as active, hidden, or deprecated, and that deleted_at is used as a soft deletion timestamp so that categories remain preserved for historical orders and catalog snapshots. This operation adheres to those semantics and only returns categories that are still logically available for use (for example, active and not soft-deleted).

To avoid recursive queries at runtime, the hierarchy is materialized in the shopping_mall_category_closures table. Each row links ancestor_category_id and descendant_category_id and stores a depth indicating the number of edges between them, with depth 0 representing a category as its own ancestor. This endpoint targets the closure table conceptually by selecting all rows whose ancestor_category_id matches the provided categoryId path parameter, then joining back to shopping_mall_categories to obtain category details for each descendant. Application logic may choose to exclude the ancestor itself (depth 0) or include it explicitly based on the intended UI behavior; this should be documented in the higher-level service documentation.

Security-wise, this operation is a read-only taxonomy lookup and typically returns non-sensitive data. It can therefore be exposed as a public endpoint (authorizationActors set to an empty array) so that both anonymous visitors and authenticated users can build navigations and filter UIs. Rate limiting can be applied at the API gateway if needed to mitigate abuse, but no authentication requirement is enforced here.

Validation rules include verifying that the supplied categoryId is a valid UUID string and that the referenced category exists and is not soft-deleted. If the category does not exist or is logically deleted, the implementation should respond with an appropriate not-found error. If the category exists but has no descendants, the operation should return an empty list with a successful status code. Error handling should distinguish between malformed identifiers (validation errors) and non-existent resources (404-style errors) so that clients can react appropriately.

This endpoint is often used together with other category-related operations such as a root-level category listing (for example, a PATCH /categories search endpoint) or a category details endpoint (for example, GET /categories/{categoryId}). Clients may first obtain a top-level list of categories, then call this descendants endpoint for a chosen node to progressively load deeper levels of the hierarchy without retrieving the entire tree at once.
operations.summary: Get all descendant shopping_mall_categories for a given category using the shopping_mall_category_closures hierarchy.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: UUID identifier of the ancestor category whose descendants should be retrieved.

responseBody.description: List of descendant categories under the specified ancestor category, represented as summary views of shopping_mall_categories.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A category must exist in shopping_mall_categories before its descendants can be queried; this POST creates the ancestor category identified later by categoryId.

operations.specification:
Search and retrieve localized representations of a specific category using the shopping_mall_category_localizations table, filtered and paginated according to client-provided criteria.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_category_localizations model, which stores localized names, descriptions, and optional SEO fields for each category and locale. Each record is linked to a category through shopping_mall_category_id and is uniquely identified per (shopping_mall_category_id, locale). The operation is scoped to a single category identified by its UUID id, supplied as a path parameter categoryId.

Clients send a structured search request in the body using the IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.IRequest DTO. This request may include filters such as locale codes, partial name search, inclusion or exclusion of soft-deleted localizations based on deleted_at, and paging and sorting options (for example, sort by locale or name). The service returns a paginated list of localization summaries of type IPageIShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.ISummary, containing fields such as id, locale, name, and key SEO fields, without exposing unnecessary internal metadata.

This is a read-only, search-style operation that does not modify records. It is meant for UI interfaces that need to list available translations for a category, for administrative panels managing translations, or for API consumers that need to inspect which locales are available for use.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of localized labels and descriptions for a given category from the shopping_mall_category_localizations table.

The shopping_mall_category_localizations model stores localized names, descriptions, and SEO text for categories. Each row is linked to a category through the shopping_mall_category_id foreign key referencing shopping_mall_categories, and it carries a locale field such as "en-US" or "ko-KR" along with localized name and optional description fields. The schema commentary emphasizes that the hierarchy itself is defined in shopping_mall_categories and shopping_mall_category_closures, while this table focuses purely on localization and SEO aspects. Each (shopping_mall_category_id, locale) pair is unique, ensuring that there is at most one localization per locale per category.

This PATCH operation accepts a request body of type IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.IRequest, which is designed to encapsulate search and pagination criteria for localizations. Typical filters include restricting results to specific locale codes, performing case-insensitive partial search on the name field, and controlling whether soft-deleted localizations (those with deleted_at set) are included or excluded. The request can also carry paging parameters such as page, pageSize, and sort instructions that align with the plainIndexes and ginIndexes defined on locale and name. The service implementation must validate that the provided categoryId corresponds to an existing category, rejecting the request with a not-found error if the category does not exist.

Because localization metadata is not inherently sensitive, this operation can typically be exposed as a public endpoint with no authentication requirement (authorizationActors is an empty array). However, in some deployments, administrative filtering may be applied so that only localizations with a category status of active or not soft-deleted are returned. The implementation must consistently respect the deleted_at semantics on shopping_mall_category_localizations: when deleted_at is not null, the localization is considered logically removed from active use but preserved for audit, and by default, such rows should be excluded from search results unless the request explicitly opts in.

The response is a paginated collection of localization summaries represented by IPageIShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.ISummary. Each item provides enough information to display the localized label, description, and possibly SEO text in management UIs, without exposing lower-level auditing or internal fields. Clients often use this endpoint in combination with a category details endpoint (for example, GET /categories/{categoryId}) and possibly with a create/update localization endpoint (POST/PUT on /categories/{categoryId}/localizations) to implement full translation management flows.
operations.summary: Search shopping_mall_category_localizations for a given category and return a paginated list of localization summaries.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the category whose localizations are being queried.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for retrieving category localizations linked to the specified category.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of localized representations of the category from shopping_mall_category_localizations, returned as summary DTOs.

operations.name: index

At least one localization row in shopping_mall_category_localizations must exist for the given category before it can be listed or searched; this POST creates a localization entry linked to the categoryId.

operations.specification:
Retrieve a single localized view of a ShoppingMall category from the shopping_mall_category_localizations table, identified by its parent category UUID and a concrete locale code.

This GET operation reads from the primary taxonomy structure defined in shopping_mall_categories and its subsidiary localization entries in shopping_mall_category_localizations. The path parameter categoryId corresponds to shopping_mall_categories.id (UUID primary key), while locale corresponds to shopping_mall_category_localizations.locale, which is unique in combination with shopping_mall_category_id.

The endpoint returns a single IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization entity representing the localized label, description, and SEO metadata for the specified locale. It does not modify any data and is therefore a pure read operation. Consumers typically call this API when rendering category navigation trees or detail pages in a specific language.

The implementation must enforce visibility according to the lifecycle and visibility fields defined in the underlying Prisma schema for both the category and its localization rows. Only categories that are considered active or visible by business rules, and localizations that are not logically hidden, should be returned. Error handling should distinguish between a non-existent category, a missing localization for the requested locale, and cases where either the category or the localization has been hidden according to those lifecycle rules.
operations.description:
Fetch a single localized representation of a ShoppingMall category for a specific locale.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_category_localizations table, which stores localized names, descriptions, and optional SEO fields for categories. The parent taxonomy structure is managed in shopping_mall_categories, where each row represents a global category node with fields such as slug, default language labels, sort ordering, and lifecycle fields that control whether the category is currently visible.

The localization model links to this taxonomy through the shopping_mall_category_id foreign key. Callers provide the categoryId path parameter, which maps directly to shopping_mall_categories.id, and the locale path parameter, which maps to shopping_mall_category_localizations.locale (for example, "en-US" or "ko-KR"). The pair (shopping_mall_category_id, locale) is unique as enforced by a unique index in the database, so at most one localization row will be returned for a given combination. The returned IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization payload includes the localized name, description, and SEO-related fields alongside standard audit metadata defined in the schema.

From a security and visibility perspective, this endpoint is intended for public storefront and client applications that need localized category labels for navigation and search. The implementation must ensure that only categories that are considered active or visible by business rules are exposed, and that localization rows that are logically hidden or archived by lifecycle flags are excluded from normal responses. If the underlying category exists but does not have a localization for the requested locale, the API should return a 404-style error indicating that no localization is available so that clients can decide whether to fall back to a default label from shopping_mall_categories.

This operation is typically used together with list-oriented endpoints such as a category tree loader and with administrative management APIs that allow creation and update of localizations. In failure scenarios, implementations should distinguish between three main cases: (1) the categoryId does not correspond to any row in shopping_mall_categories, (2) the category exists but there is no matching localization for the provided locale, and (3) either the category or the localization entry has been hidden or archived according to lifecycle rules. Each case should result in a clear error message so that client applications and monitoring tools can diagnose configuration issues in the taxonomy and localization setup.
operations.summary: Get a localized ShoppingMall category entry from shopping_mall_category_localizations by categoryId and locale.

A category localization row must exist in shopping_mall_category_localizations for the given categoryId and locale before it can be fetched.

operations.specification:
Create a new localized view of a ShoppingMall category by inserting a row into the shopping_mall_category_localizations table associated with an existing taxonomy node in shopping_mall_categories.

This POST operation uses the categoryId path parameter to identify the parent category (shopping_mall_categories.id) and expects a request body of type IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.ICreate. The body will contain fields such as locale, name, description, seo_title, and seo_description that define how the category should appear for a specific language or region.

On success, the operation returns the newly created IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization entity. The implementation must enforce the unique constraint across (shopping_mall_category_id, locale), preventing duplicate localizations for the same locale. It must also validate that the referenced category exists and is in an appropriate lifecycle state according to the schema’s fields before allowing creation of additional localizations. Attempting to create a localization for a category that is not visible or has been archived should be rejected according to business rules.
operations.description:
Register a new localized label and SEO metadata for a ShoppingMall category.

This operation writes to the shopping_mall_category_localizations table, which stores localized names, descriptions, and SEO properties for each category in a specific locale. The parent category is defined in shopping_mall_categories, a primary taxonomy model that includes fields such as slug, default language titles, and lifecycle-related fields that control whether a category is active and visible in the storefront.

The client supplies the categoryId as a path parameter, which is mapped to shopping_mall_categories.id, and sends a request body of type IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.ICreate. This DTO should include locale (for example, "en-US" or "ja-JP"), a localized name, and optional fields such as description, seo_title, and seo_description. On processing the request, the service validates that the referenced category exists, is in an allowed lifecycle state for adding localizations according to the schema’s lifecycle fields, and that the requested locale does not already have an existing localization row for this category.

From an authorization standpoint, this endpoint is restricted to administrative or catalog-management actors who are responsible for maintaining taxonomy and translations, such as admins or internal content managers. In this specification we model that using the generic "admin" actor. Storefront clients and public consumers should not call this endpoint directly; instead, they should rely on the public GET endpoints that expose already-published localizations.

The implementation should enforce input validation (non-empty locale codes, length constraints for textual fields, and reasonable limits for descriptions) and should set audit metadata such as created_at and updated_at as defined in the schema when inserting the row. In error cases, attempts to create a duplicate localization for the same (category, locale) pair should result in a conflict-style response, while attempts to localize a non-existent or lifecycle-ineligible category should result in a not-found or business-rule violation error.

This creation endpoint is intended to be used together with read endpoints such as GET /shoppingMall/categories/{categoryId}/localizations/{locale} and future update endpoints that manage changes to localized content over time. It supports the broader requirement that the platform provide a multilingual navigation experience without duplicating the structural category hierarchy in each language.
operations.summary: Create a new ShoppingMall category localization row in shopping_mall_category_localizations for a given category.

operations.specification:
Update a specific localization entry for a product category in the shopping_mall_category_localizations Prisma table. This operation targets the localization record identified by the parent category's identifier and the locale, and replaces its translatable fields (such as localized name or description) with the data provided by the client.

The endpoint is modeled as a standard PUT update operation: it requires both the category identifier and the locale in the path and an `IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.IUpdate` request body containing the mutable localization attributes. On success it returns the fully updated localization resource as `IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization` so that clients can immediately render the latest localized content.

From a business perspective, this operation is used by administrative tooling or internal content management flows to maintain localized catalog metadata. It assumes that the category itself already exists in the primary shopping_mall_categories table and that the locale being updated is valid according to platform rules.
operations.description:
Update a single category localization record for a given category and locale.

This PUT operation allows a privileged actor to modify the localized representation of a product category, such as its translated display name, marketing description, or SEO text, within the shopping mall catalog. The target record is located by combining the category identifier in the path with the locale string, ensuring that only the localization for that specific language/region variant is affected.

The request body follows the `IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.IUpdate` shape and is expected to contain only fields that are actually updatable for a localization record in the underlying Prisma model (for example localized title, subtitle, description, or other textual attributes). Immutable fields like primary keys or foreign keys to the category are not supplied by the client and remain unchanged. Validation rules such as maximum length, allowed characters, or required fields for particular locales are enforced in the service layer based on the Prisma schema and business requirements.

On success, the API responds with the updated localization object using the `IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization` DTO. This representation reflects the current persisted state including all localization fields and any system-managed audit information that is exposed via the DTO. If either the category or the locale-specific localization does not exist, the implementation should return an appropriate not-found error; if the caller lacks permission to modify catalog content, an authorization error should be returned. This operation is typically used together with list and create endpoints for category localizations in catalog management tools.
operations.summary: Update one category localization in shopping_mall_category_localizations

operations.specification:
Delete a specific localization entry for a product category from the shopping_mall_category_localizations Prisma table. This operation targets the localization identified by the parent category's identifier and the locale and removes that localized representation from the catalog so that it will no longer be used for rendering category information in that language.

The endpoint is modeled as a DELETE operation with only path parameters and no request body. It is intended for administrative or content-operations use cases where a previously configured localization must be removed entirely—for example when a locale is no longer supported or a category should fall back to default-language content.

From a data perspective, the implementation will look up the localization row using the provided category identifier and locale and then perform a permanent removal of that row from the shopping_mall_category_localizations table. Business rules may restrict deletion when a localization is required by policy; in such cases the handler should return a validation error instead of deleting.
operations.description:
Remove a single category localization record for a given category and locale.

This DELETE operation enables a privileged actor to permanently remove one localization variant of a product category. The combination of the category identifier and locale uniquely selects the targeted localization row in the shopping_mall_category_localizations table. Once deleted, clients will no longer be able to retrieve this localized representation and may fall back to other available locales according to client-side or server-side language negotiation rules.

The endpoint does not accept a request body; all necessary context is conveyed through the path parameters. The implementation is responsible for enforcing any platform-specific safeguards, such as preventing deletion of mandatory default locales, logging audit entries for governance, or ensuring that no dependent configuration is left in an inconsistent state. If the specified localization does not exist, the service should return an appropriate not-found response rather than silently succeeding.

On successful deletion, the operation can respond with an empty body or, depending on DTO design, with a simple confirmation payload. In this specification we declare no response body to keep the contract minimal, while still allowing the underlying service to throw domain-specific errors when authorization, validation, or referential integrity checks fail. This endpoint is typically used alongside create and update operations for category localizations in administrative catalog management workflows.
operations.summary: Delete one category localization from shopping_mall_category_localizations

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent product category whose localization entry is being deleted. This identifies the owning category in the shopping_mall_categories table.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Locale code of the localization record to delete (for example, "en-US" or "ko-KR"). Combined with the category identifier, this value uniquely identifies a localization row in the shopping_mall_category_localizations table.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A parent category must be created in shopping_mall_categories before any localization under that category can later be deleted.
The category localization row for the given categoryId and locale must be created in shopping_mall_category_localizations before it can be deleted via this endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation performs an advanced, paginated search over business policy definitions stored in the Prisma model `shopping_mall_business_policies`. It is intended for administrative and governance tooling inside the ShoppingMall platform so that operators can locate, review, and audit the various business policies that drive behavior such as refunds, review moderation, seller performance evaluation, and risk thresholds.

The operation follows the standard `index` pattern using HTTP PATCH for complex search criteria. The request body will reference `IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.IRequest`, which encapsulates filter fields (such as policy code, policy type, activation status, effective date ranges, and free‑text search over titles or descriptions), as well as pagination and sorting instructions. The response returns a paginated list of policy summaries using `IPageIShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.ISummary`, optimized for grid/list views in an admin console rather than full detail payloads.

This endpoint does not modify any data in `shopping_mall_business_policies`; it is strictly read‑only from a database perspective. It exists to support workflows like finding all active refund‑related policies, locating policies that will expire soon, or reviewing policies owned by a specific governance team. Only administrative actors should be able to call this endpoint because business policies directly influence platform‑wide behavior.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of business policies defined in the `shopping_mall_business_policies` table.

This operation is designed for administrative users who need to browse and search the catalog of business policies that govern the ShoppingMall platform. The underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_business_policies` is expected to contain fields such as a human‑readable name, a unique policy code, a policy category or type (for example, refunds, disputes, reviews, or seller performance), descriptive text that explains the rule in business terms, and metadata like activation flags and effective date ranges. The request body type `IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.IRequest` allows callers to filter by these attributes, perform keyword search over title or description text, and specify pagination parameters like page number, page size, and sort options.

From a security and governance standpoint, access to this endpoint must be restricted to administrative actors because business policies define how sensitive flows (such as cancellations, refunds, and disputes) behave. The `authorizationActors` field is therefore set to `["admin"]`, and the implementation should additionally ensure that only properly permissioned admin accounts can see certain policy categories if fine‑grained RBAC is configured. The endpoint itself remains read‑only: it does not create, update, or delete any records in `shopping_mall_business_policies`.

In terms of relationships, individual business policies may be connected conceptually to other entities such as policy versions, case SLA configurations, risk rules, or policy overrides. On success, it will return the full IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy representation of the stored policy, including generated identifiers and timestamps as defined in the Prisma schema.

This operation is typically invoked by administrative tooling in the ShoppingMall back office, and therefore is restricted to administrative actors. It acts as the entry point for creating new governance concepts that will later be referenced by orders, refunds, reviews, and risk subsystems across the platform.

This operation permanently deletes an existing business policy from the shopping_mall_business_policies table using its business-meaningful code identifier provided as a path parameter. The primary purpose is to allow administrative actors to remove obsolete or invalid logical policy definitions that are no longer applicable to the shoppingMall platform, such as outdated refund or review governance rules.

The endpoint consumes the policyCode as a globally unique business identifier that maps to the code field on the shopping_mall_business_policies model. The operation is expected to validate that the specified policy exists and that it is safe to delete, for example ensuring there are no active policy versions in shopping_mall_policy_versions that still reference this policy as the current governing rule set. If such constraints exist, the implementation may reject deletion with an appropriate error.

From a business perspective, this deletion is an administrative governance action and should be restricted to privileged admin users. The operation should be audited via separate admin audit logging mechanisms (e.g., shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs) but this endpoint itself only performs the primary removal of the policy definition record from shopping_mall_business_policies. Related read-only operations, such as listing policies or viewing policy versions, are expected to be implemented separately and can be used in conjunction with this delete operation during policy lifecycle management.
operations.description:
Delete an existing business policy identified by its unique policy code from the shopping_mall_business_policies table.

This operation targets the core business policy definition entity that conceptually lives in the shopping_mall_business_policies model. Each policy in that table typically represents a high-level governance concept such as refund handling rules, review moderation guidelines, seller performance thresholds, or risk evaluation frameworks. The policyCode path parameter corresponds to a business-facing unique code column on this model that is used consistently across administrative tools and documentation, making it safer and more readable than a raw UUID identifier.

When invoked, the backend must first resolve the incoming policyCode to an existing record in shopping_mall_business_policies. It should then perform domain-specific safety checks before deletion. For example, if there are policy versions in the shopping_mall_policy_versions table that are still marked as active or effective for live traffic, the system may either block deletion with a clear error or require that all such versions be retired or migrated to a different policy before this operation is allowed to succeed. This ensures that end-user behavior is never governed by a policy that has been physically removed from the system.

From a security and governance perspective, this is a high-privilege administrative operation. Only admin actors with appropriate authorization should be allowed to perform it, so the controller and service layer must enforce that the caller maps to an admin account in shopping_mall_admins with sufficient role assignments from shopping_mall_admin_roles and shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments. Additionally, implementations are strongly encouraged to record a detailed audit entry in the separate shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs snapshot table, capturing which admin removed which policy and when, along with the previous state of the record if required by compliance policies.

This delete endpoint is typically used together with companion read-only operations, such as a PATCH /businessPolicies search endpoint that lists policies, or a GET /businessPolicies/{policyCode} detail view. Administrators would locate a policy via those read endpoints, verify that no important versions remain active, and then call this DELETE /businessPolicies/{policyCode} endpoint for final removal. Error handling should clearly differentiate between non-existent policy codes (404 Not Found) and business-rule violations that prevent deletion (409 Conflict or similar).

This operation focuses on the versioned instances of business policies that are stored in the shopping_mall_policy_versions model. Each row in that table typically captures a concrete configuration of rules, thresholds, descriptive texts, and other parameters that define how a particular policy governs platform behavior at a specific point in time. Examples include a version of refund rules that defines maximum refundable amounts per order, grace periods after delivery, or conditions under which restocking fees apply.

The path parameter policyCode corresponds to a globally unique business identifier on the shopping_mall_business_policies model. The backend must first validate that a policy with this code exists and then use its primary key as a foreign key filter when querying shopping_mall_policy_versions. The request body is defined by IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.IRequest and should support common administrative filtering needs, such as searching by version status (draft, active, deprecated), effective date ranges, authoring admin, or free-text description keywords. It should also expose pagination controls (page index, page size) and sorting options (e.g., by createdAt, effectiveFrom, or status).

From an authorization standpoint, this is an administrative read operation that should be accessible only to admin actors defined in shopping_mall_admins with appropriate roles or permissions from shopping_mall_admin_roles and shopping_mall_admin_permissions. However, because it is strictly read-only and targets governance data, it can remain broadly available to most administrative roles responsible for operations, compliance, or risk management. Responses are returned in the IPageIShoppingMallPolicyVersion.ISummary format, which provides compact summary information for each version suitable for list views, while more detailed fields can be accessed via a dedicated detail endpoint for a single version. The underlying data is stored in two closely related tables: shopping_mall_business_policies, which represents the logical business policy definition (identified by a unique policy code), and shopping_mall_policy_versions, which stores individual versions for each policy. The path parameter policyCode maps to the code of a business policy in shopping_mall_business_policies, while versionCode uniquely identifies a specific version row in shopping_mall_policy_versions that belongs to that policy. The operation composes these two tables logically, but the primary focus for the response DTO is the version-level data from shopping_mall_policy_versions.

The endpoint is designed as a GET operation with no request body, returning a single IShoppingMallPolicyVersion entity that includes all configuration fields for that version (such as effective date ranges, status flags, rule sets, and textual descriptions). It is read-only and side-effect free. Authorization is restricted to administrative actors who are responsible for governance and policy management; regular customers or sellers are not expected to call this API directly. If the combination of policyCode and versionCode does not exist, the implementation must return a not-found error rather than a partial or empty object.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single business policy version record by its business-level identifiers policyCode and versionCode.

This operation reads from the shopping_mall_policy_versions table, which contains versioned instances of business policies specifying concrete rules, thresholds, and descriptive texts, and associates them with the logical business policy defined in shopping_mall_business_policies. The policyCode path parameter represents the globally unique business identifier of the policy, while versionCode represents a unique code for a specific version of that policy. Together, these codes allow governance and admin tools to look up exactly which policy configuration was in effect or is planned for a given version.

From a security and authorization standpoint, access to this endpoint should be limited to administrative or governance actors who are permitted to inspect detailed policy configuration. The authorizationActors field therefore includes only admin, and the implementation is expected to perform additional permission checks (such as role-based access control) before returning sensitive policy content. No authentication information is passed in the request body; instead, it is derived from the surrounding infrastructure (such as JWT or session middleware).

On the data level, the response body returns an IShoppingMallPolicyVersion object that mirrors the fields defined in the shopping_mall_policy_versions Prisma model, including metadata like effective and expiry timestamps, status markers (e.g., draft, active, deprecated), rule payloads, and human-readable explanations. The operation should validate that the version belongs to the specified policyCode via a foreign key or composite uniqueness constraint before returning data. If no matching row is found, the API should respond with an appropriate 404-style error, and clients should handle this by informing users that the requested policy version does not exist or may have been removed from the system.

This endpoint is typically used in conjunction with a list/search endpoint such as PATCH /businessPolicies/{policyCode}/versions, which would return paginated overviews of versions. After a client obtains a list of version codes, it can call this GET operation to drill down into a particular version for display in an admin configuration screen, for audit review, or for preparing change impact analysis.

The new version encapsulates a concrete set of rules, thresholds, states, and descriptive texts that define how the policy should behave at runtime, possibly including effective date ranges or activation flags.

The endpoint is implemented as a POST on /businessPolicies/{policyCode}/versions, taking an IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.ICreate request body that includes all required fields to create a new policy version under the specified parent policy. The service must validate that a business policy with the given policyCode exists and that any uniqueness constraints on version codes (for example, a composite @@unique([business_policy_id, version_code]) in shopping_mall_policy_versions) are respected. This ensures that within each policy, versionCode values do not collide and that the version timeline remains consistent.

Only administrative or governance actors are allowed to create new policy versions, since they directly affect how refunds, reviews, risk thresholds, or other governed behaviors function throughout the shopping mall platform. The operation does not accept or manipulate authentication credentials directly; instead, authorization is enforced by upstream middleware and by checking the caller’s roles against the governance requirements. On success, the endpoint returns the full IShoppingMallPolicyVersion representation of the newly created row so the caller can immediately see server-assigned identifiers, timestamps, and computed fields.

Create a new version of an existing business policy identified by policyCode.

This operation inserts a row into the shopping_mall_policy_versions table that is linked to the parent policy stored in shopping_mall_business_policies. The policyCode path parameter indicates which business policy the new version belongs to, while the request body carries all configuration fields required to define the behavior of that version, encapsulated in the IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.ICreate DTO. This can include effective start and end times, status values (such as draft, active, or deprecated), numeric thresholds, textual guidance, and any other rule payloads defined in the Prisma model.

The authorizationActors configuration therefore includes admin only, and the implementation is expected to enforce additional permission and audit logging logic based on shopping_mall_admins, shopping_mall_admin_roles, and related RBAC tables. If the policyCode does not correspond to an existing policy, the API should return a 404-style error. If uniqueness constraints for version codes are violated or other validation fails, a 400-style error should be returned with details of the offending fields. On success, the endpoint responds with the newly created IShoppingMallPolicyVersion object, allowing client applications to redirect users to a detail view or to continue workflow steps such as submitting the version for approval.

From the Prisma perspective, the primary entity affected is shopping_mall_policy_versions, which stores versioned instances of business policies with concrete rule sets. The path parameters resolve first to a row in shopping_mall_business_policies via policyCode, then to a child row in shopping_mall_policy_versions via versionCode scoped to that policy. The DTO IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.IUpdate will map directly onto updatable columns in shopping_mall_policy_versions, excluding identifying code columns and foreign keys. The response uses IShoppingMallPolicyVersion to return the complete, updated version snapshot including metadata such as effective periods or status if those are modeled in the schema.

This specification assumes that the operation enforces business rules such as preventing modification of locked or already-effective versions depending on fields defined in shopping_mall_policy_versions. Validation and authorization are handled at the service layer, but the API contract exposes a clear, strongly-typed editing surface for policy administrators to maintain business policies over time.
operations.description:
Update an existing business policy version under a specific business policy using the composite key of policyCode and versionCode.

This operation is designed for internal policy and governance tooling where administrators need to adjust the detailed rules of a business policy version. The target records live in the shopping_mall_business_policies and shopping_mall_policy_versions tables. The path parameter policyCode is a human-readable unique business identifier for the parent policy (for example a code representing a refund policy profile), and versionCode is a unique code scoped within that policy that identifies a concrete version instance. The operation locates the shopping_mall_business_policies row by its code, then resolves the corresponding shopping_mall_policy_versions row using the provided versionCode within that policy context.

The request body uses the DTO type IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.IUpdate, which exposes only mutable fields on shopping_mall_policy_versions. These may include fields representing textual descriptions, threshold values, percentage caps, boolean switches, and other configuration parameters that are defined as columns in the Prisma model. Immutable identifiers such as the version code itself or foreign keys back to shopping_mall_business_policies are not expected to be present in the update DTO and are instead derived from the path context. When implementing the service logic, the system should validate that the new values comply with any constraints expressed in the schema comments, such as numeric ranges, required enum domains, or flags controlling whether the version may be edited in its current lifecycle state.

Security-wise, this endpoint should normally be restricted to administrative or governance actors who are allowed to manage platform policies. In this specification, the authorizationActors field is set to ["admin"] to indicate that any authenticated admin can access it, with finer-grained RBAC enforced downstream using shopping_mall_admin_roles and shopping_mall_admin_permissions where applicable. Clients should treat this operation as an idempotent replacement of the mutable portion of the policy version: repeated calls with the same body will leave the resource in the same state.

The response body returns the updated policy version using the IShoppingMallPolicyVersion DTO. This gives callers immediate visibility into the persisted state after the update, including any server-side normalization or defaulting. Related operations that are typically used together include the creation of new versions (POST on the versions collection under a policy), retrieval of a single version (GET on this same path), and listing of all versions for a policy (PATCH on the versions collection). Together, these endpoints enable full lifecycle management of versioned business policies within the shopping mall platform.

operations.specification:
Permanently remove a specific business policy version record from the shopping_mall_policy_versions table, addressed via its parent business policy code and version code. This operation is associated with both shopping_mall_business_policies, which defines the logical policy, and shopping_mall_policy_versions, which stores its individual, versioned rule sets. The combination of policyCode and versionCode forms a composite functional identifier used to locate the target version row.

When invoked, the service will resolve policyCode to the corresponding shopping_mall_business_policies row, then locate the child shopping_mall_policy_versions row using versionCode in the scope of that policy. Upon successful authorization and validation, the version row is deleted from the database. If the Prisma schema defines referential constraints to other tables (for example, if orders, refunds, or risk cases reference specific policy versions), the implementation must either disallow deletion when such references exist or handle cascading behavior according to those schema comments and business rules.

This endpoint is intended for administrative clean-up or rollback scenarios where obsolete or incorrectly created policy versions need to be removed. It does not manage system-generated audit logs or snapshots; those remain governed by their own lifecycle rules and are not directly manipulated through this API.
operations.description:
Erase an existing business policy version under a specific business policy using the composite identifier formed by policyCode and versionCode.

The primary purpose of this operation is to give governance or platform operations staff the ability to remove outdated or invalid business policy versions from the configuration surface of the shopping mall platform. The underlying data resides in the shopping_mall_policy_versions table and is linked to its parent definition in shopping_mall_business_policies via a foreign key. The path parameters follow the business-friendly identification scheme: policyCode uniquely identifies the logical policy across the marketplace (global scope), while versionCode uniquely identifies the specific version within that policy (scoped to the parent).

On invocation, the backend will use these codes to locate the corresponding database row. Before performing the deletion, business logic should verify that removal is safe based on whatever lifecycle or reference integrity rules are expressed in the Prisma schema comments. For example, if a policy version is marked as currently effective or historically referenced by past orders, cancellations, or refunds, the implementation may reject the erase operation with an appropriate error. Any audit logging of the administrative action itself should be handled by separate infrastructure, such as shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs, and is not exposed as a manual write API.

Security considerations require that only privileged administrative actors can perform this operation. Accordingly, authorizationActors is set to ["admin"], indicating that it is not accessible to general users, customers, or sellers. The endpoint does not accept a request body and, in this specification, does not return a response body on success; clients should interpret a successful HTTP status as confirmation that the policy version has been removed. Related endpoints include the version update operation on the same path, and collection-level operations for creating or listing policy versions under a given policy.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered, paginated list of risk rule configurations from the shopping_mall_risk_rules Prisma table. It is designed for administrative risk and governance users to search and review the rules that drive the platform’s risk engine.

The underlying Prisma model shopping_mall_risk_rules is expected to define key fields such as a primary key identifier, a stable business identifier in rule_code, classification attributes like scope and severity, one or more configuration payload fields (for example a JSON-encoded expression), descriptive text, temporal fields such as effective_from and effective_until, and lifecycle audit timestamps. This endpoint exposes those fields through a summary DTO while allowing callers to filter by scope, severity, enabled flag, effective date ranges, and text search on rule_code or name.

The API uses the ShoppingMall service prefix in DTO names, returning a paginated summary collection IPageIShoppingMallRiskRule.ISummary and accepting a complex search request body IShoppingMallRiskRule.IRequest. It is read-only and does not modify any rows in shopping_mall_risk_rules. Implementations may optionally filter out records that have been logically retired if the schema defines a dedicated field for that; otherwise, filtering is performed only on fields that actually exist in the model (for example enabled flags and effective date ranges).
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of risk rule configurations stored in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table for administrative analysis.

This operation reads from the Prisma model shopping_mall_risk_rules, which represents configuration of risk evaluation rules used by the risk engine to flag suspicious activity, high-risk orders, or risky accounts. Each row typically contains a stable business identifier in rule_code, a human-readable name, a scope value indicating the entity type being evaluated (such as "account", "order", "payment", "seller", or "session"), a severity level (such as "low", "medium", "high", or "critical"), and one or more configuration payload fields (for example expression_json) that store the JSON-encoded logic or parameters for the rule. Additional columns such as description, region-related applicability fields, effective_from, effective_until, created_at, and updated_at provide narrative context and temporal or audit information.

Callers use this endpoint to search and browse risk rules with rich filtering. The request body type IShoppingMallRiskRule.IRequest should support criteria such as exact or partial matching on rule_code and name, filtering by scope and severity, limiting results to rules that are currently effective based on effective_from and effective_until, and flags to filter by an enabled/disabled indicator exposed by the schema. It can also expose options for text-style search on the name field aligned with configured indexes, and optional toggles to include or exclude any rules that have been logically retired if the Prisma model defines a dedicated retirement or soft-delete field. Pagination and sorting options (for example by created_at, updated_at, severity, or rule_code) are included so that large rule sets can be navigated efficiently in an admin UI.

Security-wise, the response exposes internal risk engine configuration and therefore should be restricted to administrative or governance actors only. The authorizationActor is set to "admin" and the authorizationActors array contains ["admin"] to indicate that only admin users may call this endpoint. The implementation should still enforce fine‑grained access control and audit access through separate logging mechanisms, especially because misuse or misinterpretation of risk rules can have significant financial and compliance impact.

This operation is typically used in combination with the detail retrieval endpoint GET /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules/{ruleCode}, which provides a full view of a single rule including its identifier, configuration payload, and descriptive metadata. A common workflow is for an admin to call PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules to locate rules matching a particular scope, severity, or identifier, and then follow up with GET /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules/{ruleCode} to inspect a specific rule in depth before editing it through a separate configuration channel or external tool. Error handling should clearly indicate invalid filter combinations (such as malformed date ranges) and return appropriate validation messages when the request body does not conform to IShoppingMallRiskRule.IRequest.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping_mall_risk_rules configurations for admins.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of risk rule summaries from shopping_mall_risk_rules that match the provided search criteria.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full configuration details of a single risk rule identified by its stable business code from the shopping_mall_risk_rules Prisma table. Instead of addressing the rule by its internal UUID primary key, the endpoint uses rule_code, which is expected to be globally unique according to the model’s unique index.

The shopping_mall_risk_rules table is expected to define rule_code as the stable business identifier for the risk rule (for example, "high_refund_rate", "multiple_failed_logins", or "suspicious_address_mismatch"). Along with rule_code, the model normally contains fields such as a human-readable name, a scope value, a severity level, one or more configuration payload fields (such as a JSON-encoded expression describing the rule logic), descriptive text, an enabled/disabled indicator, optional region-related applicability fields, effective date ranges, and audit timestamps. This endpoint returns a detailed DTO IShoppingMallRiskRule that exposes all relevant fields so that risk, governance, or admin users can inspect how the rule behaves, where it applies, and whether it is currently active.

The path parameter {ruleCode} is mapped to the rule_code column and is documented as globally unique (as enforced by a unique index on [rule_code] in the Prisma schema), ensuring that the lookup is unambiguous without requiring additional parent context such as an owning tenant. The operation is read-only and does not modify any data in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table. Implementations may optionally treat logically retired rules specially if the schema defines a soft-delete or retirement field; otherwise, they should simply return the matching row as IShoppingMallRiskRule or a not-found error if no such rule exists.

DTO type naming follows the ShoppingMall service prefix, so the response uses IShoppingMallRiskRule as the main detailed entity type. Consumers typically use this endpoint to power rule detail views in admin risk dashboards, where the full configuration payload and narrative description need to be visible for verification and audits.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed configuration information for a single risk rule identified by its rule_code from the shopping_mall_risk_rules table.

This operation targets the Prisma model shopping_mall_risk_rules, which stores configuration of risk evaluation rules used by the platform’s risk engine. The key field used for lookup is rule_code, defined as a stable business identifier and constrained to be unique by a unique index on [rule_code] in the schema. This means each value of rule_code (such as "high_refund_rate" or "multiple_failed_logins") corresponds to at most one row, and the path parameter {ruleCode} directly maps to this column. Other important columns normally include a human-readable name shown in admin tools; scope, which indicates the entity type the rule evaluates (for example, account, order, payment, seller, or session); severity, which represents the business impact level (low, medium, high, or critical); and one or more configuration payload fields (commonly a JSON-encoded expression) that represent the rule logic and parameters.

When an admin calls this endpoint with a specific ruleCode, the system queries shopping_mall_risk_rules for a row where rule_code equals the provided value and returns it as IShoppingMallRiskRule, or responds with a not-found error if no matching rule exists. The response body schema should include all relevant fields from the table: identifiers for uniqueness and cross‑references, rule_code and name for identification, scope and severity for classification, the configuration payload for the actual risk logic, description for human-readable explanation, any enabled/disabled indicator to show whether the rule is currently active in the risk engine, any region-related applicability field, and effective_from / effective_until for temporal scoping. It should also expose created_at and updated_at to support auditing and change tracking, and may include flags or derived fields that interpret these raw values.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative or governance actors because it reveals internal risk rule logic and configuration that could be abused if exposed more broadly. Therefore, authorizationActor is set to "admin" and authorizationActors is ["admin"]. Typically, this endpoint is used in tandem with PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules, where an admin first locates a list of rules, then selects a particular ruleCode and follows up with GET /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules/{ruleCode} to inspect the full configuration. Error handling should distinguish between cases where no rule exists for the given ruleCode (returning a not-found error) and unexpected failures, while also validating that the supplied ruleCode string is within expected business constraints.
operations.summary: Get detailed configuration of a single shopping_mall_risk_rules entry by its rule_code for admins.

parameters.name: ruleCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target risk rule in shopping_mall_risk_rules (global scope).

responseBody.description: Detailed risk rule configuration corresponding to the provided ruleCode from shopping_mall_risk_rules.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new risk evaluation rule in the shoppingMall_risk_rules Prisma table. It allows risk and governance administrators to define how the risk engine should flag suspicious activity, high‑risk orders, or risky accounts. Each rule persists configuration such as a unique business rule code, human‑readable name, description, rule type, severity, activation flags, and serialized condition/threshold definitions that the risk engine evaluates at runtime.

The API client supplies the complete rule definition via the request body mapped to IShoppingMallRiskRule.ICreate, which mirrors the key configurable columns of shopping_mall_risk_rules (for example: ruleCode, name, description, ruleType, severityLevel, isActive, conditionExpression, evaluationScope, and optional metadata). The backend validates uniqueness constraints (e.g., ruleCode must be globally unique), required fields, allowed enumeration values, and structural correctness of any expression or JSON condition payloads before persisting the rule.

On success, the endpoint returns the newly created rule as IShoppingMallRiskRule, reflecting the stored state in shopping_mall_risk_rules including generated identifiers and timestamps. This operation is intended for internal governance tools and is therefore restricted to administrative actors. Related endpoints include the PUT /riskRules/{ruleCode} operation for updating an existing rule and read‑only reporting or analytics APIs that consume the configured rules when evaluating orders and accounts.
operations.description:
Create a new risk evaluation rule record in the shoppingMall_risk_rules table for use by the platform risk engine.

This operation accepts a complete rule definition through the IShoppingMallRiskRule.ICreate DTO, which is designed based on the the shopping_mall_risk_rules Prisma model. Typical fields include a business‑meaningful ruleCode that acts as the primary external identifier, a human‑readable name and description explaining the rule’s purpose, a ruleType or category field indicating what kind of behavior it targets (for example, account, order, payment, or login risk), a severity or riskLevel that informs downstream handling such as blocking versus manual review, and an isActive flag signaling if the rule should be considered during evaluation.

The implementation must enforce database‑level and business‑level validation rules derived from the shopping_mall_risk_rules schema comments. For instance, ruleCode must be unique across all rules; human‑readable text fields have reasonable length limits; and conditionExpression or conditionJson fields must conform to the expression language or JSON schema used by the risk engine. If any validation fails, the API should return a clear error indicating which constraint was violated, ensuring administrators can correct misconfigurations before deployment.

From a security perspective, the endpoint is restricted to privileged administrative actors because changes to risk rules can directly affect fraud detection, customer experience, and financial exposure. Authorization middleware should ensure only admins with appropriate permissions can call this endpoint, and audit logging should record who created each rule and when. This write operation complements read‑only discovery APIs that list or inspect existing risk rules and the update endpoint PUT /riskRules/{ruleCode}, which modifies existing records while preserving historical auditability depending on the broader data retention strategy.
operations.summary: Create a new risk evaluation rule in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table.

responseBody.description: The newly created risk evaluation rule as stored in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table.

operations.name: create

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing risk evaluation rule stored in the shoppingMall_risk_rules Prisma table, identified by its unique ruleCode. It is used by governance and risk administrators to adjust thresholds, enable or disable rules, refine conditions, or reclassify severity as fraud patterns and business requirements evolve over time.

The rule to update is selected by the path parameter {ruleCode}, which corresponds to a globally unique business identifier column on shopping_mall_risk_rules. The request body uses the IShoppingMallRiskRule.IUpdate DTO, representing the subset of columns that may be modified, such as name, description, severityLevel, ruleType, isActive, conditionExpression, evaluationScope, and associated metadata. The implementation must read the existing record, apply validated changes, and persist the updated row while honoring any NOT NULL constraints, enumerated values, and length limits documented in the Prisma schema comments.

On success, the API returns the updated rule as IShoppingMallRiskRule, reflecting the latest stored state in shopping_mall_risk_rules. If no rule exists for the supplied ruleCode, the operation must return a not‑found error instead of silently creating a new rule. This endpoint is tightly coupled with the POST /riskRules creation endpoint and any read‑only listing or inspection APIs, forming the core management surface for the risk configuration layer.
operations.description:
Update an existing risk evaluation rule in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table, identified by its unique ruleCode.

This operation targets a single record in the shopping_mall_risk_rules model using the {ruleCode} path parameter. The path parameter maps to the ruleCode column, which is a human‑readable, globally unique business key that risk and governance users work with in consoles and documentation. Using ruleCode instead of an internal numeric or UUID surrogate key makes the API more expressive and less error‑prone for administrators managing large sets of rules.

The request body conforms to IShoppingMallRiskRule.IUpdate, a DTO aligned with the updatable columns on the shopping_mall_risk_rules Prisma model. Typical fields include user‑visible attributes such as name and description, ruleType and severityLevel, activation flags like isActive, and condition definitions (for example, conditionExpression or JSON structures describing thresholds and predicates). The service implementation must validate these values against the underlying schema constraints, including string length, allowed enumeration members, and any expression language or JSON schema used by the risk engine. Business rules may restrict certain transitions, such as preventing changes to immutable fields or requiring additional review when raising severity.

From a security and governance standpoint, only administrative actors should be allowed to modify risk rules, because erroneous changes could weaken fraud detection or cause excessive false positives. The endpoint should therefore be protected by admin‑level authorization checks and should integrate with audit logging facilities so that each change—including the previous and new values—is traceable. If the specified ruleCode does not correspond to an existing row, the API must return a clear not‑found error instead of creating a rule implicitly, so that callers cannot accidentally bypass the dedicated creation flow provided by POST /riskRules.
operations.summary: Update an existing risk evaluation rule in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table by ruleCode.
