parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target risk rule (global scope). This maps to the ruleCode column in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table and uniquely identifies a single risk evaluation rule across the platform.

requestBody.description: Updated properties of the risk evaluation rule, aligned with the shopping_mall_risk_rules model.

responseBody.description: The updated risk evaluation rule after persisting changes to the shopping_mall_risk_rules table.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A risk rule must first be created via POST /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules so that a record with the given business ruleCode exists in shopping_mall_risk_rules before it can be updated by ruleCode.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently disables a specific risk evaluation rule in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` Prisma table, identified by its stable business identifier `rule_code`. Instead of physically removing the row, it marks the rule as logically retired by setting the `deleted_at` timestamp and also ensures the rule is no longer active in runtime evaluation by setting `is_enabled` to false.

The rule to be disabled is selected via its `rule_code`, which is globally unique as enforced by a unique index on the `rule_code` column. The handler must look up the row where `rule_code` matches the provided path parameter, confirm that `deleted_at` is currently null, and then update the record to set `deleted_at` to the current timestamp and `is_enabled` to false. If no matching rule is found or the rule is already logically retired, the operation should respond with an appropriate not-found error.

This endpoint is designed for administrative governance of the risk engine configuration. It must validate that the rule is not currently bound by any legal hold or compliance constraint before disabling it, and it should be used together with administrative listing and detail endpoints on the same `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table that allow inspection of rule definitions before deactivation.
operations.description:
Disable (logically retire) a specific risk rule in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table by its stable business code.

This operation targets configuration rows in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` Prisma model, which represents risk evaluation rules used by the risk engine to flag suspicious activity, high-risk orders, or risky accounts. Each record has a primary key `id` (a UUID) and a stable business identifier `rule_code` used by risk services and reporting, such as "high_refund_rate", "multiple_failed_logins", or "suspicious_address_mismatch". The table also includes fields like `scope`, `severity`, `expression_json`, `description`, `applies_to_countries`, `effective_from`, `effective_until`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and a nullable `deleted_at` used for logical retirement of rules.

When this DELETE endpoint is called with a given `ruleCode` in the path, the implementation must resolve that value against the `rule_code` column, leveraging the unique index defined on `[rule_code]`. Instead of physically deleting the row, the business logic must treat "erase" as a logical retirement by setting `deleted_at` to the current timestamp and forcing `is_enabled` to false, ensuring that the risk engine no longer evaluates this rule even if its effective date window would otherwise include the current time. If the combination of `rule_code` and `deleted_at IS NULL` does not yield a row, the handler should return a not-found response so callers understand there is no active rule to disable.

From a security perspective, only privileged administrative actors responsible for risk management and governance should be able to call this operation. The `authorizationActors` value indicates that this endpoint is restricted to `admin` users; runtime authorization checks should ensure that only administrators with appropriate permissions can disable rules, because misconfiguration could materially change risk posture. Before updating the record, the implementation may also check related compliance or legal-hold models to avoid retiring rules that are required to remain in effect.

This operation is typically used after administrators review the rule via a corresponding detail endpoint like `GET /riskRules/{ruleCode}` and possibly test or inspect rule behavior via `PATCH /riskRules/evaluate`. Error handling should clearly distinguish between nonexistent or already-retired rules (404) and unexpected server errors when updating the row. The response returns the updated rule entity so that callers can confirm the final `is_enabled` and `deleted_at` state immediately after the operation completes.
operations.summary: Logically retire a ShoppingMall risk rule record in shopping_mall_risk_rules by rule_code.

parameters.name: ruleCode
parameters.description: Stable business identifier of the risk rule to disable (global scope), matching the `rule_code` column in `shopping_mall_risk_rules`, such as `high_refund_rate` or `multiple_failed_logins`. This code is globally unique and is the primary business key for identifying a risk rule configuration.

responseBody.description: The risk rule record from `shopping_mall_risk_rules` after being logically retired, including updated `is_enabled` and `deleted_at` fields so that administrators can verify the rule is no longer active in risk evaluation.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A risk rule must first be created in shopping_mall_risk_rules so that a record with the specified rule_code exists and can subsequently be logically retired by this DELETE operation.

operations.specification:
This operation evaluates one or more hypothetical or real-world scenarios against the configured risk rules defined in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` Prisma table. It does not create, update, or delete any risk-rule records; instead, it reads active rules and applies their `expression_json` logic to an input payload that describes the entity under evaluation (such as an account, order, payment, seller, or session) and returns computed risk results.

The implementation must query `shopping_mall_risk_rules` for rules that are currently active: `is_enabled = true`, `deleted_at IS NULL`, and whose `effective_from` and `effective_until` date range includes the evaluation time, if those timestamps are present. It may filter rules by the requested evaluation scope, which is conceptually aligned with the `scope` column in the table (e.g., "account", "order", "payment", "seller", or "session"). For each applicable rule, the engine interprets the `expression_json` JSON string (which encodes rule logic, thresholds, and windows) against the provided evaluation context and produces a structured response containing per-rule outcomes and overall aggregated severity.

This endpoint is read-only with respect to the risk-rule configuration; it exists to support administrative testing of rule behavior, internal risk services wanting synchronous evaluations, or simulation tools that assess potential changes before rules are updated in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table. The request and response bodies are modeled as dedicated DTOs that represent the evaluation context and output, decoupled from the underlying table schema while still referencing fields like `rule_code`, `scope`, and `severity` as part of the result projection.
operations.description:
Evaluate configured risk rules from the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table against a provided context and return detailed rule-level and aggregated risk results.

The `shopping_mall_risk_rules` Prisma model stores risk evaluation rules used by the risk engine to flag suspicious activity across accounts, orders, payments, sellers, and sessions. Each record includes a globally unique `rule_code`, a human-readable `name`, a `scope` that indicates the domain (such as "account", "order", "payment", "seller", or "session"), a `severity` level (for example "low", "medium", "high", "critical"), and an `expression_json` field that encodes the rule logic and parameters in JSON form. Additional optional fields such as `description`, `applies_to_countries`, `effective_from`, and `effective_until` allow the platform to document what the rule detects, where it applies, and during what time window it should be considered, while `is_enabled`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` govern its lifecycle.

When a caller invokes `PATCH /riskRules/evaluate`, the implementation must read from this table rather than modifying it. The handler filters rules to those that are currently active, which generally means `is_enabled` is true, `deleted_at` is null, and the current evaluation timestamp falls within any configured `effective_from` and `effective_until` range when those fields are not null. The request body modeled by `IShoppingMallRiskRuleEvaluation.IRequest` provides the evaluation scope, contextual data such as account or order identifiers, monetary amounts, country codes, and any other signals needed by the expressions encoded in `expression_json`. For each applicable rule, the engine interprets its JSON logic against the context and determines whether the rule is triggered, what severity contribution it has, and any explanatory messages.

From a security and governance standpoint, this operation should be restricted to internal risk services and authorized administrative tooling, indicated here by the `admin` authorization actor. It does not manage user authentication or sessions and does not change configuration; instead, it is used to power risk dashboards, manual case review tooling, and automated enforcement flows that need synchronous risk evaluation. Related operations include administrative CRUD endpoints on `shopping_mall_risk_rules` (for creating and updating rules) and risk case management APIs that open or update risk cases when evaluations indicate severe conditions.

Error handling must distinguish between validation errors in the request context (for example, missing required attributes for the chosen scope) and internal errors interpreting `expression_json`. Validation failures should result in a 400-level response with clear diagnostics, whereas internal interpretation errors should be logged and surfaced as 500-level responses without leaking sensitive implementation details in the message body.
operations.summary: Evaluate active ShoppingMall risk rules from shopping_mall_risk_rules against a supplied context.

requestBody.description: Risk evaluation context and parameters, including scope (such as account, order, payment, seller, or session) and the domain-specific attributes that rules from `shopping_mall_risk_rules` will inspect when interpreting their `expression_json` definitions.

responseBody.description: Detailed risk evaluation result including per-rule outcomes (identified by `rule_code`, `scope`, and `severity` from `shopping_mall_risk_rules`) and any aggregated risk scores or severity indicators for the evaluated context.

operations.name: evaluate

prerequisites.description: At least one risk rule must be created in shopping_mall_risk_rules before evaluations can yield meaningful results for the given account, order, payment, seller, or session context.

operations.specification:
This operation provides a high-level system overview dashboard for the shoppingMall platform, aggregating key performance indicators and health metrics across multiple Prisma tables. Rather than mapping directly to a single table, it composes data from core transactional entities such as `shopping_mall_orders`, `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, and other snapshot/analytics models.

The endpoint returns a denormalized dashboard DTO `IShoppingMallSystemOverviewDashboard` that consolidates marketplace-wide statistics such as total orders, revenue summaries, active customer/seller counts, refund and dispute volumes, payment and shipping performance indicators, and risk/compliance highlights. These values are computed by querying and aggregating multiple underlying models instead of exposing raw rows.

Implementation-wise, the service layer will execute several read-only queries in parallel, for example:
- Summaries from `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats` for recent days
- Aggregated seller metrics from `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`
- Aggregated customer activity from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`
- High-level KPIs from `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`
- Refund/dispute trends from `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`

The endpoint is designed as a read-only GET operation suitable for admin dashboards and operational monitoring tools.
operations.description:
Retrieve a consolidated system overview dashboard for the shoppingMall platform.

This operation exposes a read-only dashboard that summarizes the current state of the marketplace by aggregating metrics from several Prisma models including order-related snapshots, seller and customer daily statistics, and platform-level KPI snapshot tables. It does not return raw rows from tables like `shopping_mall_orders` or `shopping_mall_seller_earnings`; instead, it exposes curated metrics such as order volumes, revenue summaries, refund and dispute rates, active actor counts, and high-level performance indicators in a single DTO `IShoppingMallSystemOverviewDashboard` optimized for admin UI consumption.

From a security and authorization standpoint, the data exposed by this endpoint is sensitive because it contains global business KPIs, revenue information, and operational performance metrics. Access must therefore be restricted to administrative actors only, represented here by the `admin` authorization actor. The implementation should rely on the platform's centralized authentication and authorization mechanisms to ensure that only properly authenticated admin users can call this endpoint.

In terms of its relationship to the underlying database entities, the endpoint uses snapshot-style tables such as `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`, `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats`, `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`, and `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` as primary sources. These models are designed specifically for analytics and reporting, so the API can query relatively small, pre-aggregated datasets instead of scanning large transactional tables on every dashboard request.

No request parameters are required, and the operation does not support filtering or pagination because its purpose is to provide a single aggregated view "at a glance". Any time-bucketing (for example, showing metrics for the last 7 or 30 days) should be encapsulated by the service logic and reflected in the `IShoppingMallSystemOverviewDashboard` fields. Errors returned by this endpoint should follow the platform-standard error model, with particular care for permission errors (when a non-admin attempts access) and transient backend failures when underlying snapshot tables are unavailable.
operations.summary: Get an aggregated system overview dashboard derived from shoppingMall analytics and snapshot tables

responseBody.description: Aggregated system overview metrics for the shoppingMall platform, composed from multiple analytics and snapshot Prisma tables into a single dashboard view.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation returns aggregated geographic statistics for the shoppingMall marketplace by computing metrics grouped by geographic dimensions such as country and region. It primarily composes data from reference and analytics Prisma models including `shopping_mall_countries`, `shopping_mall_regions`, `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies`, `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`, and possibly `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` when geo-segmented metrics are available.

The endpoint exposes a DTO `IShoppingMallGeographyStatistics` that contains an array of region-level summaries. Each summary may include fields such as country/region identifiers (derived from `shopping_mall_countries` and `shopping_mall_regions`), order and revenue statistics, shipping performance metrics, payment method distributions, refund/dispute ratios, and other geo-segmented KPIs derived from the snapshot tables. This data is analytical and not tied to CRUD operations on any single table.

Implementation-wise, the service will perform read-only aggregation queries that GROUP BY geographic attributes, leveraging indexes and pre-aggregated snapshot models where available. The result is a compact structure optimized for visualization on maps or regional comparison charts in admin reporting dashboards.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated geographic statistics for orders, revenue, and operational performance across different countries and regions in the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint enables administrative users and analysts to understand how the marketplace performs across various geographies. It reads from master data tables such as `shopping_mall_countries` and `shopping_mall_regions` to obtain stable geographic identifiers and labels, and joins them with snapshot and analytics tables including `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`, and `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` to compute metrics by country and region. These statistics can include order counts, gross merchandise value, average order value, shipping SLAs, on-time delivery ratios, and refund or dispute rates, all grouped by geographic dimension.

From an authorization perspective, this data is business-sensitive because it exposes regional revenue and operational performance details. The endpoint therefore restricts access to the `admin` actor, relying on the platform's existing authentication and authorization infrastructure for enforcement. The operation is strictly read-only and does not modify any underlying Prisma models; it is intended for dashboard views, internal reporting, and decision support tools.

Unlike CRUD-style operations, this API does not support pagination of discrete records. Instead, it returns a single analytical structure `IShoppingMallGeographyStatistics` that contains region-level aggregates. Optional query parameters for time range or segmentation could be added in the future, but in this specification the endpoint has no request parameters or body and always returns the default aggregation window defined by business requirements (for example, last 30 days). Any backend errors or permission failures should be surfaced through the platform-standard error response format.
operations.summary: Get aggregated geographic performance and revenue statistics grouped by country and region for the shoppingMall platform

responseBody.description: Aggregated geographic statistics for the shoppingMall marketplace, grouped by country and region, suitable for map visualizations and regional performance dashboards.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves high-level statistical and configuration information about business policies defined in the Prisma table `shopping_mall_business_policies` and closely related policy-configuration tables such as `shopping_mall_policy_versions`, `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, and `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`. The endpoint is read-only, intended for dashboards and analytics views, not for direct policy management.

The operation returns an aggregated, denormalized structure rather than raw table rows. It exposes counts of active policies, distributions by policy type, counts of currently effective policy versions, and summary indicators such as how many policies are currently overridden or tied to special SLA configurations. It may also include simple trend indicators that can be computed from snapshot or history tables where available.

Because this endpoint serves as a statistics/overview API, it does not accept complex search criteria in the body; instead it focuses on a fixed set of metrics for administrative and governance reporting. The result is packaged into a DTO named `IShoppingMallPolicyStatistics`, which is derived conceptually from `shopping_mall_business_policies` and its related configuration tables but optimized for fast dashboard consumption.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistical information about business policies configured in the shopping mall platform.

This endpoint is conceptually based on the `shopping_mall_business_policies` table, which stores logical business policy definitions governing behaviors such as refunds, reviews, seller performance, risk thresholds, and other governance rules. Each row in that table typically represents a single named policy domain with attributes describing its purpose, scope, and the category of behavior it controls. In addition, it leverages related tables like `shopping_mall_policy_versions`, which hold versioned instances of those policies with concrete rule values and validity periods, and `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, which configure service-level agreements for cases subject to specific policies.

The response aggregates these underlying entities into high-level statistics suitable for operations, governance, or compliance dashboards. Typical metrics include the total number of business policies, how many policies are currently active versus retired, counts of policies by type or domain (for example, refund-related versus review-related), and how many effective policy versions are in force at the moment. The endpoint can also expose counts of case-SLA configurations linked to policies, as well as how many policies currently have explicit overrides recorded in `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`.

From a security standpoint, policy configuration and statistics usually contain sensitive governance information that should not be exposed to general users. Therefore, the endpoint is restricted to administrative actors only, indicated by `authorizationActors: ["admin"]`. Implementations should ensure the calling admin has sufficient permission to view governance metrics, and any additional filtering based on admin roles can be applied within business logic using RBAC information from tables like `shopping_mall_admin_roles` if needed.

The operation is read-only and implemented as a simple GET without a request body. It must not modify any data in `shopping_mall_business_policies`, `shopping_mall_policy_versions`, `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, or `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`. In error cases, such as database connectivity issues or misconfigured aggregation queries, the API should return appropriate HTTP error codes (for example, 500) and not partial or inconsistent statistics. Related endpoints include `/statistics/riskRules`, which focuses specifically on the risk-rule configuration aspect of the platform, while this endpoint presents a broader view of all business policies.
operations.summary: Get aggregated statistics for business policies from shopping_mall_business_policies.

responseBody.description: Aggregated statistical and overview data about business policies configured in the platform.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves statistical and configuration metrics for risk evaluation rules defined in the Prisma table `shopping_mall_risk_rules` and related governance tables such as `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, and `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`. It is a read-only endpoint intended for risk and fraud monitoring dashboards, security operations centers, or admin consoles.

The endpoint provides aggregated data rather than raw rule definitions only. It can include counts of risk rules by severity level, activation status, and rule category, plus derived metrics like how many risk cases have been opened in association with particular rules over a recent time period. It may also surface configuration coverage metrics, such as how many case types tied to risk rules have SLA configurations or how many rules are subject to special policy overrides.

The operation is exposed via a GET method and returns a DTO named `IShoppingMallRiskRuleStatistics`, which is derived from `shopping_mall_risk_rules` and its associated case and policy configuration tables but structured for efficient statistics rendering on administrative dashboards.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistical information and configuration coverage metrics for risk evaluation rules in the shopping mall platform.

At the data level, this endpoint is primarily associated with the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table, which defines risk evaluation rules used by the platform's risk engine to flag suspicious activity, high-risk orders, or risky accounts. Each rule typically includes metadata such as a human-readable name, severity classification, the domain it applies to (for example, orders, payments, or accounts), and flags indicating whether the rule is currently active. These rules are often connected conceptually to risk or fraud cases represented in `shopping_mall_risk_cases` and may be governed by business policies and SLA configurations defined in `shopping_mall_business_policies` and `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`.

The response of this endpoint consolidates these sources into an administrative statistics view. Common metrics include the total number of risk rules, how many are active versus disabled, distribution of rules by severity or category, and counts of rules that have triggered at least one risk case within a certain time window. It can also provide information about SLA coverage, such as how many risk case types linked to rules have defined SLA configurations, as well as whether any policy overrides recorded in `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` are currently affecting risk-related behavior.

From an authorization perspective, risk rules and their associated metrics are highly sensitive, as they reveal the internal detection posture of the platform. Therefore, access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors only, indicated by `authorizationActors: ["admin"]`. Implementations should enforce strong authentication and authorization, potentially layering fine-grained permissions on top of the basic actor check using RBAC data from models like `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and `shopping_mall_admin_permissions`.

The operation is read-only and must not change any records in `shopping_mall_risk_rules`, `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, or related tables. It also does not accept a request body; all metrics are computed using predefined aggregation logic. Should the aggregation process encounter issues, such as missing configuration tables or query errors, the API should return a clear error response with an appropriate HTTP status code. This endpoint complements `/statistics/policies`, which focuses on broader policy statistics, by concentrating specifically on the configuration and impact of risk rules.
operations.summary: Get aggregated statistics for risk rules from shopping_mall_risk_rules.

responseBody.description: Aggregated statistical and overview data about risk evaluation rules configured in the platform.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a paginated list of customer accounts from the shopping_mall_customers Prisma table within the ShoppingMall service. It is implemented as an HTTP PATCH on the /customers path to allow complex filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria to be passed in the request body, which would not be practical as query parameters.

The operation is primarily associated with the shopping_mall_customers model, which represents registered customer accounts in the marketplace. Depending on the detailed Prisma schema, this model will typically include identifiers, contact information, registration timestamps, status flags, and relationships to profiles, addresses, orders, and risk flags. The search criteria DTO IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest encapsulates the supported filters such as keyword search on name or email, registration date ranges, status filters, and possibly relationships such as presence of recent orders or risk flags.

The response returns a paginated collection of customer summary records using the IPageIShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary DTO, which provides the key fields needed for list views in administrative consoles, such as customer identifier, display name, primary contact channels, registration date, and current account status. Detailed, heavy relational data is excluded from the summary to keep list responses efficient. This operation is intended for administrative use to monitor and manage the customer base, not for end-user self-service listing.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of registered customer accounts from the ShoppingMall platform.

This PATCH /customers operation queries the shopping_mall_customers Prisma table using flexible criteria encapsulated in the IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest DTO. Typical filters include partial matching on customer name, email, or phone, registration date windows, account status (such as active, suspended, or pending verification), and possibly flags indicating high-value, risky, or recently active customers. The request DTO is designed to map directly to fields and indexes defined on shopping_mall_customers as well as selected related tables like customer profiles or risk flags, ensuring that the server-side implementation can efficiently translate the search criteria into Prisma queries.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint exposes potentially sensitive personal and behavioral information about customers. Therefore, it is restricted to administrative actors only, represented by the ["admin"] authorizationActors array. The implementation must enforce role-based access control and may apply additional row-level filtering depending on the administrator's scope. No authentication information is accepted from the client in the request body; all authorization context is derived from the authenticated admin session.

The response body uses the IPageIShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary type, which wraps a page of IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary entries together with pagination metadata such as total count, page size, and current page. Each summary entry contains a subset of fields from shopping_mall_customers that are appropriate for list display, for example the customer code or id, display name, primary email, registration timestamp, and current activation or risk status. Relationship-heavy fields and large blobs are intentionally omitted from summaries to keep the endpoint performant. Related operations that are typically used together with this one include GET /customers/{customerId} for inspecting a single customer in detail, and possibly endpoints under /orders or /riskCases for drilling down into that customer's activity.

Error handling for this operation includes validation errors when the IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest payload contains invalid combinations of filters or paging parameters, as well as standard authentication and authorization errors for non-admin callers. When filters reference fields or enumerated values that do not exist in the Prisma schema, the server must reject the request; therefore, the DTO must be kept in strict alignment with the shopping_mall_customers model and its related configuration tables.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping_mall_customers records as customer summaries.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for querying customer accounts stored in shopping_mall_customers.

responseBody.description: Paginated result set of customer summary records derived from shopping_mall_customers that match the search criteria.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information for a single customer account from the shopping_mall_customers Prisma table in the ShoppingMall service. It is implemented as an HTTP GET on the /customers/{customerId} path, where {customerId} represents the unique identifier of the customer in the underlying database, typically the primary key of the shopping_mall_customers model.

The operation reads the full customer record and, depending on the DTO definition for IShoppingMallCustomer, may also include selected denormalized information from related tables such as customer profiles, primary shipping address snapshots, or basic risk and status indicators. All fields included in the response must correspond to actual columns or derived projections based on the Prisma schema. The path parameter is required and must match the identifier type used by shopping_mall_customers, often a UUID represented as a string.

This operation supports administrative workflows for investigating customer accounts, handling disputes, or providing customer support. It is closely related to the PATCH /customers search operation, which is typically used to locate the customer first; once the relevant record is found, the client can call GET /customers/{customerId} to load the complete view. The design ensures that the detailed representation IShoppingMallCustomer complements the lighter-weight summary representation returned by list endpoints.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single customer account from the ShoppingMall platform by its unique identifier.

This GET /customers/{customerId} endpoint directly queries the shopping_mall_customers Prisma model using the provided customerId path parameter. The parameter identifies the exact row in shopping_mall_customers, usually corresponding to the model's primary key. The server validates the format of customerId according to the schema (for example, ensuring it is a well-formed UUID string when the primary key is a UUID) and returns a 404 error if no matching customer record is found. The IShoppingMallCustomer DTO returned by this operation exposes the core customer fields defined in the Prisma schema, such as identifiers, contact details, registration timestamps, and status indicators.

Because the response may contain personal and potentially sensitive data, including contact information and account state, access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors, reflected by authorizationActors set to ["admin"]. Implementations must enforce authentication and authorization consistently and may perform additional checks to ensure that the requesting admin has sufficient privileges for the referenced customer. The endpoint does not accept a request body; all input is provided through the path parameter and the authenticated context.

This operation is typically used after calling PATCH /customers to search for relevant customer accounts. Once an administrator selects a specific entry from that list, they can call GET /customers/{customerId} to view the full record and make informed decisions about support actions, risk evaluation, or policy enforcement. Error handling should cover invalid identifier formats, missing records, and insufficient permissions, returning appropriate HTTP status codes and messages, while ensuring that no information about the existence of a customer is leaked to unauthorized callers.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single detailed shopping_mall_customers record by its unique customerId identifier.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target customer in the shopping_mall_customers table, typically the primary key value such as a UUID string.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing customer account record in the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model for the ShoppingMall platform. It is responsible for applying user-initiated or admin-initiated changes to core customer account attributes such as contact information, notification preferences, and other mutable profile-related fields, while preserving immutable identifiers and system-managed audit fields defined in the Prisma schema.

The endpoint receives a `IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate` DTO in the request body, which contains only fields that are allowed to change for a customer. These typically include business-facing attributes like name, contact channels, preference flags, or marketing opt-ins as defined by the underlying `shopping_mall_customers` model, but explicitly exclude primary keys and other non-editable system fields. The handler must validate that the target customer exists, enforce any field-level validation rules derived from the Prisma schema comments, and then perform an update using the Prisma client.

The updated entity is returned as a full `IShoppingMallCustomer` representation so that clients always receive the authoritative, post-update view of the customer resource. Authorization rules such as ensuring that only an admin or the owning customer can update the account are enforced by higher-layer guards and service logic, informed by the `authorizationActor` and any role/ownership fields present in `shopping_mall_customers`.
operations.description:
Update an existing customer account stored in the `shopping_mall_customers` table and return the fully refreshed customer representation.

This operation targets the primary `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model, which represents registered customer accounts on the ShoppingMall marketplace. According to the schema comments for this model, it captures the canonical customer identity and key account attributes that drive ordering, shipping, and personalization experiences. Typical fields include a stable primary key, contact channels such as email or phone, and various status or preference flags. Immutable identifiers and system-managed timestamps are not altered by this endpoint; only fields explicitly modeled as mutable in the `IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate` DTO are accepted and applied.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is intended for authenticated flows where either the customer updates their own account or an administrator performs support or governance actions. While the `authorizationActor` metadata exposes this as a generic authenticated user endpoint, the underlying business logic must still verify that the caller is permitted to modify the requested `customerId`, for example by matching the authenticated principal to the target customer or checking administrative privileges. Validation also needs to respect constraints encoded in the Prisma schema, such as unique indexes on email or phone and any length or format expectations documented in schema comments.

In relation to other APIs, this update endpoint is typically used together with a GET customer detail operation for initial data population and with profile or address-specific APIs for data that lives in other tables such as `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` or `shopping_mall_customer_addresses`. Error handling should include clear responses when the `customerId` does not correspond to an existing row in `shopping_mall_customers`, when attempted updates violate database constraints, or when authorization checks fail before the Prisma update is executed.
operations.summary: Update a ShoppingMall customer record in the `shopping_mall_customers` table.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target customer whose account in the `shopping_mall_customers` table will be updated.

requestBody.description: Mutable customer account fields to be updated for the existing record in `shopping_mall_customers`. Only properties defined in `IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate` are accepted and processed.

responseBody.description: The fully refreshed customer account after applying the requested updates, as stored in the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model.

operations.name: update

operations.specification:
This operation performs a permanent removal of a customer account record from the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model for the ShoppingMall platform. It receives a `customerId` path parameter that identifies the target row and then issues a delete operation through the Prisma client against the `shopping_mall_customers` table.

The behavior is modeled as a hard delete at the database level unless the Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_customers` defines an alternative lifecycle pattern such as dedicated status flags or archival tables. The API contract does not expose any request body; all necessary context for deletion is conveyed by the path parameter and the authenticated principal. The handler must enforce preconditions such as verifying that the customer exists and that the caller has the necessary authorization to remove the account, potentially including checks against related tables like orders, payments, or legal holds if dictated by the broader data model and business policies.

Upon successful deletion, the operation does not return a response body, signaling that the identified customer resource has been removed from the primary `shopping_mall_customers` store. Any cascading effects—such as cleanup of related profile or session data—are implemented within the service layer according to the relationships and foreign keys defined in the Prisma schema and the platform’s compliance requirements.
operations.description:
Permanently remove an existing customer account from the `shopping_mall_customers` table using its unique identifier.

This operation focuses on the primary `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model, which holds the canonical records for registered ShoppingMall customers. When invoked with a specific `customerId`, the backing service first validates that the record exists and then executes a delete via Prisma against this model. The description comments in the schema for `shopping_mall_customers` should be treated as the authoritative source for how customer identity and lifecycle are modeled, including any notes about constraints or links to other tables such as orders, risk flags, or legal holds that might affect whether deletion is allowed at runtime.

From a security and governance perspective, this endpoint must only be accessible to principals that are allowed to remove customer accounts, such as privileged support staff, compliance operators, or tightly controlled self-service flows that meet regulatory requirements. While the `authorizationActor` metadata is kept generic here, the implementation must check the authenticated actor type and any relevant role or ownership data before invoking the Prisma delete. If the platform uses additional models like `shopping_mall_legal_holds` or audit snapshot tables, the service should either prevent deletion when such constraints apply or perform the necessary archival steps prior to removing the row from `shopping_mall_customers`.

No request body is accepted because all necessary context is supplied via the path and authentication. On success the API responds without a payload, indicating that the customer resource identified by `customerId` no longer exists in the primary table. Error handling should cover cases where the identifier does not match any existing customer, where foreign key constraints prevent deletion due to dependent data, or where authorization checks fail before reaching the Prisma layer.
operations.summary: Delete a ShoppingMall customer record from the `shopping_mall_customers` table.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target customer whose account in the `shopping_mall_customers` table will be deleted.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the profile information of a specific registered customer from the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model, using the parent customer identifier from the `shopping_mall_customers` model. It is designed as a read-only endpoint that allows clients to fetch extended profile attributes such as names, contact preferences, and other non-authentication properties associated with a customer account.

The operation uses a GET method on the `/customers/{customerId}/profile` path, where `customerId` is a path parameter representing the unique identifier of the customer in the `shopping_mall_customers` table (typically a UUID string). Internally, the implementation is expected to validate that the given customer exists and then read the corresponding row in `shopping_mall_customer_profiles`, joining or referencing `shopping_mall_customers` as needed.

The response body is modeled using the DTO type `IShoppingMallCustomerProfile`, which corresponds to the Prisma model fields of `shopping_mall_customer_profiles`. This type should encapsulate all profile attributes that are safe to expose through the API while excluding any sensitive authentication or internal system fields handled by dedicated authentication systems.
operations.description:
Retrieve the extended profile information for a single customer based on their unique customer identifier.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model, which stores non-authentication, profile-oriented data for customers that complements the core identity stored in `shopping_mall_customers`. Typical fields in this model include personal details, contact preferences, localized display options, and other attributes that are part of the customer's profile but not directly tied to login or session management. The `customerId` path parameter is used to locate the associated `shopping_mall_customers` record and then read its profile row.

From a security perspective, this endpoint should be accessible only to authenticated actors who are allowed to view the requested profile. In the simplest scenario, this is the customer themselves reading their own profile, but administrative actors might also be able to read any customer's profile in back-office tools depending on the broader authorization design. Regardless of the enforcement strategy, no authentication credentials, password hashes, or session data are ever returned, because those belong to separate authentication/session subsystems and are not part of `shopping_mall_customer_profiles`.

The implementation is expected to validate that the `customerId` is well-formed (typically a UUID string) and that a corresponding customer exists in `shopping_mall_customers`. If no matching profile record is found, the service may either return a not-found error or, depending on business rules, create a default profile on demand before returning it. Any errors such as non-existent customers, database access issues, or authorization failures should be mapped to clear HTTP error responses.

This operation is often used in conjunction with the `PUT /customers/{customerId}/profile` endpoint, which updates the same `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` record. Clients will typically call this GET endpoint to fetch current values for display in a profile editing form, allow the user to make changes, and then send those changes back via the update operation.
operations.summary: Get profile information for a customer from shopping_mall_customer_profiles

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target customer whose profile is being retrieved. This corresponds to the primary key of the customer record in the `shopping_mall_customers` table, typically represented as a UUID string.

responseBody.description: Detailed profile information for the specified customer as stored in the shopping_mall_customer_profiles table.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A customer account context must exist before its extended data can be meaningfully used; POST /shoppingMall/customer/carts creates a cart for the authenticated customer, implicitly requiring a valid customer in shopping_mall_customers, which ensures the customerId used to fetch the profile corresponds to an existing customer.

operations.specification:
This operation updates the profile information for a specific customer in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model, identified by the parent customer record in `shopping_mall_customers`. It uses the HTTP PUT method on `/customers/{customerId}/profile` to perform an idempotent update of profile fields such as personal details, contact preferences, and other non-authentication attributes.

The `customerId` path parameter identifies the customer whose profile should be updated, corresponding to the primary key in `shopping_mall_customers`. The request body must conform to the DTO type `IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.IUpdate`, which is derived from the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` schema and contains only the fields that are allowed to be updated through this API. Fields that are controlled exclusively by internal systems or authentication modules must not be exposed or writable in this DTO.

Upon successful validation and persistence, the operation returns the updated profile entity represented by `IShoppingMallCustomerProfile`, reflecting the latest state in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` table. This ensures clients can immediately see the canonical result of their update operation, including any server-side normalization or derived values applied during processing.
operations.description:
Update the extended profile information for a specific customer using their unique customer identifier and a structured profile update payload.

This operation is built around the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model, which stores profile-level information associated with customers beyond their core identity in `shopping_mall_customers`. Typical updatable fields may include display name, contact channels, marketing preferences, and other configurable settings. The `customerId` path parameter indicates which customer is being modified, and the service implementation is expected to verify that this customer exists and that the caller is authorized to perform the update.

The request body follows the `IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.IUpdate` DTO, which should mirror the allowed updatable columns of `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` while intentionally excluding any internal-only or immutable fields. Validation rules, such as maximum lengths, allowed enum values, or formatting constraints, should align directly with the underlying Prisma schema definitions and any business rules derived from the requirements documents. Invalid payloads must result in clear client error responses explaining which fields failed validation.

From a security and authorization standpoint, this endpoint should normally be accessible to the customer when updating their own profile and possibly to administrative actors operating management consoles. The actual permission checks, such as confirming that the authenticated user matches the `customerId` or has an administrative role, should be enforced in the service layer based on the platform's overall authorization strategy.

This PUT operation is typically paired with `GET /customers/{customerId}/profile`, which returns the current profile state. Client applications often retrieve the profile, present it in an editable form, and then submit an `IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.IUpdate` payload to this endpoint. On success, the API returns the updated `IShoppingMallCustomerProfile` instance so clients can reflect the persisted state in their UI.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of authentication sessions for a specific shopping_mall_customers actor, based on the shopping_mall_customer_sessions Prisma table. It is designed as an administrative read-only search endpoint that allows operators to review historical and active sessions associated with a given customerId, without providing any capability to create, update, or delete sessions.

The endpoint is implemented as a PATCH on the nested resource path "/customers/{customerId}/sessions" to support complex search criteria in the request body. The request body will use the IShoppingMallCustomerSession.IRequest DTO, which encapsulates pagination parameters, optional time range filters (such as createdAtFrom/To, lastSeenFrom/To), device or user agent filters, IP address filters, and session state flags. These fields map directly to the columns on the shopping_mall_customer_sessions model, including timestamp fields and any descriptive metadata columns documented in that schema.

The response returns a paginated collection of session summary records using the IPageIShoppingMallCustomerSession.ISummary DTO. Each summary element represents one row from shopping_mall_customer_sessions projected into a form optimized for list displays: identifiers, creation time, last activity time, status, source channel, client information, and other non-sensitive metadata. Sensitive secrets such as tokens, hashes, or credential material are never exposed in this read model, in accordance with the security guidance for session data.

This operation must enforce that only administrative actors can access another user’s session list. Even though the path is keyed by customerId, normal customers must not be allowed to enumerate or introspect their own sessions through this interface because authentication and session lifecycle management are delegated to specialized authentication services. Instead, this endpoint exists strictly for administrators performing security reviews, fraud investigations, or support troubleshooting. Internally, the implementation will validate the supplied customerId against the shopping_mall_customers table to ensure the target account exists before querying shopping_mall_customer_sessions.

The operation complements, but does not overlap with, user-facing authentication flows such as login, logout, or token refresh, which are explicitly out of scope for this service. It may be used together with higher-level risk and audit views that aggregate data from shopping_mall_actor_security_events_of_customers or shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_customers, but this endpoint itself queries only the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. Errors are returned when the customer identifier is invalid, when pagination parameters are malformed, or when the caller lacks the required admin authorization.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of authentication sessions associated with a specific customer account from the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table.

This operation serves administrative and security monitoring use cases by exposing read-only views of customer sessions. Each result row corresponds to a record in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions Prisma model, which stores per-session metadata such as creation time, last seen time, source channel, client or device identifiers, and high-level session status flags. The detailed structure of these fields follows the comments defined on the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table and its columns, ensuring that the API documentation and database schema remain aligned.

The administrator supplies the target customerId as a path parameter, which is resolved against the shopping_mall_customers table to confirm that the referenced customer account exists. The request body, defined by IShoppingMallCustomerSession.IRequest, allows the admin to specify advanced filtering conditions and pagination controls. Typical filters include time windows for when sessions were created or last active, specific IP addresses or IP ranges, device or user agent fingerprints, session status (for example active versus expired), and flags indicating whether the session was established through particular channels such as web, mobile, or partner integrations. Pagination parameters like page number, page size, and sort ordering are also included in the request DTO.

Security-wise, this endpoint is strictly restricted to administrative actors. The authorizationActors array is therefore set to ["admin"], and the controller must ensure that only authenticated admins can invoke this operation. Access to session details for arbitrary customers is sensitive because it exposes behavioral metadata that could be misused if leaked. For that reason, the response DTO IPageIShoppingMallCustomerSession.ISummary intentionally omits any secret or credential-like fields such as tokens, refresh tokens, cryptographic material, or internal security keys that may exist on the underlying session table. Only high-level, non-secret session attributes are projected into the summary rows.

From a business perspective, typical usages of this API include customer support investigating a report of suspicious account access, security and risk teams reviewing access patterns before applying account risk flags, or compliance personnel responding to legal inquiries that require an overview of recent session activity. This endpoint may be used in combination with other administrative APIs that surface account risk flags and security events, but it remains focused on the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table as the authoritative source for session lifecycle metadata. Error handling ensures that invalid customer identifiers, malformed filter criteria, or unauthorized access attempts are surfaced with clear error responses while never leaking details about non-existent accounts or internal implementation specifics.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information about a single authentication session belonging to a specific customer, using the shopping_mall_customer_sessions Prisma table as its underlying data source. It is implemented as a GET request on the nested resource path "/customers/{customerId}/sessions/{sessionId}", where customerId identifies the owning customer account and sessionId identifies the concrete session record.

The operation returns a single IShoppingMallCustomerSession DTO that maps closely to the full shape of the shopping_mall_customer_sessions model, with appropriate exclusions for any secret fields that must never be exposed over an API. Typical non-secret fields include session identifiers, timestamps such as createdAt and lastSeenAt, source channel, IP address or network metadata, device or browser attributes, logical status markers, and other descriptive columns documented in the Prisma schema comments. The strict one-to-one mapping between the DTO and the schema ensures that changes in the underlying table, such as the addition of new explanatory columns, can be carried through consistently into the API documentation and implementation.

To maintain data integrity, the implementation must first validate that the supplied customerId corresponds to an existing record in the shopping_mall_customers table, and then ensure that the given sessionId belongs to that customer. This prevents an administrator from accidentally retrieving a session that is logically associated with a different account. If either the customer or session is not found, or if the session is not linked to the specified customer, a not-found style error response is returned without revealing which part of the composite identifier was invalid.

Consistent with the architectural rule that authentication and session lifecycle management is handled by specialized subsystems, this endpoint is strictly read-only and exposed only to administrative actors. It cannot be used to create, modify, or terminate sessions; such operations are outside the scope of this service. Instead, the purpose is to enable detailed inspection of a single session during activities such as incident response, fraud investigation, or customer support troubleshooting. The operation is typically invoked after first listing sessions via PATCH /customers/{customerId}/sessions and then drilling into a particular sessionId of interest. Errors are returned when the caller lacks admin authorization, when the parameters are malformed, or when the requested session cannot be found for the indicated customer.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single customer authentication session from the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table.

This operation is designed for administrators who need to inspect the full metadata associated with a specific session belonging to a particular customer. The customerId path parameter identifies the owning customer account from the shopping_mall_customers table, while sessionId identifies a specific row in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. Together, these parameters ensure that the requested session is both valid and correctly associated with the indicated account, providing a strong contextual guarantee.

The response uses the IShoppingMallCustomerSession DTO to represent the session in detail. In alignment with the Prisma model comments for shopping_mall_customer_sessions, the DTO includes fields such as the session’s unique identifier, creation timestamp, last activity timestamp, logical status, channel or platform of origin, IP address information, device or browser descriptors, and any additional non-secret metadata necessary for security analysis or troubleshooting. Any columns in the Prisma schema that contain tokens, cryptographic material, or sensitive secrets are intentionally excluded or masked in the DTO to prevent leakage through the API surface.

From a security perspective, access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors, represented by authorizationActors set to ["admin"]. While the nested path suggests a relationship to a customer, normal customers are not allowed to use this operation for self-service session management; those capabilities remain the responsibility of the dedicated authentication service. This read-only operation fits into a workflow where an admin first searches sessions for a given customer using PATCH /customers/{customerId}/sessions and then drills down into a specific sessionId to review detailed metadata, such as confirming whether access originated from an expected location or device. Error handling ensures that invalid identifiers, mismatched customer-session relationships, or unauthorized access attempts are handled gracefully and without revealing unnecessary internal details.

operations.specification:
Design an operation for the DELETE /customers/{customerId}/sessions/{sessionId} endpoint that invalidates (logically ends) a single customer session record associated with a specific customer. This operation is associated with the shopping_mall_customer_sessions Prisma table, which is a subsidiary model representing authentication sessions for customer accounts, and with shopping_mall_customers as its parent context.

From a business perspective, this endpoint is an administrative, security-focused tool: it allows an admin (or security automation calling as admin) to remotely terminate a particular session for a given customer, typically as part of incident response, account recovery, or policy enforcement. Because authentication and session lifecycle management are handled by dedicated authentication services for end users, this operation is strictly limited to administrative read/write over the session record for governance and risk handling, not to general customer-facing logout flows.

The operation will identify the target session using two UUID identifiers in the path: customerId for the owning shopping_mall_customers row, and sessionId for the specific shopping_mall_customer_sessions row. It will perform validation to ensure that the session belongs to the specified customer before marking it as terminated or deleting the record, depending on how the Prisma model is defined. The response will not return a body, relying on HTTP status codes to indicate success or failure. Authorization will be restricted to admin actors, and no request body is required.
operations.description:
Terminate a specific customer session record for a given customer as an administrative security operation.

This DELETE operation targets a single row in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table, which stores authentication sessions for customer accounts. Each session is associated with a parent customer record in the shopping_mall_customers table, and is typically created and managed automatically by the authentication subsystem when customers log in, refresh tokens, or otherwise establish authenticated interactions. Unlike customer-facing login or logout flows, this endpoint is designed for platform administrators and security tools that need to forcibly end a known session, for example when suspicious activity is detected or when performing account recovery.

When called, the implementation first validates that the customer identified by the customerId path parameter exists in the shopping_mall_customers table, and then verifies that the session identified by sessionId exists in shopping_mall_customer_sessions and is owned by that same customer. If no matching session is found, the operation should return an appropriate 404-style error. If the session is already ended or expired according to the schema’s status or timestamp fields, the implementation may treat the operation as idempotent, returning success without making further changes.

Security and authorization are critical for this operation. Only administrative actors, represented here by the "admin" authorization actor, are allowed to call this endpoint. The administrator’s identity and permissions should be enforced by the surrounding authentication and authorization middleware, and the provider implementation should record any relevant audit information into the shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs or similar governance tables if such logging is required by the broader system. Because the session to be terminated is fully identified by the path parameters, no request body is needed, and the operation can return an empty response body on success, relying on HTTP status codes and any standard error payload formats defined elsewhere in the service.

This endpoint is typically used together with read-only session inspection endpoints, such as PATCH /customers/{customerId}/sessions for searching a customer’s active sessions or GET /customers/{customerId}/sessions/{sessionId} for viewing a single session’s details. A common workflow is for an admin to first list or inspect sessions, select the suspicious or unwanted one, and then call this DELETE operation to terminate it. Error handling should clearly distinguish between missing customers, sessions that do not belong to the given customer, and general server errors, aligning with the platform’s standard error contract.
operations.summary: Terminate a specific customer session in shopping_mall_customer_sessions for a given customer as an admin action

operations.specification:
Design an operation for the PATCH /customers/{customerId}/addresses endpoint that retrieves a filtered and paginated list of shipping addresses associated with a specific customer. This operation is directly associated with the shopping_mall_customer_addresses Prisma table, which represents current shipping addresses managed by customers, and uses the shopping_mall_customers table as the parent context via the customerId path parameter.

The operation will support flexible search, filtering, and sorting within the scope of a single customer’s addresses. The request body will be typed as IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.IRequest, encapsulating filters such as address type, country or region codes, text search on address lines, and generic pagination and sort options. The response will return a paginated summary list using IPageIShoppingMallCustomerAddress.ISummary, optimized for list and management views rather than full detail payloads for every address.

Because addresses contain personal data and are inherently sensitive, the endpoint requires authentication. Business rules typically allow customers to view and manage their own addresses, and administrators to view addresses for support or compliance purposes. In this specification we scope the interface to the customer actor, with the expectation that implementation-level authorization will enforce that the caller can only see addresses of the customer they are allowed to access (e.g., themselves or via elevated admin context).
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of shipping addresses belonging to a specific customer from the shopping_mall_customer_addresses table.

This PATCH operation is built on top of the shopping_mall_customer_addresses Prisma model, which stores current shipping address records managed by customers. Each address row is linked to a customer in the shopping_mall_customers table, and may include fields such as recipient name, address lines, city, region, postal code, country, contact phone, and optional labels like "Home" or "Office". The customerId path parameter scopes the search to a single customer, ensuring that only addresses owned by that customer are considered for retrieval and pagination.

The request body is represented by the IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.IRequest DTO type. This request structure is expected to provide standard search and pagination capabilities, including page size, page index or cursor, sort keys and sort direction, and optional filter fields such as country code, region code, address label, or free-text query across address lines. By centralizing these filters in the request DTO, the API can support complex querying without overloading query string parameters, and future enhancements (such as additional filter fields) can be accommodated without breaking the path contract.

The response body uses the IPageIShoppingMallCustomerAddress.ISummary type, a paginated collection of summary representations of customer addresses. Each summary item typically includes the minimal fields necessary to render address lists in user interfaces, such as recipient name, primary address line, city, region, country, and whether the the address is marked as default for shipping. The pagination wrapper provides metadata like total count, current page, and page size to support UI pagination controls.

Security and authorization considerations are central to this operation because it exposes personally identifiable information. The authorizationActor field is set to "customer", indicating that customer actors (and potentially admins through higher-level authorization layers) can call this endpoint. Implementation logic must further ensure that a given caller is allowed to access the addresses of the customer identified by customerId, typically by requiring that the authenticated principal’s identity matches the customer or that they have elevated roles (such as admin or support) handled by separate authorization layers. This operation is often used alongside endpoints that create, update, or delete individual addresses, as well as read-only detail endpoints such as GET /customers/{customerId}/addresses/{addressId}.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single customer shipping address resource for the shoppingMall platform. It is associated with the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` Prisma model, which represents current shipping addresses managed by customers. The endpoint is designed so that a specific address belonging to a specific customer can be fetched using the customer’s identifier and the address identifier, enabling clients to display or validate the exact address used for orders, wishlists, or other fulfillment-related workflows.

The operation uses path parameters `customerId` and `addressId` to uniquely locate the target address record. These are treated as opaque string identifiers (commonly UUIDs) that directly correspond to the primary key fields on `shopping_mall_customers` and `shopping_mall_customer_addresses`, or to their business identifiers if such codes exist in the schema. The service layer must validate that the address actually belongs to the given customer and not to another account, ensuring proper tenancy isolation.

In terms of DTOs, the response returns a detailed representation of the address using the `IShoppingMallCustomerAddress` type, which mirrors the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` schema and includes all relevant address attributes such as recipient name, postal code, address lines, city, region, country, phone number, and any address type flags (for example, whether it is the default shipping address). This detailed DTO may also include read-only metadata such as creation and update timestamps if those exist in the Prisma model.

This endpoint is read-only and does not accept a request body. It is intended to be used by authenticated customers to view their own addresses, and potentially by administrative actors when investigating customer issues or supporting customer service tasks. While the operation itself simply performs a direct lookup, the implementation should enforce authorization checks to make sure that a given customer cannot retrieve address records owned by another customer.

Related operations include the creation of addresses via `POST /customers/{customerId}/addresses` and potential list or search endpoints such as `PATCH /customers/{customerId}/addresses` (not defined here) that would return paginated collections of address summaries. Client applications typically call this GET operation after a list selection to obtain the complete details of a single address record for editing, confirmation, or display in checkout flows.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single shipping address record belonging to a specific customer based on the customer identifier and the address identifier.

This operation interacts with the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` Prisma table, which stores current shipping addresses managed by customers in the shoppingMall platform. Each record represents a concrete delivery destination that a customer has saved, including structured address components such as postal code, address lines, locality, region, and country, as well as contact details like recipient name and phone number. The `shopping_mall_customers` table provides the owning customer context referenced by the `customerId` path parameter.

When this endpoint is invoked, the service layer must first resolve the customer indicated by `customerId`, then query the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table using `addressId`, ensuring that the retrieved address row is associated with the given customer. If the relationship does not exist or the identifiers do not match, the implementation should respond with an appropriate error such as a 404 not found to avoid revealing the existence of addresses belonging to other customers.

Security-wise, this operation should typically be restricted to authenticated customer actors, represented here by the `customer` authorization actor, and potentially administrative users at the service level. The controller should obtain the caller’s identity from the authentication layer and the provider logic should enforce that the caller either owns the address or has sufficient administrative permissions to read it. No request body is accepted; all necessary identification information is carried in the path parameters.

The response uses the `IShoppingMallCustomerAddress` DTO, which is a detailed view of a customer address aligned with the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` schema. This DTO is expected to contain all fields that are safe to expose to the client, including the primary key identifier, human-readable address components, and any flags such as “is default shipping address” or “label” if they exist in the model. Any internal-only fields, such as risk flags or legal hold markers if present on the table, should either be omitted from the DTO or filtered at the mapping layer.

From a workflow perspective, this endpoint is commonly called after a client has presented a list of saved addresses and the user selects one to view or confirm details, or when navigating to an address-editing screen where the full address must be loaded for modification. It complements the address creation endpoint `POST /customers/{customerId}/addresses` and any future update or deletion endpoints, forming part of the overall customer address management feature set for the shoppingMall service.
