requestBody.description: Fields to update on the target product attribute, such as name, display name, data type, variant flag, and display order.

responseBody.description: The updated product attribute entity after applying the requested changes.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A product must exist in shopping_mall_products before its attributes can be updated; creating the product yields the productId used by this endpoint.
A specific product attribute row in shopping_mall_product_attributes must be created before it can be updated; this operation creates the attribute and returns the productAttributeId used here.

operations.specification:
Permanently delete or mark as deleted a specific product attribute from the shopping_mall_product_attributes table for a given product. The endpoint is scoped by productId and identifies the attribute via productAttributeId, ensuring that product-level context is preserved for authorization and integrity checks.

The operation does not accept a request body and focuses solely on removing the attribute identified by productAttributeId, after validating that it belongs to the product identified by productId. Depending on the implementation and the presence of the deleted_at column on shopping_mall_product_attributes, the delete behavior may either set deleted_at (logical deletion) or perform a hard delete.

The response body is null, indicating that callers should rely on HTTP status codes to determine success or failure. This operation is restricted to catalog-managing actors, represented here as ["seller"], and should be used carefully because removing attributes can affect SKU definitions and attribute value mappings in related tables.
operations.description:
Delete a specific product attribute associated with a given product from the shopping catalog.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_product_attributes table, which defines variant-capable attributes such as color or size for a product stored in shopping_mall_products. Each attribute record is linked to its owning product via shopping_mall_product_id and includes metadata like name, display_name, data_type, is_variant_dimension, display_order, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The path parameters productId and productAttributeId are both required so the system can verify that the attribute being deleted indeed belongs to the indicated product, preventing cross-product data tampering.

Only authorized actors who manage catalog data for the product—typically the owning seller or an administrator—are allowed to execute this operation. In this specification, authorizationActors is set to seller, and the actual ownership and role checks are carried out by the business logic based on the authenticated principal and the product's seller linkage via shopping_mall_products.shopping_mall_seller_id. Unauthorized attempts should be rejected with appropriate error responses, and not-found conditions must be handled when either the product or attribute does not exist or has already been removed.

The deletion behavior should be implemented in a way that respects the presence of the deleted_at column on shopping_mall_product_attributes. Implementations may choose to set deleted_at to mark the attribute as removed from active use, or to physically delete the record, depending on broader platform policies. In either case, callers will not receive a response body; instead, they should interpret a successful HTTP status code (such as 204 No Content) as confirmation that the attribute is no longer active for the product. Related catalog operations, like SKU management and attribute value maintenance, must take into account that deleted attributes should no longer be used in variant definitions or shown in seller UIs.
operations.summary: Delete a product attribute row in shopping_mall_product_attributes for a given product.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent product whose attribute is being deleted.

parameters.name: productAttributeId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product attribute record in shopping_mall_product_attributes to delete.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: The parent product record in shopping_mall_products must exist before an attribute tied to that product can be deleted; this operation creates the product and its productId.

The target product attribute in shopping_mall_product_attributes must be created before it can be deleted; this operation inserts the attribute row and provides the productAttributeId referenced here.

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a paginated list of product attribute values for a specific product attribute belonging to a given product. It is associated primarily with the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`, while also relying on `shopping_mall_products` and `shopping_mall_product_attributes` to scope the search to a concrete product and attribute.

The endpoint `PATCH /products/{productId}/attributes/{productAttributeId}/values` is designed as a complex search operation that supports pagination, filtering, and sorting over the attribute values. The `productId` and `productAttributeId` path parameters identify the parent product and attribute whose values are being queried, and the request body DTO encapsulates search criteria such as keyword filters, active flags, or other business-specific constraints defined on the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` model.

The response returns a paginated collection of summary DTOs representing attribute values, optimized for listing screens in admin tools or seller portals. Each summary item is based on the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` schema fields (such as internal identifier, display label, sort order, and status) but does not necessarily expose all low-level columns. This separation allows the backend to evolve the physical schema while keeping a stable API contract.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated collection of attribute values for a specific product attribute associated with a given product.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` Prisma table, which stores the allowed values for a particular attribute of a product, as well as the parent entities defined in `shopping_mall_products` and `shopping_mall_product_attributes`. The `productId` path parameter represents the unique identifier of the product row in `shopping_mall_products`, while `productAttributeId` points to the specific attribute row in `shopping_mall_product_attributes`. By combining these two identifiers, the system ensures that search results are scoped strictly to values belonging to the given attribute of the given product, preventing accidental leakage of values from other products or attributes.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is intended for administrative or internal management tooling where operators need to inspect or curate the catalog structure. The `authorizationActors` field is therefore set to `["admin"]`, indicating that only administrator actors should be allowed to access this search operation. Additional, finer-grained permission checks—such as whether a specific admin role can manage catalog definitions—are enforced inside the business logic, relying on the admin and RBAC tables such as `shopping_mall_admins` and `shopping_mall_admin_roles`.

The request body uses the `IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.IRequest` DTO to encapsulate search conditions, pagination parameters, and sorting options. Typical criteria may include filtering by partial display name, status flags (for example enabled/disabled), or ranges for sort order fields defined in the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` schema. The response body uses the `IPageIShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.ISummary` DTO, which represents a page of summary records derived from the same Prisma model but tailored for listing, including fields like identifier, human-readable label, and any key flags required by the UI. Errors are returned when the referenced product or attribute do not exist, when the attribute does not belong to the specified product, or when the caller lacks sufficient permissions.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with the detail retrieval endpoint `GET /products/{productId}/attributes/{productAttributeId}/values/{productAttributeValueId}`, which fetches a single attribute value with full detail. Clients will often use this search endpoint to display an overview grid, and then use the detail endpoint when a user selects a specific value to view or edit.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of product attribute values for a given product attribute (shopping_mall_product_attribute_values).

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product in the `shopping_mall_products` table whose attribute values are being queried.

parameters.name: productAttributeId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product attribute in the `shopping_mall_product_attributes` table for which allowed values from `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` should be listed.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination parameters, and sorting options for querying product attribute values belonging to the specified product attribute.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of product attribute value summary records for the specified product attribute, based on `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A product must exist in shopping_mall_products before its attributes’ values can be searched; creating a product provides a valid productId for this operation.

A product attribute definition must exist in shopping_mall_product_attributes for the given product before attribute values belonging to that attribute can be queried; this operation creates the attribute and yields a valid productAttributeId.

At least one attribute value must exist in shopping_mall_product_attribute_values for the specified product attribute in order for the search-and-list operation to return meaningful results; this operation creates such values, providing valid productAttributeValue records scoped to the given product and attribute.

This operation retrieves the full detail of a single product attribute value that belongs to a specific product attribute and product. It primarily maps to the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`, and uses `shopping_mall_products` and `shopping_mall_product_attributes` to ensure that the value is correctly scoped to its parent entities.

The endpoint `GET /products/{productId}/attributes/{productAttributeId}/values/{productAttributeValueId}` is a standard detail retrieval operation. The `productId` parameter identifies the product in `shopping_mall_products`, `productAttributeId` identifies the attribute in `shopping_mall_product_attributes`, and `productAttributeValueId` points to the concrete row in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`. The combination of these three parameters allows the backend to verify that the attribute value truly belongs to the specified attribute of the specified product before returning it.

The response DTO exposes all necessary fields from `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`, including internal identifiers, display label or name, optional description, sort order, and any flags or metadata defined in the schema. This detailed view is designed for admin or seller tooling screens where operators need to read (and possibly edit through a separate update endpoint) the precise configuration of allowed attribute values for catalog maintenance purposes.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full detail of a single product attribute value for a given product and product attribute.

This operation is grounded in the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` Prisma model, which stores the allowed value options associated with product attributes, and in the parent models `shopping_mall_products` and `shopping_mall_product_attributes`. The `productId` path parameter is the unique identifier of the product row in `shopping_mall_products`, the `productAttributeId` parameter identifies the attribute row in `shopping_mall_product_attributes`, and the `productAttributeValueId` parameter identifies the specific attribute value row in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`. The service must validate that the attribute belongs to the given product and that the attribute value belongs to that attribute before returning data.

From a security standpoint, the endpoint is restricted to administrative actors because it exposes low-level catalog configuration details. The `authorizationActors` is set to `["admin"]`, implying that only admin users (as modeled in tables such as `shopping_mall_admins` and associated RBAC tables) may access this detailed information. Additional permission checks—such as whether the admin has rights to manage catalog configuration—are handled in the business layer based on roles and permissions.

The response uses the `IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue` DTO, which is a detailed projection of the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` schema and may include all relevant fields such as value code, localized display label, sort priority, and status flags. The endpoint returns standard not-found errors when any of the three identifiers does not resolve to an existing and correctly related record, and authorization errors when the caller does not satisfy the required actor constraints. This detail endpoint is typically invoked after obtaining a list of values from `PATCH /products/{productId}/attributes/{productAttributeId}/values` when a user chooses a specific value for inspection or editing.

operations.specification:
Create a new product attribute value for a specific product attribute on a given product in the shopping mall catalog.

This operation is associated with the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` Prisma model, which represents the allowed values for a particular attribute defined on a product (for example, size "M", color "Red", or material "Cotton"). Each value belongs to a `shopping_mall_product_attributes` record, which itself is linked to a specific `shopping_mall_products` record. The endpoint is nested under `/products/{productId}/attributes/{productAttributeId}` to explicitly scope the new value to both the owning product and the attribute.

The operation accepts a JSON request body conforming to `IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.ICreate`, which contains the business fields required to register a new attribute value, such as display label, internal key/code, sort order, and any flags related to availability or behavior. Identifiers for the product and attribute are supplied exclusively through the path parameters and must not be duplicated in the body DTO; the provider implementation will combine the path context with the body fields when creating the new row in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`.

On success, the operation returns the created value as an `IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue` object. This representation should include the new value’s identifier and all relevant attributes so that clients (both seller tools and admin tools) can immediately reflect the change in their UI. Basic validation errors, such as attempting to create a duplicate value for the same attribute or violating any uniqueness constraints, should result in appropriate 4xx responses handled at the framework level.
operations.description:
Register a new allowed value for a product-level attribute defined for a specific product in the shopping mall catalog.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` table, which holds the discrete values that a given attribute can take for a product. In the underlying schema, each row is linked to a parent `shopping_mall_product_attributes` record, ensuring that the value is correctly scoped to the combination of product and attribute. The path parameters `{productId}` and `{productAttributeId}` jointly provide this context and are used by the service implementation to set the corresponding foreign keys when inserting the new record.

From a business perspective, this API is typically used by seller-facing tools or back-office admin interfaces when a merchant defines or extends their variant structure. For example, a seller configuring a "Color" attribute might add values such as "Red", "Blue", and "Green"; or for a "Size" attribute they might add "S", "M", and "L". The `IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.ICreate` DTO should therefore capture human-readable labels, any internal codes used for integrations, display ordering, and any flags controlling visibility or selection behavior. Validation must ensure that required fields are present, that text fields conform to length and content rules defined in the domain, and that the combination of attribute and value does not violate uniqueness rules.

Security-wise, this operation should be restricted to authenticated actors who are allowed to manage the product catalog, typically sellers who own the product or administrators with catalog management permissions. In this specification we use the generic `seller` actor to represent such users. The implementation should still enforce fine-grained checks such as verifying that the authenticated seller actually owns the target product, while admins may bypass that ownership constraint according to platform policy.

Related endpoints include the corresponding PUT operation on `/products/{productId}/attributes/{productAttributeId}/values/{productAttributeValueId}` for updating existing values, and potential listing endpoints for enumerating all values associated with a given attribute. Update an existing product attribute value associated with a specific product attribute and product in the shopping mall catalog.

This operation is associated with the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` Prisma model, which stores allowed values for product attributes, each linked to a `shopping_mall_product_attributes` record and, transitively, to a `shopping_mall_products` record. The implementation must enforce any constraints declared in the Prisma schema and business rules—such as maximum length for labels, allowed formats for codes, and uniqueness of the value key within the same attribute. Access to this endpoint is restricted to actors allowed to manage product catalog configuration. In this specification, the `seller` actor represents authenticated sellers operating on their own catalog entries, but the actual implementation may also allow admin actors with broader catalog management rights. operations.specification:
Delete a specific product attribute value associated with a product attribute for a given product, operating on the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table. This operation permanently removes the attribute value row identified by productId, productAttributeId, and productAttributeValueId, after verifying the hierarchical relationship: the attribute value must belong to the attribute, and the attribute must belong to the product. It is intended for administrative or seller-side catalog management tools where product attribute vocabularies are curated.

The endpoint uses UUID identifiers, as the Prisma schema defines id as the primary key for shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_product_attributes, and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values without any business code fields. The handler must resolve the path parameters to enforce that shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.shopping_mall_product_attribute_id matches the provided productAttributeId and that shopping_mall_product_attributes.shopping_mall_product_id matches the provided productId. If any of these checks fail, the operation should respond with an appropriate error (such as 404 for not found in this hierarchy).

Because this touches core catalog structure, the implementation must ensure that the attribute value is not referenced by critical downstream entities (such as SKU attribute mappings) before deletion, or else apply business rules (for example, blocking deletion when in use). The operation does not return a body on success; clients infer success from the HTTP status code. Authorization is restricted to sellers managing their own catalog or administrators with elevated rights, reflected via the seller and admin actors.
operations.description:
Delete a single product attribute value belonging to a specific product attribute of a product in the catalog.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_product_attribute_values table, whose description explains that each record defines an allowed value for a given product attribute, such as "Red" for color or "XL" for size. It also notes that these values are referenced by SKU attribute mapping tables for concrete variants. By deleting a record from this table, the system removes a permissible attribute value option from the configuration of a particular product, affecting what combinations users can select when configuring SKUs and what values can appear in filters.

The path parameters productId, productAttributeId, and productAttributeValueId correspond to the UUID primary keys of shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_product_attributes, and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values respectively. The implementation must enforce that the attribute value belongs to the attribute via the foreign key shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.shopping_mall_product_attribute_id and that the attribute belongs to the product via shopping_mall_product_attributes.shopping_mall_product_id. This ensures that callers cannot accidentally delete an attribute value from a different product or attribute context.

From a security perspective, this endpoint should only be callable by authenticated actors who are allowed to manage catalog configuration: typically the owning seller of the product or administrators. The authorizationActors array therefore includes both seller and admin, and fine-grained permission and ownership checks are applied in the service layer based on the associated seller and admin roles defined elsewhere in the schema.

Business logic should validate that the attribute value can be safely removed. Since the schema description indicates that these values are reused across many SKUs and are referenced by SKU attribute mapping tables, the implementation should either prevent deletion when the value is in active use by SKUs, or require prior cleanup of dependent SKU mappings. If the value cannot be deleted due to such constraints, the service should return a clear error indicating why. On successful deletion, the endpoint returns no response body, relying on HTTP status codes to indicate success. Related operations include managing attributes (such as listing and updating shopping_mall_product_attributes) and managing SKUs that reference these values.

operations.specification:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of SKUs (stock keeping units) for a given product, operating on the shopping_mall_skus table. Each SKU represents a concrete sellable variant of a product defined by combinations of attribute values, its own price, inventory quantity, and status. This operation provides flexible querying over SKUs belonging to a specific product, supporting catalog management and analytical scenarios.

The endpoint is scoped by productId, which must match shopping_mall_skus.shopping_mall_product_id. The request body uses a dedicated IShoppingMallSku.IRequest DTO to express filter criteria such as status, price ranges, inventory thresholds, and optional sorting and pagination parameters. The response returns a paginated list using IPageIShoppingMallSku.ISummary, which surfaces lightweight SKU information optimized for listing views—for example, SKU code, price, status, and minimal inventory information—rather than full SKU detail.

This operation is typically consumed by seller and admin UIs for managing product variants and by internal tools that require a manageable list of SKUs for further processing. Authorization is configured for sellers and administrators via seller and admin actors, with the actual permission and ownership checks enforced in the business layer based on seller relationships from shopping_mall_products and administrative privileges.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of SKUs for a specific product from the shopping_mall_skus table.

The shopping_mall_skus schema describes SKUs as stock keeping units representing concrete sellable variants of products. Each SKU belongs to a single shopping_mall_products record via the foreign key shopping_mall_skus.shopping_mall_product_id and includes core fields such as code, status, price, original_price, inventory_quantity, and low_stock_threshold, as well as a foreign key to shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states via shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id that describes availability semantics. The table description specifies that SKUs are the atomic unit for cart, order, inventory, and eligibility logic throughout the platform and that detailed adjustment history is kept in other tables.

This PATCH operation is scoped to a particular product, identified by the productId path parameter, and uses a rich request body of type IShoppingMallSku.IRequest to express filtering, sorting, and pagination requirements. Typical filters include SKU status (e.g., draft, active, inactive, discontinued, blocked_by_admin), price ranges, inventory thresholds such as low or zero inventory, and combinations of these criteria. The request model can also carry page number, page size, and sort instructions (for example, sorting by created_at, price, or inventory_quantity) to support efficient UI listing and administrative workflows.

The response body returns a paginated container IPageIShoppingMallSku.ISummary, which includes an array of SKU summary records and pagination metadata. Summary objects expose key fields like SKU code, status, price, and selected inventory indicators without the full object graph, making the payload suitable for grid views and management dashboards. The implementation is responsible for enforcing that only SKUs belonging to the specified product are returned, by constraining queries with shopping_mall_skus.shopping_mall_product_id = productId.

From a security standpoint, authorizationActors is set to both seller and admin, allowing the endpoint to be used by authenticated sellers managing their own product catalog as well as administrative staff with broader visibility. Ownership and role-specific rules—such as restricting results to SKUs under the calling seller's products or allowing broader visibility for administrators—are enforced at the service layer based on relationships to shopping_mall_products and the seller/admin models. This endpoint complements other SKU management operations like creation, update, and retrieval by ID and is designed purely for read/search behavior without modifying any data.

Retrieve detailed information for a specific SKU that belongs to a given product, based on the shopping_mall_skus Prisma table and its relationship to shopping_mall_products. This operation serves product detail pages and inventory-aware views where the client needs variant-level data such as pricing, stock state, and attribute combination for a particular SKU.

Internally, the implementation will typically join shopping_mall_skus with related tables such as shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states, and shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values to construct a rich representation of the SKU suitable for client consumption.

The response body is modeled as IShoppingMallSku, representing the main SKU entity with all fields necessary for detailed display, including its linkage to the owning product, current inventory state, and any pricing or external identifier metadata that the Prisma schema exposes. The endpoint is read-only and designed to be safe for public access, with additional visibility and availability filters applied according to shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules and related policy tables in the implementation layer.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific SKU that belongs to a given product.

This operation reads from the shopping_mall_skus Prisma table, which represents concrete sellable variants of products in the catalog. Each SKU is associated with a single product record from shopping_mall_products and may also have relationships to inventory state definitions in shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states, attribute value junction records in shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values, and external integration identifiers in shopping_mall_sku_external_ids. The operation must ensure that the requested SKU actually belongs to the specified product, reinforcing referential integrity at the API boundary in addition to the database foreign key constraints.

From a security and visibility standpoint, the handler should apply catalog visibility rules derived from shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules and related policy or block reason tables. For example, if either the product or the SKU is blocked according to shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons, or hidden for the requesting actor due to business policies, the operation should respond with a suitable error (such as 404 for hidden catalog entries) instead of exposing restricted data. Even though the endpoint is defined as public (no explicit authorizationActors), internal logic can still apply actor-specific filters based on anonymous versus authenticated users, region, or risk flags.

In addition to returning the fundamental SKU fields, implementations commonly enrich the IShoppingMallSku response with denormalized data from related tables, such as the parent product’s title and brand, selected attribute values that define the variant (size, color, etc.), and current inventory-related fields. Any error conditions such as a missing product, a missing SKU, or a SKU that does not belong to the given product should be handled explicitly and surfaced as domain-appropriate HTTP errors.

Clients typically invoke this operation from product detail pages when a user selects a particular variant, or from internal tools that need to inspect the exact SKU configuration tied to a product. Related operations include searching SKUs for a product (PATCH on a collection) or creating SKUs for a product (POST /products/{productId}/skus).
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific SKU (shopping_mall_skus) for a given product.

operations.specification:
Create a new SKU (stock keeping unit) under an existing product, using the shopping_mall_skus Prisma table as the primary persistence target and leveraging related tables such as shopping_mall_product_attributes, shopping_mall_product_attribute_values, and shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values to define the variant combination. This operation enables sellers or internal catalog operators to add concrete sellable variants to a product, specifying attributes like size and color, initial inventory state, and any external integration identifiers.

The endpoint receives the parent product identifier via the path parameter and accepts a request body described by IShoppingMallSku.ICreate. The DTO encapsulates all required fields for creating a SKU record, such as the associated product reference (which should match the path productId), base pricing, unit of measure, and initial inventory-related settings referenced from the shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states table. It may also include nested structures or references for attribute value associations (shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values) and external IDs (shopping_mall_sku_external_ids), depending on the detailed Prisma schema.

On successful creation, the operation writes to the shopping_mall_skus table and any necessary subsidiary tables, then returns the fully created SKU as IShoppingMallSku. Validation rules include checking that the product exists and is eligible to receive new SKUs, ensuring attribute combinations are valid with respect to shopping_mall_product_attributes and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values, and enforcing any uniqueness or visibility constraints defined by catalog policies. The operation is restricted to authenticated seller or admin-like actors in real deployments, but authorization is modeled here through the generic "seller" actor, with detailed role checks implemented in the business logic layer.
operations.description:
Create a new SKU for the specified product in the catalog.

This operation writes to the shopping_mall_skus Prisma table, which models concrete sellable variants of a product owned by a seller. The SKU represents a specific combination of product attributes, such as size and color, and is tied to its parent product record in shopping_mall_products via a foreign key. The request payload, defined by IShoppingMallSku.ICreate, supplies the necessary fields to construct the SKU, including identifiers that relate to inventory state definitions in shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states and, when applicable, attribute value combinations tied to shopping_mall_product_attribute_values via the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values junction table.

Before creating the record, the implementation must validate that the provided productId in the path corresponds to an existing product that belongs to the calling seller or is otherwise authorized for modification. It should also ensure that the proposed attribute combination does not violate uniqueness constraints or business rules, such as preventing duplicate SKUs with identical attribute sets for the same product. Additional business validations may include ensuring that pricing fields fall within configured bounds, that the initial inventory state is valid, and that any external identifiers conform to integrations represented by shopping_mall_sku_external_ids.

Upon successful creation, the endpoint responds with the newly created SKU serialized as IShoppingMallSku, reflecting the authoritative state of the SKU after all database-level defaults, triggers, and derived fields have been applied. Error conditions include invalid or missing product references, violations of attribute or uniqueness rules, and attempts by unauthorized actors to add SKUs to products they do not control. This operation complements read-only SKU endpoints such as GET /products/{productId}/skus/{skuId} and any SKU search/list operations exposed on the collection.
operations.summary: Create a new SKU (shopping_mall_skus) under the specified product.

operations.name: create

At least one inventory state configuration must exist in shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states so that shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id in the SKU creation payload can reference a valid state; this POST operation creates such an inventory state.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing SKU variant for a given product within the shoppingMall catalog domain. It is associated with the `shopping_mall_skus` Prisma table, which represents concrete sellable variants of products, and indirectly with `shopping_mall_products` (the parent product entity) and related subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values`, `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids`, and `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states`.

The endpoint is designed to allow authenticated sellers (and potentially admins) to modify core SKU properties such as name, merchant-facing code, pricing, inventory-related configuration, and status flags that control sellability, while keeping system-managed fields (like internal identifiers, timestamps, and denormalized aggregates) under platform control. The path parameters identify the product and SKU being updated, while the request body carries the new attribute values described by the `IShoppingMallSku.IUpdate` DTO.

From a business perspective, this operation is typically used from the seller portal when maintaining catalog data. It must enforce that the SKU being updated belongs to the specified product and is owned by the calling seller account, unless the caller is an admin with broader permissions. It should also coordinate with visibility and catalog rules defined in tables like `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` and inventory semantics defined in `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states`, ensuring that state transitions (e.g., from inactive to active) are valid given inventory levels and risk policies.

The operation returns the fully updated SKU entity as `IShoppingMallSku`, which may include denormalized or computed fields such as effective price after surcharges, derived availability flags, or aggregated rating snapshots from `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`. Error handling must cover invalid identifiers, ownership violations, concurrent modification conflicts, and business-rule violations such as attempting to activate a SKU with no sellable inventory.
operations.description:
Update an existing SKU variant for a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_skus` Prisma model, which stores concrete sellable variants for products. Each row typically includes fields such as a foreign key to the parent product in `shopping_mall_products`, seller ownership information, merchant-visible SKU code, pricing and taxation fields, and references to inventory state semantics defined in `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states`. The path parameters `productId` and `skuId` are expected to correspond to the primary key identifiers of the product and SKU, ensuring that the update is scoped to the correct product context.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint should normally be restricted to authenticated sellers that own the target product and its SKUs, and to privileged administrative actors for governance and support scenarios. The implementation must verify that the `shopping_mall_skus` record being updated is owned by the calling seller or is otherwise within the actor's permission scope. Additional validation should consider risk and policy configurations from `shopping_mall_business_policies`, `shopping_mall_policy_versions`, and `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules`, especially when state changes affect product visibility, price ranges, or eligibility for promotions.

The request body leverages the `IShoppingMallSku.IUpdate` DTO, which encapsulates mutable SKU attributes such as display name, description, merchant SKU code, base price, tax category references, inventory-related configuration, and flags controlling catalog visibility. The implementation must validate field-level constraints defined on the `shopping_mall_skus` columns (e.g., numeric ranges for price, required relationships for foreign keys) and maintain consistency with subsidiary tables like `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` or `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` when their data is affected by the update logic.

On success, the operation responds with `IShoppingMallSku`, representing the updated SKU entity with all persisted changes and any derived fields recomputed according to current business logic. Clients can use this result to refresh seller portal views or admin consoles immediately after the update. Error responses should clarify whether failures are due to invalid identifiers, authorization issues, violated business rules (such as disallowed price changes or invalid visibility transitions), or system-level problems like concurrent updates or transient database errors.
operations.summary: Update a SKU variant in the shopping_mall_skus table for a given product.

operations.name: update

The specific SKU record in shopping_mall_skus must exist before it can be updated; this POST creates the SKU identified later by skuId in the update path.
An inventory state row in shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states must exist before its UUID can be referenced by shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id when updating a SKU.
External identifier mappings in shopping_mall_sku_external_ids must exist before they can be updated via the SKU update DTO’s external_ids field; this POST creates those mappings for the SKU.

operations.specification:
This operation removes an existing SKU variant associated with a given product from the catalog perspective by performing a deletion on the underlying `shopping_mall_skus` Prisma table. It is primarily associated with `shopping_mall_skus`, but also impacts related subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values`, `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids`, and any catalog search or visibility projections (e.g., `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries`) that include the SKU.

The endpoint is used when a seller or admin decides that a particular SKU variant should no longer be available in the marketplace, such as when a size/color combination is permanently discontinued. The path parameters `productId` and `skuId` identify the precise SKU record to remove, and implementation logic must verify that the SKU belongs to the specified product and is owned by the calling seller account, unless the actor has elevated administrative privileges.

From a business rule perspective, the implementation must ensure that deleting a SKU is safe given order, payment, and fulfillment history. For example, the system may prohibit deletion of SKUs that appear in active orders in `shopping_mall_orders` and `shopping_mall_order_items`, instead requiring that such SKUs be marked inactive via fields on `shopping_mall_skus` or managed through catalog visibility rules. If hard deletion is allowed, cascading behavior must be carefully configured to maintain referential integrity for related tables. The endpoint does not accept a request body and typically returns no resource body, focusing solely on the removal action and appropriate HTTP status codes.

Error handling must cover scenarios such as non-existent product or SKU identifiers, ownership or authorization violations, business-rule violations preventing deletion, and conflicts due to concurrent catalog modifications. Logging of deletion events may be correlated with audit or risk tables such as `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs`, `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, or `shopping_mall_legal_holds` when the platform operates under strict governance requirements.
operations.description:
Delete an existing SKU variant for a specific product from the shoppingMall catalog.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_skus` Prisma model, which stores concrete sellable variants of products owned by sellers. By calling this endpoint with a specific `productId` and `skuId`, the client instructs the system to remove the corresponding row from `shopping_mall_skus`, effectively eliminating that variant from the catalog. The implementation must confirm that the SKU is indeed related to the given product, preventing accidental deletion of unrelated records.

Authorization is critical for this operation. Typically, only the seller that owns the product and its SKUs, or an administrator with elevated privileges, should be allowed to delete a SKU. Before performing the deletion, the system should validate that the caller has the necessary permissions according to actor and policy data across models such as `shopping_mall_sellers`, `shopping_mall_admins`, and any RBAC structures in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`. Additionally, business rules defined via `shopping_mall_business_policies` and `shopping_mall_policy_versions` may place restrictions on which SKUs can be removed, for example when legal holds or ongoing disputes exist.

No request body is accepted for this DELETE operation; all necessary context is conveyed via the path parameters and the authenticated actor. Upon successful deletion, the endpoint can either return an empty response or a minimal confirmation payload; in this specification we model it with no response body to keep the contract simple. Clients should handle HTTP status codes to determine whether the deletion was successful or if it failed due to authorization problems, missing resources, or business-rule constraints. Implementations should also coordinate with subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values`, `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids`, and indexing tables like `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` to ensure that any dependent data is either removed or updated appropriately.
operations.summary: Delete a SKU variant from the shopping_mall_skus table for a given product.

operations.name: erase

The SKU row in shopping_mall_skus must have been created before it can be deleted; this POST creates the SKU identified later by skuId in the DELETE path.

operations.specification:
Search and retrieve a paginated, filterable list of SKU variants from the shopping_mall_skus table.

This operation targets the ShoppingMall SKU entity represented by the Prisma model shopping_mall_skus. It exposes advanced search capabilities over core SKU fields such as code, barcode, status, price, original_price, inventory_quantity, low_stock_threshold, inventory_state, and timestamps. Because shopping_mall_skus is marked as a primary stance table and holds the authoritative inventory quantity for each SKU, this endpoint is the primary read surface for SKU-level catalog and inventory views in the ShoppingMall domain.

The request body uses IShoppingMallSku.IRequest to capture search filters (e.g., by product, status, inventory state, price range, creation period), sorting options (e.g., by created_at, updated_at, price, inventory_quantity), and pagination parameters. The response returns a paginated list container IPageIShoppingMallSku.ISummary which provides summary projections of the SKU records suitable for listing in admin consoles, seller portals, and internal tools.

This endpoint is read-only and does not alter any SKU or inventory data. It is optimized for backoffice/admin type usage because it can expose all status values (including blocked_by_admin) and see low-stock or deleted_at data that normal shoppers would not access. It is intended to be consumed by ShoppingMall admin applications and possibly internal services that require a canonical paginated read of SKU information.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of SKU records from the shopping_mall_skus table.

This operation reads from the Prisma model shopping_mall_skus, which represents stock keeping units that are the atomic sellable units in the ShoppingMall platform. Each record includes a product-level foreign key (shopping_mall_product_id), an inventory state foreign key (shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id), and business attributes such as code, barcode, status, price, original_price, inventory_quantity, low_stock_threshold, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The description comments in the schema emphasize that shopping_mall_skus is the authoritative source of current inventory quantity and SKU-level lifecycle status, and that attribute combinations and external IDs are modeled in separate tables (shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values and shopping_mall_sku_external_ids).

The request body type IShoppingMallSku.IRequest encapsulates search criteria and pagination options. Typical filters include SKU-level lifecycle status values (such as draft, active, inactive, discontinued, or blocked_by_admin), price ranges based on price and original_price, inventory thresholds using inventory_quantity and low_stock_threshold, and foreign-key based filtering by shopping_mall_product_id or inventory state. In addition, IShoppingMallSku.IRequest is expected to carry page number, page size, and sort order definitions so that the endpoint can support efficient listing and infinite-scroll style experiences in admin or seller tools.

Security-wise, the endpoint is restricted to the admin actor through authorizationActors: ["admin"]. The underlying data includes internal statuses, soft deletion timestamps (deleted_at), and potentially sensitive pricing that should not be exposed to end customers directly. Admin users can use this operation to monitor SKU health, identify low-stock situations, and audit the state of the catalog. Business logic in the service layer should enforce that only authorized administrators can access full data sets, and that any per-seller scoping or additional visibility rules are applied as needed.

The response body uses the type IPageIShoppingMallSku.ISummary to return a paginated collection of SKU summary objects along with pagination metadata. Summary projections may include commonly displayed fields like id, code, status, price, inventory_quantity, low_stock_threshold, and key timestamps, while omitting verbose or rarely used fields for performance. Related operations that complement this one are the GET /skus/{skuId} endpoint for detailed single-SKU retrieval and potential future write endpoints (create, update) that operate on the same shopping_mall_skus table. Error handling should clearly report invalid filter combinations, out-of-range pagination parameters, and authorization failures, allowing admin UI clients to provide actionable feedback to operators.
operations.summary: Search SKUs from shopping_mall_skus with filters, sorting, and pagination for admin usage.

requestBody.description: Search filters, sorting, and pagination parameters for listing ShoppingMall SKUs.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of ShoppingMall SKU summary records matching the search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A product must exist in shopping_mall_products before its SKUs can be created and later searched. Creating a product via this endpoint provides the productId used by seller SKU creation APIs that populate shopping_mall_skus.

At least one SKU record in shopping_mall_skus must exist for the search to return meaningful results. This endpoint creates SKUs under a product, populating the records queried by /shoppingMall/admin/skus.

Inventory state definitions in shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states should exist so that SKUs can reference a valid inventory state and filters like inventoryStateCode in the search request behave correctly.

operations.specification:
Retrieve detailed information for a single SKU from the shopping_mall_skus table by its primary identifier.

This operation targets the ShoppingMall SKU entity backed by the Prisma model shopping_mall_skus. It reads a single SKU row identified by its id primary key and returns a detailed projection of the SKU data via IShoppingMallSku. Because shopping_mall_skus is declared as the authoritative holder of current inventory_quantity and SKU-level lifecycle status, this endpoint is the canonical way for admin tools to inspect the full state of a specific SKU, including its business-level code, barcode, status, pricing, inventory quantity, low stock threshold, and timestamps.

The path parameter skuId carries the UUID primary key of the target record. The response body IShoppingMallSku can include all scalar fields from the model (id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id, code, barcode, status, price, original_price, inventory_quantity, low_stock_threshold, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). It may also be extended to include related entities loaded via relations, such as the associated product, inventory state, or attribute value combinations, but such compositions are handled at the DTO definition level.

This is a read-only endpoint suitable for administrative and internal tooling. It does not modify SKU or inventory data and should be optimized for quick retrieval of a single record by primary key.
operations.description:
Fetch detailed information about a single ShoppingMall SKU by its primary key from the shopping_mall_skus table.

The underlying Prisma model shopping_mall_skus stores concrete stock keeping units that represent specific sellable variants of products. According to the schema comments, each SKU belongs to a single shopping_mall_products record via shopping_mall_product_id and has a current inventory state via shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id. It also stores business identifiers like code and optional barcode, lifecycle status (such as draft, active, inactive, discontinued, or blocked_by_admin), pricing information via price and optional original_price, and inventory-related fields such as inventory_quantity and low_stock_threshold. Timestamps created_at and updated_at record when the SKU was created and last modified, while deleted_at captures when it was soft-deleted.

The path parameter skuId represents the UUID primary key of the SKU to retrieve and maps to the id field of shopping_mall_skus. When a valid identifier is provided and the caller is authorized, the operation returns an IShoppingMallSku object containing all relevant scalar fields and any relationships defined in the DTO, such as links to the owning product or the current inventory state reference. If the skuId does not correspond to any existing record, the operation should return a not-found error, allowing admin tools to handle missing resources gracefully.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is restricted to the admin actor via authorizationActors: ["admin"], because it provides full visibility into SKU status, pricing, and soft-deletion timestamps that are not intended for public consumption. In addition, business logic can enforce further checks, such as restricting access to SKUs from certain sellers based on admin permissions. This operation is typically used in conjunction with the PATCH /skus listing endpoint, where an administrator first finds a SKU in a paginated list and then drills down into its details by calling GET /skus/{skuId}. Error handling should cover invalid UUID formats, unauthorized access, and missing SKUs.
operations.summary: Get detailed information for a single SKU from shopping_mall_skus by its UUID id.

parameters.name: skuId
parameters.description: UUID primary key of the target ShoppingMall SKU (shopping_mall_skus.id).

responseBody.description: Detailed representation of the ShoppingMall SKU identified by the given primary key.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A parent product must exist in shopping_mall_products before a SKU can be created under it. This endpoint provides the productId referenced when creating the SKU.
A SKU inventory state definition must exist in shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states before SKUs can reference it, ensuring the inventory_state relation returned by this detail endpoint is valid.
The SKU itself must be created in shopping_mall_skus before it can be retrieved by its skuId. This endpoint creates the SKU record later fetched by GET /shoppingMall/admin/skus/{skuId}.

operations.specification:
List attribute value links for a specific SKU based on the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values subsidiary table, scoped by the parent SKU in shopping_mall_skus. This PATCH operation retrieves a filtered, paginated list of SKU-attribute-value link records for a single SKU, primarily for use in seller or admin product management UIs.

The underlying Prisma models are:
- shopping_mall_skus (primary): holds SKU-level data such as code, price, status, and inventory, identified by id (UUID) with a composite unique index on [shopping_mall_product_id, code].
- shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values (subsidiary): junction table linking shopping_mall_skus to shopping_mall_product_attribute_values via foreign keys shopping_mall_sku_id and shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id, with a unique index on [shopping_mall_sku_id, shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id].

This operation focuses on reading SKU attribute value links only. Because shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values is subsidiary and always managed as part of product/SKU flows, this endpoint does not expose direct creation or mutation of the link records; it merely enumerates them for a given SKU. The DTO type IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.IRequest will allow filters such as specific attribute value ids or created_at ranges, and the response uses IPageIShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.ISummary to return a paginated summary list suitable for grid or table display.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of attribute value links for a specific SKU, using the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values subsidiary table scoped by a parent SKU in shopping_mall_skus.

The primary purpose of this operation is to help seller and admin tools inspect which product attribute values have been applied to a particular SKU. Each record in shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values links a shopping_mall_skus.id via shopping_mall_sku_id to a shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.id via shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id. The description comments on shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values emphasize that this table purely models the many-to-many binding between SKUs and attribute values, with created_at, updated_at, and optional deleted_at timestamps for lifecycle tracking.

From a security standpoint, this endpoint should typically be restricted to authenticated actors that are allowed to manage or review catalog information, most commonly sellers managing their own catalog or platform admins. In this specification we use a seller actor, assuming that downstream authorization logic will enforce ownership or role checks based on the authenticated principal and the SKU in question. The operation itself is read-only and does not modify any state.

On the data side, the request body type IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.IRequest is expected to include search and pagination criteria such as page index, page size, optional filters by shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id, and created_at/updated_at ranges. Because the path already includes the parent SKU identifier as skuId, that contextual identifier must not be duplicated inside the request DTO; the implementation will always constrain shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_sku_id to the given skuId. The response type IPageIShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.ISummary will carry a list of summary rows for each link, including at minimum the link id and possibly denormalized attribute label information.

This operation will commonly be used together with SKU detail and product attribute definition endpoints. For example, a UI might first call GET /skus/{skuId} to show core SKU details, then PATCH /skus/{skuId}/attributeValues (this endpoint) to load the list of applied attributes, and finally use separate product attribute endpoints to allow adding or removing attribute values. Error handling should cover invalid or non-existent skuId, permission denials when the current actor cannot see the SKU, and standard pagination validation problems.
operations.summary: Search and list shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values records for a specific shopping_mall_skus SKU.

parameters.name: skuId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent SKU whose attribute value links are being listed. This corresponds to shopping_mall_skus.id and scopes the search to a single SKU record.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for listing SKU attribute value links associated with the specified SKU.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of SKU attribute value link summaries for the given SKU, based on shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
Retrieve the detail of a specific SKU attribute value link belonging to a particular SKU, based on the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values subsidiary table and its relationship to shopping_mall_skus.

The underlying Prisma models are:
- shopping_mall_skus (primary): represents the SKU that uses the attribute value, referenced by shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_sku_id.
- shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values (subsidiary): junction entity with primary key id (UUID), linking a SKU to a product attribute value, with timestamps created_at, updated_at, and optional deleted_at.

This GET operation returns a single IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue detail DTO representing the link identified by skuAttributeValueId, while also verifying that it belongs to the parent SKU identified by skuId. Because shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values is modeled as subsidiary, this operation exposes read-only access for inspection and debugging of SKU configuration, not for direct modification of the link record.
operations.description:
Get detailed information about a single SKU attribute value link belonging to a specific SKU, using the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values subsidiary table as the underlying data source.

In the Prisma schema, shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values defines a junction between shopping_mall_skus and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values, with its own id field as primary key and foreign key fields shopping_mall_sku_id and shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id. The model also tracks lifecycle timestamps created_at and updated_at, plus an optional deleted_at field indicating when a link has been logically removed. This operation focuses on reading one such link record so that clients can understand exactly which attribute value has been applied to a SKU and when.

Security-wise, this endpoint should be accessible only to authenticated actors that have permission to inspect catalog configuration. As with the list operation, we specify a seller actor and rely on downstream authorization to enforce that the caller can see the SKU and its attributes. The implementation must verify both that the link identified by skuAttributeValueId exists and that its shopping_mall_sku_id matches the skuId path parameter, ensuring that callers cannot access links for unrelated SKUs by guessing identifiers.

The response body type IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue will return the full representation of the link row, including identifiers, foreign key references, and timestamp metadata. Clients will typically use this operation in conjunction with the list endpoint PATCH /skus/{skuId}/attributeValues and product attribute metadata endpoints. For example, after retrieving a list of attribute links, a UI might call GET /skus/{skuId}/attributeValues/{skuAttributeValueId} to show detailed information or to prefill a confirmation dialog before an attribute removal action handled by a separate update API. Error handling should cover non-existent skuId, non-existent skuAttributeValueId, mismatches between the two, and permission denials.

operations.specification:
Create one or more SKU attribute value association records for a specific SKU in the shopping mall catalog. This operation is conceptually based on the `shopping_mall_skus` primary model and the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` subsidiary model in the Prisma schema, where each association links a concrete SKU variant to one or more predefined product attribute values (for example, color, size, or material).

The HTTP endpoint `POST /skus/{skuId}/attributeValues` accepts a path parameter `skuId` identifying the target SKU by its primary key, and a JSON request body described by `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.ICreate`. The DTO is expected to contain the attribute value references and any additional metadata needed to create the association entries, while the SKU identifier itself is derived exclusively from the path parameter to avoid duplication and inconsistencies.

On execution, the service layer must validate that the given SKU exists in `shopping_mall_skus`, that each referenced attribute value is valid for the underlying product, and that the combination of attribute values does not violate any uniqueness constraints defined in `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values`. If validation passes, new junction records are inserted and the created representations are returned to the client using the `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue` DTO.
operations.description:
Create SKU attribute value associations for a specific SKU using the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` junction table.

This operation enables a seller or catalog management process to attach concrete attribute values to a SKU so that it becomes a fully specified variant within the shopping mall product catalog. In the Prisma schema, `shopping_mall_skus` represents a sellable variant tied to a product, while `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` stores the many-to-many link between SKUs and product attribute values defined elsewhere. Each association record typically includes foreign keys to the SKU and the attribute value, and may also include additional fields such as display order, flags indicating primary attributes, or audit metadata according to the schema comments.

From an authorization perspective, this endpoint should only be accessible to authenticated actors that are allowed to manage the catalog for the seller who owns the SKU. In this specification, `authorizationActors` is set to `["seller"]` to express that intention, while fine-grained ownership checks must be implemented in the business logic. The implementation should verify that the authenticated seller is indeed allowed to modify the specified SKU, and should reject attempts to bind attribute values that do not belong to the same product or that would break integrity rules.

The request body is described by `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.ICreate`. This DTO should mirror the creatable columns of the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` model except for the SKU identifier, which is taken solely from the path. For example, it may contain one or more attribute value identifiers, optional ordering indexes, and any other configuration fields declared in the Prisma model. The server must enforce schema-level constraints such as required fields, supported ranges, and uniqueness rules and must surface validation failures using consistent error responses.

On success, the API returns an `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue` representation describing the newly created association (or the primary created association if the DTO is modeled as single-item creation). The response allows clients to confirm which attribute value is now linked to the SKU and to display it in management UIs. Typical error scenarios include missing or invalid `skuId`, attribute value identifiers that do not exist or are incompatible with the SKU’s product, and insufficient permissions. These should be mapped to appropriate HTTP status codes (for example 400 for validation errors and 403 for authorization failures). Related operations include updating an existing SKU-attribute link via `PUT /skus/{skuId}/attributeValues/{skuAttributeValueId}` and potential deletion operations if hard removal of links is supported elsewhere in the API surface.

operations.specification:
Update an existing SKU attribute value association record for a specific SKU in the shopping mall catalog. This operation targets a single row in the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` subsidiary model, which represents the link between a SKU in `shopping_mall_skus` and a particular product attribute value.

The HTTP endpoint `PUT /skus/{skuId}/attributeValues/{skuAttributeValueId}` accepts two path parameters: `skuId` identifies the parent SKU, and `skuAttributeValueId` identifies the specific association record to update. The request body is described by `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.IUpdate`, which exposes the updatable columns of the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` model, excluding the identifying foreign key and primary key values that are already provided via the path.

When invoked, the service must validate that both the SKU and the association record exist and that the association indeed belongs to the specified SKU, preventing cross-SKU modification errors. It should also enforce any business rules declared in the Prisma schema comments, such as disallowing changes that would create conflicting combinations of attribute values for the same SKU or violate uniqueness constraints. After successful validation, the record is updated and the fresh `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue` representation is returned.
operations.description:
Update a specific SKU attribute value association belonging to a given SKU using the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` table.

This operation is used when a seller or catalog administrator needs to adjust properties of an existing SKU-attribute link, such as changing flags, ordering fields, or other configurable columns defined on the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` Prisma model. The parent SKU is represented by `skuId`, and the particular association record is identified by `skuAttributeValueId`. Both identifiers are required and must consistently reference a record where the association row’s SKU foreign key matches the provided `skuId`.

As with creation, only authorized catalog managers should be allowed to perform updates. The `authorizationActors` array is set to `["seller"]` to indicate that the typical caller is a seller user managing their own catalog. In the implementation, the authenticated seller must be checked against the owner of the SKU to avoid unauthorized changes to other sellers’ data. Business rules implied by the Prisma schema—such as constraints on which fields may change after orders exist, or restrictions on modifying attribute combinations that are already in use—should be enforced and any violations communicated using structured error responses.

The request body uses the `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.IUpdate` DTO, which should include only fields that are allowed to change for an existing association. For example, if the schema differentiates between immutable attribute value references and mutable display ordering, the DTO should reflect that so that core linking fields remain stable after creation. On successful update, the endpoint responds with the updated `IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue` object, allowing clients to refresh their local state. Typical failure modes include missing records, mismatched `skuId` and `skuAttributeValueId` relationships, invalid field values, and authorization failures.

This update endpoint complements the creation endpoint `POST /skus/{skuId}/attributeValues` and any read or delete endpoints defined elsewhere, forming a coherent set of CRUD-style operations for managing SKU-attribute relationships in the shopping mall catalog domain.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a specific SKU attribute value association from a given SKU, operating primarily on the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` model in the Prisma schema. The endpoint allows authorized back-office actors to detach or erase an attribute value mapping from a SKU, which is typically used when correcting variant configurations or cleaning up invalid combinations.

The SKU itself is represented by the `shopping_mall_skus` model, while the attribute value link being removed is represented by a record in `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values`. The `skuId` path parameter identifies the parent SKU, and the `skuAttributeValueId` path parameter identifies the specific attribute value association to delete under that SKU. The implementation must validate that the specified attribute value link actually belongs to the given SKU before deletion and MUST return a 404 Not Found response if the association does not exist or is not linked to the provided `skuId`.

From a business perspective, this operation is used in catalog and inventory management flows where a seller or administrator needs to adjust variant definitions. Removing an attribute value mapping will affect how the SKU is presented in product detail pages, variant selectors, and inventory tracking logic. The deletion is a hard removal of the association record; related inventory or SKU records remain intact, but any logic relying on the removed attribute value must handle its absence gracefully. Implementations may also emit internal audit logs for catalog changes, although such logs are not exposed by this API.
operations.description:
Erase a specific attribute value association from a given SKU using the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` table as the underlying data source.

This operation targets scenarios where a SKU’s variant configuration needs to be corrected or simplified. The `skuId` path parameter identifies the parent SKU record from the `shopping_mall_skus` model, and the `skuAttributeValueId` path parameter identifies the row in `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` that links this SKU to a particular attribute value (for example, a specific color or size value). The service must first verify that the attribute value association exists and belongs to the SKU indicated by `skuId`. If there is a mismatch or the association is not found for this SKU, the implementation MUST respond with a 404 Not Found and must not delete any other association.

Security and authorization are important because modifying SKU attribute values directly affects what customers see and can purchase. This endpoint is therefore restricted to authenticated back-office actors, such as admins or internal catalog managers, represented here generically as the `admin` actor. The implementation should enforce that only users with sufficient catalog-management permissions can call this operation and should record any changes in internal audit mechanisms where required by business policy, even though those logs are not exposed by this API.

From the database perspective, the operation issues a hard delete against the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` model scoped by both the unique identifier of the attribute value association and the SKU identifier. This ensures that only the intended association is removed and prevents accidental deletion of attribute links belonging to other SKUs. The SKU record in `shopping_mall_skus` remains in place, as do the base product and attribute definitions; only the specific association row is removed. Related API operations include listing attribute values for a SKU and creating or updating SKU attribute mappings, which would use the same underlying models but different HTTP methods and request bodies.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of external identifier records associated with a specific SKU, using the `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` model as the primary data source. External IDs are used to link SKUs in the shoppingMall platform to identifiers in external systems such as ERP, WMS, marketplace channels, or partner catalogs.

The `skuId` path parameter identifies the parent SKU record in the `shopping_mall_skus` table whose external IDs are being queried. The request body uses a dedicated DTO, `IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.IRequest`, to express optional filters such as external system type, identifier patterns, and pagination or sorting options. The response returns a paginated collection of external ID summaries in the `IPageIShoppingMallSkuExternalId.ISummary` format, which is optimized for list and management views in back-office UIs.

This is a read-only operation intended primarily for internal users such as admins or catalog operators who need to inspect how a SKU is mapped to external systems. It does not modify data but must respect authorization rules so that only actors with access to catalog integration configurations can view these mappings. The underlying implementation should join or filter by the `skuId` foreign key in `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` and apply any search criteria provided in the request DTO, while ensuring consistent ordering and predictable pagination behavior for user interfaces. Implementations may also record internal audit or access logs for observability, though those are not part of this API surface.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of external identifier mappings for a specific SKU from the `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` model.

This operation serves catalog and integration management workflows where internal users need to see how a given SKU is linked to external systems. The `skuId` path parameter identifies the SKU record in `shopping_mall_skus`, and the request body of type `IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.IRequest` allows callers to provide search filters, such as targeting a specific external system, narrowing to certain identifier patterns, or selecting result ordering and page size. The operation always scopes results to the given `skuId` and does not support cross-SKU queries, ensuring that only external IDs for this SKU are returned.

Although this is a read-only endpoint, it should be protected so that only authorized back-office actors, represented here as `admin`, can access detailed external mapping information. This helps prevent the accidental disclosure of integration identifiers and configuration details. The service should validate that the referenced SKU exists before executing the query against `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids`, returning a not-found error if the SKU is invalid. Errors related to invalid pagination parameters or unsupported filter values should be reported clearly so that clients can correct their requests.

The response body uses the `IPageIShoppingMallSkuExternalId.ISummary` type to return a paginated collection of summary representations of SKU external IDs. This summary type is designed for list views that show key fields such as the external system identifier, external ID string, and status flags, without necessarily including all internal metadata. Related operations, not covered by this specific endpoint, would handle creating, updating, or deleting individual external ID mappings for a SKU and would be implemented as POST, PUT, or DELETE endpoints on related paths.
