operations.specification:
Create a new catalog block reason record in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table.

This operation accepts administrative input describing a new reusable reason why catalog entities may be blocked or removed from sale and persists it as a primary configuration entity. It writes to the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table, populating the code, name, description, severity_level, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields according to the Prisma schema definition.

The request body follows the IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.ICreate DTO, which must include at minimum the non-nullable columns code, name, and severity_level. The code must be unique across all existing block reasons, as enforced by the unique index on code in the Prisma schema; attempts to create a duplicate code should result in a conflict-style error. The severity_level is expected to be a business-level classification such as low, medium, or high; server-side validation should ensure only allowed values are accepted according to platform policy, even though the Prisma schema itself models severity_level as a generic string.

Timestamps created_at and updated_at are typically set automatically by the backend at insertion time and should not be supplied directly by clients. The deleted_at column is nullable and should be null on creation, indicating that the block reason is active. The response returns the fully populated IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason entity as stored, allowing admin tools to immediately display the configured reason or reference it in further catalog visibility rules or moderation workflows.
operations.description:
Create a new catalog block reason configuration entry in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table.

According to the Prisma schema, shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons is a primary reference table that centrally describes reasons why catalog entities such as products or SKUs are blocked or removed from sale. Each record defines a reusable business-level reason like policy_violation, legal_request, counterfeit_suspected, or safety_issue. This POST operation allows authorized administrators to register new such reasons as part of governance and policy management.

The request body must conform to the IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.ICreate structure. At minimum, it must provide values for the non-nullable string columns code, name, and severity_level. The code field is constrained by a unique index in the Prisma schema, so the implementation must validate that no existing block reason already uses the proposed code; if a duplicate is detected, the API should respond with a 409-style conflict error indicating that the machine-readable code must be unique. The name field is the human-readable label displayed in administrative UIs, and severity_level is a business classification (for example low, medium, or high) used in risk reporting and dashboards.

Optional description text may be supplied to guide admins and moderators on when this block reason should be chosen. The created_at and updated_at timestamp columns are non-nullable in the schema and should be assigned by the backend at creation time using the current system time. The deleted_at column is nullable and should remain null for newly created reasons, indicating the reason is active and may be used by visibility rules and other enforcement mechanisms.

This operation is restricted to administrative actors, as catalog block reasons represent governance configuration that affects how products and SKUs are exposed across the marketplace. The authorizationActors field therefore specifies admin. Related operations include GET /catalogBlockReasons/{catalogBlockReasonId} for retrieving a single configured reason and a potential future list/search endpoint for browsing or reporting on configured reasons. Error handling should clearly report validation failures such as missing required fields, invalid severity_level values per business rules, and unique constraint violations for code.
operations.summary: Create a new shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons configuration entry.

requestBody.description: Creation payload for a new catalog block reason, including code, name, optional description, and severity level.

responseBody.description: Newly created catalog block reason record from shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons with all fields populated.

operations.name: create

operations.specification:
Update an existing catalog block reason in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons Prisma model. This operation allows administrators or internal governance tools to modify the descriptive metadata and configuration of a reason code that explains why catalog entities such as products or SKUs are blocked or removed from sale. It targets a single record identified by its unique catalogBlockReasonId primary key.

The operation uses HTTP PUT on the /catalogBlockReasons/{catalogBlockReasonId} path to express a full update of the reason entity using a structured DTO type IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.IUpdate. Implementations should load the existing shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons row, validate the incoming fields against business rules, apply the updates, and persist the changes in a transactional way. The updated entity is then returned as an IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason representation for client confirmation and subsequent UI refresh.

This endpoint is part of the broader governance and catalog quality feature set. It is typically consumed by administrative consoles or internal back-office tools and should not be exposed to general marketplace actors such as customers or sellers.
operations.description:
Update a specific catalog block reason record maintained in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table.

This operation is designed for administrative management of catalog governance metadata. The underlying Prisma model shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons holds structured reason codes that describe why catalog entities such as products, SKUs, or other catalog items are blocked, hidden, or removed from sale in the shoppingMall platform. Typical fields in this model include a human-readable label, an internal code, a descriptive explanation, and flags that indicate whether the reason is user-visible or internal-only. When administrators need to adjust wording, update policy references, or change visibility flags without creating an entirely new reason code, they use this endpoint.

From a security and authorization perspective, this operation must be restricted to administrative actors only. Normal customers, guest users, or sellers must not gain the ability to modify catalog block reasons, since these definitions drive governance rules and can have compliance impact. The authorizationActors array therefore contains only "admin", and the actual implementation should enforce appropriate RBAC logic on top of this. Access to this endpoint should be audited so that any changes to block reasons can be traced back to the responsible administrator.

Technically, the endpoint receives a JSON payload of type IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.IUpdate in the request body. This DTO is aligned with the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons fields and supports updating mutable properties such as descriptive text, localized labels, or configuration flags. The catalogBlockReasonId path parameter uniquely identifies the target row using its primary key; the service must validate that this record exists before applying updates. If the record is not found, the service should return an appropriate not-found error.

In typical workflows, this update operation is used together with a list/index endpoint that searches or lists reasons and a create endpoint that registers new codes. For example, an admin may first search reasons via a PATCH /catalogBlockReasons operation (returning IPageIShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.ISummary), select one item from the list, load its detail via a GET /catalogBlockReasons/{catalogBlockReasonId}, and finally call this PUT endpoint to adjust the wording or flags. Error handling should clearly report validation failures on fields such as code uniqueness or invalid state transitions so that admin UIs can guide the operator to fix the input.
operations.summary: Update a catalog block reason record in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table by identifier.

parameters.name: catalogBlockReasonId
parameters.description: Primary key identifier of the catalog block reason to update in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table. This value uniquely selects the specific reason code whose descriptive metadata and configuration flags will be modified.

requestBody.description: Updated fields for the catalog block reason, mapped to mutable columns of the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table, such as descriptive text, labels, and configuration flags.

responseBody.description: The updated catalog block reason entity after applying changes, reflecting the current state of the corresponding row in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A catalog block reason must first be created in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons before it can be updated by its catalogBlockReasonId.

operations.specification:
Permanently delete an existing catalog block reason from the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons Prisma model. This operation removes a reason code that is no longer needed or that has been superseded by a different configuration. It targets a single row identified by its catalogBlockReasonId primary key and executes a hard delete at the database level.

The operation uses HTTP DELETE on the /catalogBlockReasons/{catalogBlockReasonId} path, with no request body. Implementation logic should verify that the target shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons entry exists and that business rules permit its removal, for example ensuring that the reason is not mandated by active legal holds or still referenced in immutable audit trails. Once validations pass, the service deletes the row and returns either no content or an optional confirmation payload. In this specification, responseBody is set to null, implying that the client should infer success from the HTTP status code.

As this endpoint impacts governance configuration and could affect how blocked catalog items are explained to users, it is intended exclusively for administrative tools and must be protected accordingly.
operations.description:
Erase a specific catalog block reason from the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table using its primary key identifier.

The shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons model defines reference data that describes why products, SKUs, or other catalog entities are blocked, hidden, or otherwise unavailable in the shoppingMall platform. Each record typically contains an internal code, a human-readable label, detailed explanation text, and potentially configuration flags that indicate whether the reason is exposed to customers or reserved for internal use. When a particular reason code becomes obsolete, has been merged into another policy, or must be withdrawn for governance reasons, administrators can remove it using this DELETE operation.

Access to this endpoint must be strictly limited to administrative actors, as indicated by authorizationActors set to ["admin"]. Removing a catalog block reason can change how future blocks are categorized and may impact reporting or downstream analytics. Implementations should therefore enforce RBAC checks and log all deletions in an appropriate audit mechanism, such as the shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs table, to ensure traceability. Additionally, domain rules may require that reasons referenced by immutable records (for example, existing orders or legal hold targets) are not allowed to be deleted; such constraints should be validated before performing the hard delete.

The operation accepts no request body; it relies solely on the catalogBlockReasonId path parameter to locate the target record in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons. If no matching record is found, the service should return a not-found error rather than silently succeeding. When the deletion completes, the service typically returns a 204 No Content status with an empty response body, as modeled here by a null responseBody field. This endpoint complements the create and update operations for catalog block reasons and is commonly used from admin consoles where governance staff manage the lifecycle of these codes.
operations.summary: Delete a catalog block reason record from the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table by identifier.

parameters.name: catalogBlockReasonId
parameters.description: Primary key identifier of the catalog block reason to delete from the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table. This value uniquely selects the reason code that will be permanently removed.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A catalog block reason must exist in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons before it can be permanently deleted by its catalogBlockReasonId.

operations.specification:
This operation provides an aggregated catalog overview for the ShoppingMall platform, synthesizing data primarily from core catalog-related Prisma models such as `shopping_mall_categories`, `shopping_mall_products`, `shopping_mall_skus`, `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules`, and related rating aggregate tables like `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` once those schemas are available. Rather than exposing raw table rows, the endpoint returns a denormalized dashboard-style view that helps clients render a high-level overview of the current state of the catalog in a single call.

The operation is designed as a read-only GET endpoint and therefore does not require a request body. It returns a single `IShoppingMallCatalogOverview` DTO (a computed, non-table-mapped structure) that may include counts of active products and SKUs, category tree summary information, basic rating statistics, and visibility status summaries keyed by actor type. The focus is on providing at-a-glance catalog metrics and structural information for use on landing pages, admin dashboards, or seller/customer-facing overviews.

Because it is an aggregated view, the implementation may internally query multiple Prisma models, join data, and compute derived metrics such as number of products per top-level category or percentage of products currently purchasable. No write operations or side effects occur as part of this endpoint, and it must respect catalog visibility rules so that only publicly visible entities are reflected when the endpoint is called without authentication. The endpoint is public (`authorizationActors: []`) so it can be used to build anonymous-facing catalog overview pages.
operations.description:
Retrieve a high-level overview of the ShoppingMall catalog as a single aggregated resource.

This operation is intended to serve as a catalog dashboard endpoint that aggregates important information about products, SKUs, and categories into a single response structure. While the underlying data resides in multiple Prisma models such as `shopping_mall_categories` for the global product taxonomy, `shopping_mall_products` for individual product concepts, and `shopping_mall_skus` for concrete sellable variants, the client does not interact with those tables directly through this endpoint. Instead, the system computes totals, summaries, and structural representations and returns them as a purpose-built `IShoppingMallCatalogOverview` DTO.

From a security and exposure perspective, the endpoint is intentionally defined as a public GET operation with no authentication requirements, allowing it to power public-facing landing pages and listing overviews. Even though it is public, the implementation must still respect any catalog visibility constraints configured in tables like `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` and potentially blocklisted or removed entities captured in `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons`. Only items that are considered visible to anonymous users should influence the counts and structures returned.

Internally, the operation may compose data from primary entities such as categories, products, and SKUs, as well as subsidiary and snapshot entities used for performance optimization and pre-aggregation, for example rating aggregate tables that summarize review scores per product or SKU. However, this composition is entirely read-only and occurs at query time or via precomputed materialized views; the operation does not mutate any of the underlying tables. In error scenarios, such as temporary unavailability of specific aggregates, the implementation should fail gracefully and either omit the affected sections or return an appropriate error response, while never exposing low-level database details to clients.
operations.summary: Get an aggregated ShoppingMall catalog overview derived from catalog-related tables.

responseBody.description: Aggregated overview information for the ShoppingMall catalog, including high-level category, product, SKU, and visibility summaries computed from multiple catalog-related tables.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation returns computed statistics about product availability across the ShoppingMall catalog, aggregating data from inventory- and visibility-related Prisma models such as `shopping_mall_skus`, `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states`, `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments`, and `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` when those schemas are present. Rather than exposing raw SKU or adjustment records, it summarizes how many products and SKUs are available, low in stock, out of stock, or otherwise constrained.

The endpoint is implemented as a read-only GET operation at `/catalog/statistics/productAvailability` and does not accept a request body. It returns an `IShoppingMallProductAvailabilityStatistics` DTO which is a computed, non-table-mapped structure that may contain counts and ratios of products by availability bucket, breakdowns per inventory state, and potentially segmentations by seller or warehouse category depending on business requirements. These statistics are intended for reporting, monitoring, or dashboard use rather than for transactional operations.

Internally, the implementation will likely query the SKU-level inventory state model, interpret configured inventory state semantics from `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states`, and apply catalog visibility constraints from `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` so that only sellable catalog items contribute to the public statistics. It may also consider legal holds or policy overrides in models such as `shopping_mall_legal_holds` or `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` when computing effective availability. All processing is read-only and side-effect free, and the endpoint is public to allow it to support general reporting and marketplace health indicators on public or semi-public dashboards.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics describing product availability across the ShoppingMall catalog.

This operation focuses specifically on availability-related analytics rather than general catalog structure. It computes metrics using inventory and visibility information stored in underlying Prisma models such as `shopping_mall_skus` for concrete sellable variants, `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states` for the semantic meaning of inventory statuses, and `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments` for the history of inventory changes. The result is packaged into an `IShoppingMallProductAvailabilityStatistics` DTO designed for analytical consumption.

From a security perspective, the endpoint is exposed as a public GET operation with no authentication requirements, which allows it to be used in high-level marketplace health dashboards, public statistics pages, or internal admin overviews that do not require user-specific context. Despite being public, the implementation must obey catalog visibility and governance rules configured via models such as `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules`, risk or legal hold records, and potential policy overrides. Products or SKUs that are hidden, blocked, or under legal hold must be excluded or treated according to business policy when computing availability metrics.

In terms of behavior and error handling, the operation is strictly read-only and must not modify inventory or catalog data. If certain underlying tables are temporarily unavailable or partial data is encountered, the implementation should either degrade gracefully by returning partial statistics clearly documented in the response or fail with an appropriate error response. Clients relying on this endpoint should treat it as a source of approximate real-time availability insights rather than a transactional source of truth for individual SKUs, which are handled by more specific catalog and inventory APIs.
operations.summary: Get aggregated product availability statistics for the ShoppingMall catalog.

responseBody.description: Aggregated product availability metrics across the ShoppingMall catalog, computed from SKU inventory and visibility data.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated statistics for the top-selling SKUs across the entire shoppingMall platform. It is conceptually based on sales and order-related Prisma tables such as shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, and shopping_mall_skus, even though the statistics themselves may be computed dynamically rather than stored in a single dedicated table. The endpoint returns a ranked list of SKU-level performance metrics over a configurable analysis window.

The operation supports optional query parameters via the request body for specifying the analysis period (for example, last 7 days, last 30 days, or a custom date range), limiting the maximum number of SKUs returned, and filtering by seller or product category where applicable. The statistics per SKU typically include total units sold, total revenue, average selling price, and share of overall sales.

The response body type IShoppingMallCatalogTopSellingSkuStatistics encapsulates each SKU’s identifier, reference information (product, seller), and aggregate metrics needed for dashboards and analytics views. The endpoint is read-only and designed for dashboard widgets, admin reports, and seller analytics surfaces that need to identify best-selling items.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics describing the top-selling SKUs on the shoppingMall platform over a specified analysis window.

This operation executes read-only analytical queries over order and SKU related data, including models such as shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, and shopping_mall_skus. It computes aggregate metrics like total_units_sold, total_revenue, and average_unit_price for each SKU, then ranks SKUs in descending order of sales performance. The goal is to provide a concise list of SKUs that contribute the most to platform revenue or order volume within the analysis period.

Security-wise, this statistics endpoint is intended for internal dashboards and administrative analytics. As such, it should typically be exposed only to authorized backoffice users or to internal services composing management UIs. No per-user private data is returned; all statistics are aggregated at SKU level, but access should still be controlled to prevent leakage of platform-wide commercial intelligence.

From a database perspective, the computation may rely on joins between shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items to determine which SKUs were purchased, and on shopping_mall_skus (and possibly shopping_mall_products) to resolve catalog metadata. Implementations may pre-aggregate data into snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_order_daily_stats for efficiency, but the logical contract of this API is to return a ranked list of top-selling SKUs regardless of the underlying storage strategy.

The request body type IShoppingMallCatalogTopSellingSkuStatistics.IRequest allows clients to specify optional filters such as time range, maximum result count, seller constraints, or category filters. The response body type IShoppingMallCatalogTopSellingSkuStatistics encapsulates the final list of top-selling SKUs with their aggregate metrics. Error handling should cover invalid time windows, excessively large requested limits, and cases where no sales data is available for the given criteria, returning an empty list in the latter case.

Related operations may include other catalog analytics endpoints such as block reason breakdown, general sales dashboards, or seller-specific performance reports, which together form a comprehensive analytics surface for the shoppingMall catalog.
operations.summary: Retrieve top-selling SKU statistics derived from order and SKU tables in the shoppingMall schema.

requestBody.description: Optional filters and configuration for computing top-selling SKU statistics, including analysis time window, result limit, and optional seller or category filters.

responseBody.description: Aggregated statistics for each of the top-selling SKUs that match the specified criteria, ranked by sales performance.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation returns a breakdown of catalog block reasons across products and SKUs in the shoppingMall platform. It conceptually aggregates data based on the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table (which defines standardized reasons why catalog entities may be blocked or removed from sale) and any linkage tables that record which products or SKUs are currently blocked for which reasons. The statistics describe how many entities are affected per block reason and optionally segment those counts by dimensions such as seller, category, or severity.

The endpoint is implemented as a read-only analytical query rather than simple CRUD on a single table. It may aggregate over catalog visibility and block linkage tables together with shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_skus to determine which entities are currently blocked or were blocked during a specified time window. Its primary use case is operational monitoring and governance dashboards for catalog health and policy enforcement.

The response type IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReasonBreakdownStatistics summarizes each block reason (for example, policy_violation, legal_hold, low_quality_content, or risk_flagged) along with counts of affected products and SKUs, and may include percentage share of total blocked entities. This information allows admins and governance teams to quickly identify systemic issues, uncommon block patterns, and trends over time.
operations.description:
Provide an aggregated breakdown of catalog block reasons across products and SKUs within the shoppingMall platform.

This operation is built upon catalog governance and policy enforcement models including shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and the various catalog visibility or block linkage tables that associate reasons with specific products or SKUs. For each block reason, it counts the number of active product or SKU records currently blocked, and may compute additional metrics like percentage share of total blocked entities or trend indicators if a time window is provided.

From a security and governance perspective, the endpoint is intended for admin-facing dashboards and internal monitoring tools. It exposes platform-level policy and moderation statistics, which can reveal sensitive operational details, so it is restricted to administrative actors only. While the results are aggregated and do not contain end-user personal data, they reflect internal enforcement policies and thus must not be exposed publicly.

Implementation-wise, the service may query shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons as a reference table of all possible reasons, and join it with tables that record which products or SKUs are blocked, possibly also consulting policy-related tables such as shopping_mall_business_policies or shopping_mall_policy_versions. If performance requirements are stringent, the system may maintain materialized snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots that pre-aggregate block reason counts by day; this endpoint would then read from those snapshots while still honoring requested filters.

The request body type IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReasonBreakdownStatistics.IRequest allows clients to specify filters such as time windows, specific sellers, or catalog segments. The response body type IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReasonBreakdownStatistics contains the final aggregated breakdown, with each entry detailing a block reason code, human-readable description, affected counts, and optionally derived ratios. Error handling includes validating filter parameters and safely returning an empty breakdown when no blocked entities match the criteria.

This operation is closely related to other catalog analytics endpoints such as top-selling SKU statistics or general platform KPI snapshots. Together, they support a holistic view of catalog health, policy enforcement, and commercial performance for the shoppingMall platform.
operations.summary: Return an aggregated breakdown of catalog block reasons using shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and related linkage tables.

requestBody.description: Optional filters and configuration for computing catalog block reason breakdown statistics, including time window, seller filters, and catalog segment constraints.

responseBody.description: Aggregated statistics for each catalog block reason, including counts of affected products and SKUs and optional ratio metrics.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation performs an advanced search over shopping cart headers in the `shopping_mall_carts` Prisma table. It is designed as a PATCH collection endpoint so that complex filter criteria, pagination, and sorting options can be expressed in a structured JSON request body instead of overloading query parameters.

The underlying `shopping_mall_carts` model represents cart header entities for both guest users and authenticated customers. Typical fields include unique identifiers, ownership linkage to either a registered customer or a guest user identity, timestamps for creation and last update, and state-related fields indicating whether the cart is active, converted to an order, or abandoned. While the exact fields must be taken from the Prisma schema during implementation, this operation’s DTOs (`IShoppingMallCart.IRequest` and `IPageIShoppingMallCart.ISummary`) are defined to mirror those fields and to expose only information suitable for list views.

The business purpose of this endpoint is to allow internal tools, administrative consoles, and potentially background services to query carts based on a wide range of criteria, such as ownership type (guest vs customer), activity period (last updated within a time window), cart size (number of items), monetary estimates, or status flags. It is also the preferred way to implement cart search features in back-office UIs where operators need to locate carts by email, user reference, or other correlated metadata that is represented in the cart header.

Consumers of this API send a structured search object that contains filter conditions, pagination parameters (page, pageSize), and sorting configuration (sort field and direction). The implementation must translate these criteria into a Prisma query on the `shopping_mall_carts` table, possibly joining subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_cart_items` only when necessary. The response returns a paginated list of summary projections (`IShoppingMallCart.ISummary`) rather than full detail records, in order to optimize bandwidth and latency for list screens. Each summary includes the minimal set of information required to identify and describe the cart at a glance, such as cart identifier, owner type, item count, and key timestamps.

From a security perspective, this operation is restricted to administrative actors and should not be exposed as a public endpoint. The `authorizationActors` is set to `["admin"]` to reflect that only admin-facing applications or services acting with admin privileges may perform arbitrary cart searches across all users. Any customer-facing cart lookup flows should be implemented via separate endpoints that filter by the authenticated customer or guest session context.

This operation complements the detail retrieval endpoint `GET /carts/{cartId}`, which is used to obtain full information about a specific cart. A typical workflow is that an admin UI first calls this PATCH `/carts` endpoint with search criteria to obtain a page of carts, then uses the returned cart identifiers to call the GET detail endpoint for deeper inspection of a particular cart.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping cart headers from the shopping_mall_carts table using complex filter criteria.

This operation accepts a JSON request body that conforms to `IShoppingMallCart.IRequest`, representing search filters, pagination controls, and sorting options. The implementation will map these filters to the actual fields defined in the `shopping_mall_carts` Prisma model, such as identifiers, ownership references, timestamps, and status fields, while ensuring that any optional filters are applied only when present. This design allows back-office tools to build rich search interfaces without being constrained by query string limitations.

The response payload is a paginated wrapper `IPageIShoppingMallCart.ISummary` which contains summary representations of matching carts. Each summary item is derived from `shopping_mall_carts` and includes only the key attributes necessary for list rendering—such as cart identifier, owner type (customer or guest), item count, and important timestamps—omitting heavy relationships to keep the response efficient. Additional pages can be fetched using the pagination metadata returned in this wrapper.

Security-wise, this endpoint is designed for administrative and operational use, not for direct customer or seller access. The `authorizationActors` is therefore set to `["admin"]`, and the implementation should enforce appropriate authentication and authorization checks so that only admin accounts or trusted internal services can perform cross-user cart searches. Any customer-facing cart search must instead be constrained by the authenticated account and handled by separate, user-scoped endpoints.

This operation is typically used together with the `GET /carts/{cartId}` endpoint. The PATCH `/carts` endpoint locates candidate carts via flexible search, and once a specific cart of interest is identified, the client can perform a follow-up GET call to retrieve its full details and associated line items for investigation or support workflows.
operations.summary: Search shopping_mall_carts with advanced filters and return a paginated list of cart summaries.

requestBody.description: Search filters, pagination, and sorting options for querying shopping cart headers.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shopping cart summary records that match the search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A customer must exist and typically have at least one shipping address captured via POST /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/addresses before meaningful carts tied to that customer can be created and later searched administratively.

Customer carts that will be discoverable via the admin cart search endpoint are created through POST /shoppingMall/customer/carts; at least one such cart must exist before it can appear in search results filtered by customerId.

Guest user carts that are targeted by filters using guestUserId are created via POST /shoppingMall/guestUser/carts, so this operation must have been executed to create guest carts that the admin search can later retrieve.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full detail of a single shopping cart from the `shopping_mall_carts` Prisma table identified by its unique cart identifier. It is a classic GET-by-id pattern that focuses on the cart header entity and, through its DTO, may expose related information such as cart items, ownership details, and monetary estimates, depending on how `IShoppingMallCart` is defined.

The primary data source is the `shopping_mall_carts` model, whose fields typically include a unique primary key, ownership linkage to a customer or guest user identity, timestamps, and state indicators that describe whether the cart is active, abandoned, or already converted into an order. In addition to header fields, the implementation may also join subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_cart_items` and related SKU or product tables so that the returned DTO gives a complete view of the cart’s current contents.

The business purpose of this endpoint is to support administrative and operational workflows in which an operator, support agent, or automated system needs to inspect the complete state of a specific cart—for example, when diagnosing checkout issues, verifying promotional behavior, or analyzing cart abandonment patterns. Clients obtain the `cartId` (which is represented as a UUID string in the path) from earlier search results or logging data and then call this endpoint to retrieve all relevant information about that precise cart.

Unlike the search endpoint, which returns only summary projections suitable for lists, this operation returns a detailed DTO `IShoppingMallCart` that can carry full structure suitable for rich detail views. The implementation must ensure that the data loaded and returned is consistent with the Prisma schema definitions for `shopping_mall_carts` and related entities and should avoid including excessively heavy relationships that are not useful for the immediate use case.

From a security standpoint, this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors. Because it allows direct inspection of any cart, including those belonging to arbitrary customers or guest users, it must only be callable by admin-facing systems with appropriate privileges. The `authorizationActors` value `["admin"]` communicates that only admin accounts (or services acting with admin authority) may invoke this operation. Any customer-facing cart detail retrieval should instead be implemented as a separate, user-scoped endpoint that enforces ownership constraints.

This GET `/carts/{cartId}` operation is typically invoked after the PATCH `/carts` search endpoint has been used to locate a specific cart of interest. The workflow is: search for carts with certain characteristics, select one from the paginated results, then call this detail endpoint to view all information associated with that cart.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single shopping cart detail record from the shopping_mall_carts table using its unique cart identifier.

The client supplies `cartId` as a path parameter, which is treated as the unique identifier of the cart in the underlying `shopping_mall_carts` Prisma model. If the cart exists, the service returns a detailed DTO typed as `IShoppingMallCart`, which may include header fields, ownership information, and optional nested structures such as cart items and derived monetary totals as defined in the DTO design.

If the specified cart cannot be found—for example, because the identifier is invalid or the cart has been removed—the endpoint should respond with an appropriate not-found error status. Error responses should avoid leaking sensitive information while still providing enough context for admin tools to understand that the cart does not exist. Additional validation errors may be returned if the `cartId` is malformed.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors, represented by `authorizationActors: ["admin"]`. Because it allows inspection of carts belonging to any user or guest, the controller and service layers must enforce strict authentication and authorization checks so that only admin accounts or trusted back-office systems can access this data. For customer-facing cart detail views, a separate endpoint with `authorizationActors: ["user"]` or guest context would be implemented and would additionally enforce ownership of the cart.

This endpoint is designed to be used in combination with the cart search operation PATCH `/carts`, where an admin first locates a cart based on filters and then retrieves complete information for that cart by using this GET-by-id operation.

This operation is responsible for creating the cart header entity, associating it with the correct actor identity (such as a customer or guest user reference), and setting initial state fields such as status, currency, and any configuration flags that are defined in the shopping_mall_carts schema. It does not add line items itself; those will be handled by subsequent cart item operations working against shopping_mall_cart_items.

The request body will use the IShoppingMallCart.ICreate DTO, which encapsulates all client-supplied data necessary for cart creation, excluding any server-managed fields like primary keys, timestamps, or derived status fields. The response will return the fully populated IShoppingMallCart representation so that clients can immediately use the new cart identifier in follow-up requests to manage items, merge carts, or proceed to checkout.

This operation should enforce any business rules defined around cart ownership, such as limiting the number of active carts per customer or properly linking an anonymous cart to a guest identity. It may also trigger creation of related subsidiary records (such as initial cart validation snapshots) according to the schema, but those details are encapsulated in service logic and not exposed at the API contract level.
operations.description:

Server-managed fields like cart identifiers, creation timestamps, and default statuses are populated by the backend according to the schema definitions and business defaults.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is accessible to front-end clients acting on behalf of either authenticated customers or guest users, so it should be guarded by generic user-facing protections such as rate limiting and abuse detection, but does not require an admin role. This operation is closely related to subsequent cart item and merge operations that operate on the shopping_mall_cart_items and shopping_mall_cart_merge_events tables. Clients typically call this endpoint before adding items, viewing cart summaries, or converting the cart into an order. This operation is used to modify high-level cart attributes such as ownership links, locale, currency, status flags, or other non-item properties defined on the cart header, without directly manipulating the individual cart items that reside in the shopping_mall_cart_items table.

The cartId parameter represents the unique identifier of the cart record in shopping_mall_carts; its exact format (UUID string or other) is dictated by the Prisma schema. The request body uses the IShoppingMallCart.IUpdate DTO, which includes only those fields that clients are permitted to change. System-managed fields like primary keys, audit timestamps, and derived totals remain read-only and must not be exposed for modification in the DTO. The response returns the updated IShoppingMallCart representation so that clients can confirm the current state after the update.

Business logic associated with this operation may include enforcing ownership checks (ensuring that only the customer or guest user who owns the cart can update it), validating allowed status transitions, and rejecting updates when the cart has already been converted into an order or otherwise closed according to the schema and higher-level policies. Any such rules should be implemented in the service layer while the API contract remains stable and type-safe.
operations.description:

Fields that are immutable or system-managed, such as the primary key, creation timestamp, or finalization markers, are excluded from the update DTO to preserve data integrity.

Authorization is scoped so that only the owner of the cart or the associated session can perform updates, represented here by customer or guest user actors. Implementation should additionally verify that the cart is in an updatable state—for example, not already converted into an order or locked for legal or risk reasons. If the shopping_mall_carts schema references related snapshot or audit tables, such as shopping_mall_cart_merge_events, the update operation may also append new records there to reflect significant state changes.

This endpoint is typically used in conjunction with cart item operations that manage line items in the shopping_mall_cart_items table. Clients often call it to adjust cart-level options prior to checkout, such as changing currency where allowed, toggling configuration flags, or updating metadata tied to the current shopping session. Errors should clearly indicate invalid cart identifiers, failed ownership checks, or violations of update constraints defined by the data model and business policies.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a shopping cart header record from the `shopping_mall_carts` table based on its primary key `id`. It is intended for administrative or system-level cleanup of carts that are no longer needed, such as abandoned carts that have exceeded retention policies or carts that were created in error.

The operation targets the `shopping_mall_carts` model, which stores cart-level metadata including `actor_type`, `status`, `currency_code`, timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`, `last_validated_at`), and foreign keys to either `shopping_mall_customers` or `shopping_mall_guestusers`. When this endpoint is invoked, the implementation must ensure that the specified cart exists and is eligible for deletion according to business rules (for example, ensuring it has not already been converted into an order).

Although the Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_carts` includes a `deleted_at` column used for logical removal, this API operation is documented and implemented as a hard delete of the cart row. The provider is expected to remove the corresponding record and rely on cascading or explicit deletion for related subsidiary records such as `shopping_mall_cart_items`, `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations`, and `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events`, according to configured referential actions.
operations.description:
Delete a specific shopping cart header from the `shopping_mall_carts` table identified by its primary key `id`.

This operation is designed for privileged actors such as administrators or internal maintenance services that need to remove carts that are no longer required. The targeted cart represents a collection of potential purchase items associated with either a guest user or an authenticated customer, as indicated by the `actor_type`, `shopping_mall_guestuser_id`, and `shopping_mall_customer_id` fields. Before performing the deletion, the implementation should verify that the cart is in a business-appropriate `status` (for example, `active`, `abandoned`, or `merged`) and that it has not already been converted into an order. If the cart cannot be found or is not eligible for deletion, an appropriate error response should be returned.

From a security perspective, this endpoint must be protected so that only actors with elevated privileges can invoke it. Typical authorization would require an administrative role, and additional policy checks may ensure that only certain environments or automation jobs are allowed to perform bulk cleanup. The `authorizationActors` field therefore reflects an administrative actor, and the controller layer should enforce authentication and role validation accordingly.

On the data layer, this operation interacts directly with the `shopping_mall_carts` table. Any related `shopping_mall_cart_items` and downstream subsidiary entities (such as validations and merge events) should be handled according to the database's foreign key constraints or explicit application logic to prevent orphaned data. If the Prisma schema is configured with cascading deletes, removal of the cart header will automatically propagate. Error handling should cover cases where the cart `id` does not exist and where database constraints prevent deletion, returning clear messages so that operational users understand why the deletion failed.

This endpoint is typically used in conjunction with analytical or maintenance operations that identify carts suitable for removal (for example, a separate statistics or search API that lists long-abandoned carts).

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated collection of cart line items from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table for a specific cart identified by its `shopping_mall_cart_id` foreign key. It supports advanced search, filtering, and sorting over cart items while always scoping the query to a single cart, whose identifier is provided as a path parameter.

The underlying `shopping_mall_cart_items` model represents individual SKUs and quantities that a user has added to a cart, including fields such as `quantity`, `unit_price`, `currency_code`, lightweight validation state (`last_validation_status`, `last_validation_at`), and timestamps (`added_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`). This endpoint is expected to leverage those fields in a request body DTO to provide query capabilities such as filtering by validation status, date ranges, or SKU identifiers, as well as controlling pagination and sort order.

The request body follows the `IShoppingMallCartItem.IRequest` schema, which encapsulates search criteria and pagination parameters without duplicating the cart identifier (since that is provided by the path parameter). The response body uses a paginated summary representation `IPageIShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary`, returning only the fields necessary for list views while hiding internal or heavyweight details. This pattern allows clients such as web or mobile frontends to efficiently render cart contents, showing each line item with relevant SKU, pricing, and validation status information.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of cart line items from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table for a specific cart.

This operation is used to obtain the contents of a shopping cart at the line-item level, scoped by the cart identifier supplied as the `cartId` path parameter. The underlying `shopping_mall_cart_items` table links each item to its owning cart via the `shopping_mall_cart_id` foreign key and to a specific SKU via `shopping_mall_sku_id`. Each record includes the `quantity` the customer wishes to purchase, a snapshot `unit_price` in the `currency_code` of the cart, and lightweight validation metadata such as `last_validation_status` and `last_validation_at`. The endpoint allows clients to specify search and pagination criteria through the `IShoppingMallCartItem.IRequest` payload, while ensuring that all results belong to the specified cart.

From a security standpoint, this endpoint is intended for use by actors who are allowed to view the contents of a cart. In a typical implementation, the controller and provider would enforce that the `cartId` belongs to the authenticated customer or guest session, or that the actor has administrative permissions to inspect other users' carts. For documentation purposes, the `authorizationActors` array is set to `customer`, with the understanding that fine-grained ownership checks will take place in business logic rather than at the routing level.

The response structure follows the `IPageIShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary` format, which includes pagination metadata and an array of summary representations of cart items. Each summary entry is expected to expose key readable fields that correspond to the Prisma schema, such as `quantity`, `unit_price`, currency, timestamps like `added_at`, and the latest `last_validation_status` value. The operation should handle soft-deleted items using the `deleted_at` column: by default, items with a non-null `deleted_at` should be excluded from active cart views, unless the request explicitly asks for historical data. This endpoint is commonly used alongside operations that update quantities, revalidate items, or transform the cart into an order.

This operation retrieves a single cart item from the shopping cart system based on the cart and cart item identifiers. It is associated conceptually with the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model, which represents individual line items within a shopping cart, each tied to a specific cart, product/SKU, quantity, and pricing snapshot information.

The endpoint `GET /carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}` returns the detailed representation of a specific cart item instance for scenarios such as client-side cart review, server-side validation flows, or admin/debug tooling. The implementation will query the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table filtered by the given cart identifier and cart item identifier, ensuring that the item belongs to the specified cart and that it is still active/valid according to the underlying schema rules (for example, not logically removed or invalidated by other processes, if such flags exist in the schema).

The response body is modeled as `IShoppingMallCartItem`, which is the primary DTO mapped from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model and may include related information such as SKU references, product references, and any calculated or denormalized display fields defined by the interface layer. This operation is read-only and does not modify any database state.
operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed information of a specific cart item belonging to a particular cart.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model, which stores individual line items of a shopping cart, and is logically linked to the `shopping_mall_carts` model through a foreign key relationship. Each cart item typically references a SKU record (from `shopping_mall_skus`) and may also reference product-level metadata (from `shopping_mall_products`) via relationships defined in the Prisma schema. The cart item row usually contains fields for quantity, unit price, subtotal amounts, and any additional flags or attributes relevant to pricing and availability.

Security-wise, this endpoint is designed to be used by authenticated customers or guest sessions whose identity and associated cart context are enforced by higher-level middleware or business logic, not by the operation contract itself. The implementation must verify that the caller is authorized to view the specified cart and its items, for example by checking ownership of the cart or binding to a guest session token. Because the endpoint is read-only and limited to cart contents, it can be exposed to the "customer" actor role, with further fine-grained checks happening inside the service layer.

From a functional perspective, this operation is used whenever a client needs the full representation of a specific cart line—for example, when rendering a cart detail page, confirming item details prior to checkout, or recalculating totals after promotional logic. The operation should return appropriate error responses (such as 404) when either the cart or the cart item does not exist, or when the item does not belong to the given cart context. Related operations include listing all items in a cart, adding items to a cart, and updating or removing existing cart items.

This operation creates a new cart item within an existing shopping cart and is conceptually backed by the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model. The cart itself is represented by the `shopping_mall_carts` model, and each item row corresponds to a specific SKU or product configured in the catalog (e.g., `shopping_mall_skus` and `shopping_mall_products`).

The endpoint `POST /carts/{cartId}/items` accepts a request body described by `IShoppingMallCartItem.ICreate`, which includes all required information to add an item to the specified cart, such as the SKU identifier, quantity, and any option or attribute selections required by the business rules. The service layer will validate the request against the current catalog and inventory state, potentially referencing models like `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states` and catalog visibility rules, to ensure that the item can be added (for example, that it is in stock and visible to the current actor).

On success, the operation inserts a new record into `shopping_mall_cart_items` associated with the `cartId`, performs any necessary recalculation of derived fields (such as line subtotal, tax breakdown, or applied discounts, if represented in the schema), and returns the resulting `IShoppingMallCartItem` DTO. This operation represents a core part of the cart workflow and is subject to business validations around maximum quantities, SKU availability, and policy constraints defined elsewhere in the platform.

Add a new item to the specified shopping cart and return the created cart item.

This operation writes to the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model, which stores individual cart line items linked to a parent cart row in `shopping_mall_carts`. The new cart item typically includes references to a SKU (and implicitly to a product), quantity, unit price, and any additional pricing or attribute-related metadata defined by the schema. During creation, the service must validate that the referenced cart exists and is in a state that allows modification, and that the requested SKU is orderable based on catalog visibility and inventory conditions.

From a security standpoint, the endpoint is intended for authenticated customers or guest sessions that are allowed to modify a specific cart. Higher-level middleware or business logic must ensure that the caller is indeed the owner of the given cart or is otherwise authorized to mutate its contents. Implementations should also enforce server-side checks to prevent abuse, such as verifying maximum allowable quantities, respecting purchase limits, and validating against any risk or policy rules enforced by components tied to models like `shopping_mall_business_policies` or risk-related tables.

Functionally, this operation is used when users add products to their cart from product detail pages, listings, or quick-add controls. On successful creation, the endpoint returns the fully populated `IShoppingMallCartItem` DTO so that clients can immediately update the UI with accurate pricing and availability information. In error scenarios—such as invalid cart identifiers, missing or disabled SKUs, or quantity constraint violations—the service should respond with appropriate error codes and messages, while never partially creating or leaving inconsistent cart state. Related endpoints include retrieving a single cart item, listing all items for a cart, updating an existing cart item, and removing a cart item from the cart.

operations.specification:
Update an existing shopping cart line item within a customer's active cart. This operation targets the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model, which stores individual cart line items associated with a parent `shopping_mall_carts` record representing the cart header. The endpoint allows modification of mutable fields on a cart item, typically including the quantity of a SKU and possibly optional per-line notes or client metadata, while preserving immutable identity fields such as the owning cart, SKU reference, and creation timestamps.

The operation is invoked with a PUT request to `/carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}`, where `cartId` identifies the cart header and `cartItemId` identifies the specific line item belonging to that cart. The path parameters are used to scope the update so that only the item within the specified cart is affected, and they are not repeated inside the request DTO. The request body references `IShoppingMallCartItem.IUpdate`, which is defined according to the `shopping_mall_cart_items` schema fields that are allowed to change, such as `quantity`, gift wrapping choices, or any other business-level editable properties.

From a business perspective, the update logic must validate that the cart is still in a modifiable state (for example, not already converted into an order or expired), that the SKU referenced by the cart item is still available for sale, and that the requested quantity does not exceed the allowed maximum based on inventory and policy constraints. It should also enforce ownership rules, ensuring that only the customer or guest who owns the cart can modify its items, using authentication and session context outside the operation contract itself.

Related APIs include the PATCH `/carts` or GET `/carts/{cartId}` operations that retrieve cart overviews, and POST `/carts/{cartId}/items` that adds new cart items. This update operation is typically used by the cart page or mini-cart UI whenever a user changes quantities or line-level options, and is an essential part of the shopping flow before order creation from the cart.
operations.description:
Update a specific shopping cart item within a given cart based on the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model.

This operation updates a single record in the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table that belongs to a parent cart represented by the `shopping_mall_carts` table. The `cartId` path parameter identifies the cart header that groups items for a particular customer or guest user, while the `cartItemId` path parameter identifies the exact line item within that cart. The underlying schema for `shopping_mall_cart_items` includes foreign keys to the cart, a reference to the SKU being purchased, and various quantity and pricing-related fields. Only the fields that are explicitly allowed to change by business rules are exposed through the `IShoppingMallCartItem.IUpdate` DTO.

The update behavior must respect several business constraints derived from the shopping cart requirements. First, the owning cart in `shopping_mall_carts` must be in an editable state: carts that have already been converted into orders or that are invalidated by session expiration or policy changes must reject modifications. Second, the requested quantity and any related options must be validated against current SKU availability, inventory state semantics, and catalog visibility rules, ensuring that a user cannot increase the quantity beyond what can be fulfilled or continue to hold items that have become unavailable. If the update violates inventory or policy constraints, the implementation should reject the request with a clear error that the client can surface.

Security-wise, even though this specification leaves authentication details to the surrounding infrastructure, the actual implementation must ensure that the caller is the rightful owner of the cart. For authenticated customers, this means matching `shopping_mall_carts` to the customer account derived from the session; for guest users, this means validating the guest session key. The operation does not change cart ownership or SKU identity, and does not accept any identifiers in the body to avoid conflicts with the path parameters.

This endpoint is intended to be used alongside other cart operations such as adding items, removing items, and viewing the cart, enabling a complete cart management workflow. When updates succeed, the response returns the latest representation of the updated cart item using `IShoppingMallCartItem`, allowing the client to update UI totals, taxes, and other derived amounts based on the refreshed line state.
operations.summary: Update a cart item record in the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table for a specific cart.

operations.specification:
Remove an existing shopping cart line item from a customer's active cart. This operation acts on the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model and is invoked with a DELETE request to `/carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}`. The `cartId` path parameter identifies the `shopping_mall_carts` record representing the cart header, and `cartItemId` identifies the specific `shopping_mall_cart_items` record to be removed.

The primary purpose is to allow customers or guest users to remove unwanted SKUs from their cart before completing checkout. The implementation will typically delete the cart item row or mark it as removed according to the schema design, but from an API contract perspective this operation represents a permanent removal of the line item from the active cart state. No request body is required; all identity and scoping information is carried by the path parameters.

Business rules must ensure that only cart items in an editable cart can be removed. If the cart has already been converted into an order or is otherwise locked by policy, attempts to remove items should be rejected. Additionally, the implementation must validate ownership so that only the customer or guest who owns the cart can remove its items. Removing a cart item may affect derived values such as cart totals, discounts, and eligibility checks, which will be recalculated by other parts of the system after the deletion.

This delete operation complements other cart endpoints, such as those that add items, update quantities, or return full cart contents, and is typically triggered by "remove" buttons in cart UI components. The response does not include a body, signaling success solely through HTTP status codes, which keeps the contract simple and allows clients to re-fetch the full cart state if needed.
operations.description:
Delete a specific shopping cart item from a given cart, based on the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model.

This operation removes a single row from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table that belongs to a parent `shopping_mall_carts` record. The `cartId` path parameter scopes the operation to the target cart header, while the `cartItemId` identifies the exact cart item to remove. Since the underlying Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_cart_items` ties each item to a cart and a SKU, deleting the record effectively detaches the selected SKU from the cart, ensuring it is no longer considered when computing totals or availability.

From a business and validation perspective, the cart must be in a state where edits are allowed. Carts that have already transitioned to an immutable state due to checkout completion, session expiration, risk policies, or legal holds should not accept item removals. The implementation is expected to perform these checks using the `shopping_mall_carts` model and associated policy configurations, returning appropriate error responses when deletion is not permitted.

Security considerations require that the caller be authorized to modify the cart. For authenticated customers, this implies matching the cart's customer reference to the authenticated principal; for guest users, the system must validate session keys associated with the cart. This endpoint does not require a request body and does not expose internal identifiers beyond the path parameters, simplifying client integration.

This operation works in concert with cart item creation and update endpoints to provide a complete cart management API surface. Clients commonly follow up a successful deletion with a call to a cart retrieval endpoint to refresh totals, promotions, and other computed values after the item has been removed.
operations.summary: Delete a cart item record from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table for a specific cart.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of validation records associated with all items in a specific shopping cart. It is logically based on the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations` Prisma table, which stores validation attempts or results for each cart item, and is scoped by the parent cart represented by `shopping_mall_carts`. The endpoint is intended primarily for internal or support tooling to inspect how cart items were validated, including whether inventory, pricing, or eligibility checks passed or failed.

The operation accepts a complex search request body to support filtering by validation status, type, timestamp ranges, or specific cart item identifiers when needed. It returns a paginated collection of summary DTOs representing individual cart item validation records. The path parameter `cartId` identifies the cart whose validations are being queried, while the request body carries the query criteria. This design keeps the URL focused on the cart context and uses the body for rich search semantics.

The API is read-only and does not modify any data in `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations`. It is designed to help diagnose checkout issues, debug cart behavior, or power admin-facing UIs that need to show validation histories around a given cart. Related operations include the more granular validation history retrieval for a single cart item (`PATCH /carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}/validations`), which focuses on one item rather than the complete cart.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of validation records for all items within a specific shopping cart.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations` Prisma table, which records validation events or results linked to individual cart items in `shopping_mall_cart_items`. Typical columns in this table include references to the cart item, validation type (for example inventory, price, or eligibility checks), status (such as success or failure), error codes, and timestamps. By scoping the query via the `cartId` path parameter, the API ensures that only validation records belonging to a single cart context are returned, which simplifies both querying and reasoning about the results.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is expected to be used by authenticated support staff, internal tools, or privileged actors who need to investigate cart issues. The `authorizationActors` can therefore be configured to represent such privileged roles, and additional authorization logic should confirm that the caller is allowed to see the cart referenced by `cartId`. The API itself is strictly read-only and performs no updates to `shopping_mall_carts`, `shopping_mall_cart_items`, or `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations`.

The request body uses a DTO such as `IShoppingMallCartItemValidation.IRequest` to express filtering and pagination criteria. Typical fields may include validation status filters, validation type filters, date-time ranges, and standard page/size parameters. The response returns a paginated collection like `IPageIShoppingMallCartItemValidation.ISummary`, where each summary item includes the key fields necessary to display validation results in list form. Any more detailed inspection of a single validation event could be supported by additional detail endpoints if required by the broader specification.

This operation is typically used together with `PATCH /carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}/validations`, which narrows the focus down to validations for a single item. Clients may first query all item validations for a cart to see overall patterns, then drill into a specific cart item by calling the item-scoped endpoint with the corresponding `cartItemId`.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated validation records for all items in a specific cart from shopping_mall_cart_item_validations.

Guest user carts are also recorded in shopping_mall_carts. If the validation history to be inspected belongs to a guest flow, POST /shoppingMall/guestUser/carts must be used to create the cart and its cartId before admin tooling can query cart item validations for that cart.

Cart item validations are tied to specific cart items. POST /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items creates entries in shopping_mall_cart_items that can then be validated and produce records in shopping_mall_cart_item_validations, which this endpoint reads.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of validation records associated with a single cart item within a specific cart. It is based on the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations` Prisma table and uses the combination of `cartId` and `cartItemId` path parameters to scope the query to one cart item in one cart. This finer-grained endpoint is useful when investigating validation behavior or errors tied to a particular item in the cart.

The endpoint accepts a request body containing search and pagination criteria so callers can filter by validation status, type, time ranges, or other attributes defined in the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations` schema. The response consists of a paginated collection of summary DTOs representing each validation record for the designated cart item, ordered and filtered per the request.

This API is read-only and intended for diagnostic, audit, or support tooling around the checkout and cart validation flow. It complements the cart-level validations endpoint (`PATCH /carts/{cartId}/items/validations`) by focusing on a single line item, which allows callers to drill down into item-specific validation history after identifying a problematic item from the broader cart context.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of validation records for a specific cart item within a given shopping cart.

Internally, this operation reads from the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations` Prisma model, which stores validation outcomes and metadata per cart item, and relates to `shopping_mall_cart_items` and `shopping_mall_carts`. The `cartId` path parameter identifies the owning cart, while `cartItemId` identifies the specific line item whose validations are of interest. Typical fields on the validation table include foreign keys to the cart item, validation type, status, error codes, human-readable messages, and timestamps. Implementation must ensure that both identifiers are validated and that the cart item truly belongs to the specified cart to prevent cross-cart data leakage.

From a security and authorization standpoint, the endpoint should be available only to privileged actors such as administrators, support operators, or internal services responsible for monitoring and debugging cart behavior. The `authorizationActors` reflect these actors and additional authorization checks can be implemented depending on the platform’s role model. The endpoint itself performs no modifications to any of the underlying tables and serves purely as a read model for validation history.

The request body uses a DTO such as `IShoppingMallCartItemValidation.IRequest` to specify filtering parameters (for example, retrieving only failed validations or those within a certain time window) and pagination options. The response uses `IPageIShoppingMallCartItemValidation.ISummary` to return a paginated list of summary records appropriate for list views in admin consoles or diagnostic tools. Clients often use this operation after calling the cart-scoped validations endpoint to investigate a specific problematic cart item in greater depth.
