operations.specification:
This operation creates a new shipment record for an existing customer order within the shopping mall platform. It is associated primarily with the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma table, and also relies on related subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_shipment_items`, `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`, and `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` to represent the complete fulfillment unit derived from a given order.

The endpoint accepts a path parameter `orderCode`, which is a human-readable, unique business identifier for the order at the customer-facing level. The request body is modeled by `IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate`, which encapsulates all input data needed to define a shipment derived from that order, such as which order items are included, the chosen shipping method, shipping address snapshot selection or override, and any shipment-level notes. The implementation will validate that the referenced order exists, is in a state that allows shipment creation, and that the included order items and quantities are consistent with the order and inventory rules.

On success, the operation persists a new row into `shopping_mall_shipments` and its related subsidiary tables, establishes linkage back to the corresponding `shopping_mall_orders` record, and returns the fully populated shipment representation as `IShoppingMallShipment`. This response includes shipment status, tracking information (if available at creation time), and a view of the shipment items so that clients can immediately reflect the new fulfillment unit in their UI or internal workflows.
operations.description:
Create a new shipment entity associated with an existing order identified by its business `orderCode`.

This operation is responsible for creating a shipment header record in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table together with its associated shipment items and metadata in related subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_shipment_items`, `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses`, and `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`. The caller supplies a path parameter `orderCode` to indicate which logical order in `shopping_mall_orders` is being fulfilled, and a request body `IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate` that provides shipment-specific details like which order items and quantities are being included, the shipping method to use, and any shipment-level remarks or requested handling instructions.

From a business perspective, this operation enforces that only orders in an appropriate state (for example, paid or ready-to-ship according to business rules encoded in order and payment status fields) can have shipments created. The implementation will verify that the `orderCode` maps to an existing order, that each requested shipment item refers to a valid order item from `shopping_mall_order_items`, and that the requested shipment quantities do not exceed the remaining shippable quantities taking into account prior shipments. It also validates that the indicated shipping method is allowed for the order’s region and that any address information either references a valid snapshot from `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` or provides all mandatory address fields.

Security-wise, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated actors that are allowed to create shipments. Typically this will include seller-side fulfillment systems or internal operations staff rather than customers themselves, and the concrete authorization policies will be implemented using the `authorizationActors` configuration and deeper business logic. The operation should also ensure idempotency where appropriate, for example by rejecting duplicate shipment creation for the same combination of order and items if that would violate fulfillment rules.

On successful creation, the operation returns a complete `IShoppingMallShipment` representation that includes the new shipment’s identifier or code, current status, associated order reference, shipping method, address snapshot, and shipment items. Clients commonly call this API as part of warehouse or seller fulfillment workflows, and may follow it with status-update operations or use the returned shipment information to trigger downstream events such as notifications or label printing.
operations.summary: Create a new `shopping_mall_shipments` record for an order identified by `orderCode`.

parameters.name: orderCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target order (global scope) for which a new shipment should be created.

requestBody.description: Shipment creation payload specifying shipment-level details and the order items to be included for the given order code.

responseBody.description: Newly created shipment entity associated with the specified order, including shipment items, shipping method, and address information.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: The customer order must exist before an admin can create a shipment for it, because shipments are fulfillment units derived from confirmed orders in shopping_mall_orders.
A shipping method configuration must exist in shopping_mall_shipping_methods so that the shipment’s shippingMethodId can reference a valid shipping method snapshot.
A shipping address snapshot for the order must exist in shopping_mall_shipping_addresses so that the shipment can be associated with a concrete destination address via shippingAddressId.

Order items originate from cart items; creating a cart header and items allows the checkout flow to populate shopping_mall_order_items that shipmentItems will ultimately reference via shopping_mall_order_item_id.
SKUs must exist in shopping_mall_skus so that shipment items can reference concrete variants via shopping_mall_sku_id aligned with the ordered items.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information for a specific shipment associated with a particular customer order. It is associated primarily with the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma model and leverages its relations to subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_shipment_items`, `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`, `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses`, and `shopping_mall_shipments`–to–`shopping_mall_orders` linkage.

The endpoint is addressed using two path parameters: `orderCode`, which is the human-readable business identifier of the parent order from `shopping_mall_orders`, and `shipmentCode`, which uniquely identifies a shipment within the context of that order (or globally, depending on schema-level uniqueness). Together these parameters ensure that the correct shipment is resolved unambiguously, especially in systems where shipment codes may be scoped by order or seller.

The response is modeled by `IShoppingMallShipment` and returns a complete snapshot of the shipment’s current state, including its status, associated order reference, shipping method, shipment address snapshot, and the full list of shipment items. This operation is read-only and can be used by administrative tools, seller portals, or internal fulfillment systems to inspect shipment details, debug issues, and provide accurate tracking information to end users.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a single shipment associated with a specific order, identified by the combination of `orderCode` and `shipmentCode`.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and its related subsidiary tables, such as `shopping_mall_shipment_items`, `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`, and `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses`, to construct a rich `IShoppingMallShipment` representation. The `orderCode` path parameter is used to resolve the parent order in `shopping_mall_orders`, while the `shipmentCode` parameter is used to identify the specific shipment belonging to that order. This composite identification pattern aligns with typical business requirements where shipments are created per order and represented by codes visible to sellers, internal staff, and sometimes customers.

From a business and security standpoint, this endpoint is typically restricted to administrative and operational actors such as internal admins or seller fulfillment systems. Authorization logic will ensure that only actors with rights over the given order and its shipments can access the shipment details. The implementation will validate that the order specified by `orderCode` exists and that the shipment identified by `shipmentCode` is indeed linked to that order; if not, it should return a not-found error to avoid leaking information about unrelated shipments.

The response `IShoppingMallShipment` includes the shipment’s current status in its lifecycle (for example, pending pickup, in transit, delivered, or failed), together with shipping method details, address snapshot, and all shipment items. Clients use this operation to render shipment detail screens, to support customer service workflows when investigating delivery issues, and to provide consolidated tracking information. It is often used in conjunction with list endpoints for orders or shipments to drill down into a single shipment’s full context.
operations.summary: Get a single `shopping_mall_shipments` record for an order by `orderCode` and `shipmentCode`.

parameters.name: orderCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the parent order (global scope) whose shipment is being retrieved.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the shipment within the specified order (scoped to order).

responseBody.description: Detailed shipment information for the specified order and shipment code, including items, status, and shipping metadata.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: An order must be created in shopping_mall_orders so that a shipment associated with its orderCode can exist and later be retrieved by orderCode and shipmentCode.
The specific shipment must be created in shopping_mall_shipments before it can be fetched by the detail endpoint using orderCode and shipmentCode.

operations.specification:
Update an existing shipment header associated with a specific customer order in the shopping_mall_shipments table.

This operation targets a single shipment identified by a combination of the parent order's business-facing order_code (from shopping_mall_orders) and the shipment's own shipment_code (from shopping_mall_shipments). It allows authorized actors to modify mutable shipment header properties such as shipping_status, carrier_name, tracking_number, expected_ship_date, and other timeline fields, while preserving the relational integrity to the underlying order and seller.

The implementation must resolve the shipment row by joining shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_shipments on shopping_mall_orders.id = shopping_mall_shipments.shopping_mall_order_id and then filtering by shopping_mall_orders.order_code = {orderCode} and shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code = {shipmentCode}. Once located, the shipment row is updated with the fields provided in the IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate DTO, respecting business rules around allowed status transitions and field mutability.

This endpoint should be used for primary shipment management scenarios, including marking shipments as shipped or delivered, updating carrier or tracking information, and correcting expected ship dates. It must not be used to modify order-level monetary amounts or order item allocations, which are handled via other entities such as shopping_mall_order_items or shopping_mall_shipment_items.
operations.description:
Update shipment header information for a specific shipment belonging to an order, using order_code and shipment_code as business identifiers.

This operation acts on the shopping_mall_shipments primary table, which represents shipment headers and fulfillment units derived from customer orders. Each shipment record includes core fields such as shipment_code, shipping_status, carrier_name, tracking_number, expected_ship_date, shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at, updated_at, and any deletion-related fields defined in the schema, along with foreign keys to shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_sellers, shopping_mall_shipping_addresses, and shopping_mall_shipping_methods.

The client identifies the target shipment using two path parameters: orderCode, which corresponds to shopping_mall_orders.order_code and is a business-facing order code, and shipmentCode, which corresponds to shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code and is a business-facing shipment code. This avoids exposing internal UUID identifiers (id fields) in the external API while still allowing a precise, unique lookup when combined.

The request body uses the IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate structure, which carries only shipment-level properties that are allowed to be updated after creation, such as shipping_status, carrier_name, tracking_number, expected_ship_date, and timeline fields like shipped_at and delivered_at. Implementation must enforce that immutable fields such as the shipment's association to its order (shopping_mall_order_id), seller (shopping_mall_seller_id), shipping address, and shipping method are not altered by this endpoint.

From a security perspective, this endpoint should typically be restricted to authenticated actors that have permission to manage shipments, such as sellers responsible for the shipment or administrators. The authorizationActor field is set to "seller" to model a seller actor, while fine-grained permission checks (for example, verifying that the authenticated seller matches shopping_mall_shipments.shopping_mall_seller_id) must be implemented inside the service layer.

The operation returns the updated shipment representation as IShoppingMallShipment so that clients can immediately reflect changes in their UI, including the new shipping_status, tracking information, and any updated timestamps.

Typical errors include not found (when either the orderCode does not correspond to an existing shopping_mall_orders row or the shipmentCode does not match a shipment for that order), validation errors when attempting illegal status transitions (for example, moving from delivered back to pending), and conflicts when trying to update shipments that are not allowed to be modified in their current state. Implementations may also restrict certain fields from being modified once a shipment reaches terminal states such as delivered or cancelled.
operations.summary: Update a shipment header in shopping_mall_shipments identified by order_code and shipment_code.

parameters.name: orderCode
parameters.description: Business-facing order code corresponding to shopping_mall_orders.order_code (global scope) that identifies the parent order owning the shipment.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Business-facing shipment code corresponding to shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code (scoped to the parent order) that identifies the specific shipment to update.

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the shipment header, including shipping_status, carrier and tracking information, and expected or actual shipping dates.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment header after applying the requested changes, reflecting the latest shipping_status, carrier, tracking, and timeline fields.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: The parent order must exist before its shipments can be updated, because the shipment is resolved by joining shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_shipments using the provided orderCode.
The specific shipment header must be created for the given order before its header fields (shipping_status, carrier, tracking, dates) can be updated via this seller-facing endpoint.

operations.specification:
Permanently delete an existing shipment header associated with a specific customer order from the shopping_mall_shipments table.

This operation targets a single shipment identified by the combination of the parent order's business-facing order_code (shopping_mall_orders.order_code) and the shipment's own shipment_code (shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code). Instead of marking the row for logical removal, it performs a hard delete, physically removing the shopping_mall_shipments record from the database.

The implementation must first resolve the shipment by joining shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_shipments via shopping_mall_orders.id = shopping_mall_shipments.shopping_mall_order_id, then filtering using the provided orderCode and shipmentCode values. Once the target record is found and business validations pass (for example, ensuring there are no constraints blocking deletion based on shipment status or related financial operations), the shipment row is deleted.

This endpoint is intended for use cases where a shipment was created in error or is being removed as part of corrective operational flows. It must not be used as a substitute for proper shipment status progression (for example, cancelling or reverting a delivered shipment), which should be modeled through shipment events and order/refund logic instead.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a shipment header from the shopping_mall_shipments table so that it no longer appears in operational queries or detail views.

This operation manipulates the shopping_mall_shipments table, which stores shipment headers representing fulfillment units derived from orders. Each shipment includes business-facing identifiers (shipment_code), relational links to the parent order (shopping_mall_order_id referencing shopping_mall_orders.id), the responsible seller, shipping address and method references, current shipping_status, optional carrier_name and tracking_number, and timeline fields such as expected_ship_date, shipped_at, and delivered_at.

Clients identify the target shipment using the orderCode path parameter tied to shopping_mall_orders.order_code and the shipmentCode path parameter tied to shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code. This pairing provides a stable, human-readable way to reference a specific shipment without exposing its internal UUID id while still allowing a precise lookup.

Upon successful execution, the implementation deletes the corresponding shopping_mall_shipments row from the database. Downstream list and detail operations that represent shipments must treat the deleted shipment as non-existent and should return appropriate not-found responses if clients attempt to access it again using the same identifiers.

Security-wise, this operation should only be available to authenticated actors with permission to manage shipments, typically the seller associated with the shipment or administrative staff. The authorizationActor specification uses "seller" as the primary actor that manages shipments, while the concrete implementation must enforce business rules such as checking that the caller is the owning seller or an authorized admin.

Expected error scenarios include attempting to erase a shipment that does not exist for the given orderCode and shipmentCode combination, or violating business rules that forbid deletion when certain shipment events or financial operations are present. In such cases, the service should return appropriate error responses (for example, 404 Not Found or 409 Conflict) and leave the underlying database state unchanged.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a shipment header in shopping_mall_shipments identified by order_code and shipment_code.

parameters.name: orderCode
parameters.description: Business-facing order code corresponding to shopping_mall_orders.order_code (global scope) that identifies the parent order owning the shipment to be deleted.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Business-facing shipment code corresponding to shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code (scoped to the parent order) that identifies the specific shipment to delete.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: The parent order identified by orderCode must exist before attempting to delete one of its shipments, since shipments are resolved through shopping_mall_orders joined with shopping_mall_shipments.
A shipment header must first be created for the specified order before it can be hard-deleted via this seller-facing erase operation.

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a paginated list of shipment item records associated with a specific shipment, identified by its unique shipmentCode business key. It is conceptually based on the shopping_mall_shipment_items Prisma model, which represents the association between shipments and the specific order items and SKUs they contain, and on the shopping_mall_shipments model, which owns the shipmentCode path parameter as its business identifier.

The endpoint uses the HTTP PATCH method on the /shipments/{shipmentCode}/items path to support complex search, filtering, and pagination requirements for shipment items that cannot be conveniently expressed as simple query parameters. Clients submit an IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IRequest request body containing filters such as SKU identifiers, order item identifiers, fulfillment status, or date ranges. The the server responds with a paginated IPageIShoppingMallShipmentItem.ISummary structure providing a list view of shipment items for UI grids or operational consoles.

The shipmentCode path parameter is a human-readable, globally unique business identifier for the shipment, rather than an internal UUID. This aligns with the requirement to prefer code-based identifiers where the schema exposes such codes. The business logic will validate that the referenced shipment exists in the shopping_mall_shipments table and then constrain the shipment item search to that shipment’s scope, ensuring that only items belonging to the identified shipment are returned.

This operation is read-only and does not modify shipment or shipment item state. It is typically used by seller fulfillment tools, customer service agents, or internal operations dashboards to inspect the composition of a shipment, troubleshoot fulfillment issues, and track which items were grouped into a particular shipment. It should support standard pagination controls (page number, page size) and sorting options in the request DTO, while enforcing any authorization rules required by the platform (for example, only returning items for shipments owned by the requesting seller or visible to authorized admins).
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of shipment items for a specific shipment identified by shipmentCode.

This operation targets the shipment item layer of the fulfillment domain, corresponding to the shopping_mall_shipment_items Prisma model. That model is described as an association table binding shipments to the specific order items and SKUs they contain. By using the shipmentCode path parameter, the API constrains its scope to a single shipment record from the shopping_mall_shipments table, which is the shipment header entity representing a fulfillment unit derived from one or more customer orders.

From a security and authorization standpoint, this endpoint is designed primarily for internal or privileged actors such as admins and, depending on business policy, potentially seller-side tools. In this specification, authorizationActor is set to "admin", indicating that access is restricted to administrative users in API-level documentation. In an actual implementation, additional authorization checks would ensure that only appropriately scoped admins can view shipment contents, particularly because shipment item data exposes order, SKU, and fulfillment information that is operationally sensitive.

The request body uses the IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IRequest DTO, which encapsulates all search filters, pagination parameters, and sorting options applicable to shipment items. This typically includes filters such as SKU code, order item identifier, shipment item status, created/updated timestamps, and possibly flags related to packing or tracking. The design follows the platform-wide convention of using PATCH for complex search operations with structured JSON bodies instead of GET with query parameters when the query semantics exceed simple key-value pairs.

The response body returns an IPageIShoppingMallShipmentItem.ISummary structure. The summary variant of the shipment item DTO is optimized for list presentations, containing key identifiers, human-readable labels (such as product name and SKU code), and essential status fields, but not all deep relational data. Pagination metadata (current page, page size, total count) enables efficient UI implementations that can handle large shipments. When clients need full detail for a single shipment item, they are expected to call the complementary GET /shipments/{shipmentCode}/items/{shipmentItemId} endpoint.

Error handling for this operation includes validation of the shipmentCode path parameter, ensuring it corresponds to an existing shipment. If the shipment cannot be found, a 404-like error is appropriate. If the caller lacks permission to view this shipment’s items, an authorization error is returned. Validation errors within the IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IRequest payload, such as invalid filter combinations or out-of-range pagination values, should be surfaced with clear messages so that client applications can correct the request. Because this is a read-only search endpoint, it does not perform any modifications or trigger side effects on shipments or orders.
operations.summary: Search shopping_mall_shipment_items by shipmentCode and return a paginated list of shipment items.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target shipment (global scope). This code identifies a single shipment header record in the shopping_mall_shipments table, and the search will be constrained to shipment items belonging to this shipment.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination parameters, and sorting options for filtering shipment items belonging to the specified shipment.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment item summary records for the specified shipment, constrained by the provided search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A shipment must be created in shopping_mall_shipments before its shipmentCode can be used to search associated shipment items.
SKUs must exist in shopping_mall_skus so that shipment items can reference valid shopping_mall_sku_id values for the shipped variants.
Shipment item records in shopping_mall_shipment_items must exist before they can be searched and paginated for a given shipmentCode.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information for a single shipment item associated with a particular shipment. It is built on top of the shopping_mall_shipment_items Prisma model, with a foreign-key relationship to the shopping_mall_shipments model for the parent shipment and to order/SKU-related tables for the underlying commerce entities.

The endpoint uses the HTTP GET method on the /shipments/{shipmentCode}/items/{shipmentItemId} path. The shipmentCode path parameter specifies the parent shipment using its human-readable, globally unique business code, while shipmentItemId identifies the specific shipment item record within that shipment, typically via a UUID or similar unique identifier column in shopping_mall_shipment_items. This dual-parameter pattern ensures that callers always provide both the shipment context and the concrete item identity, which can be important for enforcing composite-uniqueness or scoping rules in the database.

The operation returns a full IShoppingMallShipmentItem DTO, representing the detailed state of the shipment item, including references to the associated order item, SKU, quantities, and fulfillment status fields. Implementation logic is expected to validate that the shipment indicated by shipmentCode exists and that the shipment item with shipmentItemId truly belongs to that shipment; mismatched combinations must be treated as not found. This protects against accidental cross-shipment lookups and supports secure, predictable resource addressing.

This is a read-only operation intended primarily for administrative tools and operational back-office systems, as reflected by authorizationActor set to "admin". It allows admins or operational staff to inspect the exact composition and status of a particular shipment line when handling customer inquiries, investigating discrepancies, or reconciling shipping events with underlying orders. Because it returns detailed data, the response DTO may include fields such as tracking-related attributes, packing metadata, and timestamps defined in the Prisma schema for shopping_mall_shipment_items and closely related tables.

Error handling includes the case where either the shipmentCode does not resolve to an existing shipment, or the shipmentItemId does not resolve to a shipment item under that shipment. In either scenario, the caller should receive a clear not-found response. Authorization failures for actors not allowed to access this shipment’s data must also be handled. Since this is a pure retrieval operation, it must not modify any shipment or shipment item records, and it should be safe to call repeatedly without side effects.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a single shipment item belonging to a specific shipment.

This operation provides a fine-grained view into the shipment items stored in the shopping_mall_shipment_items table, which is described as the association between shipments and the specific order items and SKUs they contain. The shipmentCode path parameter identifies the shipment header record from the shopping_mall_shipments model, while shipmentItemId points to the concrete shipment item row. The implementation must ensure that the shipment item belongs to the shipment referenced by shipmentCode to avoid leaking information across shipments.

From an authorization perspective, this endpoint is restricted to administrative users as indicated by authorizationActor: "admin". Admins and operational support agents use this endpoint to troubleshoot fulfillment-related issues, such as confirming which SKU and quantity were shipped, verifying that the correct order item was associated, and checking timestamps or status fields associated with the shipment item. Because shipment items reveal detailed operational and customer-related information, this endpoint should be protected with strong authentication and authorization checks, in addition to the actor-level control reflected in the documentation.

The response uses the IShoppingMallShipmentItem DTO, which is the full representation of a shipment item, potentially including nested or related objects depending on how the DTO is defined from the Prisma schema. This may encompass identifiers for the related order and order item, SKU information, quantities, fulfillment status, and any tracking-related data that is stored at the shipment item level. The endpoint does not accept a request body and is safe for clients to call whenever they need to refresh the detailed view of a shipment line in a UI.

If the provided shipmentCode does not correspond to any shipment in the system, the server should respond with a not-found style error. Similarly, if shipmentItemId does not match a shipment item that belongs to the identified shipment, the operation should also result in a not-found response, rather than returning a shipment item from a different shipment. Any permission violations—for example, if a non-admin or an admin outside the appropriate scope attempts access—should be surfaced as authorization errors. As a pure read operation, this endpoint does not change database state or trigger side effects beyond logging or analytics that the system may perform automatically.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single shopping_mall_shipment_items record by shipmentCode and shipmentItemId.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the parent shipment (global scope) from the shopping_mall_shipments table. Used to scope the lookup of the shipment item.

parameters.name: shipmentItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment item within the shopping_mall_shipment_items table. This identifier must reference an item that belongs to the shipment identified by shipmentCode.

responseBody.description: Detailed shipment item information for the specified shipment item belonging to the given shipment.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A shipment header record must be created in shopping_mall_shipments so that a valid shipmentCode exists to scope the shipment item lookup.
A shipment item row must be created in shopping_mall_shipment_items so that a shipmentItemId exists and can be retrieved by this endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new shipment item associated with an existing shipment in the shoppingMall logistics domain. It is conceptually based on the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` Prisma model, which represents the association between shipment headers in `shopping_mall_shipments` and the specific order items and SKUs they contain. The endpoint uses a shipment-level identifier (`shipmentCode`) in the path to scope creation to a specific shipment, and accepts a structured JSON body describing which order item/SKU combination, quantity, and related attributes should be added as a new row in `shopping_mall_shipment_items`.

The implementation should validate that the referenced shipment exists and is in a state that allows modification (for example, not already fully delivered or locked by downstream processes). It should also verify that the referenced order item and SKU are valid and belong logically to the same order that generated the shipment, following the foreign-key and relationship structure defined in the `shopping_mall_shipments`, `shopping_mall_order_items`, and `shopping_mall_skus` models. On successful validation, it will insert a new shipment item record, link it to the shipment header, and return the created shipment item representation.

The request body type MUST follow the DTO naming convention for this service prefix and table, using `IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ICreate` as the creation DTO that mirrors the writable fields of the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` model (excluding context that comes from the path). The response body MUST be the main entity DTO `IShoppingMallShipmentItem`, representing the full shipment item including identifiers and read-only fields. Authorization should typically be restricted to actors responsible for fulfillment operations, modeled here as `admin` to represent administrative/operations staff creating shipment items on behalf of the platform or sellers.
operations.description:
Create a new shipment item row under a specific shipment in the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table, using the shipment context identified by `shipmentCode` from the parent `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

This operation is designed to work with the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` Prisma schema, whose description indicates that it is an association table binding shipments to the specific order items and SKU variants they contain. Each record in this table typically references a shipment header (from `shopping_mall_shipments`), a particular order item (from `shopping_mall_order_items`), and the SKU being shipped (from `shopping_mall_skus`), along with quantities and any other shipment-line level metadata defined in the schema. When a new shipment item is created via this API, those foreign key relationships must be respected and validated according to the database constraints.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint should be accessible only to trusted operational actors such as admins or back-office systems, represented here by the `admin` authorization actor. Regular customers must never be able to manipulate shipment items directly, since doing so would compromise the integrity of fulfillment and tracking processes. Implementation should apply role-based access control at the controller or middleware layer to ensure only authenticated admins can call this endpoint.

The request body uses `IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ICreate`, a DTO that should contain only the fields clients are allowed to set when creating a shipment item. This generally includes references to the order item and SKU, and the quantity to ship in this shipment, while omitting the shipment identifier itself because that context is derived from the `shipmentCode` path parameter. The response uses `IShoppingMallShipmentItem`, which should include all persisted fields such as the generated primary key, foreign keys, quantities, and any computed or read-only columns that the underlying Prisma model exposes.

Related operations include listing or retrieving shipment headers and items, and updating existing shipment items. For example, `PUT /shipments/{shipmentCode}/items/{shipmentItemId}` (defined separately) would be used to adjust quantities or metadata for an existing shipment item. Error handling must clearly distinguish between cases where the shipment does not exist, where it exists but is not in a modifiable state, and where the payload references invalid or mismatched order items or SKUs. Validation errors should be reported with descriptive messages to facilitate operational debugging.
operations.summary: Create a new shipment item record in the shopping_mall_shipment_items table under a specific shipment.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target shipment (global scope) in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table, used to scope creation of the shipment item to a specific shipment header.

requestBody.description: Creation payload for a shipment item to be associated with the specified shipment, excluding the shipment identifier which is derived from the `shipmentCode` path parameter.

responseBody.description: Representation of the newly created shipment item record under the specified shipment, including generated identifiers and read-only fields.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: Create a shipment header in shopping_mall_shipments so that a valid shipmentCode exists to attach shipment items to.
Create a customer order so that order items exist in shopping_mall_order_items, allowing shopping_mall_order_item_id in the shipment item to reference a real order line.
Create SKU variants in shopping_mall_skus so that shopping_mall_sku_id in the shipment item can reference an existing SKU.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing shipment item belonging to a given shipment in the shoppingMall logistics domain. It is based on the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` Prisma model, which records the association between a shipment header in `shopping_mall_shipments` and its constituent order items/SKUs. The endpoint is identified by both the shipment context (`shipmentCode`) and the shipment item identifier (`shipmentItemId`), ensuring that updates are scoped to the correct shipment and item.

The implementation should first resolve `shipmentCode` to the corresponding shipment in `shopping_mall_shipments` and verify that this shipment exists and is in a state that allows modification (for example, not fully delivered or locked). It must then locate the specific shipment item row using `shipmentItemId`, verifying that it belongs to the resolved shipment. After these validations, it applies changes from the request body to the shipment item record, respecting which fields are updatable according to the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` schema and business rules.

The request body type MUST be `IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IUpdate`, representing the allowed update fields for a shipment item, such as quantity or certain metadata fields, but not immutable identifiers. The response body MUST return the updated shipment item using the main entity DTO `IShoppingMallShipmentItem`. Authorization is restricted to administrative or operational actors represented here by the `admin` authorization actor, aligning with the need to prevent untrusted users from manipulating shipment contents.
operations.description:
Update an existing shipment item record under a specific shipment, using both the shipment context and the shipment item identifier to target the correct row in the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table.

This operation is aligned with the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` Prisma model, which is described as an association table binding shipments to the specific order items and SKUs they contain. When updating a shipment item, the service must honor the foreign-key relationships to `shopping_mall_shipments`, `shopping_mall_order_items`, and `shopping_mall_skus`, and ensure that any changes remain consistent with the underlying order and fulfillment structures. For example, increasing the quantity on a shipment item should not exceed the quantity purchased on the corresponding order item, and changing SKU references must remain within the same order context if such a change is allowed at all by business rules.

From a security standpoint, only privileged operational actors such as admins are allowed to modify shipment items, represented here by the `admin` authorization actor. The implementation should enforce this through authentication and authorization layers, ensuring that requests include valid admin credentials. Additional auditing can be implemented to track which admin performed each update to maintain an operational audit trail.

The request body uses `IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IUpdate`, which should include only those fields that can be safely modified after shipment item creation. Immutable fields such as the primary key, shipment link, and order item reference typically remain unchanged, while quantities, notes, or other operational metadata may be updatable depending on business rules and the current shipment status. The response returns the updated `IShoppingMallShipmentItem`, allowing clients to confirm the final state after the update.

This operation complements the creation endpoint `POST /shipments/{shipmentCode}/items` and any read-only endpoints for retrieving shipment items. Error handling should distinguish between missing shipment headers, missing shipment items, items that do not belong to the specified shipment, and attempts to update items on shipments that are no longer modifiable (for example, already delivered or under legal hold), returning appropriate HTTP status codes and explanatory messages.
operations.summary: Update an existing shipment item record in the shopping_mall_shipment_items table under a specific shipment.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the shipment (global scope) in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table, used to ensure that the targeted shipment item belongs to the correct shipment context.

parameters.name: shipmentItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target shipment item record within the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table to be updated.

requestBody.description: Update payload for the shipment item, containing only the fields that are allowed to be modified while the shipment remains in an editable state.

responseBody.description: Representation of the updated shipment item record after applying the requested changes.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: Create a shipment header so that a shipment with the given shipmentCode exists before updating any of its shipment items.
Create a customer order and its order items so that the shipment item being updated remains associated with a valid order context.
Ensure SKU variants exist in shopping_mall_skus so that the shipment item being updated continues to reference a valid SKU.
Create the specific shipment item row under the shipment before attempting to update it with this operation.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a specific shipment item record associated with a shipment from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_shipment_items`. The shipment is identified by its business-level unique `code` exposed as `shipmentCode` in the path, and the item is identified by its technical identifier `shipmentItemId`, which maps to the primary key of `shopping_mall_shipment_items`.

The purpose of this endpoint is to allow authorized back-office administrators or internal operations tools to remove an erroneously created shipment item from an existing shipment when business rules permit full removal instead of adjustments via other mechanisms. Because `shopping_mall_shipment_items` is a subsidiary table under `shopping_mall_shipments` and `shopping_mall_orders`, the provider implementation must validate that the referenced item actually belongs to the shipment specified by `shipmentCode` before performing the deletion.

On execution, the service will resolve the shipment using `shipmentCode` against the `shopping_mall_shipments` table, then ensure that the given `shipmentItemId` corresponds to a child row in `shopping_mall_shipment_items` that is linked to that shipment. If the association check fails, the operation should respond with a not-found style error. When the checks succeed, the matching `shopping_mall_shipment_items` row is removed from the database along with any purely dependent subsidiary records if such relationships exist (e.g., shipment-item–level tracking or audit rows defined in subsidiary tables).

This operation does not return a response body. Clients are expected to infer success from the HTTP status code. Any invariants imposed by other subsystems (such as legal hold, risk cases, or SLA violation records) must be respected by the implementation and may cause the erase to be rejected with an appropriate error if those invariants forbid removing the shipment item.
operations.description:
Erase a specific shipment item that belongs to a shipment identified by a business-level shipment code.

This DELETE operation targets the subsidiary Prisma table `shopping_mall_shipment_items`, which represents the association between a shipment header and the specific order items and SKUs that it contains. The parent shipment is modeled by the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and is exposed externally via a human-readable `code` field that is unique in a global scope or within the operational constraints of the platform. The path parameter `shipmentCode` is used to resolve this parent shipment record, while `shipmentItemId` is used to identify the concrete shipment item row, typically by its UUID primary key.

From a security and governance perspective, this endpoint should only be available to privileged back-office actors such as administrators or specialized operations staff, because it can alter the physical fulfillment representation of an order. The implementation must ensure that only actors with sufficient authority in the RBAC model can access this operation. It is also important to verify that no legal holds, risk cases, or compliance constraints recorded in tables such as `shopping_mall_legal_holds` or `shopping_mall_risk_cases` prevent modification or removal of shipment-related data. If such constraints are present, the provider must reject the request with an appropriate error.

In terms of data relationships, the operation first looks up the shipment in `shopping_mall_shipments` using `shipmentCode`. It then confirms that the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` row identified by `shipmentItemId` is linked to that shipment. If the row does not exist or belongs to a different shipment, the operation responds as if the resource does not exist to avoid leaking cross-shipment identifiers. When the item is valid and business rules allow removal, the system deletes the row and, if needed, cascades deletion to purely dependent subsidiary structures while preserving independent audit data such as `shopping_mall_shipment_events`.

This erase operation is typically used together with other shipment management APIs, such as shipment detail retrieval, shipment item listing, and shipment event logging. Clients that rely on the contents of a shipment should re-fetch shipment details after invoking this endpoint to ensure their view reflects the updated set of items. Any errors, such as attempting to delete an item from a shipment that is already delivered or locked by policy, should surface as clear, domain-appropriate error responses so that administrative tools can handle them gracefully.
operations.summary: Erase a shipment item from `shopping_mall_shipment_items` under a shipment identified by `shipmentCode`.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target shipment (global scope). This code maps to the `code` field of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and is used to resolve the parent shipment whose items are being managed.

parameters.name: shipmentItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target shipment item within the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table. This is typically the UUID primary key used to locate the specific item row that belongs to the shipment resolved by `shipmentCode`. The implementation must ensure that this item is actually associated with that parent shipment before erasing it.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A shipment header must exist in `shopping_mall_shipments` before a shipment item can be associated with it and subsequently deleted. This POST operation creates the parent shipment that is later referenced by `shipmentCode` in the delete operation.

A shipment item row in `shopping_mall_shipment_items` must be created before it can be deleted by ID. This POST operation creates the shipment item identified later by `shipmentItemId` under the shipment resolved by `shipmentCode`.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered, paginated list of shipment event records for a specific shipment from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_shipment_events`. Shipment events represent the detailed tracking timeline and operational history of a shipment, such as created, packed, label-printed, handed-to-carrier, in-transit, out-for-delivery, delivered, delivery-attempted, or returned events.

The shipment to which the events belong is identified by the path parameter `shipmentCode`, which maps to the business-level `code` field of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table. The request body carries search and filtering criteria defined by the DTO type `IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.IRequest`, which may include fields such as event type filters, time range boundaries, pagination options, and sorting preferences. Using PATCH rather than GET allows complex, structured query criteria without overloading query parameters.

On successful execution, the service returns a paginated collection of shipment event summary records using the DTO type `IPageIShoppingMallShipmentEvent.ISummary`. Each summary represents a single row from `shopping_mall_shipment_events` enriched with any necessary denormalized information (for example, human-readable status labels or carrier codes) while remaining optimized for list and timeline displays. The operation is read-only and does not modify any underlying data, making it suitable both for end-user order tracking views and for internal operations dashboards, subject to authorization policies.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shipment events for a specific shipment identified by its business-level shipment code.

This operation reads from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_shipment_events`, which stores the granular timeline of status changes and operational milestones for shipments modeled in `shopping_mall_shipments`. Each event row typically includes fields such as an event type, timestamp, optional carrier status code, and descriptive metadata that reflect how the shipment progresses from creation through delivery or return. The path parameter `shipmentCode` is used to locate the parent shipment via its `code` field and to scope the events to that shipment only.

The request body uses the DTO type `IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.IRequest`, which encapsulates advanced search parameters. These may include filters on event types (for example, only major milestones), time windows (such as events after a certain timestamp), and status families, along with pagination properties like page number and page size, and sorting preferences such as ascending or descending by event timestamp. Using a PATCH method with a structured request object allows the API to support complex future enhancements without breaking URL contracts.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is generally safe to expose more broadly because it is strictly read-only. In a typical shopping mall platform, both authenticated customers and guest users who know the appropriate tracking or order context may be allowed to see shipment events for their own orders, while administrators and seller accounts may have wider visibility. In this specification, the `authorizationActors` field is left as an empty array to denote that the concrete authentication and authorization model will be enforced by surrounding infrastructure and business logic, which will validate that the caller is entitled to view shipment information for the given `shipmentCode`.

The response body returns a paginated collection using the DTO type `IPageIShoppingMallShipmentEvent.ISummary`. Each summary entry is optimized for rendering a timeline or event list, typically including the key fields customers need for tracking (timestamp, resolved status label, and optional location or carrier message) without overfetching heavy or rarely used metadata. Clients are expected to use the pagination fields to navigate through the complete timeline when many events exist and to refresh the list periodically while a shipment is in transit.

This operation is designed to be used together with shipment detail retrieval and order detail APIs. A common usage pattern is that an order detail screen fetches the shipment associated with the order and then calls this endpoint to render the shipment tracking timeline. Errors such as supplying an unknown `shipmentCode` should result in a clear not-found style response so that clients can gracefully handle missing or invalid tracking references.
operations.summary: Search and list shipment events from `shopping_mall_shipment_events` for a shipment identified by `shipmentCode`.

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target shipment (global scope). This maps to the `code` field of `shopping_mall_shipments` and scopes the search to events belonging to that specific shipment.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, and pagination options for querying shipment events of the specified shipment.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment event summaries associated with the shipment identified by `shipmentCode`, ordered and filtered according to the request criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A shipment header in `shopping_mall_shipments` must exist to be referenced by `shipmentCode` when querying its events. This POST operation creates the shipment whose timeline will later be read by the PATCH events listing operation.

At least one shipment event row in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` must be created before it can appear in the paginated results. This POST operation creates shipment event records that the PATCH listing operation filters and returns.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single shipment event record associated with a specific shipment in the shoppingMall domain. It is logically based on the Prisma model that stores shipment event history (for example, a table such as shopping_mall_shipment_events) which captures granular milestones in the shipment lifecycle, including timestamps, event types, carrier updates, and human-readable descriptions.

The endpoint is designed so that the shipment is identified by a business-readable unique shipmentCode rather than a low-level UUID, while the individual event is addressed by a unique eventId. The operation returns a detailed DTO representing one shipment event, including all relevant attributes defined in the underlying Prisma schema such as event type, occurredAt timestamp, recordedAt timestamp, actor or system source, and any structured payload or message. It is intended primarily for read-only consumption in customer, seller, or admin shipment detail views.

From a business perspective, this operation supports order and shipment tracking flows by allowing clients to drill down into a single event from a shipment’s event timeline. It is read-only and does not modify database state. The response DTO maps one-to-one to the shipment event row in the shipment events table, potentially including joined or derived information such as human-friendly labels or carrier tracking links, but never exposes fields that do not exist in the Prisma model.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific shipment event for a given shipment in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation targets the shipment event history model (for example, shopping_mall_shipment_events), which records chronological events associated with shipments, such as "label_created", "picked_up", "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered", or "delivery_failed". Each row in that Prisma table represents a discrete event with fields including a unique identifier, a foreign key to the shipment header, an event type code, one or more timestamps, and descriptive metadata. The API exposes these columns through the IShoppingMallShipmentEvent response type so that consumers can see exactly what happened and when.

The shipment is selected using the shipmentCode path parameter, which is a business-facing identifier for the shipment and is typically globally unique or scoped according to the shipment Prisma model’s unique constraints. The eventId path parameter then identifies a single event row for that shipment. The implementation must validate that the specified event belongs to the specified shipment before returning data, and should respond with an appropriate not-found error when either the shipment or event cannot be located or when they do not belong together.

Security-wise, this is a read-only endpoint that can be exposed to authenticated end users such as customers, sellers, or admins according to higher-level authorization policies; in this specification we leave authorizationActors empty so that the realization layer can attach appropriate guards. The endpoint never alters shipment or event records and is safe for use in polling or detail views.

Typical usage is in a shipment tracking UI where a user first retrieves the list of events for a shipment (for example via a separate PATCH /shipments/{shipmentCode}/events index operation) and then calls this GET endpoint when the user requests full details about a particular event. Error handling should clearly distinguish between a missing shipment, a missing event, and authorization failures, and must not leak internal identifiers beyond what is defined in the IShoppingMallShipmentEvent contract.
operations.summary: Get a specific shipment event (shopping_mall_shipment_events) for a shipment by shipmentCode and eventId

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Business identifier code of the target shipment whose event history is being queried. This code uniquely identifies the shipment record in the underlying shipments table (global scope or scoped according to the Prisma unique constraint) and is used to ensure the event belongs to the correct shipment.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment event within the shipment event history table. This value selects a single row from the shipment events model that must be associated with the shipment identified by shipmentCode.

responseBody.description: Detailed representation of a single shipment event associated with the specified shipment, including event type, timestamps, and descriptive metadata as defined in the shopping_mall_shipment_events Prisma model.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A shipment must exist in shopping_mall_shipments before its specific event can be retrieved by shipmentCode and eventId.
The shipment event row in shopping_mall_shipment_events must be created for the given shipmentCode before it can be retrieved by GET /shoppingMall/shipments/{shipmentCode}/events/{eventId}.

operations.specification:
This operation creates and records a new shipment event in the shipment event history model for a given shipment in the shoppingMall domain. It is backed by the Prisma table that stores shipment events (for example, shopping_mall_shipment_events), which contains fields such as an event identifier, a foreign key to the shipment, an event type or status code, timestamps (occurredAt, recordedAt), optional actor or source information, and additional metadata or message payload.

The client identifies the shipment by its business-facing shipmentCode in the URL path. The request body uses the IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.ICreate DTO to carry event-specific data such as the event type, event time, and any human-readable or structured context message. On successful creation, the system persists a new row in the shipment events table linked to the shipment corresponding to shipmentCode and returns the full IShoppingMallShipmentEvent representation of the newly created record.

Business rules around event creation can include validation that the shipment exists and is in a state that accepts new events, chronological consistency checks (for example, event timestamps not preceding shipment creation), and optional enforcement of allowed transitions (e.g., preventing a "delivered" event before "out_for_delivery"). Because this table is historical in nature, events are typically append-only; this operation never overwrites existing events, and any downstream analytics or tracking UIs rely on the integrity of this history.
operations.description:
Create a new shipment event for a specific shipment and persist it in the shipment event history table.

This operation is associated with the Prisma model that records shipment events, such as shopping_mall_shipment_events, which holds one row per significant change or milestone in the shipment lifecycle. When clients call this endpoint, they provide event-specific data in the IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.ICreate request body, including at minimum the event type and relevant timestamps, while the service layer resolves the shipment foreign key based on the shipmentCode path parameter. This ensures that the event is always tied to the correct shipment header as defined in the shipments Prisma model.

From a security and authorization perspective, creation of shipment events is generally restricted to trusted actors such as internal services integrating with carriers, seller fulfillment systems, or admin tools. In this specification, authorizationActors is left empty so that the realization layer can map it to the appropriate authenticated actors (for example, a service account or admin role) based on business requirements. The endpoint must validate the existence of the referenced shipment and should fail with a clear error if shipmentCode does not correspond to any shipment or if policy rules forbid appending events.

This POST operation complements read-only tracking APIs such as GET /shipments/{shipmentCode} or GET /shipments/{shipmentCode}/events/{eventId}. While those endpoints surface previously recorded events, this one is responsible for extending the shipment’s timeline. Implementations should ensure idempotency where required (for example by de-duplicating events using an idempotency key or external event identifier when such a field exists in the Prisma schema) and must avoid creating logically inconsistent sequences of events. Any validation errors in the IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.ICreate payload must be reported with descriptive messages so that upstream systems can correct their requests.
operations.summary: Create a new shipment event (shopping_mall_shipment_events) for a shipment identified by shipmentCode

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Business identifier code of the shipment for which the new event is being recorded. This code is used to resolve the corresponding shipment header record in the shipments Prisma model before inserting the event.

requestBody.description: Payload describing the shipment event to create, including event type, timestamps, and any additional metadata required by the shopping_mall_shipment_events Prisma model.

responseBody.description: Representation of the newly created shipment event after it has been persisted in the shipment event history table and linked to the shipment identified by shipmentCode.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: A parent shipment record in shopping_mall_shipments must be created so that the new shipment event can be associated with an existing shipment identified by shipmentCode.

operations.specification:
Update an existing shipment event record associated with a shipment in the shoppingMall logistics domain. This operation is backed primarily by the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` Prisma model, which represents individual tracking and logistics events in the detailed shipping timeline for a shipment, and is linked to the `shopping_mall_shipments` model that represents shipment headers.

The endpoint identifies the parent shipment using a human-readable, business-level `shipmentCode` rather than a low-level UUID, reflecting that shipment codes are typically exposed to customers, sellers, and support agents. Within that shipment, the specific event is addressed via `eventId`, which represents the primary key of a single timeline entry in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` table (for example, the `id` column). The request body uses the `IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.IUpdate` DTO to carry mutable fields such as status detail, event description, timestamps, and carrier metadata, while immutable keys like the linkage to the shipment and primary identifiers remain fixed and are not part of the update DTO.

On successful execution, the API validates that the referenced shipment exists in `shopping_mall_shipments` using the business `shipmentCode`, confirms that the event identified by `eventId` belongs to that shipment, applies any business rules (for example, not allowing updates on events locked by legal holds), persists the modifications to the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` row, and returns the updated shipment event as an `IShoppingMallShipmentEvent` resource.
operations.description:
Update a specific shipment event in the detailed shipping timeline for a shipment identified by its business shipment code.

This operation targets a single record in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` Prisma model, which is described as an event log entry representing the detailed shipping and tracking timeline for a shipment. Each event in this table typically contains fields like an internal identifier (for example, `id`), a foreign key to `shopping_mall_shipments`, event type, status or state, timestamps, and optional carrier or tracking metadata. The event is addressed via the `eventId` path parameter, which maps to the primary key of `shopping_mall_shipment_events`, and it is always resolved in the context of the shipment identified by `shipmentCode`, ensuring that the event cannot be updated outside of its parent shipment.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is restricted to trusted operational actors such as platform administrators or internal logistics systems. In a typical shoppingMall deployment, only admin or internal service actors are allowed to correct shipment event data, and all updates should be captured by audit logging or history mechanisms if present in the schema. The operation enforces that the combination of `shipmentCode` and `eventId` is valid, returns appropriate 404 errors when resources are not found, and may surface 409/422 responses when business rules prevent certain updates.
operations.summary: Update a shipment event record in the shopping_mall_shipment_events timeline for a shipment

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target shipment (global scope). This value maps to a globally unique business code field on the `shopping_mall_shipments` table (for example, a `code` column with `@@unique([code])`) that identifies the shipment whose timeline will be modified.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Primary key identifier of the shipment event record in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` table (for example, the `id` field). This value uniquely identifies the specific tracking or logistics event to be updated for the given shipment.

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the shipment event associated with the given shipment. Only mutable fields defined in `IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.IUpdate` are allowed, such as event description, status details, timestamps, or carrier metadata. Identifiers and links to the parent shipment are not part of this payload.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment event resource after applying the requested changes, represented using the `IShoppingMallShipmentEvent` DTO mapped from the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` Prisma model.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A shipment must exist before its shipment events can be updated. POST /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderCode}/shipments creates a shopping_mall_shipments record that will later be referenced by shipmentCode in the shipment events timeline.

A shipment event must be created before it can be updated. POST /shoppingMall/shipments/{shipmentCode}/events creates a shopping_mall_shipment_events row whose id is used as eventId in the update endpoint.

operations.specification:
Permanently remove an existing shipment event record from the detailed tracking timeline associated with a shipment in the shoppingMall platform. This operation is primarily backed by the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` Prisma model, which stores granular shipping and tracking events, and is scoped to a specific shipment represented by the `shopping_mall_shipments` model.

The API identifies the parent shipment using `shipmentCode`, a business-level shipment identifier that maps to a globally unique code field on `shopping_mall_shipments` (for example, a `code` column with `@@unique([code])`). Within that shipment, the event is addressed via `eventId`, which corresponds to the primary key of a single event row in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` (for example, an `id` field). When invoked, the operation confirms that the event belongs to the shipment referenced in the path, enforces any domain constraints (for example, disallowing removal of events linked to legal holds or closed disputes if such rules exist), and then deletes the corresponding row.

The underlying schema overview for `shopping_mall_shipment_events` does not explicitly document a dedicated soft deletion column, so this operation is documented in a way that is compatible with either hard deletion (actual row removal) or an implementation that delegates to a separate status mechanism. The service layer is responsible for implementing the exact deletion semantics consistent with the Prisma model and domain rules.

Because shipment event data can affect customer-visible tracking timelines and operational auditability, this erase operation should be restricted to privileged administrative actors or internal operational tools. The endpoint does not require a request body and returns no content on success; clients can re-fetch the shipment’s events via a separate list or detail retrieval endpoint to observe the updated timeline state.
operations.description:
Erase a specific shipment event from the detailed shipping and tracking timeline for a shipment identified by its shipment code.

This operation acts on the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` Prisma model, where each record represents a discrete shipping or tracking event tied to a shipment in `shopping_mall_shipments`. The path parameters `shipmentCode` and `eventId` together ensure that the event being removed is correctly scoped: `shipmentCode` resolves the shipment header via a globally unique business code on `shopping_mall_shipments`, while `eventId` identifies the concrete event row via the primary key on `shopping_mall_shipment_events`.

From an authorization standpoint, removing shipment events is a sensitive action, because it alters the historical tracking information that might be used for customer support, dispute resolution, or operational analytics. Therefore, access to this endpoint is limited to high-privilege actors, such as platform administrators or dedicated logistics operations roles represented by the `admin` authorization actor. Business rules derived from the Prisma schema comments and related requirements documents may additionally restrict which events can be erased (for example, preventing removal of events linked to legal holds or closed disputes), and all such deletions should be captured by audit logging where available.

Functionally, the endpoint performs validation to confirm that the `eventId` belongs to the shipment identified by `shipmentCode`, applies any relevant business rules, and then deletes the event record from `shopping_mall_shipment_events`. On successful completion, it responds with no body, leaving it up to clients to re-query shipment events using other read-only endpoints. If the shipment or event does not exist, or if business rules forbid deletion, the service returns appropriate error responses such as 404 for missing resources or 409/422 for rule violations.
operations.summary: Erase a shipment event record from the shopping_mall_shipment_events timeline for a shipment

parameters.name: shipmentCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target shipment (global scope). This value maps to a globally unique business code field on the `shopping_mall_shipments` table (for example, a `code` column with `@@unique([code])`) that identifies the shipment whose timeline will be modified.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Primary key identifier of the shipment event record in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` table (for example, the `id` field). This value uniquely identifies the specific tracking or logistics event that should be erased from the shipment’s tracking timeline.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: The parent shipment must exist before a shipment event associated with it can later be deleted. POST /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderCode}/shipments creates the shopping_mall_shipments record identified by shipmentCode.

A shipment event must exist before it can be erased. POST /shoppingMall/shipments/{shipmentCode}/events creates the shopping_mall_shipment_events row whose id is later used as eventId in the delete endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the complete business and status timeline for a specific customer-facing order in the shopping mall system. It is primarily associated with the `shopping_mall_orders` Prisma table as the main header entity, while also reading from multiple subsidiary and snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`, `shopping_mall_order_payments`, `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories`, `shopping_mall_shipments`, `shopping_mall_shipment_events`, `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, and `shopping_mall_disputes`.

The endpoint is designed to return a chronological sequence of significant events related to the order lifecycle. These include order creation, confirmation, payment authorization and capture, shipment preparation, shipment dispatch, delivery, cancellation attempts, refund flows, dispute openings, and policy-related case events. Instead of exposing each underlying table separately, this operation composes data across these Prisma models into a unified, read-only timeline DTO optimized for client consumption.

The request identifies the order using a human-readable, globally unique `orderCode` rather than an internal UUID identifier. The Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_orders` is expected to define a unique business key such as `code` (with a corresponding `@@unique([code])` constraint), which is mapped here to the `{orderCode}` path parameter. The response returns an `IShoppingMallOrderTimeline` document that includes high-level order header information and an array of ordered timeline events with normalized structure and metadata.
operations.description:
Retrieve a unified, chronological business timeline for a specific order identified by its business order code.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_orders` table and multiple related history and event tables such as `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`, `shopping_mall_order_payments`, `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories`, `shopping_mall_shipments`, `shopping_mall_shipment_events`, `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, and `shopping_mall_disputes`. Each of these Prisma models typically contains descriptive fields and status codes that capture state transitions and business events during the order lifecycle. The API normalizes these into a consistent `IShoppingMallOrderTimeline` response so that clients do not need to query each table individually.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is intended for authenticated customers viewing their own orders. The `authorizationActor` is set to `customer`, and the underlying implementation must ensure that the requested order belongs to the authenticated customer account before returning any data.

In terms of validation and business rules, the `{orderCode}` parameter must map to an existing order record in `shopping_mall_orders` that is visible to the requesting customer. If the code cannot be found or is not accessible, the operation should return a suitable error (such as 404 for not found or 403 for forbidden). The response structure orders all events by their effective timestamps, ensuring a clear story line from order placement through payments, shipments, cancellations, refunds, and disputes. Related API operations include order detail retrieval (e.g., `GET /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}`) and tracking-specific views (e.g., `GET /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/tracking`), which focus on more specialized subsets of the same underlying data.
operations.summary: Get a composed lifecycle timeline for a ShoppingMall order from shopping_mall_orders and related history tables

prerequisites.description: The order timeline can only be retrieved for an existing order. POST /shoppingMall/customer/orders creates the shopping_mall_orders record (and its business order_code) that is later referenced by {orderCode} in this timeline view.
