operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full details of a single customer-written product review stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model. It is a canonical "read by identifier" endpoint that returns all primary review fields and optional related information needed for detailed views or administrative inspection.

The endpoint uses the HTTP GET method on the `/shoppingMall/reviews/{reviewId}` path, where the `reviewId` path parameter corresponds to the unique identifier of a record in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table. The parameter is represented as a string schema and can support UUID-style identifiers or any other unique key type defined in the Prisma model. The operation does not use a request body because all selection context is expressed through the path parameter.

The response body is typed as `IShoppingMallReview`, which is the detailed DTO representation of a review. It typically includes metadata such as product and SKU linkage, authoring customer, rating score, full review text content, timestamps, visibility and moderation flags, helpful vote statistics, and potentially inlined aggregates or related relationships that are safe and efficient to return as part of a single object. This design enables both customer-facing review detail views and internal back-office review inspection screens to obtain a complete view of the review via a single call.

This operation is intentionally designed with an empty `authorizationActors` array, making it suitable for exposure as a public endpoint for visible reviews. Implementations can still enforce business rules based on the review's visibility state, ensuring that hidden, blocked, or otherwise restricted reviews are either not returned or return an appropriate error (such as 404 Not Found) when requested by unauthorized contexts. Administrative tools, on the other hand, can use the same endpoint behind additional authentication and authorization layers to view non-public reviews when necessary.
operations.description:
Fetch the full details of a single product review from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table using its unique identifier.

This detail retrieval operation is centered on the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model, which contains the authoritative record for individual customer reviews and ratings. By specifying the `reviewId` path parameter, clients request one specific review and receive all primary fields necessary for rendering a detailed review view, performing moderation tasks, or debugging review-related issues.

The `reviewId` parameter is modeled as a string and should match the unique identifier used in the `shopping_mall_reviews` schema, such as a UUID or another unique key. The operation validates that the identifier is well-formed and then queries the database for a corresponding review record. If no review exists for the provided identifier, the server responds with an appropriate error status (typically 404) without exposing sensitive metadata about non-existent or restricted reviews.

The response DTO `IShoppingMallReview` is expected to represent a complete review object, including fields such as associated product or SKU references, customer information (or anonymized display name where required), rating score, full textual content, timestamps for creation and last update, moderation and visibility statuses, and any high-level computed attributes like helpful vote counts or whether the review has associated reports. Implementations may also include related snapshots or versioning information via nested DTOs if this is part of the detailed view design.

This operation declares an empty `authorizationActors` array to allow implementations to expose public reviews without authentication. Nevertheless, the internal business logic should still enforce visibility rules derived from review status fields: hidden or blocked reviews must be filtered out or protected, and only authorized administrative contexts should be able to override these restrictions. Together with the list/search endpoint on `/reviews`, this detail endpoint forms the core of the review read API surface for the shoppingMall service.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new product review in the shopping mall platform, persisting a record into the Prisma model `shopping_mall_reviews`. It allows an authenticated customer to submit a rating and textual review content for a purchased product or SKU, subject to the business rules defined for review eligibility and timing. The request body uses the DTO type `IShoppingMallReview.ICreate`, which encapsulates the rating score, review text, references to the associated order item or SKU, and any optional media or metadata fields exactly as defined in the Prisma schema and higher-level interface definitions.

The endpoint validates that the customer is eligible to post a review for the referenced product or SKU according to the rules represented indirectly by models such as `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`, and that the rating score complies with constraints established on the `shopping_mall_reviews` model (for example, minimum and maximum rating bounds, required associations, and mandatory fields). It also ensures that the review is linked to the correct customer identity based on the authenticated actor context rather than accepting arbitrary actor identifiers from the client.

Upon successful creation, the operation returns the newly created review using the detailed DTO type `IShoppingMallReview`. This type reflects the full persisted state of the `shopping_mall_reviews` row, including server-managed fields (identifiers, timestamps, and moderation status fields as defined in schema) while hiding any internal-only attributes that should not be exposed. Downstream systems such as rating aggregation jobs (e.g., `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`) can consume the created review asynchronously to update aggregate scores used throughout the catalog.
operations.description:
Create a new customer-written product review record within the shopping mall review system, backed by the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model.

This operation accepts a structured request body described by `IShoppingMallReview.ICreate`, which wraps all client-provided review attributes that correspond to columns on `shopping_mall_reviews` and its closely related entities. Typical properties include the numeric rating score, the main textual body of the review, optional title or headline fields, and references to the target product, SKU, or order item depending on how the schema models the relation. The implementation must validate that required fields from the Prisma model are present, that rating values fall within the allowed range, and that any referenced foreign keys exist and are consistent with purchase history.

From a security and authorization perspective, the endpoint is restricted to authenticated customers, represented using `authorizationActors: ["customer"]`. The backend must resolve the customer identity from the session or token, and it must never trust arbitrary customer identifiers in the payload. In addition, if the business logic requires purchase-based eligibility, the implementation should confirm that the requesting customer has a completed order containing the referenced product or SKU and that the order state and age match the rules implied by auxiliary models such as `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`.

The created review is stored as a row in `shopping_mall_reviews`, which may contain fields for moderation status, visibility flags, and timestamps that are managed exclusively by the server. While only the review header is created here, separate subsystems and tables like `shopping_mall_review_versions`, `shopping_mall_review_reports`, and `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` will manage later edits, reports, and moderation decisions. Clients consuming this API typically chain it with list or detail review retrieval APIs and with catalog endpoints that surface rating aggregates derived from `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`.

Error handling should clearly distinguish between validation failures (e.g., invalid rating or missing required associations), authorization errors (customer not allowed or ineligible to review), and internal persistence errors when writing into `shopping_mall_reviews`. In each case, the client receives structured error information while no partial review records are left in an inconsistent state.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing review record stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model. It is used when a customer edits the content or rating of their previously submitted review, or when limited mutable attributes (such as title or visibility flags that are allowed to be changed by the review owner) need to be modified. The target review is identified by the `reviewId` path parameter, which corresponds to the primary key or globally unique identifier field of the `shopping_mall_reviews` table.

The request body conforms to the DTO `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate`, which mirrors the updatable subset of columns on `shopping_mall_reviews`. Immutable fields such as the original author identity, the associated product or SKU references, and creation timestamps must not be altered through this endpoint even if they exist in the underlying schema. The implementation must load the existing record, verify ownership against the authenticated customer actor, and then apply only the permitted changes with full validation of any modified attributes.

The operation returns the updated review as `IShoppingMallReview`, reflecting the latest persisted state of the `shopping_mall_reviews` row after the update. If the platform maintains version history via `shopping_mall_review_versions`, the update logic should create a corresponding versioned snapshot entry as a side effect, but that lifecycle is internal to the service and is not exposed directly in this interface. Rating aggregates in tables like `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` may also be recomputed asynchronously based on the updated rating and visibility state.
operations.description:
Update an existing customer-written review stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` model by targeting it through the `reviewId` path parameter.

This operation lets an authenticated customer modify allowed fields of a previously created review, such as the rating score, textual content, or title, as modeled by the `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate` DTO. The payload is applied only to the review identified by the `reviewId` path parameter, which represents the unique identifier used in the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model. Before performing any changes, the service must verify that the review exists, that it belongs to the requesting customer, and that the current review status permits editing according to business rules and any relevant policy or SLA configurations.

From an authorization standpoint, the endpoint is restricted to the `customer` actor, and the backend derives the acting customer from authentication context rather than trusting IDs within the request body. If the review has been locked by moderation actions recorded through `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions`, or if policy-driven rules represented by `shopping_mall_business_policies` and `shopping_mall_policy_versions` prevent edits after a certain time window, the service must reject the update with a clear error code instead of silently ignoring the request.

When the update succeeds, the endpoint responds with the full review representation `IShoppingMallReview`, which reflects all server-managed fields (for example, updated timestamps and possibly derived moderation or visibility states). Internal subsystems such as `shopping_mall_review_versions` can be used to snapshot the previous state for audit and rollback purposes, but those details remain hidden from API consumers. Clients will usually follow this call with a GET or list operation to refresh UI state and with catalog reads that surface updated rating aggregates coming from `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`.

operations.specification:
Design a DELETE operation for removing a single product review record associated with the Prisma model `shopping_mall_reviews`. This endpoint will permanently delete an existing review identified by its unique primary key (represented here as `reviewId` in the path), assuming the Prisma model exposes an `id` field as the unique identifier.

The operation is intended to be used by authenticated actors who are permitted—according to business rules defined in the requirements—to remove a review. Depending on the final authorization implementation, this typically includes either the original review author (customer) for self-service deletion within allowed time windows, or administrative actors for moderation and governance flows. However, authorization policy is enforced at a higher layer; at the API contract level we only declare that this is an authenticated operation.

The DELETE operation does not require a request body; all necessary context is provided via the path parameter and the authenticated user. On success, the operation returns no response body, signaling that the review has been removed. Error handling covers cases such as non-existing review identifiers, authorization failures (e.g., user attempting to delete someone else’s review without proper role), and integrity constraints (for example, if legal hold or audit policies prevent deletion).
operations.description:
Permanently delete a single review resource from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table using its unique identifier.

This operation targets the underlying Prisma model that stores product reviews and ratings. Each review is uniquely identified by an internal identifier represented at the API boundary as `reviewId`. When the client invokes this endpoint, the system locates the corresponding review row and performs a hard delete in the database so that the review no longer participates in rating aggregates, product detail displays, or moderation workflows.

Security and authorization are critical for this operation. Only actors who satisfy the business rules—such as the original review author within an allowed timeframe or authorized administrative staff in charge of moderation—should be able to perform this deletion. Authorization checks are enforced by the application layer that consumes this API contract, using the authenticated actor context and review ownership information. If a caller does not have sufficient permission, the operation must fail with an appropriate authorization error instead of deleting any data.

From a data integrity perspective, the deletion may trigger recalculation of rating aggregates and denormalized statistics that depend on review data, such as per-product or per‑SKU rating summaries. Those recalculations are handled by downstream services or domain logic and are not part of the API contract. Clients can pair this delete operation with list and aggregate endpoints—for example, listing reviews for a product or fetching rating aggregates—to confirm updated state after the removal.

On success, the endpoint returns an empty response body with an appropriate success status code, signaling that the review record has been removed from persistent storage. If the specified `reviewId` does not exist, the system will typically return a not‑found error. If the record is protected due to compliance or legal constraints, the system will return an error describing why the deletion cannot be performed.

Design a PATCH operation that retrieves a filtered, paginated list of product reviews, operating primarily on the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model and related aggregates. This endpoint is used to search and browse reviews for a specific product identified by `productId` while supporting additional filters and sorting criteria.

The path segment `/products/{productId}/reviews` indicates that the primary scope of this operation is reviews belonging to a single product. The `productId` parameter is used to constrain the search space to reviews associated with that product. The request body uses a dedicated DTO type `IShoppingMallReview.IRequest`, which encapsulates client‑supplied search filters (such as rating ranges, presence of images, date ranges, or review states), pagination parameters (page size, page index or cursor), and ordering instructions (e.g., newest first, highest rating, most helpful).

The response body returns a paginated collection of review summaries using the DTO `IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary`. Each summary entry provides all information commonly needed for list rendering—such as rating value, truncated content, author display information, created timestamp, and basic moderation status—while omitting heavy or rarely used fields such as full audit history. This design provides an efficient interface for product detail pages and review listing views, while more detailed review information can be fetched via separate detail endpoints if needed.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of reviews for a specific product from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table.

This operation allows clients to list reviews that belong to a single product, identified by the `productId` path parameter, and to apply additional query criteria through the request body. The request DTO `IShoppingMallReview.IRequest` is responsible for carrying pagination options (such as page size and cursor or page index), filter conditions (for example, minimum and maximum rating, presence of review text, or time windows), and sorting preferences (such as newest first, highest or lowest rating, or helpfulness ordering). By encapsulating these options in the body of a PATCH request, the API supports complex search semantics without overloading query parameters.

From a security and authorization perspective, this operation is designed primarily for end‑user consumption on product detail and review listing pages. It typically exposes only reviews that are considered visible according to platform policies—such as excluding reviews removed by moderation, hidden due to policy violations, or restricted by legal requirements. The API contract itself remains simple, and the actual visibility rules are implemented in the domain logic backing this operation. Rate limiting and abuse protection can be applied at the gateway level to prevent scraping or excessive querying.

The response encapsulates the results in a paginated container `IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary`. Each summary element focuses on fields required for list rendering and quick scanning—rating score, short content preview, timestamps, and lightweight author display information—helping the client generate efficient UIs. Additional list metadata such as total count or cursor tokens is delivered via the page wrapper. Clients may chain this operation with more specialized endpoints, such as review detail retrieval or rating aggregate operations, to build rich product review experiences.

Error cases include passing an invalid or non‑existent `productId`, sending invalid pagination parameters, or specifying filter combinations that violate validation rules defined in `IShoppingMallReview.IRequest`. In such scenarios, the service must return structured error responses with clear messages, enabling clients to correct their requests.

Create a new customer-written product review associated with the shopping_mall_reviews table. This POST /products/{productId}/reviews operation allows an authenticated customer to submit a rating and optional textual content for a given product, with optional SKU-level specificity when the review targets a particular variant. The underlying Prisma model shopping_mall_reviews defines the canonical current version of each review, linking it to shopping_mall_products via shopping_mall_product_id, to shopping_mall_customers via shopping_mall_customer_id, and optionally to shopping_mall_skus and shopping_mall_order_items for verified purchase semantics.

The operation will accept a request body typed as IShoppingMallReview.ICreate, which encapsulates fields such as rating (integer, typically 1–5), optional title, optional body, a flag for whether the review is incentivized, and any additional metadata required by business rules. The productId path parameter will be mapped to the shopping_mall_product_id foreign key; the authenticated customer will be mapped to shopping_mall_customer_id; SKU and order item linkage will be validated according to review eligibility policies that may be represented in shopping_mall_review_eligibilities or order-related tables.

On success, the endpoint returns the newly created review as IShoppingMallReview, including computed attributes such as helpfulness_score (initially zero), visibility_status (e.g., visible or pending_moderation), moderation_state (e.g., unreviewed), and flags like verified_purchase and incentivized. Business logic must enforce the unique constraint on (shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_id) so that each customer can only have one active review per product/SKU combination; attempts to create a duplicate review should result in a validation error. The endpoint must also respect soft deletion semantics implemented via deleted_at in shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_products, ensuring that reviews cannot be created for soft-deleted products and that deleted reviews are not considered when checking uniqueness.
operations.description:
Create a new product review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table for the specified product.

This operation is invoked as POST /products/{productId}/reviews and is intended for authenticated customers who have purchased or otherwise become eligible to review a product. The productId path parameter identifies the target product and is mapped internally to the shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_product_id foreign key referencing shopping_mall_products.id. The request body, represented by the IShoppingMallReview.ICreate DTO, contains user-provided review details such as the integer rating on a discrete scale, optional short title, and optional free-form body text, alongside any flags indicating incentivized context. The application logic determines the correct visibility_status and moderation_state values based on platform policies, typically starting as visible or pending_moderation.

From a security and authorization standpoint, this operation requires an authenticated customer actor and should only be exposed to users mapped to shopping_mall_customers. The service must validate that the caller is allowed to review the product, commonly by verifying that a completed order item exists for the product or SKU in question and that review timing windows defined by business policy have not been violated. If the customer is not eligible, or if a review already exists for the same (customer, product, sku) key as constrained by the unique index on (shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_id), the endpoint must return a clear error rather than creating a duplicate record.

At the database level, the operation will insert a new row into shopping_mall_reviews, setting rating, title, body, verified_purchase, incentivized, and initializing helpfulness_score to zero. It must also populate created_at and updated_at timestamps, and must leave deleted_at as null to indicate that the review is active. The visibility_status, moderation_state, and verified_purchase fields should reflect review and moderation policies described in the schema comments, distinguishing between visible, hidden, pending_moderation, and removed, and between approved and flagged states. Related systems such as shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates and shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates may react to review creation asynchronously to update aggregate scores.

Clients typically call this endpoint after the customer has visited an order history or product page that indicates review eligibility. Related operations include any future endpoints for updating a review, retrieving a customer’s own reviews, or listing reviews for a product. Error conditions to handle include invalid or missing rating values, attempts to review non-existent or deleted products, conflicts with the unique constraints on the shopping_mall_reviews table, and authorization failures when the caller is not the expected customer actor.

operations.specification:
Retrieve a single customer-written product review from the shopping_mall_reviews table by its identifier for a given product. This GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId} operation provides a detailed view of a specific review, leveraging the Prisma model shopping_mall_reviews as the primary data source and joining to shopping_mall_products to ensure that the review belongs to the indicated product.

The reviewId path parameter is mapped to shopping_mall_reviews.id, while productId represents the parent shopping_mall_products.id and acts as a guard to prevent cross-product access: the implementation must verify that shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_product_id equals the resolved productId. The response will be typed as IShoppingMallReview and will contain fields such as rating, optional title and body, visibility_status, moderation_state, verified_purchase, incentivized, helpfulness_score, and the created_at/updated_at timestamps. The soft deletion column deleted_at in shopping_mall_reviews is honored so that reviews with a non-null deleted_at are not returned to normal clients.

This operation is generally read-only and may be publicly accessible or restricted based on visibility_status and moderation_state. For example, only reviews whose visibility_status is visible should be returned to general consumers, while hidden or pending_moderation reviews might be reserved for seller or admin tools and require different authorization actors. The implementation should rely on the visibility and moderation semantics documented on the shopping_mall_reviews columns to filter out entries that should not be shown, and it may also consult precomputed aggregates like shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates for ancillary data if needed, though the main payload remains the single review entity.

The endpoint returns a 404-style error when either the product does not exist, the review does not exist, or the review’s shopping_mall_product_id does not match the requested productId. It should also treat reviews with non-null deleted_at as not found for standard user-facing contexts. Related operations include creating a review via POST /products/{productId}/reviews and list/search endpoints for product reviews that return collections or summaries instead of a single detailed record. This detailed retrieval endpoint can be used by product detail pages, review permalinks, or moderation consoles depending on configured authorization policies.
operations.description:
Fetch detailed information for a specific product review stored in the shopping_mall_reviews table, ensuring it belongs to the specified product.

This GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId} operation is designed to return the canonical current version of a single review as persisted in shopping_mall_reviews. The reviewId path parameter corresponds directly to shopping_mall_reviews.id, while productId identifies the parent product via shopping_mall_products.id and is used to constrain the query so that only a review whose shopping_mall_product_id matches the productId is returned. The result is serialized as IShoppingMallReview, exposing fields such as the integer rating, optional title and free-form body, visibility_status indicating whether the review is publicly visible, moderation_state describing its moderation lifecycle, boolean flags for verified_purchase and incentivized status, the integer helpfulness_score used for ranking, and timestamps created_at and updated_at.

From an access-control perspective, this endpoint is typically safe to expose publicly for reviews that are intended to be visible to all users. The implementation must, however, enforce the visibility semantics encoded in the visibility_status and moderation_state columns of shopping_mall_reviews. Reviews flagged as hidden, pending_moderation, or removed should be excluded or handled according to business rules; a common approach for customer-facing contexts is to treat such reviews as not found. Soft deletion is implemented via the deleted_at column on shopping_mall_reviews, so the handler must ensure that rows with a non-null deleted_at are not returned in normal responses.

Internally, the service will perform a query filtered by both id and productId-matching shopping_mall_product_id to guarantee product association. If no row satisfies these constraints, it should respond with a not-found error rather than exposing cross-product or soft-deleted data. Integrators using this API should pair it with collection endpoints that list or search reviews for a product, using this detailed endpoint primarily for deep links or drill-down interactions. Any changes to visibility or moderation state are applied through separate administrative or moderation endpoints and are reflected automatically when this retrieval endpoint is called.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing product review associated with a specific product in the shoppingMall domain. It targets the Prisma table that stores customer-written product reviews, which corresponds to the logical model "shopping_mall_reviews". The operation allows modification of mutable review fields such as rating score, review title, review body, visibility flags, or other editable attributes, while preserving immutable fields like the original author and creation timestamp.

The endpoint uses a nested resource path structure `/products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}` to clearly express that the review is conceptually tied to a particular product. The `productId` path parameter identifies the parent product whose review set is being addressed, and the `reviewId` parameter identifies the specific review record within the reviews table. Even if the underlying Prisma schema enforces referential integrity independently, the API design requires both identifiers so that business logic can verify that the targeted review indeed belongs to the specified product.

The request body follows the standard DTO naming convention for the ShoppingMall service and must use a dedicated update DTO type. This type_name is `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate`, representing a structured payload that contains only those fields that are allowed to be updated on a review. The response returns the updated review entity using the primary DTO type `IShoppingMallReview`, ensuring that clients receive the complete current state of the review after the update has been applied. The operation is mainly used by authenticated customers editing their own reviews or by administrative actors performing moderation-related updates, with permission checks implemented at the business logic layer based on the caller's role and the review's ownership.
operations.description:
Update an existing product review that belongs to a specific product, reflecting changes such as rating adjustment, edited review text, or status flags in the underlying reviews table.

This operation is associated with the Prisma model that stores product review records, conceptually represented by the `shopping_mall_reviews` table. That table typically includes fields for the review's unique identifier, the product identifier, the author (customer) identifier, the numeric rating value, textual content fields like title and body, and additional metadata for visibility or moderation. When this endpoint is called, the service loads the target review using the `reviewId` and verifies that its `product_id` (or corresponding foreign key) matches the `productId` supplied in the path, ensuring that clients cannot accidentally or maliciously update a review linked to a different product.

The request body uses the `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate` DTO, which encapsulates only mutable aspects of a review. While the exact field set is defined by the DTO schema, typical examples include updated rating score within the allowed rating scale, modifications to the textual content within configured length constraints, and flags reflecting whether a review is edited, hidden by the author, or subject to moderation. Validation logic ensures that values respect business rules such as minimum and maximum rating, required content for certain states, and any locale-specific restrictions on content.

From a security and authorization perspective, this operation should be restricted to authenticated actors. Ordinary customers may only update reviews they authored themselves, while administrative users may have extended permissions to adjust moderation-related fields. These checks are implemented in provider/service logic based on the authenticated user context. The API contract itself exposes a single, consistent update interface for all authorized actors.

In terms of error handling, the operation returns an error when the specified review does not exist, when it does not belong to the product identified by `productId`, or when the caller lacks sufficient permissions to perform the requested update. Validation failures on the `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate` payload—such as rating values out of range or text fields exceeding allowed length—are reported with appropriate validation error responses. Related operations in the same review domain include creating a review for a product, retrieving individual reviews, listing all reviews for a product, and deleting a review when necessary.
operations.summary: Update a specific product review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table for a given product.

responseBody.description: The updated product review entity after applying the requested changes, projected from the shopping_mall_reviews table into the primary ShoppingMall review DTO.

operations.name: update

The specific review identified by {reviewId} must exist in shopping_mall_reviews for the given {productId} before it can be updated via this operation.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes an existing product review that is associated with a specific product in the shoppingMall domain. It manipulates data in the Prisma model that corresponds to the `shopping_mall_reviews` table, which stores individual customer-written product review records. By design, the operation addresses a single review identified through a composite path of `/products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}`, clearly expressing that the review is conceptually scoped to a particular product.

The endpoint accepts two path parameters: `productId`, identifying the parent product, and `reviewId`, uniquely identifying the review to be removed. Service logic uses both values to ensure that the review being deleted is indeed related to the specified product, providing an additional layer of safety on top of any database-level foreign key constraints. If the underlying schema uses cascade rules or related aggregates (such as rating summary tables), the deletion logic is responsible for triggering any necessary updates to those related entities, like recalculating average rating scores for the product.

This delete operation does not accept a request body and does not return a detailed representation of the deleted review. Instead, it focuses on side effects at the data layer—removing the review record from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and updating any dependent aggregates or caches as defined by business rules. The deletion is typically restricted to the author of the review, within allowable time windows, or to administrative actors performing moderation and governance tasks, with these rules enforced by higher-level authorization mechanisms in the service layer.
operations.description:
Delete an existing product review that belongs to a specific product by removing its corresponding record from the shopping_mall_reviews table.

This operation is tied to the Prisma model that stores product reviews, conceptually represented by the `shopping_mall_reviews` table. That table contains one row per review, including identifiers for the associated product and customer, the rating score, textual content, and other metadata. When this endpoint is called, the service locates the review using `reviewId` and verifies that its product relationship matches the `productId` provided in the path. If the review cannot be found, or if it does not belong to the indicated product, the operation fails with an appropriate error response.

The endpoint is implemented as an HTTP DELETE and therefore does not accept a request body. On successful execution, the review record is removed from persistent storage, and the system may update related aggregates such as precomputed product rating statistics to reflect the absence of this review. Clients that maintain their own caches should treat a successful response as confirmation that the review no longer exists and should be removed from any local lists or detail views.

From an authorization perspective, the operation should be accessible only to authenticated actors. Customers are generally allowed to delete their own reviews under business-defined conditions, such as within specific time windows after creation, while administrative users can remove reviews that violate content policies or legal requirements. These rules are enforced by application-level access control logic wrapping this operation. Error cases include attempts to delete non-existent reviews, mismatched product identifiers, and operations initiated by callers without sufficient permissions.

The review identified by {reviewId} must first be created in shopping_mall_reviews for the specified {productId} before this delete operation can remove it.

operations.specification:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of customer product reviews associated with a specific SKU, operating on the shopping_mall_reviews table with SKU scoping.

This PATCH /skus/{skuId}/reviews operation provides a SKU-level view over the canonical review records stored in shopping_mall_reviews. It supports complex search, filtering, and sorting based on rating, visibility_status, moderation_state, verified_purchase, incentivized, helpfulness_score, and temporal fields such as created_at and updated_at. The request body carries structured search criteria and pagination options in the IShoppingMallReview.IRequest DTO, while the response returns a page of summary review projections as IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary.

The operation requires a valid skuId path parameter that must map to an existing shopping_mall_skus.id. The search logic must additionally ensure that only reviews whose shopping_mall_sku_id equals the provided skuId are considered, or, depending on requirements, that product-level reviews (with null SKU) can optionally be included when they share the same product as the SKU.

This endpoint is intended for customer- and storefront-facing read scenarios, not for moderation tooling. It must therefore only return reviews whose visibility_status and moderation_state represent user-visible content, for example visible and approved. Reviews with pending_moderation, hidden, or removed states must be excluded from normal responses unless extended in an admin-only variant handled elsewhere in the system.

Pagination and sorting should be implemented using the plainIndexes defined on shopping_mall_reviews, especially the (shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_id, visibility_status) and (shopping_mall_customer_id, created_at) indexes, to ensure efficient access patterns when filtering by SKU and ordering by recency or helpfulness_score. The endpoint must not expose or rely on internal GIN-backed full-text columns beyond what the DTO design allows.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filtered list of reviews for a specific SKU as stored in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

This operation focuses on customer-written product reviews and ratings that are linked to a particular SKU through the shopping_mall_sku_id foreign key. The underlying table stores a rating integer, optional title and body text, visibility_status, moderation_state, verified_purchase and incentivized flags, helpfulness_score, and timestamps such as created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The endpoint must use these fields to apply business rules: it should only surface reviews whose visibility_status represents user-visible content and whose deleted_at is null so that soft-deleted records are excluded from normal storefront views.

Security-wise, this is a read-only endpoint that can be exposed publicly for browsing reviews on product detail pages. However, it should still obey moderation decisions reflected in moderation_state, hiding flagged or removed content from general users. Any actor-specific differences in what is visible (for example, admins seeing hidden content) must be handled by separate admin endpoints with different authorizationActors configuration, not by this public SKU-level listing.

In terms of database relationships, each returned review row from shopping_mall_reviews is connected to shopping_mall_customers via shopping_mall_customer_id, to shopping_mall_products via shopping_mall_product_id, optionally to shopping_mall_skus via shopping_mall_sku_id, and, when present, to shopping_mall_order_items via shopping_mall_order_item_id. The implementation may use these relations to enforce verified_purchase semantics or to compute derived fields in the IShoppingMallReview.ISummary projection, without exposing raw foreign key identifiers unnecessarily. The request payload IShoppingMallReview.IRequest must support pagination, sort order (for example by created_at or helpfulness_score), rating filters, and potentially flags such as verified_purchase-only.

This endpoint is closely related to other review operations such as creating a review for a SKU and listing reviews at product level without SKU scoping. However, those are distinct operations with their own paths and DTOs. Error handling should cover invalid skuId values (no such SKU), attempts to sort or filter on unsupported fields, and request bodies that fail validation. In all cases, the response format remains a paginated list wrapper using IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary, possibly with empty data arrays when no matching reviews are found.
operations.summary: Search and list reviews from shopping_mall_reviews scoped to a specific SKU.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target SKU whose reviews are being listed.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summaries associated with the specified SKU and matching the given search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A SKU record must exist in shopping_mall_skus before reviews can be listed for it. This operation creates a SKU under a product and yields the skuId used by the SKU‑scoped review listing endpoint.

operations.specification:
Create a new customer-written review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table for a specific SKU, tied to an order item eligibility record.

This POST /skus/{skuId}/reviews operation accepts review creation data in the IShoppingMallReview.ICreate DTO and persists a new row in shopping_mall_reviews. It operates in conjunction with shopping_mall_review_eligibilities and shopping_mall_skus to ensure that only customers who have actually purchased the corresponding SKU (or product) and whose eligibility status is valid can create a new review. The skuId path parameter must map to shopping_mall_skus.id and is used, together with information in the request body, to populate the shopping_mall_sku_id and shopping_mall_product_id foreign keys on the review.

The creation logic must respect the unique constraints on shopping_mall_reviews, in particular the composite unique index on (shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_id) and the unique index on shopping_mall_order_item_id. These constraints enforce business rules such as at most one review per customer per product/SKU combination and at most one review per order item. If an attempt is made to create a second review that would violate these uniqueness guarantees, the operation must fail with an appropriate error rather than silently overwriting existing content.

This endpoint is reserved for authenticated end-customer actors and must not be used by sellers or admins to inject or edit customer reviews. On success it returns the fully-populated review entity using the IShoppingMallReview DTO, including rating, title, body, visibility_status (typically initialized to a default like visible or pending_moderation based on policy), moderation_state, verified_purchase and incentivized flags derived from review eligibility and program participation, helpfulness_score initialized to zero, and created_at/updated_at timestamps. The deleted_at field remains null at creation.

The POST operation depends conceptually on prior business flows that generate shopping_mall_review_eligibilities records from delivered order items. Implementations should validate that the referenced eligibility (if any) is in a suitable status such as eligible, update it to used, and back-link the created review via shopping_mall_review_id. Error handling must cover cases such as invalid skuId, ineligible customer, expired eligibility, or request payloads that fail validation constraints on rating scale, title/body length, and required fields enforced by the IShoppingMallReview.ICreate schema.
operations.description:
Create a new review row in shopping_mall_reviews for a given SKU based on a customer’s purchase and review eligibility.

This operation enables a customer to submit a rating and optional textual feedback for a specific SKU, with the SKU context supplied by the skuId path parameter. The shopping_mall_reviews table stores rating as a required integer on a predefined scale, optional title and body fields for the content, visibility_status and moderation_state strings to represent whether the review is visible, pending, or removed, and boolean flags verified_purchase and incentivized that encode whether the review is backed by a completed order and whether any incentive was involved. At creation time, the application must initialize these fields according to business policy and ensure that created_at and updated_at timestamps reflect the submission time while deleted_at remains null.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint should be limited to authenticated customer actors who are the rightful owners of the relevant order item and review eligibility in shopping_mall_review_eligibilities. The implementation must validate that the currently authenticated customer matches shopping_mall_customer_id in the eligibility, that the eligibility’s status is eligible, and that any eligible_from/eligible_until window is respected. The skuId path parameter must reference a SKU whose product and variant information align with the eligibility’s product/SKU references, helping to prevent cross-SKU or cross-product review misuse.

Relationally, the new review links shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_skus, and optionally shopping_mall_order_items via their respective foreign keys. The presence of a unique index on (shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_id) means that the service must handle uniqueness violations gracefully, returning a clear error when a duplicate review is attempted rather than creating multiple rows for the same combination. Additionally, when a review is successfully created, the corresponding shopping_mall_review_eligibilities record should be updated with its shopping_mall_review_id to mark the eligibility as consumed. This endpoint complements listing operations that read from shopping_mall_reviews but does not itself expose moderation workflows, which are implemented through separate admin-focused APIs.
operations.summary: Create a new SKU-scoped review record in shopping_mall_reviews for an eligible customer.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the SKU that is being reviewed.

operations.name: create

Customer reviews are only allowed for purchased items. Creating an order establishes the purchase context and corresponding order items required for review eligibility, so that the SKU being reviewed is actually part of a completed order.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single product review associated with a specific SKU in the shoppingMall platform. It is primarily associated with the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma table, which stores customer-written product reviews and ratings, while also indirectly depending on `shopping_mall_skus` for the SKU identifier that scopes which product variant the review belongs to.

The endpoint `GET /skus/{skuId}/reviews/{reviewId}` is designed as a detail retrieval operation that returns full review information for display in product detail pages, order history views, and moderation tools. The `skuId` path parameter identifies the concrete SKU variant, and the `reviewId` path parameter identifies the specific review record in `shopping_mall_reviews`. The response body uses the `IShoppingMallReview` DTO, which represents the detailed review entity including rating score, textual content, creation timestamps, and linkage to the underlying SKU and customer where appropriate.

This operation is read-only and does not modify any database state. It is suitable for use by public clients, authenticated customers, or internal tools, depending on how authorization is configured at the service level. The operation does not require a request body, and it strictly retrieves the existing review if it exists and is visible according to business rules such as moderation status and visibility flags stored in `shopping_mall_reviews` and related tables.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single detailed review for a specific SKU using its review identifier.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma table, which is described as storing customer-written product reviews and ratings. Each row in this table represents a single review created by a customer about a product or SKU, and typically includes fields such as rating score, textual content, created/updated timestamps, visibility or moderation status, and foreign keys linking to the SKU and customer entities. The `skuId` path parameter allows consumers to scope the lookup to a specific SKU record from `shopping_mall_skus`, while the `reviewId` parameter identifies the concrete review row in `shopping_mall_reviews` that should be returned in the response.

From a security and authorization perspective, this GET operation is designed to be consumable by general clients and does not inherently require a specific authenticated actor at the interface contract level. Actual access control, such as hiding reviews that are under moderation, blocked for policy violations, or restricted by risk rules, should be implemented in the business logic layer based on flags stored in `shopping_mall_reviews`, as well as related configuration tables like `shopping_mall_business_policies` and `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions`. The API must ensure that only reviews that are allowed to be displayed under current policy rules are returned to the caller.

In terms of database relationships, the implementation will typically join or otherwise use foreign keys from `shopping_mall_reviews` to `shopping_mall_skus`, and possibly to `shopping_mall_products` and customer entities, to ensure that the requested `reviewId` actually belongs to the specified `skuId`. This prevents callers from accessing reviews outside of the intended SKU context. If no matching review for the given `skuId` and `reviewId` pair is found, the operation should respond with an appropriate not-found error.

This operation is commonly used together with list or search endpoints such as `PATCH /skus/{skuId}/reviews` that return multiple reviews, and with update or moderation endpoints like `PUT /skus/{skuId}/reviews/{reviewId}` for editing existing reviews. Clients will first discover a review identifier via list or search APIs and then call this detail endpoint to fetch the full review record for display or further processing.

responseBody.description: Detailed review information for the specified SKU and review identifier, as stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and mapped to the `IShoppingMallReview` DTO.

A review must be created for the specified SKU before it can be retrieved with this detail endpoint; this POST creates shopping_mall_reviews rows that provide the reviewId used here.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing product review associated with a specific SKU in the shoppingMall platform. It is directly associated with the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma table, which stores customer-written product reviews and ratings, and indirectly linked to `shopping_mall_skus` to ensure that the review being updated belongs to the specified SKU variant.

The endpoint `PUT /skus/{skuId}/reviews/{reviewId}` is a full-update operation that accepts an `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate` request body representing the fields of the review that can be modified, such as rating score, textual content, and potentially visibility or metadata fields depending on the business rules. The implementation must validate that the `reviewId` exists in `shopping_mall_reviews`, that it is associated with the given `skuId` from `shopping_mall_skus`, and that the actor performing the update (typically the original customer author or an authorized admin/moderator) is allowed to modify this review according to policy definitions, moderation workflows, and risk rules.

On success, the operation persists the changes to the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and returns the updated review as `IShoppingMallReview`. It does not create new records; instead, it modifies the existing one. The operation may also trigger secondary effects such as recalculating aggregates in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` or `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`, or creating history entries in `shopping_mall_review_versions` or moderation-related tables, but those side effects are internal to the service and not exposed directly by this API contract.
operations.description:
Update an existing review for a specific SKU in the shoppingMall marketplace.

This operation writes to the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma table, which contains customer-written product reviews and ratings, and is the authoritative source for review content and scores. The `skuId` path parameter identifies the SKU from `shopping_mall_skus` that the review is associated with, and the `reviewId` parameter identifies the specific review row within `shopping_mall_reviews` that should be updated. The request body uses the `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate` DTO to convey the updatable fields, such as rating, review text, and other editable attributes defined in the domain model.

From a security perspective, this PUT operation should typically be restricted to authenticated actors, such as the customer who originally authored the review or administrators and moderators with elevated permissions. In this specification, the `authorizationActors` field is set to `["customer"]` to reflect that primary use case, while still allowing the implementation to layer on additional role checks for sellers or admins when they are performing moderation or governance tasks. The provider logic must enforce stricter ownership checks and role-based rules based on `shopping_mall_business_policies`, such as restricting how long after creation a review can be edited or what types of changes are allowed.

In terms of relationships and business logic, the implementation must verify that the specified `reviewId` actually belongs to the given `skuId` to avoid cross-SKU updates. After successfully updating the review, the service may recompute rating aggregates stored in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` tables so that product and SKU rating displays remain consistent. It may also append a new record to `shopping_mall_review_versions` to preserve historical content for auditing and compliance purposes, and potentially create or update entries in `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` if the update is part of a moderation workflow.

This operation is commonly used in conjunction with the detail retrieval endpoint `GET /skus/{skuId}/reviews/{reviewId}` and list/search endpoints for reviews, allowing clients to display a review, present an editing UI (when allowed), submit updates using this PUT endpoint, and then refresh the display using the GET endpoint to show the latest persisted state.
operations.summary: Update a shoppingMall review record for a specific SKU in shopping_mall_reviews

responseBody.description: The updated review record after applying changes to the `shopping_mall_reviews` table, mapped to the `IShoppingMallReview` DTO.

operations.name: update
