The PUT operation updates an existing review; a review for the given SKU must first be created via this POST so that a reviewId exists to update.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes an existing product review associated with a specific SKU in the shoppingMall domain. It targets the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table, which stores customer-written product reviews and ratings, and is scoped by the SKU identifier and the individual review identifier.

The endpoint is designed for administrative moderation and governance workflows where an administrator needs to remove review content that violates platform policies, such as abusive language, fraud, spam, or legal issues. The handler will validate that the referenced review exists, that it is associated with the given SKU, and that the caller has appropriate administrative permissions before performing the deletion.

This is a hard delete operation at the API level: once invoked, the underlying review record in shopping_mall_reviews is removed from persistent storage along with any dependent subsidiary records that logically depend on it, such as moderation actions, helpful votes, and reports, according to referential integrity rules implemented in the service layer or database schema. Related snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_review_versions may be preserved independently for audit purposes depending on business rules, but they are not directly manipulated by this endpoint.
operations.description:
Delete a specific review record that belongs to a particular SKU in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation works against the shopping_mall_reviews table, which represents customer-written product reviews and rating data for products and SKUs. Each review is uniquely identified in the API by a reviewId path parameter, while the skuId path parameter provides additional scoping to ensure that the review being removed is indeed associated with the specified SKU. The implementation must validate the relationship between the review and the SKU using the underlying Prisma schema relations before proceeding with deletion.

From a security and governance perspective, this endpoint is restricted to admin actors. The authorization layer must ensure that only authenticated administrative users can invoke this operation, as deleting review content can affect the integrity of marketplace information and may have compliance implications. The service logic should also ensure that the deletion is consistent with higher-level business policies defined in tables such as shopping_mall_business_policies and shopping_mall_policy_versions when those are applied to review moderation.

When the delete is executed, the underlying record in shopping_mall_reviews is removed from the primary review dataset. Implementation may also cascade deletions or apply clean-up to subsidiary tables like shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes, shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions, and shopping_mall_review_reports depending on foreign key constraints and business requirements. Snapshot or audit-oriented tables such as shopping_mall_review_versions, shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs, or other compliance-related entities are typically preserved for traceability and are not directly affected by this API call.

Clients using this endpoint should treat the operation as irreversible: once a review has been deleted through this interface, it should no longer appear in any customer-facing listings, rating aggregates, or seller analytics. If the system maintains precomputed aggregates such as shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates or shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates, the service implementation must trigger appropriate recalculation routines so that average ratings, counts, and other statistics remain consistent after the review removal.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a specific review from shopping_mall_reviews for a given SKU

parameters.name: skuId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the SKU whose associated review is being deleted. This identifier scopes the reviewId to a specific SKU so that the system can confirm the review belongs to the correct SKU context before deletion.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table that should be permanently removed from the system.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A SKU row in shopping_mall_skus must exist before an admin can delete a review tied to skuId. Creating a SKU under a product via this endpoint yields the skuId consumed by the delete operation.

A SKU‑scoped review in shopping_mall_reviews must exist before it can be deleted by skuId and reviewId. This endpoint creates such a review and returns the reviewId referenced by the admin delete operation.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of product reviews written by a specific customer in the shoppingMall platform. It is primarily built on top of the shopping_mall_reviews table, which stores customer-written ratings and textual feedback for products and SKUs, and it constrains the query by the customer identifier provided in the path.

The endpoint supports complex search and pagination requirements through a request body DTO that captures filtering, sorting, and paging options. Typical filters include rating ranges, review creation date windows, review status (e.g., visible, pending moderation, hidden), product or SKU association, and keyword search within the review text. These capabilities are expressed via the IShoppingMallReview.IRequest schema, which is tailored to the underlying Prisma model fields and business requirements around reviews.

The response returns a paginated collection of review summary objects using the IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary type. Each summary record focuses on fields needed for list displays, such as rating score, short text snippet, creation timestamp, and basic product/SKU linkage, rather than the full detailed review object. The pagination wrapper includes metadata like current page, page size, and total count, enabling efficient rendering of review history for the given customer in web or mobile clients.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of product reviews authored by a specific customer, with advanced filtering and sorting options.

This operation interacts primarily with the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma model, which represents customer-written reviews and ratings for products and SKUs. The path parameter customerId identifies the customer whose reviews should be listed, and the service implementation will join this identifier to the appropriate foreign key in the reviews table (for example, a customer or account reference field) to ensure only reviews authored by that customer are returned.

The request body is defined by the IShoppingMallReview.IRequest schema and provides rich search semantics. Clients can filter reviews by rating value, creation date range, visibility or moderation status, associated product or SKU identifiers, and free-text search in the review title or body where supported by the schema. The DTO also carries pagination parameters such as page number and page size, as well as sorting instructions (for example, newest first, oldest first, highest rating, or lowest rating) that are translated into appropriate database queries when interacting with shopping_mall_reviews and related tables like shopping_mall_products or shopping_mall_skus.

The response uses the IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary type to return a page of summary records optimized for list views. Each summary typically includes core review metadata (such as rating, headline, truncation of the body text, and timestamps) together with enough product or SKU information to render a meaningful list to the customer. The pagination envelope exposes total counts and navigation hints so that clients can implement infinite scrolling or traditional paged navigation.

From a security standpoint, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated customers accessing their own reviews. The authorization layer represented by the "customer" actor ensures that the caller is a valid customer account. The service implementation must additionally enforce ownership checks so that a customer can only retrieve reviews they have authored, even if they attempt to specify a different customerId in the path. The endpoint does not expose internal moderation-only fields or other sensitive attributes; those remain available only through separate admin-facing APIs.

This operation is commonly used in "My Reviews" or account history pages where customers review and manage the feedback they have left across the marketplace. It may be combined with other endpoints for editing, hiding, or reporting reviews depending on the overall feature set defined elsewhere in the API surface.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping_mall_reviews authored by a specific customer

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer whose authored reviews should be retrieved from the shopping_mall_reviews table.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering options, and pagination parameters used to retrieve the customer’s reviews.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary records authored by the specified customer, including pagination metadata for client-side navigation.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Customer-scoped business workflows assume the customer identified by customerId already exists and participates in order-related flows. Creating a cancellation request for that customer implies a valid customer row and associated orders in the domain, ensuring that authored reviews for this customer can be meaningfully queried.

To list reviews authored by a customer, at least one review must have been created. This endpoint creates a new review row in shopping_mall_reviews for an authenticated customer, providing review data that will later appear in the paginated listing for the same customerId.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new product review authored by a specific customer, and is conceptually associated with the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model as the primary persistence target, while also depending on related catalog entities such as products and SKUs that the review ultimately references. The endpoint is scoped by a `customerId` path parameter, which represents the unique identifier of the customer authoring the review; the request body carries the structured payload describing rating, textual content, and target product or SKU, modeled by the DTO type `IShoppingMallReview.ICreate`.

From a business perspective, this operation is invoked after a customer has purchased an item and becomes eligible to submit a review according to the review eligibility rules that are represented in tables like `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` and potentially validated against order and fulfillment records. The handler must verify that the the authenticated caller corresponds to the `customerId` in the path, that the customer is allowed to review the specified product or SKU (e.g., has a completed order), and that the review satisfies platform rules regarding content, rating scale, and duplication (such as one review per order item or per product depending on policy).

Upon success, the system persists the new review in `shopping_mall_reviews`, may also create related rows such as initial entries in `shopping_mall_review_versions` for audit history, and triggers asynchronous processes that update rating aggregates in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`. The newly created review object is returned as a detailed DTO `IShoppingMallReview`, enabling the client to immediately display the customer's own review including generated identifiers, timestamps, and moderation status flags where appropriate.
operations.description:
Create a new review for a product or SKU authored by the specified customer.

This operation allows an authenticated customer to submit a product review associated with their own account, referenced by the `customerId` path parameter. The server must treat `customerId` as the unique identifier of the customer author in the underlying `shopping_mall_reviews` table, ensuring that the created row’s customer reference matches the path parameter and the authenticated principal. The request body uses the `IShoppingMallReview.ICreate` structure to provide the rating score, textual content, and information about which product or SKU is being reviewed, along with any optional metadata such as title or media references as defined in the DTO.

Before inserting a new row into `shopping_mall_reviews`, the implementation should enforce business rules derived from the review requirements. These include validating that the referenced product or SKU exists in the catalog, that the customer has actually purchased or otherwise legitimately interacted with that item, and that a review eligibility record in `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` indicates the customer is allowed to submit a review at this time. The service must also enforce rating scale constraints, content length limits, and any prohibited content rules specified at the business-policy level, potentially linked to `shopping_mall_business_policies` or policy versions, rejecting requests that violate these constraints with appropriate error responses.

From a security and authorization standpoint, only authenticated customers should be able to call this endpoint, and they must only create reviews on their own behalf; the path `customerId` must match the authenticated customer’s identifier. The endpoint does not allow sellers, admins, or guest users to create customer reviews through this channel. Attempts to forge another customer’s `customerId` should be rejected with an authorization error.

On successful creation, a new row is persisted into `shopping_mall_reviews` and may be accompanied by initial versioning in `shopping_mall_review_versions` to support future content edits and audit history. The system may also schedule or perform synchronous updates to aggregate rating tables such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`, ensuring that list and detail views reflect the latest customer feedback. The response returns a fully populated `IShoppingMallReview` instance, which includes identifiers, timestamps, rating values, and any moderation or publication-state flags so that the client can immediately display the review or indicate that it is pending moderation. Related operations include retrieving customer reviews for display and administrative moderation endpoints that act on the same underlying review records.
operations.summary: Create a new review row in shopping_mall_reviews for the specified customer.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer who is authoring the review. This identifier is used to set the customer reference in shopping_mall_reviews and must match the authenticated customer.

requestBody.description: Payload containing rating, textual content, and target product or SKU information for creating a new review associated with the given customer.

responseBody.description: Detailed representation of the newly created review, including identifiers, timestamps, rating values, and any moderation-related flags.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: A confirmed order in shopping_mall_orders is required for a customer to have actually purchased items, which is the foundation for review eligibility and verified_purchase semantics before creating a review for that customer.

Creating a review tied directly to a specific shopping_mall_order_items row ensures the review can later be associated with verified purchase and eligibility logic; this POST creates such an order-item-scoped review that the customer-level review flow can rely on.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the detailed representation of a single review authored by a specific customer, focusing on the review stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model and its related entities. The endpoint is scoped by two path parameters: `customerId`, which denotes the customer who owns the review, and `reviewId`, which uniquely identifies the review row to be fetched. Together, these parameters ensure that the caller accesses a review in the context of its author, which can be used for ownership checks and user-facing pages such as "My Reviews".

The operation reads from `shopping_mall_reviews` to obtain core review fields such as rating, textual content, creation and update timestamps, and publication or moderation status. It may also join or separately load related data including historical versions from `shopping_mall_review_versions`, helpful vote information from `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`, and report or moderation data from `shopping_mall_review_reports` and `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions`, depending on what the `IShoppingMallReview` DTO is designed to include for customer-facing views.

Unlike administrative moderation endpoints, this customer-scoped retrieval is intended primarily for the review’s author or potentially for general display when showing a customer’s profile and their reviews. Business rules typically require that private moderation notes, internal flags, or sensitive identifiers not be exposed to the customer. The operation therefore must carefully shape the response according to what `IShoppingMallReview` permits, exposing only customer-visible fields while still providing enough detail for the customer to view or manage their own review, such as editing in a separate update endpoint or understanding its current visibility status on product pages.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single review authored by a specific customer using the customer and review identifiers.

This operation returns a detailed view of a single review row from `shopping_mall_reviews`, identified by the `reviewId` path parameter and scoped under a `customerId` representing the review’s author. The handler must ensure that the returned review actually belongs to the specified customer, which protects against accidentally exposing reviews across accounts when using composite keys or shared identifiers. If the review is not associated with the given `customerId`, the operation should return a not-found or authorization error rather than leaking another customer’s data.

The response is modeled as `IShoppingMallReview`, capturing the rating, textual content, timestamps, and any other customer-visible metadata such as whether the review is currently published, pending moderation, hidden, or removed according to platform policies. Internally, the implementation may consult associated tables like `shopping_mall_review_versions` to determine the current active content, `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` to include helpful vote counts, and potentially `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` when enriching the response with related rating context. However, sensitive moderation or internal governance details from tables like `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` should be filtered out or omitted from this customer-facing DTO as required by the business rules.

From an authorization perspective, this endpoint is primarily intended for authenticated customers viewing their own reviews via account history or profile pages. The platform may also decide to allow public access if the review is publicly visible, but the default design here uses `authorizationActor` of `customer` to emphasize that customer identity and ownership are significant for this view. The operation is closely related to list endpoints such as a paginated index of all reviews for a given customer, and to write endpoints for creating or updating reviews, all of which operate on the same `shopping_mall_reviews` data while observing review eligibility and moderation requirements.
operations.summary: Get a detailed review row from shopping_mall_reviews for a specific customer by reviewId.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer who owns the review, used to scope the lookup in shopping_mall_reviews and enforce ownership checks.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to retrieve from shopping_mall_reviews.

responseBody.description: Detailed representation of the requested review record associated with the specified customer.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: The detailed review referenced by reviewId must already exist in shopping_mall_reviews for the specified customer before it can be retrieved; this POST creates a review row that the GET operation can then look up by its identifier.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing product review record associated with a specific customer in the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma table. It is designed for the shopping mall platform where registered customers can modify their previously submitted reviews, such as adjusting rating scores, editing review text, or toggling visibility-related flags that are permitted by business rules.

The endpoint is scoped by both `customerId` and `reviewId`, ensuring that the update always occurs in the context of a particular customer’s review. Business logic in the implementation must verify that the `reviewId` belongs to the specified `customerId` and that the current actor has permission to perform this change. The request body follows the `IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate` DTO, which contains only fields that are allowed to be modified after initial creation (for example, rating value, title, body text, and certain non-system status flags, depending on the exact Prisma schema definition).

The operation returns the fully updated `IShoppingMallReview` representation, reflecting all persisted changes. It should integrate with related entities such as products or SKUs only indirectly (through existing foreign keys), and must also coordinate with any aggregation tables like rating aggregates, which may be recalculated or updated asynchronously. Validation must consider constraints defined on the `shopping_mall_reviews` model such as rating bounds, content length, and any flags controlling moderation state or editability windows.
operations.description:
Update a specific product review written by a customer, using the underlying `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model as the source of truth.

This operation allows a customer (or an authorized administrative actor, depending on business rules) to modify an existing review that is already stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table. The path parameters identify both the customer and the review, and the server-side logic must confirm ownership or proper authorization before applying updates. Typical editable fields include the rating score, review title, and review body text. The exact editable fields and validation rules are derived from the comments and constraints defined on the `shopping_mall_reviews` model, such as minimum and maximum rating values and content length limits.

From a security and authorization standpoint, this operation generally requires an authenticated user context. When the actor is a customer, the implementation must ensure that the `customerId` in the path corresponds to the authenticated account and that the targeted review is indeed authored by that customer. When invoked by privileged actors like admins or moderators (if allowed by the business requirements), additional checks around moderation policies and edit tracking should be applied, potentially recording audit information in separate system-managed tables.

In terms of database relations, the review record is typically linked to a product or SKU via foreign keys in `shopping_mall_reviews`. While those relations are not directly modified by this endpoint, updates to fields like rating may trigger recalculation of aggregates in tables such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` or `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`. These recalculations may be done synchronously or via background jobs, but in all cases the updated review data returned in the response must reflect the new state stored in `shopping_mall_reviews`.

Related operations include the creation of reviews (using a POST endpoint on a customer- or order-scoped path) and deletion of reviews (using the DELETE operation on the same path). Clients typically call this update operation from a “edit my review” UI, where the current review content is first fetched, then modified, and finally submitted here to persist the new values.
operations.summary: Update a specific customer review record in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer who owns the review being updated. This value is used to scope the review to a specific customer account and must match the authenticated actor when invoked by a customer.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review record in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table that will be updated.

requestBody.description: Payload containing fields to update on the target review, following the editable properties defined for the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model.

responseBody.description: The updated review entity as stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table after applying the requested changes.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: The review record in shopping_mall_reviews identified by {reviewId} must exist before it can be updated. This POST operation creates a new review for the specified customer, producing the reviewId later used by the update endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a specific product review record associated with a customer from the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma table. It is intended for scenarios where a review must be removed, either by the owning customer or by authorized administrative actors according to the platform’s review and moderation policies.

The endpoint is parameterized with both `customerId` and `reviewId`, ensuring that the deletion is always executed within the context of a particular customer’s review. The business logic must verify that the specified review belongs to the given customer and that the caller has sufficient permission to remove it. Because this operation removes the record, any dependent aggregates or denormalized statistics (such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` or `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`) must be updated accordingly to reflect the absence of the deleted review.

The operation does not accept a request body, as all necessary identification information is provided by the path parameters. A successful deletion results in an empty response body, while appropriate error responses should be returned if the review does not exist, does not belong to the customer, or cannot be deleted due to business rules (for example, legal hold, dispute status, or moderation locks).
operations.description:
Delete a specific product review belonging to a customer from the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model.

This operation targets a single row in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table, identified by the `reviewId` path parameter and scoped to the `customerId` path parameter. Before performing the deletion, the server must validate that the review exists, that it is associated with the given customer, and that the current actor is permitted to remove it. For customer-initiated deletions, this usually means verifying that the authenticated customer matches `customerId`. For administrative actors such as moderators or admins, additional governance rules may apply, including logging the deletion reason in audit-specific tables.

From a security and governance perspective, removing a review may have side effects on other parts of the system. The platform should ensure that any rating aggregates or search index entries that previously incorporated this review are recalculated or adjusted after deletion. In some compliance scenarios, metadata about the deletion may be recorded in snapshot or audit tables instead of preserving the full original content in the primary `shopping_mall_reviews` record.

This operation is typically used together with the review creation and update endpoints to give customers and administrators full lifecycle control over review content. Client applications may call this endpoint from “delete my review” workflows or moderation tools where an admin removes content that violates policies. Errors should clearly distinguish between “not found”, “forbidden”, and “conflict with business rules” cases so that clients can provide accurate feedback to end users.
operations.summary: Delete a specific customer review record from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer who owns the review to be deleted. Used to scope the review to a particular customer account and must match the authenticated actor for customer-initiated deletions.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review record in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table that will be deleted.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: The review in shopping_mall_reviews referenced by {reviewId} must exist before it can be deleted. This POST endpoint creates the customer-scoped review that the delete operation will later remove.

operations.specification:
List all customer product reviews associated with a specific order line item, based on the shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_order_items tables. This GET operation targets the primary reviews table shopping_mall_reviews but identifies the relevant rows via the foreign key shopping_mall_order_item_id, which links each review to a particular order item in shopping_mall_order_items. The endpoint is nested under /orderItems/{orderItemId}/reviews to express that we are retrieving reviews that are scoped to a single order line rather than all reviews for a product.

The operation returns a collection of review entities in a summary form suitable for order-detail pages or post‑purchase review management. Core fields exposed include rating, title, body, visibility_status, moderation_state, verified_purchase, incentivized, helpfulness_score, and timestamps, as defined in shopping_mall_reviews. The identifier orderItemId is the UUID primary key of shopping_mall_order_items.id and is used purely as a filter key; the underlying implementation will query shopping_mall_reviews using the shopping_mall_order_item_id foreign key.

No request body is required because all necessary context is in the path parameter. The response body uses a DTO such as IShoppingMallReview.ISummary or IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary to encapsulate a list of reviews along with any optional pagination metadata if the implementation applies pagination. This operation is read-only and does not modify any data in shopping_mall_reviews or shopping_mall_order_items.
operations.description:
Retrieve all product reviews that have been written for a specific order line item.

This operation exposes customer review information stored in the shopping_mall_reviews table, filtered by the foreign key shopping_mall_order_item_id that links a review back to the line item in shopping_mall_order_items from which eligibility was derived. The underlying schema defines rating as a discrete integer value, optional title and body fields for the textual content, visibility_status for determining whether a review is visible in customer-facing contexts, moderation_state for tracking moderation workflows, and flags such as verified_purchase and incentivized for compliance and transparency. It also includes a helpfulness_score integer and created_at / updated_at / deleted_at timestamps for lifecycle tracking and soft deletion behavior.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is read-only and can be exposed with an appropriate authorization model depending on the UI that calls it. For example, it may be available to authenticated customers viewing their own order history, or to internal tools that display reviews by order item. The authorizationActors array for this specification uses the role "customer" to represent the authenticated customer actor; more granular checks such as whether the customer owns the underlying order or is allowed to see certain visibility_status values should be enforced in business logic on top of the raw shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_order_items data.

The operation is tightly coupled to the shopping_mall_order_items table via the path parameter orderItemId, which corresponds to shopping_mall_order_items.id. The implementation will translate this into a filter on shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_order_item_id. Reviews that are soft‑deleted via deleted_at or are in non‑public visibility_status or moderation_state values may be excluded or included depending on the caller’s privileges. Related operations include creating a review for a given order item using POST /orderItems/{orderItemId}/reviews and broader product‑level review listing endpoints that work directly off shopping_mall_reviews, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_skus. Errors include invalid UUID formats, missing order items, or absence of any reviews, which should result in an empty list rather than an error.
operations.summary: List reviews from shopping_mall_reviews for a specific shopping_mall_order_items row.

parameters.name: orderItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target order item whose associated reviews should be listed. This corresponds to shopping_mall_order_items.id and is used to filter shopping_mall_reviews via shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_order_item_id.

responseBody.description: Collection of review summary objects representing reviews linked to the specified order item, derived from shopping_mall_reviews and suitable for display on an order detail view.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A customer order must be created first because each order item belongs to an order header; without an order, there can be no order items to review.
At least one review row in shopping_mall_reviews must exist for the order item before it can be listed; this POST operation creates those review records bound to the given orderItemId.

operations.specification:
Create a new customer product review associated with a specific order line item, persisting data into the shopping_mall_reviews table while verifying that the referenced order item exists in shopping_mall_order_items. The endpoint is scoped under /orderItems/{orderItemId}/reviews, where orderItemId is the UUID primary key of shopping_mall_order_items.id. The server uses this identifier to populate shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_order_item_id and to derive the associated shopping_mall_product_id and optional shopping_mall_sku_id, ensuring that the review is correctly tied to the purchased catalog entities and enforces verified purchase semantics.

The request body follows the IShoppingMallReview.ICreate DTO, which encapsulates client‑supplied properties such as rating, optional title, and optional body, along with any client‑visible flags that the business rules permit the author to influence. Fields including visibility_status, moderation_state, verified_purchase, incentivized, helpfulness_score, and timestamps are derived or managed by backend logic in accordance with the Prisma schema descriptions. The response body returns the created review as IShoppingMallReview, reflecting the canonical current version stored in shopping_mall_reviews.

This operation is write‑sensitive and must enforce multiple validation rules: the orderItemId must reference an existing, eligible shopping_mall_order_items row; the current customer must be the same as shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_customer_id (derived from the session and order ownership); rating must be within the supported integer scale; and any uniqueness constraints, such as the composite unique index on (shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_id) and the unique constraint on shopping_mall_order_item_id, must be respected to prevent duplicate reviews for the same purchase.
operations.description:
Create a new customer review for a product based on a specific order item.

This operation writes into the shopping_mall_reviews table, which stores customer‑written product reviews and ratings. The table defines rating as an integer on a discrete scale (for example 1–5), optional title and body fields for textual content, visibility_status and moderation_state to drive publication and moderation workflows, booleans verified_purchase and incentivized for compliance requirements, a helpfulness_score integer that is updated by later helpful vote events, and created_at / updated_at / deleted_at timestamps for lifecycle management and soft deletion. Each review row is linked back to shopping_mall_customers via shopping_mall_customer_id, to shopping_mall_products via shopping_mall_product_id, optionally to shopping_mall_skus via shopping_mall_sku_id, and to the originating purchase through shopping_mall_order_item_id referencing shopping_mall_order_items.id.

Security and permissions are critical for this endpoint. Only authenticated customers who own the underlying order item should be allowed to create a review for it, and the system must enforce that a given order item or (customer, product, sku) combination adheres to the uniqueness constraints declared in shopping_mall_reviews: a unique index over (shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_sku_id) and a separate unique index on shopping_mall_order_item_id. The implementation should verify that the targeted order item is in a state that permits reviews according to business rules (for example delivered or completed) and that no existing review already satisfies these uniqueness conditions. The path parameter orderItemId is therefore not repeated inside the IShoppingMallReview.ICreate payload; it is taken exclusively from the URL to avoid duplication.

The operation should also respect business rules for initial visibility_status and moderation_state, such as starting in pending_moderation before being visible, and automatically mark verified_purchase based on the presence of a valid shopping_mall_order_item_id linked to a completed order in shopping_mall_orders. Related endpoints include listing reviews for an order item via GET /orderItems/{orderItemId}/reviews and broader product‑level review retrieval operations. Error handling must cover invalid or non‑existent orderItemId values, attempts to create duplicate reviews that violate unique constraints, rating values outside the allowed range, and forbidden attempts by customers who do not own the underlying purchase.
operations.summary: Create a new shopping_mall_reviews row for a given shopping_mall_order_items row.

parameters.name: orderItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the order item for which the customer is submitting a review. This corresponds to shopping_mall_order_items.id and is used to populate shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_order_item_id and derive related product and SKU links.

requestBody.description: Payload containing rating and optional textual content for the new review, omitting path‑scoped identifiers such as orderItemId that are derived from the URL.

responseBody.description: The newly created review entity as stored in shopping_mall_reviews, including identifiers, ratings, content, visibility and moderation state, and metadata flags.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: The customer must first place an order so that a shopping_mall_orders header and corresponding shopping_mall_order_items line items exist; the review being created references one of these order items.

Creating refund request items establishes additional post-purchase state tied to specific order items, which may be required by business workflows that gate review creation on certain refund or issue-resolution conditions for that line item.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of review version snapshot records from the shopping_mall_review_versions Prisma table for administrative and governance use cases. The underlying model is a snapshot-style table that stores historical versions of customer-written product reviews, including previous rating values, titles, and body texts, along with metadata such as who changed the review and when.

The endpoint is designed as a collection-level search API over all review versions in the marketplace, independent of any specific parent review. Clients can supply complex search criteria in the request body, such as ranges for created/updated timestamps, filters by reviewId, customer account, product or SKU, and moderation status flags. The endpoint returns a paginated list of summary DTOs representing individual review version snapshots, optimized for list browsing in back-office tools and audit consoles.

The response type is modeled as IPageIShoppingMallReviewVersion.ISummary, which uses a standard pagination wrapper around lightweight review version summaries. The request payload follows the IShoppingMallReviewVersion.IRequest pattern used across the service for search/filter operations, and it must not duplicate path parameters because this top-level endpoint has no path parameters. All authorization is restricted to administrative actors, as historical review content often contains sensitive information and is required for compliance, legal hold review, and dispute resolution workflows.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of review version snapshot records from the shopping_mall_review_versions table.

The shopping_mall_review_versions Prisma model is described as a snapshot table that maintains historical versions of customer-written product reviews and ratings. Each row represents a point-in-time version of a review, typically including fields such as the review identifier, the associated customer and product or SKU, the rating score, title, body text, and timestamps that indicate when this particular version became active. Additional columns commonly store moderation-related metadata and possibly references to the actor who performed the edit or moderation action.

This operation is intended primarily for administrative consumers and back-office systems that need to investigate the evolution of review content over time. Typical use cases include fraud and abuse investigations, handling of review-related disputes, and compliance checks where auditors must see exactly what content was visible at specific points in time. Because the endpoint can expose previous versions that are no longer publicly visible, including versions that may violate content policies, access is limited to admin actors through the authorization layer.

The request body uses the IShoppingMallReviewVersion.IRequest DTO to express search parameters. Clients can filter by associated review identifiers, customer or seller accounts, product or SKU identifiers, rating value ranges, time windows (such as "versions modified in the last 30 days"), and moderation states. Sorting and pagination parameters are also provided in the request DTO so that the resulting IPageIShoppingMallReviewVersion.ISummary response can be navigated efficiently. The summary representation is optimized for list displays and may omit large text fields or store them in truncated form, while still including enough context (reviewId, version number, rating, key timestamps) to quickly identify relevant versions.

Security and performance considerations are central to this operation. Only users with admin-level privileges are allowed to access it, and heavy queries should be protected by rate limiting and sensible defaults for page size to avoid accidental full-table scans. Error handling should return clear validation messages when search criteria are malformed, while internal errors should be logged with sufficient context to support auditing on the shopping_mall_review_versions table. Related APIs include the per-review version listing at PATCH /reviews/{reviewId}/versions, which focuses on the history of a single review, and any review moderation endpoints that update the underlying shopping_mall_reviews table and automatically create new version snapshots.
operations.summary: Search and paginate review version snapshots across the shopping_mall_review_versions table for admins.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, sorting, and pagination options for querying review version snapshots.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of review version snapshot summaries matching the specified search criteria.

Creating a customer review ensures that shopping_mall_review_versions entries tied to its review_id may exist for the search filters that use review_id.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of review version snapshot records from the shopping_mall_review_versions Prisma table, scoped to a single parent review identified by its reviewId in the shopping_mall_reviews table. While shopping_mall_review_versions is a global snapshot table, this endpoint narrows its scope to show only the history of one specific review, making it suitable for detail pages in admin consoles or investigation tools.

The endpoint is implemented as a PATCH method on the nested resource path /reviews/{reviewId}/versions. The path parameter reviewId identifies the target review whose historical versions should be returned. The request body uses the IShoppingMallReviewVersion.IRequest DTO to express additional filters such as version creation time ranges, rating value ranges, or moderation states, as well as sorting and pagination directives. The request DTO must not contain the reviewId again; instead, the implementation combines the path parameter and request body filters against the shopping_mall_review_versions table.

The response type is IPageIShoppingMallReviewVersion.ISummary, a paginated container of summary DTOs for each version snapshot of the specified review. Each summary record includes key metadata like the associated reviewId, version sequence number or identifier, rating score, key timestamps, and possibly truncated title/body content, so that administrators can quickly scan the history of changes. This design aligns with the snapshot nature of the underlying Prisma model and supports governance, compliance, and dispute-resolution processes that require a clear audit trail for individual reviews.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of historical versions for a single review from the shopping_mall_review_versions snapshot table, filtered and scoped by the reviewId path parameter.

The shopping_mall_review_versions Prisma model serves as a snapshot repository for all changes made to customer-written reviews stored in the shopping_mall_reviews table. Every time a review is edited, moderated, or otherwise altered, a new snapshot can be recorded in this table with fields that capture both the new review content and the relevant metadata such as rating, title, body text, and timestamps. This allows the platform to reconstruct the full history of any review, which is essential for transparency, dispute resolution, and regulatory compliance.

This operation focuses on the history of one specific review, addressed via the required path parameter reviewId. The parameter represents the primary identifier of the review in the shopping_mall_reviews table and is used to constrain the query over shopping_mall_review_versions. In addition to this path constraint, clients can provide further search criteria in the IShoppingMallReviewVersion.IRequest request body—such as limiting results to versions within a given date range, filtering by rating changes, or sorting versions by creation time in ascending or descending order. The request body MUST NOT attempt to override the reviewId; the implementation derives that constraint purely from the path parameter.

The response is a paginated collection represented by IPageIShoppingMallReviewVersion.ISummary. Each summary entry is designed for list rendering, typically including reviewId, version identifier or sequence, rating, a subset of content fields, and important timestamps (e.g., when the version was created or became effective). Because historical review data may include previously moderated or redacted content, access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors through the authorization layer. Errors such as referencing a non-existent reviewId, malformed filters, or invalid pagination parameters must be reported with clear, structured error responses, and internal issues should be logged with sufficient detail for later analysis on both shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_review_versions data.

This endpoint complements the global review version search at PATCH /reviewVersions, which can search across all reviews, by providing a focused, per-review history view that is commonly used in admin detail pages and investigative workflows.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a specific historical version of a customer-written product review from the shopping_mall_review_versions table, scoped by the parent review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table. It is designed for auditability, moderation workflows, and transparency use cases where clients need to inspect exactly what content was stored at a given version identifier.

The endpoint is modeled as a GET operation on the path "/reviews/{reviewId}/versions/{versionId}". The path parameters represent the parent review identifier (reviewId) and the concrete version identifier (versionId). The underlying Prisma models are shopping_mall_reviews (primary table for current review records) and shopping_mall_review_versions (snapshot table that stores immutable historical versions of review content and metadata). The operation does not accept a request body and returns a single detailed DTO representing the selected review version.

The response type is IShoppingMallReviewVersion, following the DTO naming convention for the snapshot model shopping_mall_review_versions. It is expected to include fields such as the version's unique identifier, associated review identifier, version index, author and rating fields as they were at that time, content text, timestamps, and any moderation-related flags captured on the snapshot record. The operation must enforce that the version belongs to the given parent review, using a composite key constraint such as [review_id, id] or [review_id, version_number] as defined in the Prisma schema.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single historical version of a product review for inspection and audit purposes.

This operation targets the snapshot model shopping_mall_review_versions, which is described in the Prisma schema as a historical versions table for review content used for audit and change tracking. Each record in shopping_mall_review_versions is logically attached to a parent record in shopping_mall_reviews, which itself stores the current, user-visible representation of a product review and rating written by a customer. The snapshot table preserves prior states of the review, including rating score, title, body text, and possibly moderation flags, so that the platform can reconstruct what the review looked like at specific moments in time.

The caller must supply two path parameters: reviewId identifies the parent review in shopping_mall_reviews, and versionId identifies a concrete snapshot entry in shopping_mall_review_versions that belongs to that review. The implementation must validate that the snapshot indeed corresponds to the given review, typically by querying on a composite condition such as review_id = reviewId AND id = versionId, or another composite unique key as specified in the Prisma schema. If no matching snapshot is found, the operation should respond with a not-found error, rather than leaking unrelated review version data.

From a security perspective, this operation is intended primarily for internal dashboards, administrative tools, or potentially for end users viewing their own edit history, depending on business rules defined in the requirements documents. Because review history can expose content that was later moderated or removed, the handler must enforce appropriate authorization checks: for example, only admins may see all versions for all reviews, while a given customer may only see versions for reviews they authored. The authorizationActors is left as ["admin"] to represent an administrative read access pattern; more granular customer-facing endpoints can be added separately if required.

The response body uses the DTO type IShoppingMallReviewVersion, which reflects the schema of shopping_mall_review_versions. This type should include audit-related fields such as created_at timestamps, version index, and content snapshots, but it must not assume additional fields like deleted_at unless they exist explicitly in the Prisma schema. Related operations include the standard review detail retrieval on shopping_mall_reviews (e.g., GET /reviews/{reviewId}) and list-search operations on review versions if defined (e.g., PATCH /reviews/{reviewId}/versions). Together, these endpoints support comprehensive moderation, dispute resolution, and legal audit workflows for review content changes over time.
operations.summary: Get a specific historical review version from shopping_mall_review_versions by reviewId and versionId.
