operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a single helpful vote record associated with a product review. It is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma model, which stores individual helpful-vote actions that customers make on reviews. Each record in that table typically links a specific review to the customer who cast the vote and may include metadata such as when the vote was created.

The API is designed as a DELETE operation on the `/reviewHelpfulVotes/{helpfulVoteId}` path, where `helpfulVoteId` uniquely identifies a helpful vote row in the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table. The endpoint expects the client to already know this identifier, typically obtained from list or detail endpoints related to reviews or helpful votes. When invoked, the backend must validate that the record exists, that it is not under any legal hold or restricted by governance constraints, and that the requesting actor is authorized to remove it (for example, the original customer who cast the vote, or an administrator enforcing moderation policies).

From a business perspective, deleting a helpful vote updates the engagement metrics for the associated review and may trigger recalculation of aggregates stored in `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`-derived counters or in related aggregate tables such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` or `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` if these aggregates incorporate helpful-vote counts. The operation should execute atomically so that the vote is removed and all related counters remain consistent. Any failure in validation or database constraints should result in an appropriate error response, such as 404 when the `helpfulVoteId` does not exist, or 403 when the caller lacks permission to remove the vote.
operations.description:
Delete a specific helpful vote record from the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table by its unique identifier.

This operation targets a single row in the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma model, which represents an individual instance where a customer has marked a review as helpful. Each helpful vote is conceptually tied to a review and a voter account, and removing it will reduce the visible helpful-vote count for that review in customer-facing interfaces.

The request is a DELETE to `/reviewHelpfulVotes/{helpfulVoteId}` and takes the `helpfulVoteId` as a path parameter. The implementation must look up the corresponding `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` record, verify that it exists, and enforce any authorization rules defined in business policies, such as only allowing the customer who originally cast the vote or privileged administrative actors to remove it. If the record cannot be found, the backend should respond with a not-found error.

When the record is successfully removed, the system should also ensure that any derived aggregates or cached counters that depend on helpful-vote counts for the associated review are updated consistently. This may involve recalculating counts or decrementing counters maintained alongside review entities or in dedicated aggregate tables. Error handling must ensure that partial updates do not leave the system in an inconsistent state; if any part of the delete or aggregate-update workflow fails, the whole transaction should be rolled back and an appropriate error response returned.
operations.summary: Remove a review helpful vote from the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table by identifier.

parameters.name: helpfulVoteId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the helpful vote record in the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table that should be removed.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A review helpful vote record must exist before it can be deleted, so a POST to /shoppingMall/customer/reviewHelpfulVotes is required to create the helpful vote identified later by helpfulVoteId.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated list of helpful vote records associated with a specific review from the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma model. The underlying table stores one row per helpful-vote action, linking a review to the customer who voted and capturing timestamps and any relevant metadata. This endpoint is intended for use cases where clients need to inspect or analyze which customers have marked a review as helpful, or to support moderation tools and analytics.

The API is implemented as a PATCH request to `/reviews/{reviewId}/helpfulVotes`. The `reviewId` path parameter identifies the parent review (from the `shopping_mall_reviews` model), and the request body contains search, filter, and pagination criteria in the `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IRequest` DTO. Typical filters might include voter account identifiers, creation-time ranges, or status flags if the schema supports them. The endpoint responds with a paginated collection using `IPageIShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ISummary`, which returns summary representations of helpful-vote records optimized for list views.

From a business perspective, this operation is useful for both customer-facing and administrative contexts. For example, a customer may be able to see whether they themselves have voted a review as helpful, while administrators may retrieve larger lists for moderation, abuse detection, or audit workflows. The implementation must ensure that query filters are correctly applied against the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table, that pagination is efficient, and that only permitted fields are exposed according to the caller's authorization level. It should also handle edge cases such as requesting pages beyond the available range or providing conflicting filter criteria by returning clear, structured error responses.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of helpful-vote records for a specific review from the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table.

This operation accepts a PATCH request to `/reviews/{reviewId}/helpfulVotes`, where the `reviewId` path parameter identifies the parent review whose helpful votes are being queried. The request body uses the `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IRequest` structure to convey search conditions such as voter identifiers, creation timestamp ranges, and sorting and pagination options. This design enables complex queries that go beyond simple URL query parameters, while keeping the HTTP method read-only with respect to server state.

The response is a paginated collection of summary representations of helpful-vote records, encapsulated in `IPageIShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ISummary`. Each summary object is expected to include enough information to identify the helpful vote, understand who cast it, and when, without exposing unnecessary or sensitive details. The pagination envelope provides metadata such as total count, current page, and page size so that clients can build navigation UIs.

Security and authorization considerations depend on the calling actor. In a customer context, the platform may limit the visibility of voter identities or restrict access to only the current customer's own votes. In an administrative context, actors such as moderators or admins may have broader access to all helpful votes for a review for purposes like abuse detection, auditing, or analytics. The implementation should enforce these rules consistently and validate all input criteria from the request body to prevent invalid filters or excessive result sizes.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new helpful vote on an existing product review in the shopping mall platform. It is associated with the Prisma table `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`, which stores individual helpful vote records linked to a specific review and cast by a specific customer or actor.

The endpoint accepts a POST request at `/reviews/{reviewId}/helpfulVotes`, where `reviewId` uniquely identifies the target review. The request body contains the data necessary to register a helpful vote, such as the actor casting the vote and any contextual metadata defined in the `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ICreate` DTO. The operation validates that the referenced review exists in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and that the caller is eligible to vote according to business rules (for example, a customer cannot vote on their own review, and duplicate helpful votes from the same actor for the same review are prevented based on unique constraints in the Prisma model).

On success, the operation persists a new row into `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` and returns the created helpful vote object as `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote`. This allows client applications to immediately reflect the updated helpful state (for instance, updating helpful count indicators) and to maintain consistency with the underlying database representation.
operations.description:
Create a new helpful vote entry for a specific product review identified by `reviewId` in the shopping mall platform.

This operation is tightly coupled with the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma model, which is designed to store each individual helpful vote as a separate row. Columns in this table typically include a reference to the `shopping_mall_reviews` primary key, a reference to the voting actor (such as a customer from `shopping_mall_customers`), timestamps for auditing, and any additional metadata needed for analytics or abuse detection. The `reviewId` path parameter corresponds to the parent review row in `shopping_mall_reviews`, and the request data in `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ICreate` will map directly onto the non-relational fields of `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`.

From a security and permissions perspective, this endpoint is intended for authenticated end users, represented here more specifically as the `customer` actor, since helpful votes on product reviews are cast by customers who have purchased or interacted with the product. The service layer is expected to enforce business rules such as preventing a customer from voting more than once on the same review, preventing authors of a review from voting on their own content, and potentially rate-limiting helpful votes to mitigate abuse. These rules are supported by the schema design of `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`, which may include unique constraints on combinations like `(review_id, customer_id)`.

The request body type `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ICreate` should include only the fields necessary to create a valid helpful vote record, excluding any values derived from the authenticated session (such as customer identity) or from the path parameter (the review reference). These contextual identifiers are taken from the URL and the authentication token and should not be duplicated in the DTO. On success, the response returns an `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote` instance that reflects the newly created row from the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table, including generated identifiers and timestamps, allowing the client to maintain an accurate local representation and to compose this operation with other review-related endpoints such as listing reviews or retrieving review aggregates.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single helpful vote record associated with a specific product review in the shopping mall platform. It is based on the Prisma table `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`, which records each helpful vote as an individual row.

The endpoint uses a GET request at `/reviews/{reviewId}/helpfulVotes/{helpfulVoteId}`. The `reviewId` path parameter identifies the parent review row from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table, while `helpfulVoteId` identifies the specific helpful vote row within `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`. Together, these parameters ensure that the requested helpful vote is retrieved within the correct review context and that the combination aligns with any composite uniqueness constraints defined in the schema (for example, ensuring that a helpful vote belongs to the specified review).

On success, the operation returns the detailed helpful vote representation as `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote`, allowing clients to show information such as when the vote was cast, by which customer (when business rules permit exposing such information), and any additional metadata used for analytics or moderation. This operation can be useful for administrative tooling as well as for customer-facing experiences that need to inspect a particular helpful vote in detail.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific helpful vote for a given product review using both the review identifier and the helpful vote identifier.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma model, which stores detailed information about each helpful vote, including its association to a `shopping_mall_reviews` row, customer identifiers, timestamps, and any contextual fields defined in the schema. The `reviewId` parameter ensures that the returned helpful vote is scoped to the correct parent review, while `helpfulVoteId` selects the exact vote row within the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is modeled as accessible to the `customer` actor, consistent with how helpful votes are created and managed. The implementation may further restrict access depending on business requirements—for example, limiting visibility to the customer who cast the vote, to the review author, or to administrative tools, while protecting privacy. The service layer should also handle scenarios where either the review or the helpful vote does not exist or where they are not related, returning appropriate error responses.

The response body uses the `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote` DTO, which should mirror the fields of the underlying `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` record that are safe and relevant to expose via the API. No request body is required for this GET operation; all necessary identification is provided via the path parameters and validated by the service logic before fetching the record.

operations.specification:
Update an existing helpful vote record for a product review in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table. This operation allows an authenticated customer to change their helpful vote state on a specific review, for example toggling between marking a review as helpful or withdrawing that mark, depending on how the underlying Prisma model represents the vote. The operation is bound to a parent review identified by reviewId and a specific helpful vote identified by helpfulVoteId, ensuring that updates are always scoped to the correct review–vote pair.

The implementation will load the existing record from the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes model using the composite key of the review and helpful vote identifiers. It will then apply the fields provided in the IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IUpdate DTO, such as a boolean flag or related metadata, while enforcing all constraints defined in the Prisma schema (for example, that the associated review exists and the actor performing the update is the same customer who originally created the vote). The operation returns the updated helpful vote entity as an IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote object for immediate client-side consistency.

From a business perspective, this endpoint is typically used when a customer wants to change their mind about whether a review was helpful or when the platform offers richer semantics such as weighting or additional context for a vote. Because helpful votes contribute to product- and review-level aggregates stored in related tables such as shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates or shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates, the service implementation may also trigger recomputation or asynchronous updates of those aggregates after a successful update.
operations.description:
Update an existing helpful vote associated with a specific product review.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma model, which holds individual helpful vote records attached to customer-written reviews stored in the shopping_mall_reviews table. Each helpful vote is conceptually owned by a customer and tied to a single review, and may include fields such as the customer identifier, the review identifier, and one or more flags or timestamps that represent the current state of the vote. When a client calls this API, the backend locates the corresponding helpful vote using the reviewId and helpfulVoteId path parameters, verifies that the record exists, and then applies the update payload defined by the IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IUpdate DTO.

Security and authorization are critical for this operation. Only authenticated customers should be allowed to update their own helpful votes, and the implementation must ensure that a customer cannot modify a helpful vote that was created by a different account. Additionally, the service should validate that the referenced review itself is still active and eligible for helpful voting according to review and moderation policies, which may be configured using other policy-related tables in the schema. Attempts to update a vote for a non-existent review, a deleted or blocked review, or a vote that the caller does not own must result in appropriate error responses such as 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden.

On the data consistency side, the operation must ensure that any business rules described in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes schema comments are respected, such as immutability of certain fields (e.g., creator identity) or restrictions on how frequently a customer can change their vote. After a successful update, the implementation may recompute downstream aggregates used to power features like "most helpful reviews" by updating derived statistics in snapshot or aggregate tables like shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates or shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates. Clients typically use this endpoint together with the helpful vote creation and deletion APIs to provide a seamless UX for toggling helpful status on reviews.
operations.summary: Update a helpful vote record for a review in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table.

operations.specification:
Permanently remove an existing helpful vote record for a product review from the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table. This operation allows an authenticated customer to withdraw their helpful vote from a review, effectively indicating that they no longer want their vote to contribute to helpfulness calculations or visibility algorithms.

The endpoint uses the combination of reviewId and helpfulVoteId path parameters to locate the specific helpful vote within the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes model that is associated with a particular review. Once found, the record is deleted from the database, subject to any constraints or protections defined in the Prisma schema, such as foreign key references to shopping_mall_reviews and customer account tables. The service may also trigger recalculation or asynchronous adjustment of aggregate metrics that rely on helpful vote counts.

From a business logic standpoint, this API is part of the broader review interaction model. It should ensure that only the customer who originally cast the helpful vote can remove it, and that the corresponding review is still in a state where interaction is allowed. Removing a helpful vote must update any relevant aggregates, including counts or weighted scores used in tables like shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates or shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates, so that the UI reflects the current reality of customer sentiment.
operations.description:
Delete an existing helpful vote associated with a specific product review so that it no longer contributes to helpfulness metrics.

This operation acts on the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma model, which maintains individual helpful vote entries for reviews stored in the shopping_mall_reviews table. A helpful vote is typically created when a customer indicates that a review was helpful, and this DELETE endpoint allows that customer to withdraw the vote entirely. The backend identifies the target record using the reviewId and helpfulVoteId path parameters, and then performs a hard delete of that record from the database in accordance with constraints defined by the schema.

From a security perspective, only authenticated customers should be able to remove their own helpful votes. The implementation must verify that the caller is the owner of the helpful vote and that the associated review is still eligible for interaction based on review moderation state and policy configurations. If the helpful vote does not exist, belongs to another account, or is associated with a review that can no longer be interacted with, the service must respond with appropriate error codes such as 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden.

After a successful deletion, the system should ensure that any downstream aggregates based on helpful votes remain accurate. This may involve updating or recomputing aggregate metrics stored in related snapshot or aggregate tables such as shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates and shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates, which are used to power features like sorted review lists and product rating summaries. Clients typically invoke this endpoint as part of a toggle interaction, coupled with the helpful vote creation and update APIs.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered, paginated list of helpful vote records associated with a specific customer in the shoppingMall platform. It is primarily associated with the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma table, which stores individual helpful vote entries, and it also relates to `shopping_mall_reviews` for contextual information about which reviews were voted on. The endpoint is designed as a PATCH on `/shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes` to support complex querying scenarios such as filtering by review, time range, and helpfulness direction while maintaining RESTful semantics for read-only, search-like interactions.

The operation uses the `customerId` path parameter to scope results to a single customer, ensuring that only helpful votes cast by that customer are returned. The request body type `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IRequest` encapsulates search criteria such as pagination, sorting, and optional filters (e.g., by review, by createdAt range). The response type `IPageIShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ISummary` represents a paginated collection of summary view objects for helpful votes, optimized for list displays in customer profile or activity history screens.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to authenticated customers and administrative actors, but in this specification we model the primary self-service use case under the `customer` actor. Backend authorization logic can additionally allow admins via separate mechanisms, while ensuring that a normal customer can only see their own helpful votes. This design keeps the API surface minimal while allowing flexible policy enforcement in service logic.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of helpful vote records created by a specific customer in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table, which records when a customer marks a product review as helpful or not. Each record typically references the customer account, the review that was voted on, and metadata such as the helpfulness flag and timestamps. While the Prisma schema may also describe relations to the `shopping_mall_reviews` and `shopping_mall_customers` tables, this endpoint focuses on exposing an activity history from the perspective of a single customer identified by the `customerId` path parameter.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint should only be accessible to authenticated customer actors. In typical usage, a customer will call this endpoint to view their own voting history; additional administrative tooling can be implemented using separate admin-focused endpoints if necessary. The `authorizationActor` is therefore set to `customer`, with finer-grained ownership checks implemented in the service layer.

The request body of type `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IRequest` is designed to carry search and pagination parameters instead of using numerous query string parameters. It can include page number, page size, sort options (such as newest-first or by review rating), and optional filters like specific review identifiers or date ranges. The use of PATCH for complex search is consistent with the platform's pattern for list and search operations that require structured JSON bodies.

The response body returns a `IPageIShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ISummary` structure, which encapsulates a list of summary representations of helpful votes along with pagination metadata such as total count and page information. Each summary entry is expected to contain core fields of the helpful vote (such as identifiers, helpfulness flag, and timestamps) and may include denormalized snippets of the related review for display convenience, depending on how the DTO is defined elsewhere in the system.

Related operations include the detail retrieval endpoint `GET /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes/{helpfulVoteId}`, which returns a full detailed representation of a single helpful vote record, and any review detail endpoints that allow navigation from a helpful vote to the underlying review content.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information about a single helpful vote record cast by a specific customer in the shoppingMall platform. It is associated with the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma table, where each row represents a customer's indication that a particular review was helpful (or potentially not helpful), and may also traverse relationships to `shopping_mall_reviews` and `shopping_mall_customers` to construct a rich detail view.

The endpoint is exposed as a GET on `/shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes/{helpfulVoteId}`. The `customerId` path parameter scopes access to a particular customer's activity, ensuring the service can enforce that a normal customer only accesses their own helpful vote records, while administrative users may have broader read authority through separate admin endpoints. The `helpfulVoteId` path parameter uniquely identifies the helpful vote record within the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table.

The response type `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote` represents the full detail view of a helpful vote, including all relevant fields defined in the Prisma schema, such as identifiers, foreign keys to the review and customer, helpfulness indicators, timestamps, and any denormalized information necessary for a complete understanding of the vote. No request body is required for this read-only retrieval operation.

Authorization is limited to authenticated `customer` actors in this specification, with the implementation responsible for performing ownership checks so that a customer can only access their own records. Administrative reading patterns can be modeled via dedicated admin endpoints if required. This endpoint is typically used from a customer profile or activity detail screen when the user wants to inspect a specific voting action they previously took.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full detailed representation of a single helpful vote record associated with a given customer.

This operation primarily interacts with the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table in the Prisma schema, which stores individual helpful vote events. Each helpful vote row links a customer to a review they have voted on and includes additional fields such as a helpful flag, creation time, and possibly audit metadata. The combination of `customerId` and `helpfulVoteId` in the path allows the application to verify that the requested helpful vote belongs to the specified customer.

From a security standpoint, the endpoint requires authentication and is exposed to the `customer` actor. Implementation logic should ensure that a standard customer can only access their own records. The use of path parameters rather than query parameters for identifiers ensures clear resource addressing and aligns with RESTful conventions.

The response body type `IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote` is expected to expose all relevant fields associated with the helpful vote, potentially including embedded or related information about the underlying review such as its identifier, rating, and partial content, depending on how the DTO is modeled. This rich representation helps clients present contextual detail screens or debug issues with voting behavior.

This operation is closely related to the list endpoint `PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes`, which returns multiple helpful votes in a paginated fashion. Clients typically use the list endpoint to browse a customer's voting history and then call this detail endpoint for a specific entry when more information about that vote is needed.

The specific helpful vote identified by helpfulVoteId must first be created in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes before this detail endpoint can retrieve it.

operations.specification:
Create a new helpful vote record for a review by a specific customer, operating on the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma table while validating against the shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_customers tables.

This POST /customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes endpoint allows a caller to record whether a given customer has found a particular review helpful or not. It will create a new row in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes with the foreign keys shopping_mall_review_id and shopping_mall_customer_id, and the boolean is_helpful, as well as managed timestamps created_at and updated_at.

The operation must enforce the unique constraint on [shopping_mall_review_id, shopping_mall_customer_id] defined in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes schema so that a customer can only have one active helpfulness vote per review. If a duplicate is attempted, the service should return an appropriate error rather than silently overwriting. It should also ensure that the referenced review exists in shopping_mall_reviews and that the customer specified in the path exists in shopping_mall_customers and matches the authenticated principal.

Business logic should also take into account the visibility_status and moderation_state of the target review in shopping_mall_reviews. For example, votes may be disallowed on reviews that are removed or hidden. After successful creation, downstream processes may update the derived helpfulness_score column on shopping_mall_reviews to keep aggregated metrics in sync, but that aggregation logic is outside the scope of this interface specification.
operations.description:
Create a new helpfulness vote by a customer for a specific review.

This operation creates a record in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table, which, according to its Prisma schema, is the authoritative log for helpful votes on reviews. Each record links a review (shopping_mall_review_id) from shopping_mall_reviews to a customer (shopping_mall_customer_id) from shopping_mall_customers and records whether the vote is helpful or not via the is_helpful boolean column. The schema also defines created_at and updated_at timestamps that the application should manage automatically as part of the persistence layer.

The Prisma schema for shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes declares a unique index on [shopping_mall_review_id, shopping_mall_customer_id], which guarantees that one customer can cast at most one vote per review. This API must respect that constraint by validating that no existing row with the same review and customer exists before inserting a new record. If such a row is present, the service should reject the request with a conflict-style error instead of creating duplicate logical votes.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated customers, represented by the "customer" actor in authorizationActors. The customerId path parameter must represent the same logical customer as the authenticated principal in shopping_mall_customers, so implementation should enforce an ownership check rather than allowing arbitrary customers to be impersonated by supplying a different customerId. The operation should also verify that the referenced review in shopping_mall_reviews exists and, based on its visibility_status and moderation_state columns, is in a state where voting is allowed.

This endpoint works together with any analytical or aggregation processes that update the helpfulness_score column on shopping_mall_reviews. After new votes are created, other internal routines can recompute or incrementally adjust helpfulness_score using the authoritative log in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes. Related operations include updating an existing vote (PUT /customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes/{helpfulVoteId}) when the customer changes their mind, and potential administrative review operations that inspect helpful voting patterns for abuse or fraud signals.

operations.name: create

operations.specification:
Update an existing helpful vote record for a specific customer, operating on the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma table and maintaining referential integrity with shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_customers.

This PUT /customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes/{helpfulVoteId} endpoint allows a caller to modify the is_helpful flag of an existing helpfulness vote previously cast by the customer. The target row is identified by its primary key id in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes (exposed as helpfulVoteId in the path) and is constrained to belong to the customer identified by customerId.

The operation must ensure that the underlying foreign key relationships remain valid: the linked review in shopping_mall_reviews and customer in shopping_mall_customers must exist, and the row must correspond to the same customer as the authenticated principal. It must also enforce business rules related to the review’s moderation_state and visibility_status, disallowing changes to votes on reviews that are no longer eligible for voting. Upon successful update, the updated_at timestamp in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes is refreshed, and downstream aggregation logic may adjust helpfulness_score for the associated review in shopping_mall_reviews based on the new vote value.

The unique index on [shopping_mall_review_id, shopping_mall_customer_id] in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes is not directly modified by this operation, since it updates an existing row rather than creating a new one. However, the implementation should still ensure that updates do not try to reassign the vote to a different review in a way that would violate this constraint. The primary purpose of this endpoint is to let customers toggle or change their helpfulness decision, such as switching from helpful to not helpful or vice versa.
operations.description:
Update an existing helpfulness vote by a customer for a review.

This operation targets a single row of the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table, identified by its primary key id (helpfulVoteId) and scoped to a specific customer via the customerId path parameter. According to the Prisma schema, each helpful vote includes foreign keys to shopping_mall_reviews (shopping_mall_review_id) and shopping_mall_customers (shopping_mall_customer_id), a boolean is_helpful indicating whether the vote is positive or negative, and created_at and updated_at timestamps. The update API primarily allows modification of is_helpful, and the persistence layer updates updated_at accordingly.

The unique index on [shopping_mall_review_id, shopping_mall_customer_id] ensures there is at most one vote per customer per review. Since this endpoint modifies an existing record rather than inserting a new one, the uniqueness constraint remains satisfied as long as the implementation does not rebind the vote to a different review in a conflicting way. Typical business behavior is to keep the review association immutable and only allow the is_helpful flag to change, representing the customer changing their mind about whether the review is helpful.

From the security standpoint, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated customers. The customerId in the path must correspond to the authenticated principal from shopping_mall_customers, and the helpfulVoteId must reference a vote whose shopping_mall_customer_id matches the same customer. This prevents one customer from altering another customer’s helpfulness votes. Additionally, implementations should consider the state of the underlying review in shopping_mall_reviews, such as visibility_status and moderation_state, and may forbid changes to votes on reviews that have been removed or locked by moderation.

This update operation complements the creation endpoint POST /customers/{customerId}/helpfulVotes. Together, they maintain an accurate log of customer helpfulness feedback in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes, which in turn supports derived metrics such as the helpfulness_score column on shopping_mall_reviews that can be used for ranking and surfacing reviews in the catalog UI.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a single helpful vote record associated with a customer from the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma table. It is used when a customer chooses to retract a previously submitted helpful vote on a product review, or when administrative tooling needs to clean up invalid or abusive vote data.

The endpoint identifies the target vote via the {customerId} and {helpfulVoteId} path parameters. The {customerId} parameter corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_customers table, representing the customer who originally cast the helpful vote. The {helpfulVoteId} parameter corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table, uniquely identifying the specific vote entry to delete.

On successful execution, the provider layer must ensure that the vote belongs to the given customer before deletion, to prevent users from removing votes that are not theirs. The implementation should also update any derived aggregates, such as the counts in shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates or shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates, to keep helpful-vote statistics consistent, if those aggregates depend on helpful votes.
operations.description:
Delete a single review helpful vote record associated with a specific customer.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table, which stores individual "helpful" vote records that customers cast on product reviews. Each record links a customer to a review and indicates that the review was considered helpful by that customer. Over time, customers may change their mind or perform cleanup of their voting history, and administrators may need to remove fraudulent or abusive helpful votes. This endpoint supports those workflows by removing the corresponding vote row from the database.

The endpoint requires two identifiers in the path: {customerId}, which references the customer in the shopping_mall_customers table, and {helpfulVoteId}, which references the vote in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table. The service implementation must verify that the vote being deleted is indeed owned by the specified customer. If the vote does not exist, or if it belongs to a different customer, the operation should respond with a not-found or authorization-style error rather than silently doing nothing.

From a security perspective, this operation is restricted to authenticated customers and potentially administrators. A normal customer is only allowed to delete their own helpful votes, while administrators may have broader powers to manage vote data across the platform for moderation or data correction purposes. The authorization layer should rely on the authenticated actor information combined with the customerId path parameter to enforce these rules.

Although the operation focuses on the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table, it may interact with related tables such as shopping_mall_reviews, shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates, and shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates. If helpful vote counts are pre-aggregated for performance, the implementation should decrement any relevant counters or trigger asynchronous recomputation after a vote is removed. Related operations include creating a helpful vote, listing helpful votes for a customer or a review, and retrieving product or SKU rating aggregates which may rely on the underlying helpful-vote data.

Error handling should distinguish between a vote that cannot be found, a vote that the customer is not allowed to delete, and unexpected server-side failures. Clients can use these error responses to present clear feedback to users, such as indicating that a vote was already removed or never existed, or that they do not have permission to manipulate another user's votes.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the current rating aggregates for a specific product from the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates Prisma table. It is designed to provide precomputed rating statistics, such as average score, count of ratings, and possibly distributions, for a single product identified by its productId.

The rating aggregates table is maintained by background jobs or transactional logic that reacts to events on the shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes tables. By querying the aggregates instead of raw reviews, the endpoint offers fast access to up-to-date rating information suitable for product detail pages, listing views, and analytics surfaces.

The path parameter {productId} corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_products table and is used to locate the associated aggregate row in shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates. The response returns a single aggregate object representing the product's rating metrics at query time. If no aggregate exists yet, the implementation may return a default aggregate (for example, with zero counts) or a not-found response, depending on the business rules.
operations.description:
Fetch precomputed rating aggregate information for a single product using the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates table.

This operation is built on top of the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates table, which stores precomputed rating statistics for products in the shoppingMall platform. Rather than scanning all reviews in shopping_mall_reviews or recalculating metrics every time a client requests product ratings, the system maintains this aggregate table as a fast-access representation of current rating state. A typical aggregate record may include average rating, total number of ratings, counts per rating score, and optionally helpful-vote-weighted metrics that incorporate data from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes.

Clients call this endpoint by passing a {productId} path parameter that corresponds to the product's primary key in the shopping_mall_products table. The service then looks up the corresponding aggregate row in shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates. If the aggregate exists, the endpoint returns a detailed aggregate DTO describing the product's rating metrics. If the aggregate has not yet been created, the implementation can decide whether to synthesize a default aggregate with neutral values or to return an error that signals the absence of rating data.

From a security standpoint, product rating aggregates are generally safe to expose publicly, because they summarize anonymized user feedback without revealing individual customer identities or sensitive information. For that reason, this endpoint is typically left open to all clients without requiring authentication, allowing product detail pages and catalog listings to retrieve rating metrics efficiently. However, the service should still include defensive checks to ensure only non-sensitive fields from shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates are exposed.

This operation is closely related to other review and rating APIs, such as endpoints that let customers create, update, or delete reviews in shopping_mall_reviews, endpoints that manage helpful votes in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes, and SKU-level rating aggregate endpoints that query shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates. Those write operations must keep the aggregate tables up to date, either synchronously or via background processing, so that this read-only endpoint always returns consistent rating information. Error handling should clearly differentiate "no rating data yet" scenarios from actual server errors, enabling clients to decide whether to display placeholder messages or error states.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the rating aggregate metrics for a specific SKU from the shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates table. It is designed to provide denormalized, read-only analytical data summarizing customer review scores and rating distributions for the SKU identified by skuId.

The endpoint returns a precomputed aggregate structure rather than raw review records. It will query the snapshot/aggregate table that stores metrics such as average rating, total review count, distribution of star scores, and possibly separate counts for verified purchases. Because this table is derived from the primary shopping_mall_reviews table and related entities, the operation is strictly read-only and does not modify any data.

The business purpose is to allow product detail and SKU selection pages to quickly display rating summaries without executing heavy aggregation queries over reviews in real time. Implementations must ensure that skuId corresponds to an existing SKU primary key in the shopping_mall_skus model and that the aggregates table has up-to-date data for that SKU. If no aggregate exists yet for a valid SKU, the endpoint should return a not-found error or a well-defined empty aggregate depending on business rules.
operations.description:
Retrieve the rating aggregate metrics for a specific SKU using its unique identifier.

This operation reads from the shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates model, which stores precomputed rating statistics associated with SKUs from the shopping_mall_skus table. Typical fields in this aggregate model include the average score, total number of reviews, and counts for each rating level. These aggregates are generated by background jobs or triggers based on the shopping_mall_reviews and related snapshot tables, ensuring efficient read performance for frequently accessed rating information.

From a security perspective, this endpoint exposes only non-sensitive analytical information about a SKU, so it can generally be made publicly accessible without authentication. However, implementers may still choose to apply rate limiting to prevent abusive scraping. The operation does not reveal any personally identifiable information or individual review content, only summarized numbers.

The path parameter skuId is expected to be the primary identifier of the SKU in the shopping_mall_skus model. The handler must validate that the identifier is well-formed and then attempt to load the matching aggregate record from shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates. If either the SKU does not exist or no aggregate has yet been generated, the implementation should return an appropriate error response code (such as 404) with a clear error payload, even though such error schema is not detailed here.

This endpoint is typically used together with list- and search-level rating analytics endpoints, as well as detailed review listing endpoints that operate on shopping_mall_reviews. Client applications can first display the aggregate metrics from this endpoint and then allow the user to drill down into individual reviews through separate APIs.

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves paginated rating aggregate metrics for products using the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates table as its primary source. It is designed as a collection-level analytical endpoint for ranking and filtering products based on their rating statistics.

The request body accepts complex search criteria and pagination parameters wrapped in the IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.IRequest DTO. Typical filters may include minimum and maximum average rating, minimum review count, product category, seller, or other catalog dimensions, as well as sorting options such as highest rated or most reviewed. The response returns a paginated collection of summary records represented by IPageIShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.ISummary, optimized for listing views or dashboards.

At the database level, this endpoint composes data primarily from shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates, which itself is derived from shopping_mall_reviews and potentially shopping_mall_products. Implementations should leverage appropriate indexes to efficiently support filtering and sorting over rating metrics and related foreign keys. The operation does not alter any records and is strictly read-only, making it suitable for caching at the application or CDN layer when permitted by business rules.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of product rating aggregates using flexible filters and sorting options.

This operation reads from the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates model, which stores precomputed rating statistics for products in the shopping_mall_products table. Fields commonly include average rating, total review count, and per-score distribution counts. The aggregates are computed asynchronously from underlying review data stored in shopping_mall_reviews and its snapshot models, providing fast access to rating summaries for catalog and discovery experiences.

The request body of type IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.IRequest allows clients to specify search criteria such as ranges for average rating, minimum review thresholds, target categories or tags, and sorting preferences. It also carries pagination parameters, including page number, page size, and possibly cursor-based options depending on the DTO definition. Implementers must validate incoming criteria, enforce maximum page sizes, and apply safe defaults to protect performance.

The response returns a paginated collection of rating aggregate summaries wrapped in IPageIShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.ISummary. Each summary contains enough information for list views, such as product identifier, representative display information, and the core rating metrics. Sensitive data and full product details are intentionally omitted, as they are available from dedicated product retrieval APIs.

From an authorization perspective, the endpoint generally returns non-sensitive analytical information and can be made publicly accessible for use in search result pages, category listings, and marketing components. Nevertheless, the system should apply rate limiting and potentially IP-based throttling to prevent scraping or abuse. This endpoint is conceptually related to SKU-level aggregate retrieval and review listing APIs, enabling clients to first query rating aggregates at the product level and then drill into specific SKUs or individual reviews using other operations.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a paginated list of SKU-level rating aggregate records from the `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` Prisma table. It is designed as a read-only analytical endpoint that exposes precomputed statistics about customer ratings for concrete SKU variants, such as average rating, total rating count, and per-score distribution.

The underlying table `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` is marked as `material: true` and `stance: "subsidiary"`, indicating that it is maintained by background jobs or database triggers as a materialized aggregate view rather than by direct user writes. Each row is uniquely associated with a single SKU via the foreign key `shopping_mall_sku_id` and captures derived metrics including `average_rating`, `rating_count`, and the counts for each rating bucket from `rating_1_count` through `rating_5_count`, together with `last_computed_at` to indicate when the aggregates were last refreshed.

This API does not modify any data in the aggregate table. Instead, it provides flexible search, filtering, and sorting capabilities suitable for catalog pages, analytics dashboards, and seller tools that need to query rating quality per SKU at scale. Example filters that the request DTO `IShoppingMallSkuRatingAggregate.IRequest` can support include ranges on `average_rating`, minimum `rating_count`, specific SKU identifiers, seller or product scoping via joins to `shopping_mall_skus`, and time-based constraints on `last_computed_at` to ensure freshness. The response uses `IPageIShoppingMallSkuRatingAggregate.ISummary` to return a paginated list optimized for list and grid displays.

Because the aggregate table is subsidiary and material, client applications must treat this endpoint as eventually consistent with respect to the underlying `shopping_mall_reviews` data. Implementations should document that some delay may occur between new review submissions and updated aggregate values. No creation, update, or deletion APIs are provided for `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`; recomputation is handled by internal services according to business policies. Security-wise, the data is read-only and does not contain PII, so the operation can be exposed publicly or with minimal authentication, while still allowing internal rate limiting to protect infrastructure from abusive high-frequency queries.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve SKU rating aggregate records from the `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` table with advanced filtering and pagination.

This endpoint operates on the materialized aggregate view `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`, whose description states that it stores precomputed rating aggregates per SKU variant. Each row is linked to `shopping_mall_skus` via `shopping_mall_sku_id` and includes fields like `average_rating`, `rating_count`, bucket-specific counts `rating_1_count` through `rating_5_count`, and `last_computed_at` to indicate when these metrics were last recomputed. Since the table is flagged as `material: true` and `stance: "subsidiary"`, it is maintained by background processes rather than direct user edits.

From a security and access perspective, this operation is read-only and safe to expose broadly because it surfaces aggregate quality signals rather than raw user content or personally identifiable information. The `authorizationActors` array is therefore left empty to indicate that no specific actor type is required at the routing level; any further access control (for example, hiding non-public SKUs or applying regional visibility rules derived from `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules`) can be implemented deeper in the service layer using the caller's context.

The operation is implemented as a `PATCH /ratingAggregates/skus` search endpoint to allow a rich structured request body while remaining idempotent. The request body uses `IShoppingMallSkuRatingAggregate.IRequest`, which can include filter fields such as SKU identifiers, ranges over `average_rating`, minimum `rating_count`, and time ranges on `last_computed_at`, as well as pagination and sorting options (for example sorting by `average_rating` descending or `rating_count` descending). The response body `IPageIShoppingMallSkuRatingAggregate.ISummary` encapsulates a page of summary rows where each summary contains key metric fields needed for listing views, including the average rating, total rating count, rating bucket counts, and the timestamp of last computation.

Related APIs would typically include product-level aggregates from `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and endpoints that retrieve raw reviews from `shopping_mall_reviews`. Client applications commonly call this SKU aggregate search in conjunction with product catalog search endpoints, using the SKU IDs returned by catalog search to request rating statistics in a separate call or by embedding these aggregates in a denormalized search index. Error handling focuses on validating the search parameters in the request DTO, ensuring that numeric ranges for `average_rating` or `rating_count` are coherent, and returning clear messages when provided filters are invalid or unsupported. Since the table is read-only, no concurrency or conflict errors occur at this layer.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves review eligibility records from the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` Prisma table using flexible filtering and pagination. The `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` model is a subsidiary table that represents when a customer is allowed to create a product or SKU review based on delivered order items.

Each row in `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` links to several primary entities through foreign keys: `shopping_mall_customer_id` references the eligible customer from `shopping_mall_customers`, `shopping_mall_order_item_id` references the underlying line item in `shopping_mall_order_items`, `shopping_mall_product_id` identifies the product in `shopping_mall_products`, `shopping_mall_sku_id` optionally identifies a SKU variant in `shopping_mall_skus`, and `shopping_mall_review_id` optionally points to the created review in `shopping_mall_reviews` if the eligibility has been consumed. The table also includes business-rule fields such as `status` (with values like eligible, used, expired, or revoked), `eligible_from`, optional `eligible_until`, and audit timestamps `created_at` and `updated_at`.

This endpoint is designed as a read-only search/index API that supports use cases including determining which products a customer can currently review, back-office monitoring of review eligibility flows, and analytics on how many eligibilities are in each state. The request body type `IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IRequest` can provide filters on customer IDs, product or SKU IDs, order item context, `status`, and eligibility windows (for example, eligibilities currently active where `eligible_from` is in the past and `eligible_until` is in the future or null). The response type `IPageIShoppingMallReviewEligibility.ISummary` returns a paginated list of summary rows suitable for list and dashboard views.

The unique index on `[shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_order_item_id]` enforces at most one eligibility per customer and order item combination, which simplifies queries when looking for a specific customer's permission on a given purchase. Because the table has `stance: "subsidiary"`, write operations such as creation, status transitions, and linking to reviews are handled by internal workflows tied to order lifecycle events and review creation in `shopping_mall_reviews`. This search endpoint strictly avoids modifying data and is safe to call frequently from user-facing flows and internal tools.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of review eligibility records from the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` table.

The `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` table is described as holding "eligibility records indicating when customers are allowed to write reviews" and is marked with `stance: "subsidiary"`. Each record connects a customer (`shopping_mall_customer_id` referencing `shopping_mall_customers`), an order item (`shopping_mall_order_item_id` referencing `shopping_mall_order_items`), and the product or SKU (`shopping_mall_product_id` and optional `shopping_mall_sku_id`) that may be reviewed. When a review has been created, the eligibility can be linked to it via `shopping_mall_review_id` pointing to `shopping_mall_reviews`. The model also tracks `status` to express business states such as eligible, used, expired, or revoked, as well as `eligible_from`, optional `eligible_until`, and audit timestamps `created_at` and `updated_at`.

This `PATCH /reviewEligibilities` endpoint is a general-purpose search operation that leverages a structured request body rather than query parameters to support complex filters. The request DTO `IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IRequest` is expected to allow filtering by customer, product, SKU, order item, eligibility `status`, and time ranges on `eligible_from` and `eligible_until`. It should also carry pagination controls such as page size and cursor or offset, and optional sorting instructions, for example sorting by `eligible_from` or `created_at` descending. The response encapsulated in `IPageIShoppingMallReviewEligibility.ISummary` returns only the fields required for list views and dashboards, abstracting away internal fields not needed by clients.

Security and authorization considerations depend on the caller. Because eligibilities expose customer-specific review rights tied to their purchases, this operation should be restricted to customer-facing contexts and back-office tools, not to anonymous users. Accordingly, the `authorizationActors` field uses the concrete actor `"customer"` which aligns with the customer account model in the Prisma schema. Framework-level authentication ensures that only authenticated customers can invoke this endpoint in self-service flows, while administrative tooling can reuse it with internal credentials and additional server-side checks.

This search operation is typically used in conjunction with review creation APIs that require an active eligibility ID to be presented, enforcing rules like one review per purchase and time-bounded review windows. Downstream analytics services may also query this endpoint or its underlying table to compute funnel metrics such as eligibility-to-review conversion rates and the distribution of eligibility statuses across the customer base. Errors primarily arise from invalid filter combinations, such as malformed identifiers or contradictory time range constraints, and should be reported with clear validation messages referencing the corresponding request fields.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single review eligibility record from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` by its unique identifier. It is designed to allow internal administrative or service-layer consumers to inspect whether a particular customer is allowed to write a review for a given product or SKU, including contextual information such as the underlying order, timing windows, and any restriction flags stored on the eligibility record.

The operation is implemented as a simple read-only lookup by primary key on the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` model. It does not modify any data and is idempotent. The primary purpose is to support review moderation tools, troubleshooting flows, or other back-office processes that need to confirm the current eligibility state calculated by the main transaction flows (e.g., after delivery, before expiration).

This API is intentionally scoped as an administrative/read endpoint. Creation and update of eligibility records are handled by business processes (for example, when orders reach specific shipment or completion statuses), not by this operation. The GET operation only exposes the persisted eligibility attributes and their relationships so that authorized callers can fully understand why a given eligibility is in its current state.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single review eligibility record from the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` table using its unique identifier.

This operation reads the persisted review eligibility data that determines whether a given customer can currently create or update a product or SKU review. The underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` stores fields such as references to the customer account, the relevant product or SKU, the associated order or order item, window start and end timestamps that control when reviews are permitted, and flags indicating whether eligibility has already been consumed or revoked according to business rules described in the reviews and ratings requirements.

The endpoint is read-only and safe to call repeatedly. It does not recompute eligibility; instead, it returns the stored state, which is typically written by order and fulfillment flows when key lifecycle events occur (for example, after an order item is delivered or a cooling-off period elapses). Because the underlying table is part of the review governance domain, the response can also include information about why eligibility is currently blocked (such as policy, risk, or abuse-related flags) when such fields exist in the Prisma model.

From a security perspective, this operation is restricted to administrative actors. Normal customers and sellers do not directly query raw eligibility records; they interact with higher-level review flows that implicitly check eligibility. Administrators, risk/governance staff, or internal tools with the `admin` actor role can use this endpoint to debug review flows, investigate abuse reports, or verify the timing rules configured in business policies. If the requested identifier does not correspond to any existing eligibility record, the implementation should return an appropriate not-found error according to the platform’s standard error handling conventions.

This GET operation complements other review-related endpoints such as listing reviews, creating reviews (which must check eligibility), or viewing review moderation actions. It focuses solely on exposing the single eligibility record so that its fields and relationships can be inspected in detail without altering the stored state.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single review eligibility (`shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`) record by its identifier.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing review eligibility record in the Prisma table `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` identified by its unique identifier. It is primarily intended for administrative or automated back-office workflows that need to correct or override previously computed eligibility states, such as extending the eligibility window, revoking eligibility due to policy violations, or marking eligibility as consumed when a review has been manually imported or adjusted.

The implementation performs a lookup by primary key on `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` using the supplied `eligibilityId` path parameter, then applies the update fields provided in the request body DTO `IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IUpdate`. Only fields permitted by that DTO—such as eligibility status, window start/end timestamps, or descriptive notes—may be changed. The operation must validate that the requested changes are consistent with business rules derived from the reviews and ratings requirements and any policy constraints defined in related business policy tables.

Because `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` records are system-managed artifacts tied to orders and deliveries, this PUT endpoint is intentionally restricted to administrative actors. Normal customers or sellers cannot use this API to gain eligibility or bypass rules; their eligibility is determined automatically by order and fulfillment flows. The update operation should include concurrency safeguards and error handling for cases where the record does not exist, is under legal hold, or cannot be modified due to policy restrictions.
operations.description:
Update an existing review eligibility record stored in the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` table.

This operation allows an authorized administrator or internal service to modify selected fields of a review eligibility record, such as its active status, the start and end timestamps that bound the review window, or internal notes and flags that explain why eligibility has been granted, suspended, or revoked. The concrete set of updatable fields is defined by the `IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IUpdate` DTO and should mirror the mutable columns of the Prisma model `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`, excluding immutable identifiers and foreign keys that tie the record to specific customers, products, SKUs, or orders.

The operation uses the `eligibilityId` path parameter to locate the target record. If the record cannot be found, the implementation must return an appropriate not-found response. Before applying updates, the service should enforce business and governance rules derived from the reviews and ratings requirements, ensuring that changes do not violate policy constraints—for example, preventing eligibility from being reopened after a hard expiration defined by business policies, or ensuring that eligibility cannot be silently granted when associated orders have been refunded or are under dispute.

From a security and authorization standpoint, this endpoint is restricted to the `admin` actor. Direct external manipulation of review eligibility by customers or sellers is not permitted; their eligibility is instead derived from order and delivery events. Administrative users can use this endpoint to correct data inconsistencies, execute policy-driven overrides, or synchronize eligibility states with external systems. On success, the API returns the updated eligibility record reflecting all persisted changes. If validation fails, the service should respond with detailed error messages describing which business rule or constraint was violated.

This PUT operation complements read-only inspection of eligibility via the corresponding GET endpoint and integrates with higher-level review creation and moderation workflows that depend on accurate eligibility data.
operations.summary: Update an existing review eligibility (`shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`) record by its identifier.

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a filtered, paginated collection of review eligibility records for a specific customer. It is primarily associated with the Prisma table `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`, which models when and for which products or orders a customer is allowed to submit reviews.

The endpoint is scoped by a single customer, identified through the `customerId` path parameter that corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customers` table. Within that scope, the operation queries `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` and any related entities (such as orders, order items, products, or SKUs) according to the business rules defined in the review and ratings domain.

The request body uses `IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IRequest` to express complex search criteria, such as filtering by product, SKU, order, eligibility window, eligibility status (e.g., eligible, expired, already-used), and pagination and sorting options. The response returns a paginated list of summary objects `IPageIShoppingMallReviewEligibility.ISummary`, optimized for list display in customer-facing or admin-support UIs.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of review eligibility records for a specific customer.

This operation focuses on records in the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` Prisma model, which represent business decisions about when a customer is allowed to write a review, typically tied to completed orders or delivered shipments. The table captures which entity (product, SKU, order item) can be reviewed, the timeframe in which a review is allowed, and the current status of that eligibility (for example, whether a review has already been written using that eligibility).

The `customerId` path parameter identifies the target customer and maps to the primary key in the `shopping_mall_customers` table. Only eligibilities associated with this customer are included in the result set. The request body type `IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IRequest` is used to express filters such as specific product or SKU identifiers, order identifiers, date ranges for eligibility start or end, status flags, and pagination controls like page number, page size, and sort order. These fields should align with the columns and relations defined on `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` and its foreign keys.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is intended for authenticated customers accessing their own eligibilities, or for internal support tooling where additional authorization checks ensure that the requesting actor is allowed to see the customer's review eligibility data. The operation itself does not change any data; it only reads from `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` and related tables. Rate limiting and access control should be implemented at the application layer based on the `authorizationActors` configuration.

This operation is typically used together with the detail endpoint `GET /customers/{customerId}/reviewEligibilities/{eligibilityId}`. A client first calls this search endpoint to list relevant eligibilities and then uses the detail endpoint to fetch all fields for a specific eligibility when preparing a review-writing UI or troubleshooting review issues.

This operation retrieves the full details of a single review eligibility record for a specific customer. It directly targets the Prisma table `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`, using the eligibility's primary key along with the owning customer's identifier to ensure proper scoping.

The path contains two identifiers: `customerId`, which maps to the primary key of `shopping_mall_customers`, and `eligibilityId`, which maps to the primary key of `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`. The combination ensures that the retrieved review eligibility record belongs to the specified customer, preventing cross-account data exposure.

The response body uses the DTO type `IShoppingMallReviewEligibility`, which should reflect the full column set of the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` model and its most important relations (for example, references to products, SKUs, and orders). This allows clients to understand exactly what can be reviewed, the eligibility timeframe, and whether the eligibility has already been consumed by a submitted review.
operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed review eligibility record for a specific customer and eligibility identifier.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` Prisma model, which defines the conditions under which a customer is allowed to submit a product or SKU review. The record may include references to the underlying order, order item, product, or SKU, as well as fields indicating the start and end of the eligibility period, current status, and any constraints such as minimum days after delivery.

The `customerId` path parameter identifies the owner of the eligibility and corresponds to a row in `shopping_mall_customers`. The `eligibilityId` parameter identifies a specific row in `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities`. Implementation should enforce that the `eligibilityId` belongs to the given `customerId`, typically by checking a foreign key relationship or a customer reference field on the eligibility record before returning it.

From a security standpoint, this endpoint is intended for authenticated customers viewing their own review eligibility detail, or for internal tools with additional permission checks to allow support staff or admins to inspect eligibility records on behalf of a customer. The operation is strictly read-only: it does not update any fields in `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` or related tables. If no matching record is found or if the eligibility does not belong to the customer, the implementation should return an appropriate error such as 404 (Not Found).

This detail endpoint complements the list endpoint `PATCH /customers/{customerId}/reviewEligibilities`. Clients typically use the list endpoint to discover relevant eligibilities and then call this endpoint to load full details when preparing to present review-writing options or to troubleshoot why a given review is allowed or blocked.
