operations.specification:
Design a PATCH /inventoryAdjustments operation for searching and listing inventory adjustment events stored in the Prisma table shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments. This endpoint will provide a paginated, filterable, and sortable view over atomic inventory adjustment records, which are append-only events per seller, SKU, and warehouse. The request body will use IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.IRequest to capture search criteria such as seller, SKU, warehouse, reason, direction, date ranges, and free-text notes. The response body will return a paginated list of summary objects IPageIShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.ISummary, optimized for list and reporting use cases rather than full detail payloads.

The operation is intended primarily for internal tools (admin consoles and possibly seller portals when scoped) to audit stock changes, investigate discrepancies, and drive analytics. It must respect the append-only semantics of shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments: records are never updated to change quantity_delta or links, so the query is purely read-only. Relationships to shopping_mall_skus, shopping_mall_seller_warehouses, and shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons can be reflected in the summary DTO for contextual fields such as SKU code, warehouse code, and reason code/name.

The endpoint should support pagination parameters inside the IRequest DTO (page, limit, sort field, sort direction) rather than query parameters, following the platform convention that complex searches use PATCH with a JSON body. It must not allow creation or modification of adjustment events; those are produced by separate inventory workflows.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of inventory adjustment events from the shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments table.

This operation exposes the append-only inventory adjustment log that the platform uses to track atomic changes in stock at the level of seller, SKU, and warehouse. Each record in shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments represents a single change to inventory, identified by its id primary key and linked to a seller (seller_id), a SKU (sku_id referencing shopping_mall_skus.id), a warehouse (seller_warehouse_id referencing shopping_mall_seller_warehouses.id), and a standardized reason (inventory_adjustment_reason_id referencing shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons.id). The direction column captures whether the event is an increase or decrease from the event’s own perspective, and quantity_delta records the numeric amount added or removed.

The request body, typed as IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.IRequest, allows clients to specify rich search criteria for these events. Typical filters include seller identifiers, SKU identifiers, warehouse identifiers, inventory_adjustment_reason_id, direction, and business-level reference_type/reference_id pairs used to correlate adjustments with external documents or workflows. Date range filters on occurred_at and created_at enable time-window reporting such as "all adjustments in the last 24 hours" or "all corrections performed during an inventory audit period". The IRequest structure also encapsulates pagination (page index, page size) and sorting options, for example ordering by occurred_at descending or grouping by seller and SKU for dashboard views.

The response returns a paginated list of summary objects using the IPageIShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.ISummary DTO. Each summary entry focuses on fields that are most useful for list screens and overviews: identifiers, direction, quantity_delta, occurred_at, and key denormalized context like SKU code, warehouse code/name, and adjustment reason code/name where available. By using a dedicated summary type rather than the full entity, the API keeps payloads compact for high-volume log queries while remaining consistent with the underlying Prisma schema fields.

Security-wise, this endpoint should be restricted to authenticated back-office users such as admins who need to audit inventory behavior, and possibly to seller actors when scoped to their own seller_id. For this specification we mark authorizationActors as ["admin"], assuming that seller-scoped views will either reuse this operation with additional guards or be exposed via a separate facade. Implementation must enforce that no write operations occur: the endpoint performs read-only queries against shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments and never creates or mutates rows. For compliance and performance, implementations should respect the existing indexes on seller_id, sku_id, seller_warehouse_id, inventory_adjustment_reason_id, and occurred_at when constructing queries so large search windows remain efficient.

This search operation is commonly used together with the detail retrieval endpoint GET /inventoryAdjustments/{inventoryAdjustmentId}. Clients first call this PATCH operation to obtain a list of candidate adjustments, then follow up with the detail API for any specific entry that requires deeper inspection or outside-system correlation.

Design a GET /inventoryAdjustments/{inventoryAdjustmentId} operation that returns detailed information about a single inventory adjustment event stored in the Prisma table shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments. The response body type IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment will expose all relevant fields from the schema, including seller_id, sku_id, seller_warehouse_id, inventory_adjustment_reason_id, direction, quantity_delta, reference_type, reference_id, note, occurred_at, created_at, and updated_at, as well as any related contextual data that the DTO chooses to include from associated entities like shopping_mall_skus, shopping_mall_seller_warehouses, and shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons.

This operation is strictly read-only and used primarily for audit, investigation, and support workflows, where an admin or back-office user needs to see the full context of a specific inventory change. It must not alter the adjustment record, honoring the append-only semantics described in the Prisma schema documentation. If the requested id does not exist, the implementation should return a 404-style error according to platform-wide error handling conventions rather than a partial response.

The endpoint complements the list/search operation on PATCH /inventoryAdjustments by allowing clients to drill down into a single event after locating it via filters or external links. It should be restricted to administrative actors, consistent with the sensitive nature of inventory histories and the potential insights into seller operations.
operations.description:
Retrieve full detail for a single inventory adjustment event from the shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments table.

This operation targets a single row in shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments, identified by its id primary key, exposed as the inventoryAdjustmentId path parameter. Each adjustment represents an atomic stock change for a combination of seller, SKU, and warehouse, with seller_id pointing to the owning seller in shopping_mall_sellers, sku_id referencing the specific SKU in shopping_mall_skus, and seller_warehouse_id referencing the warehouse in shopping_mall_seller_warehouses where the physical change occurred. The inventory_adjustment_reason_id field links to shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons, which provides the standardized business reason code and human-readable description.

The response body uses the IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment DTO to return all core columns from the Prisma schema: direction, quantity_delta, reference_type, reference_id, note, occurred_at, created_at, and updated_at, along with foreign-key identifiers. Implementations may also enrich the DTO with related context, such as SKU code and status, warehouse code and name, and adjustment reason code, while remaining faithful to the underlying schema comments. The occurred_at timestamp represents when the stock change actually took place, which might differ from created_at, allowing late recording of events discovered during audits. The updated_at field is intended primarily for metadata changes and should not be used to infer quantity changes, which are immutable per event.

From a security and governance standpoint, this endpoint should be exposed only to privileged users, so authorizationActors is set to ["admin"]. Admin consoles and internal tools can use this detail view to support investigations into stock discrepancies, reconcile inventory with external systems using the reference_type and reference_id fields, or review the free-text note attached to the adjustment for human explanations. Seller_session_id, admin_id, and admin_session_id foreign keys, when populated, give clear traceability about who initiated the adjustment, which is essential for compliance and audit reporting.

This detail retrieval endpoint is typically used after a user has first performed a search via PATCH /inventoryAdjustments to find candidates by time range, reason, or SKU, then selected a specific adjustment to inspect. If the provided inventoryAdjustmentId does not match any row, the implementation should return an appropriate not-found error response without revealing information about other entries, aligning with platform-wide error-handling and security practices.

This operation creates a new inventory adjustment event in the shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments table for the ShoppingMall platform. It represents an atomic change to inventory for a specific seller, SKU, and warehouse, with an associated standardized reason code from shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons and references to related entities such as shopping_mall_seller_warehouses and shopping_mall_skus.

The endpoint accepts a JSON payload conforming to IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.ICreate that includes all required business fields: the seller identity, the target SKU, the warehouse where inventory is stored, the signed quantity delta (positive for increases, negative for decreases), the adjustment reason, optional notes or external references, and metadata such as who triggered the adjustment and in what context. The API validates referential integrity against the Prisma models, ensuring that the referenced seller, SKU, warehouse, and reason records exist and are in appropriate states.

On successful creation, the operation persists a new row in shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments and returns the created adjustment as an IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment entity, which includes the canonical identifiers, normalized quantities, timestamps, and resolved references where appropriate. Downstream processes, such as recalculation of current inventory positions or triggering notifications, are handled by the service layer based on this adjustment record rather than by clients directly.
operations.description:
Create a new atomic inventory adjustment record for a specific seller, SKU, and warehouse using the shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments Prisma model.

This operation is intended for internal inventory management workflows where administrators or seller-side tooling need to explicitly record corrections, manual stock counts, damage write-offs, or other non-transactional movements. The incoming request body is mapped to the fields of shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments, including foreign keys to shopping_mall_skus, shopping_mall_seller_warehouses, and shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons. The description and notes fields (as defined in the schema) allow capturing human-readable context for audit and reporting.

Security-wise, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated administrative actors, represented by the "admin" authorization actor. Business logic must additionally ensure that the caller is permitted to adjust inventory for the targeted seller or warehouse segment, leveraging role-based permissions defined elsewhere (for example, shopping_mall_admin_roles and shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments). The API should enforce that quantity deltas obey business rules (e.g., not reducing stock below allowed minimums when such constraints are expressed in related configuration tables) and that adjustment reasons are valid according to shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons.

The created inventory adjustment integrates with other inventory and analytics tables; for example, subsequent batch jobs or triggers might use these adjustment records to update aggregated seller performance snapshots in shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots or to reconcile against seller warehouse stock records. Clients typically call this endpoint in conjunction with listing or detail views for SKUs and warehouses, but creation itself is encapsulated here. Error handling should include clear responses for invalid references, illegal quantity deltas, or attempts to adjust inventory in warehouses or SKUs that are locked by legal holds or risk cases managed via shopping_mall_legal_holds and shopping_mall_risk_cases.

Typical request criteria may include filtering by seller identity, date ranges (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly snapshots), order volume thresholds, revenue ranges, or performance indicators such as cancellation rate or refund rate as defined in the Prisma schema comments on `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots`. The response summaries include the key metrics from each snapshot row (for example, counts of orders, gross merchandise value, net revenue after refunds, and derived KPIs), as well as the snapshot timestamp that anchors each record in time.

Because snapshot tables are system-generated and often populated by scheduled jobs or analytical pipelines, this operation does not allow clients to modify or delete data. Instead, it focuses on efficient read access with robust filtering and pagination semantics. It is suitable for seller-facing analytics pages, internal operations dashboards, and administrative reporting tools that need historical views of seller order metrics without exposing any write capabilities on the snapshot data itself.

These measures may include daily or periodic counts of placed orders, completed orders, cancelled orders, refunded orders, and derived financial metrics such as gross merchandise value, net revenue, and average order value. The description comments on this model emphasize its role as a time-series data source for monitoring and analytics rather than as a directly editable transactional table.

Clients submit a request body conforming to `IShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot.IRequest`, which encapsulates search filters, time range constraints, and pagination instructions. For example, the request may specify a particular seller or set of sellers, a date window (such as the last 30 days), thresholds for specific metrics, or sorting preferences like ordering snapshots by snapshot date descending. The server uses these criteria to construct queries against the snapshot table and returns a page of summary records that are small and efficient enough to support UI rendering and charting scenarios.

Security and authorization considerations should treat this data as potentially sensitive performance information about sellers. While the snapshot table is system-generated, access control decisions in the business logic must ensure that individual sellers can only see their own metrics and that broader or cross-seller views are restricted to privileged actors such as admins or internal analysts. However, the endpoint itself is modeled generically, and the concrete authorization policies are enforced in the service layer.

Related operations include the single-record retrieval endpoint `GET /sellerOrderMetricsSnapshots/{snapshotId}`, which returns detailed data for a specific snapshot, and other analytics endpoints that may aggregate across multiple snapshot tables. The response body is typed as `IShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot`, which exposes all detailed fields of the snapshot record, including the snapshot timestamp, seller reference, aggregated counts, financial metrics, and any derived performance indicators annotated in the schema comments.

This operation is intended for use cases that require a full, detailed view of a specific snapshot, such as drilling down from a list of snapshots shown in an analytics dashboard, performing internal investigations of seller performance anomalies, or reconciling reported metrics with raw order and payment data. Because snapshot data is often used for compliance and historical reporting, the API emphasizes correctness and completeness of the returned record while leaving update and deletion responsibilities to system-level batch processes rather than interactive clients.
operations.description:

When a client calls this endpoint, the service looks up the snapshot row whose primary key matches the `snapshotId` path parameter. The underlying Prisma model for `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots` typically includes a unique ID field, a snapshot timestamp, foreign keys or identifiers for the seller whose metrics are summarized, and a variety of aggregated and derived fields. These fields may include metrics such as the number of orders placed, fulfilled, cancelled, or refunded during the snapshot period; total gross merchandise volume; net revenue after refunds and chargebacks; average order value; and other KPIs described in the schema comments.

The returned DTO `IShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot` is designed to reflect the full set of fields available on the Prisma model, providing consumers with a comprehensive view of the snapshot. This level of detail is suitable for deep analysis, debugging, or exporting metrics for further offline processing. Since the table is classified as a snapshot, clients must treat records as immutable point-in-time facts; any correction or re-computation of metrics would be handled by back-office jobs or analytic recalculation pipelines that rewrite or insert new snapshot rows rather than by this endpoint.

Authorization policies should ensure that only appropriately privileged actors can access snapshot records. For example, a seller analyst may only be permitted to fetch snapshots for their own seller account, while administrators with broader governance responsibilities can access records across multiple sellers. The endpoint itself is read-only, so security concerns focus on enforcing visibility rules rather than protecting against mutations. operations.description:

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` Prisma model, which is defined as a snapshot-style table capturing aggregated key performance indicators (KPIs) for each seller at a given point in time. Typical fields on this table include a reference to the seller account, a snapshot timestamp or logical period key, and various numeric metrics such as total orders, gross merchandise value (GMV), net revenue after refunds, cancellation and refund ratios, chargeback counts, dispute counts, average shipping lead times, on-time delivery rates, and average review ratings. The schema comments for this model typically emphasize that records are append-only and generated by background analytics jobs or reporting pipelines rather than through direct user interaction.

From a security and governance perspective, this operation is exposed to administrative and operational back-office actors who are responsible for monitoring marketplace health, enforcing policies, and identifying underperforming or risky sellers. Because the underlying table contains derived metrics rather than sensitive personal data, access control is primarily about ensuring that only authorized staff or automated governance services can read platform-wide performance analytics. The endpoint is defined as read-only and does not permit modification or deletion of snapshot records; creation of new rows is handled exclusively by internal batch processes or streaming analytics jobs in accordance with business requirements around reporting frequency and KPI definitions.

In terms of business behavior, the `IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.IRequest` request DTO allows clients to filter snapshots by seller identifier, seller code or handle, snapshot date ranges, aggregation period (such as day, week, or month), and acceptable ranges for key metrics (for example, only sellers with on-time shipment rate below a threshold, or dispute rates above a given percentage). Pagination and sorting options in the request support use cases where operators need to browse top or bottom performers, drill down into specific risk segments, or export subsets of data for offline analysis. The response uses the `IPageIShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.ISummary` type to return a page of snapshot summaries, including total count and page metadata along with compact metric fields suitable for list and dashboard displays.

Related operations include the detail retrieval endpoint `GET /sellerPerformanceSnapshots/{snapshotId}`, which returns a single snapshot record with full detail via the `IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot` DTO. Typical workflows involve first calling this listing operation to identify sellers or periods of interest, and then calling the detail endpoint to inspect the exact metric breakdown for a particular snapshot. Any foreign key dependencies, such as references from billing, payout, or audit tables, must either be absent or handled via cascade rules defined in the schema; otherwise, the operation must reject the deletion request.

From a business logic perspective, deletion of seller subscription rows should be tightly controlled and typically reserved for administrative tooling or internal maintenance flows, because subscriptions often have financial and compliance implications. Before deletion, the implementation may enforce checks to ensure that the subscription is in a terminal state, that there are no outstanding invoices or payouts linked to it, and that legal hold or audit policies do not require the record to be retained. The response body is null because the primary purpose of this endpoint is the side effect of removal rather than data retrieval.
operations.description:

This operation performs a hard delete against the shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions Prisma model, targeting the specific subscription identified by the subscriptionId path parameter. It is intended for administrative use cases such as cleaning up test data, removing erroneous entries created during onboarding or migration, or enforcing manual data correction tasks where retaining the historical subscription record is not required. When the request is processed, the system first validates that the subscription exists and that it can be safely removed according to business rules and integrity constraints.

Security and authorization are critical for this endpoint. Only administrative actors, represented here by the "admin" authorization actor, are allowed to invoke the erase operation. The implementation should verify that no policy-based restrictions, such as legal holds or audit retention requirements, prevent the deletion of the targeted subscription. Additionally, it should confirm that there are no unresolved financial relationships, such as unpaid invoices, unsettled payouts, or open disputes, that depend on this subscription record. If such constraints exist, the operation must fail gracefully and return an error explaining why deletion is not permitted.

The operation is directly related to the shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions table and indirectly interacts with any dependent tables that reference subscriptions by foreign key. Error handling should clearly differentiate between cases where the subscriptionId does not correspond to any existing record, where referential integrity prevents deletion, and where authorization or policy violations occur. Because the main outcome is the removal of data, the endpoint does not return a resource representation in the response body, and clients should rely on HTTP status codes to determine success or failure.

This erase operation is typically used alongside other lifecycle endpoints such as creation, update, and retrieval of seller subscriptions. While those endpoints manage the ongoing state of subscriptions, this one is reserved for permanent cleanup or exceptional correction scenarios, ensuring that sensitive operations on subscription data are deliberate, auditable, and restricted to trusted actors.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a seller subscription record from the shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions table.

operations.specification:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of seller fee charge records operating on the Prisma table `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`.

This PATCH operation is the primary list/search endpoint for individual fee and commission charges applied to sellers. It allows back-office finance and operations users to query fee charges across sellers, orders, refunds, and payout batches with rich filtering by seller, fee_type, effective_date range, amount ranges, platform revenue flag, and related order or payout identifiers.

The request body uses the DTO `IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.IRequest`, which encapsulates search criteria (e.g., sellerId, orderId, feeTypes[], currency, isPlatformRevenue, effectiveDateFrom/To, createdAtFrom/To, minAmount/maxAmount) along with generic pagination and sorting parameters. The response returns a paginated collection of fee charge summaries using the DTO `IPageIShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.ISummary`, which is optimized for list views and financial reconciliation screens.

Typical consumers of this API are internal admin tools or financial reporting services that need to inspect and reconcile fee charges derived from orders, refunds, and payout processes. Because `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` is marked as a primary table, the endpoint should, by default, focus on active, non-deprecated records as defined by the actual Prisma schema, with any historical or logically removed records only included when explicitly requested via the search criteria.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of seller fee charge records from the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` table.

Each record in this table represents an individual fee or commission applied to a seller. The schema describes `fee_type` as a business category (such as `transaction_commission`, `platform_service_fee`, `subscription_fee`, `advertising_fee`, or `adjustment`, where the concrete enum values are defined in the Prisma model), `currency` as the currency code, `amount` as the fee magnitude, and `tax_amount` as the tax portion expressed in the same currency. The boolean `is_platform_revenue` field indicates whether the fee contributes to platform revenue, and `effective_date` specifies the business date to use for revenue recognition and reporting. Timestamp fields `created_at` and `updated_at` capture when the charge was created and last updated. If the actual Prisma model includes a nullable `deleted_at` column, that field can be used to retain logically removed charges for audit and reconciliation use cases.

From a relational perspective, the table links to `shopping_mall_sellers` through `seller_id` (the seller to whom the fee applies), and may optionally link to `shopping_mall_orders` via `order_id`, to `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` via `payment_refund_id`, and to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` via `seller_payout_item_id`. These relationships enable financial back-office tools to trace the origin of each charge to a specific order, refund, or payout settlement item and to join charges into broader revenue and settlement reports.

This operation is intended for internal administrative actors who need to explore, audit, or reconcile fee charges over time. Typical filters include seller-centric searches (all charges for a seller in a date range), product or order-centric analysis (all charges tied to a given order or refund), and accounting-oriented extractions (all platform-revenue charges for a given effective_date or period). The `IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.IRequest` type should therefore support filters aligned with the table’s indexed fields, such as `seller_id`, `effective_date`, `fee_type`, and `order_id`, as well as pagination and sort options based on `effective_date`, `created_at`, or `amount`.

Security-wise, this endpoint exposes sensitive financial data about sellers and platform revenue. It must not be available to ordinary customers or sellers. Instead, `authorizationActor` is set to `"admin"`, indicating that only administrator accounts, as defined in the broader system’s actor model (`shopping_mall_admins` and associated RBAC), may invoke this operation. The implementation should additionally enforce access control and audit logging at the service layer, recording which admin executed which filters and at what time.

Related operations include the detail retrieval `GET /shoppingMall/admin/sellerFeeCharges/{feeChargeId}` (to fetch the full detail of a single charge for drill-down) and higher-level analytics endpoints that aggregate charges by fee_type, seller, or period. Error handling should surface validation issues (such as invalid date ranges or unsupported fee_type values) as 400-level responses, and internal errors in the underlying query or database connectivity as 500-level responses.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of seller fee charges from `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`.

Seller payout batches in shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches must be created via POST /shoppingMall/admin/payoutBatches, enabling the downstream creation of payout items that fee charges may reference and that can be used in search flows that analyze settlement relationships.

Seller payout items in shopping_mall_seller_payout_items must be created via POST /shoppingMall/admin/payoutBatches/{batchCode}/items so that fee charges can reference specific payout items and be queried using sellerPayoutItemId in financial reconciliation scenarios.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the detailed information of a single seller fee charge record from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` by its primary key.

This GET operation is the canonical detail view for a fee or commission applied to a seller. It is typically used by admin and finance tools to drill down from a list of charges into the exact attributes of a specific charge, including its type, amount, tax portion, effective_date, platform revenue flag, and any related order, refund, or payout item references.

The endpoint uses a single path parameter `feeChargeId`, which corresponds to the `id` field of `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` (`uuid`). The response body uses `IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge` to return the full entity representation, including relational identifiers (`seller_id`, `order_id`, `payment_refund_id`, `seller_payout_item_id`) and all plain fields such as `fee_type`, `description`, `currency`, `amount`, `tax_amount`, `is_platform_revenue`, `effective_date`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. If the actual Prisma schema includes a nullable `deleted_at` field, that column can indicate that the record has been logically removed while remaining available for audit and reconciliation.

Consumers of this operation include accounting reconciliation tools, dispute and refund investigation UIs, and internal audit dashboards. The endpoint is read-only and does not modify any data; it simply surfaces the current persisted state of the fee charge record.
operations.description:
Fetch complete details of a specific seller fee charge from the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` table using its primary key.

The underlying schema defines `id` as the primary key (a UUID), which uniquely identifies each fee charge row. This operation’s `feeChargeId` path parameter maps directly to that `id` column. Upon successful retrieval, the response returns a full `IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge` object, which includes relational foreign keys (`seller_id`, `order_id`, `payment_refund_id`, `seller_payout_item_id`) along with the primary business fields.

The `fee_type` field communicates the business category of the fee, such as transaction commissions, platform service fees, subscription fees, advertising fees, or adjustments, with the precise enum names defined by the Prisma model. The `description` field, when present, provides a human-readable explanation of why the fee exists. `currency` indicates the currency code of the charge, and `amount` captures the magnitude of the fee. `tax_amount` contains any associated tax portion, and `is_platform_revenue` indicates whether this fee contributes to the platform’s own revenue versus being a pass-through amount owed to third parties. `effective_date` is particularly important for revenue recognition and reporting, as it determines which accounting period this charge belongs to.

The timestamp fields `created_at` and `updated_at` indicate when the fee charge was recorded and last updated, supporting audit trails and chronological investigations. When present in the Prisma schema, a nullable `deleted_at` field can be used to signal that the charge has been logically removed while still being kept available for audit and reconciliation purposes. Consumers of this endpoint should interpret a non-null `deleted_at` as an indication that the charge is no longer considered active, but may still be relevant for historical financial analysis.

From a security perspective, this endpoint exposes detailed fee data about sellers and platform revenue. As such, it is restricted to administrative actors via `authorizationActor: "admin"`. The service implementation should enforce authorization, and it is recommended to log access for auditing, especially when fee charges relate to chargebacks, disputes, or compliance cases. Error handling should return 404 when no fee charge exists for the provided `feeChargeId`, and appropriate 400-level errors for malformed UUID identifiers. Related endpoints include the list/search operation `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/sellerFeeCharges` for retrieving multiple charges and any future analytics endpoints that aggregate or summarize charges across time or entities.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new seller fee charge record in the shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges table. It is intended to be called by internal backoffice or billing workflows (typically operated by admins) when the platform needs to record a fee or commission charge against a seller. The API accepts structured information describing which seller is being charged, which underlying business event or order the fee relates to, how much is charged, the currency and breakdown of the fee, and any associated metadata such as the billing cycle, subscription plan, or manual adjustment reason.

The created record in shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges becomes part of the seller’s financial ledger and can later be aggregated into payout calculations in conjunction with shopping_mall_seller_earnings and shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches. The operation must validate that the referenced seller exists in shopping_mall_sellers and that referenced orders, subscription plans, or other foreign-key targets are valid according to the Prisma schema constraints. Business rules such as non-negative amounts, supported currencies, and compatible fee types must be enforced according to the schema’s enum fields and numeric constraints.

Although the exact columns of shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges are defined in the Prisma schema, the DTO IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.ICreate is expected to mirror those fields that are settable at creation time, omitting system-managed fields such as primary keys, timestamps, or derived totals. The API responds with the full IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge representation so that callers can immediately see the canonical stored state of the fee charge, including generated identifiers and any computed values.
operations.description:
Create a new seller fee charge entry in the shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges table.

This operation is responsible for persisting a single fee or commission charge that the platform applies to a seller. Typical use cases include transaction-based commissions on orders, subscription plan fees, promotional package fees, manual adjustment charges, or penalty fees. The request body type IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.ICreate encapsulates the input fields required to describe the charge, such as the seller identifier, optional linkage to an order or payout, the fee type, the monetary amount and currency, and optional descriptive metadata like notes or human-readable reason text. Fields such as createdAt or internal primary keys are managed automatically by the persistence layer and are not accepted from the client.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint should only be accessible to privileged actors responsible for financial operations, such as admins or finance automation processes. It is not intended for public use or direct seller invocation, because allowing sellers to arbitrarily create fee charges would break financial integrity. The authorizationActors array therefore includes only "admin" to represent that calls must be authenticated as an administrative actor, while additional RBAC checks can be implemented on top of this classification.

In terms of database relationships, the Prisma model shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges is expected to reference the primary seller record from shopping_mall_sellers, and may also reference orders, payments, or subscription entities depending on the schema design. The implementation behind this API must enforce referential integrity by validating that all referenced IDs or codes exist and are in a state that permits attaching a fee charge. If the schema defines enumerated fee types or statuses, the IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.ICreate DTO must restrict clients to those allowed enum values.

Validation rules should include non-negative monetary amounts, supported currency codes, and any conditional requirements such as requiring an order reference for order-based charges or a subscription reference for subscription-based fees. When validation fails, the API should return appropriate error responses (e.g., 400 for invalid input, 404 for missing related records). On success, the response body uses the IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge type, representing the persisted record including its immutable identifier and any system-managed timestamps or computed fields, allowing downstream systems to immediately correlate this fee charge with payouts, invoices, or analytics.

This creation endpoint is typically used in combination with the update endpoint PUT /sellerFeeCharges/{feeChargeId}, which allows modifying mutable aspects of an existing seller fee charge, such as labels or certain status fields where business rules permit updates.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing seller fee charge record stored in the shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges table. It is designed for administrative or financial backoffice workflows that need to correct or adjust fee charge details after initial creation, subject to business rules. Examples include updating descriptive notes, adjusting fee classification, correcting linkage to an order or payout before settlement, or toggling certain mutable status fields if the schema permits.

The fee charge to update is identified by the path parameter {feeChargeId}, which corresponds to the primary key of shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges (typically a UUID string). The request body follows the IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.IUpdate DTO, which exposes only those fields that are legally mutable after creation, aligned with the Prisma schema’s semantics. System-managed fields such as the primary key, creation timestamp, and immutable financial amounts that must not change after a certain point should not be updatable via this DTO.

On successful validation and update, the API returns the full IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge representation so that callers can observe the canonical, updated state. The operation must handle error conditions such as non-existent feeChargeId, attempts to modify fields that are immutable according to business rules, or updates that conflict with the state of related entities such as settled payouts or locked accounting periods.
operations.description:
Update an existing seller fee charge record in the shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges table identified by its unique feeChargeId.

This operation allows privileged administrative workflows to modify selected aspects of an existing seller fee charge. The feeChargeId path parameter is a string identifier that uniquely identifies a single record in shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges; in typical Prisma schemas this would be a UUID, and the implementation should treat it as an opaque identifier, validating format as necessary. The request body, typed as IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.IUpdate, contains only the subset of fields that remain mutable after creation, such as textual notes, external references, or specific status flags that business rules allow to be changed.

From a security standpoint, only actors with administrative or financial authority should be able to update seller fee charges, since changes can directly affect platform–seller financial reconciliation. Therefore, authorizationActors is set to ["admin"]. The concrete authorization layer behind this API should ensure that the calling principal is an authenticated admin and may further apply fine-grained permission checks based on admin roles defined in tables like shopping_mall_admin_roles and shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.

When processing an update request, the service must first verify that a seller fee charge with the given feeChargeId exists in shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges. If not found, it should return a not-found error. If found, it should validate that the specific fields being modified are allowed to change at the current lifecycle stage. For example, if the schema and business rules treat certain financial amounts as immutable after the charge has been included in a settled payout batch, attempts to change those fields should be rejected. Similarly, if relationships to orders, payments, or subscriptions are constrained, the service must verify that any new references point to valid and compatible records.

On success, the endpoint returns the updated IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge instance, reflecting all persisted changes. This endpoint is typically used alongside POST /sellerFeeCharges for initial creation and read-oriented endpoints (not defined here) for listing or querying seller fee charges for reporting and reconciliation purposes.

operations.specification:
Provide an analytics search endpoint that returns paginated seller order metrics snapshots from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots`. This operation is designed as a read-only analytical query over snapshot data, not direct CRUD on transactional orders. It should allow admins or backoffice tools to retrieve time-series metrics for one or many sellers with flexible filtering by seller, snapshot_date ranges, timezone, and basic metric thresholds (for example, minimum GMV or high cancellation counts).

The request body will use a DTO like `IShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot.IRequest` to capture filters (sellerId list, date range, timezone, numeric range filters), pagination, and sorting preferences. The response will be a paginated collection of summary rows using `IPageIShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot.ISummary`, optimized for analytics dashboards rather than full transactional detail. Because the underlying Prisma model is marked with stance "snapshot", this endpoint must be read-only and should never modify or delete records.

The operation is intended for internal analytics and governance use, typically behind admin tooling, to support dashboards, monitoring screens, and offline analysis exports. It should be implemented efficiently using the unique index on `[seller_id, snapshot_date, timezone]` and secondary indices on `[snapshot_date, seller_id]`, `[seller_id, gmv_amount]`, and `[seller_id, orders_cancelled_count, orders_refunded_count]` to enable performant filtering and sorting on these dimensions.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of seller order metrics snapshots from the `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots` table.

This endpoint operates exclusively on the snapshot table that stores aggregated metrics per seller and snapshot period, including fields such as `orders_placed_count`, `orders_paid_count`, `orders_cancelled_count`, `orders_refunded_count`, `gmv_amount`, `nmv_amount`, `shipping_fee_amount`, `refund_amount`, and `chargeback_amount`. It respects the `snapshot_date` and `timezone` columns to ensure that day boundaries and reporting periods are interpreted consistently with the business timezone (for example, Asia/Seoul), as described in the Prisma schema comments.

The request body DTO `IShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot.IRequest` is expected to provide filter criteria like one or more `sellerId` values, a date or datetime range over `snapshot_date`, an optional timezone filter, and optional numeric range filters on key metrics (such as minimum GMV or high cancellation/refund counts). It also carries pagination controls (page number, page size) and sorting options, allowing analytics users to order results by `snapshot_date`, `gmv_amount`, `orders_cancelled_count`, or other indexed columns. The implementation should map these filters to efficient Prisma queries that leverage the unique index on `[seller_id, snapshot_date, timezone]` as well as the additional indexes defined in the schema.

Security-wise, this endpoint exposes sensitive operational data about seller performance and should therefore be restricted to administrative actors only. The `authorizationActors` array is set to `["admin"]`, and the actual RBAC implementation must ensure that only authenticated admin users can call it. Sellers or customers should not access this snapshot data directly; instead they may see derived aggregates via separate, role-appropriate endpoints if required by the business.

From a business workflow perspective, this analytics search operation is expected to be used in conjunction with higher-level dashboard views that summarize platform KPIs, risk monitoring tools that flag abnormal cancellation or refund behavior per seller, and offline data export pipelines. Since the underlying table is append-only snapshot data maintained by background jobs, no create, update, or erase operations are provided for this model; it is treated as a system-managed data source for read-only analytics. Error handling should validate that the requested date range is reasonable, that pagination parameters are within configured bounds, and that any seller identifiers provided actually exist, returning appropriate 4xx errors when validation fails.

operations.specification:
Define an analytics search endpoint that returns paginated seller performance snapshots from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots`. This table stores precomputed KPIs per seller at given snapshot dates, including `order_defect_rate`, `refund_rate`, `cancellation_rate`, `late_shipment_rate`, `chargeback_rate`, `average_rating`, `rating_count`, `dispute_open_count`, and an optional categorical `tier` such as new, standard, premium, or high_risk.

The endpoint will accept a request body DTO `IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.IRequest` capturing filters like seller identifiers, snapshot_date ranges, timezone, numeric KPI ranges (for example, refund_rate between 0 and 0.1, or chargeback_rate above a threshold), and categorical tier filters. Pagination and sorting controls are also part of this DTO, allowing callers to page through many sellers and sort by key KPIs or by snapshot date.

As the underlying Prisma model is marked with stance "snapshot", this operation must be strictly read-only and is intended for admin analytics tools, risk engines, and governance dashboards. It should leverage the unique index on `[seller_id, snapshot_date, timezone]` and additional indices on `[snapshot_date, seller_id]`, `[seller_id, order_defect_rate]`, and `[seller_id, tier]` to efficiently filter and order data.

The response will be a paginated summary collection using the DTO type `IPageIShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.ISummary`, which contains enough information for list views and dashboards without necessarily exposing every low-level column, while still reflecting the main KPI fields described in the Prisma schema comments.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of seller performance snapshots from the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` table for analytics and risk monitoring.

This endpoint exposes precomputed performance metrics per seller and snapshot window, including fractional KPIs such as `order_defect_rate`, `refund_rate`, `cancellation_rate`, `late_shipment_rate`, and `chargeback_rate`, all defined as numbers between 0 and 1 in the Prisma schema. It also returns rating-related fields like `average_rating` and `rating_count`, dispute-related metrics via `dispute_open_count`, and an optional string `tier` classification that encodes business-defined segments such as new, standard, premium, or high_risk. The `snapshot_date` and `timezone` fields provide the temporal context and business timezone used for the analysis window.

The request body `IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.IRequest` includes filters for seller IDs, snapshot_date range, timezone, and KPI thresholds so that admins and risk analysts can slice the dataset to focus on problematic or high-performing sellers. It also supports filtering by `tier`, enabling use cases like listing all `high_risk` sellers with high `chargeback_rate` in the last N days. Pagination and sorting are part of the same DTO, so list views and dashboards can page through large result sets and order by key metrics, such as highest refund_rate or lowest average_rating, using the indexes defined in the schema to maintain query performance.

From a security and governance perspective, this endpoint provides sensitive operational and risk-related data and must be limited to administrative tooling. The `authorizationActors` is set to `["admin"]`, and downstream authorization logic must ensure that only appropriately privileged admin accounts can query this data. The table itself is populated and updated by background computation processes, and there are no write APIs for these snapshots; any corrections or recomputations happen internally and are reflected in subsequent reads. This endpoint is typically used alongside other analytics and case-management APIs, such as endpoints that retrieve details of specific disputes, refunds, or risk cases for sellers flagged by these performance metrics.

Error handling should validate the structure of filters (for example, that rates are between 0 and 1 and date ranges are valid), enforce sane pagination limits, and respond with clear 4xx errors when invalid filters are supplied. 5xx responses should be reserved for internal errors, such as database connectivity issues, and must not leak implementation details.

operations.specification:
This operation provides a high-level seller dashboard overview for the shopping mall platform, aggregating information from multiple ShoppingMall domain tables that are directly relevant to a seller’s daily operations. It does not map to a single Prisma model; instead, it composes data from primary entities such as shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_seller_earnings, shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats, shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots, and shopping_mall_reviews, as well as related subsidiary tables like shopping_mall_order_status_histories and shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates.

The endpoint is designed to power a seller’s main dashboard screen by returning consolidated KPIs such as total sales for recent periods, current open orders by status, payout summaries, inventory alerts derived from shopping_mall_skus and shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments, and review or rating summaries. Rather than exposing raw transactional rows, this API returns an aggregated view shaped into a dedicated DTO type (IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard) that hides internal schema complexity while aligning closely with the seller’s business needs.

From an implementation perspective, this operation will typically execute several read-only queries, possibly in parallel, against the aforementioned Prisma models, aggregating them in memory or through database-level grouping (e.g., daily sales sums, counts of orders per status, rolling rating averages). No write operations occur through this endpoint, and it is strictly read-only with respect to the underlying tables. The seller identity is resolved from the authenticated context, and all queries are scoped to that seller’s records, for example by filtering shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_seller_earnings by seller ID. This preserves tenant isolation and ensures that each seller only sees their own metrics.
operations.description:
Retrieve a consolidated seller dashboard overview aggregating KPIs and status summaries from multiple ShoppingMall domain tables.

This GET operation is intended for authenticated sellers who need a single, fast-loading overview of their commercial performance and operational workload. It reads from core transactional tables such as shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items to compute metrics like current open orders, recently completed orders, and revenue totals for recent time windows. It also composes data from shopping_mall_seller_earnings and shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches to summarize pending and completed payouts, and from shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats or shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots where available to present trend lines over days or weeks.

The response type IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard is a dedicated dashboard DTO that sits conceptually above the underlying Prisma models. While the database contains detailed rows for orders, payments, and earnings, this dashboard type exposes only aggregated and curated fields such as counts, amounts, and small highlight lists (e.g., top 5 selling products, latest few orders). This separation keeps the public API stable even if the internal Prisma schema evolves, and allows the backend to adjust aggregation logic without breaking clients.

Security-wise, the endpoint requires a seller context (authorizationActors: ["seller"]). The implementation must derive the seller identity from the authentication layer and ensure that all reads are filtered to that seller’s data in tables like shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_skus, shopping_mall_seller_warehouses, and shopping_mall_reviews. No cross-seller data leakage is permitted, and any attempt to manipulate scopes via query parameters should be ignored in favor of the authenticated seller ID.

The operation is read-only and does not modify any of the referenced tables such as shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots or shopping_mall_order_daily_stats. Error handling should differentiate between generic server errors, missing seller profiles (e.g., no shopping_mall_seller_profiles row yet), and temporary data unavailability from analytical snapshot tables. Clients can use this endpoint together with more detailed list/search APIs on orders, payouts, and reviews to drill down from the high-level KPIs provided here.
operations.summary: Get a consolidated seller overview dashboard aggregating data from ShoppingMall seller-related tables.

responseBody.description: Aggregated seller dashboard overview including KPIs, summaries, and small highlight lists for the authenticated seller.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed analytical information about seller fees and commissions within the ShoppingMall platform. It focuses primarily on financial and fee-related tables such as shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges, shopping_mall_seller_earnings, shopping_mall_seller_payout_items, shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches, and shopping_mall_orders, as well as potentially referencing snapshot and statistics tables like shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats, shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots, and shopping_mall_payment_method_stats for aggregated time-series analysis.

The endpoint is designed as a complex search and analytics query, therefore it uses the PATCH method with a structured request body type IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.IRequest. This request can express filtering criteria such as date ranges, fee types, associated order or payout status constraints, and aggregation preferences (e.g., group by day, group by fee category). The underlying implementation will map these filters onto Prisma queries and aggregation operations over the fee and earning tables, ensuring that only fee records associated with the authenticated seller are considered.

The response is returned as a paginated analytical dataset using IPageIShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.ISummary, where each summary row represents an aggregated fee metric (for example, total commission per day, total platform fees by category, or fee share per payment method) derived from the transactional tables. This operation is read-only across all involved models and is optimized for analytical insights, not for operational management of individual fee rows.
operations.description:
Search and analyze seller fee and commission metrics across the ShoppingMall financial tables with flexible filters and aggregation options.

This PATCH operation enables authenticated sellers to understand how platform fees, commissions, and other financial charges are being applied to their business over time. It reads from core financial models such as shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges, shopping_mall_seller_earnings, and shopping_mall_seller_payout_items to compute totals and breakdowns. Depending on the requested granularity, it may also incorporate data from shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_payment_methods, and snapshot tables like shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats or shopping_mall_payment_method_stats to provide richer analytical context.

The request body IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.IRequest allows callers to specify time windows (for example, a particular month or quarter), fee categories or types, minimum or maximum amounts, and grouping dimensions (such as by day, by order, or by fee category). The implementation must translate these criteria into safe, scoped queries that only touch records linked to the authenticated seller ID, ensuring strong tenant isolation. Any pagination, sorting, or aggregation options provided in the request are applied to the result set before returning it to the client.

The response body uses IPageIShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.ISummary to deliver a paginated collection of summarized fee analytics rows, each containing pre-computed metrics such as total fee amount, count of contributing transactions, and optional contextual data like fee rate or effective commission percentage. This design keeps the wire format efficient while still providing enough information for sellers to build dashboards, export reports, or perform reconciliation.

Security considerations require that only sellers (authorizationActors: ["seller"]) access this endpoint, and that fee data is always scoped to the authenticated seller. The operation is read-only, does not modify tables like shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges or shopping_mall_seller_earnings, and is intended to be used alongside operational endpoints on orders and payouts for deeper drill-down into specific transactions when needed.
operations.summary: Search and analyze ShoppingMall seller fee and commission metrics with flexible filters and aggregations.

requestBody.description: Filter, pagination, and aggregation options for querying seller fee and commission analytics.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of summarized seller fee analytics rows derived from ShoppingMall financial tables.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves analytics for seller subscription behavior in the shoppingMall platform. It is conceptually based on aggregating data from the seller subscription–related Prisma models, in particular the primary table `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` together with configuration from `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` and revenue/fee impact from `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`. The endpoint is designed as a read-only analytical query that returns computed metrics over time rather than raw subscription rows.

The operation supports complex analytical queries over seller subscription data, such as filtering by time range, subscription plan, seller, subscription status, and marketplace segment. It is implemented as a PATCH method to allow a structured JSON body with multiple optional filters, grouping options, and pagination instructions without overloading query string parameters.

The request body is represented by `IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.IRequest`, which encapsulates filter criteria (date ranges like subscription start/end windows, plan identifiers, seller identifiers, current vs historical status), aggregation dimensions (grouping by day, week, month, plan, or seller), and pagination/sorting for the resulting metric buckets. The response type `IPageIShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.ISummary` returns a paginated collection of metric summaries where each element summarizes subscription counts, active vs cancelled counts, churn metrics, and potentially revenue and fee aggregates associated with subscriptions in the chosen time and grouping scope.

This endpoint is read-only and does not modify `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` or related tables. It is intended primarily for internal analytics dashboards, admin operators, and possibly seller-performance backoffice tools. Since it is analytics-oriented and may operate over large data sets, the implementation should leverage efficient aggregation queries and appropriate database indexes over subscription timestamps, plan keys, and seller identifiers.
operations.description:
Retrieve analytical statistics about seller subscriptions on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation provides a flexible analytics interface over the seller subscription domain, which in the database is primarily modeled by the `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` table together with `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` and `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`. While the underlying tables store atomic facts such as individual subscription records, plan metadata, and associated fees, this API exposes higher-level metrics such as how many sellers are subscribed to each plan, how subscriptions evolve over time, and how churn or upgrades behave across different seller segments.

The request body structure `IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.IRequest` allows clients to specify rich filters and analytical dimensions. Typical filters include subscription creation or activation date ranges, cancellation or expiry windows, plan codes or identifiers, seller identifiers or seller segments, and subscription lifecycle status (e.g., active, cancelled, expired). Analytical options can include grouping by calendar period (day, week, month), by subscription plan, by seller, or by combinations of these dimensions. It may also include options to restrict results to specific marketplaces or regions when the schema models such attributes. Pagination and sorting fields help clients navigate large result sets in a consistent way.

The response `IPageIShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.ISummary` returns a paginated list of summary metric objects. Each summary row typically includes identifiers for the grouping keys (such as period and plan), counts of new subscriptions, active subscriptions at the end of the period, cancellations and expirations, churn rates, and potentially derived measures such as monthly recurring revenue or average subscription duration computed from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` and related fee records. These summaries are intended for dashboard tiles, time-series charts, and tabular analytics views rather than direct transaction-level detail.

Security-wise, this endpoint exposes sensitive operational metrics about seller behavior and platform revenue, so it should be restricted to administrative or internal analytics actors. In this specification we use a generic `admin` actor, with the expectation that the actual implementation layer will enforce role-based access control based on the `shopping_mall_admins`, roles, and permissions models. The operation is read-only—no mutation of subscription or billing data occurs, and callers cannot influence subscription state through this API. Errors should be returned when invalid filter combinations are provided (such as an end date earlier than a start date) or when the requested grouping or sorting fields are not supported by the analytics engine.

Related operations may include more detailed subscription listings for individual sellers or plans, as well as other analytics endpoints that cover seller earnings, payouts, and performance snapshots. Together, these APIs enable a comprehensive analytical view of the seller subscription lifecycle within the shoppingMall ecosystem.
operations.summary: Retrieve aggregated analytics for seller subscriptions based on shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions and related tables.

requestBody.description: Filter, grouping, and pagination criteria for computing seller subscription analytics over shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions and related models.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves analytics about seller inventory adjustments in the shoppingMall platform. It is conceptually based on aggregating data from the `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments` primary table in combination with reference data such as `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons`, SKU definitions from `shopping_mall_skus`, and warehouse information from `shopping_mall_seller_warehouses`. The endpoint is a read-only analytical query that returns aggregated metrics derived from adjustments rather than individual adjustment records.

The endpoint uses the PATCH HTTP method to accept a complex JSON request body, modeled as `IShoppingMallSellerInventoryAdjustmentAnalytics.IRequest`. This request allows clients to specify filters such as date ranges (e.g., when adjustments occurred), seller identifiers, warehouse identifiers, SKU identifiers, and adjustment reason codes. It also supports configuring aggregation dimensions—for example grouping by time bucket, seller, warehouse, adjustment reason, or SKU category—as well as pagination and sorting parameters for navigating large analytics result sets.

The response body type `IPageIShoppingMallSellerInventoryAdjustmentAnalytics.ISummary` represents a paginated list of analytical summary rows. Each summary row aggregates metrics such as total quantity increased and decreased, net inventory change, number of adjustment events, and breakdowns by reason types (e.g., damage, shrinkage, manual correction, inbound receipt normalization) as recorded in `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments` and its related reason and SKU tables. This endpoint is designed for dashboards and reports that help sellers and admins understand inventory health, operational efficiency, and loss drivers across products and warehouses.

As a read-only analytics endpoint, it does not perform any mutation on `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments` or underlying master data. Implementation must favor efficient querying strategies, using indexes on timestamps, seller identifiers, warehouses, SKUs, and reason codes, and may rely on materialized views or snapshot tables for high-volume deployments.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated analytics for seller inventory adjustments recorded in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments` table as its primary fact source. That schema stores atomic inventory change events for combinations of seller, SKU, and warehouse, along with metadata such as the adjustment quantity delta, timestamp, and linkage to a standardized reason from `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons`. By aggregating these events rather than returning raw rows, this API enables stakeholders to understand patterns such as how often manual corrections are needed, which warehouses experience high shrinkage, or which SKUs frequently require damage adjustments.

The request model `IShoppingMallSellerInventoryAdjustmentAnalytics.IRequest` encapsulates rich filtering and grouping capabilities. Typical parameters include an adjustment timestamp range, seller IDs or seller segments, warehouse identifiers from `shopping_mall_seller_warehouses`, SKU identifiers from `shopping_mall_skus`, and specific adjustment reason codes. Clients may also specify aggregation dimensions such as grouping by day, week, month, seller, warehouse, adjustment reason, or SKU. Pagination controls and sorting options are included so that results can be consumed efficiently by dashboards or exported in multiple pages if necessary.

The response type `IPageIShoppingMallSellerInventoryAdjustmentAnalytics.ISummary` delivers a paginated collection of summary objects, each representing an aggregated analytics bucket for the chosen dimension(s). Fields in each summary typically include keys for the grouping dimensions (e.g., period, seller, warehouse, reason, SKU), total adjustment event count, total increased quantity, total decreased quantity, net quantity change, and potentially derived metrics like average adjustment size. These metrics are computed over the filtered subset of `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments` and are meant to be consumed by admin backoffice tools, seller performance dashboards, and risk or audit teams.

From a security perspective, this endpoint exposes potentially sensitive operational data about inventory movement and irregularities. Therefore, access should be restricted to administrative or internal analytics actors. In this specification, we model this as `authorizationActors: ["admin"]`, with the understanding that the implementation will enforce finer-grained roles and permissions using the admin and RBAC tables such as `shopping_mall_admins`, `shopping_mall_admin_roles`, and related assignments. The API is strictly read-only. It must validate that requested filters and groupings are supported and return appropriate errors for invalid combinations or malformed date ranges. Related endpoints may include more detailed inventory adjustment listings or seller performance snapshots that complement this analytics view.
operations.summary: Retrieve aggregated analytics for seller inventory adjustments based on shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments and related tables.

requestBody.description: Filter, grouping, and pagination criteria for computing seller inventory adjustment analytics over shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments and related models.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of seller inventory adjustment analytics summaries computed from shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments and related models.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of administrator role definitions from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. The `shopping_mall_admin_roles` model is the primary master table for RBAC roles in the shoppingMall platform, providing human-readable codes and names that are assigned to admin accounts through role-assignment tables. This endpoint is designed primarily for governance and platform-operations use cases where administrators need to browse, search, and audit available admin roles.

The operation is implemented as a collection search endpoint using the HTTP PATCH method at path `/adminRoles`. It accepts a structured search payload of type `IShoppingMallAdminRole.IRequest`, which encapsulates filtering conditions (for example by role code, role name, activation status, or creation date), pagination controls (page index, page size), and sorting options (for example sort by code or createdAt). The response is a paginated result of role summaries using `IPageIShoppingMallAdminRole.ISummary`, optimized for grid/table listings in an admin console UI.

Although the underlying table may contain detailed metadata such as descriptions, internal flags, and audit fields, the summary DTO is expected to expose only the fields necessary for listing, avoiding over-exposure of internal-only attributes. This endpoint does not modify any data; it only reads from `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. It is intended for use by authenticated admin actors and will typically be combined in the front end with the detail endpoint `GET /adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}` for drill-down into a specific role definition.

The business logic for this operation should enforce authorization so that only platform administrators (or equivalent high-privilege actors) can call it. It should also apply safe defaults for pagination and maximum page size to protect database performance. When filters are invalid or inconsistent (for example, malformed code patterns), the implementation must return clear validation errors rather than silently ignoring them.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of administrative role definitions from the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table.

This endpoint allows privileged platform operators to search, filter, and page through the set of admin roles that exist in the shoppingMall RBAC configuration. Each admin role in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` typically has a stable, human-readable code, a descriptive name, and additional metadata such as descriptions, priority, or status fields that are used to control what permissions are groupable and assignable to admin users. The response type `IPageIShoppingMallAdminRole.ISummary` is expected to focus on the key identification attributes needed for list views, such as the role code, name, and high-level status.

Because this operation reads sensitive configuration that governs which administrators can perform which actions, it must be restricted to high-privilege actors only. The `authorizationActors` field is therefore set to `["admin"]`, indicating that only authenticated admin accounts are allowed to access this endpoint. Fine-grained permission checks can then be implemented based on additional admin-permission tables, ensuring that only certain roles can manage RBAC configuration.

The request payload uses `IShoppingMallAdminRole.IRequest` to capture search criteria, pagination, and sorting instructions. Typical filters might include exact or prefix matching on `adminRoleCode`, partial matching on role name, and date-range filters on creation or update timestamps. Implementations should validate the shape and allowed values of these filters before executing queries, returning descriptive errors for unsupported combinations. Pagination parameters (such as `page`, `limit`, or `offset`) must be honored to avoid returning unbounded result sets.

This operation is commonly used together with the detail retrieval endpoint `GET /adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}`, which allows an admin to click into a specific role from the list and see its full configuration. UI flows may call this list endpoint repeatedly as users adjust search filters, change sort order, or navigate between pages. Any server-side errors, such as database connectivity issues or unexpected filter combinations, should be surfaced with clear error messages and appropriate HTTP status codes while never exposing internal implementation details.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of admin roles from shopping_mall_admin_roles

requestBody.description: Search filters, pagination, and sorting options for listing admin roles from shopping_mall_admin_roles.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of admin role summary records matching the provided filters.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the detailed definition of a single administrator role from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_admin_roles`, identified by its globally unique business code. The `shopping_mall_admin_roles` model represents RBAC role definitions for the shoppingMall platform, including a stable `code` field (here exposed as `adminRoleCode`), human-readable name, descriptions, and any additional configuration fields that describe the role's purpose and scope.

The endpoint is exposed as `GET /adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}` and returns a single role object of type `IShoppingMallAdminRole`. The use of `adminRoleCode` rather than an internal numeric or UUID identifier aligns with the requirement to prefer human-readable unique codes when the Prisma model defines a unique `code` column, making URLs more meaningful and easier to work with in admin tools and documentation.

This operation is read-only and is typically used by admin consoles when an operator selects a role from a list view to inspect or edit its configuration. It reads from `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and may also be used in conjunction with subsidiary tables such as admin role assignments or admin permissions, although those relationships are not directly part of this response DTO and can be fetched via separate endpoints if needed.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full definition of a specific admin role from the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table using its unique role code.

This endpoint is designed for high-privilege administrative use cases where an operator needs to inspect the configuration of an existing RBAC role. Each role in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` is expected to have a unique business identifier code, exposed here as the `adminRoleCode` path parameter. The system uses this code to look up the corresponding row and returns an `IShoppingMallAdminRole` DTO containing detailed information such as the role's name, descriptions, and any status or metadata fields defined in the schema.

Security is critical for this operation because admin roles control what actions administrators can perform. Access is therefore restricted to admin actors, as reflected by `authorizationActors: ["admin"]`. Implementations should further enforce fine-grained RBAC checks to ensure that only admins with appropriate permissions can view RBAC configuration. If the supplied `adminRoleCode` does not correspond to any existing role, the endpoint must return a clear not-found error (for example, HTTP 404) without revealing internal database details.

This detail operation is typically used alongside the list/search endpoint `PATCH /adminRoles`, which allows admins to find roles of interest. From a UI standpoint, an operator might search for a role by name or code, select it from the list, and then use this endpoint to display the full role configuration, including fields that are not shown in the summary list. Any validation errors related to the path parameter, such as invalid encoding or disallowed characters, should be handled gracefully with informative error messages.
operations.summary: Get detailed information for a single admin role from shopping_mall_admin_roles by code
