operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated daily sales statistics for the shoppingMall platform over a specified date range.

This operation focuses on analytical data rather than a single transactional row. Internally, it composes information from primary business entities like orders, order items, and payments to compute metrics such as total order count, total gross merchandise value (GMV), net revenue after refunds, and average order value per day. These computations rely on the fields and status lifecycles defined in the Prisma models for orders and payments, but the result is exposed as a denormalized statistics DTO rather than raw rows.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is restricted to administrative or internal analytics users. The authorizationActors field is therefore set to ["admin"], and additional permission checks can be implemented in business logic to ensure that only users with appropriate governance or finance roles can access sensitive financial summaries. Rate limiting and caching are recommended because the operation may involve heavy aggregations over large datasets.

The response body uses the IShoppingMallSalesByDayStatistics type, which encapsulates an array or collection of per-day metric objects alongside metadata such as the applied date range and time zone normalization rules. If requested date ranges are invalid (for example, endDate before startDate or too wide a range), the operation should return a validation error. If no data exists for part of the requested range, the implementation may either return zero-filled days or omit those days, depending on business reporting requirements.
operations.summary: Get aggregated daily sales statistics computed from shoppingMall transactional tables.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Inclusive start date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD). When omitted, the implementation may default to a recent period such as the last 30 days.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Inclusive end date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD). When omitted, the implementation may default to the current date.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: Optional IANA time zone identifier (for example, Asia/Seoul or UTC) that determines how order timestamps are bucketed into calendar days. If omitted, the system default time zone is used.

responseBody.description: Aggregated daily sales metrics for the requested date range, including per-day counts and monetary totals.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation returns daily seller performance metrics for the shoppingMall platform, aggregating data per seller per day across underlying tables such as shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_seller_earnings, and shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats. It is an analytical endpoint that does not expose raw transactional rows but instead provides a structured summary suitable for dashboards and monitoring tools.

For each day in the requested period and for each seller included by filter criteria, the system computes indicators such as total orders handled, items sold, gross merchandise value (GMV), net earnings after commissions and refunds, cancellation and refund rates, and possibly performance KPIs derived from snapshot tables like shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats. These metrics are exposed through the IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceByDayStatistics DTO, which is a dedicated analytical view.

The operation supports optional filtering via query string, including date range filters and optional seller identifiers (for example, sellerCode or sellerId), enabling both platform-wide overviews and single-seller drill-down views. The implementation must enforce validation on input parameters and reasonable limits on the number of sellers and the length of the time window to control query cost.
operations.description:
Retrieve daily performance statistics for one or more sellers on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation aggregates data by seller and day to provide a time series of performance indicators such as orders processed, items sold, gross and net revenues, commissions charged, refund counts, and refund ratios. It composes data from transactional and financial tables (including orders, order items, and seller earnings) as well as any existing seller_daily_stats snapshot tables, combining them into a single response optimized for reporting and dashboards.

From an authorization perspective, access is restricted to administrative users who require a cross-seller view of marketplace health, or to internal operations teams responsible for governance and performance management. Therefore, authorizationActors is set to ["admin"]. Seller-level dashboards visible to individual sellers should typically be implemented through a separate, seller-scoped endpoint that applies additional filters based on the authenticated seller identity.

The response type IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceByDayStatistics is a computed DTO that includes a collection of per-seller, per-day metric objects, plus summary metadata for the requested period. Input validation should ensure that the date range is valid and that any provided seller identifiers correspond to existing sellers. If no metrics exist for the given filters, the endpoint should respond successfully with an empty collection rather than an error, signaling that there was simply no activity in the requested window.
operations.summary: Get aggregated daily performance statistics for sellers on the shoppingMall platform.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Inclusive start date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD). When omitted, a sensible default such as the last 30 days may be used.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Inclusive end date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD). When omitted, the implementation may default to the current date.

parameters.name: sellerId
parameters.description: Optional identifier of a specific seller whose performance should be analyzed. If omitted, the operation returns performance metrics for all sellers, potentially with internal limits or pagination applied by implementation.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: Optional IANA time zone identifier (for example, Asia/Seoul or UTC) that determines how timestamps are bucketed into calendar days for performance computation. If omitted, the system default time zone is used.

responseBody.description: Aggregated daily seller performance metrics for the requested date range and seller filters.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves daily customer activity statistics for the shoppingMall platform. It is conceptually based on snapshot and analytics tables such as shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats, shopping_mall_order_daily_stats, and related aggregates, but it does not expose raw rows from those tables directly. Instead, it returns a computed view that summarizes per-day metrics that are useful for business monitoring dashboards.

For each calendar day in the requested range, the operation returns metrics like number of newly registered customers, number of active customers who performed at least one meaningful action (such as placing an order or adding items to cart), total orders placed by customers, gross merchandise value (GMV) attributed to customer orders, and potentially ancillary engagement metrics derived from the underlying snapshot tables. The response is structured as a list of daily records ordered by date, suitable for feeding admin analytics UIs or reporting tools.

This endpoint is read-only and designed primarily for administrative and analytical use. It does not manipulate any underlying snapshot or transactional tables; instead, it performs SELECT queries and aggregations across snapshot tables like shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats and shopping_mall_order_daily_stats. The implementation should ensure that any joins or aggregations are efficient and leverage existing snapshot structures rather than computing everything from raw transactional data on the fly for large ranges.
operations.description:
Retrieve time-series statistics that describe how customers behave on the shoppingMall platform on a day-by-day basis.

This operation is intended for analytics and dashboards. It allows authorized administrative actors to fetch, for a given date range, per-day metrics that summarize customer behavior at the marketplace level. Typical metrics derived from snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats and shopping_mall_order_daily_stats include newly registered customers, returning active customers, number of customers who placed at least one order, number of orders placed, and gross merchandise value (GMV) generated by those orders. Additional metrics like average order value per active customer or engagement ratios may also be computed from the same snapshots without exposing individual customer records.

From a security and permissions standpoint, this endpoint should be restricted to administrative users because it exposes sensitive, platform-wide business performance data. The operation does not return personally identifiable information about individual customers; it returns only aggregated, per-day statistics. Still, rate limiting and access control are important to prevent abuse and to ensure that only authorized staff can access business KPIs.

The operation conceptually relies on snapshot-oriented Prisma models such as shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats and shopping_mall_order_daily_stats, which store per-day aggregates of counts and monetary values rather than raw events. These tables are populated by offline or near-real-time jobs, and the API simply reads them. No POST, PUT, or DELETE APIs are provided for these snapshot tables, in accordance with the requirement that system-generated analytical data is not manually manipulated through APIs.

Administrators can combine this endpoint with other analytics APIs, such as campaign performance or refund and dispute statistics, to form a holistic view of marketplace health. For example, GET /statistics/customerActivityByDay can be used alongside GET /statistics/campaignPerformanceByDay to understand whether specific campaigns are driving sustainable customer activity or only short-lived spikes. Error handling should include validation of date ranges and clear responses when no data exists for a requested period.
operations.summary: Retrieve daily customer activity statistics based on shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats and related snapshot tables.

responseBody.description: Time-series of daily customer activity statistics over the requested period, including counts of new and active customers, order counts, and GMV aggregated per day.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves daily marketing and campaign performance statistics for the shoppingMall platform. It is conceptually associated with snapshot and analytics tables such as shopping_mall_campaign_metrics and shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots, which store pre-aggregated metrics per campaign and date, rather than exposing individual impressions or click events.

For each day in the requested period, and for each active or relevant marketing campaign, the operation returns metrics such as impressions, clicks, click-through rate (CTR), conversions (for example, orders attributed to the campaign), conversion rate, attributed revenue or GMV, and possibly cost-related metrics if available in the underlying snapshot tables. The goal is to provide a compact, analytics-ready structure that powers marketing dashboards and reporting tools without requiring the client to perform complex SQL across multiple tables.

Like other analytics endpoints, this operation is read-only. It does not modify the underlying Prisma models such as shopping_mall_campaign_metrics. Instead, it reads snapshot rows and aggregates them into a normalized API response structure, ensuring that all type names follow the IShoppingMall prefix conventions. It is designed to scale for typical date ranges used in dashboards (for example, the last 30, 90, or 365 days) and should be implemented using efficient indexed queries over the snapshot tables.
operations.description:
Fetch day-by-day campaign performance statistics for marketing and pricing campaigns on the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint provides administrative users with a structured time-series view of how each campaign performs over time. Data is sourced from snapshot-style Prisma models such as shopping_mall_campaign_metrics and potentially shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots, which aggregate lower-level events and transactional data into daily metrics. The returned statistics can include impressions, clicks, click-through rate (CTR), conversions or orders attributed to the campaign, conversion rates, attributed GMV or revenue, and other derived KPIs based on the snapshot schema.

From a security and governance perspective, access to this endpoint should be restricted to administrative actors because it exposes sensitive business performance data about campaigns, costs, and revenues. The endpoint returns aggregated KPIs only and does not reveal personally identifiable user information or raw event-level data. Proper authorization checks, combined with rate limiting, should be applied to prevent misuse.

The endpoint is tightly coupled with snapshot tables like shopping_mall_campaign_metrics, which are populated by background jobs or external analytics pipelines. No write operations are exposed for these models, in line with the principle that system-generated analytics data must not be directly modified by external clients. Implementers should ensure that queries are optimized with appropriate indexes and that any filtering or grouping by campaign identifier and date is performed on the server side.

This operation is often used alongside other statistics endpoints, such as GET /statistics/customerActivityByDay, to correlate campaign performance with overall customer behavior and platform KPIs. Error handling should clearly indicate when requested campaigns or date ranges have no data, allowing clients to handle empty responses gracefully in dashboards.
operations.summary: Retrieve daily campaign performance statistics based on shopping_mall_campaign_metrics and related snapshot tables.

responseBody.description: Time-series of daily campaign performance statistics per campaign over the requested period, including impressions, clicks, conversions, revenue, and derived KPIs.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves daily payment method performance statistics for the shoppingMall platform, aggregating data from snapshot-oriented reporting tables such as `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` and potentially other payment-related entities like `shopping_mall_order_payments`, `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`, and `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`. It is designed as a read-only analytical endpoint that exposes precomputed or on-the-fly aggregated metrics per payment method per day, such as total transaction count, gross volume, net revenue after refunds, refund rate, chargeback rate, and failure ratios.

The endpoint is modeled as a simple GET operation without a request body because the primary filter dimension is the calendar date, which can be expressed through query parameters (for example, a specific day or a date range). The response contract is expressed using a DTO named `IShoppingMallPaymentMethodPerformanceByDay`, which represents a denormalized view of multiple underlying tables rather than a single Prisma model. Internally, these metrics will typically be computed by grouping payment data by payment method and date using SQL aggregations over the payment-related models.

From a business perspective, this endpoint supports operations, finance, and risk teams in tracking how each payment method performs over time, identifying underperforming methods, and monitoring refund and chargeback behavior. Because it operates on aggregated data and snapshot tables, it is strictly read-only and does not expose or allow any modification of system-generated records.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated payment method performance metrics per day for the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint returns analytical statistics that are conceptually based on the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` snapshot model and related payment entities such as `shopping_mall_payment_methods`, `shopping_mall_order_payments`, and `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`. The snapshot table is described as "Daily aggregated metrics per payment method", meaning that for each payment method and day, the system records precomputed counts and monetary totals. The API surfaces those aggregates in a convenient, report-friendly format, without exposing the raw transactional rows. Each item in the response corresponds to a particular payment method on a particular business date, including fields such as the payment method identifier or code, the reference date, total number of payments, total authorized amount, settled volume, refund amounts, refund count, chargeback count, and any KPIs derived from these values such as refund rate or chargeback rate.

Because this data is derived from payment and refund tables that include sensitive financial information, the endpoint is restricted to administrative actors responsible for operations, finance, or risk oversight. Raw card or account details are never included; instead, only business metrics and method-level aggregates are returned. Implementation should ensure that access is audited and that the underlying queries respect any data retention or legal hold constraints that may be defined through models like `shopping_mall_legal_holds` or `shopping_mall_risk_cases`.

The operation is read-only and does not accept a request body. Any filtering by date, payment method, or other dimensions should be implemented as query parameters in the controller and translated into WHERE conditions over the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` snapshot and its related dimension tables. Errors should be returned when the requested date range is too wide for performance or if provided filter values are invalid or refer to non-existent payment methods. Related operations include daily order statistics and other KPI snapshots such as those in `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, which can be combined by client applications to build comprehensive dashboards.
operations.summary: Retrieve daily payment method performance statistics from snapshot-based shopping_mall_payment_method_stats data.

responseBody.description: Daily performance metrics per payment method over the requested period, derived from snapshot tables and payment-related entities.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves daily shipping performance statistics for the shoppingMall platform, aggregating data from reporting and snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` together with core fulfillment entities like `shopping_mall_shipments`, `shopping_mall_shipment_events`, and `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`. It exposes a read-only analytical view per shipping method and per day, including metrics such as shipment count, on-time delivery rate, average transit time, late delivery count, cancellation count, and possibly re-delivery attempts.

The API is implemented as a GET endpoint without a request body, because the primary way clients interact with it is by specifying date ranges or high-level filters through query parameters. Its response schema is modeled as `IShoppingMallShippingPerformanceByDay`, which represents a denormalized, analytical DTO rather than a direct representation of any single Prisma model. Internally, the service will typically query `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`, a snapshot table described as holding "Daily aggregated shipping and delivery performance metrics, optionally per shipping method", and join it with `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` to enrich results with human-readable metadata.

From a business standpoint, this endpoint enables operations and logistics teams to monitor shipping quality across carriers and methods, quickly identify problematic lanes or partners, and ensure that the marketplace meets its service-level expectations. Because it uses aggregated and historical data, the operation does not modify any records and is safe to call frequently by dashboards and reporting tools.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated shipping and delivery performance metrics per day for each shipping method on the shoppingMall platform.

The underlying data is primarily sourced from the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` snapshot model, which provides "Daily aggregated shipping and delivery performance metrics, optionally per shipping method". Each snapshot row typically contains a business date, a reference to a shipping method, and precomputed metrics such as the number of shipments initiated, number of shipments delivered, percentage delivered on or before the promised date, average delivery duration, and counts of delivery failures or exceptions. Additional contextual information about shipping methods comes from the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` model, while event-level details such as status changes and tracking scans are recorded in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` and `shopping_mall_shipments`.

Access to this endpoint should generally be restricted to administrative and operations roles, as it exposes operational performance data that may be sensitive from a commercial or contractual perspective. The response never includes customer PII or order-level details; instead it focuses on aggregated KPIs needed for performance management, SLA tracking, and continuous improvement initiatives. Usage of these statistics may also be subject to governance constraints defined in tables such as `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` and `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`, which determine how on-time performance and SLA breaches are interpreted.

The operation does not accept a request body; clients specify the reporting date or date window via query parameters, which should be validated for reasonable bounds. The service implementation should optimize queries against `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` to ensure fast response times even when the platform has accumulated many years of data. Errors should be returned if filters are invalid or if the requested range exceeds configured limits. This endpoint is commonly used alongside other KPI snapshot APIs such as platform-level KPIs in `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots` and order statistics in `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats` to provide a holistic operational dashboard.
operations.summary: Retrieve daily shipping and delivery performance statistics from shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats snapshot data.

responseBody.description: Daily shipping performance metrics per shipping method and day over the requested period.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves daily aggregated statistics related to refunds and disputes for the entire shoppingMall platform. It is primarily backed by the snapshot table `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`, which stores precomputed, day-level metrics derived from operational tables such as `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, `shopping_mall_disputes`, `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`, and related histories.

The endpoint exposes a read-only, analytical view optimized for dashboards and reporting. Clients can use it to show trends of refund volume, refund amounts, dispute counts, and other dispute-related KPIs over a date range. Because this operates on a snapshot/analytic model, there are no write operations; the data is populated by background jobs or ETL processes and only queried via this API.

The operation is implemented as a `GET` without a request body. It allows optional query parameters for the date range and simple filtering (for example, limiting to a specific seller or customer segment if such dimensions exist in the snapshot schema). The response returns a list of daily records in chronological order using the DTO type `IShoppingMallRefundAndDisputeStats.ISummary`, with each element representing a single day’s aggregated metrics.
operations.description:
Retrieve a time series of daily refund and dispute statistics aggregated at the platform level.

This operation reads from the Prisma model `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`, which is documented as a snapshot table providing daily aggregated statistics for refund and dispute activity across the platform. While the exact fields are defined in the Prisma schema, they typically include a business date, counts of refund requests opened and closed on that date, refund amounts by status, counts of disputes created and resolved, and potentially platform-level ratios or rates derived from underlying transactional tables such as `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`, and `shopping_mall_disputes`.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is designed for administrative and operational reporting rather than end-user consumption. The `authorizationActors` field should therefore restrict access to an administrative actor such as `admin`. Business logic in the service layer can additionally enforce that only appropriately privileged operators can view platform-wide KPIs that might reveal sensitive commercial information, such as total refund volume or dispute rates per day.

The relationship to the underlying database entities is entirely read-only. The snapshot table `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` is populated by backend batch jobs or streaming analytics pipelines that aggregate data from primary order, payment, refund, and dispute tables. This endpoint never creates, updates, or deletes snapshot rows; it only queries them. The query uses the business date range parameters to filter the snapshot table and returns the results ordered by date so that clients can easily render charts.

In terms of validation rules and business logic, the endpoint validates that provided date query parameters, if any, are well-formed and represent a valid range (for example, `fromDate` not after `toDate`). If no dates are supplied, a sensible default range such as the last 30 days can be applied in the implementation. If the requested range is excessively large, the service may cap it or apply pagination to protect performance.

This operation is typically used together with other analytics endpoints such as the platform KPI analytics described at `/analytics/platformKpis`. A dashboard might first call this endpoint to render a line chart of daily refund and dispute KPIs, and then call `/analytics/platformKpis` to retrieve a broader set of aggregated platform indicators for the same time period. Error handling includes returning an empty list when no snapshot data exists for the specified range and using standard HTTP error responses when query parameters are invalid or when the caller lacks sufficient permissions.
operations.summary: Retrieve daily platform-level refund and dispute statistics from the shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats snapshot table.

parameters.name: fromDate
parameters.description: Inclusive start date for the statistics range, in ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date format. When provided, only `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` rows with a business date on or after this value are returned.

parameters.name: toDate
parameters.description: Inclusive end date for the statistics range, in ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date format. When provided, only `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` rows with a business date on or before this value are returned. Must not be earlier than `fromDate` when both are specified.

responseBody.description: List of daily refund and dispute statistics records for the specified date range, each summarized as a single day-level snapshot derived from `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. The array may be empty if no data exists for the given range.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated platform-level KPIs for the shoppingMall marketplace using the snapshot table `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`. Unlike the more granular day-by-day statistics exposed via `/statistics/refundAndDisputeByDay`, this endpoint focuses on higher-level, possibly multi-metric KPI bundles that can drive executive dashboards and monitoring views.

The underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots` is a snapshot table that stores precomputed KPIs over specific reporting periods. Each snapshot row may contain metrics such as total GMV, order counts, active customers and sellers, refund ratios, dispute rates, conversion metrics, and other key performance indicators defined by business stakeholders. The exact set of fields is specified in the Prisma schema and must be respected by the DTO `IShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot` and its variants.

The endpoint is implemented as a `PATCH` operation to allow complex filter criteria in the request body via the DTO `IShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot.IRequest`. Clients can specify filters such as snapshot period (daily, weekly, monthly), date ranges, and possibly segment dimensions (for example, market, region, or channel) depending on the schema. The response returns a paginated collection using `IPageIShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot`, enabling clients to iterate over multiple KPI snapshot records if the result set is large.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve aggregated platform-level KPI snapshot records for the shoppingMall platform.

This operation reads from the Prisma model `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, which is defined as a snapshot table containing aggregated platform-level KPIs over arbitrary reporting periods. Fields in this model typically include a snapshot identifier or date, the type of period being summarized (for example, daily, weekly, or monthly), and a collection of numeric indicators such as total order volume, gross merchandise value, active customer and seller counts, refund ratios, dispute ratios, and other metrics important for monitoring the marketplace’s health.

From a security perspective, platform KPI data is normally reserved for administrative and analytical roles. The `authorizationActors` therefore restricts access to an `admin` actor. The implementation can further cross-check the authenticated admin’s roles and permissions, potentially backed by models such as `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`, to ensure that only authorized staff can see KPIs that may expose sensitive commercial information.

This endpoint uses a `PATCH` method with a request body of type `IShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot.IRequest` to support flexible search criteria. Clients can specify filters such as date ranges, snapshot period type, and other dimensions defined in the Prisma schema. The service layer translates these filters into queries against `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, applying ordering (for example, by snapshot date descending) and pagination. The response is a paginated object `IPageIShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot` that encapsulates both the KPI snapshot records and standard pagination metadata.

In typical usage, this operation is called by administrative dashboards or analytics tools. For example, an operations dashboard might call this endpoint to retrieve the latest daily KPI snapshot, while a reporting tool might query multiple monthly snapshots for a trend view. This endpoint complements more specialized statistical endpoints like `/statistics/refundAndDisputeByDay`, allowing dashboards to combine detailed per-metric time series with high-level KPI snapshots in a single UI.

Error handling includes validating that the search criteria in `IShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot.IRequest` are consistent (for instance, that the requested period type is supported and that date ranges are valid). When no KPI snapshots match the query, the endpoint returns an empty page with zero items, allowing clients to handle the absence of data gracefully without treating it as an error.
operations.summary: Search aggregated platform-level KPI snapshot records from the shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots snapshot table.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination options for filtering platform KPI snapshot records from `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, including period type, date ranges, and other dimensions as defined by the schema.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of platform-level KPI snapshot records matching the search criteria, derived from the `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots` snapshot table.

IShoppingMallCustomerJoin.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for a self-service customer registration (join) operation in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO collects the minimal credential and context information required to create a new row in the shopping_mall_customers table and to immediately establish a first authenticated session in shopping_mall_customer_sessions. It maps to the core identity columns while keeping sensitive persistence details such as password_hash internal to the backend.

The payload contains the email and plain text password that will be validated and transformed into the password_hash column, as well as connection metadata (ip, href, referrer) that is stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions for audit and security analysis. The ip value is optional because it can be derived by the server, while href and referrer are required business fields used for session context and marketing attribution.

email.description:
Unique email address the customer will use as their primary login identifier and for account-related communication.

This value is validated for proper email format and checked against the unique index on shopping_mall_customers.email to ensure no existing account already uses it. On success, it is persisted directly into the email column of the shopping_mall_customers row.

password.description:
Plain text password provided by the registering customer.

The backend hashes this value according to the platform’s credential policy and stores the result in the password_hash column of shopping_mall_customers. The raw password is never persisted and is only used transiently for hash generation and validation.

oneOf.description:
Client IP address observed when the customer initiates the join request.

When provided, this value is written into the ip column of a new shopping_mall_customer_sessions row for security auditing, anomaly detection, and regional analysis. If omitted or null, the server may infer the IP from the transport connection instead.

Client IP address in IPv6 format observed when the customer initiates the join request.

When provided, this value is written into the ip column of a new shopping_mall_customer_sessions row for security auditing, anomaly detection, and regional analysis. If omitted or null, the server may infer the IP from the transport connection instead.

Explicitly indicates that the client does not supply an IP address in the payload.

When null, the server is expected to infer the remote IP address from the underlying HTTP request instead of relying on this field.

ip.description:
Client IP address associated with the registration request.

This optional field is primarily used for security analytics, fraud detection, and geo-based risk scoring when creating a row in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.ip. When omitted or null, the backend derives the IP from the incoming connection metadata.

href.description:
Full URL (href) of the page where the customer began the registration flow.

This value is stored in the href column of shopping_mall_customer_sessions and provides contextual information for security reviews, marketing attribution, and behavioral analytics. It should be the exact browser URL, including query parameters, at the moment of joining.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the registration was initiated.

The value is written into the referrer column of shopping_mall_customer_sessions, enabling the platform to analyze traffic sources, detect unusual referral patterns, and support campaign attribution for new customer registrations.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized customer response DTO returned by authentication-related endpoints for the shoppingMall platform.

This schema represents the successful authentication state of a customer actor after join, login, or refresh operations that operate on the shopping_mall_customers table in combination with session and security metadata. It exposes only safe, high-level identity and token information while keeping internal security fields such as password_hash and low-level audit data hidden from clients.

The DTO is anchored by the customer’s primary key id and includes the current account status flags used by frontends to adapt user experience (for example preventing actions when suspended). It also contains an embedded authorization token structure that carries access and refresh tokens associated with a corresponding shopping_mall_customer_sessions record or equivalent server-side token store, allowing the client to perform subsequent authenticated requests on behalf of the customer.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated customer.

This value is the primary key from the shopping_mall_customers.id column and is used throughout the system as the stable reference for the customer account, including ownership of carts, orders, reviews, and security-related records.

email.description:
Email address of the authenticated customer account.

The value mirrors the email column in shopping_mall_customers and is the primary login identifier and notification channel used by the platform. It allows client applications to display the signed-in identity and manage account-level features such as email change flows.

status.description:
Current business status of the customer account.

This field corresponds to the status column in shopping_mall_customers and indicates whether the customer is active, suspended, blocked, or in another business-defined state. Clients may use it to conditionally enable or disable certain flows and to explain restrictions to the user in the interface.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the customer’s email address has completed the verification process.

This value reflects the email_verified column in shopping_mall_customers and is used by clients to prompt verification flows, gate features behind verified identities, or display badges and warnings in account-related UI components.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this customer.

The value is derived from shopping_mall_customers.last_login_at and provides an audit-friendly indicator for the last time the account was successfully authenticated through a login or equivalent flow.

Indicates that the customer has not successfully logged in yet.

This corresponds to a null value in shopping_mall_customers.last_login_at for accounts that have been created but have never completed a standard login cycle.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login associated with this customer account.

When present, it communicates the last known authentication activity from the shopping_mall_customers.last_login_at column. When null, it reflects that the account is newly created or has not yet logged in using standard login flows.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer account was created.

This field surfaces the created_at column from shopping_mall_customers and serves as the canonical account creation time for display in profile pages, audit trails, and support tooling.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer account record was last updated.

The value mirrors the updated_at column in shopping_mall_customers and changes whenever the core profile or authentication metadata is modified as part of regular account management or system operations.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the customer account when present.

When set, this value corresponds to the `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_customers` and indicates that the account has been logically removed from active use while references such as orders and reviews remain preserved.

Business processes and queries treat non-null `deleted_at` as a signal to exclude the account from most active user flows.

Null value indicating that the customer account is not soft-deleted.

Active and suspended accounts that remain part of the live system typically leave this column unset.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion marker for the customer account.

A non-null value indicates that the account has been logically deleted in accordance with business or compliance rules, while a null value means the account remains active in the logical data model.

Downstream queries and services consult this timestamp to exclude soft-deleted accounts from normal operations while retaining them for historical or legal purposes.

IShoppingMallCustomerLogin.IRequest.description:
Request payload for customer self-login.

Contains the customer's primary login identifier and password along with session context information required to establish a new shopping_mall_customer_sessions row. This DTO is used when a customer actively logs in with credentials, and therefore must include connection metadata (href and referrer, and optionally ip) for security auditing and risk analysis.

email.description:
Customer email address used as the unique login identifier.

Must correspond to the email column in shopping_mall_customers and is validated using standard email format rules.

password.description:
Plain text password provided by the customer for authentication.

This value is compared against the stored hashed password (e.g., password_hash) in shopping_mall_customers by the backend. Clients MUST NOT pre-hash this value.

oneOf.description:
Optional client IP address for the login attempt.

When provided, should represent the IP address of the customer initiating the login, in IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address for the login attempt.

When present, this value is stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.ip for security and auditing purposes. If omitted or null, the server may derive the IP from the HTTP request instead.

href.description:
Current page URL at the moment of login.

Captured in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.href to record the exact location from which the login was initiated (for example, a specific login page or redirect target).

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led the customer to the login page.

Captured in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.referrer to support security investigation, funnel analysis, and risk evaluation related to the login event.

IShoppingMallCustomerRefresh.IRequest.description:
Request payload for refreshing a customer authentication token.

Carries the refresh token previously issued to the customer during login or a prior refresh operation. The backend validates this token against server-side state (typically anchored to shopping_mall_customers and shopping_mall_customer_sessions) and, if valid, issues new JWT tokens without requiring credential re-entry.

refreshToken.description:
Refresh token issued to the customer during a prior authentication event.

This opaque string identifies the long-lived authentication state used to obtain new access tokens. It is validated against server-side session or token storage and must not be shared with untrusted parties.

IShoppingMallSellerAuthJoin.IRequest.description:
Request payload for seller self-registration on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents the data that a new seller submits when creating a seller account. It carries the seller’s login identifier and chosen password in plain text form, along with session context fields used to create an initial authentication session record.

It maps conceptually to the `shopping_mall_sellers` model for identity data and to `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` for connection metadata, but it does not expose any system-managed or security-sensitive storage fields such as `id`, `password_hash`, lifecycle timestamps, or status flags.

email.description:
Business contact email address that will be used as the unique login identifier for the seller.

This value maps to the `email` column of the `shopping_mall_sellers` table, which has a uniqueness constraint. The email must be normalized and must satisfy platform password and account policies regarding allowed domains and formatting.

password.description:
Plain text password chosen by the seller during registration.

The backend will validate this value against the platform’s password policy (minimum length, character classes, and other complexity rules) and then derive and store a secure `password_hash` in the `shopping_mall_sellers.password_hash` column. Clients must never send a pre-hashed password here; hashing is always handled server-side.

oneOf.description:
IPv4 address from which the seller initiates the join request.

This value is used as connection metadata when creating a row in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions.ip`. It may be populated by the client for SSR or proxy scenarios; if omitted, the backend can infer the IP from the transport layer.

IPv6 address from which the seller initiates the join request.

This alternative representation is also stored in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions.ip` for environments where IPv6 is used. The backend may normalize or validate this before persistence.

Null can be used when the client does not explicitly provide an IP value.

In this case, the backend is expected to determine the effective IP address from the incoming HTTP request metadata when creating the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` record.

ip.description:
Client-reported IP address associated with the join attempt.

This value participates in populating `shopping_mall_seller_sessions.ip` for the initial seller session created after successful registration. It is optional from the API perspective because the server can derive the IP from the connection, but providing it explicitly improves audit accuracy in proxied or SSR environments.

href.description:
Full URL of the page from which the seller initiated the registration request.

This value is written into `shopping_mall_seller_sessions.href` for the initial session. It enables downstream analytics, attribution, and security investigations by capturing the exact application route involved in the join flow.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL observed when the seller initiated registration.

This value is stored in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions.referrer` for the created session and is used to analyze traffic sources and detect unusual navigation patterns that may indicate abuse or fraud during seller onboarding.

IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized seller response returned from join, login, and refresh operations.

This DTO encapsulates the authenticated seller’s identity derived from the `shopping_mall_sellers` table, together with the authorization token bundle that the client must use for subsequent authenticated requests. It is the canonical shape of the response body for seller authentication flows and is produced by `/auth/seller/join`, `/auth/seller/login`, and `/auth/seller/refresh`.

The identity portion exposes only non-sensitive fields from `shopping_mall_sellers`, never including confidential storage fields such as `password_hash`. The token portion groups access and refresh tokens in a single object, allowing clients to manage session state while keeping token semantics clearly separated from seller profile data.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller account in the shoppingMall platform.

This corresponds to the primary key `id` column of the `shopping_mall_sellers` table. It is used as the stable subject identifier in JWTs and as the foreign key target for subordinate tables such as `shopping_mall_seller_sessions`, risk flags, and security events.

email.description:
Business contact email address of the seller.

This value mirrors the `email` column from `shopping_mall_sellers`, which acts as the unique login identifier for the seller. It is included here so that clients can confirm which account is currently authenticated and display the seller’s primary email address in account-related UI.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the seller account at the time the token was issued.

This value is derived from the `status` column in `shopping_mall_sellers`, which may contain states such as `pending_review`, `active`, `suspended`, or `terminated`. Clients can use it to adjust UI behavior (for example, warning suspended sellers) while enforcement of permissions remains a server-side responsibility.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the seller’s email address has completed the platform’s verification process.

This flag is sourced from the `email_verified` column of `shopping_mall_sellers`. It allows clients to prompt the seller to verify their email when required for certain operations, without exposing any underlying verification tokens or workflows.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the seller account record.

This property is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_sellers` and is automatically set by the system when the seller is first registered.

It is commonly used for auditing, analytics, and temporal filtering in reports.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the seller account record.

This field corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_sellers`. The system updates it whenever mutable attributes on the seller account change.

It is useful for synchronization workflows, cache invalidation, and operational monitoring.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the seller account, or null when the account is logically active.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column on `shopping_mall_sellers`. When non-null, it indicates that the seller account has been soft deleted or deactivated at the recorded moment in time.

Consumers should treat records with a non-null `deleted_at` as removed from normal operational flows while still preserving them for audit or legal purposes.

profile.description:
Extended profile information composed into the seller detail view.

This association represents the 1:1 relationship from `shopping_mall_sellers` to `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` and provides public-facing and operational profile attributes such as store name, description, and support contact channels.

Including the profile within the seller detail DTO allows administrative and backoffice clients to retrieve core account data and profile information in a single atomic read operation without issuing separate profile queries.

IShoppingMallSellerAuthLogin.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for seller login on the shopping mall platform.

Carries the seller’s login identifier and plaintext password, along with session context metadata used to create a `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` record. The password will be verified against the `password_hash` column in `shopping_mall_sellers`. The session fields are used to populate contextual columns such as `ip`, `href`, and `referrer` in the seller session table.

This DTO is used by the `/auth/seller/login` endpoint, which has `authorizationType: "login"` and `authorizationActor: null`, meaning it is a self-login operation and MUST include session context fields. The backend will never accept pre-hashed passwords here; it always expects the raw password string for verification and will not read any seller ID from the body.

email.description:
Seller’s login email address.

This value is used to look up the seller row in `shopping_mall_sellers` via the unique index on `shopping_mall_sellers.email`. It must be a syntactically valid email address and is treated as the primary login identifier for seller accounts.

password.description:
Plain-text password supplied by the seller for authentication.

The backend compares this value against the stored `password_hash` in `shopping_mall_sellers` using a secure password verification algorithm. Clients MUST NOT send pre-hashed passwords; hashing is handled entirely by the server.

This field is never stored or logged in plain text and is only used transiently for credential verification during the login request.

oneOf.description:
Client IP address for the login session, when explicitly provided by the client.

Represents the IP address from which the seller is attempting to log in. When present, this value may be recorded into the corresponding `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` row for security analytics and audit purposes.

If omitted or set to null, the server may derive the IP address from the underlying HTTP request metadata instead.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address associated with this login attempt.

When provided, it should contain a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address string. If null or absent, the server may attempt to infer the IP from the transport layer. This value is used for populating IP-related fields in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` and for later security analysis.

href.description:
Absolute URL of the page from which the seller initiated the login request.

This value is stored as part of the seller session context (for example in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions.href`) to support security investigations, UX analytics, and anomaly detection. It should be the full URL (including scheme, host, path, and query) of the current page where the login form was submitted.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led the seller to the login page.

Typically corresponds to the browser’s `document.referrer` value at the moment the login form is submitted. This value is used to populate referrer-related fields in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` and can assist in security investigations and traffic analysis.

If there is no referrer (for example, direct navigation), clients may send an empty string or a canonical placeholder URL according to frontend conventions.

IShoppingMallSellerAuthRefresh.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for refreshing seller authentication tokens using a long-lived refresh token.

This DTO is consumed by the `/auth/seller/refresh` endpoint, which has `authorizationType: "refresh"` and `authorizationActor: null`. The refresh token acts as the credential for this operation. The backend will validate the token, ensure the associated seller in `shopping_mall_sellers` is still active and not logically deleted, and may cross-check the corresponding `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` row for expiry or revocation.

Unlike the login request, this DTO does not include credentials such as email or password and does not require session context fields, because the session was already established during the original login or join operation.

refreshToken.description:
Opaque refresh token previously issued to the seller.

This token is used to derive the seller identity and session context without re-supplying email and password. It must be a valid, non-expired, non-revoked token generated by the authentication subsystem.

The backend will verify this token’s signature, expiration, and revocation status, then look up the underlying seller and session records before issuing new JWT tokens.

IShoppingMallAdminJoin.ICreate.description:
Data required to register a new shopping mall administrator account.

This DTO captures the business-facing registration fields for creating a record in the shopping_mall_admins table while establishing the initial admin authentication context. It is designed specifically for the POST /auth/admin/join operation and intentionally avoids exposing internal database columns such as password_hash or deleted_at.

The service layer maps this structure to the underlying Prisma model by hashing the provided plain-text password into the password_hash column, initializing lifecycle fields like status and email_verified according to platform policy, and populating created_at and updated_at with the current system time. This DTO is also responsible for carrying the session context fields (ip, href, referrer) necessary to create an initial row in shopping_mall_admin_sessions when the join operation implicitly logs the admin in and issues JWT tokens.

email.description:
Admin email address that serves as the unique login identifier.

This value is mapped to the email column of shopping_mall_admins and must be unique across all administrator accounts due to the unique index on that column. The join operation validates this constraint and rejects any attempt to reuse an existing email, returning an appropriate error to the client.

From a business perspective, this email is also used for administrative notifications and security communications such as password reset or account alerts.

password.description:
Plain-text password used to secure the administrator account.

The raw value supplied in this field is never stored directly in the database. Instead, the backend hashes it and persists the result into the password_hash column of shopping_mall_admins. This indirection allows the API contract to remain stable even if the password storage scheme changes.

Password strength rules, such as minimum length or required character classes, are enforced at the service layer based on platform security policies.

oneOf.description:
Client IP address recorded for the initial admin session.

When provided, this value is stored in the ip column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions and used for auditing, anomaly detection, and security investigations. It should contain a valid IPv4 or IPv6 representation of the remote address from which the join request originated.

Client IP address recorded for the initial admin session.

When provided, this value is stored in the ip column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions and used for auditing, anomaly detection, and security investigations. It should contain a valid IPv4 or IPv6 representation of the remote address from which the join request originated.

Null value when the server derives the IP address from the transport layer instead of the client payload.

When this variant is used, the backend infers the IP address from headers or connection metadata rather than trusting a client-supplied value.

ip.description:
Client IP address associated with the initial authentication session created during admin registration.

This field is mapped conceptually to the ip column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions and helps build a high-fidelity audit trail. It is optional because many deployments prefer to derive the IP server-side, but including it allows integration patterns such as SSR frontends or proxies that explicitly forward the originating address.

When omitted or set to null, the service can still populate the session IP using trusted request metadata.

href.description:
Full URL from which the admin registration request was initiated.

This value is recorded in the href column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions and provides precise context about the page or route where the join flow was completed. It is critical for auditing, troubleshooting misconfigurations, and analyzing abuse patterns across different entry points.

Clients should send the exact browser or frontend URL, including query parameters, to maintain an accurate session trail.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL observed when the admin initiated the registration flow.

This value is mapped to the referrer column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions and allows the platform to understand which page or external site directed the user into the join endpoint. It is useful for security review, campaign attribution, and detecting suspicious origin patterns.

If there was no referrer (for example, a direct navigation), clients may send an empty string or omit the field per frontend convention, but servers may normalize values according to their own logging strategy.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized administrator context returned after successful join, login, or refresh operations.

This DTO encapsulates both the logical administrator identity derived from `shopping_mall_admins` and the token information required for the admin to authenticate subsequent API calls. It is the standardized response type for `POST /auth/admin/join`, `POST /auth/admin/login`, and `POST /auth/admin/refresh`.

The structure now exposes the administrator identity in two complementary ways:

- A normalized `admin` association that reuses `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary` to provide a concise, reusable view of the admin entity and its relationships.
- A set of scalar fields (id, email, status, email_verified, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) that mirror key columns from `shopping_mall_admins` for backward compatibility and direct consumption by existing clients.

Sensitive database columns such as `password_hash` are never exposed. This DTO remains focused on identity, lifecycle state, and token information needed by frontends and middleware to manage authenticated admin sessions.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrator account.

This value corresponds to the `id` primary key column of `shopping_mall_admins` and uniquely identifies the admin across all backend subsystems. It is embedded in issued JWTs and used by downstream services to correlate actions, audit logs, and governance decisions with a specific administrator.

Clients should treat this identifier as opaque and never attempt to infer semantics from its value or format beyond it being a UUID.

email.description:
Email address of the authenticated administrator.

This field mirrors the `email` column of `shopping_mall_admins` and represents the primary login name and notification address for the admin. Exposing it in the authorization payload lets frontends display or confirm the identity currently logged in and can be used to prefill UI elements such as account settings forms.

The value is read‑only from the perspective of this DTO; changing an admin’s email is handled through dedicated profile or account management operations.

status.description:
Business status of the administrator account at the time of token issuance.

This value reflects the `status` column in `shopping_mall_admins` and communicates whether the admin is active, suspended, disabled, or in any other platform‑defined lifecycle state. It allows clients and middleware to adjust UI behavior or block sensitive actions if the account is not fully active.

The exact allowed literals are governed by business rules in the database and service layer; consumers should treat the string as descriptive state and avoid hard‑coding assumptions beyond documented enums.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the administrator’s email address has been verified.

This flag mirrors the `email_verified` column of `shopping_mall_admins` and is evaluated by authentication and governance flows to decide if additional verification steps are required before granting access to certain features. For example, an unverified admin might be forced through a verification process before modifying critical configuration.

Clients can use this field to prompt the user to complete verification workflows when necessary.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin account was created.

This property is mapped from the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table. It records the exact moment the admin record was first persisted and is typically stored in UTC as an ISO 8601 date‑time string.

Operational dashboards, audit tooling, and analytics features use this value to understand account age, onboarding cohorts, and historical governance changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the admin account record.

This field corresponds to the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model. The system updates it whenever mutable attributes of the admin are modified, providing a reliable indicator of the last configuration change.

Support agents and governance tools rely on this value to investigate when changes were applied and to reconcile with audit log entries.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account, or null when still active.

This property is derived from the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table. When the admin account has been logically deleted or deactivated under a soft‑delete policy, this field contains the date‑time of that action.

When the account is still logically active, the value is null. Business logic uses this field together with `status` to determine whether the admin should be treated as operational, archived, or subject to legal hold and retention constraints.

admin.description:
Summary view of the administrator account associated with this authorization context.

This association reuses `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary` to provide a normalized, lightweight representation of the admin entity derived from the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model. It contains the key identity, status, and lifecycle fields needed for dashboards, navigation headers, and audit user interfaces without exposing internal authentication details.

Consumers should prefer this nested `admin` object when they need to display or reason about the administrator entity itself, while the top‑level scalar fields remain available for backward compatibility and simpler integration scenarios.

IShoppingMallAdminLogin.ICreate.description:
Request payload for administrator login on the shopping mall platform.

This DTO carries the credential pair used to authenticate an existing admin account, along with session context metadata that will be persisted into the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. It is designed specifically for the POST /auth/admin/login operation and maps to the business behavior described for locating an admin by email and validating the supplied password against the stored password_hash.

The email field identifies the candidate admin record in shopping_mall_admins using its unique index. The password field contains the plain-text password that will be verified server-side; it never corresponds directly to the password_hash column and is not stored as-is. The ip, href, and referrer fields provide contextual information for session creation, filling the corresponding columns in shopping_mall_admin_sessions so that each login can be audited and analyzed for risk and abuse.

This type must be used only for credential-based authentication flows. It must not be reused for generic admin updates or profile changes, and it intentionally excludes any actor identity fields such as admin IDs, which are derived after authentication succeeds.

email.description:
Unique email address used as the primary login for the admin account.

This value is used to query the shopping_mall_admins table via its unique index on the email column to locate a candidate administrator record. The address must follow standard email formatting rules and should correspond to an internally managed admin identity, not a customer or seller account.

Authentication logic treats this field as case-insensitive according to business rules, but the original casing may still be stored for display purposes.

password.description:
Plain-text password submitted by the administrator for authentication.

The application uses this value only for verification against the stored password_hash column in the shopping_mall_admins table. It is never stored directly and is always processed through a secure password hashing routine on the server side.

Length and complexity requirements, such as minimum characters or required character classes, are enforced by the authentication service rather than encoded explicitly in this schema.

oneOf.description:
IPv4 address from which the admin initiated the login request.

This value is stored in the ip column of the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table when present and supports audit, risk analysis, and anomaly detection. The server may override or ignore any client-supplied value in favor of the network-level source IP it observes.

When omitted or null, the backend uses its own logic to resolve the effective IP address.

IPv6 address from which the admin initiated the login request.

Like the IPv4 representation, this value is mapped into the ip column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions for auditing and security analytics. The backend may normalize or replace the client-provided value based on trusted request metadata.

If neither IPv4 nor IPv6 is provided, the server falls back to its own derived client IP.

Null value indicating that the client does not explicitly provide an IP address.

In this case, the server determines the effective source IP for the session using transport-level metadata such as connection details or proxy headers, and still records that IP in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions.ip column.

This allows the API to remain flexible when clients cannot reliably provide an IP address directly.

ip.description:
Client IP address associated with the login attempt.

This optional field allows the caller to provide an explicit IP address which will be persisted into the ip column of the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. It supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats and is primarily used for audit and security analytics.

If null or omitted, the backend falls back to using the observed network source IP. Servers are free to ignore misleading client-provided values and rely on trusted connection metadata instead.

href.description:
Full URL at which the admin initiated the login.

This value is recorded in the href column of the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table so that each session can be traced back to the exact entry point in the administrative interface. It typically contains the absolute URL of the login page or application route from which the credential form was submitted.

Capturing this information assists in debugging, user support, and security investigations by showing the context in which the login occurred.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL present when the login request was made.

The authentication service persists this value into the referrer column of the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. It represents the page or external site that led the administrator to the login URL and is useful for analyzing navigation flows and detecting unusual access paths.

If the admin navigated directly to the login page, this may be an empty string or a canonical landing page URL depending on client behavior and configuration.

IShoppingMallAdminRefresh.ICreate.description:
Request payload for refreshing administrator JWT tokens using an existing session.

This DTO is used by the POST /auth/admin/refresh endpoint to rotate access and refresh tokens for an already authenticated admin, based on persisted state in the shopping_mall_admins and shopping_mall_admin_sessions tables. Instead of including credentials, it carries a refresh token that has been issued previously by the login or join flow.

The refreshToken field identifies the logical session and admin via metadata encoded within the token. The href and referrer fields provide additional context for the refresh request and can be used to update or create a corresponding session row in shopping_mall_admin_sessions, particularly for tracking where and how token rotation occurs. An optional ip field allows explicit client IP reporting, but servers may replace or ignore it in favor of trusted source information.

This type must not include any admin ID or session ID fields. The backend derives those from the presented refresh token and validates them against the current database state before issuing new tokens.

refreshToken.description:
Opaque refresh token string previously issued to the admin.

The authentication subsystem decodes or validates this token to recover identifiers that map to a specific admin row in shopping_mall_admins and a session row in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. It is treated as a sensitive credential and must be transported and stored securely by clients.

On receipt, the server checks that the associated session has not expired and that the underlying admin account remains eligible for access before issuing new tokens.

oneOf.description:
IPv4 address associated with the refresh request.

When provided, this value can be used to update or validate the ip context of the session in shopping_mall_admin_sessions, supporting risk analysis for token rotation activity. The server may normalize or override this value using its own connection metadata.

If omitted or null, the backend resolves the effective IP from the incoming request as usual.

IPv6 address associated with the refresh request.

Like the IPv4 representation, this value feeds into session audit data and may help detect anomalous refresh patterns. It is mapped to the ip column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions when accepted by the backend.

When not provided, the server uses its own view of the client IP address for session context.

Null value indicating that the client does not send an explicit IP address.

In this case the server determines and records the IP address from network-level metadata when updating or creating a session in shopping_mall_admin_sessions. This keeps the refresh operation robust when the client cannot accurately report an address.

Security policies still apply based on the server-resolved address.

ip.description:
Client IP address associated with the token refresh request.

This optional field mirrors the session context semantics of the login DTO. It can be recorded in the corresponding shopping_mall_admin_sessions row to track where refresh activity originates and to support anomaly detection.

If null or omitted, the server calculates the IP from the actual connection source. Implementations should treat any client-supplied IP as advisory only and prefer trusted transport metadata.

href.description:
Full URL at which the refresh request was initiated.

This value is used to enrich or update the session context in shopping_mall_admin_sessions, enabling operators to see which administrative views or front-end routes are responsible for token rotations. It typically reflects the URL of the page that silently or explicitly triggered the refresh.

Recording this information improves observability into how long-lived admin sessions behave in practice.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL present when the refresh call was made.

As with login, this value may be stored in the referrer column of shopping_mall_admin_sessions for visibility into navigation patterns associated with token rotation. It can indicate which part of the admin workflow led to the refresh event.

When the admin interacts directly from a bookmarked page or non-standard flow, this field helps reconstruct that context for audit and debugging purposes.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.IJoin.description:
Request payload for initializing a logical guest user identity in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by the public guest registration (join) endpoint to create a new row in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table without any password or email credentials. It captures optional correlation information that can be used to relate the guest identity to device or browser context, while leaving all system-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` to be populated by the backend.

The resulting guest identity can later be associated with sessions, security events, and risk flags through subsidiary tables, but those relations are not provided directly in this request body.

external_reference.description:
Optional external or device-based reference used to correlate guest sessions for this logical guest identity.

This value typically represents a cookie identifier, device fingerprint, or other correlation key collected on the client side under applicable privacy rules. The Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_guestusers` describes this column as an optional string intended for correlating guest sessions, and it is not required to be unique or globally meaningful.

Clients may omit this field entirely when no such correlation identifier is available or desired.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization response DTO for guest user authentication and token refresh operations.

This schema represents the payload returned by guestUser join and refresh endpoints when authentication or token renewal succeeds. It encapsulates the logical guest user identifier along with a nested authorization token component that the client must store for subsequent authenticated or refresh calls.

The underlying logical identity is stored in the shopping_mall_guestusers table, but this DTO intentionally exposes only minimal identity context and the authorization token structure. Persistence details such as session rows, risk flags, carts, and orders remain internal to the backend and are not surfaced through this auth-focused response.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user logical identity.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_guestusers record that represents the anonymous visitor. It remains stable across join and refresh operations as long as the identity is not logically removed.

Clients use this identifier only for correlation and debugging; authorization decisions are based on the access token rather than this raw id.

external_reference.description:
Optional external or device-based correlation reference for the guest user.

The value is stored in the nullable `external_reference` column of the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table and typically contains a cookie identifier, device fingerprint, or other pseudonymous key that allows the platform to group related guest activity under a single logical identity.

When `null`, the guest identity was either created without any such reference or the reference has been cleared in accordance with privacy and data minimization policies.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest user identity record was created.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table. It reflects the instant when the platform first persisted this guest identity, such as the first time the visitor added an item to a cart or otherwise triggered identity creation.

The timestamp is represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and is frequently used in lifecycle analysis, retention reporting, and time-based segmentation of guest traffic.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest user record was last updated.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table. It is automatically advanced whenever any mutable column in the row changes, including system-driven maintenance updates or changes to `external_reference`.
