Consumers can use this timestamp to detect recently modified guest identities, drive incremental synchronization logic, or implement cache invalidation strategies for admin tools that display guest details.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the guest user identity.

This property is backed by the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table. When `deleted_at` is `null`, the guest record is considered active from a data-retention perspective. When it contains an ISO 8601 date-time value, the record is logically deleted but retained to preserve the integrity of historical relations to sessions, carts, or orders and to satisfy audit or compliance requirements.

Downstream services and admin tools should treat non-null `deleted_at` values as an indicator that the guest identity should not be used for new business operations while still being available for read-only historical analysis.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this guest user identity was first recorded by the platform.

This field is provided as a convenience for clients that wish to display or log when the guest session was initially created, but it is not required for authorization or token validation logic.

lastActiveAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent recorded interaction associated with this guest user, such as updating a cart or initiating checkout.

isConvertedToCustomer.description: Flag indicating whether this guest user has been converted or linked to a fully registered customer account according to business rules.

countryCode.description: ISO-style country code inferred or explicitly associated with this guest user, used for regional reporting and governance. The exact format and allowed values follow the shopping_mall_countries master data.

regionCode.description: Optional region or subdivision code that refines the geographic context of this guest user, aligned with shopping_mall_regions master data.

hasCarts.description: Indicates whether this guest user currently has one or more carts associated with it. This is a derived, read-only projection for admin convenience.

hasOrders.description: Indicates whether this guest user is linked to one or more placed or in-progress orders. This is a derived, read-only projection useful during investigations.

riskFlagCount.description: Total number of risk flags associated with this guest user via shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_guestusers linkage records. Represents the breadth of risk concerns, not the severity of each flag.

maxRiskSeverity.description: Maximum severity score among all risk flags attached to this guest user. Higher values correspond to higher perceived risk according to the configured risk engine.

hasRecentSecurityEvents.description: True when there are one or more recent security events linked to this guest user in shopping_mall_actor_security_events_of_guestusers according to internally defined recency thresholds.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.IRefresh.description:
Request DTO for refreshing JWT tokens for an existing guest user identity.

This schema models the refresh-token based request used by the guestUser refresh endpoint to obtain new access (and possibly refresh) tokens without re-creating the underlying logical guest user identity in the shopping_mall_guestusers table.

Clients send this payload when an existing access token is close to expiry. The backend validates the refresh token against guest user session records and issues a new authorization payload if the token is valid and the guest identity is still active.

refresh_token.description:
Opaque refresh token previously issued to the guest user during the join flow or a prior refresh.

The token is treated as an application-level secret and is never introspected by the client. It must be sent in the request body, not as a query parameter, to minimize leakage through logs and intermediaries.

The backend validates this value against stored guest session or token records and rejects the request if the token is expired, revoked, or does not map to a valid guest identity.

IShoppingMallConfig.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination request DTO for querying configuration records stored in the shopping_mall_configs model.

This schema is used by administrative listing endpoints such as /shoppingMall/admin/configs and /shoppingMall/admin/configs/byNamespace to express rich search criteria, pagination options, and sorting preferences when browsing global configuration entries.

The filters are intentionally flexible and optional so that callers can combine namespace, key, environment, and text searches as needed. Pagination and ordering fields ensure that large configuration sets can be navigated efficiently in management tools without overloading the backend or client.

page.description:
Zero-based page index to retrieve from the configuration listing.

When omitted, the backend should default to the first page. The combination of page and limit controls the window of configuration records returned in the IPageIShoppingMallConfig.ISummary response.

Administrative clients should avoid requesting excessively large page indexes when the total number of records is unknown.

limit.description:
Maximum number of configuration records to include in a single page of results.

Backends typically enforce an upper bound for this value to prevent very large result sets from degrading performance. When the client omits this field, a sensible default page size configured at the service level is applied.

Administrative tools can adjust this parameter to show more or fewer configuration entries per screen depending on usability requirements.

namespace.description:
Optional namespace filter limiting results to configuration entries within a specific logical grouping.

Typical namespaces include domain-oriented categories such as "checkout", "catalog", "reviews", or "risk" that correspond to the namespace column in shopping_mall_configs.

When provided, only configuration rows whose namespace matches this value (according to the implementation's comparison rules) will be considered.

config_key.description:
Optional configuration key filter that restricts results to entries with a specific key or matching a key pattern.

This field corresponds to the config_key column in shopping_mall_configs and is typically used for direct lookup of a known configuration or for prefix-based searches depending on implementation.

Administrative clients may combine this with namespace to narrow down to a single configuration document or a small conceptual group.

environment.description:
Optional environment filter selecting configuration entries applicable to a particular deployment environment.

This value relates to the environment column in shopping_mall_configs and may take values such as "production", "staging", or "development". Filtering by environment allows administrators to inspect and compare configuration state for different runtime contexts.

If omitted, the backend may return configurations across all environments or apply a default environment, depending on business rules.

is_active.description:
Optional flag indicating whether only active or only inactive configuration entries should be returned.

This field maps to the is_active column in shopping_mall_configs and is commonly used to hide historical or deprecated configurations from default listing views.

When omitted, the backend may return both active and inactive records or apply a default filter to active entries only, according to administrative tooling requirements.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to configuration keys, descriptions, or values.

Implementations typically use this field to perform case-insensitive substring matching or full-text search across selected columns such as config_key, description, and value_json within shopping_mall_configs.

This enables administrators to quickly discover configuration entries related to a given concept without knowing exact keys or namespaces.

order_by.description:
Optional name of the field used to sort configuration records in the result set.

Common values include "created_at", "updated_at", "namespace", or "config_key", all of which correspond to columns in the shopping_mall_configs table. When omitted, the backend applies a sensible default, such as ordering by updated_at descending.

Administrative UIs may present this as a selectable column in the list header.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction applied together with order_by to determine how configuration records are ordered.

Typical values are "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending. If this field is omitted, the backend assumes a default direction that aligns with the default order_by column.

Incorrect or unsupported values should be validated and rejected with a clear error message to avoid ambiguous sorting behavior.

IShoppingMallConfig.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a global configuration entry in the shoppingMall platform.

This summary type is designed for list views, lightweight lookups, and embedding configuration references into other DTOs without exposing the full configuration payload or audit history.

It focuses on the key business identifiers and state flags that uniquely identify a configuration document and indicate whether it is currently active, while omitting the potentially large JSON value blob used internally by application services.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the configuration set.

This value maps directly to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model and is used as the stable technical identifier when referencing the configuration from other services or logs.

namespace.description:
Logical namespace grouping for this configuration set.

This field corresponds to the `namespace` column in the `shopping_mall_configs` table and is used to group related configuration keys, such as `"checkout"`, `"catalog"`, `"reviews"`, or `"risk"`, to avoid collisions and improve organization in administration UIs.

config_key.description:
Business-level key that identifies the configuration entry within the given namespace.

This property maps to the `config_key` column of the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model and, together with `namespace` and `environment`, uniquely identifies a configuration document from a business and operational perspective.

environment.description:
Environment in which this configuration entry is applicable.

This directly reflects the `environment` column in the `shopping_mall_configs` table. Typical values include `"production"`, `"staging"`, or `"development"`, and they allow multiple configuration values for the same logical key to coexist across different deployment environments.

description.description:
Human-readable explanation of what this configuration controls.

This corresponds to the nullable `description` column of the `shopping_mall_configs` model. It is intended for administrators and operators to understand the purpose and impact of a configuration entry when browsing or editing it. When `null`, no additional explanatory text has been provided for this configuration.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this configuration entry is currently active for its namespace, key, and environment.

This maps to the `is_active` column in the `shopping_mall_configs` table. Runtime configuration loaders typically consider only entries where `is_active` is `true` when resolving effective configuration values.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration entry was first created.

This property is mapped from the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model and represents the initial insertion time, supporting auditability and sorting of configuration history in administrative tools.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration entry was last updated.

It corresponds to the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_configs` table and is refreshed whenever the configuration value or its metadata changes, enabling operators to track the most recent modification time.

IShoppingMallConfig.description:
Full entity representation of a global configuration row in the `shopping_mall_configs` table.

This schema models the current persisted state of a configuration entry, including identifiers, JSON payload, and lifecycle timestamps.
It is returned to administrative clients after read or update operations so they can see the effective configuration and audit-related metadata.

id.description:
Primary key of the configuration entry.

This UUID uniquely identifies the row in the `shopping_mall_configs` table and is used as the path parameter `configId` in administrative APIs.
The identifier is generated by the system and is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

namespace.description:
Logical namespace grouping for this configuration set.

Namespaces separate configuration domains such as checkout, catalog, reviews, or risk.
They are part of the unique business key that distinguishes different configuration documents.

config_key.description:
Business-level key identifying a particular configuration within its namespace.

Application code uses this key together with `namespace` and `environment` to look up the active configuration document at runtime.
The combination `(namespace, config_key, environment, is_active)` is enforced as unique for active entries.

environment.description:
Environment to which this configuration applies.

Typical values include `production`, `staging`, and `development`.
Clients use this value when querying for environment-specific configuration in multi-environment deployments.

description.description:
Optional human‑readable description of the configuration.

This text helps administrators understand what the configuration controls and how changes may affect the platform.
When `null`, no additional description has been recorded for this configuration entry.

value_json.description:
Configuration payload encoded as JSON text.

The string contains structured parameters such as numeric thresholds, lists of feature flags, or nested objects.
The platform is responsible for parsing and validating this JSON according to the relevant business rules when loading configuration into memory.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this configuration entry is currently active.

Only active entries are considered by runtime configuration loaders when selecting the effective configuration for a given `(namespace, config_key, environment)` pair.
Inactive entries remain in the database for audit history or rollback scenarios but are ignored for live behavior.

created_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this configuration entry was first created.

The value is stored in the database as a datetime column and is managed exclusively by the persistence layer.
Clients can use it for audit displays or to reconstruct configuration history.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this configuration entry was last updated.

Every successful modification that changes any column of the configuration row should update this field.
Consumers can compare `updated_at` values when implementing cache invalidation or change detection.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the configuration entry.

When `null`, the configuration is considered logically present.
When populated with a datetime value, the configuration is treated as deleted for business purposes but is kept in the database for compliance and auditing.

IShoppingMallConfig.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new configuration entry in the `shopping_mall_configs` table.

This type is used by administrative APIs such as `POST /shoppingMall/admin/configs` to register new configuration documents that control platform behavior. It captures the business-level namespace, configuration key, environment, and JSON-encoded configuration payload along with optional descriptive metadata and the initial active state.

System-managed fields like `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are not accepted from clients and are populated by the backend when the configuration row is persisted.

namespace.description:
Logical namespace grouping for the new configuration entry.

Examples include values such as `checkout`, `catalog`, `reviews`, or `risk`. Namespaces separate configuration domains and prevent key collisions between unrelated features.

This value must satisfy the uniqueness constraints in combination with `config_key`, `environment`, and `is_active` so that at most one active configuration exists for the same logical scope.

config_key.description:
Business-level key identifying the configuration within its namespace.

This should be a stable, machine-readable identifier such as `maxCartItems`, `reviewAutoApproveThreshold`, or `riskRuleSet`. It is used by application code to look up configuration values programmatically.

The combination of `namespace`, `config_key`, `environment`, and `is_active` must be unique, so callers should avoid creating overlapping active configurations with the same key.

environment.description:
Target environment in which this configuration will apply.

Typical values include `production`, `staging`, or `development`. Using explicit environment codes allows separate configuration sets per environment while still sharing the same namespace and key structure.

The backend may enforce a known set of environment identifiers or treat this as a free-form string depending on platform policy.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description explaining the purpose and impact of the configuration.

Administrators and operators rely on this field when browsing configuration lists to understand what a key controls and how it should be tuned.

When omitted or null, the configuration will be created without additional descriptive text, which can make future maintenance more difficult.

value_json.description:
JSON-encoded configuration payload to be stored in the `value_json` column.

The payload is provided as a string containing valid JSON and may represent nested structures such as objects, arrays, numbers, and booleans that define feature flags, limits, or other parameters.

The backend should validate that the string can be parsed as JSON and that it satisfies any domain-specific constraints before persisting the configuration.

is_active.description:
Initial active state for the configuration entry.

When true, the configuration becomes part of the active set for its (namespace, config_key, environment) combination immediately after creation. When false, the configuration is stored but not considered by normal runtime resolution until it is explicitly activated through a subsequent update.

Because the database enforces uniqueness across `namespace`, `config_key`, `environment`, and `is_active`, callers must avoid creating multiple active entries for the same logical scope.

IShoppingMallConfig.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for global configuration entries stored in the `shopping_mall_configs` table.

This schema represents the subset of configuration fields that may be modified after initial creation for a specific configuration row.
It is used by administrative tools to adjust configuration metadata and JSON payloads while preserving immutable identifiers and audit fields managed by the system.

namespace.description:
Logical namespace grouping for this configuration set.

Examples include values such as `checkout`, `catalog`, `reviews`, or `risk`.
This field may be updated when configurations are reorganized across namespaces, subject to business rules that prevent collisions in the `(namespace, config_key, environment, is_active)` combination.

config_key.description:
Business-level key identifying the particular configuration within its namespace.

Together with `namespace`, `environment`, and `is_active`, this key uniquely identifies an active configuration.
In many deployments this key is treated as immutable, but the DTO keeps it as an updatable field so that policy can decide whether renames are allowed.

environment.description:
Environment in which this configuration is effective.

Typical values include `production`, `staging`, or `development`.
Administrators may adjust the environment if a configuration is being promoted or re-scoped across environments, but the implementation may choose to treat it as immutable if required by governance.

description.description:
Human‑readable explanation of what this configuration controls.

This field is optional and can be updated at any time to improve operator understanding, document rollout plans, or clarify risk implications of the configuration value.
Setting this property to `null` clears the description.

value_json.description:
JSON-encoded configuration payload.

The string must contain syntactically valid JSON representing structured parameters such as thresholds, feature flags, or per-feature settings.
The backend is responsible for validating the shape of this JSON against internal rules before persisting changes.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this configuration entry is currently active.

Administrators can toggle this field to enable or disable a particular configuration without deleting it.
Combined with the unique constraint over `(namespace, config_key, environment, is_active)`, this flag ensures that only one active configuration exists for a given logical key and environment at a time.

IShoppingMallCountry.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying country master records from the `shopping_mall_countries` table.

This schema encapsulates rich search criteria, sorting preferences, and pagination parameters used by administrative UIs, onboarding flows, and checkout forms when retrieving lists of supported countries.
The backend converts the supplied filters into Prisma queries against the `shopping_mall_countries` model, respecting indexes on country codes, English names, activation flags, and sort order.

page.description:
Index of the page to retrieve when paginating country search results.

The value is expected to be a non-negative integer, with `0` typically representing the first page when a zero-based convention is used.
If omitted, the service defaults to the first page according to its configured pagination strategy.

limit.description:
Maximum number of country summary records to return in a single page.

This value should be a positive integer. The service may enforce an upper bound to protect system performance and to prevent excessively large responses.
When omitted, an implementation-defined default page size is applied so that clients can perform simple queries without specifying a limit explicitly.

search.description:
Free‑text search term applied to country attributes such as `country_code` or `name_en`.

The service typically performs case‑insensitive matching and may leverage full‑text indexes where available.
Empty or omitted values mean that no generic text search filter is applied.

country_code.description:
Optional filter for a specific canonical country code defined by the `country_code` column in `shopping_mall_countries`.

When provided, this filter restricts results to the single matching country if it exists.
The value is expected to match the platform's chosen ISO‑style code format, such as ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 or alpha‑3.

name_en.description:
Optional filter for the English display name `name_en` of the country.

Implementations may perform exact or partial, case‑insensitive matching depending on requirements.
This filter is useful for administrative search tools and internal configuration UIs that manage country master data.

is_active.description:
Optional filter for the `is_active` flag on countries.

When set to `true`, only currently enabled countries are returned, which is typically the default for checkout and address entry flows.
When set to `false`, callers can inspect disabled or deprecated country entries for administrative purposes.

sort_field.description:
Optional name of the primary field used to sort search results.

Typical allowed values include `sort_order`, `name_en`, and `country_code`, which correspond to indexed or commonly sorted columns in the `shopping_mall_countries` table.
Implementations should validate this value against an internal allow‑list of sortable columns and may reject or ignore unsupported field names to ensure deterministic and safe ordering.

sort_direction.description:
Sorting direction applied to the specified `sort_field`.

Allowed values are usually `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. If this property is omitted, the service generally defaults to ascending order or to a configuration-specific default that is documented for the API.
When neither `sort_field` nor `sort_direction` is specified, results should fall back to a sensible default ordering such as `(is_active desc, sort_order asc)` to keep active countries and primary markets near the top of selection lists.

IShoppingMallCountry.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a supported country in the shoppingMall platform.

This type is optimized for use in country selection lists, lightweight lookups, and as an embedded reference in other DTOs, exposing only the key business attributes and status flags instead of the full master record.

It provides the canonical country code, default English display name, optional phone dialing prefix, and ordering and activity flags used to control visibility in user interfaces and configuration flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the country record.

This property is mapped from the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_countries` Prisma model and is used as the stable technical identifier when referencing a country from other entities, logs, or administrative tooling.

country_code.description:
Canonical country code for this record, typically an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 value.

This maps directly to the `country_code` column of the `shopping_mall_countries` table and serves as the primary business identifier when integrating with external systems or managing country-specific configuration.

name_en.description:
Default English display name of the country.

This field reflects the `name_en` column in the `shopping_mall_countries` Prisma model and is used as the primary label in user interfaces when localization is not applied or when English is selected as the display language.

phone_code.description:
Optional international calling code prefix associated with the country.

This corresponds to the nullable `phone_code` column in the `shopping_mall_countries` table and is used when formatting or validating phone numbers for this country. When `null`, no standard phone code is configured for this record.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this country is currently enabled for use in addresses, shipping flows, and related business processes.

This property maps to the `is_active` column in the `shopping_mall_countries` Prisma model. Only countries with `is_active = true` are typically shown in customer-facing selection lists, while inactive countries may still be referenced by legacy orders or addresses.

sort_order.description:
Integer value controlling the ordering of this country in selection lists.

It is taken from the `sort_order` column of the `shopping_mall_countries` table. Lower values are shown earlier, allowing administrators to prioritize common or important countries in dropdowns and other UI components.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this country record was created.

This property originates from the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_countries` Prisma model and provides audit information about when the country was first registered in the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this country record was last updated.

It maps to the `updated_at` column of the `shopping_mall_countries` table and changes whenever the display name, phone code, active flag, or sort order is modified.

IShoppingMallCountry.description:
Country master entity used across the shoppingMall platform.

This type represents a single row from the `shopping_mall_countries` Prisma model. It defines the canonical list of countries that can be referenced by addresses, regions, shipping configuration, and reporting.

Each country is identified by a UUID primary key and a business-level `country_code` that is typically aligned with ISO 3166-1 alpha codes. Lifecycle fields such as `is_active`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` control availability and track historical changes.

id.description:
Primary key of the country record.

This is the internal unique identifier used by the database and foreign key relations from other tables such as `shopping_mall_regions` and customer addresses.

country_code.description:
Canonical country code used as the primary business identifier across the platform.

The value typically corresponds to an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 code and is unique in the system according to the Prisma unique index on `country_code`.

name_en.description:
English display name of the country.

This field is used wherever no locale-specific country label is available and acts as the default human-readable name in administrative tools and public UIs.

phone_code.description:
Optional international calling code prefix for the country.

When present, it can be used for phone number formatting and validation logic in customer and seller contact information flows.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this country is currently enabled for use.

Only active countries should be offered for selection in address forms, shipping configuration, and similar workflows. Deactivating a country hides it from new operations but does not remove existing references.

sort_order.description:
Ordering value that controls how countries are presented in selection lists.

Lower values are typically displayed earlier, allowing business operators to prioritize frequently used countries at the top of dropdowns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this country record was initially created.

Stored as a database datetime, it is used for auditing, reporting, and troubleshooting configuration changes over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this country record was last updated.

The value is refreshed on each modification of the country metadata, enabling change history analysis and synchronization with external systems.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the country record.

When set, the country is logically removed from new selection lists and operations but retained in the database for historical references such as past orders and addresses.

IShoppingMallCountry.ICreate.description:
DTO used by administrative clients to create a new country master record.

This schema maps to the writable fields of the shopping_mall_countries Prisma model that are relevant at insert time. It is consumed by the POST /shoppingMall/admin/countries endpoint to onboard new countries into the platform configuration.

The payload must include the canonical business country_code and English display name. Optional fields allow admins to set the dialing code, activation status, and ordering preferences at creation time, while system-managed fields such as id and timestamps are generated automatically by the backend.

country_code.description:
Canonical country code that will serve as the stable business identifier for the new country.

This value must be unique across all rows in the shopping_mall_countries table and typically follows ISO 3166-1 conventions or a platform-specific set of codes.

APIs that address a country via path parameters, such as GET /shoppingMall/countries/{countryCode}, rely on this code rather than the database primary key.

name_en.description:
English display name for the country to be presented in user interfaces.

This value is required for every new country and is used as the default label in selection lists and configuration screens when no additional localization is applied.

It should be human-readable and match the expected naming conventions used by the business and users.

phone_code.description:
Optional international dialing prefix for the country, such as "+1" or "+82".

When provided, this value supports phone number entry and formatting features. When null, no default calling code is configured for the new country.

Validation logic may enforce a specific pattern or formatting rule for this field according to platform requirements.

is_active.description:
Activation flag determining whether the new country is immediately usable on the platform.

When set to true, the country will appear in address and shipping destination selection lists after creation. When false, the country record is created but should not be offered for new selections until later activation by an admin.

This field allows safe staging of configuration changes without affecting live user flows prematurely.

sort_order.description:
Initial ordering position for the new country within selection lists.

This value determines how the country is ranked relative to others when rendered in UIs. Lower numbers are typically placed earlier, allowing admins to feature certain markets more prominently.

If not provided, the backend may apply a default ordering strategy; however, explicitly setting this value gives precise control over display order.

IShoppingMallCountry.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying mutable properties of a country master record in the shopping_mall_countries table.

This type is used by administrative configuration endpoints to adjust human-facing attributes of a country, such as its English display name, phone calling code, active flag, and sort order, while preserving immutable identifiers like id and country_code.

Only fields that are explicitly allowed to change at runtime are exposed here. System-managed timestamps are not directly writable by clients; updated_at is refreshed by the service when a successful update operation is applied.

name_en.description:
English display name of the country shown in selection lists and configuration screens.

This value corresponds to the name_en column in shopping_mall_countries and can be adjusted by admins to improve readability or localization fallback behavior.

phone_code.description:
Optional international calling code prefix for the country.

Maps to the phone_code column in shopping_mall_countries. When provided, it should follow telephony conventions (for example "+1", "+82"). Setting this to null clears any previously configured calling code.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this country is available for new operations such as address selection, shipping, and tax handling.

When set to false, the country is typically hidden from new selections but existing historical records that reference the country remain valid for reporting and audit.

sort_order.description:
Integer value controlling display ordering of the country in selection lists.

Lower values are rendered earlier in lists. This corresponds to the sort_order column in shopping_mall_countries and can be tuned by admins to prioritize commonly used countries.

IShoppingMallRegion.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating regions within a specific country in the shoppingMall platform.

This type is submitted in the body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/countries/{countryCode}/regions endpoint to express pagination options, sorting preferences, and filter criteria when listing regions belonging to the given country.

The server combines these parameters with the countryCode path argument and executes a read-only query over the shopping_mall_regions table, returning a paginated list of region summaries.

page.description:
1-based index of the results page to retrieve.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default such as page 1. Values less than 1 are typically rejected or normalized to 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of region records to return in a single page.

Used together with page to drive pagination over shopping_mall_regions. Implementations commonly enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive payload sizes.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to region name or code.

Backends may implement this as a case-insensitive partial match against name_en and/or code in shopping_mall_regions to help users quickly locate a region.

is_active.description:
Optional filter on the active state of regions.

When true, only regions with is_active = true are returned. When false, only disabled regions are returned. When null or omitted, no filtering by active state is applied.

region_type.description:
Optional filter by the semantic classification of the region.

Corresponds to the region_type column in shopping_mall_regions, which may contain values like "state", "province", "city", or custom business types. When provided, the list is restricted to regions with the exact matching region_type; when null or omitted, all types are included.

order_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort region results.

Typical values include "name_en" for alphabetical ordering or "sort_order" for explicit display-order control. When null or omitted, the backend applies its default sort, often by sort_order then name_en.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction indicator for the order_by field.

Common values are "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending order. When null or omitted, the backend uses its default direction, usually ascending.

IShoppingMallRegion.description:
Detailed representation of a region belonging to a specific country in the shoppingMall platform.

This type models a single row from the `shopping_mall_regions` Prisma model. Regions represent sub-national or logical areas such as states, provinces, cities, or business-defined groupings used for shipping, pricing, risk segmentation, and policy scoping.

Each region is linked to exactly one country via the `shopping_mall_country_id` foreign key and is identified by a business-level `code` that is unique within that country according to the composite unique index on `[shopping_mall_country_id, code]`. The type exposes configuration attributes such as `name_en`, optional `region_type`, an activation flag, and sort ordering as well as lifecycle timestamps. It also includes a country summary object so API consumers can understand the region’s parent context without issuing additional requests.

id.description:
Primary key of the region.

This UUID uniquely identifies the region row in `shopping_mall_regions` and is used internally for joins from shipping policies, warehouses, and other configuration tables.

country.description:
Parent country to which this region belongs.

This object is derived from the `shopping_mall_country_id` foreign key and provides a lightweight view of the country, including its primary key, business code, and display name, so that clients do not need an additional API call to understand the region’s country context.

code.description:
Business-level identifier code for the region within its parent country.

The value may represent an ISO subdivision code, an internal region identifier, or another canonical code used for shipping and pricing configuration. It is unique per country as enforced by the composite unique index on `[shopping_mall_country_id, code]`.

name_en.description:
English display name of the region.

This is the default human-readable label used in administrative tools, configuration screens, and user-facing dropdowns when locale-specific labels are not available.

region_type.description:
Optional semantic classification of the region.

Typical examples include values such as `state`, `province`, `city`, or custom business-defined types. The value is used for reporting, analytics, and UI grouping but is not required for region identity.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this region is currently active for use.

Active regions are eligible to appear in address selection forms, shipping configuration, and risk rules. Inactive regions are hidden from new operations but remain in the database for historical reference.

sort_order.description:
Display ordering value within the parent country.

Lower values appear earlier when listing regions for a given country, allowing operators to control region ordering in UIs such as dropdowns and configuration screens.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this region record was created.

It is stored as a database datetime and used for auditing and historical analysis of geographic configuration changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this region record was last updated.

This value is updated whenever mutable fields such as `name_en`, `region_type`, `is_active`, or `sort_order` change, enabling operators to track configuration history.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the region.

When populated, the region is considered logically removed from new address validation and configuration flows but remains available for reference in historical orders, shipments, and reports.

IShoppingMallRegion.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new region under a specific country in the shoppingMall platform.

This type is used as the request body for the `POST /shoppingMall/admin/countries/{countryCode}/regions` endpoint. The parent country is selected by the `countryCode` path parameter, which corresponds to `shopping_mall_countries.country_code`, so the request body does not contain any country identifier field.

Clients provide the region’s business code, English display name, optional semantic type, activation flag, and display ordering. System-managed fields such as `id`, `shopping_mall_country_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are populated by the backend and must not be supplied by API callers.

code.description:
Business-level identifier code for the new region within the selected country.

This value must be unique for the resolved country according to the composite unique index on `[shopping_mall_country_id, code]`. It may follow ISO subdivision conventions or internal coding schemes used by the business.

name_en.description:
English display name for the region being created.

This label will be shown in administrative tools and user-facing lists when appropriate localization is not available.

region_type.description:
Optional semantic classification of the region, such as `state`, `province`, `city`, or a custom business-defined type.

If omitted or set to null, the system treats the region as an unclassified area, which is acceptable when only the name and code are required.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the region should be active immediately after creation.

When set to true, the region becomes eligible for use in address validation, shipping configuration, and risk rules. When false, the region exists but is not offered for new operations until activated later.

sort_order.description:
Display ordering value for the region within the selected country.

Lower values sort earlier in region dropdowns and configuration lists, enabling operators to present frequently used regions near the top.

IShoppingMallRegion.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying an existing ShoppingMall region in the `shopping_mall_regions` table.

This DTO represents the subset of region attributes that are allowed to change after initial creation, such as the English display name, semantic region type, activation flag, and display ordering within a country.

It is used by administrative tools and internal services when maintaining geographic configuration that influences shipping availability, risk segmentation, and address validation behavior. System-maintained fields like identifiers and timestamps are intentionally omitted from this request shape and are managed exclusively by backend logic.

name_en.description:
Updated English display name of the region.

This value is shown in administrative and customer-facing UIs as the primary label for the region when English is the active locale. It should remain unique enough within a given country to avoid user confusion but is not constrained by a uniqueness index at the database level.

When omitted, the existing `name_en` value for the region remains unchanged.

region_type.description:
Optional semantic classification of the region being updated, such as `state`, `province`, `city`, or another business-defined type.

This field is primarily used for reporting, analytics, and UI grouping, allowing the platform to distinguish between different kinds of geographic units without relying solely on naming conventions.

When set to null, any previous classification is cleared and the region becomes untyped from this perspective.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the region should be considered active after the update.

When `true`, the region can be used for shipping rules, risk segmentation, and address validation workflows, assuming other business constraints permit it.

When `false`, the region must no longer be offered for new operations such as address entry or shipping selection, but historical references in orders and addresses remain valid. Omitting this property leaves the current activation state unchanged.

sort_order.description:
Updated display ordering value for the region within its country.

Lower values appear earlier in region selection lists and administrative grids, enabling fine‑grained control over how regions are presented to users and operators.

When omitted, the existing sort order is preserved. When provided, the service may enforce additional business rules to avoid conflicting or ambiguous ordering within the same country.

IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.IReque.description:
Search and filter request payload for listing region shipping policies in the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table for a specific region.

This DTO is used by administrative and internal tooling to query configuration records that control whether, how, and under what constraints shipping is allowed to a region. It encapsulates pagination, sorting, and filter criteria while relying on the API path parameters to provide the region context.

All filters in this object are optional and are combined with the region resolved from `{countryCode}` and `{regionCode}` in the request path. System-managed identifiers, timestamps, and foreign keys are not expected from callers and are applied by the backend when constructing the underlying Prisma query.

page.description:
Zero‑based or one‑based page index for the search result, depending on the platform’s standard pagination convention.

This value is used together with `limit` to determine which slice of matching shipping policy records is returned to the caller. When omitted, the service falls back to a sensible default page index, typically the first page of results.

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipping policy records to return in a single page of results.

This value limits how many `IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.ISummary` entries are included in the response `data` array and is subject to a system‑defined upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

When not provided, a default page size is applied by the service.

policy_name.description:
Optional free‑text filter for matching the `policy_name` column of region shipping policies.

Consumers can use this field to search for policies by their human‑readable names when browsing or auditing configuration for a given region.

When set to null or omitted, no name‑based filtering is applied and all policies for the resolved region are eligible for the result set.

is_shipping_allowed.description:
Optional filter flag corresponding to the `is_shipping_allowed` column on `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies`.

When `true`, only policies that explicitly allow shipping in the region are returned. When `false`, only policies that block shipping are returned. When null or omitted, this dimension is not used to filter the result set.

This flag is commonly used by administrative tools to quickly inspect which regions are blocked or enabled for shipping under different policy configurations.

allows_cod.description:
Optional filter flag that maps to the `allows_cod` column and indicates whether cash‑on‑delivery or pay‑on‑delivery is permitted by the policy.

When `true`, only policies that allow COD in the region are included. When `false`, only policies that explicitly disallow COD are included. When null or not supplied, COD allowance is not used as a filter.

This filter is useful for evaluating or adjusting payment and risk strategies for specific regions.

effective_from_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the `effective_from` timestamp in the search criteria.

When provided, only policies whose `effective_from` is greater than or equal to this value, or whose `effective_from` is null but otherwise satisfy other filters, are considered active from the given point in time.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date‑time string. When null or omitted, no lower bound is enforced on the effective start time.

effective_from_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the `effective_from` timestamp in the search criteria.

When present, policies whose `effective_from` is later than this value may be excluded from the result set, allowing callers to focus on policies that became effective within a particular window.

The value must be formatted as an ISO 8601 date‑time string. When null or omitted, no upper bound on `effective_from` is applied.

effective_until_from.description:
Optional lower bound filter applied to the `effective_until` timestamp of region shipping policies.

This field can be used to inspect policies that expire on or after a certain date, such as when reviewing upcoming configuration changes for a region.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date‑time string. When null or omitted, the lower bound on `effective_until` is not constrained.

effective_until_to.description:
Optional upper bound filter for the `effective_until` timestamp in search queries.

When defined, only policies whose `effective_until` is before or equal to this value are returned, which is useful for analyzing policies that are scheduled to end within a given timeframe.

The value must be supplied as an ISO 8601 date‑time string. When null or omitted, `effective_until` is not restricted by an upper bound.

sort_by.description:
Optional field specifying which logical column or attribute should be used to sort the result set of region shipping policies.

Common values include keys mapped to `policy_name`, `created_at`, or effective date fields, depending on the platform’s standardized sort options.

When null or not provided, the service uses its default ordering, typically by creation time or policy name within the resolved region.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction applied together with `sort_by` when ordering the shipping policy search results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order, with the default determined by the service when this field is null or absent.

Providing this field allows callers to control the visual ordering of policies in administrative grids and internal tools.

IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.description:
Region-level shipping policy configuration for the shopping mall platform.

This entity represents a single shipping policy that applies to a specific logical region of the marketplace, as defined in the `shopping_mall_regions` model and scoped by a parent country from `shopping_mall_countries`.

Each record defines whether shipping is allowed to the region, whether cash-on-delivery is permitted, optional order amount thresholds, and the effective time window of the policy. It is used at checkout and shipping option calculation time to determine whether an order can be shipped and which constraints or risk rules apply.

Policies are soft-deletable and versionable via timestamps. Historical shipments keep their own snapshots so modifications to this table do not retroactively affect past orders.

id.description:
Primary key of the region shipping policy.

This is the unique identifier of the policy record in the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table and is used internally by backend services and admin tools.

Clients typically obtain this value via listing or creation operations and then reuse it in detail, update, or deletion requests.

shopping_mall_region_id.description:
Identifier of the region this shipping policy is bound to.

This value maps directly to the `shopping_mall_region_id` foreign key column on the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` Prisma model and points to a single row in the `shopping_mall_regions` table. It provides the technical linkage that scopes the policy to a specific region within a country.

While most external APIs use `countryCode` and `regionCode` path parameters to resolve the region in a business-friendly way, this UUID remains the internal, stable reference used by the database and by admin tools, analytics jobs, and debugging workflows that operate directly on the underlying data.

policy_name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping policy for the region.

This name is used primarily in administrative consoles and configuration UIs so operators can quickly recognize and select the appropriate policy.

The combination of the owning region and `policy_name` is unique and prevents duplicate policy names within a single region.

region.description:
Summary of the region to which this shipping policy applies.

This object references the associated `shopping_mall_regions` record in a lightweight form so that clients can understand the geographic scope of the policy without inspecting raw foreign key IDs.

Only summary fields such as region code, name, and country context are exposed here to avoid circular references and keep the payload efficient.

shipping_method_group.description:
Optional identifier of a shipping method group or profile preferred for this region.

This may map to a logical group of carriers, service levels, or delivery products configured elsewhere in the system.

When present, shipping engines use this value to select or filter which shipping options are offered to customers in the region.

min_order_amount.description:
Minimum order amount for which this policy can be applied.

If set, orders with a total amount below this value are not eligible for shipping under this policy and may be blocked or routed to alternative handling.

The value is expressed in the platform base currency and should be non-negative.

max_order_amount.description:
Maximum order amount for which this policy is applicable.

If set, orders having a total amount above this value will not use this policy and may require special handling or a different shipping configuration.

The value is expressed in the platform base currency and should be non-negative.

allows_cod.description:
Indicates whether cash-on-delivery (COD) or pay-on-delivery is allowed for this region.

When `true`, customers located in this region may be offered COD payment methods, subject to global payment configuration and risk rules.

When `false`, COD options are suppressed even if globally available, ensuring region-level compliance or operational constraints.

is_shipping_allowed.description:
Global switch determining whether any shipping is allowed to this region.

When `false`, checkout for addresses mapped to this region must be blocked or prevented from reaching a shippable state, regardless of other configuration values.

When `true`, shipping is permitted but may still be restricted by other constraints such as order amount bounds or risk rules.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes for operators describing special conditions or background for this region policy.

This field is typically used to capture business context, exceptions, or coordination details with logistics partners.

It is not interpreted by automated logic but is essential for human review and governance.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this policy becomes effective.

When `null`, the policy is considered effective immediately from creation time or system initialization.

When provided, this allows scheduling future activation of a policy without requiring a separate deployment or manual toggle.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which this policy is no longer considered active.

When `null`, the policy has no predefined expiration and remains active until explicitly modified or soft-deleted.

When provided, this allows automatic sunset of a policy at a predetermined time, supporting campaign or promotion windows.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp for this region shipping policy record.

The value is set by the system at insert time and never changes thereafter, providing a stable historical reference for audits.

It is used in operational reporting and debugging to understand when a policy entered the system.

updated_at.description:
Last modification timestamp for this region shipping policy record.

The system updates this value whenever mutable columns are changed, allowing clients and auditors to detect recent configuration changes.

This field is useful for cache invalidation, synchronization, and human review workflows.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the region shipping policy.

When `null`, the policy is considered active and participates in business logic subject to effective dates and other constraints.

When set, higher-level logic should treat the record as logically removed and exclude it from normal policy resolution, while still preserving it for historical analysis and compliance.

IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.ICreat.description:
Creation payload for a region-level shipping policy configuration.

This DTO captures the business-editable fields required to define a new shipping policy for a specific region within a country on the shopping mall platform.

The region association itself is derived from the `countryCode` and `regionCode` path parameters of the API and is not supplied in the body, ensuring that scoping cannot be manipulated by clients.

Only configuration fields such as policy name, order amount thresholds, allowed COD flag, and effective dates are provided here. System-managed fields like `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are generated by the backend and must not be included by clients.

policy_name.description:
Human-readable name for the new region shipping policy.

This value must be unique within the target region, as constrained by the unique index on `(shopping_mall_region_id, policy_name)` in the underlying Prisma model.

It is displayed in operator UIs and used to distinguish between multiple policies configured for the same region.

shipping_method_group.description:
Optional identifier of a shipping method group or profile that this new policy will use.

This may refer to an external or internal code representing a set of carriers or service levels and is resolved by downstream shipping configuration.

When omitted or set to null, the platform may fall back to default shipping methods or other region-level configuration.

min_order_amount.description:
Minimum order amount required for the policy to be applicable.

If set, orders with a total below this value cannot use this policy during checkout, and the service should surface a clear error or alternative options.

The value is expressed in the platform base currency and should be non-negative.

max_order_amount.description:
Maximum order amount allowed for the policy to be applied.

If set, orders exceeding this amount are excluded from using this policy and may require special handling or a different configuration.

The value is expressed in the platform base currency and should be non-negative.

allows_cod.description:
Flag indicating whether the new policy permits cash-on-delivery (COD) or pay-on-delivery payments in the associated region.

When `true`, COD payment methods can be offered to customers located in this region assuming global payment settings and risk checks also allow it.

When `false`, COD is disabled for this region regardless of global defaults.

is_shipping_allowed.description:
Flag indicating whether shipping is allowed at all under this new policy for the associated region.

When `false`, the platform must block or prevent checkout flows that attempt to ship to addresses mapped to this region while this policy is effective.

When `true`, shipping is permitted subject to additional constraints such as order amount thresholds and risk rules.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes describing the intent, scope, or special conditions of this new region shipping policy.

These notes are shown in internal tools and configuration interfaces to help administrators maintain and review policy decisions.

They are not interpreted by automated logic and can be left null if no extra explanation is required.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which the new policy becomes effective.

When provided, the policy should not be used before this moment, allowing administrators to schedule future activation.

When omitted or set to null, the policy is considered effective immediately upon creation.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which the new policy ceases to be effective.

When provided, this allows automatic expiration of the policy at a specific time, which is useful for campaigns or temporary regional changes.

When omitted or set to null, the policy has no scheduled expiration and remains active until updated or soft-deleted.

IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.IUpdat.description:
Mutable fields for updating an existing region-level shipping policy configuration in the shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies table.

This DTO is used by administrative APIs that modify shipping capabilities and constraints for a specific region, such as enabling or disabling shipping, constraining order amount ranges, toggling COD availability, or adjusting the effective validity window of a policy.

Only business-editable columns from the underlying Prisma model are exposed here. Immutable identifiers like the primary key and foreign keys are excluded from the request body and are instead resolved from the URL path or server-side context.

policy_name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping policy for this region.

Used mainly in admin tools and configuration UIs to distinguish multiple policies for the same region. When provided, it must be a non-empty string after trimming whitespace.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of a shipping method group or profile that this region prefers.

Typical values are business-defined codes that map to carrier sets or service levels. When set, the value must correspond to a configured shipping method group in the platform.
Null when no specific shipping method group is bound to this policy and default platform rules should apply.

shipping_method_group.description:
Optional identifier of a preferred shipping method group for this region.

This value, when present, points to a higher-level configuration that defines which carriers or shipping services are used to fulfill orders to this region.

oneOf.description:
Minimum order total required for shipping under this policy.

Expressed in the platform base currency. Must be zero or a positive value when provided.
Null when there is no minimum order amount constraint for applicability of this policy.

min_order_amount.description:
Minimum order amount threshold for this shipping policy.

When set, orders with a total amount below this value are not eligible for shipping under this policy and may be rejected or forced to use a different policy.

oneOf.description:
Maximum order total for which this policy applies.

Expressed in the platform base currency. Must be greater than or equal to the minimum order amount when both are provided.
Null when no upper bound on order amount is enforced by this policy.

max_order_amount.description:
Maximum order amount threshold for this shipping policy.

When set, orders whose total exceeds this value cannot use this policy and must be routed to alternative handling, such as manual review or a high-value shipping workflow.

allows_cod.description:
Flag indicating whether cash-on-delivery or pay-on-delivery is allowed for this region under this policy.

When true, COD is permitted subject to global payment configuration and any additional risk rules; when false, COD is blocked even if enabled at a higher level.

is_shipping_allowed.description:
Flag indicating whether the platform allows any shipping to this region under this policy.

When false, checkout flows that resolve to this region must block shipping and prevent order confirmation, regardless of other configuration values.

oneOf.description:
Free-form notes text with operator-facing explanations or comments about this policy.

Often used to record business rationale, special conditions, or links to internal documentation.
Null when no operator notes are stored for this policy.

notes.description:
Optional operator notes attached to this shipping policy.

These notes are not exposed to end users and are intended for internal operational and configuration documentation.

oneOf.description:
Start timestamp from which this policy becomes effective.

Must be an ISO 8601 date-time string. When set, the policy should not be applied to orders with creation timestamps before this moment.
Null when the policy is considered effective immediately or since its creation.

effective_from.description:
Optional start of the time window during which this policy is effective.

If provided, the backend enforces that only orders created at or after this timestamp can use this policy during shipping calculations.

oneOf.description:
End timestamp after which this policy is no longer considered active.

Must be an ISO 8601 date-time string. When set, the policy should not be applied to orders created after this moment.
Null when there is no scheduled expiration for this policy.

effective_until.description:
Optional end of the time window during which this policy is effective.

If provided, the backend must ensure that orders created after this timestamp do not use this policy when determining shipping options.

IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying shopping_mall_categories records.

This DTO is consumed by the PATCH /shoppingMall/categories endpoint to retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of category summaries from the global ShoppingMall category taxonomy.

Clients use this schema to express flexible criteria such as parent category constraints, visibility status, leaf-only filters, name search, and page and size configuration for efficient navigation and discovery UIs.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated responses.

When omitted, the server should fall back to a sensible default such as 1. Values less than 1 should be rejected or normalized to 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of category records to return in a single page.

This value controls page size for list and navigation views. The server should enforce an upper bound to protect performance, even if the client sends a larger number.

oneOf.description:
UUID of the parent category whose direct children should be included in the result set.

When provided, the query typically returns categories whose parent_id matches this value; a null parent_id filter can be used to target root categories.
Null to indicate that no explicit parent category filter is applied, allowing categories from any part of the hierarchy to be returned.

parent_id.description:
Optional filter on the parent category relationship.

Use this field to restrict results to children of a specific category or, when left null, to search across the entire taxonomy depending on other filters.

oneOf.description:
Lifecycle status value of categories to include in the result set.

Typical values based on the underlying model description include "active", "hidden", and "deprecated". Servers may restrict allowed values to the set recognized by the shopping_mall_categories.status column.
Null when no specific lifecycle status filter is applied and the server uses its default visibility rules.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status filter for returned categories.

Commonly used to restrict the list to active categories only or to allow administrative tools to query hidden or deprecated categories explicitly.

oneOf.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether to restrict results based on the is_leaf marker in the category model.

When true, only categories currently marked as leaves are returned. When false, only non-leaf categories are returned.
Null when the leaf/non-leaf distinction should not be used as a filter.

is_leaf.description:
Optional filter indicating whether to include only leaf or non-leaf categories.

This helps UIs render pickers that restrict selection to terminal categories or to structural nodes used solely for grouping.

oneOf.description:
Free-text search term used to match categories by name_en, slug, or other indexed text fields.

The backend typically performs case-insensitive partial matching or uses a full-text search index over the relevant columns.
Null when no free-text search term is applied and results are determined solely by structural filters and pagination.

search.description:
Optional free-text search string for category discovery.

Supports user-driven search experiences over the category taxonomy, such as typing into an autocomplete field or a filter box in an admin console.

oneOf.description:
Name of the field used to sort results.

Typical options include "sort_order" for navigation ordering, "name_en" for alphabetical lists, or "created_at" for recency-based views. The server should validate the value against an allowed set of sortable fields.
Null when the server should apply its default ordering, commonly by sort_order and then name_en.

order_by.description:
Optional sort key controlling the ordering of returned categories.

Lets clients request a specific ordering strategy while still allowing the server to enforce safe and efficient sort fields.

oneOf.description:
Direction of sorting for the selected order_by field.

Typical values are "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending order. Servers may normalize case and reject unsupported values.
Null when the default direction associated with the chosen order_by field should be used.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the selected order_by field.

When provided, it determines whether results are returned in ascending or descending order for the chosen sort key.

IShoppingMallCategory.description:
Represents a single product category within the global shoppingMall taxonomy.

This type maps directly to the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and exposes the public, non-sensitive fields required to render catalog navigation, category pickers, and administrative tools.

Each category participates in a hierarchical tree through its optional `parent` reference and the associated closure records in `shopping_mall_category_closures`. Localized labels are provided separately through `shopping_mall_category_localizations`, while this structure focuses on the canonical English name and operational attributes such as status and ordering.

Consumers use this DTO when they need the detailed representation of a single category record, for example after an admin update or when inspecting category metadata in management UIs.

id.description:
Primary key of the category.

This value corresponds to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_categories` table and uniquely identifies a category node in the taxonomy.

Clients should treat this identifier as an opaque UUID string and use it when referencing a category in admin operations and internal links.

slug.description:
URL-friendly unique slug for the category among its siblings.

This field mirrors the `slug` column in `shopping_mall_categories` and is used in external-facing links, SEO-friendly URLs, and integrations.

The slug is unique in the scope of a single parent category, ensuring that sibling categories do not conflict when building nested paths.

name_en.description:
Default English display name for the category.

This value corresponds to the `name_en` column and is used whenever a more specific localization is not requested or available.

Front-end applications may still prefer localized labels from `shopping_mall_category_localizations`, but `name_en` provides a stable fallback and administrative display label.

description_en.description:
Optional English description explaining the scope and intended use of the category.

This property maps to the nullable `description_en` column. When present, it provides human-readable guidance for catalog managers and may be surfaced in SEO metadata or category landing pages.

If null, the category has no additional English description beyond its name.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the category controlling its visibility and assignment rules.

This reflects the `status` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` model. Typical values include `active`, `hidden`, and `deprecated`, though the exact enumeration is enforced at the business logic level rather than in the schema.

UI and query logic should respect this value to decide whether a category can be shown to users or used as a target for new product assignments.

sort_order.description:
Numeric ordering value used among sibling categories.

This property mirrors the non-null `sort_order` column. Lower values appear earlier in navigation menus or sorted lists, allowing administrators fine control over display ordering.

Consumers should treat this value as a stable, implementation-specific ordering hint rather than a user-facing attribute.

is_leaf.description:
Indicates whether the category is currently considered a leaf node in the hierarchy.

This reflects the `is_leaf` boolean column and is used for UI optimizations, such as determining whether to show expand/collapse controls.

A leaf category is typically eligible for direct product assignment, whereas non-leaf nodes primarily serve as structural navigation containers.

parent_id.description:
Identifier of the parent category, if any.

This property corresponds to the nullable `parent_id` column of `shopping_mall_categories` and establishes a direct parent–child relationship between categories.

Root categories have a null `parent_id`, while nested categories reference their immediate parent. Deeper hierarchy queries are resolved via `shopping_mall_category_closures` rather than this field alone.

created_at.description:
Timestamp capturing when the category record was created.

This directly reflects the non-null `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` model.

Clients may use this value for audit displays, admin logs, or chronological sorting, but it is managed exclusively by the backend.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the category record.

The value comes from the `updated_at` column and is automatically maintained by the persistence layer when changes are applied.

Consumers can use this field to detect recent modifications or to implement optimistic concurrency strategies.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the category, if applicable.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column. When non-null, the category is considered soft-deleted: it is preserved for historical orders and reporting but is no longer available for new assignments or public navigation.

Client applications typically exclude categories with a non-null `deleted_at` when presenting current catalog structures, unless an explicit "show deleted" mode is enabled for admins.

IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall category used for lightweight navigation, listing, and reference scenarios.

This summary representation is optimized for menu trees, breadcrumb trails, and category selection widgets where only the most important identifying and display-related fields are required rather than the full administrative detail.

Data for this type is sourced from the shopping_mall_categories Prisma model, which defines the global product category taxonomy including hierarchy, status flags, and soft-delete semantics.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category.

This value maps directly to the primary key `id` in the `shopping_mall_categories` table and is used across the platform to reference this category in relationships, navigation structures, and catalog rules.

slug.description:
URL-friendly slug that identifies the category in external-facing links and integrations.

The slug is unique among sibling categories (enforced by a composite unique constraint with `parent_id`) and is used to build SEO-friendly URLs and internal routing keys for navigation.

name_en.description:
Default English name of the category for display.

This field is taken from `name_en` in `shopping_mall_categories` and is used when localization is not applied or when an English administrative context is in use. It provides a human-readable label suitable for both storefront UI and back-office tools.

description_en.description:
Optional English description that explains the scope, usage, or business meaning of the category.

When present, this text comes from `description_en` in `shopping_mall_categories` and can be used in tooltips, detailed category pages, or administrative UIs to clarify the intent of this category.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the category controlling visibility and availability for new product assignments.

Typical values include `active`, `hidden`, and `deprecated`, and they are stored in the `status` column of `shopping_mall_categories`. Application logic uses this status together with soft-delete semantics to determine whether the category should appear in navigation or be selectable for catalog operations.

sort_order.description:
Ordering value used to control display order among sibling categories.

This corresponds to `sort_order` in `shopping_mall_categories`. Lower values are displayed earlier in menus and lists, allowing administrators to fine-tune the visual arrangement of categories within the same parent.

is_leaf.description:
Flag indicating whether the category is currently considered a leaf node in the hierarchy.

This boolean maps to `is_leaf` in `shopping_mall_categories` and is primarily used for UI optimizations and validation rules. When `true`, the category is typically eligible for direct product assignment, while non-leaf categories may be considered navigational grouping nodes.

parent_id.description:
Identifier of the parent category in the taxonomy, if any.

This field reflects the `parent_id` foreign key in `shopping_mall_categories`. A null value indicates that the category is a root-level category. Client code can use this field to reconstruct basic parent-child relationships when more detailed ancestor information is not required.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this category was created.
