The value mirrors `created_at` in `shopping_mall_categories` and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. It is primarily used in back-office analytics, auditing, and sorting scenarios where recency of category creation matters.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this category was last updated.

This field corresponds to `updated_at` in `shopping_mall_categories` and allows clients and administrative tools to understand when category metadata such as names, slugs, or status flags were most recently changed.

IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new ShoppingMall category in the global product taxonomy.

This type defines the client-supplied fields required to insert a new row into the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model via admin-facing endpoints such as `POST /shoppingMall/admin/categories`.
It focuses on business attributes describing the category while excluding all system-managed fields like primary keys and timestamps, which are filled in by the backend.

Only administrative actors are permitted to use this DTO in production APIs, and the implementation must enforce additional business rules such as uniqueness of sibling slugs and valid parent relationships when processing it.

parent_id.description:
Optional identifier of the parent category under which this new category will be created.

When provided, this value must reference an existing `id` in the `shopping_mall_categories` table and establishes a parent–child relationship in the taxonomy.
When `null`, the new category will be treated as a root category with no parent, and closure or hierarchy tables will be updated accordingly by internal services.

slug.description:
URL-friendly slug for the new category, unique within the chosen parent.

This value is written to the non-null `slug` column in `shopping_mall_categories` and is used for path-based routing, navigation, and integrations.
The backend must validate that no other category with the same `parent_id` and `slug` combination already exists to respect the unique index on these fields.

name_en.description:
Default English name for the new category.

This property corresponds to the required `name_en` column and provides the primary label shown in storefront navigation and admin interfaces.
It should be concise but descriptive enough for customers and administrators to understand the scope of the category.

description_en.description:
Optional English description that further explains the category’s purpose and scope.

If supplied, this value is stored in the nullable `description_en` column and may be displayed on category landing pages and in catalog management tools.
When omitted or explicitly set to null, the category will not have a default English description, and UIs may simply show only the name.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status for the new category.

This value is persisted into the non-null `status` column and determines whether the category is immediately active in navigation, hidden from public catalog views, or marked as deprecated for limited use.
Admin tools should restrict this field to allowed business values and may provide presets such as `active`, `hidden`, or `deprecated` depending on organizational policies.

sort_order.description:
Initial sort order index for this category among its siblings.

This integer value is saved to the non-null `sort_order` column and influences the relative display position of the category when rendered alongside other categories under the same parent.
Lower numbers appear earlier; admins can later update this value via dedicated update operations to fine-tune navigation ordering.

is_leaf.description:
Flag indicating whether the category should initially be treated as a leaf node.

This boolean is written to the `is_leaf` column and is typically set to `true` for categories that will receive products directly and not have child categories, or `false` for structural categories expected to have descendants.
Subsequent changes to the hierarchy may cause internal processes to adjust this flag, but initial intent is captured from this field during creation.

IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying an existing shoppingMall category.

This DTO corresponds to mutable fields of the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and is used as the request body for admin-only update operations such as `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/categories/{categoryId}`.

All properties in this type are optional to support partial updates, allowing callers to send only the fields they intend to change. System-managed and identity fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally excluded and cannot be updated through this DTO.

Server-side logic is responsible for enforcing business rules when applying updates, including validating slug uniqueness within the sibling scope, preventing cyclic parent–child relationships when `parent_id` changes, honoring lifecycle and visibility transitions expressed through `status`, and keeping `is_leaf` and `sort_order` consistent with the actual category hierarchy.

This DTO should be used exclusively in trusted administrative contexts, as updates can impact catalog navigation, search behavior, and downstream analytics that rely on the global category taxonomy.

slug.description:
New URL-friendly slug for the category, unique among its siblings.

When provided, this value updates the `slug` column in `shopping_mall_categories`. It should remain stable for external integrations and SEO-sensitive URLs.

The backend must enforce uniqueness within the scope of the parent category and may reject conflicting updates.

name_en.description:
Updated English display name for the category.

This value replaces the `name_en` column and affects how the category appears in administrative interfaces and as a fallback label when localization is not applied.

Changing this field does not affect localized records in `shopping_mall_category_localizations`, which remain responsible for language-specific labels.

description_en.description:
New English description for the category, or null to clear the existing description.

When set to a non-empty string, the value updates the `description_en` column to provide additional guidance about the category's scope and intended usage.

Setting this field to null removes any existing description, leaving only the name as the primary English label.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status for the category.

This property modifies the `status` column, allowing administrators to move categories between states such as `active`, `hidden`, or `deprecated` according to business rules.

The implementation must ensure that status transitions do not violate catalog integrity, for example by hiding categories that are still critical for active products without appropriate fallbacks.

sort_order.description:
Revised ordering value among sibling categories.

This updates the `sort_order` column and controls the relative position of the category in navigation menus and selector lists.

Lower values appear earlier. Clients typically submit small integer adjustments when reordering categories via drag-and-drop UIs.

is_leaf.description:
Optional override for whether the category should be considered a leaf node.

This property updates the `is_leaf` column and is used primarily for administrative maintenance and optimizations.

Applications should ensure that leaf flags remain consistent with the actual hierarchy (for example, non-leaf categories generally have children), often recalculating this value based on structural changes.

parent_id.description:
Identifier of the new parent category, or null to promote this category to a root.

Updating this field changes the `parent_id` column and effectively moves the category to a different location in the hierarchy.

The backend must enforce rules to prevent cycles, ensure that referenced parent categories exist, and update closure records in `shopping_mall_category_closures` accordingly.

IShoppingMallCategoryTreeNode.description:
Single node within the hierarchical shoppingMall category tree.

This type represents a denormalized view combining core category fields from `shopping_mall_categories` with hierarchical composition through the `children` property.

Each node can be used to render navigation elements, breadcrumbs, and selectors without additional queries, and the full tree is obtained via the `IShoppingMallCategoryTree` root type.

id.description:
Identifier of the category represented by this node.

This matches the `id` column of the underlying `shopping_mall_categories` record and uniquely identifies the node in the tree.

Clients should use this value when triggering category-specific actions such as filtering products or navigating to a category page.

slug.description:
URL-friendly slug for the category represented by this node.

This slug mirrors the `slug` column in `shopping_mall_categories` and is suitable for constructing readable URLs, deep links, and SEO-friendly paths.

In combination with ancestor slugs, it can form hierarchical URL structures for category pages.

name_en.description:
English display name of the category for this node.

This corresponds to the `name_en` column and serves as the default label when localization is not applied.

Front-end clients may still choose to override this with localized labels from `shopping_mall_category_localizations`, but including it here allows basic rendering with a single API call.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the category at this node.

The value is copied from the `status` column of the underlying `shopping_mall_categories` record and is used by callers to decide whether to render or dim this node in navigation components.

Typical values include operational states such as `active`, `hidden`, or `deprecated`, and the backend constructs the tree so that only appropriately visible nodes are included for public usage.

sort_order.description:
Ordering hint for this node relative to its siblings at the same depth.

This numeric value is derived from the `sort_order` column and is used to sort siblings when rendering.

Lower numbers typically appear earlier in menus and lists, providing fine-grained control over category presentation.

is_leaf.description:
Indicates whether this node is currently considered a leaf within the tree.

This value mirrors the `is_leaf` column from `shopping_mall_categories` and allows clients to determine if further expansion is possible.

Leaf nodes usually represent categories that directly accept product assignments, whereas non-leaf nodes primarily organize subtrees.

children.description:
List of direct child category nodes under this node.

Each element is another `IShoppingMallCategoryTreeNode`, enabling recursive traversal of the full hierarchy down to leaves.

The server constructs this list by combining `shopping_mall_categories` with hierarchical information (for example from `shopping_mall_category_closures`), ensuring that children are ordered according to `sort_order`.

IShoppingMallCategoryTree.description:
Hierarchical representation of the full shoppingMall category tree.

This read model aggregates data from the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and its associated hierarchy representation (such as `shopping_mall_category_closures`) to provide a single-call snapshot of the entire taxonomy.

Clients use this structure to render navigation menus, category pickers, and administrative overviews without issuing multiple per-level queries, traversing the tree via the `roots` collection of `IShoppingMallCategoryTreeNode` entries.

roots.description:
Top-level category nodes that form the roots of the category tree.

Each root represents a category with no parent (that is, a null `parent_id` in `shopping_mall_categories`) and serves as the entry point into a subtree of nested categories.

Consumers iterate over these nodes and their recursive `children` to construct the complete hierarchical navigation for the catalog.

IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.IReque.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating localized representations of a single category.

This type encapsulates filter and pagination criteria that control which rows from the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` table are returned for a given category. It is designed to be sent in the body of search-style operations (such as PATCH on `/shoppingMall/categories/{categoryId}/localizations`) that return a paginated list of localization summaries.

Typical usage includes administrative translation management UIs and API consumers that need to list or inspect available localizations for editing or review. The DTO focuses on query parameters only and does not map directly to a single Prisma row, so it does not carry an `x-autobe-prisma-schema` marker.

page.description:
Page number for pagination when listing localizations.

Page counting is 1-based by convention in most API designs: `1` represents the first page of results. Combined with `pageSize`, this controls which slice of the ordered localization set is returned.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of localization records to return in a single page.

This value limits result size for performance and usability reasons. Implementations should enforce an upper bound even if clients supply a very large value, to avoid excessive result sets and resource usage.

locale.description:
Optional locale code used to filter localizations, such as `en-US`, `ko-KR`, or `ja-JP`.

When provided, only localizations whose `locale` column matches this value in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` are eligible for inclusion in the result. When null or omitted, all locales for the category may be considered, subject to other filters.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to localized name fields.

Implementations typically use this value to perform a case-insensitive partial match on the `name` column of `shopping_mall_category_localizations`, leveraging text indexes where available. When null or empty, no name-based filtering is applied.

includeDeleted.description:
Flag indicating whether soft-deleted localizations should be included in the search results.

When `true`, rows whose `deleted_at` column is non-null in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` may be returned alongside active localizations. When `false` or null, only active (non-deleted) localizations are returned, reflecting the default business behavior for most UIs.

sortBy.description:
Optional field name that determines the primary sort key for the localization list.

Common values include `locale` and `name`, aligning with indexes defined on the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` table. When omitted or null, the service may use a sensible default ordering such as locale ascending and name ascending.

sortDirection.description:
Optional sort direction for the primary sort field.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted or null, the implementation applies its default sort direction, usually ascending.

IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.description:
Localized representation of a ShoppingMall product category used by storefront and catalog-management clients.

This entity models one row in the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` table and represents how a single logical category from `shopping_mall_categories` should be displayed for a concrete locale such as `"en-US"` or `"ko-KR"`.

Each record is uniquely identified by its own UUID primary key as well as the composite of `(shopping_mall_category_id, locale)`. It carries translatable presentation fields (localized name and description) plus optional SEO metadata that can be rendered in page titles and meta tags.

Lifecycle and audit timestamps track when the localization was created, last updated, or soft-deleted, allowing the platform to distinguish between active localizations and those that are archived or hidden while still preserving history for audit and debugging.

In addition, this DTO exposes a summary projection of the parent category via the `category` association, enabling clients to render both the localized label and the core category context in a single read operation without relying on raw foreign key identifiers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category localization row.

This value corresponds to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` table and is generated by the database or persistence layer.

Clients receive this identifier in read responses and may use it for internal caching or correlation, but they do not provide or modify it in create or update operations.

locale.description:
Locale code for this localization entry such as `"en-US"`, `"ko-KR"`, or `"ja-JP"`.

The value corresponds to the `locale` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and, combined with the underlying foreign key to `shopping_mall_categories`, is uniquely constrained in the database.

Storefront and administrative clients use this field when selecting appropriate translations for users based on their language and region preferences.

name.description:
Localized display name of the category for the given locale.

This value is stored in the `name` column of `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is typically shown in navigation menus, breadcrumbs, and category headers when the user is viewing the site in this locale.

It should be concise, human-friendly, and follow the brand and localization guidelines for the target language.

description.description:
Optional localized description of the category that elaborates on its scope, usage, or marketing message.

This field maps to the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations`. When present, it can be rendered on category landing pages or in help tooltips to explain what kinds of products belong under this category.

If the value is `null`, no localized description is defined and clients may fall back to default text or omit extended description sections entirely.

seo_title.description:
Optional localized SEO title string for the category page.

This field corresponds to the nullable `seo_title` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is intended for use in HTML `<title>` tags or equivalent metadata when rendering localized category pages.

When provided, it should follow search engine optimization and localization guidelines; when `null`, clients may fall back to using the localized name or a default pattern instead.

seo_description.description:
Optional localized SEO description text used in page metadata for the category.

It is backed by the nullable `seo_description` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is typically surfaced as the meta description shown in search results snippets.

If no value is set (null), automated or default descriptions may be used instead, depending on business rules and SEO strategy.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this localization record was first created.

The value is taken from the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is stored in an immutable fashion for audit and historical analysis.

Clients normally treat this field as read-only metadata and may use it for debugging, change tracking, or administrative reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this localization record was last modified.

This value comes from the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is refreshed on each successful update to any mutable localization field.

It allows client applications and administrators to understand the freshness of translation content and to detect whether data has changed since it was last cached.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this localization row.

The field maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations`. When `null`, the localization is considered active from a lifecycle standpoint.

When populated with a timestamp, the localization is logically archived or hidden from normal storefront responses while still preserved in the database for audit, rollback, or troubleshooting workflows.

category.description:
Summary view of the parent category that this localization belongs to.

This association replaces the raw foreign key field that points to `shopping_mall_categories` and gives clients immediate access to key category attributes (such as code, display name, and hierarchy hints) alongside the localized label.

By exposing a summary object instead of a bare identifier, the DTO follows the belongs-to association rule and allows consumers to render category context without issuing an additional lookup by ID.

IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.ICreat.description:
Request body shape for creating a new localized representation of a ShoppingMall category.

This DTO is used by administrative or catalog-management APIs such as `POST /shoppingMall/admin/categories/{categoryId}/localizations` to insert a row into `shopping_mall_category_localizations` for a specific parent category.

It contains only the mutable, business-level fields that clients are allowed to supply when registering a new localization: the locale code, localized name, optional descriptive text, and optional SEO metadata fields. System-managed audit fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` as well as the foreign key to the category are not accepted here and are instead supplied or generated by the backend based on the path parameters and persistence rules.

locale.description:
Locale code for which this localization is being created, for example `"en-US"`, `"ko-KR"`, or `"ja-JP"`.

This value will be persisted into the non-nullable `locale` column of the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` table and combined with the parent category identifier (taken from the path) to enforce the unique `(shopping_mall_category_id, locale)` constraint.

Callers must choose a locale code that is valid for the platform and not already used for the same category.

name.description:
Localized display name of the category in the specified locale.

This value is saved into the `name` column of `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and will typically be rendered in navigation, search filters, and page headers when the storefront is presented in this locale.

It should be concise, user-friendly, and compliant with localization and branding guidelines for the target language.

description.description:
Optional localized descriptive text for the category in the target locale.

When provided, this field is stored in the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and can be displayed on category detail pages to explain what products are included or how the category should be interpreted.

Clients may either omit this field or send it as `null` when no extended localized description is required.

seo_title.description:
Optional localized SEO title for the category page in this locale.

The value is written to the nullable `seo_title` column of `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is intended to be used in page `<title>` tags or comparable metadata.

If omitted or set to `null`, the backend or client may fall back to a default derived from the localized name or other configuration.

seo_description.description:
Optional localized SEO description string for this category in the given locale.

This field populates the nullable `seo_description` column of `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and can be used as the meta description for search engines and social previews.

Callers can leave this value undefined or `null` when no dedicated SEO description is required, in which case downstream systems may rely on generic descriptions or category content instead.

IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.IUpdat.description:
Update DTO for a single category localization record in the shopping mall catalog.

This type represents the subset of fields on `shopping_mall_category_localizations` that are allowed to change when editing an existing localization entry identified by the combination of `shopping_mall_category_id` and `locale`.

It is used as the request body for the admin-facing PUT operation that updates localized metadata such as translated category name, description, and SEO texts. Immutable fields such as the primary key, foreign key to the category, locale identifier, and audit timestamps are intentionally excluded from this DTO and are controlled exclusively by the backend and database layer.

name.description:
Localized category name for the given locale.

This value is displayed to end users when they browse the catalog in the corresponding language or region. It should be concise, user-friendly, and respect any length or character-set conventions defined by the product team.

description.description:
Optional localized description text for the category.

When provided, this text gives users additional context about the category in the target language. When set to `null`, any previously stored description may be cleared depending on service implementation rules.

seo_title.description:
Optional localized SEO title for the category.

This field is typically used in HTML `<title>` tags or other metadata. When omitted or `null`, the system may fall back to the main category name or a default SEO strategy.

seo_description.description:
Optional localized SEO description for the category.

This value is used for search engine snippets and social previews in the configured locale. Leaving it `null` allows SEO tooling or the application to derive descriptions automatically from other fields.

IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying business policy definitions.

This type encapsulates the filters, free-text search options, and pagination instructions used by administrative tools when listing records from the `shopping_mall_business_policies` table.

It is designed to support complex search screens in admin consoles, allowing operators to narrow down policies by stable code, human-readable name, functional category, activation status, and text search over descriptive content while also controlling page size, page index, and sort ordering.

policy_code.description:
Optional exact policy code filter.

When provided, restricts results to a specific policy identified by its stable business identifier (for example `refund_standard`, `review_content`, or `seller_performance`). When `null` or omitted, no filter is applied on the `policy_code` column.

name.description:
Optional partial or exact name filter.

Used to search for policies whose human-readable name matches or contains the given string. Actual matching behavior (exact, case-insensitive, or partial) is implemented in the service or repository layer.

category.description:
Optional category filter corresponding to the `category` column on `shopping_mall_business_policies`.

Typical values include domains such as `refund`, `review`, `seller`, `risk`, or `shipping`. When specified, only policies in the given category are returned.

is_active.description:
Optional activation-state filter.

When `true`, restricts results to policies whose `is_active` flag is enabled. When `false`, returns only inactive or retired policies. When `null`, no filter is applied on activation state.

search.description:
Optional free-text search query.

This value is used to search over text-oriented fields such as policy name and description, leveraging the underlying GIN or full-text search capabilities configured for the `shopping_mall_business_policies` table.

page.description:
Optional 1-based page index for pagination.

When omitted or `null`, the service should fall back to a sensible default (for example page 1). Combined with `limit`, it controls which slice of results is returned to the admin UI.

limit.description:
Optional page size indicating the maximum number of records to return.

When omitted or `null`, the backend applies a default page size and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance. Typical values range between 20 and 100 depending on UI requirements.

sort_by.description:
Optional sort key specifying which column or logical field to order by.

Common values include `created_at`, `updated_at`, `name`, `policy_code`, or `category`. The exact set of accepted keys is validated server-side to prevent arbitrary SQL injection.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for ordering results.

Expected values are typically `asc` or `desc`, indicating ascending or descending order for the selected `sort_by` field. When `null`, the service applies its default ordering (for example, newest policies first).

IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.description:
Logical business policy definition used to group and identify concrete rule configurations across time.

This type represents rows from the shopping_mall_business_policies Prisma model and provides the stable, business-facing identifier and metadata for a policy, such as refund rules, review moderation, or risk thresholds.

It is referenced by version entities and governance tooling when selecting which policy area to inspect or configure.

id.description:
Primary key of the business policy.

This UUID uniquely identifies a logical business policy definition inside the shopping mall governance subsystem and is used internally to join with version records.

policy_code.description:
Stable business identifier for the policy.

Examples include values like `"refund_standard"`, `"review_content"`, or `"seller_performance"`. This code is globally unique and is the primary way external systems and admin tools refer to this policy independent of specific versions.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the business policy.

Displayed in admin dashboards, configuration screens, and audit tools to help users quickly understand what this policy governs.

category.description:
Broad classification of the policy domain.

Typical examples are `"refund"`, `"review"`, `"seller"`, `"risk"`, or `"shipping"`. This field is used to filter and group policies in backoffice UIs and reporting.

description.description:
Detailed description of the business policy and its intent.

This text is authored by governance teams to explain which platform behaviors the policy covers and may be used for documentation and training material.

is_active.description:
Logical activation flag for the business policy definition.

When true, the policy is considered part of the active governance set and can have active versions selected. When false, the policy is logically retired but its versions remain for audit and historical lookups.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this business policy definition was created.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date-time value and used by audit and reporting flows to understand when the policy was onboarded to the platform.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this business policy definition was last updated.

Updated automatically whenever core fields such as name, category, or activation status change, supporting governance audit trails.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the business policy.

When non-null, the policy is considered logically deleted or retired. Historical references from policy versions or cases continue to work, but the policy is typically hidden from normal admin lists.

IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new business policy definition in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_business_policies` Prisma model and carries only the fields that administrators are allowed and required to specify when registering a new policy.

System-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are excluded because they are generated and maintained by the backend. The `policy_code` field must be unique across all policies and becomes the primary business identifier used in API paths and rule engines.

policy_code.description:
Unique business identifier code for the policy.

Must be globally unique within the `shopping_mall_business_policies` table and is used in API paths like `/shoppingMall/admin/businessPolicies/{policyCode}`.

Typical patterns include readable, domain-specific codes such as `refund_standard`, `review_content`, or `seller_performance`.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the new business policy.

Displayed in administrative dashboards and configuration tools to help operators quickly understand the policy’s intent.

category.description:
Domain classification for the policy.

Examples include `refund`, `review`, `seller`, `risk`, or `shipping`. The category is used for filtering, reporting, and grouping policies in admin UIs.

description.description:
Optional long-form description of the policy.

Can contain detailed business context, usage notes, or links to related documentation.

May be omitted or set to null when a concise name and category are sufficient.

is_active.description:
Initial activation flag for the new policy.

When set to `true`, the policy becomes available for use immediately once created.

When set to `false`, the policy is created in an inactive state so that rule versions and downstream configuration can be prepared before activation.

IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying mutable fields of a logical business policy definition in the shopping_mall_business_policies table.

This type is used by administrative update operations that identify the target policy by its stable business policy_code and then apply changes to descriptive and classification fields. It intentionally excludes immutable identifier fields and system-managed timestamps so that only business-facing attributes such as name, category, description, and activation flags can be changed.

Typical usage is in admin consoles and governance tools where operators adjust high-level policy metadata while detailed rule sets are managed through related policy version records in shopping_mall_policy_versions. All properties are optional to support partial updates; validation rules and immutability constraints are enforced in the service layer and database schema.

policy_code.description:
Stable business identifier for the policy, such as "refund_standard", "review_content", or "seller_performance".

Used by backoffice tools and downstream systems to reference the policy independent of specific versions. In update scenarios this field is optional and, when allowed by business rules, can be used to rename or re-code an existing policy record while preserving its identity.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the policy.

Displayed in administrative dashboards, configuration tools, and audit reports to help operators quickly recognize the purpose of the policy.

category.description:
Broad classification of the policy domain.

Examples include "refund", "review", "seller", "risk", or "shipping" and are used for filtering, grouping, and analytics across the policy catalog.

description.description:
Detailed description of the policy and its business intent.

Allows administrators to document what behaviors the policy governs, how it is expected to be applied, and any special considerations or edge cases. When null or omitted, the existing description is left unchanged during an update.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this policy is currently active for selection and evaluation.

When set to true, the policy remains eligible to have active versions associated with it; when false, the policy is logically retired from new use while remaining available for historical reference.

IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying versioned instances of a business policy stored in the shopping_mall_policy_versions table.

This type is used in administrative list and search operations that retrieve policy version records for a specific parent policy, typically identified by its business policy_code in the URL path. It encapsulates pagination controls, sorting preferences, and filter criteria such as status and effective date ranges so that admin UIs can present concise tables of relevant versions.

All properties are optional and can be combined by callers as needed. The backend uses these fields to build WHERE and ORDER BY clauses over the shopping_mall_policy_versions model while always scoping results to the parent policy resolved from the path parameter.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

Used together with limit to control which slice of the version list is returned to the caller. When omitted, the service should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page of results.

Supports API-level control over list size for admin grids. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

status.description:
Optional filter for policy version status such as "draft", "active", or "retired".

When provided, only versions whose status matches the specified value are returned. When null or omitted, versions of all statuses may be included subject to other filters.

effective_from_gte.description:
Lower bound filter for the effective_from timestamp of policy versions.

When provided, only versions whose effective_from is greater than or equal to this value are considered. This helps admins focus on versions that became applicable after a certain point in time.

effective_from_lte.description:
Upper bound filter for the effective_from timestamp of policy versions.

When provided, only versions whose effective_from is less than or equal to this value are included. This is often combined with effective_from_gte to define an effective date window.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to version titles or body_markdown content.

Allows administrators to quickly locate versions mentioning particular concepts, rule names, or phrases within the policy text.

order_by.description:
Field name indicating which column should be used for sorting results.

Typical values include "created_at", "effective_from", or "status" and are interpreted by the backend to build the ORDER BY clause for the shopping_mall_policy_versions query.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction for the result set, such as "asc" for ascending or "desc" for descending order.

When omitted, the service may apply a sensible default such as descending by created_at or effective_from so that the newest versions appear first.

IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.description:
Concrete version of a business policy capturing configuration, rule payloads, and lifecycle metadata.

This type maps directly to rows in the shopping_mall_policy_versions Prisma model and represents a single numbered or coded version of a broader business policy defined by IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy. Each version can encode effective periods, operational status, human-readable policy body, and optional machine-readable parameters.

Policy versions are used by governance and risk engines to determine which set of rules were or will be in effect for a given time window. Admin tooling uses this type for detailed views, auditing, and lifecycle management such as drafting, activating, or retiring policy versions.

id.description:
Primary key of the policy version.

This UUID uniquely identifies a specific version record of a business policy, regardless of its business-level version code.

policy.description:
Logical business policy that owns this version.

The parent entity provides the stable policy_code, human-readable name, and category, allowing governance tooling to display context such as which policy family this version belongs to.

version_code.description:
Business-facing identifier for this policy version.

Examples include values like `"v1"`, `"2024-01"`, or semantic version strings. The combination of `policy.code` and `version_code` is unique and is used in API paths to address this version.

title.description:
Short title summarizing the key intent of this policy version.

Often displayed as the main heading in admin policy viewers and approvals workflows to help users quickly identify the version's purpose.

body_markdown.description:
Full policy body rendered as Markdown.

Contains the human-readable rule text that may be shown to admins, and in some cases surfaced to customers or sellers as the official policy wording for this version.

parameters_json.description:
Optional JSON-encoded structured parameters for programmatic policy evaluation.

This string typically contains serialized JSON with thresholds, numeric limits, time windows, flags, or other configuration used by enforcement engines to make automated decisions based on this policy version.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of this policy version.

Typical values include `"draft"`, `"active"`, and `"retired"`. Only active versions should normally be used for new decisions, while draft and retired versions support staging and historical analysis.

effective_from.description:
Date and time from which this policy version becomes applicable.

When null, the version is considered effective immediately when its status allows it. When set, engines must compare evaluation timestamps against this value to decide whether the version is in effect.

effective_until.description:
Date and time after which this policy version should no longer be applied.

When null, the version has no scheduled expiry and remains valid until explicitly retired or superseded by another version according to business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this policy version row was created.

Supports audit trails, governance reporting, and the ability to reconstruct which policy text existed at a specific moment in time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this policy version row was last updated.

Updated whenever mutable configuration fields such as body_markdown, parameters_json, or status are changed.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this policy version.

When non-null, the version is excluded from normal selection, even if its effective date window would otherwise include a given time, but it remains available for historical audit and case reconstruction.

IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.ICreate.description:
Creation payload for registering a new business policy version under an existing policy.

This DTO is used as the request body for the POST operation that creates rows in the `shopping_mall_policy_versions` table scoped to a parent `shopping_mall_business_policies` record identified by `policyCode` in the path.

It exposes only the fields that callers are allowed to set at creation time. Identifiers and linkage to the parent policy are derived from the request context, while timestamps are managed by the backend.

version_code.description:
Business-facing identifier for the new policy version.

Must be unique within the scope of the parent policy identified by `policyCode`. Common patterns include simple increments such as `"v1"`, calendar-based codes like `"2024-01"`, or semantic versions such as `"1.0.0"`.

title.description:
Short title summarizing the intent of the new policy version.

Displayed prominently in admin configuration UIs and approval workflows, helping governance users distinguish this version from earlier or later ones.

body_markdown.description:
Full policy text expressed as Markdown for the new version.

Contains the human-readable rules, explanations, and obligations that define the policy behavior associated with this version.

parameters_json.description:
Optional JSON string containing structured rule parameters for automated evaluation.

When provided, this field should be valid JSON encoding numeric thresholds, time windows, flags, or other configuration the enforcement engine uses to implement the policy at runtime.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status for the new policy version.

Typical values include `"draft"` for versions under review, `"active"` for versions that should be immediately used for new decisions, and `"retired"` for historical or disabled configurations. Business rules may restrict which statuses are allowed at creation time.

effective_from.description:
Planned start timestamp from which this policy version becomes applicable.

If omitted or null, the effective start may default to the creation time or be controlled purely by the status. When set, scheduling logic uses this timestamp to determine when the version should start governing decisions.

effective_until.description:
Optional expiry timestamp after which this policy version should no longer be applied.

When provided, it defines the upper bound of the version's intended lifecycle. When null, the version remains in effect until explicitly retired or superseded according to governance workflows.

IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.IUpdate.description:
Mutable update DTO for a specific business policy version stored in the shopping_mall_policy_versions table.

This type is used by administrative and governance tooling when editing an existing policy version that has already been created under a parent business policy. It exposes only those columns on shopping_mall_policy_versions that are conceptually updatable after creation, while immutable identifiers such as the foreign key to shopping_mall_business_policies and the version_code remain bound to the path parameters (policyCode and versionCode) and are therefore not present here.

Service implementations should map each property directly to the corresponding Prisma model column, apply validation based on schema comments (for example allowed status values, date range consistency, and JSON validity for structured parameters), and enforce lifecycle rules such as whether an active or expired version may be edited. This DTO does not contain any actor identity fields; authorization for who may update policy versions must be enforced from the authenticated admin context instead of request body fields.

title.description:
Short title or heading summarizing the key intent of this policy version.

This maps to the title column in shopping_mall_policy_versions and is shown in administrative views and audit tools. When updated, the new value should remain concise while clearly distinguishing this version from others under the same business policy.

body_markdown.description:
Full policy body content expressed as Markdown text.

This property corresponds to the body_markdown column of shopping_mall_policy_versions. It contains the human‑readable text of the policy rules shown to internal users and, when applicable, surfaced to customers or sellers. Updates typically occur when the legal or business wording of the policy is refined without changing the structural parameters.

parameters_json.description:
Optional JSON-encoded structured parameters for programmatic evaluation.

This property maps to the parameters_json column of shopping_mall_policy_versions. When present, it should contain a valid JSON string that encodes threshold values, time windows, flags, or other rule parameters interpreted by policy evaluation engines. Setting this to null clears previously stored parameters and implies that only the narrative content governs behavior, or that defaults are used elsewhere.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the policy version such as draft, active, or retired.

This property is stored in the status column of shopping_mall_policy_versions and determines whether the version can be selected for new decisions or only kept for historical reference. Service implementations should only accept values that are valid within the business‑defined status domain and may restrict transitions (for example preventing direct changes from retired back to active).

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this policy version becomes applicable, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This maps to the effective_from column in shopping_mall_policy_versions. When set, the version should only be considered during evaluations at or after this instant; when null, the version is considered effective immediately once activated. Updates must ensure that the value, in combination with effective_until, does not create inconsistent or overlapping ranges within the same business policy.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which this policy version is no longer applicable, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This property corresponds to the effective_until column of shopping_mall_policy_versions. A null value means that the version has no scheduled expiry and remains applicable until explicitly retired or superseded. When populating this field, callers should ensure the date is equal to or later than effective_from when both are present so that the valid period is non‑negative.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the policy version.

This property is backed by the deleted_at column of shopping_mall_policy_versions. In normal administrative flows this is managed by dedicated delete or retire operations rather than general updates, but the DTO allows setting or clearing the value when the platform exposes such controls. A non‑null value indicates that the version is logically deleted and must be excluded from active selection even if its effective dates would otherwise include the evaluation time.

IShoppingMallBusinessPolicy.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for shopping mall business policies.

Represents a condensed view of a high-level business policy that governs marketplace behavior such as refunds, cancellations, reviews, seller performance, or risk handling. It is directly backed by the `shopping_mall_business_policies` Prisma model and surfaces the key identifying and classification fields required for list views, selection UIs, and cross-entity references.

This summary intentionally does not include version-level rule content, Markdown policy bodies, or parameter payloads. Instead, it focuses on stable identifiers (`policy_code`), human-readable naming, domain classification (`category`), active/inactive status, and lifecycle timestamps so that administrative and analytical clients can efficiently understand which policies exist and which are currently in use.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the business policy.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_business_policies` table and is used to reference the policy from other entities such as policy versions, overrides, cases, or dashboards.

code.description:
Stable business policy code used for configuration, integration, and human-readable references.

Backed by the `policy_code` column in the `shopping_mall_business_policies` table, this code acts as a durable identifier such as `refund_standard`, `review_content`, or `seller_performance`. It is typically unique and preferred over the raw UUID in admin tools, logs, and configuration files.

name.description:
Display name of the business policy.

The name is shown in admin consoles, audit views, and configuration pages so that operators can quickly recognize the purpose of the policy, for example "Standard Refund Policy" or "Premium Seller Performance Policy".

category.description:
High-level domain category for the business policy.

This value corresponds to the `category` column in `shopping_mall_business_policies` and classifies the policy into broad domains such as `refund`, `review`, `seller`, `risk`, or `shipping`. It is used for filtering, navigation, and analytics when administrators work with large sets of policies.

description.description:
Functional description of what this policy governs and how it is intended to be used.

Typically derived from the `description` column on the `shopping_mall_business_policies` model, it explains the business intent of the policy at a high level so that operators and integrators can understand its role without reading the full rule text or legal copy.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this logical policy is currently active within the platform.

This flag reflects the `is_active` column on `shopping_mall_business_policies`. Active policies are considered when selecting which versions should be applied in runtime decision flows, while inactive policies are retained for audit and historical reference but normally excluded from active behavior selection.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this business policy definition was created, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The value mirrors the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_business_policies` and is used in audit views, governance reporting, and operational dashboards to understand when the policy first entered the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this business policy definition was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value comes from the `updated_at` column on `shopping_mall_business_policies` and helps administrators understand how recently the policy configuration was modified, which is useful for troubleshooting behavioral changes and tracking policy maintenance activity.

IShoppingMallRiskRule.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for listing risk rule configurations stored in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table.

Administrative risk and governance tools use this type when querying the catalogue of risk rules that drive the platform’s risk engine. It provides rich filtering across dimensions such as rule code, name, scope, severity, enablement status, effective date ranges, and country applicability, while also supporting pagination and sorting for efficient browsing of large rule sets.

Each property in this DTO maps conceptually to one or more columns on shopping_mall_risk_rules, but the DTO itself is a request model and therefore does not carry the x-autobe-prisma-schema marker. Service implementations should translate the criteria into Prisma queries that respect indexes on scope, severity, enabled flag, and effective dates, and must ensure that invalid combinations—such as inverted date ranges—are rejected with clear validation errors rather than producing ambiguous results.

page.description:
1-based index of the result page to retrieve.

This controls which slice of the matching risk rules is returned. When omitted, implementations commonly default to the first page. Callers use this together with limit to paginate through the full rule set in an admin UI.

limit.description:
Maximum number of risk rule records to return in a single page.

This value is used to cap the result size for each request. Service implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large pages that could degrade performance, even if callers provide a higher value.

rule_code.description:
Optional exact-matching filter on the stable business identifier of a risk rule.

When provided, only rules whose rule_code column matches this value are included in the result set. This is typically used when the caller knows the precise code and wants to verify its configuration in the listing context.

name.description:
Optional filter on the human-readable name of the risk rule.

Implementations may treat this as either an exact match or a partial, case-insensitive search over the name column in shopping_mall_risk_rules, taking advantage of configured text indexes. When null or omitted, name is not used as a filter.

scope.description:
Optional filter for the scope in which the risk rule operates.

This corresponds to the scope column of shopping_mall_risk_rules and typically takes values such as account, order, payment, seller, or session. When set, only rules whose scope matches the provided value are returned; when null, all scopes are considered.

severity.description:
Optional filter for the business severity level of risk rules.

This property maps to the severity column on shopping_mall_risk_rules, where common values include low, medium, high, and critical. Filtering by severity allows admins to focus on high‑impact rules during audits or troubleshooting.

is_enabled.description:
Optional filter controlling whether only enabled, only disabled, or all risk rules are returned.

This criterion reflects the is_enabled column on shopping_mall_risk_rules. When true, only currently active rules are listed; when false, only disabled rules are included; when null, the filter is not applied and both enabled and disabled rules are returned.

effective_at.description:
Optional point-in-time filter used to select rules that are effective at a specific instant.

When provided, the implementation should return only those rows where the effective_from and effective_until columns on shopping_mall_risk_rules encompass this timestamp according to the platform’s inclusion rules. A null value indicates that no effective date window filtering is applied.

country_code.description:
Optional ISO country code used to filter rules by geographical applicability.

This property is evaluated against the applies_to_countries column of shopping_mall_risk_rules when that column is populated with a JSON-encoded array of country codes. When provided, only rules that are considered applicable to the specified country are returned; when null, global and all-region rules are included without country-based restriction.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to rule_code, name, or description fields.

This enables administrators to quickly locate risk rules using partial keywords or phrases. Implementations may map this to full-text search across indexed columns or to simple case-insensitive LIKE queries, depending on the database capabilities.

order_by.description:
Optional field name indicating which column should be used to sort the results.

Typical values include created_at, updated_at, rule_code, severity, or scope. When null, a sensible default ordering such as created_at descending or rule_code ascending should be applied.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the primary ordering field, typically asc or desc.

When omitted or null, implementations should default to a stable, documented direction such as desc for time-based columns. The value must be validated so that only allowed directions are accepted.

IShoppingMallRiskRule.description:
Represents a single risk evaluation rule configuration stored in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table.

Each record defines how the risk engine should evaluate a specific fraud or risk scenario, including a stable business identifier (`rule_code`), human‑readable name, scope of evaluation, severity level, serialized rule expression, and optional applicability and lifecycle metadata.

Risk rules are referenced by other risk and case management components whenever they explain why activity was flagged, blocked, or escalated. They are also used in administrative dashboards where governance and risk teams inspect, tune, and audit risk configuration over time.

id.description:
Primary key of the risk rule.

This UUID uniquely identifies a single row in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table and is used internally for joins and low‑level references. It is generated by the database or application layer and is never supplied by API clients when creating rules.

rule_code.description:
Stable business identifier for the risk rule.

Values are human‑meaningful codes such as `high_refund_rate`, `multiple_failed_logins`, or `suspicious_address_mismatch`. This field is constrained by a unique index on `[rule_code]`, making it the primary external key used by APIs and reporting.

Administrative operations like GET/PUT/DELETE `/shoppingMall/admin/riskRules/{ruleCode}` use this code in the path parameter to locate the target rule.

name.description:
Human‑readable display name of the risk rule.

This text is shown in admin risk dashboards, configuration consoles, and audit tools to help administrators quickly recognize the intent of the rule without parsing its technical expression.

scope.description:
Business scope in which this risk rule operates.

Typical values describe the type of entity the rule evaluates, such as `account`, `order`, `payment`, `seller`, or `session`. The scope guides risk services on which data model or event stream to apply the rule to and helps administrators filter rules by domain.

severity.description:
Business severity level that indicates the risk impact of this rule.

Common categories include `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. Downstream workflows and dashboards can use this field to prioritize investigations, determine whether to block activity automatically, or route cases for manual review.

expression_json.description:
JSON‑encoded representation of the rule logic or parameters.

The stored JSON contains condition expressions, thresholds, time windows, and other parameters that the risk engine interprets at runtime. Its exact schema is owned by the risk engine, but this field always contains valid JSON text and is required for rule evaluation.

description.description:
Optional narrative description of what this risk rule detects and how it should be handled.

Administrators use this text to document detection rationale, edge cases, and recommended remediation actions for governance, support, and audit purposes. When null, no additional free‑form documentation was provided at creation time.

is_enabled.description:
Indicates whether this rule is currently active in risk evaluation.

When `true`, the risk engine considers this rule during evaluations for its scope and effective date window. When `false`, the rule definition is retained for history but is ignored in runtime evaluations even if its effective dates would include the current time.

applies_to_countries.description:
Optional JSON‑encoded array of ISO country codes where this rule is applicable.

When populated, the JSON text typically encodes an array such as `["US", "KR"]`, limiting the rule to those regions. When null, the rule is considered global and may apply regardless of country context.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this risk rule becomes effective.

If set, the risk engine should evaluate this rule only for events occurring at or after the given instant. When null, the rule is effective immediately upon creation or enablement, subject to `is_enabled` and `deleted_at` state.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which this risk rule is no longer considered during evaluation.

If set, the rule automatically expires after the given instant even if `is_enabled` remains true. When null, the rule has no scheduled expiry and stays effective until explicitly disabled or logically retired.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of this risk rule record.

Recorded when the rule is first inserted into `shopping_mall_risk_rules`. Administrators and auditors use this field to understand when the rule was introduced into the risk configuration.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of this risk rule record.

This value is refreshed whenever the rule configuration changes, such as when modifying its expression, severity, or enabled status. It supports change tracking and audit trails for risk governance.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating logical retirement of the rule.

When non‑null, the rule is considered logically retired and must not be used for new evaluations, regardless of its `is_enabled` value or effective date range. Administrative APIs like DELETE `/shoppingMall/admin/riskRules/{ruleCode}` set this field instead of physically deleting the row.

IShoppingMallRiskRule.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new risk evaluation rule in the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table.

This DTO captures all configurable fields that administrators must supply when defining a rule for the risk engine, including the stable business identifier (`rule_code`), naming and classification attributes, and the JSON expression that encodes rule logic and thresholds.

It is used by the `POST /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules` endpoint and is restricted to administrative actors, ensuring only privileged users can add or change risk evaluation behavior on the platform.

rule_code.description:
Stable business identifier for the new risk rule.

This code must be globally unique across all records in `shopping_mall_risk_rules`, as enforced by the unique index on `[rule_code]`. Typical values include tokens like `high_refund_rate`, `multiple_failed_logins`, or `suspicious_address_mismatch` that convey the rule’s purpose to risk and governance users.

name.description:
Human‑readable name of the risk rule.

Displayed in administrative risk dashboards and configuration tools so that operators can quickly recognize and search for the rule. Names should be concise yet descriptive of the detected pattern.

scope.description:
Scope in which this rule operates.

Defines the domain or entity type the rule evaluates, such as `account`, `order`, `payment`, `seller`, or `session`. The risk engine uses this value to route events and entities to the appropriate ruleset.

severity.description:
Business severity classification for this rule.

Used to indicate the potential impact or risk level associated with matches, typically using categories such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. Downstream workflows can use severity to decide between soft flags, manual review, or automatic blocking.

expression_json.description:
JSON‑encoded expression or parameter set defining the rule logic.

The value must be a syntactically valid JSON string representing conditions, thresholds, and optional time windows that the risk engine understands. The exact schema of this JSON is defined by the risk engine and validated server‑side before persisting.

description.description:
Optional extended explanation of what this rule detects and how it should be handled.

Administrators can use this to document rationale, edge cases, and remediation guidance. When omitted or null, no additional narrative description is stored for the rule.

is_enabled.description:
Initial enabled state of the rule.

When `true`, the rule becomes eligible for evaluation as soon as it is created and its effective date window allows. When `false`, the rule is stored but inactive until explicitly enabled via an update operation.

applies_to_countries.description:
Optional JSON‑encoded array of country codes limiting where the rule applies.

If supplied, it should be a JSON string representing an array of ISO country codes such as `["US", "KR"]`. When null or omitted, the rule is treated as globally applicable.

effective_from.description:
Optional timestamp from which the rule becomes effective.

If provided, the rule should only be applied to events occurring at or after this instant. When null, the rule is considered effective immediately upon creation provided it is enabled and not logically retired.

effective_until.description:
Optional timestamp after which the rule should no longer be evaluated.

If provided, the rule automatically expires after this instant even if it remains enabled. When null, there is no scheduled expiry and the rule remains in force until disabled or logically retired.

name.description:
Human‑readable name of the risk rule.

Displayed in administration consoles, risk dashboards, and configuration tools so that governance users can quickly recognize the purpose of the rule. Must be a concise but descriptive label that clearly distinguishes this rule from others.

scope.description:
Scope in which this rule operates, mapped directly to the scope column on shopping_mall_risk_rules.

Typical values include logical domains such as "account", "order", "payment", "seller", or "session", indicating what type of entity the rule evaluates. Implementations may validate this field against an internal enumeration of supported scopes.

severity.description:
Business severity level for this rule, corresponding to the severity column in shopping_mall_risk_rules.

Common values are "low", "medium", "high", or "critical" and are used by the risk engine and operations teams to prioritize alerts, escalations, and automated actions when the rule is triggered.

expression_json.description:
JSON‑encoded representation of the rule logic or parameters, mapped to the expression_json column in shopping_mall_risk_rules.

Contains the structured configuration that the risk engine interprets when evaluating events, including thresholds, time windows, and conditional predicates. The backend should validate that this string contains syntactically valid JSON before persisting it.

description.description:
Optional detailed explanation of what this risk rule detects, mapped to the nullable description column.

Can document detection patterns, example scenarios, and recommended remediation actions so that case reviewers and administrators understand why and how the rule fires.

is_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether this rule is currently active in risk evaluations, corresponding to the is_enabled column.

When true, the rule is considered by the risk engine (subject to effective date constraints); when false, the rule is preserved but ignored at runtime without being physically deleted.

applies_to_countries.description:
Optional JSON‑encoded array of ISO country codes where this rule is applicable, mapped to the applies_to_countries column.

When non‑null, the risk engine should restrict evaluation of this rule to the specified countries. A null value means that the rule is global and applies regardless of country.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this risk rule becomes effective, aligned with the effective_from column in shopping_mall_risk_rules.

When provided, evaluations that occur before this instant must not consider the rule active. A null value means the rule becomes effective immediately according to other activation flags.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which this risk rule is no longer considered in evaluations, mapped to the effective_until column.

When provided, evaluations that occur after this instant must ignore the rule even if it is enabled. A null value indicates no scheduled expiry for the rule.

IShoppingMallRiskRule.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for a ShoppingMall risk evaluation rule stored in the shopping_mall_risk_rules table.

This type models the set of fields that governance and risk administrators are allowed to change when adjusting an existing rule, such as the human‑readable name, descriptive text, severity level, activation flags, applicability, and effective date window.

It is used as the request body for the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/riskRules/{ruleCode} endpoint and is applied to an existing record identified by its unique rule_code business key in the shopping_mall_risk_rules Prisma model. System‑managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are not accepted from the client and are updated by the backend implementation only.

IShoppingMallRiskRuleEvaluation.IRequest.description:
Request payload for evaluating active ShoppingMall risk rules against a provided context.

This DTO describes the evaluation scope (such as account, order, payment, seller, or session) and the domain-specific attributes required by risk rules stored in `shopping_mall_risk_rules`. The payload is designed to be generic enough for multiple scopes while still providing structured fields for commonly used identifiers and monetary values. Additional arbitrary context attributes can be supplied via the `context` object for use by rule expressions encoded in `expression_json`.

scope.description:
Logical evaluation scope that determines which subset of risk rules will be applied.

Typical values align with the `scope` column of `shopping_mall_risk_rules`, such as `"account"`, `"order"`, `"payment"`, `"seller"`, or `"session"`. Implementations may define additional scopes as needed, but callers should use documented values only.

evaluationTimestamp.description:
Timestamp at which the risk evaluation is considered to occur.

The engine uses this value to determine which rules are active based on their `effective_from` and `effective_until` windows. When omitted, the server typically uses the current time.

accountId.description:
Optional identifier of the account being evaluated.

For `account` scope this usually represents a customer ID, seller ID, admin ID, or guest user ID depending on the evaluation context. It may also be used as a generic actor identifier in other scopes.

orderId.description:
Optional identifier of the order being evaluated in `order`-centric scopes.

When the evaluation is about a specific order (for example, pre-fulfillment checks), this field carries the platform order ID.

paymentId.description:
Optional identifier of the logical payment being evaluated in `payment`-centric scopes.

This typically corresponds to a record in the order payments model used by the risk engine.

sellerId.description:
Optional identifier of the seller involved in the evaluation.

Used when evaluating seller-related risk rules, such as suspicious behavior or performance anomalies.

sessionId.description:
Optional identifier of the authentication or browsing session that triggered the evaluation.

Useful for rules inspecting repeated activity, device fingerprints, or session anomaly patterns.

countryCode.description:
Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code associated with the evaluated context.

This might represent the billing country, shipping country, or account country depending on the scope, and is often used with country-specific risk rules.

currencyCode.description:
Optional three-letter ISO 4217 currency code associated with the evaluated monetary amounts.

Risk rules may use this value to apply currency-specific thresholds or behaviors.

amount.description:
Primary monetary amount associated with the evaluation context.

For example, this might be the order grand total, payment amount, or cumulative transaction value used in risk thresholds.

ipAddress.description:
IP address associated with the evaluated event.

Rules may inspect this for geolocation anomalies, risk lists, or velocity checks. Format is not strictly validated here but is expected to represent a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address string.

userAgent.description:
User agent string of the client that triggered the evaluation.

Rules may inspect this value to detect automated traffic, unsupported clients, or suspicious device patterns.

context.description:
Arbitrary JSON object containing additional attributes required by rule expressions.

Keys and value shapes are implementation-specific and may include nested objects or arrays. This bag of attributes allows the risk engine to evolve without changing the public DTO for every new signal.

IShoppingMallRiskRuleEvaluation.description:
Detailed risk evaluation result produced by applying active ShoppingMall risk rules to a supplied context.

This DTO contains both per-rule outcomes and overall aggregated indicators that can be used by calling services, administrative tools, or dashboards. It echoes the evaluation scope and selected identifiers, then lists every rule that was considered along with whether it was triggered, its severity, and any explanatory details. Optional aggregate fields summarise the overall risk level, score, or counts of triggered rules for quick decision-making.

scope.description:
Scope that was used when selecting and evaluating risk rules.

Typically mirrors the `scope` requested in `IShoppingMallRiskRuleEvaluation.IRequest` and aligns with the `scope` column in `shopping_mall_risk_rules` (for example `"account"`, `"order"`, `"payment"`, `"seller"`, or `"session"`).

evaluationTimestamp.description:
Timestamp at which the evaluation was executed on the server.

This value reflects the moment used when checking rule effective windows (`effective_from` / `effective_until`) and may differ slightly from any timestamp provided by the caller.

contextId.description:
Optional identifier representing the primary entity evaluated.

Depending on the scope, this may echo an account ID, order ID, payment ID, seller ID, or session ID from the request. It is provided to simplify correlation with external systems and logs.

rulesEvaluatedCount.description:
Total number of risk rules that were considered during this evaluation.

This includes rules that did not trigger as well as those that did trigger. The value is always non-negative and reflects the number of `shopping_mall_risk_rules` records that matched the evaluation scope and activity window at the time of evaluation.

rulesTriggeredCount.description:
Number of risk rules that were triggered (evaluated to true) for the provided context.

This value is always less than or equal to `rulesEvaluatedCount` and represents the subset of rules whose conditions matched the evaluation context. It can be used as a quick indicator of how many risk conditions were met.

highestSeverity.description:
Highest severity level among all triggered rules, if any.

Typical values align with the `severity` column in `shopping_mall_risk_rules`, such as `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, or `"critical"`. When no rules trigger this field may be null or omitted depending on implementation.

aggregatedScore.description:
Optional numeric aggregate score representing overall risk for the evaluated context.

Implementations may compute this by combining per-rule scores, severity weights, or other heuristics. A higher value typically indicates more severe or numerous risk triggers. When not used, this field can be omitted to indicate that only qualitative severity is reported.

rules.description:
Collection of per-rule evaluation outcomes for all rules that were considered under the selected scope.

Each entry corresponds to one configuration row in `shopping_mall_risk_rules` that matched the evaluation scope and effective window. It exposes identifiers, severity, trigger status, and optional explanatory details suitable for dashboards and risk analysis tools.

IShoppingMallRiskRuleEvaluationRuleResul.description:
Per-rule evaluation outcome for a single risk rule drawn from `shopping_mall_risk_rules`.

Each element records basic identifying information about the rule (such as `rule_code`, `name`, `scope`, and `severity`), whether it triggered for the evaluated context, and any structured details or human-readable messages explaining the result. These entries enable risk analysts, dashboards, and automated enforcement flows to understand exactly which rules influenced the final risk assessment.

ruleCode.description:
Globally unique code of the risk rule as stored in `shopping_mall_risk_rules.rule_code`.

This identifier is stable across rule updates and is suitable for logging, alerting, and correlation with configuration management tooling.

name.description: Human-readable name of the risk rule, generally reflecting its purpose or detection pattern.

scope.description:
Scope of the risk rule, aligned with `shopping_mall_risk_rules.scope` and the evaluation request scope.

Examples include `"account"`, `"order"`, `"payment"`, `"seller"`, or `"session"`.

severity.description:
Configured severity level of the rule, as stored in `shopping_mall_risk_rules.severity`.

Common values include `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, and `"critical"`. Clients can use this to drive alerting thresholds and UI emphasis.

triggered.description:
Indicates whether the rule condition evaluated to true for the given context.
