A value of `true` means the rule was triggered and should be taken into account for risk decisions. A value of `false` means the rule did not detect a condition of interest.

scoreContribution.description:
Optional numeric contribution of this rule to the aggregated risk score.

Implementations that compute an overall score can use this field to expose how much weight this particular rule added when it triggered.

message.description:
Optional human-readable message describing why the rule did or did not trigger.

This is primarily intended for use in risk dashboards, analyst tools, and logs. It should avoid exposing sensitive internal implementation details of `expression_json` while still providing actionable explanations.

details.description:
Optional structured details object containing machine-readable explanation data.

Keys and values are implementation-specific and may include threshold comparisons, matched attributes, or counters that help downstream systems or analysts interpret the outcome.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewDashboard.description:
Aggregated system overview dashboard for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO provides a consolidated, read-only snapshot of key marketplace performance, activity, and health indicators intended for administrative dashboards and operational monitoring tools. It composes metrics from snapshot and analytics tables such as `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`, `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats`, `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`, and `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`.

The purpose of this type is to allow admins to understand the current state of the platform "at a glance" without querying raw transactional tables. It focuses on aggregated counts, revenue summaries, trend indicators, and high-level risk or dispute metrics rather than exposing individual orders, payments, or accounts.

generatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this dashboard view was generated.

Clients can use this value to understand the freshness of the underlying metrics and to avoid caching stale data for too long.

timeWindow.description:
Human-readable description of the primary reporting window represented by the dashboard data.

Examples include `"last_24_hours"`, `"last_7_days"`, or `"month_to_date"`. The exact semantics are determined by the backend implementation and configuration.

orders.description:
Order-related metrics section of the dashboard.

Provides counts and averages describing order creation and lifecycle outcomes over the reporting window.

revenue.description:
Revenue-focused metrics section of the dashboard.

Summarizes gross merchandise volume, net revenue, and refund or dispute-related financial impact.

actors.description:
Actor activity metrics section of the dashboard.

Highlights active and newly onboarded customers and sellers for the reporting window.

payments.description:
Payment performance metrics section of the dashboard.

Shows payment volumes and success or failure rates across all payment methods.

shipping.description:
Shipping and delivery performance metrics section of the dashboard.

Summarizes shipment volumes, delivery outcomes, and latency indicators.

refundsAndDisputes.description:
Refund and dispute activity metrics section of the dashboard.

Provides an overview of refund requests, approved refunds, and dispute volumes.

riskAndCompliance.description:
Risk and compliance activity metrics section of the dashboard.

Highlights open and newly created risk cases, policy overrides, and related admin notifications.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewOrdersSection.description:
Order-related metrics portion of the shoppingMall system overview dashboard.

This section summarizes order volumes and basic lifecycle distribution over the selected reporting window using snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`. It is optimized for quick comprehension by administrators monitoring marketplace activity and overall order health.

The metrics are precomputed aggregates for a defined reporting window and are not tied to individual orders. They are typically presented alongside other system overview sections such as revenue, payments, shipping, and risk in a single dashboard payload.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of orders created within the primary reporting window.

This count includes all orders regardless of their final lifecycle state and is typically used as the baseline order volume indicator for the selected period.

completedOrders.description:
Number of orders that reached a completed or fulfilled state within the reporting window.

This value helps administrators understand how many orders successfully passed through the full fulfillment lifecycle in the selected period.

cancelledOrders.description:
Number of orders that were cancelled during the reporting window, regardless of who initiated the cancellation.

This count is used to monitor cancellation behavior and can be correlated with customer satisfaction, inventory issues, payment failures, or risk rules.

refundedOrders.description:
Number of orders that had at least one refund processed during the reporting window.

The metric increments when any refund event is associated with an order, even if the refund was partial, and is used to gauge refund-related friction or post-payment problems.

averageOrderValue.description:
Average order value over the reporting window.

Typically computed as total gross merchandise value divided by the number of completed orders in the period, expressed in the platform’s base currency with fractional amounts allowed.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewRevenueSectio.description:
Revenue-focused metrics portion of the shoppingMall system overview dashboard.

This section summarizes core financial indicators derived from snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`, and platform-level KPI snapshots over a defined reporting window. It is intended to give administrators a quick sense of gross merchandise volume, net revenue, and the financial impact of refunds and disputes.

All monetary values are aggregated for the selected reporting window and are typically expressed in the platform’s base currency. They are designed for high-level monitoring and trend analysis rather than detailed accounting reconciliation.

grossMerchandiseVolume.description:
Total gross merchandise volume (GMV) over the reporting window.

This usually represents the sum of order line item values before discounts and refunds, expressed in the platform’s base currency with support for fractional amounts.

netRevenue.description:
Estimated net revenue for the platform over the reporting window.

This typically reflects gross merchandise volume minus refunds, discounts, and any platform-specific adjustments or fees consistent with business reporting practices, expressed in the platform’s base currency.

refundAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded to customers during the reporting window, including both full and partial refunds.

This value aggregates refund transactions recorded against orders and payments and is used to understand the financial impact of cancellations, returns, and service issues.

disputeLossAmount.description:
Total monetary amount lost due to chargebacks or dispute resolutions against the platform during the reporting window.

The metric aggregates losses from dispute and chargeback cases and helps administrators monitor risk exposure, fraud, and dispute-handling quality from a financial perspective.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewActorsSection.description:
Actor-focused metrics portion of the shoppingMall system overview dashboard.

This section highlights current and recent activity levels for core actors in the marketplace such as customers and sellers, using snapshot tables like `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` and `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`. It aims to provide a quick understanding of platform engagement and growth.

activeCustomers.description:
Estimated number of active customers during the reporting window.

The precise definition of "active" is determined by business rules, such as having placed an order, logged in, or otherwise engaged with the platform.

newCustomers.description: Number of new customer accounts created during the reporting window.

activeSellers.description: Estimated number of sellers with at least one qualifying activity (such as new listings or fulfilled orders) during the reporting window.

newSellers.description: Number of new seller accounts onboarded during the reporting window.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewPaymentsSecti.description:
Payment-related metrics portion of the shoppingMall system overview dashboard.

This section consolidates high-level payment method performance and reliability indicators based on snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` and related aggregates. It helps admins quickly detect anomalies in payment success rates or shifts in method usage.

totalPayments.description: Total count of logical payment attempts recorded during the reporting window, across all payment methods.

successfulPayments.description: Number of payments that completed successfully during the reporting window.

failedPayments.description: Number of payments that failed or were declined during the reporting window.

paymentSuccessRate.description:
Overall payment success rate for the reporting window expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

Typically computed as `successfulPayments / max(totalPayments, 1)`.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewShippingSecti.description:
Shipping and delivery metrics portion of the shoppingMall system overview dashboard.

This section provides a simplified view of outbound shipment volumes and high-level delivery performance indicators for a selected reporting window. It is designed for operators and administrators who need a quick understanding of how shipping is performing without drilling into detailed logistics or shipment-event timelines.

Values are typically derived from snapshot or analytics tables such as `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` and related shipment models. All metrics are non-negative aggregates over the reporting window and are expected to be returned together as part of a broader system overview dashboard response rather than as a standalone resource.

shipmentsCreated.description:
Total number of shipments created during the reporting window.

This is a non-negative aggregate count of shipment headers that entered the system (for example, rows inserted into `shopping_mall_shipments`) within the same time range used for the rest of this section. Implementations should ensure that canceled or logically deleted shipments are handled consistently with the business definition of "created".

shipmentsDelivered.description:
Number of shipments marked as delivered during the reporting window.

This is a non-negative aggregate count of shipments that transitioned into a final "delivered" or equivalent status in the underlying shipment or shipping performance tables during the same reporting window. It is used to compare shipped volume versus successfully completed deliveries.

onTimeDeliveryRate.description:
Proportion of shipments delivered on or before their expected delivery time during the reporting window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

The numerator is the count of shipments that met the on-time criteria, and the denominator is the total number of shipments that were delivered in the same reporting window. A value of 1 indicates that all delivered shipments were on time, while 0 indicates that none were on time.

averageDeliveryTimeHours.description:
Average end-to-end delivery time for shipments delivered during the reporting window, measured in hours.

This value is typically computed as the arithmetic mean of per-shipment delivery durations (for example, delivery timestamp minus shipment creation timestamp) for all shipments delivered within the reporting window. It should be a non-negative number and may include fractional hours to reflect partial hours of transit time.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewRefundsAndDis.description:
Refund and dispute metrics portion of the shoppingMall system overview dashboard.

This section summarizes return, refund, and dispute activity for a selected reporting window using aggregated counts sourced from analytics and case-management tables such as `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` and related refund, cancellation, and dispute models. It provides a compact view of customer satisfaction and operational friction related to post‑order issues.

The metrics are non-negative aggregates intended for high-level monitoring and trend visualization. Detailed drill-down views, such as per-case or per-order inspection, are handled by dedicated refund, cancellation, and dispute endpoints rather than this overview section.

refundRequests.description:
Number of refund requests created during the reporting window.

This is a non-negative aggregate count of refund request headers (for example, rows in `shopping_mall_refund_requests`) whose creation timestamp falls within the reporting window. It reflects overall customer demand for refunds, regardless of whether those requests were later approved or rejected.

approvedRefunds.description:
Number of refund requests that were approved and led to refunds during the reporting window.

This is a non-negative aggregate count of refund cases that reached an approved or completed state and resulted in monetary refunds within the same reporting window. Implementations should align the counting rule (for example, based on approval timestamp or refund execution timestamp) with the platform’s reporting standard.

openDisputes.description:
Current count of open disputes across the platform at the time the dashboard was generated.

This is a non-negative snapshot count of dispute cases (for example, rows in `shopping_mall_disputes`) that are in any business state considered "open" (such as pending review, investigating, or awaiting evidence) when the overview is produced. It is not limited to disputes created in the current reporting window.

newDisputes.description:
Number of new disputes opened during the reporting window.

This is a non-negative aggregate count of dispute cases whose creation timestamp falls within the reporting window. It helps administrators understand how many new high-severity conflicts entered the pipeline during the same period that other refund and dispute metrics are measured.

IShoppingMallSystemOverviewRiskAndCompli.description:
Risk and compliance metrics portion of the shoppingMall system overview dashboard.

This section provides a snapshot of key governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) indicators at the time the dashboard is generated. Each metric is a non‑negative integer count computed from underlying risk case management, policy override, and administrative notification data sources such as `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`, and admin notification queues.

The DTO is read‑only and is designed to be embedded into a broader system overview dashboard for administrators, risk owners, and compliance officers. It helps stakeholders quickly understand the volume of active risk cases, recent case inflow, how often standard policies are being overridden, and the number of outstanding governance‑related tasks that still require attention.

Values in this structure are aggregates over a business‑defined reporting window (for example, today, the last 7 days, or the current month). The snapshot does not expose individual case or notification records; instead, it focuses on concise, high‑level indicators that can be trended over time and correlated with other operational KPIs.

openRiskCases.description:
Total number of currently open risk or fraud cases at the time the dashboard snapshot is generated.

This value is derived by counting risk case records (for example, rows in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`) that are in an active or unresolved status such as `OPEN`, `INVESTIGATING`, or `ESCALATED`. Closed, canceled, or otherwise resolved cases are excluded so that the metric represents the active workload facing risk and governance teams.

The value is always a non‑negative integer and is useful for monitoring the size of the risk case backlog, setting staffing expectations, and detecting periods where operational capacity may be under strain.

newRiskCases.description:
Number of new risk or fraud cases opened during the configured reporting window.

This metric is typically calculated by counting risk case records whose creation timestamp falls within the window used to generate the dashboard (for example, the last day or last week). It includes cases regardless of their current resolution state; even if a case is opened and closed on the same day, it contributes to the new‑case count for that period.

The value is a non‑negative integer and helps administrators identify sudden increases in risk activity, validate the impact of new controls or campaigns, and compare the volume of new cases against historical baselines.

policyOverrides.description:
Number of explicit policy override events recorded during the reporting window.

Policy overrides represent situations where a configured business policy or rule was consciously bypassed, relaxed, or overridden by an authorized actor. Examples include approving a refund that exceeds normal thresholds, bypassing a risk rule for a specific transaction, or temporarily relaxing an SLA requirement. Each override event is typically persisted in a table such as `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`.

The value is a non‑negative integer and acts as an indicator of how often normal policies are being circumvented. High or increasing override counts may warrant a review of policy design, governance approval flows, or training for operational teams.

adminNotifications.description:
Number of outstanding administrative notifications or tasks related to risk, compliance, or governance.

This metric usually counts notification or task records from an administrative queue (for example, `shopping_mall_admin_notifications`) that are still open, unread, or unresolved at the time the dashboard is generated. Items that have been completed, dismissed, or archived do not contribute to the count.

The value is a non‑negative integer that helps highlight pending actions for administrators, such as queued approvals, escalated incidents, compliance checks, or time‑sensitive governance tasks that must be processed to keep risk and compliance workflows healthy.

IShoppingMallGeographyStatistics.description:
Aggregated geographic statistics for the shoppingMall marketplace, grouped by country and region.

This DTO is optimized for administrative dashboards and analytical visualizations such as maps and regional comparison charts. It aggregates data from master geography reference tables (for example, `shopping_mall_countries`, `shopping_mall_regions`, and region‑level shipping policies) together with snapshot and analytics tables that capture order volume, revenue, shipping performance, and refund or dispute activity.

Use this structure as the response body for read‑only analytical endpoints that expose marketplace performance metrics by geographic dimension. The payload is intentionally compact and denormalized so that dashboard clients can render geographic overviews without issuing additional per‑region API calls.

regions.description:
List of region‑level aggregated statistics, each representing a country or sub‑region and its associated KPIs over the configured aggregation window (for example, the last 30 days).

Each element corresponds to a single logical geographic segment, typically either a whole country or a specific (country, region) combination derived from reference data in `shopping_mall_countries` and `shopping_mall_regions`. Metrics in each region object are computed from analytics and snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`, and `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`.

The array may be empty when there is no data that matches the current filters or reporting period (for example, in a newly launched marketplace with no orders yet). When it contains data, the ordering of regions is implementation‑defined and may follow business‑specific rules such as descending revenue, descending order count, or alphabetical country name.

IShoppingMallGeographyStatisticsRegion.description:
Region-level aggregated statistics for the shoppingMall marketplace.

Each instance represents a single geographic segment (country or region) and includes identifiers, labels, and computed KPIs such as order volume, revenue, shipping SLA performance, and refund/dispute ratios. Values are typically derived from analytics and snapshot tables like shopping_mall_order_daily_stats, shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats, and shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.

countryCode.description: ISO country code (e.g., "US", "KR") derived from the shopping_mall_countries reference table. Used as a stable identifier for top-level geographic grouping.

countryName.description: Human-readable country name for display in dashboards and maps. Comes from the shopping_mall_countries master data table.

oneOf.description: Optional region or subdivision code within the country (for example, state or province), derived from the shopping_mall_regions table when applicable. For purely country-level aggregates this may be an empty string.

regionCode.description: Optional region or subdivision code within the country (for example, state or province), derived from the shopping_mall_regions table when applicable. For purely country-level aggregates this may be an empty string.

oneOf.description: Optional human-readable label for the region within the country. When no sub-regions are modeled, this may be null or an empty string and the aggregate should be interpreted as country-level only.

regionName.description: Optional human-readable label for the region within the country. When no sub-regions are modeled, this may be null or an empty string and the aggregate should be interpreted as country-level only.

totalOrders.description: Total number of customer orders associated with this geographic region over the aggregation window. Derived from shopping_mall_order_daily_stats and related order fact tables.

totalRevenue.description: Total gross merchandise volume (GMV) or revenue for orders in this region over the aggregation window. Currency handling is implementation-specific but typically uses the platform’s primary settlement currency.

averageOrderValue.description: Average order value for this region, computed as totalRevenue divided by totalOrders over the aggregation window. Zero when there are no orders.

onTimeDeliveryRate.description: Ratio (0–1) of shipments in this region that met configured shipping SLAs. Derived from shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats and region shipping policies. Values close to 1 indicate strong delivery performance.

averageDeliveryDays.description: Average number of days between shipment creation and final delivery for orders in this region. Derived from shipping performance analytics. Lower values indicate faster delivery.

refundRate.description: Ratio (0–1) of orders or order items in this region that resulted in approved refunds over the aggregation period. Derived from shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats and related refund tables.

disputeRate.description: Ratio (0–1) of orders or payments in this region that resulted in disputes or chargebacks. Derived from shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats and dispute-related tables.

primaryPaymentMethodDistributions.description: Distribution of successfully completed payments by primary payment method (for example, credit card, bank transfer, e-wallet) within this region. Useful for understanding payment mix by geography.

oneOf.description: Optional free-form commentary or annotation about this region’s performance, for example highlighting anomalies, campaigns, or operational issues. This is not required for computation and may be an empty string.

notes.description: Optional free-form commentary or annotation about this region’s performance, for example highlighting anomalies, campaigns, or operational issues. This is not required for computation and may be an empty string.

IShoppingMallGeographyStatisticsPaymentM.description:
Aggregated share metrics for a specific payment method within a geographic region.

This object represents how frequently a given payment method is used and how much revenue it contributes for the region over the aggregation window.

paymentMethodCode.description: Stable code or identifier of the payment method (for example, "CARD", "BANK_TRANSFER", "EWALLET"). Typically corresponds to a record in shopping_mall_payment_methods or a similar reference table.

paymentMethodName.description: Human-readable name of the payment method for display purposes (e.g., "Credit Card", "Bank Transfer").

usageCount.description: Number of successful payments using this method in the region over the aggregation window.

usageShare.description: Fraction (0–1) of all successful payments in the region that used this method. Typically, the sum of usageShare across all methods in a region is close to 1.

revenueShare.description: Fraction (0–1) of total revenue in the region that was processed via this payment method. This may differ from usageShare when average order values vary by payment method.

IShoppingMallPolicyStatistics.description:
Aggregated statistical and overview data about business policies configured in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents a denormalized, read-only analytics view that is computed from multiple underlying configuration tables, including `shopping_mall_business_policies`, `shopping_mall_policy_versions`, `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, and `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`. Each field exposes a high-level counter or distribution that summarizes the current state of business policy coverage, lifecycle, and complexity across the marketplace.

The structure is optimized for administrative governance, operations, and compliance dashboards rather than for direct CRUD manipulation of policy entities. Implementations typically materialize these values at query time using aggregation queries rather than persisting the DTO as-is. Clients can use the metrics to answer questions such as "How many policies are active?", "Which domains have the most overrides?", and "How many policy changes occurred in the last N days?"

totalPolicies.description:
Total number of business policy definitions registered in `shopping_mall_business_policies`, regardless of whether they are currently active or retired.

This counter includes all logical policy records that exist in the system at the time of computation. It is commonly used as a baseline metric for understanding overall policy surface area and for validating that more granular breakdowns, such as per-domain or per-type counts, are complete.

activePolicies.description:
Number of business policies that are currently active and considered effective at the time the statistics are computed.

Implementations typically determine activity based on policy-level status flags and on the existence of at least one effective policy version in `shopping_mall_policy_versions`. This metric helps governance and operations teams understand how many policies are actively influencing runtime behavior.

retiredPolicies.description:
Number of business policies that have been retired or are no longer active.

In many configurations this value is expected to match `totalPolicies - activePolicies` when policies are in exactly one of the active or retired states. This metric is useful for understanding the historical churn of policies and for validating lifecycle management practices.

policiesByDomain.description:
Distribution of policies grouped by logical domain or category, such as refunds, reviews, seller performance, risk, or shipping.

Each array element is an `IShoppingMallPolicyStatisticsDomainSummary` object that aggregates counts for a single domain. When the statistics are computed without additional filters, implementations typically ensure that the union of domain-specific counters is consistent with the top-level policy counts, enabling dashboards to render stacked charts or tables by domain.

effectivePolicyVersions.description:
Total number of policy version records that are currently effective across all policies, based on validity periods and activation flags in `shopping_mall_policy_versions`.

This metric reflects the concrete rule payloads that are in force at the moment, which may be greater than or equal to `activePolicies` depending on how many active versions a single policy can have. It is commonly used to gauge configuration complexity and the operational cost of managing policy versions.

policiesWithOverrides.description:
Number of policies that currently have one or more explicit overrides recorded in `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`.

Overrides typically represent exceptions to default policy behavior, such as special handling for particular actors, regions, or product segments. A high value here can indicate complex governance requirements or areas where the default policy set is heavily customized and may need consolidation.

caseSlaConfigCount.description:
Number of case SLA configuration records in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` that are currently active and associated with one or more business policies.

These SLA configurations define target response and resolution times for cases such as cancellations, refunds, and disputes. This metric helps administrators understand how extensively SLA rules are applied across policies and whether additional coverage or simplification is needed.

policyTypeDistributions.description:
Distribution of policies by type or finer-grained classification, such as `REFUND_WINDOW`, `RETURN_SHIPPING`, `REVIEW_MODERATION`, or `RISK_SCORE_THRESHOLD`.

While domain-level grouping focuses on broad functional areas, type-level grouping provides a more detailed view of how many policies fall into each specific behavioral category. Dashboards can use this array to render per-type charts or tables, helping stakeholders understand where policy density is highest.

recentPolicyChangeWindowDays.description:
Length of the lookback window, in days, used when computing the `recentPolicyChanges` counter.

This value is typically supplied as an input to the statistics query or configured centrally for dashboards. Including it in the response allows clients to label charts and tables precisely (for example, "Changes in the last 30 days") and to confirm that they are interpreting the change metrics over the correct time horizon.

recentPolicyChanges.description:
Number of policy- or policy-version-level changes that occurred within the last `recentPolicyChangeWindowDays` days.

Implementations usually include creations, updates, activations, and deactivations of policy definitions or their versions. This metric provides a simple indicator of change velocity in the policy framework and can be used in governance dashboards to highlight periods of intense configuration activity.

IShoppingMallPolicyStatisticsDomainSumma.description:
Summary statistics for business policies within a specific logical domain or category, such as refunds, reviews, risk, seller performance, or shipping.

A domain groups related policies under a shared business area so that governance dashboards can show how many policies exist in each area and how complex each domain has become over time. Each instance of this DTO corresponds to one domain and is typically displayed as a row in a table or as a slice in a chart alongside other domains.

domainCode.description:
Stable, machine-oriented code for the business policy domain, such as `REFUND`, `REVIEW`, `RISK`, `SELLER`, or `SHIPPING`.

This value is intended for programmatic use, filtering, and joining with other analytics structures. It should remain stable over time so that dashboards and reports can rely on it as a key when aggregating or comparing historical data.

domainName.description:
Human-readable name of the business policy domain used in governance dashboards and reports.

Clients may localize this label for display purposes while still relying on `domainCode` as the stable identifier. Typical values mirror business terminology familiar to operations and compliance teams, such as "Refunds" or "Review Moderation".

totalPolicies.description:
Total number of business policies that belong to this domain.

This count is scoped strictly to the domain identified by `domainCode`. In an unfiltered view, the sum of `totalPolicies` across all domain summary rows should be consistent with the top-level `totalPolicies` metric from `IShoppingMallPolicyStatistics`.

activePolicies.description:
Number of policies in this domain that are currently active.

This counter reflects domain-scoped active policies based on the same activity criteria used for the top-level statistics. When aggregated across all domains, these values should align with the global `activePolicies` metric when the same filters are applied.

overriddenPolicies.description:
Number of policies in this domain that currently have one or more entries in `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`, indicating special-case overrides or exceptions.

This metric highlights domains where the default policy set is heavily customized. In governance dashboards, high override counts in a particular domain can signal configuration complexity, potential policy drift, or the need to revisit the baseline policy design.

IShoppingMallPolicyStatisticsTypeDistrib.description:
Distribution metrics for business policies grouped by a more granular policy type or classification.

This DTO is used as a small, reusable analytics bucket inside higher‑level policy statistics responses such as IShoppingMallPolicyStatistics. Whereas policy "domain" typically groups policies by broad business area (for example, refunds, reviews, risk, or seller performance), the policy "type" dimension represented here allows product, risk, and operations teams to drill into more specific categories such as refund windows, return shipping rules, review moderation policies, or risk score thresholds.

Each instance describes a single policy type and the number of active or logically relevant policy definitions that fall into that classification. It is primarily consumed by administrative dashboards, governance reports, and BI tools that visualize how many distinct policies exist in each type bucket and how policy complexity is distributed across the platform.

Consumers commonly render these rows in bar charts, tables, or donut charts to identify areas where policy sprawl may be high, where coverage might be thin, or where additional rationalization and documentation efforts are needed.

typeCode.description:
Machine-readable code representing a business policy type or classification.

Typical examples include values such as `"REFUND_WINDOW"`, `"RETURN_SHIPPING"`, `"REVIEW_MODERATION"`, or `"RISK_SCORE_THRESHOLD"`. This code is stable and is intended for use in configuration, analytics queries, and programmatic integration, rather than for direct display to end users.

The set of supported type codes is defined by the business policy framework and should be treated as a controlled vocabulary when constructing dashboards or reports.

typeName.description:
Human‑readable label for the policy type used in dashboards, administration consoles, and analytical reports.

This value provides a localized or presentation‑friendly name for the `typeCode`, such as "Refund Window", "Return Shipping Policies", or "Review Moderation Rules". It should be suitable for display in charts, tables, and filter pickers without additional transformation.

In multi‑locale deployments, this label may be rendered according to the administrator’s or analyst’s preferred language, while the underlying `typeCode` remains stable for identification.

policyCount.description:
Total number of policies that belong to this policy type across all domains and versions included in the current analytics scope.

This count typically reflects the number of logical policy records whose type classification matches `typeCode`, filtered by whatever time window, status, or scope was applied in the surrounding query. For example, it might count only active policies, policies effective within a reporting period, or policies owned by a particular governance team.

The value is always a non‑negative integer and is primarily used for ranking, visualizing distribution across types, and detecting areas with unusually high or low policy density.

IShoppingMallRiskRuleStatistics.description:
Aggregated statistical and configuration overview for risk evaluation rules in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is designed for administrative dashboards, risk monitoring tools, and governance consoles that need a high‑level view of how risk rules are configured and how actively they are being triggered across the platform. It exposes only derived metrics and distributions rather than individual rule rows, making it efficient to render in charts and summary widgets.

The data is derived primarily from the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` model, which defines the individual risk evaluation rules used by the risk engine to flag suspicious activity, high‑risk orders, or risky accounts. Additional context is drawn from related governance tables such as `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, and `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` so that dashboards can correlate rule posture, case volume, SLA coverage, and override activity in a single response.

Typical use cases include:
- Showing how many rules exist, how many are active versus disabled, and how those rules are distributed by severity.
- Visualizing how many rules have generated risk cases in a recent time window and how those cases are currently distributed by status.
- Assessing SLA coverage for risk‑related case types and monitoring how many active policy overrides are currently affecting risk behavior.

The fields are aggregated at query time and are read‑only from the client’s perspective. They are meant to be refreshed periodically by the UI to provide near‑real‑time visibility into the platform’s risk configuration and operational workload.

total_rules.description:
Total number of risk rules defined in the platform.

This value counts all rows in `shopping_mall_risk_rules` that are within the logical scope of the analytics query, usually including both enabled and disabled rules but excluding soft‑deleted records. It gives governance and risk teams a quick sense of the size and complexity of the rule set they maintain over time.

active_rules.description:
Number of risk rules that are currently enabled for evaluation by the risk engine.

This metric is typically computed over `shopping_mall_risk_rules` rows where an `is_enabled` (or equivalent) flag is true and `deleted_at` is null. It answers the question "How many rules are actually live and influencing risk decisions right now?" and is often compared against `total_rules` to understand how much of the ruleset is actively in use.

disabled_rules.description:
Number of risk rules that are currently disabled and not actively used in risk evaluation.

This count usually includes rules where `is_enabled` is false but the record is still retained for audit, experimentation, or future re‑activation. Monitoring this number alongside `active_rules` helps teams identify stale or deprecated rules that may require cleanup or review.

rules_by_severity.description:
Breakdown of risk rule counts grouped by severity level.

Each entry in this array represents a single severity bucket, such as `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, or `"critical"`, together with the number of rules configured at that severity. The severity values and semantics come from the severity taxonomy defined in `shopping_mall_risk_rules`.

Dashboards typically use this array to render bar charts, stacked columns, or distribution pies that show the configuration posture of the risk engine and help teams understand whether the ruleset is overly concentrated in low‑severity warnings or skewed toward high‑impact interventions.

rules_with_recent_cases.description:
Number of unique risk rules that have triggered at least one risk case during the configured recent time window.

This metric is computed by joining risk signals or rule‑to‑case linkage data with `shopping_mall_risk_cases` and counting distinct rules that appear as the source of at least one case within the time range defined by the analytics query. It helps risk teams quickly see how many rules are actually firing in practice, as opposed to being configured but dormant.

Comparing this number to `active_rules` can highlight rules that are live but rarely triggered, which may warrant tuning or retirement.

case_counts_by_status.description:
Aggregated counts of risk cases grouped by their current status within the selected time window or scope.

Status values typically include states such as `"open"`, `"under_review"`, and `"closed"` taken from the `status` column of `shopping_mall_risk_cases`. Each bucket shows how many cases are currently in that state, helping teams understand operational workload, backlog, and closure performance at a glance.

Dashboards commonly present this distribution as a bar chart or stacked indicator so operations teams can quickly spot imbalances or increasing backlogs in specific statuses.

sla_coverage_rate.description:
Ratio indicating how many relevant risk‑related case types have explicit SLA (Service‑Level Agreement) configurations.

The value is typically expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1 and is derived from `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` compared against the set of active case types linked to risk rules and risk cases. A value close to 1.0 suggests that most risk‑related cases have formal SLA coverage, whereas lower values can indicate governance gaps or areas where SLAs still need to be defined.

This metric is often rendered as a percentage in dashboards and used as a governance KPI for risk and compliance teams.

overrides_active_count.description:
Number of currently active policy overrides that affect risk‑related behavior.

This count is derived from `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` rows whose status indicates that the override is active and whose `effective_from` / `effective_until` (or equivalent) fields indicate that the override is in force at the time of the query. Active overrides can temporarily change thresholds, disable rules, or adjust scoring behavior.

Monitoring this number helps governance teams understand how often normal risk policies are being bypassed or modified, and it can be used as an input to oversight and audit processes.

IShoppingMallRiskRuleStatistics.IRuleSev.description:
Single bucket representing the number of risk rules configured at a given severity level.

This schema is used inside `IShoppingMallRiskRuleStatistics.rules_by_severity` to describe how the risk ruleset is distributed across severity categories such as low, medium, high, or critical. Each bucket corresponds to one severity value from the underlying `shopping_mall_risk_rules` configuration.

Dashboards and BI tools typically aggregate these buckets into charts that visualize the risk posture of the platform, helping teams understand whether the majority of rules are informational warnings, moderate interventions, or high‑severity blockers and alerts.

severity.description:
Severity level label for this bucket.

Typical values include labels such as `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, or `"critical"`, and they correspond directly to the severity taxonomy stored on the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` records. The set of valid values is defined by the risk governance framework and should be interpreted consistently across all analytics and dashboards.

Clients should treat this field as a display‑ready label or key that can be used for chart legends, filters, or grouped tables.

count.description:
Number of risk rules with the given severity level.

This value is computed by grouping the relevant `shopping_mall_risk_rules` rows by severity and counting the number of rules in each group, typically after applying filters such as active status, domain, or time window. The count is always a non‑negative integer and is used to compare the relative prevalence of rules at different severities in configuration views and analytics.

IShoppingMallRiskRuleStatistics.ICaseSta.description:
Single bucket representing the number of risk cases currently at a particular status.

This schema is used inside `IShoppingMallRiskRuleStatistics.case_counts_by_status` to present how the workload of risk cases is distributed across lifecycle states such as open, under review, or closed. Each bucket aggregates cases with the same status value.

Operations and governance dashboards rely on these buckets to monitor queues, identify backlogs, and measure how effectively the team is progressing cases through investigation to resolution over time.

status.description:
Status label of the risk cases represented by this bucket.

Values are taken from the `status` column of `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, for example `"open"`, `"under_review"`, or `"closed"`. Additional statuses may exist depending on the platform’s risk case workflow configuration.

Client applications can use this value to label chart segments, table rows, or filters when exploring distribution and backlog patterns.

count.description:
Number of risk cases that currently have the indicated status within the scope of the analytics query.

This number is computed by grouping `shopping_mall_risk_cases` rows by status and counting the records that match the selected time window, actor filters, or other criteria. The value is always a non‑negative integer and is central to visualizing operational workload and tracking changes in case volume over time.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria plus pagination options for querying customer accounts from shopping_mall_customers.

This DTO is used by administrative search operations such as PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/customers to request a paginated list of customers that match the specified filters. It maps directly to indexed columns on shopping_mall_customers and selected related tables to support efficient querying without exposing any authentication or session fields.

All properties are optional so that callers can send only the filters they need. When multiple filters are supplied, they are combined according to server-side business logic, typically as an intersection (AND) of criteria for security and predictability.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination.

If omitted, the server typically defaults to the first page. Must be a positive integer when provided.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

When omitted, a server-defined default page size is used. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive result sets.

search.description:
Free-form search keyword applied to customer-identifying fields.

Typically matched against fields such as email or display name in shopping_mall_customers to support quick lookup by administrators.

status.description:
Filter for the current business status of customer accounts.

Values correspond to the status column in shopping_mall_customers, such as active, suspended, or blocked. When provided, only customers with the given status are returned.

email.description:
Exact or case-insensitive match filter for customer email address.

Maps to the email column in shopping_mall_customers and is particularly useful when administrators know the exact identifier.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the account creation time range filter.

When supplied, only customers with created_at greater than or equal to this timestamp are included in the results.

created_until.description:
Upper bound of the account creation time range filter.

When supplied, only customers with created_at less than or equal to this timestamp are included in the results.

IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall customer account for administrative and analytic list screens.

This summary DTO is optimized for list views, cross-entity references, and embedding into responses where only high-level customer information is required. It deliberately excludes security-sensitive authentication details such as `password_hash`, while exposing identifiers, contact information, business status, and key lifecycle timestamps.

The schema closely mirrors the non-sensitive columns of the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model. It includes audit timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`) and the soft-deletion marker (`deleted_at`) so that administrators can understand how recently an account was modified and whether it has been logically removed. Nullable timestamps such as `last_login_at` and `deleted_at` are surfaced as optional values to reflect their nullable nature in the underlying database.

Typical usage includes list responses for PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/customers, drill-down summaries in admin consoles, and embedding within higher-level governance, risk, or analytics views where full customer detail DTOs would be unnecessarily heavy.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer account on the shoppingMall platform.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customers` table and is used to join with related entities such as profiles, addresses, sessions, carts, orders, reviews, and risk flags. It is generated once at account creation time and remains stable for the lifetime of the account, including periods when the account might be soft-deleted.

email.description:
Customer email address used as the primary login identifier and main communication channel.

The value corresponds to the `email` column in the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model and is globally unique across all customers. It is used for credential-based authentication as well as for sending transactional notifications, account alerts, and policy updates.

status.description:
Business status of the customer account, such as `active`, `suspended`, or `blocked`.

The value is sourced from the `status` column in the `shopping_mall_customers` table and controls what the customer is allowed to do across the platform. Administrative tools, risk engines, and moderation processes use this field to decide which operations should be enabled, restricted, or denied for the account.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the customer’s email address has successfully passed the configured verification flow.

This property reflects the non-nullable `email_verified` column of the `shopping_mall_customers` model. A value of `true` means the email has been confirmed, typically granting the customer access to the full set of platform features. A value of `false` usually implies that additional verification is required or that certain actions should be limited until verification is complete.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this customer, represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This value is mapped from the nullable `last_login_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customers` table and is updated whenever the customer completes a successful authentication event.

When null, indicates that the customer has not completed a successful login yet.

Newly registered, imported, or inactive accounts may have `last_login_at` set to null until their first successful authentication is recorded.

last_login_at.description:
Nullable timestamp of the customer’s most recent successful login event.

When present, the value is an ISO 8601 date-time string derived from the `last_login_at` column in `shopping_mall_customers` and can be used to highlight recent activity in administrative or analytic views. When null, it indicates that no successful login has been recorded for the account.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer account record was initially created in the shopping mall database.

The value mirrors the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model. It is typically set at registration time and is used for onboarding analytics, age-of-account calculations, and audit trails that require knowledge of when the account first appeared on the platform.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the customer account record.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customers` table and is refreshed whenever the underlying account row is modified, such as when profile details, status, or risk flags are changed. Administrators and auditors can use this value to understand how recently the account data was changed and to investigate recent operational or governance activity affecting the customer.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when the customer account was soft-deleted, represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This value is taken from the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model and marks the moment the account was logically removed from active use while preserving historical references.

Null when the customer account is not soft-deleted.

A null value means the `deleted_at` column is unset and the account is considered logically active from a data lifecycle perspective, subject to its `status` and other governance controls.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the customer account, reflecting logical removal rather than physical deletion.

When non-null, this value mirrors the `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_customers` and indicates that the account has been placed in a soft-deleted state for compliance, risk, or operational reasons while preserving referential integrity. When null, it signals that the account has not been soft-deleted. Administrative list views and governance tooling can use this field together with `status` to distinguish active, suspended, blocked, and logically removed accounts.

IShoppingMallCustomer.description:
Detailed representation of a registered customer account in the ShoppingMall marketplace.

This DTO maps directly to the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model and exposes the core account identity and lifecycle fields used by administrative tools and internal services. It is typically returned from detail endpoints such as `GET /shoppingMall/admin/customers/{customerId}` after the caller has located a specific customer via search APIs.

The schema focuses on business-visible account attributes including identifiers, contact address, status flags, and key timestamps that describe registration, last login, and soft deletion state. It intentionally excludes authentication-secret internals beyond the fact that a password hash exists in the database, ensuring that sensitive hash material is never serialized into API responses.

Other customer-related structures such as extended profiles, addresses, sessions, and risk flags live in separate tables and may be exposed through additional DTOs or nested summaries when required by higher-level flows. This base entity remains a faithful, one-to-one view of the primary customer row in `shopping_mall_customers` while remaining safe for administrative and internal consumption.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer account in the `shopping_mall_customers` table.

This value corresponds to the primary key column `id` in the Prisma model and is used as the stable reference in all relationships, URLs, and foreign keys.

Clients receive this identifier from list or search operations and then supply it as the `{customerId}` path parameter when calling detail or update endpoints.

email.description:
Login and contact email address of the customer.

This field maps to the non-null, unique `email` column in `shopping_mall_customers`. It serves both as the primary authentication identifier and as the destination for account-related notifications such as verification, password reset, and order updates.

The platform enforces uniqueness at the database level so that each email corresponds to at most one active customer account.

status.description:
Business status of the customer account.

This property directly reflects the `status` column from the Prisma model and indicates the high-level lifecycle state of the account, such as `active`, `suspended`, or `blocked`. The exact set of supported values is governed by business policy and may be represented as an enum in higher-level code.

Downstream services and administrative tools rely on this status to enforce login permissions, restrict operations for high-risk or closed accounts, and drive reporting or risk workflows.

email_verified.description:
Flag indicating whether the customer has successfully verified their email address.

This value mirrors the non-null `email_verified` column on `shopping_mall_customers`. When `true`, the customer has completed the verification flow defined in the authentication requirements and the platform can treat the email as a trusted contact channel.

When `false`, certain features may be limited until verification succeeds, and administrative tools may highlight accounts that require follow-up or re-verification.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this customer, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is taken from the nullable `last_login_at` column on `shopping_mall_customers` and is updated whenever the customer completes a valid authentication flow.

It is commonly used by admins and risk engines to understand recent activity and detect dormant or potentially compromised accounts.

Null value when the customer has never logged in successfully.

Newly created accounts that have not completed a login flow, or historical rows where login tracking was not yet enabled, may leave this field unset.

last_login_at.description:
Most recent successful login timestamp for the customer, or null if no successful login has occurred.

This field allows administrative and risk-related tooling to reason about recency of customer activity without exposing any session internals or secrets.

The value is maintained by authentication flows that operate on the `shopping_mall_customers` row whenever login succeeds.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the customer account.

This property maps to the non-null `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_customers` and records when the account row was first inserted.

It is useful for reporting, lifecycle analysis, and governance tasks that depend on the age of accounts, such as retention policies or eligibility for certain campaigns.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the customer account row.

This mirrors the `updated_at` column in the Prisma model and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields on the record change.

Administrative tools and audit flows can rely on this value to understand how recently account attributes were modified and to detect stale information.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the customer account when present.

When set, this value corresponds to the `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_customers` and indicates that the account has been logically removed from active use while references such as orders and reviews remain preserved.

Business processes and queries treat non-null `deleted_at` as a signal to exclude the account from most active user flows.

Null value indicating that the customer account is not soft-deleted.

Active and suspended accounts that remain part of the live system typically leave this column unset.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion marker for the customer account.

A non-null value indicates that the account has been logically deleted in accordance with business or compliance rules, while a null value means the account remains active in the logical data model.

Downstream queries and services consult this timestamp to exclude soft-deleted accounts from normal operations while retaining them for historical or legal purposes.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate.description:
Mutable subset of fields for updating an existing ShoppingMall customer account.

This DTO represents the allowed changes to a row in the `shopping_mall_customers` Prisma model when handling update operations such as `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}`. It is intentionally limited to business-facing attributes that may be edited after account creation, and it excludes immutable identifiers and system-managed timestamps.

Because update operations work against an existing row identified by a path parameter, the primary key `id` and lifecycle columns like `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are not part of this schema. Authentication secrets such as `password_hash` are also excluded, as password changes are expected to occur through dedicated authentication endpoints that enforce stronger verification. Consumers should use this type only for account metadata updates permitted by business policy, while backend services remain responsible for enforcing uniqueness and validation rules derived from the underlying Prisma schema.

email.description:
New contact and login email address for the customer, if being changed.

This field updates the unique `email` column in `shopping_mall_customers` when provided. Because the database enforces uniqueness, attempts to set an email that already belongs to another active account will result in a constraint violation.

Business logic may require re-verification when the email changes, and may temporarily adjust the `email_verified` flag until verification completes.

status.description:
Updated business status for the customer account.

When present, this value overwrites the `status` column in `shopping_mall_customers` and can be used by administrative tools to move an account between states such as `active`, `suspended`, or `blocked`.

Only administrative flows should be allowed to modify this field, and service-layer guards must ensure that customers cannot arbitrarily change their own status.

email_verified.description:
Override for the email verification flag, used in administrative flows.

Providing this field updates the `email_verified` column in the underlying Prisma model. It is typically manipulated only by internal systems or admins in response to successful verification workflows or manual corrections.

Customer self-service flows should not set this field directly; instead they should drive the verification process that results in a controlled status transition.

IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.description:
Extended profile information for a registered shopping mall customer.

This DTO represents non-authentication profile attributes stored in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model. It complements the core identity fields in `shopping_mall_customers` by storing personal details and preferences that are safe to expose through customer-facing and administrative APIs. Typical contents include the customer’s full name, phone contact details, locale preference, and time zone settings, all of which are separate from authentication credentials and low-level session data.

The profile DTO is used as the response body for profile read and update operations, such as `GET /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/profile` and `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/profile`. It deliberately omits internal identifiers like `shopping_mall_customer_id` and soft-deletion markers, instead exposing a summarized `customer` relation for convenience. All system-managed timestamps are read-only and maintained exclusively by the backend to support auditing, reporting, and troubleshooting flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer profile record in `shopping_mall_customer_profiles`.

This value is typically a UUID string assigned when the profile row is created and remains immutable for the lifetime of the profile. It is used by internal systems, support tooling, and audit logs to reference the profile row in a stable way.

customer.description:
Owning customer account associated with this profile.

This field represents the belongs-to association from `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` to the parent `shopping_mall_customers` row. Instead of exposing the raw foreign key column `shopping_mall_customer_id`, the API returns a lightweight `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` view so that clients can obtain basic customer context without issuing additional lookup requests.

full_name.description:
Customer’s full name as stored in the profile.

This field corresponds to the `full_name` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` table and is typically used for display in UI surfaces, shipping labels, invoices, and customer service tools. The value may be nullable in the database, allowing profiles to exist before a name is supplied, and business validation rules such as minimum length or character restrictions are enforced in the service layer rather than at the schema level.

phone_number.description:
Primary phone number associated with the customer profile.

This field maps to the `phone_number` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model. It should contain a normalized phone number string suitable for contact and delivery coordination, often including country or region codes. Exact formatting and validation rules, such as E.164 normalization, are imposed by the application layer and not encoded directly in this schema.

locale.description:
Preferred locale code for content and user interface rendering for this customer.

The value corresponds to the `locale` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` table and typically follows BCP 47 language tag conventions such as `en-US`, `ko-KR`, or `ja-JP`. The platform can use this preference when selecting localized product content, transactional emails, notifications, and other customer-facing text.

time_zone.description:
Preferred time zone identifier for this customer, used when presenting times and scheduling-related information.

This field maps directly to the `time_zone` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` model and usually stores an IANA time zone identifier such as `Asia/Seoul` or `America/Los_Angeles`. Applications can rely on this value to render order histories, shipment timelines, and notifications in the customer’s local time context, while internal storage and analytics may continue to use UTC timestamps.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the customer profile record was created.

The value mirrors the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` table and is managed exclusively by the backend. It is useful for auditing profile lifecycle events, reporting on customer onboarding, and supporting operational investigations. Clients should treat this field as read-only metadata.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the customer profile record was last updated.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model and is automatically refreshed by the system whenever mutable profile attributes change. It enables clients, administrators, and analytics processes to track the recency of profile edits and can be used as part of concurrency-control or cache-invalidation strategies.

IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.IUpdate.description:
Mutable subset of customer profile fields that can be updated through the profile update API.

This DTO serves as the request body for operations such as `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/profile`. It is derived from the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` Prisma model and intentionally restricts updates to non-system, non-authentication fields such as the customer’s full name, phone number, locale preference, and time zone settings.

Actor identity and ownership are conveyed via the URL path parameter `customerId` and the authenticated context, so foreign keys like `shopping_mall_customer_id` as well as system-managed columns `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are never included here. All properties are optional so that clients can send partial updates; any omitted field leaves the current stored value unchanged.

full_name.description:
New full name for the customer profile.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `full_name` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` table after passing server-side validation. If omitted from the request payload, the stored full name remains unchanged.

phone_number.description:
Updated primary phone number for the customer profile.

Clients can supply a new phone number string to update the `phone_number` column in `shopping_mall_customer_profiles`. The backend is responsible for validating and normalizing the value according to the platform’s phone-number rules. When this field is not included in the request, the existing phone number is preserved.

locale.description:
Updated preferred locale code for the customer’s UI and content experience.

This value updates the `locale` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` model and should be provided as a BCP 47 language tag such as `en-US` or `ko-KR`. If the property is omitted, the customer’s previously configured locale preference is retained.

time_zone.description:
Updated preferred time zone identifier for this customer.

When present, this field updates the `time_zone` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_profiles` table with an IANA time zone identifier such as `Asia/Seoul`. If not included in the request, the current time zone preference is left unchanged, allowing clients to update other profile fields independently.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing authentication sessions belonging to a specific customer from the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table.

This DTO is used by administrative actors to filter customer sessions when calling the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/customers/{customerId}/sessions endpoint. It supports pagination, time‑window filtering, and basic attribute filters such as IP address and source channel while remaining read‑only and non‑destructive.

page.description: 1-based page index to retrieve when listing customer sessions. If omitted, the first page is returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to return in a single page. The backend may enforce an upper bound regardless of the requested value.

createdAtFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound of the session creation timestamp window. When provided, only sessions created at or after this instant are returned. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

createdAtTo.description: Inclusive upper bound of the session creation timestamp window. When provided, only sessions created at or before this instant are returned. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

lastSeenFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound of the last-seen activity timestamp window. When provided, only sessions whose last activity occurred at or after this instant are returned. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

lastSeenTo.description: Inclusive upper bound of the last-seen activity timestamp window. When provided, only sessions whose last activity occurred at or before this instant are returned. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

ipAddress.description: Optional exact-match filter on the client IP address recorded for the session. Supports typical IPv4 or IPv6 textual representations, depending on the underlying schema.

userAgent.description: Optional filter on the recorded user agent or device descriptor associated with the session. Implementations may perform case-insensitive or partial matching depending on business rules.

channel.description: Optional logical channel or platform filter indicating how the session was established (for example, "web", "mobile", or an internal code defined by the shopping_mall_customer_sessions model).

status.description: Optional session status filter that narrows results to sessions in a particular logical state such as active, expired, or revoked. Exact values follow the business rules encoded in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.description:
Detailed representation of a single customer authentication session that is persisted in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table.

This DTO is returned by the GET `/shoppingMall/admin/customers/{customerId}/sessions/{sessionId}` endpoint and is used by administrative and security personnel to inspect the full non‑secret metadata associated with a specific login session. It exposes all core columns from the underlying Prisma model, including identifiers and connection context such as IP address, entry URL, and referrer URL, while omitting any credential or token material that must never cross an API boundary.

In addition to the raw persisted fields, the DTO can carry derived or business-level attributes such as logical session status, channel classification, user agent descriptors, and last-seen timestamps. These values help incident responders, fraud analysts, and support operators understand how the session behaved over time and from which client environment it originated. The mapping between these properties and the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` schema is designed to remain stable so that changes to the database comments and structure can be reflected consistently in API behavior and documentation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the session record in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table.

This value corresponds to the primary key column `id` and uniquely identifies a specific authenticated session for audit, security, and troubleshooting workflows.

customerId.description:
Unique identifier of the customer account that owns this session.

The value mirrors the `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key column in `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` and references a row in the `shopping_mall_customers` table. It allows administrative tools to correlate this session with other customer-scoped data such as orders, risk flags, and security events.

ip.description:
Client IP address observed when the session was established.

This property is a direct projection of the `ip` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` Prisma model. It captures the remote address used at login time and is used for security analytics, anomaly detection, and customer support investigations.

href.description:
Full URL (href) that the customer accessed when this session was created.

The value comes from the `href` column on the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table and typically represents the entry page or endpoint that initiated the authentication flow. It helps operators understand which surface or feature the customer was using when they logged in.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that was recorded when the session was created.

This property reflects the `referrer` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` model and is commonly used for marketing attribution, risk scoring, and forensic analysis of suspicious login activity.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session was first created after successful authentication.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It serves as the canonical session start time for audit logs and time-based filters.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp at which the session was explicitly terminated, invalidated, or expired due to inactivity.

When present, this value is mapped from the nullable `expired_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

Indicates that the session is still considered active according to the current business rules and cleanup policies.

When `expiredAt` is null, the underlying `expired_at` column in `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` has not yet been set, and the session remains open from the platform’s perspective.

expiredAt.description:
Nullable timestamp representing when the session stopped being active.

A non-null value indicates that the session has ended due to logout, expiration, or forced invalidation, whereas a null value indicates that the session remains active and may still be used by the customer.

lastSeenAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent recorded activity associated with this session.

Although not directly surfaced in the simplified Prisma excerpt, this property represents the last time the platform observed meaningful interaction under this session. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC when present and is null when only the initial creation event is available.

status.description:
Logical status of the session from the platform’s perspective.

Typical values include states such as `active`, `expired`, or `revoked`, depending on how session lifecycle policies are configured. Implementations derive this value from persisted state and business rules so that administrators can quickly assess whether a session is still valid or has been terminated.

channel.description:
Logical channel or platform classification describing how the session was established.

Examples include `web`, `mobile`, or specific partner integration identifiers. This value helps segment session activity by client type for analytics, troubleshooting, and security reviews. When null, no specific channel classification has been recorded.

ipAddress.description:
Optional normalized or preprocessed representation of the client IP address.

While the raw connection address is stored in the `ip` column and exposed through the `ip` property, this field may contain a canonicalized, masked, or geo-enriched variant used by internal tooling. When present, it should remain consistent with the underlying `ip` value; when null, only the raw `ip` is available.

userAgent.description:
Captured user agent or device descriptor string that describes the client software or hardware used for the session.

This may include browser user agent strings, mobile device identifiers, or other descriptors recorded by the authentication stack. It is primarily used for fraud analysis, anomaly detection, and support troubleshooting, and may not be persisted as a dedicated Prisma column in all deployments.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.description:
Current customer shipping address entity in the shoppingMall platform.

This type represents the full, client-visible form of a customer-managed shipping address stored in the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` primary table. Each record belongs to exactly one customer account from the `shopping_mall_customers` model and can be used as a source for order and shipment address snapshots.

The schema exposes structured address components, ownership linkage, optional contact details, and lifecycle timestamps from the underlying Prisma model.
