Foreign key properties such as `shopping_mall_customer_id`, `shopping_mall_country_id`, and `shopping_mall_region_id` are technical identifiers that express relationships to customer and geography master tables; in higher-level views or summary DTOs these relations may be complemented by business keys or summary objects for usability, while the detail DTO keeps the underlying links explicit.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this customer shipping address record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table and uniquely distinguishes an address among all addresses in the system. Clients receive this identifier when creating or listing addresses and use it for subsequent update or delete operations and for establishing snapshots in related order and shipment tables.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer that owns this address.

This value corresponds to the primary key of a record in the `shopping_mall_customers` table. It binds the address to a specific customer account and is used by the backend to enforce ownership and authorization checks.

In many customer-facing APIs the customer context is already carried via the path (for example, `/customers/{customerId}/addresses`), so this field primarily acts as an explicit foreign key for persistence, administration, and cross-domain joins rather than a value that clients need to submit or manipulate directly.

shopping_mall_country_id.description:
Identifier of the country in which this address is located.

This value references a row in the `shopping_mall_countries` master data table and expresses the BELONGS‑TO relation between an address and its country. It is a technical foreign key rather than a human-readable country code, and other DTOs or views may expose complementary country code or summary information while this detail DTO keeps the raw link intact for internal processing.

The relation is used to drive shipping eligibility, taxation logic, risk evaluation, and geographic analytics within the platform.

shopping_mall_region_id.description:
Optional identifier of the region or state associated with this address.

When present, this value references a row in the `shopping_mall_regions` table, refining the geographic relation within the selected country. It is a nullable technical foreign key; null indicates that no specific region subdivision applies or has been recorded for this address.

This relation allows region-level shipping policies and analytics to be attached to addresses without embedding region details directly in the address entity.

recipient_name.description:
Name of the person or organization that will receive shipments at this address.

This field is part of the intrinsic composition of the address entity and is stored directly on the address record. It is shown on shipping labels and used by carriers to identify the intended recipient at the delivery location.

line1.description:
First line of the street address for this shipping location.

Typical values include street name and building or house number, such as "123 Main St" or "Building A, 45 Industrial Road". This is a core compositional field of the address entity and is not modeled as a separate related object.

line2.description:
Optional second line of the street address for this shipping location.

This field is commonly used for apartment numbers, suites, floor indicators, or additional routing instructions such as "Apt 5B" or "2nd Floor, Suite 210". It is nullable and forms part of the composed address structure rather than a standalone relation.

city.description:
City, town, or locality component of the shipping address.

This field describes the municipality or local region required by postal systems and carriers to route the shipment correctly. It is stored as a simple scalar on the address entity and participates in geographical analytics alongside the country and region foreign keys.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code associated with this address.

The value must follow the postal code format used in the country specified by `shopping_mall_country_id`. It is used by postal services and shipping carriers for sorting, routing, and validating the address and is part of the address composition rather than a separate related entity.

phone_number.description:
Optional phone number that carriers can use to contact the recipient for deliveries to this address.

This field is a scalar property of the address and does not represent a separate contact entity. It enables last-mile delivery coordination and can be omitted or set to null if the customer chooses not to store a phone number on the address.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this address is the customer's default shipping address.

When true, this address is preferred for new orders and may be preselected in user interfaces. Business rules usually ensure that at most one active address per customer is marked as default at any given time.

Logically, this flag influences how the one‑to‑many relationship between a customer and their addresses is interpreted, but it does not change the cardinality or introduce reverse collections from address back to customer.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this address record was first created.

The value is stored as a date-time in the database and represents the moment the address was initially added to the customer's address book. It is managed by the backend and is useful for audit, ordering, and lifecycle analytics but is not part of any additional relation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this address record was most recently updated.

The value changes whenever a mutable field of the address is modified, enabling audit and synchronization workflows. It is maintained by the backend persistence layer and does not introduce further relations beyond the core address entity itself.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this address record.

When null, the address is considered active and available for use in new orders. When set to a date-time value, the address has been soft deleted and should be treated as inactive in most user interfaces while remaining available for historical and audit purposes.

This field supports logical deletion semantics without changing the underlying relationships to customer, country, region, or downstream snapshots that may reference the address.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request for listing customer shipping addresses.

This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/customers/{customerId}/addresses endpoint and encapsulates query parameters for retrieving a paginated list of addresses owned by a specific customer.

It supports standard pagination and sorting options along with optional filters such as free‑text query on address components and narrowing by country or region. By concentrating these parameters in a structured object, the API can evolve search capabilities without altering the path or query string contract.

page.description:
1‑based index of the results page to retrieve.

Clients use this value together with the pageSize field to navigate through the customer’s address list. When omitted, the service should assume the first page.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of address records to return in a single page.

This controls the size of the data slice returned by the server. Reasonable upper bounds may be enforced by the implementation to protect performance and response size.

sortKey.description:
Field name used to sort the address list.

Typical values include created_at, updated_at, recipient_name, or is_default. The implementation may restrict allowed keys and default to a stable ordering such as newest first when not provided.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the sortKey field.

Common values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. The service should validate input and default to descending when unspecified.

countryId.description:
Optional filter that restricts results to addresses in a specific country.

The value corresponds to shopping_mall_country_id on the underlying model and enables UIs to display address lists for a chosen shipping country only.

regionId.description:
Optional filter that limits results to addresses within a particular region or state.

This maps to shopping_mall_region_id in the database and is especially useful in large countries or when region‑based shipping rules apply.

q.description:
Free‑text search query applied to human‑readable address components.

Implementations typically apply this string against fields like recipient_name, line1, line2, city, or postal_code to help customers quickly find a specific address entry in a long address list.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new customer shipping address in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO captures the writable subset of fields from the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` model that a client is allowed to supply when adding a new address to a customer's address book. It includes all business-relevant address components—recipient details, street address, locality, postal code, and optional contact information—along with an optional flag to indicate whether the new address should become the default shipping destination.

The ownership link to the customer (`shopping_mall_customer_id`) and server-managed fields such as the primary key and lifecycle timestamps are set internally by the backend based on the authenticated customer and the `customerId` path parameter. Clients must not attempt to send identity or audit fields in this DTO; the API extracts those from the path and authentication context instead.

Foreign key style fields such as `shopping_mall_country_id` and `shopping_mall_region_id` reference master data rows (countries and regions) rather than human-friendly business codes. In higher-level APIs or views these may be complemented by code-based identifiers or summary objects, but at this DTO layer they are technical links to the normalized geography tables.

shopping_mall_country_id.description:
Identifier of the country in which this new address is located.

The value must reference an existing record in the `shopping_mall_countries` master data table. It is a technical foreign key rather than a human-readable country code and is primarily used for relational integrity and server-side validation.

From a relational perspective this field links the address to the country master entity that drives shipping eligibility, tax logic, and geographic analytics.

shopping_mall_region_id.description:
Optional identifier of the region or state associated with this new address.

When provided, this value should reference an existing record in the `shopping_mall_regions` table for the selected country. It can be null for countries or use cases where region is not required or not applicable.

Relationally this field ties the address to a more granular geographic subdivision which can be used for region-specific shipping policies, analytics, and regulatory handling.

recipient_name.description:
Name of the person or organization that will receive shipments at this address.

Clients should provide a clear, human-readable value suitable for printing on shipping labels, such as the customer's full name or a combination of company and contact name. This field is part of the compositional data that defines the address itself and is created atomically with the address record.

line1.description:
First line of the street address for the new shipping location.

This field should contain the main street and building or house number information required for carriers to locate the destination, for example "221B Baker Street" or "742 Evergreen Terrace". It is a core component of the address composition and is stored directly on the address entity.

line2.description:
Optional second line of the street address for the new shipping location.

Clients can use this field for apartment numbers, suites, floor indicators, or additional directional information, such as "Apt 4C" or "Suite 500". It can be omitted or set to null if no additional detail is required.

Like `line1`, this property is part of the composed address structure and is persisted together with the address record in a single atomic operation.

city.description:
City, town, or locality for the new shipping address.

The value should follow the postal addressing conventions for the selected country and is used together with the postal code for routing and validation by carriers. It is a simple scalar property of the address entity and participates in downstream search and analytics for geographic distribution of orders.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code associated with the new address.

The value must follow the format used in the selected country and is validated for correctness where possible. It is a key part of shipping rate calculations and carrier routing and is stored as part of the address composition rather than via a separate relation.

phone_number.description:
Optional phone number associated with the recipient at this address.

Providing a reachable phone number can improve delivery success rates by allowing carriers to contact the recipient if there are access issues or clarifications needed. The platform may apply formatting or validation rules appropriate to its supported regions.

This property is a direct scalar value on the address entity and not a separate related contact record, so it is created and updated atomically with the rest of the address.

is_default.description:
Optional flag indicating whether this new address should be set as the customer's default shipping address.

When true, the system will mark this address as preferred for future orders, potentially unsetting any previous default address for the same customer according to business rules. When false or omitted, the address is added without changing the current default selection.

From a relational and behavioral standpoint this flag influences how the owning customer–address one‑to‑many relationship is interpreted, but it does not change the structural shape of the relation itself.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.IUpdate.description:
Payload for updating an existing customer shipping address in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO exposes the subset of `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` fields that are allowed to change after an address has been created. It is used by the address update endpoint, which scopes the operation by both customer and address identifiers supplied in the path parameters.

All properties are optional to support partial updates, but any provided value must satisfy the same validation rules as on creation. Ownership and lifecycle fields are managed by the backend and are not part of this type.

Foreign key style properties (`shopping_mall_country_id`, `shopping_mall_region_id`) continue to represent links to master geography tables rather than human-facing codes, and changing them effectively re‑targets the address to different country or region rows while keeping the address entity and its relation to the customer intact.

shopping_mall_country_id.description:
New country identifier for this address, if the country is being changed.

The value must reference an existing record in the `shopping_mall_countries` table. Changing the country may require additional validation to ensure compatibility with existing orders or region and postal code values.

Relationally, updating this property repoints the address to a different country master row while preserving the owning customer–address relationship and any snapshots that have already been taken for past orders.

shopping_mall_region_id.description:
New region or state identifier for this address, or null to clear the existing region.

When provided, the value must reference an existing `shopping_mall_regions` record that is valid for the selected country. Setting this field to null removes any region association from the address.

From a relationship perspective this property refines or relaxes the link between the address and a specific geographic subdivision within the selected country while leaving the core ownership and address composition unchanged.

recipient_name.description:
Updated recipient name for this address.

Use this field when the person or organization that should receive shipments at this location has changed or when the name formatting needs correction. This is part of the composed address data and can be updated without altering the underlying customer or geography relations.

line1.description:
Updated first address line for this shipping location.

This field can be modified when the building number, street name, or core street address information needs to be corrected or refined. It remains a scalar compositional property on the address entity and is updated atomically with the rest of the address fields supplied in this request.

line2.description:
Updated second address line for this shipping location, or null to clear it.

Clients can use this to add, modify, or remove apartment numbers, suites, floor indicators, or similar additional address details. It affects only the intrinsic address structure and does not alter the relationships to customer, country, or region.

city.description:
Updated city, town, or locality for this address.

This value should remain consistent with the selected country and postal code and reflect any changes in the local addressing requirements. It continues to be stored directly on the address and participates in downstream search and analytics but does not change relation cardinalities.

postal_code.description:
Updated postal or ZIP code associated with this address.

Use this field when the postal code needs correction or when the address has changed such that a different code now applies. This is a compositional field of the address entity and is updated without touching related entities.

phone_number.description:
Updated phone number for delivery contact at this address, or null to remove the existing number.

Clients can modify this when the recipient’s preferred contact number changes or when a phone number was previously missing and now needs to be added. The phone number is a simple scalar property on the address and does not represent a separate related contact entity.

is_default.description:
Updated default shipping address flag for this address.

Setting this field to true marks the address as the customer’s default shipping destination and may cause other addresses for the same customer to lose their default status. Setting it to false leaves the address active but not preferred.

This flag influences how the one‑to‑many customer–addresses relationship is interpreted at the business layer but does not introduce additional relations or reverse collections on the address entity itself.

page.description:
Page number for paginated retrieval of customer address snapshots.

Represents the 1-based index of the result page to return. If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page. Combined with `limit`, it determines the result window over the ordered snapshot set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of customer address snapshot records to return in a single page.

Used together with `page` to control pagination size. Implementations typically enforce an upper bound to protect performance and prevent excessively large responses.

orderByCreatedAt.description:
Sort direction for the `created_at` timestamp of customer address snapshots.

Accepts logical values like `"asc"` or `"desc"` to indicate whether older or newer snapshots should appear first. When omitted, the service usually defaults to descending order (newest snapshots first) for audit and customer service scenarios.

createdAtFrom.description:
Lower bound for snapshot creation time when filtering customer address snapshots.

When provided, only snapshots whose `created_at` timestamp is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are included. Use this to constrain the history window for audit or investigation purposes.

createdAtTo.description:
Upper bound for snapshot creation time when filtering customer address snapshots.

When provided, only snapshots whose `created_at` timestamp is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are included. Used together with `createdAtFrom` to define a time-range filter over historical address snapshots.

countryId.description:
Filter for snapshots captured with a specific country in the structured address.

When set, only snapshots whose `shopping_mall_country_id` matches this UUID are returned. This is useful for analyzing historical addresses by country or restricting results to a customer's addresses in a particular jurisdiction.

regionId.description:
Filter for snapshots captured with a specific region or state in the structured address.

When provided, restricts results to snapshots whose `shopping_mall_region_id` matches this UUID. Because the underlying Prisma field is nullable, this filter is optional and typically applied only when regional drill-down is required.

searchText.description:
Free-text search term applied over human-readable address components in snapshot records.

This value can be matched against fields such as `recipient_name`, `line1`, `line2`, `city`, or `postal_code` to quickly find snapshots that contain a particular name, street, or locality. Implementations often back this with a full-text index for efficient querying.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddressSnapshot.IRe.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating customer address snapshot history.

Encapsulates the pagination, sorting, and domain-specific filter criteria used when retrieving records from the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` model. It is used as the request body of the PATCH operation that lists snapshots for a specific customer.

The DTO focuses on search behavior and does not correspond directly to a single Prisma table row. Instead, it allows clients to specify how many snapshots they want, how those snapshots should be sorted by creation time, and which temporal or geographic filters should be applied. Optional filters allow callers to narrow the result set by date range, country, region, or free-text address search, without exposing any system-internal fields.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer address snapshot record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` table and is used to refer to a specific historical address instance in audit trails, customer service flows, and related domain entities such as orders or shipments.

customer.description:
Summary of the customer who owned the address at the time the snapshot was created.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` model and resolved into a lightweight `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` projection for read operations.

It allows consumers to understand which customer the snapshot belongs to without exposing raw customer IDs or requiring extra API calls, while still relying on path parameters and authorization for strong ownership checks.

shopping_mall_customer_address_id.description:
Optional reference to the live customer address record from which this snapshot was derived.

When present, this UUID points to a row in `shopping_mall_customer_addresses`. It may be null if the original address record has since been deleted or if the snapshot was created from transient data that was never stored as a reusable address in the customer address book.

This linkage is primarily intended for internal correlation between immutable snapshots and the customer’s current address book, rather than for end-user navigation.

country.description:
Summary of the country associated with this snapshot at creation time.

This field is the resolved association for the `shopping_mall_country_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` table. It exposes a lightweight `IShoppingMallCountry.ISummary` projection, giving clients access to human-readable country labels and codes without requiring additional API calls.

The snapshot preserves the country context as it was at the moment of capture, ensuring that historical shipping and tax decisions can be understood even if master data evolves later.

region.description:
Optional summary of the region or state associated with this snapshot at creation time.

This field corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_region_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` model and, when present, is resolved into an `IShoppingMallRegion.ISummary` projection.

It provides sub-national context (such as state, province, or administrative region) used for shipping, taxation, and analytics, while remaining nullable for addresses that do not use regional classification.

recipient_name.description:
Recipient name captured when the snapshot was created.

Represents the exact person or entity name as entered during checkout or address registration. It is stored verbatim to preserve how the recipient information appeared at the time of use, even if the customer later updates their profile or address book.

line1.description:
First address line of the historical shipping address.

Typically contains primary street information such as house number, street name, or building name. This value is copied directly into the snapshot from the source address at the time of capture and is never modified afterward.

line2.description:
Second address line of the historical shipping address, if supplied.

Often used for additional address detail such as apartment, suite, floor, or building wing. This field is nullable to reflect that many addresses do not require a second line.

city.description:
City or locality component of the historical shipping address.

Captured exactly as provided at snapshot creation time to support precise reconstruction of shipping labels, customer communications, and audit views.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code of the historical shipping address.

Preserved as originally provided so that past shipping labels, courier lookups, and tax determinations can be understood in their original context, even if postal code formats or validation rules change later.

phone_number.description:
Phone number associated with the address at the time the snapshot was created.

Used for historical contact reference in case of delivery issues or customer service investigations. This value is optional and may be null if no phone number was provided.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this snapshot record was created.

Represents the moment at which the address information was captured from the customer-facing workflow. Snapshots are append-only: once created, they are never updated or soft-deleted, so this timestamp is the primary temporal reference for the historical record.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddressSnapshot.description:
Detailed representation of a historical customer address snapshot as stored in `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots`.

Each record captures a point-in-time copy of a customer's shipping address as it existed when used for an order, shipment, or related business event. The entity includes immutable address and contact fields and resolves key associations—such as the owning customer, country, and region—into summary DTOs for atomic read operations.

Snapshots are immutable and append-only, providing a stable historical view that is safe for audit, compliance, dispute resolution, and customer service investigations. Even if a customer later edits or deletes their current addresses, this entity preserves how the address looked at the time of use, including the original recipient name, street lines, city, postal code, country, region, and phone number.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddressSnapshot.ISu.description:
Summary view of an immutable snapshot of a customer address in the shopping mall platform.

Snapshots capture the exact address details as they were at the time of a related business event, such as order placement or refund processing, and are never updated or soft-deleted.

This summary DTO is tailored for list and reference use cases where the consumer needs to understand what address was used historically without loading the full snapshot or related entities.

It maps directly to the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` Prisma model while exposing only the most important identifying and display fields for audit and history views.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the address snapshot record.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` table and is used to reference a particular historical version of a customer address.

It is generated once at snapshot creation time and never changes.

recipient_name.description:
Recipient name as captured at the time the snapshot was created.

This value maps to the `recipient_name` column in `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` and may differ from the customer’s current address book entries if they have since edited their addresses.

It is the authoritative historical value for documents such as invoices, order histories, and audit logs.

line1.description:
First address line captured in the snapshot.

The property reflects the `line1` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` table and stores the primary street or location information as it was when the related business event occurred.

Even if the live address has been changed or removed, this value preserves the historical shipping or billing location.

line2.description:
Second address line captured for the snapshot, if any.

This field mirrors the nullable `line2` column in `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` and is commonly used for apartment numbers, suites, or additional location details.

When no second line was provided at snapshot time, the value is null.

city.description:
City or locality value stored in the snapshot.

The property is backed by the `city` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` table and represents the municipality or locality at the time of the event.

Because snapshots are immutable, this field enables accurate reconstruction of historical shipping labels and documents.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code at the time the snapshot was created.

This value corresponds to the `postal_code` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` model and may not match the customer’s current address book if they have moved.

It is used for historical reporting, compliance documents, and reproducing past order information.

phone_number.description:
Phone number captured in the snapshot for delivery or contact purposes.

The property reflects the nullable `phone_number` column of `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` and records whatever contact number was provided at the time.

This value is particularly important for audit trails and for reconstructing the exact contact information that was originally used.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the snapshot record itself was created.

This field maps to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` and indicates when the historical copy of the address was taken, typically aligned with an event such as order confirmation or refund initiation.

Snapshots are append-only, so this timestamp is never updated and there is no soft-deletion, making it suitable for long-term audit and compliance records.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request payload for querying seller accounts on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by administrative search operations, such as the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/sellers endpoint, to express complex query criteria, pagination controls, and sorting preferences over the shopping_mall_sellers table and its related profile and metrics tables.

The request focuses on discoverability and management of sellers rather than data mutation, and therefore does not map one-to-one to any specific row. Instead, it encapsulates filters over fields like email, status, creation date ranges, and related business concepts such as verification or risk flags.

All properties are optional so that callers can combine them flexibly. Validation logic in the service layer should normalize empty or null-like values and apply sensible defaults for pagination and sorting when fields are omitted.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated seller search results.

When omitted, the service should default to the first page. Values less than 1 should be rejected or coerced to 1 by the implementation to avoid ambiguity and ensure consistent pagination semantics.

limit.description:
Maximum number of seller rows to return in a single page of results.

This value is advisory and subject to server-side maximums. The backend should clamp excessively large values to a safe upper bound to protect performance and avoid returning huge payloads in a single response.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to seller-identifying fields such as email or store name.

Implementations typically perform a case-insensitive search over the login email from shopping_mall_sellers and the store_name from shopping_mall_seller_profiles. Empty strings should be treated as if no search term was provided.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status filter for seller accounts.

Common values include business states such as pending_review, active, suspended, or terminated, matching the semantics of the status column in shopping_mall_sellers. When provided, only sellers in the specified status are included in results.

email.description:
Optional exact-match filter on the seller login email.

When present, this filter restricts results to the seller whose email column in shopping_mall_sellers matches this value exactly, subject to normalization rules such as lower-casing.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the seller account creation timestamp.

When set, only sellers whose created_at in shopping_mall_sellers is greater than or equal to this value are returned. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit timezone offset.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the seller account creation timestamp.

When set, only sellers whose created_at in shopping_mall_sellers is less than or equal to this value are returned. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit timezone offset.

orderBy.description:
Field name to use when ordering seller search results.

Typical values include created_at for recent sellers first and email or store_name for alphabetical lists. The actual set of allowed values is determined by the service implementation and should align with indexed columns in shopping_mall_sellers or joined views.

orderDirection.description:
Direction in which results should be ordered when orderBy is provided.

Allowed values are usually asc for ascending order and desc for descending order. If omitted, the implementation should select a sensible default, often descending by creation date for administrative views.

IShoppingMallSeller.description:
Core ShoppingMall seller account entity.

This type represents the primary seller account stored in the `shopping_mall_sellers` Prisma model. It captures authentication-related fields, lifecycle status, and high-level account metadata used by admin and backoffice features.

The seller entity is the root identity for all seller-related operations and is referenced throughout the platform by catalog, order, payout, and risk management components. In detailed views, it also composes the seller’s 1:1 profile record to provide a consolidated representation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller account.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_sellers` table. It is generated by the system and never provided by clients in request bodies.

It is used as a stable reference from related entities such as seller profiles, products, SKUs, earnings, and payouts.

email.description:
Business contact email address of the seller.

This value maps to the `email` column of `shopping_mall_sellers` and is used both as a login identifier and as a primary communication channel for the seller.

It must be unique across all sellers and respect the uniqueness constraint defined in the Prisma schema.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the seller account.

This field maps to the `status` column in `shopping_mall_sellers`. Typical values include business states such as `pending_review`, `active`, `suspended`, or `terminated` as described by the business rules.

Service logic and authorization checks should use this field to decide whether a seller may log in, manage catalog entries, or receive payouts.

email_verified.description:
Flag indicating whether the seller's email address has been verified.

This property reflects the `email_verified` column of `shopping_mall_sellers`. When true, the platform has confirmed the seller's ownership of the email address through a verification workflow.

Downstream features such as login, notification delivery guarantees, or risk scoring may depend on this flag.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the seller account record.

This property is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_sellers` and is automatically set by the system when the seller is first registered.

It is commonly used for auditing, analytics, and temporal filtering in reports.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the seller account record.

This field corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_sellers`. The system updates it whenever mutable attributes on the seller account change.

It is useful for synchronization workflows, cache invalidation, and operational monitoring.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the seller account, or null when the account is logically active.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column on `shopping_mall_sellers`. When non-null, it indicates that the seller account has been soft deleted or deactivated at the recorded moment in time.

Consumers should treat records with a non-null `deleted_at` as removed from normal operational flows while still preserving them for audit or legal purposes.

profile.description:
Extended profile information composed into the seller detail view.

This association represents the 1:1 relationship from `shopping_mall_sellers` to `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` and provides public-facing and operational profile attributes such as store name, description, and support contact channels.

Including the profile within the seller detail DTO allows administrative and backoffice clients to retrieve core account data and profile information in a single atomic read operation without issuing separate profile queries.

IShoppingMallSellerProfile.description:
Extended profile information for a seller account in the ShoppingMall platform.

This type models the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` Prisma table, which stores public-facing and operational profile attributes associated with a seller, separate from core authentication data in `shopping_mall_sellers`. It includes the store name, descriptive text, and public support contact channels that are shown to customers or used in communications.

Each profile is linked 1:1 to a seller account through the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key. The profile maintains its own lifecycle timestamps including creation, last update, and optional soft-deletion to support audit trails and reversible deactivation scenarios. When used as the primary resource, it also exposes a lightweight summary of the owning seller account for contextual display.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller profile record.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. It is generated and managed by the system and is used internally to reference the profile entity in joins, logging, and administrative tools.

Client applications can treat this as an opaque identifier when working with seller profile data.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller account that owns this profile.

This field maps to the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table and references the `id` primary key of the `shopping_mall_sellers` model. The relation is enforced as 1:1 so that each seller has at most one profile.

It is primarily used by backend services to join profile information with seller account data for administration, reporting, and consistency checks.

store_name.description:
Public store name presented to customers for this seller.

This value comes from the `store_name` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. It is the primary branding string exposed across catalog listings, order details, and seller pages.

Business rules may enforce non-empty content and reasonable length limits to ensure clear and concise branding.

store_description.description:
Long-form description of the seller’s store, or null when not provided.

This property reflects the `store_description` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table and allows sellers to describe their brand, policies, and story in more detail than the store name alone.

When null, no extended description is available. When populated, client applications typically show this text on seller detail or storefront pages.

support_email.description:
Dedicated customer support email address for the seller, or null when not configured.

This maps to the `support_email` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. It is used for customer-facing communication channels such as order inquiries or support requests when the seller wants to expose a specific inbox distinct from the authentication email.

If null, the platform may fall back to default contact mechanisms defined elsewhere in the system.

support_phone.description:
Customer support phone number for the seller, or null when not provided.

This property corresponds to the `support_phone` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. It is used in order confirmations, help pages, or seller detail screens where a phone contact is appropriate.

Formatting conventions (such as inclusion of country codes) are governed by business rules and UI validation but the database stores the raw string value.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller profile was created.

This field reflects the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. It records the moment the profile record was inserted, either during initial seller onboarding or when a profile is first created for an existing seller.

It is immutable once set and is commonly used for audit trails, chronological reporting, and display in administrative tools.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller profile was last updated.

This value is taken from the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table and is refreshed every time a change is persisted to the profile record.

Clients and operators can use it to detect stale data, resolve concurrency concerns, or display last-modified information in management consoles.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the seller profile, or null when the profile is active.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. When set, it indicates that the profile has been logically removed from active use but retained for historical or compliance reasons.

Consumers should treat records with non-null `deleted_at` as inactive and generally exclude them from normal customer-facing displays unless a specific archival view is required.

seller.description:
Lightweight summary of the seller account that owns this profile.

This association provides contextual information such as seller identity, contact email, and lifecycle status without re-embedding the full seller detail type, preventing circular expansion between seller and profile representations.

It is especially useful when the profile is retrieved as the primary resource—for example, in seller portals or admin consoles—so that callers can display both profile attributes and key seller account metadata in a single response.

IShoppingMallSeller.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for the ShoppingMall seller account entity.

This request body type is used by administrative or backoffice operations to modify mutable fields on an existing seller record stored in the `shopping_mall_sellers` Prisma model. It allows partial updates to contact information and lifecycle status while keeping immutable identifiers such as the primary key under system control.

Only fields that are present on the underlying Prisma model and considered safe to change at runtime are exposed. Actor identity fields, primary keys, and audit timestamps are excluded from client input and managed by the backend.

email.description:
New business contact email address for the seller account.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `email` in the `shopping_mall_sellers` table. The platform must enforce the unique constraint on the `email` column and reject update attempts that would violate uniqueness.

Changing this value may also require additional verification workflows, and service logic should decide whether to reset the `email_verified` flag or trigger a verification flow.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the seller account.

This field updates the `status` column in `shopping_mall_sellers`. Typical states include business concepts such as `pending_review`, `active`, `suspended`, or `terminated` as defined in business requirements.

Admin flows use this field to control whether a seller can access the portal, accept orders, or receive payouts, and additional validation should prevent illegal state transitions if required.

email_verified.description:
Override flag for whether the seller's email is considered verified.

Setting this value updates the `email_verified` column on `shopping_mall_sellers`. Backoffice workflows may use this field to mark an email as verified or unverified based on out-of-band processes.

Implementations should ensure that direct toggling of this flag is restricted to privileged actors, as it influences authentication and risk logic.

IShoppingMallSellerProfile.IUpdate.description:
Data used to update an existing seller profile in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO mirrors the updatable columns of the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` Prisma model and is used as the request body type for profile update operations such as `PUT /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId}/profile` and `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/profile`. It allows a seller or an authorized administrator to change display and contact information for a seller’s storefront.

All fields are optional to support partial updates: any property omitted from the request body will remain unchanged in the underlying profile record. Nullability semantics are respected based on the Prisma schema, so nullable columns can be explicitly cleared by sending `null`, while non-nullable columns must be omitted entirely if the client does not intend to modify them.

store_name.description:
New public store name for the seller, if it needs to be changed.

When provided, this value updates the `store_name` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. It should follow business rules for non-empty content and maximum length to ensure consistent branding across the platform.

If omitted, the existing store name remains unchanged.

store_description.description:
New long-form description for the seller’s store, or null to clear the current description.

This property corresponds to the `store_description` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. When a non-null string is provided, it replaces any existing description with the new content.

When explicitly set to null, the platform will remove the current description. If omitted from the request body, the existing description is preserved.

support_email.description:
Updated dedicated support email address for the seller, or null to remove the configured address.

This field maps to the `support_email` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. A non-null value should be a valid email address under business validation rules and will be used in customer-facing support flows.

If set to null, any existing dedicated support email is cleared and fallback contact mechanisms may apply. If omitted, the stored support email remains unchanged.

support_phone.description:
Updated customer support phone number for the seller, or null to clear the current phone number.

The property is backed by the `support_phone` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` table. A non-null string updates the stored phone number and may be displayed in order communications or seller detail pages.

Providing null removes the existing phone number, while omitting the field leaves the current value intact.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an authenticated seller session used for security monitoring, admin overviews, and account activity listings.

This summary is derived from the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` Prisma model and exposes only non-sensitive session metadata such as identifiers, connection information, and temporal boundaries. It is intended for read-only contexts, not for authentication token handling.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller session.

This corresponds to the primary key `id` column in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` and uniquely identifies a single login session instance for audit and tracking purposes.

ip.description:
IP address from which the seller established this session, as recorded at login time.

This value is backed by the `ip` column on `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` and is typically stored in textual representation (IPv4 or IPv6). It is primarily used for anomaly detection, fraud investigation, and geolocation-based risk analysis.

href.description:
Full URL used by the seller when initiating this authenticated session.

This corresponds to the `href` column of `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` and captures the exact entry URL at login time, which can indicate which surface, campaign, or portal region was used to start the session.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL captured when the seller established the session.

This maps to the `referrer` column of `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` and is used for attribution, funnel analysis, and to help detect suspicious navigation paths during security review.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller session was created after successful authentication.

This value comes from the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` and is represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string. It marks the precise login time for the session and is essential for chronological activity analysis.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session ended or expired, or null if the session is still considered active.

This field maps to the nullable `expired_at` column on `shopping_mall_seller_sessions`. When populated, it indicates that the session is closed due to logout, timeout, or administrative termination; when null, monitoring tools can treat the session as ongoing.

seller.description:
Summary representation of the seller account that owns this session.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key in response DTOs and provides convenient access to key seller identity and status fields for administrative and security analysis tools, while avoiding circular references and unnecessary additional lookups.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing seller authentication sessions.

This request DTO is used as the body for list operations targeting the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` Prisma model, typically in administrative endpoints such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/sellers/{sellerId}/sessions`. It allows callers to specify pagination parameters and optional filters over session metadata.

By encapsulating these parameters in a structured request body, the API supports complex query combinations (such as date-range filters and IP matching) while remaining read-only and avoiding query string length limitations.

page.description:
Requested page number for the session list, starting from 1.

When provided, this value selects which logical page of results should be returned. If omitted, the service may default to the first page according to platform-wide conventions.

The combination of `page` and `pageSize` determines how the result window is positioned within the full set of matching sessions.

pageSize.description:
Number of session records to return per page.

This field controls the maximum size of the `data` array in the `IPageIShoppingMallSellerSession.ISummary` response. If not specified, a service-defined default page size is applied, subject to upper bounds to protect performance.

Clients may tune this value based on UI needs, as long as they remain within allowed limits.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp filter, or null to avoid constraining by start time.

When provided as a non-null ISO 8601 date-time string, only sessions whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this timestamp are considered in the result set.

Explicitly passing null signals that no lower bound should be applied, while omitting the field delegates to service defaults.

created_to.description:
Exclusive upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp filter, or null to avoid constraining by end time.

A non-null value limits results to sessions with `created_at` strictly less than this timestamp, allowing callers to construct time-window queries for login activity.

Setting the field to null removes the upper time bound, and omitting it leaves behavior to service defaults.

expired_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the `expired_at` timestamp filter, or null when not filtering on session expiry start.

When non-null, this value causes the query to include only sessions whose `expired_at` is greater than or equal to the specified timestamp. This is useful when investigating sessions that ended within a particular time window.

If null, no lower bound on `expired_at` is applied. If the field is omitted entirely, the service may ignore this criterion.

expired_to.description:
Exclusive upper bound for the `expired_at` timestamp filter, or null to omit an expiry end constraint.

A non-null value limits the result set to sessions whose `expired_at` is strictly less than this timestamp, allowing for precise time-boxed queries on session termination.

Null indicates that the upper bound should not be enforced; omitting the field yields service-specific default behavior.

ip.description:
Optional filter for sessions by originating IP address.

When provided as a non-null string, only sessions with an `ip` value exactly matching this string are included in the results. This is useful for investigations centered on a particular address.

Setting the field to null or omitting it instructs the service not to restrict sessions based on IP address.

referrer.description:
Optional filter for sessions by referrer URL prefix or exact value, depending on implementation.

A non-null string can be used to narrow results to sessions whose `referrer` field matches or begins with the specified value according to service-defined matching semantics.

Providing null or excluding this property means no filtering is applied based on the `referrer` column.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.description:
Administrative view of a single seller authentication session in the shoppingMall platform.

Represents one authenticated login session created when a seller signs into the seller portal. Each record corresponds to a row in the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` Prisma table and includes metadata such as the owning seller, connection IP address, initial URL, referrer URL, and session lifetime timestamps.

This DTO is designed for privileged administrative inspection of seller access history, security investigations, and compliance audits. It does not include any password or credential material and must only be exposed to admin actors.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller authentication session.

This maps to the `id` primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` table and is generated by the system when the session is created.

seller.description:
Summary information of the seller account that owns this authentication session.

This field is derived from the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` table and references the corresponding seller row in `shopping_mall_sellers`.

Using the summary view ensures administrators can immediately see key seller details (such as email, status, and verification state) alongside session metadata without issuing additional lookups.

oneOf.description:
IP address observed when the seller established this session.

Typically stored in standard textual representation of IPv4 or IPv6 (for example, `192.0.2.1` or `2001:db8::1`).

ip.description:
IP address observed when the seller established this session.

Can be null if the IP address was not captured or is unavailable.

href.description:
Full URL used by the seller at session establishment.

Captured from the HTTP request that created the session and useful for reconstructing navigation context during investigations.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the session was established.

Provides additional context about where the seller came from before logging in, which can be useful for security and UX analysis.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller session was created.

Represents the moment the seller successfully authenticated into the seller portal.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when this seller session expired or was invalidated.

Represents the effective end of the session lifetime.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller session expired or was invalidated.

Null when the session is still considered active or when expiration time is not recorded.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request payload for listing administrator accounts on the shoppingMall platform.

Encodes pagination, sorting, and filter options that can be translated into queries against the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model and related role/profile tables. This DTO is used by privileged admin actors to discover and manage other administrator accounts for governance and operations.

All fields are optional, allowing callers to combine multiple criteria. Implementations must apply only filters that correspond to actual columns and relations defined in the underlying Prisma schema.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve when using offset-based pagination.

If omitted, implementations may default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of administrator records to return in a single page.

Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets.

search.description:
Free-text search keyword applied across selected identifier fields for administrators.

Typically matched against email, login name, or display name columns, depending on the `shopping_mall_admins` schema.

status.description:
Optional filter for administrator account status.

Maps to the status field in `shopping_mall_admins` (for example, enabled or disabled) and should only accept values that exist in the underlying enum or constrained column.

role_codes.description:
Optional filter restricting results to administrators that are assigned to one or more roles.

Each value should correspond to a role code or identifier defined in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and linked via `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`.

created_from.description:
Lower bound for administrator account creation timestamp.

Only admins with `created_at` greater than or equal to this value should be included when the filter is applied.

created_to.description:
Upper bound for administrator account creation timestamp.

Only admins with `created_at` less than or equal to this value should be included when the filter is applied.

order_by.description:
Field name used to sort administrator search results.

Implementations should restrict this to a safe subset of sortable columns such as `created_at`, `email`, or display name.

oneOf.description:
Direction for result sorting when `order_by` is specified.

`asc` sorts in ascending order and `desc` in descending order.

Direction for result sorting when `order_by` is specified.

`asc` sorts in ascending order and `desc` in descending order.

order_direction.description:
Direction for result sorting when `order_by` is specified.

`asc` sorts in ascending order and `desc` in descending order.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an administrator account on the shoppingMall platform.

This summary DTO is optimized for list views, lightweight embeddings in other entities, and administrative dashboards where a compact representation of an admin is sufficient.

It exposes only non-sensitive, business-facing fields and hides all authentication internals such as password hashes, while still providing enough information to identify the admin and understand their current status in the system.

The schema is directly aligned with the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model and uses a subset of its columns that are safe and useful to show in summary contexts.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin account.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and is used to reference the administrator in other entities, audit logs, and administration flows.

In client applications it is commonly used as a stable identifier when navigating to admin detail pages or wiring administrative actions to a specific account.

email.description:
Email address of the admin used as the primary login identity.

This field maps to the `email` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and is globally unique across admin accounts, ensuring each admin can be identified by a single email.

In list and summary views this value is typically displayed as the main human-readable identifier alongside the admin’s status.

status.description:
Business status of the admin account, such as active, suspended, or disabled.

This field maps to the `status` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and is used to control and visualize whether the admin can currently authenticate and perform operations.

Client applications can use this value to badge list items, filter admin lists, or restrict certain UI actions when the status is not active.

email_verified.description:
Flag indicating whether the admin’s email address has been verified or otherwise confirmed as valid.

This property is backed by the `email_verified` boolean column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and is commonly used in governance workflows to ensure that only verified accounts can access sensitive administrative functions.

UI layers may surface this field as a verification badge or use it to drive additional verification prompts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin account was initially created.

This field corresponds to the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and represents the moment the administrator record was first persisted.

It is frequently used in audit views, chronological sorting, and age-of-account analytics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the admin account record.

The value maps directly to the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and changes whenever mutable fields on the admin record are modified.

Client applications may display this field in detail views or use it to detect stale data in local caches.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account, or null when the account is still logically active.

This property is backed by the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and allows the platform to preserve historical records while excluding soft-deleted admins from normal operational flows.

In most list and summary contexts this value is either hidden or used only for specialized governance views that need to include deactivated accounts.

IShoppingMallAdmin.description:
Administrator account entity for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a single admin row from the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model, enriched for read operations that retrieve administrator information for governance and operational tooling. It exposes identifying information, status flags, and lifecycle timestamps needed to understand who the admin is and how the account is currently configured.

The schema is used as the response body for admin detail retrieval and update operations. It intentionally excludes sensitive authentication material such as the underlying password hash while still reflecting business-relevant state from the admin record.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin account.

This field maps directly to the primary key `id` column of the `shopping_mall_admins` table and is generated by the system when the admin account is created. It is used as the stable reference in all admin-focused operations, links to audit logs, and relationships to role assignments.

Clients use this identifier in path parameters such as `/shoppingMall/admin/admins/{adminId}` and must treat it as an opaque UUID string without attempting to derive meaning from it.

email.description:
Login email address for the admin account.

This field corresponds to the `email` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model. It is the primary login identifier for administrators and must be unique across all admin accounts, as enforced by a unique index in the database.

The value must be a syntactically valid email address and is commonly used for contact, notification, and auditing purposes in back-office tooling.

status.description:
Business status of the admin account.

This field maps to the `status` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table and indicates the current lifecycle or accessibility state of the admin. Typical values include active, suspended, disabled, or other business-defined codes that drive whether the admin can log in and perform actions.

Client applications may use this value to control which operations are available in administrative UIs, and governance processes may transition this status in response to policy, risk, or HR events.

email_verified.description:
Flag indicating whether the admin's email address has been verified.

This field reflects the `email_verified` column of the `shopping_mall_admins` model and denotes whether the platform has successfully validated ownership of the email address associated with the admin account.

Verification may be achieved through one-time links, identity checks, or other processes, and downstream features such as security-sensitive operations can require this flag to be true before allowing execution.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin account was created.

This property is mapped from the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table. It records the exact moment the admin record was first persisted and is typically stored in UTC as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

Operational dashboards, audit tooling, and analytics features use this value to understand account age, onboarding cohorts, and historical governance changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the admin account record.

This field corresponds to the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model. The system updates it whenever mutable attributes of the admin are modified, providing a reliable indicator of the last configuration change.

Support agents and governance tools rely on this value to investigate when changes were applied and to reconcile with audit log entries.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account, or null when still active.

This property is derived from the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table. When the admin account has been logically deleted or deactivated under a soft-delete policy, this field contains the date-time of that action.

When the account is still logically active, the value is null. Business logic uses this field together with `status` to determine whether the admin should be treated as operational, archived, or subject to legal hold and retention constraints.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Mutable subset of the admin account fields used for update operations.

This DTO is consumed by the admin update endpoint to change allowed business attributes of an existing admin record in the `shopping_mall_admins` Prisma model. It intentionally omits immutable identifiers and system-managed timestamps such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`, which are controlled by the backend.

Typical use cases include adjusting an admin's contact email, toggling activation or suspension status, or correcting verification flags under controlled operational processes. All properties are optional, enabling partial updates where only the provided fields are modified.

email.description:
New login email address for the admin account, if being changed.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `email` column in the `shopping_mall_admins` table, subject to validation and uniqueness checks. It must be a syntactically valid email address and must not conflict with other admin accounts.

If omitted, the email remains unchanged. Implementations may require additional verification flows before fully trusting the updated address.

status.description:
Updated business status for the admin account.

When included, this value updates the `status` column for the target row in `shopping_mall_admins`. It allows operators or automated governance workflows to move the admin between states such as active, suspended, or disabled.

Service logic should enforce valid transitions and prevent critical misconfigurations, such as disabling all super-admins or violating internal policy rules.

email_verified.description:
Updated email verification flag for the admin.

Providing this property allows privileged operations to mark an email as verified or unverified by updating the `email_verified` column in `shopping_mall_admins`. This is typically performed by backend processes in response to verification flows, not by end users.

If omitted, the existing verification state is preserved. Business logic should ensure that only trusted actors and workflows are allowed to flip this flag.

IShoppingMallAdminProfile.description:
Administrator profile entity for the shoppingMall platform.

This type represents the extended profile information for an administrator, mapped directly from the `shopping_mall_admin_profiles` Prisma model. It stores non-credential metadata for admin accounts such as human-readable names and optional contact phone numbers, separate from the core authentication data stored in `shopping_mall_admins`.

The profile is logically linked to a single admin account through a 1:1 relationship. It is used by internal dashboards, audit logs, and governance tools to display who performed administrative actions and to support internal coordination workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin profile.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_admin_profiles` table and is generated by the system when the profile record is created.

Clients only receive this value in responses; it is never supplied in create or update DTOs.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the administrator account that this profile belongs to.

This field corresponds to the foreign key that links `shopping_mall_admin_profiles` to `shopping_mall_admins` and enforces a 1:1 relationship between an admin account and its profile.

The value is determined by server-side logic based on the admin being managed and is returned for reference in responses. It is not accepted from clients in profile update request DTOs, because ownership relations are system-managed.

admin.description:
Summary view of the administrator account that owns this profile.

This association provides contextual information about the admin—such as identifier, login email, and status—when the profile is viewed independently, for example from profile-centric search screens or audit tooling.

It is modeled as a BELONGS-TO reference and therefore uses the `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary` variant to avoid circular references, while still giving clients enough information to display who the profile belongs to without making an additional admin detail call.

full_name.description:
Full name of the administrator as displayed in internal tools and audit logs.

This value is optional and may be null when an admin has not configured a human-readable full name. When present, it should contain the administrator's complete name that will be shown in dashboards, notifications, and governance reports.

phone_number.description:
Optional phone number for the administrator used for internal coordination or escalation.

This field may be null when no phone number has been registered. Implementations can apply additional validation rules such as E.164 format or organization-specific phone number policies at the service layer.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin profile record was created.

The value is managed entirely by the database or persistence layer and reflects the moment the profile row was inserted into `shopping_mall_admin_profiles`. Clients receive this for display and audit purposes only and must not attempt to modify it.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin profile record was last updated.

This value is automatically updated whenever mutable profile fields change. It is useful for audit trails and for client applications that need to detect whether a profile has changed since it was last loaded.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the admin profile record.

When this field is null, the profile is considered active and usable in the platform. When set to a date-time value, the profile is treated as soft-deleted, allowing the system to preserve historical data and audit trails while excluding the record from normal operational queries.

IShoppingMallAdminProfile.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating extended profile information of an administrator based on the `shopping_mall_admin_profiles` Prisma model.

This schema exposes only the mutable profile fields `full_name` and `phone_number`, which correspond directly to the nullable string columns of the same names on `shopping_mall_admin_profiles`. Ownership, identity, and lifecycle metadata such as `id`, `shopping_mall_admin_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally excluded because they are managed exclusively by the backend according to authentication context and business rules.

The update contract follows a partial update pattern. Omitting a property leaves the existing value unchanged, while explicitly providing `null` clears the stored value in the database. This allows clients to distinguish between "no change" and "clear this field" semantics when updating an administrator’s profile information.

full_name.description:
Updated full name for the administrator as displayed in internal dashboards and audit logs.

If provided as a non-null string, the system will persist the new value into `shopping_mall_admin_profiles.full_name`, subject to any length and content validation rules enforced by the service layer. If explicitly set to null, the profile will clear any previously stored full name, resulting in a null column value. If this property is omitted from the request body, the existing full name stored in the database remains unchanged.

phone_number.description:
Updated phone number for the administrator used for internal coordination and escalation.

When supplied as a non-null string, this value replaces the current value in `shopping_mall_admin_profiles.phone_number` after passing any configured format and validation checks (for example, organization-specific phone number policies). When explicitly set to null, any existing phone number is removed and the corresponding column is set to null. If this property is omitted from the request body, the stored phone number is left unchanged.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.description:
Admin authentication session entity backed by the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` Prisma model.

This type represents a single administrator authentication session, capturing when and from where the admin accessed the platform. It is used for security auditing, governance, and investigation of potential misuse by privileged users.

The entity is managed exclusively by the authentication/session infrastructure. Application code reads these records to display session history and diagnose security incidents but does not create or arbitrarily mutate them outside of authentication flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin session.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` record and is used as the `sessionId` path parameter when retrieving a specific session for an admin.

The value is generated by the authentication subsystem when the session is created and is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin account that owns this session.

This field corresponds to the foreign key referencing the `shopping_mall_admins` table and links the session to its parent administrator.

In API operations, this value is typically conveyed as the `adminId` path parameter rather than being exposed as an editable request field.

ip.description:
IP address from which the admin initiated the session.

The value is captured at login time from the incoming request and stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table for audit and risk analysis.

Typical values are IPv4 or IPv6 textual representations; the exact validation is enforced by the backend according to infrastructure policy.

href.description:
Full URL used when the admin session was created.

This value indicates the page or route where the administrator initiated the login that produced this session record.

It is useful for tracing entry points into the admin console during security investigations and for understanding UX flows that lead to authentication.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL at the time of login.

The referrer shows which page or external site led the administrator to the login page where this session originated.

Security and analytics tooling can use this information to detect unusual access patterns, phishing attempts, or unexpected navigation flows.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session was created.

This value reflects when the authentication subsystem successfully established the session after validating admin credentials.
