It is stored as an immutable creation time in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table and is used extensively in filtering and ordering session history.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session ended or expired, or null if still active.

When set, this field indicates that the session is no longer valid because it has either expired according to policy or has been explicitly terminated by logout or security processes.

When null, the session is considered active or its termination has not yet been recorded; callers should interpret null in combination with authentication subsystem state when evaluating active sessions.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying administrator sessions for a specific admin account.

This DTO is used as the request body for the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/admins/{adminId}/sessions` endpoint, enabling complex filtering of rows in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table beyond what query parameters alone can express.

Clients use this type to specify pagination, sorting, and optional constraints on fields such as creation time ranges or IP address patterns when reviewing admin security sessions.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve when paginating admin session search results.

The first page is typically 1, and higher values advance through the result set.

If omitted, the backend will apply its own default page index for the session search.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page of results.

This field controls page size for the admin session search operation and should respect system-imposed upper bounds for performance and security.

If not provided, the server will choose a default limit appropriate for admin session listings.

sort_by.description:
Field name by which to sort admin session results.

Typical values include fields such as `created_at` or `expired_at` so that administrators can review newest or oldest sessions first.

The concrete set of allowed sort keys is enforced by the backend based on columns in `shopping_mall_admin_sessions`.

oneOf.description:
Direction in which to sort admin session records.

Use `"asc"` to sort from oldest to newest by the selected sort field, or `"desc"` to reverse the order and see the most recent sessions first.

If omitted, the server applies its default direction, which is often descending by creation time for security review use cases.

Direction in which to sort admin session records.

Use `"asc"` to sort from oldest to newest by the selected sort field, or `"desc"` to reverse the order and see the most recent sessions first.

If omitted, the server applies its default direction, which is often descending by creation time for security review use cases.

sort_direction.description:
Direction in which to sort admin session records.

Use `"asc"` to sort from oldest to newest by the selected sort field, or `"desc"` to reverse the order and see the most recent sessions first.

If omitted, the server applies its default direction, which is often descending by creation time for security review use cases.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the session creation timestamp range filter.

When provided, only sessions whose `created_at` is greater than or equal to this timestamp will be included in the results.

Use this in combination with `created_to` to constrain the search window for admin sessions by time.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the session creation timestamp range filter.

When provided, only sessions whose `created_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp will be returned.

Using both `created_from` and `created_to` allows admins to focus on sessions within a specific investigation period.

ip.description:
Optional filter for admin sessions by client IP address.

This value can be used to restrict results to sessions that originated from a specific IP or a representation understood by backend matching logic, such as a CIDR or partial match.

The exact semantics of IP filtering are defined by the implementation and may include exact equality or pattern-based matching.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.IRequest.description:
Search, filtering, and pagination criteria for listing guest user accounts from the shopping_mall_guestusers table for administrative oversight and governance.

This DTO is used exclusively by the admin-facing PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/guestUsers search endpoint. It allows platform operators to retrieve paginated, filterable lists of guest users based on creation timestamps, last-activity windows, free-text search, risk flags, and existence of related artifacts such as carts or orders.

All fields are optional filters; omitting a field means that criterion is not applied. This schema does not map directly to a single Prisma model and therefore does not use x-autobe-prisma-schema.

page.description: 1-based page index of results to retrieve. When omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of guest user rows to return in a single page. The backend may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

search.description: Optional free-text search term applied to key identity fields of guest users such as display name, email-like identifiers, or tracking tokens depending on the concrete schema. When empty or omitted, no free-text filtering is applied.

createdFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound of the guest user creation timestamp range filter. Only guest users created at or after this instant are included.

createdTo.description: Inclusive upper bound of the guest user creation timestamp range filter. Only guest users created at or before this instant are included.

lastActiveFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound of the last-activity timestamp window. Only guest users whose last recorded activity is at or after this instant are included.

lastActiveTo.description: Inclusive upper bound of the last-activity timestamp window. Only guest users whose last recorded activity is at or before this instant are included.

hasCarts.description: When true, only guest users that have one or more associated carts are returned. When false, only guest users without any associated carts are returned. When omitted, cart association is not used as a filter.

hasOrders.description: When true, only guest users that are linked to one or more orders (for example, early-stage or guest checkouts) are returned. When false, only guest users with no such links are returned. When omitted, this criterion is ignored.

hasRiskFlags.description: When true, restricts results to guest users that have one or more associated risk flags in the shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_guestusers linkage tables. When false, restricts to users without any risk flags. When omitted, this filter is not applied.

riskSeverityFrom.description: Optional minimum inclusive risk severity score used when risk-related filters are enabled. The concrete scoring scale is defined by the business but typically increases with risk.

riskSeverityTo.description: Optional maximum inclusive risk severity score used when risk-related filters are enabled. The concrete scoring scale is defined by the business but typically increases with risk.

oneOf.description: Primary sort field to apply when ordering search results. Admin consoles commonly allow sorting by creation time, last activity time, or derived risk severity.
Primary sort field to apply when ordering search results. Admin consoles commonly allow sorting by creation time, last activity time, or derived risk severity.
Primary sort field to apply when ordering search results. Admin consoles commonly allow sorting by creation time, last activity time, or derived risk severity.

orderBy.description: Primary sort field to apply when ordering search results. Admin consoles commonly allow sorting by creation time, last activity time, or derived risk severity.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for the selected orderBy field. Use asc for ascending and desc for descending ordering.
Sort direction for the selected orderBy field. Use asc for ascending and desc for descending ordering.

orderDirection.description: Sort direction for the selected orderBy field. Use asc for ascending and desc for descending ordering.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.description:
Guest user identity entity for the shoppingMall platform mapped directly to the `shopping_mall_guestusers` Prisma model.

Each record represents a logical identity for an unauthenticated or semi-anonymous visitor who may own transient business data such as temporary carts or wishlists before converting into a registered customer. The table provides a stable identifier for analytics, basic risk analysis, and linkage to session and cart data.

Because this schema is bound to the `shopping_mall_guestusers` Prisma model, it exposes only the columns that physically exist in that table. Any higher-level projections such as aggregated risk scores or embedded session summaries are modeled in separate, non–Prisma-mapped DTOs.

id.description:
Primary key of the guest user identity.

This property corresponds exactly to the `id` column in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table and is generated as a UUID. It is used as the stable join key when linking guest identities to sessions, carts, wishlists, and risk or security artifacts.

Clients should treat this value as opaque and immutable over the lifetime of the guest user record.

external_reference.description:
Optional external or device-based correlation reference for the guest user.

The value is stored in the nullable `external_reference` column of the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table and typically contains a cookie identifier, device fingerprint, or other pseudonymous key that allows the platform to group related guest activity under a single logical identity.

When `null`, the guest identity was either created without any such reference or the reference has been cleared in accordance with privacy and data minimization policies.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest user identity record was created.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table. It reflects the instant when the platform first persisted this guest identity, such as the first time the visitor added an item to a cart or otherwise triggered identity creation.

The timestamp is represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and is frequently used in lifecycle analysis, retention reporting, and time-based segmentation of guest traffic.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest user record was last updated.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table. It is automatically advanced whenever any mutable column in the row changes, including system-driven maintenance updates or changes to `external_reference`.

Consumers can use this timestamp to detect recently modified guest identities, drive incremental synchronization logic, or implement cache invalidation strategies for admin tools that display guest details.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the guest user identity.

This property is backed by the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table. When `deleted_at` is `null`, the guest record is considered active from a data-retention perspective. When it contains an ISO 8601 date-time value, the record is logically deleted but retained to preserve the integrity of historical relations to sessions, carts, or orders and to satisfy audit or compliance requirements.

Downstream services and admin tools should treat non-null `deleted_at` values as an indicator that the guest identity should not be used for new business operations while still being available for read-only historical analysis.

IShoppingMallGuestuserSession.IRequest.description:
Filter and pagination request payload for searching guest user session records associated with a specific guest user.

This DTO is used by administrative actors to retrieve a paginated list of guest user sessions from the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table for a single guest identity. It focuses on time-range filters and basic pagination, avoiding over-specification of fields that are not guaranteed by the database schema.

The request body is submitted to the PATCH `/shoppingMall/admin/guestUsers/{guestUserId}/sessions` endpoint where the parent guest user is identified by the `guestUserId` path parameter. The combination of this DTO and the path parameter allows admins to narrow down sessions for investigation or auditing without exposing or requiring any actor identity fields in the payload itself.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve in the paginated result set.

The first page is typically `1`. If not provided, the implementation should fall back to a sensible default page index. Values less than `1` should be rejected by validation or normalized to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to include in a single page of results.

This value controls pagination size for the guest user session list. The backend may enforce an upper bound to protect performance and prevent excessively large responses.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the `created_at` timestamp when filtering guest user sessions.

Provide an ISO 8601 date-time string to return sessions created at or after this moment in time.
Indicates that no lower bound is applied for `created_at` when filtering guest user sessions.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp of guest user sessions.

When provided as an ISO 8601 date-time string, only sessions created at or after this time will be included. When null or omitted, the list is not constrained by a lower creation time bound.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the `created_at` timestamp when filtering guest user sessions.

Provide an ISO 8601 date-time string to return sessions created at or before this moment in time.
Indicates that no upper bound is applied for `created_at` when filtering guest user sessions.

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp of guest user sessions.

When provided as an ISO 8601 date-time string, only sessions created at or before this time will be included. When null or omitted, the list is not constrained by an upper creation time bound.

IShoppingMallGuestuserSession.description:
Detailed representation of a guest user session stored in the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table.

Each record models a logical browsing or interaction session for a guest user on the shoppingMall platform. It links back to a guest identity in `shopping_mall_guestusers` and captures key metadata such as IP address, entry URL, referrer URL, and timestamps.

This DTO is used primarily in administrative and security contexts, for example when investigating suspicious behavior, reconstructing access patterns, or performing compliance checks on guest activity. It intentionally focuses on persisted session data available in the Prisma model while exposing the related guest user as a summary object for atomic read operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user session.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` record and uniquely identifies a single session instance across the platform.

guestUser.description:
Summary representation of the guest user who owns this session.

This object replaces the raw foreign key to `shopping_mall_guestusers` and provides enough identity and display information for administrators to understand which logical guest user the session belongs to without additional lookups.

ip.description:
IP address observed for this guest session.

The value is captured when the session is created and may be used for security analysis, fraud detection, or basic geo-based insights. It should be stored and processed in accordance with privacy and compliance requirements.

href.description:
Entry URL that initiated the guest session.

This field captures the full URL or route where the guest session first began. It helps administrators understand the navigation context or campaign entry point for the session.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL associated with the start of the guest session.

The referrer provides information about the previous page or external site that led the visitor to the shoppingMall platform. It is useful for traffic analysis and tracing user journeys.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest session record was created.

This value is typically set when the session is first established and is used as the primary time reference when ordering or filtering session history.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the guest session expired or was explicitly terminated.

Represents the end of the usable lifetime of the session. Depending on platform rules, this may be set by inactivity timeout, explicit logout, or session revocation.
Indicates that the session has not yet expired or that no expiration has been recorded for this session.

expired_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when the guest session expired or was terminated.

When present, it marks the end of the session lifetime. When null, the session may still be considered active or its expiration may not have been persisted yet, depending on business logic.

IShoppingMallAccountRiskFlag.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying account risk flags across actors and linkages.

This type models the rich, body-based search criteria used by administrative and risk-operations tools when listing account risk flags from the `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` table and its linkage tables for specific actors such as customers, sellers, admins, or guest users.

It encapsulates pagination, sorting, and filter parameters while remaining read-only and side-effect free. The fields map to columns and common query dimensions on the risk flag model such as actor type, severity, active status, and creation/update time windows.

page.description:
1-based index of the page to retrieve.

Used by administrative search screens for paginated navigation over risk flag results. When omitted, implementations commonly default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

Controls the page size of risk flag search results. Implementations usually enforce an upper bound to protect performance and memory usage.

order_by.description:
Name of the risk flag field used for sorting search results.

Typical values align with sortable columns of `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags`, such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, `severity`, or `code`. Implementations should validate this value against a whitelist of supported sort keys to avoid invalid queries.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction for ordered search results.

Accepts conventional values like `asc` or `desc` to control ascending or descending ordering. If omitted, the backend usually defaults to descending creation time so that the newest risk flags appear first.

actor_type.description:
Filter for the type of actor that the risk flag applies to.

This corresponds to the `actor_type` column of `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags`, with values such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `guestuser`. When provided, only flags matching the given actor type are included in the result set.

severity.description:
Filter for the business severity level of risk flags.

Maps directly to the `severity` column in `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags`, where typical values include `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. When supplied, results are restricted to flags that have the specified severity.

active.description:
Filter indicating whether to return only currently active or only inactive risk flags.

When set to `true`, the search is limited to flags whose `active` column is true and that have not been logically retired. When set to `false`, it can be used to inspect historical or cleared flags for audit and investigation purposes.

code.description:
Optional filter that matches the machine-oriented risk code of flags.

This value corresponds to the `code` column in `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags`, which stores identifiers such as `HIGH_REFUND_RATE` or `SUSPICIOUS_LOGIN_PATTERN`. It is typically used for narrowing search results to a specific risk classification.

created_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the creation timestamp range filter applied to risk flags.

When provided, only flags whose `created_at` column is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are returned.

created_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the creation timestamp range filter applied to risk flags.

When provided together with `created_from`, constrains results to flags created within the specified time window, based on the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags`.

IShoppingMallAccountRiskFlag.description:
Account risk flag entity for the shopping mall risk management subsystem.

Represents a canonical risk or trust flag associated with an account or actor, such as a customer, seller, admin, or guest user. Each record captures a specific risk code, severity, and explanatory reason which can be used by automated risk engines and human administrators to influence verification, throttling, or suspension decisions.

This table is the primary owner of risk flag metadata, including lifecycle timestamps and soft deletion. Concrete linkage to specific actor records (for example, a particular customer or seller) is handled via dedicated subtype tables so that this model remains normalized and reusable across multiple actor types.

id.description:
Primary key of the account risk flag.

This UUID uniquely identifies a single risk flag record within the shopping mall risk management subsystem.

It is generated by the system when the record is created and is used as the stable identifier in path parameters such as riskFlagId.

actor_type.description:
Actor type to which this risk flag conceptually applies.

Stores a normalized string such as "customer", "seller", "admin", or "guestuser" indicating what kind of account or actor this flag targets.

This value is used for filtering, reporting, and routing decisions but does not itself implement the foreign key to actor tables; those links are represented by dedicated subtype tables.

code.description:
Machine-readable risk code for this flag.

Contains a short, structured identifier such as "HIGH_REFUND_RATE" or "SUSPICIOUS_LOGIN_PATTERN" that risk engines and reporting tools can use for rule evaluation.

The code is expected to be unique enough in combination with actor context to avoid ambiguity when aggregating or analyzing risk information.

reason.description:
Human-readable explanation of why this risk flag exists.

Typically contains descriptive text that explains the circumstances, evidence, or rule outcome leading to the creation of this flag.

This field is nullable to support minimalistic or purely code-driven flags, but when populated it should provide enough context for admin review and investigations.

severity.description:
Business severity level of the risk flag.

Represents how serious the associated risk is from a business and governance standpoint. Typical values include categories like "low", "medium", "high", or "critical".

Risk engines and operational tooling use this severity to prioritize handling, trigger additional checks, or escalate to human review.

active.description:
Indicates whether this risk flag is currently active.

When true, the flag is considered in risk evaluation, policy enforcement, and UI indicators. When false, the flag is treated as cleared, superseded, or no longer relevant.

Deactivating a flag allows keeping historical context without fully deleting the record.

expires_at.description:
Optional expiration timestamp for the risk flag.

When set, this timestamp indicates when the flag should automatically stop being considered during risk evaluation, for example for temporary or time-bounded concerns.

A null value means the flag does not automatically expire and must be cleared or deactivated explicitly.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the risk flag record.

Represents the exact moment when this risk flag was first persisted in the database.

This system-managed field is used for audit trails, chronological reporting, and debugging of risk evaluations over time.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the risk flag record.

Tracks the most recent time any mutable field of this flag was modified, including severity, reason, or active status.

This system-managed field supports auditability and allows consumers to detect stale or recently changed risk classifications.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the risk flag.

When populated, indicates that the record has been logically deleted and should normally be excluded from standard queries and dashboards while still being retained for audit and compliance purposes.

A null value means the record is considered active in terms of storage and may still be visible depending on the active flag and business filters.

IShoppingMallAccountRiskFlag.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new account risk flag in the shopping mall risk management subsystem.

Used by administrative or governance tooling to register a new risk or trust flag in the `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` Prisma table. The DTO captures all business-controllable fields needed at creation time, while system-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are generated and maintained by the backend.

Each property in this DTO corresponds directly to a column on the `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` model, preserving the same business semantics and validation rules. Nullable columns (such as `reason` and `expires_at`) are modeled as optional/nullable fields, and non-nullable columns required for creation (`actor_type`, `code`, `severity`, `active`) are enforced through the `required` array. Ownership linkage to specific actors (customers, sellers, admins, or guest users) is handled through dedicated linkage tables, not through this DTO.

Clients use this type when creating new risk flags via administrative APIs such as `POST /shoppingMall/admin/accountRiskFlags`. Implementations should apply the same validation and business constraints defined at the Prisma and domain levels, ensuring that codes, severities, and actor types stay consistent with the configured risk rules and governance policies.

actor_type.description:
Actor type that this new risk flag targets.

Must specify which broad actor category the flag is conceptually associated with, such as "customer", "seller", "admin", or "guestuser".

The value is validated against business rules and risk configuration to ensure only supported actor types are used.

code.description:
Machine-readable risk code for the new flag.

Should be a stable, structured identifier such as "HIGH_REFUND_RATE" or "SUSPICIOUS_LOGIN_PATTERN" that uniquely distinguishes this risk classification within its business context.

The backend enforces uniqueness and consistency constraints based on the Prisma schema and configured risk rules.

reason.description:
Optional explanatory text describing why the risk flag is being created.

Provides human-readable context for administrators and governance teams, outlining the evidence, events, or rules that triggered this flag.

May be set to null for purely code-based flags, but detailed descriptions are recommended for auditability.

severity.description:
Business severity of the risk being recorded.

Determines how aggressively the platform should react to this risk flag, for example by requiring extra verification, limiting actions, or initiating manual review.

Typical accepted values follow categories like "low", "medium", "high", or "critical", with concrete validation implemented in business logic.

active.description:
Initial active state of the new risk flag.

When true, the flag becomes effective immediately after creation and participates in risk evaluation and policy enforcement.

When false, the flag is stored but not considered active until later activation by administrative workflows.

expires_at.description:
Optional initial expiration timestamp for the risk flag.

If provided, defines the point in time after which the flag should automatically stop being considered during risk evaluation, supporting temporary or time-limited flags.

If null or omitted, the flag remains in effect until explicitly deactivated or adjusted.

IShoppingMallAccountRiskFlag.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing account risk flag in the shopping mall risk management subsystem.

Represents a partial-update view of the `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` Prisma model where all properties are optional and correspond 1:1 to mutable columns on the table. Identity and audit fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally excluded because they are system-managed and immutable from the API consumer’s perspective.

This type is used together with a path parameter (for example, `riskFlagId` in `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/accountRiskFlags/{riskFlagId}`) to identify the target record. Any field that is present in the request body is validated according to the same rules that apply at creation time and then applied to the existing record, allowing administrators and governance tooling to adjust severity, explanations, actor type, activation state, or expiration settings without recreating the flag.

Because all fields are optional, clients may send minimal payloads containing only the attributes that need to change. This supports flexible administrative workflows such as deactivating a flag, extending its expiration, or refining its description while preserving historical context and other unchanged attributes.

actor_type.description:
Updated actor type associated with this risk flag, if the business process allows reclassification.

While typically stable, some governance workflows may permit changing the `actor_type` to reflect corrected understanding of the affected actor category.

Implementations should enforce any constraints around whether this field can actually be changed.

code.description:
Updated machine-readable risk code for the flag.

Can be used to rename or refine the structured identifier for this risk classification while preserving linkage to related records.

Any change must still satisfy uniqueness and consistency constraints defined in the database schema and risk configuration.

reason.description:
Updated human-readable explanation for the risk flag.

Allows administrators to add, refine, or clear descriptive context explaining why the flag exists or how it should be interpreted.

Setting this field to null removes the existing explanation, leaving only the code and severity as indicators.

severity.description:
Updated business severity for the risk flag.

Enables governance teams to escalate or de-escalate the perceived seriousness of the associated risk, for example based on new evidence or policy changes.

The value must still conform to the accepted severity categories enforced by business logic.

active.description:
Updated active state of the risk flag.

Can be used to activate, deactivate, or re-enable a flag as part of risk review workflows, without deleting the record.

When set to false, the flag remains stored but is no longer considered during active risk evaluation.

expires_at.description:
Updated expiration timestamp for the risk flag.

Allows adjusting the time window during which the flag is considered effective, including extending, shortening, or removing automatic expiry.

Setting this field to null removes any previously configured expiration, making the flag open-ended until explicitly changed again.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityEvent.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for querying actor security events across the shoppingMall platform.

This schema encapsulates pagination, sorting, and rich filter criteria that administrators use to retrieve subsets of security telemetry stored in the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` table and its linkage tables for customers, sellers, admins, and guest users.

It is designed for complex PATCH-based search endpoints where query parameters would be insufficient to express the full set of supported conditions, and it is strictly read-only from a data-modification perspective.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated search results.

Administrators use this field to navigate through multiple result pages when querying large volumes of actor security events. When omitted, the server should apply a sensible default such as the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page of search results.

This field controls pagination size for queries against the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` table. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect performance and avoid accidentally retrieving excessively large result sets.

actor_type.description:
Optional filter for the logical actor type associated with the security event, such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `guestuser`.

This corresponds to the `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` Prisma model and allows administrators to limit results to a specific actor class when investigating incidents or performing audits.

event_type.description:
Optional filter for the machine-readable event type recorded in `shopping_mall_actor_security_events.event_type`.

Typical values include identifiers such as `LOGIN_FAILED`, `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`, `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED`, or `SESSION_REVOKED`, and platform-specific event categories added by security subsystems.

from_created_at.description:
Optional lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp of security events to include in the result set.

When provided, only events created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp from the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events.created_at` column are eligible to appear in the response.

to_created_at.description:
Optional upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp of security events to include in the result set.

When provided, only events created at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp from the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events.created_at` column are eligible to appear in the response.

ip.description:
Optional filter for the IP address recorded with each security event.

This value corresponds to the `ip` column in the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` model, which may be null when an IP address is not available. When provided, it allows administrators to investigate events that originated from a particular IP address or range, depending on server-side matching rules.

user_agent.description:
Optional filter for the user agent string associated with security events.

This maps to the nullable `user_agent` column in the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` table and is useful when analysts want to focus on events from specific devices, browsers, or automation tools.

metadata.description:
Optional filter against the `metadata` column in `shopping_mall_actor_security_events`, which stores JSON-encoded or otherwise structured context as a string.

Implementations may support exact matches, substring matches, or more advanced search strategies using the associated GIN index for metadata, enabling flexible correlation and investigation scenarios.

order_by.description:
Field name used for sorting actor security events in the result set.

Typical values correspond to columns in `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` such as `created_at` or `event_type`. Implementations should restrict this to a safe whitelist of sortable fields to prevent misuse.

order_direction.description:
Direction of sort ordering for the `order_by` field, such as `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending.

This allows administrators to view the newest events first, oldest events first, or apply other supported sort directions when reviewing security telemetry.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityEvent.description:
Materialized actor security event record persisted in the shopping mall platform.

This type represents a single row in the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` Prisma model. It captures the actor type, event type, optional technical context such as IP, user agent, and metadata, along with system-managed identifiers and timestamps.

It is returned from administrative and internal APIs that list or inspect security incidents affecting customers, sellers, admins, or guest users, and serves as the authoritative view for audit and risk analysis workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the security event.

This value is generated by the database or persistence layer and is used as the primary key when referencing this event from linkage tables and higher level audit tooling.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that this security event concerns.

Common values include `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, and `guestuser`. It defines which actor family the event is about and is used with linkage tables to reach the concrete subject entity.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable code describing the category of security event.

Examples include `LOGIN_FAILED`, `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`, `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED`, or `SESSION_REVOKED`. Downstream risk engines and reporting tools rely on this code for classification and aggregation.

ip.description:
Optional IP address associated with the security event.

When present, this is usually the remote address from which the action originated and is used for anomaly detection, geolocation checks, and investigations. It may be null when the IP is not known or not applicable.

user_agent.description:
Optional HTTP user agent string captured for the event.

Provides information about the device, browser, or client library involved in the incident. Useful for device fingerprinting, pattern analysis, and detecting suspicious automation, but may be null when not collected.

metadata.description:
Optional JSON-encoded or otherwise structured metadata stored as a string.

Contains additional arbitrary context such as correlation identifiers, external references, or detailed structured information used during investigations. The concrete shape of this content is determined by the producers of security events.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the security event was recorded.

This value represents the creation time of the row in the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` table and is used in chronological listings, retention policies, and time-based analytics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the security event record was last updated.

In most cases this remains equal to `created_at`, but it may change if additional metadata or corrections are applied to the event for audit or investigation purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the security event.

When null, the event is considered active and visible to normal queries. When set, it indicates that the event should be excluded from routine listings but preserved for audit, legal, or compliance needs according to data-retention policies.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityEvent.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new actor security event in the shopping mall platform.

This type is used by privileged administrative or backend components to persist a new security event row into the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` table. It captures the actor type, concrete subject linkage via actor-specific IDs when available, the semantic event type, and optional technical context such as IP address, user agent, and free-form metadata.

The server is responsible for enforcing business rules, linking this header record to actor-specific linkage tables when concrete actor identifiers are present, and setting system-managed timestamps. Consumers must provide business-meaningful values that allow later analysis and investigation of the security incident.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that this security event concerns.

This value distinguishes which family of actor the event is associated with, such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `guestuser`. It is used together with concrete actor identifiers to route the event to the appropriate linkage table and to support filtering and analytics over different actor segments.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable code describing what kind of security event occurred.

Typical examples include values such as `LOGIN_FAILED`, `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`, `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED`, or `SESSION_REVOKED`. Downstream analytics and alerting pipelines rely on this code to classify and aggregate incidents.

ip.description:
Optional IP address associated with the security event.

When present, this is usually the remote address from which the action originated and is used for anomaly detection, correlation, and investigations. It may be omitted or null when the IP is not known or not applicable.

user_agent.description:
Optional HTTP user agent string captured for the event.

This value helps identify the device, browser, or client library involved in the incident. It is useful for device fingerprinting, pattern analysis, and detecting suspicious automation. It may be null when not collected.

metadata.description:
Optional JSON-encoded or otherwise structured metadata stored as a string.

This field provides additional arbitrary context about the event, such as correlation IDs, upstream system references, or structured details needed for later forensic analysis. The platform does not impose a schema on this field but expects callers to serialize content consistently.

IShoppingMallActorSearch.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for performing a unified cross-actor search over customers, sellers, admins, and guest users.

This type encapsulates complex filter criteria, pagination configuration, and sorting hints needed by the search engine that composes results from multiple actor-related Prisma models. It allows administrators and internal operators to locate actors by contact information, identifiers, status flags, and registration periods in a single API call.

Fields are intentionally optional so that callers can supply only the filters relevant to their use case while still controlling page size and sorting semantics.

query.description:
Optional free-text query applied across common actor fields.

The search implementation may match this value against names, emails, phone numbers, or other indexed textual fields across customers, sellers, admins, and guest users to provide a broad discovery capability.

actor_types.description:
Optional list of actor types to restrict the search to.

Typical values are the canonical actor categories used by the platform, such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, and `guestuser`. These values are case-sensitive and must match the actor-type dimension used in the underlying Prisma tables and search index.

When provided, only actors whose type is included in this list are considered. When null or omitted, all supported actor types are eligible. Back-end validation should reject unsupported actor type values rather than silently ignoring them.

emails.description:
Optional list of email addresses to filter by.

If specified, the search narrows results to actors whose primary email matches one of the provided values, enabling precise lookup for support or investigation workflows. Each entry must be a syntactically valid email address.

phone_numbers.description:
Optional list of phone numbers to filter actors by.

The exact normalization rules are implementation-specific, but typical usage is to supply fully formatted international numbers to locate actors by their registered contact number. Implementations should document the expected phone number format (for example E.164) and apply consistent normalization before matching.

status.description:
Optional high-level status filter applied uniformly across actor types.

Common values include `active`, `suspended`, `disabled`, and `under_review`, reflecting business policy configuration for account lifecycle and risk handling. The exact set of allowed statuses is governed by policy, and callers should only use documented values.

When null, actors of any status may be returned. Back-end validation should reject unknown status values to avoid silently returning misleading results.

registered_from.description:
Optional lower bound for actor registration time.

When provided, only actors whose registration timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are included in results, supporting time-windowed investigations and reporting. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC (for example `2025-01-01T00:00:00Z`).

registered_to.description:
Optional upper bound for actor registration time.

When provided together with `registered_from`, it defines a closed registration date range for the search. Used alone, it limits results to actors created before this point in time. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

Administrative UI clients typically start at page 1 and increment this value to fetch subsequent pages of actor search results. Values less than 1 are invalid and should be rejected by validation.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

The implementation may enforce an upper bound (for example 100 or 200) to protect the system, but callers can use this field to request smaller or larger pages within that limit. Values less than 1 are invalid and should be rejected.

sort_by.description:
Optional name of the field to sort results by.

Typical sortable fields include `created_at` (actor registration timestamp), `email`, `actor_type`, `status`, or an internal identifier such as `id`. The exact list of supported sort keys is implementation-specific, but callers should only use documented field names.

When null, a sensible default ordering such as `created_at` descending is applied. Back-end validation should reject unknown sort field names instead of silently ignoring them.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the ordered results.

Expected values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. The value is case-sensitive and must match one of these tokens when provided.

When null, the implementation applies its default direction for the selected `sort_by` field, typically `desc` for time-based fields such as `created_at`. Unknown values should be rejected by validation.

IShoppingMallActorRiskSummary.description:
Aggregated risk summary view for actors on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is a denormalized, read‑only projection built from multiple risk‑related Prisma tables, primarily `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags`, the four linkage tables that connect those flags to concrete actors (`shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_customers`, `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_sellers`, `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_admins`, `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_guestusers`), and the higher‑level governance table `shopping_mall_risk_cases`.

It is optimized for administrative dashboards and governance tools rather than for direct CRUD over any single table. Each property exposes pre‑computed counts and aggregated severities grouped by actor type, allowing admins to quickly understand overall exposure and to identify which parts of the ecosystem require further investigation.

items.description: Risk summary metrics for a single actor type such as customer, seller, admin, or guestuser.

perActorType.description:
Collection of aggregated risk metrics grouped by high‑level actor type.

Each element represents one logical actor category (for example customers or sellers) and provides totals such as the number of active flags and open risk cases for that category. Implementations typically derive these groups from the `actor_type` column in `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` and the associated linkage tables.

totalActiveFlags.description:
Total number of currently active account risk flags across all actor types.

This value is computed from `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` by counting rows where `active` is true and `deleted_at` is null, regardless of which concrete actor the flag is linked to. It gives administrators a single high‑level indicator of overall risk signal volume in the system.

totalOpenRiskCases.description:
Total number of open or otherwise non‑terminal risk cases across the platform.

Implementations usually compute this from `shopping_mall_risk_cases` by filtering on non‑terminal `status` values (such as "open" or "under_review") and a null `deleted_at`. It indicates how many cases still require investigation or resolution by governance staff.

IShoppingMallActorRiskSummaryPerActorTyp.description:
Per-actor-type slice of the aggregated risk summary for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a single logical actor category such as customer, seller, admin, or guestuser and exposes consolidated, read-only risk metrics derived from risk-related Prisma tables. Typical implementations build each instance by joining `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` with its corresponding linkage tables for a specific actor type and, where relevant, by correlating those flags with `shopping_mall_risk_cases` and other governance entities.

The structure is intentionally compact so that administrative dashboards and governance consoles can render multiple actor types side by side while still conveying severity through counts and simple breakdowns. All numeric properties are non-negative integer metrics that are computed on demand by analytical SELECT queries; they are not persisted as-is in a single Prisma model.

This schema is not a direct 1:1 mapping of any particular Prisma model. Instead, it functions as an aggregated read model that summarizes the current and recent risk posture for one actor category within the marketplace.

actorType.description:
Identifier of the actor category that this risk summary entry describes.

Typical values correspond to the actor categories used in risk and security logging, such as "customer", "seller", "admin", or "guestuser". The exact set of values is determined by the platform’s configuration and is usually aligned with columns such as `actor_type` in risk- and security-related tables (for example `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` and `shopping_mall_actor_security_events`).

actorCount.description:
Approximate number of distinct actors of this type that currently have at least one risk flag or open risk case.

This value is a non-negative integer that is usually computed by counting distinct actor identifiers in the relevant linkage table (for example `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags_of_customers.shopping_mall_customer_id` for customers) with active flags or open cases. It helps administrators gauge how widespread risk is within this actor category at a given point in time.

activeFlagCount.description:
Total number of active risk flags for this actor type.

This metric is a non-negative integer that is typically derived from `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` joined through the appropriate linkage table for this actor type, filtered to `active = true` and `deleted_at IS NULL`. It provides a direct measure of how many risk signals are currently raised for this category, regardless of how many distinct actors they are attached to.

openRiskCaseCount.description:
Number of non-terminal risk cases associated with this actor type.

This is a non-negative integer count that is generally computed from `shopping_mall_risk_cases` by filtering on non-terminal `status` values and limiting to cases whose `primary_subject_type` or related linkage points at actors of this type. It indicates the current case-handling workload for the governance and risk management team in this category.

criticalFlagCount.description:
Number of active risk flags for this actor type that are classified as critical severity.

This non-negative integer metric is usually produced by filtering `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` by a `severity` column mapped to the critical tier (for example a value such as "critical") and by restricting to `active = true` and `deleted_at IS NULL`. Dashboards use this number to distinguish between routine risk signals and high-impact issues that may require immediate attention.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityOverview.description:
Aggregated security overview for actors on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is a denormalized, read-only analytical projection built primarily from `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` and its four linkage tables that connect those events to concrete actors: `shopping_mall_actor_security_events_of_customers`, `shopping_mall_actor_security_events_of_sellers`, `shopping_mall_actor_security_events_of_admins`, and `shopping_mall_actor_security_events_of_guestusers`. Implementations may also incorporate contextual information from risk-related tables such as `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` and their linkage tables to highlight actors that are both risky and active from a security perspective.

The structure is designed for administrative dashboards and security consoles to provide at-a-glance insight into authentication failures, account lockouts, password resets, and other security-relevant incident patterns across different actor categories. It is computed on demand by issuing analytical SELECT queries with aggregation and optional window functions and is never used to directly persist data back into Prisma models.

This schema does not correspond to a single Prisma model. Instead, it functions as a composite read model that summarizes security posture across actor types for a chosen analysis window, complementing more detailed per-event and per-actor APIs.

items.description: Security overview metrics for a single actor type such as customer, seller, admin, or guestuser.

perActorType.description:
Collection of security overview metrics grouped by actor type.

Each element in the array summarizes recent security behavior for one actor category, including counts of failed logins, successful logins, password reset activity, and correlations with active risk flags. Implementations usually keep this array small and focused on the platform’s configured actor categories (for example customers, sellers, admins, and guest users), making it easy for dashboards to compare security posture across actor groups without scanning raw event logs.

totalSecurityEventCount.description:
Total number of security events considered in this overview across all actor types.

This value is a non-negative integer typically derived from `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` over the configured time window and filter set, without exposing individual event rows. It provides a quick sense of overall security event volume on the platform and can be used alongside the `perActorType` breakdown to detect global spikes or quiet periods in security-related activity.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityOverviewPerAct.description:
Per‑actor‑type slice of the security overview.

This DTO aggregates security‑related signals for a specific actor type such as customers, sellers, admins, or guest users. The data is derived from `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` and the corresponding linkage table for that actor type, counting events by kind and summarizing recent security posture.

These metrics are intended for monitoring and incident response, enabling security and governance staff to spot abnormal patterns within each actor category without querying raw log tables directly.

actorType.description:
Identifier of the actor category that this security overview entry describes.

Typical values mirror the `actor_type` column in `shopping_mall_actor_security_events`, such as "customer", "seller", "admin", or "guestuser". The exact set of values is defined by the security logging configuration.

recentFailedLoginCount.description:
Count of failed login attempts for this actor type within the configured time window.

Implementations generally count security events whose `event_type` corresponds to failed authentication (for example LOGIN_FAILED) and that are linked to actors of this type through the relevant linkage table. This metric helps detect brute‑force attempts or credential stuffing campaigns.

recentSuccessfulLoginCount.description:
Count of successful login events for this actor type within the configured time window.

The value is typically derived from security events whose `event_type` denotes a successful authentication and that are associated with this actor type. Comparing this to failed login counts can highlight unusual behavior patterns.

recentPasswordResetCount.description:
Number of password reset–related events for this actor type within the configured time window.

This includes events such as PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED or PASSWORD_RESET_COMPLETED recorded in `shopping_mall_actor_security_events`. Spikes can indicate targeted attacks or broad security hygiene campaigns.

activeRiskFlagCount.description:
Number of actors of this type that currently have at least one active risk flag.

This metric is computed by correlating data from `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags` and the appropriate linkage table for this actor type, filtering to `active = true` and `deleted_at IS NULL`. It provides a quick link between security events and ongoing risk assessment for the same actor group.

IShoppingMallProduct.description:
ShoppingMall product entity representing a core sellable product concept in the marketplace.

This type corresponds directly to the `shopping_mall_products` Prisma model and exposes a full detail view that is safe for public product detail pages. It includes core catalog attributes from the primary table such as ownership, identifiers, descriptive content in the default locale, brand and model metadata, lifecycle status flags, and primary image reference.

The `IShoppingMallProduct` DTO is used as the response body for product detail operations such as `GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}` and as the normalized return type for create and update operations. It intentionally omits sensitive or internal-only fields (for example internal risk flags or governance markers) while preserving all public-facing product fields required by the ShoppingMall UI.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.id` and is generated by the database as a UUID. It is the primary key used by all product detail, update, and relationship operations and appears in API paths such as `/shoppingMall/products/{productId}`.

Clients receive this value in responses but never provide it in create or update request DTOs.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who owns this product.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.shopping_mall_seller_id` and references the owning seller row in `shopping_mall_sellers`. It establishes product ownership and is used for authorization checks, back-office reporting, and cross-entity joins.

For most UI use cases, clients should rely on the `seller` association for display and contextual information, and treat this raw UUID as a technical identifier for advanced integrations and analytics.

seller.description:
Owning seller of this product expressed as a summary view.

This association is derived from the foreign key `shopping_mall_seller_id` and provides the essential seller context needed to render catalog and product detail pages without additional API calls.

The summary includes identifying and display-oriented fields for the seller while avoiding deep nesting, enabling safe embedding in product responses without circular references.

code.description:
Business-level product code that is unique per seller.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.code`. It is a human-readable or integration-oriented identifier that sellers use in their own systems to reference the product.

The pair `(shopping_mall_seller_id, code)` is unique, allowing sellers to reuse the same code scheme independently of one another. It must be stable over time so that external systems can rely on it for synchronization and reporting.

title.description:
Primary product title in the default locale.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.title`. It is the main display name used for the product in cases where more specific localized content is not available.

The title is shown prominently on product detail pages, in SEO contexts, and may also be used as a baseline value when generating localized records in `shopping_mall_product_localizations`.

summary.description:
Short summary description of the product in the default locale.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.summary`. It is optimized for list and grid views, where only a brief textual overview is displayed alongside images and prices.

The summary should provide concise, high-level information about the product’s purpose and key features while remaining readable at a glance.

description.description:
Detailed product description in the default locale.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.description`. It contains extended information such as features, specifications, usage guidance, packaging details, and any other narrative content shown on the product detail page.

Localized variants of this description may be stored in `shopping_mall_product_localizations`, but this field is always populated for the default locale and used as a fallback when localized data is missing.

brand.description:
Brand associated with the product, when applicable.

This field maps to the optional column `shopping_mall_products.brand`. It typically contains the commercial brand or manufacturer name used for customer-facing display.

When the product is unbranded or the brand is not specified, this value is null. When populated, it can be used for browse filters, search facets, and brand-specific landing pages.

model_name.description:
Model name or number that further identifies the product.

This field maps to the optional column `shopping_mall_products.model_name`. It is commonly used for electronics, appliances, and other technical goods where model identifiers are important for comparison and support.

When present, it can be used in search indexing and for precise matching in integration scenarios. When the product does not have a meaningful model identifier, this field is null.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the product.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.status`. Typical business-level values include `draft`, `active`, `inactive`, `discontinued`, or `admin_unpublished`, although the exact enumeration is managed at the business logic level rather than enforced here.

The status governs whether the product is visible or purchasable in the catalog. Combined with catalog visibility rules and block reasons, it helps determine whether list and detail endpoints may expose the product to end users.

primary_image_uri.description:
URI of the primary product image.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.primary_image_uri`. It points to the main image used in product lists and detail pages, typically hosted in a CDN or object storage.

When null, the client may fall back to default placeholder imagery or attempt to derive a primary image from related tables such as `shopping_mall_product_images`.

default_locale.description:
Default locale used for title and descriptions.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.default_locale` and stores an IETF language tag such as `en-US` or `ko-KR`. It identifies the base language of the `title`, `summary`, and `description` fields.

Localization services and clients use this value to determine how to fall back from localized content in `shopping_mall_product_localizations` and to drive language-specific display behavior.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the product record was created.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.created_at` and is managed by the database or persistence layer. It records the instant at which the product first entered the catalog.

The value is useful for administrative reports, catalog freshness indicators, and sort options such as "newest" in product listings.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the product record was last updated.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_products.updated_at` and is maintained by the system whenever any mutable product field changes.

Clients can use this value for cache invalidation, change tracking, and display of "last updated" information on administrative screens.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the product was soft-deleted, if applicable.

This field maps to the nullable column `shopping_mall_products.deleted_at`. When null, the product is considered active in terms of storage; when populated, the product has been soft-deleted in order to preserve historical references from orders and reviews.

Application code and query layers typically exclude soft-deleted products from public listings and detail pages unless an administrative view explicitly opts in to showing deleted records.

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying ShoppingMall products.

This type is used as the request body for the product search operation `PATCH /shoppingMall/products`. It encapsulates rich search criteria, pagination controls, and sort configuration for retrieving product summaries from the `shopping_mall_products` table.

All fields in this DTO are optional filters or controls. The server applies reasonable defaults when values are omitted, such as default page size or default sort order. Clients can combine multiple filters to narrow the catalog results and integrate with UI elements such as category navigation, tag chips, and search bars.

page.description:
Page number for traditional offset-based pagination.

This field indicates the 1-based page index to retrieve when using page/limit style pagination. The server uses it together with `limit` to compute the result offset.

If omitted, the implementation typically defaults to the first page. When large result sets are expected, cursor-based pagination may be preferred via the `cursor` field.

limit.description:
Maximum number of product records to return in a single page.

This field controls the page size for list queries. The server enforces an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses, even if the client specifies a very large number.

If omitted, a platform-default page size is applied. Clients can tune this value based on the UI layout, such as 20 or 40 items per page in a grid view.

cursor.description:
Opaque cursor token for cursor-based pagination.

This field is used when the client follows cursor-based pagination links returned by the server. The token encapsulates position information in the result set and is treated as an opaque string by clients.

Clients should not attempt to construct or interpret cursor values themselves; they simply pass back the value returned in previous responses when requesting the next or previous page.

search.description:
Free-text search query applied to the product catalog.

This field typically maps to full-text or search-index backed queries using columns such as `title` and `summary` and potentially other denormalized search index tables like `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries`.

Clients use this field to implement keyword search boxes. The exact search semantics—such as tokenization, stemming, and ranking—are defined by the search subsystem rather than this DTO.

status.description:
Optional filter on the product lifecycle status.

When provided, this field restricts results to products whose `shopping_mall_products.status` matches the given value. Typical business values include `active`, `inactive`, `draft`, `discontinued`, or `admin_unpublished`.

If omitted, the default behavior is usually to return only publicly visible and purchasable products, as defined by business rules that combine status with visibility and block reason tables.

seller_id.description:
Optional filter restricting results to products owned by a specific seller.

This field is a filter counterpart of `shopping_mall_products.shopping_mall_seller_id`. When present, only products whose owning seller matches this UUID are returned.

It is commonly used for seller storefront and backoffice views where the UI only needs to show the catalog belonging to a particular seller account.

category_code.description:
Optional filter for a single category code in the navigation taxonomy.

This field allows clients to restrict results to products linked to a specific category, as defined by the category master data tables such as `shopping_mall_categories` and junctions like `shopping_mall_product_categories`.

It is typically used when a user navigates into a specific category page or when the UI needs to constrain search results to one primary category.

min_created_at.description:
Lower bound filter for product creation timestamp.

When provided, only products whose `shopping_mall_products.created_at` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This enables views such as "recently added" catalogs or analytics-driven segments.

Combined with `max_created_at`, it allows the client to request products created within a specific time window.

max_created_at.description:
Upper bound filter for product creation timestamp.

When provided, only products whose `shopping_mall_products.created_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp are included in the results.

It is typically used together with `min_created_at` to define a creation-date range for catalog queries.

sort_by.description:
Field or logical key describing how to sort the results.

Common values include `newest`, `oldest`, `title`, or business-specific composite keys such as `best_selling` or `recommended`. The server maps this logical key to actual order-by expressions over `shopping_mall_products` and related tables.

If omitted, the implementation may default to a commonly used sort such as `newest` or relevance-based ordering when `search` is provided.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when `sort_by` supports ascending or descending choices.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. For some logical sort keys such as `newest` or `best_selling`, the server may ignore this value and enforce a fixed direction.

When omitted, the service applies a sensible default direction based on the chosen `sort_by` field.

IShoppingMallProduct.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new ShoppingMall product owned by a seller.

This type maps writable business fields of the shopping_mall_products model that are required when a seller registers a new core product in the catalog. It excludes system-managed fields such as the primary key and timestamps, as well as ownership fields that are resolved from the authenticated seller context.

Use this DTO as the request body of POST /shoppingMall/seller/products. The service layer enriches the payload with the owning seller identifier and persists it into shopping_mall_products, optionally triggering internal indexing and auditing workflows.

code.description:
Business-level product code unique per seller.

This value corresponds to the shopping_mall_products.code column and is used for internal references, integrations, and seller-side management of products. The combination of shopping_mall_seller_id and code is unique, so codes only need to be unique within the scope of a single seller.

Clients should provide a stable identifier that they can reuse across integrations and imports, such as an ERP product code.

title.description:
Primary product title in the default locale.

This value maps to shopping_mall_products.title and is used on product detail pages, search results, and catalog listings when no localized title overrides are available.

Provide a concise but descriptive title that clearly identifies the product for buyers.

summary.description:
Short summary description of the product in the default locale.

This field maps to shopping_mall_products.summary and is typically shown in list views and compact product cards.

Keep this text brief while still conveying the essential characteristics of the product.

description.description:
Detailed description of the product in the default locale.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_products.description and should contain extended information such as features, specifications, usage instructions, and any other details that help buyers make informed decisions.

Rich content and clear structure are recommended, although formatting rules are enforced at the presentation layer rather than in this DTO.

brand.description:
Optional brand associated with the product.

This maps to shopping_mall_products.brand and can be left null when the product is not associated with a particular brand.

When provided, use a human-readable brand name that is consistent with how the brand appears elsewhere in the catalog.

model_name.description:
Optional model name or number identifying the specific product model.

This field maps to shopping_mall_products.model_name and is useful when the product has a manufacturer-defined model code that buyers recognize.

It may be null for generic products without a strong model identity.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the product.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_products.status and controls high-level catalog behavior such as visibility and eligibility for sale.

Typical values include draft, active, inactive, discontinued, or admin_unpublished; the exact set is enforced by domain rules rather than the DTO type system.

primary_image_uri.description:
URI of the primary product image.

This field maps to shopping_mall_products.primary_image_uri and points to a pre-uploaded image resource used in list and detail views.

Clients should always pass a fully-qualified URI. When null, the product may render with a placeholder image until additional media records are attached.

default_locale.description:
Default locale code for the product content.

This value maps to shopping_mall_products.default_locale and should be an IETF language tag (for example, "en-US" or "ko-KR").

The default locale is used when no dedicated localization record exists for a consumer’s preferred language.

IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing ShoppingMall product row in shopping_mall_products.

This type exposes only mutable business fields of the product, allowing sellers or admins to revise product information without changing system-managed columns such as the primary key or timestamps. All properties are optional so that callers can send partial updates containing only the fields that should be changed.

Use this DTO as the request body of PUT /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId} and PUT /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}. The target product is identified solely by the path parameter productId and is never duplicated inside this DTO.

code.description:
New business-level product code unique per seller.

When provided, this value updates shopping_mall_products.code for the product. The uniqueness constraint on the pair (shopping_mall_seller_id, code) still applies, and the update will fail if the new code conflicts with another product of the same seller.

Omit this property when the product code should remain unchanged.

title.description:
Updated primary product title in the default locale.

This maps to shopping_mall_products.title and is used across catalog views when localized overrides are not available.

Omit this field to keep the existing title.

summary.description:
Updated short summary description of the product in the default locale.

This field maps to shopping_mall_products.summary. It is usually displayed in compact list views and product cards.

Omit this field if the summary should not be changed.

description.description:
Updated detailed description of the product in the default locale.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_products.description and should contain rich information that helps buyers understand the product.

Omit this field when the existing detailed description is still valid.

brand.description:
Updated brand associated with the product, or null to clear it.

This property maps to shopping_mall_products.brand. Providing a non-null string will change the stored brand name; providing null will remove any previously set brand value.

Omit this property entirely to leave the current brand unchanged.

model_name.description:
Updated model name or number for the product, or null to clear it.

This maps to shopping_mall_products.model_name. Use this field to adjust manufacturer or model identifiers visible to buyers.

Omit this property to keep the existing model name intact.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the product.

This value updates shopping_mall_products.status and may affect visibility or eligibility for sale according to business rules.

Common status values include draft, active, inactive, discontinued, or admin_unpublished; the exact allowed set is enforced at the domain layer.

If omitted, the current status value is preserved.

primary_image_uri.description:
Updated URI of the primary product image, or null to remove it.

This property maps to shopping_mall_products.primary_image_uri. Providing a non-null URI will update the image used on product list and detail pages; providing null will clear the current primary image.

Omit this property if the primary image should not be changed.

default_locale.description:
Updated default locale code for the product content.

This value updates shopping_mall_products.default_locale and should be an IETF language tag such as "en-US" or "ko-KR".

Omit this field to keep the existing default locale unchanged.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching, filtering, and paginating product image records associated with a specific product.

Used as the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/images operation. Encapsulates client-driven controls for page size, page index, sorting, and optional filters such as visibility or image role. This DTO does not include any product identifiers; the parent product context is always provided by the path parameter productId.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve for the product image search.

If omitted, the backend should default to the first page. Clients use this together with pageSize to perform pagination over the product’s image collection.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of product image records to return in a single page.

This value is subject to server-side caps to prevent excessively large responses. Typical values range from 10 to 100 depending on UI requirements.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort product images within the result set.

Common sortable fields include display order within the gallery and creation timestamp. The exact list of supported sort fields is defined by the backend implementation.

Examples:
- "display_order"
- "created_at"

sortDirection.description:
Direction in which search results should be ordered for the selected sortBy field.

Expected values are:
- "asc"  for ascending order
- "desc" for descending order
