If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default based on the chosen sort field, such as ascending display order or descending creation date.

visibleOnly.description:
Optional filter flag indicating whether only currently visible/active product images should be returned.

When true, the backend should exclude internal, draft, or logically deleted images from the result set so that the response contains only images intended for display in public product galleries.

primaryOnly.description:
Optional filter flag requesting only images that are marked as primary for a product.

When true, the backend should restrict the result set to images flagged as primary in the underlying Prisma model, which is typically used to highlight key visual assets for the product.

IShoppingMallProductImage.description:
Detailed DTO representing a single product image resource associated with a product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This type mirrors the fields of the subsidiary Prisma model that stores product image metadata (for example, `shopping_mall_product_images`). Each record represents a gallery-style image attached to a parent product stored in `shopping_mall_products`. The DTO exposes identifiers, ownership linkage to the parent product, image location, accessibility metadata, display ordering, and audit timestamps.

Used as the response body for operations that retrieve or mutate individual product images, such as `GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/images/{productImageId}`, `POST /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/images`, and `PUT /shopping_mall/seller/products/{productId}/images/{productImageId}`.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product image record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_images` table and is generated by the system when the image is created. It is stable for the lifetime of the record and is used by API operations and internal services to reference this specific image.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product to which this image belongs.

This field corresponds to the foreign key `shopping_mall_product_id` referencing `shopping_mall_products.id` in the Prisma schema. It enforces the strict parent–child relationship between a product and its gallery images at the database level.

In API designs that use nested resource paths such as `/shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/images/{productImageId}`, the parent product identifier is typically supplied and validated through the `productId` path parameter, and this property reflects the same relationship in the persisted record. Implementations must ensure that the `shopping_mall_product_id` stored here always matches the product identified in the URL when the DTO is returned.

image_uri.description:
Canonical URI of the image or media resource backing this product image.

Typically points to an object in a CDN or object storage service and is used by clients to render the product image in galleries, thumbnails, and detail views. The value must be a well-formed URI and, in most deployments, will be an HTTPS URL to a trusted storage domain.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text for the image used to support accessibility technologies and improve SEO.

When provided, this text should succinctly describe the image content so that screen readers and other assistive tools can convey its meaning to users. When null, no dedicated alt text exists and downstream consumers may fall back to other contextual fields such as the product title.

display_order.description:
Numeric value controlling the order in which this image appears within the product’s gallery.

Lower values are typically displayed earlier. The Prisma schema enforces a uniqueness constraint on the pair `(shopping_mall_product_id, display_order)` so that no two images for the same product share the same position, which allows deterministic ordering of gallery images.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this product image record was created.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_product_images` and is generated by the system, usually in UTC and ISO 8601 format. Clients use this information for auditing, debugging, and chronological sorting but never supply or modify it directly.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this product image record was last updated.

The value is stored in the `updated_at` column and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields such as `image_uri`, `alt_text`, or `display_order` change. It helps clients determine whether a cached representation of the image metadata is still current.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp for this product image record, or null when the image is considered active.

When non-null, the record is logically removed from normal listings, though it may still exist in the database for audit and recovery purposes. Application-level queries that expose active images to end users should typically filter out rows where `deleted_at` is set.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for a new product image in the shoppingMall catalog.

This type is used when attaching an additional gallery-style image to an existing product record stored in the `shopping_mall_products` table. Each instance corresponds to a new row in the subsidiary `shopping_mall_product_images` model, which is always managed within the lifecycle of its parent product.

The DTO includes only fields that the client is allowed to supply at creation time. Server-controlled attributes such as the primary key `id`, audit timestamps, and soft-delete markers are excluded. The parent product relationship is provided via the API path parameter and must not be duplicated in this body.

image_uri.description:
Absolute or resolvable URI of the image or media resource to associate with the product.

This value typically points to a pre-uploaded asset in an object storage service or CDN. The backend persists this URI into the `image_uri` column of the `shopping_mall_product_images` Prisma model and later uses it when rendering product galleries in client applications.

The URI must be a valid, well-formed URI string. Implementations may additionally enforce scheme, host, and path constraints, such as requiring HTTPS and restricting allowed domains to the platform's configured storage providers.

alt_text.description:
Optional human-readable alternative text describing the image for accessibility.

This text is stored in the `alt_text` column of the `shopping_mall_product_images` model and is intended to be rendered as the HTML `alt` attribute or similar accessibility metadata. Screen readers and other assistive technologies rely on this description when the image cannot be displayed or when users navigate non-visual interfaces.

When provided, the text should succinctly describe the visual content or purpose of the image. When omitted or explicitly set to null, downstream consumers may fall back to product titles or other contextual information.

display_order.description:
Numeric ordering value used to control the sequence of images in the product gallery.

This value is persisted in the `display_order` column of the `shopping_mall_product_images` Prisma model. Images for the same product are typically sorted in ascending order by this field so that lower numbers appear earlier in the gallery.

The Prisma schema defines a unique index on `(shopping_mall_product_id, display_order)`, so each image for a given product must have a distinct `display_order` value. API implementations should validate that the provided value does not conflict with existing images of the same product and may normalize or re-sequence values when images are inserted, updated, or removed.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing product image record in the shoppingMall catalog.

This type is used by endpoints that target a specific row in the `shopping_mall_product_images` Prisma model, typically scoped beneath a parent product path such as `/shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/images/{productImageId}`. It represents the subset of fields that can be changed after the image has been created.

All properties are optional so that clients can perform partial updates. Immutable and system-managed fields such as `id`, `shopping_mall_product_id`, `created_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally excluded from this DTO. The owning product is determined from the URL path and must not be duplicated inside the body.

image_uri.description:
New URI of the image or media resource associated with the product image record.

When supplied, this replaces the value stored in the `image_uri` column of the `shopping_mall_product_images` model. It is typically used when the underlying asset has been re-uploaded, moved to a different storage location, or replaced entirely.

The value must be a valid URI string. Implementations may enforce additional constraints, such as requiring secure HTTPS URLs or restricting hosts to known storage providers.

alt_text.description:
Updated human-readable alternative text for the image, or null to clear the current description.

This field maps to the `alt_text` column of the `shopping_mall_product_images` Prisma model and is primarily used to improve accessibility for users relying on assistive technologies. Updating this value allows sellers or administrators to refine image descriptions without changing the underlying asset.

When set to a non-empty string, it should concisely describe the image content or purpose. When explicitly set to null, the stored `alt_text` will be cleared, and downstream consumers may fall back to other contextual information such as product titles.

display_order.description:
Updated numeric ordering value for the image within its product gallery.

This value updates the `display_order` column in the `shopping_mall_product_images` table. Changing it allows clients to reorder images relative to other images of the same product, with lower numbers generally appearing first.

Because the Prisma schema enforces a unique index on `(shopping_mall_product_id, display_order)`, the service must ensure that the new value does not collide with another image for the same product. When a conflict would occur, implementations may either reject the update with a conflict error or internally rebalance display positions according to platform-specific business rules.

IShoppingMallProductLocalization.description:
Product localization entity for the shoppingMall catalog.

This schema represents a single localized content record for a product stored in the `shopping_mall_product_localizations` table. Each localization is always attached to exactly one parent product from `shopping_mall_products` via the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key, which is surfaced here as the `product_id` field to keep naming consistent with other API entities.

Localizations are managed by sellers or admins as part of product management workflows. They support multiple locales per product, with a composite uniqueness constraint on `(shopping_mall_product_id, locale)` so that a product cannot have duplicate localizations for the same language tag.

Timestamps track creation, last update, and optional soft deletion. Business logic uses the locale field together with the parent product identifier supplied either in the URL or in this DTO to select the most appropriate localized content for end users and back-office tools.

id.description:
Primary key of the product localization record.

This value uniquely identifies a row in `shopping_mall_product_localizations`. It is generated by the system and is used by API paths and internal references when addressing a specific localization.

Clients receive this identifier in responses but never provide it in create requests, as it is assigned by the backend.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that this localization belongs to.

This field corresponds directly to the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_product_localizations` Prisma model and references `shopping_mall_products.id`.

Together with `locale`, `product_id` participates in a composite uniqueness constraint so that each product can have at most one localization per locale. Client applications and internal services can use this field to correlate localization rows with their parent product entity without relying solely on URL scoping.

locale.description:
IETF BCP 47 language tag for this localization.

Examples include `en-US`, `en`, `ko-KR`, or `ja-JP`. The value determines which localized content variant should be used for a given user or administrative context.

The pair `(product_id, locale)` is unique at the database level so that a product can have at most one localization per locale, even though the parent product identifier is also available in the surrounding API path for many operations.

title.description:
Localized product title for the given locale.

This title is shown in catalog list views, product detail pages, and search results when the user’s locale matches this localization.

Length and formatting constraints follow the underlying Prisma schema and business rules for product naming in the shopping mall catalog.

summary.description:
Localized short summary of the product for this locale.

The summary is suitable for card or list layouts and is often shown as a teaser description next to the title in catalog and search results.

It should be concise but informative enough to let users understand the product at a glance, complementing the localized title and detailed description.

description.description:
Localized detailed product description.

This field contains full marketing copy, specifications, and any other descriptive text for the product in the given locale.

It is typically rendered on the product details page and may support rich text formatting at the application layer, even though it is stored as plain text in the underlying Prisma model.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this localization record was created.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_product_localizations` and recorded in UTC.

It is managed entirely by the system and is not provided by clients in create or update requests; consumers use it for audit, ordering, and display purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this localization record was last updated.

The value is stored in the `updated_at` column and is refreshed automatically whenever localized content changes.

Clients use this for cache invalidation, synchronization, and administrative inspection but never modify it directly.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this localization, if applicable.

When null, the localization is considered active and eligible for use in storefront or management views, subject to higher-level visibility rules.

When set to a timestamp, the localization is treated as logically deleted but may remain in the database for audit, troubleshooting, or potential recovery. Application logic can filter out records with a non-null `deleted_at` to hide removed localizations from normal flows.

IShoppingMallProductLocalization.IReques.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing localized product content records belonging to a specific product.

This request DTO is used by the PATCH `/shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/localizations` operation to express complex filtering, sorting, and pagination rules in the request body instead of query parameters. It allows administrative clients to retrieve a subset of `shopping_mall_product_localizations` records for a particular product based on locale and free-text search.

Typical usage includes selecting one or more locales to include, searching within localized titles or summaries, and controlling page size and sort order to support efficient catalog management workflows in admin tools.

page.description:
Page number for paginated localization results.

The value is a 1-based index indicating which slice of the full result set should be returned. When omitted, the server may default to the first page.

Administrative clients typically increment this value as users navigate through pages of localization records in the catalog management UI.

limit.description:
Maximum number of localization records to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for the paginated response. It must be a positive integer, and the server may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

Choosing an appropriate limit helps balance response payload size with the number of round trips required when browsing large sets of product localizations.

locales.description:
Optional list of locale codes to filter localization records by.

When provided, only localization records whose `locale` field matches one of the specified IETF language tags (such as `en-US` or `ko-KR`) will be included in the results.

If omitted or empty, the operation may return localizations for all locales associated with the specified product, subject to any additional filters such as search text.

search.description:
Free-text search phrase applied to localized title and summary fields.

Implementations typically use this value to perform case-insensitive matching or full-text search against the `title` and `summary` columns in `shopping_mall_product_localizations` for the scoped product.

This allows administrators to quickly locate specific localizations by keyword when managing a large catalog with many languages.

oneOf.description:
Field name to use when ordering localization results.

Supported values include `created_at` to sort by creation time and `updated_at` to sort by last modification time. Additional sort fields can be introduced by extending the enum and the underlying implementation.

The chosen field is applied together with `orderDirection` to produce deterministic paging behavior across requests.

Field name to use when ordering localization results.

Supported values include `created_at` to sort by creation time and `updated_at` to sort by last modification time. Additional sort fields can be introduced by extending the enum and the underlying implementation.

The chosen field is applied together with `orderDirection` to produce deterministic paging behavior across requests.

orderBy.description:
Field name to use when ordering localization results.

Supported values include `created_at` to sort by creation time and `updated_at` to sort by last modification time. Additional sort fields can be introduced by extending the enum and the underlying implementation.

The chosen field is applied together with `orderDirection` to produce deterministic paging behavior across requests.

oneOf.description:
Direction of sorting applied to the `orderBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order (oldest first when sorting by timestamps) and `desc` for descending order (newest first). The default behavior when this property is omitted is implementation-specific but is commonly `desc` for recency-based views.

Consistent sort ordering is important to avoid duplicate or skipped records when the client paginates through the result set.

Direction of sorting applied to the `orderBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order (oldest first when sorting by timestamps) and `desc` for descending order (newest first). The default behavior when this property is omitted is implementation-specific but is commonly `desc` for recency-based views.

Consistent sort ordering is important to avoid duplicate or skipped records when the client paginates through the result set.

orderDirection.description:
Direction of sorting applied to the `orderBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order (oldest first when sorting by timestamps) and `desc` for descending order (newest first). The default behavior when this property is omitted is implementation-specific but is commonly `desc` for recency-based views.

Consistent sort ordering is important to avoid duplicate or skipped records when the client paginates through the result set.

IShoppingMallProductLocalization.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new product localization.

This schema defines the request body for creating a new record in `shopping_mall_product_localizations` for an existing product. It includes business fields that callers must supply such as locale, localized title, summary, and detailed description.

The parent product context is provided via the API path parameter (for example `productId`), so identity fields like `shopping_mall_product_id`, as well as system-managed timestamps and primary keys, are excluded from this DTO. Only actors that are allowed to manage the target product, typically sellers or admins, are permitted to use this DTO in create operations.

locale.description:
IETF BCP 47 language tag for the new localization.

Examples include `en-US`, `en`, `ko-KR`, or `ja-JP`. The locale must not duplicate an existing localization for the same product due to the composite uniqueness constraint on `(shopping_mall_product_id, locale)`.

Validation should ensure the tag follows platform-supported locale formats.

title.description:
Localized product title to associate with this product and locale.

This value will be used in list and detail views when the user’s locale matches this localization.

Callers should follow platform conventions for title length and content quality.

summary.description:
Localized short summary text describing the product.

The summary is designed for listing contexts such as catalog grids or search results where a brief description is required.

It should be concise and informative, complementing the localized title.

description.description:
Localized detailed description of the product.

This field carries full marketing and descriptive content that appears on the product details page when rendered in this locale.

Rich text formatting, if supported, is handled at the application layer, while this field stores the underlying textual content.

IShoppingMallProductLocalization.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing product localization record in the `shopping_mall_product_localizations` table.

This schema defines the request body for the product localization update operation, where the target record is identified by path parameters such as `productId` (from `shopping_mall_products`) and `productLocalizationId` (from `shopping_mall_product_localizations`). The DTO intentionally includes only the mutable business fields of the localization row—`locale`, `title`, `summary`, and `description`—and omits identity fields, foreign keys, and system-managed timestamps (`id`, `shopping_mall_product_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`).

Every property in this DTO is optional so that callers can perform partial updates. When a property is omitted, the existing value in the corresponding Prisma columns is preserved. Implementations must still enforce the uniqueness constraint on `(shopping_mall_product_id, locale)` defined in the Prisma schema and apply validation rules for text length, formatting, and locale codes. This DTO is primarily used by seller and admin tools to adjust localized product copy without altering product ownership or core catalog structure.

locale.description:
New IETF BCP 47 language tag for this localization, mapped to the `locale` column of `shopping_mall_product_localizations`.

Examples include values such as `en-US`, `en`, `ko-KR`, or `ja-JP`. Changing this field during an update affects which audience sees this localization and participates directly in the composite unique index `(shopping_mall_product_id, locale)` defined in the Prisma model.

When this property is omitted from the request, the existing locale value remains unchanged. When provided, the service implementation must ensure that the new locale does not introduce a duplicate `(product, locale)` combination and that it conforms to the expected locale format and any business validation rules applied at the database or application layer.

title.description:
Updated localized product title for this locale, corresponding to the `title` column in `shopping_mall_product_localizations`.

This field is the primary localized name shown in catalog lists, product detail pages, and search results when the user’s locale matches this localization. Typical constraints follow the underlying Prisma schema and business rules for product titles, such as maximum length and character set considerations.

If this property is omitted, the current title stored in the localization record is preserved. When a new value is supplied, it should represent a complete replacement of the previous title and may trigger downstream processes such as search index updates or cache invalidation.

summary.description:
Updated localized short summary text for this product localization, mapped to the `summary` column in `shopping_mall_product_localizations`.

The summary is optimized for listing and card-style views, where a concise description gives customers a quick understanding of the product. It often appears alongside the localized title in category listings, search result grids, and recommendation widgets.

When this property is omitted in an update request, the existing summary value remains unchanged. When provided, it should contain a complete replacement summary that respects any length limits and content guidelines defined for summaries in the catalog domain.

description.description:
Updated localized detailed description text for this product, stored in the `description` column of `shopping_mall_product_localizations`.

This field typically contains full marketing copy, technical specifications, feature lists, and any other rich descriptive content used on the localized product detail page. Although stored as plain text in the Prisma schema, application layers may interpret or render it as structured or rich text depending on client capabilities.

If this property is not included in the request body, the previously stored detailed description is preserved. When a new value is provided, it should be treated as a full replacement of the existing description and is subject to any validation rules for maximum length, encoding, or prohibited content defined by the platform’s business policies.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination criteria for retrieving product–category association records for a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO is used as the request body for `PATCH` list operations that query the logical junction between `shopping_mall_products` and `shopping_mall_categories`, typically implemented via the `shopping_mall_product_categories` table and related hierarchy tables such as `shopping_mall_category_closures`. It allows clients to express pagination, sorting, and simple filters while keeping URL query parameters minimal and avoiding overly complex query strings.

The DTO is a logical search model rather than a direct representation of any single Prisma entity. It is shared across customer-, seller-, and admin-facing endpoints that list categories for a product, so the server is responsible for applying additional authorization and visibility rules (for example, hiding blocked or deprecated categories from customers while still exposing them to admins). All properties in this schema are optional, enabling callers to supply only the controls they need while the backend fills in sensible defaults.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve when listing product–category associations for a given product.

When omitted, the implementation typically defaults to the first page (page = 1), returning the first slice of matching category relationships. Values less than 1 are considered invalid and should either be normalized to 1 or rejected according to the API’s validation policy.

This field is purely a pagination control and does not affect which records match the filters; it only selects which portion of the ordered result set is returned to the client.

limit.description:
Maximum number of product–category association records to return in a single page.

If not provided, the service applies a default page size (for example, 20 or 50 records per page) and may enforce an upper bound even when a larger value is requested, to protect performance and prevent accidental large scans.

Clients can tune this value based on UI needs—for example, using smaller limits for mobile views or larger limits for admin tools that need to inspect more rows at once.

orderBy.description:
Logical field name that determines the sort key for the product–category association list.

Typical values map to stable properties derived from `shopping_mall_categories` or the junction model, such as a category’s English name (for example, `name_en`), a display order value (for example, `sort_order`), or a hierarchy-related key (for example, a path or depth column). The exact set of supported values is defined by the implementation and may be documented separately as part of API guidelines.

When omitted, the backend uses a sensible default ordering—commonly by `sort_order` within the parent category hierarchy—to produce predictable navigation trees. If an unsupported value is supplied, the implementation should either fall back to a default or return a validation error, depending on platform policy.

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort direction for the field specified in `orderBy`.

When this value is used, category relationships are ordered from lowest to highest according to the chosen sort key (for example, alphabetically by name or numerically by sort_order).

Descending sort direction for the field specified in `orderBy`.

When this value is used, category relationships are ordered from highest to lowest according to the chosen sort key (for example, reverse alphabetical name or highest sort_order first).

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field when listing product–category associations.

Only two values are allowed: `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. If `orderDirection` is omitted, the service uses a default—typically `asc`—consistent with the default `orderBy` field.

This field has no effect if the implementation ignores ordering or if `orderBy` is not supported; in such cases, the server should document its behavior and may still apply a stable internal order for pagination.

categoryCodes.description:
Optional list of category codes or identifiers used to restrict which categories are returned for the product.

Each element typically corresponds to a unique category identifier such as a slug or business code defined in the `shopping_mall_categories` model (for example, a value stored in `slug` or a separate code column). When this array is provided and non-empty, only product–category associations whose target category matches one of the specified codes will be included in the result.

If this property is omitted or the array is empty, no filtering by category code is applied and all matching associations (subject to other criteria and visibility rules) are eligible to be returned.

isPrimary.description:
Optional filter indicating whether to restrict results based on a primary-category flag for the product–category association.

When set to `true`, the server should return only associations that are marked as primary (for example, when the junction table distinguishes a main category from secondary ones). When set to `false`, the server should return only non-primary associations. When set to `null` or omitted, no filtering is applied and both primary and secondary associations may be returned.

This filter is meaningful only if the underlying schema includes a concept of primary category for the product. Implementations that do not track such a flag may ignore this property or treat all associations as non-primary while documenting the behavior clearly.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.description:
Product–category link entity in the shoppingMall catalog.

This type represents a single row in the `shopping_mall_product_categories` junction table, which models the many-to-many relationship between core products in `shopping_mall_products` and navigation categories in `shopping_mall_categories`.

Each record indicates that a specific product is assigned to a specific category and may carry additional metadata such as whether the category is primary for that product. Soft deletion is supported to preserve historical assignment data for audit and reporting while allowing new active links to be created.

id.description:
Primary key of the product–category association.

This value uniquely identifies a single link between a product and a category in the `shopping_mall_product_categories` table.

It is generated by the system when the association is created and is used in path parameters such as `productCategoryLinkId` when updating or managing the link.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that is assigned to the category.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_products.id` and indicates which product this junction row belongs to.

In API design, this value is typically implied by the `productId` path parameter and therefore does not need to be sent by clients in create or update DTOs.

shopping_mall_category_id.description:
Identifier of the category to which the product is assigned.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_categories.id` and determines where the product appears within the global category taxonomy used for navigation and discovery.

The referenced category must exist and be active according to business rules enforced by the service layer.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this category is the primary category for the product.

At most one active (non-deleted) row per product should be marked primary, enforced at the application level. When true, this link is treated as the main category context for merchandising, SEO, and default navigation views.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this category assignment was created.

The value is managed by the system and reflects the moment the product–category link row was first inserted into the `shopping_mall_product_categories` table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this category assignment was last updated.

The value is maintained by the system and changes whenever mutable fields such as `is_primary` are modified for this junction row.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when this category assignment was soft-deleted, if applicable.

When null, the link is considered active. When set to a date-time value, the association is logically deleted but retained for audit and historical reporting purposes, and should not be treated as a current category assignment in normal catalog queries.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for adding a new product–category association for a specific product.

This type models the payload for `POST /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/categories` where the parent product is determined by the `productId` path parameter.

Clients use this DTO to specify which category the product should be linked to and whether the link is primary. System-managed fields such as identifiers and timestamps are excluded from the request body and populated by the backend when the new junction row is created.

shopping_mall_category_id.description:
Identifier of the category to which the product will be assigned.

This value must reference an existing record in the `shopping_mall_categories` table belonging to the global product category taxonomy. The service validates that the category is allowed for the product and that the combination of product and category does not violate the unique constraint on `shopping_mall_product_id` and `shopping_mall_category_id`.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this category should be marked as the primary category for the product.

When set to true, the application should ensure that at most one active link per product is primary by adjusting or validating other links. When false, the category acts as an additional, non-primary classification for navigation and merchandising.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing product–category association.

This type is used by `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/categories/{productCategoryLinkId}` to change mutable metadata of a junction row in `shopping_mall_product_categories` that links a product to a category.

Foreign keys to the product and category remain immutable and are never accepted in this DTO. Instead, clients update flags such as `is_primary` while the product and category identifiers are enforced by the path context and existing database row.

is_primary.description:
Updated primary-category flag for this product–category link.

When present, this field toggles whether the associated category is treated as the primary category for the product. Application logic must ensure that at most one active link per product is primary and may enforce additional consistency rules when this flag is changed.

IShoppingMallProductTag.description:
Product tag master entity used by the ShoppingMall platform to classify and organize products for discovery, search, and curated navigation.

Each record in this schema corresponds directly to a row in the `shopping_mall_product_tags` Prisma model and represents a reusable tag concept that can be attached to many products via the `shopping_mall_product_tag_links` junction table. Tags provide a human‑readable label and a URL‑friendly slug, and they are managed primarily by administrators or catalog managers.

The entity is soft‑deletable through the `deleted_at` timestamp, allowing tags to be removed from active use without losing historical references. The schema exposes creation and update timestamps so that admin tools and reporting systems can track when tags were introduced or modified, and it respects all uniqueness and indexing rules defined on the underlying Prisma model.

id.description:
Primary key of the product tag.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_product_tags.id` and uniquely identifies a tag record within the ShoppingMall catalog. It is generated by the system and is used as the authoritative identifier for read, update, and delete operations.

Clients receive this identifier in responses and must use it in path parameters such as `/shoppingMall/admin/productTags/{productTagId}` when addressing a specific tag.

name.description:
Canonical tag label used for classification and search.

This field maps directly to `shopping_mall_product_tags.name` and represents the primary human‑readable name of the tag as seen in administrative UIs and, when applicable, in customer‑facing experiences.

The value must be unique across all tags as enforced by a unique index on the underlying Prisma model, allowing administrators and catalog managers to refer to tags unambiguously by name.

slug.description:
URL‑friendly slug version of the tag name used in navigation or search URLs.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_product_tags.slug` and is intended for use in SEO‑friendly URLs, navigation paths, or search parameters where a stable, lowercase, hyphenated token is preferred over the raw tag name.

Uniqueness is enforced at the database level, ensuring that each slug identifies at most one tag and enabling deterministic routing and reverse lookups based on slug values.

description.description:
Optional description explaining how the tag should be used in curation or search.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_tags.description` and allows catalog managers or administrators to store internal guidance about the intent and proper usage of the tag.

When present, UIs can display this text in configuration screens to help other operators understand the tag’s semantics; when null, no additional explanatory text has been provided.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the tag was created.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_product_tags.created_at` and records the exact time at which the tag row was first inserted into the database.

It is managed by the system and is typically used in audit views, chronological reports, and sorting operations when administrators need to review recently added tags.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the tag was last updated.

This property reflects `shopping_mall_product_tags.updated_at` and is updated whenever the tag’s mutable fields—such as name, slug, or description—are modified.

Administrative tools and monitoring processes can use this value to detect recently changed tags, drive cache invalidation, or support synchronization with external catalog systems.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the tag was soft‑deleted, if applicable.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_tags.deleted_at` and is null for active tags. When set, it indicates that the tag has been logically removed from active use while preserving historical references for reporting or audit purposes.

Consumers of this DTO should treat a non‑null value as a signal that the tag is no longer intended for normal catalog operations, even though the underlying record is still stored in the database.

IShoppingMallProductTag.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for performing advanced, filterable, and paginated searches over product tag records in the ShoppingMall catalog.

This type is used as the request body for the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/productTags` operation, allowing administrative tools and catalog management UIs to submit structured search criteria rather than relying on simple query‑string parameters. The fields in this DTO are interpreted by the backend to build Prisma `where`, `orderBy`, `skip`, and `take` clauses against the `shopping_mall_product_tags` model.

Typical use cases include searching by free‑text keywords in the tag name or slug, constraining results by creation or update date ranges, and retrieving specific pages of tags for list views. The DTO is intentionally read‑only with respect to the underlying data and carries no authentication or actor identifiers; authorization is handled by the surrounding admin context of the operation.

search.description:
Optional free‑text search keyword applied to tag name or slug.

When provided, the backend interprets this value as a search string that may be matched against fields such as `name` and `slug` in the `shopping_mall_product_tags` table, using a database‑appropriate search strategy (for example, `ILIKE` or full‑text search).

When null, no free‑text filtering is applied and results are constrained only by the other structured filters and pagination parameters in this request.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound of the tag creation timestamp range filter.

If set, only tags whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this timestamp from the `shopping_mall_product_tags` model are included in the result set. This is useful for retrieving tags created after a certain point in time, such as during a specific administrative campaign or reporting window.

When null, no minimum creation date constraint is applied.

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound of the tag creation timestamp range filter.

If provided, the search returns only tags whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this timestamp, allowing administrators to restrict results to a defined historical window.

When null, there is no maximum creation date constraint and older tags are not filtered out unless limited by other criteria.

updated_from.description:
Optional lower bound of the last‑update timestamp range filter.

This field can be used to retrieve tags whose `updated_at` value in `shopping_mall_product_tags` is greater than or equal to the specified timestamp, which is useful when reviewing recently modified tags or driving synchronization tasks.

A null value indicates that no minimum update time filter is applied.

updated_to.description:
Optional upper bound of the last‑update timestamp range filter.

When set, only tags with `updated_at` less than or equal to this timestamp are returned, enabling administrators to focus on changes within a bounded time window.

If null, no maximum update time constraint is enforced and all tags, regardless of their update time, are eligible to be returned subject to other filters.

page.description:
1‑based page index indicating which slice of the result set to return.

This value is combined with `page_size` to compute the `skip` offset in the underlying Prisma query against `shopping_mall_product_tags`. For example, a page of 1 with a page size of 20 represents the first 20 records that match the search criteria, whereas page 2 represents the next 20 records.

Clients should treat this value as required, defaulting to 1 when not explicitly set in higher‑level APIs or UI components.

page_size.description:
Maximum number of tag records to return in a single page of results.

This field controls the `take` parameter of the Prisma query when searching `shopping_mall_product_tags`, defining how many tag summaries are included in the response’s `data` array. Typical values might range from 10 to 100 depending on UI needs and performance considerations.

Server‑side logic may enforce an upper bound regardless of the requested value to protect the database from overly large queries while still honoring pagination semantics.

sort_by.description:
Optional field name used to determine the primary sort key for the result set.

Common values include column names such as `name`, `slug`, `created_at`, or `updated_at` from the `shopping_mall_product_tags` Prisma model. The backend validates the provided field and maps it to the corresponding `orderBy` clause.

When null, a default sort order (for example, `created_at` descending or `name` ascending) is applied according to platform conventions.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the primary sort key, typically `asc` or `desc`.

When provided, this value is combined with `sort_by` to construct the Prisma `orderBy` clause for queries against `shopping_mall_product_tags`. If null, the server applies its default sort direction, which is usually ascending for alphabetical fields like `name` and descending for temporal fields like `created_at`.

Callers should align their usage with documented platform conventions to avoid surprising sort behavior in UI components.

IShoppingMallProductTag.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall product tag used for tag lists, filters, and lightweight references from products.

This summary exposes the core identifying fields of a tag such as ID, name, and slug so that applications can build tagging UIs, search filters, and suggestion lists without loading the full tag record or historical metadata.

It is derived from the `shopping_mall_product_tags` Prisma model and intentionally omits long-form descriptions and audit metadata to keep payloads compact in list contexts.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product tag.

This corresponds to the primary key `shopping_mall_product_tags.id` and is used to reference the tag from products, tag links, and administrative tooling.

name.description:
Canonical human-readable label of the tag.

The name is shown in tag chips, search filters, and management UIs and is typically unique across all tags to avoid confusion in customer-facing experiences.

slug.description:
URL-friendly slug version of the tag name.

The slug is unique and is primarily used in SEO-friendly URLs, search query parameters, and integration points that require a stable, compact identifier distinct from the tag ID.

IShoppingMallProductTag.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new product tag in the shopping_mall_product_tags table.

Used by administrative or catalog‑management tooling to register reusable product tags that can later be linked to products via shopping_mall_product_tag_links. Contains only fields that the client is allowed to set when defining a new tag. System‑managed fields like identifiers and timestamps are excluded from this create DTO.

The DTO focuses on capturing the business identifier code, human‑readable label, and optional descriptive metadata for the tag rather than mirroring database columns one‑to‑one. It is designed to be stable for API consumers even if underlying storage details evolve.

code.description:
Business identifier code for the product tag.

This code is used by admin tools and internal systems to reference the tag programmatically and to enforce uniqueness constraints at the database level. It should be human‑readable, stable over time, and safe to use in URLs and configuration values (for example, using lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens).

When creating a tag, callers must always provide this code. The same value is later exposed through the main tag representation so that administrative UIs and integrations can consistently refer to the tag.

label.description:
Human‑readable display label for the tag.

Shown to admins, sellers, and potentially customers wherever tags are rendered in UI surfaces such as product detail pages, search filters, or admin consoles. The label should clearly communicate the meaning of the tag in a concise form.

This field is required on creation and is typically what users see when selecting or browsing tags.

description.description:
Optional free‑form description or explanatory text for the tag.

Can be used by catalog managers to document the intended meaning, usage guidelines, or internal notes about when this tag should or should not be applied to products. Typical examples include clarifying whether the tag is seasonal, region‑specific, or reserved for certain product lines.

This field may be omitted entirely during creation when no additional explanatory text is needed. When omitted, the tag is still fully functional using only its code and label.

isActive.description:
Flag indicating whether this tag is currently active in the catalog.

Inactive tags typically do not appear as selectable options in admin or seller tooling and may not be used for new product associations, while existing associations may still be preserved for historical or analytical purposes.

If omitted on creation, the platform’s business logic or defaulting rules determine the initial active state (for example, defaulting to true so that newly created tags are immediately usable).

IShoppingMallProductTag.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing product tag in the shopping_mall_product_tags table.

Used by administrative or catalog‑management tooling to modify mutable fields of a tag such as its display label, description, or visibility flags. The target record is identified by the productTagId path parameter, not by any field in this DTO. All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates without resending unchanged values.

The DTO is intentionally decoupled from the exact database column layout and focuses on the business attributes that administrators are allowed to change. It can safely evolve over time without forcing one‑to‑one coupling with storage details, as long as the service layer performs the appropriate mapping.

code.description:
Updated business identifier code for the product tag.

If provided, the new value must remain unique among all tags according to the uniqueness constraints defined on the shopping_mall_product_tags model. Renaming codes should be done carefully because they may be referenced by configuration, search facets, or external integrations.

When omitted, the existing code stored for the tag remains unchanged.

label.description:
Updated human‑readable display label for the tag.

If present, this value replaces the existing label and is used wherever the tag is shown in admin, seller, or customer‑facing interfaces. The new label should continue to reflect the semantics implied by the tag’s code and intended usage.

When omitted, the current label is preserved without modification.

description.description:
Updated free‑form description for the tag.

If provided, this text replaces the existing description and can document the current business meaning or usage guidelines for the tag. For example, administrators can clarify that the tag is deprecated, seasonal, or restricted to specific product categories.

When this property is omitted, the existing description remains unchanged. To explicitly clear a description, platform‑specific semantics (such as sending an empty string) may be used if supported by the implementation.

isActive.description:
Updated active/disabled state of the tag.

Setting this to false typically hides the tag from selection in admin or seller tooling for new product associations while preserving existing historical data and analytics. Setting it to true re‑enables the tag for normal use.

When omitted, the current active state of the tag is retained, allowing callers to update other fields without inadvertently changing visibility.

IShoppingMallProductTagLink.description:
Detailed DTO representing a single association row between a product and a tag in the shopping_mall_product_tag_links table.

This type models one concrete product–tag link as stored in the database, including identifiers for the link itself, the owning product, and the referenced tag, along with basic audit timestamps. It is returned by read operations such as GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/tags/{productTagLinkId} so that tools like seller consoles and admin back offices can inspect exactly how a tag attachment is recorded.

The link belongs to a specific product and references a tag master record from the shopping_mall_product_tags table. It is conceptually subordinate to the product and is typically created and managed through nested endpoints under a product context. In addition to the raw foreign keys, this DTO can optionally expose lightweight summary views of the associated product and tag for richer, more self-contained read scenarios.

The schema also exposes a soft-delete timestamp so that administrative tools and governance workflows can distinguish between active tag links and links that have been logically removed but still retained for audit history.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this product–tag link record.

This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_product_tag_links row and is used as productTagLinkId in path parameters for detail lookups and management operations.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the product in shopping_mall_products that owns this tag link.

This value corresponds to the foreign key column that points to the `shopping_mall_products` table and establishes which product the tag is attached to. It is validated by the server when resolving nested routes such as `/shoppingMall/products/{productId}/tags/{productTagLinkId}` to guarantee that the link belongs to the specified product.

product_tag_id.description:
Identifier of the tag in shopping_mall_product_tags that is associated with the owning product through this link.

This value corresponds to the foreign key column that points to the `shopping_mall_product_tags` table and identifies which tag label has been attached to the product. It is typically used in uniqueness constraints to prevent the same tag being attached multiple times to the same product.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this product–tag link was first created.

Stored as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string and useful for audit trails, chronological displays, and debugging when tag associations were established on catalog products.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this product–tag link was last updated.

Represented as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string and refreshed whenever mutable attributes of the link change. It helps clients and administrators understand when the link was last modified without inspecting separate audit logs.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this product–tag link was soft-deleted, if applicable.

When the link is active, this field is absent or null, meaning the association is currently in effect. When populated, it records the moment the link was logically removed. Administrative tools, reporting pipelines, and governance workflows can use this field to filter out inactive links, reconstruct historical tagging states, or analyze how tagging strategies evolved over time without permanently losing the underlying data.

product.description:
Optional lightweight summary of the product that owns this link.

This association is provided as a convenience in read scenarios where callers need to display product context alongside the tag link without performing an additional lookup. It is derived from the `product_id` foreign key and is not required for persistence operations or create requests.

product_tag.description:
Optional lightweight summary of the tag that is linked to the product.

This association is derived from the `product_tag_id` foreign key and allows read-side consumers to render tag labels and basic attributes without issuing separate requests for tag details. It is read-only and not required when creating or updating link rows.

IShoppingMallProductTagLink.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new association row between a product and a tag in the shopping_mall_product_tag_links table.

This type is used as the request body for POST /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/tags, where the owning product context is provided by the productId path parameter. The client supplies only the information needed to select which tag to attach and any additional link-level metadata that is not derived from context or managed by the system.

Server-side logic merges the path-level productId with the fields of this DTO to construct a full shopping_mall_product_tag_links row, generate the link identifier, and populate audit timestamps.

product_tag_id.description:
Identifier of the tag in shopping_mall_product_tags that will be linked to the specified product.

The client must provide the UUID of an existing tag master record. The server will validate that this tag exists and that attaching it does not violate uniqueness or other business constraints.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.description:
Represents a product-specific attribute definition within the shopping mall catalog.

Each record corresponds to a single attribute such as color, size, or capacity that can be attached to SKUs of a single product. The attribute defines its internal name, customer-facing display label, data type semantics, and whether it participates in SKU variant uniqueness.

Attributes are always scoped to exactly one product through a foreign key relation to the `shopping_mall_products` table. They are used both for building SKU variant combinations and for powering faceted search and filtering in buyer-facing catalog experiences.

Lifecycle metadata such as creation, update, and soft-deletion timestamps allow audit of configuration changes and safe removal of attributes without immediately purging them from the database.

id.description:
Primary key of the product attribute.

This is a UUID value that uniquely identifies a single attribute definition row in the `shopping_mall_product_attributes` table. It is generated by the system and used as a stable reference key from administrative tools and internal services.

Clients receive this identifier in read responses but never provide or modify it in write operations.

name.description:
Internal attribute name used in configuration.

This value is typically a concise machine-oriented identifier such as `color`, `size`, or `capacity`. It is used in seller tools, internal rules, and SKU configuration logic to reference the attribute.

The combination of the owning product and this `name` value is unique, preventing duplicate attribute names for the same product.

display_name.description:
Customer-facing label for the attribute.

This is the human-readable name shown in buyer experiences such as product detail pages and filter panels. Examples include "Color", "Size", or "Storage Capacity".

It may differ from the internal `name` field to better match merchandising language or localized presentation requirements.

data_type.description:
Logical data type of values captured by this attribute.

The data type describes how allowed attribute values and SKU bindings should be interpreted and validated. Typical examples include `string`, `int`, or `double`, but the exact set of supported types is controlled by business logic.

Search, filtering, and validation pipelines rely on this field to apply appropriate comparison and serialization rules for attribute values.

is_variant_dimension.description:
Indicates whether this attribute participates in SKU variant uniqueness.

When `true`, this attribute is treated as a variant dimension for building SKU combinations, such as color or size in apparel. The cart, order, and inventory logic will consider distinct values of this attribute as separate sellable variants.

When `false`, the attribute is informational only and does not contribute to SKU uniqueness, but may still be displayed and used for filtering.

display_order.description:
Ordering index used to display attributes consistently in UIs.

Lower values appear earlier when rendering attribute lists on product detail pages or filter sidebars. This allows sellers and admins to control the presentation sequence of attributes.

The field is typically a non-negative integer and can be adjusted as merchandising priorities change.

product.description:
Owning product for this attribute represented as a lightweight summary.

This association replaces the raw foreign key to the `shopping_mall_products` table and provides sufficient context for clients to understand which product the attribute belongs to without performing an additional lookup.

The summary view avoids circular references and keeps responses efficient while still following the rule that belongs-to relations are expressed as `.ISummary` objects in response DTOs.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the attribute definition was created.

The value is stored with full date and time precision in UTC and is populated automatically by the persistence layer when the row is first inserted.

It is used for audit, debugging, and chronological sorting in administrative tools.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the attribute definition was last updated.

This field is automatically refreshed whenever any mutable column of the attribute row is changed. It reflects the most recent modification time from the catalog management perspective.

Consumers can use this timestamp to detect configuration drift or to implement cache invalidation strategies.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp for the attribute, if it has been removed.

When `null`, the attribute is considered active and may be used for SKU configuration and catalog filtering. When set to a date-time value, the attribute has been soft-deleted and should generally be treated as inactive in user-facing contexts.

Soft deletion enables safe rollback and historical analysis without immediately removing rows from the underlying table.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for defining a new variant-capable attribute for a specific product in the shopping mall catalog.

This type is used when an authorized actor such as a seller or admin creates a new attribute row in the `shopping_mall_product_attributes` table for an existing product in `shopping_mall_products`. Each record represents an attribute like color, size, or capacity that can later be bound to concrete SKU variants and exposed in faceted filters.

The DTO intentionally omits system-managed columns such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`, as well as the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key. The owning product is determined from the `productId` path parameter of the API operation, and lifecycle timestamps are handled by the persistence layer. Validation must ensure that the `(shopping_mall_product_id, name)` pair remains unique per product according to the Prisma unique index.

name.description:
Internal attribute name such as `color`, `size`, or `capacity` used in configuration and uniqueness constraints.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.name` and is primarily used by back-office tools and SKU configuration logic rather than end users. It must be unique per product in combination with `shopping_mall_product_id`, as enforced by the `(shopping_mall_product_id, name)` unique index, and should be stable over time because downstream systems and integrations may key off this value.

Typical values are lowercased identifiers without spaces (for example `color` or `capacity_liters`). Business validation should prevent empty strings and may enforce additional naming conventions depending on platform policy.

display_name.description:
Human-readable attribute label shown to customers in product detail pages and filter UIs.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.display_name` and is optimized for presentation rather than internal processing. It can contain spaces, localized phrases, and marketing-friendly wording such as "Color", "Size", or "Storage Capacity".

Clients should provide a non-empty string appropriate for the product's default locale. Additional localization for other locales, if required, is typically handled by separate localization tables rather than this field.

data_type.description:
Logical data type of the attribute value such as `string`, `int`, or `double` used for validation and filtering.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.data_type` and drives how attribute values are parsed, validated, and indexed. For example, numeric attributes may support range filters, while string attributes are typically used for equality filters.

The platform should restrict this value to a known set of supported types through business validation (for example `string`, `int`, `double`, `boolean`), even though the underlying column is represented as a generic string in the database schema.

is_variant_dimension.description:
Flag indicating whether this attribute participates in SKU variant uniqueness.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.is_variant_dimension`. When set to true, distinct values of this attribute help determine unique SKU combinations (for example, a SKU is uniquely identified by a combination of color and size attributes).

When false, the attribute is treated as non-variant metadata used for filtering or display only and does not contribute to SKU key uniqueness. This distinction influences how SKU-generation logic and validation rules are applied.

display_order.description:
Numeric ordering value used to sort attributes in product detail views and filter user interfaces.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.display_order`. Lower numbers typically appear earlier in attribute lists shown to customers and in back-office configuration screens.

Calling clients should provide a non-negative integer. The service layer may normalize or reassign display orders when multiple attributes are created or updated in sequence to keep ordering dense and predictable.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing product attribute definition associated with a specific product.

This type is used by catalog management operations that update rows in the `shopping_mall_product_attributes` table identified by a combination of `productId` and `productAttributeId` path parameters. It allows changing mutable fields such as the internal name, display label, data type, variant flag, and display ordering while preserving the association to the owning product and system-managed metadata.

All properties are optional to support partial updates. System-managed fields like `id`, `shopping_mall_product_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally excluded from this DTO and remain controlled by the persistence layer. Business logic must continue to enforce the `(shopping_mall_product_id, name)` uniqueness constraint when the `name` field is modified.

name.description:
New internal attribute name such as `color` or `size` used in configuration, if it is being changed.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.name`. When supplied, the service must ensure that the new name does not violate the unique `(shopping_mall_product_id, name)` constraint for the owning product. It should follow the same naming conventions as on creation and remain stable where possible so that downstream systems are not disrupted.

If omitted, the existing attribute name is left unchanged.

display_name.description:
Updated human-readable label for the attribute that is shown to customers in product details and filter widgets.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.display_name`. When provided, it replaces the previous label and should remain meaningful and localized for the primary catalog language.

If omitted from the update request, the display name remains as previously stored.

data_type.description:
Updated logical data type for the attribute values, such as `string`, `int`, or `double`.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.data_type`. Changing the data type can affect how attribute values are validated and indexed and may have implications for existing SKU attribute values and filters. Implementations should carefully validate and, where necessary, restrict data type changes to avoid inconsistencies.

If not included in the request, the attribute retains its current data type.

is_variant_dimension.description:
Updated flag indicating whether this attribute participates in SKU variant uniqueness.

This maps to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.is_variant_dimension`. Changing this flag from false to true makes the attribute part of the SKU uniqueness definition, while changing from true to false may require SKU regeneration or validation to ensure existing combinations remain consistent.

If this property is not included in the update payload, the attribute retains its previous variant-dimension behavior.

display_order.description:
New numeric ordering value that controls where this attribute appears relative to other attributes in product and filter UIs.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_attributes.display_order`. Adjusting the display order allows merchandisers and sellers to prioritize certain attributes visually.

If omitted, the current display order remains unchanged. When multiple attributes are updated simultaneously, the service may normalize ordering to prevent conflicts or gaps.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a product-level attribute within the shopping mall catalog.

This type is optimized for list and embedding scenarios, such as showing the attributes configured for a product or presenting filter dimensions in a catalog UI, without loading full relational graphs or large text fields.

It exposes only the key identifiers and display fields needed to render attribute lists and drive variant and filtering behavior, while omitting heavy composition relations and internal bookkeeping fields.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product attribute.

This is the primary key of the underlying `shopping_mall_product_attributes` record and is used to reference the attribute from clients and other APIs.

It remains stable for the lifetime of the attribute, even if other fields such as names or display configuration are updated.

name.description:
Internal attribute name used for configuration and administrative tools.

Typical examples include logical identifiers such as `color`, `size`, or `capacity`. This is primarily intended for system administrators and back-office UIs rather than customer-facing views.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name of the attribute shown to customers in product detail pages and filter UIs.

It is derived from the `shopping_mall_product_attributes.display_name` column and is what end users will usually see when selecting or filtering variants (for example, "Color" or "Size").

is_variant_dimension.description:
Flag indicating whether this attribute participates in SKU variant uniqueness for the product.

When `true`, combinations of this attribute's values and other variant attributes help define distinct SKUs. When `false`, the attribute may still be used for filtering or display but does not directly form part of SKU uniqueness.

display_order.description:
Numeric ordering index used to sort attributes in UIs.

Lower numbers generally appear earlier in product detail views or filter panels, ensuring a consistent presentation order for attributes such as size, color, and material.

The value is treated as a non-negative integer and is typically managed by sellers or administrators through catalog configuration tools.

product.description:
Owning product for this attribute represented as a lightweight summary.

Providing this association in the summary DTO gives list and embedded views enough context about which product the attribute belongs to, without requiring separate API calls to resolve the product by ID.

This follows the convention that belongs-to relations in response DTOs use `.ISummary` types and avoids exposing raw foreign key identifiers in summary views.

IShoppingMallProductAttribute.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing product attribute definitions for a specific product.

This DTO is used by read-only search endpoints that return a paginated set of `IShoppingMallProductAttribute.ISummary` records. It allows callers to filter by attribute properties such as name, display name, data type, and variant-dimension flag, and to control paging and ordering.

The product context is always derived from the endpoint path parameter (for example `productId`), which the service binds to the `shopping_mall_product_attributes.shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key. For this reason, the request type does not contain any product identifier field and is focused purely on search behavior within the attribute set for that already-scoped product.

page.description:
Index of the page of results to retrieve.

In typical UIs this is treated as a one-based page index where the value `1` selects the first page of results. When omitted, the implementation may default to the first page.

The value conceptually maps to `IPage.IPagination.current` in the response pagination object and is used together with `limit` to iterate through large result sets.

limit.description:
Maximum number of attribute records to return in a single page.

This acts as a page size hint for the server and conceptually maps to `IPage.IPagination.limit` in paginated responses. Reasonable values often range from 10 to 100 depending on UI needs and performance considerations.

If not specified, the service applies a sensible default page size that balances performance and usability.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to attribute names and display names.

When provided, the implementation may perform a case-insensitive match against `shopping_mall_product_attributes.name` and `shopping_mall_product_attributes.display_name` to return attributes whose identifiers or labels contain the search term.

If omitted, no free-text search filter is applied.

name.description:
Exact or prefix filter on the internal attribute name.

Use this field to narrow results to attributes whose internal `shopping_mall_product_attributes.name` matches or begins with a given token, such as `color` or `size`. The precise matching semantics (exact, prefix, or partial) are determined by the service implementation.

If not supplied, attributes are not restricted by their internal name.

display_name.description:
Filter on the customer-facing display name of attributes.

This allows UIs to search attributes by the labels seen by end users, for example "Color" or "Storage Capacity". Implementations may support exact, prefix, or partial matching against `shopping_mall_product_attributes.display_name`.

Leaving this field empty disables filtering by the display label.

data_type.description:
Filter restricting results to attributes with a specific data type.

When provided, only attributes whose `shopping_mall_product_attributes.data_type` column matches the requested logical type (for example `string`, `int`, or `double`) will be returned. This is useful when managing or analyzing attributes of a particular kind.

If omitted, attributes of all supported data types are included.

is_variant_dimension.description:
Filter indicating whether to restrict results by the variant-dimension flag.

Set this field to `true` to return only attributes that participate in SKU variant uniqueness, or `false` to return only attributes that are non-variant informational attributes. When `null` or omitted, no filtering on this flag is applied and both kinds of attributes are returned.

This field is nullable so that clients can explicitly express "no preference" when constructing typed request bodies.

order_by.description:
Field name used to order attribute results.

Supported values typically include attribute columns such as `display_order`, `created_at`, or `name`. The server validates the provided field and applies a stable sort based on it when generating the `IPageIShoppingMallProductAttribute.ISummary` response.

If not specified, the implementation falls back to a default ordering, often `display_order` ascending followed by a deterministic tiebreaker.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending sort orders. When omitted, the server applies its default direction, which is usually chosen to make sense with the selected `order_by` field (for example ascending by `display_order` or descending by `created_at`).

Clients should treat this as a hint that is validated by the service; unsupported values are normally rejected by request validation.

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.description:
Represents a concrete allowed value for a product-level attribute within the shopping mall catalog.

Each record models a single permissible option such as "Red" for a color attribute or "XL" for a size attribute. It is always owned by a specific product attribute row, which itself is scoped to a particular product. This allows different products to have their own tailored sets of variant values even when attribute names are similar.

This type is returned in read operations that manage attribute values for catalog configuration tools. It exposes identifiers, linkage to the owning attribute through an association object, the canonical value keys used for uniqueness, and display-oriented fields and sort order for UI rendering, along with basic lifecycle timestamps used for administration and troubleshooting.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product attribute value.

This corresponds to the primary key column `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.id` and is generated by the system when the value record is created.

Client applications use this identifier when addressing a specific value for retrieval, update, or deletion operations.

attribute.description:
Owning product attribute that defines the context for this value.
