In the underlying schema, the relation is represented by the foreign key column `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.shopping_mall_product_attribute_id`. Instead of exposing that raw identifier, this DTO surfaces a denormalized `IShoppingMallProductAttribute.ISummary` view so that clients can immediately see attribute metadata such as name, display name, data type, and variant-dimension flags.

This property is therefore a relational projection built from a join between `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` and `shopping_mall_product_attributes`, and not a direct Prisma scalar column. API consumers should rely on this summary object when displaying or inspecting values in configuration tools.

value.description:
Canonical representation of the attribute value.

Stored in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.value`, this field is used for uniqueness checks per attribute and is typically a stable, integration-friendly key such as `RED`, `XL`, or `COTTON`.

Clients should treat this value as a business identifier within the scope of the owning product attribute, and must avoid collisions with existing values for the same attribute to satisfy the database unique index.

display_value.description:
Human-readable display value shown to users in selection UIs.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_value` and may differ slightly from the canonical `value` to provide a friendlier label, localization handling, or marketing-oriented copy.

Frontends normally render this field to buyers when presenting possible choices for a product attribute in filters, detail pages, and variant pickers.

display_order.description:
Numeric order used to sort values in user interfaces.

Backed by `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_order`, lower numbers typically appear first in dropdowns or option lists. Implementations often use a small non-negative integer range and may apply a default when values are created without an explicit sort position.

This ordering index is purely presentational but should be managed carefully to keep the UI ordering predictable and to avoid confusing customers when attribute values are added or re-sequenced.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this attribute value was first created.

The value comes from `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.created_at` and is set automatically by the persistence layer using the database server clock.

It is primarily useful for administrative audit views, debugging, and temporal analytics around catalog changes or rule-based synchronization jobs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this attribute value was last updated.

Sourced from `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.updated_at`, this field reflects the most recent modification to any mutable property of the value, including its label, canonical key, or display order.

It can be used for incremental synchronization, cache invalidation, change feeds, and operations dashboards that display recently modified configuration items.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this attribute value was soft-deleted, if applicable.

This maps to `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.deleted_at`. A null value means the record is currently active and considered part of the live configuration.

When populated, the record is logically removed from normal selection flows but may remain visible in internal admin tools for audit, recovery workflows, and historical analysis.

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.IRequ.description:
Search and filtering DTO for querying product attribute values belonging to a specific product attribute.

This request body is used by body-based search endpoints such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/attributes/{productAttributeId}/values`. It encapsulates pagination settings, sorting preferences, and optional filter criteria that are applied to rows in the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` table scoped by the `productId` and `productAttributeId` path parameters.

All fields in this DTO are optional and can be combined freely to narrow or shape the result set. The owning product and product attribute are always supplied via path parameters, so this DTO focuses purely on how to search, page, and sort attribute values, not on identifying which product or attribute to query.

The results of this search are returned as an `IPageIShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.ISummary` page object, with pagination metadata in `pagination` and individual attribute value summaries in `data`.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which slice of results to retrieve within the paginated result set.

This value is mapped to `IPage.IPagination.current` in the response. When omitted, the backend typically defaults to the first page (for example, `current = 1`). The implementation converts this index to a zero-based offset internally when querying `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`.

Clients should always treat this field as 1-based to avoid off-by-one errors when navigating result pages.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to include in a single page of results.

This value maps directly to `IPage.IPagination.limit` in the paginated response. If not provided, the service applies a sensible default and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance (for example, a default of 20 with a maximum of 100).

Clients can tune this field to balance payload size and number of round-trips when listing attribute values for a product attribute.

search.description:
Free-text search term used to filter attribute values by text fields.

Implementations generally apply this term to columns such as `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_value` and `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.value`, often using case-insensitive, partial matching. This allows administrators and catalog managers to quickly locate matching options among many attribute values.

If omitted, no free-text filtering is applied and all values matching other criteria are considered.

min_display_order.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the `display_order` field when filtering values.

When provided, only values whose `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_order` is greater than or equal to this number are included in the result set. This is useful for range-based filtering, incremental loading, or reviewing subsets of values by order segment.

If omitted, no minimum bound on `display_order` is enforced beyond any global business constraints.

max_display_order.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the `display_order` field when filtering values.

When provided, only values whose `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_order` is less than or equal to this number are returned. In combination with `min_display_order`, this defines an inclusive range over the `display_order` index.

If omitted, no maximum bound on `display_order` is applied beyond any global business constraints.

include_deleted.description:
Flag indicating whether soft-deleted attribute values should be included in the search results.

Soft deletion is represented by the nullable `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.deleted_at` column. When this flag is `true`, the result set may include records where `deleted_at` is non-null, allowing administrators to review or potentially restore logically deleted values.

When the flag is `false` or omitted, only active records where `deleted_at` is null are returned, which is the typical behaviour for day-to-day catalog management and UI listing screens.

order_by.description:
Name of the field used for sorting the result set of attribute values.

Commonly supported values include column-oriented identifiers such as `display_order`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`, which correspond to columns on `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`. The exact set of allowed values is defined by the implementation and may be validated before executing the query.

If an unsupported field name is provided, the server may reject the request with a validation error or fall back to a default ordering, depending on platform policy. When omitted, the backend applies its default sort order, typically ascending by `display_order` or descending by `created_at`.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering results according to `order_by`.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. Implementations usually treat these values as case-insensitive, but clients should prefer lower-case values to avoid ambiguity.

If omitted, the service applies its default direction for the chosen `order_by` field, such as ascending order for `display_order` or descending order for `created_at`. When combined with an invalid direction string, the server may return a validation error or ignore the provided direction and use a default.

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.ICrea.description:
Request body schema for creating a new product attribute value under a specific product attribute.

This DTO is directly backed by the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values` Prisma model and captures the user-provided business fields needed to insert a new row. It maps to the following non-system columns:
- `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.value`
- `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_value`
- `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_order`

Fields such as the primary key `id`, the foreign key `shopping_mall_product_attribute_id`, and system-managed timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`) are NOT present in this DTO. The owning product and attribute context are supplied exclusively via path parameters (`productId` and `productAttributeId`), and system-managed columns are set automatically by the persistence layer.

Using this DTO, sellers and administrators can register new allowed values (for example sizes or colors) for a given product attribute while preserving a stable API contract even if the physical schema evolves internally.

value.description:
Canonical representation of the attribute value to be created.

This string is stored in the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.value` column and is typically used as a stable, programmatic key within the scope of a single product attribute. For example, values such as `RED`, `BLUE`, `S`, `M`, or `L` can be used to represent color or size options.

The combination of `shopping_mall_product_attribute_id` (derived from the `{productAttributeId}` path parameter) and this `value` field is subject to a uniqueness constraint. Creating a duplicate canonical value for the same attribute will usually result in a validation error from the server.

display_value.description:
Human-readable label of the attribute value as shown in user interfaces.

This field is written into the `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_value` column and is what customers and operators see when selecting options in dropdowns, swatch controls, or filter sidebars. It may mirror the canonical `value` or use more user-friendly wording, spacing, or casing, for example `"Red"`, `"Dark Blue"`, or `"Extra Large"`.

In localized storefronts, this label may be combined with other localization mechanisms to present locale-appropriate text while the underlying canonical `value` remains stable for business logic and integrations.

display_order.description:
Ordering index that controls how this value is positioned relative to other values for the same attribute.

This integer is persisted in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_order` and is used for sorting lists of attribute values in management tools and storefront UIs. Lower numbers generally appear earlier in option lists, allowing catalog managers to present options in a logical or marketing-driven sequence (for example, sizes in the order XS, S, M, L, XL).

Typical values are small non-negative integers, but the exact range is determined by platform policy. Clients may adjust this value over time to refine the presentation order without changing the underlying canonical `value`.

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.IUpda.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing product attribute value associated with a particular product attribute.

This DTO exposes only the mutable business fields of an attribute value, leaving identifiers and ownership context to be supplied by the enclosing endpoint path. All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates, changing only the aspects of the value that need modification.

The target row is identified by the path parameters `productId`, `productAttributeId`, and `productAttributeValueId`, and the service layer merges these path identifiers with any provided fields when updating `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`.

value.description:
New canonical representation of the attribute value, if it needs to be changed.

When supplied, this will update `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.value`. The new value must remain unique within the scope of the owning attribute according to the database constraint.

If omitted, the existing canonical key is preserved.

display_value.description:
New human-readable label for the attribute value, if it is being revised.

This updates `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_value` and allows catalog managers to correct wording, localization, or branding details.

If not provided, the current display label remains unchanged.

display_order.description:
Updated ordering index for this value within the list of values on the same attribute.

Applied to `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_order`, this allows reordering of options without altering their identity.

If omitted, the existing sort order is preserved.

IShoppingMallSku.IRequest.description:
Filter, sorting, and pagination request schema for searching ShoppingMall SKU records.

This DTO is used by PATCH-based search endpoints operating on the shopping_mall_skus table, both in seller-scoped and admin-scoped contexts. It allows clients to provide rich search criteria over SKU lifecycle status, pricing ranges, inventory thresholds, inventory state semantics, and temporal windows, while also specifying pagination and sorting behavior.

The schema is intentionally read-only with respect to the underlying database and does not map to a single Prisma model via x-autobe-prisma-schema, because it represents query parameters rather than a persisted entity. It centralizes search behavior for endpoints like /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/skus, /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/skus, and /shoppingMall/admin/skus.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which page of results to retrieve.

Clients use this value together with pageSize to perform paginated navigation over SKU search results. The implementation should treat values less than 1 as 1 and may enforce an upper bound to prevent very deep pagination requests.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of SKU summary records to return in a single page.

Typical admin and seller portal use cases use page sizes between 20 and 100. The backend implementation should enforce a sensible maximum (for example, 100 or 200) regardless of the client-supplied value to protect system performance.

productId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to SKUs that belong to a specific product.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_skus.shopping_mall_product_id and is particularly important for collection endpoints that are not already scoped by a productId path parameter, such as /shoppingMall/admin/skus. For product-scoped endpoints that already include productId in the path, this property should be omitted so that the path parameter is the single source of truth.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status filter for SKUs.

Typical values include business lifecycle states such as draft, active, inactive, discontinued, and blocked_by_admin. When provided, the backend should restrict results to SKUs whose status column in shopping_mall_skus matches this value exactly.

statusList.description:
Optional list of lifecycle status values to filter by.

When provided, the backend should restrict results to SKUs whose status column is contained in this list. This is useful for combining several lifecycle buckets in a single query. If both status and statusList are supplied, the implementation should either prioritize status or treat the combination as an intersection, according to service-specific rules.

items.description: Lifecycle status value for a SKU, such as draft, active, inactive, discontinued, or blocked_by_admin.

inventoryStateCode.description:
Optional filter by inventory state semantics using the inventory state code.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.code via the foreign key shopping_mall_skus.shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id. Typical codes include in_stock, out_of_stock, preorder, and similar business-level inventory state identifiers.

minPrice.description:
Optional lower bound for SKU base price filtering.

When provided, only SKUs whose price column in shopping_mall_skus is greater than or equal to this value should be returned. The value is expressed in the platform base currency and should be non-negative.

maxPrice.description:
Optional upper bound for SKU base price filtering.

When provided, only SKUs whose price column in shopping_mall_skus is less than or equal to this value should be returned. The value is expressed in the platform base currency and should be greater than or equal to minPrice when both are present.

minInventoryQuantity.description:
Optional lower bound for current on-hand inventory quantity.

This value is compared against shopping_mall_skus.inventory_quantity. It is commonly used to find SKUs that are low or out of stock (for example, values of 0 or 1) or to locate SKUs above certain stock thresholds.

maxInventoryQuantity.description:
Optional upper bound for current on-hand inventory quantity.

This value is compared against shopping_mall_skus.inventory_quantity. It is useful for locating low-stock SKUs when combined with a small threshold, or for diagnostic queries around abnormally high inventory levels.

lowStockOnly.description:
Flag indicating that only SKUs considered to be in a low-stock state should be returned.

When true, the backend should restrict results to SKUs where low_stock_threshold is not null and inventory_quantity is less than or equal to low_stock_threshold. This flag provides a convenient shortcut for common operational views in seller and admin portals.

includeDeleted.description:
Flag indicating whether soft-deleted SKUs should be included in the result set.

When false or omitted, the backend should exclude SKUs whose deleted_at column is not null. When true, the search may include soft-deleted records for audit or forensic purposes, particularly in admin-only views.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for SKU creation timestamp filtering.

When provided, only SKUs with created_at greater than or equal to this timestamp should be returned. The value must be expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound for SKU creation timestamp filtering.

When provided, only SKUs with created_at less than or equal to this timestamp should be returned. The value must be expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

updatedFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for last update timestamp filtering.

When provided, only SKUs with updated_at greater than or equal to this timestamp should be returned. This is particularly useful for incremental synchronization jobs and admin audit views.

updatedTo.description:
Optional upper bound for last update timestamp filtering.

When provided, only SKUs with updated_at less than or equal to this timestamp should be returned. It is often combined with updatedFrom to define a time window for changed SKUs.

sortField.description:
Name of the field used for sorting the SKU result set.

Typical values include created_at, updated_at, price, inventory_quantity, and status. The backend implementation must validate the supplied field name against an allowed list to prevent unsafe or ambiguous sorting instructions.

oneOf.description:
Direction of sorting for the specified sort field.

The value asc sorts results in ascending order and desc sorts in descending order. When omitted, the backend should default to descending creation time or another sensible default for the specific endpoint.

Direction of sorting for the specified sort field.

The value asc sorts results in ascending order and desc sorts in descending order. When omitted, the backend should default to descending creation time or another sensible default for the specific endpoint.

sortDirection.description:
Direction of sorting for the specified sort field.

The value asc sorts results in ascending order and desc sorts in descending order. When omitted, the backend should default to descending creation time or another sensible default for the specific endpoint.

IShoppingMallSku.description:
Detailed representation of a ShoppingMall SKU (stock keeping unit) as stored in the shopping_mall_skus table.

Each IShoppingMallSku instance models a concrete sellable variant of a product, uniquely identified by its id and associated with exactly one parent product from shopping_mall_products via a BELONGS-TO association. It carries business identifiers such as a SKU code and optional barcode, lifecycle status values that control visibility and sellability, pricing information, and authoritative current inventory quantity.

The DTO is used in detailed read responses for endpoints like GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/skus/{skuId} and GET /shoppingMall/admin/skus/{skuId}. It aligns field-for-field with the shopping_mall_skus Prisma model for scalar properties while transforming contextual foreign keys into summary association objects so that clients can render SKU details without additional lookups.

id.description:
Primary key of the SKU record.

This field maps directly to shopping_mall_skus.id and uniquely identifies a specific SKU variant across the entire platform. It is generated by the system and is immutable after creation.

product.description:
Parent product summary that owns this SKU.

This association represents the BELONGS-TO relation from shopping_mall_skus to shopping_mall_products. It replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_product_id` in the read model so that clients can immediately access key product context (such as title or brand) without issuing additional API calls.

inventory_state.description:
Inventory state summary describing the availability semantics of this SKU.

This association represents the BELONGS-TO relation from shopping_mall_skus to shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states. It replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id` in the read model and exposes a summarized view of the SKU's inventory state (for example, in_stock, out_of_stock, preorder) for catalog and admin screens.

code.description:
Business-level SKU code used to identify this variant in seller and internal workflows.

The code is unique per product, as enforced by the composite unique constraint on (shopping_mall_product_id, code) in the shopping_mall_skus schema. Sellers and administrators rely on this value for catalog maintenance, reporting, and integrations with external systems.

oneOf.description:
Barcode or similar machine-readable identifier associated with this SKU.

This value may hold EAN, UPC, QR, or other barcode formats used in physical warehouse and point-of-sale operations. It is optional and may be null when a barcode is not assigned or required.

barcode.description:
Barcode or similar machine-readable identifier associated with this SKU.

This value may hold EAN, UPC, QR, or other barcode formats used in physical warehouse and point-of-sale operations. It is optional and may be null when a barcode is not assigned or required.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the SKU controlling its visibility and sellability.

Typical business values include draft for SKUs under preparation, active for SKUs that are currently sellable, inactive for temporarily disabled SKUs, discontinued for permanently retired variants, and blocked_by_admin for SKUs hidden due to policy or governance decisions. The exact value is stored in the shopping_mall_skus.status column and is interpreted by catalog and checkout logic.

price.description:
Current selling price of the SKU in the platform base currency.

This value maps to shopping_mall_skus.price and represents the primary amount used when calculating line totals in carts and orders. It should always be non-negative and may be combined with original_price to display discount information.

oneOf.description:
Optional reference price for the SKU used to display discounts.

This value maps to shopping_mall_skus.original_price and, when present, represents a previous or list price that can be shown alongside the current price to illustrate markdowns or promotional pricing. It should be non-negative and is null when no such reference price is tracked.

original_price.description:
Optional reference price for the SKU used to display discounts.

This value maps to shopping_mall_skus.original_price and, when present, represents a previous or list price that can be shown alongside the current price to illustrate markdowns or promotional pricing. It should be non-negative and is null when no such reference price is tracked.

inventory_quantity.description:
Authoritative current on-hand inventory quantity for this SKU.

This field maps to shopping_mall_skus.inventory_quantity and is the primary quantity used by catalog, cart, and order logic to determine whether the SKU can be sold. It does not include external reservations or future replenishments and is updated by inventory adjustment workflows in conjunction with seller warehouse data.

oneOf.description:
Optional threshold at or below which the SKU is considered low stock.

This value maps to shopping_mall_skus.low_stock_threshold and is used to trigger seller or admin alerts when inventory_quantity falls at or below this threshold. It is null when no explicit low-stock threshold has been configured for the SKU.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Optional threshold at or below which the SKU is considered low stock.

This value maps to shopping_mall_skus.low_stock_threshold and is used to trigger seller or admin alerts when inventory_quantity falls at or below this threshold. It is null when no explicit low-stock threshold has been configured for the SKU.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the SKU record was created.

This field maps to shopping_mall_skus.created_at and provides an audit trail for when the SKU first entered the catalog. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset and is managed exclusively by the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the SKU record was last updated.

This field maps to shopping_mall_skus.updated_at and changes whenever mutable fields on the SKU are modified. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset and is maintained by the system for auditing and synchronization purposes.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the SKU was soft-deleted, if applicable.

This field maps to shopping_mall_skus.deleted_at and is populated when the SKU is logically removed from active catalog views while retaining historical references for orders and reports. It is null when the SKU has not been soft-deleted.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the SKU was soft-deleted, if applicable.

This field maps to shopping_mall_skus.deleted_at and is populated when the SKU is logically removed from active catalog views while retaining historical references for orders and reports. It is null when the SKU has not been soft-deleted.

IShoppingMallSku.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for defining a new stock keeping unit (SKU) variant under an existing product.

This type maps to the `shopping_mall_skus` Prisma model and is used when sellers or catalog operators add a new concrete sellable variant for a product. It captures business fields required to persist the SKU row itself, such as merchant-facing code, pricing, inventory quantity, and the chosen inventory state semantics.

The parent product context is provided by the `productId` path parameter of the API operation, so the foreign key to `shopping_mall_products` is never accepted from the client. System-managed identifiers and timestamps are also excluded and will be populated by the backend and database.

When a SKU participates in a variant grid (for example, color and size combinations), the attribute/value links are represented via the subsidiary table `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values`. For creation, this DTO exposes those relationships as an array of attribute value IDs so that the backend can populate the junction table in a single atomic transaction together with the main SKU row.

External integration identifiers that reference other systems, such as WMS or ERP, are modeled by `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids`. The nested `external_ids` collection is designed to let clients attach those identifiers at the same time the SKU is created, again participating in the same transaction boundary as the core SKU fields.

code.description:
Business-level SKU code that is unique per product.

This code is visible to sellers and internal operators and may also be exposed to external systems. It is used in conjunction with the parent product to satisfy the unique constraint on `(shopping_mall_product_id, code)` and should therefore be stable once created.

Typical values follow merchant-specific SKU naming conventions and are often used in search, reporting, or external integration payloads.

barcode.description:
Optional barcode or similar machine-readable identifier used in physical warehouse and logistics flows.

When provided, this value usually contains an EAN, UPC, or QR-related payload and may be scanned at packing stations or retail points of sale. It is nullable because not all SKUs will have a barcode assigned at creation time.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the SKU such as `draft`, `active`, `inactive`, `discontinued`, or `blocked_by_admin`.

This field controls whether the SKU is eligible for inclusion in catalog views and order flows. Creation flows typically start a SKU in a non-active state until all catalog validations are satisfied, but exact semantics are governed by business policies.

price.description:
Current selling price for this SKU in the platform base currency.

The value must be non-negative and should comply with any business rules for minimum and maximum pricing for the associated product or seller. Discounts and promotions are applied on top of this base price by other subsystems.

original_price.description:
Optional reference or list price used for showing discounts and price comparison.

When provided, this price is typically higher than or equal to `price` and is used in UI elements such as strikethrough prices to show savings. It is nullable for SKUs where no list price is applicable.

inventory_quantity.description:
Authoritative current on-hand inventory quantity for this SKU.

This value initializes the starting stock level recorded in the `shopping_mall_skus` table. Subsequent adjustments will be performed through dedicated inventory adjustment flows and should not reuse this creation DTO.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Optional threshold at or below which the SKU is considered low stock.

When set, back-office and seller-facing tools can use this threshold to trigger alerts or visual indicators when `inventory_quantity` falls to or below this value. If null, default thresholds derived from seller or global configuration may apply.

shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id.description:
Identifier of the inventory state semantics applied to this SKU at creation time.

This field references `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.id` and determines how the platform interprets the SKU in terms of sellability, such as `in_stock`, `out_of_stock`, or `preorder`. The chosen state must be compatible with the provided `inventory_quantity` and business rules.

attribute_value_ids.description:
List of product attribute value identifiers that define this SKU's variant combination.

Each entry references `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.id` for the parent product identified by the `productId` path parameter. The backend uses this collection to create rows in `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values`, binding the SKU to its attribute values such as size and color.

The combination of values should obey uniqueness rules per product so that no two SKUs share the exact same attribute set.

external_ids.description:
Collection of external system identifiers to associate with the new SKU.

Each element describes a mapping between this SKU and an external system, such as a warehouse management system, ERP, or marketplace integration. These records will be persisted in `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` within the same transaction that creates the core SKU entity to keep integration state consistent.

IShoppingMallSku.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing stock keeping unit (SKU) variant under a product.

This type maps to the `shopping_mall_skus` Prisma model and is used when sellers or administrators change mutable aspects of an existing SKU. Typical updates include adjusting merchant-facing codes, changing pricing, tweaking low stock thresholds, or modifying the inventory state semantics to reflect availability changes.

All properties are optional so that clients can send partial updates; any field that is omitted will remain unchanged in the database. System-managed fields such as the primary key, foreign keys to the parent product, and timestamps are excluded and controlled by the backend and database engine.

When variant-defining attributes or integration identifiers need to change, the DTO exposes arrays for attribute value IDs and external identifier definitions. These arrays act as high-level control fields for subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` and `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids`. The implementation decides whether providing these arrays replaces the existing collections or applies incremental changes, but the DTO structure is designed to support atomic SKU updates together with related subsidiary records.

code.description:
New business-level SKU code unique per product.

When supplied, this value replaces the existing SKU code and must still satisfy the unique constraint scoped to the parent product. It is commonly used when merchants reorganize their catalog coding schemes or correct earlier data entry mistakes.

barcode.description:
Updated barcode or machine-readable identifier, or null to clear the existing value.

Providing a non-empty string will replace the stored barcode used in warehouse and logistics operations. Supplying null removes the barcode association from the SKU so that no barcode is considered configured for this variant.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the SKU, such as switching between `active`, `inactive`, `discontinued`, or other catalog states.

Status transitions are governed by catalog visibility and risk policies. For example, moving a SKU to an active state may require sufficient inventory levels and passing content or compliance checks.

price.description:
Updated selling price for this SKU in the platform base currency.

When provided, this replaces the existing `price` value. Price changes may be subject to business rules, approval workflows, or audit requirements depending on platform configuration.

original_price.description:
Updated reference or list price, or null to remove the current list price.

Use this property to adjust discount presentations in the storefront. Setting it to null indicates that no list price should be displayed for this SKU.

inventory_quantity.description:
New authoritative on-hand inventory quantity for the SKU.

Although inventory levels are often adjusted through dedicated adjustment flows, some administrative tools may allow direct overwrites via this field. Any direct changes should still be logged and reconciled to maintain a clear audit trail of stock movements.

low_stock_threshold.description:
New low stock threshold value, or null to clear the per-SKU threshold.

When changed, the updated threshold immediately influences alerting and visual indicators in seller and admin tools. If cleared, default configuration from higher-level settings may apply instead.

shopping_mall_sku_inventory_state_id.description:
Identifier of a new inventory state semantics record for this SKU.

Changing this reference updates how the platform interprets the SKU's availability, for example moving from `in_stock` to `preorder` or `out_of_stock`. The chosen state must comply with inventory and risk policies and may affect whether the SKU can be added to carts or orders.

attribute_value_ids.description:
Replacement set of product attribute value identifiers that define this SKU's variant combination.

This field does not correspond to a direct column on `shopping_mall_skus`. Instead, it controls the junction records stored in the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` table for this SKU. When supplied, the backend treats the array as the authoritative list of attribute value IDs and updates the associated `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` rows accordingly (for example, by replacing the existing set or applying an upsert strategy).

The combination of attribute value IDs must remain valid for the parent product and must not conflict with combinations used by other SKUs belonging to the same product.

external_ids.description:
Updated collection of external system identifier mappings linked to this SKU.

This field is a high-level control structure for subsidiary records in the `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` table rather than a direct column on `shopping_mall_skus`. Each entry in the array represents an update to an existing external identifier or the introduction of a new mapping, following the shape of `IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.IUpdate`.

Depending on business rules and implementation, supplying this array can either replace the full set of existing `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` rows for the SKU or be interpreted as a set of targeted upsert operations. It complements the dedicated creation endpoint `/shoppingMall/admin/skus/{skuId}/externalIds` by allowing bulk maintenance of external identifiers as part of a broader SKU update operation.

IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.ICreate.description:
DTO used when creating a new external system identifier mapping for a specific SKU.

This request body corresponds to the writable columns of the `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` Prisma model on insert, excluding system‑managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`, and excluding the foreign key to the SKU.

The parent SKU is identified by the `skuId` path parameter in the API operations, so the server side fills `shopping_mall_sku_id` from the URL path rather than trusting a client‑supplied value. Callers supply the external system code and the identifier value used by that system, subject to uniqueness constraints enforced by the database.

system_code.description:
Code of the external system that provides or consumes this identifier.

Typical values represent integration endpoints such as ERP systems, WMS platforms, or marketplaces. The specific allowed codes are controlled by business configuration, but this field is modeled as a generic string in the schema.

This value participates in unique indexes together with `external_id` and `shopping_mall_sku_id`, so callers must not reuse the same code in conflicting mappings.

external_id.description:
Identifier string used by the external system to refer to the target SKU.

This is the exact value expected by the external integration, such as a listing ID, item code, or SKU code. The combination of `system_code` and `external_id` is unique across all rows according to the Prisma schema.

Implementations should validate basic format and length constraints where applicable and return a clear error if a uniqueness violation would occur.

IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.IUpdate.description:
DTO used to update an existing external system identifier mapping for a SKU.

This request body exposes the subset of fields on `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` that are allowed to change after creation, following a partial‑update pattern where all properties are optional. System‑managed fields such as `id`, `shopping_mall_sku_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are not writable and must never appear in the request.

The target record is identified via a combination of URL path parameters (the parent SKU identifier and the current external identifier), and the implementation applies any provided changes while enforcing uniqueness and validation rules from the Prisma schema.

system_code.description:
Updated code of the external system associated with this mapping, if a change of integration code is permitted.

When present, this value replaces the existing system code in the `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` row. The server must ensure that changing the code does not violate uniqueness constraints for the combination of SKU and system code.

If omitted, the current system code is left unchanged.

external_id.description:
Updated external identifier value used by the external system for this SKU.

When provided, the implementation updates the `external_id` column, subject to uniqueness rules on `(system_code, external_id)`. Business rules may restrict when or whether this field can change, especially if downstream systems already rely on the previous identifier.

If omitted, the existing external identifier remains unchanged.

IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination request parameters for listing SKU attribute value links belonging to a specific SKU.

This DTO is used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/seller/skus/{skuId}/attributeValues endpoint to filter and page through records in the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values junction table. It never carries the SKU identifier itself, because skuId is provided via the URL path and the backend constrains shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_sku_id automatically.

The fields focus on generic list behaviors such as pagination, optional filtering by related product attribute value, and basic created_at / updated_at range filters. These parameters are interpreted by the query layer when selecting from shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values joined with shopping_mall_product_attribute_values for seller catalog tools.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination when listing SKU attribute value links.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default such as page 1. This value is combined with pageSize to determine the offset into the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values result set for the given SKU.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page of SKU attribute value links.

If omitted, the backend uses a service-level default page size. Very large values may be clamped to protect system performance when scanning shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values for a given SKU.

shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id.description:
Optional filter restricting results to links that reference a specific product attribute value.

When provided, only shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values rows whose shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id matches this UUID are returned for the scoped SKU. This is useful when checking whether a SKU is already bound to a particular attribute value.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the created_at timestamp range filter applied to SKU attribute value links.

When set, only shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values records with created_at greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included. This helps tools focus on recently added attribute links.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the created_at timestamp range filter applied to SKU attribute value links.

When set together with or without created_from, only shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values records with created_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included in the page.

updated_from.description:
Lower bound of the updated_at timestamp range filter applied to SKU attribute value links.

Use this when a client needs to see only links that have been modified since a particular point in time based on the shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.updated_at field.

updated_to.description:
Upper bound of the updated_at timestamp range filter applied to SKU attribute value links.

When set, only links whose updated_at is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned. It can be combined with updated_from to define a closed interval of interest.

id.description:
Primary key of the SKU-attribute-value link.

This identifier uniquely represents a single association between a SKU and a specific product attribute value in the shopping mall catalog. It corresponds directly to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.id` in the Prisma schema and is used across the system to reference or update this particular junction record.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU that uses the attribute value.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_sku_id` and references the primary key of a record in `shopping_mall_skus`. It indicates which concrete SKU variant the linked attribute value applies to and is used internally to join from associations back to their owning SKU.

shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id.description:
Identifier of the product attribute value applied to the SKU.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id` and references a record in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`. It specifies the exact attribute value (for example, a particular color or size) that is bound to the SKU through this association.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU attribute value link was created.

The value is stored as `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.created_at` and is managed by the system to reflect when the junction record was first inserted. It is useful for auditing, reporting, and understanding when variant configurations were introduced.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU attribute value link was last updated.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.updated_at` and is automatically maintained whenever the association record is modified. It helps track the latest change time for catalog maintenance and synchronization tasks.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU attribute value link was soft-deleted, if applicable.

This nullable field corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.deleted_at`. When `null`, the association is considered active. When set to a date-time value, it indicates the point at which the link was logically removed from the catalog while still being retained for historical or audit purposes.

IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.description:
SKU attribute value association entity linking a concrete SKU to a specific product attribute value.

This type represents rows in the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` junction table, which models the many-to-many relationship between `shopping_mall_skus` and `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`. Each record describes a single attribute value that has been applied to a SKU, contributing to the full variant configuration of that SKU.

The entity includes the primary key `id`, foreign keys to the SKU and attribute value, and audit timestamps for creation, last update, and optional soft deletion. It is used in read responses for endpoints that manage or inspect SKU-attribute relationships in the shopping mall catalog.

shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id.description:
Identifier of the product attribute value to associate with the target SKU.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id` and specifies which predefined attribute value (for example, a particular color or size) should be linked to the SKU identified in the path. The server validates that the value exists and is compatible with the SKU’s underlying product before creating the association.

IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a SKU attribute value association for a specific SKU.

This DTO is used by the `POST /shoppingMall/seller/skus/{skuId}/attributeValues` endpoint to create new records in the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` junction table. It exposes the columns that must be supplied by the client to link an existing product attribute value to the SKU referenced by the `skuId` path parameter.

The SKU identifier itself is intentionally omitted from this payload and is instead taken exclusively from the URL path, preventing duplication and potential inconsistencies between body and path values. Server-side logic uses the combination of `skuId` and `shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id` to enforce uniqueness and integrity rules defined in the Prisma schema.

IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing SKU attribute value association.

This DTO is consumed by the `PUT /shoppingMall/seller/skus/{skuId}/attributeValues/{skuAttributeValueId}` endpoint to modify allowed fields of a `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` record. In the current Prisma schema, the junction model only contains identifying foreign keys and audit timestamps, all of which are immutable or system-managed from the perspective of business updates.

As a result, there are no user-editable columns exposed in this update payload. The endpoint therefore functions as a structural hook for potential future extensions and for enforcing authorization and existence checks on the association record, even though no mutable fields are currently available in the request body.

IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.description:
Represents an external system identifier mapping associated with a specific SKU in the shopping mall catalog.

Each record links a SKU from the `shopping_mall_skus` table to an identifier understood by an external system such as an ERP, WMS, or marketplace integration. This allows the platform to correlate its internal SKU with partner systems for catalog synchronization, inventory updates, and order flows.

The parent SKU context is always supplied by the surrounding API, typically via the `skuId` path parameter in endpoints such as `/shoppingMall/admin/skus/{skuId}/externalIds` and `/shoppingMall/admin/skus/{skuId}/externalIds/{skuExternalId}`. This DTO therefore focuses on the external identifier itself and its audit metadata, without duplicating the SKU foreign key.

This entity is treated as a subsidiary configuration object: it is always managed in the context of a parent SKU and is not something end customers interact with directly. Operations on this type are typically restricted to administrative or integration tooling.

The underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` defines the database fields, constraints, and indexes for these mappings, including uniqueness rules across system codes and external identifiers.

id.description:
Primary key of the SKU external identifier record.

This value uniquely identifies a single external identifier mapping row in the `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` table.

It is generated by the database or persistence layer and is returned in read responses so that tooling and debug logs can refer to a specific mapping unambiguously.

system_code.description:
Code identifying the external system that owns or understands this identifier.

Examples include ERP codes, WMS codes, marketplace integrations, or other third‑party system identifiers. The exact value set is governed by business configuration but the field itself is persisted as a generic string.

Uniqueness constraints in the underlying Prisma model ensure that the combination of SKU and system code, and the combination of system code and external identifier string, cannot conflict.

external_id.description:
Identifier value used by the external system for this SKU.

This is the concrete identifier string that the external system expects when referring to the SKU, such as a marketplace listing ID, an ERP item code, or another integration‑specific key.

The combination of `system_code` and `external_id` is unique across the table according to the Prisma schema, preventing accidental duplication of the same external identifier mapping.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this external identifier mapping was created.

The value is set by the system when the row is inserted into `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` and reflects the creation time in UTC.

Clients can use this field for auditing, troubleshooting synchronization flows, or ordering mappings by creation time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this external identifier mapping was last updated.

Each time mutable fields on the record are modified, the system updates this column to reflect the latest change time in UTC.

Consumers can rely on this field to detect stale cache entries or to drive incremental synchronization logic with external systems.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when this external identifier mapping was soft‑deleted, if applicable.

When the value is a date‑time string, the row is considered logically deleted or inactive according to business rules, but retained for audit or recovery purposes.

When the value is null, the mapping is considered active. Applications can filter out soft‑deleted rows by checking for non‑null `deleted_at` values.

IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters used to retrieve external identifier mappings for a specific SKU.

This DTO is used as the request body for search-style operations on the `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids` table, scoped by a parent `skuId` path parameter. It allows callers to provide optional filters related to the external system code or external identifier string, as well as pagination and sorting configuration.

The combination of this request object with the `skuId` path parameter enables flexible back-office views over SKU integration mappings without exposing low-level database details.

system_code.description:
Optional filter for the external system code.

When provided, the search will only return SKU external identifier records whose `system_code` matches this value. This is useful when a SKU has multiple external IDs across different systems and the caller is interested in a single integration channel.

If `null` or omitted, no additional filtering on external system code is applied beyond the required `skuId` path parameter.

external_id.description:
Optional filter for the external identifier string.

Callers can use this to narrow results to mappings whose `external_id` matches the specified value or, depending on implementation, a normalized form such as a case-insensitive comparison. This is primarily useful for reconciliation tools that already know an external ID and want to locate its mapping.

If `null` or omitted, no direct filter by external identifier is applied and results may include all external IDs for the given SKU.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results, starting from 1.

When provided with a positive integer value, it selects which slice of the full result set should be returned. If `null` or omitted, the implementation applies a default page index, typically page 1.

Clients should always provide both `page` and `limit` together when they need deterministic paging behavior across subsequent calls.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page of results.

When specified with a positive integer value, it controls the page size for the SKU external ID search. If `null` or omitted, the service applies a sensible default page size that balances performance with usability.

Implementations may enforce an upper bound on this value to prevent excessively large result sets from being requested in a single call.

order_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort the external ID results.

Typical values include logical columns such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `system_code`, depending on what the service implementation supports. The exact set of allowed values is determined by the backend but should be documented consistently with this schema.

If `null` or omitted, a default ordering (for example, by `created_at` descending) is applied.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the ordered result set.

Implementations commonly support values such as `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. This field applies to the column specified by `order_by`.

If `null` or omitted, the service will use its default sort direction, typically descending for timestamp-based orderings.

IShoppingMallSkuInventoryState.description:
SKU inventory state entity used by the shopping mall platform to describe inventory semantics for SKUs.

Represents a reference record in the shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states table that defines how inventory in a specific state behaves in catalog, cart, and checkout flows. Each row has a UUID primary key id, a unique machine-readable code (for example, in_stock or preorder), a human-readable name for configuration tools, an optional description explaining business semantics, a boolean is_purchasable flag indicating whether SKUs in this state may be purchased, and audit timestamps tracking lifecycle events.

This type is used in admin-facing APIs for viewing and managing inventory state definitions and is referenced by SKU records to interpret inventory behavior across the platform.

id.description: UUID primary key of the SKU inventory state record in shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.

code.description: Machine-readable unique code for this inventory state (for example, in_stock, preorder, out_of_stock). Must be unique across all inventory state records.

name.description: Human-readable name of the inventory state used in administrative tools and configuration UIs.

description.description: Optional free-form description explaining the semantics and business behavior of this inventory state. May be null when no additional details are required.

is_purchasable.description: Flag indicating whether SKUs in this state are allowed to be added to carts and converted into orders. True for purchasable states such as in_stock; false for non-purchasable states such as discontinued or blocked.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this inventory state record was first created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this inventory state record was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Optional timestamp indicating when this inventory state record was soft-deleted. Null when the record is active.

IShoppingMallSkuInventoryState.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new SKU inventory state in the shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states table.

Used by admin-only configuration APIs to define additional inventory state semantics that can be referenced by SKUs. The client provides the unique machine-readable code, human-readable name, optional description of behavior, and explicit is_purchasable flag. The server generates id and manages created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields.

code.description: Machine-readable unique code for the new inventory state (for example, in_stock, preorder, discontinued). Must be unique across all existing inventory states.

name.description: Human-readable name of the inventory state for use in admin and configuration interfaces.

description.description: Optional description giving additional details about this inventory state's semantics. May be omitted or null when no extra explanation is necessary.

is_purchasable.description: Flag indicating whether SKUs in this state are allowed to be added to carts and converted into orders. True if the state is purchasable; false otherwise.

IShoppingMallSkuInventoryState.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing SKU inventory state identified by its UUID id.

Allows administrative tools to modify modifiable attributes of an inventory state such as its name, optional description, is_purchasable flag, and, where allowed by business rules, the machine-readable code. Ownership and audit fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are managed exclusively by the backend and are not part of this DTO.

code.description: New machine-readable unique code for this inventory state, if a code change is allowed by business rules. Must remain unique across all inventory state records when provided.

name.description: Updated human-readable name of the inventory state as displayed in admin tools.

description.description: Updated optional description explaining the semantics of this inventory state. Use null to clear an existing description.

is_purchasable.description: Updated flag indicating whether SKUs in this state may be purchased. True for purchasable states and false for non-purchasable states.

IShoppingMallSkuInventoryState.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a SKU inventory state configuration used across the shopping mall catalog.

This DTO exposes the key identifying and behavioral fields that describe how inventory in a given state should be treated by catalog, cart, and checkout logic. It is suitable for list views, configuration UIs, and as an embedded reference from SKU or product DTOs.

The summary deliberately omits large or rarely used fields, but preserves enough information for admins and services to understand whether items in this state are purchasable and how the state should be labeled in user interfaces.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU inventory state record.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.id` and acts as the primary key across the platform. It is assigned by the system and does not change over time.

Client applications reference this identifier when attaching an inventory state to SKUs or when retrieving specific configuration records.

code.description:
Machine-readable code that uniquely identifies this inventory state.

The value maps to `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.code` and is constrained to be unique across all inventory states. Typical examples include `in_stock`, `out_of_stock`, `preorder`, or `discontinued`.

Services and frontends use this code in business rules, configuration files, and UI logic where a stable, readable identifier is preferable to an opaque UUID.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the inventory state to display in administrative tools or internal dashboards.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.name` and provides a concise label that operators can easily interpret.

While the code is optimized for machines, the name is optimized for people and may be localized or adjusted for clarity over time.

is_purchasable.description:
Flag indicating whether SKUs in this inventory state can be added to carts and converted into orders.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.is_purchasable` and is a primary driver of cart and checkout behavior. When true, catalog and checkout flows treat items in this state as sellable; when false, attempts to purchase such SKUs should be blocked or redirected.

Business rules around backorders, preorders, or discontinued items can be implemented by combining this flag with the `code` and `description` fields.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory state record was created.

The value corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.created_at` and is stored in UTC. It is useful for auditing changes to the inventory state catalog and understanding when specific states were introduced.

This field is immutable and can be used for chronological reporting or debugging configuration changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory state record was last updated.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_sku_inventory_states.updated_at` and is automatically updated whenever the name, code, description, or behavioral flags of the inventory state change.

Client applications can use this value to detect configuration drift, implement cache invalidation strategies, or sort by most recently modified states.

IShoppingMallSkuInventoryState.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request payload for retrieving a paginated list of SKU inventory state definitions.

This DTO is consumed by the inventory state search endpoint to capture pagination controls, sorting preferences, and optional filter criteria such as code fragments, name fragments, and purchasability flags.

It is designed for administrative consoles and configuration tools that need flexible query capabilities over the reference inventory state table.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which slice of results to retrieve.

If omitted, the backend may default this to the first page according to platform-wide pagination defaults.

limit.description:
Maximum number of inventory state records to return in a single page of results.

The server may enforce an upper bound regardless of the requested size to ensure operational stability.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to fields such as `code`, `name`, or `description`.

Implementations can use this field to implement simple keyword search behavior without exposing per-field filters. When not provided, all records are eligible to be returned subject to other filters.

is_purchasable.description:
Optional filter indicating whether to restrict results to purchasable or non-purchasable inventory states.

When `true`, only states with `is_purchasable = true` should be returned. When `false`, only non-purchasable states should be returned. When null or omitted, no filter on purchasability is applied.

order_by.description:
Name of the column or logical field to use when ordering inventory state records.

Common values include `code`, `name`, and `created_at`. Implementations should validate this field against an allowlist of sortable properties to avoid exposing internal details or causing inefficient queries.

order_direction.description:
Direction of sorting to apply when ordering records by `order_by`.

Typical accepted values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. Service implementations may normalize casing or provide strict enum validation at runtime.

IShoppingMallCatalogVisibilityRule.description:
Catalog visibility rule entity representing a single configuration row from the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table.

Each record models a business-managed rule that controls which products or SKUs are visible to which actors under which conditions in the shopping mall catalog. A rule can be scoped globally or narrowed to a seller, product, or SKU using foreign key references, and may further be constrained by actor type and region.

Visibility rules are created and maintained by administrative actors. They are time-bound and stateful through enabled and effective period fields, and are fully auditable via creator and timestamp columns. Service logic uses these rules when deciding whether particular catalog entries should be displayed in search, navigation, or detail pages for a given actor and context.

id.description:
Primary key of the catalog visibility rule.

This is the unique UUID identifier stored in `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules.id` and is used as the stable reference key in all read, update, and delete operations.

APIs that fetch or mutate a specific visibility rule use this value in their path parameters, and internal services reference it when linking audit, monitoring, or analytics records to a particular rule.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who created this visibility rule.

This field stores a foreign key to `shopping_mall_admins.id` and establishes authorship and governance responsibility for the rule.

It is populated by the backend based on the authenticated admin actor and is not supplied directly by clients in create or update DTOs.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Optional seller scope for this visibility rule.

When present, this UUID references `shopping_mall_sellers.id` and indicates that the rule applies only to catalog entities owned by the specified seller.

If null, the rule is not restricted to a single seller and may apply globally or be refined by other scoping fields such as product or SKU.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Optional product-level scope for this visibility rule.

When set, this field references `shopping_mall_products.id` and constrains the rule to a specific product concept in the catalog.

If null, the rule does not target a single product and may instead apply more broadly (for example, at seller or SKU level) depending on other scoping columns.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Optional SKU-level scope for this visibility rule.

When populated, this UUID references `shopping_mall_skus.id` and indicates that the rule specifically targets a concrete sellable variant.

If null, the rule applies at a broader scope such as product or seller level, or globally when no other scoping columns are set.

rule_type.description:
Type of the visibility rule expressing the primary behavioral category.

Typical values include business-defined labels such as `hide`, `show_only_to_registered`, or `region_restricted`, as configured by platform policy.

Service implementations interpret this field to decide how to apply the rule when evaluating catalog visibility for a given actor and context.

actor_type.description:
Optional actor type that this visibility rule targets.

When present, this value distinguishes which actor group the rule applies to, for example `guestUser`, `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`, depending on the platform’s configured vocabulary.

If null, the rule is actor-agnostic and may apply to any actor unless further constrained by additional business logic.

region_code.description:
Optional region or market code used when the rule is region-specific.

This field typically stores a standardized region identifier such as a country or market code, and is evaluated alongside other rule conditions to restrict visibility in particular geographies.

When null, the rule is not tied to a specific region and may apply across all regions unless limited by other policy mechanisms.

enabled.description:
Indicates whether this visibility rule is currently active.

When true, the rule is considered by the catalog visibility engine whenever matching products or SKUs are evaluated for a given actor and context.

When false, the rule is logically disabled and should be ignored for runtime visibility decisions while remaining available for audit and historical inspection.

starts_at.description:
Optional timestamp from which the visibility rule becomes effective.

If set, this `date-time` value specifies the lower bound of the rule’s active window. The rule is applied only for requests occurring at or after this instant.

When null, the rule is effective immediately upon creation or since an unspecified past time, subject to its `enabled` flag and other conditions.

ends_at.description:
Optional timestamp after which the visibility rule is no longer applied.

When provided, this `date-time` value marks the upper bound of the rule’s active period, and the rule is considered inactive for requests occurring after this instant.

If null, the rule has no predefined end date and remains eligible for evaluation until explicitly disabled or soft-deleted.

reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation describing why this rule exists.

This field provides governance, audit, and operational context, such as the business policy, campaign, compliance requirement, or incident that motivated the rule.

Administrative tools typically surface this text when reviewing, approving, or debugging catalog visibility configurations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the visibility rule record was created.

This `date-time` value reflects when the row was first inserted into `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` and is managed by the persistence layer.

It is used for audit trails, chronological sorting in administrative lists, and time-based reporting on rule creation activity.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the visibility rule record was last updated.

This field is automatically refreshed whenever mutable columns of the rule are changed and is stored in `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules.updated_at`.

Clients can use it to detect recent changes, display last modification information in management UIs, or implement optimistic concurrency strategies if required.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp for the visibility rule, if it has been logically removed.

When this `date-time` value is non-null, the record is considered deleted from an operational standpoint but retained for audit and historical analysis.

Business logic and query layers typically exclude rows with a non-null `deleted_at` from active rule evaluation, unless explicitly requested for governance or forensic views.

admin.description:
Summary representation of the administrator who created this visibility rule.

This object provides human-readable context such as the admin’s name or identifier for audit and management UIs without requiring an additional API call to fetch admin details.

It is derived from the `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key and follows the platform-wide `.ISummary` pattern for actor entities.

seller.description:
Optional summary representation of the seller to which this rule is scoped.

When non-null, this object describes the seller whose catalog entries are affected by the rule, enabling administrative tools to show seller context directly in rule listings.

It is resolved from the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key when that field is not null.

product.description:
Optional summary representation of the product targeted by this rule.

When present, this object gives high-level product context (such as name or code) so that admins can understand which product a rule applies to without issuing a separate product lookup.

It is resolved from the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key when that field is not null.

sku.description:
Optional summary representation of the SKU variant targeted by this rule.

When non-null, this object provides concise SKU-level detail so that administrators can see exactly which variant is impacted by the rule.

It is resolved from the `shopping_mall_sku_id` foreign key when that field is not null.

IShoppingMallCatalogVisibilityRule.IRequ.description:
Search and filtering request model for querying catalog visibility rules.

This DTO is used by administrative search endpoints, such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/catalogVisibilityRules`, to express complex filter criteria over the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table. It allows callers to narrow results by rule status, scope, actor and region, effective period, and text-based reason content while controlling pagination and sorting.

The structure is optimized for list and management views, enabling governance and operations teams to efficiently locate, review, and audit visibility rules that affect catalog exposure across products, SKUs, sellers, and regions.

page.description:
Zero-based page index for paginated catalog visibility rule search.

This integer selects which result page to return when combined with `limit`. A value of 0 represents the first page, 1 the second page, and so on.

If omitted, service implementations commonly default to the first page according to platform-wide pagination conventions.

limit.description:
Maximum number of catalog visibility rules to return in a single page.

This integer controls the page size for search results and is used together with `page` to implement offset-based pagination.

Implementations typically enforce an upper bound to protect performance and may apply a default when the client omits this value.

enabled.description:
Optional filter on the active status of visibility rules.

When true, only rules with `enabled = true` are included in the result set. When false, only disabled rules are returned.

If null or omitted, no filter on the enabled flag is applied and both active and inactive rules may appear depending on other conditions.

rule_type.description:
Optional filter on the rule type category.

This value is matched against the `rule_type` column of `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules`, allowing administrators to search for rules of a particular behavioral class such as `hide`, `show_only_to_registered`, or `region_restricted` depending on configured semantics.

When null, the search does not constrain results by rule type.

actor_type.description:
Optional filter on the targeted actor type for catalog visibility rules.

When provided, the search returns only rules whose `actor_type` matches the supplied value, for example `guestUser`, `customer`, `seller`, or `admin` based on platform terminology.

If null, rules are not filtered by actor type and both actor-specific and actor-agnostic rules may be included.

region_code.description:
Optional filter on region or market code for visibility rules.

This field is compared against `region_code` in `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` so that administrators can list rules that affect a particular country or regional market.

When null, the search does not restrict results by region code and may return rules that apply globally or to multiple regions.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Optional filter restricting results to rules scoped to a specific seller.

When this UUID is provided, only visibility rules whose `shopping_mall_seller_id` matches the value are returned, helping administrators analyze the rule set for a particular seller account.

If null, rules are not filtered by seller scope and both seller-specific and non-seller-scoped rules may be included.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Optional filter limiting results to rules tied to a specific product.

When set, the search includes only rules whose `shopping_mall_product_id` equals the provided UUID, enabling review of all visibility rules affecting a single product concept.

If null, the query does not constrain results by product-level scope.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Optional filter narrowing results to rules associated with a specific SKU variant.

When this UUID is supplied, only rules where `shopping_mall_sku_id` matches the value are returned, allowing focused investigation of SKU-level visibility.

If null, the search does not filter by SKU-level scope and may include rules at broader scopes.

starts_at_from.description:
Optional lower bound filter on rule effective start time.

When provided, the search returns only rules whose `starts_at` is greater than or equal to this timestamp, or whose `starts_at` is null and thus effectively active before this instant depending on business interpretation.

If null, no minimum constraint is applied to the rule start time in the query.

starts_at_to.description:
