Optional upper bound filter on rule effective start time.

This `date-time` value, when present, filters results to rules whose `starts_at` is less than or equal to the specified instant, supporting discovery of rules that began within a certain window.

When null, the query does not impose an upper bound on the `starts_at` column.

ends_at_from.description:
Optional lower bound filter on the rule end time.

Administrators can use this field to find rules whose `ends_at` occurs on or after the specified timestamp, or rules without an end time depending on query logic, in order to analyze rules that remain active into a particular period.

If null, no minimum constraint is applied to the `ends_at` column.

ends_at_to.description:
Optional upper bound filter on the rule end time.

When set, this `date-time` value limits results to rules whose `ends_at` is less than or equal to the specified moment, aiding analysis of rules expiring within a given timeframe.

If null, the search does not apply an upper bound to `ends_at`.

reason_query.description:
Optional free-text search filter applied to the rule reason field.

This string can be used with full-text or partial matching over the `reason` column, allowing administrators to locate rules associated with a particular campaign, incident, or policy keyword.

When null, the search does not constrain results based on the textual contents of the reason field.

IShoppingMallCatalogVisibilityRule.ICrea.description:
Creation DTO for catalog visibility rules in the shopping mall platform.

This type represents the input payload used by administrators when defining a new visibility rule that controls which products or SKUs are visible to which actors under which conditions. It maps to the shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules primary table but intentionally excludes system-managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

Each rule can optionally target a specific seller, product, or SKU via foreign key identifiers and can further constrain visibility by rule type, actor type, region, and temporal validity window. The DTO is designed so that the backend can safely associate the creating admin using the authenticated context rather than accepting admin identifiers from the client.

rule_type.description:
Type of the visibility rule, such as hide, show_only_to_registered, or region_restricted.

This value determines the behavioral semantics of the rule when the catalog engine evaluates whether a product or SKU should be visible to a given actor. Implementations should validate this against the allowed rule categories configured for the platform.

actor_type.description:
Optional actor type the rule targets, for example guestUser, customer, seller, or admin.

When provided, the rule only applies to actors of the specified type. When null, the rule is considered actor-agnostic and may apply to all relevant actors depending on other rule dimensions.

region_code.description:
Optional region or market code used when the visibility rule is region-specific.

If supplied, the rule constrains visibility based on geographic or logical region, allowing different catalog exposure policies across markets.

enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether this visibility rule is currently active.

When true, the rule participates in catalog visibility evaluation. When false, the rule is effectively disabled but retained for audit history and potential future reactivation.

starts_at.description:
Optional timestamp from which the rule becomes effective, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

If null, the rule is considered effective immediately upon creation. Implementations should ensure that, when both starts_at and ends_at are present, starts_at is earlier than or equal to ends_at.

ends_at.description:
Optional timestamp after which the rule no longer applies, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

If null, the rule has no explicit end date and will remain effective until disabled or soft-deleted. Service logic may still impose additional lifecycle constraints depending on governance policy.

reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of why this visibility rule exists.

This field is primarily used for governance, auditing, and administrative UI displays so that operators can quickly understand the intent behind each rule.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Optional UUID identifier of the seller that this rule applies to, when the rule is seller-scoped.

When provided, the rule affects catalog visibility for items associated with the specified seller. When null, the rule is not limited to a specific seller.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Optional UUID identifier of the product that this rule targets, when the rule is product-specific.

If present, the rule applies to the designated product and potentially its SKUs, depending on how the visibility engine interprets product-level rules.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Optional UUID identifier of the SKU that this rule targets, when the rule is SKU-specific.

When provided, the rule narrowly focuses on a particular SKU variant within the catalog. This allows fine-grained control over visibility at the SKU level apart from broader product or seller rules.

IShoppingMallCatalogVisibilityRule.IUpda.description:
Update DTO for existing catalog visibility rules in the shopping mall platform.

This type is used by administrative operations that modify visibility rule records already stored in the shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules table. It exposes only mutable business fields and omits system-managed values such as id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, and the creating admin identifier.

All properties are optional to support partial updates, allowing administrators to adjust specific aspects of a rule—such as its enabled state, actor targeting, region scope, temporal window, or descriptive reason—without resubmitting the entire rule definition.

rule_type.description:
Updated type of the visibility rule, such as hide, show_only_to_registered, or region_restricted.

If supplied, this replaces the existing rule_type and may change how the rule participates in catalog visibility calculations. Implementations should validate the new value against the allowed rule categories.

actor_type.description:
Updated actor type that the rule targets, for example guestUser, customer, seller, or admin.

Setting this to a non-null value narrows the rule to the specified actor group, while explicitly setting it to null removes any actor-type constraint so the rule can apply more broadly.

region_code.description:
Updated region or market code for region-specific visibility behavior.

Providing a non-null value constrains the rule to a particular region, whereas setting it to null removes the region-specific limitation.

enabled.description:
Updated enabled flag indicating whether the rule should be active after the modification.

Toggling this flag is the primary way administrators can temporarily disable or re-enable a visibility rule without deleting it.

starts_at.description:
Updated start timestamp from which the rule becomes effective, using ISO 8601 date-time format.

This can be provided to adjust when the rule begins to apply or explicitly set to null to make the rule effective without a formal start boundary. Service logic should continue to enforce that starts_at is not later than ends_at when both are present.

ends_at.description:
Updated end timestamp after which the rule no longer applies, using ISO 8601 date-time format.

Administrators can use this to schedule rule sunset dates or clear the end boundary by setting it to null so that the rule remains in effect indefinitely until disabled or deleted.

reason.description:
Updated human-readable reason explaining why this visibility rule exists or why it has been changed.

Useful for audit logs and administrative user interfaces to give operators clear context for the rule and its lifecycle history.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Updated UUID identifier of the seller to which this rule should be scoped, if any.

Changing this value re-scopes the rule to a different seller or clears the seller-specific constraint when explicitly set to null. Implementations must ensure that the referenced seller exists and that re-scoping complies with governance policies.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Updated UUID identifier of the product that this rule targets, if any.

Admins can adjust this to move the rule to a different product or remove the product-level constraint by setting it to null. Service logic should verify that the product exists and is compatible with other rule dimensions.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Updated UUID identifier of the SKU that this rule targets, if any.

This allows finely re-scoping the rule to a specific SKU variant or clearing the SKU-specific constraint when set to null. The implementation should validate that any non-null SKU identifier refers to an existing SKU linked to the associated product and seller as expected.

IShoppingMallCatalogSearchAttributeFilte.description:
Attribute-based facet filter used as part of advanced catalog search requests.

Each instance describes a filter on a single logical attribute, identified either by a human-readable key or by a stable attribute identifier, and one or more allowed values selected by the user.

The filter constrains the search results such that only products or SKUs matching the specified attribute values are considered. This enables rich faceted navigation experiences where shoppers refine results using checkboxes and chips for attributes like size, color, or material.

This DTO does not directly map to a Prisma model, but conceptually interacts with product-level attribute definitions in shopping_mall_product_attributes and allowed values in shopping_mall_product_attribute_values when the search engine interprets it.

attributeKey.description:
Logical key of the attribute to filter on.

This key corresponds to a semantic identifier used by the catalog search engine to map the filter to an underlying product attribute definition. Examples include "color", "size", "material", or domain-specific attribute names.

Clients should use stable keys defined by the catalog configuration instead of free-form strings to ensure consistent behavior across searches and to avoid filters that cannot be resolved on the backend.

items.description:
Identifier of an allowed attribute value to include in the filter.

These IDs typically correspond to records in shopping_mall_product_attribute_values or an equivalent value table that enumerates discrete options for the attribute. Each value represents a single selectable facet, such as a specific color or size.

When multiple values are provided for a single attribute, entries that match any of the listed values should be considered a match for that attribute filter.

attributeValueIds.description:
List of selected attribute value identifiers used to constrain search results.

Within a single filter, multiple values are combined with OR semantics, meaning that catalog entries must match at least one of the values to satisfy this attribute constraint.

Across different attribute filters in the `attributeFilters` collection, constraints are typically combined with AND semantics so that results must satisfy all active attribute filters simultaneously. This structure allows clients to express rich combinations of attribute facets while keeping the request payload compact and machine-friendly.

IShoppingMallCatalogSearchSort.description:
Sorting configuration for advanced catalog search requests.

This DTO captures the primary field to sort by and the direction of sorting, such as relevance, creation time, price, or popularity. Encapsulating sort in a dedicated object allows the API to evolve to support more sophisticated multi-field sorting strategies without breaking existing clients.

While not directly backed by a Prisma model, the selected sort key and direction influence how queries are constructed against shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries and related tables like shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_skus, and rating aggregates.

field.description:
Logical field indicating which aspect of the catalog entries to sort by.

Common values include:

- "relevance": Sort by search engine score based on the query and index configuration.
- "newest": Sort by product or SKU creation time to surface the latest additions.
- "price_asc": Sort by current effective price ascending.
- "price_desc": Sort by current effective price descending.
- "popularity": Sort by popularity measures such as sales volume or view counts.
- "rating": Sort by average rating derived from aggregates.

The backend should validate supplied values against supported sort modes and fall back to a default such as "relevance" when an unsupported value is provided.

oneOf.description:
Direction of sorting for sortable fields that support both ascending and descending orders.

Allowed values are:

- "asc": Sort in ascending order.
- "desc": Sort in descending order.

For semantic fields like "relevance" or "popularity" where only a single natural direction exists, the backend may ignore this field or treat a missing value as an instruction to use the default direction. To reduce ambiguity, clients should always send a direction for fields where both orders are meaningful, particularly for numeric fields like price or creation time.

Direction of sorting for sortable fields that support both ascending and descending orders.

Allowed values are:

- "asc": Sort in ascending order.
- "desc": Sort in descending order.

For semantic fields like "relevance" or "popularity" where only a single natural direction exists, the backend may ignore this field or treat a missing value as an instruction to use the default direction. To reduce ambiguity, clients should always send a direction for fields where both orders are meaningful, particularly for numeric fields like price or creation time.

direction.description:
Direction of sorting for sortable fields that support both ascending and descending orders.

Allowed values are:

- "asc": Sort in ascending order.
- "desc": Sort in descending order.

For semantic fields like "relevance" or "popularity" where only a single natural direction exists, the backend may ignore this field or treat a missing value as an instruction to use the default direction. To reduce ambiguity, clients should always send a direction for fields where both orders are meaningful, particularly for numeric fields like price or creation time.

IShoppingMallCatalogSearchIndexEntry.IRe.description:
Request DTO capturing advanced catalog search criteria for the shoppingMall storefront.

This structure models the high-level search query, faceted filters, sorting options, and pagination parameters that clients send to perform catalog searches across products and SKUs. It is conceptually backed by the denormalized search index stored in shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries and related catalog entities such as shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_skus, categories, tags, and rating aggregates.

The DTO is designed to support common e‑commerce search experiences including free-text keyword search, category and tag filtering, price ranges, attribute-based facet selections, seller filters, and various sort orders like relevance, newest, price ascending/descending, and popularity.

It also contains locale and regional hints so the backend can choose appropriate localized text and enforce catalog visibility policies per region and language. Implementations may additionally interpret caller context such as inferred country or authenticated user, but this context is outside the scope of the request body itself.

query.description:
Free-text search query string entered by the user.

This value is typically tokenized and matched against the denormalized search_text field in shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries, which aggregates product and SKU titles, summaries, tags, and attribute labels.

Implementations should apply full-text search semantics such as stemming, language-specific analyzers, and relevance scoring based on this query. Clients should trim leading and trailing whitespace before sending and avoid excessively long strings; the API enforces a maximum length to prevent abuse and overly expensive queries.

items.description:
Identifier of a catalog category used for filtering.

These IDs correspond to records in shopping_mall_categories or related category closure tables that define the catalog taxonomy. When supplied, the search should restrict results to products and SKUs that are associated with at least one of the specified categories via linkage tables such as shopping_mall_product_categories.

Backends may expand these IDs to include descendants based on category_closures if the search should include subcategories.

categoryIds.description:
List of category identifiers to filter search results.

When present, the search should only return catalog entries belonging to one or more of the specified categories. This enables faceted navigation flows where users narrow the product set by selecting categories from the taxonomy tree.

If omitted, the search is not constrained by category membership and may return products from any category, subject to other filters and catalog visibility rules.

items.description:
Identifier of a product tag used as a search facet.

These IDs correspond to tag records in shopping_mall_product_tags that represent semantic labels like "eco-friendly", "bestseller", or campaign-specific tags. Products are linked to tags through shopping_mall_product_tag_links.

Filtering by tag limits results to products or SKUs associated with at least one of these tags.

tagIds.description:
List of tag identifiers to constrain search results.

This facet allows clients to filter products based on curated tag sets, such as promotional campaigns or thematic collections. When provided, only entries whose underlying products are linked to at least one of the tags will be eligible for inclusion in the result set.

If omitted, tag-based filtering is not applied and results are governed by other criteria such as categories, price ranges, and attributes.

items.description:
Identifier of a seller whose catalog entries should be included.

These values correspond to primary keys in shopping_mall_sellers and represent merchant accounts on the marketplace. When used as a filter, only products and SKUs owned by these sellers will be considered by the search.

This facet is useful for building seller-specific storefronts and views in multi-seller marketplaces.

sellerIds.description:
Optional filter restricting results to catalog entries belonging to specific sellers.

When set, the search engine should limit results to products and SKUs whose owning seller is in the provided list. This supports scenarios like browsing a particular seller’s storefront or applying seller-based refinements alongside other facets.

If omitted, results may include items from any seller, subject to visibility rules and other constraints.

minPrice.description:
Lower bound of the price range filter expressed in the platform’s base currency.

When provided together with maxPrice, the search should only return SKUs whose current effective selling price falls within the inclusive [minPrice, maxPrice] interval. If provided alone, it acts as a minimum price threshold with no explicit upper bound.

The field is optional so that callers can omit price constraints entirely or only constrain one side of the range.

maxPrice.description:
Upper bound of the price range filter expressed in the platform’s base currency.

When supplied together with minPrice, the search should only return SKUs priced at or below this value while also respecting the lower bound. If sent alone, it acts as an exclusive upper bound while allowing any non-negative minimum.

Implementations should validate that maxPrice is not lower than minPrice when both are provided and return a validation error via the platform’s standard error envelope if the range is invalid.

onlyInStock.description:
Flag indicating whether the search should restrict results to SKUs that are currently in stock.

When true, the backend should filter out entries whose underlying SKU inventory state or inventory_quantity indicates that the item is not purchasable, for example due to zero quantity or an inventory state representing out_of_stock.

When false or omitted, the search may include out-of-stock items depending on business rules, which can be useful for browsing but less suitable for purchase-intent views.

items.description:
Individual attribute filter describing a single facet on a particular attribute and selected values.

Each filter corresponds conceptually to a product attribute definition in shopping_mall_product_attributes and one or more selected allowed values from shopping_mall_product_attribute_values. By combining multiple attribute filters, clients can express variant-level constraints such as size, color, material, or other product-specific facets.

attributeFilters.description:
Collection of structured attribute-based facet filters.

These filters allow clients to constrain search results based on product or SKU attributes such as size, color, material, or technical characteristics. Each entry describes a single attribute and one or more allowed values, and multiple filters are combined conjunctively so that resulting entries must satisfy all active attribute constraints.

This mechanism is essential for supporting rich faceted navigation in large catalogs where users refine results using attribute pickers and checkboxes.

sort.description:
Sorting configuration determining result ordering.

This object encapsulates the primary sort key and direction to apply to the search result set. Typical choices include relevance (score-based), newest arrivals, price ascending or descending, popularity, or rating-based ordering.

When not provided, the backend should default to relevance or another sensible platform-wide default. By modeling sort as an object rather than separate scalar fields, the API can evolve to support more complex multi-field sorting strategies while keeping the contract coherent.

page.description:
One-based index of the results page to retrieve.

This parameter, combined with pageSize, controls pagination over the full result set. A value of 1 refers to the first page of results, while higher values retrieve subsequent pages.

Implementations should enforce upper bounds on page to prevent excessively deep pagination that could lead to poor performance or stale results. Clients are expected to maintain their own pagination state and adjust this value as users navigate through pages of search results.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of results to return in a single page.

This parameter constrains the size of the data array in the paginated response. The API enforces a reasonable upper limit, such as 100, to balance flexibility for clients against performance and resource considerations on the backend.

If omitted, the server should apply a sensible default page size appropriate for common listing views, such as 20 items, and may cap overly large client-specified values down to the maximum.

locale.description:
Preferred locale for localized catalog content represented as an IETF language tag, such as "en-US" or "ko-KR".

The backend uses this hint when selecting localized titles, summaries, and other content from tables like shopping_mall_product_localizations. When a localization for the requested locale is unavailable, the system may fall back to the product’s default_locale defined in shopping_mall_products.

Including the locale also allows the search engine to apply locale-specific analyzers and ranking strategies for full-text search, improving relevance for different languages.

regionCode.description:
Code identifying the shopper’s logical or geographic region for catalog visibility and availability decisions.

This value typically corresponds to a record in shopping_mall_regions or may be derived from the combination of country, state, and other context. It allows the backend to apply region-specific shipping policies, catalog visibility rules, or regulatory restrictions when selecting which products and SKUs to include in the search results.

If omitted, the system may infer region from other context such as IP geolocation or account settings, but providing an explicit regionCode yields more predictable behavior in distributed client applications.

IShoppingMallCatalogSearchIndexEntry.description:
Detailed representation of a single catalog search index entry used by the shoppingMall platform's catalog search engine.

This DTO mirrors the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` Prisma model and exposes the denormalized text and scoring data that power full‑text search over products and SKUs. It is primarily consumed by administrative tools and diagnostic workflows rather than end‑user applications.

Each record may reference either a product, a SKU, or both, and carries locale‑specific normalized search text along with a boost score and lifecycle timestamps for index maintenance and soft deletion. For administrative convenience, minimal product and SKU summaries are embedded instead of raw foreign key identifiers.

id.description:
Primary key of the catalog search index entry.

This value corresponds directly to `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.id` in the database and uniquely identifies a single index row used by the search engine.

locale.description:
Locale code of the indexed content, such as `en-US` or `ko-KR`.

This field mirrors `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.locale` and determines which language and regional settings the `search_text` was prepared for.

search_text.description:
Concatenated and normalized text used by the search engine for full‑text queries.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.search_text` and typically aggregates product titles, summaries, attribute labels, tags, and other search‑relevant text for the associated product or SKU.

boost_score.description:
Precomputed numeric boost score that influences ranking for this index entry.

This value mirrors `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.boost_score` and is used by the search layer to bias results based on factors such as popularity, recency, or business rules.

product.description:
Optional minimal product summary associated with this search index entry.

When the underlying Prisma column `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.shopping_mall_product_id` is non‑null, this property contains an `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary` representation of that product for quick administrative inspection. When the index entry is SKU‑only or the product reference is absent, this field is null.

sku.description:
Optional minimal SKU summary associated with this search index entry.

When the underlying Prisma column `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.shopping_mall_sku_id` is non‑null, this property contains an `IShoppingMallSku.ISummary` representation of that SKU, allowing administrators to understand which concrete variant the index row represents. When the entry is product‑only or the SKU reference is absent, this field is null.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this index entry was initially created or last fully rebuilt.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.created_at` and is recorded in ISO 8601 date‑time format.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when non‑structural metadata for this index entry was last updated.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.updated_at` and typically reflects maintenance operations on the index row rather than changes to the underlying product or SKU.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when this index entry was soft‑deleted, if applicable.

This property mirrors `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries.deleted_at`. A null value indicates the entry is currently active in the index, while a non‑null value means it has been logically removed but may still exist in storage for audit or recovery purposes.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request parameters for querying catalog block reasons in the shoppingMall admin context.

This DTO is used by the PATCH `/shoppingMall/admin/catalogBlockReasons` endpoint to express complex search criteria, pagination, and ordering when listing records from the `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons` Prisma model. It allows administrative clients to control which block reasons are returned without modifying any underlying data.

Typical filters include free‑text search over the human‑readable name or description, severity‑level filtering, and activation or soft‑deletion awareness. Pagination parameters prevent unbounded result sets in admin tooling, and sort options allow consistent ordering in list views.

page.description:
Zero‑based page index used for paginating block reason results.

Clients use this field together with `limit` to page through records from `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons`. When omitted, implementations commonly default to the first page (index 0).

limit.description:
Maximum number of catalog block reason records to return in a single page.

This value constrains the size of the result set produced from `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons`. Servers should enforce an upper bound to protect performance even if the client supplies a large number.

search.description:
Optional free‑text search expression applied to catalog block reasons.

Implementations typically match this value against fields such as `code`, `name`, or `description` of the `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons` table to help administrators quickly find relevant reasons.

severity_levels.description:
Optional list of severity levels to filter catalog block reasons by.

Values in this array are matched against `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.severity_level`, which may contain business classifications such as `low`, `medium`, or `high` as described in the Prisma schema.

include_deleted.description:
Flag indicating whether soft‑deleted catalog block reasons should be included in the result set.

When `true`, records with a non‑null `deleted_at` in `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons` may be returned for audit or historical inspection. When `false` or omitted, only non‑deleted block reasons are typically listed.

order_by.description:
Optional field name used for sorting catalog block reasons in the result list.

Typical values might reference sortable columns on `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons`, such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, `code`, or `severity_level`. Implementations should validate and restrict this to a safe subset of allowed fields.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction for the `order_by` field, such as `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending order.

When omitted, a sensible default ordering should be applied by the server, often descending by `created_at` or another primary audit field.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a catalog block reason definition used in admin consoles, governance tools, and reporting.

This DTO exposes the core identifying and classification fields for a block reason so that operators can understand why a catalog entity has been blocked without loading the full detailed record. It is directly backed by the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons Prisma model, which defines id, code, name, optional description, severity_level, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at columns used for governance configuration.

The summary intentionally focuses on stable identifiers, severity classification, and audit timestamps. It omits the potentially longer free-form description field to keep list views compact, while still including deleted_at as an optional soft-delete timestamp so that UIs and reports can distinguish between active and logically retired block reasons at a glance.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the catalog block reason.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.id and is a server-generated UUID used to reference a specific reusable block reason configuration in governance rules, catalog visibility logic, and reporting.

code.description:
Machine-readable code representing the catalog block reason.

This value maps to shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.code and is typically a stable identifier such as "policy_violation", "legal_request", or "counterfeit_suspected" used in governance rules, integrations, and analytics. The Prisma model enforces a unique index on this column so that each code can be safely referenced without ambiguity in configuration and reporting flows.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the block reason suitable for display in admin user interfaces.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.name and provides a concise label that explains the nature of the block reason to operational staff and moderators. List and search results commonly show this name together with the code and severity level.

severity_level.description:
Business-level severity classification for this block reason, such as "low", "medium", or "high".

This field maps to shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.severity_level and is used in risk and compliance reporting to group and filter block reasons by impact level or urgency. The Prisma schema defines a plain index on this column so that analytics and list endpoints can efficiently filter and aggregate by severity level across large datasets.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the block reason record was created.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.created_at and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format, supporting auditing of when a particular reason was introduced into the system and enabling time-based reporting over the lifecycle of governance configuration.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the block reason record was last updated.

This maps to shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.updated_at and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. It reflects the most recent change to the reason's code, name, severity classification, or descriptive guidance so that operators and auditors can see how recently a configuration was reviewed or modified.

deleted_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when this block reason was soft-deleted, if applicable.

This property corresponds to the nullable shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.deleted_at column. It is null for active reasons that are still available for new enforcement actions. When non-null, it records the date and time at which the reason was logically retired from active use while remaining available for historical reporting and for interpreting past catalog visibility decisions.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.description:
Represents a single catalog block reason configuration record stored in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table.

Each record describes a reusable business-level reason, such as policy_violation, legal_request, counterfeit_suspected, or safety_issue, that explains why catalog entities like products or SKUs are blocked or removed from sale in the shoppingMall platform.

This entity is treated as primary reference data for governance and moderation flows. It is referenced by catalog visibility rules, moderation decisions, refund and dispute workflows, and internal reporting dashboards.

The schema mirrors the underlying Prisma model fields exactly, including the UUID primary key, unique machine-readable code, human-readable name, optional long-form description, severity classification, and audit timestamps including soft-delete information.

Read operations such as GET /shoppingMall/admin/catalogBlockReasons/{catalogBlockReasonId} return this type to admin tools and internal services that need the complete semantics of a given block reason record.

id.description:
Primary key identifier of the catalog block reason.

This UUID value corresponds to the id column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and uniquely identifies a single block reason configuration across the platform.

Admin-facing APIs such as GET /shoppingMall/admin/catalogBlockReasons/{catalogBlockReasonId} and PUT /shoppingMall/admin/catalogBlockReasons/{catalogBlockReasonId} use this value in their path parameters to select the target record.

code.description:
Machine-readable code representing the catalog block reason.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable code column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and is constrained by a unique index at the database level.

Codes are short, stable identifiers such as policy_violation, legal_request, counterfeit_suspected, or safety_issue that can be referenced by catalog visibility rules, moderation workflows, and reporting logic.

Because code is unique, it can also be used as an alternative lookup key in internal services and batch processes.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the catalog block reason.

This field maps to the non-nullable name column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and provides the label shown in administrative consoles and governance tools.

The name should be concise but descriptive enough that operators can quickly understand the intent of the block reason when selecting it from dropdowns or reviewing historical decisions.

description.description:
Optional long-form description explaining when this block reason should be used.

This property corresponds to the nullable description column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons. When present, it provides detailed guidance for admins and moderators about appropriate usage, edge cases, and any related policy links.

When null, only the name and code fields are available to describe the reason, and UIs should handle the absence of a detailed description gracefully.

severity_level.description:
Business-level severity classification of the block reason.

This field maps to the non-nullable severity_level column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons. It is modeled as a free-form string in the Prisma schema but is typically constrained at the business layer to a finite set of values such as low, medium, or high.

A plain index exists on severity_level to support filtering and aggregation in governance and risk reports. Admin tools may use this value to group reasons by severity or to highlight high-impact reasons in dashboards.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the catalog block reason record was created.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable created_at column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and is usually assigned automatically by the backend when a new reason is inserted.

The value is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string and is used for auditing, change tracking, and temporal reporting on when specific block reasons were introduced into the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the catalog block reason record was last updated.

This field maps to the non-nullable updated_at column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and is updated whenever mutable fields such as name, description, or severity_level are changed by administrators.

Admin tools and audit logs use this timestamp to show when configuration was last reviewed or modified, which is important for compliance and governance processes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete timestamp indicating when the block reason was logically retired, if applicable.

This property corresponds to the nullable deleted_at column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons. When non-null, it indicates the reason has been deactivated or logically removed from normal use but is still retained for historical reporting and referential integrity.

Application logic and admin UIs should treat non-null deleted_at values as a signal that the reason should no longer be offered for new enforcement decisions, while still showing it in historical records where it was previously applied.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.ICreate.description:
Request body structure for creating a new catalog block reason record in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table.

This DTO is consumed by the POST /shoppingMall/admin/catalogBlockReasons operation and represents the administrative input required to register a reusable reason code that can explain why catalog entities such as products or SKUs are blocked or removed from sale.

The structure intentionally omits system-managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The backend is responsible for generating the UUID primary key and audit timestamps and for initializing deleted_at as null for active reasons.

Business validation should enforce that the code value is unique across all existing records and that severity_level matches allowed classifications such as low, medium, or high as defined by platform policy.

code.description:
Machine-readable code for the new catalog block reason.

This value will be stored in the non-nullable code column of shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and must be unique across all records, as enforced by a unique index in the Prisma schema.

Typical examples include policy_violation, legal_request, counterfeit_suspected, or safety_issue. Admin tools should guide operators to choose codes that are stable and descriptive, since they are referenced by governance logic and reports.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the new catalog block reason.

This property maps to the non-nullable name column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and will be displayed in administrative UIs, moderation tools, and reporting dashboards.

Names should be concise but sufficiently descriptive so that admins and moderators can easily select the appropriate reason during enforcement workflows.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of the new catalog block reason.

When provided, this text will be stored in the nullable description column of shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and can include policy references, usage guidance, and clarifications about applicable scenarios.

If omitted or set to null, downstream tools will rely on the name and code fields alone to describe the reason.

severity_level.description:
Severity classification for the new catalog block reason.

This field is written to the non-nullable severity_level column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons. Although the Prisma schema models it as a generic string, business rules typically restrict it to values such as low, medium, or high to support risk reporting and prioritization.

Validation in the create handler should enforce the allowed set of severity levels and reject values that do not conform to platform policy to keep reporting and governance logic consistent.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReason.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing catalog block reason stored in the shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons table.

This type is used exclusively by administrative governance tools to adjust mutable metadata of a block reason, such as its human‑readable name, machine‑readable code, descriptive explanation, or severity classification.

Only fields that are conceptually editable by admins are exposed here. System‑managed identifiers and timestamps remain immutable and are therefore excluded from this DTO.

code.description:
Machine‑readable code representing the block reason, such as policy_violation or legal_request.

This value is used as a stable identifier in configuration, reporting, and integration points. It must be unique across all rows in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons due to the unique index on the code column, but in this update DTO it is optional so that callers can choose whether to change it.

When provided, implementations must validate that the new code does not conflict with an existing record and respects any additional business naming rules.

name.description:
Human‑readable name of the block reason displayed in administrative tools.

Admins typically use this field as the primary label in dropdowns, search results, and detail pages. It should be concise but descriptive enough so that reviewers can quickly understand the purpose of the reason.

When updating, changes to this field should be immediately reflected in governance and catalog quality UIs.

oneOf.description:
Updated detailed description of when this block reason should be used.

This free‑form text can contain policy references, examples, or operational guidance that helps admins apply the reason consistently.

When present, the value overwrites the existing description in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.description.
Explicitly clear the existing detailed description so that the block reason no longer has any extended explanatory text associated with it.

description.description:
Optional updated detailed description of when this block reason should be used.

This field maps directly to the nullable description column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and supports both setting a new explanation and clearing an existing one by passing null.

Clients should include this property only when they intend to modify the description; omitting it leaves the current value unchanged.

severity_level.description:
Updated business‑level severity classification for this block reason, such as low, medium, or high.

The value maps to the severity_level column in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons and is used by reporting and risk dashboards to prioritize enforcement activity.

Implementations may enforce an allowed set of values at the service layer even though the underlying column is stored as a string.

IShoppingMallCatalogOverview.description:
Aggregated catalog overview DTO for the ShoppingMall platform.

This type is a denormalized, read‑only projection that synthesizes information from multiple catalog‑related Prisma models such as shopping_mall_categories, shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_skus, shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules, and rating aggregate tables. It is designed to power landing pages and dashboard widgets that need a single call to understand the overall state of the catalog.

The overview focuses on high‑level counts, health indicators, and structural hints rather than exposing raw table rows. It is safe to return to anonymous clients as long as the underlying query layer respects catalog visibility rules and excludes blocked or restricted entities for public actors.

totalCategoryCount.description:
Total number of non‑deleted categories currently defined in the shopping_mall_categories taxonomy.

This count helps clients display overall catalog breadth and can be used for monitoring taxonomy growth over time.

The implementation should typically exclude categories that are soft‑deleted via the deleted_at column, but may include hidden or deprecated categories if business rules require them to remain countable for analytics.

activeProductCount.description:
Number of products in shopping_mall_products that are currently active and eligible for display under standard catalog visibility rules.

This value is computed by filtering products on their status column (for example, status = 'active') and applying any additional governance constraints such as visibility rules or legal holds.

Clients can use this field to show how many products are available for browsing in the marketplace at a given moment.

activeSkuCount.description:
Number of SKUs in shopping_mall_skus that are currently active and considered sellable.

The exact definition of "active" should align with status and inventory semantics—for example, status = 'active' and a non‑negative inventory_quantity combined with a non‑blocking inventory state.

This count provides a lower‑level view of catalog depth than activeProductCount, since each product may expose multiple SKUs.

topLevelCategoryCount.description:
Number of root‑level categories in the shopping_mall_categories hierarchy where parent_id is null.

This value is useful for summarizing how many major entry points exist in the navigation tree shown to customers.

Implementations usually exclude soft‑deleted categories from this count but may still consider hidden or deprecated categories based on business rules.

oneOf.description:
Global average rating across all products that have at least one included review, typically in the 0.0–5.0 range.

This value is usually derived from the average_rating column in shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates and represents a coarse indicator of overall catalog quality from a customer perspective.

Rounding behavior and whether unrated products are included or excluded should be documented at the API level.
Indicates that no rating information is available—either because no reviews exist yet or rating aggregation has not been computed.

averageProductRating.description:
Optional global average rating across all products that have review data.

The value, when present, is typically computed using pre‑aggregated averages from shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates to avoid scanning individual reviews.

Clients should treat null as "no rating data available" rather than as a numeric zero.

visibleProductCountForGuests.description:
Number of products that are visible to unauthenticated guest users after applying catalog visibility rules and block reasons.

This count is a subset of activeProductCount and takes into account rule rows in shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules as well as any catalog block reasons and governance decisions that remove items from the public catalog.

Public landing pages can use this to show how many items a first‑time visitor can browse without signing in.

visibilityRuleCount.description:
Total number of visibility rules currently stored in shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules regardless of their enabled state.

This metric indicates how much governance configuration exists around catalog exposure—for example, seller‑specific restrictions, region‑based rules, and actor‑specific access controls.

More detailed rule data should be obtained via dedicated administrative endpoints rather than through this high‑level overview.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the overview snapshot was last computed or refreshed.

This value allows clients and monitoring tools to understand the recency of the aggregated metrics and detect stale data if background jobs fail.

The timestamp should be expressed in ISO 8601 date‑time format with timezone information, typically in UTC.

IShoppingMallProductAvailabilityStatisti.description:
Aggregated, computed product availability statistics for the ShoppingMall catalog.

This schema represents analytical metrics derived from inventory and visibility data across products and SKUs, such as how many SKUs are available, low in stock, out of stock, or otherwise constrained. It is not directly mapped to a single Prisma table; instead, it is a read-only, computed view used for dashboards and reporting.

totalProducts.description: Total number of distinct products in the catalog that are considered in this availability computation after applying catalog visibility and governance rules.

totalSkus.description: Total number of distinct SKUs (stock keeping units) included in the availability computation after applying catalog visibility and governance rules.

availableSkuCount.description: Number of SKUs currently considered fully available for sale (in stock and visible in the catalog according to visibility rules).

lowStockSkuCount.description: Number of SKUs that are technically available but classified as low stock based on configured inventory thresholds (for example, inventory below a business-defined warning level).

outOfStockSkuCount.description: Number of SKUs that are currently out of stock and therefore not sellable, even if they may still be visible for informational purposes depending on catalog visibility configuration.

blockedOrHiddenSkuCount.description: Number of SKUs that are currently blocked, hidden, or otherwise unavailable for sale due to catalog visibility rules, risk flags, legal holds, or policy overrides.

availabilityByState.description: Breakdown of SKU counts and ratios per logical inventory state (for example, AVAILABLE, LOW_STOCK, OUT_OF_STOCK), aligned with semantics defined in inventory-state configuration.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when these availability statistics were last computed or refreshed.

IShoppingMallProductAvailabilityByState.description:
Aggregated availability metrics for a single logical inventory state.

Each instance describes how many SKUs fall into a particular inventory state (such as AVAILABLE, LOW_STOCK, OUT_OF_STOCK, or other custom states defined by business configuration) and the relative ratio of that state compared to all considered SKUs.

stateCode.description: Machine-readable code of the inventory state (for example, AVAILABLE, LOW_STOCK, OUT_OF_STOCK, BLOCKED), matching the configured inventory state identifiers used by the inventory system.

label.description: Human-readable label for the inventory state intended for display in dashboards or reports.

skuCount.description: Number of SKUs that are currently classified into this inventory state.

skuRatio.description: Proportion of SKUs in this inventory state relative to all SKUs considered in the computation, expressed as a value between 0 and 1.

IShoppingMallCatalogTopSellingSkuStatist.description:
Request parameters for computing top-selling SKU statistics on the shoppingMall platform.

Allows callers to specify the analysis window, maximum number of SKUs to return, and optional filters such as seller or category constraints. All fields are optional; when omitted, the implementation applies sensible defaults (for example, a default time range and a default maximum result count).

startDate.description: Inclusive start of the analysis window in ISO 8601 date-time format. When omitted, the service may default to a preconfigured period such as the last 7 days.

endDate.description: Exclusive end of the analysis window in ISO 8601 date-time format. When omitted, the service may default to the current time or a preconfigured period end.

periodPreset.description: Optional preset identifier for common analysis windows. Typical values might include "last_7_days", "last_30_days", or "last_90_days". When provided, it may override explicit startDate and endDate depending on implementation rules.

limit.description: Maximum number of top-selling SKUs to return. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets.

sellerId.description: Optional filter limiting statistics to SKUs owned by a specific seller.

categoryId.description: Optional filter limiting statistics to SKUs whose products belong to a specific catalog category.

IShoppingMallCatalogTopSellingSkuStatist.description:
Aggregated statistics for top-selling SKUs on the shoppingMall platform.

Represents a ranked list of SKU-level performance metrics over a specified analysis window. Each entry summarizes how a particular SKU has performed in terms of units sold, revenue contribution, pricing, and share of overall sales. Intended for admin-facing dashboards, internal analytics surfaces, and reporting tools.

This schema does not map directly to a single Prisma table; instead, it is computed from order and SKU related models such as shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_skus, and optionally snapshot tables like shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.

items.description: Ranked list of top-selling SKU statistics matching the specified analysis criteria. The array is ordered in descending order of sales performance (for example, by total units sold or total revenue).

IShoppingMallCatalogTopSellingSkuStatist.description:
Single SKU-level statistics entry in the top-selling SKU rankings.

Provides associated SKU, product, and seller summaries along with aggregated performance metrics over the requested analysis period. Designed for use in admin analytics dashboards, catalog performance views, and seller reporting surfaces.

Association fields reuse core `.ISummary` DTOs so that analytics clients receive enough context to render informative tables and visualizations without issuing additional detail fetches for each SKU, product, or seller.

sku.description:
Summary information for the SKU whose performance is being summarized.

Provides the primary identifier and key catalog attributes (such as SKU code, label, and possibly thumbnail or status) so that analytics dashboards can clearly identify the variant without extra API calls.

product.description:
Summary information for the product that owns this SKU.

Supplies human-readable product details such as name and primary imagery, enabling analytics and catalog performance views to group or interpret SKU-level metrics at the product level.

seller.description:
Summary information for the seller that owns this SKU.

Provides seller identity and display attributes (for example, name and basic KPIs) so that dashboards can segment and compare top-selling SKUs by seller without separate lookups.

totalUnitsSold.description:
Total number of units of this SKU sold during the specified analysis window.

Represents the absolute quantity sold and is typically used as the primary ranking criterion for top-selling lists when focusing on volume rather than revenue.

totalRevenue.description:
Total revenue generated by this SKU during the analysis window, expressed in the platform’s base currency (for example, USD).

This metric is computed as the sum of line-level extended prices for all order items referring to the SKU within the analysis period.

averageUnitPrice.description:
Average selling price per unit for this SKU over the analysis window.

Typically computed as `totalRevenue / totalUnitsSold` when at least one unit has been sold. When no units were sold, implementations should treat this value as 0 or omit the SKU from the result set entirely.

shareOfUnits.description:
Proportion of this SKU’s units sold relative to total units sold across all SKUs in the analysis window.

Expressed as a fractional value between 0 and 1. For example, a value of 0.25 indicates that this SKU accounts for 25% of all units sold in the selected period.

shareOfRevenue.description:
Proportion of this SKU’s revenue relative to total revenue across all SKUs in the analysis window.

Expressed as a fractional value between 0 and 1. For example, a value of 0.10 indicates that this SKU contributes 10% of total revenue in the selected period.

rank.description:
Rank of this SKU within the result set for the selected analysis criteria.

A value of 1 represents the highest-performing SKU under the applied sort metric (for example, highest `totalUnitsSold` or `totalRevenue`), with larger integers representing lower ranks.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReasonBreakdown.description:
Request parameters for computing catalog block reason breakdown statistics in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by administrator-facing analytics and governance tools to describe how the server should aggregate statistics about why products and SKUs are blocked from the catalog. It encapsulates the time window, seller and category scope, inclusion of historical blocks, grouping strategy, and pagination hints that drive the shape and volume of the resulting analytics data.

The request does not map directly to a single Prisma table. Instead, the implementation typically joins reference data such as `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons` with catalog visibility or block linkage tables, product and SKU entities, and optionally policy-related tables. The filters in this request control which block records participate in the aggregation and how the results are grouped for reporting.

All properties in this DTO are optional. They are modelled as nullable fields so that clients can explicitly send `null` to rely on server defaults or omit constraints, while still allowing precise control when a filter or grouping needs to be applied. Servers should document and implement sensible defaults for unspecified or null fields, such as defaulting to a recent time window or a canonical grouping mode.

from.description:
Inclusive start of the time window for considering block events or current blocked state, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

When this value is `null`, the server interprets the query as having no explicit lower bound and may default to a preconfigured historical range or treat the window as open-ended on the past side, depending on analytics policy.

to.description:
Exclusive end of the time window for considering block events or current blocked state, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

When this value is `null`, the server typically interprets the query as "up to now" and uses the current time as the exclusive upper bound, or a configured reporting cutoff if such a policy exists.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers that restricts the breakdown to catalog entities owned by specific sellers.

When this array is empty or not provided, the analytics include products and SKUs from all sellers. When one or more seller IDs are supplied, only block records associated with those sellers are considered in the aggregation.

categoryCodes.description:
Optional list of catalog category codes used to limit the breakdown to products or SKUs that belong to specific navigation categories.

If no category codes are supplied, the query spans all categories. When one or more codes are provided, only block records for entities assigned to those categories (or their descendants, depending on implementation) are included in the statistics.

includeInactive.description:
Flag indicating whether the breakdown should include catalog entities that are no longer actively blocked (historical or inactive block records).

When `false` or omitted, the aggregation normally focuses on entities that are currently blocked at query time. When `true`, the server may include historical blocks within the specified time window, allowing administrators to analyze trends and remediation effectiveness over time.

groupBy.description:
Optional grouping strategy that controls how the server segments the breakdown entries.

- `"reason"`: Aggregate purely by block reason across the entire catalog so that each entry represents a single reason code and its counts.
- `"reason_and_seller"`: Further segment by owning seller so that each entry is unique by block reason and seller, enabling per-seller comparisons.
- `"reason_and_category"`: Further segment by catalog category so that each entry is unique by block reason and category, useful for analyzing problematic catalog segments.

When this value is `null`, the server falls back to its default grouping strategy, which is typically equivalent to `"reason"` but may be configured differently by the platform.

page.description:
Optional 1-based page index for paginating breakdown entries when the result set is large.

When this value is `null`, the server usually defaults to the first page (page 1). Together with `limit`, this field allows clients to page through large numbers of breakdown entries without requesting all results at once.

limit.description:
Optional maximum number of breakdown entries to return in a single response page.

When this value is `null`, the server applies a reasonable default page size such as 50 or 100. Servers may enforce an upper bound (for example, 1000) regardless of the requested value to protect system performance and ensure predictable analytics behavior.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReasonBreakdown.description:
Aggregated statistics describing why catalog entities (products and SKUs) are blocked in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is returned by administrator-facing analytics endpoints that provide an overview of catalog health and policy enforcement. It summarizes the population of blocked products and SKUs across one or more block reasons, optionally segmented by seller, category, or other dimensions as requested in the associated filter DTO. The structure is tailored for dashboard widgets, reports, and investigation tools used by governance and operations teams.

The statistics are derived by combining reference data such as `shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons` with catalog visibility or block linkage tables and product/SKU entities. Implementations may also draw on materialized snapshot tables (for example, `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`) to efficiently compute the totals and per-reason entries over a requested time window. Together with other analytics models, this DTO helps administrators identify systemic issues, monitor the effectiveness of policies, and prioritize remediation work.

totalBlockedProducts.description:
Total number of distinct product records that are currently or historically blocked within the scope defined by the request filters.

This value is always present and non-negative. It is typically used as a denominator when computing ratios for each breakdown entry and provides a quick, high-level measure of how much of the product catalog is impacted by block reasons.

totalBlockedSkus.description:
Total number of distinct SKU records that are currently or historically blocked within the scope defined by the request filters.

This value complements `totalBlockedProducts` by showing the impact at the SKU level, which is often higher than the product count because a single product can have multiple blocked variants. It is also commonly used as a denominator for SKU share ratios in the breakdown entries.

entries.description:
List of aggregated breakdown entries, each representing statistics for a single block reason and, depending on the grouping strategy, optionally a specific seller or category segment.

Every entry contains the block reason code and human-readable labels, counts of affected products and SKUs, and optional ratio metrics that relate those counts back to `totalBlockedProducts` and `totalBlockedSkus`. Clients typically render this collection as tables, charts, or drill-down views in admin dashboards.

IShoppingMallCatalogBlockReasonBreakdown.description:
Single catalog block reason breakdown entry representing aggregated statistics for one block reason, optionally scoped to a particular seller or category segment.

This type is typically derived from shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons (for the reason code and description) and joined with catalog visibility or block linkage tables that indicate which products and SKUs are blocked for that reason in the filtered time window and scope.

reasonCode.description: Stable machine-readable code of the catalog block reason (for example, "policy_violation", "legal_hold", "low_quality_content", or "risk_flagged"). This value corresponds to the canonical code stored in shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons.

reasonLabel.description: Human-readable label or title for the block reason, derived from shopping_mall_catalog_block_reasons or related localization tables. Suitable for direct display in admin dashboards.

reasonDescription.description: Optional human-readable description that explains the semantics of the block reason and typical scenarios in which it is applied. This is usually sourced from reference data or policy documentation.

sellerId.description: Optional seller identifier when the breakdown is grouped at the reason-and-seller level. Null when the grouping does not include a seller dimension.

sellerName.description: Optional descriptive name of the seller associated with this breakdown entry. Only populated when a sellerId is present and grouping includes seller segmentation.

categoryCode.description: Optional category code when the breakdown is grouped at the reason-and-category level. Null when the grouping does not include a category dimension.

categoryName.description: Optional human-readable name of the category associated with this breakdown entry. Only populated when a categoryCode is present and grouping includes category segmentation.

blockedProductCount.description: Number of distinct product records that are blocked for this reason (and optional segment) within the filtered scope.

blockedSkuCount.description: Number of distinct SKU records that are blocked for this reason (and optional segment) within the filtered scope.

productShareRatio.description: Optional ratio indicating the share of blocked products represented by this entry, typically computed as blockedProductCount / totalBlockedProducts for the response. Expressed as a fractional value between 0 and 1. May be null when totals are zero or ratios are not computed.

skuShareRatio.description: Optional ratio indicating the share of blocked SKUs represented by this entry, typically computed as blockedSkuCount / totalBlockedSkus for the response. Expressed as a fractional value between 0 and 1. May be null when totals are zero or ratios are not computed.

IShoppingMallCart.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying shopping cart headers from the shopping_mall_carts table in an admin-facing context.

Admin tools and internal services use this DTO to submit complex search criteria to the shopping cart search endpoint. Filters typically include ownership type (guest vs customer), references to customer or guest identities, activity windows based on creation or last-update timestamps, cart state, and basic cart metrics like item counts or estimated monetary totals. Pagination and sorting fields control how results are paged and ordered.

page.description: Optional 1-based page index for paginating shopping cart search results. When null or omitted, the implementation typically defaults to the first page.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of cart summaries to return per page. When null or omitted, the server applies a default page size (for example, 20 or 50) and may enforce an upper bound even if a larger value is supplied.

sortBy.description:
Optional field indicating which cart attribute to sort by.
- "createdAt": sort by cart creation timestamp.
- "updatedAt": sort by last update timestamp.
- "itemCount": sort by number of items in the cart.
- "estimatedTotal": sort by estimated monetary total of the cart.
When null or omitted, the implementation may default to "updatedAt".

sortDirection.description: Optional sort direction applied to the chosen sortBy field. Accepted values are "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending order. When null or omitted, the server selects a sensible default, typically "desc" for recency-based sorts.

ownerType.description:
Optional filter restricting results to carts owned by registered customers, guest users, or any owner type.
- "customer": only carts associated with a shopping_mall_customers record.
- "guest": only carts associated with a shopping_mall_guestusers record.
- "any": no restriction on owner type.
When null or omitted, the implementation treats this as equivalent to "any".

customerId.description: Optional filter for carts belonging to a specific registered customer, identified by the customer’s UUID. Only applicable when ownerType is null, "any", or explicitly "customer".

guestUserId.description: Optional filter for carts associated with a particular guest user logical identity, identified by a UUID. Only applicable when ownerType is null, "any", or explicitly "guest".

email.description: Optional case-insensitive email filter allowing admins to search carts that can be correlated with a customer or contact email address. The exact mapping to underlying fields depends on how cart headers or related contact snapshots store email addresses.

status.description:
Optional cart lifecycle status filter.
- "active": carts currently in use and not yet converted to orders or considered abandoned.
- "converted": carts that have been successfully converted into orders.
- "abandoned": carts that have remained inactive beyond a configured threshold and are considered abandoned.
- "any": no restriction on lifecycle status.
When null or omitted, the implementation treats this as equivalent to "any".

minItemCount.description: Optional lower bound on the number of items contained in the cart. When specified, only carts whose item count is greater than or equal to this value are returned.

maxItemCount.description: Optional upper bound on the number of items contained in the cart. When specified, only carts whose item count is less than or equal to this value are returned.

minEstimatedTotal.description: Optional lower bound on the estimated monetary total of the cart, expressed in the platform’s base currency (for example, USD). When specified, only carts whose estimated total is greater than or equal to this value are returned.

maxEstimatedTotal.description: Optional upper bound on the estimated monetary total of the cart, expressed in the platform’s base currency. When specified, only carts whose estimated total is less than or equal to this value are returned.

createdFrom.description: Optional inclusive lower bound for cart creation timestamps, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). When set, only carts created at or after this timestamp are considered.

createdTo.description: Optional exclusive upper bound for cart creation timestamps, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). When set, only carts created before this timestamp are considered.

updatedFrom.description: Optional inclusive lower bound for cart last update timestamps, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). When set, only carts whose last update occurred at or after this timestamp are considered.

updatedTo.description: Optional exclusive upper bound for cart last update timestamps, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). When set, only carts whose last update occurred before this timestamp are considered.

IShoppingMallCart.description:
Shopping cart header entity representing an in-progress shopping session for either a guest user or an authenticated customer.

This DTO exposes the core fields of the `shopping_mall_carts` Prisma model, including identity, actor type, lifecycle status, currency, and audit timestamps. It is used as the detailed cart representation returned from cart detail and mutation operations in admin, customer, and guest user contexts.

In addition to raw header fields, this type also carries optional, read-only summary projections such as derived totals and light references to the owning actor and cart items. These additional properties are computed by the service layer from related tables like `shopping_mall_cart_items`, `shopping_mall_customers`, and `shopping_mall_guestusers` and do not introduce new database columns. Sensitive authentication and session fields are deliberately excluded so that this DTO can be safely exposed through public and administrative APIs.

id.description:
Primary key of the cart.

This value is generated by the backend according to the `shopping_mall_carts.id` Prisma definition and uniquely identifies a single cart header row.

Clients receive this identifier in responses and reuse it in subsequent cart item, update, merge, and checkout operations. It is read-only from the API consumer’s perspective and never accepted in create or update DTOs.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that conceptually owns the cart.

Business values align with the underlying `shopping_mall_carts.actor_type` column and typically include `"guestuser"` for anonymous flows and `"customer"` for authenticated customer accounts.

Service logic uses this value together with the corresponding owner summary to route authorization checks and to determine which set of cart operations are valid for the current session.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the cart.

Typical business values include `"active"`, `"converted_to_order"`, `"merged"`, and `"abandoned"`, matching the semantics described in the `shopping_mall_carts.status` Prisma column.

Back-office jobs and API endpoints rely on this field for filtering and for enforcing which operations are permitted, for example preventing updates on carts already converted into an order.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code configured for prices in this cart.

All monetary values associated with items in this cart are expected to be expressed in this currency, matching the `shopping_mall_carts.currency_code` Prisma column.

Business rules may restrict which currencies are allowed per region or per customer, and conversion logic should ensure consistent use of this code across all line item calculations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart header was first created.

The value is persisted in `shopping_mall_carts.created_at` and is assigned by the database or ORM layer at insert time.

It is useful for auditing cart age, analyzing abandonment patterns, and driving clean-up processes for stale carts. This field is strictly system-managed and is not accepted in create or update requests.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart header was last modified.

The value corresponds to `shopping_mall_carts.updated_at` and is updated whenever mutable cart header fields or associated relationships change in a way that affects the cart header.

Operational tooling uses this timestamp to understand recent activity on the cart, while background maintenance tasks use it to identify inactive carts for archival or clean-up.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp when the cart has been logically removed.

The value is stored in `shopping_mall_carts.deleted_at` and, when non-null, marks the cart as logically deleted while retaining it for analytics, audit trails, or legal retention.

Most business queries and APIs treat carts with a non-null deleted_at as excluded unless explicitly querying for historical or soft-deleted data.

Null value indicating that the cart is currently active and has not been soft deleted.

When this branch is selected, the cart is considered logically present and eligible for normal business operations, subject to its status and other constraints.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion marker for the cart.

This value reflects the `shopping_mall_carts.deleted_at` column and is null for active carts. When populated with a date-time value, the cart is considered logically removed but retained for compliance or analytics.

API consumers should treat non-null values as an indication that the cart should not be used for normal shopping flows, even though it remains queryable for historical inspection.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp of the last comprehensive validation of the cart and its items.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_carts.last_validated_at` and is set when a validation routine verifies item availability, pricing, promotions, and other business rules.

Downstream processes and UI clients may surface this value to indicate the freshness of pricing or eligibility checks before checkout.

Null value indicating that no full validation timestamp has been recorded yet.

Carts may start in an unvalidated state and will receive a non-null timestamp once the system runs a complete validation pass.

last_validated_at.description:
Last time the cart and its line items were fully validated against availability, pricing, and business policies.

This property mirrors `shopping_mall_carts.last_validated_at` and is updated by validation routines triggered before checkout or by periodic background jobs.
