Clients and operators use this information to decide whether an additional validation step is required before converting the cart into an order, especially in environments with frequently changing inventory or pricing.

oneOf.description:
Summary information for the owning customer when this cart is customer-based.

This lightweight projection is computed from the related `shopping_mall_customers` and possibly associated profile tables to provide quick context such as display name or contact hints.

It is an optional, read-only convenience view that avoids repeated lookups in administrative screens and diagnostics tools.

Null when the cart is not associated with a registered customer.

In this case the cart is either guest-based or the customer information is intentionally omitted from the current projection.

owner_customer.description:
Optional summary projection of the registered customer who owns the cart.

This field is not a direct Prisma column but a derived view built from the `shopping_mall_customers` model and related profile data. It is populated only when `actor_type` indicates a customer cart and the backend chooses to include this context in the response.

The summary keeps payload size modest while still allowing administration tools and support dashboards to quickly understand which customer a cart belongs to without issuing additional queries.

oneOf.description:
Summary information for the owning guest user when this cart is guest-based.

This object is constructed from the `shopping_mall_guestusers` model and any associated context suitable for diagnostic or analytical views without exposing sensitive identifiers.

It is provided primarily for administrative and analytics use cases where understanding guest activity patterns is important.

Null when the cart is not associated with a guest user or the projection is intentionally omitted.

Customer-owned carts or purely technical flows will typically leave this value null.

owner_guestuser.description:
Optional summary projection of the guest user identity associated with the cart.

Like `owner_customer`, this property is a derived convenience view, not a direct database column. It is populated when the cart belongs to a guest user and when the response context benefits from exposing lightweight guest identity information.

User-facing APIs may omit this field entirely, whereas admin-facing endpoints often include it to support investigation of anonymous shopping behavior.

items_snapshot.description:
Optional snapshot of the current cart items for detail views.

This array is built from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table and related SKU or product metadata, providing a compact summary of each line item such as SKU reference, quantities, and pricing components.

While not a direct column on `shopping_mall_carts`, this projection allows cart detail endpoints to return a complete view of the cart in a single response. For list endpoints or highly constrained contexts, the implementation may omit this field to keep payloads small.

estimated_total_amount.description:
Derived monetary estimate representing the total value of the cart.

This value is computed from cart items, discounts, and surcharges and is expressed in the cart’s `currency_code`. It is not a direct database column but a convenience field exposed to simplify UI rendering and reporting.

Clients should treat this value as indicative rather than final, as a fresh validation step before checkout may adjust the total if inventory or pricing conditions have changed.

IShoppingMallCart.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new shopping cart header in the shopping mall domain.

This DTO is used by customer- and guest-facing cart creation endpoints to establish a new `shopping_mall_carts` row representing an in-progress shopping session. It captures only business inputs that the client is allowed to control and omits all system-managed fields such as primary keys, audit timestamps, soft deletion markers, and validation timestamps.

Ownership is expressed through the actor type combined with an optional owner reference appropriate to the context. In customer-authenticated flows the owning customer identifier is derived from the authentication token rather than provided in this DTO, while guest flows may rely on a separate session mechanism to associate the cart with a guest user identity. The server is responsible for enforcing that the actor information is consistent and for assigning suitable default status and currency when they are not explicitly supplied.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that will own the newly created cart.

Typical business values include `"guestuser"` for anonymous carts and `"customer"` for registered customer carts. The combination of this value and the authenticated context determines which foreign key on `shopping_mall_carts` is populated.

Implementations should validate that the actor type is compatible with the current authorization context and reject invalid combinations, such as requesting a customer cart while authenticated as a purely guest session.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status to assign to the cart, if the client wishes to override the default.

Common initial values include `"active"` for carts that are immediately usable and business-specific variants that represent preconfigured states. If omitted, the backend applies the default status defined in the `shopping_mall_carts` model or business configuration.

Clients should normally leave this field empty unless they implement specialized flows that require a particular starting state.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code to use for all monetary values within this cart.

When provided, this value must be supported by the platform and appropriate for the customer’s region or pricing context. If omitted, the backend infers a default currency from regional configuration, customer preferences, or global settings.

Once the cart contains items, changing the currency may require special handling, so it is recommended that clients choose the intended currency at creation time whenever possible.

IShoppingMallCartOwnerCustomerSummary.description:
Lightweight summary of a registered customer who owns a cart.

This type is a projection built from the `shopping_mall_customers` table and its related profile data and is designed specifically for embedding within cart representations. It exposes only non-sensitive identification and display fields that are useful in administrative tools and diagnostic views.

Using a summary type instead of the full customer entity prevents accidental exposure of private or authentication-related information while still letting operators quickly recognize which user a cart belongs to.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer account.

This corresponds to the primary key of the related `shopping_mall_customers` row and allows navigation to full customer details in administrative tooling.

It is read-only in the context of cart responses and is not supplied when creating or updating carts.

display_name.description:
Human-friendly name used to identify the customer in operator dashboards and logs.

This value is typically derived from customer profile fields such as full name, nickname, or business name and is chosen to provide quick visual recognition in lists and detail screens.

The exact construction may vary by deployment but should avoid including sensitive information while remaining sufficiently descriptive for internal users.

IShoppingMallCartOwnerGuestUserSummary.description:
Lightweight summary of a guest user identity associated with a cart.

This projection is built from the `shopping_mall_guestusers` model and any non-sensitive metadata that helps distinguish one guest session from another in operational tooling. It is intended for internal and analytical scenarios rather than for direct end-user display.

Using a constrained summary type ensures that guest-related secrets or tracking details are not accidentally exposed through cart APIs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user logical identity.

This maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_guestusers` record associated with the cart and allows internal systems to correlate multiple carts and sessions for the same guest.

As with customer identifiers, this field is read-only in cart responses and is not part of any cart creation or update request.

label.description:
Operational label or short descriptor used to differentiate guest identities in administrative views.

Implementations may derive this from coarse-grained metadata such as country, device type, or a hashed token representation, provided that no personally identifiable or sensitive information is exposed.

The exact semantics are deployment-specific but should remain stable enough to be meaningful in logs and dashboards.

IShoppingMallCartItemSummary.description:
Compact summary of a single cart line item suitable for embedding in cart detail responses.

This projection is derived primarily from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table along with linked product and SKU entities. It surfaces the essential attributes needed to render a cart view, such as the referenced SKU, quantity, unit price, and extended price, while omitting internal identifiers that are not required at the cart header level.

The summary is intentionally read-only and is not used for create or update operations; dedicated cart item endpoints operate directly on cart item DTOs for mutating line items.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart item row.

This value maps to the primary key of the underlying `shopping_mall_cart_items` record and allows targeted operations on individual items through dedicated cart item endpoints.

In the context of the cart summary, it is primarily useful for diagnostics, debugging, and as a stable key for UI rendering.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU associated with this cart item.

This field points to the corresponding `shopping_mall_skus` row and is used by downstream logic to join product metadata, pricing rules, and inventory information.

Client applications typically use this value only indirectly, relying instead on richer product information loaded from catalog APIs when needed.

product_name.description:
Display name of the product or variant associated with this cart item.

The value is denormalized from catalog entities for convenience so that cart detail views can display meaningful labels without additional catalog lookups.

It should reflect the user-facing name at the time the item was added to the cart, even if catalog data later evolves.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the SKU that the customer or guest user has placed into the cart for this line item.

This value is sourced from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` quantity column and must be a positive integer. Validation logic ensures that it complies with minimum and maximum purchase constraints defined by the business.

Changes to quantity are typically performed through dedicated cart item update operations rather than by editing this summary structure directly.

unit_price.description:
Unit price of the SKU at the time it was added to the cart, expressed in the cart’s currency.

This value is calculated from pricing rules and stored with the cart item to preserve price consistency even if catalog prices change later.

It is used together with quantity and any applied discounts to compute the extended price for the line item.

line_total.description:
Extended price for the line item, generally equal to unit price multiplied by quantity and adjusted for any line-level discounts.

This value is derived from `shopping_mall_cart_items` monetary columns or computed at read time to provide a ready-to-display monetary total per item.

The sum of all line totals, together with shipping and surcharges, contributes to the cart’s overall estimated total amount.

IShoppingMallCart.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for shopping mall cart headers stored in the `shopping_mall_carts` table.

This schema represents the set of mutable cart header fields that a client is allowed to change through cart update operations for both customer and guest user actors. It is used by the `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}` and `PUT /shoppingMall/guestUser/carts/{cartId}` endpoints in combination with the `cartId` path parameter, which uniquely identifies the target cart record.

Only fields that are conceptually updatable at the cart header level are included here. System-managed identifiers and lifecycle timestamps such as creation, update, soft deletion, and validation markers are excluded from this DTO to preserve data integrity and ensure that critical audit information is controlled exclusively by backend services and the database.

actor_type.description:
Actor type that owns the cart.

The value must be consistent with which foreign key is associated to the cart in the `shopping_mall_carts` model. Business usage expects values such as `"guestuser"` when the cart belongs to a guest user identity, or `"customer"` when the cart is owned by an authenticated customer account.

Updating this field allows service logic to adjust how the cart is resolved to an owner, particularly in guest-to-customer merge scenarios, while still enforcing strict ownership checks and preventing arbitrary reassignment between unrelated accounts.

status.description:
Current business status of the cart.

Typical values include `"active"`, `"converted_to_order"`, `"merged"`, or `"abandoned"`, and they are used by business rules and background processing to determine how the cart is treated. For example, a cart marked as converted or merged may be considered read-only for further modifications.

Service implementations should validate allowed state transitions when this field is updated, ensuring that carts cannot be moved into illegal or unsupported statuses relative to their historical lifecycle.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code for pricing within this cart.

All monetary values for cart items are expected to be expressed using this currency, and downstream order creation will rely on it for total calculations. Example values include `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"` depending on the marketplace configuration.

Changing the currency may trigger revalidation of item prices and availability rules, and therefore should typically be restricted to carts that have not yet reached finalization stages.

IShoppingMallCartItem.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating cart line items stored in the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table.

This schema represents filter, sort, and pagination parameters that a client can submit when listing cart items for a specific cart through the `PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items` endpoint. The `cartId` itself is supplied as a path parameter and therefore is intentionally omitted from this DTO to prevent duplication and potential inconsistencies.

Business logic uses the fields defined here to scope results to non-deleted items, apply optional validation status filters, and control how results are ordered and paginated for display in cart views on web or mobile clients.

page.description:
Page index for paginated results.

This is a 1-based index indicating which page of cart items should be returned. When omitted, the service may default to the first page. Combined with `limit`, it determines the offset in the underlying query over `shopping_mall_cart_items`.

Clients typically increment this value to load additional pages of cart items when implementing infinite scroll or traditional page-by-page navigation.

limit.description:
Maximum number of cart items to return per page.

This controls the page size for pagination over `shopping_mall_cart_items`. Backend implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect performance and resource usage, even if a larger value is requested.

Common values include 10, 20, or 50 depending on UX design and the average number of line items expected in a cart.

last_validation_status.description:
Filter for the last validation status of cart items.

The value is compared against the `last_validation_status` column of `shopping_mall_cart_items`, which commonly stores business-level states such as `"ok"`, `"out_of_stock"`, or `"price_changed"`. When present, only items whose last validation status matches this filter are returned.

Use this field to highlight problematic items in the cart, for example by requesting only items with non-OK statuses so that users can focus on resolving validation issues before checkout.

sort_by.description:
Sort key determining the primary ordering of cart items.

Typical allowed values include `"added_at"`, `"created_at"`, or `"updated_at"`, reflecting columns of the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table that define temporal ordering. Implementations may constrain the accepted set of values to avoid unsafe or unnecessary sorts.

When omitted, the default sort is commonly by `added_at` descending so that the most recently added items appear first.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction applied to the chosen sort key.

Common business values are `"asc"` for ascending or `"desc"` for descending order, and they determine how cart items are ordered relative to the selected `sort_by` column.

If this field is not provided, services typically default to descending order to emphasize the most recent additions or updates at the top of the list.

IShoppingMallCartItem.description:
Full read model for a shopping cart line item stored in the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table.

This DTO is returned from cart item read or update operations, including the PUT `/shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}` endpoint. It represents a single SKU entry within a cart, including quantity, pricing snapshot, currency, lightweight validation state, and audit timestamps.

In addition to raw foreign key identifiers referencing the cart and SKU, it also exposes a lightweight `sku` summary association so that clients can render human‑readable product variant information without issuing separate SKU detail calls.

id.description:
Primary key of the cart item.

This is the unique identifier of the row in `shopping_mall_cart_items` and corresponds to the `id` column in the Prisma model.

shopping_mall_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the cart header that owns this item.

This value references `shopping_mall_carts.id` and groups line items under a single cart for a particular customer or guest session.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU being purchased in this cart item.

This value references `shopping_mall_skus.id` and determines which concrete product variant the cart line refers to. It is primarily used by the backend for joins and validations; for UI rendering, prefer the `sku` summary association.

quantity.description:
Requested quantity of the SKU in this cart item.

The value is stored as an integer and represents how many units of the SKU the cart currently holds. Business validation ensures that it is positive and within allowed inventory and policy limits.

unit_price.description:
Snapshot unit price of the SKU in the cart currency at the time it was last recalculated.

This value is stored as a double precision number and is used to compute line subtotals at checkout. It reflects the price at the time of the last cart recalculation, not necessarily the current catalog price.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code associated with `unit_price`.

This code should match the currency of the owning cart, and it indicates the monetary unit for all price calculations on this line item.

last_validation_status.description:
Result of the most recent lightweight validation for this item.

Typical values include states such as `"ok"`, `"out_of_stock"`, or `"price_changed"`. The field is nullable when no validation has been performed yet.

last_validation_at.description:
Timestamp of the last validation status update.

When present, this value indicates when the system last evaluated the validity of this cart line with respect to inventory, pricing, or policy checks.

added_at.description:
Timestamp when the item was first added to the cart.

This is set when the cart item row is initially created and remains unchanged for the lifetime of the item, even if quantities or other fields are updated later.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart item record was created.

This is the audit creation time for the row in `shopping_mall_cart_items` and usually matches or is very close to `added_at`.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart item was last modified.

The system updates this value whenever mutable fields such as `quantity` are changed, providing an audit trail of modifications.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the cart item.

When non-null, the item is logically removed from the cart while its data is preserved for analytics or historical reporting. Active cart items have this field set to null.

sku.description:
Summary view of the SKU variant associated with this cart item.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_skus` and provides human‑readable context such as SKU code and variant name for rendering cart UIs without additional SKU detail requests.

IShoppingMallCartItem.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for adding a new cart item to an existing cart.

This type is used as the request body of `POST /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items` and maps to the subset of `shopping_mall_cart_items` fields that must be provided by the client when creating a new line item.

Ownership and identity fields such as the cart identifier and primary key are supplied by the path parameters and the database itself, so they are intentionally excluded from this DTO. Server-side logic injects the correct `shopping_mall_cart_id`, manages timestamps, and computes validation metadata after the item is created.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU to add to the cart.

This field maps directly to `shopping_mall_cart_items.shopping_mall_sku_id` and selects the specific variant from the `shopping_mall_skus` table that the customer wishes to purchase.

The server validates that the SKU exists, is visible to the caller, and is orderable before inserting the cart line.

quantity.description:
Requested quantity of the chosen SKU.

This value is persisted into `shopping_mall_cart_items.quantity` and must be a positive integer. Business rules may enforce additional maximum limits based on inventory, risk rules, or per-order caps.

If a client sends an excessive amount or violates policy, the server must reject the creation request rather than silently truncating the quantity.

IShoppingMallCart.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall cart header used for list, search, and badge-style contexts.

This DTO provides a compact projection of the `shopping_mall_carts` entity, exposing only key scalar fields and owner summaries that are needed to render cart lists or analytics overviews. It is intended for use in paginated responses such as admin cart search and any `IPageIShoppingMallCart.ISummary` wrappers.

Compared to the full `IShoppingMallCart` detail DTO, this summary omits heavy composition data such as item snapshots and focuses on identity, lifecycle state, ownership context, and optional aggregate metrics like estimated total amount.

id.description:
Primary key of the cart.

This identifier corresponds to `shopping_mall_carts.id` and uniquely identifies the cart header.

List and search APIs use this value for linking to the full cart detail view and for driving subsequent operations that act on a specific cart.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that conceptually owns the cart.

The value is copied from `shopping_mall_carts.actor_type` and typically indicates whether the cart belongs to a guest user or a registered customer.

It allows list screens and analytics to group and filter carts by ownership model without loading full detail information.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the cart.

Common values such as `"active"`, `"converted_to_order"`, `"merged"`, or `"abandoned"` mirror the `shopping_mall_carts.status` column.

In summary views this field is used to quickly identify which carts are actionable, which have been converted into orders, and which should be treated as historical or abandoned.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code configured for prices in this cart.

This value reflects `shopping_mall_carts.currency_code` and indicates the currency in which the cart’s monetary values are expressed.

List views and dashboards may use this field for grouping by currency or for displaying price-related information alongside the cart summary.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart header was first created.

Sourced from `shopping_mall_carts.created_at`, this field is helpful for sorting and filtering carts by creation time in list and analytics views.

It also assists operators in identifying old or potentially abandoned carts without loading the full detail representation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart header was last modified.

This value mirrors `shopping_mall_carts.updated_at` and is used in list contexts to understand recent activity on the cart.

It is especially useful for dashboards and search results that focus on recently changed or recently validated carts.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp when the cart has been logically removed.

When present, this value indicates that the cart is considered logically deleted even though the row remains in the database for audit and analytics purposes.

Null when the cart is currently active and not soft deleted.

Most list and search operations will either exclude logically deleted carts by default or clearly mark them using this field when they are included.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion marker for the cart in summary views.

The semantics match those of the `shopping_mall_carts.deleted_at` column and the corresponding field on the detail DTO, enabling list screens to distinguish active from logically deleted carts without loading full detail.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the cart and its items were last fully validated.

In summary contexts, this value allows operators or automated systems to quickly see how fresh the validation is for a given cart.

Null when no full validation timestamp has been recorded.

Carts that have never been validated or whose validation predates a major business event may be candidates for revalidation, which can be inferred directly from this field in summary responses.

last_validated_at.description:
Last time the cart and its line items were fully validated, as reflected on the cart header.

This field is included in the summary DTO to support list and analytics screens that must reason about validation freshness without requiring separate detail lookups.

oneOf.description:
Summary information for the registered customer who owns the cart, when applicable.

This projection is derived from the `shopping_mall_customers` model and associated profile data and is included here to provide immediate ownership context in cart lists and admin dashboards.
Null when the cart is not associated with a registered customer, for example in guest-only flows or when ownership details are intentionally suppressed in the current view.

owner_customer.description:
Optional summary projection of the registered customer who owns the cart.

Including this field in the summary DTO allows list and search endpoints to convey ownership context alongside cart state without requiring separate customer lookups or loading the full cart detail representation.

oneOf.description:
Summary information for the guest user identity that owns the cart, when applicable.

This projection comes from the `shopping_mall_guestusers` model and provides coarse-grained identification in administrative and analytical views.
Null when the cart is not associated with a guest user or when the current view focuses only on customer-owned carts.

owner_guestuser.description:
Optional summary projection of the guest user identity associated with the cart.

This field enables list and analytics views to distinguish guest-based carts and to surface limited guest context without exposing sensitive identifiers or loading full guest user details.

estimated_total_amount.description:
Derived monetary estimate representing the total value of the cart, when available.

The value is computed from cart items, discounts, and surcharges and is expressed in the cart’s `currency_code`. It is included in summary views so that list and dashboard screens can surface an approximate cart value without loading full item details.

Because this field is derived by service logic, it may be omitted or treated as advisory in contexts where a fresh validation step is required before checkout.

IShoppingMallSku.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a SKU (stock keeping unit) sourced from the `shopping_mall_skus` Prisma model.

This DTO intentionally exposes only a minimal subset of the underlying columns that are essential for identifying and rendering a concrete sellable variant in list views, references, and analytics projections. It surfaces the primary key `id` and the business‑level SKU `code` directly from the `shopping_mall_skus` table while omitting operational details such as inventory quantities, pricing, and lifecycle status, which are handled by richer entity or analytics DTOs.

In addition to these database-backed identifiers, the schema includes a computed `name` field that is derived from the parent product and the chosen attribute values (for example, combining the product name with size and color). This field does not map to a dedicated column on `shopping_mall_skus`; instead, it is produced by the application layer to provide a friendly, human‑readable label that can be displayed in user interfaces without requiring additional joins or client-side composition. The summary type is designed to be embedded into other DTOs such as cart items, order lines, and inventory views where a lightweight SKU identity is required without loading the full catalog record.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU record.

This value is the primary key of the SKU row in the `shopping_mall_skus` table and serves as the canonical reference used in cart items, orders, inventory adjustments, and analytics snapshots.

Clients must treat this identifier as opaque: its internal structure has no business meaning, and it is generated by the system to ensure global uniqueness across all SKUs.

code.description:
Business-level SKU code that identifies the variant in day‑to‑day operations.

The code is typically unique per seller or per catalog context and may appear on labels, invoices, warehouse documents, and internal reports. It is stored as a string column on the `shopping_mall_skus` model and is suitable for use in search boxes, operational UIs, and integrations where humans or external systems refer to a SKU by a readable code.

Although the code is stable for most of the SKU lifecycle, governance rules may allow controlled changes; clients should not assume that the code is immutable in the same way as `id`.

name.description:
Human‑readable name or title of the SKU variant presented to end users and operators.

Unlike `id` and `code`, this field is typically **computed by the application layer** rather than stored as a dedicated column on the `shopping_mall_skus` table. Implementations commonly derive it by combining the parent product name with key attribute values such as size, color, or other variant options, producing labels like "T‑Shirt / Blue / M".

The name is used widely in list views, analytics, and reporting to help operators, customer support, and customers quickly recognize the precise variant without having to interpret raw attribute codes or perform additional catalog lookups.

IShoppingMallCartItem.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying mutable fields of a shopping cart line item backed by the `shopping_mall_cart_items` Prisma model.

This type is used by the PUT `/shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}` operation to update an existing cart item that belongs to a specific cart. The cart identity (`shopping_mall_cart_id`) and SKU identity (`shopping_mall_sku_id`) are supplied via path parameters and are treated as immutable for the lifespan of the cart item. System-managed audit columns such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, and soft‑deletion timestamps are also excluded from this DTO and are maintained exclusively by the server.

Only business inputs that a customer can legitimately change on an existing cart line are exposed here. At present this is limited to the `quantity` field, which represents the number of units of a given SKU that the user wishes to purchase. Derived or validation‑related fields such as `last_validation_status` and `last_validation_at` are recalculated by the backend during validation and are intentionally not accepted in the update payload; clients should read those values from the cart item read model rather than attempting to set them directly.

quantity.description:
Requested quantity of the SKU in this cart item.

This value must be a strictly positive integer and is revalidated against inventory availability, per‑SKU or per‑cart purchase limits, and other business policies whenever it changes. The server may clamp, reject, or adjust the quantity if it violates these rules, returning appropriate validation errors or an updated cart item state.

Clients typically send this field when a customer changes the quantity control on a cart page or mini‑cart UI. When omitted from the payload, the existing quantity stored in `shopping_mall_cart_items` remains unchanged.

IShoppingMallCartItemValidation.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering DTO for querying cart item validation records.

This type is used by admin-facing operations such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/carts/{cartId}/items/validations` and `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/carts/{cartId}/items/{cartItemId}/validations` to express filter criteria and pagination parameters when listing validation events stored in the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations` table.

It does not map directly to a Prisma row; instead, it represents query parameters for read-only search use cases over the validation history of one cart or a single cart item.

status.description:
Optional filter for validation outcome status.

When provided, only validation records whose `status` column matches this value (for example `"success"`, `"error"`, or `"adjusted"`) are returned. When null or omitted, validations of all statuses are considered.

validation_type.description:
Optional filter for the business type of validation.

Typical values include `"add_to_cart"`, `"cart_view"`, or `"checkout"` and correspond to the `validation_type` column in `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations`. When specified, only records of the given type are included.

createdAtFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for filtering by `created_at` timestamp.

When provided, only validation records created at or after this timestamp are returned. This allows narrowing the search window to a recent time period. The field name uses camelCase to align with other request DTOs such as `IShoppingMallCartMergeEvent.IRequest`.

createdAtTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for filtering by `created_at` timestamp.

When provided, only validation records created at or before this timestamp are returned. Used together with `createdAtFrom` to define a time range. The field name uses camelCase to match the broader API schema naming convention.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

This is a 1-based index indicating which page of results to retrieve. When omitted, implementations typically default to the first page.

limit.description:

IShoppingMallCartMergeEvent.IRequest.description:

This type is used by administrative analytics and audit endpoints to express complex search criteria, including cart and actor scoping, time range filters, item count thresholds, and pagination/sorting options. It does not directly map to a single Prisma model row but controls how merge event records are selected and ordered in responses.

page.description:

Used together with the limit field to control which slice of the result set is returned. Must be a positive integer; defaults are applied by the backend when omitted.

Filter by the target actor type recorded on the merge event.

This corresponds to the target_actor_type column on shopping_mall_cart_merge_events, indicating the actor that owns the resulting cart after the merge, such as a customer account or another guest session.

reasonQuery.description:

IShoppingMallCartMergeEvent.description:
Detailed representation of a single shopping cart merge event recorded in the `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` table.

This DTO is returned by admin audit endpoints when operators inspect an individual merge operation. It exposes the core identifiers, actor classifications, cart foreign keys, quantitative item counts, optional free‑form reason text, and the event creation timestamp captured at the time of the merge. The field set is a direct projection of the underlying Prisma model so that every non-nullable column is represented and every nullable column is exposed with appropriate nullability.

Consumers use this schema to support investigation, debugging, fraud and risk analysis, and compliance workflows. When combined with separate lookups for customers, guest users, and carts, it provides a precise audit trail of how a guest or secondary cart was merged into a primary cart, how many items were preserved, how many were dropped, and why. The DTO itself intentionally contains only scalar identifiers and counts; higher-level services and UIs are responsible for resolving these identifiers into richer domain objects when needed.

Because merge events are immutable audit records created automatically by system processes, no create or update request variants are defined for this type. All fields in this response are read‑only and reflect the state of the merge event at the time it was recorded.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart merge event.

This value corresponds to the primary key of a row in the `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` table and is generated by the database or application layer when a merge event is recorded. It remains stable for the lifetime of the audit record and is used as the canonical reference when fetching a specific merge event via the admin APIs.

source_actor_type.description:
Classification of the source actor on the merge event.

Typical values describe whether the source side of the merge came from a guest user, a registered customer account, or some system-initiated process. The exact set of codes is defined by business rules around cart ownership and may be extended over time as new actor types are introduced.

Services reading this field should treat it as a business code that determines which foreign key fields are expected to be populated on the source side (for example, when the source actor is a guest user, `source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id` is normally non-null).

target_actor_type.description:
Classification of the target actor that owns the resulting cart after the merge.

The value typically indicates a registered customer or another actor type allowed to own persistent carts. It is stored as a string code so that business logic can route merged carts to the appropriate ownership context and apply correct authorization checks.

Like `source_actor_type`, this value guides which related identifiers are expected to be populated on the target side, such as `target_shopping_mall_customer_id` for customer-owned carts.

source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id.description:
Identifier of the source guest user associated with this merge event, when applicable.

This field corresponds to the `source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id` foreign key on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` and points to a logical guest user identity. It is populated when the source actor type describes a guest user whose temporary cart is being merged into a more durable cart, and it is null when the source actor is not a guest user.

target_shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the target customer associated with this merge event, when applicable.

This field corresponds to the `target_shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` and references a row in `shopping_mall_customers`. It is commonly non-null when a guest cart is being merged into the authenticated customer’s cart, but may be null for other merge scenarios that do not involve a registered customer.

source_shopping_mall_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the source cart whose contents were merged into the target cart.

This field maps to the `source_shopping_mall_cart_id` column on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` and references a row in `shopping_mall_carts`. It may be null in edge cases where a merge conceptually occurred without a concrete source cart record, but in normal guest‑to‑customer and cart‑to‑cart merges it contains the identifier of the cart that lost ownership of the surviving items.

target_shopping_mall_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the target cart that received merged contents and remained active after the merge.

This field maps to the `target_shopping_mall_cart_id` column on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` and references the cart that becomes or remains the user-visible cart after the merge completes. It is typically populated for standard merge flows and may be used to link directly from an audit record back to the surviving cart for further inspection.

merged_item_count.description:
Number of cart line items successfully merged from the source cart into the target cart during this event.

The count reflects the quantity of line items that passed all validation, availability, and policy checks at the time of the merge. It is derived from the `merged_item_count` column on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` and is used in analytics and risk evaluation scenarios to understand how much of the original cart content was preserved.

dropped_item_count.description:
Number of cart line items that could not be merged and were dropped during this merge event.

This value comes from the `dropped_item_count` column on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` and typically increases when items are no longer available, violate current policies, or conflict with the target cart’s constraints. High dropped item counts can signal friction in the merge process or potential risk conditions that warrant further investigation.

reason.description:
Optional business reason or additional context for the merge event.

When present, this field contains a short code or descriptive text explaining why the merge was performed or which strategy was used (for example, a cart merge policy name or a human‑readable note recorded for debugging). It mirrors the `reason` column on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` and may be null when no explicit reason was captured at the time of the merge.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this merge event record was created.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` as a `DateTime` and typically represents the exact moment when the merge completed and the audit row was written. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string (usually in UTC) and is used for chronological ordering, time‑range filtering, and correlation with other audit and analytics records.

IShoppingMallWishlist.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for listing customer or admin wishlists in a paginated way.

This schema encapsulates the filter criteria, pagination settings, and sorting options that both customer‑facing and admin‑facing wishlist list endpoints expect. The shopping mall APIs require callers to provide explicit pagination (`page`, `limit`) and baseline sorting information (`orderBy`, `orderDirection`), along with at least one business status filter (`status`), so that result sets are predictable, consistent, and safe to page through.

The DTO itself carries no authentication or ownership information; the effective scope of the query (for example, the current customer vs cross‑customer admin searches) is determined by the authenticated actor and the specific endpoint. Optional properties such as `search` and `createdFrom`/`createdTo` allow clients to refine queries further without changing the underlying structure of the DTO.

page.description:
Zero‑based page index used for pagination when listing wishlists.

Clients use this value together with `limit` to navigate through large result sets. A value of `0` typically represents the first page, `1` the second, and so on. Negative values are not allowed and should be rejected by validation logic; services may also enforce an upper bound on the page index to protect performance.

limit.description:
Maximum number of wishlist summaries to return in a single page.

This controls the page size for list operations. Typical values are in a moderate range (for example, 10–100 items per page) to balance UI responsiveness and server load. The backend may enforce a maximum even if clients request a larger limit, clamping values to a safe range to prevent abuse or accidental overload.

search.description:
Free‑text search keyword applied to wishlist names or descriptions.

This field allows users or admins to locate wishlists by partial name, label, or notes. Implementations usually perform case‑insensitive matching against the `name` column and possibly additional text fields, following the indexing strategy defined for `shopping_mall_wishlists`. When omitted or empty, search filtering is not applied and all wishlists matching other filters are considered.

status.description:
Business status filter for wishlists, such as `active` or `archived`.

This value constrains results to wishlists whose `status` column in `shopping_mall_wishlists` matches the supplied code. Clients are expected to provide a valid status string recognized by the business layer; common examples include lifecycle states like `active`, `archived`, or other domain‑specific codes. When multiple statuses need to be queried, the API may accept a composite code or expose additional endpoints depending on design, but this field is always required for the basic list operation.

createdFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the wishlist creation timestamp range filter.

When set, only wishlists with a `created_at` value greater than or equal to this timestamp are included in the results. The value is expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string (typically in UTC or with an explicit offset). If omitted, no lower time bound is applied and older wishlists may be returned as long as they satisfy other filters.

createdTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the wishlist creation timestamp range filter.

When set, only wishlists with a `created_at` value less than or equal to this timestamp are returned. The value is an ISO 8601 date‑time string and is typically used together with `createdFrom` to define a time window, such as wishlists created in the last 30 days. If omitted, no upper time bound is applied beyond any general retention or archiving rules.

orderBy.description:
Name of the field used for sorting wishlist results.

Typical values correspond to logical fields such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `name`, even if the exact column names differ internally. The backend validates this value against a whitelist of supported sort keys and maps it to safe underlying columns or expressions. Providing this field is required so that both client and server have a well‑defined, deterministic ordering for pagination.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering wishlist results.

The value is usually one of a small set of direction codes such as `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending ordering. The backend validates this field and applies it consistently with the `orderBy` key to ensure deterministic ordering across pages. This field is required so that paging through results yields stable, repeatable sequences even when data changes slowly over time.

IShoppingMallWishlist.description:
Customer-owned wishlist entity for saving products of interest in the shopping mall platform.

This type represents the main wishlist record backed by the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model. Each wishlist belongs to a single authenticated customer and is used to organize products or variants the customer wants to track outside of the cart and order flows.

The wishlist entity includes identifying information, human-readable naming, lifecycle status, ownership information, and audit timestamps. The owning customer is exposed as a summary object instead of a raw foreign key identifier to provide immediate contextual information while keeping the persistence details internal.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist.

This field corresponds to the primary key column `id` of the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table. It is generated by the system when the wishlist is created and is used as the stable identifier in API paths and internal relations.

Clients use this value in operations that target a specific wishlist, such as updates, retrieval, or item management.

customer.description:
Summary information about the customer who owns this wishlist.

This association replaces the underlying foreign key column `shopping_mall_customer_id` from the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is resolved through a relation to the `shopping_mall_customers` model.

Exposing the owner as `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` allows both customer-facing and administrative clients to see who owns the wishlist without issuing additional lookup calls, while avoiding circular references and keeping the FK column itself out of the public API surface.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the wishlist such as "Default", "Gifts", or "Later".

This value is stored in the `name` column of the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table. It is intended to be shown in customer-facing UIs wherever wishlists are listed or selected.

The name should be concise but descriptive enough for the customer to recognize the purpose of the list.

description.description:
Optional longer description or notes about the purpose of this wishlist.

This maps to the nullable `description` column on `shopping_mall_wishlists`. When present, it can contain free-form text that explains how the customer intends to use the list or any additional notes.

When not provided or explicitly set to null, client applications may omit this field in list UIs or detail headers.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this is the customer's default wishlist.

This field is backed by the non-nullable `is_default` column on `shopping_mall_wishlists`. When true, the wishlist is treated as the implicit target when the customer saves items without choosing a specific list.

Only one wishlist per customer should normally be marked as default according to business rules enforced in the service layer.

status.description:
Business status of the wishlist such as "active" or "archived".

This field is stored in the non-nullable `status` column of `shopping_mall_wishlists`. It is used by business logic to control whether a wishlist is visible in standard customer flows or treated as archived or disabled while retaining its contents for analytics.

Client applications typically treat only active wishlists as selectable for item additions, while archived lists may appear in history or management screens.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist was created.

This value reflects the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table. It is assigned by the system at insert time and never changes.

Clients can use this field to sort wishlists chronologically or to display creation information to customers.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist was last updated.

This field mirrors the `updated_at` column on `shopping_mall_wishlists`. It is updated whenever mutable attributes of the wishlist change or when associated operations trigger an update.

Consumers can use it for freshness indicators or to detect changes when synchronizing local caches.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the wishlist.

This field corresponds to the nullable `deleted_at` column on `shopping_mall_wishlists`. When null, the wishlist is considered logically active subject to its `status`. When set to a timestamp, the wishlist has been soft-deleted and should be excluded from normal customer interactions.

Analytics and administrative tooling can still reference wishlists with a non-null `deleted_at` for historical or compliance purposes.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a customer-owned wishlist in the shopping mall platform.

This summary DTO is optimized for list views and lightweight embeddings where only key identifying and descriptive fields are required, rather than the full wishlist with all relational details.

It is derived directly from the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model and exposes only non-sensitive, business-facing fields to clients, including a summary of the owning customer instead of the raw foreign key identifier.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist.

This is the primary key from the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is used to retrieve the full wishlist detail or to perform update and management operations.

Clients typically treat this value as an opaque identifier.

customer.description:
Summary information about the customer who owns this wishlist.

This field replaces the underlying FK column `shopping_mall_customer_id` from the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is resolved via the relation to `shopping_mall_customers`.

Having an `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` here allows list views and embedded contexts to show who owns each wishlist without additional API calls, while keeping actor relations modeled consistently across the platform.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the wishlist such as "Default", "Gifts", or "Later".

This label helps customers distinguish between multiple wishlists when navigating list views.

It is also used for search, filtering, and display in profile or account sections.

description.description:
Optional longer description or notes about the purpose of this wishlist.

When present, this text can be shown in extended list rows or hover tooltips to provide additional context.

When null, the wishlist has no additional description beyond its name.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this is the customer's default wishlist.

The default wishlist is typically used implicitly when a customer saves items without explicitly selecting a target list.

At most one active wishlist per customer should have this flag set to true at a time according to business rules.

status.description:
Business status of the wishlist such as "active" or "archived".

This value controls whether the wishlist appears in standard customer flows and may also be used for analytics segmentation.

Implementations usually constrain this to a small set of status codes enforced at the application layer.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist was created.

The value is stored as a DateTime in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and reflects the initial creation moment of the wishlist record.

It is useful for sorting, auditing, and showing relative age in list views.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist was last updated.

Any modification to core wishlist attributes, such as name, description, or default flag, should update this value.

Clients can use it to detect recent changes and to implement optimistic UI refresh logic.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the wishlist.

When null, the wishlist is considered active for normal business operations.

When set to a DateTime value, the wishlist is logically removed from standard customer flows but remains available for analytics, audit, or restoration workflows depending on governance rules.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new customer-owned wishlist.

This DTO is used by the wishlist creation endpoint that allows an authenticated customer to register a new wishlist. It focuses on business-level fields that a client can supply when defining the list, while omitting ownership and system-managed fields such as identifiers and timestamps.

The backend derives the owning customer from the authentication context and initializes default values and audit fields based on the underlying `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model and business rules.

name.description:
Human-readable name for the wishlist, such as "Default", "Gifts", or "Later".

This value will be stored in the `name` column of `shopping_mall_wishlists`. It should be concise and customer-friendly, as it will be displayed wherever wishlists are listed or selected.

Validation rules from the business specification may enforce minimum and maximum length constraints that should be checked before persistence.

description.description:
Optional longer description or notes about the purpose of this wishlist.

When provided, this maps to the nullable `description` field in `shopping_mall_wishlists`. Clients can use it to store additional context or instructions that help distinguish this list from others.

If omitted or explicitly set to null, the wishlist will have no descriptive text beyond its name.

is_default.description:
Optional flag indicating whether the new wishlist should be treated as the customer's default wishlist.

If true, the service layer may unset the default flag on other wishlists owned by the same customer according to business rules. If false or null, the wishlist will be created as a non-default list unless platform configuration specifies otherwise.

This property influences the `is_default` column on `shopping_mall_wishlists`, but final behavior is controlled by server-side logic.

status.description:
Initial business status of the wishlist, such as "active" or "archived".

This value maps to the non-nullable `status` column of `shopping_mall_wishlists` and is required so that clients explicitly choose the lifecycle state for the wishlist at creation time. Typical implementations validate the supplied status against an allowed set of business states and reject invalid values.

Although the service may still provide sensible defaults in some flows, this field is required in the public API contract to keep the creation semantics explicit and aligned with the underlying database constraints.

IShoppingMallWishlist.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing customer-owned wishlist.

This DTO is used by the wishlist update endpoint that targets a specific wishlist identified by a path parameter. It exposes only mutable fields that customers are allowed to change, such as the wishlist name, description, and visibility or status flags.

System-managed fields including identifiers, ownership relations, and audit timestamps are intentionally excluded. The service layer merges the provided fields into the existing record in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table while enforcing ownership and business rules.

name.description:
New human-readable name for the wishlist.

When supplied with a non-null value, this replaces the existing `name` in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` record. Setting the value to null explicitly clears the name if business rules permit; otherwise the server should reject the update as invalid.

If this property is omitted, the current wishlist name remains unchanged.

description.description:
Updated description or notes about the purpose of this wishlist.

Providing a non-null value updates the `description` column on `shopping_mall_wishlists`. Supplying null explicitly clears any existing description, while omitting the property leaves the current description untouched.

Clients can use this to refine or remove descriptive text without affecting other wishlist attributes.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this wishlist should become or remain the default wishlist for the customer.

When set to true, the backend typically marks this wishlist as the default for the owning customer and, as part of the same transaction, ensures that other wishlists for that customer are no longer marked as default, enforcing the single-default invariant.

When set to false, the wishlist is explicitly marked as non-default. When set to null or omitted, the existing default status is preserved. Regardless of client input, server-side business rules guarantee that at most one active wishlist per customer is marked as default at any given time.

status.description:
Updated business status of the wishlist, such as "active" or "archived".

Providing a non-null value requests a status change and is validated against allowed state transitions before updating the `status` column in `shopping_mall_wishlists`. This can be used, for example, to archive or re-activate a wishlist.

When null or omitted, the current status is preserved. Implementations may reject unsupported transitions (such as re-activating a wishlist that has been hard-locked by policy), returning appropriate validation errors to the client.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for querying wishlist items that belong to a specific wishlist.

This DTO is used as the request body for the wishlist items search endpoint under a given wishlist. It encapsulates pagination, sorting, and optional filter fields that are applied when listing items from the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table for a particular wishlist header. The wishlist context itself is provided by the path parameter and must not be duplicated here.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve when paginating wishlist items.

Defaults to the first page if omitted. Must be a positive integer when provided.

limit.description:
Maximum number of wishlist item records to return in a single page.

Used to control page size when querying shopping_mall_wishlist_items. Upper-bounded to prevent excessive payload sizes.

oneOf.description:
Sorting directive for wishlist items within the wishlist.

- `created_at_desc`: Most recently added items first
- `created_at_asc`: Oldest added items first

Additional sort modes can be added in the future in a backward compatible way.

Sorting directive for wishlist items within the wishlist.

- `created_at_desc`: Most recently added items first
- `created_at_asc`: Oldest added items first

Additional sort modes can be added in the future in a backward compatible way.

sort.description:
Sorting directive for wishlist items within the wishlist.

- `created_at_desc`: Most recently added items first
- `created_at_asc`: Oldest added items first

Additional sort modes can be added in the future in a backward compatible way.

productId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to items associated with a specific product.

Represents the identifier of a product in the product catalog models related to shopping_mall_products.

skuId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to items associated with a specific SKU.

Represents the identifier of a SKU variant from shopping_mall_skus. When provided together with productId, both constraints must match.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for wishlist item creation time.

When provided, only items whose creation timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are returned. Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. Use null to explicitly indicate no lower bound.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for wishlist item creation time.

When provided, only items whose creation timestamp is less than or equal to this value are returned. Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. Use null to explicitly indicate no upper bound.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.description:
Wishlist item entity stored in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table.

Each record represents a single product or SKU that a customer has saved into one of their wishlists. It links a wishlist header from `shopping_mall_wishlists` to catalog entities in `shopping_mall_products` and optionally `shopping_mall_skus`, and tracks ordering and lifecycle timestamps for the item.

This DTO is used as the full response representation for wishlist item operations, such as creation and update endpoints. It exposes only business-safe columns from the Prisma model and keeps soft‑deletion visible so that clients can understand when an item has been logically removed while still retaining it for analytics or historical display use cases.

id.description:
Primary key of the wishlist item.

This value is generated by the backend from the `id` column of `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` and uniquely identifies a single wishlist line.

Clients receive this identifier in responses and reuse it when they need to address the same wishlist item in update or deletion operations.

shopping_mall_wishlist_id.description:
Identifier of the wishlist header that owns this item.

This maps to `shopping_mall_wishlist_items.shopping_mall_wishlist_id` and is a foreign key to `shopping_mall_wishlists.id`. It expresses the parent–child relationship between the wishlist and its items.

In APIs, the wishlist context is already provided by the URL path parameters, but this field remains in the response so clients can correlate items back to their wishlist header when working with denormalized result sets.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that has been saved to the wishlist.

This directly represents the `shopping_mall_product_id` column and references `shopping_mall_products.id`. Every wishlist item must point at a concrete product in the catalog.

Frontend applications can use this value for low-level correlation or diagnostics, while the `product` summary relation provides the richer, display-friendly view for most use cases.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Optional identifier of the specific SKU variant saved for this wishlist item.

This corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_sku_id` column that references `shopping_mall_skus.id`. It is set when the customer saved a concrete variant (for example, a specific size or color) rather than only the base product.

When null, the wishlist item tracks the product at a generic level and the customer can still choose a concrete SKU at checkout time. For normal rendering, use the `sku` summary relation when present.

position.description:
Relative ordering position of the item within the wishlist.

This value is taken from the `position` column and is used to preserve the sequence in which items are displayed. Lower numbers are shown earlier in the list.

The application may reassign positions when users reorder items or when items are inserted or removed from the wishlist.

added_at.description:
Business timestamp at which the customer added the item to the wishlist.

It maps to the non‑nullable `added_at` column. This is conceptually distinct from `created_at` and represents the moment the item was logically added by the user.

Clients can use this value to show "added on" labels or to sort wishlist entries by the time they were saved.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist item record was created in the database.

This field is populated from the `created_at` column and is managed by the persistence layer or database triggers.

It is typically very close to `added_at` but is oriented toward auditing and system diagnostics rather than end‑user messaging.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this wishlist item record.

Backed by the `updated_at` column, this field changes whenever mutable attributes of the wishlist item—such as position or optional metadata—are modified.

Clients can use this field for cache invalidation heuristics or to display "last updated" indicators when necessary.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this wishlist item.

This corresponds directly to the nullable `deleted_at` column. When null, the item is considered active and visible in the wishlist. When set, the item has been logically removed from the wishlist but retained for historical analysis or audit purposes.

API consumers may decide to hide soft‑deleted items in standard wishlist views while still being able to analyze them in back‑office reporting or recovery tools.

product.description:
Summary view of the catalog product saved in this wishlist item.

This is a BELONGS-TO association derived from `shopping_mall_product_id` and points to the `shopping_mall_products` entity wrapped as `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary`. It contains the lightweight fields needed to render wishlist entries, such as product name, primary image, and pricing context.

Using a summary object here allows clients to render wishlists in a single API call without issuing additional product detail requests for each item, while still avoiding circular references and heavy nested graphs.

sku.description:
Optional summary view of the SKU variant saved for this wishlist item.

When `shopping_mall_sku_id` is non-null, this property provides a lightweight representation of the `shopping_mall_skus` record as `IShoppingMallSku.ISummary`. It typically includes key variant attributes such as size, color, and variant-level pricing used to display the saved choice in the wishlist.

When there is no concrete SKU selected, this property is null and the item should be treated as saved at the product level, with variant selection deferred to the cart or checkout flows.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new wishlist item in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table.

This DTO is used by the wishlist item creation endpoint that attaches a new line to an existing wishlist header identified by the `wishlistId` path parameter. It includes only the fields that clients are allowed to provide when adding an item; system‑managed fields such as identifiers and timestamps are excluded from the request body.

The server uses the path parameter to determine the owning wishlist and derives audit information internally, ensuring that ownership and lifecycle metadata cannot be tampered with by clients.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that the customer wants to save to the wishlist.

This value is written into the `shopping_mall_product_id` column and must reference an existing record in `shopping_mall_products`. The backend validates that the product is visible and eligible to be stored on a wishlist according to catalog and business rules.

Clients typically obtain this identifier from catalog listings or product detail APIs before invoking the wishlist item creation operation.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Optional identifier of the specific SKU variant that the customer saved.

When provided, this value is persisted to the nullable `shopping_mall_sku_id` column and must reference a valid `shopping_mall_skus.id` associated with the chosen product. It allows customers to save precise variants (such as size and color combinations) in their wishlists.

When omitted or null, the wishlist item tracks the product at a generic level and the customer can still choose a concrete SKU later during the purchase flow.

position.description:
Desired ordering position for the new wishlist item.

If a value is supplied, the backend may use it as a hint for where to insert the item in the wishlist while still enforcing any internal normalization of positions.

If null or omitted, the service typically appends the item to the end of the wishlist using an automatically calculated position based on existing items.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing wishlist item stored in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table.

This DTO is consumed by the wishlist item update endpoint, which is scoped by both `wishlistId` and `wishlistItemId` path parameters. It exposes only those columns that are intended to be mutable after creation, following the business rules and comments defined on the Prisma model.

Ownership, foreign key relationships, and system‑managed audit fields remain immutable and are therefore not present in this schema. The server enforces that the targeted item belongs to the specified wishlist and to the authenticated customer before applying any changes.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Optional updated SKU variant associated with the wishlist item.

Changing this value updates the `shopping_mall_sku_id` column. It allows customers to refine or adjust the exact variant they have saved—for example, switching from one size to another—while retaining the same wishlist line.

When explicitly set to null, the association to a specific SKU is removed and the item reverts to tracking only the base product. The backend validates that any provided SKU belongs to the same product and is eligible for wishlist storage.

position.description:
New desired ordering position of the wishlist item within the parent wishlist.

When supplied, the service updates the `position` column to reflect the requested ordering and may rebalance positions for other items in the wishlist to preserve a consistent sequence.

If omitted or null, the position of the item remains unchanged. Clients can use this field to implement features such as drag‑and‑drop reordering in wishlist UIs.

IShoppingMallWishlistMergeEvent.description:
Wishlist merge event audit entity for the shopping mall platform.

This type represents a single row from the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` Prisma model, which records guest-to-customer or wishlist-to-wishlist merge operations. Each record captures the source and target actors and wishlists, counts of successfully merged and dropped items, an optional textual reason, and the timestamp when the merge occurred.

The entity is classified as a subsidiary audit table and is append-only from the business perspective. It is used by administrative tools and customer-facing history views to understand how a given wishlist was formed over time, to analyze merge quality, and to support investigation of merge policies and edge cases. It relates directly to `shopping_mall_wishlists`, `shopping_mall_customers`, and `shopping_mall_guestusers`.

id.description:
Primary key of the wishlist merge event.

This field corresponds to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` Prisma model and uniquely identifies a single merge event record.

Clients use this identifier to retrieve detailed information for a specific merge event and to correlate list results with detail views or logs.

source_actor_type.description:
Type of the source actor that owned the original wishlist or temporary state being merged.

In typical flows this value is set to "guestuser" to denote that the source wishlist belonged to a guest user session. However the field is modeled as a flexible string to allow for additional actor types if future flows support other merge origins.

Service logic uses this value together with `source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id` and other nullable foreign keys to decide which actor reference is populated for a given event.

target_actor_type.description:
Type of the target actor that received the merged wishlist items.

For customer-login flows this value is usually "customer" and indicates that the target wishlist and customer identity are stored in `shopping_mall_customers` and `shopping_mall_wishlists`.

Downstream analytics and monitoring tools can use this field to segment merge statistics by target actor category and to support future extension of merge behaviors.

merged_item_count.description:
Number of wishlist items that were successfully merged from the source wishlist into the target wishlist during this event.

This value reflects how many individual items were preserved and transferred according to merge policies and visibility rules.

It is useful for analyzing merge effectiveness, tracking expected versus actual preservation of user intent, and identifying abnormal events where few or no items were merged.

dropped_item_count.description:
Number of wishlist items that could not be merged from the source wishlist into the target wishlist during this event.

Items may be dropped because products are no longer visible or purchasable, because they violate catalog policies, or because merge deduplication rules consider them redundant.

High dropped counts can be used to trigger risk or quality alerts, to refine business policies, or to explain to customers why some items did not appear after login.

reason.description:
Optional free-form textual reason or context for the merge event.

Typical values may include merge policy identifiers, human-readable explanations of conflict resolution strategies, or diagnostic notes produced by the merge engine.

Because this field is nullable, events without additional context simply have `reason` set to null, while analytical queries can perform text search over non-null reasons.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist merge event occurred.

This field comes from the non-null `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` Prisma model and records the moment when the merge operation was completed and persisted.

It is used for chronological ordering in list views, temporal filtering in analytical queries, and correlation with other time-based logs and metrics.

source_guestuser.description:
Summary information about the source guest user, when the merge originated from a guest session.

This object is derived from the `source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_guestusers`. When populated it provides a lightweight representation of the guest actor, such as technical identifiers or basic tracking metadata.

The field is nullable because some merge events may not involve a guest user, or because source identity cannot be resolved in specific scenarios.

target_customer.description:
Summary information about the target customer who received the merged wishlist items.

This object is derived from the `target_shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_customers`. It contains a minimal set of fields needed to identify and display the customer in the context of merge history.

The field is nullable to handle cases where the target actor is not a registered customer or where the reference cannot be resolved.

source_wishlist.description:
Summary of the source wishlist whose items were merged into the target wishlist.

This object corresponds to the `source_shopping_mall_wishlist_id` foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_wishlists` and provides identifying information such as the wishlist id and human-readable label.

It is nullable when the merge did not originate from a concrete wishlist record, for example when reconstructing from transient session state.

target_wishlist.description:
Summary of the target wishlist that absorbed items during the merge event.
