This object is derived from the `target_shopping_mall_wishlist_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_wishlists` and represents the wishlist that the customer continues to see after the merge.

It is nullable in edge cases where the target wishlist cannot be resolved, but in normal flows it is populated and aligns with the wishlist identified by the customer-facing APIs.

IShoppingMallWishlistMergeEvent.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for querying wishlist merge events.

This type is used as the body for PATCH-based search endpoints over the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` audit table, including both customer-scoped and admin-scoped operations. It encapsulates complex filter criteria, temporal ranges, and analytic constraints that would be cumbersome to express purely as query string parameters.

The same request structure is reused for customer-facing history views and administrative analytics dashboards. In customer-scoped endpoints the wishlist context is supplied by the path parameter and MUST NOT be duplicated here, while in admin-scoped endpoints the filters can freely specify target customers, guest users, and wishlists across the entire system.

source_actor_type.description:
Optional filter on the type of the source actor involved in merge events.

Typical values correspond to the `source_actor_type` column in `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events`, such as "guestuser". Supplying a non-null value restricts results to events where the source actor type matches; leaving it null means no filtering by source actor type.

This field is especially useful in administrative analytics where multiple merge sources may be supported over time.

target_actor_type.description:
Optional filter on the type of the target actor that received merged wishlist items.

Values align with the `target_actor_type` column in `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events`, for example "customer". When provided, only events with the specified target actor type are returned; when null, events for all target types are included.

This filter helps separate customer-facing merges from other potential flows that target different actor categories.

source_guestuser_id.description:
Optional filter on the source guest user identity associated with merge events.

When non-null, only events whose `source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id` matches this UUID from `shopping_mall_guestusers.id` are returned. A null value means no restriction by source guest user.

This field is primarily used in administrative and analytics contexts to trace how specific guest identities were merged into customer accounts over time.

target_customer_id.description:
Optional filter on the target customer who received merged wishlist items.

A non-null value restricts results to events where `target_shopping_mall_customer_id` equals this UUID from `shopping_mall_customers.id`. When null, the query does not apply any filter by target customer.

This filter is useful for both admin tools and customer-support workflows when investigating how a particular customer’s wishlist was formed from earlier guest or secondary lists.

source_wishlist_id.description:
Optional filter on the source wishlist whose items were merged.

When provided, only events where `source_shopping_mall_wishlist_id` equals this UUID from `shopping_mall_wishlists.id` are returned. A null value disables filtering by source wishlist.

This field supports administrative analysis of how specific wishlists contributed items to other lists during merge operations.

target_wishlist_id.description:
Optional filter on the target wishlist that received merged items.

When non-null, the query returns only events whose `target_shopping_mall_wishlist_id` matches this UUID from `shopping_mall_wishlists.id`. When null, no explicit filter is applied on the target wishlist.

Admin endpoints use this field to scan merge history for a particular wishlist, while customer-scoped endpoints rely on the `wishlistId` path parameter instead of this property.

min_merged_item_count.description:
Optional lower bound filter on the `merged_item_count` column.

When set, only merge events where the number of successfully merged items is greater than or equal to this value are returned. When null, no lower bound on merged items is applied.

Administrators can use this field to focus on high-volume merges or to exclude trivial events where very few items were merged.

max_merged_item_count.description:
Optional upper bound filter on the `merged_item_count` column.

If provided, only merge events with a merged item count less than or equal to this value are included. Null indicates that no explicit upper bound is enforced.

This field is typically used together with `min_merged_item_count` to constrain results to a specific numeric range of merge sizes.

min_dropped_item_count.description:
Optional lower bound filter on the `dropped_item_count` column.

When specified, the query returns only events where the number of dropped items is greater than or equal to this value. A null value disables this threshold.

Operational dashboards can use this filter to highlight potentially problematic merges where many items could not be preserved.

max_dropped_item_count.description:
Optional upper bound filter on the `dropped_item_count` column.

Providing a value restricts results to events where the dropped item count is less than or equal to the specified threshold. Null removes the upper limit.

Combined with `min_dropped_item_count`, this supports focused analysis of merges within a specific drop rate band.

reason_query.description:
Optional substring or full-text search criterion applied to the `reason` column of merge events.

When non-null, the backend performs a text search, commonly backed by the `gin` index on the `reason` field in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` table. This allows analysts to retrieve events associated with particular merge policies, error codes, or diagnostic messages.

If null, no text search filter is applied and all reasons are acceptable.

created_from.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp range filter.

When set to a non-null ISO 8601 date-time string, only merge events whose `created_at` is greater than or equal to this moment are returned. A null value indicates no lower time bound.

This field is typically used in conjunction with `created_to` to analyze wishlist merges over a specific reporting period.

created_to.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp range filter.

If provided, only merge events whose `created_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp are included in the result set. When null, no upper time limit is enforced.

Consumers should ensure that `created_from` and `created_to`, when both present, form a logically ordered range to avoid empty or degenerate result sets.

page.description:
Optional page number for paginated merge event results using a 1-based index.

When non-null, this value indicates which page of results to retrieve. If null, the backend applies its default page index, typically 1.

Clients should pair this field with `limit` to control list navigation, and server implementations must enforce safe bounds on allowed page numbers.

limit.description:
Optional maximum number of merge event records to include in a single page of results.

A non-null value specifies the page size and must respect service-level constraints for minimum and maximum sizes. Null instructs the backend to use a sensible default page size.

This field is essential for efficient paging through large audit histories and for balancing latency with payload size.

sort_by.description:
Optional sort key for ordering wishlist merge events in the result set.

Common values include "created_at", "merged_item_count", or "dropped_item_count", aligning with columns in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` table. When null, the backend uses its default sort ordering, typically descending by `created_at`.

Clients should choose sort keys that are supported by the service; unsupported values should be validated and rejected with a clear error response.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction applied together with `sort_by` when ordering results.

Typical values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. If null, the backend uses its default direction, generally descending for time-based fields.

This field allows analytical tools and reporting UIs to switch between oldest-first and newest-first views or to rank events by counts.

IShoppingMallCartValidationResult.description:
Validation result for a specific shopping cart before checkout.

Represents the outcome of running business validation logic on a cart and its items. It indicates whether the cart is currently eligible for checkout, lists blocking errors that must be resolved, and includes non-blocking warnings that the customer should be made aware of. This DTO aggregates results derived from shopping_mall_carts, shopping_mall_cart_items, SKU and catalog visibility checks, and related validation logic, without exposing internal validation log tables.

Typically returned by the POST /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/validate endpoint. Clients use this to decide whether to allow the customer to proceed to checkout, to surface item-level issues, and to show any advisory messages.

cartId.description:
Unique identifier of the validated cart in the shopping_mall_carts table.

This corresponds to the cartId path parameter used in the validation request and is included here so that clients can safely correlate the validation result with the cart instance they are working with.

isValid.description:
Overall validation flag for the cart.

true when there are no blocking errors and the cart is considered eligible to proceed to checkout under current business rules. false when at least one blocking error exists that prevents checkout.

blockingErrors.description:
Collection of blocking validation errors that prevent checkout from proceeding.

Each entry describes a specific rule violation at cart or item level (for example, SKU no longer available, insufficient inventory, price becoming invalid, or catalog visibility restrictions). When this array is non-empty, isValid will be false.

warnings.description:
Collection of non-blocking validation warnings.

Warnings advise the customer about important but non-fatal conditions, such as minor price changes, upcoming expirations, or softer policy constraints. Warnings do not prevent checkout, but clients are expected to surface them so that customers can make an informed decision.

validatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the validation was performed, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

This allows clients to understand how fresh the validation result is and to decide whether a re-validation is necessary before creating an order.

IShoppingMallCartValidationError.description:
Blocking validation error for a cart or cart item.

Represents a condition that must be resolved before checkout can proceed, such as an inactive SKU, insufficient inventory, or an invalid price. Errors may apply to the cart as a whole or to a particular cart item.

code.description:
Machine-readable error code identifying the specific validation rule that failed.

Codes are stable identifiers used by clients to implement rule-specific handling or localization, for example: CART_SKU_INACTIVE, CART_INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, CART_PRICE_MISMATCH.

message.description:
Human-readable explanation of the validation error.

Intended to be displayed to end users or support staff. May be localized by the client based on the code if desired.

cartItemId.description:
Identifier of the affected cart item in the shopping_mall_cart_items table, when the error is item-specific.

If the error applies to the cart as a whole (for example, cart is empty), this field may be omitted or set to null using a different DTO variant if needed.

IShoppingMallCartValidationWarning.description:
Non-blocking validation warning for a cart or cart item.

Represents an advisory condition that does not prevent checkout but should be communicated to the customer, such as a small price change, limited remaining stock, or shipping constraints that do not violate policy.

Warnings can optionally be scoped to a specific cart via `cartId`, or to a particular cart line via `cartItemId`. This DTO is used alongside `IShoppingMallCartValidationResult` and `IShoppingMallCartValidationError` to give clients a complete picture of potential issues detected during pre-checkout validation.

code.description:
Machine-readable warning code describing the type of condition detected.

Examples include `CART_PRICE_UPDATED`, `CART_LOW_STOCK`, `CART_SHIPPING_DELAY`, and other enumerated business codes that can be localized and mapped to user-facing messages in the client layer.

message.description:
Human-readable warning message explaining the detected condition.

Intended primarily for presentation in the user interface, either directly or after localization based on the warning code. The text should be concise but clear enough to guide the customer about any potential impact on checkout.

cartId.description:
Identifier of the affected cart in the `shopping_mall_carts` table when the warning applies to the cart as a whole.

Use this field for conditions such as global shipping constraints, payment eligibility issues, or other cart-level validations that are not tied to a single cart item. It mirrors the `cartId` field used in `IShoppingMallCartValidationResult` so that clients can easily correlate warnings with a specific cart.

cartItemId.description:
Identifier of the affected cart item in the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table when the warning is item-specific.

Use this field for conditions such as low stock, price changes, or attribute mismatches that only impact a single line in the cart. For warnings that apply to the entire cart, this field can be omitted while `cartId` remains populated.

IShoppingMallCartCheckoutPreview.IReques.description:
Request DTO carrying checkout context and options used to compute a preview for a specific cart.

This object allows the client to supply non-persistent checkout parameters that influence pricing, shipping, and payment calculations for the targeted cart. Typical inputs include the customer-selected shipping method, candidate payment method, coupon or promotion codes, and optional delivery region information when not yet fixed on the cart.

The backend uses these values together with the current cart contents and configuration tables to compute a read-only checkout preview, without mutating cart or order state. Identifiers here use business codes (for example, shipping and payment method codes) to remain consistent with path parameters and other ShoppingMall request DTOs.

shipping_method_code.description:
Business code of the shipping method the customer intends to use for this checkout preview.

This should correspond to the `methodCode` used in shipping method endpoints (for example, `/shoppingMall/shippingMethods/{methodCode}`) and map to a record in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`. When omitted, the service may fall back to a default or previously selected method on the cart.

payment_method_code.description:
Business code of the payment method the customer intends to use for this checkout preview.

This should match the `paymentMethodCode` used in payment method endpoints and reference a configured payment method such as a card, bank transfer, or e-wallet option. The method is used to determine payment-related surcharges and eligibility rules.

coupon_codes.description:
List of coupon or promotion codes that the customer wishes to apply to this checkout preview.

The service validates each code against business policy and pricing rules and incorporates any applicable discounts into the computed price breakdown. Invalid or ineligible codes should be surfaced back through preview messages rather than failing the HTTP request outright.

country_code.description:
Business code of the destination country for shipping and tax calculations when the delivery region is not fully determined by the cart.

Together with `region_code`, this identifies a specific region record in `shopping_mall_regions` (for example, a composite unique constraint on `country_code` and `region_code`) and allows region-specific shipping policies and tax rules to be resolved unambiguously.

region_code.description:
Business code of the destination region for shipping and tax calculations when not already fixed on the cart.

When used together with `country_code`, this selects a single logical region from `shopping_mall_regions`, which in turn drives the choice of entries in `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` and related configuration tables.

IShoppingMallCartCheckoutPreview.description:
Detailed checkout preview result for a specific cart in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO encapsulates a comprehensive, read-only projection of how the current cart would be transformed into an order under the given checkout context. It includes per-item price breakdowns, aggregated totals, anticipated taxes and surcharges, shipping costs, and flags indicating whether checkout can proceed.

The preview is computed using shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items combined with relevant configuration and snapshot tables such as payment methods, payment method surcharges, shipping methods, and region shipping policies. It does not represent a persisted order and should not be treated as an authoritative financial record, but rather as a user-facing "review and confirm" payload.

cart_id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart for which this checkout preview was generated.

This matches the primary key of the shopping_mall_carts record that served as the basis for the computation.

items.description:
Array of line-level checkout preview items derived from shopping_mall_cart_items and related SKU and product data.

Each element describes a single logical line item, including base pricing, discounts, tax components, and any allocated shipping or surcharge shares used to compute order-level totals.

totals.description:
Aggregated monetary totals computed for the entire cart under the provided checkout context.

Totals include subtotal, discount totals, tax totals, shipping fees, payment surcharges, and the final payable amount that would be charged if the customer proceeds to order creation and payment.

allowed_to_checkout.description:
Flag indicating whether checkout is currently allowed for this cart under the evaluated rules.

A value of true means the cart passes all business validations required for order creation and payment authorization. A value of false indicates that one or more blocking issues exist, which should be explained in the messages field.

messages.description:
List of informational, warning, or error messages related to this checkout preview.

Messages can describe validation failures, partially applied discounts, unavailable items, stock limitations, or any other business conditions that affect the preview or the ability to complete checkout.

IShoppingMallCartCheckoutPreviewItem.description:
Line-level checkout preview item representing a single cart line and its computed monetary breakdown.

This object aggregates information from the underlying cart item, associated product and SKU, and pricing configuration. It exposes base price, applied discounts, tax amounts, and allocated shipping or surcharge components for one logical item line in the cart.

cart_item_id.description:
Identifier of the cart item that this preview line corresponds to.

This typically matches the primary key of a record in shopping_mall_cart_items and is used by clients to correlate preview lines with existing cart UI elements.

product_name.description:
Display name of the product associated with this cart item.

The value is resolved from the product catalog and may incorporate localization or variant-specific naming rules.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the concrete SKU selected for this cart item.

This value maps to a record in shopping_mall_skus and is used for inventory checks, price determination, and variant resolution.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the SKU included in this cart line for the purpose of this checkout preview.

The value reflects any adjustments made during validation or eligibility computation and is used to scale monetary amounts in this preview line.

unit_price.description:
Base unit price of the SKU for this cart item prior to discounts, taxes, and surcharges.

This value is derived from the product catalog and current pricing rules in effect at the time of preview generation.

discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied to this line item as part of the checkout preview.

This may include contributions from coupons, promotions, or other business rules that reduce the effective line price.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount calculated for this line item in the preview.

The computation uses tax rules associated with the region, product category, and other configuration tables relevant to tax policy.

shipping_fee_share.description:
Portion of the total shipping fee that is allocated to this line item for presentation purposes.

This value is useful for displaying per-item shipping costs but does not represent a separate charge; the final payable shipping total is provided at the order summary level.

surcharge_share.description:
Portion of any payment method surcharges or similar fees that is allocated to this line item in the preview.

This allocation is primarily for display and analysis and may not directly correspond to how charges are recorded in financial ledgers.

line_total.description:
Final total amount for this line item after applying discounts, taxes, shipping allocation, and surcharge allocation.

This value represents the effective cost attributable to this cart line within the overall checkout preview.

IShoppingMallCartCheckoutPreviewTotals.description:
Aggregated monetary totals for a cart checkout preview.

This structure summarizes the monetary impact of all items, discounts, taxes, shipping fees, surcharges, and other order‑level adjustments included in a checkout preview. Values are computed at request time and are not persisted directly in a Prisma model.

All amounts are expressed in the effective checkout session currency (for example, the platform base currency or the currency selected for the order). Implementations should treat all fields as non‑negative monetary totals after rounding to the smallest currency unit, typically two decimal places for standard fiat currencies.

The fields in this object are designed to be internally consistent: `subtotal` reflects pre‑discount item totals, `discount_total` reduces that amount, `tax_total` and `shipping_total` add location‑ and method‑specific costs, `surcharge_total` represents payment‑method or service fees, and `payable_total` is the final amount expected to be authorized or captured if the order is placed using the previewed options.

subtotal.description:
Total pre‑discount amount of all cart items, computed as the sum of item unit prices multiplied by their quantities before applying any discounts, coupons, or promotions.

The value is expressed in the checkout session currency and should be non‑negative. Implementations typically round to two decimal places using the platform’s standard monetary rounding rules.

discount_total.description:
Total monetary value of all discounts applied to the cart in this preview, including coupons, promotions, loyalty credits, and item‑level or order‑level markdowns.

The value is expressed in the checkout session currency and is non‑negative. It represents the aggregate reduction applied to the pre‑discount item subtotal, and it should not exceed `subtotal` for a well‑formed preview.

tax_total.description:
Total tax amount computed for the entire cart in the context of this preview.

The value aggregates tax contributions from all line items and applicable shipping or surcharge components based on the active tax configuration and the customer’s shipping region. It is expressed in the checkout session currency and should be non‑negative after rounding to the platform’s standard monetary precision.

shipping_total.description:
Total shipping fee that would be charged for this cart under the selected shipping method, carrier, and destination region.

The value is derived from shipping configuration and policy tables, expressed in the checkout session currency, and must be non‑negative. It reflects the total shipping charges that will be included in `payable_total` if the order is placed using the previewed options.

surcharge_total.description:
Total monetary amount of payment‑method surcharges or similar service fees applied at the order level for the selected payment option.

The value is typically computed from payment method surcharge configuration (for example, records in payment method surcharge tables), expressed in the checkout session currency, and must be non‑negative. It is included in `payable_total` when the corresponding payment method is used.

payable_total.description:
Final total amount that the customer would be expected to pay if this checkout preview were executed as an actual order.

This amount is expressed in the checkout session currency and must be non‑negative. It reflects the combined effect of the item `subtotal`, `discount_total`, `tax_total`, `shipping_total`, and `surcharge_total` after applying the platform’s rounding rules. Clients should treat this value as the authoritative figure for payment authorization and display in order confirmation screens.

IShoppingMallCartCheckoutPreviewMessage.description:
Message element describing validation results, informational notes, or warnings associated with a cart checkout preview.

These messages provide human‑readable and machine‑interpretable feedback about the previewed checkout state, such as blocking errors that prevent order placement, non‑blocking warnings (for example, quantity reductions due to limited stock), and informational hints about applied discounts or policy‑driven adjustments.

The structure is designed to be lightweight and can be repeated in arrays. Backends should use the `code` field as a stable identifier for programmatic handling and localization, while clients primarily display the `text` field to end users according to the severity indicated by `level`.

code.description:
Machine‑readable code identifying the message type or category.

This value is intended to be stable over time and suitable for use as a key in localization catalogs or client‑side handling logic (for example, `CHECKOUT_STOCK_UNAVAILABLE`, `CHECKOUT_ADDRESS_REQUIRED`, or `CHECKOUT_DISCOUNT_APPLIED`). Producers should avoid embedding user‑specific or dynamic text in this field.

level.description:
Severity level of the message, such as `info`, `warning`, or `error`.

Backends should restrict this field to a small, well‑defined set of values so that clients can implement consistent visual treatments and behavior. For example, `info` messages provide neutral context, `warning` messages indicate non‑blocking issues that may affect expectations, and `error` messages typically indicate conditions that block checkout until resolved.

text.description:
Human‑readable description of the message suitable for direct display to end users.

The text may be localized and should clearly explain the underlying condition or rule, and when appropriate, suggest remediation steps that allow the customer to proceed. Clients should not rely on the exact phrasing of this field for logic and should instead use `code` and `level` when making behavioral decisions.

IShoppingMallWishlist.IMoveItemToCartReq.description:
Request payload for moving a specific wishlist item into the authenticated customer’s active shopping cart.

This DTO is used by the POST /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/moveItemToCart operation and represents only the per-item and cart-behavior parameters that cannot be derived from the path or the authenticated customer context. The wishlist itself is identified exclusively by the `wishlistId` path parameter and the customer is determined from the JWT, so no wishlist or customer identity fields appear in this body.

The fields in this type are aligned with the underlying wishlist and cart item schemas such as `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` and `shopping_mall_cart_items`. It provides the wishlist item identifier and an optional merge strategy for how the item should be applied into the cart when a matching SKU already exists there.

wishlist_item_id.description:
Identifier of the wishlist item that should be moved into the cart.

This value corresponds to the primary key of a row in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table and must belong to the wishlist identified by the `wishlistId` path parameter. The backend validates ownership and that the item is currently in a movable state (for example, product visible and SKU purchasable).

merge_strategy.description:
Optional strategy that controls how the item’s quantity should be merged into the existing cart when a line with the same SKU is already present.

Typical business values include:
- `increase` – increment the existing cart line quantity by the wishlist item quantity.
- `replace` – replace the existing cart line quantity with the wishlist item quantity.

If omitted, the service applies the platform’s default merge strategy configured for wishlist-to-cart transitions.

IShoppingMallWishlist.IMoveItemToCartRes.description:
Result payload for moving a wishlist item into the authenticated customer’s active shopping cart.

This DTO is returned by the POST /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/moveItemToCart operation and provides a consolidated view of the updated wishlist and cart state after the move has completed. It is designed to allow clients to refresh both wishlist and cart sections of the UI with a single round trip.

The structure exposes a normalized wishlist representation, an updated cart representation bound to the same customer, and an optional list of informational messages that describe any partial success scenarios such as reduced quantity moves caused by inventory constraints or catalog visibility changes encountered during the workflow.

wishlist.description:
Updated high-level representation of the wishlist after the move operation.

The summary reflects any changes caused by the move, such as the removal or status change of the moved item, as well as updated counts or status flags that the client can use to redraw wishlist summaries. It does not contain deep item arrays; use the dedicated wishlist item listing endpoints for full detail when needed.

cart.description:
Snapshot of the customer’s active cart state after the wishlist item has been moved.

This summary includes sufficient information for listing cart contents and totals in the UI without forcing a separate cart retrieval call. It represents the cart header and a summarized set of items after the new line has been inserted or an existing line has been updated according to the merge behavior.

messages.description:
Optional list of informational messages about the outcome of the move operation.

Each entry communicates non-fatal conditions such as quantity adjustments due to stock limits, catalog visibility changes that prevented some sub-items from being moved, or other validation warnings that the client may surface to the user alongside the updated wishlist and cart views.

items.description: Human-readable message describing a non-fatal condition or additional detail about the move operation result.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICopyItemToCartReq.description:
Request payload for copying a single wishlist item into the authenticated customer’s active shopping cart.

This DTO is used by the copyItemToCart operation on shopping_mall_wishlists. It identifies which wishlist item should be copied and how the resulting cart line should be handled in terms of quantity and merge behavior. The wishlist itself is identified by the path parameter and therefore is not duplicated here.

The structure closely follows the shopping_mall_wishlist_items and shopping_mall_cart_items Prisma models, focusing on the item identifier, SKU linkage, and desired quantities without exposing ownership or system-managed fields.

wishlist_item_id.description:
Identifier of the wishlist item to be copied into the cart.

This corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table. The server uses this value together with the wishlistId path parameter and the authenticated customer context to validate ownership and existence of the item before copying it into the cart.

desired_quantity.description:
Desired quantity for the cart line that will be created or updated.

When omitted, the service will typically default to a quantity of 1 or reuse the quantity semantics defined by business rules. When provided, the value must be a positive integer and is validated against inventory and purchase-limit rules that map to SKU and catalog constraints.

merge_behavior.description:
Strategy to use when the target cart already contains a line item for the same SKU.

Typical values include logical modes such as "increase" or "replace". When set to "increase", the system adds the desired_quantity to the existing cart quantity. When set to "replace", the existing cart quantity is overwritten with desired_quantity. If omitted, the platform’s default merge policy for wishlist-to-cart flows is applied.

client_context.description:
Optional opaque string supplied by the client to help correlate this copy operation with client-side state or telemetry.

This value is not persisted in core wishlist or cart tables but may be logged or used for diagnostics in friction or UX analytics workflows.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICopyItemToCartRes.description:
Result payload returned after copying a wishlist item into the authenticated customer’s active cart.

This DTO provides a post-operation snapshot containing high-level wishlist and cart views so that a client can update its UI without performing additional fetches. The wishlist portion focuses on the specific item and its availability, while the cart portion highlights the resulting cart item and any quantity or pricing changes that occurred during validation.

The structure is derived from the shopping_mall_wishlists, shopping_mall_wishlist_items, shopping_mall_carts, and shopping_mall_cart_items Prisma models but is intentionally denormalized for convenience. It does not expose ownership or actor identity fields and omits low-level audit details while still reflecting key business states and validation outcomes.

wishlist.description:
Summary view of the source wishlist and the specific item that was copied.

This object allows the client to understand whether the wishlist and the item remain active and whether any availability warnings were detected during the copy attempt.

cart.description:
Summary view of the customer’s active cart after the copy operation.

It focuses on the affected cart item, including the final quantity and pricing snapshot, along with a compact representation of overall cart status.

messages.description:
List of informational or warning messages generated while processing the copy operation.

Messages can include reasons why quantities were adjusted, why certain merge behaviors were applied, or why an item could not be fully honored (for example, partial inventory). These messages are suitable for direct or adapted display in client UIs.

items.description:
Single informational or warning message related to the wishlist-to-cart copy operation.

Typical examples include human-readable descriptions of validation failures, partial quantity adjustments, or catalog visibility changes encountered during processing.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICopyItemToCartRes.description:
Compact representation of the wishlist and item involved in a copy-to-cart operation.

This view is centered around the source wishlist and the particular wishlist item that the customer attempted to copy. It surfaces a small set of fields that are useful for refreshing client state, such as whether the wishlist is still active and whether the specific item is currently considered copyable.

The shape is mapped from shopping_mall_wishlists and shopping_mall_wishlist_items, omitting ownership, audit, and system-control fields. It focuses on human-facing attributes like wishlist name and item status flags used by UX flows.

wishlist_id.description:
Identifier of the wishlist from which the item was copied.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_wishlists.id and matches the wishlistId path parameter used in the operation.

wishlist_name.description:
Human-readable name of the wishlist.

It is mapped from the name field of shopping_mall_wishlists and helps clients display or confirm which wishlist was involved in the copy operation.

wishlist_status.description:
Current business status of the wishlist, such as "active" or "archived".

This value is mapped from the status field of shopping_mall_wishlists and informs whether the wishlist is still visible in normal customer flows.

item_id.description:
Identifier of the wishlist item that was copied.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_wishlist_items.id for the source item record.

item_position.description:
Relative position of the item within the wishlist.

This value is mapped from the position field of shopping_mall_wishlist_items. It can be used by clients to update local ordering or to scroll to the relevant row when highlighting the item.

item_copyable.description:
Flag indicating whether the wishlist item is currently copyable to cart according to validation rules.

This reflects checks across related product and SKU visibility, inventory, and catalog policies. If false, the copy operation may have failed or only partially succeeded.

item_availability_message.description:
Optional human-readable message describing the availability status of the wishlist item.

This may include reasons the item could not be fully copied, such as discontinued SKUs, blocked catalog entries, or inventory shortages.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICopyItemToCartRes.description:
Compact representation of the customer’s cart after a wishlist item has been copied.

This view highlights the overall state of the active cart and the specific cart item affected by the copy operation. It is derived from the shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items models but omits actor linkage, audit details, and low-level validation history, focusing instead on the information needed by cart UIs following the copy.

The object exposes high-level cart status, the currency used for pricing, and an embedded representation of the updated or newly created cart item, including quantity and pricing snapshots.

cart_id.description:
Identifier of the customer’s active cart after the copy operation.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_carts.id and is the cart that received the copied wishlist item.

cart_status.description:
Current business status of the cart, such as "active", "merged", or "converted_to_order".

This value is mapped from the status field of shopping_mall_carts and indicates whether the cart is still open for further edits.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code for all monetary amounts in the cart.

This is mapped from shopping_mall_carts.currency_code and should match the unit_price currency used on individual cart items.

item.description:
Representation of the specific cart item that was affected by the copy operation.

The cart item view shows the resulting quantity and pricing snapshot, together with lightweight validation status information so that clients can give immediate feedback about the success of the copy.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICopyItemToCartRes.description:
Representation of the single cart item that was created or updated by a wishlist copy operation.

This view is mapped from the shopping_mall_cart_items model and focuses on the SKU being purchased, the final quantity, and the latest validation outcome. It deliberately omits ownership and audit fields such as shopping_mall_cart_id, added_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at, while exposing currency and price data that match the cart header.

The object allows clients to refresh a single line item in cart UIs after the wishlist copy without requiring a full cart reload. It is a read-only projection optimized for UI refresh and analytics flows and is not intended to mirror every column of the underlying Prisma model.

cart_item_id.description:
Identifier of the cart item that was created or updated as a result of copying from the wishlist.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_cart_items.id and uniquely identifies the line in the cart. It is always present and can be used by clients to target subsequent update or delete operations against the cart item.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU represented by this cart item.

This value is mapped from shopping_mall_cart_items.shopping_mall_sku_id and links back to the SKU in the product catalog for further detail lookups. It is always non-empty for valid cart items.

quantity.description:
Final quantity of the SKU in the cart after the copy and any merge or validation adjustments.

This value is mapped from the quantity field of shopping_mall_cart_items and is guaranteed to be a positive integer if the item remains valid in the cart. Clients can use it to update quantity controls and to recalculate line subtotals in the UI.

unit_price.description:
Snapshot unit price of the SKU in the cart’s currency at the time of copy and last recalculation.

This is mapped from shopping_mall_cart_items.unit_price and reflects the price actually used for order creation if the customer proceeds to checkout. It represents a point-in-time price snapshot and may differ from the SKU’s current list price if pricing has changed since the snapshot was taken.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code for unit_price.

This value is mapped from shopping_mall_cart_items.currency_code and should match the currency_code of the cart header. It enables clients to display price values with the correct currency symbol and formatting rules.

last_validation_status.description:
Outcome of the most recent lightweight validation for this cart item, such as "ok", "out_of_stock", or "price_changed".

This is mapped from shopping_mall_cart_items.last_validation_status and mirrors the latest validation record from shopping_mall_cart_item_validations where relevant. The field is optional and may be absent or null when no validation has been performed yet for this item.

last_validation_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent validation applied to this cart item.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_cart_items.last_validation_at and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format so that clients can reason about the freshness of the validation state. The field is optional and will typically be present only when last_validation_status has a meaningful value.

IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalytics.IRequ.description:
Request payload for querying friction analytics over shopping carts.

This DTO describes the time window, segmentation dimensions, and optional filters that control how friction metrics are aggregated across shopping_mall_carts, shopping_mall_cart_items, shopping_mall_cart_item_validations, and related models. It is designed for internal analytics and administration use rather than end-user flows.

The structure focuses on describing an analytics query, not on mapping directly to a single Prisma table. It allows callers to express which carts should be included in the calculation and how the results should be grouped without exposing any customer-identifying fields.

time_range.description:
Time range over which to compute cart friction analytics.

The implementation uses this range to filter carts and related events by their creation or activity timestamps, typically based on cart created_at and validation timestamps.

segmentations.description:
List of segmentation dimensions used to break down analytics results.

Typical segment keys include coarse-grained dimensions such as "region", "device_type", "seller", or "category". The backend validates supported values and may reject requests that specify unsupported or incompatible segmentations.

items.description:
Segmentation dimension identifier, such as "region", "device_type", "seller", or "category".

The set of accepted values is controlled by the analytics implementation and may be restricted to a documented list to ensure predictable query complexity.

filters.description:
Optional filter block used to constrain which carts and items are included in the analytics computation.

Filters can scope the analysis to particular sellers, product categories, regions, or cart statuses without changing the segmentation dimensions of the returned aggregates.

include_time_series.description:
Flag indicating whether the response should include time-series buckets in addition to overall aggregates.

When true, the backend computes per-interval metrics (for example daily or hourly) within the requested time range, enabling charting of friction trends over time.

max_bucket_count.description:
Upper bound on the number of time-series buckets or segments to return.

This value helps protect the analytics system from accidentally expensive queries by limiting the granularity of returned time slices or segmented result sets.

IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalytics.ITime.description:
Time range constraint used when querying cart friction analytics.

This object defines the lower and upper bounds of the analysis window and may optionally specify the bucketing granularity for time-series results. The range is typically applied to cart created_at timestamps and relevant validation or interaction events.

The fields are expressed as ISO 8601 date-time strings to align with common analytics and reporting tooling, and they are interpreted in the service’s canonical time zone or as UTC depending on deployment configuration.

from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the analysis window.

Carts and events with timestamps greater than or equal to this value are eligible to be included in the analytics computation.

to.description:
Exclusive upper bound of the analysis window.

Carts and events with timestamps earlier than this value are eligible to be included. When omitted, the implementation typically defaults to the current time.

bucket_granularity.description:
Optional logical granularity used for time-series bucketing, such as "hour", "day", or "week".

When provided together with include_time_series in the parent request, this value guides how the system groups events into time buckets.

IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalytics.IFilt.description:
Optional filter block controlling which carts and items participate in friction analytics.

The filter object provides coarse-grained constraints on the population under analysis, such as restricting to specific regions, sellers, or cart statuses. It is deliberately actor-agnostic and avoids customer-identifying fields, focusing instead on segmentation-safe attributes.

Individual properties are all optional so that a caller can specify any combination of filters without being forced to supply all dimensions.

region_codes.description:
List of region codes that carts must belong to in order to be included in the analysis.

Region codes typically correspond to entries in shopping_mall_regions or to externally configured region identifiers used by shipping and pricing policies.

items.description:
Region code used for filtering carts and related events.

These codes are treated as opaque identifiers by the analytics system and are matched against region assignments derived from cart or address data.

seller_ids.description:
List of seller identifiers that should be included in the analysis.

Each identifier corresponds to shopping_mall_sellers.id and enables computation of friction metrics only for carts that contain items belonging to the given sellers.

items.description:
Identifier of a seller to be included in the analytics filter.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_sellers.id and is used to restrict metric computation to carts linked to specified sellers.

category_ids.description:
List of category identifiers used to filter carts based on the categories of items they contain.

Each identifier typically corresponds to a record in shopping_mall_categories or related classification tables and allows analysis of friction by catalog area.

items.description:
Identifier of a product category used in analytics filters.

The value matches the primary key of a category record and is used to select carts whose items map to those categories.

cart_statuses.description:
Subset of cart statuses that should be considered in the analytics computation, such as ["active", "abandoned", "converted_to_order"].

These values are matched against the status field in shopping_mall_carts and allow focusing analysis on specific lifecycle states.

items.description:
Cart status value used in analytics filters.

The value must conform to the status vocabulary configured for shopping_mall_carts, such as "active", "merged", "abandoned", or "converted_to_order".

IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalytics.description:
Aggregated friction analytics for shopping cart behavior in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a denormalized, analytics-oriented snapshot derived from multiple cart-related Prisma models, including `shopping_mall_carts`, `shopping_mall_cart_items`, `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations`, and `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events`. It is intentionally not mapped 1:1 to any single table; instead, it exposes precomputed aggregates and distributions that are convenient for dashboards and reporting tools.

The structure is the canonical response shape for the `/shoppingMall/admin/carts/analytics/friction` endpoint. Callers first send an analytics query (`IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalytics.IRequest`) that specifies a desired analysis window, segmentation dimensions, and optional filters. The backend then normalizes those inputs, executes the necessary queries and aggregations, and returns this DTO containing:

- The effective time range that was actually used when running the computation (`timeRange`).
- A list of per‑segment analytics records (`segments`) that break down friction metrics by dimensions such as region, device type, seller, or category.
- A holistic view of friction metrics across the entire analyzed population (`overall`), independent of segmentation.

All information exposed by this schema is aggregated at cohort or segment level. Personally identifiable customer data is never included in this object, aligning with the platform’s privacy and compliance requirements for administrative analytics. The DTO is designed to be stable over time so that dashboards, BI tooling, or exported reports can rely on its shape without depending on internal schema changes in underlying transactional tables.

timeRange.description:
Effective analytics time range used when computing cart friction metrics.

This value is the **normalized** time window that the analytics engine actually applied after interpreting the client’s request-level time range. The service may adjust the originally requested bounds (for example, clamping to data retention limits, aligning to bucket boundaries, or filling in missing endpoints) and then exposes the finalized `from`/`to` values through this structure.

Consumers should treat this field as the source of truth for dashboards and subsequent drill‑down calls, rather than assuming it is identical to the `time_range` sent in `IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalytics.IRequest`. The underlying structure is shared with other analytics responses via `IShoppingMallAnalyticsTimeRange` and always uses ISO 8601 `date-time` strings.

segments.description:
List of computed cart friction analytics segments for the requested query.

Each segment represents a cohort defined by one or more segmentation dimensions such as region, device type, seller, or product category. For each segment, the system aggregates cart-level and line-item-level signals into metrics like cart counts, abandonment rates, validation failure distributions, and optional time‑series breakdowns.

The segments array can be empty when the effective time range contains no eligible carts after applying filters. When populated, clients typically render each entry as a row in a table, a series in a chart, or a card in an analytics dashboard.

overall.description:
Overall cart friction analytics across all carts included in the analysis window.

This object aggregates the same core metrics that appear at the segment level—such as total carts, abandonment behavior, and validation failure distributions—but does so for the entire population matching the effective filters and time range, without any segmentation applied.

Dashboard experiences often use this section to populate high‑level KPI cards or summary charts, while the `segments` collection provides finer‑grained drill‑down views by region, device type, seller, or category.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsTimeRange.description:
Normalized time range description used in analytics responses.

Represents the concrete time window that the analytics computation actually used, which may differ slightly from the client’s request due to defaults, clamping to retention boundaries, or normalization to bucket edges.

This type is not backed by a single Prisma model and is shared across multiple analytics DTOs within the shopping mall platform.

from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the analytics time window, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

The value may be derived from the client request or adjusted by the server when enforcing retention policies or filling in defaults.

to.description:
Exclusive upper bound of the analytics time window, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

The value usually corresponds to the end of the requested period or the current time, and may be aligned to the selected time bucket granularity.

IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalyticsSegmen.description:
Segment-level cart friction analytics for a specific cohort in the shopping mall platform.

This schema represents aggregated cart behavior metrics for a single cohort defined by one or more segmentation dimensions such as region, device type, seller, or category. Each instance corresponds to one logical "segment" within a larger friction analytics response and contains both identifying metadata and pre-aggregated metrics.

Metrics contained in this segment are derived from cart headers, cart items, and validation events over a specified analysis window. Values are already aggregated and normalized so that API consumers do not need direct access to raw transactional tables or detailed validation logs.

Typical use cases include rendering segmented charts and tables in administrative analytics dashboards, comparing friction across regions or channels, and identifying cohorts with unusually high abandonment or validation failure rates.

segmentKey.description:
Opaque identifier for this segment within a single analytics response.

The key is stable only within the scope of the response in which it is returned. Clients can use this key to correlate chart series, table rows, or drill‑down interactions, but should treat its internal structure as an implementation detail that may change over time.

dimensions.description:
Segmentation dimensions that define this cohort.

Each populated field in this object (for example, region, deviceType, sellerId, categoryId) describes how the carts included in this segment are grouped. The dimensions describe the cohort context only and do not themselves contain numerical metrics.

carts.description:
Cart population metrics scoped to this segment.

Includes counts such as the total number of carts created, active carts, carts that reached checkout, and average items per cart, after applying the segment’s dimension filters and analytics time range.

abandonment.description:
Cart abandonment-related metrics for this segment.

Represents how carts in this cohort progress through or drop out of the checkout funnel. Metrics typically include overall abandonment rate, average time to checkout for carts that progressed, and counts of carts abandoned before or during checkout, all computed using only carts that match the segment dimensions and time window.

validationFailures.description:
Distribution of cart item validation failures for this segment.

Summarizes how often different validation failure reasons (for example, out-of-stock, price-changed, or SKU-disabled) occurred for carts and cart items belonging to this segment during the analysis window. The distribution is pre-aggregated and designed for dashboard visualization rather than raw event replay.

timeSeries.description:
Optional time-series breakdown of key friction metrics for this segment.

When present, this object contains an ordered series of buckets that apply the same segment dimensions but additionally split metrics by a configured time granularity (such as hour, day, or week). Each bucket exposes cart counts and validation failure metrics for its interval, enabling trend analysis for this specific cohort.

IShoppingMallCartFrictionAnalyticsOveral.description:
Global cart friction analytics across all segments for a given analysis window.

This schema represents top-level aggregated cart friction metrics computed over the entire population of carts that match the analytics query filters, independent of any segmentation. It is typically used for KPI cards, summary tiles, and high-level charts that show the overall state of cart health and friction.

Metrics in this object are derived from the same underlying cart, cart item, and validation data as the segment-level analytics but aggregated across the full cohort before any segmentation is applied. When a response includes both overall and per-segment analytics, this schema provides the "global" benchmark against which individual segments can be compared.

carts.description:
Overall cart population metrics across all carts in the analysis window.

These values include all carts that satisfy the filters of the analytics request, regardless of region, device type, seller, or other segmentation dimensions. They are often used as denominators or reference values when interpreting segment-level metrics.

abandonment.description:
Overall cart abandonment metrics for the full cohort defined by the analytics request.

This property summarizes funnel progression and drop‑off behavior across all relevant carts, including global abandonment rate, average time to reach checkout, and counts of carts abandoned before or during checkout. It serves as a platform- or query-wide baseline for comparing specific segments.

validationFailures.description:
Overall distribution of cart item validation failures by reason across the entire cohort.

The distribution aggregates validation failures from all carts and cart items that match the analytics filters, without distinguishing between different segments. It is useful for identifying platform-wide sources of friction such as widespread inventory shortages or systemic pricing discrepancies.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsDimensions.description:
Segmentation dimensions used to define analytics cohorts.

Each property is optional and, when present, indicates that the corresponding dimension is part of the cohort definition. Multiple dimensions may be combined to form a single segment (for example, region + deviceType + seller).

regionCode.description: Region code (for example, ISO 3166-2 or platform-specific region identifier) associated with this cohort, if segmentation by region is requested.

deviceType.description: Logical device category used during the session, such as "desktop", "mobile_web", or "mobile_app".

sellerId.description: Opaque identifier of the seller whose catalog or orders contribute to this cohort, when segmentation by seller is requested. This ID is not directly attributable to a natural person and is intended for internal admin analytics usage only.

categoryId.description: Identifier of the primary product category used for segmentation in this cohort, when category-based segmentation is requested.

IShoppingMallCartCounts.description:
Cart population metrics for analytics.

Provides basic counts related to cart creation and progression towards checkout within a cohort or overall dataset.

totalCarts.description: Total number of distinct carts created within the analytics window for this cohort or overall dataset.

activeCarts.description: Number of carts that remained active (not checked out or deleted) by the end of the analytics window.

cartsReachedCheckout.description: Number of carts that reached the checkout stage at least once within the analytics window.

averageItemsPerCart.description: Average number of cart items per cart, computed over all carts in the cohort or overall dataset.

IShoppingMallCartAbandonmentMetrics.description:
Aggregated cart abandonment metrics for a specific analysis window and cohort of shoppers.

This schema represents how often carts are abandoned at different stages of the checkout funnel, together with a normalized abandonment rate. It is designed for use in analytics dashboards and reporting views, rather than as a direct persistence model.

The metrics are typically computed over a well-defined analytics window, such as a day, week, or campaign period, and may be scoped to particular segments (for example, country, device type, or traffic source). Implementations can derive these metrics from cart, order, and checkout event logs while ensuring consistent filtering criteria.

The structure is intentionally compact so that it can be embedded inside higher-level friction analytics responses or combined with additional dimensions such as geography, seller, or marketing campaign without excessive payload size.

cartAbandonmentRate.description:
Overall cart abandonment rate as a fraction between 0 and 1 for the selected analysis window.

In most implementations this is computed as `(number of carts that did not convert to completed orders) / (total number of carts considered in the cohort)`. The definition of "conversion" should be stable and clearly documented in the analytics pipeline to keep this metric comparable over time.

The value is provided as a unitless ratio rather than a percentage so that clients can render it as either a fraction or a percentage according to their presentation needs.

averageTimeToCheckoutSeconds.description:
Average elapsed time in seconds from cart creation to first checkout attempt for carts that reached the checkout stage at least once within the analysis window.

Only carts that actually attempt checkout are included in this average; carts abandoned before checkout are excluded from the denominator. This makes the metric useful for understanding friction within the active checkout funnel, separate from early-stage browsing abandonment.

Consumers can use this metric alongside abandonment counts to spot unusually long pre-checkout intervals that might signal UX issues or performance problems.

abandonedBeforeCheckoutCount.description:
Number of carts that were abandoned before ever reaching the checkout stage in the selected analysis window.

These are carts where users added items but never initiated a checkout workflow. High values can indicate issues such as unclear pricing, missing shipping information, or general lack of purchase intent.

This count is a raw integer and is typically interpreted together with cartAbandonmentRate and overall cart population metrics to understand top-of-funnel friction.

abandonedDuringCheckoutCount.description:
Number of carts that reached the checkout stage at least once but did not complete an order in the selected analysis window.

These abandonment events happen after the user has already committed to the checkout flow and therefore are often more critical from a conversion perspective. Common causes include payment failures, shipping cost surprises, or validation errors discovered late in the process.

This count is a raw integer and is often broken down further in other analytics models by payment method, shipping method, or validation failure types for root-cause analysis.

IShoppingMallCartValidationFailureDistri.description:
Aggregated distribution of cart item validation failures for a given analysis window and cohort.

This schema summarizes how frequently cart validation checks fail, grouped by failure reason. Typical validation checks include inventory availability, price consistency, product visibility, and catalog or policy constraints. The model focuses on counts and reason codes rather than exposing individual SKUs or cart items, which keeps it safe for use in administrative dashboards and high-level analytics.

The distribution is usually computed from validation events recorded during cart updates and checkout validation steps. It helps product and operations teams identify systemic sources of friction, such as recurring out-of-stock conditions or frequent pricing mismatches, without leaking sensitive per-item or per-customer details.

totalValidationFailures.description:
Total number of cart item validation failure events recorded within the analysis window.

Each validation attempt that fails for a cart line item or cart-level rule is counted as a single failure event, even if multiple failures occur on the same cart. This allows teams to understand the aggregate volume of failures handled by the validation layer.

Downstream analytics may normalize this value by total validation attempts or cart population to compute failure rates, but this schema intentionally exposes the raw count so that clients can perform their own rate calculations.

byReason.description:
List of per-reason validation failure buckets that together approximate the total failure distribution.

Each entry in the array groups all validation failures sharing the same logical reason code, such as "OUT_OF_STOCK" or "PRICE_CHANGED". The sum of `failureCount` across all buckets will typically be less than or equal to `totalValidationFailures`, depending on whether the analytics pipeline includes an "other" or fallback bucket.

Clients can use this data to rank failure reasons by impact, build charts that highlight the most common sources of cart validation friction, and monitor how the distribution changes over time as catalog, pricing, and policy configurations evolve.

IShoppingMallCartValidationFailureReason.description:
Bucket of cart validation failures for a single logical failure reason.

This schema is used as an element within the cart validation failure distribution and represents how often a particular reason caused validation to fail. It separates the raw count of failure events from the number of distinct carts impacted, which helps distinguish widespread low-frequency issues from localized high-severity problems.

The bucket does not expose SKU, cart, or customer identifiers directly. Instead, it focuses on aggregate counts that can safely be rendered in administrative dashboards and analytics tools without compromising privacy or leaking sensitive catalog details.

reasonCode.description:
Machine-readable code that identifies the validation failure reason represented by this bucket.

Typical examples include values such as `"OUT_OF_STOCK"`, `"PRICE_CHANGED"`, `"SKU_DISABLED"`, or `"POLICY_BLOCKED"`. The exact taxonomy of reason codes is defined by the validation subsystem and should remain stable over time so that historical analytics remain comparable.

User interfaces can map this code to localized, human-readable labels to explain the failure reason in charts, tables, and diagnostic views.

failureCount.description:
Total number of validation failure events that occurred for this specific reason within the analysis window.

Every time a validation rule associated with `reasonCode` fails, the analytics pipeline increments this counter. Multiple failures can be recorded for the same cart if the condition is evaluated repeatedly or across multiple items in the cart.

This metric is useful for ranking failure reasons by raw event volume and identifying areas where the system is repeatedly blocking or adjusting cart contents.

affectedCartCount.description:
Number of distinct carts that experienced at least one validation failure with this reason code during the analysis window.

While `failureCount` captures the total number of failure events, `affectedCartCount` focuses on breadth of impact across the cart population. A high `affectedCartCount` suggests that many shoppers are encountering the same issue, even if each cart only fails once.

Comparing `affectedCartCount` with `failureCount` helps teams distinguish between a few problematic carts that fail many times versus a common issue affecting many carts a small number of times.

IShoppingMallCartFrictionTimeSeries.description:
Time-series breakdown of key cart friction metrics.

Provides bucketed analytics data across the requested time window, allowing visualization of trends for cart creation, abandonment, and validation failures over time.

granularity.description: Time granularity used for the series buckets (for example, "hour", "day", or "week").

buckets.description: Ordered list of time-series buckets covering the requested time window.

IShoppingMallCartFrictionTimeSeriesBucke.description:
Single bucket within a time-series of cart friction metrics.

Represents metrics for a discrete time interval such as a specific hour or day.

from.description: Inclusive start timestamp for this bucket interval in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

to.description: Inclusive end timestamp for this bucket interval in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

cartCounts.description: Cart population metrics restricted to this bucket interval.

validationFailures.description: Validation failure metrics restricted to this bucket interval.

IShoppingMallWishlistEngagementAnalytics.description:
Analytics query parameters defining the time range, segmentation dimensions, and filters for wishlist engagement analysis.

This DTO is used by admin and internal analytics clients to request aggregated wishlist engagement metrics from the ShoppingMall platform. It describes the analysis window, desired segmentation dimensions, and optional filters such as focusing on particular sellers or product categories. The underlying analytics engine executes read-only queries over shopping_mall_wishlists, shopping_mall_wishlist_items, shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events, and related tables to compute the response.

timeRange.description: Time range over which wishlist engagement analytics should be computed.

items.description: Name of a segmentation dimension to apply for analytics bucketing (for example, "region", "deviceType", "seller", "category").

segmentBy.description: List of segmentation dimensions that should be applied in the analytics computation. The server interprets each string as a logical dimension name and returns per-segment analytics in the response.

sellerIds.description: Optional filter limiting analytics to wishlists or wishlist items associated with the specified seller identifiers. When omitted or empty, analytics are computed across all sellers.

categoryIds.description: Optional filter limiting analytics to products in the specified category identifiers. When omitted or empty, analytics consider all categories.

minActivityCount.description: Optional minimum activity threshold used to filter out segments or cohorts that do not reach a certain number of events (for example, total wishlist item adds). Segments below this threshold may be omitted from the response to reduce noise in analytics dashboards.

IShoppingMallWishlistEngagementAnalytics.description:
Aggregated engagement analytics for customer wishlists in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a read-only analytical view derived from multiple underlying wishlist-related tables, primarily `shopping_mall_wishlists`, `shopping_mall_wishlist_items`, and `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events`. It consolidates metrics such as counts, ratios, and time-series breakdowns to describe how customers interact with wishlists, how often items transition from wishlists into orders, and how engagement evolves over time.

The data returned by this schema is anonymized and aggregated at cohort or segment level, never exposing raw customer identifiers. It is intended for use in internal dashboards and administrative analytics tools, guiding product, marketing, and operations decisions around wishlist features and retention strategies.

totalWishlistCount.description:
Total number of wishlists observed in the specified analysis window.

This count includes all active wishlists that existed at any point within the time range defined by the request parameters, regardless of whether customers interacted with them during that period. Soft-deleted or archived wishlists are typically excluded unless the analytics engine is explicitly configured to include them for historical analysis.

activeWishlistCount.description:
Number of active wishlists that recorded at least one engagement event in the analysis window.

An engagement event typically includes item additions, removals, or merges involving the wishlist. This metric helps distinguish merely existing wishlists from those that customers actively use when comparing engagement across cohorts or over time.

averageItemsPerWishlist.description:
Average number of items per active wishlist during the analysis window.

The value is calculated as the total number of wishlist items (from `shopping_mall_wishlist_items`) associated with active wishlists divided by the number of active wishlists. It provides a coarse-grained measure of how heavily customers use wishlists to track products, without exposing individual list contents.

itemAddEvents.description:
Total count of item-add events recorded in wishlists over the analysis window.

This metric is derived from timestamped changes in `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` or corresponding audit streams and counts each time a product or SKU is added to any wishlist. It is useful for understanding how often customers discover products they want to save for later rather than purchasing immediately.

itemRemoveEvents.description:
Total count of item-remove events recorded in wishlists over the analysis window.

The metric counts deletions or logical removals of wishlist items, excluding system-maintenance operations such as cleanup of invalid products. Comparing this value with `itemAddEvents` provides insight into churn within wishlists and can help detect patterns such as customers frequently curating their saved items.

wishlistToOrderConversionRate.description:
Ratio expressing how frequently wishlist items eventually lead to orders within the analysis window.

This value is typically computed as the number of unique wishlist items or sessions that transitioned into successful orders divided by the total number of wishlist items or engaged sessions, depending on the analytical definition adopted by the platform. It is expressed as a numeric fraction between 0 and 1, where higher values indicate more effective conversion from saved items to actual purchases.

dailyEngagement.description:
Time-series breakdown of wishlist engagement metrics at a daily granularity.

Each entry in this array corresponds to a specific calendar day within the requested analysis range and bundles per-day counts such as active wishlists, add/remove events, and conversions. This structure allows clients to visualize trends and seasonality in wishlist usage across the selected time period, for example in line charts or bar charts in administrative dashboards.

segmentBreakdowns.description:
Optional segmentation buckets that break down engagement metrics by dimensions such as region, device group, or product category.

Each bucket aggregates the same types of metrics as the overall analytics but constrained to a particular segment key. The set of segments returned is driven by the segmentation options specified in the analytics request and never includes raw customer identifiers to preserve privacy and comply with governance rules.

IShoppingMallWishlistEngagementAnalytics.description:
Per-day wishlist engagement statistics bucket used inside `IShoppingMallWishlistEngagementAnalytics`.

Each instance summarizes engagement metrics for a single calendar day within the requested analysis period, combining counts of active wishlists, item add/remove events, and wishlist-to-order conversions for that specific day.

These records are derived from timestamped activity in tables such as `shopping_mall_wishlists`, `shopping_mall_wishlist_items`, and related order entities, and are suitable for plotting time-series charts in administrative dashboards.

date.description:
Calendar date represented in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) for which the metrics in this bucket are calculated.

The date is aligned with the platform's notion of business day boundaries and is used as the x-axis key when visualizing time-series charts of wishlist engagement.

activeWishlistCount.description:
Number of wishlists that recorded at least one engagement event on this specific date.

An engagement event can include adding an item, removing an item, or a merge operation that affected the wishlist. This metric emphasizes daily activity rather than cumulative state across days.

itemAddEvents.description:
Total number of wishlist item-add events recorded on this date.

Each event corresponds to a user saving a product or SKU to a wishlist, based on timestamps from `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` or related event streams. It helps measure discovery and saving behavior per day.

itemRemoveEvents.description:
Total number of wishlist item-remove events recorded on this date.

This metric counts explicit user-driven removals of items from wishlists and may exclude system-cleanup actions. Combined with `itemAddEvents`, it provides a view of how curated or volatile wishlists are for the given day.

conversionCount.description:
Number of wishlist-related conversions that occurred on this date.

A conversion typically represents an order where at least one purchased item can be traced back to a prior wishlist item according to the platform's attribution rules. This metric is aggregated at the day level to support analysis of how strongly wishlist usage leads to purchases over time.

IShoppingMallWishlistEngagementAnalytics.description:
Segment-level wishlist engagement statistics bucket used inside `IShoppingMallWishlistEngagementAnalytics`.

Each instance aggregates the same family of metrics as the top-level analytics object but constrained to a particular segment key such as region, device category, or product category group. Segmentation dimensions and keys are defined by the analytics request and configuration.

These buckets enable comparative analysis across cohorts while preserving privacy by avoiding direct exposure of individual customer or account identifiers.

segmentKey.description:
Identifier of the segment to which this analytics bucket belongs.
