The value is a stable key derived from the selected segmentation dimension, for example a region code (such as "KR"), device category (such as "MOBILE"), or product category path. Client applications are responsible for translating this key into localized display labels when needed.

segmentType.description:
Logical type of the segment represented by `segmentKey`.

Typical values indicate the dimension used for segmentation, such as "region", "device", "customer_cohort", or "category". This field allows consumers to understand how to interpret the associated key and how to group or label the metrics on dashboards.

totalWishlistCount.description:
Total number of wishlists that belong to or are attributed to this segment within the analysis window.

The definition of attribution depends on the segment type; for example, for region segments it may be based on the customer's primary region, while for product-category segments it may be based on the primary category of items stored in the wishlist.

activeWishlistCount.description:
Number of wishlists in this segment that recorded at least one engagement event during the analysis window.

This helps identify which cohorts are more engaged with wishlist features compared to their overall share of wishlists or traffic.

itemAddEvents.description:
Total number of wishlist item-add events within this segment during the analysis window.

The meaning of the segment depends on configuration, but in all cases the metric represents how frequently users in the cohort save new products or SKUs to their wishlists.

itemRemoveEvents.description:
Total number of wishlist item-remove events within this segment during the analysis window.

Comparing this metric to `itemAddEvents` and `activeWishlistCount` by segment is useful for detecting cohorts with particularly volatile or highly curated wishlist behavior.

wishlistToOrderConversionRate.description:
Wishlist-to-order conversion ratio for this segment over the analysis window.

It is calculated using the same business formula as the top-level `wishlistToOrderConversionRate` metric but restricted to customers, traffic, or products that fall into this specific segment. Higher values indicate that wishlist usage by this segment more frequently leads to completed orders.

IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving paginated order headers from the `shopping_mall_orders` table.

This DTO is used by administrative and backoffice tooling to query large volumes of orders with rich filters. It supports pagination, sorting, and a variety of constraint fields including order code fragments, customer or guest identity filters, monetary ranges, status sets, and time windows.

All filters are applied in a read-only manner and are intended to be combined flexibly. Unknown fields should be ignored by the implementation, while syntactically invalid values (such as malformed dates or reversed ranges) should result in validation errors at the API layer.

page.description:
Zero-based index of the page of results to retrieve.

This value controls the offset into the result set. It should be greater than or equal to 0, with 0 representing the first page. If omitted, implementations typically default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of order summary records to return in a single page.

Administrative clients should respect platform-configured upper bounds for this value to avoid excessive result sizes. For example, a typical maximum might be 100 or 200 items per page. If not provided, a reasonable default such as 20 or 50 may be used by the service.

orderCode.description:
Filter for orders matching a specific business-facing order code or a prefix thereof.

Implementations can treat this as an exact match or a case-insensitive partial match depending on configuration. The order code corresponds to the `order_code` column in `shopping_mall_orders` and is the primary identifier shown to customers and support staff.

customerKeyword.description:
Free-form search keyword applied to customer-identifying fields associated with the order.

Depending on implementation, this may match customer display name, email address, or phone number stored in related tables. It is intended for support and backoffice users to quickly locate orders when they know customer information but not the exact order code.

sellerId.description:
Optional filter that limits results to orders that contain at least one item belonging to the specified seller.

This value represents the unique identifier of a seller account in the seller domain. The underlying query typically joins `shopping_mall_orders` with tables such as `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers` to enforce this constraint.

items.description:
Individual status value to include when filtering the set of orders.

Status values correspond to the business-level lifecycle states encoded in the `current_status` column of `shopping_mall_orders`, such as `awaiting_payment`, `payment_confirmed`, `preparing_shipment`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, or `refunded`. Clients should pass only values recognized by the platform configuration.

statusIn.description:
Optional list of order lifecycle statuses used to include only orders whose current status is within the given set.

If this field is provided and non-empty, the query restricts results to orders whose `current_status` matches any of the specified values. When omitted or empty, no status-based inclusion filter is applied at the order header level.

minGrandTotalAmount.description:
Lower bound for the `grand_total_amount` of orders to be included in the search results.

This filter is applied against the `grand_total_amount` column in `shopping_mall_orders` and is expressed in the order's currency as defined by `currency_code`. It can be combined with `maxGrandTotalAmount` to define an inclusive monetary range.

maxGrandTotalAmount.description:
Upper bound for the `grand_total_amount` of orders to be included in the search results.

When combined with `minGrandTotalAmount`, this allows administrators to focus on orders in specific value bands, such as high-value orders for risk review or low-value orders for promotional tracking. Implementations should enforce that the minimum is not greater than the maximum when both are provided.

placedAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the order placement timestamp range used for filtering.

This field corresponds to the `placed_at` column in `shopping_mall_orders` and is represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or the platform's canonical time zone. Only orders placed on or after this instant are included when the filter is present.

placedAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the order placement timestamp range used for filtering.

Combined with `placedAtFrom`, this allows administrators to retrieve orders created within a specific time window such as a day, week, or promotional period. Implementations should validate that `placedAtTo` is not earlier than `placedAtFrom` when both are supplied.

includeCancelled.description:
Flag indicating whether orders in cancelled states should be included in the result set.

If set to false, the search may automatically exclude orders whose `current_status` falls into configured cancelled categories. When true or omitted, cancelled orders may be included if they match other filters or status conditions.

includeFullyRefunded.description:
Flag indicating whether orders that have been fully refunded should be included in the results.

Administrative users sometimes wish to analyze only net-active revenue orders or, conversely, focus on refunded orders for risk and quality analysis. This flag allows the query to be tuned according to those goals.

sortField.description:
Name of the field used to sort the resulting order list.

Common values include `placed_at`, `grand_total_amount`, or `order_code`. Implementations should maintain a whitelist of supported sort fields and respond with a validation error if an unsupported value is provided to avoid ambiguous or expensive sort operations.

sortDirection.description:
Direction in which the result set should be sorted by the chosen `sortField`.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending ordering. If omitted, the default may be descending by placement date so that the most recent orders appear first in administrative views.

IShoppingMallOrder.description:
Detailed administrative view of a single marketplace order stored in the `shopping_mall_orders` table.

This DTO aggregates the order header with customer or guest ownership, high‑level monetary summary, current lifecycle status, and key timestamps from the primary order record.

In addition, it composes related information from subsidiary models, including order line items, monetary snapshots, shipments, payments, refunds, disputes, and status histories, using summary or detail DTOs for each related entity. The structure is designed for admin and internal customer‑support tooling and deliberately avoids circular references while exposing enough context for investigation and operations.

Sensitive internal implementation details such as low‑level reconciliation identifiers or secret keys are excluded so that the schema can safely be exposed to trusted administrative clients and API consumers without leaking security‑sensitive data.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order row in `shopping_mall_orders`.

This is the primary key used internally by the platform and in data relationships. External actors typically use `orderCode` instead of this UUID when referencing the order in user interfaces or communications.

order_code.description:
Business‑facing order code for this order.

This value is unique within `shopping_mall_orders` and is the primary identifier shared with customers, sellers, support staff, and external systems. It appears in UIs, emails, invoices, and deep links and is the path parameter in operations that locate orders by business code instead of raw UUID.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary values on this order.

Every monetary amount in related structures (line items, snapshots, payments, refunds) is denominated in this currency. Typical examples include `"USD"`, `"KRW"`, or `"EUR"`.

current_status.description:
Current high‑level lifecycle status of the order.

Typical values include conceptual states such as `"awaiting_payment"`, `"payment_confirmed"`, `"preparing_shipment"`, `"shipped"`, `"delivered"`, `"cancelled"`, or `"refunded"`. Detailed status transitions are tracked in `shopping_mall_order_status_histories` and exposed through `statusHistories` for audit and timeline views.

item_count.description:
Total count of order line items at the time of order confirmation.

This denormalized value reflects the number of rows in `shopping_mall_order_items` for this order and is used for quick listing and sanity checks in administrative tools.

grand_total_amount.description:
Total amount charged to the customer for this order in `currency_code`.

The value includes item subtotals, discounts, shipping fees, surcharges, and taxes according to the monetary snapshot flagged as final. It provides the canonical payable total for high‑level reporting and reconciliation.

placed_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer confirmed checkout and the order was created.

Business workflows treat this as the moment the order entered the system for lifespan calculations, SLA tracking, and chronological reporting.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order row was first persisted in the database.

Usually equal to or very close to `placed_at`, but kept separate for strict database‑level auditing and to distinguish business confirmation time from physical persistence.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this order record was last updated.

Any change to header attributes such as status, monetary summary, or associations to related entities (for example, cart reference) should update this field.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this order.

When null the order is active and visible in normal administrative views. When set, the order is logically removed from standard listings but retained for legal, audit, or analytical purposes.

customer.description:
Summary of the registered customer who owns this order, when the order is associated with a customer account.

The summary is derived from `shopping_mall_customers` and exposes key identity and status fields that are safe and useful for administrative inspection. When the order was placed as a guest checkout, this property is null and the `guestUser` property is used instead.

guestUser.description:
Summary of the guest user that owns this order when the order is not linked to a registered customer account.

The summary is derived from `shopping_mall_guestusers` and provides minimal identity context such as device or external references without implying full account status. When the order is owned by a registered customer, this field is null and the `customer` property is used instead.

items.description:
Array of detailed order line items that make up this order.

Each element corresponds to a row in `shopping_mall_order_items` and contains SKU snapshots, quantities, and line‑level monetary amounts. The collection gives a complete view of what the customer purchased at confirmation time without requiring additional queries.

priceSnapshots.description:
Historical monetary snapshots for this order.

Each entry represents a decomposed breakdown of subtotals, discounts, shipping fees, surcharges, taxes, and total amounts at a given point in time, based on `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots`. At most one snapshot per order is marked as final and is considered the authoritative monetary summary.

statusHistories.description:
Chronological history of status transitions for this order.

Records mirror rows from `shopping_mall_order_status_histories` and are used by administrative clients to inspect the lifecycle of an order, including who caused each change, the previous and new statuses, and business reasons.

shipments.description:
List of shipment headers associated with this order.

Each shipment corresponds to a row in `shopping_mall_shipments` and represents a fulfillment unit, typically scoped to a single seller and destination. Nested shipment items expose which order items and SKUs are allocated to each shipment, enabling support staff to track multi‑seller and multi‑parcel deliveries.

payments.description:
Logical payments created for this order.

Entries map to `shopping_mall_order_payments` and summarize payable amounts, captured and refunded totals, chosen payment methods, and business‑level payment status. Multiple payments support partial or split payment scenarios and provide the backbone for refund and chargeback handling.

paymentStatusHistories.description:
Status history records for all payments belonging to this order.

These entries are derived from `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories` and allow administrators to examine how payment state evolved over time, including provider status changes and manual overrides.

refunds.description:
Refund operations executed against payments for this order.

Elements correspond to `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` and summarize requested, approved, and actually refunded amounts along with statuses and reasons. Nested refund items give item‑level breakdowns when applicable.

disputes.description:
Dispute cases associated with this order.

Each entry provides a summary view over a row in `shopping_mall_disputes`, exposing identifiers, type, severity, status, and core timestamps. Administrative tools use this list to quickly see whether the order is involved in higher‑level disputes, with full dispute details retrievable via dedicated dispute APIs.

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new customer‑facing order.

This DTO encapsulates all business data required to convert a transient cart or set of SKU selections into a durable order header together with its subsidiary entities such as line items and initial monetary snapshot.

It is intended for customer‑facing checkout flows and therefore omits system‑managed identifiers and timestamps, while requiring enough information to validate catalog visibility, inventory, payment configuration, and shipping options before persisting an order.

Authentication and session context are responsible for determining the owning customer or guest user. The caller MUST NOT provide customer or guest identity IDs in this DTO; those relations are populated by the backend based on the authenticated actor.

cart_id.description:
Identifier of the cart from which this order is being created, when applicable.

When provided, it should reference a row in `shopping_mall_carts` that belongs to the authenticated customer or guest session. The backend uses this link for validation, migration, and audit; when the order is built directly from an ad‑hoc set of items, this field may be null.

currency_code.description:
Currency code in which the order should be denominated.

This must be a valid ISO 4217 code and must match the currency used for pricing of the SKUs and surcharges in the request. The backend will reject combinations that violate catalog or configuration rules.

items.description:
Array of line items that the customer is purchasing in this order.

Each element describes a specific SKU, quantity, and optional line‑level pricing hints. The backend validates these items against catalog, visibility, and inventory rules, then persists authoritative `shopping_mall_order_items` rows and derives monetary snapshots from them.

shipping_address_id.description:
Identifier of the customer shipping address to use for this order, when referencing a previously saved address.

This should reference a row in `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` that belongs to the authenticated customer. When the client provides an inline, non‑saved address snapshot instead, this field is null and `shipping_address_snapshot` is used.

shipping_address_snapshot.description:
Inline snapshot of shipping address details to be used for this order when not referencing a saved address.

The backend persists this snapshot into `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` or a related snapshot table tied to the order so that changes to saved addresses do not retroactively change historical orders.

shipping_method_id.description:
Identifier of the shipping method chosen for this order.

The value references `shopping_mall_shipping_methods.id` and must be compatible with the destination region, items in the basket, and platform configuration. When business rules automatically determine shipping methods, this field may be null and computed server‑side.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method configuration that the customer has selected for initial payment.

The value references `shopping_mall_payment_methods.id` and indicates which payment orchestration path should be used. In flows where the payment method is chosen later, this field may be null and filled during payment initiation.

buyer_memo.description:
Optional free‑form note from the buyer to the seller or platform regarding this order.

Common uses include delivery instructions or additional context that should be visible in seller and fulfillment tools. The backend may apply length limits according to platform policy.

platform_note.description:
Optional internal note from the platform or automated systems stored at order creation time.

Although not typically provided by customer‑facing clients, this field can be used by internal flows to tag orders with risk or campaign information from the outset.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a guest user identity in the shoppingMall platform.

This summary DTO is used in list views, references, and contexts where only identification and high-level lifecycle timestamps of a guest user are required.
It intentionally omits any sensitive implementation details while preserving enough information for analytics, debugging, and cross-entity navigation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_guestusers` table and is used to join with guest sessions, temporary carts, wishlists, and risk-related records.
External systems and internal services use this identifier when they need to correlate multiple guest-related artifacts over time.

external_reference.description:
Optional external or device-based reference linked to this guest user.

Typical values include cookie identifiers, device fingerprints, or other privacy-aware correlation keys used to group anonymous browsing behavior.
When `null`, the guest was created without any stable external reference or the reference has been cleared according to privacy rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest user identity was created.

This value reflects the first time the platform recognized a new guest identity, such as first cart interaction or similar pre-registration activity.
It is stored directly from the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_guestusers` and is useful for lifecycle and retention analysis.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user record was last updated.

Changes may be triggered by new linked sessions, merges, risk annotations, or cleanup operations that touch the guest identity.
This field maps to the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_guestusers` and helps operators understand the recency of activity associated with the guest.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the guest user identity.

When non-null, the guest record is considered logically deleted for most business flows, while still preserved for historical reference and integrity of related entities such as sessions or carts.
This value maps to the `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_guestusers` and is important for compliance and data-retention oriented reporting.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
Shopping mall order line item representing a single purchased SKU within a customer-facing order.

This DTO is a read-optimized projection over the shopping_mall_order_items table, enriched with contextual references to its parent order, the purchased SKU, and the responsible seller that are required for detailed order item views in customer channels.

The entity captures immutable monetary and product snapshot data at the time of order confirmation, while also exposing stable identifiers and audit timestamps to support history views, analytics, and troubleshooting workflows. Fulfillment events such as shipments remain accessible via shipment-centric endpoints rather than being embedded here as unbounded aggregations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this order item record.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_order_items.id and is used as the technical identifier for cross-entity references and internal processing.

Clients should treat this value as an opaque identifier and use it together with the parent order context when necessary for lookups and troubleshooting.

line_number.description:
Sequential position of this line item within its parent order, starting from 1.

This mirrors shopping_mall_order_items.line_number and is primarily used to ensure stable ordering of lines in order detail views, exports, and customer communication.

Consumers may rely on this value for display ordering but should not attempt to infer business meaning beyond its sequencing role.

product_name.description:
Snapshot of the product name at the time of order confirmation.

This value is copied from the catalog into shopping_mall_order_items.product_name so that historical order representations remain stable even when product names change later in the catalog.

It is intended for display in customer order detail screens, invoices, and support tooling without requiring live joins to the product catalog tables.

sku_name.description:
Snapshot of the SKU or variant label at the time of order confirmation.

This mirrors shopping_mall_order_items.sku_name and allows customers and operators to understand the chosen variant (for example size or color) without additional catalog joins.

The field is immutable from the order perspective and serves as a historical record even if the live SKU label evolves over time.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the SKU purchased on this order line.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_order_items.quantity and is expected to be a positive integer that represents the committed purchase quantity at the time of order confirmation.

Downstream fulfillment logic uses this quantity as the basis for validating partial shipments and returns, while analytics systems rely on it when computing unit-level metrics.

unit_price.description:
Per-unit selling price for the SKU at the time of order confirmation, in the order currency.

This mirrors shopping_mall_order_items.unit_price and is captured before any line-level discounts are applied to support transparent pricing, tax calculations, and audit scenarios.

Clients should prefer this field, together with quantity and discount information, when reconstructing detailed monetary breakdowns for the line item.

line_subtotal.description:
Subtotal for this order line before any discounts, calculated as quantity multiplied by unit_price.

This is stored in shopping_mall_order_items.line_subtotal to provide a stable monetary snapshot that can be reused for reporting, reconciliation, and invoice generation without recomputing from raw inputs.

Consumers should treat this value as immutable historical data tied to the moment of order confirmation.

line_discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied to this line across all discount mechanisms at the time of order confirmation.

This mirrors shopping_mall_order_items.line_discount_amount and normally aggregates seller-funded and platform-funded discounts that directly affect this line.

Analytics and financial systems use this value to attribute discount spend, while UI clients can show per-line discount information alongside the base price.

line_total.description:
Final payable amount for this order line after line-level discounts, but before order-level fees, surcharges, and taxes.

This mirrors shopping_mall_order_items.line_total and participates in the derived order-level monetary snapshots stored in shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.

For most customer-facing use cases, this is the primary per-line amount displayed as the effective price paid for the quantity of this SKU.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item record was created in the database.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_order_items.created_at and typically matches the order confirmation time for the parent order.

The field is useful for chronological auditing, debugging of late mutations, and time-based analytics of order composition.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item record was last updated.

This mirrors shopping_mall_order_items.updated_at and reflects any permissible post-creation changes such as metadata adjustments that do not violate pricing or inventory invariants.

It helps operators and automated processes detect recent changes and is typically used only for operational and diagnostic purposes.

order.description:
Summary representation of the parent order that owns this line item.

This object provides customer-facing context such as the business order code, current status, currency, and key timestamps without embedding full order-level collections.

It is derived from shopping_mall_orders and related snapshot tables and is modeled as IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary to prevent recursive expansion and to keep the order item detail DTO focused on line-level concerns.

sku.description:
Summary representation of the purchased SKU for this order line.

This object provides catalog context such as the SKU code and human-readable name derived from shopping_mall_skus and related catalog tables, modeled as IShoppingMallSku.ISummary to avoid deep catalog recursion in the order item view.

Clients can use this summary to navigate to product detail pages or internal catalog tools when more comprehensive SKU information is required.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller responsible for fulfilling this order line.

This reference is resolved via the mapping defined in shopping_mall_order_item_sellers and provides essential seller identity and status information while keeping the embedded DTO lightweight.

It allows customer-facing and operational UIs to show which merchant is responsible for the line item without introducing back-references that could cause circular schemas.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for a single order line item to be included when creating an order.

Each object specifies which SKU is being purchased, in what quantity, and optional hints for pricing or naming snapshots.

The backend validates the SKU against catalog, visibility, and inventory rules, then persists authoritative line item rows and computes monetary values based on current pricing configuration.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU that the customer is purchasing on this line.

This value must reference an existing `shopping_mall_skus.id` that is visible and sellable according to catalog rules at the time of order creation.

quantity.description:
Quantity of this SKU to purchase on this line.

The value must be a positive integer and is subject to per‑SKU and per‑order quantity limits enforced by the backend.

IShoppingMallOrderPriceSnapshot.description:
Order-level monetary snapshot record capturing a decomposed view of how an order’s payable amount was constructed at a specific point in time.

This type maps directly to the `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots` Prisma model and is used in read operations where clients need to inspect historical pricing states for an order, such as customer support views, dispute handling workflows, or financial audit tools.

Each snapshot records individual monetary components including item subtotal, discounts, shipping fees, surcharges, taxes, and a grand total, along with a flag indicating whether the snapshot is the final authoritative state and a creation timestamp for chronological ordering.

id.description:
Primary key for the order price snapshot row.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes one price snapshot from all others across the platform and is typically represented as a UUID string in external APIs.

item_subtotal_amount.description:
Sum of item-level subtotals for the order at the time of the snapshot.

This amount reflects the aggregated pre-discount merchandise value across all order items, calculated before applying any line-level or order-level discounts.

item_discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied at line level across all items when this snapshot was recorded.

This includes discounts funded by sellers, the platform, or campaigns that are modeled as per-item reductions rather than as global order-level adjustments.

order_discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied at the overall order level in this snapshot.

Typical contributors include coupon codes, cart-level promotions, or other promotions that are calculated on the overall order rather than per line item.

shipping_fee_amount.description:
Total shipping fee amount charged to the customer in this snapshot.

This may be zero when free-shipping promotions or seller policies eliminate shipping costs, or when shipping is absorbed entirely by the platform or merchant.

payment_surcharge_amount.description:
Total payment method surcharge charged to the customer in this snapshot, if applicable.

This value can represent either platform-owned payment fees or pass-through surcharges that arise from specific payment instruments, as dictated by payment configuration policies.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount calculated for the order at the time of the snapshot.

This may be zero for tax-exempt customers, products, or jurisdictions, or when the platform operates in an environment where tax is handled externally.

grand_total_amount.description:
Total amount to be charged to the customer according to this snapshot.

Conceptually, this value equals the item subtotal minus line and order discounts plus shipping fees, surcharges, and taxes, subject to the platform’s rounding rules and currency handling implementation.

is_final.description:
Flag indicating whether this snapshot represents the final confirmed monetary state for the order.

Business logic typically treats the most recent snapshot with `is_final = true` as the authoritative view for reporting, reconciliation, and customer-facing price displays.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was created in the database.

This value is used to order snapshots chronologically, assist in time-based reporting, and provide an audit trail of how the order’s pricing state evolved over its lifecycle.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.description:
Represents a single historical status transition for an order in the shopping mall platform.

Each record documents how an order's high-level business status changed at a specific point in time, including the previous status, the new status, and when the change occurred. The history row is always associated with exactly one order and may optionally reference the actor type that triggered the transition (customer, seller, or admin).

These records are used to build detailed audit trails, debug order lifecycle issues, and support compliance reporting without overloading the main order header table. They allow customer support tools, seller consoles, and administrative back offices to inspect the precise sequence of status changes over the lifetime of an order.

In addition to raw foreign key identifiers for internal joins, the schema also exposes association objects for the customer, seller, and admin actors so that consumers can access actor context without performing additional API calls.

id.description:
Primary key for the order status history row.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes a single status transition entry across the entire system and is used when fetching or updating a specific history record.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Reference to the order whose status changed.

This field links the history row to the corresponding order record in the `shopping_mall_orders` table and is used to group a sequence of status transitions for the same order.

Because the order typically aggregates its own status history in collections, this parent foreign key is intentionally kept as a scalar identifier rather than a nested order object to avoid circular references.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Optional reference to the customer who triggered this status change, when applicable.

This field is populated when the status transition originates from a customer action, such as placing an order, confirming delivery, or requesting a cancellation. It is null when the change is made by a seller, admin, or automated system.

For consumer-facing APIs, use the `customer` association object instead of this raw identifier whenever actor details are required.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Optional reference to the seller who triggered this status change, when applicable.

This identifier is set when a seller-side operation causes the status change, such as confirming shipment, rejecting an order, or updating fulfillment information. It is null when the actor is a customer, admin, or automated workflow.

For read models, prefer the `seller` association object over this raw UUID when displaying seller information.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Optional reference to the admin who triggered this status change, when applicable.

The field is used when administrative tools or governance workflows apply or correct statuses on orders, such as resolving disputes, applying manual overrides, or performing data corrections.

Client applications should use the `admin` association object to render admin context instead of relying on this identifier alone.

from_status.description:
Previous status value before this transition.

This value represents the order status immediately before the change captured by this record. It is null when this row represents the very first status assigned to the order, such as the initial creation status.

to_status.description:
New status value applied to the order as a result of this transition.

The value mirrors the business-level status values used in `shopping_mall_orders.current_status`, such as `PENDING`, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`, or `DELIVERED`. It defines the effective status of the order after the transition is applied.

reason_code.description:
Optional machine-readable reason code for the status change.

Typical values include tokens such as `payment_confirmed`, `customer_cancelled`, `system_timeout`, or other structured identifiers used by internal systems and reports to classify why the status changed.

reason_detail.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of why this status change occurred.

The text is intended for operators, support staff, and auditors, and can include free-form notes summarizing what happened, who requested it, and any contextual details that help interpret the transition.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change took effect from a business perspective.

This field reflects the effective time of the transition in the order lifecycle, which may differ from the persistence time if events are backfilled or corrected later.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this history row was persisted.

The value records when the system stored the status transition record in the database and can be used to reason about ingestion delays or replay operations.

customer.description:
Customer summary associated with this status change, when the transition was triggered by a customer actor.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_customer_id` and exposes a lightweight view of the customer so that clients can render actor context without a separate customer lookup.

The value is null when the status change did not originate from a customer, such as when it was performed by a seller, admin, or background process.

seller.description:
Seller summary associated with this status change, when the transition was triggered by a seller actor.

The association is resolved from `shopping_mall_seller_id` and provides a lightweight view of the seller account responsible for the change.

When the status change is not seller-driven, this field is null.

admin.description:
Admin summary associated with this status change, when the transition was triggered by an administrative actor.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_admin_id` and exposes basic administrator identity context for audit displays.

For customer- or seller-driven transitions, this field is null.

IShoppingMallShipment.description:
Shipment header entity representing a single fulfillment unit derived from customer orders in the shopping mall platform.

Each `IShoppingMallShipment` instance corresponds to one row in the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma model. The record captures high‑level logistics information such as a internal UUID, business-visible shipment code, current shipping status, carrier and tracking details, and key timestamps in the shipment lifecycle.

In addition to scalar header fields, this DTO also surfaces key association and composition relations needed for atomic read operations: the parent order summary, the responsible seller, the selected shipping method and shipping address snapshot, and the collection of shipment items that bind the shipment to concrete order items and SKUs.

id.description:
Primary key of the shipment header in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

This is an internal identifier generated by the database and used by internal systems. External APIs generally prefer `shipment_code` as the business-facing identifier, but `id` is still exposed in the DTO for debugging and cross‑service correlation when appropriate.

shipment_code.description:
Business-facing shipment code used to identify this shipment in URLs, UI screens, and operational tools.

The value maps to the `shipment_code` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and is unique across all shipments, as enforced by the table’s unique index. Administrative and seller-facing endpoints commonly use this code as a path parameter instead of the internal `id`.

shipping_status.description:
Current status of the shipment in its logistics lifecycle.

This field reflects the `shipping_status` column on `shopping_mall_shipments`. Common statuses include `pending`, `preparing`, `ready_for_pickup`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, and `cancelled`. Concrete values and transition rules are governed by business policies and validation logic in the service layer.

oneOf.description:
Non-null carrier name for this shipment.

Represents the shipping carrier or logistics provider responsible for physical delivery, such as a parcel service or local courier company.
Null value when no carrier has been assigned yet or when the shipment type does not use a named carrier.

carrier_name.description:
Name of the carrier handling this shipment when known.

The value corresponds to the nullable `carrier_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`. It is typically set once the shipment is handed off to a logistics provider.

oneOf.description:
Non-null tracking number assigned by the carrier.

The value can be used in external tracking portals or internal integrations to trace shipment progress.
Null value when tracking is not yet available or not applicable for this shipment.

tracking_number.description:
Carrier-assigned tracking identifier associated with the shipment, when available.

This field mirrors the nullable `tracking_number` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and may remain null for shipments that are not yet shipped or for carriers that do not support tracking.

oneOf.description:
Expected ship date/time as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

Represents when the shipment is planned to leave the seller or warehouse, supporting SLA and expectation management.
Null value when no planned ship date has been scheduled or recorded.

expected_ship_date.description:
Planned date and time when the shipment is expected to leave the seller or warehouse.

This field maps to the nullable `expected_ship_date` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and is used for operational planning and customer communication.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the shipment actually entered the carrier network or was marked as shipped.

Set when the fulfillment process marks the shipment as physically handed off or dispatched.
Null value when the shipment has not yet been shipped or the event has not been recorded.

shipped_at.description:
Date and time when the shipment was first marked as shipped or handed over to the carrier.

This value mirrors the nullable `shipped_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and is a key milestone for tracking delivery performance.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when delivery to the customer was confirmed.

Recorded once the shipment is successfully delivered at the destination as reported by the carrier or internal systems.
Null value when the shipment has not yet been delivered or when delivery confirmation is not available.

delivered_at.description:
Date and time when the shipment was confirmed delivered to the customer, when applicable.

This field maps to the nullable `delivered_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and is used to close out the shipment lifecycle and support delivery-related KPIs.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment header row was created in the database.

The value comes directly from the non-null `created_at` column on `shopping_mall_shipments` and allows callers to understand when the shipment was initially registered.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment header row was last updated.

Sourced from the non-null `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`, this field reflects the most recent modification to shipment header fields such as status, tracking information, or carrier details.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when this shipment was soft-deleted.

Used to hide shipments from normal operational views while preserving them for historical and audit purposes.
Null value when the shipment is active and has not been soft-deleted.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the shipment header, when applicable.

This corresponds to the nullable `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and is used by the application’s soft-delete and archival mechanisms.

order.description:
Summary view of the customer-facing order that this shipment fulfills.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key and the order’s business `order_code`. Exposing the order summary here allows clients to navigate from shipments back to their originating orders without additional lookups.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller responsible for fulfilling this shipment.

The data is resolved from the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key pointing to the seller account that owns the items being shipped. Surfacing this association enables admin and seller tools to attribute fulfillment activity to the correct seller entity.

shipping_method.description:
Summary of the shipping method configuration applied to this shipment.

This association corresponds to the `shopping_mall_shipping_method_id` foreign key and exposes the customer-visible shipping service (for example, standard, express, or same-day) selected by the checkout or fulfillment workflow.

shipping_address.description:
Immutable snapshot of the destination shipping address used for this shipment.

The snapshot is resolved from the `shopping_mall_shipping_address_id` foreign key and typically mirrors the shipping address snapshot also used for the parent order. Exposing it here allows clients to display the full delivery destination details directly from the shipment resource.

items.description:
Collection of shipment item rows that bind this shipment header to specific order items and SKUs.

Each element represents a `shopping_mall_shipment_items` row and specifies which order line and SKU are being shipped and in what quantity. This composition enables clients to see the complete contents of the shipment in a single API call.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.description:
Shipment item entity representing the association between a shipment header and a specific order item and SKU.

Each record corresponds to a concrete quantity of a particular order item SKU that is allocated to a shipment in the shoppingMall logistics domain. It binds together the shipment header from `shopping_mall_shipments`, the purchased line from `shopping_mall_order_items`, and the inventory variant from `shopping_mall_skus` through foreign key identifiers.

This entity is used by fulfillment and operations flows to reconcile shipped quantities against ordered quantities without duplicating catalog or pricing information. It participates in partial shipments, backorders, and complex multi-seller or multi-warehouse scenarios while preserving a clear audit trail of what was shipped in each shipment unit. Client applications that need rich shipment, order item, or SKU context are expected to load those entities separately using the corresponding identifiers rather than relying on embedded summary objects.

id.description:
Primary key for the shipment item row.

This identifier is generated by the database layer and uniquely distinguishes each shipment item within the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table. It is used throughout internal services and APIs as the stable reference for this shipment item.

Clients receive this value in read responses but must never attempt to provide or override it in create or update requests.

shopping_mall_shipment_id.description:
Identifier of the parent shipment header that this item belongs to.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_shipment_id` column in the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table and references `shopping_mall_shipments.id`. It ties the line item to a specific shipment unit for fulfillment, tracking, and reconciliation.

When combined with other keys such as the order item and SKU identifiers, this field allows services to query all items contained in a shipment and to reconstruct shipment-level compositions for operational dashboards.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Identifier of the order line item being shipped by this shipment item.

This field maps to the `shopping_mall_order_item_id` column and references the primary key of a row in `shopping_mall_order_items`. It provides the link back to the original purchase snapshot that defined the product, SKU, quantity, and monetary amounts.

Fulfillment and reconciliation logic use this identifier to ensure that shipped quantities do not exceed the ordered quantity and to show which portions of an order line have already been shipped or remain outstanding.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU variant included in this shipment item.

This property corresponds to the `shopping_mall_sku_id` column in `shopping_mall_shipment_items` and references `shopping_mall_skus.id`. It identifies the exact catalog variant that was picked and packed for this shipment line.

By following this identifier to the SKU entity, services can obtain stable information about attributes like size, color, and inventory state without embedding that data directly in the shipment item record.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the order item allocated to this shipment.

The value must be a positive integer and cannot exceed the remaining unshipped quantity for the corresponding order item in `shopping_mall_order_items`. It represents how many units of the ordered SKU are included in this particular shipment unit.

Fulfillment logic uses this value to compute shipped totals, support partial shipments, and ensure that the sum of shipment quantities across all related shipment items does not surpass the ordered quantity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment item row was created.

The timestamp is recorded by the persistence layer at insertion time and reflects when the shipment item first entered the system. It is stored using a precise time format that preserves timezone and ordering semantics.

Clients can use this value for chronological views, auditing, and reconciliation workflows but must treat it as read-only metadata.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment item row was last updated.

Whenever mutable fields such as quantity or operational metadata change, this timestamp is refreshed to reflect the latest modification time. It is managed by the underlying database or ORM layer rather than being set directly by API callers.

This field supports audit requirements, conflict detection, and troubleshooting by allowing consumers to see when the shipment item was most recently altered.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.description:
Logical payment entity for a customer-facing order in the shopping mall platform.

This type models a single row in the `shopping_mall_order_payments` Prisma table, which represents a business-level payment obligation associated with one order stored in `shopping_mall_orders`. Each record captures how much should be paid, how much has actually been captured, and how much has been refunded or chargebacked over time.

The entity is tightly linked to three key actors in the payment domain: the owning customer in `shopping_mall_customers`, the target order in `shopping_mall_orders`, and the configured payment method in `shopping_mall_payment_methods`. It is also referenced by subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts`, `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories`, `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`, and `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` that track attempts, lifecycle transitions, refunds, and disputes.

This DTO is used as a detailed response shape in customer and admin payment detail views and must not expose any authentication secrets. It reflects the current state of a logical payment, including monetary aggregates, currency, and business status used to drive order eligibility to ship and to process refunds or chargebacks. Association context such as order, customer, or payment method details should be retrieved through dedicated APIs using the identifiers exposed by this type.

id.description:
Primary key of the logical order payment.

This value corresponds to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_order_payments` table and uniquely identifies a single logical payment across the entire platform.

It is used by admin and customer-facing APIs as a stable identifier when fetching or referencing specific payment records.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order that this logical payment belongs to.

This field maps to the `shopping_mall_order_id` column of `shopping_mall_order_payments` and references the primary key of a row in `shopping_mall_orders`.

It is kept as a raw UUID so that services and analytics jobs can efficiently join or filter on order-level identifiers when working directly with payment records.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who owns the order and the payment.

This field corresponds to the `shopping_mall_customer_id` column and references the primary key in `shopping_mall_customers`.

It is primarily used server-side and in administrative tooling to enforce ownership checks and to join payments with customer accounts for reporting, risk analysis, and account history views.

shopping_mall_payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method used for this logical payment.

This value maps to the `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` column and references the primary key in `shopping_mall_payment_methods` that describes the configured payment instrument or method.

It allows the platform to link payments back to their configuration, including surcharges defined in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`, for reconciliation and analytics.

payment_sequence.description:
Sequence number of this payment within the order, starting from 1.

This field comes from the `payment_sequence` column and is combined with `shopping_mall_order_id` to form a unique business key within a single order. It allows multiple logical payments per order, representing partial payments, split payments, or retries with different methods.

APIs such as `/shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId}/payments/{paymentSequence}` rely on this value to address one specific payment without exposing internal identifiers.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for this payment.

This value maps to the `currency_code` column and records the three-letter currency code (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, `KRW`) in which all monetary amounts of this payment are denominated.

Clients and reporting systems use this field to format amounts correctly and to aggregate payments per currency.

payable_amount.description:
Total amount that should be paid for this logical payment in `currency_code`.

This field corresponds to the `payable_amount` column and represents the gross amount that the platform expects to collect for this payment, including items, taxes, and any customer-facing fees that belong to this payment.

It is used as the baseline when reconciling captured, refunded, and chargebacked amounts and when evaluating whether an order is fully paid.

captured_amount.description:
Total amount that has been successfully captured or confirmed as paid.

This value comes from the `captured_amount` column and tracks how much of the `payable_amount` has actually been collected so far through successful payment attempts.

It is updated as gateways confirm captures, and it drives business rules that determine whether an order can proceed to shipment and fulfillment.

refunded_amount.description:
Total amount that has been refunded for this payment across all completed refunds.

This property maps to the `refunded_amount` column and aggregates the sum of all refund operations registered against this payment, typically via records in `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` and `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items`.

It is used to derive statuses like partially refunded or fully refunded and to ensure that refunds do not exceed the originally captured amount.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total amount that has been chargebacked for this payment.

This field represents the value of chargebacks recorded against the payment, stored in the `chargeback_amount` column and usually backed by rows in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`.

It helps risk and finance teams understand financial exposure due to disputes and is factored into business status and revenue reporting.

business_status.description:
Business-level status of the payment lifecycle.

This string comes from the `business_status` column and encodes the current logical status of the payment, such as `pending`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `chargeback`, or `cancelled`.

Services and front-end clients use this field to drive UI states, permitted actions, and eligibility checks for shipping, refunding, or further processing.

provider_status_code.description:
Provider-specific status code summarizing the last known gateway state, or null when not available.

This value corresponds to the nullable `provider_status_code` column and may carry compact status codes or state identifiers returned by the external payment provider.

It is primarily used for debugging, reconciliation, and support tooling and is not meant to be interpreted directly by end users.

provider_reference.description:
Reference identifier from the payment provider for this logical payment, or null.

This field maps to the nullable `provider_reference` column and typically stores values such as payment intent IDs, transaction IDs, or similar provider-side primary keys.

It enables correlation between internal payment records and provider systems during reconciliation, dispute handling, and support investigations.

metadata.description:
Optional serialized metadata associated with this payment.

This property represents the nullable `metadata` column and commonly stores structured JSON or other serialized data containing provider details, internal diagnostic notes, or integration-specific attributes.

Its exact structure is platform-defined and should be treated as opaque by generic clients, but it remains valuable for internal tooling and observability.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment record was created.

This field aligns with the non-nullable `created_at` column and records when the logical payment row was first inserted into the database.

It is used for timeline views, auditing, and reporting, as well as for filtering or ordering payment lists by creation time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment record was last updated.

This property corresponds to the `updated_at` column and changes whenever mutable fields such as `business_status`, `provider_status_code`, or monetary aggregates are updated.

It allows clients and jobs to detect recent activity, implement optimistic concurrency strategies, and build change histories in combination with status history tables.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusHistory.description:
Detailed history row describing a single status transition for an order payment.

Each instance represents one atomic change of the business payment status and, optionally, the provider status code. It forms part of an append‑only audit trail that describes how the payment evolved from initiation to completion, failure, refund, or any other terminal state.

These records are primarily used by administrators, risk and finance teams, and debugging tools, rather than by regular end‑users, and they provide both structured codes and free‑form explanations for each transition.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the status history record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories` table and is used to reference this specific transition in audit logs and admin tools.

orderPayment.description:
Logical order payment whose status changed in this history row.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` foreign key and exposes a lightweight summary of the parent payment so that auditors and admin tools can understand the context of the transition without issuing additional queries.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the administrator who performed a manual status change.

This references `shopping_mall_admins.id` and is present only when a human admin explicitly triggered or approved the transition.
Null when the status transition was performed automatically by the system or by an external provider callback with no direct admin actor.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Optional identifier of the admin that triggered this status transition.

For system‑driven or provider‑driven transitions this field remains null, while for manual overrides or investigations it records the responsible administrator.

oneOf.description:
Non‑null previous business‑level status value before the change.

Represents the prior high‑level payment state that this transition is leaving, such as `"pending"`, `"authorized"`, or `"failed"`.
Null when this is the first recorded status for the payment and there is no prior business status to reference.

previous_business_status.description:
Business status value before this transition occurred.

The field may be null for the very first status history row and is otherwise used to reconstruct the complete timeline of business‑level state changes.

new_business_status.description:
New business‑level status value after this transition.

This captures the resulting high‑level payment state such as `"authorized"`, `"captured"`, `"refunded"`, or `"cancelled"`, and is the primary indicator of what changed in this history row.

oneOf.description:
Non‑null provider‑specific status code before the transition.

This may reflect gateway‑level states such as `"AUTHORIZED"` or `"PENDING_CAPTURE"` depending on the external integration.
Null when no provider‑specific status was recorded prior to this transition or for the first status row.

previous_provider_status_code.description:
Provider‑specific status code prior to the change, when available.

This field enables low‑level inspection of provider state transitions beyond the normalized business statuses stored in the payment record.

oneOf.description:
Non‑null provider‑specific status code after the transition.

The value depends on the connected payment gateway and can be used for reconciliation or advanced troubleshooting.
Null when the provider did not supply a status code or when the transition does not affect provider‑side state.

new_provider_status_code.description:
Provider‑specific status code after the transition, if supplied by the external payment service.

Combined with the previous provider status code, this allows reconstruction of the low‑level state machine as seen by the gateway.

oneOf.description:
Non‑null structured reason code explaining why this transition happened.

Typical examples include values such as `"payment_confirmed"`, `"refund_completed"`, or `"manual_override"`, and the exact vocabulary is managed by business policy configuration.
Null when no structured reason code is associated with this status change or when only a free‑form message is available.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code describing the cause of the status change.

It is primarily used for analytics, policy enforcement, and consistent reporting across different payment providers and automation flows.

oneOf.description:
Non‑null free‑form message or note providing human‑readable context for the transition.

This may contain user‑visible explanations, internal notes, or system‑generated messages that complete the meaning of the `reason_code`.
Null when no additional textual explanation was provided at the time of the transition.

reason_message.description:
Optional human‑readable message giving more detail about why the payment status changed.

This field is especially helpful for operations teams performing manual investigations and for long‑term audit trails.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change record was created.

The value corresponds to the moment the system persisted the transition event to durable storage, forming part of the ordered audit timeline.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this history record was last updated.

In most implementations the row is effectively immutable and `updated_at` will equal `created_at`, but the field allows future extensions where metadata may evolve.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.description:
Represents a single refund transaction executed against a logical order payment in the shoppingMall platform.

This entity models refund activity at the payment level, tying directly to a parent record in `shopping_mall_order_payments` through the `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` foreign key and distinguishing multiple refunds on the same payment through the `refund_sequence` column. Each row captures the lifecycle of one refund attempt or process, including requested, approved, and actually refunded amounts, status transitions, and gateway references.

The record is used by financial operations, risk teams, and dispute tooling to audit refund flows, reconcile with payment providers, and enforce business constraints derived from policy models. It is the authoritative source for monetary totals refunded against a payment and participates in calculations that determine the remaining refundable balance for subsequent refund operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` table and is generated by the system on creation. It is used as an immutable identifier when joining to analytical tables, audit logs, and external reporting pipelines.

Client code should treat this value as opaque and never attempt to infer business meaning from it.

shopping_mall_order_payment_id.description:
Identifier of the logical order payment that this refund is applied to.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_refunds.shopping_mall_order_payment_id` and references `shopping_mall_order_payments.id`. Together with `refund_sequence`, it forms the business-level composite key that uniquely identifies a refund within a payment.

In external admin APIs, this value is typically provided as a path parameter (`orderPaymentId`) and may not be redundantly exposed as a mutable input field in create or update DTOs.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who approved or executed the refund, when applicable.

This field references `shopping_mall_admins.id` and links the refund to the administrative actor responsible for the decision or the operational execution. It may be null for system-initiated or automated refunds where no explicit admin user is recorded.

The value is set and updated exclusively by server-side business logic; client callers cannot arbitrarily assign or modify it.

oneOf.description:
Summary view of the administrator who approved or executed the refund.

This association is resolved from `shopping_mall_admin_id` and provides convenient access to the admin’s key identity fields – such as name, contact, and role – without requiring an additional lookup.

The field may be null when the refund was created or progressed by automated system processes that do not have a concrete admin account attached.
Null value when there is no concrete administrator associated with this refund, for example, for system-generated or automated refunds.

admin.description:
Administrator association providing contextual information about who approved or executed the refund.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key and exposes an `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary` object so that clients can display actor context alongside refund amounts and statuses in a single read operation.

When no concrete admin account is attached to the refund, this field is null, and consumers should treat the refund as system-driven or automated from a human actor perspective.

refund_sequence.description:
Sequence number of this refund for the given payment, starting from 1.

Within a single logical order payment (`shopping_mall_order_payments.id`), each refund is assigned a monotonically increasing `refund_sequence` beginning at 1. The pair `(shopping_mall_order_payment_id, refund_sequence)` is unique and enforced by the Prisma unique index.

This sequence is used in API paths such as `/payments/{orderPaymentId}/refunds/{refundSequence}` to reference individual refunds in a human-readable and deterministic way.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code in which this refund is denominated.

The value typically matches the currency of the parent payment and must follow the standard three-letter uppercase ISO 4217 format (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, `KRW`).

Downstream financial reconciliation and reporting processes rely on this code to aggregate and convert refund amounts correctly.

requested_amount.description:
Amount initially requested to be refunded at the business level.

This value reflects the amount that a customer, seller, or admin has requested to be returned to the payer. It is captured at the time of refund initiation before policy evaluation and provider interaction.

Business rules may limit this amount based on order totals, already-refunded amounts, and policy thresholds, and discrepancies between requested, approved, and refunded amounts are used for audit and dispute analysis.

approved_amount.description:
Amount that was approved for refund according to business policy.

This field records the monetary amount that internal policy checks, risk rules, or manual review have allowed to be refunded. It may be equal to or less than `requested_amount` depending on eligibility rules.

Approval amounts are used to drive subsequent payment gateway operations and are critical for ensuring that refunds do not exceed allowed limits for the underlying order payment.

refunded_amount.description:
Amount that the payment provider confirms has actually been refunded to the customer.

This value is typically updated after successful communication with the payment gateway or financial institution. It represents the final financial outcome and may be less than `approved_amount` if the provider partially processed the request.

Accounting, reconciliation, and KPI computations rely on this field as the definitive measure of refunded funds.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the refund transaction.

The status encodes the business and technical state of the refund, with documented examples including values such as `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `completed`, and `failed`. Implementations may use a constrained enumeration at the service layer to enforce valid transitions.

Downstream systems use this field to drive workflows, to decide whether additional actions are required, and to surface the refund state in administrative dashboards.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code associated with this refund.

When present, the value should map to a controlled vocabulary of refund reasons defined by the business, such as policy violation categories, product issues, or customer dissatisfaction codes.

Structured codes allow consistent aggregation, reporting, and policy enforcement across large volumes of refund data.

reason_message.description:
Optional free-text explanation describing the motivation for the refund.

This field is typically authored by customer support agents, operations staff, or automated systems, and provides human-readable context that complements the structured `reason_code`.

It is used heavily in audits, dispute handling, and customer communication, and may be localized according to the language preferences of agents or customers.

provider_reference.description:
Optional refund transaction reference from the external payment provider.

When available, this string contains the identifier used by the payment gateway or acquiring bank to track the refund transaction. Examples include PSP refund IDs, acquirer reference numbers, or bank transaction IDs.

This reference is essential for reconciliation, troubleshooting provider issues, and supporting chargeback or dispute processes involving external financial institutions.

metadata.description:
Optional serialized metadata with provider or internal diagnostic details.

Typical contents include JSON or key-value encoded snippets recording provider response payloads, internal flags, or risk signals related to this refund. The exact structure is left intentionally flexible to support evolving integration requirements.

Implementations should treat this field as opaque text at the API boundary while using strict internal validation and logging when writing values.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund record was created.

The value is stored as a timezone-aware timestamp and reflects when the refund entity first entered the system, either via an administrative action or an automated workflow.

It is immutable after creation and widely used for chronological sorting, SLA tracking, and historical reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund record was last updated.

Every successful modification to mutable fields on the refund should update this timestamp, enabling consumers to detect changes and implement optimistic concurrency control if required.

Operational tools and auditors rely on this value to understand when the latest decision or status change occurred for the refund.

IShoppingMallDispute.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a platform-level dispute case in the shopping mall ecosystem.

This DTO is optimized for list screens, dashboards, and cross-linking from related resources such as orders, refunds, risk cases, legal holds, admins, and SLA configurations. It exposes key identifiers, classification attributes, high-level lifecycle timestamps, and lightweight association objects, while omitting the full dispute timeline and evidence payloads.

The structure is mapped directly from the shopping_mall_disputes table and respects its relationships to orders, refund requests, payments, risk cases, legal holds, admins, and SLA configurations while remaining lightweight enough for high-volume queries and UI rendering.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute record.

This field corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_disputes table and is used to reference the dispute in all subsequent operations and links.

Clients should treat the value as an opaque UUID that uniquely identifies a dispute across the platform.

dispute_code.description:
Business-visible identifier for the dispute case.

The dispute code is used in admin tools, audits, and external communications to reference a dispute in a human-friendly way, for example when sharing a case with support or external partners.

It is unique across the platform and can be safely displayed to users and operators without exposing internal database identifiers.

type.description:
High-level dispute type describing the business nature of the case.

Typical values include categories such as payment_chargeback, refund_dispute, or policy_violation, but the platform may configure additional types.

Client applications can use this field to group or filter disputes in dashboards and workflow queues.

severity.description:
Business-defined severity level of the dispute.

Examples include low, medium, high, or critical, and the exact value set is governed by business configuration.

Severity is used to prioritize dispute handling and to drive SLA expectations or escalation rules.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the dispute.

Common statuses are open, under_investigation, resolved, and closed, but the concrete status model is defined by business policy.

Workflow engines and admin tools use this field to drive transitions, queues, and visibility of pending work.

summary.description:
Short human-readable summary describing the nature of the dispute.

This field provides a concise explanation suitable for list and overview screens so operators can understand the case at a glance.

When null, the dispute may still be in an early stage where no summary has been authored yet.

opened_at.description:
Timestamp when the dispute was opened.

This value marks the creation or activation time of the dispute lifecycle and is used to calculate durations, age, and SLA performance.

It is stored as a precise datetime in the underlying database and serialized using ISO 8601 format.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when a resolution decision was made for the dispute.

This field is null while the dispute is still being worked on or investigated, and is populated when a final decision has been recorded.

It is useful for measuring handling times and auditing the resolution phase of the lifecycle.

closed_at.description:
Timestamp when the dispute was fully closed.

Closing a dispute typically happens after resolution when no further actions are expected, such as after all follow-up tasks and communications have completed.

The value remains null until the dispute reaches that terminal stage.

order.description:
Primary order associated with this dispute when the case is order-centric.

This association is resolved from the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key in `shopping_mall_disputes` and provides a lightweight view of the customer-facing order.

When null, the dispute either does not relate to a specific order or the linkage has not been established.

refundRequest.description:
Refund request that triggered or is central to this dispute, when applicable.

The association is derived from the `shopping_mall_refund_request_id` column and surfaces a summary of the refund case so that operators can quickly navigate between dispute and refund contexts.

Null indicates that the dispute is not tied to a specific refund request.

paymentChargeback.description:
Payment chargeback record associated with this dispute, when the dispute is initiated by or tightly coupled to a chargeback.

This object is resolved from the `shopping_mall_payment_chargeback_id` foreign key and provides high-level insight into the chargeback case without requiring a separate detail call.

If null, no direct chargeback association exists for this dispute.

riskCase.description:
Risk case that tracks broader fraud or risk analysis related to this dispute.

The association originates from the `shopping_mall_risk_case_id` foreign key and exposes a summary view of the related risk case.

When null, the dispute is either not part of a formal risk case or linkage has not yet been configured.

legalHold.description:
Legal hold that constrains modifications or deletions related to this dispute data.

This association is resolved from the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_id` foreign key and indicates that legal or compliance requirements are in effect for this dispute and its related records.
