Null signifies that no legal hold currently applies to the dispute.

ownerAdmin.description:
Administrator currently assigned as the owner or primary handler of this dispute.

The association is based on the `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key and provides a compact summary of the admin account responsible for managing the case.

When null, the dispute may be unassigned, handled by a shared queue, or assigned via another mechanism outside of this field.

slaConfig.description:
SLA configuration governing this dispute, defining response or resolution targets.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` foreign key and surfaces a summary of the SLA rule set that applies to the case.

Null indicates that either a default SLA applies implicitly or no explicit SLA configuration has been associated with the dispute.

IShoppingMallShippingAddressSnapshot.ICr.description:
Inline shipping address snapshot used when creating an order without referencing a pre‑saved customer address.

This DTO captures the address and contact details as they were at order creation time so that subsequent changes to customer addresses do not retroactively alter historical orders.

Implementations typically persist this data into `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` or a related snapshot table tied to the order or shipment.

recipient_name.description:
Full name of the recipient who will receive the shipment at this address.

Used on shipping labels and in carrier interactions.

phone_number.description:
Primary phone number for the recipient.

Carriers and support staff rely on this number for delivery coordination or issue resolution; format validation may be applied according to regional rules.

country_code.description:
ISO country code for the destination country.

Must be compatible with configured shipping regions and available shipping methods.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code for the destination address.

Used by carriers and rate engines to determine routing and pricing.

state_or_region.description:
State, province, or primary administrative region component of the address.

Helps with regional compliance and shipping calculations.

city.description:
City, town, or locality component of the address.

Displayed on labels and used in carrier routing.

address_line1.description:
First line of the street address.

Typically contains building number and primary street information.

address_line2.description:
Second line of the street address for additional details.

Often used for apartment numbers, building names, or other supplemental information.

IShoppingMallOrder.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying mutable aspects of a confirmed shopping mall order header when exposed to customer-facing flows.

In the current specification, the customer update endpoint `/shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}` does not allow clients to alter any header fields that directly map to columns on the `shopping_mall_orders` table. Business rules route customer-visible transitions such as cancellations, status transitions, or monetary changes through dedicated endpoints and DTOs (for example, cancellation or refund requests and payment-related flows).

As a result, this DTO is intentionally defined as an empty object with no direct properties. It acts as a placeholder that can be extended in future iterations when additional, strictly controlled, customer-editable header fields (that map to real Prisma columns) are introduced. Until then, the absence of properties makes it explicit that the endpoint does not accept arbitrary header mutations and prevents phantom fields from diverging from the underlying `shopping_mall_orders` schema.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching, filtering, and paginating order items that belong to a specific order.

This type encapsulates the query semantics for retrieving `shopping_mall_order_items` rows under a resolved parent order identified by its business `order_code`. It is used by the PATCH `/shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/items` endpoint to let clients control page size, sort order, and lightweight item-level filters without exposing low-level database details.

Pagination parameters are designed to align with the global `IPage.IPagination` pattern so that response payloads and request bodies share consistent naming semantics (`current` and `limit`). Optional filter fields allow implementations to restrict results to subsets of items (for example, by SKU, item-level status, or fulfillment state) when such concepts exist in the underlying schema and business rules.

current.description:
1-based page index for the paginated result set.

This value determines which logical page of order item summaries should be returned and aligns with `IPage.IPagination.current` in the corresponding response wrapper. Values less than 1 are not valid at the contract level; callers should send `1` for the first page, and implementations may choose a default of `1` when the property is omitted.

limit.description:
Maximum number of order item summaries to return in a single page.

This value aligns with `IPage.IPagination.limit` in paginated responses and controls how many records are included in one page of results. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect the system from excessive payload sizes and may apply a sensible default when the property is omitted (for example, 20–100 items per page depending on UI and performance considerations).

sortBy.description:
Field name used for sorting the order items within the result set.

Typical supported values include identifiers such as `"created_at"`, `"line_number"`, or `"product_name"` depending on the underlying schema and indexing strategy. Unsupported field names should either be rejected with a validation error or mapped to a safe default sort order to preserve deterministic paging behavior.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the ordered item list.

Allowed logical values are `"asc"` for ascending and `"desc"` for descending ordering with respect to the chosen `sortBy` field. When omitted, the implementation should apply a domain-appropriate default, such as ascending by `line_number` so that items appear in their natural order within the order.

skuId.description:
Optional filter by the underlying SKU identifier associated with the order items.

This value typically corresponds to `shopping_mall_skus.id` and allows clients to narrow results to items that reference a particular SKU within the order. Implementations must ensure that filtered results remain constrained to the parent order resolved from `{orderCode}` and do not leak items from other orders, even if the same SKU appears elsewhere.

minQuantity.description:
Optional lower bound filter on item quantity.

When provided, only order items whose quantity is greater than or equal to this value should be returned. This can be useful for analytical tools or special handling flows where bulk quantities matter, such as identifying unusually large line items or high-volume purchases.

maxQuantity.description:
Optional upper bound filter on item quantity.

When provided, only order items whose quantity is less than or or equal to this value should be included in the result set. When combined with `minQuantity`, the two values define an inclusive quantity range filter applied to order items under the target order, allowing clients to focus on a specific range of purchase quantities.

status.description:
Optional filter for an order item–level status or business state, when such a concept is modeled in the implementation.

Typical usages include filtering to items that are considered active, cancelled, returned, or otherwise classified at the line level. The exact vocabulary is defined by the service implementation; clients should treat this field as a logical filter key rather than assuming a fixed set of values in this contract.

When omitted, all items that belong to the parent order and pass other filters are eligible to be returned, regardless of their item-level status.

fulfillmentState.description:
Optional filter representing the high-level fulfillment or shipping state of items under the order.

Implementations may support values such as `"pending_shipment"`, `"partially_shipped"`, `"shipped"`, or `"delivered"` depending on how shipment allocation is modeled between `shopping_mall_order_items` and `shopping_mall_shipments`. This filter allows clients to retrieve, for example, only items that still need shipping or only items that have already been shipped.

When omitted, items are not constrained by fulfillment state and results are determined solely by other filters such as SKU or quantity.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IUpdate.description:
Mutable subset of customer-facing metadata for a shopping mall order item that can be updated from the customer channel.

This DTO intentionally omits all identifiers, SKU references, quantities, and monetary snapshot fields from `shopping_mall_order_items` so that pricing, inventory, and legal invariants remain immutable after order confirmation.

It is used by customer-scoped endpoints such as `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/items/{orderItemId}` to adjust non-financial attributes only, for example personalization details or presentation flags that do not alter the economic substance of the order line.

customer_note.description:
Optional free-text note attached to this order line from the customer perspective.

This field can be used to capture instructions, contextual comments, or internal references that are safe to change without impacting pricing, inventory, or legal compliance. Implementations may persist this into a dedicated metadata column or structured JSON field associated with the order item.

Updates to this property must not modify any monetary values or SKU references associated with the order item.

gift_wrap.description:
Flag indicating whether this order line should be treated as gift-wrapped or receive special presentation handling.

This boolean is an example of a non-financial, customer-controlled preference that can be toggled after order creation as long as fulfillment rules allow it. Changing this value must not adjust historical price snapshots or underlying SKU assignments, though it may influence downstream fulfillment workflows or presentation labels.

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing a customer-facing order header in the shopping mall platform.

This type is optimized for use in order list views, dashboards, and lightweight embeddings where consumers need to see the identity, status, and monetary summary of an order without loading all underlying line items and related entities.

It maps directly to the `shopping_mall_orders` Prisma model and exposes only high-level, non-sensitive fields such as the business order code, currency, item count, monetary total, and lifecycle timestamps. Detailed line items, shipments, payments, and status histories are obtained via dedicated detail and relation APIs using the exposed identifiers and codes.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order record.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_orders` table and is used internally across subsystems to relate order items, shipments, payments, and analytics records back to this order.

order_code.description:
Business-facing order code shown to customers and used in communications.

This code is typically a human-friendly identifier such as a formatted sequence (for example `"2025-11-000123"`) and is unique at the platform level so that customers and support staff can reliably reference a specific order.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code used for all monetary values in this order.

Examples include `"USD"` or `"KRW"`. All amounts such as grand total and item prices are expressed in this currency for consistent presentation and reconciliation.

current_status.description:
Current high-level business status of the order.

Typical values include labels such as `"awaiting_payment"`, `"payment_confirmed"`, `"preparing_shipment"`, `"shipped"`, `"delivered"`, `"cancelled"`, or `"refunded"`. Detailed transition history is normalized into `shopping_mall_order_status_histories` but this field provides the latest user-visible state for filtering and display.

item_count.description:
Total number of order line items captured at the time of order confirmation.

This value is a denormalized convenience count derived from related `shopping_mall_order_items` records and is used for summary display and quick filtering without loading the full line item collection.

grand_total_amount.description:
Final monetary amount charged to the customer for this order in the order currency.

The value includes item subtotals, discounts, shipping fees, surcharges, and taxes, according to the business rules that were in effect at the moment the order was confirmed. It is suitable for display in order history lists and revenue summaries.

placed_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer confirmed checkout and the order was placed.

This is the primary business event time for the order lifecycle and is used for order history sorting, reporting, and SLA calculations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the order row was first persisted in the database.

In most flows this closely matches `placed_at`, but it is stored separately to preserve the exact persistence time used by database-level auditing and replication.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the order row was last updated.

This field changes when summary attributes such as the current status or denormalized counters are modified and is useful for monitoring recent changes to an order.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this order, if applicable.

When null, the order is considered active and appears in normal customer and operations views. When populated, the order is logically removed from standard listings but retained for audit, compliance, or reporting purposes.

IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a seller account on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is designed for list views, references in other entities, and analytics outputs where only high‑level identification and status are required. It intentionally omits authentication details and sensitive lifecycle metadata.

The summary makes it easy to associate aggregate metrics or operational entities, such as warehouses and inventory adjustments, with the owning seller.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller account.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the seller record in the database and is used as the stable reference across all seller‑related entities.

Clients should treat the identifier as opaque and must not attempt to infer business meaning from its structure.

email.description:
Business contact email address used as the seller’s login and primary communication channel.

The email is unique per seller and is suitable for display in admin tooling and, where appropriate, internal dashboards.

For external surfaces, consider redacting or partially masking this value depending on privacy requirements.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the seller account, such as pending_review, active, suspended, or terminated.

Application logic interprets this string as an enum that drives which actions are allowed for the seller, including product publishing, order handling, and payout eligibility.

Consumers should not hard‑code status transitions but may use the value for conditional rendering and filtering in management UIs.

emailVerified.description:
Flag indicating whether the seller’s contact email has been verified.

Verification status is important for security and compliance policies and may be required before certain high‑risk operations, such as withdrawing funds or enabling public catalog exposure.

Analytics and governance tools can use this indicator to segment sellers by trust level and onboarding progress.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the seller account was created.

This value reflects the initial onboarding time and is useful for cohort analysis, time‑based filtering, and debugging of early‑lifecycle behaviors.

The timestamp is expressed in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

IShoppingMallOrderItemSeller.description:
Seller mapping entity linking a single order line item to the seller responsible for fulfilling it in multi-seller orders.

This type is the detailed representation of rows from the `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers` Prisma model. Each record associates exactly one `shopping_mall_order_items` row with one `shopping_mall_sellers` row, enforced by a unique constraint on `shopping_mall_order_item_id`.

The entity is primarily used in administrative and operational tooling to understand which seller owns which line within an order and to drive downstream fulfillment, settlement, and dispute flows.

id.description:
Primary key for the seller mapping row.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers.id` and uniquely identifies a mapping between an order item and a seller.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Foreign key referencing the order line item that this mapping describes.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers.shopping_mall_order_item_id`, which in turn links to `shopping_mall_order_items.id`. The column is unique and non-nullable, enforcing a one-to-one relationship between each order item and its seller mapping.

Administrative tools and internal services can use this identifier to correlate mapping records with order item APIs, perform reconciliation, and debug complex multi-seller order scenarios without relying solely on nested DTO expansions.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Foreign key referencing the seller that is responsible for fulfilling the mapped order item.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers.shopping_mall_seller_id`, which points to `shopping_mall_sellers.id`. The column is non-nullable and is a core part of the business link used for fulfillment, settlement, risk evaluation, and dispute handling.

When combined with the nested `seller` summary, this raw identifier allows administrative and back-office tools to perform low-level investigations and joins using only UUIDs where necessary.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this mapping row was created.

Stored directly from `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers.created_at` and used for audit trails and temporal analysis of assignment events.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this mapping row was last updated.

This reflects the most recent modification time for the mapping, including reassignment or metadata changes.

order_item.description:
Summary view of the order item associated with this mapping.

This reference is derived from the `shopping_mall_order_items` table and provides lightweight context about the purchased SKU and quantities without loading full order or shipment graphs.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller account owning this order item.

Data originates from the `shopping_mall_sellers` model and typically includes business identity and lifecycle state, enabling administrative UIs to display which merchant is responsible for the line.

IShoppingMallOrderItemSeller.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying seller mappings of order items under a specific order.

This request DTO is used by the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderCode}/itemSellers` operation to scope queries against `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers` within the context of a single order, while also providing pagination and sorting controls.

It is designed for administrative and operational tooling, allowing back-office users to filter by seller, time range, or ordering preferences without exposing low-level database details.

page.description:
Zero-based page index used for pagination when listing seller mappings.

Implementations typically treat this as the page number starting from 0 or 1 depending on platform conventions; clients should follow the documented behavior of the specific deployment.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

Backends should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive result sizes and may apply a default when this field is omitted.

seller_id.description:
Optional filter restricting results to mappings owned by a specific seller.

When provided, only `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers` rows whose `shopping_mall_seller_id` matches this value are included in the result set.

order_item_id.description:
Optional filter restricting results to a specific order item within the scoped order.

When provided, only the mapping related to the given `shopping_mall_order_items.id` is returned if it exists.

sort_by.description:
Field name used to sort seller mappings within the page.

Common values include `created_at` or `updated_at`, but exact supported fields depend on implementation and should be documented per environment.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction applied to the `sort_by` field when ordering results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order; unknown values should be rejected by validation or normalized by the backend.

IShoppingMallOrderItemSeller.ISummary.description:
Summary view of the seller mapping for a single shopping mall order item.

This type provides the minimal information needed to understand which seller owns or fulfills a given line item, without expanding full seller profile details.

It is primarily used in multi-seller order flows where each order line may belong to a different seller and the platform needs a lightweight way to reference that ownership.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller mapping row for an order item.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers` table and is used to track seller-line relationships in settlement and logistics flows.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Identifier of the order item covered by this seller mapping.

The mapping enforces a one-to-one relationship with `shopping_mall_order_items.id`, ensuring that each line item is associated with exactly one seller in multi-seller orders.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller responsible for supplying or fulfilling this order item.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and exposes a lightweight view of the seller entity, allowing administrative and operational UIs to display seller context (such as name or business identifiers) without additional lookups.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller mapping row was created.

The creation time typically matches or closely follows the creation time of its parent order item and is stored in UTC for consistent audit trails.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller mapping row was last updated.

Updates may occur when correcting data inconsistencies or during exceptional operational processes, but in normal flows the mapping is effectively immutable.

IShoppingMallOrderItemSeller.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying the seller mapping of a specific order item.

This schema maps to the `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers` Prisma model, which represents the one-to-one link between an order line item and the seller responsible for fulfilling it. It is used by administrative and back-office tools when reassigning ownership of an order item from one seller to another under controlled circumstances.

Only business-editable fields that make sense to change after initial creation are exposed here. System-managed identifiers and timestamps are excluded from the request body and are handled automatically by the backend when the mapping row is updated.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who should become responsible for the target order item.

This value must reference an existing row in `shopping_mall_sellers.id` and typically is only changed by privileged admin workflows. When provided, the implementation must validate that the seller is active and allowed to fulfill the SKU associated with the order item.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an individual order line item within a shopping mall order.

This summary focuses on the immutable monetary and quantity snapshot that was captured at order confirmation time, along with basic identification fields needed for list and detail views.

It is optimized for use in order detail screens, seller order dashboards, and aggregated order listings where full relational expansion of the order item is not required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order item row.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_items` table and is used to reference or look up this specific line item across APIs and internal services.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the parent order that owns this line item.

This links the order item to its `shopping_mall_orders` header record and is used in order detail views and internal reconciliation flows.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU that was purchased on this line.

The SKU points to a concrete variant from the product catalog in `shopping_mall_skus`, while the textual snapshot fields on this entity preserve the name and human-readable details as of order time.

line_number.description:
Sequential position of this line within the parent order.

Line numbers are 1-based and provide stable ordering for displaying order items in customer and seller interfaces.

product_name.description:
Snapshot of the product name at the time of order.

This is stored as immutable text so that later changes to the catalog product name do not affect historical order presentations or financial audit trails.

sku_name.description:
Snapshot of the SKU or variant label at the time of order.

This text helps users and operators quickly identify which variant was selected without requiring additional catalog joins.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the SKU purchased on this line.

The quantity must be a positive integer and is used together with unit pricing fields for monetary calculations and inventory updates.

unit_price.description:
Per-unit selling price for this SKU at the moment of order confirmation, in the order currency.

The value is captured before any line-level discounts and is used together with `quantity` to derive the original line subtotal for audit and reporting.

line_subtotal.description:
Subtotal for this line before discounts, typically calculated as `quantity × unit_price`.

The subtotal is stored as a snapshot to simplify downstream reporting, reconciliation, and tax computation flows.

line_discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied specifically to this order line.

This can include both seller-funded and platform-funded promotions. The value is always a non-negative monetary amount in the order currency.

line_total.description:
Final payable amount for this order line after all line-level discounts have been applied but before any order-level fees or taxes.

This field is part of the order monetary snapshot and is used for settlement, invoice generation, and analytic aggregations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item row was created.

The value is stored in UTC and represents the moment the order item snapshot was first persisted, typically at order confirmation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item row was last updated.

Updates are rare and usually relate to technical adjustments or data corrections; business semantics treat order item monetary fields as immutable after confirmation.

IShoppingMallOrderPriceSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for retrieving price snapshot records associated with a specific order.

This schema is used as the request body for the PATCH `/shoppingMall/orders/{orderCode}/priceSnapshots` operation. It provides pagination, sorting, and basic temporal filtering when querying snapshot rows from the `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots` table that belong to a single order resolved by its business `orderCode`.

All filters are optional; when omitted, the backend should return a sensible default page of snapshots ordered by creation time. The structure is designed to match common list/search patterns across the platform while remaining tightly aligned with the underlying Prisma model fields.

page.description:
1-based index of the result page to return.

If omitted, the implementation should treat this as requesting the first page of results. This is a purely logical pagination cursor and does not map directly to any column in `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots`.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot records to return in a single page.

This controls page size for the result set. Implementations may enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses. This value does not correspond to a concrete Prisma column; it is a query-time control parameter.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the snapshot creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only snapshot rows with `created_at` greater than or equal to this value are eligible for the result set. Use it together with `toCreatedAt` to constrain the time window of interest. When null or omitted, no lower time bound is applied.

toCreatedAt.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the snapshot creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only snapshot rows with `created_at` less than or equal to this value are returned. Use it together with `fromCreatedAt` to define a closed time range. When null or omitted, no upper time bound is applied.

sortBy.description:
Name of the primary field used to sort snapshot records within the order scope.

Typical values include `created_at` when ordering by snapshot creation time. Implementations should restrict this to a whitelist of supported sortable columns on `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots` and fall back to a default when an unsupported value is supplied.

oneOf.description:
Direction in which the result set should be ordered with respect to the selected `sortBy` field.

Use `"asc"` for ascending order (oldest first) and `"desc"` for descending order (newest first). When omitted, the implementation should default to a sensible ordering such as `desc` by `created_at`.

Direction in which the result set should be ordered with respect to the selected `sortBy` field.

Use `"asc"` for ascending order (oldest first) and `"desc"` for descending order (newest first). When omitted, the implementation should default to a sensible ordering such as `desc` by `created_at`.

sortDirection.description:
Direction in which the result set should be ordered with respect to the selected `sortBy` field.

Use `"asc"` for ascending order (oldest first) and `"desc"` for descending order (newest first). When omitted, the implementation should default to a sensible ordering such as `desc` by `created_at`.

IShoppingMallOrderPriceSnapshot.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new order price snapshot associated with a specific order.

This DTO maps directly onto the `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots` Prisma model fields that are populated when a snapshot is created, excluding system-managed identifiers and timestamps. It is used by administrative and internal services to capture a decomposed monetary view of an order at a particular moment in its lifecycle.

The server associates the new snapshot with the target order resolved from the path parameter (for example, `orderCode` mapped to `shopping_mall_orders.id`) and automatically generates primary key and creation timestamp values while enforcing monetary consistency rules at the application layer.

item_subtotal_amount.description:
Sum of item-level subtotals for the order to record in the new snapshot.

This should reflect the aggregated pre-discount merchandise value across all order items at the time the snapshot is taken, before any line-level or order-level discounts are applied.

item_discount_amount.description:
Total line-level discount amount to persist in the new snapshot.

The value should represent the combined effect of all per-item discounts, including seller-funded, platform-funded, and campaign-based reductions applied at the item level.

order_discount_amount.description:
Total order-level discount amount to store for this snapshot.

Typical contributors include coupon redemptions, cart-level promotions, or other global adjustments that apply to the order as a whole rather than to individual line items.

shipping_fee_amount.description:
Total shipping fee amount to record in the snapshot for the targeted order.

This value may be zero when free shipping promotions apply or when shipping costs are fully absorbed by the seller or platform rather than the customer.

payment_surcharge_amount.description:
Total payment method surcharge amount for this snapshot.

Use this field to capture additional fees associated with the payment method selected for the order, such as gateway surcharges or card-type-specific fees, when such surcharges are modeled as part of the customer-facing total.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount to persist for the order at the snapshot time.

This amount should reflect all applicable taxes determined by jurisdiction, product classification, or customer profile for the order’s monetary state being captured.

grand_total_amount.description:
Total payable amount for the order represented by this new snapshot.

This value should be internally consistent with the other monetary components (subtotal, discounts, shipping, surcharges, and taxes) according to the platform’s rounding and calculation rules.

is_final.description:
Flag indicating whether the snapshot being created should be marked as the final confirmed monetary state for the order.

When set to `true`, downstream processes commonly treat this snapshot as authoritative for reporting, reconciliation, and customer- or seller-facing breakdowns of the order’s price.

IShoppingMallOrderPriceSnapshot.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing order price snapshot record in the shopping mall platform.

Represents the subset of monetary decomposition fields on a row in the `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots` table that are allowed to be modified after initial creation. This DTO is used by administrative and back‑office tooling when correcting or adjusting decomposed monetary components (such as item subtotals, item‑ and order‑level discounts, shipping fees, surcharges, taxes, and the grand total) for a specific order snapshot.

The DTO intentionally excludes system‑managed fields such as identifiers, foreign keys to orders, and creation timestamps. All properties are optional so that callers can update only the specific components that need correction, while the service layer revalidates overall consistency between the monetary parts.

Business validation rules, such as non‑negative amounts, consistency between components, and currency correctness, are enforced in the service layer using the same semantics as the `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots` Prisma model.

item_subtotal_amount.description:
Updated sum of item‑level subtotals for the order at the time of the snapshot.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.item_subtotal_amount` and represents the aggregated pre‑discount merchandise value across all order items. Must be a non‑negative monetary amount in the order’s currency.

item_discount_amount.description:
Updated total discount amount applied at line level across all items in this snapshot.

This maps to `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.item_discount_amount` and includes discounts funded by sellers, the platform, or campaigns that are modeled as per‑item reductions. Must be a non‑negative monetary amount.

order_discount_amount.description:
Updated total discount amount applied at the overall order level in this snapshot.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.order_discount_amount` and typically covers cart‑level promotions, coupons, or other global adjustments that apply to the order as a whole. Must be a non‑negative monetary amount.

shipping_fee_amount.description:
Updated total shipping fee amount charged to the customer in this snapshot.

This reflects `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.shipping_fee_amount`. The value may be zero when free‑shipping promotions or seller policies eliminate shipping costs, or when shipping is fully absorbed by the platform. Must be a non‑negative monetary amount.

payment_surcharge_amount.description:
Updated total payment method surcharge amount charged to the customer in this snapshot.

This maps to `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.payment_surcharge_amount` and can represent either platform‑owned payment fees or pass‑through surcharges that arise from specific payment instruments. Must be a non‑negative monetary amount.

tax_amount.description:
Updated total tax amount calculated for the order at the time of the snapshot.

This reflects `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.tax_amount` and may be zero for tax‑exempt customers, products, or jurisdictions. Must be a non‑negative monetary amount and should remain consistent with applicable tax policy configurations.

grand_total_amount.description:
Updated grand total amount to be charged to the customer according to this snapshot.

This corresponds directly to `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.grand_total_amount`. Conceptually, it is expected to equal item_subtotal_amount minus discounts plus shipping_fee_amount, payment_surcharge_amount, and tax_amount, subject to the platform’s rounding rules. Must be a non‑negative monetary amount.

is_final.description:
Updated flag indicating whether this snapshot represents the final confirmed monetary state for the order.

This maps to `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.is_final`. Business logic typically treats the most recent snapshot with `is_final = true` as the authoritative view for reporting, reconciliation, and customer‑facing price displays.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for retrieving paginated order status history entries for a specific order.

This DTO is used as the request body of the PATCH `/shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/statusHistories` endpoint and expresses complex filtering, sorting, and pagination options over the `shopping_mall_order_status_histories` table for a single order identified by the path parameter `orderCode`.

It intentionally does not duplicate the `orderCode` path parameter. Instead, it focuses on filters such as status values, time windows, and the actor type that triggered transitions, as well as generic pagination and sorting controls.

All fields are optional; when omitted, reasonable defaults such as returning the most recent history entries first should be applied by the service layer.

page.description:
Page index for pagination when listing status history entries.

Pagination is 1-based unless otherwise documented by the implementation. If omitted, the first page is typically returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of status history records to return per page.

Service layer should enforce an upper bound (for example, 100 or 200) to prevent excessive result sizes. If omitted, a sensible default page size is applied.

status_from.description:
Optional filter to include only history entries whose `from_status` matches the given value.

Represents the status value before the transition. The concrete set of allowed values is defined by the order status domain (e.g., `PLACED`, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`).

status_to.description:
Optional filter to include only history entries whose `to_status` matches the given value.

Represents the status value after the transition. The concrete set of allowed values is defined by the order status domain (e.g., `PLACED`, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`).

changed_by_actor_type.description:
Optional filter by the high-level actor type that triggered the status change.

Typical values include conceptual actors such as `"customer"`, `"seller"`, `"admin"`, or `"system"`. The exact list is determined by the business domain and implementation.

changed_from.description:
Optional start of the time range filter for status change timestamps.

When provided, only history entries whose change timestamp is greater than or equal to this value (inclusive) are returned. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or including an explicit offset.

changed_to.description:
Optional end of the time range filter for status change timestamps.

When provided, only history entries whose change timestamp is less than or equal to this value (inclusive) are returned. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or including an explicit offset.

order_by.description:
Optional field name to sort the status histories by.

Common values include `"changed_at"` (the transition timestamp) or `"id"`. The service implementation should validate the requested field against an allowed whitelist.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the returned records.

Expected values are `"asc"` for ascending order or `"desc"` for descending order. If omitted, descending order by change timestamp is typically used so that the most recent transitions appear first.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new order status history entry for a specific order.

This DTO is used by administrative or internal system endpoints to append a new status transition to the timeline of an existing order. It carries the new status, the effective timestamp, and optional contextual metadata such as the previous status, structured reason codes, and free-text explanations.

The target order is identified by a path parameter (typically an `orderCode`) and resolved server-side to `shopping_mall_order_id`, so the request body does not contain the order identifier. Actor identifiers are also determined by the authenticated admin or by trusted backend logic, so only optional descriptive fields and status values are supplied by the client.

from_status.description:
Previous status value before this transition.

When supplied, this should match the order's current status at the time the transition is applied. It can be omitted or set to null when the server infers the prior status from the current order state.

to_status.description:
New status value to apply to the order as a result of this transition.

This value must conform to the set of valid business status values used for `shopping_mall_orders.current_status`, such as `PENDING`, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`, or `DELIVERED`, and will become the order's effective status after the transition is recorded.

reason_code.description:
Optional machine-readable reason code describing why this status change is being recorded.

Clients can provide structured codes such as `payment_confirmed`, `customer_cancelled`, or `system_timeout` to enable downstream reporting, analytics, and rule-based processing.

reason_detail.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of the status change.

This free-text field allows operators or automation systems to store explanatory notes that customer support, sellers, or auditors can later review when examining the order's status history.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change took effect from a business perspective.

For real-time transitions, this will typically be the current time. For backfilled or corrected data, it can represent an earlier point in time when the event actually occurred in the order lifecycle.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for an existing order status history record in the shopping mall platform.

This type is used by administrative or back-office tools when they need to correct or enrich a previously stored status transition entry in the `shopping_mall_order_status_histories` table. Typical use cases include fixing an incorrect status code, adjusting the effective timestamp when backfilling historical data, or updating explanatory notes.

Only business attributes of the history record are updatable. Identifiers and foreign keys that link the record to its order and actors are immutable and therefore intentionally excluded from this DTO. The implementation should combine values from this DTO with path parameters and authenticated actor context to perform the update safely.

System-managed audit fields such as `id`, `shopping_mall_order_id`, and `created_at` are intentionally not present in this schema so that clients cannot tamper with core audit information or lifecycle metadata.

oneOf.description: Non-empty status code string representing the previous status before the transition.
Null when explicitly clearing or leaving the previous status unspecified in the correction scenario.

from_status.description:
Previous status value before this transition.

This corresponds to the `from_status` column in `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`. It is nullable in the database because the initial status transition of an order may not have a prior status. When provided in an update, it must represent a valid business status string understood by the order lifecycle engine.

oneOf.description: Status code string representing the target status after this transition.
Null when the `to_status` should not be changed by this update request.

to_status.description:
New status value applied to the order as a result of this transition.

This maps to the `to_status` column in `shopping_mall_order_status_histories` and is required for every history record at persistence time. When updating, the value must remain consistent with allowed order lifecycle states and transitions. Changing this value effectively corrects what status the order was considered to be in at the `occurred_at` moment, which can affect downstream analytics and SLA calculations.

oneOf.description: Non-empty reason code string that is meaningful within the business domain.
Null when the reason code should be cleared or is not applicable for this history entry.

reason_code.description:
Machine-readable reason code explaining why this status change occurred.

This corresponds to the optional `reason_code` column in `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`. It is typically used by automated systems to categorize transitions, such as `payment_confirmed`, `customer_cancelled`, or `system_timeout`. Updating this field allows administrators to refine or correct categorization for reporting and audits.

oneOf.description: Descriptive free-form text explaining the status change in human-readable terms.
Null when removing an existing explanation or when no explanation is required.

reason_detail.description:
Human-readable explanation describing why this status change occurred.

This field maps to `reason_detail` in `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`. It is intended to contain descriptive text that customer support and operations teams can read when investigating the order lifecycle, including free-form notes or copied communication snippets. In an update, this field can be set, refined, or cleared based on new information.

oneOf.description: ISO 8601 date-time string representing the corrected moment the status change took effect.
Null when the occurred-at timestamp should not be changed by this update request.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change took effect from a business perspective.

This property corresponds to `occurred_at` in `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`. Adjusting this value in an update is a sensitive operation because it changes the temporal positioning of the status event in the order’s lifecycle timeline. Implementations should ensure that updated timestamps remain logically consistent with other history entries and business rules.

IShoppingMallOrderCustomerContact.description:
Read model for a customer contact information snapshot associated with an order.

This type represents a persisted snapshot row from the shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts table, which stores the contact_name, contact_email, and optional contact_phone that were valid at the time an order was placed or confirmed. The snapshot is used by order detail views, notification systems, customer support tools, and compliance reporting to ensure that historical communications use immutable, time-correct contact data.

The model intentionally omits persistence-level identifiers and foreign key fields so that external consumers interact with this snapshot only through its owning order (via orderCode in the path) and focus purely on the business contact information and its lifecycle timestamps.

contact_name.description:
Customer name captured for order-related communications at the time of placement.

This property is sourced from the contact_name column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and is used by email templates, invoices, and support tooling to address the recipient in a manner consistent with the original checkout experience.

contact_email.description:
Email address captured for order confirmations and subsequent notifications.

The value maps to the contact_email column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and is treated as an immutable historical snapshot. Systems such as notification services and customer support portals use this email when referencing past orders, independent of later profile changes.

contact_phone.description:
Optional phone number captured for order-related communication at the time of placement.

This property corresponds to the contact_phone column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and may be null when no phone number was provided or when phone-based communication is not required. When present, it is typically used by customer support and logistics staff for time-sensitive inquiries.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this contact snapshot row was created.

This field is mapped from the created_at column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and records the exact moment the snapshot was persisted, supporting temporal analysis of order lifecycle events and audit requirements.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this contact snapshot row was last updated.

The value reflects the updated_at column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and changes whenever the contact_name, contact_email, or contact_phone fields are modified through administrative correction flows or maintenance processes.

IShoppingMallOrderCustomerContact.ICreat.description:
Create DTO for capturing a customer contact information snapshot for an order.

This type models the minimal set of contact attributes that must be provided when creating a new snapshot row in the shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts table. It is used by administrative or internal system flows that need to persist the customer name, email, and optional phone number that were valid at the time of order placement or confirmation.

The DTO does not expose any system-managed identifiers or timestamps, and it does not accept order or customer linkage identifiers. Those relations are resolved by the backend from the surrounding context, such as the orderCode path parameter and any associated customer account linkage in shopping_mall_orders.

contact_name.description:
Customer-facing name used for order-related communications at the time of placement.

This value maps directly to the contact_name column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and is required for identifying the human recipient in notifications, invoices, and support interactions. It should reflect the name that was current during checkout, even if the customer later updates their profile.

contact_email.description:
Email address used for order confirmations and subsequent notifications at the time of placement.

This field maps to the contact_email column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and must contain a syntactically valid email address. The stored value is treated as a historical snapshot so that later profile changes do not alter past notification targets.

contact_phone.description:
Optional phone number used for order-related communication at the time of placement.

This property corresponds to the contact_phone column in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and may be null when no phone number was provided or when phone-based communication is not required. When present, it should contain a dialable phone number formatted according to the business or regional conventions of the platform.

IShoppingMallOrderCustomerContact.IUpdat.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing customer contact information snapshot tied to an order.

This type is used by administrative tools or internal maintenance processes to correct or adjust previously stored contact snapshot data in the shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts table. Typical use cases include fixing an incorrectly captured email address, updating a misspelled name, or adding a missing phone number.

All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates. System-managed identifiers, timestamps, and foreign key relations to orders and customers are excluded from this DTO and are instead managed by the backend using the surrounding operation context, such as the orderCode path parameter and existing snapshot row.

contact_name.description:
Updated customer-facing name for order-related communications.

When provided, this value overwrites the existing contact_name in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts and should reflect the corrected name that downstream notifications and support tools must use going forward while still representing the original order context.

contact_email.description:
Updated email address for order confirmations and subsequent notifications.

If supplied, this value replaces the current contact_email stored in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts. It must remain a syntactically valid email address and is typically changed only to correct errors captured at checkout or to align with verified contact details.

contact_phone.description:
Updated phone number for order-related communication, or null to clear the stored phone value.

Providing a non-null string replaces the existing contact_phone in shopping_mall_order_customer_contacts, whereas explicitly setting this property to null clears the stored phone number. Omitting the property leaves the current phone value unchanged.

IShoppingMallShippingAddress.description:
Immutable snapshot of a shipping address used for a specific customer order in the shopping mall domain.

This entity mirrors a single row in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` Prisma model and captures the recipient and destination details as they existed at the time of checkout. It is designed to be historically stable so that logistics workflows, dispute handling, and compliance investigations can rely on the exact address originally used, even if the customer later changes their address book entries.

The snapshot is associated to a single order in `shopping_mall_orders` and may optionally be linked back to a customer address snapshot in `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots`. It is not meant to be edited arbitrarily after creation, though soft deletion via `deleted_at` can be applied under legal and governance rules.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this shipping address snapshot.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and is used to uniquely reference this immutable snapshot in relational links and API responses.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order that uses this shipping address snapshot.

This is a foreign key to `shopping_mall_orders.id` and ties the address snapshot to a single order header so that order-detail views and shipment logic can resolve the correct destination information.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the underlying customer address snapshot from the identity domain that this shipping address was derived from.

When present, this value points to `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots.id` and indicates that the address was selected from the customer’s saved addresses at checkout, rather than entered ad-hoc.

Null when the shipping address was entered ad‑hoc at checkout and is not backed by a reusable customer address snapshot.

This allows the platform to distinguish between derived snapshots and one‑off addresses provided only for this order.

shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshot_.description:
Optional link back to the customer address snapshot that this shipping address was derived from, if any.

If the address came from a saved customer address entry, this field contains the corresponding snapshot ID; otherwise it is null for ad‑hoc addresses.

recipient_name.description:
Name of the person or entity that should receive the shipment as captured at checkout.

This is displayed on shipping labels and is used by carriers and support teams when handling delivery issues or identity verification for the package recipient.

line1.description:
Primary street address line or equivalent first line of address information.

Typical values include building number and street name or other country‑specific primary address text that uniquely identifies the delivery location.

oneOf.description:
Secondary address line captured at checkout, such as apartment, suite, floor, or building information.

This line is optional and is used to refine the delivery location within a larger building or housing complex when applicable.

Null when no secondary address information was provided at checkout.

Many addresses do not require an additional line, so this value is omitted in those cases.

line2.description:
Optional second line of the street address, such as apartment, suite, or building complement.

Present when the customer provided additional address detail; otherwise null to indicate that a single line is sufficient.

city.description:
City or locality component of the shipping address at the time of order confirmation.

This value is used for carrier routing, tax calculation, and regional reporting, and should reflect whatever locality string the customer entered or selected.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code for the shipping destination.

The format depends on the destination country and is stored exactly as entered so that carrier systems and address validation tools can consume it reliably.

country_code.description:
ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 country code representing the destination country.

This standardized two‑letter code is used for shipping rules, customs handling, and localization logic, and should always match a valid entry in the platform’s country master data.

oneOf.description:
Region, state, or province information associated with the shipping address, when applicable.

Typical examples include US states, Canadian provinces, or other sub‑national regions used by carriers and tax rules.

Null when the country’s addressing scheme or the particular address does not require a region component.

This allows the schema to support both region‑based and region‑less postal systems without forcing artificial values.

region.description:
Optional region, state, or province component of the address.

Used for jurisdictions that require a second‑level administrative area in addition to the city and country fields.

oneOf.description:
Contact phone number associated with the shipping address, as entered at checkout.

Carriers and customer support use this number to coordinate deliveries, handle failed delivery attempts, or clarify address details with the recipient.

Null when a phone number was not provided or is not required by the shipping method.

Some flows or countries may not require a phone contact, so this field is optional.

phone_number.description:
Optional phone number for contacting the recipient regarding delivery.

Helps carriers and support teams resolve delivery issues, but may be omitted when business rules or customer preferences permit.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot row was created in the database.

Represents the moment the address was persisted for the order, usually at checkout confirmation or when a shipping address is first attached to the order.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot row was last updated.

Updates typically occur only for system‑level maintenance, soft‑deletion toggles, or governance operations, as the address snapshot is conceptually immutable for business purposes.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when this snapshot was soft‑deleted or logically hidden from normal queries.

Used to comply with data lifecycle policies while preserving the record for legal, audit, or dispute‑resolution purposes when necessary.

Null when the snapshot is active and visible to normal business queries.

Most records remain in this state unless a soft‑delete action or governance policy changes their visibility.

deleted_at.description:
Optional soft‑deletion timestamp for this shipping address snapshot.

When set, the snapshot is considered logically deleted for day‑to‑day operations but can still be accessed for audit, legal hold, or compliance workflows.

IShoppingMallOrderShippingAddress.ICreat.description:
Request body for creating and attaching a shipping address snapshot to an existing order identified by its business `orderCode`.

This DTO contains all of the address components that the customer (or authorized actor) must supply at checkout: recipient name, street address, locality, postal code, country, and optional region and phone number. The API operation uses the `orderCode` path parameter to resolve the target order in `shopping_mall_orders`, while this body provides only the address details that will be copied into `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` as an immutable snapshot.

Actor identity and order ownership are inferred from authentication context, not from this DTO. Server‑side logic is responsible for enforcing that only the appropriate customer or authorized staff can create or modify the shipping address snapshot for a given order and for validating the address against country and region master data when required.

recipient_name.description:
Name of the person or entity that should receive the shipment.

Clients should send the full recipient name exactly as it should appear on shipping labels and courier documentation.

line1.description:
Primary street address line or equivalent first line of address information.

This field must contain enough detail, in combination with other components, for carriers to locate the delivery address in the target country.

oneOf.description:
Optional second line of the address, typically used for apartment, suite, building, floor, or other complementary information.

Include this value when the destination requires additional detail beyond the main street address.

Null when no secondary address information is needed for this shipment.

Clients may omit this value or explicitly send null when a single line is sufficient.

line2.description:
Second address line for apartment, suite, or building details when applicable.

This field is optional and can be omitted or set to null for addresses that do not require an additional line.

city.description:
City or locality of the shipping destination.

The value should reflect the customer‑facing locality string expected by carriers in the destination country or region.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code for the shipping destination.

Clients must supply the code exactly as used by the local postal system so that carrier integrations and address validation routines can function correctly.

country_code.description:
ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 country code of the destination country.

The platform uses this two‑letter code to apply country‑specific shipping rules, taxes, and validation logic, and it must correspond to a supported entry in the marketplace configuration.

oneOf.description:
Region, state, or province component of the address for countries that require it.

Examples include US states, Canadian provinces, or other second‑level administrative divisions relevant to shipping and tax rules.

Null when the destination country or specific address does not require a region or state field.

In such cases, carriers and tax engines rely on city and country alone.

region.description:
Optional region, state, or province information to refine the address.

This field is recommended where local postal standards or carrier requirements expect a sub‑national region alongside the city and country.

oneOf.description:
Contact phone number that carriers or support staff can use to reach the recipient about delivery.

Format is not strictly enforced by the schema but should be provided in a locally recognizable form, including country code when appropriate.

Null when a phone number is not provided or is not required for the selected shipping method.

Some flows or jurisdictions allow shipments without a contact number, in which case this field can be omitted or set to null.

phone_number.description:
Optional phone number associated with the shipping destination.

Providing a contact number can improve delivery success rates, but it is not mandatory in all flows or jurisdictions.

IShoppingMallOrderShippingAddress.description:
Shipping address snapshot associated with a specific customer order in the shopping mall domain.

This type represents the denormalized shipping address values actually used for fulfillment of a single order, including recipient information, structured postal address components, and contact details captured at checkout time.

The snapshot is tied to an order and, optionally, to an underlying customer address snapshot. It is immutable from a historical perspective so that later changes to customer address book entries do not retroactively affect existing orders.

Instances of this schema are typically returned from order-related APIs that expose the effective shipping address for a given orderCode, and may also be reused in shipment APIs that require the same address context.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipping address snapshot row.

This is the primary key of the underlying `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and is used internally to join shipments and other logistics records to the correct address snapshot.

Clients typically do not need to know or provide this value directly; it is exposed in read models for debugging, traceability, and deep-linking purposes.

order.description:
Order to which this shipping address snapshot belongs.

This relation provides the business-level context such as orderCode, currency, and lifecycle information when the address is viewed independently from the order resource.

The underlying foreign key is `shopping_mall_order_id`, but this property exposes the order as a summary view instead of a raw ID for easier client consumption.

customerAddressSnapshot.description:
Optional link to the customer address snapshot this shipping address was derived from.

When present, it references a record in `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots` that contains the original customer-facing address book entry.

When null, the address was entered specifically for this order and is not tied to a reusable address book item.

recipient_name.description:
Name of the person or organization designated to receive the shipment.

Captured as free text at checkout and returned exactly as stored so that labels and notifications match user expectations.

This field is required for all shipping destinations.

line1.description:
Primary street address line for the destination.

Typical values include house number and street name, building name, or other primary addressing details used by carriers to locate the recipient.

This field is always required and must contain non-empty content.

line2.description:
Secondary address line such as apartment, suite, floor, or additional building information.

This field is optional and may be null when no additional addressing details are needed.

When provided, it augments `line1` to improve delivery precision.

city.description:
City or locality component of the shipping address.

The precise semantics depend on the destination country's addressing system, but it generally represents the municipality or locality recognized by postal services.

This value is required for most destinations and is returned as a simple string without further normalization.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code component of the shipping address.

The exact format varies by country, and validation rules may be enforced according to country-specific patterns.

This field is required for destinations that use postal codes and is stored exactly as provided during checkout.

country_code.description:
Destination country of the shipping address expressed as an ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 country code.

The value determines applicable shipping options, tax rules, and address validation logic.

This field is always required and must correspond to a known country in the platform's country master data.

region.description:
Region, state, or province component of the shipping address when applicable.

For countries with sub‑national divisions, this value helps carriers and internal systems route shipments correctly.

The field is optional and may be null for destinations where such information is not used or not provided.

phone_number.description:
Contact phone number associated with the shipping address.

Carriers and customer support may use this number to resolve delivery issues or communicate time‑sensitive information.

The field is optional and may be null when no phone contact is provided, subject to business rules and regional requirements.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot record was created in the database.

The value reflects the moment the address snapshot was first persisted, typically aligned with order confirmation or shipment creation.

It is stored in UTC and returned to clients as an ISO 8601 date‑time string.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot record was last modified.

Updates may occur when allowable address corrections are applied before fulfillment, or when internal systems adjust metadata.

The field is managed by the system and is not directly editable by API clients.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this shipping address snapshot.

When null, the snapshot is considered active and should be used in normal query results.

When set, it indicates that the snapshot has been logically removed from standard views while retained for legal, audit, or retention policy reasons.

IShoppingMallOrderShippingAddress.IUpdat.description:
Request body for updating the shipping address snapshot of an existing order.

This DTO is mapped to the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` Prisma model, which stores snapshot rows of shipping addresses linked to orders. It intentionally exposes only the customer-editable address columns from that table—such as name, street lines, city, postal code, country code, region, and phone number—and does not surface foreign keys (`shopping_mall_order_id`, `shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshot_id`) or system-managed timestamp fields (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`).

The DTO is used by the `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderCode}/shippingAddress` operation to apply corrections or adjustments to the shipping address for a given `orderCode`. All properties are optional to support partial updates: callers include only the fields they intend to change. For nullable fields, the value semantics are:
- Provide a non-null value to replace the existing value in the snapshot.
- Provide `null` to explicitly clear the stored value (where allowed by Prisma nullability).
- Omit the property entirely to leave the existing database value unchanged.

This design ensures that updates remain consistent with the immutable snapshot concept of `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` while still allowing controlled corrections before fulfillment according to business rules.

recipient_name.description:
Updated recipient name for the shipment.

This property maps directly to the non-null `recipient_name` column of the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` Prisma model. When provided, the new value replaces the current recipient name stored in the shipping address snapshot associated with the target order.

Callers should include this field only when the displayed recipient needs to change (for example, correcting a spelling error or changing the intended recipient). If omitted, the existing `recipient_name` value in the snapshot remains unchanged.

line1.description:
Updated primary street address line for the shipping destination.

This value corresponds to the non-null `line1` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and typically contains house number, street name, building name, or other primary addressing details used by carriers.

When supplied, it replaces the current `line1` value in the snapshot. If this field is not included in the request body, the existing database value for `line1` is preserved without modification.

line2.description:
Updated secondary address line such as apartment, suite, floor, or additional building details.

This property is aligned with the nullable `line2` column on the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` Prisma model. It is optional in the request and supports three distinct behaviors:
- Provide a non-null string to replace the existing `line2` value in the snapshot.
- Provide `null` to explicitly clear any previously stored secondary address line.
- Omit the property entirely to keep the current `line2` value unchanged.

This tri-state behavior allows clients to precisely control whether the secondary address information is updated, removed, or left untouched.

city.description:
Updated city or locality component of the shipping address.

This field maps to the non-null `city` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and represents the municipality or locality recognized by postal services at the time of shipment.

When present in the request, the supplied value replaces the existing city stored in the snapshot. If omitted, the current `city` value remains as-is in the database.

postal_code.description:
Updated postal or ZIP code for the shipping destination.

The value corresponds to the non-null `postal_code` column of the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` Prisma model. It should adhere to the postal format rules of the destination country, with server-side validation enforcing business and formatting constraints where applicable.

Including this property causes the existing postal code in the snapshot to be replaced. If the property is not included in the request body, the existing `postal_code` remains unchanged.

country_code.description:
Updated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the shipping address.

This property maps to the non-null `country_code` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and determines the destination country used for shipping options, taxation, and address validation.

Changing the country may significantly affect logistics behavior; therefore, business rules may restrict when this field can be updated. When present, the new code replaces the stored `country_code` value in the snapshot. If omitted, the previously stored country code is retained.

region.description:
Updated region, state, or province information for the shipping address when applicable.

This property corresponds to the nullable `region` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` Prisma model and is used in countries where sub-national divisions are necessary for accurate routing.

The field supports three behaviors:
- A non-null string value replaces the existing `region` in the snapshot.
- A `null` value clears any currently stored region information.
- If the property is omitted from the request, the stored `region` value is left unchanged.

This behavior allows fine-grained control over regional information without forcing clients to re-send existing values.

phone_number.description:
Updated contact phone number associated with the shipping address.

The value maps to the nullable `phone_number` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and is used by carriers and support teams to resolve delivery issues or coordinate time-sensitive communication with the recipient.

Behavior is as follows:
- Provide a non-null string to replace the existing contact number.
- Provide `null` to explicitly remove any stored phone number from the snapshot.
- Omit this property to preserve the current `phone_number` value held in the database.

Implementations may enforce additional validation such as E.164 formatting or region-specific phone rules at the service layer.

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.description:
Shipping method configuration entity used by the shopping mall platform.

This schema is a direct projection of a single row in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` Prisma model, which defines business-level shipping methods referenced during checkout and fulfillment. Each record includes a stable method code, human-readable display name, optional service-level description, and system-managed timestamps that track when the configuration was created and last updated.

Orders and shipments reference these records to understand which shipping service was selected without coupling directly to external carrier tables or transient configuration structures. Administrative APIs use this type as the primary read model when creating, updating, listing, and inspecting shipping method configurations, and analytics layers can rely on it as the authoritative snapshot of shipping method metadata at the time of aggregation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipping method record.

This property corresponds to the primary key `id` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` Prisma model and is generated by the system when a new shipping method row is inserted. It is used internally to relate this configuration to other records and for low-level database operations.

Clients receive this value in read responses (such as detail or list views) but must not supply or modify it in creation or update DTOs; those flows identify shipping methods by the business-level `method_code` instead.

method_code.description:
Machine-readable shipping method code used as a stable business identifier.

This field maps to the unique `method_code` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table. It is designed to be stable over time and is commonly embedded in URLs, configuration files, and integrations (for example, values like `"standard"`, `"express"`, or carrier-specific codes).

Because a unique index is enforced at the database level, attempts to create or rename methods to a duplicate code must be rejected by the service layer. Downstream systems and logs typically use this code rather than the internal `id` for human interaction and audit trails.

display_name.description:
Human-readable shipping method name presented in user interfaces.
