This property is backed by the non-null `display_name` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` Prisma model and is shown to customers, sellers, and administrators in checkout screens, order details, and configuration tools.

The value should be concise yet descriptive (for example, "Standard Shipping" or "Next-Day Courier"), and localization responsibilities are typically handled at the application layer using this stored canonical label as a base.

service_level_description.description:
Optional free-form description of the service level and expectations associated with this shipping method.

This field aligns with the nullable `service_level_description` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table. It can contain details such as typical delivery windows, carrier SLAs, handling notes, or restrictions that help administrators and possibly customers understand the behavior of the method.

When null, no additional description has been configured and clients should either omit extended descriptions or rely on other metadata. Administrative update operations may set this value, update it, or explicitly clear it by sending `null` in the corresponding update DTO.

created_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this shipping method record was first created in the database.

This property represents the non-null `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` Prisma model and is set automatically by the persistence layer at insertion time. It is stored in UTC and exposed to clients as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

The value is read-only from the API perspective and is useful for auditing configuration lifecycle events and ordering configuration records chronologically.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp recording the most recent update to this shipping method record.

This field corresponds to the non-null `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table. It is automatically refreshed by the backend whenever any mutable configuration field (such as `display_name` or `service_level_description`) is changed.

Clients can use this property for cache invalidation, synchronization checks, and administrative auditing of configuration changes. As with `created_at`, it is read-only for API consumers and is always returned as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string.

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request for retrieving a paginated list of shipping methods.

This DTO is used as the request body for the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/shippingMethods` endpoint, which supports complex search, filtering, and sorting on top of the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table.

It encapsulates common pagination controls, free-text search, and optional sort configuration in a structured JSON payload rather than using query-string parameters, making it suitable for rich admin UIs and internal tooling.

page.description:
Zero-based index of the page to retrieve in the paginated shipping method list.

Clients use this together with `limit` to navigate through large result sets. When omitted, the backend may default to the first page (for example, 0).

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipping method records to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for the search results. Implementations typically enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large pages that could harm performance.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term used to filter shipping methods by human-readable attributes.

Backends commonly apply this term to fields such as `display_name`, `method_code`, or `service_level_description` using a `LIKE` or full-text matching strategy. When null, no free-text search is applied and only other filters or default criteria are used.

sort_by.description:
Optional column key indicating which field should be used to sort the shipping methods.

Typical values include `"method_code"`, `"display_name"`, `"created_at"`, or `"updated_at"`. When null, the backend applies its default ordering, such as by creation time or method code.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction applied to the `sort_by` column.

Only two values are allowed when this field is not null:
- `"asc"` for ascending order
- `"desc"` for descending order

When null or omitted, the backend may choose a sensible default, such as ascending order for the configured `sort_by` column.

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new shipping method configuration.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` Prisma model and is used by administrative clients to introduce new shipping methods that can be referenced by orders and shipments.
It exposes only business-editable fields and omits system-managed columns such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`, which are populated by the backend.

The DTO is designed for use with administrative endpoints such as `POST /shoppingMall/admin/shippingMethods`, which are restricted to admin actors.
Business logic must enforce uniqueness of `method_code` and may perform additional validation against region and policy configuration tables before persisting the new record.

method_code.description:
Machine-readable shipping method code that uniquely identifies this method across the platform.

This value is stored in the `method_code` column of the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table and is constrained by a unique index.
Administrative callers must choose a stable identifier such as `"standard"`, `"express"`, or a carrier-specific key that will not change over time.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping method that will be shown in checkout and administrative UIs.

This property maps to the non-null `display_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`.
Typical values include labels like "Standard Shipping", "Next-Day Delivery", or "Express Courier" and should be concise but descriptive.

service_level_description.description:
Optional description of the service level and expectations for this shipping method at the time of configuration.

This value is persisted in the nullable `service_level_description` column and may describe delivery windows, carrier SLAs, or any other human-readable notes.
Callers can omit this field or explicitly send null when no additional explanation is required.

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing shipping method configuration.

This DTO is used by administrative endpoints such as `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/shippingMethods/{methodCode}` to modify properties of an existing row in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table.
It supports partial updates of business-editable columns and continues to exclude system-managed fields, which remain under backend control.

The target record is identified externally by its stable `method_code` path parameter, so `method_code` itself is not included as an updatable property in this DTO.
Implementations should validate that the referenced method exists and enforce business rules such as preventing invalid combinations of display labels and service descriptions.

display_name.description:
Optional new human-readable name for the shipping method.

When provided, this value updates the `display_name` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table and will be reflected wherever the method is displayed in user interfaces.
If omitted, the existing display name is preserved.

service_level_description.description:
Optional replacement for the service level description associated with this shipping method.

Supplying a non-null string updates the `service_level_description` column, while explicitly providing null clears any previously stored description.
If this property is omitted entirely, the current description remains unchanged.

IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.description:
Filter, sorting, and pagination criteria for querying shipment headers from the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

This request DTO is used by multiple PATCH list operations for shipments (admin-wide search, and order-scoped listings for customer, seller, and admin). It centralizes common search capabilities so all shipment list endpoints share a consistent contract.

The structure focuses on shipment-level fields and pagination concerns rather than deep relational graphs. It is designed for backoffice dashboards and order detail pages that need efficient, server-side filtering without exposing low-level database implementation details.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination.

Clients use this to request a particular page when browsing large result sets. When omitted, the server should default to the first page according to platform-wide pagination defaults.

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipment records to return in a single page.

This value is used to control page size for list responses. The server may enforce an upper bound to protect performance and avoid excessive payload sizes.

sort_by.description:
Field name used for sorting shipment results.

Typical values include keys mapped to shipment header fields such as `created_at`, `shipped_at`, `delivered_at`, or `shipping_status`. Exact supported values are defined by the implementation, but the API contract ensures one stable text field communicates the chosen primary sort.

oneOf.description: Ascending sort order for the chosen field. Shipments with earlier values appear first.
Descending sort order for the chosen field. Shipments with later values appear first.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction for the primary sort field.

`asc` sorts in ascending order and `desc` sorts in descending order. When omitted, the server applies a sensible default for the chosen `sort_by` field.

shipment_code.description:
Exact shipment code or partial pattern used to filter shipments.

This corresponds to the business-facing `shipment_code` stored in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table, allowing users to quickly locate a specific shipment when they know its code.

items.description:
Single shipment status value used as part of a filter set.

Typical values correspond to the `shipping_status` column of `shopping_mall_shipments`, such as `pending`, `preparing`, `ready_for_pickup`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, or `cancelled`.

shipping_statuses.description:
List of shipment status values to filter by.

When provided, only shipments whose `shipping_status` column matches one of the values in this array are included in the result set.

carrier_name.description:
Carrier name filter applied to shipments.

When set, restricts results to shipments whose `carrier_name` in `shopping_mall_shipments` matches the given value or pattern, depending on implementation (exact match vs. partial search).

tracking_number.description:
Tracking number filter applied to shipments.

This is useful for troubleshooting or locating a shipment when the carrier tracking identifier is known. The underlying implementation typically searches the `tracking_number` column on `shopping_mall_shipments`.

created_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for filtering by shipment `created_at` timestamp.

Only shipments whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are included. This supports date-range queries in dashboards and order detail views.

created_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for filtering by shipment `created_at` timestamp.

Only shipments whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are included. Used together with `created_from` for bounded time-window searches.

shipped_from.description:
Lower bound for filtering by `shipped_at` timestamp.

When set, limits results to shipments that were shipped on or after the specified ISO 8601 date-time value.

shipped_to.description:
Upper bound for filtering by `shipped_at` timestamp.

When set, limits results to shipments that were shipped on or before the specified ISO 8601 date-time value.

delivered_from.description:
Lower bound for filtering by `delivered_at` timestamp.

This helps identify shipments delivered after a particular point in time, useful for reporting and SLA analysis.

delivered_to.description:
Upper bound for filtering by `delivered_at` timestamp.

Used together with `delivered_from` to restrict the result set to shipments delivered within a particular window.

IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate.description:
Create request DTO for registering a new shipment header and its associated shipment items in the shopping mall logistics domain.

This structure is used by administrative or fulfillment actors to materialize a shipment in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table, optionally scoped to a specific order when the API path already provides the `orderCode`. The DTO only contains fields that are not system-managed and that are allowed to be specified by clients at creation time.

The payload focuses on selecting the target order (when not implied by the path), defining the shipping address and method snapshots, and providing the shipment line allocations through subsidiary create DTOs.

Authentication context and system timestamps are supplied by the backend and therefore are not represented here as writable fields.

orderCode.description:
Business-facing order code that identifies the parent order from which this shipment is derived.

This field is required in contexts where the API endpoint does not already provide the order context in the URL path (for example, `POST /shoppingMall/admin/shipments`). When the endpoint includes `orderCode` in the path (for example, `POST /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderCode}/shipments`), this property must be omitted so that the server relies solely on the path parameter and avoids conflicting identifiers.

shippingAddressId.description:
Identifier of an existing shipping address snapshot to associate with this shipment.

The value must be a valid UUID corresponding to an `id` in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table. When provided, the implementation links the shipment to that existing address snapshot, which typically represents the destination captured at order confirmation.

In some implementations, the shipping address may be implicitly derived from the order’s shipping address snapshot, in which case this property can be omitted. When explicit override or selection is required, this field must carry the UUID of the desired shipping address snapshot.

shippingMethodId.description:
Identifier of the shipping method record selected for this shipment.

The value must be a valid UUID referencing an `id` in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table. This selection determines the logical shipping service (for example, standard or express) applied to the shipment and is used to persist a stable method snapshot at the time of creation.

Business logic may enforce that only shipping methods compatible with the order’s destination region and configuration are accepted. Implementations should validate that the supplied UUID refers to an active, applicable shipping method configuration.

shippingStatus.description:
Initial shipping status for the new shipment header, persisted into the `shipping_status` column of `shopping_mall_shipments`.

Typical values include states like `pending`, `preparing`, or `ready_for_pickup`. Business rules may restrict which initial statuses are allowed for newly created shipments, and subsequent transitions are recorded via updates and shipment event timelines.

carrierName.description:
Name of the carrier that will handle this shipment, corresponding to the `carrier_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

This field is optional and may be null when the carrier has not yet been assigned at creation time. Examples include specific courier brands or postal services. When set, it should match the naming conventions used by operations and reporting systems.

trackingNumber.description:
Carrier-provided tracking identifier for this shipment, mapped to the `tracking_number` column.

For most creation flows this value is null, as tracking information is usually attached only when the shipment is handed over to the carrier. When known at creation time, it can be supplied here so that recipients and operations teams can immediately track the shipment.

expectedShipDate.description:
Planned date and time when the shipment is expected to leave the seller or warehouse, mapped to `expected_ship_date`.

The string must follow ISO 8601 date-time format with timezone information. Null indicates no explicit expectation has been set. This value is typically used for SLA tracking, capacity planning, and customer-facing expectations in order tracking views.

shipmentItems.description:
Collection of shipment item allocations that bind this shipment header to specific order items and SKUs.

Each element creates a row in `shopping_mall_shipment_items` and links the shipment to a particular order line and SKU with a specified quantity. The set of items must respect business constraints such as not exceeding the remaining unshipped quantity for any order item and aligning with the SKUs originally purchased on the order.

IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate.description:
Update request DTO for modifying mutable fields of an existing shipment header in the shopping mall logistics domain.

This structure is used by administrative or seller fulfillment actors to adjust shipping lifecycle data such as status, carrier and tracking details, and key logistics timestamps in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

Immutable relationships—such as the association to the parent order, seller, shipping address snapshot, or shipping method—are intentionally excluded and cannot be changed through this DTO. System-managed timestamps and soft deletion markers are also managed by the backend and therefore are not writable here.

shippingStatus.description:
New shipping status value to be written into the `shipping_status` column of `shopping_mall_shipments`.

Updates are subject to business rules that constrain allowed status transitions, for example preventing reversal from a terminal `delivered` state back to a pre-shipment state. Implementations should validate the transition graph and potentially record detailed events in the shipment timeline.

carrierName.description:
Updated name of the carrier handling this shipment, mapped to the `carrier_name` column.

Set to a non-null string to record the active carrier, or to null when clearing previously stored carrier information is required by business processes. This field is often modified when shipments are rerouted through a different logistics provider.

trackingNumber.description:
Updated tracking identifier supplied by the carrier, persisted in the `tracking_number` column.

This field is commonly set when a shipment moves into a `shipped` or `in_transit` state, and may be cleared or corrected if an error occurred. Implementations should validate that the value follows the expected patterns for the associated carrier when such rules exist.

expectedShipDate.description:
Revised expected shipment departure date and time for the `expected_ship_date` column.

The value must be expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string when provided. Null indicates that no specific expected ship date is currently tracked. This field is often adjusted when fulfillment capacity or carrier pickup schedules change.

shippedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the shipment actually entered the carrier network or was marked as shipped, mapped to the `shipped_at` column.

Supplied as an ISO 8601 date-time string when the shipment moves into a shipped state; null indicates that the shipment has not yet been shipped or that the timestamp is being reset according to business rules. This field is central for measuring outbound processing time and carrier handoff latency.

deliveredAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the shipment was confirmed delivered to the destination, mapped to the `delivered_at` column.

Provided as an ISO 8601 date-time string when the shipment reaches a delivered state. Null means the shipment has not yet been delivered or that the delivery timestamp is being cleared in exceptional workflows such as returns or corrections of erroneously reported delivery events.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new shipment item row under a specific shipment.

This type models the writable fields when an admin or operational system adds a line to an existing shipment identified by a `shipmentCode` in the request path. It captures which order item and SKU are being shipped and how many units are allocated to that shipment.

Server-side logic injects additional context such as the shipment identifier from the path and system-managed timestamps. Clients should use this DTO only for creation scenarios and must not include read-only or system-managed fields.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Identifier of the order item to ship in this shipment item.

The value must reference an existing row in the `shopping_mall_order_items` table that belongs to the same order context as the shipment identified by `shipmentCode`. Business rules enforce that the shipment item does not exceed the remaining unshipped quantity of this order item.

This field is mandatory on creation and anchors the shipment item to the original purchase line.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU variant being shipped in this shipment item.

It must reference an existing SKU in the `shopping_mall_skus` table and should match the SKU used on the referenced order item. This linkage enables variant-specific reconciliation, reporting, and inventory calculations.

API implementations typically validate that the chosen SKU is compatible with the associated order item and shipment context before persisting the record.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the order item to allocate to this shipment.

The quantity must be a positive integer and is validated against the remaining unshipped quantity of the associated order item. Creating multiple shipment items for the same order item and SKU is allowed as long as the cumulative shipped quantity does not surpass the ordered quantity.

This value determines how many physical units of the SKU are expected to be included in the shipment for logistics and tracking purposes.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shipment item row that links shipments to specific order items and SKUs.

This summary is intended for list views and nested usage inside shipment detail responses where only identification, linkage, and quantity information are required, without exposing every possible internal field.

It reflects the core business purpose of the shipment item table: to represent how much of a given order item (and its concrete SKU) has been allocated into a particular shipment, supporting partial shipments, backorders, and reconciliation of shipped versus ordered quantities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment item row.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table and uniquely distinguishes one shipment allocation record from another, even when they refer to the same order item or shipment.

shipment.description:
Summary of the parent shipment that contains this item.

This association provides lightweight shipment context such as shipment code and high-level status, enabling list screens and nested shipment views to render meaningful information without loading the full shipment entity separately.

orderItem.description:
Summary of the underlying order line that this shipment item fulfills.

This object exposes key information about the purchased item and ordered quantity, allowing clients to reconcile how much of the original order line has been shipped or remains pending when inspecting shipment items in aggregate.

sku.description:
Summary of the SKU variant that is being shipped in this item.

The summary includes core variant identifiers and short descriptive fields that are sufficient for list views, packing slips, and operational dashboards without loading the full SKU detail.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the order item that is included in this specific shipment item record.

The quantity must be a positive integer and must not exceed the remaining unshipped quantity for the associated order item. It is used to support partial shipments and detailed fulfillment reconciliation across multiple shipments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment item record was created.

This field is stored as a DateTime in the `shopping_mall_shipment_items` table and is primarily used for auditing, debugging, and timeline reconstruction of fulfillment operations.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment item record was last updated.

This value reflects the most recent modification time for the row, such as adjustments to the allocated quantity or corrections applied during operational workflows.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request parameters for listing shipment items under a specific shipment.

This DTO is used as the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/shipments/{shipmentCode}/items endpoint and encapsulates pagination, sorting, and filter criteria targeting shipment items in the shopping_mall_shipment_items table. It is always scoped to a single shipment identified by the shipmentCode path parameter, which refers to a header row in the shopping_mall_shipments model.

Unlike entity or summary DTOs that mirror a single Prisma model, this request type represents query semantics rather than a persisted row. It aggregates common search patterns for administrative tooling, seller operations consoles, and customer service workflows to inspect how order items and SKUs have been allocated into a particular shipment.

The server may apply default pagination and sorting when corresponding fields are omitted. All filter fields are optional and can be combined to narrow the result set, while still allowing callers to execute broad searches when only shipmentCode is provided in the path.

page.description:
Page number for pagination starting from 1.

Clients use this value together with pageSize to navigate through large result sets when inspecting shipment items belonging to a shipment. When omitted, the server should fall back to a sensible default such as the first page (1) so that basic queries work without explicitly supplying pagination controls.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of shipment item records to return in a single page.

The server may enforce an upper bound (such as 100) to protect performance and prevent excessively large responses. Callers can tune this value within the allowed range to balance page load time against the amount of data shown in a single grid or list view.

orderBy.description:
Field name used to sort shipment item results within the specified shipment scope.

Typical values include created_at or quantity, depending on how operational users prefer to browse shipment items. If omitted, the server applies its default ordering strategy, which is usually based on creation time or a stable primary-key based ordering to provide deterministic pagination.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the orderBy field.

Use "asc" for ascending order so that smaller or earlier values are returned first, which is often desirable when listing items from oldest to newest.

Sort direction applied to the orderBy field.

Use "desc" for descending order so that larger or more recent values are returned first, which is often useful for monitoring the most recent shipment items or changes.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the orderBy field.

Only two values are supported: "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. When omitted, the server may choose its own default direction for the selected orderBy field, typically descending for time-based sorts.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Optional filter constraining results to shipment items created for a specific order item.

When this value is provided, only shipment item rows whose shopping_mall_order_item_id matches the given UUID will be included in the response. This is useful for reconciling how a particular order line was split across one or more shipments for troubleshooting and audit purposes.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Optional filter constraining results to shipment items for a specific SKU.

Operational staff can use this filter to understand how a particular catalog SKU variant is allocated within the target shipment, which is helpful during warehouse operations, picking, and investigations into inventory discrepancies.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the creation timestamp interval used for filtering shipment items.

Only shipment item rows with created_at greater than or equal to this value will be considered when the filter is provided. This allows administrators to restrict searches to recent shipment allocations or to a specific analysis window without scanning the full historical dataset.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the creation timestamp interval used for filtering shipment items.

Only shipment item rows with created_at less than or equal to this value will be considered when the filter is provided. In combination with created_from, it enables time-boxed searches for shipment items created within a particular date-time range.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing shipment item row under a specific shipment.

This type represents the subset of shipment item fields that may be safely modified after creation, such as adjusting shipped quantity before the shipment is finalized. It is used together with a `shipmentCode` and `shipmentItemId` in the request path to target the correct record.

Immutable identifiers including the primary key, shipment reference, order item reference, and SKU reference are not exposed here, ensuring that updates cannot break core relational integrity. System-managed timestamps are also excluded from the request and are refreshed automatically by the persistence layer.

quantity.description:
New quantity of the order item allocated to this shipment item.

When provided, this value replaces the existing quantity for the shipment item, subject to validation that it remains positive and does not cause the total shipped quantity for the associated order item to exceed the ordered quantity.

If omitted, the quantity remains unchanged. This field is optional in the update DTO to support partial updates where only some attributes are modified.

IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.description:
Represents a single shipment event in the detailed shipping and tracking timeline for a specific shipment.

Each record corresponds to a discrete event such as a carrier scan, internal status transition, or manual admin adjustment that occurred during the lifecycle of a shipment. The row is stored in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` Prisma model and is linked to its parent shipment header in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

Shipment events are append-only historical facts that power tracking UIs, operational dashboards, and SLA investigations. They provide a high‑resolution audit trail that complements the high‑level `shipping_status` field on the parent shipment and can be used to reconstruct the full journey of a parcel over time.

id.description:
Primary key for the shipment event row.

This is a server‑generated UUID that uniquely identifies a single tracking or logistics event within the shipping timeline. Clients use this identifier in admin and tooling APIs when they need to reference or update a specific event record.

event_type.description:
Machine‑readable type of event associated with this shipment timeline entry.

Typical examples include values such as `status_change`, `carrier_scan`, `address_correction`, or `manual_override`. Downstream analytics and tracking UIs can group or filter events by this field to provide meaningful progress views and operational reports.

status.description:
Optional shipping status value associated with this event.

When present, this value usually mirrors or refines the `shipping_status` values maintained on the parent `shopping_mall_shipments` record (for example, `pending`, `preparing`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, or `cancelled`). It is `null` for events that do not represent a status change, such as informational carrier scans or metadata updates.

description.description:
Optional human‑readable description that gives additional detail about what happened in this event.

This text is suitable for display in customer‑facing shipment tracking timelines as well as internal support or admin tools, and can summarize carrier messages, internal workflow notes, or corrections applied by operators.

event_time.description:
Timestamp when the event occurred from a business perspective.

This is usually the time recorded by the carrier system or the internal logistics workflow and may differ from the time the row was persisted. It is used to sort and display the the shipment timeline chronologically and to evaluate SLA commitments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment event record was persisted in the database.

This value is generated by the system when the event row is created and can be used for auditing, troubleshooting ingestion delays, or comparing event occurrence time versus recording time.

shipment.description:
Parent shipment header to which this event belongs, represented as a lightweight summary rather than a raw foreign key.

This association replaces the internal `shopping_mall_shipment_id` column and provides the contextual shipment information needed by tracking UIs and admin tools (such as shipment code, current shipping status, and core routing details) without exposing database-specific identifiers.

IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing shipment events belonging to a specific shipment.

This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH `/shoppingMall/shipments/{shipmentCode}/events` endpoint to express complex query conditions that would not fit well in query parameters, such as filtering by event types, constraining time ranges, and paginating long timelines.

Clients use this structure to tailor shipment tracking views for customers, support agents, or internal dashboards by combining filters, sort preferences, and pagination controls.

page.description:
1‑based page index for pagination over the shipment event timeline.

When omitted, the implementation should treat this as requesting the first page of results. Combined with `limit`, this controls which segment of the event list is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipment events to return in a single page.

This value is used together with `page` to slice the ordered event list, and implementations may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

eventTypes.description:
Optional list of event type codes to include in the result.

When provided, only events whose `event_type` matches one of the specified values are returned; when empty or omitted, events of all types are eligible.

status.description:
Optional filter on the `status` field of shipment events.

When set to a non‑null value, only events whose `status` exactly matches this value are included; when omitted or explicitly null, events are not filtered by status.

fromEventTime.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the event time window.

Only events with `event_time` greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned when provided; when omitted or null, no lower time bound is applied.

toEventTime.description:
Exclusive upper bound of the event time window.

Only events with `event_time` strictly earlier than this timestamp are returned when provided; when omitted or null, no upper time bound is applied.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordering shipment events by their `event_time`.

Use `asc` to return events from oldest to newest, or `desc` to return the most recent events first. When omitted, implementations commonly default to descending order for tracking UIs.

Sort direction for ordering shipment events by their `event_time`.

Use `asc` to return events from oldest to newest, or `desc` to return the most recent events first. When omitted, implementations commonly default to descending order for tracking UIs.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for ordering shipment events by their `event_time`.

Use `asc` to return events from oldest to newest, or `desc` to return the most recent events first. When omitted, implementations commonly default to descending order for tracking UIs.

IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an individual shipment event that appears on a shipment's tracking timeline.

Each shipment event captures a discrete occurrence associated with a shipment, such as a carrier scan, status transition, address correction, or manual operator adjustment. The summary type is designed for use in shipment detail responses and tracking views where a concise, but informative, representation of the event is sufficient.

This DTO complements the higher-level shipping status stored on the shipment header by providing fine-grained chronological records used for customer-facing tracking, support investigations, and SLA monitoring.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment event row.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` table and uniquely identifies a single timeline entry within a shipment's event history.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable type of the shipment event.

Typical values include technical event categories such as `status_change`, `carrier_scan`, `address_correction`, or `manual_override`. Downstream systems and UIs use this field to decide how to interpret and display the event.

oneOf.description:
Shipping status value associated with this event when the event represents a status transition.

This string should mirror valid `shipping_status` values on the parent shipment (for example, states such as `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, or `delivered`).

Null when the event does not correspond to a shipping status change.

In this case the event still carries semantic meaning via `event_type` and `description`, but does not alter the parent shipment's high-level status.

status.description:
Optional shipping status value related to this event.

When present, it mirrors the `shipping_status` concept of the parent shipment for this point in time; when absent (null), the event represents an informational or operational occurrence without a status transition.

oneOf.description:
Human-readable description of the shipment event.

This text may be shown in customer-facing tracking timelines or internal tools to explain the meaning of the event with more nuance than `event_type` alone.

Null when there is no additional human-readable description beyond the `event_type` and `status` fields.

This allows the system to store purely structural or system-generated events without redundant free-form text.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description providing additional detail about the event.

Customer-facing UIs and internal dashboards can display this text to explain carrier updates, manual interventions, or system-generated activities in a more understandable way.

event_time.description:
Business timestamp representing when the shipment event occurred.

This time may be derived from carrier feeds, external systems, or internal processing and is used to build an accurate chronological timeline of shipment progress and SLA evaluation.

IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new shipment event associated with an existing shipment.

This DTO captures the business details of the new timeline entry, such as the event type, the time the event occurred, and optional status and description fields. The backend resolves the foreign key to `shopping_mall_shipments` from the `shipmentCode` path parameter and any internal lookup logic, so clients never send shipment identifiers directly.

The create operation is append‑only: each successful call adds a new row into `shopping_mall_shipment_events` without modifying existing events. It is typically used by trusted services integrating with carriers, seller fulfillment systems, or admin tools that need to record granular shipping progress.

event_type.description:
Machine‑readable type of event that is being recorded for the shipment.

Examples include `status_change`, `carrier_scan`, `address_correction`, or `manual_override`. The exact set of values is governed by business rules and carrier integrations, and clients should follow the platform’s documented event type catalog.

status.description:
Optional shipping status value associated with this event.

When provided, this status should be one of the allowed shipment status values used by the platform (for example, `pending`, `preparing`, `ready_for_pickup`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, or `cancelled`). It may be omitted or set to null for events that are informational and do not change the shipment status.

description.description:
Optional human‑readable description or message for this shipment event.

This text can contain carrier messages, internal notes, or customer‑visible explanations about the event and may be shown in tracking timelines or support tooling. When omitted or null, the platform may rely solely on `event_type` and `status` to describe the event.

event_time.description:
Business timestamp when the event occurred.

This should be the time reported by the carrier system or the internal logistics process, not necessarily the time when the API call is made. It is used to sort events chronologically in the shipment timeline and to evaluate shipping and delivery SLAs.

IShoppingMallShipmentEvent.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating mutable fields of an existing shipment event in the shipment timeline.

This DTO is used by admin or internal logistics tools to correct or enrich previously recorded shipment events in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` table. Only non‑key, mutable fields such as the event type, status, human‑readable description, or event occurrence time can be changed; identifiers and the link to the parent shipment remain immutable and are addressed via path parameters.

All properties in this update schema are optional and follow a partial‑update semantics: any field omitted from the payload is left unchanged in the stored event record. Authorization and higher‑level business rules determine whether a given event is eligible for modification (for example, events locked due to legal holds must not be altered).

event_type.description:
Updated machine‑readable type of the shipment event, if it needs to be corrected.

This field follows the same semantics as in the create DTO and the underlying Prisma model (for example, values such as `status_change`, `carrier_scan`, `address_correction`, or `manual_override`). When omitted, the existing event type remains unchanged.

status.description:
Updated shipping status value for this event, or null to clear it.

When provided, the value should be one of the allowed shipment status strings consistent with the shipment header (such as `pending`, `preparing`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, or `cancelled`). If omitted, the stored status is left as‑is; if explicitly set to null, the status association for this event is removed.

description.description:
Updated human‑readable description for the event, or null to clear it.

Use this field to correct or refine the text shown in tracking timelines or operational tools. When omitted, the current description remains unchanged; when explicitly set to null, any previously stored description is removed.

event_time.description:
Corrected business timestamp for when the event occurred.

This can be updated if the original time was incorrect or needs to be aligned with carrier data. When omitted, the original event_time value is preserved.

IShoppingMallOrderTimeline.description:
Order lifecycle timeline view for a customer-facing order in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO composes read-only data from the shopping_mall_orders header table and its related history and case tables, including shopping_mall_order_status_histories, shopping_mall_order_payments, shopping_mall_payment_status_histories, shopping_mall_shipments, shopping_mall_shipment_events, shopping_mall_cancellation_requests, shopping_mall_refund_requests, and shopping_mall_disputes.

The purpose of this type is to provide a single, chronological narrative of the order from placement through payments, logistics, cancellations, refunds, and disputes, optimized for customer and support UI consumption rather than direct table mapping.

order.description:
High-level summary of the order header information, including business order code, currency, totals, status, and key timestamps.

This object is derived primarily from shopping_mall_orders and is tailored for timeline and tracking UIs rather than exposing the entire order entity.

events.description:
Chronologically ordered list of timeline events representing important lifecycle moments for this order.

Each element aggregates information from one or more underlying history or case tables and normalizes it into a consistent event structure that can be rendered in a visual timeline.

IShoppingMallOrderTimeline.IOrderSummary.description:
Condensed order header summary used in the order timeline view.

This type focuses on the minimal set of fields required to understand which order is being inspected and its current overall status, including business order code, monetary grand total, item count, currency, and high-level lifecycle timestamps.

It is based on shopping_mall_orders but intentionally omits internal identifiers and fields that are not needed in a customer-facing timeline context.

order_code.description:
Business-facing order code as stored on shopping_mall_orders.order_code.

This value is shown to customers and support agents and is the primary human-readable key used to identify the order in UIs and communications.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for this order as stored in shopping_mall_orders.currency_code.

All monetary amounts in the associated timeline and related payment/refund information are denominated in this currency.

current_status.description:
Current high-level business status of the order, mapped from shopping_mall_orders.current_status.

Typical values include statuses such as awaiting_payment, payment_confirmed, preparing_shipment, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded, and they are used for quickly understanding the overall lifecycle position of the order.

item_count.description:
Total number of order line items as stored in shopping_mall_orders.item_count.

This value is a denormalized summary used for quick display in timeline headers and does not replace the authoritative detail stored in shopping_mall_order_items.

grand_total_amount.description:
Grand total amount charged for the order, taken from shopping_mall_orders.grand_total_amount.

This amount includes items, discounts, shipping, surcharges, and taxes according to business rules applied at the time of order confirmation.

placed_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer confirmed checkout and the order was placed, mapped from shopping_mall_orders.placed_at.

This is typically the earliest business event in the timeline sequence and provides the starting point for the order history.

IShoppingMallOrderTimeline.IEvent.description:
Normalized representation of a single event in the order lifecycle timeline.

Each event corresponds to one or more rows from the underlying history, payment, shipment, cancellation, refund, or dispute tables, such as shopping_mall_order_status_histories, shopping_mall_order_payments, shopping_mall_payment_status_histories, shopping_mall_shipments, shopping_mall_shipment_events, shopping_mall_cancellation_requests, shopping_mall_refund_requests, and shopping_mall_disputes.

The purpose of this type is to present a unified event structure that can be rendered on a chronological timeline, regardless of its technical origin, while preserving essential metadata such as event category, effective time, status transitions, and short human-readable messages.

id.description:
Stable identifier for this timeline event, typically derived from the underlying primary key of the source record.

This id enables clients to uniquely reference events for features such as deep-linking, tooltips, or support tooling, even though the timeline DTO itself is read-only.

event_category.description:
High-level category describing the type of event represented in this timeline entry.

Examples include order_status, payment, shipment, cancellation, refund, or dispute. This category helps clients visually group events and apply appropriate icons or colors.

event_type.description:
More specific machine-readable event type within the broader event_category.

For example, payment_authorized, payment_captured, shipment_created, shipment_delivered, cancellation_requested, refund_approved, or dispute_opened. Values are derived from status fields and reason codes in the underlying Prisma tables.

effective_at.description:
Timestamp representing when this event took effect from a business perspective.

This is usually mapped from fields such as occurred_at on shopping_mall_order_status_histories, event_time on shopping_mall_shipment_events, requested_at or decided_at on cancellation/refund tables, or opened_at / resolved_at on disputes. The timeline is primarily ordered by this field.

title.description:
Short human-readable title summarizing the event for display in timeline lists and headings.

The title is derived from event_category, event_type, and underlying domain data, and should remain concise while clearly explaining what happened.

description.description:
Detailed human-readable description of the event that can be shown in expanded timeline views or tooltips.

This text aggregates relevant fields such as reason messages, status transitions, and contextual details from the originating Prisma rows so that users and support agents can understand the context without drilling into each raw table. It is always provided for events included in the unified timeline.

status_before.description:
Status value representing the previous state before this event, when the event corresponds to a status transition.

Typical values are derived from fields such as from_status on shopping_mall_order_status_histories, previous_business_status on shopping_mall_payment_status_histories, or similar previous status fields on other history tables. This property may be omitted for event types that do not represent a status change.

status_after.description:
Status value representing the new state after this event, when the event corresponds to a status transition.

Typical values are derived from fields such as to_status on shopping_mall_order_status_histories, new_business_status on shopping_mall_payment_status_histories, or similar new status fields. This property may be omitted for event types that are purely informational and do not represent a discrete state change.

amount_delta.description:
Monetary delta associated with this event in the order currency, such as a captured payment amount or refunded amount.

This field helps surface the financial impact of payment- or refund-related events and is typically mapped from captured_amount, refunded_amount, or similar computed values at the time of the event. It is omitted for event types that do not carry any monetary impact.

IShoppingMallOrderTracking.description:
Logistics-focused tracking view for a customer-facing order in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO composes read-only data from shipment-oriented tables such as shopping_mall_shipments and shopping_mall_shipment_events, while also including contextual information from shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_shipping_addresses, and shopping_mall_shipping_methods where necessary.

The purpose of this type is to provide customers with a clear, concise picture of the current shipping state of their order, including shipment summaries, carrier and tracking information, destination address snapshot, and a chronological list of carrier or logistics events per shipment.

order.description:
High-level summary of the order contextual information used in the tracking view.

This summary is similar to the timeline order summary but is tailored for logistics, emphasizing status, totals, and the presence or absence of active shipments.

shipments.description:
List of shipment-level tracking views associated with this order.

Each shipment entry describes a seller-specific fulfillment unit, including carrier and tracking information, destination address snapshot, shipping method, and a chronological list of shipment events as seen by the logistics system.

IShoppingMallOrderTracking.IOrderSummary.description:
Condensed order summary specifically tailored for use within the logistics tracking view.

This type exposes the business order code, currency, overall order status, grand total, and placed_at timestamp, providing sufficient context for customers to confirm which order they are tracking.

It is derived from shopping_mall_orders and intentionally avoids exposing internal technical identifiers while mirroring the key customer-facing attributes needed for shipping and delivery tracking pages.

order_code.description:
Business-facing order code stored on shopping_mall_orders.order_code.

This is the same value used in path parameter {orderCode} and in customer communications such as emails, receipts, and support references.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for this order as stored in shopping_mall_orders.currency_code.

All displayed amounts in the tracking view correspond to this currency.

current_status.description:
Current high-level business status of the order taken from shopping_mall_orders.current_status.

Even though this view focuses on logistics, this status provides a quick overview of the broader order lifecycle, especially during pre-shipment phases.

grand_total_amount.description:
Grand total amount charged for the order, mapped from shopping_mall_orders.grand_total_amount.

It gives customers and support agents a quick sense of the monetary size of the shipment being tracked.

placed_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was placed by the customer, corresponding to shopping_mall_orders.placed_at.

This timestamp is helpful to validate that the tracking view matches the expected order age and lifecycle stage.

IShoppingMallOrderTracking.IShipment.description:
Shipment-level tracking view associated with a particular order.

This type aggregates fields from shopping_mall_shipments, including shipping_status, carrier and tracking identifiers, and fulfillment timestamps, together with contextual information from shopping_mall_shipping_addresses and shopping_mall_shipping_methods.

It also contains an ordered list of shipment events based on shopping_mall_shipment_events, enabling clients to present a detailed shipment history, including carrier scans, status transitions, and exception handling steps.

shipment_code.description:
Business-facing shipment code, taken from shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code.

This identifier is used in internal and seller-facing tools and can also be shown to customers when multiple shipments exist for a single order.

shipping_status.description:
Current shipping status for this shipment, reflecting shopping_mall_shipments.shipping_status.

Common values include pending, preparing, ready_for_pickup, shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, delivery_failed, returned, or cancelled. They summarize the logistics lifecycle for this shipment.

carrier_name.description:
Name of the carrier handling this shipment, derived from shopping_mall_shipments.carrier_name.

This value is typically a courier company or logistics provider name and may be null when the shipment has not yet been assigned to a specific carrier.

tracking_number.description:
Tracking number assigned by the carrier, mapped from shopping_mall_shipments.tracking_number.

Customers can use this identifier on external carrier portals when available; the platform may also use it to poll carrier APIs for updated events.

expected_ship_date.description:
Optional expected ship date for this shipment, matching shopping_mall_shipments.expected_ship_date.

It indicates when the shipment is planned to leave the seller or warehouse and is useful for displaying promised dispatch time frames. This field may be null if not defined by the business process.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment was actually shipped, mapped from shopping_mall_shipments.shipped_at.

This field becomes non-null once the shipment has entered the carrier network or is otherwise marked as shipped.

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment was confirmed delivered, matching shopping_mall_shipments.delivered_at.

This field is null until delivery is completed or confirmed.

shipping_address.description:
Snapshot of the destination shipping address associated with this shipment.

This object is derived from shopping_mall_shipping_addresses and optionally shopping_mall_customer_address_snapshots and is used to show where the shipment is destined without exposing underlying identity tables directly.

shipping_method.description:
Snapshot of the shipping method information for this shipment.

Derived from shopping_mall_shipping_methods, it includes the method code and display name used to present the service level to customers.

events.description:
Chronologically ordered list of shipment events associated with this shipment.

These events are composed from shopping_mall_shipment_events and contain detailed tracking information such as carrier scans, status changes, and internal logistics notes.

IShoppingMallOrderTracking.IShippingAddr.description:
Snapshot summary of the destination shipping address used for a shipment.

This type maps to shopping_mall_shipping_addresses and exposes only the fields necessary for customer-facing tracking views, such as the recipient name, key address lines, city, postal code, country, and optional region and contact phone.

The goal is to present where the shipment is going without exposing internal address identifiers or identity-specific linkage details.

recipient_name.description:
Name of the recipient for this shipment, mapped from shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.recipient_name.

This value is what carriers and delivery personnel use to identify the consignee at the destination.

line1.description:
First line of the street address, matching shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.line1.

This typically contains the primary street and building information for the destination.

line2.description:
Second line of the street address, matching shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.line2.

This field is optional and may contain apartment, suite, unit, or additional location details when provided.

city.description:
City or locality component of the shipping address, as stored in shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.city.

Displayed to the customer and support for verification and routing clarity.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code for the shipping destination, mapped from shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.postal_code.

This value is used by carriers and logistics systems for routing and delivery.

country_code.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the shipping address, taken from shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.country_code.

It identifies the destination country in a standardized format, enabling both UI display and downstream integration with carriers.

region.description:
Optional region, state, or province for the shipping address, matching shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.region.

This value supplements city and postal code to clarify the destination, especially in countries where regions are critical for logistics.

phone_number.description:
Optional contact phone number associated with this shipping address, matching shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.phone_number.

Used for carrier notifications or delivery coordination with the recipient when permitted by policy.

IShoppingMallOrderTracking.IShippingMeth.description:
Snapshot summary of the shipping method applied to a shipment.

This type maps to shopping_mall_shipping_methods and provides the method code and display name, along with an optional service level description, enabling customers to understand whether the shipment uses standard, express, or another configured delivery service.

It is designed as a compact, read-only view for tracking pages and order detail screens.

method_code.description:
Machine-readable shipping method code from shopping_mall_shipping_methods.method_code.

Typical values include labels such as standard, express, or provider-specific codes, and they are primarily used internally for routing and pricing logic.

display_name.description:
Human-readable shipping method name, mapped from shopping_mall_shipping_methods.display_name.

This label is presented to customers and sellers to describe the delivery service, for example "Standard Shipping" or "Express Courier".

service_level_description.description:
Optional description for the shipping service level, taken from shopping_mall_shipping_methods.service_level_description.

This text can outline expected delivery windows, handling characteristics, or other information relevant to customer expectations.

IShoppingMallOrderTracking.IShipmentEven.description:
Detailed event from the shipping and tracking timeline of a specific shipment.

This type maps to shopping_mall_shipment_events and provides an event_type, optional shipping status, an optional human-friendly description, and the event_time stored in the database.

It is used to build the per-shipment tracking history shown in order tracking and support tooling, and may reflect both carrier-originated and system-originated updates.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable event type, matching shopping_mall_shipment_events.event_type.

Typical values include status_change, carrier_scan, address_correction, manual_override, or other domain-specific codes that categorize the kind of tracking event.

status.description:
Optional shipping status value associated with this event, mapped from shopping_mall_shipment_events.status.

When present, this status should mirror or refine values used in shopping_mall_shipments.shipping_status, such as in_transit, out_for_delivery, or delivered.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description providing more detail about this shipment event, matching shopping_mall_shipment_events.description.

This may contain carrier messages, internal logistics notes, or customer-visible text suitable for tracking UIs.

event_time.description:
Timestamp when the event occurred, taken from shopping_mall_shipment_events.event_time.

The shipment’s event history is usually ordered by this field to present a chronological view of tracking updates.

IShoppingMallShipmentTracking.description:
Read-model DTO representing a comprehensive tracking view for a single shipment in the shopping mall platform.

This schema aggregates shipment header information from the `shopping_mall_shipments` table together with related snapshot and event data from subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_shipment_events`, `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`, and `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses`. It is designed for customer and guest user tracking experiences rather than for direct persistence.

The tracking view exposes a human-friendly shipment code, high-level shipping status, carrier and tracking identifiers, key lifecycle timestamps, the resolved shipping method metadata, the destination shipping address snapshot, and an ordered list of timeline events that describe the shipment journey. It mirrors the business semantics documented in the Prisma models while remaining stable as a public API contract.

shipmentCode.description:
Business-facing shipment code associated with this shipment.

This value corresponds to the `shipment_code` column in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and is the human-readable identifier customers and sellers see in order and tracking UIs. It is globally unique across the platform and is used as the path parameter `shipmentCode` in tracking APIs.

shippingStatus.description:
Current high-level shipping status for the shipment.

This field reflects the `shipping_status` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and aggregates the latest state derived from the shipment and its events. Typical values include `pending`, `preparing`, `ready_for_pickup`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, or `cancelled`. Exact enumerations are defined at the business rule level and recorded in the shipment and event records.

carrierName.description:
Name of the carrier responsible for delivering this shipment, if assigned.

When present, this value corresponds to the `carrier_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and may represent courier brands, postal services, or logistics providers. It is null when a carrier has not yet been selected or when the shipment is fulfilled via a method that does not expose a named carrier.

trackingNumber.description:
Carrier-provided tracking number associated with this shipment, if available.

When populated, this value corresponds to the `tracking_number` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and can be used to cross-reference external carrier portals. It is null when the shipment does not yet have a carrier tracking identifier or when the chosen shipping method does not support tracking.

expectedShipDate.description:
Estimated date and time when the shipment is expected to leave the seller or warehouse.

This field is derived from the `expected_ship_date` column in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and is used for SLA management and customer expectations. It is null when no expected ship date has been scheduled or recorded for the shipment.

shippedAt.description:
Timestamp when the shipment was first handed off to the carrier or marked as shipped.

This field corresponds to the `shipped_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`. It typically reflects the moment the package enters the carrier network, based on either internal system events or carrier-confirmed scan events.

deliveredAt.description:
Timestamp when the shipment was recorded as successfully delivered, if applicable.

This value mirrors the `delivered_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and represents the final delivery confirmation. It is null when the shipment has not yet been delivered or if the shipment ultimately failed or was returned.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the shipment record was initially created in the system.

This field corresponds to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and indicates when the shipment header was first persisted, usually shortly after order confirmation or shipment creation by a seller.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the shipment record was last updated in the system.

This field mirrors the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and changes whenever shipment-level fields such as status, carrier assignment, or timing information are modified.

shippingMethod.description:
Shipping method metadata associated with this shipment.

The information is derived from the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table and represents the method selected at order or shipment creation time, including the internal method code, customer-facing display name, and optional service level description.

shippingAddress.description:
Destination shipping address snapshot used for this shipment.

This object is composed from the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and captures the full recipient and address details that were effective when the shipment was created. It is immutable for the life of the shipment and is unaffected by subsequent changes to the customer address book.

events.description:
Chronologically ordered list of shipment tracking events.

Each element corresponds to a row in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` table for this shipment and captures one discrete step in the shipment lifecycle, such as status changes, carrier scans, address corrections, or manual overrides. The array is typically sorted by event time ascending to represent the full tracking timeline.

IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingShippingMet.description:
Snapshot of the shipping method configuration associated with a shipment.

This object maps directly to a row in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table at the time the shipment was created, exposing the internal method code, customer-facing display name, and an optional service level description.

Using a dedicated type allows shipment tracking responses to cleanly embed method metadata while decoupling clients from any internal configuration tables that may evolve independently from persisted snapshots.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipping method record.

This field corresponds to the primary key `id` in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` and uniquely identifies the method configuration used when the shipment was created.

methodCode.description:
Machine-readable shipping method code used internally by the platform.

This value is derived from the `method_code` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` and typically encodes categories such as `standard`, `express`, or carrier-specific service identifiers. It is used for routing logic and analytics, not usually displayed directly to end users.

displayName.description:
Human-readable shipping method name presented to customers and sellers.

This field corresponds to the `display_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` and contains labels such as "Standard Shipping" or "Express Courier" that appear in checkout and tracking UIs.

serviceLevelDescription.description:
Optional free-form description of the shipping service level.

This value is taken from the `service_level_description` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` and can describe expected delivery windows, handling notes, or other service characteristics. It is null when no additional description is configured.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this shipping method record was originally created.

This mirrors the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` and is primarily useful for internal auditing and configuration history.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this shipping method record was last updated.

This value corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` and changes whenever method metadata such as labels or descriptions are modified.

IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingShippingAdd.description:
Snapshot of the destination shipping address used for an order and its shipments.

This object directly reflects a row in the `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` table and exposes the recipient and address details exactly as captured at checkout. It is immutable for that order and shipment, ensuring that historical records remain stable even if the customer later edits their address book.

The snapshot may optionally reference a customer address snapshot record in the identity domain, but this schema focuses on the flattened address fields required to display shipping destinations and support carrier interactions.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipping address snapshot.

This field maps to the primary key `id` in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and uniquely identifies the stored snapshot row for the order and its derived shipments.

recipientName.description:
Name of the person or entity designated to receive the shipment.

This value is taken from the `recipient_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and is captured exactly as entered at checkout for display on labels and tracking details.

line1.description:
First line of the street address or primary address information.

This field corresponds to the `line1` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and usually contains street, building, or house information.

line2.description:
Second line of the street address, if provided.

This value mirrors the `line2` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and is commonly used for apartment numbers, suites, or additional building details. It is null when no second line was provided.

city.description:
City or locality portion of the shipping address.

This field maps to the `city` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and is used for carrier routing and display in shipment tracking views.

postalCode.description:
Postal or ZIP code for the shipping destination.

The value is derived from the `postal_code` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and must follow the formatting rules of the destination country.

countryCode.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code indicating the destination country.

This field corresponds to the `country_code` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and enables consistent country-level routing and analytics.

region.description:
Region, state, or province component of the address, when applicable.

This value mirrors the `region` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and may be required for certain countries to ensure accurate delivery.

phoneNumber.description:
Contact phone number associated with the shipping address, if provided.

This field corresponds to the `phone_number` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and is often used by carriers to coordinate delivery or by support teams during investigations.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot row was created.

This mirrors the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and generally coincides with order confirmation time.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this shipping address snapshot row was last updated.

This value corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses` and only changes if a correction or administrative update is applied to the snapshot.

deletedAt.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this address snapshot, if it has been logically removed from typical queries.

This field reflects the `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses`. It allows the platform to hide obsolete or invalid snapshots from normal views while preserving them for legal and audit purposes.

IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingEvent.description:
Single tracking or status event associated with a shipment.

This object corresponds to a row in the `shopping_mall_shipment_events` table and represents a discrete point in the shipment timeline, such as a status change, carrier scan, or manual adjustment recorded by the platform.

Events are typically ordered by their business-level `event_time` to construct a complete, human-readable history of shipment progress in the tracking view.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment event row.

This field mirrors the primary key `id` in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` and uniquely identifies the recorded event for internal auditing and correlation.

eventType.description:
Machine-readable classification of the shipment event.

This value is taken from the `event_type` column in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` and may include categories such as `status_change`, `carrier_scan`, `address_correction`, or `manual_override`. It enables filtering and analytics over event streams.

status.description:
Optional shipping status value associated with this event.

When present, this field mirrors the `status` column in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` and typically aligns with the same status vocabulary used by the `shipping_status` column on `shopping_mall_shipments`. It is null for events that do not represent a status transition.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description that explains the event.

This value corresponds to the `description` column in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` and is intended for use in customer- and agent-facing UIs to provide context such as carrier messages or internal notes.

eventTime.description:
Business-effective timestamp when the event occurred.

This field maps to the `event_time` column in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` and should be used as the primary sort key when presenting the shipment timeline. It may originate from carrier data or internal system time.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this event row was persisted in the system.

This mirrors the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipment_events` and is primarily used for storage auditing and debugging purposes.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusAnalytics.IReque.description:
Filter and configuration parameters for computing order status analytics.

This request DTO allows admin users to specify time range, segmentation, and grouping options for aggregating orders from shopping_mall_orders and related snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_order_daily_stats. It is used as the request body for the order status analytics endpoint.

from.description: Start of the time range (inclusive) to consider when aggregating order statuses. Must be earlier than or equal to `to` and provided in ISO 8601 date-time format.

to.description: End of the time range (inclusive) to consider when aggregating order statuses. Must be equal to or later than `from` and provided in ISO 8601 date-time format.

granularity.description: Desired aggregation granularity for analytics buckets. Common values include "day", "week", and "month". This determines how time is bucketed when computing statistics.

oneOf.description: Optional identifier of a seller to restrict analytics to orders associated with that seller. When null, analytics are computed across the entire marketplace.

sellerId.description: Optional identifier of a seller to restrict analytics to orders associated with that seller. When null, analytics are computed across the entire marketplace.

oneOf.description: Optional logical segment identifier for customers (for example, VIP segment, new customers, or regional groups). When provided, analytics are restricted to orders belonging to customers in this segment.

customerSegment.description: Optional logical segment identifier for customers (for example, VIP segment, new customers, or regional groups). When provided, analytics are restricted to orders belonging to customers in this segment.

statusFilter.description: Optional list of order statuses to include in the analytics. When provided, only orders whose current status is in this list are considered.

limitBuckets.description: Maximum number of analytics buckets to return. Used to protect dashboards from excessively large result sets and to support pagination or top-N style views.

offsetBuckets.description: Offset applied when slicing the ordered list of analytics buckets. This can be used to implement pagination across buckets.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusAnalytics.description:
