Aggregated analytics model representing order status distributions and related metrics across the marketplace or filtered segments.

This schema is used as the response body for administrative order status analytics. It represents pre-computed or on-demand aggregated statistics derived primarily from shopping_mall_orders and, optionally, snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_order_daily_stats. Each instance captures metrics for one or more segments or buckets, suitable for dashboards and reporting tools.

The structure focuses on grouping dimensions (such as overall marketplace, per seller, or per status) and aggregated measures including counts and ratios. It is read-only, analytics-only data and never maps directly to a single Prisma row.

buckets.description: List of aggregated analytics buckets, each representing order status statistics for a specific grouping key (for example, global marketplace, per seller, per day, or per status).

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this analytics payload was generated by the system. Useful for cache validation and dashboard refresh logic.

timeRange.description: Time range over which the analytics were computed. Mirrors the interpreted filter range rather than raw request input.

grouping.description: Effective grouping configuration used when computing the analytics, such as granularity and dimensions (status, seller, date).

IShoppingMallOrderStatusAnalytics.IBucke.description:
Single analytics bucket representing aggregated order status metrics for a specific combination of grouping dimensions in the shopping mall order domain.

A bucket typically corresponds to a particular status or to a combination of status, time period, and optional segmentation dimensions such as seller, country, or channel. Each bucket exposes precomputed counts and ratios that support operational monitoring, dashboards, and reporting derived from transactional tables like `shopping_mall_orders` and related status history models.

This DTO is used inside higher-level order status analytics responses (for example, `IShoppingMallOrderStatusAnalytics`) and is not persisted directly. All numeric fields are server-computed aggregates; clients should treat them as read-only analytics values and must not attempt to infer raw event-level data from a single bucket.

key.description:
Opaque identifier for this analytics bucket combining the effective grouping dimensions.

In simple cases the key can be just an order status code (for example, `PAID` or `DELIVERED`). In more complex segmentations it can be a composite key that concatenates a date, status, and optional actor or geography information (for example, `2024-01-01|PAID` or `APAC|DELIVERED`). Clients should not depend on a specific key format and should treat it strictly as an identifier for charting and correlation.

label.description:
Human-readable label for this bucket suitable for display in charts, tables, and dashboards.

Common examples include localized status labels such as `Paid`, `Shipped`, `Delivered`, or richer labels that combine a date and status like `2024-01-01 – Paid` or `Seller A – Delivered`. The label is intended purely for presentation and may be localized depending on the analytics endpoint.

status.description:
Primary order lifecycle status represented by this bucket.

Typical values include business-level statuses such as `pending`, `pending_payment`, `paid`, `fulfilled`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, or `refunded`. The exact set of values is aligned with the order status definitions used in `shopping_mall_orders` and related status history models, and may be documented in business policy or configuration tables.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of orders that fall into this bucket according to the applied filters and grouping dimensions.

This count is the primary volume metric for the bucket and typically equals the sum of all terminal and in‑progress status counts that conceptually belong to the bucket. It is always a non‑negative integer derived from transactional data at query time.

pendingPaymentOrders.description:
Number of orders in pending‑payment or equivalent early payment states within this bucket.

This metric helps operators understand how many orders are waiting for successful payment confirmation at the time represented by the bucket. The exact status mapping to "pending payment" is determined by business rules configured in the order lifecycle and payment subsystems.

paidOrders.description:
Number of orders in a paid state within this bucket.

These are orders that have successfully completed payment authorization and capture according to the payment subsystem, but that may not yet be fulfilled or shipped. The value is a non‑negative count derived from `shopping_mall_orders` and payment status history.

fulfilledOrders.description:
Number of orders that have reached a fulfilled state (picked and packed) within this bucket.

Fulfilled orders are typically ready for handover to carriers but may not yet have left the warehouse. Exact mapping of underlying technical statuses to the fulfilled concept is defined by the order fulfillment configuration for the platform.

shippedOrders.description:
Number of orders that have been handed over to shipping carriers and marked as shipped within this bucket.

This count reflects orders that are in transit to customers. The platform usually derives this from shipment headers and shipment event timelines tied back to the originating orders.

deliveredOrders.description:
Number of orders successfully delivered to customers within this bucket.

Delivered orders are considered completed for most revenue and fulfillment metrics. The definition of "delivered" may rely on explicit carrier delivery events, customer confirmation, or automatic assumptions configured in business policies.

cancelledOrders.description:
Number of orders that were cancelled before completion within this bucket, regardless of who initiated the cancellation.

This metric aggregates customer‑initiated cancellations, seller‑initiated cancellations, and administrative cancellations as long as they are mapped to a cancellation lifecycle state in the order domain.

refundedOrders.description:
Number of orders that have at least one refund operation associated with them within this bucket.

The count can include fully refunded orders as well as partially refunded ones. It is derived from payment refund records linked to orders and is used to understand post‑purchase adjustment volume for the given segment.

pendingRatio.description:
Proportion of orders in a pending or early stage relative to `totalOrders` for this bucket.

The value is a server‑computed floating‑point number in the range from 0 to 1 inclusive, typically calculated as a subset of "pending" statuses divided by `totalOrders`. This field is optional: analytics implementations may omit it when a ratio is not meaningful (for example, when `totalOrders` is zero) or when the specific bucket configuration does not track a pending ratio.

completedRatio.description:
Proportion of orders in a completed state (usually delivered) relative to `totalOrders` for this bucket.

The value is a server‑computed floating‑point number in the range from 0 to 1 inclusive, often computed as `deliveredOrders / totalOrders`. This property is optional and may be omitted when `totalOrders` is zero, when the concept of "completed" does not apply to the bucket configuration, or when the backend chooses to expose only raw counts without ratios.

cancelledRatio.description:
Proportion of cancelled orders relative to `totalOrders` for this bucket.

The value is a server‑computed floating‑point number in the range from 0 to 1 inclusive, typically computed as `cancelledOrders / totalOrders`. This property is optional and may be absent when there are no cancelled orders, when `totalOrders` is zero, or when the analytics endpoint is configured to expose only counts without ratio metrics.

IAnalyticsTimeRange.description:
Generic time range model used for analytics queries across the shopping mall platform.

The type captures an explicit start and end timestamp for aggregating metrics, and is reused by multiple analytics DTOs such as review volume analytics, moderation analytics, payment summaries, and order status analytics. It defines the temporal window over which underlying transactional and snapshot tables are scanned.

Timestamps are supplied in ISO 8601 `date-time` format, typically in UTC (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`). Implementations commonly normalize input values to a canonical timezone and precision before executing queries, and they validate that the `to` value is greater than or equal to `from`. Individual analytics endpoints may impose additional limits on maximum window length or restrict how far back in time clients are allowed to query.

from.description:
Start timestamp of the analytics window in ISO 8601 `date-time` format, typically expressed in UTC.

The `from` value is usually treated as inclusive, meaning events at or after this timestamp are considered in the analytics window. Implementations may truncate or round the value to a coarser granularity (for example, to the beginning of the minute or hour) depending on the specific analytics endpoint.

to.description:
End timestamp of the analytics window in ISO 8601 `date-time` format, typically expressed in UTC.

Most analytics endpoints require `to` to be greater than or equal to `from`; if the values are equal, the window is interpreted as a single instant or the smallest supported unit. Some endpoints treat `to` as exclusive, others as inclusive, and the exact semantics are documented at the operation level. Implementations may also enforce maximum window length and return validation errors when the requested period is too long.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusAnalytics.IGroup.description:
Effective grouping configuration used when computing order status analytics.

Represents how buckets are organized along time and dimension axes, such as by status only, by status per day, or by seller and status.

granularity.description: Granularity used for time-based aggregation, such as "day", "week", or "month".

dimensions.description: List of non-time grouping dimensions used for bucketing analytics results. Examples include "status", "seller", or "region".

IShoppingMallShippingPerformanceAnalytic.description:
Analytics query parameters defining time range, grouping, filters, and pagination for shipping performance statistics.

This request DTO is used by administrative actors to query shipping and delivery performance analytics backed by snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats and related marketplace statistics tables. It controls the time window, grouping dimensions, and additional filters for computing aggregated shipping metrics.

from.description: Start of the time range (inclusive) for which shipping performance statistics should be computed. Must be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format and be earlier than or equal to `to`.

to.description: End of the time range (inclusive) for which shipping performance statistics should be computed. Must be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format and be equal to or later than `from`.

granularity.description: Time granularity for aggregations, such as "day", "week", or "month". This determines how snapshot records are bucketed along the time axis.

groupBy.description: List of grouping dimensions to apply when computing shipping performance metrics. Typical values include "shippingMethod", "country", "region", or "seller".

oneOf.description: Optional seller identifier used to restrict analytics to shipments and orders associated with a specific seller. When null, analytics are computed across all sellers.

sellerId.description: Optional seller identifier used to restrict analytics to shipments and orders associated with a specific seller. When null, analytics are computed across all sellers.

oneOf.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code filter limiting analytics to shipments destined for a specific country.

countryCode.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code filter limiting analytics to shipments destined for a specific country.

oneOf.description: Optional logical region code filter aligning with shopping_mall_regions or related configuration tables.

regionCode.description: Optional logical region code filter aligning with shopping_mall_regions or related configuration tables.

oneOf.description: Optional shipping method code used to limit analytics to a specific shipping option or carrier-defined method.

shippingMethodCode.description: Optional shipping method code used to limit analytics to a specific shipping option or carrier-defined method.

page.description: 1-based page index for paginated analytics results. Used together with `limit` to control which slice of the aggregated result set is returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of aggregated analytics rows to return in a single page. Upper-bounded by system configuration to protect analytics infrastructure.

IShoppingMallShippingPerformanceAnalytic.description:
Summary view of daily shipping and delivery performance analytics for the shopping mall platform.

Each instance represents an aggregated metrics row derived from the underlying `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` snapshot table for a particular shipping method code and calendar date.

This summary DTO is optimized for list and dashboard views where operations and logistics teams monitor fulfillment speed, on-time delivery rates, and failure patterns over time.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this shipping performance statistics snapshot row.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.id` and is used as the primary key when referencing or caching a particular analytics record.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these shipping performance metrics are calculated.

This value comes from `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.stats_date`. Although conceptually date-only, it is represented as a full ISO-8601 `date-time` string, and the time component SHOULD be normalized to midnight UTC for consistency across the analytics pipeline.

shipping_method_code.description:
Business code identifying the shipping method or carrier/service combination used for aggregation.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipping_method_code`. It can represent logical methods such as `standard`, `express`, or carrier-specific codes and is used to group and filter analytics across time.

shipping_method.description:
Summary information about the shipping method configuration associated with this analytics row.

This association is derived via `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shopping_mall_shipping_method_id` to the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` model and exposed as `IShoppingMallShippingMethod.ISummary` so that dashboards and analytics clients can display human‑readable method metadata (such as method name and carrier) without issuing additional lookup calls.

shipment_created_count.description:
Number of shipments created on this date using this shipping method.

This value is taken from `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_created_count` and represents the count of distinct shipment records that entered the "created" state for the associated method and date.

shipment_shipped_count.description:
Number of shipments that transitioned to a shipped state on this date using this shipping method.

This maps to `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_shipped_count` and is useful for understanding fulfillment throughput and backlog resolution on a daily basis.

shipment_delivered_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as delivered on this date using this shipping method.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_delivered_count` and helps measure successful delivery volume per method and day.

shipment_delivery_failed_count.description:
Number of shipments that entered a delivery failed state on this date using this shipping method.

This exposes `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_delivery_failed_count` and is used to monitor failed deliveries that may require customer support or logistics intervention.

shipment_returned_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as returned to sender on this date using this shipping method.

This is derived from `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_returned_count` and allows tracking of return logistics and potential issues such as incorrect addresses or refused deliveries.

median_fulfillment_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from order payment confirmation to shipment handover (fulfillment cycle) for shipments associated with this method on this date.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.median_fulfillment_time_hours`. It is a double-precision number representing the median, not the mean, to better capture typical operational performance without being overly influenced by extreme outliers.

median_transit_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from shipment handover to delivery confirmation (transit cycle) for shipments using this method delivered on this date.

This exposes `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.median_transit_time_hours` and is used to evaluate carrier performance and route efficiency for each shipping method.

on_time_delivery_rate.description:
Proportion of shipments delivered on or before their expected delivery time threshold for this method on this date.

This comes from `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.on_time_delivery_rate` and is represented as a floating-point value between 0 and 1, where 1 means 100% of deliveries were considered on time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping performance stats row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.created_at` and indicates when the snapshot was initially computed and persisted.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping performance stats row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.updated_at` and is updated whenever the statistics for the same `(shipping_method_code, stats_date)` combination are recalculated or adjusted.

IShoppingMallOrderSearch.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for performing advanced administrative searches over orders in the shoppingMall domain.

This type encapsulates complex search criteria, pagination, and sorting instructions that are applied primarily to the `shopping_mall_orders` table and its subsidiary relations such as `shopping_mall_order_items`, `shopping_mall_order_status_histories`, `shopping_mall_order_payments`, and `shopping_mall_shipments`.

It is designed for back-office and operational tooling where administrators need to locate orders by code, customer identity, seller identity, statuses, and time ranges while safely constraining result sizes through pagination and ordering options.

order_codes.description:
Optional list of business-facing order codes to match exactly.

When provided, the search is restricted to orders whose `order_code` is in this set. Values correspond to `shopping_mall_orders.order_code` and should be human-friendly identifiers such as formatted sequences.

items.description: Order code to match against `shopping_mall_orders.order_code`. Typically a human-readable identifier such as a formatted sequence.

customer_ids.description:
Optional list of customer identifiers whose orders should be returned.

Each value corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.shopping_mall_customer_id`. When provided, only orders owned by these customers are considered. This field is intended for administrative tools and must not be accepted from end-customer self-service contexts.

items.description: Customer identifier referencing `shopping_mall_customers.id`.

guestuser_ids.description:
Optional list of guest user identifiers whose orders should be returned.

Each value corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.shopping_mall_guestuser_id`. When provided, only orders placed by these guest users are considered.

items.description: Guest user identifier referencing `shopping_mall_guestusers.id`.

seller_ids.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers used to find orders that contain items owned by these sellers.

Filtering by seller requires joins through subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_order_items` and `shopping_mall_order_item_sellers`. This filter is typically used for seller performance analysis or dispute investigation.

items.description: Seller identifier referencing `shopping_mall_sellers.id`.

current_statuses.description:
Optional list of order-level current status values to match against `shopping_mall_orders.current_status`.

Examples include values such as "awaiting_payment", "payment_confirmed", "preparing_shipment", "shipped", "delivered", "cancelled", or "refunded" depending on configured business states.

items.description: Order status value that should match `shopping_mall_orders.current_status`.

payment_statuses.description:
Optional list of payment business status values used to filter orders by the state of related payments.

Values are applied to `shopping_mall_order_payments.business_status` through joins and may include states such as "pending", "paid", "partially_refunded", "refunded", "chargeback", or "cancelled".

items.description: Payment business status value that should match `shopping_mall_order_payments.business_status`.

shipment_statuses.description:
Optional list of shipment status values used to filter orders by the state of their associated shipments.

Values correspond to `shopping_mall_shipments.shipping_status` and may include states such as "pending", "preparing", "ready_for_pickup", "shipped", "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered", "delivery_failed", "returned", or "cancelled".

items.description: Shipment status value that should match `shopping_mall_shipments.shipping_status`.

created_from.description:
Lower bound for the order creation time window, inclusive.

When provided, only orders whose `shopping_mall_orders.created_at` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned. Use ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC or with explicit timezone offset.

created_to.description:
Upper bound for the order creation time window, inclusive.

When provided, only orders whose `shopping_mall_orders.created_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned. Use ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC or with explicit timezone offset.

placed_from.description:
Lower bound for the business "placed_at" time window, inclusive.

This filter is applied to `shopping_mall_orders.placed_at`, which captures when the customer confirmed checkout. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

placed_to.description:
Upper bound for the business "placed_at" time window, inclusive.

This filter is applied to `shopping_mall_orders.placed_at` and restricts results to orders placed no later than this timestamp.

updated_from.description:
Lower bound for the last update time window, inclusive.

When provided, only orders whose `shopping_mall_orders.updated_at` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned. This is useful for polling or incremental synchronization scenarios.

updated_to.description:
Upper bound for the last update time window, inclusive.

When provided, only orders whose `shopping_mall_orders.updated_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned.

min_grand_total_amount.description:
Optional minimum bound for the order grand total amount.

When provided, only orders whose `shopping_mall_orders.grand_total_amount` is greater than or equal to this value are returned.

max_grand_total_amount.description:
Optional maximum bound for the order grand total amount.

When provided, only orders whose `shopping_mall_orders.grand_total_amount` is less than or equal to this value are returned.

item_sku_ids.description:
Optional list of SKU identifiers used to find orders that contain particular SKUs.

Filtering by SKU requires joins to `shopping_mall_order_items` and `shopping_mall_skus`. This is useful for product-specific investigations and analytics.

items.description: SKU identifier referencing `shopping_mall_skus.id`.

free_text.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to a configured subset of textual order fields.

Typical implementations apply this term to fields such as `order_code`, customer-visible names, or product titles using full-text search or ILIKE-based matching.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination over the result set.

When omitted, implementations commonly default to the first page. This value is combined with `limit` to compute offset in the query.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

This value should respect an upper bound configured at the platform level to prevent excessively large responses.

sort_key.description:
Optional logical sort key that selects which order field is used for ordering the results.

Common values include logical names such as "created_at", "placed_at", "grand_total_amount", or "current_status". The exact set of supported keys is defined by the implementation.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction applied to the chosen `sort_key`.

Typical values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. When omitted, a sensible default such as descending creation time should be used.

IShoppingMallOrderSearch.ISummary.description:
Summary view of customer orders for search and list screens in the shopping mall platform.

Each instance represents the high-level state of a single order, derived from the `shopping_mall_orders` primary table, and is optimized for order history, admin search, and operational dashboards where detailed line items are not required.

This summary DTO purposely excludes nested order items, shipments, and payment details to keep responses lightweight, while still exposing key identifiers, monetary totals, lifecycle timestamps, and status information for filtering and sorting.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order record.

This value is the primary key `shopping_mall_orders.id` and is used as the canonical reference when loading full order detail or performing order-specific operations.

order_code.description:
Business-facing order code shown to customers and used in communications, invoices, and support interactions.

This maps to `shopping_mall_orders.order_code`, which is typically a human-friendly formatted sequence and is unique across the platform to allow easy sharing and search by both customers and staff.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code used for all monetary values in this order, such as `USD` or `KRW`.

This property is backed by `shopping_mall_orders.currency_code` and is important for correctly displaying amounts and performing currency-aware analytics.

current_status.description:
Current high-level business status of the order.

This value is read from `shopping_mall_orders.current_status` and can represent states such as `awaiting_payment`, `payment_confirmed`, `preparing_shipment`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, or `refunded`. The precise lifecycle is further detailed in the `shopping_mall_order_status_histories` table but is summarized here for quick filtering and display.

item_count.description:
Total count of order line items at the time of order confirmation.

This is a denormalized convenience value mapped from `shopping_mall_orders.item_count` and is useful for quick overview without loading the full `shopping_mall_order_items` collection.

grand_total_amount.description:
Total amount charged to the customer for this order in the order currency.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.grand_total_amount` and already includes item subtotals, discounts, shipping fees, surcharges, and taxes according to the business rules applied at confirmation time.

placed_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer confirmed checkout and the order record was created.

This value comes directly from `shopping_mall_orders.placed_at` and is typically used to sort order history and time-based analytics.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order row was first persisted in the database.

This maps to `shopping_mall_orders.created_at` and may be identical or very close to `placed_at`, depending on how the application creates and finalizes order records.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this order row was last updated, including status transitions and summary field changes.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.updated_at` and is useful for detecting recently modified orders in operational views.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this order, if it has been logically removed from standard views.

This property is based on `shopping_mall_orders.deleted_at`. It is `null` for active orders and set to a concrete timestamp when an order is soft-deleted for business, legal, or compliance reasons while still being retained for audit purposes.

IShoppingMallShipmentSearch.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for performing advanced searches over shipments in the shoppingMall domain.

This type encapsulates shipment-level search criteria, pagination, and sorting instructions that are primarily applied to the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and its subsidiary relations such as `shopping_mall_shipment_items`, `shopping_mall_shipment_events`, `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses`, and `shopping_mall_shipping_methods`.

It is designed for use by authenticated customers, sellers, and internal tools to locate shipments based on codes, order references, carriers, tracking numbers, statuses, and time ranges while keeping result sets bounded with paging options.

shipment_codes.description:
Optional list of shipment codes to match exactly.

Each value corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code` and is used to restrict results to specific fulfillment units.

items.description: Shipment code to match against `shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code`.

order_codes.description:
Optional list of order codes used to find shipments belonging to those orders.

Values are matched against `shopping_mall_orders.order_code` via the `shopping_mall_shipments.shopping_mall_order_id` relation.

items.description: Order code corresponding to `shopping_mall_orders.order_code`.

order_ids.description:
Optional list of order identifiers whose shipments should be returned.

Each identifier corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipments.shopping_mall_order_id` referencing `shopping_mall_orders.id`. This filter is typically used by internal tools rather than customer-facing UIs.

items.description: Order identifier referencing `shopping_mall_orders.id`.

seller_ids.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers whose shipments should be returned.

Each identifier corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipments.shopping_mall_seller_id` referencing `shopping_mall_sellers.id`. This filter is particularly useful for seller dashboards and performance monitoring.

items.description: Seller identifier referencing `shopping_mall_sellers.id`.

shipping_statuses.description:
Optional list of shipping status values to match against `shopping_mall_shipments.shipping_status`.

Examples include internal status codes such as "pending", "preparing", "ready_for_pickup", "shipped", "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered", "delivery_failed", "returned", or "cancelled".

items.description: Shipping status value that should match `shopping_mall_shipments.shipping_status`.

carrier_names.description:
Optional list of carrier names used to filter shipments by the logistic provider.

Values match `shopping_mall_shipments.carrier_name` and can be used to identify shipments handled by a particular courier or carrier group.

items.description: Carrier name to match against `shopping_mall_shipments.carrier_name`.

tracking_numbers.description:
Optional list of tracking numbers used to locate specific shipments.

Values correspond to `shopping_mall_shipments.tracking_number` and are commonly used in customer-facing tracking flows and support investigations.

items.description: Tracking number to match against `shopping_mall_shipments.tracking_number`.

destination_country_codes.description:
Optional list of destination country codes used to filter shipments by delivery country.

Values correspond to `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.country_code` and must be ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes such as "US" or "KR".

items.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code taken from `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.country_code`.

destination_regions.description:
Optional list of destination regions or states used to filter shipments.

Values correspond to `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.region` and may represent states, provinces, or other regional subdivisions depending on the country.

items.description: Region or state value matching `shopping_mall_shipping_addresses.region`.

created_from.description:
Lower bound for the shipment creation time window, inclusive.

This filter applies to `shopping_mall_shipments.created_at` and is commonly used for time-based dashboards and monitoring.

created_to.description:
Upper bound for the shipment creation time window, inclusive.

This filter applies to `shopping_mall_shipments.created_at` and restricts results to shipments created no later than this timestamp.

shipped_from.description:
Lower bound for the time window in which shipments entered the shipped state.

This filter is applied to `shopping_mall_shipments.shipped_at` and is useful for analyzing fulfillment performance.

shipped_to.description:
Upper bound for the time window in which shipments entered the shipped state.

This filter is applied to `shopping_mall_shipments.shipped_at` and restricts results to shipments shipped no later than this timestamp.

delivered_from.description:
Lower bound for the delivery time window, inclusive.

This filter is applied to `shopping_mall_shipments.delivered_at` and is useful for delivery performance and SLA analysis.

delivered_to.description:
Upper bound for the delivery time window, inclusive.

This filter is applied to `shopping_mall_shipments.delivered_at` and restricts results to shipments delivered no later than this timestamp.

page.description:
1-based page index for navigating through the shipment search result set.

When omitted, implementations should default to the first page. This value is combined with `limit` to determine the underlying query offset.

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipment records to return in a single page.

Back-end implementations should enforce a sensible upper bound to avoid excessively large responses.

sort_key.description:
Optional logical sort key that selects which shipment attribute is used for ordering the results.

Common options include logical names such as "created_at", "shipped_at", "delivered_at", or "shipping_status" as defined by the implementation.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction applied to the chosen `sort_key`.

Typical values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. A default such as descending creation time should be used when omitted.

IShoppingMallShipmentSearch.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shipment used in shipment search and list responses.

This type provides a lightweight representation of shipment headers for the shopping mall platform, optimized for search results, dashboards, and listing screens where many shipments are shown at once.

It focuses on identifiers, key status fields, main timeline markers, and the most important BELONGS-TO associations (order, seller, and shipping method) without including heavy relational graphs such as shipment items or detailed event logs. More detailed inspection uses the full shipment detail DTO associated with the same Prisma model.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and is used internally and across services to reference this shipment row.

In list views it is usually not shown directly to end users but is essential for navigation to shipment detail views and for backend correlation.

shipment_code.description:
Business-facing shipment code used for seller and customer communication.

The value is derived at business level, often from the originating order code with a suffix or using a dedicated shipment sequence. It is human friendly and is the primary identifier visible in customer and seller UIs.

The underlying database column is unique, enabling efficient lookup when users search by shipment code.

shipping_status.description:
Current shipping status of the shipment.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `preparing`, `ready_for_pickup`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, or `cancelled`.

Search and list views primarily use this field to filter and cluster shipments by lifecycle stage, and backoffice tools may provide status-specific actions based on this value.

carrier_name.description:
Name of the carrier responsible for moving this shipment, or null when not yet assigned.

When present it typically contains the courier or logistics provider name that both sellers and customers recognize, and can be used as a filter in shipment search.

If the shipment has not yet been tendered to a carrier or if the platform does not track carrier information, this value remains null.

tracking_number.description:
Tracking number assigned by the carrier for this shipment, or null when tracking is not yet available.

Search screens may allow users to quickly confirm the tracking identifier without drilling into full shipment detail, and operations staff can filter based on tracking numbers when resolving incidents.

When not supported by the carrier or before label creation, this value is null.

expected_ship_date.description:
Expected date and time when the shipment is planned to leave the seller or warehouse, or null when there is no committed expectation.

This information is useful for proactive communication, SLA monitoring, and prioritization in operational dashboards.

The value is recorded as an ISO 8601 date-time in the same timezone convention as the rest of the platform.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment first entered the carrier network or was marked as shipped.

This helps measure lead times between order placement, fulfillment, and actual dispatch, and is frequently used in performance and SLA analyses.

Null indicates that the shipment has not yet been shipped according to business rules.

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment was confirmed delivered to the customer, if such confirmation exists.

Shipment search lists often surface this time for completed shipments to help support inquiries and customer self-service history views.

When delivery has not occurred or has not been recorded yet, this value is null.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment record was created.

In search and analytics contexts this is the canonical creation moment used for default sorting, filtering by creation window, and general operational reporting.

The value directly reflects the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_shipments`.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment record was last updated.

This field allows list views and background processes to identify recently changed shipments, for example when statuses change or tracking information is refreshed.

It mirrors the `updated_at` column of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

order.description:
Summary of the customer-facing order that this shipment fulfills.

This BELONGS-TO association corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key on `shopping_mall_shipments` and provides immediate context for which order the shipment belongs to.

Including the order summary in search results allows operators and customers to recognize the shipment by order code and basic order information without issuing additional API calls.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller responsible for fulfilling this shipment.

This BELONGS-TO association corresponds to the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key on `shopping_mall_shipments` and identifies the merchant or seller account that owns the shipped items.

The seller summary is especially important in multi‑seller marketplaces, where shipment search screens and dashboards need to group and filter shipments by seller context.

shipping_method.description:
Summary of the shipping method configuration that was applied to this shipment, or null when no explicit method snapshot is available.

This BELONGS-TO association corresponds to the `shopping_mall_shipping_method_id` foreign key on `shopping_mall_shipments` and captures the core attributes of the chosen shipping method, such as method code and display name.

Providing the shipping method summary in the shipment search view helps users and administrators quickly understand how the shipment is being delivered without loading the full shipping method configuration.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request payload for querying configured payment methods in the shopping mall platform.

Used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/paymentMethods endpoint to support complex search criteria, pagination, and sorting for payment method configurations defined in the shopping_mall_payment_methods model and related surcharge configuration tables. This DTO allows admin clients to discover payment methods by status, region or country availability, supported currencies, provider type, business code, and capability flags such as refund or installment support.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts from 1. When omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return per page. When omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default and enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

search.description: Free-text search keyword applied to business-facing fields such as display_name, description, or code to help admins quickly locate relevant payment methods.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle status of the payment method configuration, such as active, disabled, or deprecated.

providerType.description: Filter by provider or gateway family classification, such as card_processor, bank_gateway, wallet, or cod.

codes.description: Optional list of specific payment method business codes to include in the result set. Each code corresponds to the unique code column of shopping_mall_payment_methods.

allowedCountries.description: Filter to payment methods that are available in at least one of the specified ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes based on their configured availability rules.

allowedRegions.description: Filter to payment methods that are available within one or more logical regions as configured in region-related tables. Region identifiers are platform-specific logical keys.

allowedCurrencies.description: Filter to payment methods that support at least one of the given three-letter ISO 4217 currency codes.

supportsRefunds.description: When true, restrict results to payment methods that support refund operations according to their configuration. When false, restrict to methods that do not support refunds. When omitted, no filter is applied.

supportsInstallments.description: When true, restrict results to payment methods that support installment or recurring payment use cases. When false, restrict to methods that explicitly do not support installments. When omitted, no filter is applied.

sortBy.description: Field name to sort by, such as display_name, code, created_at, or a business-defined display_order field.

sortDirection.description: Sort direction for the result set. Typical values are asc for ascending order and desc for descending order.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.description:
Payment method configuration used by the shoppingMall platform during checkout.

Each record represents a conceptual payment method such as a card processor, bank transfer, wallet, or cash-on-delivery option that can be offered to customers. It stores business-facing identifiers, display labels, provider classification, availability constraints, and audit timestamps.

This schema is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` Prisma model and is returned to administrative clients when creating or updating payment methods, or when inspecting configured payment rails in backoffice tools.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the payment method configuration.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` table and is generated by the system. Clients use this value only for display or internal correlation; configuration APIs should primarily address records by their business `code`.

The value is immutable after creation and is never supplied by clients in create or update DTOs.

code.description:
Business identifier code of the payment method.

This value is stored in the `code` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods` and is constrained to be globally unique by a database unique index. Typical examples are short, stable identifiers such as `"card"`, `"bank_transfer"`, or `"wallet"`.

The code is used both in admin operations and internal logic to reference a specific payment method. It should remain stable over time because other tables, business rules, and external integrations may depend on it.

display_name.description:
Human‑readable name of the payment method.

This value is stored in the `display_name` column and is shown to administrators and, depending on UI design, possibly to customers in checkout flows. Examples include `"Credit Card"`, `"Bank Transfer"`, or `"Cash on Delivery"`.

The display name can be updated over time to improve UX or clarify behavior, without changing the underlying business `code`.

description.description:
Optional long description of the payment method.

This corresponds to the nullable `description` column. It can capture additional business context, configuration notes, or guidance for admin operators such as limitations, integration details, or rollout plans.

When `null`, no additional descriptive text is stored for this payment method.

provider_type.description:
Provider family or gateway type backing this payment method.

This value is stored in the `provider_type` column and describes the high‑level payment provider category, such as `"card_processor"`, `"bank_gateway"`, `"wallet"`, or `"cod"`. It is used by backend logic to route checkout flows to the appropriate integration stack.

The set of provider types is governed by platform business rules, and admins should choose values that match configured gateway integrations.

allowed_currencies.description:
Optional expression listing currencies allowed for this payment method.

This field maps to the nullable `allowed_currencies` column. It typically stores a serialized representation such as a comma‑separated list of ISO 4217 currency codes (for example `"KRW,USD"`).

When `null`, the payment method does not impose additional currency restrictions beyond global platform policy.

allowed_countries.description:
Optional expression listing countries in which this method is allowed.

This corresponds to the nullable `allowed_countries` column. It usually contains a serialized list or expression of ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 country codes (for example `"KR,US"`).

When `null`, the payment method is not restricted to specific countries beyond higher‑level shipping or compliance rules.

min_amount.description:
Optional minimum order amount required to use this payment method.

This field maps to the nullable `min_amount` double column. When set, it expresses a lower bound in the order currency below which the payment method should not be offered at checkout.

When `null`, no method‑specific lower bound is enforced, and global or policy‑level rules apply instead.

max_amount.description:
Optional maximum order amount allowed for this payment method.

This corresponds to the nullable `max_amount` double column. It provides an upper bound in the order currency above which this payment method is not suitable, for example to avoid risk for very large payments.

When `null`, no method‑specific upper bound is enforced besides platform or provider limits.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the payment method.

This value is stored in the non‑null `status` column and indicates whether the method is usable in checkout flows. Typical values include `"active"` for methods that can be selected by customers and `"disabled"` for methods temporarily or permanently unavailable.

Business logic should interpret this status together with higher‑level policies to decide if the method can be presented or used for new orders.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment method configuration was created.

This value comes from the non‑null `created_at` column and is set by the backend when the row is inserted. It represents the moment the configuration first became available in the system.

Clients can use this information for auditing, sorting, or displaying the age of the configuration but never control it directly.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to this payment method configuration.

This field is backed by the non‑null `updated_at` column and is automatically updated whenever mutable columns such as `display_name`, `description`, or `status` change.

Admin tools can rely on this value to detect stale data or highlight recently modified payment methods.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new payment method configuration in the shoppingMall platform.

This type is used as the request body of the admin POST `/shoppingMall/admin/paymentMethods` endpoint. It captures all business‑level fields required to define a conceptual payment method backed by a given provider type. The payload maps to non‑derived, writable columns of the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` Prisma model, excluding system‑managed identifiers and timestamps.

Administrative clients use this DTO to onboard new payment rails or enable new ways for customers to pay, such as credit cards, bank transfers, or wallets. The backend is responsible for enforcing uniqueness of the `code` field, populating `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`, and applying additional business validation around amounts and availability constraints.

code.description:
Unique business identifier code for the payment method being created.

This field populates the `code` column in `shopping_mall_payment_methods` and must be globally unique, as enforced by a database unique index. Examples include `"card"`, `"bank_transfer"`, or other stable identifiers that are referenced by configuration and business rules.

Once created, this code is expected to remain stable, because it may be used in URLs, policy definitions, and integration mappings.

display_name.description:
Human‑readable display name for the new payment method.

The value is written to the `display_name` column and appears in admin UIs and possibly in customer‑facing checkout flows, subject to UI design. It should clearly describe the payment option, such as `"Credit Card"` or `"Bank Transfer"`.

Admins can later update this field through the update API to refine wording without changing system behavior.

description.description:
Optional extended description or notes describing the payment method.

This maps to the nullable `description` column. It can include operational guidelines, risk notes, or integration details that help administrators understand how and when the method should be used.

When omitted or set to null, no additional descriptive text is stored for this method at creation time.

provider_type.description:
Provider or gateway family type for the payment method.

This field populates the non‑null `provider_type` column and indicates how the backend should route transactions, for example `"card_processor"`, `"bank_gateway"`, `"wallet"`, or `"cod"`.

The allowed values are governed by platform configuration and must match supported integrations in the payment processing layer.

allowed_currencies.description:
Optional expression describing which currencies may use this payment method.

When provided, the value is written to the nullable `allowed_currencies` column and typically contains a serialized list of ISO 4217 codes (for example `"KRW,USD"`). The backend interprets this expression when deciding if the method is available for a specific order currency.

If omitted or null, the method does not define additional currency limits beyond global or provider rules.

allowed_countries.description:
Optional expression describing which countries may use this payment method.

This field maps to the nullable `allowed_countries` column and usually holds a serialized list of ISO 3166‑1 alpha‑2 country codes (for example `"KR,US"`). It constrains the regions in which the payment method can be offered at checkout.

When omitted or null, the method can be considered broadly available unless restricted by higher‑level policies.

min_amount.description:
Optional minimum order amount that must be met to use this payment method.

The value is stored in the `min_amount` double column and is expressed in the order currency. Backoffice validation and business rules typically require this to be non‑negative and less than or equal to any configured `max_amount`.

If omitted or null, no method‑specific lower bound is imposed beyond global constraints.

max_amount.description:
Optional maximum order amount allowed when using this payment method.

This value is written to the `max_amount` double column. It can be used to prevent very large payments via certain methods that are unsuitable or high‑risk for large tickets. Implementations usually require this to be non‑negative and greater than or equal to `min_amount` when both are present.

If omitted or null, there is no explicit upper bound beyond provider or policy‑level limits.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status of the new payment method.

This populates the non‑null `status` column, with typical values such as `"active"` to make the method available immediately, or `"disabled"` to keep it configured but not selectable by customers until later activation.

Admin workflows and governance policies may restrict which status values are allowed during creation based on review or approval processes.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing payment method configuration identified by its business code.

This type is used as the request body of the admin PUT `/shoppingMall/admin/paymentMethods/{paymentMethodCode}` endpoint. It represents the set of mutable fields on the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` model that administrators are allowed to change after creation, such as display labels, descriptive text, availability constraints, and lifecycle status.

Immutable fields like the internal `id` and the business `code` are intentionally excluded from this DTO. The backend uses the path parameter `{paymentMethodCode}` to locate the record and then applies only the fields provided in this payload, updating `updated_at` automatically.

display_name.description:
New human‑readable display name for the payment method.

When provided, this value updates the `display_name` column and changes how the method is labeled in admin tools and potentially checkout flows. It is optional in the update DTO so that callers can modify only other aspects when needed.

If omitted, the existing display name remains unchanged.

description.description:
Updated extended description or notes for the payment method.

Supplying a non‑null value replaces the content of the `description` column with new text that can describe business context, restrictions, or integration details. Passing `null` explicitly clears any existing description.

If the property is omitted entirely, the current description is left unchanged.

provider_type.description:
Updated provider or gateway family type for the payment method.

When included, this value overwrites the `provider_type` column and may change how the platform routes payments for this method, for example switching between different gateway integrations.

If omitted, the existing provider type is preserved. Governance processes may restrict changing this field in production environments.

allowed_currencies.description:
Updated expression of allowed currencies for this payment method.

Providing a non‑null value updates the `allowed_currencies` column, changing which order currencies are eligible to use this method. Supplying `null` explicitly clears any existing currency filter so that higher‑level rules apply.

If omitted, the current currency configuration is not modified.

allowed_countries.description:
Updated expression of allowed countries for this payment method.

A non‑null value writes a new serialized country list or expression into the `allowed_countries` column. Passing `null` explicitly removes any stored country restriction so that only global policies govern availability.

If the property is omitted, the existing country configuration remains unchanged.

min_amount.description:
Updated minimum order amount required to use this payment method.

Supplying a number writes a new value to the `min_amount` column, while explicitly passing `null` removes the minimum amount constraint and clears the column. Business validation should still ensure the relationship with `max_amount` is consistent.

If omitted, the current minimum amount configuration is not changed.

max_amount.description:
Updated maximum order amount allowed for this payment method.

A numeric value updates the `max_amount` column, while `null` explicitly removes the maximum constraint. The backend should validate that any new value is non‑negative and compatible with `min_amount` when both are defined.

If omitted, the existing maximum amount stays in effect.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the payment method.

When provided, this field changes the `status` column to reflect the new availability state, such as switching between `"active"` and `"disabled"`. Business rules may restrict certain transitions based on policies or outstanding obligations.

If omitted, the payment method keeps its current status.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodSurcharge.IReq.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying surcharge configurations of a specific payment method in the shopping mall.

This type is used by administrative search operations such as the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/paymentMethods/{paymentMethodCode}/surcharges` endpoint to express flexible filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria when listing records from the `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` Prisma model.

The fields in this request do not map one-to-one to database columns and therefore do not use the `x-autobe-prisma-schema` linkage. Instead, they provide higher-level query controls such as minimum and maximum bounds, status flags, and generic search keywords that the backend translates into Prisma query conditions.

page.description:
Zero‑based page index for pagination.

This value determines which logical page of surcharge results to return when querying `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`. The backend combines this with `limit` to calculate the offset in the result set. When omitted, the server typically uses a default page index such as 0.

Clients should avoid negative values. Values that exceed the number of available pages will usually result in an empty `data` array while still returning valid pagination metadata.

limit.description:
Maximum number of surcharge records to return in a single page.

This value is used together with `page` to implement paginated access to `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` for a given payment method. The backend may enforce an upper bound to protect performance and prevent excessively large responses.

Typical values are in the range of 10 to 100 depending on the admin UI requirements. When omitted, a server‑side default limit is applied.

search.description:
Free‑text search keyword applied to surcharge records.

The backend can use this value to match against human‑readable fields of `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`, such as descriptive labels, policy descriptions, or scope codes. The exact matching behavior (contains, prefix, or full‑text search) is determined by the implementation.

This field is optional and should be left empty when no free‑text filtering is required.

minOrderAmount.description:
Lower bound of the order amount range filter, expressed in the order currency.

When provided, only surcharge configurations whose applicable order amount range intersects or lies above this value should be returned. It is typically mapped to the `min_order_amount` or combined with `max_order_amount` in the `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` table.

Use this parameter to locate surcharges that affect medium or high value orders while excluding rules that only apply to very small transactions.

maxOrderAmount.description:
Upper bound of the order amount range filter, expressed in the order currency.

When set, the search should limit results to surcharge configurations whose applicable range intersects or lies below this value. It is usually evaluated against the `max_order_amount` column of `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`.

This parameter is useful for finding surcharges that target smaller orders or verifying that no unintended fees apply beyond a certain total.

currencyCode.description:
ISO 4217 currency code used to filter surcharge configurations.

If specified, only surcharge rules in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` whose `currency_code` matches this value (or are defined as currency‑agnostic according to business logic) will be returned. Examples include "USD", "EUR", or "KRW".

Administrative tools use this filter to inspect surcharges that are specific to a single settlement currency for the payment method.

scopeCode.description:
Business scope identifier used to narrow surcharge configurations.

This field corresponds conceptually to the `scope_code` column in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`, which may represent segmentation such as region codes, sales channels, or customer segments. When provided, the search focuses on surcharge rules whose configured scope matches this value.

Use this filter when reviewing or debugging surcharges that apply only in a particular region or channel.

isPlatformRevenue.description:
Filter flag indicating whether to return only platform‑owned or pass‑through surcharges.

When set to true, the search should restrict results to surcharge configurations whose `is_platform_revenue` column is true, meaning the fee is retained as platform revenue. When set to false, only surcharges that are passed through to external parties, such as payment gateways or carriers, should be returned.

Omitting this field disables filtering by revenue ownership and returns surcharges of both types.

refundablePolicy.description:
Filter on the textual refundable policy associated with surcharges.

This value conceptually maps to the `refundable_policy` column in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`, where business rules such as "refundable", "non_refundable", or more detailed policy identifiers may be stored. When provided, the backend can filter or partially match against this descriptor.

Use this filter to locate surcharge rules with a specific refund behavior or to verify that all required policies have corresponding configurations.

sortBy.description:
Name of the field used to sort the surcharge result set.

The allowed values are implementation‑specific but typically include column names or logical sort keys such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, `min_order_amount`, or `currency_code`. The backend uses this value to construct an ordered Prisma query when reading from `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`.

If omitted, a default ordering—often by creation time or primary key—is applied.

sortDirection.description:
Direction of result ordering for the selected `sortBy` field.

The value is usually interpreted as either ascending (for example, "asc") or descending (for example, "desc"). The backend combines this with `sortBy` when ordering surcharge records retrieved from `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`.

When not supplied, the server may assume ascending order or apply a configured default so that list behavior remains predictable.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodSurcharge.ICre.description:
Creation DTO for registering a new payment method surcharge rule in the shopping mall platform.

This type is used in administrative endpoints such as `POST /shoppingMall/admin/paymentMethods/{paymentMethodCode}/surcharges` to accept configuration parameters for a surcharge row that will be inserted into the `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` Prisma model. The path parameter `paymentMethodCode` selects the owning payment method, while this DTO describes how the surcharge behaves.

All actor identity and ownership information is derived from the authenticated admin context and the `paymentMethodCode` path, so this type excludes any foreign key or audit fields that are managed by the backend. Only business‑level configuration values are accepted here; system fields such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are generated automatically when the record is stored. Optional configuration columns that are nullable in Prisma are represented here by omitting the corresponding properties from the request body when they are not needed, and the backend will persist them as `null` values in the database.

scope_code.description:
Optional business scope identifier that constrains where this surcharge applies.

In the underlying `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` model, this maps to the `scope_code` column and can encode concepts such as a region, channel, or customer segment. When this property is omitted from the request, the surcharge may be treated as globally applicable for the parent payment method and persisted as a null column value.

Administrative users can define multiple surcharge rows with different scope codes to express differentiated fee policies across markets or channels.

currency_code.description:
Optional ISO 4217 currency code for which this surcharge configuration applies.

This property corresponds to the `currency_code` column in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`. When it is provided, it restricts the surcharge to orders settled in the given currency (for example, "USD", "EUR", or "KRW"). When the property is omitted from the payload, the backend treats the configuration as currency‑agnostic for the parent payment method and stores a null column value accordingly.

Using currency‑specific surcharge rows allows fine‑tuning of fees to account for gateway pricing differences or regional regulations.

min_order_amount.description:
Minimum order amount threshold at or above which this surcharge rule becomes applicable.

The value is stored in the `min_order_amount` column of `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` and is expressed in the order currency resolved for the payment. If this property is not included in the request body, the surcharge has no explicit lower bound and the database column is left null.

Admins use this field to define surcharges that only affect medium or large transactions, such as high‑value card payments where additional fees are justified.

max_order_amount.description:
Maximum order amount threshold up to which this surcharge rule applies.

This property maps to the `max_order_amount` column in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`. When specified, orders whose total amount exceeds this value will not use this particular surcharge. If the property is omitted from the request, no explicit upper bound is enforced and the column is stored as null.

Combining `min_order_amount` and `max_order_amount` enables definition of tiered fee structures where different surcharges are applied to different value bands.

fixed_fee_amount.description:
Fixed fee amount to be added when this payment method is used and this surcharge rule matches.

The value is written into the `fixed_fee_amount` column of `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` and is expressed in the relevant order or settlement currency. It should be non‑negative and may be omitted when the surcharge is purely percentage‑based, in which case the column will be stored as null.

A fixed fee component is typically used for gateway per‑transaction charges or handling costs that do not scale with order value.

percentage_fee_rate.description:
Percentage fee rate applied to the payable amount when this surcharge rule is active.

This property corresponds to the `percentage_fee_rate` column in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` and is commonly represented as a human‑readable percentage (for example, `2.5` for 2.5%). Implementations should clarify whether this value is interpreted as a plain percentage or as a fraction. When the property is omitted from the request, the surcharge is considered to have no percentage component and the column is persisted as null.

Percentage surcharges are commonly used for card processing fees or other charges that should grow proportionally with the order total.

is_platform_revenue.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether the surcharge amount is retained as platform revenue.

The value is persisted in the `is_platform_revenue` column of `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges`. When set to true, the surcharge is treated as income for the marketplace operator. When false, it is considered a pass‑through fee owed to third‑party providers such as payment gateways or logistics partners.

This distinction is important for financial reporting, seller settlement, and compliance with fee disclosure regulations.

refundable_policy.description:
Textual code or description that expresses how this surcharge behaves in refund scenarios.

This field maps to the `refundable_policy` column in `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` and can contain values such as "refundable", "non_refundable", or structured identifiers tied to business policy tables. When the property is omitted, the platform applies its default refund behavior for the surcharge and persists a null column value if no policy is explicitly configured.

By capturing the refundability of surcharges explicitly when needed, the platform can compute refund amounts consistently and explain fee behavior to customers and sellers.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodSurcharge.description:
Payment method surcharge configuration entity for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a single surcharge or fee rule associated with a configured payment method. It is backed by the `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` Prisma model and linked to a parent payment method in `shopping_mall_payment_methods` through the `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` foreign key.

Each record defines optional scoping dimensions such as business scope code, currency, and order amount range, along with monetary fee parameters and refund behavior. It is used by administrative tooling to inspect, audit, and manage surcharge behavior that affects customer-facing pricing and platform revenue.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the surcharge configuration.

This value maps directly to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` Prisma model and is generated by the system when the surcharge row is created. It is used by admin APIs and internal services to reference and update a specific surcharge rule.

paymentMethod.description:
Parent payment method configuration that this surcharge belongs to.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` from the underlying Prisma model and provides a DTO-friendly view of the payment method using its summary representation.

Admin tools can use this summary to show which payment method a surcharge is attached to without issuing additional API calls for basic identification and labelling.

scope_code.description:
Optional business scope identifier for this surcharge rule.

The value typically represents a region code, sales channel code, customer segment, or any other business-defined scope token. When null, the rule applies to all scopes for the given payment method and currency. Application services should interpret this field according to higher-level business policy configuration.

currency_code.description:
Optional ISO 4217 currency code to which this surcharge configuration applies.

When a non-null value is present, the surcharge is evaluated only for orders using this specific currency. When null, the rule applies to all currencies for the associated payment method, subject to other constraints like amount ranges.

min_order_amount.description:
Optional minimum order amount threshold for applicability of this surcharge.

If provided, this value indicates the lowest order total for which the surcharge rule is valid. Orders with a total below this threshold should not have this surcharge applied. When null, there is no explicit minimum bound from the surcharge perspective.

max_order_amount.description:
Optional maximum order amount threshold for applicability of this surcharge.

If provided, this value defines the highest order total for which the surcharge rule applies. Orders with a total above this amount should not use this particular rule. When null, there is no explicit maximum bound and the rule may apply up to any order size, subject to other constraints.

fixed_fee_amount.description:
Optional fixed fee amount added when this surcharge rule is applied.

This value represents a flat monetary increment in the order currency or designated currency context. When non-null, it is combined with percentage-based fees as defined by business logic, and must be non-negative at the service validation layer.

percentage_fee_rate.description:
Optional percentage fee rate applied to the payable amount when this rule is in effect.

The numeric value is expressed as a percentage (for example `2.9` for a 2.9% surcharge). When specified, the platform calculates a proportional fee based on the appropriate base amount. Validation rules should ensure that the configured rate is within acceptable business bounds and non-negative.

is_platform_revenue.description:
Flag indicating whether this surcharge is platform-owned revenue or pass-through.

When set to true, the surcharge is considered platform revenue and may be accounted for as income to the marketplace. When false, the surcharge is treated as a pass-through fee collected on behalf of external parties such as payment gateways, banks, or carriers.

refundable_policy.description:
Optional textual policy describing how this surcharge behaves during refunds.

Typical values include terms such as "refundable", "non_refundable", or more complex expressions codified by business policy. Downstream refund logic uses this field in combination with other configuration and policy tables to determine what portion of surcharges can be returned to customers.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this surcharge rule was created.

This maps to the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` table and is managed by the system. It provides an audit trail for administrators and reporting tools to understand when the rule first became available.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this surcharge rule was last updated.

This corresponds to the `updated_at` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` Prisma model and is automatically refreshed whenever configuration for the rule changes. It is useful for troubleshooting, auditing, and synchronization with external configuration caches.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodSurcharge.IUpd.description:
Update payload for modifying an existing payment method surcharge configuration.

This DTO exposes the fields of `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges` that administrators are allowed to change after creation. It is used by admin-facing APIs such as `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/paymentMethods/{paymentMethodCode}/surcharges/{surchargeId}` to adjust fee ranges, scoping conditions, and refund behavior.

All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates, and the service layer enforces domain rules such as non-negative amounts and logical min/max combinations. Identity and audit fields are intentionally excluded from updates and managed exclusively by the backend.

scope_code.description:
Optional new business scope identifier for this surcharge rule.

When provided, this value replaces the existing scope code, allowing administrators to reassign or clear the business segment, region, or channel context to which the surcharge applies.

currency_code.description:
Optional new ISO 4217 currency code for this surcharge configuration.

Updating this field changes the currency-specific applicability of the rule. Setting it to null indicates that the surcharge should apply to all currencies supported by the parent payment method, subject to other business constraints.

min_order_amount.description:
Optional new minimum order amount for which the surcharge is valid.

If set, this value overrides the previous minimum threshold. Setting it to null removes the lower bound so that the rule can apply starting from zero, subject to other validation rules in the service layer.

max_order_amount.description:
Optional new maximum order amount for which the surcharge is valid.

If present, this value replaces the previous upper bound. Providing null clears the upper limit, allowing the surcharge to apply to orders of any size within the constraints of other rules.

fixed_fee_amount.description:
Optional updated fixed fee amount to apply when this surcharge is used.

This field lets administrators change or clear the flat fee portion of the surcharge. Service-level validation ensures that any supplied amount is non-negative and remains consistent with business policies for fee configuration.

percentage_fee_rate.description:
Optional updated percentage fee rate applied to the payable amount.

When provided, this value replaces the existing percentage rate. The numeric value is expressed as a percentage (for example `2.9` for 2.9%), and must satisfy non-negativity and reasonable upper limit constraints enforced by the service layer.

is_platform_revenue.description:
Optional flag specifying whether the surcharge represents platform revenue after update.

If provided, this value overrides the previous `is_platform_revenue` setting. Setting it to true marks the surcharge as income to the platform, whereas false indicates a pass-through fee to an external provider. When omitted, the existing setting is preserved.

refundable_policy.description:
Optional updated policy text describing refund behavior for this surcharge.

Administrators can use this field to change how refunds should handle the surcharge, for example when business policies are updated. Setting the value to null removes any explicit textual policy, leaving interpretation to higher-level defaults or other configuration tables.
