IShoppingMallOrderPayment.IRequest.description:
Search, filtering, and pagination criteria for querying logical order payments stored in the `shopping_mall_order_payments` table.

This request DTO is used by multiple read-only payment listing operations (customer-, seller-, guest-, and admin-scoped). It models pagination controls and a flexible set of optional filters over the payment records, allowing callers to narrow results by order, method, status, amount, and time ranges without exposing any system-managed or sensitive internal fields.

The structure focuses on fields that are meaningful from a business and reporting perspective while remaining independent of any particular actor. Implementations combine these criteria with actor-specific scoping (such as customer ownership or admin visibility rules) at the service layer rather than in the DTO itself.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated payment search results.

When omitted, implementations typically default to the first page. This value is combined with `limit` to determine the skip/offset for queries over `shopping_mall_order_payments`.

Clients should use small positive integers to avoid requesting excessively distant pages that could degrade query performance.

limit.description:
Maximum number of payment records to return in a single page.

This acts as the page size for pagination and is commonly capped by the backend (for example 50 or 100) to protect system performance. When omitted, a reasonable default limit is applied.

Very large limits should be avoided to keep result payloads small and response times predictable.

items.description: Unique identifier of an order in the `shopping_mall_orders` table used as a filter constraint.

orderIds.description:
Optional list of order identifiers to restrict the search to payments belonging to specific orders.

When provided, only payments whose `shopping_mall_order_id` matches one of these values are eligible for inclusion in the result. This is useful when a client needs to inspect payments for a small set of known orders.

The list should remain reasonably small; combining this filter with additional criteria such as status or date ranges can further narrow the result set.

items.description: Unique identifier of a payment method in the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` table used as a filter constraint.

paymentMethodIds.description:
Optional list of payment method identifiers used to filter by configured payment methods.

Each value should correspond to a row in `shopping_mall_payment_methods`. When provided, only payments created with one of the specified methods are returned.

This filter is useful for reporting on specific methods such as particular card brands, wallets, or offline payment channels.

items.description: Business-level payment status value stored in `shopping_mall_order_payments.business_status` (for example `pending`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `chargeback`, or `cancelled`).

businessStatuses.description:
Optional set of business-level payment status values to include in the search.

Values correspond to the `business_status` column of `shopping_mall_order_payments` and represent the platform’s interpretation of the payment lifecycle (for example `pending`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `chargeback`, or `cancelled`).

When present, only payments whose `business_status` is one of the provided values are returned, enabling focused views such as "only refunded payments" or "only chargebacks".

items.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code (for example `USD`, `EUR`, `KRW`).

currencyCodes.description:
Optional list of ISO 4217 currency codes used to restrict the search to payments denominated in particular currencies.

Each entry filters against the `currency_code` column in `shopping_mall_order_payments`. This is useful for multi-currency deployments where operations or reporting may focus on a subset of currencies.

If omitted, payments in all supported currencies are eligible for inclusion, subject to other filters.

minPayableAmount.description:
Optional lower bound for the payable amount constraint, expressed in the same currency as the payment record.

When provided, only payments with `payable_amount` greater than or equal to this value are included. This supports searching for higher-value payments or excluding very small transactions from views and reports.

Backends may enforce reasonable minimums and maximums to protect query performance and prevent overflow issues.

maxPayableAmount.description:
Optional upper bound for the payable amount constraint, expressed in the same currency as the payment record.

When provided, only payments with `payable_amount` less than or equal to this value are included. This is commonly combined with `minPayableAmount` to define an amount range of interest.

If both bounds are set, the implementation should validate that `minPayableAmount` is not greater than `maxPayableAmount` to avoid contradictory filters.

createdFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the creation timestamp range filter, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Only payments with `created_at` greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This allows clients to focus on payments created after a specific point in time, for example the beginning of a reporting period.

When used together with `createdTo`, it defines the temporal window of interest for payment creation.

createdTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the creation timestamp range filter, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Only payments with `created_at` less than or equal to this timestamp are included. This is typically combined with `createdFrom` to constrain results to a specific reporting window, such as a day, month, or quarter.

Backends should interpret the range inclusively and may normalize the value for day-level queries when appropriate.

sortBy.description:
Field key used to determine the sort ordering of payment search results.

Typical values include logical field names such as `created_at`, `payable_amount`, or `business_status`. Exact allowed values are enforced by the backend, which maps them to underlying columns and indexed fields.

When omitted, the implementation usually sorts results by descending `created_at` so that the newest payments appear first.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the field selected by `sortBy`.

Accepted logical values are typically `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order, though the backend may support a limited set of values only. When omitted, descending order is commonly assumed, especially when sorting by `created_at`.

Clients should avoid mixing inconsistent `sortBy` and `sortDirection` combinations that would yield confusing result ordering.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.ICreate.description:
Creation payload for a new logical payment record in the `shopping_mall_order_payments` table.

This DTO is used by the order-scoped payment creation operation to register a new logical payment for an existing order. It captures payment method selection, currency, payable amount, and optional provider-specific context while deferring all system-managed values and foreign keys that are derived from the order and authenticated actor.

At persistence time, the service uses the authenticated customer and the `orderId` path parameter to populate `shopping_mall_customer_id` and `shopping_mall_order_id`, and it maps the chosen `payment_method_id` onto the `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` foreign key column. An appropriate initial `business_status` value and timestamp fields are set internally according to business rules rather than being supplied directly by the client.

Implementations map these fields directly onto the Prisma `shopping_mall_order_payments` model when inserting a new record, while also initializing related entities such as payment attempts and status histories according to business rules.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the configured payment method to use for this payment, referencing `shopping_mall_payment_methods.id`.

The chosen method determines how the platform will process the payment (for example card, wallet, bank transfer, or offline method) and which surcharges or fees may apply. Internally, this value is mapped to the `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_order_payments` when the new payment row is created.

Business logic validates that the selected method is compatible with the target order, customer, and marketplace policies before creating the payment record.

currency_code.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code indicating the currency in which this payment is denominated.

This value is persisted to the `currency_code` column of `shopping_mall_order_payments` and must align with the currency of the associated order or cart according to platform configuration.

Backends typically validate against a whitelist of supported currencies to prevent accidental use of unsupported or deprecated currency codes.

payable_amount.description:
Total amount that should be paid for this logical payment, expressed in the currency indicated by `currency_code`.

This value is mapped to `payable_amount` in `shopping_mall_order_payments` and represents the gross chargeable amount including items, taxes, and customer-facing fees that belong to this specific payment share of the order.

The amount must be non-negative and is usually validated against the outstanding balance of the order to prevent overpayment or inconsistent partial-payment configurations.

provider_reference.description:
Optional provider-level reference identifier associated with this logical payment, such as a payment intent ID or checkout session ID.

When supplied, this value is stored in `provider_reference` in the `shopping_mall_order_payments` table and can be used to correlate the platform’s payment record with an external payment gateway entity.

Clients may omit this field or set it to null when the provider reference will be generated after creation by asynchronous gateway orchestration or other internal processes.

provider_status_code.description:
Optional provider-specific status value that summarizes the last known state of the payment at the external gateway.

This field maps to `provider_status_code` on `shopping_mall_order_payments` and is typically used when the gateway returns a compact status indicator at the time of payment initiation.

Most flows will either leave this field empty or null at creation or populate it with an initial provider state such as `CREATED` or `INITIATED`, depending on integration design.

metadata.description:
Optional serialized metadata payload associated with this payment, commonly encoded as JSON.

The value is stored in the `metadata` column of `shopping_mall_order_payments` and can contain structured information required for downstream reconciliation, integration diagnostics, or internal tracing.

Because the structure is opaque to the API contract, clients and backends must agree out-of-band on its schema and size limits to avoid storing excessively large or malformed payloads. This field may be omitted or explicitly set to null when no additional metadata is required.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for adjusting mutable attributes of a logical order payment.

This DTO is mapped to the `shopping_mall_order_payments` Prisma model but only exposes fields that are allowed to change after creation according to business rules. Identifiers and core relationships—such as `id`, `shopping_mall_order_id`, `shopping_mall_customer_id`, `shopping_mall_payment_method_id`, and `payment_sequence`—are derived from the URL and persisted record and must never be supplied or modified by clients.

Typical use cases include administrative workflows and internal services updating `business_status` as reconciliation progresses, correcting `provider_status_code` or `provider_reference` when new information arrives from the gateway, adjusting aggregate monetary fields when late events are processed, or attaching additional diagnostic `metadata`. This type is primarily used by admin or back-office endpoints and should not be exposed directly to untrusted end users.

currency_code.description:
Updated ISO 4217 currency code for the payment, if it needs correction.

While currency is usually immutable once a payment is created, this optional field allows controlled updates in exceptional administrative workflows where data has to be corrected after the fact.

Implementations should enforce strict validation and may choose to disallow changes in normal circumstances.

payable_amount.description:
New total payable amount for this logical payment, if adjusted.

This optional property corresponds to `payable_amount` in the Prisma model and may be modified by trusted components to correct or realign payment amounts with the underlying order pricing snapshot.

Any change here must remain consistent with associated order price snapshots and refund behaviors, and should typically be accompanied by appropriate audit events.

captured_amount.description:
Updated total captured amount that has been successfully collected.

This field mirrors the `captured_amount` column and is usually driven by reconciliation jobs or payment gateway callbacks rather than by direct client input.

Implementations must ensure that the value does not exceed `payable_amount` and that status histories in `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories` remain consistent with the captured amount.

refunded_amount.description:
Updated total refunded amount for this payment.

This property corresponds to `refunded_amount` and is typically maintained by refund processing flows that create records in `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` and `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items`.

When updated through this DTO, the service must validate that the value does not exceed the captured amount minus any chargebacks and that it aligns with existing refund records.

chargeback_amount.description:
Updated total chargeback amount registered against this payment.

This field maps to `chargeback_amount` and reflects the cumulative value of chargeback events stored in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`.

Adjustments to this value must be tightly controlled and audited, as they directly impact revenue and risk reporting.

business_status.description:
New business-level status for the payment lifecycle.

This optional field aligns with `business_status` and is used by administrative tools and platform workflows to move a payment between states such as `pending`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `chargeback`, or `cancelled`.

Service logic must enforce valid state transitions and may write corresponding entries to `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories` to preserve an audit trail.

provider_status_code.description:
Updated provider-specific status code, or null to clear it.

This mirrors the `provider_status_code` column and may be changed when a gateway reports a new state or when data is corrected during reconciliation.

Implementations should keep this value in sync with the latest known provider status and consider adding status history entries when significant changes occur.

provider_reference.description:
Updated provider reference identifier for this payment, or null.

This property corresponds to `provider_reference` and typically stores the payment intent ID or transaction ID supplied by the external provider.

It may be adjusted when correcting mapping errors between the platform and the provider, and such changes should be carefully audited.

metadata.description:
Updated serialized metadata associated with the payment.

This optional field maps to `metadata` and allows callers to attach or replace structured diagnostic information, integration-specific attributes, or other internal notes.

Because the structure is platform-defined, callers should treat it as opaque and ensure that any changes remain valid according to internal conventions.

IShoppingMallOrderPaymentAttempt.IReques.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for listing payment attempt records for a specific logical order payment.

This type is used as the request body for the PATCH collection search operation that lists `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts` under a given parent payment. It allows administrators to filter attempts by status, time range, amount bounds, and provider result characteristics, and to control pagination and sorting behavior.

The path parameter `orderPaymentId` supplies the parent logical payment context and is not duplicated here. All filters in this DTO are optional and are applied only when provided, so callers can combine multiple criteria or omit them entirely to get an unfiltered paginated list within the scoped parent payment.

page.description:
Page index for pagination when listing payment attempts.

This is typically a 1-based index where `1` represents the first page of results. When omitted, the backend uses a sensible default such as the first page.

Used together with `limit` to slice the attempt timeline into manageable chunks for administrative UIs.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page of payment attempt results.

The backend should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets that could impact performance. When omitted, a reasonable default page size is applied.

Used together with `page` to implement standard offset-based pagination over the attempt records of the specified parent payment.

status.description:
Optional filter for the status of payment attempts.

Typical values include lifecycle states such as `pending`, `success`, `failed`, `error`, or `expired`. When provided, only attempts whose status matches the given value are returned.

This supports use cases like focusing on failed attempts for troubleshooting or listing only successful charges for reconciliation.

items.description:
Single status value used within the `statusIn` filter list.

Each element should be a valid attempt status such as `pending`, `success`, `failed`, `error`, or `expired` as defined by business rules.

The backend will match attempts whose status is one of the provided values.

statusIn.description:
Optional multi-value filter for attempt status.

When present, the backend returns attempts whose status is contained in this list. This is useful for grouping several terminal states together, for example `['failed', 'error']` when investigating problem cases.

If both `status` and `statusIn` are provided, the implementation should document and apply a deterministic precedence rule, typically treating them as an intersection or preferring the more specific field.

minAmount.description:
Optional lower bound filter for the attempt amount.

When provided, only attempts whose `amount` is greater than or equal to this value (in the payment currency) are included in the result. This helps narrow down high-value retries or large financial exposures.

The value should be expressed in the same currency and units as the `amount` column in `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts`.

maxAmount.description:
Optional upper bound filter for the attempt amount.

When provided, only attempts whose `amount` is less than or equal to this value (in the payment currency) are included in the result. This is useful when focusing on small micro-authorization attempts or capping the amount range for risk analysis.

The value should be expressed in the same currency and units as the `amount` column in `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts`.

startedFrom.description:
Optional filter representing the inclusive lower bound of the attempt creation time.

When set, only attempts whose `created_at` timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are returned. This allows callers to fetch attempts within a given time window, such as recent retries during a specific incident timeline.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

startedTo.description:
Optional filter representing the inclusive upper bound of the attempt creation time.

When set, only attempts whose `created_at` timestamp is less than or equal to this value are returned. It is typically used together with `startedFrom` to define a window.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

providerReference.description:
Optional filter for the provider-level transaction reference associated with the attempt.

This is matched against the `provider_reference` column of `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts`, which usually stores gateway transaction IDs or intent identifiers. Implementations may perform exact or partial matching depending on requirements.

Useful for debugging and reconciliation when an external transaction ID is known.

failureCode.description:
Optional filter for the failure or error code reported by the payment provider.

When provided, only attempts whose `failure_code` matches this value are returned. This is typically a gateway-specific code representing why the attempt failed or errored.

Helps operational teams quickly retrieve all attempts impacted by a specific provider-side error condition.

sortBy.description:
Field name to sort the attempt list by.

Common values include `created_at`, `updated_at`, `status`, or `amount`. If omitted, the backend typically sorts by `created_at` in descending order to show the most recent attempts first.

The implementation should validate the supplied field name against a whitelist to prevent unexpected or unsupported sorting.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction for the attempt list.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, a sensible default such as `desc` is applied to show the most recent attempts first.

Used in combination with `sortBy` to control how payment attempts are presented in administrative UIs.

IShoppingMallOrderPaymentAttempt.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for initiating a new payment attempt record under a specific logical order payment.

This type is used as the request body for the POST operation that creates a `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts` row scoped to a parent payment identified by the `orderPaymentId` path parameter. The path parameter is injected by the backend into the `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` foreign-key column and MUST NOT be included in this DTO.

The DTO captures business-level input such as the attempt amount, descriptive context, and correlation identifiers. Fields like status and timestamps are system-managed and therefore excluded. The payment method reference is resolved using the related payment configuration and is not provided directly by callers in this administrative endpoint.

amount.description:
Amount to attempt to authorize or capture for this payment attempt.

This value is stored in the `amount` column of the `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts` table and represents the monetary value that the gateway should process in the payment currency. Implementations may validate that it matches or is within allowed bounds relative to the parent logical payment.

Must be a non-negative number and should comply with the precision rules of the configured currency.

provider_reference.description:
Optional initial provider transaction reference or correlation identifier.

In some advanced flows, an upstream system or orchestration service may already have a tentative transaction or intent identifier from the payment provider. This field allows that identifier to be recorded at attempt creation time so that later reconciliation and event matching are easier.

When not available at creation, this field is typically populated by the gateway integration once the attempt has been dispatched.

failure_code.description:
Optional pre-classified failure or error code associated with this attempt at creation time.

This is rarely set when creating a new attempt, but can be used for bookkeeping when the attempt record is being backfilled from historical payment logs or external reconciliation systems where the outcome is already known.

For normal forward-processing flows, this field is left empty on creation and updated by the payment integration as required.

failure_message.description:
Optional human-readable message describing the reason for failure when the attempt is known to be unsuccessful at creation time.

Similar to `failure_code`, this field is mainly used when importing or reconstructing attempts from external systems where the outcome has already been determined. For new live attempts, it is typically left blank and populated only if the gateway indicates an error.

Messages stored here should be suitable for internal operational use and may be distinct from any customer-facing explanations.

raw_response.description:
Optional serialized raw response payload provided at creation time.

This is most commonly used when inserting attempt records based on pre-existing gateway logs or when the integration pattern supplies an immediate raw payload along with the initial creation request. The field can store JSON or other structured content as text for later analysis.

For typical live attempts, this field is initially empty and populated by the processing logic once the provider interaction completes.

IShoppingMallOrderPaymentAttempt.description:
Represents a single concrete payment attempt executed against a logical order payment in the shoppingMall platform.

Each row captures one technical try to authorize or capture funds through a specific payment method and provider for a parent logical payment stored in the `shopping_mall_order_payments` model. Attempts are used to support retries, provider changes, and operational workflows without altering the canonical logical payment record.

This entity is primarily used for audit, troubleshooting, reconciliation, and risk analysis. It records detailed status, monetary amount, provider references, failure information, timestamps, and contextual associations to the logical order payment and payment method so that operators and automated systems can understand the history and outcome of each payment try without additional lookups.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this payment attempt.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts` table and uniquely identifies a single concrete payment try within the shoppingMall platform.

It is generated by the system when the attempt record is created and is used by internal services, monitoring tools, and administrative consoles to reference this specific attempt.

shopping_mall_order_payment_id.description:
Identifier of the parent logical order payment this attempt belongs to.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_payments.id` and establishes the ownership relationship between the logical payment and this concrete attempt.

All attempts for the same logical payment share this value, and together with `attempt_sequence` it can be used to group and order attempts for operational analysis or low-level reconciliation that needs direct foreign-key values.

shopping_mall_payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method actually used in this attempt.

This references `shopping_mall_payment_methods.id` and indicates which configured payment method or gateway configuration was applied when executing this try.

It allows systems to distinguish between different gateways or configurations used across multiple attempts for the same logical payment, such as retries with a different provider, while keeping the underlying foreign-key column visible for auditing tools.

attempt_sequence.description:
1-based sequence number of this attempt for the given logical payment.

The sequence starts from 1 for the first attempt of a particular `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` and increments by 1 for each subsequent attempt.

The pair `(shopping_mall_order_payment_id, attempt_sequence)` is unique and can be used to address a specific attempt via API paths and internal logic.

status.description:
Current status of this payment attempt.

Typical values include states such as "pending", "in_progress", "success", "failed", "error", or "expired" as defined by business rules.

This field reflects the latest known outcome of the attempt and is updated as integrations with external payment providers progress and finalize.

amount.description:
Monetary amount that this attempt tried to authorize or capture.

The amount is denominated in the currency associated with the parent payment and represents the value sent to the payment provider for this specific try.

It may match the full logical payment amount or be a partial amount depending on the retry or reconciliation strategy in effect.

provider_reference.description:
Provider-specific reference associated with this payment attempt.

Common examples include gateway transaction identifiers, intent IDs, or acquirer references returned by the external payment provider.

The value may be null when no reference is available, for example if the attempt failed before a transaction identifier was issued or if the provider does not supply one.

failure_code.description:
Optional failure or error code reported by the payment provider for this attempt.

When the attempt does not succeed, providers often return a machine-readable code indicating the reason, such as insufficient funds, expired card, or technical errors.

This field is null for successful attempts or for attempts that have not yet reached a final failure state.

failure_message.description:
Optional human-readable message describing why the attempt failed or encountered an error.

The message is typically derived from provider responses or internal error handling logic and is suitable for internal support and operational troubleshooting.

This field is null when the attempt is successful or when no explanatory message is available.

raw_response.description:
Optional serialized raw response payload from the payment provider for this attempt.

Implementations may store the original JSON or other structured response as a string to support deep debugging, audits, and dispute handling.

The value can be null when raw response storage is disabled, when no response was received, or when the integration chooses not to persist provider payloads.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this payment attempt record was created.

The value is stored in UTC and set by the system at insertion time based on the current server time.

It is used for chronological ordering of attempts, time-based reporting, and audit trails related to payment processing activities.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this payment attempt record was last updated.

The value is stored in UTC and refreshed whenever mutable fields such as status, failure information, or reconciliation-related metadata are changed.

It allows consumers to detect recent changes and supports operational monitoring of payment attempt lifecycle transitions.

orderPayment.description:
Summary of the logical order payment that owns this attempt.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` and exposes a domain-friendly summary view of the parent payment for operational tools.

Using the summary form avoids circular expansion while still allowing administrators to understand the payment context for the attempt without issuing an additional read for the parent payment.

paymentMethod.description:
Summary of the payment method configuration actually used for this attempt.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` and provides a concise view of the payment method or gateway that was applied for this concrete try.

Using the `.ISummary` variant prevents deep recursive expansion but gives enough detail for operators to distinguish payment channels and investigate provider-specific behavior.

IShoppingMallOrderPaymentAttempt.IUpdate.description:
Payload for updating mutable fields of an existing payment attempt in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by administrative and backoffice operations to adjust status and diagnostic information on a specific `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts` record identified by the combination of `orderPaymentId` and `attemptSequence` in the request path.

Only fields that are considered mutable by business rules are included here. Core identifiers and structural attributes such as the parent payment link, attempt sequence, and original amount must remain unchanged to preserve the integrity of the payment audit trail.

status.description:
Updated status of the payment attempt.

This field can be used to move the attempt through allowed lifecycle transitions, such as from "pending" to "success" or to a failure state after reconciliation.

Business rules must validate that the transition is permitted and consistent with the state of the parent payment and any related financial records.

provider_reference.description:
Updated provider-specific reference for this attempt, if the integration learns a finalized transaction identifier later.

Administrative workflows may populate or correct this value during reconciliation when delayed or corrected references are received from the payment provider.

Setting this property to null explicitly clears the stored reference when appropriate under governance rules.

failure_code.description:
Updated failure or error code describing the reason for an unsuccessful attempt.

This field can be adjusted when reconciliation or deeper investigation reveals a more accurate or standardized failure classification than the initial response.

Setting the property to null removes any previously stored failure code when business rules allow such clean-up.

failure_message.description:
Updated human-readable message explaining why the attempt failed or encountered an error.

Operational teams may refine or supplement the original message to improve clarity for future audits and investigations.

Assigning null explicitly clears the message when it is no longer desired or when policies require removal of verbose provider texts.

raw_response.description:
Updated serialized raw response from the payment provider for this attempt.

This field may be set or adjusted when additional or corrected response payloads are ingested during reconciliation or incident analysis.

Setting the value to null explicitly removes previously stored raw payloads if retention policies require it.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusHistory.ICreat.description:
Create DTO for appending a new payment status history record linked to a logical order payment.

This type is used as the request body of the POST /shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/statusHistories endpoint. It models the business-level transition of an order payment across statuses and, optionally, provider status codes, as persisted in the shopping_mall_payment_status_histories table.

The foreign key to the parent payment (shopping_mall_order_payment_id) and the admin actor are supplied by path parameter and authentication context respectively, and timestamps are system-managed. Callers provide the previous and new status values and any explanatory reason information.

previous_business_status.description:
Previous business_status value before this transition.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.previous_business_status. It may be null when there is no meaningful prior status to record, for example for the first observable transition in the payment lifecycle.

new_business_status.description:
New business_status value after this transition.

This field maps to shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.new_business_status and captures the resulting high-level payment state such as "pending", "paid", "partially_refunded", "refunded", or "chargeback". Business rules determine which codes are valid and which transitions are allowed from the payment's current state.

previous_provider_status_code.description:
Previous provider_status_code value before this transition, if any.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.previous_provider_status_code and represents the last known status code from the payment gateway or processor before the change being recorded. It may be null when no prior provider code was available.

new_provider_status_code.description:
New provider_status_code value after this transition, if any.

This field maps to shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.new_provider_status_code and stores the provider-specific state associated with this status change, such as a gateway authorization result or capture confirmation code. It may be null when no provider code applies or when the change is purely internal.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code describing why the status change occurred.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.reason_code. Typical examples include codes such as "payment_confirmed", "refund_completed", "manual_override", or other platform-specific identifiers used for analytics and audit purposes.

reason_message.description:
Optional human-readable explanation providing more detail about the status change.

This maps to shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.reason_message and may include operational notes, error messages from external providers, or internal comments that help explain the context of the transition in a way that is understandable to operators and auditors.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusHistory.IUpdat.description:
Update payload for a payment status history record associated with a logical order payment.

This DTO is used by administrative and backoffice workflows to correct or enrich an existing row in the shopping_mall_payment_status_histories table. Typical use cases include fixing incorrect status codes, improving explanatory messages, or aligning provider status information after reconciliation.

All fields are optional to support partial updates, but business rules should restrict which fields may be changed depending on the age and state of the record. For example, some environments may disallow changing the business status after a certain cutoff while still permitting adjustments to reason_message for clarity.

oneOf.description:
Corrected previous business status value to record for this history entry.

When provided, this should represent the payment’s business status immediately before the transition defined by new_business_status for this record.
Explicitly clear the stored previous_business_status value for this history entry, typically only allowed in repair scenarios.

previous_business_status.description:
Previous business status value to store for this history record.

Use this field to fix or adjust the prior state captured in the history when earlier data entry or system mapping errors are discovered.

oneOf.description:
Updated business status that this history entry should represent after correction.

This value should remain within the set of allowed payment business status values and must remain consistent with the overall payment lifecycle for the associated order payment.
Explicitly clear the new_business_status value when a correction requires the status to be removed, which should be rare and tightly controlled.

new_business_status.description:
New business status value to record for this history entry.

Admins can use this to correct incorrectly logged transitions or to reclassify a status when business rules change, subject to governance controls.

oneOf.description:
Revised provider‑specific status code that should be stored as the previous provider state for this history record.

This may be updated when improved information is received from the payment gateway or when mapping issues are corrected.
Explicitly remove the previous provider status code for this history entry, leaving it unset.

previous_provider_status_code.description:
Provider status code that was in effect before this history transition.

Updating this field helps keep the technical audit trail aligned with the most accurate gateway information available.

oneOf.description:
Updated provider status code to associate with the new state for this history record.

Used when a more accurate or standardized gateway status code becomes available after the original record was created.
Explicitly clear the new provider status code for this history entry.

new_provider_status_code.description:
Provider status code to record for the state after this transition.

This field helps diagnose integration problems and explain discrepancies between internal and provider‑reported statuses.

oneOf.description:
New or corrected structured reason code describing why this payment status change occurred.

For example, this might be updated from a generic code to a more precise variant such as "refund_partial_amount" or "chargeback_won".
Explicitly clear the structured reason code when it is no longer appropriate for this history record.

reason_code.description:
Structured reason code explaining the cause of the status change.

Adjusting this value is common when refining taxonomy for reporting or when earlier categorizations are discovered to be inaccurate.

oneOf.description:
Updated human‑readable explanation for this status change.

Admins may edit this to improve clarity, fix typos, or add more diagnostic detail after an incident review.
Explicitly clear the human‑readable explanation associated with this history entry.

reason_message.description:
Free‑form explanation of the status change associated with this history record.

This field is frequently edited in backoffice tools to ensure that future readers can easily understand what happened and why.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing payment refund records that belong to a specific logical order payment.

This DTO is used as the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/refunds endpoint. The path parameter orderPaymentId provides the payment context, so this type intentionally contains only search filters, sort options, and pagination controls and never duplicates the parent payment identifier.

Consumers use this type from back‑office and finance tools to retrieve a paginated list of refund summaries for review, reconciliation, and audit workflows.

status.description:
Optional filter on the business status of refunds to include in the result.

Typical values align with the status column of shopping_mall_payment_refunds, such as "pending", "approved", "rejected", "completed", or "failed". When omitted, refunds of all statuses for the target payment may be returned.

items.description:
Single refund status value to include in a multi‑status filter list.

Values should correspond to business status codes stored in the shopping_mall_payment_refunds.status column, such as "pending", "approved", "rejected", "completed", or "failed".

statusList.description:
Optional list of refund statuses to include when filtering.

Use this when the caller needs to retrieve refunds across multiple statuses in a single request, for example both "pending" and "approved" refunds.

minRequestedAmount.description:
Lower bound for the requested_amount column when filtering results.

When provided, only refund records whose requested_amount is greater than or equal to this value are eligible for inclusion in the page.

maxRequestedAmount.description:
Upper bound for the requested_amount column when filtering results.

When provided, only refund records whose requested_amount is less than or equal to this value are eligible for inclusion in the page.

minApprovedAmount.description:
Lower bound for the approved_amount column when filtering.

Use this to restrict the search to refunds where at least this amount was approved according to the shopping_mall_payment_refunds.approved_amount field.

maxApprovedAmount.description:
Upper bound for the approved_amount column when filtering.

Use this to restrict the search to refunds where no more than this amount was approved, based on the shopping_mall_payment_refunds.approved_amount field.

minRefundedAmount.description:
Lower bound for the refunded_amount column when filtering.

When set, only refund records whose refunded_amount is greater than or equal to this value are included, based on the shopping_mall_payment_refunds.refunded_amount field.

maxRefundedAmount.description:
Upper bound for the refunded_amount column when filtering.

When set, only refund records whose refunded_amount is less than or equal to this value are included, based on the shopping_mall_payment_refunds.refunded_amount field.

reasonCode.description:
Optional filter on the structured business reason code for the refund.

This value should match entries stored in the shopping_mall_payment_refunds.reason_code column and usually corresponds to standardized refund reasons defined by business policy.

createdFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the creation timestamp filter.

Only refund records whose created_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime value are returned when this property is provided.

createdTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the creation timestamp filter.

Only refund records whose created_at timestamp is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime value are returned when this property is provided.

sortBy.description:
Field to use for ordering the refund search results.

Typical supported values include "created_at", "requested_amount", "approved_amount", and "refunded_amount". Implementations may restrict this to a whitelist of sortable columns in shopping_mall_payment_refunds.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering results by sortBy.

Use "asc" for ascending order or "desc" for descending order. When omitted, the default sort direction is typically descending by created_at so that the most recent refund records appear first.

page.description:
1‑based page index for pagination.

When provided, this indicates which page of results to return. Page numbering conventionally starts at 1, and values less than 1 should be treated as 1 by the implementation.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund records to include in a single page of results.

This controls the page size for the search. Implementations should enforce a sensible upper bound to protect database and API performance, even if the client supplies a larger value.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.ICreate.description:
Creation payload for registering a new refund operation against a specific logical order payment.

This DTO is used as the request body of the POST /shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/refunds endpoint. The orderPaymentId path parameter supplies the parent payment context, so this type must never include a shopping_mall_order_payment_id field and focuses solely on refund business data.

Administrative and finance tools use this type to request or record refunds with details such as amounts, currency, reasons, and optional administrator metadata. The backend is responsible for validating business rules, binding the refund to the parent payment, populating system fields like identifiers and timestamps, and creating any subsidiary item‑level records.

When a refund is created in a pending state, some monetary fields (especially refunded_amount) may not yet reflect funds actually returned to the customer. Implementations typically default refunded_amount to 0 for pending refunds and only increase it as the payment provider confirms completed refund transactions.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for this refund.

This must correspond to the currency of the parent payment in shopping_mall_order_payments.currency_code. The backend should validate that the currency is supported and consistent with the original payment.

requested_amount.description:
Amount initially requested to be refunded at the business level.

This value is stored in the shopping_mall_payment_refunds.requested_amount column. The backend enforces that this amount does not exceed the remaining refundable balance for the parent payment and conforms to platform policy for minimum and maximum refund amounts.

approved_amount.description:
Amount that has been approved for refund according to business rules at the time of creation.

This value is stored in shopping_mall_payment_refunds.approved_amount and might match requested_amount for immediately approved refunds, or be lower when only a partial portion of the requested amount is approved up front.

Clients are required to provide this field so that the service can clearly distinguish between what was requested and what has actually been approved at creation time.

refunded_amount.description:
Amount that is considered refunded at creation time.

For workflows where the refund is already completed when the record is inserted, this can be set equal to approved_amount. For more common deferred or pending refunds, this value is typically 0 at creation and is later updated by server-side logic as the payment provider confirms actual refund processing.

If the client omits this field, the backend SHOULD default it according to the configured workflow (for example, 0 for pending refunds) rather than requiring callers to manually supply an initial system value.

status.description:
Initial status of this refund operation.

Typical values align with business states used in shopping_mall_payment_refunds.status, such as "pending", "approved", "rejected", "completed", or "failed". The specific allowed transitions and meanings are defined by marketplace policies and payment integration behavior.

reason_code.description:
Structured reason code explaining why this refund is being created.

This should correspond to standardized refund reasons defined by business policy, and is stored in shopping_mall_payment_refunds.reason_code. It allows downstream reporting and analytics to group refunds by common cause.

reason_message.description:
Free‑form explanatory text describing the refund reason in more detail.

This value is stored in shopping_mall_payment_refunds.reason_message and is typically used by support or finance teams to understand the context of the refund beyond the structured reason_code.

provider_reference.description:
Optional refund transaction reference identifier from the external payment provider.

When known at creation time, this maps to shopping_mall_payment_refunds.provider_reference and allows reconciliation between the marketplace and the payment gateway or acquirer.

metadata.description:
Serialized metadata payload with additional provider or internal diagnostic details about this refund.

Implementations commonly use JSON text in this field to store non‑relational information needed for troubleshooting, reconciliation, or integration with external systems. The raw value is persisted in shopping_mall_payment_refunds.metadata.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating mutable attributes of an existing refund transaction in the `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` table.

This type is used as the request body for administrative endpoints such as `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/refunds/{refundSequence}`. The target refund row is identified by the path parameters `orderPaymentId` and `refundSequence`, which map to `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` and `refund_sequence` respectively, so those key fields are not included in the update DTO.

Only fields that are conceptually mutable after creation are exposed here. Service logic uses this DTO to drive status transitions, adjust approved and provider-confirmed amounts within policy constraints, and refine explanatory metadata while preserving the integrity of immutable identifiers and creation metadata.

status.description:
New lifecycle status to apply to the refund, when a status transition is requested.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `completed`, or `failed`, with the exact set enforced at the domain layer. The implementation must validate that the requested transition is allowed given the current status and business rules.

If omitted, the refund status remains unchanged.

approved_amount.description:
Revised amount approved for refund according to business policy.

This field can be supplied to increase or decrease the approved refund amount within the limits enforced by the parent payment and policy configuration. It must never cause the cumulative approved or refunded amounts for the payment to exceed allowed thresholds.

If omitted, the previously stored `approved_amount` value is preserved.

refunded_amount.description:
Updated amount that the payment provider confirms has been refunded to the customer.

This value is typically set or adjusted based on callbacks or reconciliation runs with the payment gateway. It must remain non-negative and must not exceed the approved or logically refundable amount determined by the order payment.

If omitted, the stored `refunded_amount` remains unchanged.

reason_code.description:
Updated structured reason code for the refund, or null to clear it.

Use this field to refine or correct the classification of the refund after further investigation. Setting the value to null removes any previously recorded code, while providing a non-null value overwrites the existing code.

If omitted, the current `reason_code` is left as-is.

reason_message.description:
Updated free-text explanation for the refund, or null to clear it.

This field allows admins or automated processes to enhance or correct the narrative description used for audits and internal communication. Supplying null explicitly clears any existing message.

If omitted, the current `reason_message` stored on the refund is unchanged.

provider_reference.description:
Updated refund transaction reference from the external payment provider, or null to clear.

This allows the system to record or adjust the external gateway reference used for reconciliation and dispute management. Setting null removes any prior reference, while a non-null value overwrites the existing one.

If omitted, the existing `provider_reference` value is preserved.

metadata.description:
Updated serialized metadata payload associated with the refund, or null to clear.

Clients and background jobs can use this field to store or revise provider payloads, diagnostic information, or internal flags relevant to this refund. When null is supplied, any previously persisted metadata is removed.

If omitted, the current `metadata` content remains unchanged.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefundItem.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination request DTO for listing refund item breakdown records stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` table.

This request type is used exclusively by the PATCH `/shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/refunds/{refundSequence}/items` operation to retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of refund line items associated with a particular payment refund. It encapsulates generic pagination and sorting parameters together with refund-item-specific filters.

The DTO does not include any authentication or actor identity fields. Authorization for accessing refund breakdown data is handled by the admin authentication context of the calling operation rather than by this request payload itself.

page.description:
1-based page index specifying which page of refund item results to retrieve.

This value works together with `limit` to control pagination over the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` search results. When omitted or set to a value below 1, the backend typically normalizes it to page 1 so that callers always receive a valid page of data.

Use this field in conjunction with `limit` to implement standard next/previous paging controls in admin UIs.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund item records to include in a single page of results.

This value defines the page size for the refund item listing. When not provided, the backend applies a sensible default page size, and it may also enforce an upper bound to protect performance and prevent accidentally requesting excessively large pages.

Client applications should choose a limit that balances usability (fewer pages) with response size and performance, and should be prepared for the service to cap very large requested limits.

orderItemId.description:
Optional filter for restricting results to refund item rows that reference a specific order item.

This value corresponds to the primary key of a row in `shopping_mall_order_items` that is linked through the `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key of `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items`. When provided, only refund breakdown lines for that order item will be returned.

minLineRefundAmount.description:
Lower bound filter for the `line_refund_amount` of refund item records.

When set, only refund item rows whose `line_refund_amount` is greater than or equal to this value will be included. This is useful for focusing on higher-value refund allocations during financial reviews or reconciliation.

maxLineRefundAmount.description:
Upper bound filter for the `line_refund_amount` of refund item records.

When set, only refund item rows whose `line_refund_amount` is less than or equal to this value will be included. This helps narrow down search results to smaller or moderate refund allocations in detailed financial analysis.

createdFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound DateTime filter on the `created_at` timestamp of refund item records.

Only refund item rows whose `created_at` timestamp is greater than or equal to this value will be returned. This supports time-window based investigations for recent or historical refund activities and should be provided as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

createdTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound DateTime filter on the `created_at` timestamp of refund item records.

Only refund item rows whose `created_at` timestamp is less than or equal to this value will be included in the result set. Together with `createdFrom`, this allows range queries over refund item creation times and should be supplied as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort the resulting refund item list.

The value must correspond to a sortable field that the backend implementation recognizes for refund item search (for example `"created_at"` or `"line_refund_amount"`). If an unsupported field name is supplied, the service may ignore the directive or fail validation depending on implementation.

Admins should prefer documented sort keys to ensure consistent ordering behavior across environments and versions of the API.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the `sortBy` field when ordering refund item results.

Use `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. When omitted, the backend typically defaults to a descending order for time-based fields such as `created_at`, but exact defaults are defined by the service implementation.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefundItem.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for a single refund line item in the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` table.

This type is used by the POST `/shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/refunds/{refundSequence}/items` operation to create one granular refund breakdown record under a specific payment and refund sequence. Each created row represents how much of a single order item is being refunded, as well as the quantity associated with that refund.

The DTO does not carry the parent payment or refund identifiers (`orderPaymentId` and `refundSequence`); those are obtained from the URL path parameters of the calling operation and used by the backend to link the new record to the corresponding `shopping_mall_order_payments` and `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` rows. System-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are excluded because they are generated and maintained by the persistence layer.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Identifier of the order item whose charge is being refunded in whole or in part.

This field maps directly to the `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key column of `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` and must reference an existing row in the `shopping_mall_order_items` table. The backend uses this linkage to validate that the refund quantity and amount do not exceed what was originally ordered and paid for this item.

refunded_quantity.description:
Quantity of the referenced order item that is being refunded.

This value corresponds to the `refunded_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items`. It supports fractional quantities for platforms that allow partial units, and must be non-negative. The backend will validate that the cumulative refunded quantity for the order item does not exceed the quantity originally ordered and still eligible for refund.

unit_price_amount.description:
Unit price amount used as the basis for calculating the refund for this line item.

This property maps to the `unit_price_amount` column and represents the monetary amount per unit in the currency associated with the parent refund in `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`. It is typically derived from the original order item price but may be adjusted according to business rules such as discounts or promotions.

line_refund_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded for this order item line within the context of the current refund operation.

This property is persisted in the `line_refund_amount` column and usually equals `refunded_quantity * unit_price_amount` minus any adjustments that apply to this particular refund scenario. The payment service validates that the sum of line-level refund amounts for an order item does not exceed the original charged amount when aggregated across multiple refunds.

oneOf.description:
Non-null reason code value describing why this refund item is being created.

Typical values include business-specific tokens such as `damaged`, `wrong_item`, or `customer_remorse`. The exact set of allowed codes is governed by higher-level policy configuration and may be enforced by validation logic in the service layer.

Null value indicating that no item-specific reason code is specified for this refund line.

When null, the refund reason may be derived from the parent refund, related refund request records, or dispute metadata rather than from this individual item breakdown.

reason_code.description:
Optional item-specific reason code linked to the refund breakdown row.

This property corresponds to the nullable `reason_code` column. When present, it allows more granular categorization of refund causes at the line-item level, which can be compared against configuration in policy or analytics tables. When omitted or null, reporting systems rely on parent-level reason information instead.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefundItem.description:
Represents a single item-level refund breakdown row for a payment refund within the shopping mall platform.

Each record corresponds to a portion of a refund allocated to a specific order item and is stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` Prisma model. It links a parent refund operation from `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` and an order item from `shopping_mall_order_items`, capturing how much quantity and monetary value of that item is being refunded.

This DTO is used in administrative payment and refund workflows to show detailed refund breakdowns per SKU or order line. It exposes numeric quantities and amounts along with metadata such as item-level reason codes and audit timestamps, enabling finance and operations teams to analyze refund behavior at a granular level.

id.description:
Primary key of the refund item record.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes a single row in the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` table. It is generated by the system when the refund item is created and is used as the stable reference for subsequent read or update operations.

Clients receive this value in responses but never supply it in create or update DTOs.

paymentRefund.description:
Summary of the parent payment refund operation to which this item-level breakdown belongs.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_payment_refund_id` foreign key and provides essential context about the refund header, such as its sequence, status, and aggregate amounts, without requiring an additional API call.

The summary is represented by `IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.ISummary`, which is a lightweight view of the refund header entity stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` table.

orderItem.description:
Summary of the order item whose charge is being refunded in whole or in part.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key and exposes key information about the underlying order line and SKU while keeping the representation compact.

The summary is represented by `IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary`, which is a lightweight view of the order item entity stored in the `shopping_mall_order_items` table.

refunded_quantity.description:
Quantity of the order item that is being refunded in this refund item row.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.refunded_quantity` and supports fractional quantities when the platform allows partial units or weight-based products. It must be non-negative and should not exceed the originally ordered quantity for the associated order item.

Business rules that validate refund requests will typically enforce that the sum of refunded quantities across all refund items for the same order item does not exceed the original ordered quantity.

unit_price_amount.description:
Unit price amount used as the monetary basis for this refund item.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.unit_price_amount` and is expressed in the currency of the parent refund record in `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`. It usually represents the unit-level price inclusive of any relevant adjustments at the time of purchase.

Back-office tools use this amount along with `refunded_quantity` to validate that the line-level refund amount is consistent with the original charge and any applicable business policies.

line_refund_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded for this order item in the context of the parent refund operation.

The value comes from `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.line_refund_amount` and is expressed in the same currency as the parent refund. It should normally equal the product of `refunded_quantity` and `unit_price_amount`, possibly adjusted by taxes, discounts, or other business rules.

Validation logic must ensure that the sum of all `line_refund_amount` values under a given refund does not exceed the refundable balance of the associated payment or order items.

reason_code.description:
Optional reason code that describes why this particular order item is being refunded.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.reason_code` and may contain values such as `"damaged"`, `"wrong_item"`, or `"customer_remorse"`. The actual vocabulary may be aligned with structured reason code catalogs in other tables.

When null, no item-specific reason has been provided and the refund reason is assumed to be covered by higher-level refund request or case records.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this refund item record was created.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.created_at` and is set by the system at insertion time. It allows auditors and analysts to trace when item-level refund decisions were recorded for a payment.

Clients treat this timestamp as read-only metadata and can use it for chronological sorting or time-based reporting of refund activity.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this refund item record was last updated.

The field corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.updated_at` and is automatically maintained by the system whenever editable fields such as quantities, amounts, or reason code are modified.

Operations dashboards and audit tools can use this value to detect recent changes to refund allocations and to support conflict detection in concurrent editing scenarios.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefundItem.IUpdate.description:
Mutable subset of fields for modifying an existing item-level payment refund breakdown row.

This DTO is applied to records in the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` table after the initial creation of a refund item. It allows administrative workflows to adjust numeric quantities and amounts or to update the item-level reason code while preserving the structural relationships to the parent refund and order item.

Update operations that consume this schema must enforce business rules defined for the payment and refund lifecycle, such as prohibiting changes once a refund has reached a terminal status or preventing the cumulative refunded quantities and amounts from exceeding original order and payment values.

refunded_quantity.description:
New quantity of the order item to be considered refunded in this refund item row.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `refunded_quantity` in `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items`. It must remain non-negative and should not cause the total refunded quantity across all refund items for the associated order item to exceed the originally ordered quantity.

If omitted, the quantity component of the refund item remains unchanged.

unit_price_amount.description:
Updated unit price amount used as the monetary basis for this refund item.

Supplying this field updates `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.unit_price_amount`. Any changes must remain consistent with the currency and pricing context of the parent refund record and the original order item pricing.

If not included in the request, the existing unit price amount is preserved.

line_refund_amount.description:
Revised total monetary amount to refund for this specific order item under the parent refund.

This value updates `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items.line_refund_amount` when provided. It should remain non-negative and should not cause the aggregate refunded amounts for the relevant payment or order item to exceed the total paid amount.

If omitted, the previously stored line refund amount remains in effect.

reason_code.description:
Updated item-level reason code explaining why this order item is being refunded.

When a non-null string is supplied, it replaces the existing `reason_code` in the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` record with a new explanation such as `"damaged"` or `"wrong_item"`. When explicitly set to null, it clears any existing item-level reason so that only higher-level refund reasons apply.

If this property is not included in the request, the current reason code value is left unchanged.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and filtering chargeback records associated with a specific logical order payment in the shoppingMall platform.

This schema is used as the request body of the PATCH `/shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/chargebacks` search endpoint. It does not map directly to a Prisma model table but instead encapsulates query parameters such as pagination, status filters, date ranges, and amount ranges that control how rows from `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` are selected and ordered.

The fields defined here are interpreted purely as search criteria and do not persist to the database. They allow administrative users to perform back-office investigations over the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table while keeping the URL clean and avoiding excessively long query strings.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination when listing chargeback records.

This value determines which slice of the overall filtered result set should be returned. If omitted, the server typically defaults to the first page. Values less than 1 are invalid and should be rejected at validation time.

limit.description:
Maximum number of chargeback records to return in a single page.

This value is used together with `page` to control pagination over the filtered chargeback list. Implementations should enforce an upper bound (for example 100 or 200) even if the client sends a higher value to prevent excessive result sizes.

status.description:
Optional business status filter applied to chargeback records.

When provided, only chargebacks whose `status` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` matches this value are included. Typical values may include "open", "won", "lost", or other business-defined stages. If omitted, chargebacks are not filtered by status.

stage.description:
Optional lifecycle stage filter for chargeback records.

This corresponds to the `stage` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and may represent scheme- or processor-specific stages such as first presentment, pre-arbitration, or arbitration. When supplied, only chargebacks in the specified stage are returned.

createdAtFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the chargeback creation timestamp range filter.

When set, only chargeback records whose `created_at` value in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` is on or after this timestamp are included in the result. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

createdAtTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the chargeback creation timestamp range filter.

When specified, only chargeback records whose `created_at` value in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` is on or before this timestamp are included in the result. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

disputedAmountMin.description:
Minimum disputed amount filter for chargeback records.

This value selects only records where the `disputed_amount` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` is greater than or equal to the specified threshold. It is expressed in the same currency as the `currency_code` column, typically matching the payment currency.

disputedAmountMax.description:
Maximum disputed amount filter for chargeback records.

When provided, only chargebacks whose `disputed_amount` is less than or equal to this value are returned. It is commonly used together with `disputedAmountMin` to define a numeric range of interest for investigations or reporting.

providerReference.description:
Free-text filter applied to the provider reference identifier for chargebacks.

This value is intended to match the `provider_reference` column of `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`, which often contains the external dispute or case identifier supplied by the payment processor, card scheme, or acquiring bank. Implementations may treat this as an exact match or perform a case-insensitive partial match depending on indexing strategy.

sortBy.description:
Field name used for sorting the chargeback search results.

Typical sortable fields include `created_at`, `disputed_amount`, or `status`. The concrete set of allowed values should be enforced by the server implementation to avoid arbitrary column exposure. When omitted, the default sort order is usually by `created_at` descending.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied together with `sortBy` when ordering search results.

Supported values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. If omitted, the server typically defaults to `"desc"` so that the most recent chargebacks appear first.

Sort direction applied together with `sortBy` when ordering search results.

Supported values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. If omitted, the server typically defaults to `"desc"` so that the most recent chargebacks appear first.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied together with `sortBy` when ordering search results.

Supported values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. If omitted, the server typically defaults to `"desc"` so that the most recent chargebacks appear first.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new chargeback record associated with a specific logical order payment in the shoppingMall platform.

This schema maps directly to the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table and is used as the request body of the POST `/shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/chargebacks` endpoint. It captures the business fields that a back-office or automated reconciliation process must provide when a card issuer, bank, or payment provider opens a chargeback case against a payment.

The `orderPaymentId` itself is supplied as a path parameter and therefore is not part of this DTO. System-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are excluded and will be generated by the backend when persisting the new row. Administrative identity is resolved from authentication context, so no admin identifier is accepted from the client in this DTO.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code of the disputed amount for the chargeback.

This value is written directly into the `currency_code` column of `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and should usually match the currency of the underlying logical order payment. It enables consistent reporting and ensures correct interpretation of `disputed_amount` and `chargeback_amount` values.

disputed_amount.description:
Amount disputed by the issuer or payment provider for this chargeback.

This numeric value corresponds to the `disputed_amount` column of `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`. It represents the total amount that the external party has challenged, in units of the currency identified by `currency_code`. Implementations may enforce non-negative values and apply domain-specific rounding rules.

chargeback_amount.description:
Amount that has actually been withdrawn from the platform due to this chargeback, if any.

This field maps to the `chargeback_amount` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and is typically less than or equal to `disputed_amount`. It reflects the financial impact already realized on the platform or seller side at the moment of record creation.

reason_code.description:
Optional provider or scheme-defined chargeback reason code.

When supplied, this string is stored in the `reason_code` column and can encode scheme-specific categories such as fraud, card-not-present, or product-not-received. It is used by risk and operations teams for classification and reporting. If omitted, the record may rely on free-form notes in `metadata` instead.

status.description:
Business status of the chargeback case at creation time.

This value is persisted into the `status` column of `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and reflects the current resolution stage from a business perspective. Common values include flags such as "open", "won", "lost", or other platform-specific states. Downstream workflows and reporting may rely on this field to track the lifecycle of disputes.

stage.description:
Optional lifecycle stage for the chargeback within card scheme or processor flows.

This maps to the `stage` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and usually captures technical scheme stages such as first presentment, pre-arbitration, or arbitration. It allows financial operations teams to understand where the case currently sits in the external dispute process. If unknown or not applicable, this field may be omitted or left empty.

provider_reference.description:
