Clients use this field together with `limit` to navigate through a large collection of payout items associated with a payout batch. If omitted, the service may fall back to a sensible default such as page 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of payout items to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size of search results for payout items under the specified batch. The backend should enforce an upper bound to protect performance, even if clients request larger page sizes.

status.description:
Optional payout item status filter applied within the specified batch.

This value typically corresponds to business status codes defined on `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, such as "pending", "included", "paid", or "reversed". When provided, only payout items whose status matches this code are considered in the result set.

minPayoutAmount.description:
Optional lower bound for the payout amount filter.

When set, only payout items whose payout amount is greater than or equal to this value are included in the search results. The amount is interpreted in the batch currency configured on the parent payout batch.

maxPayoutAmount.description:
Optional upper bound for the payout amount filter.

When set, only payout items whose payout amount is less than or equal to this value are included in the search results. Combined with `minPayoutAmount`, this enables range-based financial queries for settlement analysis.

paidFrom.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound of the payout item paid-at timestamp.

When specified, only payout items with `paid_at` greater than or equal to this value are returned. This is useful for locating items paid during a particular settlement window inside the selected batch.

paidTo.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound of the payout item paid-at timestamp.

When specified, only payout items with `paid_at` less than or equal to this value are returned. Use together with `paidFrom` to represent a time range for settlement events.

createdFrom.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound on the payout item creation time.

This filter allows administrators to search for payout items created after or at a certain point in time, supporting operational monitoring for newly added items within the batch.

createdTo.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound on the payout item creation time.

When provided, only payout items created before or at this point in time are included. Together with `createdFrom`, this supports windowed queries aligned with accounting or operational cutoffs.

orderBy.description:
Optional sort field used when ordering payout item search results.

Typical values correspond to sortable properties such as "created_at", "paid_at", or "payout_amount". The backend should validate the provided field name against an allowed list to prevent invalid ordering expressions.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the search results for payout items.

Allowed values are conceptually "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. The field works in combination with `orderBy` to control the ordering of payout items within the specified batch.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.ICreate.description:
Creation request schema for adding a new seller payout item to an existing payout batch.

This DTO is used by administrative settlement flows that persist individual payout lines in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table under a parent batch identified by its business code in the API path. It captures the monetary amount to be paid, the currency, and links to the originating seller earning record.

The server attaches the payout item to the target batch based on the `{batchCode}` path parameter and applies additional business rules around eligibility, status initialization, and consistency with related earnings and payouts. System-managed identifiers, timestamps, and fields derived from the payout batch itself are not accepted from clients and are handled exclusively by the backend.

shopping_mall_seller_earning_id.description:
Identifier of the seller earning record that this payout item will settle.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_earnings.id` and establishes the concrete earning instance that is being included in the payout batch. The backend validates that the earning exists, is eligible for payout, and is not already associated with another payout item.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code of the payout amount for this item.

Although the currency will usually match the currency configured on the parent payout batch, it is accepted explicitly to ensure clarity in multi-currency configurations and to support validation that the payout item aligns with batch and earning currency rules.

payout_amount.description:
Monetary amount to be paid out for the referenced seller earning within this batch.

This value typically matches the `net_earning_amount` on the associated earning record, but it can differ when partial payouts or adjustments are required. The backend is responsible for validating that the amount is consistent with financial rules and does not violate configured limits or reconciliation constraints.

status.description:
Initial business status of the payout item when it is created.

Typical values include codes such as "pending", "included", or "scheduled", representing the lifecycle starting point of the payout line. Subsequent transitions to "paid" or "reversed" are controlled by payout processing logic and are not handled by this creation request.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.description:
Seller payout item entity stored in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table.

Each record represents a granular payout line that belongs to a seller payout batch and links a specific seller earning to that batch. It materializes how much of a given earning is paid out in a particular payout run, including currency, payout amount, lifecycle status, and audit timestamps.

This type is primarily used in administrative and finance tooling for back-office users who manage settlement runs. It is returned by endpoints that read or mutate payout items within batches identified by business batch codes, and it is the authoritative representation of payout items for downstream reconciliation and reporting.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payout item.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` row and is generated by the database. It is used as the stable reference in URLs and internal joins.

Clients receive this value in responses but never provide or modify it in create or update payloads.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code of the payout amount.

The value typically matches the currency of both the parent payout batch and the underlying seller earning, ensuring that all financial amounts are settled in a consistent currency.

Examples include `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"` depending on marketplace configuration.

payout_amount.description:
Monetary amount paid out for this earning in this batch.

The amount is usually equal to the net earning amount after deducting platform fees and adjustments, but it can differ when partial payouts or corrections are applied.

Downstream reconciliation and finance reports rely on this value to track how much was actually remitted to the seller in the context of this payout batch.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of this payout item.

Typical statuses include values such as `"pending"`, `"included"`, `"paid"`, or `"reversed"`, reflecting whether the item is awaiting export, has been included in a payout file, has been confirmed as paid, or has been reversed due to chargebacks or corrections.

Admin workflows and validation logic use this status to control which operations are allowed on the payout item at any given time.

paid_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout item was confirmed as paid to the seller.

The value is `null` until the payout process reaches a stage where payment is confirmed by the settlement or banking system. Once set, it records the moment the payout became effectively completed.

Reporting and audit tools use this timestamp to analyze payment timelines and settlement latency.

reversed_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout item was reversed.

This field is populated when a previously scheduled or completed payout is reversed, for example because of negative adjustments, chargebacks, or other corrections identified by risk or finance teams.

When `reversed_at` holds a non-null value, the `status` field is typically set to a terminal reversal state, and the item is treated as no longer payable.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout item was created.

The value is assigned by the system when the payout item row is first inserted into `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`. It provides the creation time of the settlement line within the payout batch lifecycle.

This field supports chronological analysis of payout construction and is useful in debugging and compliance reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout item was last updated.

The system refreshes this field whenever mutable attributes of the payout item change, such as status transitions or adjustments to payout amounts that are allowed by business rules.

Change-tracking mechanisms and admin audit logs rely on this timestamp to identify recent modifications to payout items.

payoutBatch.description:
Parent payout batch that owns this payout item.

This association points to the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches` record that groups this item with other seller earnings in the same settlement run.

Exposing the batch as a summary object allows clients to see contextual information such as batch code, scheduled date, and batch status without needing additional API calls.

sellerEarning.description:
Underlying seller earning settled by this payout item.

This association references the `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` record that describes how the earning was generated (for example, from which order or order items) and its net amount before it was picked up for payout.

Providing this as a summary object gives finance operators immediate insight into the origin of the payout line while avoiding redundant foreign key IDs in the response payload.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for a seller payout item stored in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table.

This type is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` Prisma model and represents the subset of columns that are allowed to change after the row has been created. It excludes identity and ownership fields such as `id`, foreign key columns, and audit timestamps, ensuring that only business-approved attributes of the payout item can be modified.

The DTO is consumed by administrative finance tools that operate on payout batches identified by a business `batchCode`. It is used for partial updates of existing payout item records, such as adjusting payout status, correcting payout amounts within strict financial policies, or updating paid and reversed timestamps to align with settlement and reconciliation events.

currency_code.description:
Updated ISO 4217 currency code of the payout amount.

This field maps directly to the `currency_code` column of the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` Prisma model. In normal scenarios the currency should remain aligned with the parent payout batch and the underlying earning, but exceptional administrative corrections may be allowed when misconfigurations are discovered.

Back-office implementations must enforce that any change to `currency_code` stays consistent with the parent batch record in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches` and the associated earning in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings`, preventing inconsistent multi-currency payout lines in a single batch.

payout_amount.description:
Updated monetary amount to be paid out for this earning in this batch.

This property corresponds to the `payout_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table. Finance administrators can use it to correct payout amounts within the boundaries of business rules, for example to fix rounding issues, apply small manual adjustments, or align payouts with corrected earnings.

The service layer must validate that new `payout_amount` values remain coherent with the related earning’s `net_earning_amount`, any previous payouts for the same earning, and configured commission and adjustment rules so that financial records and seller statements remain internally consistent.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the payout item.

This value reflects the `status` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` model and controls how the item participates in payout processing. Typical values include states such as `pending`, `included`, `paid`, or `reversed`, although the exact vocabulary is defined by business policy.

The update handler must enforce valid status transitions, for example moving from `pending` to `included` and then to `paid`, or to `reversed` when payouts are rolled back. Attempts to move away from terminal statuses or to perform transitions that conflict with legal holds or reconciliation outcomes should be rejected to preserve a reliable financial audit trail.

paid_at.description:
Updated timestamp indicating when the payout item was confirmed as paid.

This property maps directly to the `paid_at` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table and is nullable. When non-null, it should record the instant at which the payout was confirmed by the banking system or payout provider for this specific item.

Administrative workflows may set or adjust `paid_at` while reconciling with external reports, or clear the value when a payout is reverted before final confirmation. Any changes to `paid_at` must remain consistent with the `status` field (for example, a non-null `paid_at` should not coexist with a strictly pre-payment status) so that time-based reports and settlement timelines remain accurate.

reversed_at.description:
Updated timestamp when the payout item was reversed.

This property is bound to the `reversed_at` column of the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` Prisma model and is used to record the moment a previously scheduled or completed payout is reversed. Reversals may be triggered by negative adjustments, chargebacks, disputes, or other corrective actions initiated by risk or finance teams.

When `reversed_at` is set to a non-null value, the `status` column is typically transitioned to a terminal reversal state, and the payout item should no longer be considered payable. Updates that change `reversed_at` must be validated to ensure they are compatible with business rules, legal hold requirements, and the historical sequence of payout events.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodAnalytics.IReq.description:
Request payload for querying aggregated analytics statistics for payment methods across the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO encapsulates analytical query parameters for a read-only endpoint that aggregates data from payment-related Prisma models and snapshots, including `shopping_mall_payment_methods`, `shopping_mall_order_payments`, `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts`, `shopping_mall_payment_status_histories`, `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`, `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`, and `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats`. Although it is not mapped to a single Prisma table, its fields are designed to filter and group over those underlying data sources.

Administrators and analysts use this request type to define a time range, choose which payment methods and regions to analyze, configure grouping and time granularity, fine-tune value-based filters, and control sorting and pagination of the aggregated result rows. The response is a paginated collection of `IShoppingMallPaymentMethodAnalytics.ISummary` objects wrapped in `IPageIShoppingMallPaymentMethodAnalytics.ISummary`.

from.description:
Inclusive start of the analysis time window in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value bounds the earliest timestamp of payment-related records and snapshot rows that participate in the aggregation. It is typically interpreted in UTC or a platform-wide reporting timezone and must be less than or equal to `to`.

Choosing an appropriately sized window helps keep queries performant and aligns the analytics with reporting periods such as days, weeks, or months.

to.description:
Exclusive end of the analysis time window in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Records and snapshot rows with timestamps greater than or equal to this value are excluded from the aggregation, making the window effectively half-open `[from, to)`. The `to` timestamp must be greater than or equal to `from` and is typically chosen to align with the end of a reporting period.

Together with `from`, this field defines the time range that determines which payments, refunds, chargebacks, and snapshot entries are considered for the computed KPIs.

paymentMethodCodes.description:
Optional list of payment method codes used to restrict the analytics to specific payment rails.

Each entry should correspond to a `code` value from the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` Prisma model (for example `"card"`, `"bank_transfer"`, or a gateway-specific code). When this array is omitted or empty, all configured payment methods are eligible for inclusion in the aggregation.

Using this filter allows dashboards to focus on a subset of methods, such as card payments only, or to compare performance between a small set of methods without processing the entire catalog of payment options.

regionCodes.description:
Optional list of marketplace region codes used to scope analytics to specific geographies.

Values typically correspond to region or country codes defined in master data tables such as `shopping_mall_regions` and `shopping_mall_countries` (for example `"US"`, `"KR"`, or internal region identifiers). When omitted or left empty, the analytics query includes data from all supported regions.

Applying region filters allows operators to compare payment method performance across countries or sub-regions and to spot geography-specific issues such as localized provider failures.

oneOf.description:
Grouping dimension identifier for the analytics query.

When `paymentMethod` is present in `groupBy`, aggregated rows are split by payment method code. Each result row then corresponds to a specific method (and any other grouping keys, such as date or region).

Grouping dimension identifier for the analytics query.

When `date` is present in `groupBy`, metrics are further grouped into time buckets determined by the `granularity` field (for example daily or weekly buckets). This enables time-series analysis per payment method or region.

Grouping dimension identifier for the analytics query.

When `region` is present in `groupBy`, metrics are broken down by region code so that each result row corresponds to a specific geographic area in combination with other grouping dimensions.

items.description:
Grouping dimension identifier for the analytics query.

The `groupBy` array controls how aggregated metrics are sliced into distinct result rows. Supported dimensions are:
- `paymentMethod`: group metrics by payment method code.
- `date`: group metrics by time bucket determined by the `granularity` field.
- `region`: group metrics by region code.

The combination of these values defines the grouping keys of each `IShoppingMallPaymentMethodAnalytics.ISummary` row returned by the endpoint.

groupBy.description:
List of grouping dimensions used to aggregate analytics results.

The contents of this array determine whether the output is grouped by payment method, time, region, or a combination of those dimensions. For example, `groupBy: ["paymentMethod", "date"]` yields per-method, per-time-bucket summaries, while `groupBy: ["region"]` yields region-only aggregates.

If `groupBy` is omitted or empty, the server may default to a sensible grouping strategy such as overall totals per payment method or a global aggregate, depending on platform policy.

oneOf.description:
Time granularity used when grouping analytics by date.

The `hour` value instructs the analytics engine to aggregate metrics into hourly buckets within the `[from, to)` window, which is useful for short-term monitoring and troubleshooting incidents that unfold over hours.

Time granularity used when grouping analytics by date.

The `day` value aggregates metrics into daily buckets and is typically used for operational dashboards and high-level performance monitoring.

Time granularity used when grouping analytics by date.

The `week` value groups metrics into weekly buckets, supporting medium-term trend analysis across multiple weeks.

Time granularity used when grouping analytics by date.

The `month` value aggregates metrics into calendar-month buckets, which is suitable for long-term financial and risk reporting.

granularity.description:
Time granularity used when grouping analytics by date.

This field only takes effect when `groupBy` includes the `date` dimension; when `date` is not part of `groupBy`, `granularity` is ignored. It determines the size of the time buckets (for example hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly) used to group payment method metrics over the `[from, to)` interval.

Choosing finer granularity yields more detailed time series at the cost of more result rows, while coarse granularity provides a compact overview across longer periods.

minTotalAmount.description:
Optional lower bound filter for total aggregated monetary amounts in each analytics slice.

When provided, result rows whose aggregated monetary metric (for example total paid amount or GMV processed by the method) falls strictly below this value may be excluded from the response. The exact metric used for filtering is defined by the analytics implementation and documentation.

Setting `minTotalAmount` can help focus on slices that are materially significant, avoiding clutter from very low-volume combinations of payment method, region, and date.

maxTotalAmount.description:
Optional upper bound filter for total aggregated monetary amounts in each analytics slice.

When provided, result rows whose aggregated monetary metric exceeds this value may be excluded from the response, allowing operators to isolate lower-value segments or check behavior below certain thresholds.

Combined with `minTotalAmount`, this field defines an inclusive numeric window for the aggregated amount used in analytics, applied per result row rather than per individual transaction.

includeRefunds.description:
Flag indicating whether refund-related metrics should be included in the analytics computation.

When set to `true`, the analytics engine calculates and exposes refund-related values such as refund counts, refunded amounts, and refund ratios derived from sources like `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`. When `false`, those metrics may be omitted from the response or computed as zeros, depending on the implementation.

Toggling this flag allows clients to trade off between query complexity and insight: disabling refunds can make computation cheaper when only pure payment performance is of interest.

includeChargebacks.description:
Flag indicating whether chargeback-related metrics should be included in the analytics computation.

When `true`, additional KPIs such as chargeback counts and chargeback amounts (sourced from `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and related tables) are calculated and surfaced in the analytics summaries. When `false`, those chargeback-specific metrics are typically skipped to reduce query complexity.

This option is useful for switching between general payment performance views and risk-focused views that require chargeback insights.

oneOf.description:
Sort by the aggregated total monetary amount metric for each analytics row.

This option is typically used to rank payment methods or slices by volume processed within the selected time range.

Sort by the number of payments or attempts associated with each analytics row.

This is useful when analyzing popularity or usage frequency of different payment methods or segments.

Sort by the success rate metric for each slice.

This allows operators to quickly identify payment methods or segments with particularly high or low success rates.

Sort by the refund rate metric for each slice.

This helps identify payment methods, regions, or time periods with elevated refund activity when `includeRefunds` is enabled.

Sort by the chargeback rate metric for each slice.

This is particularly useful for risk teams when `includeChargebacks` is enabled, highlighting segments with anomalously high chargeback behavior.

sortBy.description:
Field used to sort the aggregated analytics rows in the response.

Supported values correspond to derived metrics such as total processed amount, payment count, success rate, refund rate, or chargeback rate for each aggregated row. The exact mapping between sort field and underlying metric is defined by the analytics implementation but should be documented alongside the endpoint.

Sorting is applied after aggregation and in combination with `sortDirection`, and affects the order of rows returned within each page controlled by `page` and `limit`.

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort order for the selected `sortBy` metric.

Rows with smaller metric values appear first within the page.

Descending sort order for the selected `sortBy` metric.

Rows with larger metric values appear first within the page.

sortDirection.description:
Direction in which to sort the aggregated analytics rows.

Use `asc` to obtain rows in ascending order of the chosen `sortBy` metric and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the server may choose a sensible default (commonly `desc` for metrics like total amount or count) to present the most significant slices first.

Sort direction interacts with pagination: combined with `page` and `limit`, it determines which segments appear on each page of results.

page.description:
Page index for paginated analytics results, starting from 1.

This field controls which page of aggregated rows is returned. For example, `page = 1` with a given `limit` retrieves the first page of analytics slices according to the chosen sort order, and `page = 2` retrieves the next page.

If omitted, the server may default to the first page (typically page 1) as a convenience for callers that do not need fine-grained pagination control.

limit.description:
Maximum number of analytics summary rows to return in a single page.

This value is applied after aggregation, sorting, and filtering, and therefore determines how many `IShoppingMallPaymentMethodAnalytics.ISummary` rows appear in each response page. It should be set to a reasonable value to balance completeness of information and response size.

If omitted, the server may apply a platform-default limit (for example 20, 50, or 100) to prevent excessively large pages while still returning a useful subset of the analytics results.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentSummary.IRe.description:
Filter and configuration parameters for computing an administrative payment analytics summary over a bounded time window.

This request DTO is used by administrator or operations actors to specify the required date range, the aggregation granularity, and optional scoping filters for the payment summary endpoint. The analytics engine may clamp the effective range to internal retention limits or maximum window sizes to protect performance and resource usage.

The request is purely read-only and does not map directly to any single Prisma model. Instead, it drives aggregation queries over multiple payment-related tables, including logical payments, attempts, status histories, refunds, chargebacks, and snapshot statistics. Optional filters behave as inclusive constraints; when omitted, the platform applies defaults that typically compute KPIs across all relevant data within the requested period.

from.description:
Inclusive start of the analysis window in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

The server may normalize this value to internal bucket boundaries (for example, the beginning of an hour or day) and may clamp it to the earliest date for which payment analytics data is retained.

to.description:
Exclusive end of the analysis window in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). Must be greater than `from` and within the system-defined maximum range.

If the requested range exceeds the maximum supported length, the server may reject the request with a validation error or automatically shorten the window while reflecting the effective range in the response.

granularity.description:
Desired time bucketing granularity for time-series metrics within the summary.

The selected granularity controls how the analytics engine partitions the `[from, to)` window when building `timeSeries` buckets (for example, hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly).

paymentMethodCodes.description:
Optional inclusive filter of payment method codes to include in the aggregation.

When provided, only payments whose configured payment method code appears in this list are considered in the computed KPIs. When omitted or provided as an empty array, the analytics engine treats this as "no payment‑method restriction" and includes all configured payment methods that participate in the underlying data set.

sellerIds.description:
Optional inclusive filter of seller identifiers used to scope the analytics.

When this array contains one or more seller UUIDs, only payments logically associated with those sellers are included in the aggregations. When omitted or provided as an empty array, analytics are computed across all sellers in the platform that match the remaining filters.

minAmount.description:
Optional minimum processed amount filter applied to logical payments before aggregation.

The value is interpreted in the platform’s analytics base currency and should be non‑negative. When both `minAmount` and `maxAmount` are supplied, the server expects `minAmount` to be less than or equal to `maxAmount`; invalid combinations may result in a validation error or automatic normalization.

maxAmount.description:
Optional maximum processed amount filter applied to logical payments before aggregation.

The value is interpreted in the platform’s analytics base currency and should be non‑negative. When used together with `minAmount`, this upper bound defines an inclusive range of payment amounts to include in the analysis window.

includeHighRisk.description:
Flag indicating whether payments that have been flagged as high‑risk by the risk engine should be included in the aggregation.

When set to `true`, metrics such as total processed amount and success/failure counts will include high‑risk payments that passed through the system. When set to `false`, those payments are excluded from the KPIs. When omitted, platform policy or configuration determines whether high‑risk payments are included by default.

includeDisputed.description:
Flag indicating whether payments associated with chargebacks or dispute cases should be included in the aggregated metrics.

Setting this flag to `true` ensures that refunded, charged back, or disputed payments contribute to totals and derived ratios (such as refund rate or chargeback rate). When `false`, those payments are excluded from the primary aggregates. When omitted, the platform applies its default behavior, which may differ between environments or tenants.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentSummary.description:
Aggregated analytics view of payment performance across the ShoppingMall platform for a given time range and filter set.

This DTO does not map 1:1 to any single Prisma model. Instead, it represents a computed summary that combines metrics derived from multiple payment-related tables, including logical payments, payment attempts, payment status histories, refunds, chargebacks, and snapshot statistics tables.

The summary is returned as the response body of an admin‑only analytics endpoint and is optimized for BI dashboards, monitoring tools, and internal reporting rather than direct persistence. The `totals` section always reflects the full population of payments that match the effective filters and time window, while each optional breakdown array exposes more detailed views where requested or applicable.

Depending on the request parameters and platform configuration, some breakdown arrays may be omitted entirely or may be present but empty. Clients must be prepared to handle all three states: property absent, present with an empty array, or present with populated entries.

timeRange.description:
Time window over which all metrics in this summary have been computed.

The values in this structure describe the *effective* range after any clamping, normalization to bucket boundaries, or defaulting that the server performed on the original request.

granularity.description:
Time bucketing granularity used for time-series breakdowns in this summary.

This value corresponds to the granularity requested by the client or a server-selected default and is used when interpreting the `timeSeries` buckets.

totals.description:
High-level aggregate payment KPIs for the requested range.

The totals section typically includes metrics such as total processed amount, logical payment counts, successful and failed payments, refund amounts, chargeback amounts, and average ticket size. These metrics are computed across the entire population of payments that match the effective filters, regardless of whether more granular breakdown arrays are present.

byMethod.description:
Optional breakdown of payment metrics by payment method code (for example, card, bank_transfer, or wallet).

This array may be omitted when the client does not request method-level breakdowns, when such breakdowns are disabled for the environment, or when no data is available for the selected filters. When present but empty, it indicates that the query executed successfully but no payments matched the filters for any method.

byStatus.description:
Optional breakdown of payment metrics by primary payment status (for example, succeeded, failed, or pending).

As with `byMethod`, this array may be absent when status-level breakdowns are not requested or relevant. An empty array conveys that there was no matching payment activity in the specified time window under the given filters.

bySeller.description:
Optional breakdown of payment metrics scoped per seller over the requested time range.

Each element in this array aggregates KPIs such as total processed amount and success/failure counts for a single seller. The property may be omitted to reduce payload size when seller-level analytics are not needed, or it may be present with zero elements when no seller matched the filters.

timeSeries.description:
Optional time-series buckets containing metrics per time interval (for example, per hour or per day) within the requested range.

Each bucket aligns with the configured `granularity` and contains its own `totals` block describing metrics for that slice of time. The property may be omitted entirely when the client is interested only in overall totals and non-temporal breakdowns or when the analytics engine decides not to compute a time-series for performance reasons.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsRefundSummary.description:
Aggregated analytics summary of refunds and related post-payment adjustments across the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a computed, read-only analytical view that summarizes refund and dispute behavior over a requested time range. It is not backed by a single Prisma table but composes data from payment refunds, refund requests, refund items, refund reasons, refund status histories, disputes, dispute events, SLA configurations, SLA violations, and precomputed snapshot statistics. It is intended for internal administrative dashboards and governance tooling, not for public clients.

timeRange.description: Normalized time range actually used to compute the analytics, after applying any internal bounding or defaulting logic.

filters.description: Effective filter configuration that was applied when generating this summary, including any inferred or defaulted values.

totals.description: High-level aggregate metrics for refund volume, amounts, and ratios over the selected time range and filters.

reasonBreakdowns.description: Breakdown of refund metrics by structured refund reason code, including counts and total refunded amounts per reason.

slaMetrics.description: SLA-related metrics for refund and dispute handling, such as average processing times and SLA breach counts or rates.

disputeCorrelation.description: Metrics describing how refunds correlate with disputes and chargebacks, for example the percentage of refunds that escalated into disputes.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsRefundSummary.IReq.description:
Request payload for computing an aggregated analytics summary of refunds and related post-payment adjustments.

Callers must provide a mandatory date range describing the analysis window and may optionally specify dimensions and filters such as grouping by reason code or seller, minimum refund amount, or inclusion/exclusion of certain case types. The backend validates that referenced reason codes and sellers exist and that the requested time range and grouping are within performance-safe bounds.

from.description: Start of the analysis window (inclusive) in ISO 8601 date-time format. Must not be later than `to`. Business rules or system limits may further constrain how far back this can be set.

to.description: End of the analysis window (exclusive) in ISO 8601 date-time format. Must not be earlier than `from`. Combined with `from` it may be validated against maximum allowed span for analytics queries.

oneOf.description: Optional grouping dimension for the analytics output. `reason` groups by refund reason code, `seller` groups by seller, `status` groups by high-level refund or case status, and `none` disables grouping to return only top-level aggregates.

Optional grouping dimension for the analytics output. `reason` groups by refund reason code, `seller` groups by seller, `status` groups by high-level refund or case status, and `none` disables grouping to return only top-level aggregates.

Optional grouping dimension for the analytics output. `reason` groups by refund reason code, `seller` groups by seller, `status` groups by high-level refund or case status, and `none` disables grouping to return only top-level aggregates.

Optional grouping dimension for the analytics output. `reason` groups by refund reason code, `seller` groups by seller, `status` groups by high-level refund or case status, and `none` disables grouping to return only top-level aggregates.

groupBy.description: Optional grouping dimension for the analytics output. `reason` groups by refund reason code, `seller` groups by seller, `status` groups by high-level refund or case status, and `none` disables grouping to return only top-level aggregates.

minRefundAmount.description: Optional minimum refunded amount filter. Only refunds with total amount greater than or equal to this value are included in the analytics.

includeCaseTypes.description: Optional whitelist of business-level refund or case types to include, such as policy-driven refunds, goodwill gestures, fraud-related refunds, or refunds caused by system errors.

excludeCaseTypes.description: Optional blacklist of business-level refund or case types to exclude from the analytics.

sellerIds.description: Optional list of seller identifiers used to restrict analytics to specific sellers. If omitted or empty, analytics covers all sellers.

reasonCodes.description: Optional list of structured refund reason codes to restrict the analysis. Values must match codes configured in the refund reason catalog.

includeDisputes.description: Whether to include refunds that are associated with disputes when computing metrics. When false, only non-disputed refunds are considered for certain aggregates.

includeChargebacks.description: Whether to include refunds that are directly or indirectly related to chargeback cases in the analytics results.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentTotals.description:
High-level aggregate payment metrics for a given analysis window.

These KPIs typically appear at the top of an analytics dashboard to provide a quick overview of payment performance.

totalProcessedAmount.description: Total monetary amount successfully processed in the analysis window, expressed in the platform's base currency or a normalized currency used for analytics.

totalPayments.description: Total number of logical payments processed in the analysis window, regardless of status.

successfulPayments.description: Number of logical payments that reached a successful terminal status (e.g., captured or succeeded).

failedPayments.description: Number of logical payments that reached a failure terminal status.

refundedAmount.description: Total monetary amount refunded within the analysis window, regardless of when the original payments occurred.

chargebackAmount.description: Total monetary amount associated with chargebacks within the analysis window.

averageTicketSize.description: Average processed amount per successful payment in the analysis window.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentByMethod.description:
Payment performance metrics aggregated per payment method code for a given analysis window.

This DTO represents a single analytics bucket keyed by a payment method code (for example, `card`, `bank_transfer`, or a provider-specific code). Each bucket summarizes how customers have used that payment method over a reporting window, including volume, success/failure distribution, and optional monetary aggregates.

The payload is typically returned as part of payment analytics dashboards, administrative reports, or monitoring APIs. It is read-only and derived from underlying order and payment tables rather than being persisted directly. Implementations should treat the metrics as a snapshot for the requested time range and filter set.

Some monetary metrics such as `totalProcessedAmount` and `averageTicketSize` may be omitted when the analysis is configured to exclude financial information (for example, in privacy-restricted views) or when the data source does not provide reliable monetary aggregates. Clients must therefore always treat these numeric fields as optional and handle their absence gracefully.

paymentMethodCode.description:
Canonical payment method code used to group analytics metrics.

This value should align with the business codes configured in the payment method reference tables (for example, `card`, `bank_transfer`, `virtual_account`, or provider-specific identifiers). The same code is used consistently across reporting periods so that analytics can be compared over time.

Clients use `paymentMethodCode` as the primary key when rendering charts or tables that compare payment performance across different methods.

totalProcessedAmount.description:
Total monetary amount successfully processed using this payment method within the analysis window.

The value is usually expressed in the marketplace’s base currency (for example, KRW or USD) and represents the sum of captured or settled payments. It should exclude cancelled or fully refunded payments, depending on the business definition of "processed" used by the analytics implementation.

This field may be omitted when monetary aggregation is disabled for the query, when the underlying data source does not support reliable financial totals, or when the status filter makes the amount not meaningful. Consumers must handle the case where `totalProcessedAmount` is not present.

totalPayments.description:
Total number of payment attempts associated with this payment method during the analysis period.

This count includes both successful and failed attempts and can also include pending or in-progress payments, depending on how the analytics query is configured. It is primarily used as the denominator when calculating method-level adoption and failure rates.

In a typical configuration, `totalPayments` should be greater than or equal to `successfulPayments + failedPayments`, with any difference representing intermediate or ignored statuses (for example, pending or cancelled before processing).

successfulPayments.description:
Number of payment attempts using this method that reached a business-defined successful state within the analysis window.

A successful payment normally corresponds to an authorized and captured transaction that contributes to revenue. The exact mapping between payment gateway states and the `successfulPayments` count is determined by the payment integration and business rules.

This value is used together with `totalPayments` and `failedPayments` to derive success ratios and conversion metrics for the payment method.

failedPayments.description:
Number of payment attempts using this method that ended in a failure state during the analysis window.

Failures typically include hard declines, authorization failures, validation errors, and technical errors that prevented the payment from completing. Whether timeouts or user-aborted attempts are counted as failures depends on the analytics configuration.

Analysts commonly compare `failedPayments` to `totalPayments` and `successfulPayments` to understand error rates and to identify underperforming payment methods or external provider issues.

averageTicketSize.description:
Average monetary amount per successful payment using this method over the analysis window.

The value is generally calculated as `totalProcessedAmount / successfulPayments` for the subset of payments that are considered successful and monetarily valid. It is useful for understanding the typical order size and customer spending behavior for a specific payment method.

This field can be omitted when `totalProcessedAmount` is not computed, when there are no successful payments in the bucket, or when the analytics implementation chooses not to expose derived averages. Callers must therefore not rely on `averageTicketSize` being present in all responses and should guard against division-by-zero assumptions.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentByStatus.description:
Payment performance metrics aggregated per primary payment status for a given analysis window.

Each instance represents an analytics bucket for a canonical payment status (for example, `succeeded`, `failed`, `pending`, or business-specific status codes). The DTO summarizes how many payments fall into that status and, where applicable, the total monetary amount associated with those payments.

This schema is typically used in dashboards and monitoring APIs that visualize status distributions (such as success versus failure rates) and in operational reports that track payment pipeline health over time. It is a read-only analytical projection derived from underlying payment and order records.

Because not all statuses have a meaningful monetary total (for example, `pending` or `cancelled_before_capture`), the `totalProcessedAmount` field is optional and is usually populated only for terminal statuses where amounts are well-defined.

status.description:
Canonical primary status name for the payment group represented by this bucket.

Typical values might include `succeeded`, `failed`, `pending`, `cancelled`, or platform-specific status codes that normalize gateway or acquirer responses into a unified vocabulary. The exact set of statuses depends on the payment domain model used by the platform.

Clients should treat `status` as an opaque key suitable for filtering, grouping, and labeling charts, rather than attempting to infer semantics from its free-form string alone.

totalProcessedAmount.description:
Total monetary amount associated with payments in this status bucket within the analysis window, when a meaningful amount can be determined.

For terminal success-like statuses (such as `succeeded`), this typically represents the sum of captured or settled amounts. For failure-like or intermediate statuses, the field may be undefined or excluded, because there is no clear notion of a processed amount.

Consumers must treat this field as optional: if it is absent for a given `status`, that usually indicates either that the status does not have a well-defined monetary total (for example, `pending`) or that the analytics query was configured to omit financial aggregates.

count.description:
Number of payments that fall into this status bucket over the selected analysis period.

This count is the primary volume metric for the bucket and is commonly used to compute ratios and distributions, such as the percentage of `succeeded` versus `failed` payments. It should reflect the same status classification rules that are used when generating `status` values.

When visualizing status distributions, the sum of `count` across all returned status buckets should correspond to the total number of payments considered by the analytics query, subject to any filters or exclusions applied.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentBySeller.description:
Per-seller payment analytics metrics for a given reporting window.

This schema aggregates high-level payment KPIs for a single seller over a specific analysis range, such as a day, week, or arbitrary analytics time window. It is typically produced by reporting and analytics queries that read from the logical order payment domain tables rather than from raw payment gateway transaction logs.

The metrics focus on logical order payments associated with a seller, allowing operators and BI tools to compare performance across sellers, identify outliers, and monitor trends in payment success and failure. Each instance of this schema represents one seller and can be combined into lists, ranking tables, or chart series in dashboards.

Values in this model are commonly derived from pre-aggregated snapshot or analytics tables for performance reasons. They are not meant to be used for low-level financial reconciliation but instead serve business-facing monitoring and trend-analysis use cases.

sellerId.description:
Unique identifier of the seller for whom metrics are aggregated.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the seller account in the seller domain tables (for example, the `shopping_mall_sellers` model). The same identifier is reused consistently across seller-facing and admin-facing analytics DTOs so that dashboards can cross-link seller analytics with seller profile and operational views.

totalProcessedAmount.description:
Total monetary amount successfully processed for this seller in the analysis window.

The value represents the sum of processed payment amounts for logical order payments attributed to this seller during the reporting period. It is expressed in the platform’s normalized analytics currency (typically the marketplace base currency) and is usually aggregated from underlying Decimal or numeric columns in the payment domain.

Implementations may apply rounding suitable for analytics and dashboard display, but the underlying precision should be sufficient for comparing seller performance, computing averages, and generating charts or KPI cards.

totalPayments.description:
Total number of logical payments associated with this seller in the analysis window.

This count includes all logical order payments attributed to the seller during the specified time range, regardless of their final status. It is generally greater than or equal to both `successfulPayments` and `failedPayments`.

Use this field when computing overall conversion rates, funnel metrics, or comparing payment volumes between sellers and across different time periods.

successfulPayments.description:
Number of logical payments that reached a successful terminal status for this seller in the analysis window.

A "successful" payment is one that has transitioned into a captured, settled, or otherwise revenue-bearing terminal state according to the payment lifecycle defined in the platform. These payments contribute to recognized revenue and are typically included in `totalProcessedAmount`.

This metric is often used in conjunction with `totalPayments` and `failedPayments` to calculate success ratios, monitor payment health, and identify sellers with unusually high or low payment conversion rates.

failedPayments.description:
Number of logical payments that ended in a failure terminal status for this seller in the analysis window.

Failed payments include hard declines, unrecoverable gateway errors, or business rule failures that prevent the payment from being completed. Payments that are retried and later succeed are usually counted as separate logical attempts according to the platform’s payment modeling.

This metric is used to monitor payment health for a seller, correlate issues with specific payment methods or geographic regions, and trigger risk or support workflows when failure rates exceed defined thresholds.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentTimeBucket.description:
Time-bucketed payment analytics metrics for a specific interval within an analysis window.

This schema represents a single bucket in a time series of payment analytics results, for example an hourly, daily, or weekly bucket. Each bucket captures aggregated metrics for all relevant payments that fall within the specified time range, using the same metric definitions as `IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentTotals`.

Buckets are typically generated by analytics queries using a fixed granularity, such as hour or day, and are aligned to UTC boundaries to ensure consistent charting and comparison. They are intended for use in dashboards and reporting views that visualize trends over time, such as line charts or bar charts of payment volume, processed amounts, and success rates.

bucketStart.description:
Inclusive UTC start timestamp of this bucket in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The bucket covers all payment events whose effective timestamp is greater than or equal to this value (`bucketStart`). Implementations usually align this value to the configured bucket granularity boundary (for example, the top of the hour or the start of the day) in UTC so that consecutive buckets form a continuous timeline without gaps or overlaps.

bucketEnd.description:
Exclusive UTC end timestamp of this bucket in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The bucket includes payment events in the half-open interval `[bucketStart, bucketEnd)`, meaning events with timestamps greater than or equal to `bucketStart` and strictly less than `bucketEnd`. This convention ensures that adjacent buckets do not double-count events and can be stitched together to cover an entire analysis period without overlap.

totals.description:
Aggregate payment metrics limited to this bucket's time interval.

The structure and semantics of this object match `IShoppingMallAnalyticsPaymentTotals`, but the values are computed only for payments whose timestamps fall within `[bucketStart, bucketEnd)`. This allows downstream consumers to render time-series graphs and perform per-bucket comparisons using a consistent set of metrics across the entire timeline.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsRefundTotals.description:
Top-level aggregate refund metrics over the selected time range and filters.

These metrics are computed from payment refund records, refund items, and related payment/order data and are intended to give a quick overview of refund scale and impact.

totalRefundCount.description: Total number of refund records observed in the analysis window after all filters have been applied.

totalRefundAmount.description: Total monetary amount refunded over the analysis window. The currency context is defined by platform configuration or surrounding documentation.

refundRateByOrders.description: Ratio of orders that resulted in at least one refund during the analysis window, typically expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

refundRateByPayments.description: Ratio of payments that resulted in at least one refund during the analysis window, typically expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

averageRefundAmount.description: Average refunded amount per refund record in the analysis window.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsRefundFilters.description:
Effective filter configuration used when generating a refund analytics summary.

This structure echoes the original request filters but may also include derived or defaulted values that were applied by the backend, making the analytical result self-describing.

oneOf.description: Grouping dimension actually used for the analytics, copied from the request or defaulted if omitted.
Grouping dimension actually used for the analytics, copied from the request or defaulted if omitted.
Grouping dimension actually used for the analytics, copied from the request or defaulted if omitted.
Grouping dimension actually used for the analytics, copied from the request or defaulted if omitted.

groupBy.description: Grouping dimension actually used for the analytics, copied from the request or defaulted if omitted.

minRefundAmount.description: Minimum refunded amount threshold that was applied. May be null if no threshold was used.

includeCaseTypes.description: Business-level refund or case types that were explicitly included in the analytics. Empty when no inclusion filter was applied.

excludeCaseTypes.description: Business-level refund or case types that were explicitly excluded from the analytics. Empty when no exclusion filter was applied.

sellerIds.description: Seller identifiers that were used to restrict analytics, if any. Empty when analytics covers all sellers.

reasonCodes.description: Structured refund reason codes that were used to restrict the analytics, if any.

includeDisputes.description: Flag indicating whether refunds associated with disputes were included in the analytics.

includeChargebacks.description: Flag indicating whether refunds related to chargeback cases were included in the analytics.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsRefundReasonBreakd.description:
Aggregated refund metrics grouped by a structured refund reason code.

Each instance represents a single analytics row for one configured refund reason such as `customerChangedMind`, `itemNotAsDescribed`, or another catalogued reason. The row combines both count and monetary metrics for all refund activity that matches the reason within a specific analysis window and optional filter set.

The data in this DTO is derived from refund and refund-request domain tables rather than raw transactional rows. It is intended for use in administrative dashboards, monitoring tools, and reporting services that need to understand how refund volume and financial impact are distributed across configured refund reasons.

reasonCode.description:
Structured refund reason code used as the primary grouping key in the analytics result.

The value must correspond exactly to a configured reason code from the refund request reason catalog so that dashboards and reports can reliably aggregate and compare metrics over time. Client applications should treat this code as a stable identifier and avoid making assumptions about its display format or localization.

Typical examples include values such as `customerChangedMind`, `itemNotAsDescribed`, or `shipmentDelayedBeyondExpectation`, depending on how the platform defines the refund reason taxonomy.

reasonLabel.description:
Human-readable label or description of the refund reason that is suitable for direct display in administrative dashboards, reports, and monitoring tools.

This label is often localized or drawn from the same catalog that defines `reasonCode`. It provides a friendly, descriptive string for analysts and operators while still mapping one-to-one to the underlying structured `reasonCode`.

Client applications can safely render this value in charts and tables, but should continue to use `reasonCode` for programmatic logic and cross-system correlation.

refundCount.description:
Number of refund records that fall under this reason code within the selected analysis window and filter configuration.

The value is a non-negative integer derived by counting refund or refund-request records whose configured reason matches `reasonCode`. It reflects the the volume of refund activity attributed to this reason and is commonly used for comparisons across different reasons.

Analytics dashboards typically visualize `refundCount` as bar charts, tables, or ranking lists to highlight which reasons are driving the most refund traffic.

refundAmount.description:
Total refunded amount summed over all refunds with this reason code in the analysis window.

The value represents a non-negative monetary aggregate in the platform’s primary reporting currency (for example, a single normalized currency such as USD, or the platform base currency). It is computed as the sum of the amounts actually refunded on each qualifying refund record.

This metric is typically used to understand financial impact by reason code, to identify costly refund drivers, and to prioritize operational or policy improvements.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsRefundSlaMetrics.description:
SLA-related metrics summarizing how refund and dispute cases perform against configured service-level targets.

This DTO captures time-based and breach statistics such as average and median resolution times, along with the number and rate of cases that violated SLA rules. All metrics are computed for a specific analysis window and filter context, typically defined by the calling analytics endpoint.

Values are derived from refund request status histories, case SLA configuration records, and SLA violation tables. The DTO is primarily consumed by operational, governance, and risk dashboards that need to monitor case-handling efficiency, detect SLA drift, and drive process improvements.

averageResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average time in hours between refund or dispute case creation and final resolution for the selected analysis window.

The measurement is typically computed from the timestamp of the initial case creation event to the timestamp of a terminal state such as "approved", "rejected", or "cancelled". Only completed cases are usually included in this metric so that the average is not distorted by still-open work.

A lower value generally indicates faster handling of cases. Sudden increases in this metric may signal capacity issues, process bottlenecks, or policy changes that slow down resolution.

medianResolutionTimeHours.description:
Median time in hours between refund or dispute case creation and final resolution for the selected analysis window.

The median is less sensitive to extreme outliers than the average, making it useful for understanding the typical customer experience even when a few cases take unusually long to resolve. Like the average, the measurement is taken from the case creation timestamp to the terminal resolution timestamp.

Comparing median and average resolution times helps operators quickly see whether outliers are skewing overall performance or whether the bulk of cases are consistently handled within expectations.

slaBreachCount.description:
Number of refund or dispute cases in the analysis window that breached their configured service-level agreement (SLA) targets.

A breach is usually recorded when a case remains unresolved beyond the time limits or conditions defined in the applicable SLA configuration for its type, priority, or channel. The count is always a non-negative integer and is derived from SLA violation records or evaluated from timestamps and SLA rules.

Tracking this number over time allows operations and governance teams to see whether process changes, staffing adjustments, or policy updates are improving or degrading SLA adherence.

slaBreachRate.description:
Proportion of refund or dispute cases in the analysis window that breached their SLA targets, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

In most implementations this value is calculated as `breachedCases / totalEligibleCases` for the selected time range and filter criteria. A value of `0` means no cases breached SLA, while a value near `1` indicates that almost all tracked cases fell outside their SLA constraints.

Client applications commonly present this fraction as a percentage (for example, `0.15` rendered as `15%`) to make the metric easier to interpret in reports and dashboards. Sustained high breach rates typically trigger deeper investigation and corrective actions.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsRefundDisputeCorre.description:
Metrics describing how refund activity correlates with disputes and chargebacks.

These values are intended to give risk and governance teams insight into how often refunds escalate into higher-severity dispute workflows or are related to chargeback activity.

refundsWithDisputesCount.description: Number of refunds that are associated with at least one dispute record in the analysis window.

refundsWithDisputesRate.description: Proportion of refunds that escalated into disputes, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

refundsRelatedToChargebacksCount.description: Number of refunds that are directly or indirectly associated with payment chargeback cases in the analysis window.

refundsRelatedToChargebacksRate.description: Proportion of refunds that are related to chargeback cases, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

IShoppingMallChargebackAnalyticsSummary.description:
Aggregated analytical summary of payment chargeback activity across the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a read‑only, computed view that is derived primarily from the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma model together with related payment and order entities. It is not backed by a dedicated table; instead, its values are calculated on demand through SQL aggregations over the underlying transactional records.

The schema focuses on key risk and finance indicators such as the total count of chargeback cases, monetary amounts in dispute, amounts actually charged back, and net financial impact after recoveries. It also carries the date range and filter context used when computing the analytics so that dashboards and reporting tools can clearly understand which slice of data the metrics represent.

In addition to overall platform metrics, the DTO supports optional segmented breakdowns (for example by payment method, issuer country, or seller) through the `segments` property. Each segment exposes the same family of metrics restricted to a specific grouping dimension. This enables administrative dashboards to render charts and tables that compare patterns across payment configurations, providers, or seller cohorts.

All fields are strictly read‑only and are intended for administrative actors only. No mutation of chargeback, payment, or order data is possible through this schema. When no data matches the requested filters, the backend should still populate this structure with zeroed metrics so that consuming clients never need to special‑case empty responses.

context.description:
Context describing the filters and time window that were applied when computing this summary.

The context structure captures the analysis period (for example the chargeback creation date range), the chargeback statuses included, and any segmentation or grouping dimensions requested by the caller. This ensures that consumers of the analytics can reliably interpret the numeric metrics and understand which subset of historical chargeback data they correspond to.

totalChargebackCount.description:
Total number of chargeback records that matched the specified filters.

This count represents the volume of distinct chargeback cases opened by issuers, payment providers, or banks within the requested analysis window and filter conditions. It is a pure count of cases and does not attempt to deduplicate by order or payment; each logical chargeback record in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` contributes at most one unit to this total.

totalDisputedAmount.description:
Total disputed amount aggregated across all matching chargeback records.

This value is the sum of the `disputed_amount` column of `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` for all records that satisfy the request filters. It is typically expressed in the main reporting currency for the analytics run and may involve currency normalization if chargebacks exist in multiple currencies.

totalChargebackAmount.description:
Total amount that has actually been charged back (withdrawn) from the platform for the matched cases.

This metric aggregates the `chargeback_amount` column from `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` over the filtered set of rows. It reflects the realized financial loss or exposure from chargebacks, after the provider or scheme has executed the chargeback against the platform.

netLossAmount.description:
Net loss amount for the platform after considering chargeback reversals, recoveries, and any other adjustments over the analyzed chargeback set.

While `totalChargebackAmount` represents the raw sum of charged‑back amounts, this metric aims to capture the net impact after internal recoveries, settlements, or write‑offs. Depending on implementation, it may be derived by subtracting recovered amounts or offsets from the total chargeback amount.

chargebackRate.description:
Chargeback rate over the analyzed population of processed payments.

This metric expresses what fraction of eligible payments resulted in chargebacks for the given filters and time range. It is typically computed as a ratio such as `chargeback_count / total_payments_count` or using a monetary basis such as `disputed_amount / processed_volume`. The exact definition is implementation specific but should remain consistent across analytics consumers.

segments.description:
Optional list of segmented sub‑summaries that break down chargeback activity by a grouping dimension.

Each segment represents the same metrics—counts, amounts, and rates—restricted to a specific value of a chosen dimension (for example a payment method, issuer country, provider, or seller). When the caller did not request segmentation, this array may be empty and clients should rely on the top‑level totals only.

IShoppingMallChargebackAnalyticsSummary..description:
Request payload describing filters and configuration for generating a chargeback analytics summary.

This DTO is accepted by the administrative analytics endpoint that aggregates data from `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and related payment entities. It allows risk and finance operators to specify the time window, status filters, and optional grouping configuration used to compute an aggregate view of chargeback activity.

The request is purely read‑only in effect: it does not create or modify any chargeback records or payments. Instead, it instructs the backend analytics service how to filter and group existing data for reporting purposes. The backend should validate ranges and filter combinations to avoid excessively heavy queries and respond with an appropriate summary even when no matching data exists.

fromDate.description:
Inclusive start of the analysis window in UTC ISO 8601 format.

Only chargeback records whose relevant timestamp (typically the creation or opening time) is greater than or equal to this value will be considered in the analytics. If omitted by the client, the backend may apply a system‑defined default look‑back period.

toDate.description:
Exclusive end of the analysis window in UTC ISO 8601 format.

Chargeback records with timestamps greater than or equal to this value are excluded from the aggregation. When not provided, the backend may default to the current time or an implementation‑specific maximum horizon.

statusFilters.description:
Optional list of chargeback business statuses to include in the aggregation.

Each element describes a value of the `status` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` (for example `"open"`, `"won"`, `"lost"`, or `"writing_off"`). When the array is empty or omitted, the analytics will typically include all statuses unless restricted by system configuration.

groupBy.description:
Optional grouping dimension controlling how segmented analytics should be generated.

Common values include `"payment_method"`, `"issuer_country"`, or `"seller"`. When omitted or set to an empty string, the backend should compute only the global summary and return an empty `segments` array in the response.

paymentMethodCodes.description:
Optional list of payment method identifiers to restrict the analytics to.

When provided, only chargeback records whose associated payments use one of the specified methods will be considered. The exact coding of payment methods is implementation specific but should remain stable within the platform.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers to scope the analytics window to.

When present, the summary and segments will only consider chargeback cases arising from payments or orders associated with the specified sellers. This is typically used on administrative dashboards to focus on a subset of sellers or to investigate specific risk patterns.

cursor.description:
Optional cursor token used for paginated or incremental analytics retrieval.

While most chargeback analytics are computed in a single aggregation pass, certain implementations may support incremental fetching or continuation tokens for complex queries. When present, this value instructs the backend to resume an earlier analytical query from the specified position.

IShoppingMallChargebackAnalyticsContext.description:
Filter and time‑window context used to compute a chargeback analytics summary.

This type does not correspond to a physical Prisma model; it is a pure DTO that captures how the backend constrained and aggregated the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and related payment records. Its values are derived directly from the request that initiated the analytics query and allow consumers to understand which slice of historical data the summary metrics represent.

The context tracks the analysis period, optional chargeback status filters, and optional grouping dimensions such as payment method or seller. It may also include coarse information about which payment methods or providers were included in the dataset so that dashboards can display labels and filter chips that match the numbers shown in the summary.

This structure is purely descriptive and read‑only. It should be treated as metadata that travels together with the numeric metrics in `IShoppingMallChargebackAnalyticsSummary` and its segments so that analytics consumers never lose track of the constraints under which numbers were calculated.

fromDate.description:
Inclusive start of the analysis window in UTC ISO 8601 format.

The backend populates this field with the effective lower bound on the chargeback creation or reference timestamp used when aggregating data. It typically matches the `fromDate` requested by the client, possibly adjusted to internal boundary rules (for example truncating to midnight or applying a maximum look‑back window).

toDate.description:
Exclusive end of the analysis window in UTC ISO 8601 format.

This value represents the upper bound of the time range used when selecting chargeback records for aggregation. It usually corresponds to the `toDate` requested by the client, normalized as necessary for query implementation. The interval `[fromDate, toDate)` defines the exact time slice over which metrics were computed.

statusFilters.description:
List of chargeback business statuses that were included in the aggregation.

Each element corresponds to a value of the `status` column from `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` (for example `"open"`, `"won"`, `"lost"`, or `"writing_off"`). When empty, the analytics should be interpreted as covering all statuses unless restricted by other system defaults.

groupBy.description:
Grouping dimension that the backend used when populating segmented analytics.

Typical examples include `"payment_method"`, `"issuer_country"`, or `"seller"`. When this value is null, the summary has been computed without segmentation and the `segments` array in `IShoppingMallChargebackAnalyticsSummary` will normally be empty.

currencyCode.description:
Reporting currency code used for aggregated monetary amounts.

When the underlying chargeback records span multiple currencies, the backend normalizes amounts into a single reporting currency for analytics. This field holds the ISO 4217 currency code that applies to the numeric monetary metrics in the parent summary and segments.

IShoppingMallChargebackAnalyticsSegment.description:
Segmented analytics metrics for a single chargeback grouping bucket.

This DTO mirrors the structure of `IShoppingMallChargebackAnalyticsSummary` but is scoped to one concrete value of a chosen dimension such as a specific payment method, issuer country, or seller. It allows dashboards to present per‑segment comparisons while preserving a consistent metric vocabulary.

Segments are computed from the same underlying `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` records and related payments as the top‑level summary, but each segment is restricted to records belonging to its own grouping key. The `key` and optional `label` fields identify the bucket, while count, amount, and rate metrics show the localized impact for that bucket.

All fields are read‑only, analytical values. The DTO does not represent a persisted entity and cannot be used to mutate any underlying chargeback or payment records.

key.description:
Machine‑readable identifier of the grouping bucket represented by this segment.

For example, when grouping by payment method, `key` might hold an internal payment method code; when grouping by seller, it might hold a seller ID or seller code. Clients should treat this value as opaque and rely on `label` for human‑friendly presentation.

label.description:
Human‑readable label describing this segment bucket.

The label is intended for display in dashboards, tables, and charts. It may represent a localized payment method name, issuer country name, or seller display name depending on the grouping dimension used when generating the analytics.

chargebackCount.description:
Number of chargeback cases that fall into this specific segment bucket.

This count is calculated using the same filtering and time‑window constraints as the parent summary but restricted to chargeback records whose grouping attribute matches this segment's `key`.

disputedAmount.description:
Total disputed amount for chargebacks in this segment, expressed in the summary's reporting currency.

It aggregates the `disputed_amount` values from `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` for records that match both the global filters and this segment's grouping value.

chargebackAmount.description:
Total amount that has actually been charged back (withdrawn) from the platform for this segment.

This is the sum of `chargeback_amount` for chargeback records contained in this bucket. It reflects realized financial exposure associated with the specific grouping value, such as a particular payment method or seller.

netLossAmount.description:
Net loss amount for the platform for this segment after considering recoveries and adjustments.

The metric is computed using the same algorithm as the top‑level `netLossAmount` but restricted to the subset of records matching this segment. It helps identify segments that disproportionately contribute to platform losses.

chargebackRate.description:
Chargeback rate for this segment relative to the underlying processed payments in the same bucket.
