The rate is typically computed as a ratio of chargeback volume or value to total payments volume or count for the same grouping key. It allows direct comparison of risk levels across different payment methods, geographies, or seller cohorts.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsSummary.description:
Aggregated analytical summary of seller earnings across the shoppingMall marketplace.

This DTO represents the result of read-only analytical queries over the shopping_mall_seller_earnings table and related payout/order entities. It is designed for admin-facing dashboards and reports that need metrics such as gross and net earnings, counts of earnings records, and optional breakdowns by dimensions like seller, time bucket, or payout status. It is not mapped to a single Prisma model row and is computed dynamically at request time.

totalGrossEarnings.description:
Total gross earnings amount aggregated across all matching seller earnings records within the requested filter scope.

This value usually represents the sum of pre-fee seller earnings as stored in shopping_mall_seller_earnings and is expressed in the platform's base currency or the reporting currency chosen by the caller.

totalNetEarnings.description:
Total net earnings amount aggregated across all matching seller earnings records within the requested filter scope.

Net earnings typically represent earnings after platform fees, commissions, and other deductions. The precise business computation is implemented in service logic, but this field always returns the final net value used for reporting.

earningsRecordCount.description:
Total number of individual seller earnings records that matched the filters used to build this summary.

This count reflects how many rows from shopping_mall_seller_earnings contributed to the aggregation and is useful for sanity checking and pagination-like analytics.

orderCount.description:
Number of distinct orders that contributed to the seller earnings included in this summary.

This metric is derived from the order references linked from shopping_mall_seller_earnings rows and helps admins understand how widely distributed the earnings are across orders.

averageEarningsPerOrder.description:
Average earnings amount per order within the filtered data set.

This is typically computed as totalNetEarnings divided by orderCount (or totalGrossEarnings divided by orderCount depending on business rules). When orderCount is zero, this field should be zero as well to avoid division-by-zero issues for consumers.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code in which the numeric amounts of this summary (for example, totalGrossEarnings and totalNetEarnings) are expressed.

When the underlying data spans multiple currencies, the service may normalize to a reporting currency based on business rules; this field indicates which currency the aggregated amounts refer to.

bySeller.description:
Optional breakdown of seller earnings by seller.

Each entry represents aggregated metrics for an individual seller within the filter scope, enabling dashboards that rank or compare sellers by their earnings.

byTimeBucket.description:
Optional time-bucketed breakdown of aggregated seller earnings.

Each entry represents metrics for a specific time bucket such as a day, week, or month, depending on the grouping options passed in the corresponding request DTO. This is useful for charting trends over time.

bySubscriptionPlan.description:
Optional breakdown of aggregated seller earnings by seller subscription plan.

Each entry represents aggregated metrics for one subscription plan, enabling admins to understand how different plans contribute to overall earnings.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsSummary.IRequ.description:
Request payload for computing an aggregated analytical summary of seller earnings.

This DTO is consumed by the administrative analytics endpoint that aggregates data from `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` and related entities such as orders, payments, and payout batches. It allows financial and operational stakeholders to specify the time frame, seller scope, earning status filters, and grouping configuration required to build dashboards and reports about seller performance and payout obligations.

The request is strictly read‑only with respect to the underlying data: it does not create, modify, or delete any earning, order, or payout records. Instead, it drives how the analytics query selects and groups existing `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` rows. The backend implementation should validate that range and filter combinations are reasonable and may impose limits to protect system performance.

fromDate.description:
Inclusive start of the settlement or earning analysis window in UTC ISO 8601 format.

Only `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` records whose relevant timestamp (for example `created_at` or an earning effective date) is greater than or equal to this value will be considered when computing the summary.

toDate.description:
Exclusive end of the settlement or earning analysis window in UTC ISO 8601 format.

Earning records with timestamps greater than or equal to this value are excluded from the aggregation. Together with `fromDate`, this defines the precise time slice used for analytics.

businessStatuses.description:
Optional list of earning business statuses to include in the aggregation.

Each element corresponds to a value of the `business_status` column in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` (for example `"pending"`, `"eligible"`, `"paid_out"`, or `"reversed"`). When omitted or empty, the backend may include all statuses except those treated as logically deleted by business rules.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers to restrict the analytics scope.

When provided, only earnings rows whose `shopping_mall_seller_id` matches one of the specified IDs will contribute to the computed metrics. This is useful for analyzing a subset of sellers or investigating particular accounts.

groupBy.description:
Optional grouping dimension used to generate segmented seller earnings summaries.

Typical values include `"seller"`, `"payout_batch"`, `"subscription_plan"`, or a time‑based bucket such as `"day"` or `"month"`. When omitted or an empty string, the backend should compute only the overall summary and return no segments.

currencyCode.description:
Preferred reporting currency code for the aggregated monetary amounts.

If earning records span multiple currencies, the backend normalizes values into the specified ISO 4217 code for consistency in analytics. When omitted, the system's default reporting currency is used.

minNetEarningAmount.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `net_earning_amount` for earnings included in the aggregation.

When provided, only records with a net earning amount greater than or equal to this value will be considered. This can be used to exclude small noise records from analytics views.

maxNetEarningAmount.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `net_earning_amount` for earnings included in the aggregation.

When set, any earnings record whose net amount exceeds this value will be excluded. This can be useful for focusing on typical transactions while ignoring outliers in certain analytical scenarios.

cursor.description:
Optional cursor token used when the backend supports incremental or paginated seller earnings analytics.

In many cases, seller earnings summaries are computed in a single aggregation. However, when the result set or computation is large, implementations may expose continuation tokens. Supplying a cursor instructs the backend to resume a previous analytical query from the indicated position instead of starting a new one.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsSummary.IBySe.description:
Per-seller segment of aggregated seller earnings metrics.

This DTO is used inside IShoppingMallSellerEarningsSummary to provide a breakdown of earnings at the seller level, allowing administrative dashboards to compare performance across sellers.

sellerId.description:
Unique identifier of the seller for whom these earnings metrics have been aggregated.

This corresponds to the primary key of the seller entity associated with shopping_mall_seller_earnings records.

sellerName.description:
Display name of the seller associated with this segment.

This is provided for convenience so that clients do not need an additional lookup to display seller labels in dashboards.

totalGrossEarnings.description: Gross earnings amount aggregated for this specific seller within the filtered scope.

totalNetEarnings.description: Net earnings amount aggregated for this specific seller within the filtered scope, typically after fees and commissions.

earningsRecordCount.description: Number of seller earnings records that contributed to this seller-level aggregation.

orderCount.description: Number of distinct orders that contributed to the earnings for this seller within the filter scope.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsSummary.IByTi.description:
Time-bucketed segment of aggregated seller earnings metrics.

Each instance represents aggregated earnings for a specific time window (for example, a day, week, or month), depending on the grouping configuration specified in the request DTO.

bucketLabel.description:
Human-readable label for the time bucket.

Examples include an ISO date such as "2025-01-31" for daily buckets or a year-month string such as "2025-01" for monthly buckets. The exact format is determined by the implementation but should be stable for client-side charting.

bucketStart.description:
Inclusive start timestamp of the time bucket in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Used to unambiguously identify the time window represented by this aggregation segment.

bucketEnd.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the time bucket in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Together with bucketStart, defines the time range of this segment.

totalGrossEarnings.description: Gross earnings amount aggregated across all sellers within this time bucket.

totalNetEarnings.description: Net earnings amount aggregated across all sellers within this time bucket.

earningsRecordCount.description: Number of seller earnings records that fall into this time bucket.

orderCount.description: Number of distinct orders contributing to earnings in this time bucket.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsSummary.IBySu.description:
Per-subscription-plan segment of aggregated seller earnings metrics.

This DTO is used inside IShoppingMallSellerEarningsSummary to show how total earnings distribute across seller subscription plans.

subscriptionPlanId.description:
Unique identifier of the subscription plan associated with this segment.

This identifier refers to a record in the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans table or equivalent subscription catalog.

subscriptionPlanName.description:
Human-readable name of the subscription plan for which earnings have been aggregated.

Provided so that analytics clients can render labels without additional lookups.

totalGrossEarnings.description: Gross earnings aggregated for sellers on this subscription plan within the filter scope.

totalNetEarnings.description: Net earnings aggregated for sellers on this subscription plan within the filter scope.

sellerCount.description: Number of distinct sellers on this subscription plan that contributed to the earnings in this segment.

IShoppingMallPayoutAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Filter and aggregation configuration for computing the seller payout analytics summary in the admin analytics endpoint.

This DTO is used as the PATCH request body for `/shoppingMall/admin/analytics/payouts/summary`. It allows administrative callers to specify time ranges, seller scopes, payout statuses, currencies, and grouping dimensions that control how payout-related metrics are aggregated. The analytics engine reads these parameters to construct read-only queries primarily over `shopping_mall_seller_earnings`, `shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches`, and `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`.

Only the `groupBy` field is required. All other fields (`from`, `to`, `sellerIds`, `payoutStatuses`, `currency`, and `includeUnsettledEarnings`) are optional filters or configuration flags. When optional fields are omitted, the backend applies platform-specific defaults, such as using a recent default date range or including all sellers, statuses, and settlement states.

This request model does not map 1:1 to a single Prisma model row. Instead, it defines the analytical projection window and segmentation for summary results that are returned as `IShoppingMallPayoutAnalytics.ISummary` and related breakdown DTOs.

from.description:
Optional inclusive start of the analytics time range, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When provided together with `to`, the analytics engine restricts payout and earning records to those that fall on or after this timestamp. When omitted, the implementation may default to a business-defined recent window (for example, the last 30 days) or the earliest relevant data, depending on platform policy.

The value must represent a valid timestamp in the platform’s reporting time zone, and, when `to` is also provided, `from` must be earlier than `to` to form a non-negative duration.

to.description:
Optional exclusive end of the analytics time range, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When provided together with `from`, the analytics engine restricts payout and earning records to those that fall before this timestamp. When omitted, the implementation may treat the effective end of the range as the current time or another platform-defined cut-off.

The value must represent a valid timestamp in the platform’s reporting time zone. If both `from` and `to` are supplied, `to` must be strictly later than `from`.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers whose payouts should be included in this analytics query.

Each element should correspond to a valid `shopping_mall_sellers.id` value. When this array is provided and non-empty, the analytics engine restricts computations to earnings and payouts associated with these sellers only.

When the field is omitted or the array is empty, the analytics scope is broadened to include all sellers on the platform, subject to other filters such as time range and payout status.

payoutStatuses.description:
Optional list of payout lifecycle statuses to include in the analytics computation.

Typical values come from the platform’s payout lifecycle vocabulary (for example, `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, or similar domain-specific labels). The exact allowed values are defined by the payout domain model and must be used consistently by clients.

When this field is provided, only payout batches and items whose status is contained in this list are used when computing totals. When omitted, payouts in all statuses are considered unless the implementation applies additional defaults.

groupBy.description:
Required list of dimensions by which to group the payout analytics summary.

Each element indicates a grouping axis such as seller, time bucket, currency, or subscription plan. The analytics engine uses these values to decide which breakdown arrays and aggregation keys to produce in `IShoppingMallPayoutAnalytics.ISummary`.

Supported values are defined in `IEShoppingMallPayoutAnalyticsGroupBy`. Clients can specify multiple dimensions in one request to obtain composite breakdowns as supported by the implementation.

currency.description:
Optional ISO 4217 currency code indicating the reporting currency for aggregated monetary amounts.

When provided, the analytics subsystem may convert underlying payout and earning amounts into this reporting currency, using platform-defined foreign exchange rules if the underlying data is multi-currency. When omitted, the implementation may either aggregate amounts in their native settlement currencies and expose them via currency groupings, or apply a platform-default reporting currency.

Clients should use standardized three-letter currency codes such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW` to ensure predictable behavior.

includeUnsettledEarnings.description:
Flag indicating whether earnings that have not yet been fully settled into payout batches should be included in the analytics computation.

When `true`, the analytics may combine both amounts already assigned to payout batches and amounts that are still in an unsettled state in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings`, allowing administrators to compare potential future payouts with completed ones.

When `false`, only amounts that are already associated with completed or otherwise eligible payout batches are counted, focusing the analytics strictly on settled payouts.

oneOf.description:
Group payout analytics by seller.

When this value is used, the analytics engine produces per-seller aggregates, such as total gross amount, commissions, net earnings, and paid or pending payout amounts for each seller. This dimension is typically used for ranking, comparing, and monitoring the performance of individual sellers on the platform.

Group payout analytics by time bucket.

When this value is used, the analytics engine aggregates metrics into discrete time buckets (for example, by day, week, or month) derived from the effective time range and any analytics granularity configuration. This dimension is useful for trend analysis and time-series charts that show how payouts evolve over time.

Group payout analytics by settlement or reporting currency.

When this value is used, the analytics engine aggregates metrics per currency code so that administrators can see how payouts are distributed across currencies. This dimension is especially useful in multi-currency marketplaces where settlement currencies differ by seller or region.

Group payout analytics by seller subscription plan.

When this value is used, the analytics engine aggregates payout metrics per subscription plan defined in seller subscription configuration tables. This dimension helps administrators understand payout behavior and earnings distribution across different seller subscription tiers or service offerings.

IEShoppingMallPayoutAnalyticsGroupBy.description:
Enumeration of supported grouping dimensions for payout analytics.

Each value describes a distinct axis along which payout-related metrics can be aggregated in the admin analytics endpoint. Clients combine one or more of these values in `IShoppingMallPayoutAnalytics.IRequest.groupBy` to define how the resulting `IShoppingMallPayoutAnalytics.ISummary` should be segmented.

The choice of grouping dimensions directly influences which breakdown arrays and keys appear in the analytics response and enables dashboards to present per-seller tables, time-series graphs, currency splits, or subscription-plan-based comparisons.

IShoppingMallPayoutAnalytics.ISummary.description:
Aggregated analytics summary of seller payouts across the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents an analytics-friendly view summarizing seller earnings and payout status derived primarily from `shopping_mall_seller_earnings`, `shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches`, and `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`. Instead of exposing raw transactional rows, it surfaces pre-aggregated metrics that can be consumed directly by reporting dashboards, admin consoles, and financial monitoring tools.

The summary focuses on a specific analysis window defined by the request, and it may be further constrained by seller scopes, payout status filters, or grouping preferences such as seller, currency, or time buckets. It provides both top-level aggregates (for example, total gross earnings across all included sellers) and optional arrays of per-seller and per-period breakdowns when the caller requests grouped analytics.

Although this type is conceptually backed by multiple Prisma models, it does not map 1:1 to a single table row. Instead, it is a computed read model that combines and aggregates rows from earnings and payout-related tables. Service implementations should therefore treat it as a pure analytics projection, keeping the numerical relationships between fields consistent with the underlying accounting logic and avoiding partial or inconsistent population of related metrics.

totalGrossAmount.description:
Total gross merchandise amount included in the analytics result.

This corresponds to the sum of `gross_amount` values from `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` that match the requested filters such as time range, seller scope, and payout status. It represents the full value of underlying transactions before any commissions, fees, or discounts are applied.

Downstream consumers typically use this field as the starting point for revenue and GMV (gross merchandise value) analysis, trend charts, and comparison against net earnings and paid-out amounts.

totalCommissionAmount.description:
Total commission amount charged by the platform in the analytics result.

This value is derived from the sum of `commission_amount` fields in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` for all earnings that satisfy the effective filters. It reflects platform revenue collected as commissions over the analysis window.

Finance, accounting, and business operations teams use this metric to understand monetization effectiveness, to compare against gross amounts and discounts, and to reconcile with general ledger data.

totalSellerDiscountAmount.description:
Total amount of discounts funded by sellers within the analytics scope.

The value is computed by summing `seller_discount_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` for all matched earnings records, after applying any requested filters. It captures the aggregate volume of price reductions that sellers themselves have subsidized.

This metric is often used to analyze seller promotional behavior, measure the cost of seller-driven discounting programs, and compare seller-subsidized promotions against platform-funded incentives.

totalPlatformDiscountAmount.description:
Total amount of discounts funded by the platform within the analytics scope.

It corresponds to the aggregated `platform_discount_amount` values in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` for the selected filters. This represents the net promotional cost borne by the platform itself, such as coupon campaigns or sponsored discounts.

Analysts and finance teams use this metric to evaluate marketing spend effectiveness, track the cost of platform incentives over time, and reconcile discount-related expenses against campaign budgets and performance metrics.

totalNetEarningAmount.description:
Total net earning amount owed to sellers in the analytics result.

This is the aggregated `net_earning_amount` from `shopping_mall_seller_earnings`, representing earnings after commissions and seller-funded discounts have been applied but before payout batch status is taken into account. In other words, it is what sellers should receive from the platform for the included transactions, regardless of whether the funds have already been paid out.

This metric is commonly used as the baseline for payout planning, settlement forecasting, and comparison with both paid and pending payout amounts.

totalPaidOutAmount.description:
Total amount that has already been paid out to sellers in the analytics scope.

This value is computed from `payout_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` for payout items that match the filters and whose status indicates that they have been successfully executed (for example, completed payouts). It reflects cash or clearing amounts that have left the platform toward sellers during the analysis window.

Reconciliation processes, settlement reporting, and treasury operations reference this field when validating that paid amounts match expectations derived from the earnings data and configured payout policies.

totalPendingPayoutAmount.description:
Total amount that is still pending payout to sellers in the analytics scope.

This amount is derived by comparing eligible `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` against their associated payout items and payout batch statuses. It typically represents net earnings that have not yet been associated with a completed payout batch, including amounts in intermediate or scheduled states.

Operations and finance teams use this metric to monitor outstanding liabilities to sellers, prioritize payout batch creation or execution, and detect unusual accumulation of unsettled earnings for specific cohorts or time periods.

currencyCode.description:
Primary ISO 4217 currency code for aggregated monetary values in this summary.

In single-currency deployments, all monetary amounts exposed by this DTO are assumed to be in this currency (for example, "USD", "EUR", or "KRW"). In multi-currency environments, the analytics layer may either normalize values into a designated reporting currency or, when normalization is not applied, leave this field empty or use a sentinel value and rely on breakdowns for per-currency views.

Client applications should treat this field as the canonical currency for interpreting top-level aggregates and should fall back to more detailed breakdowns or additional context when multi-currency reporting is enabled.

timeRange.description:
Time range over which the analytics summary was computed.

This structure reflects the effective time window actually used by the analytics engine, which may be derived from the request DTO, truncated to respect data retention boundaries, or normalized to bucket-aligned start and end times. It ensures that consumers can unambiguously understand the temporal scope of all aggregated metrics.

When rendering charts or reports, clients should display this range alongside the numeric metrics so that operators and analysts can clearly see the period that the summary covers.

sellerBreakdowns.description:
Optional array of per-seller payout analytics breakdown entries.

Each element summarizes payout-related metrics for a single seller, including gross amounts, commissions, discounts, net earnings, and paid versus pending payout amounts. These rows are typically generated when the caller includes a grouping dimension such as `seller` in the request.

Admin dashboards and finance tools use this collection to power per-seller tables, leaderboards, and drill-down views, enabling operators to identify top performers, outliers, or sellers with unusually high pending balances.

periodBreakdowns.description:
Optional array of time-bucketed payout analytics breakdown entries.

Each entry represents analytics computed for a specific time bucket, such as a day, week, or month, depending on the grouping configuration used in the request. The buckets together span the overall `timeRange`, and their individual `from` and `to` values describe precise per-period boundaries.

This array is typically used for charting trends and visualizing the evolution of earnings, commissions, and payout activity over time. Clients can plot gross versus net earnings, paid versus pending payouts, and other key metrics as time-series graphs sourced directly from this data.

IShoppingMallPayoutAnalyticsSellerBreakd.description:
Per-seller payout analytics breakdown entry.

Each instance summarizes key payout-related metrics for a single seller, such as total earnings, commissions, discounts, net payouts, and pending amounts within the requested analytics scope. It effectively represents a seller-level slice of the aggregated payout data and is typically used when the caller requests grouping by seller or when dashboards present rankings and drill-down views.

This type is designed for use in tables and charts that group analytics by seller, supporting operational monitoring of payout status, reconciliation workflows, and finance-driven analyses such as profitability, discount behavior, or payout delays per seller. It does not correspond to a single Prisma row but instead aggregates data from earnings and payout-related tables for that seller.

sellerId.description:
Unique identifier of the seller whose payouts are summarized in this breakdown.

This ID corresponds to `shopping_mall_sellers.id` and is the primary key used to join analytics metrics back to core seller records. It enables client applications to navigate from analytics tables to seller management views, risk dashboards, or configuration screens.

Because this value is a UUID, it should be treated as opaque by clients and passed through exactly when invoking follow-up APIs that expect a seller identifier.

sellerDisplayName.description:
Human-readable display name of the seller.

This value is typically derived from `shopping_mall_seller_profiles` or a similar profile table and is intended solely for UI presentation in dashboards and reports. It helps administrators and operators visually identify the seller associated with this breakdown row without needing to interpret raw identifiers.

The field may be absent or empty for partially configured sellers or in data export scenarios where only identifiers are required, so consumers should not treat it as a strict key for joins or lookups.

currencyCode.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for this seller-specific breakdown.

All monetary amounts in this breakdown entry are expressed in this currency, which normally matches the seller's settlement currency or a reporting currency used for normalized analytics. Examples include "USD", "EUR", or "KRW".

In multi-currency environments, different breakdown entries may use different `currencyCode` values when per-seller analytics is computed in each seller’s natural currency, and clients should clearly label or separate such rows when rendering combined views.

grossAmount.description:
Total gross merchandise amount associated with this seller in the analytics scope.

It is computed from `gross_amount` values in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` filtered by the seller and the effective time range. This number reflects the full value of the seller's underlying transactions before commissions and discounts are taken into account.

Dashboards commonly use this field to compare seller sales volume, identify top-performing sellers, and track changes in gross sales over time.

commissionAmount.description:
Total commission amount charged to this seller in the analytics scope.

This value is derived from `commission_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` and represents platform fees collected from this seller during the analysis window. It reflects the monetization impact of this seller’s activity on the platform.

Finance and operations teams use this field to understand the revenue contribution of each seller, to reconcile commission income, and to detect anomalies such as unexpectedly high or low commission rates.

sellerDiscountAmount.description:
Total amount of seller-funded discounts applied in this analytics scope for this seller.

It is aggregated from `seller_discount_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` records belonging to the seller. The metric quantifies how much cost the seller has absorbed in the form of promotions or price reductions they fund directly.

This metric can be combined with sales and net earnings data to evaluate the effectiveness and intensity of the seller's own discounting strategy and to identify sellers that heavily rely on promotions.

platformDiscountAmount.description:
Total amount of platform-funded discounts associated with this seller in this analytics scope.

The value comes from `platform_discount_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` records for the seller and indicates the size of incentives funded by the platform but applied on this seller's catalog. It represents the promotional cost the platform incurs in connection with this seller.

This metric is useful for marketing, finance, and account management teams when assessing the return on investment (ROI) of platform-funded campaigns targeting specific sellers or seller segments.

netEarningAmount.description:
Net earning amount owed to the seller in this analytics scope.

This is the aggregated `net_earning_amount` from `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` records belonging to the seller, after commissions and seller-funded discounts have been considered but before payout execution is taken into account. It effectively represents the amount the platform intends to settle with the seller for the included transactions.

Clients use this value to compare with `paidOutAmount` and `pendingPayoutAmount`, to calculate payout realization ratios, and to identify sellers whose net earnings are growing or declining over time.

paidOutAmount.description:
Total amount already paid to this seller within the analytics scope.

This amount is derived from `payout_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` associated with this seller, restricted to payout items whose status indicates a completed or otherwise finalized payout. It reflects the portion of the seller’s earnings that has been settled through actual payouts during the analysis window.

Reconciliation processes, settlement dashboards, and financial reports rely on this value to verify that executed payouts match expectations derived from earnings and payout configuration rules.

pendingPayoutAmount.description:
Total amount still pending payout to this seller within the analytics scope.

The backend computes this by comparing eligible earnings against associated payout items and payout batch statuses for the seller, identifying net earnings that have not yet been fully settled. It may include amounts scheduled for upcoming payout batches, amounts in intermediate states, or amounts not yet assigned to any batch.

Operations and finance teams use this metric to monitor outstanding obligations per seller, prioritize payout processing, and detect potential issues such as unusually large or aging pending balances for specific sellers.

IShoppingMallPayoutAnalyticsPeriodBreakd.description:
Time-bucketed payout analytics breakdown entry.

Each entry represents aggregated payout-related metrics for a specific reporting period such as a day, week, or month. It is typically used for charting trends and analyzing payout performance over time.

The period key is a human-readable or ISO-based label that the frontend can use when plotting the breakdown in chronological order.

periodKey.description:
Identifier for the reporting period represented by this breakdown entry.

Common examples include formatted dates like "2025-03-15" for daily buckets, "2025-W11" for weekly buckets, or "2025-03" for monthly buckets, depending on the aggregation strategy chosen in the request.

from.description:
Start timestamp of the reporting period that this breakdown covers.

This value is useful for precise alignment with the analytics time line and may differ from the overall query start when used in multiple buckets.

to.description:
End timestamp of the reporting period that this breakdown covers.

The backend uses this value together with `from` to define the exact record selection window for this bucket, which can be used by charting components for tooltips and labels.

grossAmount.description:
Total gross merchandise amount included in this period bucket.

This is derived by aggregating `gross_amount` from `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` for records whose timestamps fall within the period range.

commissionAmount.description:
Total commission amount charged in this period bucket.

It is computed from `commission_amount` values in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` that belong to this period and helps visualize platform revenue over time.

netEarningAmount.description:
Total net earning amount owed to sellers in this period bucket.

The value is derived from `net_earning_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_earnings` and supports trend analysis of seller earnings.

paidOutAmount.description:
Total amount paid out to sellers in this period bucket.

This value is aggregated from `payout_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` for payout items whose paid timestamps fall into the period range.

pendingPayoutAmount.description:
Total amount still pending payout in this period bucket.

The backend computes this by comparing eligible earnings and their associated payout items to determine the outstanding balance within this time slice.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IReques.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for listing cancellation requests in administrative tools.

This type is used by the `/shoppingMall/admin/cancellationRequests` PATCH operation to express complex search criteria, pagination options, and sorting preferences for rows in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` Prisma table. It is a request-only DTO and does not represent a persistent entity; instead, it encapsulates query parameters that are translated by the backend into SQL conditions and ordering.

Only filter and control properties are included. System-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, or actor foreign keys are not accepted as entity data through this DTO. When an optional filter or sort property is omitted, no constraint is applied for that dimension, allowing callers to mix and match filters based on their operational or analytical needs.

page.description:
Page index for pagination when listing cancellation requests.

This is a 1-based page index where `1` represents the first page of results. The backend uses this value together with `limit` to compute the offset into the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` result set. Values less than 1 may be rejected or normalized according to server-side pagination rules.

limit.description:
Maximum number of cancellation request summaries to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for the `/shoppingMall/admin/cancellationRequests` query. The backend typically enforces a reasonable upper bound to prevent excessively large responses, and clients should select values that balance user experience needs with performance considerations.

status.description:
Optional filter on the current lifecycle status of cancellation requests.

The value is compared against the `status` column of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` table. Typical business codes include values such as `"pending"`, `"approved"`, `"rejected"`, or `"expired"`, but the exact set is governed by business policy. If omitted, cancellation requests are not filtered by status.

requestedByActorType.description:
Optional filter on the actor type that initiated the cancellation request.

This corresponds to the `requested_by_actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` Prisma model. Common logical values include `"customer"`, `"seller"`, and `"admin"`. When omitted, requests from all actor types are included in the result set.

orderId.description:
Optional filter for cancellation requests associated with a specific order.

This value is matched against the foreign key column `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_order_id`. When provided, only cancellation requests linked to the given order are returned.

customerId.description:
Optional filter to narrow results to requests created by a specific customer.

It maps to the nullable foreign key `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_customer_id` and is primarily used in admin support views that focus on the activity of a single registered customer. When not provided, customer-originated requests are not filtered by customer identity.

sellerId.description:
Optional filter to narrow results to requests initiated by or associated with a specific seller.

This field is mapped to `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_seller_id` and helps operations or governance teams monitor seller-driven cancellations. If omitted, seller-related cancellation requests are not restricted to a particular seller.

adminId.description:
Optional filter to narrow results to requests created or submitted by a specific admin actor.

The value corresponds to the nullable foreign key `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_admin_id`. It is useful for audit and workload analysis of administrative actions related to cancellations. When absent, the query does not limit results by admin identity.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for the creation timestamp of cancellation requests, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When provided, only records whose `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` is greater than or equal to this value are included. This allows administrators to focus on recent activity or specific historical windows.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound for the creation timestamp of cancellation requests, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When set, only records whose `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` is less than or equal to this value are returned. Used together with `createdFrom`, it defines a closed or half-open reporting window for the query.

sortBy.description:
Logical sort key that determines the ordering of the cancellation request list.

Typical values correspond to logical column identifiers such as `"created_at"`, `"requested_at"`, or `"status"`. The backend maps these logical keys to actual columns in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` and applies the sort direction from `sortDirection`. When omitted, the server applies its default ordering, usually by recency.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied together with `sortBy` to order the result set.

Expected values are typically `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. The backend validates and normalizes this string, defaulting to its preferred direction when the value is not provided. If `sortBy` is omitted, this field may be ignored by the server.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.description:
Cancellation request entity representing a high-level request to cancel an order or specific order items in the shopping mall domain.

This type maps directly to the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` Prisma model and exposes all business-relevant fields needed for administrative and customer-service style views. It captures who initiated the request, which order it targets, the overall scope of the cancellation, lifecycle status, structured and free-text reasons, and key timestamps for auditing and SLA tracking.

The DTO is used by read operations such as retrieving a single cancellation request by its identifier. It is a detail response type, so it returns the core scalar fields from the Prisma table and additionally provides summarized views of related entities such as the order, initiator actor, and SLA configuration for complete context in a single call.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this cancellation request record.

This value maps to the primary key column `id` of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` table and is generated by the database. It is used as the stable identifier in API paths such as `/shoppingMall/admin/cancellationRequests/{cancellationRequestId}` and is immutable after creation.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order that this cancellation request targets.

This field corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key column that links the cancellation request to a row in `shopping_mall_orders`. It allows backend services to load the full order context and to enforce business rules such as whether the order can still be cancelled.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the customer who initiated the cancellation request when the requester is a registered customer.

This field maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` and references a row in `shopping_mall_customers`. It is set when the actor type is `customer` and the request is associated with a specific customer account.

Null when the cancellation request is not associated with a registered customer actor.

For example, requests initiated by sellers or administrators, or cases where the customer identity cannot be resolved, will leave this field unset.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Foreign key identifier of the customer related to this cancellation request, when applicable.

Use this value for direct joins or correlation in analytics and back-office tools, especially when you need to work with ids rather than the embedded `customer` summary object.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the seller who initiated the cancellation request or whose order items are affected when the seller is treated as the requesting actor.

This value maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` and references `shopping_mall_sellers`.

Null when no specific seller actor is associated as the requester for this cancellation case.

For example, customer-initiated or admin-initiated cancellation requests will typically leave this field unset.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Foreign key identifier of the seller associated with this cancellation request when the actor type is `seller` or when the case is otherwise seller-scoped.

This id complements the `seller` summary object and is useful for batch processing, joins, and advanced reporting where explicit identifiers are required.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the administrator who created or took over this cancellation request on behalf of another actor.

This value maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` and references `shopping_mall_admins`.

Null when the cancellation request has not been explicitly created or owned by a specific administrator.

Customer- or seller-originated requests that have not been reassigned may leave this field unset.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Foreign key identifier of the administrator associated with this cancellation request when it is created, managed, or overridden by back-office staff.

This id provides a direct link to the admin account behind the case and complements the `admin` summary object used in the response.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the SLA configuration that governs this cancellation case.

This value maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` and references `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. When present, it indicates which SLA rule set defines response and resolution expectations for this request.

Null when no specific case SLA configuration row is associated with this cancellation request.

In this situation, default or implicit SLA behavior may apply, or the case may be outside standard SLA tracking.

shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id.description:
Foreign key identifier of the case SLA configuration applied to this cancellation request, when one is explicitly configured.

This field is the id counterpart to the `slaConfig` summary object and is useful for analytics, SLA compliance reporting, and direct joins in internal tooling.

request_code.description:
Business-visible identifier for the cancellation request.

This field corresponds to the `request_code` column and is a human-friendly code used in communications and customer-service tools. It is unique per order according to the `shopping_mall_order_id, request_code` unique index and helps both internal operators and customers refer to a specific request.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the cancellation request.

This value maps to the `status` column in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` and represents the high-level state such as `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `expired`. It drives workflow behavior and is used heavily in operational dashboards and SLA tracking.

scope_type.description:
Scope of the cancellation described by this request.

This field maps to the `scope_type` column and indicates whether the request covers the full order or only specific items. Typical values include semantics like `full_order` or `partial_items`, and downstream workflows use it to determine which order lines and payments are affected.

oneOf.description:
Structured code describing the standardized reason for the cancellation request.

This value corresponds to the `reason_code` column and is typically chosen from a predefined set like `change_of_mind` or `ordered_by_mistake`, enabling analytics and policy-based handling.
Null when no structured reason code was provided and only a free-text description exists.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code for the cancellation.

The field is used to categorize cancellation motives in a machine-readable way for reporting, risk evaluation, and policy enforcement. It may be omitted when the platform only captures free-text explanations.

oneOf.description:
Free-text description explaining why the cancellation is requested.

This maps to the `reason_description` column and contains the narrative written by the requester, often describing specific circumstances or additional details not captured by `reason_code`.
Null when no free-text explanation was provided.

reason_description.description:
Optional free-text explanation of the cancellation request.

This field complements `reason_code` with human-readable detail that can be reviewed by support agents and administrators. It is indexed with a GIN index to support text search and analytics on cancellation reasons.

requested_by_actor_type.description:
Actor type that initiated the cancellation request.

This value comes from the `requested_by_actor_type` column and identifies whether the requester was a `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or another supported actor category. It is critical for authorization checks, analytics, and routing of the case to the appropriate operational queues.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was initially created.

This field corresponds to the `requested_at` column and represents the moment the platform recorded the request. It is used for SLA calculations and audit timelines, and it may be equal to or near `created_at` depending on implementation details.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request reached a terminal decision.

This is stored in the `decided_at` column and is set when the request is approved, rejected, or otherwise finalized. It is used for SLA compliance analysis and reporting on handling times.
Null when the cancellation request is still in a non-terminal state such as pending or under review.

decided_at.description:
Optional timestamp when a final decision was made on the request.

This field remains null for in-progress cancellations and is populated when a decision is recorded. It supports SLA calculations and post-case analytics about response times.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request row was created in the database.

The `created_at` column is system-managed and provides the durable creation time for audit and ordering of cancellation requests. It may be used in combination with `requested_at` for temporal analysis.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request row was last updated.

This field maps to the `updated_at` column and changes whenever mutable attributes of the cancellation request are modified, such as status, reasons, or SLA configuration. It supports concurrency control and change auditing.

order.description:
Summary of the order associated with this cancellation request.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_order_id` and provides high-level order context such as business order code, customer, and status. It allows administrative and customer-service tools to display relevant order information alongside the cancellation without requiring additional API calls.

customer.description:
Summary of the customer who initiated the cancellation request when the actor type is `customer`.

When present, this association is resolved from the `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key and exposes a lightweight view of the customer such as name and key identifiers. It is null when the request is not customer-initiated or when no customer is associated.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller associated with the cancellation request when the actor type is `seller`.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and provides a compact representation of the seller account involved in the cancellation. It is null when the request is not seller-initiated or when no seller is associated.

admin.description:
Summary of the administrator associated with the cancellation request when the actor type is `admin` or when an admin has taken ownership of the case.

This association is resolved from the `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key and provides a lightweight view of the admin user for audit and governance purposes. It is null when no administrator is directly associated with the request.

slaConfig.description:
Summary of the SLA configuration applied to this cancellation case.

When the `shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` foreign key is set, this association exposes key SLA attributes such as target response times and escalation policies. It is null when no specific SLA configuration is linked and default platform policies apply.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new cancellation request.

This type is used by client applications when opening a cancellation case via the `POST /shoppingMall/customer/cancellationRequests` endpoint. It captures all client-supplied business data required to persist a new row in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, such as the target order, scope, and reasons.

Actor identity fields such as customer, seller, or admin identifiers are intentionally excluded from this DTO because they are injected server-side from the authenticated context. System-managed fields like `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are also omitted, as they are generated by the backend. The structure focuses on inputs describing what should be cancelled and why.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order for which the cancellation is being requested.

This value is written into the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key column and must reference an existing row in `shopping_mall_orders`. The backend uses it to validate that the order is in a cancellable state and to derive related context such as items and payments.

request_code.description:
Business-visible code for the cancellation request within the scope of the order.

This field populates the `request_code` column and must be unique per order as enforced by the `(shopping_mall_order_id, request_code)` unique index. Clients can either generate this value according to business rules or rely on the backend to normalize or override it.

status.description:
Initial status to assign to the cancellation request.

Although many implementations default this to a `pending` or equivalent value, the field maps to the `status` column and may be exposed here to support advanced flows or administrative callers. Business rules should validate that the provided status is a valid starting state in the cancellation lifecycle.

scope_type.description:
Scope of the cancellation requested.

The value is stored in the `scope_type` column and indicates whether the request covers the entire order or only specific order items. Typical semantics include `full_order` for whole-order cancellations or `partial_items` when only certain lines are to be cancelled.

oneOf.description:
Structured code representing the standardized reason for the cancellation.

This value is written to the `reason_code` column and should match a configured set of allowed codes, such as `change_of_mind` or `ordered_by_mistake`, enabling downstream analytics and rule-based handling.
Null when no structured reason code is specified and only a free-text explanation is provided.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code for the cancellation request.

When present, this field categorizes the request according to predefined business reason codes. It may be omitted for ad-hoc or free-form explanations.

oneOf.description:
Human-readable explanation describing why the cancellation is requested.

This value populates the `reason_description` column and can contain details about the circumstances or expectations of the requester. It is useful for support agents reviewing the case.
Null when the requester does not provide a free-text description and only uses a structured reason code.

reason_description.description:
Optional free-text description for the cancellation request.

This field complements `reason_code` with narrative detail that can assist human decision making. It may be left null if the platform only uses structured reasons.

oneOf.description:
Client-provided timestamp representing when the cancellation was initiated.

If supplied, this value is written into the `requested_at` column and may reflect the originating client time. Many implementations instead ignore this field and set `requested_at` server-side at creation time.
Null when the client does not specify a requested-at timestamp and the backend will derive it automatically.

requested_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when the cancellation was initiated.

This property allows advanced clients to pass an explicit initiation time, though typical flows let the backend assign `requested_at` using the current server time. When omitted or null, the server is expected to set the column value itself.

requested_by_actor_type.description:
Actor category that initiated the cancellation request.

This field is stored in the `requested_by_actor_type` column and describes whether the requester is a `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or another supported actor type. In the customer-facing endpoint context, it is expected to hold a value such as `customer` and may be validated or overridden by backend logic.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields for updating an existing cancellation request header in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` Prisma model and is used by administrative or back-office flows to change lifecycle and decision-related attributes of a previously created cancellation request while preserving immutable identifiers and foreign keys.

The update is typically driven by business workflows such as approving or rejecting a request, assigning or changing SLA configurations, or refining structured and free-text reasons, and must always comply with the constraints and status transition rules imposed at the service layer.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the cancellation request, such as `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `expired`.

Business logic enforces which status transitions are permitted depending on the current state, associated order state, and downstream refund or dispute handling. The exact list of status codes is defined at the domain level and validated server-side.

scope_type.description:
Scope of the cancellation request, for example `full_order` or `partial_items`.

Although this field is often fixed at creation time, the update DTO allows changing it when business rules permit re-scoping the request, such as converting a full-order cancellation into a partial one before a decision is finalized.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code selected from policy-defined values such as `change_of_mind` or `ordered_by_mistake`.

When present, it should match one of the configured cancellation reason codes so that reporting, analytics, and policy evaluation can rely on normalized values. When omitted or null, only the free-text reason description may be used for human review.

reason_description.description:
Optional free-text explanation describing why the cancellation is requested.

This text is typically provided by the requester or updated by back-office staff to clarify context. It is indexed for search and may be used by SLA, risk, or dispute handling teams to understand the narrative of the case.

requested_by_actor_type.description:
Actor type that initiated the cancellation request, for example `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`.

Although usually determined at creation, administrative flows may adjust this value when correcting misclassified requests or when re-attributing responsibility for the request based on subsequent investigation.

decided_at.description:
Timestamp at which the cancellation request reached a terminal decision such as approved or rejected, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is typically set by the system when a decision is recorded but is exposed in the update DTO so that administrative tools can correct or backfill decision timestamps when necessary under strict governance controls.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequestItem.IRe.description:
Search and filter parameters for listing item-level cancellation lines that belong to a specific cancellation request.

This DTO is used as the request body of the PATCH `/shoppingMall/cancellationRequests/{cancellationRequestId}/items` operation and drives filtering, sorting, and pagination over the `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items` table.

It is intentionally separate from the underlying Prisma model so that it can express query concepts such as date ranges and pagination metadata without being constrained to the physical columns of the table.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination over cancellation request items.

Clients use this in combination with `limit` to step through result sets when a cancellation request contains many item lines.

limit.description:
Maximum number of cancellation request items to return in a single page.

The server enforces an upper bound to protect performance and may apply a default when the client omits this value.

order_item_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to a specific order item, identified by its UUID.

When provided, only item lines whose underlying `shopping_mall_order_item_id` matches this value are returned, which is useful for drilling into how a particular order item participates in one or more cancellation requests.

requested_quantity_min.description:
Optional lower bound filter for the requested cancellation quantity.

When set, only items whose `requested_quantity` is greater than or equal to this value are included, which is useful for focusing on large-quantity cancellations.

requested_quantity_max.description:
Optional upper bound filter for the requested cancellation quantity.

When set together with `requested_quantity_min`, it defines an inclusive range of requested quantities to be included in the results.

created_from.description:
Optional start of the creation timestamp range to filter item lines, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When provided, only cancellation request items whose `created_at` is greater than or equal to this value are returned, allowing time-windowed analysis of cancellation activity.

created_to.description:
Optional end of the creation timestamp range to filter item lines, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When used together with `created_from`, it defines a closed interval on the `created_at` field, enabling list views constrained to a specific reporting period.

reason_search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied against the item-level `reason_description` field.

The underlying column is GIN-indexed to support efficient search. This parameter enables users to quickly find cancellation items mentioning particular keywords or phrases in their explanations.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequestItem.description:
Cancellation request item line representing an order item level cancellation within a specific cancellation request.

Each instance models a single line from the `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items` table and belongs to exactly one parent cancellation request in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`. It references a concrete purchased order item from `shopping_mall_order_items` and captures the quantity requested to be cancelled along with any item-level reason description.

The DTO is used by read operations that need to expose detailed item-level cancellation information, including which order line is affected, how many units are being cancelled, and explanatory metadata required for customer service, auditing, and analytics workflows.

id.description:
Primary key of the cancellation request item row.

This UUID uniquely identifies the item-level cancellation line within the `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items` table and is used as the authoritative identifier for retrieval and update operations.

cancellationRequest.description:
Parent cancellation request that owns this item-level line.

This is a BELONGS-TO association to the header entity stored in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, transformed into a lightweight summary view so that consumers can understand which cancellation case this line belongs to without issuing additional API calls.

The referenced summary exposes key header information such as the cancellation request identifier, overall status, and high-level context suitable for list and detail UIs.

orderItem.description:
Order item being cancelled by this cancellation request line.

This BELONGS-TO association replaces the raw foreign key to `shopping_mall_order_items` and provides a compact summary of the underlying purchased line item, including identifiers and core descriptive fields.

Using a summary reference here lets clients render which SKU or product is being cancelled without fetching the full order item detail separately, while still avoiding deep circular references.

requestedQuantity.description:
Quantity of the order item that the requester wants to cancel.

This is a positive integer measured in the same units as the original order quantity on `shopping_mall_order_items.quantity`. Business validation ensures it does not exceed the original quantity minus any already-cancelled or refunded quantity.

reasonDescription.description:
Optional item-specific cancellation explanation written by the requester.

When provided, this text supplements or overrides the header-level reason from `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.reason_description`, allowing more granular justification at the individual line level. When not relevant, it is null.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request item record was created.

The value is taken directly from `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items.created_at` and is used for auditing, reporting, and time-based analysis of cancellation flows.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request item record was last updated.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items.updated_at` and moves forward whenever mutable fields on the item-level cancellation line are changed.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequestItem.ICr.description:
Request body schema for creating a new cancellation request item under an existing cancellation request.

This DTO is used by POST operations that attach one or more item-level cancellation lines to a header record in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`. It collects the target order item identifier and the quantity the actor wishes to cancel, plus an optional line-level reason description.

The parent cancellation request identifier is provided via the URL path, so it is intentionally excluded from this body. Server-side logic validates that the referenced order item belongs to the same order as the parent request and that the requested quantity complies with order and policy constraints before inserting into `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items`.

orderItemId.description:
Identifier of the order item to be cancelled on this new line.

This value will be stored in `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items.shopping_mall_order_item_id` and must reference a valid row in `shopping_mall_order_items` that is associated with the same order as the parent cancellation request.

requestedQuantity.description:
Quantity of the referenced order item that the actor requests to cancel.

The server enforces that this is a positive integer and that it does not exceed the outstanding cancellable quantity for the corresponding `shopping_mall_order_items.quantity` after prior cancellations and refunds.

reasonDescription.description:
Optional free-text reason specific to this cancellation line.

When provided, this message describes why this particular order item is being cancelled and is stored in `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items.reason_description`. If omitted or null, only the header-level reason on `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` applies.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequestItem.IUp.description:
Update DTO for a single cancellation request item row stored in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items` table.

This type is used when a customer, seller, or admin updates modifiable business fields of an existing cancellation request item while the parent cancellation request is still in an editable lifecycle state. It intentionally excludes immutable identifiers and foreign key relations, which are controlled by the server and validated against the parent `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` record.

Typical use cases include changing the requested cancellation quantity or adjusting item-level explanatory notes before the cancellation request is finalized. Ownership, parent linkage, and audit timestamps are all system-managed and therefore not present in this DTO.

requestedQuantity.description:
New quantity of the underlying order item that should be cancelled as part of this cancellation request item.

This value must be a non‑negative integer and must respect order‑level constraints such as the originally ordered quantity and any amounts that have already been cancelled or refunded for the associated `shopping_mall_order_items` row.

Business rules in the service layer revalidate this field on each update, and attempts to increase the quantity beyond allowed thresholds should be rejected.

reasonDescription.description:
Optional updated free‑text explanation for why this particular order item is being cancelled.

Use this field when the item‑level rationale differs from the header‑level `reason_description` stored on the parent `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` record. When set to null, previously stored item‑level comments may be cleared according to business rules.

The content should be user‑provided and may be subject to moderation, length limits, or profanity filtering implemented by the application.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying refund requests stored in the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` table.

This type is used by administrative consoles, seller tools, and internal dashboards to perform complex, paginated searches over refund cases. It encapsulates filter criteria such as lifecycle status, creation and decision date ranges, associated order or payment identifiers, requesting actor metadata, and free‑text reason matching.

Pagination and sorting controls are also included so that clients can request specific pages of data and order results by important business fields like creation timestamp or status. The actual visibility of records is enforced by the backend according to the authenticated actor’s role and permissions.

page.description:
1‑based index of the page to retrieve when performing a paginated refund request search.

If omitted, the implementation typically defaults to the first page. Values less than 1 should be treated as invalid by the service layer, and very large values may be capped to protect performance.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund request summary rows to return in a single page of results.

Clients should choose values that balance data density and performance, for example 20, 50, or 100. The backend may enforce an upper bound regardless of the requested value to prevent overly heavy queries.

orderBy.description:
Logical field name used to sort refund request search results.

Common choices include fields derived from the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` table such as `requested_at`, `decided_at`, or `status`. The concrete set of sortable fields is defined by the implementation, and unsupported values should result in validation errors.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field when returning refund request search results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. The service layer may normalize or validate the value and fall back to a default when an unsupported direction is provided.

status.description:
Optional filter restricting results to refund requests currently in a specific lifecycle status.

Status values usually correspond to business states modeled in the `shopping_mall_refund_requests.status` column, such as `requested`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `completed`. When omitted, all statuses are eligible for inclusion subject to other filters.

orderId.description:
Optional filter limiting the search to refund requests associated with a particular order.

The value corresponds to the primary key of a `shopping_mall_orders` record referenced by `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_order_id`. Use this when focusing on all refund cases for a single order.

orderPaymentId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to refund requests tied to a specific logical order payment.

The value corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_order_payment_id`. When set to null explicitly, implementations may treat it as a request to match refund requests that are not bound to any particular payment record, depending on business rules.

requestedByActorType.description:
Optional filter specifying which actor type initiated the refund requests to be returned.

Typical values mirror the `requested_by_actor_type` column of `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, such as `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`. When omitted, refund requests created by any actor type may be included, subject to authorization constraints.

currencyCode.description:
Optional filter restricting results to refund requests denominated in a particular currency.

The value should match `shopping_mall_refund_requests.currency_code`, typically using ISO 4217 codes such as `USD` or `KRW`. This is useful for finance and reconciliation views segmented by currency.

reasonDescriptionQuery.description:
Optional free‑text search term applied to the `reason_description` column of refund requests.

Clients can use this to locate cases whose explanations contain particular words or phrases, enabling operations teams to quickly identify patterns or specific incidents.

requestedFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the creation timestamp range filter for refund requests.

When provided, only refund requests with `requested_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime value should be included in the result set. Use null to indicate no lower bound on the time range.

requestedTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the creation timestamp range filter for refund requests.

When provided, only refund requests with `requested_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime value should be returned. Use null to indicate no upper bound on the time range.

decidedFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the decision timestamp range filter for refund requests.

This filter targets the `decided_at` column, allowing consumers to search for refund cases that reached a terminal decision on or after the specified point in time. When null, no lower bound on decision time is applied.

decidedTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the decision timestamp range filter for refund requests.

Only refund requests whose `decided_at` timestamp is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 datetime value should be included when the filter is set. A null value indicates that no upper decision‑time bound is imposed.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.description:
Refund request entity for the shopping mall governance domain.

Represents a high-level refund case initiated by a customer, seller, or admin after or around delivery. Each record links to an order and optionally a specific payment and cancellation request, and it stores the requested and approved monetary amounts, currency, selected structured reason, free-text explanation, and lifecycle timestamps.

This DTO is a direct projection of the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` Prisma model, exposing only business-relevant fields required by administrative and governance tools. It provides association summaries for related actors and configuration entities, while preserving the parent order identifier as a raw ID to avoid deep circular expansions.

id.description:
Primary identifier of the refund request.

This is the unique UUID primary key of the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` row. It is used as the canonical identifier in API paths such as `/shoppingMall/admin/refundRequests/{refundRequestId}` and should be treated as opaque by clients.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order for which this refund is requested.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_order_id` and links the refund request to a single order record in `shopping_mall_orders`. It remains as a raw ID in this DTO so that refund requests can be linked to orders without recursively embedding the full order structure.

orderPayment.description:
Logical order payment associated with this refund request, when the refund is tied to a specific payment record.

When non-null, this object provides a summary view derived from `shopping_mall_order_payments` and corresponds to the foreign key `shopping_mall_order_payment_id`. It allows administrators to understand which payment is being adjusted without performing a separate lookup by ID.

customer.description:
Customer who initiated the refund request, when the requester is a customer actor.

This summary corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_customer_id` and references a row in `shopping_mall_customers`. It provides lightweight identity and profile context for governance flows without embedding the full customer entity.

seller.description:
Seller who initiated or is directly involved in this refund request, when the requester is a seller actor.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_seller_id` and points to a record in `shopping_mall_sellers`. It lets administrators see the responsible merchant and basic seller information in a single refund request read.

admin.description:
Administrator who created or registered this refund request in manual or exceptional flows.

This summary corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_admin_id` and references a row in `shopping_mall_admins`. It is typically populated for platform-driven adjustments or governance-triggered refund cases.

primaryReason.description:
Primary structured reason selected for this refund request.

This association is based on `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id` and references a record in `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons`. It allows consistent classification and analytics of refund drivers across the platform.

linkedCancellationRequest.description:
Linked cancellation request when the refund stems from an existing cancellation case.

This object corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id` referencing `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`. It gives reviewers immediate access to the related cancellation context without additional lookups.
