slaConfig.description:
Service-level agreement configuration that governs expected response and resolution times for this refund request.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` and references `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. It enables governance tooling to show which SLA rule applies to this case and to correlate SLA performance with actual lifecycle timestamps.

request_code.description:
Business-visible identifier for the refund request.

This string is stored in `shopping_mall_refund_requests.request_code` and is used in customer, seller, and admin interfaces and communications to reference the case. It is unique per order, enforced by a composite unique index `(shopping_mall_order_id, request_code)`.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the refund request.

The value mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_requests.status` and indicates the business state such as `requested`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `completed`. Exact allowed values are enforced at the service and policy level, and transitions are typically recorded in dedicated history tables.

requested_total_amount.description:
Total monetary amount requested to be refunded, expressed in the order currency.

This numeric field corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.requested_total_amount`. It represents the gross amount the requester is asking to be returned, prior to any approval logic or partial adjustments. The currency is specified by `currency_code` and should be consistent with the linked order.

approved_total_amount.description:
Total monetary amount approved to be refunded after review.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.approved_total_amount`. It remains null until a reviewer makes a decision and can reflect partial approval when only part of the requested amount is granted. The value is expressed in the same currency as `requested_total_amount`.

currency_code.description:
Currency code associated with requested and approved refund amounts.

This is the ISO 4217 currency code stored in `shopping_mall_refund_requests.currency_code`, typically matching the currency of the associated order, such as `USD` or `KRW`. All monetary totals on the refund request are denominated in this currency.

reason_description.description:
Free-text explanation describing the reason for the refund request.

This value comes from `shopping_mall_refund_requests.reason_description` and supplements any structured reason selected via `primaryReason`. It captures detailed context provided by the requester or by admins during case creation and review.

requested_by_actor_type.description:
Type of actor who initiated the refund request.

This string corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.requested_by_actor_type` and indicates whether the case was opened by a `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`. It is used for governance, analytics, and eligibility checks in surrounding workflows.

requires_return.description:
Flag indicating whether physical goods must be returned as part of resolving this refund request.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.requires_return`. When true, logistics and warehouse processes must be engaged to handle product returns; when false, the refund may be processed without a physical return.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was created in the system.

This value is `shopping_mall_refund_requests.requested_at` and marks the business start time of the case for SLA measurement and analytics. It typically matches or closely follows the `created_at` timestamp.

decided_at.description:
Timestamp when a final approval or rejection decision was made on the refund request.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.decided_at`. It remains null while the case is still under review and is set at the point where the platform or responsible actor reaches a terminal decision.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund was fully processed and completed from a financial perspective.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.completed_at` and is usually set once all associated payment refunds and operational steps have been successfully executed for the case.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request record was created in the database.

This is the `shopping_mall_refund_requests.created_at` column used for auditing and ordering by creation time. It is system-managed and never modified directly by clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request record was last updated.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.updated_at` and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields on the refund request are changed as part of governance workflows.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new refund request in the shopping mall governance domain.

This DTO captures the fields that a client must or may provide when opening a new refund case against an existing order. It mirrors the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` Prisma model while excluding system-managed properties such as `id`, `request_code`, `status`, and audit timestamps, which are initialized by the backend.

The create payload focuses on linking to the target order and optional payment, specifying the requested refund amount and currency, indicating whether goods should be returned, and providing structured and free-text reasons together with actor context. Service logic uses these values to enforce business rules, derive initial lifecycle status, and associate the case with the correct SLA configuration.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order for which this refund is requested.

Clients must supply the UUID of an existing order in `shopping_mall_orders` to anchor the refund case. This value populates `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_order_id` and determines the primary business context for the request.

shopping_mall_order_payment_id.description:
Identifier of the specific order payment that this refund request is associated with, when applicable.

When provided, this field sets `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_order_payment_id` and should reference a payment row in `shopping_mall_order_payments` belonging to the same order. It is useful for partial or split refunds tied to particular payment segments.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer on whose behalf the refund request is opened.

This value populates `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_customer_id` and must reference a record in `shopping_mall_customers` when the requester is a customer. In flows where the customer identity comes from the authenticated session, this field may be derived server-side rather than sent by the client.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller on whose behalf the refund request is opened.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_seller_id` and should reference `shopping_mall_sellers` in seller-initiated refund scenarios, such as concessions or goodwill adjustments. In authenticated seller flows, the service can infer this from the session context.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin creating the refund request when it is initiated manually by an internal operator.

The value is written into `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_admin_id` and should reference a row in `shopping_mall_admins`. In back-office tools, this will usually be derived from the authenticated admin account rather than supplied by the front-end payload.

shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id.description:
Identifier of the primary structured reason selected for the refund request.

When provided, this populates `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id` and must reference a configuration row in `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` that has `applies_to_refund` enabled. It allows downstream analytics and policy enforcement on reason codes.

shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id.description:
Identifier of a linked cancellation request when the refund originates from a cancellation case.

This field is written to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id` and should reference a record in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`. It connects the refund case to earlier cancellation workflows for unified governance and reporting.

shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id.description:
Identifier of the SLA configuration that should govern this refund request, when a specific SLA rule applies.

When set, this populates `shopping_mall_refund_requests.shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` and must reference `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. Policy tooling can use this to enforce or monitor response and resolution deadlines for the case.

requested_total_amount.description:
Total amount requested to be refunded in the order currency.

Clients must supply this numeric value to populate `shopping_mall_refund_requests.requested_total_amount`. The amount should be consistent with the linked order and associated payments, and is subject to validation rules that prevent over-refunds.

currency_code.description:
Currency code for the requested refund amount.

This string is written to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.currency_code` and must be a supported ISO 4217 currency such as `USD` or `KRW`. Implementations should validate that it matches the currency used on the associated order.

reason_description.description:
Free-text explanation describing why the refund is requested.

This value populates `shopping_mall_refund_requests.reason_description` and gives human-readable context on the issue, often written by the customer or a support agent. It supplements any structured reason code and may be null when only the structured reason is used.

requested_by_actor_type.description:
Actor type on whose behalf the refund request is being created.

This field fills `shopping_mall_refund_requests.requested_by_actor_type` and should indicate whether the request is initiated by a `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`. Service logic uses this to validate which of the actor linkage fields is expected and to route the case appropriately.

requires_return.description:
Flag indicating whether the refund process requires goods to be returned.

This boolean is written to `shopping_mall_refund_requests.requires_return`. When true, subsequent workflows must coordinate return shipping and warehouse operations; when false, the platform may allow refunds without physical returns according to business policy.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing refund request record in the shopping mall domain.

This type follows a partial update pattern: all properties are optional, and omitting a property from the request body means "do not change" the corresponding field on the underlying `shopping_mall_refund_requests` row. Callers send only those fields whose values they intend to adjust as part of an administrative or governance workflow.

The DTO represents the subset of refund request properties that are allowed to change after the refund case has been created, such as status transitions driven by admins, monetary approval values, descriptive context, and lifecycle timestamps that are managed by privileged services. Fields that define identity or immutable relationships – such as the linked order, payments, and the actor who originally requested the refund – are intentionally excluded so that ownership and linkage remain stable over the lifecycle of the case.

Service implementations are responsible for enforcing business rules around which actors may update which fields, how status transitions are validated, and how timestamp fields must relate to the original request and payment events. Typical callers of this DTO are internal admin tools, case management services, or automated policy engines rather than end-user clients.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the refund request.

Typical values include business-level states such as `requested`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `completed`, as defined by the platform’s refund workflow. When this property is provided in the update DTO, the service should treat it as a request to transition the refund case into the specified state, subject to validation of allowed transitions.

When this property is omitted from the request body, the existing status on the underlying `shopping_mall_refund_requests` record must remain unchanged. Clients should not attempt to clear the status; the field is conceptually required on the entity and should always contain a valid state.

approved_total_amount.description:
Total monetary amount approved to be refunded for this request, expressed in the same currency as the underlying order.

When this property is supplied with a numeric value, it represents the updated approval decision for the overall refund amount, typically set or adjusted during case review by an admin or automated decision engine. Business logic must ensure that the amount does not exceed what was actually paid and that it is consistent with the breakdown stored in line-level refund request items and payment refund items.

When this property is omitted, the existing approved amount on the refund request remains unchanged. A null value should only be used in specialized administrative flows to explicitly clear a previously stored approval amount in accordance with strict business rules; general clients should either omit the field or send a concrete numeric value.

reason_description.description:
Free-text explanation that provides additional context for the refund request beyond the structured reason code.

When a non-null string is supplied, the service should treat this as an updated narrative explaining why the refund is being requested or how the situation has evolved (for example, internal investigation notes or customer-provided clarifications). Because this field may contain audit-relevant information, implementations often maintain complementary history tables or audit logs when it changes.

When this property is omitted from the update payload, the existing free-text description is left unchanged. When explicitly set to null, the service may interpret this as a request to clear the stored description, but such behavior should be controlled by policy to avoid accidental loss of important case context.

requires_return.description:
Flag indicating whether physical goods must be returned in order to complete this refund request.

On the underlying `shopping_mall_refund_requests` model, this field is a non-nullable boolean that indicates whether return logistics (for example, labels, drop-off instructions, or warehouse intake) are required before the refund can be finalized. When this property is provided with `true` or `false` in the update DTO, the service should treat it as an explicit change to that underlying flag.

When this property is omitted from the request body, the existing value of `requires_return` must remain unchanged. A null value in this DTO should not generally be used by client code; instead, callers should either omit the property (no change) or send a concrete boolean when they intend to update the requirement. If the service ever supports clearing the flag via null, that behavior must be explicitly defined and restricted to privileged administrative flows.

decided_at.description:
Timestamp at which a final decision (such as approved or rejected) was recorded for this refund request, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When a non-null value is provided, it should represent the authoritative moment at which the decision was taken, usually set by internal case management services or automated decision engines. Implementations must maintain chronological consistency with `requested_at` and may restrict who can set or modify this timestamp and under which circumstances.

When this property is omitted, the existing decision timestamp (if any) remains intact. Setting this property to null in the update payload should generally be avoided by normal clients; if supported, clearing the decision timestamp must be treated as a special administrative operation that explicitly revises the case history under controlled governance rules.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the financial side of the refund was fully processed and completed, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

A non-null value indicates that all associated payment operations (such as refunds or reversals at the payment provider) have been successfully executed and reconciled. This field is typically maintained by backend payment or settlement services that react to provider callbacks or internal accounting workflows, rather than by interactive client applications.

When this property is omitted in the update DTO, the existing completion timestamp is left unchanged. Setting this property explicitly, especially to null, should be reserved for specialized operational tooling and must be carefully governed to avoid corrupting the financial timeline of the case.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestItem.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering DTO for querying refund request items associated with a single refund request.

This type is used in PATCH search operations to retrieve a paginated and optionally filtered collection of item-level records from the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` table for a specific refund request. All properties are optional: omitting a property from the request body means that the corresponding filter or sort option is not applied, and the backend falls back to its default behavior.

The DTO focuses on list-oriented concerns such as pagination, ordering, and basic domain filters (status and requested-amount ranges). It does not modify any refund item state; instead, it is purely a read/query model that helps administrative clients and internal tools explore line-level breakdowns of a refund case.

page.description:
Page number for pagination when listing refund request items.

This value is typically treated as a 1-based index, where `1` refers to the first page of results. When omitted, the backend should default to the first page according to its configured pagination strategy. Values less than 1 should be either rejected or normalized to the minimum supported page number.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund request items to return in a single page of results.

This parameter controls the page size for the query. When omitted, the service should fall back to a reasonable default limit (for example, 20, 50, or 100 items per page) and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance. Values less than 1 or greater than the configured maximum should be rejected or normalized by the implementation.

status.description:
Optional filter on the domain-specific processing status of refund request items.

When provided with a non-null value, this field restricts the result set to items whose status matches the given value according to the platform’s line-level status semantics (for example, `pending`, `approved`, or `rejected`). The exact vocabulary is defined by business rules and may be validated by the service.

When omitted or explicitly set to null, no status-based filtering is applied and items of all statuses that belong to the targeted refund request are eligible for inclusion in the results.

min_requested_amount.description:
Lower bound filter on the requested refund amount for individual refund request items.

When provided with a numeric value, only items whose requested amount is greater than or equal to this threshold (in the relevant currency) will be returned. This is useful for focusing on higher-value lines during administrative review or financial analysis.

When this property is omitted or set to null, no lower bound is applied. If both `min_requested_amount` and `max_requested_amount` are supplied, the service should ensure that the resulting inclusive range is coherent before executing the query.

max_requested_amount.description:
Upper bound filter on the requested refund amount for individual refund request items.

When provided with a numeric value, only items whose requested amount is less than or equal to this threshold (in the relevant currency) are eligible for inclusion in the result set. This can be used to isolate lower-value refund lines or to constrain the inspected range.

When this property is omitted or set to null, no upper bound is applied. When used together with `min_requested_amount`, the two values define an inclusive numeric range that the implementation should validate for consistency.

order_by.description:
Optional field indicating which attribute to use when ordering refund request items in the result set.

Typical values include column names that make sense for administrative review, such as `created_at`, `requested_amount`, or other sortable properties of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` model. The service should restrict this field to a whitelist of supported sort keys to avoid invalid or unsafe ordering expressions.

When this property is omitted or set to null, the backend should apply its default ordering strategy, most commonly by creation time descending so that the newest items appear first.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering refund request items.

When provided, this value should typically be `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending order, and it is interpreted in conjunction with `order_by`. If an unsupported value is supplied, the service should reject the request or normalize it according to policy.

When this property is omitted or set to null, the backend should default to the most appropriate direction for the selected `order_by` field (for example, descending for time-based fields like `created_at`). If `order_by` is also omitted, both fields are ignored and the service uses its built-in default sort order.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestItem.description:
Refund request item entity representing a single monetary line within a refund case.

Each record belongs to exactly one refund request from `shopping_mall_refund_requests` and optionally links to an order item, a payment refund item, and a structured line-level reason. It provides the fine‑grained breakdown of how a high‑level refund request impacts specific items or payment components.

This type is used primarily as the detail response DTO for APIs that read or manipulate refund request items. It exposes all non‑sensitive fields from the underlying Prisma model and is designed to be embedded in refund request detail views or returned directly by item-level operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund request item record.

This matches the primary key column `id` in the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` table and is generated by the system when the record is created.

Clients use this value in path parameters when updating or referencing a specific refund request item.

shopping_mall_refund_request_id.description:
Identifier of the parent refund request that owns this item.

This corresponds to the foreign key column `shopping_mall_refund_request_id` and always points to a row in `shopping_mall_refund_requests`. It ensures that every line item is clearly associated with a single refund case.

In read responses this field allows clients and back‑office tools to correlate line items with their parent refund request.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Identifier of the related order item when the refund line targets a specific purchased item.

This maps to the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_order_item_id` in the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` table and points to a record in `shopping_mall_order_items`.

It is null when the refund line is not associated with a particular order item, for example when refunding only fees or adjustments.

shopping_mall_payment_refund_item_id.description:
Identifier of the underlying payment refund item that implements this refund line.

This corresponds to the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_payment_refund_item_id` referencing `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items`. It links business‑level refund lines with low‑level payment provider refund operations.

The field is null when payment refund items have not yet been created or when the line is purely conceptual at the request stage.

shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id.description:
Identifier of the structured refund reason specific to this line, when present.

This value maps to the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id` and references `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons`. It allows line‑level reasons that may differ from the parent refund request’s primary reason.

When null, only the parent refund request’s reason and free‑text description apply.

requested_quantity.description:
Quantity to be refunded for the associated item when the refund is quantity‑based.

This corresponds to the nullable integer column `requested_quantity`. For item‑level refunds it indicates how many units are being requested for refund.

The field is null when the refund line is amount‑only and not tied to item quantity, for example when refunding fees or manual adjustments.

approved_quantity.description:
Quantity approved for refund after review when the refund is quantity‑based.

This maps to the nullable integer column `approved_quantity`. It is typically populated by internal staff or automated rules once a decision is made on the requested quantity.

The value remains null until the line has been processed or when quantity is not applicable for this refund item.

requested_amount.description:
Monetary amount requested to be refunded for this line, in the order currency.

This field is derived from the non‑nullable double column `requested_amount` and represents the exact amount the requester wants refunded for the associated item or component.

It is always provided for each refund request item and is used in conjunction with `currency_code` and parent totals for reconciliation.

approved_amount.description:
Monetary amount approved to be refunded for this line after review.

This corresponds to the nullable double column `approved_amount`. It captures the final approved refund amount in the same currency used for the order.

The field is null while the refund item is still under review or when a decision has not yet been recorded.

currency_code.description:
Currency code for the requested and approved amounts on this line.

This maps to the non‑nullable string column `currency_code`. It typically matches the currency of the parent order (for example `USD` or `KRW`).

Clients should treat this as the authoritative currency for interpreting `requested_amount` and `approved_amount` values.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request item record was created.

This field directly reflects the non‑nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` table and is set by the system at insert time.

Consumers can use it to order items chronologically or to audit when a particular line was first registered.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request item record was last updated.

This value comes from the non‑nullable `updated_at` column and is automatically maintained by the system whenever the row changes.

It allows clients and operators to detect recent modifications and to implement optimistic concurrency or stale data checks if needed.

orderItem.description:
Associated order item summary for this refund line, when the refund targets a specific purchased item.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_order_items` via the `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key. It exposes a compact view of the order line, such as product, quantity, and pricing, supporting investigation and decision workflows.

The value is null when the refund line is not linked to a particular order item or when the association cannot be resolved.

paymentRefundItem.description:
Associated payment refund item summary that implements this refund line at the payment provider level.

This association comes from `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` and is linked via `shopping_mall_payment_refund_item_id`. It allows admin tools to understand how this high‑level refund request item maps to concrete payment refund entries.

The value is null until a payment refund item has been created or when the line does not correspond directly to a single payment refund item.

reason.description:
Structured refund request reason attached specifically to this line, when present.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` master table using `shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id`. It provides a human‑readable classification of the refund cause, such as defect type or delivery issue, to support reporting and governance.

The value is null when no line‑level reason has been recorded and only parent-level or free‑text explanations apply.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestItem.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new line-level refund request item under an existing refund request.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` Prisma model and includes all business fields required to express which order item or payment component is affected, along with the requested refund quantity and amount. System-managed fields such as primary keys and timestamps are excluded because they are generated by the backend.

Clients use this type when calling creation endpoints like `POST /shoppingMall/customer/refundRequests/{refundRequestId}/items` or `POST /shoppingMall/admin/refundRequests/{refundRequestId}/items`, passing only the business data necessary to define the refund line while the server injects the parent refund request identifier from the path and populates audit fields automatically.

orderItemId.description:
Identifier of the order item that this refund line targets, when the refund is associated with a specific order item.

This corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key. When provided, it must reference an existing row in `shopping_mall_order_items` that belongs to the same order underlying the parent refund request. When left `null`, the refund may instead be tied to a payment-level component via `paymentRefundItemId`.

paymentRefundItemId.description:
Identifier of the payment refund item that implements this refund line at the payment provider level, if already known.

This maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_payment_refund_item_id` foreign key. It is typically omitted or `null` at initial creation when the payment refund has not yet been created, and may be populated later by internal processing once the payment subsystem has produced a corresponding refund item.

reasonId.description:
Identifier of the structured refund reason associated with this line, when a specific reason code should be attached.

This is the nullable `shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id` foreign key. It should reference a row in `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` and allows callers to classify the line with a granular reason such as "damaged item" or "wrong size" in addition to any header-level reasons.

requestedQuantity.description:
Quantity of units being requested for refund in this line, for quantity-based refunds.

This payload property maps to the nullable `requested_quantity` column. Callers should provide a positive integer when the refund is defined in terms of how many units of the original order line are being refunded, or `null` when the refund is defined purely in monetary terms without an explicit quantity.

requestedAmount.description:
Monetary amount being requested for refund for this line, expressed in the specified currency.

This corresponds to the non-nullable `requested_amount` column. The value should represent the portion of the order or payment the actor wishes to refund on this single line and must respect platform rules regarding maximum refundable amounts.

currencyCode.description:
Currency code for the requested refund amount for this line.

This property maps to the non-nullable `currency_code` column and typically stores a three-letter ISO currency code aligned with the currency of the associated order. All monetary amounts in this DTO are interpreted in this currency.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestItem.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing refund request item record.

This type represents the set of mutable fields on `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` that a client or internal tool may adjust after initial creation. Typical updates include changing requested quantities, adjusting amounts, or altering line‑level reason associations while the parent refund request is still in an editable state.

Identity and audit fields such as `id`, `shopping_mall_refund_request_id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are excluded from this DTO because they are system‑managed or supplied via path parameters. The DTO is intentionally designed for partial updates: all properties are optional, and the service layer applies only the fields that are provided in the request body.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Updated identifier of the associated order item when changing which purchased item this refund line targets.

This field maps to the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_order_item_id`. Providing a non‑null value re‑associates the refund item with a different order item, subject to validation against the parent order.

Sending null clears the association when the refund line should no longer be tied to a specific order item.

shopping_mall_payment_refund_item_id.description:
Updated identifier of the payment refund item implementing this refund line.

This corresponds to the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_payment_refund_item_id`. It is typically controlled by internal processes that synchronize with payment providers.

Clients should generally avoid changing this field directly unless the use case explicitly requires correcting the linkage to a payment refund item.

shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id.description:
Updated structured reason associated with this refund request item.

This maps to the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id` referencing `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons`. Changing this field allows refinement of the line‑level reason separate from the parent refund request.

Providing null removes the explicit line‑level reason so that only the parent request reason and free‑text explanations apply.

requested_quantity.description:
New requested quantity for this refund item when the refund is quantity‑based.

This field corresponds to the nullable `requested_quantity` column. Updating it lets the requester correct or refine how many units are being refunded on this line.

Setting this property to null indicates that the refund item should no longer be treated as quantity‑based and might be interpreted purely in terms of monetary amount.

approved_quantity.description:
Updated approved quantity for this refund item when quantity‑based review decisions change.

This value maps to the nullable `approved_quantity` column. It is usually managed by reviewers or automated decision logic to reflect partial or full approval of the requested quantity.

Null indicates no decision has been recorded or that quantity does not apply to this item.

requested_amount.description:
Updated monetary amount requested to be refunded for this line.

This property is tied to the non‑nullable `requested_amount` column in the database but is optional in the update DTO, allowing partial updates. When present, it replaces the previously stored requested amount, subject to validation rules for maximum refundable totals.

Providing null is typically not allowed by business rules even though the DTO technically supports it for alignment with the schema; service logic should treat null as invalid if the line must always have a requested amount.

approved_amount.description:
Updated approved monetary amount for this refund item.

This corresponds to the nullable `approved_amount` column. Reviewers or administrative tools set this to indicate the final approved refund amount at the line level.

Passing null clears any previously recorded approved amount, which may be used when re‑opening or re‑evaluating a refund request item.

currency_code.description:
Updated currency code for the requested and approved amounts on this line.

This maps to the non‑nullable `currency_code` column. In most cases the currency should remain consistent with the parent order; changing it is uncommon and should be tightly controlled by business rules.

When null is provided, service logic should decide whether to reject the update or derive the currency from the parent order rather than leaving the database column unset.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestStatusHistory..description:
Search and filter DTO for querying status history entries of a specific refund request.

This type encapsulates pagination, sorting, and filter options that clients can send in the body of the status history search endpoint. It is designed to work with the `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories` table, which records status transitions for refund requests.

By using a flexible request structure instead of simple query parameters, the API can support rich back‑office use cases such as investigating particular phases of a refund lifecycle, filtering by actor type, or narrowing down to specific time ranges.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve in a paginated result set.

This value is typically 1‑based, where 1 refers to the first page. If omitted, the service may default to the first page.

Clients should combine this with `limit` to implement cursor‑like pagination for status history timelines.

limit.description:
Maximum number of status history records to return in a single page.

This controls the page size for the search results. Reasonable defaults and upper bounds should be enforced by the service to protect performance.

Operators can adjust this value to balance between fewer requests and payload size when browsing long histories.

sort_direction.description:
Direction in which status history entries should be ordered, such as ascending or descending by time.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending. When omitted, implementations commonly default to descending so that the most recent transitions appear first.

Service logic validates the provided value and applies it to the chosen sort field, usually `occurred_at` or `created_at`.

from_occurred_at.description:
Lower bound for the transition time window used when filtering status history records.

When provided, only entries with `occurred_at` greater than or equal to this timestamp should be included in the result set. This helps operators focus on recent or specific investigation periods.

Null indicates that no lower time bound is applied.

to_occurred_at.description:
Upper bound for the transition time window used when filtering status history records.

When provided, only entries with `occurred_at` less than or equal to this timestamp are returned. This allows narrowing the search to a specific date or time interval.

Null means there is no upper time constraint and all later history entries are eligible.

to_status.description:
Filter for the new status value after the transition, as stored in the `to_status` column.

When a value is supplied, only history entries whose `to_status` matches the provided status code are returned. This is useful for focusing on particular lifecycle states, such as `approved` or `rejected`.

Null indicates that no filter is applied based on the destination status.

changed_by_actor_type.description:
Filter for the actor type that caused the status change, matching the `changed_by_actor_type` column.

Valid values depend on the platform’s actor model and typically include identifiers such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `system`. Using this filter helps auditors or operators focus on changes initiated by particular actor categories.

When null, the search does not restrict results by actor type.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestStatusHistory.description:
Detailed refund request status transition record within the shoppingMall platform.

This schema represents a single row in the `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories` table, which acts as an append-only audit log of all lifecycle state changes for a refund request captured in `shopping_mall_refund_requests`. Each history entry documents the previous and new status values, the actor who caused the transition, an optional human-readable explanation, and precise timestamps used for compliance and dispute analysis.

The record is logically a child of a specific refund request and may be associated with different actor types over time, including customers, sellers, admins, or automated system processes. It is primarily consumed by administrative and governance tooling to reconstruct the full history of a refund case and to validate that business and SLA rules were followed across the entire lifecycle.

The fields in this DTO mirror the underlying Prisma model while excluding any session or credential information. They are safe for server-to-admin UI exposure but must still be protected behind appropriate authorization so that only authorized admin actors can access sensitive internal notes or actor attribution details.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this status history record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories` table and uniquely identifies a single lifecycle transition event for a refund request.

It is generated by the system when the history row is inserted and is used for direct retrieval and audit references.

shopping_mall_refund_request_id.description:
Identifier of the parent refund request whose status changed in this history entry.

This field links the history record to a specific row in the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` table, forming a parent–child relationship where each refund request may have many associated status transitions.

Consumers can use this value to group and order all history entries for a refund request when reconstructing its lifecycle timeline.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the customer involved in this status change, when the transition was initiated or directly impacted by a customer actor.

When present, this field references a row in `shopping_mall_customers` indicating which customer triggered or influenced the lifecycle change, for example by submitting a new refund request, providing additional information, or canceling a request.

It is nullable because many transitions, such as admin-driven decisions or automated status progressions, do not have a specific customer actor.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Customer actor identifier associated with this status change, when applicable.

This value is set only when a customer directly triggered or was the primary actor for the transition, and remains null for seller, admin, or system-driven state changes.

It references the `shopping_mall_customers` model for analytical and audit use cases but is not required for every history entry.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the seller involved in this status change, when a seller action caused or acknowledged the transition.

When populated, this field points to a record in `shopping_mall_sellers` and helps attribute decisions such as seller approvals, rejections, or additional information requests related to the refund case.

It is null when the actor is instead a customer, an admin, or an automated process.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Seller actor identifier recorded for this status change, when relevant.

This field is used when a seller response or decision updates the refund request lifecycle, enabling detailed attribution and conflict resolution analysis.

It is optional and null for customer-only or admin-only transitions.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the admin who performed or recorded this status change.

When present, this value references a row in `shopping_mall_admins` indicating which administrative user modified the refund request status or logged an internal decision.

It is null when the transition was made by a customer, seller, or automated system component.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Admin actor identifier for the lifecycle transition, when the change was executed or confirmed by an administrator.

This field supports governance and audit requirements by clearly attributing manual interventions to specific admin accounts.

It is optional and remains null for non-admin-initiated status changes.

oneOf.description:
Previous status value of the refund request before this transition.

This textual code reflects the state from which the refund request moved, such as `requested`, `under_review`, or `approved`. It is primarily used for reconstructing the timeline of state changes and determining how long a request remained in a particular status.

The field may be null for the very first history entry of a refund request, where there is no prior state to reference.

from_status.description:
Refund request status prior to this lifecycle transition, when available.

This field is null for the initial creation event where the refund request did not have a previous state, and non-null for subsequent transitions where the system can log the originating status.

It enables precise tracking of step-by-step state progressions throughout the lifecycle of a refund case.

to_status.description:
New status value of the refund request after this transition.

This string captures the resulting lifecycle state, such as `requested`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `closed`, depending on the platform's configured refund status model.

It is always present and is the primary signal used by analytics, monitoring, and UI components to describe what change occurred at this point in the history.

changed_by_actor_type.description:
Actor type label describing who triggered this status change.

Typical values include high-level categories such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `system`, corresponding to the nature of the actor responsible for the transition. This value complements the specific actor identifier fields and simplifies grouping and filtering history records by actor class.

It is always populated and is especially useful for reporting, risk analysis, and SLA evaluation across different actor segments.

oneOf.description:
Optional free-text explanation describing why this status change occurred.

This field may contain customer-visible explanations, internal notes, or operational comments entered by admins or generated by automated workflows. It can include contextual details such as links to related policies, references to external systems, or summary descriptions of the decision.

Because this content may contain sensitive or internal-only information, client applications must respect authorization policies when rendering it.

reason_description.description:
Human-readable commentary or explanation for the status transition, when provided.

The description can be used to enrich case views for admins or support teams by clarifying the rationale behind a status movement, but it is not guaranteed to be present for every history entry.

Its content should be handled carefully to avoid leaking sensitive details to unauthorized viewers.

occurred_at.description:
Effective timestamp of the status change event.

This timestamp records when the new status took effect in the business sense, which is typically the same as the creation time of the history record but may differ if the system needs to retroactively log an event.

It is used for time-based analytics, SLA evaluation, and chronological reconstruction of the refund request lifecycle.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this status history record was created in the database.

This value reflects when the platform persisted the entry in `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories`, which is usually at or immediately after the time of the underlying status transition.

It is primarily used for auditing persistence behavior and verifying processing pipelines.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this status history record was last updated.

Although history records are conceptually append-only, certain implementations may allow limited corrections or enrichment (for example, fixing typos in comments), in which case this timestamp reflects the most recent modification.

If the implementation never updates history records, this value will typically match `created_at` and still provides a consistent temporal field for sorting and diagnostics.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestReason.IReques.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing refund request reasons in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used as the request body for the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/refundRequestReasons` operation, which retrieves a paginated collection of refund request reason summaries from the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` catalog. It encapsulates pagination parameters, sorting preferences, and domain-specific filters so that administrative tools can efficiently query the configured reason codes.

The schema focuses on configuration discovery rather than transactional data and is intended for internal admin usage. It allows callers to restrict results to active or inactive reasons, filter by applicability to refunds or cancellations, and perform lightweight text search over codes and labels.

All fields are optional so that callers can provide only the filters they need. Reasonable defaults for pagination and sorting should be applied server-side when values are omitted to keep the API ergonomic while still protecting performance and preventing unbounded result sets.

page.description:
Page index for paginated retrieval of refund request reasons.

This value specifies which page of results to return when combined with the `limit` field. A value of `1` represents the first page. When omitted, the server should apply a sensible default, typically the first page.

Administrative UIs can use this field to implement next/previous navigation through large catalogs of reasons without loading the entire dataset at once.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund request reason records to include in a single page.

This parameter controls the page size for results and helps protect the platform from overly large queries. When not provided, the server should select a reasonable default within documented bounds and may enforce an upper limit even if clients request a larger size.

Choosing an appropriate `limit` value allows admin users to balance between the number of visible rows and UI performance.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to refund request reason codes and labels.

This filter allows admins to quickly find specific reasons by entering fragments of the code or human-readable name. Implementations typically perform case-insensitive matching and may search across multiple columns such as `code`, `name`, and `description` in the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` table.

It is optional and can be left empty when only structured filters are needed.

oneOf.description:
Flag indicating whether to restrict results based on the active status of refund request reasons.

When set to `true`, only reasons with `is_active = true` should be returned. When set to `false`, only inactive or disabled reasons should be listed.

If omitted, the server may default to showing only active reasons or apply business-specific rules documented by the platform.

is_active.description:
Optional filter on the activation state of refund request reasons.

This property allows administrators to quickly switch between active, inactive, or all reasons when managing the catalog. Passing `null` or omitting the property typically results in the server choosing a default behavior, such as returning only active reasons.

It is modeled as nullable to make the intent explicit even when no filter is desired.

oneOf.description:
Filter indicating whether returned reasons must be applicable to refund flows.

When `true`, only reasons with `applies_to_refund = true` in `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` should be included in the result set. When `false`, callers can target reasons that are not used for refund operations, such as cancellation-only or internal reasons.

If omitted or null, this filter is not applied and reasons are not constrained by their refund applicability flag.

applies_to_refund.description:
Optional filter on whether reasons apply to refund requests.

This property helps admins focus on reasons that are relevant for post-payment refund cases, for example when reviewing or cleaning up reasons that are never used in refund workflows.

It can be combined with `applies_to_cancellation` to find reasons that apply to both or only one of the two flows.

oneOf.description:
Filter indicating whether returned reasons must be applicable to cancellation flows.

When set to `true`, only reasons whose `applies_to_cancellation` flag is true should be returned. When `false`, results should exclude those cancellation-related reasons and instead show reasons that are either refund-only or internal.

If this field is not provided or is null, no explicit filter on cancellation applicability is enforced by the query.

applies_to_cancellation.description:
Optional filter on whether reasons apply to order cancellation requests.

This field allows governance or operations staff to audit and manage reasons specifically used in pre-fulfillment cancellation workflows, as opposed to post-fulfillment refund flows.

Using this filter in combination with the refund applicability filter enables fine-grained configuration views for mixed-use, refund-only, or cancellation-only reason codes.

order_by.description:
Field name used to sort the refund request reasons in the result set.

Typical values might include `code`, `name`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`, depending on what columns the implementation allows for ordering. When omitted, the server should default to a stable and well-documented sort order, such as by display order then code.

Invalid or unsupported values should be validated and rejected with a clear error response to prevent ambiguous behavior.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering refund request reasons.

Common values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. Implementations may restrict accepted values to this small set and should normalize case if necessary.

If not provided, the server should default to a sensible direction consistent with the chosen `order_by` field, typically ascending for codes and names, or descending for timestamps.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestReason.description:
Refund request reason master data record for the shopping mall platform.

This type represents a single standardized reason code that can be attached to refund or cancellation requests across the marketplace. Each record corresponds to a configuration entry in the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` Prisma model and is used by customers, sellers, and admins when they need to classify why a refund or cancellation is being requested.

The entity is managed primarily by governance and operations teams rather than end-users. It provides machine-friendly identifiers, human-readable labels, and boolean flags that control where and how the reason may be used. Historical references in refund flows and reporting always point back to this configuration to ensure stable semantics over time.

id.description:
Primary key of the refund request reason.

This identifier is generated by the system when a new reason is created and uniquely identifies the configuration row inside the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` table.

Client applications generally use the business `code` field for lookups and display; `id` is mainly used internally by backend components and data pipelines.

code.description:
Unique machine-friendly code representing the refund or cancellation reason, such as `damaged_item` or `customer_changed_mind`.

This value is stored in the `code` column of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` model and is globally unique across all reasons, enforced by a unique index. It is the primary business key used by frontends, workflow engines, and reporting to reference a particular reason.

Clients should treat this code as stable over time; once created and referenced by refund or cancellation records, it should not be repurposed for a different semantic meaning.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the refund or cancellation reason.

This field contains the label shown in administrative tools and, when appropriate, in end-user interfaces. It is typically short and concise, such as "Item arrived damaged" or "Wrong item delivered".

Localization of labels, if needed, should be handled by higher-level localization systems rather than by duplicating records in this table.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of when this refund or cancellation reason should be used.

The underlying Prisma model allows this field to be nullable, so it can be omitted for simple reasons or filled with internal guidance for admins and operations staff. Examples include clarifying which edge cases fall under this reason or instructions about evidence requirements.

Client applications may choose to surface this text in admin consoles or help tooltips but should avoid exposing internal-only guidance to end-users if the wording targets internal staff.

applies_to_cancellation.description:
Indicates whether this reason can be used for cancellation requests.

When `true`, the reason is considered valid in cancellation flows that operate before or during the fulfillment stage of an order. For example, an "order placed by mistake" reason may apply to cancellations but not to refunds after shipment.

Business logic in cancellation APIs should filter available reasons based on this flag to prevent users from selecting reasons that do not conceptually match the cancellation context.

applies_to_refund.description:
Indicates whether this reason can be used for refund requests.

When `true`, the reason is eligible for post-order refund flows such as "item damaged" or "not delivered". This flag is read by refund request creation services to determine which reasons may be selected for a given refund scenario.

Platform reporting and risk analysis may also group and filter refund statistics by reasons that have this flag set.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating if this reason is currently allowed for new refund or cancellation requests.

When `true`, the reason is available for selection in user interfaces and workflow engines, subject to any additional policy constraints. When `false`, the reason is effectively deprecated: existing references remain valid for historical data, but clients should not allow it to be selected for new cases.

Deactivation is the preferred way to retire a reason without breaking existing references from `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, or related aggregates.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request reason record was created.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` and is managed by the system. It provides an audit trail for when the configuration entry first became available.

Clients typically use this field for administrative views or reporting rather than for business behavior in runtime flows.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request reason record was last updated.

This field mirrors the `updated_at` column in the Prisma model and is automatically set by the persistence layer whenever the reason's configuration changes, such as toggling activation flags or editing descriptive text.

Administrative tools can use this timestamp to highlight recently modified reasons or to support troubleshooting and audit scenarios.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestReason.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new refund request reason configuration.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` Prisma model and is used by administrative APIs to onboard additional standardized reasons that can be selected in refund and cancellation flows. It focuses on the business and configuration fields that governance and operations teams control, while leaving system-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` to be populated by the backend.

The create payload defines the unique `code`, human-readable label, optional description, and boolean flags that determine where and how the reason is applicable. It is validated against business rules to ensure uniqueness of `code` and consistency of the applicability flags before a new master-data record is persisted.

code.description:
Unique machine-friendly code representing the refund or cancellation reason to be created.

This value will be stored in the `code` column and must be globally unique across all records in `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons`. Typical examples include `damaged_item`, `wrong_item_shipped`, or `customer_changed_mind`.

Once created and referenced by refund or cancellation records, this code should not be repurposed for different semantics; deactivation via `is_active` is preferred instead of code reuse.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the refund or cancellation reason.

This label will be shown in administrative consoles and, where appropriate, in end-user interfaces as the visible reason text. It should be concise and clearly describe the scenario, for example "Item arrived damaged" or "Order placed by mistake".

The platform may rely on this field in reports and dashboards, so changes should be coordinated with stakeholders when existing reasons are edited.

description.description:
Optional detailed explanation or internal notes about when this reason should be used.

If provided, the text is stored in the `description` column of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` table. It can describe the intended business scenarios, edge cases, or evidence expectations associated with this reason.

When `null` or omitted in the request, the reason will still be valid but will not carry additional explanatory text beyond its `name`.

applies_to_cancellation.description:
Flag specifying whether this new reason should be available for cancellation workflows.

When set to `true`, cancellation-related APIs and UIs may present this reason as a selectable option when users cancel orders or individual order items before fulfillment. When `false`, the reason is excluded from cancellation contexts and may be restricted to refund scenarios only.

Correctly configuring this flag is important to avoid user confusion and to keep analytics for cancellations logically separated from refund behavior.

applies_to_refund.description:
Flag specifying whether this new reason should be available for refund workflows.

A value of `true` indicates that refund request creation flows may reference this reason, for example when a product is damaged or not delivered. A value of `false` limits the reason to other flows such as pure cancellations.

Governance teams should align this setting with policy and reporting requirements so that refund statistics by reason remain meaningful.

is_active.description:
Initial activation status for the new reason.

When `true`, the reason becomes immediately usable in applicable flows (refund and/or cancellation) after creation, subject to feature flags and other policy checks. When `false`, the reason is created in an inactive state and cannot be selected until explicitly activated in a later update.

Using an inactive initial state is useful when preparing configuration changes ahead of a coordinated rollout or when testing behavior in non-production environments.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestReason.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing refund or cancellation reason in the shopping mall platform.

This type maps to the mutable configuration columns of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` Prisma model, which catalogs structured reason codes used across refund and cancellation flows. It allows administrators to change human‑readable labels, descriptive guidance, applicability flags, and activation status while preserving the immutable business key supplied via the URL path.

The DTO is used specifically by the `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/refundRequestReasons/{reasonCode}` operation. The `reasonCode` path parameter identifies which record to update, so the request body contains only mutable fields and does not repeat or modify that identity value. All properties in this DTO are optional to support partial updates; the service layer applies only the fields that are present in the payload.

name.description:
Human‑readable display name of the refund or cancellation reason.

This value is shown in administrative tooling, reporting dashboards, and possibly in curated UI lists when staff manage refund flows. Typical examples include "Customer changed mind", "Item damaged", or "Payment issue".

When present in the update payload, the backend replaces the existing name with the supplied value after applying any domain validation rules (for example, length or reserved word checks).

description.description:
Long‑form descriptive text that explains when and how this reason should be used.

This prose is written primarily for internal staff and administrators to ensure consistent classification of refund and cancellation scenarios. It can include guidance, edge‑case examples, and policy references.

Passing `null` clears the existing description, while omitting the property leaves the current value unchanged.

applies_to_cancellation.description:
Flag indicating whether this reason is available for use on cancellation requests.

When true, business logic may allow customers, sellers, or admins (depending on their role) to select this reason when initiating or processing cancellation flows. When false, the reason should not be presented in cancellation reason pickers but remains valid historically for analytics.

Updating this flag affects only future behavior and does not alter historical records that already reference the reason.

applies_to_refund.description:
Flag indicating whether this reason is available for use on refund requests.

When true, the reason can be selected when creating or managing refund cases that rely on the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` and `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` tables. When false, the reason is hidden from new refund flows while still remaining in historical records.

Typical configurations enable this flag for reasons like `damaged_item` or `not_delivered` that conceptually apply to monetary refunds.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this reason is currently active and selectable in new cancellation or refund flows.

When set to false, the reason becomes effectively deprecated for new use but remains available for historical reporting and analytics. Admins may deactivate reasons that were incorrectly configured, are no longer aligned with policy, or have been superseded by more precise alternatives.

Deactivation must not violate legal or governance constraints, especially when the reason is referenced by legal holds, SLA configurations, or policy versions.

IShoppingMallDispute.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for retrieving a paginated list of disputes from the `shopping_mall_disputes` table.

This request body is consumed by the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/disputes` endpoint and encapsulates rich filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria that administrators use to build dispute work queues. It allows filtering by status, type, severity, related order and refund identifiers, date ranges, and ownership, as well as controlling page size and sort order.

All fields in this DTO are optional. When a property is omitted, that dimension is not constrained and the backend applies its default behavior, including reasonable defaults for pagination and sorting. Service-level validation may still enforce additional rules such as requiring at least one filter or constraining allowed values for certain fields.

page.description:
1‑based index of the result page to retrieve.

This controls which slice of the overall dispute result set is returned. When omitted, the implementation should default to the first page. Values less than 1 should be rejected as invalid input.

limit.description:
Maximum number of dispute summaries to return in a single page.

This value is used in conjunction with `page` to calculate offset and page size in the query against `shopping_mall_disputes`. Service‑level limits may cap this value to a reasonable upper bound to protect performance and prevent abuse.

status.description:
Lifecycle status filter for disputes, such as `open`, `under_investigation`, `resolved`, or `closed`.

When specified, only disputes whose `status` field in `shopping_mall_disputes` matches the given value are returned. The allowed set of status codes is governed by business configuration and may be enforced at the validation layer.

type.description:
High‑level dispute type filter.

Typical values align with the `type` column in `shopping_mall_disputes`, for example `payment_chargeback`, `refund_dispute`, or `policy_violation`. When provided, only disputes of the given type are included in the results.

severity.description:
Severity level filter for disputes.

This corresponds to the `severity` column and is used to prioritize workload in admin dashboards. Common values include `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `critical`. When present, the query restricts results to disputes with the specified severity.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Filter by the primary order associated with the dispute.

When supplied, only disputes whose `shopping_mall_order_id` matches this UUID are returned. This is commonly used when navigating from an order detail view to see all related disputes.

shopping_mall_refund_request_id.description:
Filter by the refund request associated with the dispute.

If set, the search is constrained to disputes where `shopping_mall_refund_request_id` equals the provided UUID, enabling workflows that start from a refund case and pivot into disputes.

shopping_mall_payment_chargeback_id.description:
Filter by the payment chargeback associated with the dispute.

This is particularly relevant for chargeback‑originated disputes where the `shopping_mall_payment_chargeback_id` column links the dispute to a specific payment chargeback record.

shopping_mall_risk_case_id.description:
Filter by the risk case associated with the dispute.

Allows risk and governance teams to retrieve disputes tied to a particular risk investigation tracked in the `shopping_mall_risk_cases` table.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Filter by the admin currently assigned as the owner of the dispute.

When specified, the search returns only disputes whose `shopping_mall_admin_id` field matches this UUID. This is used to build personal queues for individual admins or to balance workloads across the team.

opened_from.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range filter for disputes.

When set, only disputes with `opened_at` greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This parameter is typically used together with `opened_to` to limit results to a specific reporting window. It can also be supplied alone to express an open-ended range from a given time onward.

opened_to.description:
End of the creation timestamp range filter for disputes.

When set, only disputes with `opened_at` less than or equal to this timestamp are included. Combined with `opened_from`, it defines a closed interval for dispute creation time. It can also be supplied alone to express an open-ended range up to a given time.

sort_field.description:
Name of the field used to sort the dispute results.

Common values include `opened_at`, `resolved_at`, `severity`, or `status`. The backend should restrict this to a whitelist of sortable columns to avoid exposing internal implementation details or enabling inefficient queries. When omitted, the implementation typically defaults to sorting by `opened_at` in descending order.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering dispute results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending. When omitted, the service may default to descending order so that the most recently opened or updated disputes appear first.

IShoppingMallDispute.description:
Dispute header entity for the ShoppingMall platform.

This type models the core record stored in the `shopping_mall_disputes` Prisma table. It represents high-level disputes covering conflicts around orders, refunds, chargebacks, or policy violations and is the central object used by customers, sellers, and admins to track case status.

The schema focuses on business-visible attributes and primary relationships such as linked orders, refund requests, and risk or legal context. It surfaces both scalar identifiers and contextual summary relations so that a single GET response can provide a complete dispute view without forcing clients to issue multiple follow-up API calls.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_disputes` table and is used internally by the platform for joins and low-level lookups. It is not normally exposed in URL paths, which instead use `dispute_code` as a stable business identifier.

dispute_code.description:
Business-visible identifier for the dispute case.

The `dispute_code` column on `shopping_mall_disputes` is globally unique and is the stable business key used in URLs and notifications. All update and retrieval operations that reference a dispute by code depend on this value to locate the correct row.

type.description:
High-level dispute type classification.

Typical values include categories such as `payment_chargeback`, `refund_dispute`, or `policy_violation`. The exact allowed set is governed by platform policy configuration and may be validated against business rules defined in policy-related tables.

severity.description:
Business-defined severity level for this dispute.

Severity is used for prioritization and operational workflows. Common patterns include levels such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`, and may influence SLA deadlines and escalation behavior tied to `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the dispute.

Represents the main state of the dispute in its lifecycle, such as `open`, `under_investigation`, `resolved`, or `closed`. Status transitions are typically tracked in subsidiary event tables and may be constrained by SLA and legal hold rules.

summary.description:
Short human-readable summary of the dispute.

This field contains a concise description used in dashboards and list views to quickly understand the nature of the dispute. It is optional and may be null when a summary has not been recorded.

description.description:
Detailed description of the dispute.

Provides full narrative context and notes about the situation. It is primarily intended for admin and risk team consumption and can be used to capture investigation findings and background details.

opened_at.description:
Timestamp when the dispute was opened.

This value marks the time when the dispute record was created or first moved into an active state. It is used as an anchor for SLA calculations and reporting on dispute volume over time.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when the dispute was resolved.

Recorded when a final resolution decision is made, such as acceptance, rejection, or other terminal outcome. Null when the dispute has not yet been resolved.

closed_at.description:
Timestamp when the dispute was fully closed.

Represents the moment when no further actions are expected on the dispute, which may follow the resolution time in cases where post-resolution tasks must be completed. Null when the dispute is still open or under investigation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute record was created.

This is the system-level creation time of the row in `shopping_mall_disputes`, used for auditing and chronological reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute record was last updated.

Automatically updated when mutable fields on the dispute header change. It is useful for synchronization and cache invalidation in client applications.

order_id.description:
Internal UUID of the primary order associated with this dispute.

Backed by the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key column that links the dispute to a row in `shopping_mall_orders`. Null when the dispute is not directly tied to a single order record.

refund_request_id.description:
Internal UUID of a related refund request.

Maps to `shopping_mall_refund_request_id`, connecting the dispute to an entry in `shopping_mall_refund_requests` when the dispute is refund-centric. Null when not applicable.

payment_chargeback_id.description:
Internal UUID of an associated payment chargeback case.

Stores the value of `shopping_mall_payment_chargeback_id` when the dispute originates from or is linked to a payment chargeback. Null when there is no direct chargeback relationship.

risk_case_id.description:
Internal UUID of the related risk case.

Backed by `shopping_mall_risk_case_id`, linking the dispute to a row in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`. This is used when disputes are part of broader fraud or risk investigations.

legal_hold_id.description:
Internal UUID of a legal hold record constraining this dispute.

Derived from `shopping_mall_legal_hold_id` and used when the dispute falls under specific legal preservation requirements that prevent modifications or deletions.

owner_admin_id.description:
Internal UUID of the admin currently owning or handling this dispute.

Reflects the `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key, pointing to a row in `shopping_mall_admins`. It is used by admin tooling to assign and route disputes among handlers.

case_sla_config_id.description:
Internal UUID of the SLA configuration governing this dispute.

Matches `shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` and indicates which row in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` defines the expected response and resolution timings for this dispute type.

order.description:
Optional contextual summary of the order primarily associated with this dispute.

When `order_id` is present, this relation provides a lightweight `IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary` so that operators can see core order details alongside the dispute without issuing a separate order lookup. It is null when the dispute is not directly tied to a single order.

refundRequest.description:
Optional contextual summary of the refund request associated with this dispute.

When `refund_request_id` is set, this relation surfaces a compact `IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ISummary` to give immediate visibility into the main refund case that the dispute concerns. It is null when no refund request is linked.

paymentChargeback.description:
Optional contextual summary of the payment chargeback linked to this dispute.
