When `payment_chargeback_id` references a row in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`, this property exposes a summary view so finance and risk teams can inspect the chargeback context without additional API calls. It is null when the dispute is not chargeback-based.

riskCase.description:
Optional contextual summary of the risk case associated with this dispute.

When `risk_case_id` points to a record in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, this relation provides a compact view of the broader risk investigation, helping governance and fraud teams understand the surrounding case landscape. It is null when no risk case is linked.

legalHold.description:
Optional contextual summary of the legal hold that constrains this dispute.

When `legal_hold_id` references a row in `shopping_mall_legal_holds`, this property surfaces key legal hold metadata, allowing admins and compliance staff to see preservation constraints directly in the dispute view. It is null when the dispute is not subject to a specific legal hold.

ownerAdmin.description:
Optional summary of the administrator currently owning or handling this dispute.

When `owner_admin_id` is set, this relation exposes a compact `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary` so that dashboards and case lists can show handler information without additional admin lookups. It is null when the dispute is unassigned or handled through a shared queue.

slaConfig.description:
Optional summary of the SLA configuration governing this dispute.

When `case_sla_config_id` is present, this relation surfaces the corresponding `IShoppingMallCaseSlaConfig.ISummary` so that operators can immediately see the SLA expectations that apply to the dispute without querying SLA configuration APIs separately. It is null when the dispute is not bound to a specific SLA configuration row.

IShoppingMallDispute.ICreate.description:
Request body DTO for creating a new dispute case in the ShoppingMall platform backed by the `shopping_mall_disputes` Prisma model.

This type captures the subset of dispute header fields that are writable by clients at creation time, such as subject classification, initial severity, free-form description, and references to related business entities like orders, refund requests, or chargebacks.

System-managed attributes including primary key, lifecycle timestamps, ownership, SLA configuration linkage, and legal hold associations are excluded and are instead populated by the backend according to platform policies and Prisma defaults.

dispute_code.description:
Optional business-visible identifier for the dispute case used across admin tools and communications.

If provided, this value will be stored in `shopping_mall_disputes.dispute_code` and must respect the uniqueness constraint enforced at the database level.

In many deployments the server generates this code automatically from a sequence or pattern, in which case clients should omit the field or explicitly send null so that the backend assigns a value.

type.description:
High-level dispute type, such as `payment_chargeback`, `refund_dispute`, `policy_violation`, or another configured type.

This value is persisted into `shopping_mall_disputes.type` and determines which workflows, policies, and SLA configurations are applied to the case.

Clients must supply a value that is valid within the business policy configuration; validation logic in the service will reject unknown or unsupported types.

severity.description:
Initial severity level chosen for the dispute, such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_disputes.severity` and is used to prioritize queues, notifications, and workload distribution.

Policies may restrict which actors can assign higher severities; for example, customers might be constrained to a limited set while admins can escalate severity.

summary.description:
Short human-readable summary describing the nature of the dispute for quick scanning in dashboards.

On creation this is stored in `shopping_mall_disputes.summary` and typically comes from a free-form text field in the UI such as "Non-delivery of order" or "Unauthorized charge".

If omitted or null, the system may derive a default summary from the dispute type and related entities, but providing a concise summary is recommended for usability.

description.description:
Detailed description of the dispute written by the initiating actor.

The content is saved to `shopping_mall_disputes.description` and can contain multi-paragraph text explaining the problem, relevant history, and desired outcome.

Because it may include sensitive information, platform operators should ensure that only authorized parties (for example, involved sellers and admins) can view the full text.

opened_at.description:
Optional explicit timestamp indicating when the dispute was opened from a business perspective.

If provided, the value will be written to `shopping_mall_disputes.opened_at`; otherwise, the backend will typically set it to the current server time at creation.

Custom timestamps are primarily useful for backfilling historical disputes or integrating external dispute events; most interactive clients should omit this field.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Optional reference to the order primarily associated with this dispute, stored in `shopping_mall_disputes.shopping_mall_order_id`.

When the dispute concerns a specific checkout or fulfillment, clients should populate this field with the UUID of the corresponding order record from `shopping_mall_orders`.

If the dispute is not tied to a single order, the field should be omitted or set to null and relevant context can be provided in the free-form description.

shopping_mall_refund_request_id.description:
Optional reference to the refund request that triggered or is central to this dispute, persisted in `shopping_mall_disputes.shopping_mall_refund_request_id`.

Use this field when the initiating actor is disputing a decision or outcome associated with an existing refund case in `shopping_mall_refund_requests`.

When omitted or null, the dispute is treated as not being centered on a specific refund request and may rely on other identifiers such as order id or payment chargeback id.

shopping_mall_payment_chargeback_id.description:
Optional reference to a payment chargeback record associated with this dispute, written to `shopping_mall_disputes.shopping_mall_payment_chargeback_id`.

This is typically set when the dispute originates from or is tightly coupled to a chargeback stored in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`.

If the dispute does not involve a formal chargeback, clients should omit or null this field and instead rely on order or refund references to provide context.

shopping_mall_risk_case_id.description:
Optional reference to a risk case that tracks broader risk analysis related to this dispute, stored in `shopping_mall_disputes.shopping_mall_risk_case_id`.

This is mainly used by internal admin or risk tooling when creating disputes from an existing `shopping_mall_risk_cases` record, so that both entities remain linked.

For customer-initiated disputes from the storefront, this field is generally left null and risk cases, if any, are created separately by backend workflows.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaConfig.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a case SLA configuration rule for cancellations, refunds, and disputes within the shopping mall platform.

This type is optimized for listing and quick inspection scenarios where operators or configuration UIs need to display current SLA rules without loading full policy graphs. It exposes the main identifying fields, actor and case classification, and time thresholds that define the SLA behavior.

Use this schema when embedding SLA configuration information in administrative dashboards, policy overviews, and rule selection widgets, or when returning paginated collections of SLA rules.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the case SLA configuration.

This property maps directly to the `id` primary key column in the `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` Prisma model and is a stable UUID for the lifetime of the configuration record.

It is used as the canonical reference when updating or deactivating a specific SLA rule.

shopping_mall_business_policy_version_id.description:
Optional identifier of the business policy version associated with this SLA rule.

This field corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_business_policy_version_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, which references `shopping_mall_policy_versions`.

When present, it ties the SLA thresholds to a concrete policy version for governance and audit; when null, the SLA may represent a global or default rule not bound to a specific version document.

case_type.description:
Logical type of case that this SLA applies to, such as `cancellation`, `refund`, or `dispute`.

The value is stored in the non-nullable `case_type` column on `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` and is used to scope the SLA rule to a particular case domain.

Clients should treat this as a constrained string domain governed by business configuration and use it for filtering and grouping SLA rules by case category.

actor_role.description:
Actor role whose behavior is governed by this SLA, for example `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`.

This property maps to the non-nullable `actor_role` column in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. It indicates which participant in the case lifecycle must meet the timing expectations defined by this rule.

It is commonly used in administrative tools to segment SLA policies per role and to drive notification or escalation logic for specific actor types.

action_type.description:
Action that is constrained by this SLA, such as `initial_response` or `final_decision`.

This value is stored in the non-nullable `action_type` column on `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. It describes which stage or step in the case handling workflow the timing thresholds apply to.

Using this field, clients can differentiate SLA rules for early acknowledgment, investigation, and final resolution actions within the same case type.

target_duration_seconds.description:
Target time window, in whole seconds, within which the governed action should be completed.

This property directly corresponds to the non-nullable `target_duration_seconds` integer column in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. It represents the primary SLA threshold measured from the relevant case start time or previous event.

Operational tooling and background monitors use this value to compute due times, trigger escalations, and flag potential SLA breaches.

warning_duration_seconds.description:
Optional warning offset, in whole seconds, before the SLA breach time at which a warning should be raised.

This field maps to the nullable `warning_duration_seconds` column on `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. When set, it allows the platform to generate early notifications or dashboard indicators ahead of the actual SLA deadline.

When null, no explicit pre-breach warning is configured and the system may only signal at or after the point of SLA violation.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this SLA rule is currently active for new cases.

This property reflects the non-nullable `is_active` column in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. Active rules are eligible to be applied when new cancellation, refund, or dispute cases are created.

Administrators can toggle this flag to phase in or retire SLA configurations without removing historical records used for audit and reporting.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA configuration record was created.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` and is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time.

It is used for auditing configuration lifecycle events and for time-based filtering when analyzing policy evolution.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA configuration record was last updated.

This property maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column on `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. It is automatically updated whenever configuration details such as durations, case type, or activation state change.

Clients can leverage this field to detect stale data in local caches and to present change history in administrative interfaces.

IShoppingMallDisputeParty.description:
Represents a single party participating in a dispute case within the shopping mall governance domain.

Each record links a dispute from the shopping_mall_disputes table to a concrete actor entity such as a customer, seller, admin, or an external party. It captures the actor type, the party's specific role in the dispute, an optional display name for use in admin tools, and audit timestamps.

This DTO is optimized for administrative dispute management views where staff need to understand who is involved in a dispute and how they are classified, while relying on separate APIs to retrieve full customer, seller, or admin profiles when required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute party record.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_dispute_parties table and is used to reference this party in update, retrieval, and audit operations.

It is generated by the system at creation time and is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

actor_type.description:
High-level classification of the participating actor in the dispute.

Typical values include customer, seller, admin, or external, and are used to interpret which underlying actor foreign key is populated (for example shopping_mall_customer_id when the actor is a customer).

Admin tools rely on this field to route governance workflows and to decide which additional profile information can be loaded for the party.

role.description:
Role of this party in the context of the dispute.

Examples include complainant, respondent, witness, or observer, and may be further specialized according to platform policy.

Governance and risk dashboards use this field to display how each party is positioned within the dispute and to filter or group parties by their procedural stance.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable name shown in administrative dispute tools for this party.

When the party is a customer, seller, or admin, this value is often derived from the corresponding profile; for external parties it may be manually entered by staff.

The field is nullable to support cases where no friendly label is available and the UI falls back to an identifier-based representation.

dispute.description:
Summary information about the parent dispute to which this party belongs.

This reference is derived using the shopping_mall_dispute_id foreign key from the shopping_mall_dispute_parties table and points to the primary dispute record in shopping_mall_disputes.

Including this summary allows admin tooling to see core dispute attributes alongside the party without requiring a separate dispute detail fetch for basic context.

customer.description:
Customer actor associated with this dispute party when actor_type indicates a customer.

This object is populated when shopping_mall_customer_id is set on the underlying record and provides a lightweight summary of the customer for governance interfaces.

When the party is not a customer, this property is null so that UIs can reliably distinguish which underlying actor type is active.

seller.description:
Seller actor associated with this dispute party when actor_type indicates a seller.

It is derived from the shopping_mall_seller_id foreign key and provides summary-level seller information such as basic identity and status for administrative views.

If the party is not a seller this property is null, allowing clients to handle actor-type specific rendering logic without ambiguity.

admin.description:
Admin actor associated with this dispute party when actor_type indicates an administrative participant.

The value is driven by the shopping_mall_admin_id foreign key on the shopping_mall_dispute_parties row and contains a compact summary of the admin account.

For non-admin parties this property is null so that administrative tools can clearly see whether the party corresponds to an internal staff member.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute party record was first created.

The value is stored in the created_at column of the shopping_mall_dispute_parties table and reflects the moment the party was attached to the dispute.

It is managed exclusively by the backend and is useful for auditing, timeline reconstruction, and SLA calculations.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute party record was last updated.

It reflects the most recent modification of any mutable attribute on the row, such as role or display_name, and is sourced from the updated_at column.

Admin tools can use this value to detect stale information and to sequence changes in the dispute history.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvent.description:
Dispute event DTO representing a single timeline entry in the lifecycle of a dispute.

This type is backed by the `shopping_mall_dispute_events` Prisma model and exposes all business-relevant fields required for administrative inspection, including the event type, status transition, actor context, description, and timestamps. Each instance corresponds to a single immutable history record associated with a parent dispute in `shopping_mall_disputes`.

The DTO is designed for admin and governance tools that need to render a detailed, auditable view of what happened during dispute handling, while omitting low-level implementation details. It may be enriched on the read side with contextual information about the related dispute and parties through separate DTOs when needed, but this base type focuses on the event record itself.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute event.

This field maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_dispute_events` table and is generated by the system when the event record is created. It is used by admin tools and APIs to address a specific event, such as in paths like `/disputes/{disputeCode}/events/{disputeEventId}`.

Clients never supply this value in create or update requests; it is read-only and always present on responses.

dispute.description:
Summary of the dispute to which this event belongs.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_dispute_id` foreign key in the read DTO and exposes key dispute information needed to understand the context of the event without additional lookups.

Using the `.ISummary` variant prevents circular references while still providing human-readable identifiers and status for the parent dispute.

admin.description:
Admin actor who performed or recorded this event, when applicable.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key and provides a summarized view of the administrator responsible for the action, including identity and key profile fields used in admin tooling.

The property is nullable because some events may be system-generated or initiated by non-admin actors.

customer.description:
Customer associated with this event when the event is customer-initiated or customer-facing.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key and allows admin interfaces to present customer identity and basic profile details in the event timeline.

When null, the event does not directly involve a customer actor.

seller.description:
Seller associated with this event when the event is seller-initiated or seller-facing.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and enables timelines to show which seller participated in the event, using a lightweight seller summary.

When null, the event does not directly involve a seller actor.

event_type.description:
Business-level type or category of the dispute event.

This field corresponds to the `event_type` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and captures the semantic meaning of the event, such as `created`, `note_added`, `status_changed`, `escalated`, or `evidence_added`.

Downstream consumers such as admin UIs and reporting systems rely on this value to group and filter events, drive iconography in timelines, and enforce business rules tied to specific event categories.

oneOf.description:
Dispute status before this event occurred, when the event represents a status transition.

This value mirrors the `status_before` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and usually matches one of the allowed statuses defined on the parent `shopping_mall_disputes` record, such as `open`, `under_investigation`, `resolved`, or `closed`.

For events unrelated to status changes this field may be null.

status_before.description:
Previous dispute status recorded at the time of this event.

Used primarily for auditing and analytic purposes, this field enables reconstruction of the status timeline for a dispute and helps diagnose how and when state changes occurred.

It is optional and left null for events that do not involve a status transition.

oneOf.description:
Dispute status after this event occurred, when the event changes the dispute status.

This field reflects the `status_after` column and should align with the set of statuses supported by the `shopping_mall_disputes` model. It records the new state reached as a result of the business action represented by the event.

For non-status-changing events this property may remain null.

status_after.description:
New dispute status that resulted from this event, if a status transition occurred.

Together with `status_before` this property provides a clear audit trail of how a dispute moved through its lifecycle and supports SLA and policy analysis.

It is nullable to accommodate events that do not modify dispute status.

oneOf.description:
Human-readable description or note text explaining this event.

This value corresponds to the `description` column in `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and typically contains free-form text entered by admins or generated by the system to summarize what happened.

It is used heavily in admin and governance interfaces to provide narrative context around each timeline entry.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of the event suitable for display in admin timelines and audit logs.

The description can include reasons for the action, instructions for follow-up, or any other commentary that helps reviewers understand the significance of the event.

The field is optional and may be null for purely system-driven or self-explanatory event types where no additional text is needed.

occurred_at.description:
Business timestamp indicating when this event occurred.

This field maps to the `occurred_at` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and should reflect the time of the underlying business action rather than the time of record insertion alone.

It is distinct from `created_at` to allow recording of historical or externally sourced events whose effective time precedes their registration in the system.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp for this dispute event record.

This value corresponds to the `created_at` column and is set automatically when the row is inserted into `shopping_mall_dispute_events`. It provides an immutable audit marker for when the event was persisted.

Clients cannot modify this field; it is read-only and always present in responses.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp for this dispute event record.

This field maps to the `updated_at` column and is updated whenever mutable fields on the event are changed according to business rules. It supports basic concurrency control, cache invalidation, and audit queries.

Like `created_at`, it is managed by the system and not directly controlled by clients.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvidence.description:
Dispute evidence DTO representing a single evidence artifact attached to a dispute case in the shopping mall platform.

This type is backed by the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model, which stores metadata and references for documents, images, message logs, or external system records that support the investigation and resolution of a `shopping_mall_disputes` row. Each evidence row is always linked to exactly one dispute and may optionally be linked to a specific dispute event.

The DTO exposes business-relevant metadata such as evidence type, title, human-readable description, and a URI pointing to the actual evidence content managed by external storage. It also includes the dispute identifier, optional dispute event linkage, and optional actor identifiers for the admin, customer, or seller who provided the evidence. Timestamps are mapped directly from the Prisma schema and allow consumers to understand when the evidence was created and last updated.

In addition, this DTO surfaces lightweight association summaries for the related dispute, dispute event, and participating actors so that callers can render rich administrative views without issuing additional lookups when those relations are eagerly loaded.

id.description:
Primary key of the dispute evidence.

This value corresponds to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` table and uniquely identifies a single evidence artifact within the platform.

It is generated by the system and is used by administrative APIs and tooling to reference and retrieve concrete pieces of dispute evidence.

shopping_mall_dispute_id.description:
Identifier of the dispute that this evidence supports.

This field maps to the `shopping_mall_dispute_id` foreign key column on the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` table and references the parent row in `shopping_mall_disputes`.

It is used internally to enforce that every evidence record belongs to exactly one dispute and to scope evidence retrieval to the proper dispute context.

shopping_mall_dispute_event_id.description:
Identifier of the specific dispute event that introduced this evidence, when applicable.

This field corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_dispute_event_id` foreign key column in `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` and points to a row in `shopping_mall_dispute_events`.

When null, the evidence is associated directly with the dispute but not with a particular timeline event.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who attached this evidence, when the evidence was supplied by an administrator.

This field maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key column and references the `shopping_mall_admins` table.

When null, the evidence was not submitted by an admin or the actor is represented by another actor-specific foreign key.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who provided this evidence, when relevant.

This field corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key in `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` and references `shopping_mall_customers`.

When null, the evidence was not directly attributed to a customer actor.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who provided this evidence, when relevant.

This field maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and references the `shopping_mall_sellers` table.

When null, the evidence was not directly submitted by a seller actor.

evidence_type.description:
Type of evidence stored in this record.

This value is taken from the non-nullable `evidence_type` column of the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model and is expected to represent categories such as `image`, `document`, `message_log`, or `external_reference`.

Downstream business logic and administrative UIs rely on this type to determine how to render, filter, and process the attached evidence content.

title.description:
Short title or label that describes this evidence in administrative tools.

This field maps to the nullable `title` column and is used to provide a concise, human-readable name for the evidence, such as "Customer screenshot" or "Payment provider statement".

When null, only the evidence type or URI may be available to identify the evidence item.

description.description:
Detailed description or notes about what this evidence shows or why it is relevant.

This property corresponds to the nullable `description` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` table and typically contains free-form text entered by an admin, customer, or seller.

It is used by dispute handlers to quickly understand the context of the evidence without immediately opening the underlying resource.

uri.description:
URI pointing to the stored evidence content in external storage or another system.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `uri` column on the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` model and should contain a fully qualified URI that the platform or back-office tools can dereference.

Only metadata and URIs are stored in this table; the actual binary content lives in separate storage services that are referenced via this URI.

checksum.description:
Optional checksum or hash of the evidence content for integrity verification.

This property reflects the nullable `checksum` column in the Prisma schema. It is typically populated with a cryptographic hash (such as SHA-256) of the underlying evidence bytes.

When present, downstream systems can compare the stored checksum with recalculated values to detect tampering or unexpected modifications of the evidence content.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute evidence record was created.

This value is taken from the non-nullable `created_at` column on the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` table and is set by the system at insertion time.

It allows consumers to reconstruct the temporal order in which different evidence items were attached to a dispute and to build timelines for auditing or investigation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute evidence record was last updated.

This property maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` model and is automatically maintained by the system whenever mutable fields of the evidence change.

It provides visibility into recent edits or corrections made to an evidence entry, which is important for auditability and governance.

dispute.description:
Summary of the dispute that this evidence supports.

This association is a lightweight view over the parent `shopping_mall_disputes` row and is populated when the evidence is loaded together with its dispute context.

Clients can use this summary to render dispute-level information (such as code, status, and high-level subject) alongside the evidence without issuing a separate dispute lookup.

dispute_event.description:
Summary of the dispute event that introduced this evidence, when applicable.

This association references a single row from `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and is populated when the evidence is linked to a specific timeline event in the dispute lifecycle.

When null, the evidence is associated with the dispute in general rather than a particular event in the timeline.

admin.description:
Summary of the administrator recorded as the submitter of this evidence, when applicable.

This association is a lightweight view over the `shopping_mall_admins` actor and is typically populated when `shopping_mall_admin_id` is not null.

It allows dispute consoles and governance tools to show who attached the evidence without requiring an additional admin lookup.

customer.description:
Summary of the customer who provided this evidence, when applicable.

This association is backed by `shopping_mall_customer_id` and exposes a compact view of the customer actor involved in the dispute.

When present, it helps operators understand which customer contributed the evidence in multi-actor disputes.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller who provided this evidence, when applicable.

This association is backed by `shopping_mall_seller_id` and exposes a compact view of the seller actor involved in the dispute.

When present, it helps operators quickly identify the merchant that supplied the evidence in the context of the dispute.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaViolation.description:
Case SLA violation entity representing a single detected breach of a configured SLA rule for cancellation, refund, or dispute cases.

This type maps directly to a row in the `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` Prisma model and is used mainly by administrative and governance tooling. It exposes the violated SLA configuration, the concrete business case that missed its deadline, timestamps for detection, and classification attributes that allow operations and risk teams to analyze SLA performance over time.

The entity is read-only from the perspective of API consumers and is typically retrieved via detail-style GET operations. It links to SLA configuration and specific case entities using summary relations that provide business context without exposing raw foreign key columns or large child collections.

id.description:
Primary key of the case SLA violation.

This identifier uniquely represents a single SLA breach record in the `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` table and is used as the stable reference in detail retrieval APIs and audit trails.

shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id.description:
Identifier of the cancellation request whose handling breached this SLA, when the violation is tied to a cancellation case.

This field is nullable because not all SLA violations are cancellations. When populated, it links the violation to a specific row in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` for deep-dive investigation and cross-referencing with cancellation workflows.

case_type.description:
Type of business case that violated the SLA.

This value mirrors the `case_type` column in the `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` table and typically distinguishes between major case categories such as `cancellation`, `refund`, or `dispute`. It is used heavily in reporting, filtering, and policy analysis for SLA performance per case class.

actor_role.description:
Role of the actor that was expected to satisfy the SLA for this case.

Common examples are `seller`, `admin`, or `customer`, matching the values used in SLA configuration. This attribute helps governance teams identify which actor group is consistently missing response or resolution targets and drives process or policy changes.

action_type.description:
Action governed by the SLA that was violated.

Typical values include conceptual actions such as `initial_response` or `final_decision`. Together with `case_type` and `actor_role`, it allows the system to pinpoint which specific lifecycle step breached its configured time window.

breach_duration_seconds.description:
Number of seconds by which the SLA was exceeded beyond the configured target duration.

This integer is calculated at detection time using the SLA target and the actual completion or reference timestamps. It is used in analytics and risk dashboards to quantify the severity of SLA breaches and to identify systemic delays.

detected_at.description:
Timestamp when the system detected that this SLA violation had occurred.

This value typically reflects when monitoring logic or scheduled jobs concluded that the SLA window had been exceeded. It is distinct from the original deadline and is important for understanding monitoring latency and alerting timeliness.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA violation record was created in the database.

The value is managed by the persistence layer and is used for auditing and time-based filtering of violation records, for example when generating operational reports for a given period.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA violation record was last updated.

Updates can occur when additional classification or linkage information is attached after the initial detection, such as linking the violation to new analytics or policy entities.

slaConfig.description:
Summary view of the SLA configuration that was violated.

This relation is derived from the underlying `shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` foreign key and provides compact context about the SLA rule, including case type, actor role, action type, and target duration, without exposing internal identifiers or full configuration payloads.

cancellationRequest.description:
Optional summary of the cancellation request associated with this SLA violation.

When the violation relates to a cancellation case, this property exposes a lightweight view of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` row so that admins can quickly understand the underlying business situation without making additional API calls. It is null for non-cancellation case types.

refundRequest.description:
Optional summary of the refund request associated with this SLA violation.

When the violation relates to a refund case, this property exposes a lightweight view of the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` row so that admins can quickly understand the underlying business situation without querying the refund API separately. It is null for non-refund case types.

dispute.description:
Optional summary of the dispute associated with this SLA violation.

When the case type is a dispute, this property references a compact `IShoppingMallDispute.ISummary` object, giving operators immediate access to high-level dispute details alongside the SLA breach information. It is null when the violation does not involve a dispute case.

IShoppingMallDispute.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for mutable fields of a ShoppingMall dispute.

This DTO is used as the request body for `PUT /shoppingMall/{actor}/disputes/{disputeCode}` operations and maps to the `shopping_mall_disputes` Prisma table. It intentionally includes only those columns that are considered mutable after creation, such as display metadata, categorization, severity, and certain lifecycle timestamps.

Immutable identifiers and core relationships—like the primary key, the business `dispute_code`, and foreign keys to orders or payments—are excluded and must not be changed via this DTO. Actor identity and permissions are derived from authentication context (customer, seller, or admin) and from related tables such as `shopping_mall_dispute_parties`.

type.description:
Updated high-level dispute type classification.

If provided, this value changes the conceptual category of the dispute, such as switching between `payment_chargeback`, `refund_dispute`, or `policy_violation`. Implementations should validate that transitions between types are allowed by business policy before applying the change.

severity.description:
Updated business-defined severity level for the dispute.

Typical values include `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. Changing severity may impact operational handling, SLA expectations, or escalation behavior configured in case and policy tables.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the dispute.

Allowed values are constrained by the platform's dispute workflow, for example `open`, `under_investigation`, `resolved`, or `closed`. Implementers must enforce valid status transitions and prevent updates that conflict with legal holds or SLA violation states.

summary.description:
New short summary for the dispute, or null to clear it.

Used to update the human-readable summary line that appears in dashboards and list views. When set to null, any previously stored summary is removed.

description.description:
New detailed description or notes for the dispute, or null to clear.

This field carries extended context written by authorized actors, such as customers, sellers, or admins. It can be updated to reflect current understanding of the dispute, but should not be used for immutable audit information that belongs in event tables.

opened_at.description:
Revised dispute opened timestamp, or null when no change is intended.

Most implementations treat `opened_at` as effectively immutable, but the field is modeled here as updatable to support exceptional administrative corrections. When provided, the new value must remain consistent with the dispute's overall lifecycle history.

resolved_at.description:
Updated resolution timestamp, or null to clear previous resolution.

This value marks when a final decision was made on the dispute. It should typically only be set when transitioning into a resolved status and may be cleared or adjusted by admins in the case of corrections or reopened disputes.

closed_at.description:
Updated closure timestamp, or null to represent a reopened dispute.

`closed_at` should be set when the dispute is fully closed and no more actions are expected. Setting the field to null can represent reopening the case, subject to business rules and legal constraints.

IShoppingMallDisputeParty.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for listing dispute parties of a specific dispute.

This DTO is used as the request body for `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/disputes/{disputeCode}/parties` and defines how the `shopping_mall_dispute_parties` table should be queried. It combines pagination, optional filtering by actor type and role, and basic keyword search over display-oriented fields.

The filters are always scoped to the dispute identified by the `disputeCode` path parameter; the request body never carries the dispute identifier itself to avoid duplication and ensure a single authoritative source in the URL path. Admin tools use this payload to implement rich list views and search experiences when inspecting who is involved in a dispute.

page.description:
Page number for pagination when listing dispute parties.

The first page is typically represented as `1`. If omitted, implementations may choose a sensible default such as page 1. This value is combined with `limit` to compute offsets when querying the `shopping_mall_dispute_parties` table.

limit.description:
Maximum number of dispute party records to return in a single page.

Used together with `page` to control pagination window size. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent overly large result sets that could impact performance.

actor_type.description:
Filter for the type of party involved in the dispute, or null for no filtering.

Typical actor types include `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `external`. When provided, only records whose `actor_type` column matches the given value are returned.

role.description:
Filter for the party role within the dispute, or null for no filtering.

Common roles include `complainant`, `respondent`, `witness`, or `observer`. When supplied, the query is restricted to parties whose `role` column matches the requested value.

display_name.description:
Free-text search fragment for the party display name, or null for no name-based search.

When provided, the implementation should match this value against the `display_name` column of `shopping_mall_dispute_parties`, commonly using case-insensitive or partial search semantics to support flexible lookup.

IShoppingMallDisputeParty.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new dispute party associated with an existing dispute.

This DTO captures the actor classification, the party's role in the dispute, optional override display name, and exactly one underlying actor reference depending on the actor_type. The parent dispute is identified externally by the disputeCode path parameter and mapped to shopping_mall_dispute_id by the backend.

It is intended for administrative workflows where staff attach customers, sellers, admins, or external entities to a dispute case without exposing internal identifiers for the dispute itself in the request body.

actor_type.description:
Type of the participating actor being attached to the dispute.

Typical values include customer, seller, admin, or external, and the backend uses this value to validate which of the optional actor reference fields is populated.

Governance and risk logic relies on this classification to route the case to appropriate review queues and to enforce type-specific validation rules.

role.description:
Role of the party within the dispute being created.

Common roles are complainant, respondent, witness, or observer, and platform policy may define additional standardized values used in reporting.

This field guides how the party appears in administrative interfaces and may also influence SLA and escalation behavior for the dispute.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable label to show for this party in admin tools.

For internal actors such as customers, sellers, or admins it may be left null so that the backend derives a name from the profile; for external parties it is often used to capture the organization or contact name.

Providing a value here allows staff to customize how the party appears in dispute dashboards without altering the underlying actor profile.

customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer actor when the dispute party represents a customer.

This UUID corresponds to a row in the shopping_mall_customers table and must be provided only when actor_type indicates a customer.

The backend enforces consistency between actor_type and this field and resolves it to populate the shopping_mall_customer_id foreign key.

seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller actor when the dispute party represents a seller.

It references a primary key in the shopping_mall_sellers table and is valid only when actor_type indicates a seller-type participant.

Admin tools use this reference to attach the correct merchant account to the dispute while the backend maps it to the shopping_mall_seller_id foreign key.

admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin actor when the dispute party represents an internal administrative participant.

The value should correspond to an existing record in the shopping_mall_admins table and is allowed only when actor_type designates an admin.

This field enables governance workflows to explicitly track which staff member or team representative is formally attached as a party within the dispute case.

IShoppingMallDisputeParty.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields for updating a dispute party entity stored in the `shopping_mall_dispute_parties` table.

This DTO is used by administrative and governance tools when editing an existing dispute party that is already linked to a specific dispute through URL path parameters. It exposes only attributes that are safe to change after creation, such as the party role classification and display label metadata, while keeping identity and foreign key fields immutable and managed by the path context and backend logic.

Typical use cases include correcting the party role (for example complainant vs. respondent), updating how the party is shown in back-office UIs, or applying governance-driven reclassification during dispute handling, without altering the underlying linkage to customers, sellers, or admins.

actor_type.description:
Type of this dispute party, such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `external`.

This value controls which underlying actor linkage fields are expected to be populated in the `shopping_mall_dispute_parties` table and is used by governance tools to interpret the party’s origin. When updated, the service layer must enforce consistency with the actual actor bindings and business rules for dispute handling.

role.description:
Business role that this party plays in the dispute, for example `complainant`, `respondent`, `witness`, or `observer`.

Changing this field allows administrators to reclassify how the party participates in the case as new information becomes available. Implementations should restrict values to a configured set of roles consistent with dispute policy.

display_name.description:
Display name used in admin and governance tools when referring to this dispute party.

When present, this value may override or snapshot a label derived from the underlying actor profile, especially for external organizations or counterparts that do not have a native account in the platform. When set to null, the backend may fall back to default naming derived from the associated actor record.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvent.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving a paginated list of dispute events from the `shopping_mall_dispute_events` table for a particular dispute.

This DTO is used by administrative and governance UIs to query the event timeline of a dispute identified by its business `disputeCode` path parameter. It allows callers to specify time windows, event-type filters, and pagination controls so that large timelines can be explored efficiently without loading all events at once.

The operation using this schema is read-only and is typically combined with dispute header and evidence views to provide a complete picture of the dispute lifecycle and support auditing and investigative workflows.

page.description:
Page index for pagination when listing dispute events.

This value is usually 1-based or 0-based depending on the platform convention and is interpreted together with the `limit` field to determine which slice of the event timeline should be returned. When omitted, the backend will use a sensible default page index.

limit.description:
Maximum number of dispute event records to return in a single page.

This value allows clients to control the density of the event timeline. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect performance and avoid accidentally requesting excessively large pages.

event_types.description:
Optional list of event type identifiers to include in the result set, such as `created`, `status_changed`, `note_added`, `evidence_added`, or other configured types.

When provided, only events whose `event_type` field matches one of the requested values are returned. This enables operators to focus on particular kinds of activity in long-running disputes.

occurred_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the event occurrence timestamp range, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When set, only events whose `occurred_at` value is greater than or equal to this timestamp are considered. When null or omitted, no lower bound is applied.

occurred_to.description:
Exclusive or inclusive upper bound (depending on implementation) of the event occurrence timestamp range, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When set, only events whose `occurred_at` value is less than (or less than or equal to) this timestamp are considered. When null or omitted, no upper bound is applied.

sort_field.description:
Name of the field used to sort dispute events in the result set, such as `occurred_at` or `created_at`.

If omitted or null, the backend typically defaults to ordering by `occurred_at` ascending or descending according to `sort_direction`. Values should be restricted to a safe whitelist to prevent arbitrary sorting on unsupported columns.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction for the event list, commonly `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending.

When omitted or null, the backend applies its default ordering policy, usually descending by occurrence time so that the most recent events appear first in admin timelines.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvent.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new dispute event in the dispute timeline.

This type is used as the request body for `POST /shoppingMall/admin/disputes/{disputeCode}/events` and maps to the `shopping_mall_dispute_events` Prisma model. It includes only those fields that clients are allowed to supply when appending a new event to an existing dispute identified by its business code.

Server-managed fields such as the primary key `id`, the foreign key `shopping_mall_dispute_id`, and audit timestamps are not part of this DTO and are populated by the backend using the path parameter and current execution context. Actor identifiers for admins, customers, or sellers are likewise derived from authentication and business logic rather than being trusted from the request payload.

event_type.description:
Business-level type or category of the dispute event to create.

This property maps to the `event_type` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and determines how the event will be interpreted in the dispute timeline. Typical values include categories such as `created`, `note_added`, `status_changed`, `escalated`, or `evidence_added`, depending on the platform's configured taxonomy.

Downstream workflows, UI rendering, and policy checks may rely on this value to trigger appropriate behavior.

oneOf.description:
Dispute status prior to the event, when explicitly recording a status transition.

This value is written into the `status_before` column and should correspond to the dispute's status at the time the event occurred, using the same status codes as `shopping_mall_disputes`.

For events that do not alter state or where previous status is inferred automatically, this field can be omitted or set to null.

status_before.description:
Optional previous status of the dispute at the time this event occurred.

Supplying this value makes the event's effect on the dispute lifecycle explicit, improving auditability and easing reconstruction of status histories.

If omitted, the service may derive the prior status from the current dispute record where appropriate.

oneOf.description:
Dispute status after the event, when the event represents a status change.

This value is written into the `status_after` column and should use one of the allowed status codes defined for `shopping_mall_disputes`, such as `under_investigation`, `resolved`, or `closed`.

For non-transition events or when the new status is determined by server-side logic, this field may be left null.

status_after.description:
Optional new status of the dispute resulting from this event.

Including this field explicitly documents how the event changes dispute state and supports consistent status timelines. When business rules handle state transitions automatically, the service may override or ignore this value according to policy.

If no status change occurs, this property should be omitted or set to null.

oneOf.description:
Free-form human-readable description or note content for the event.

This value is stored in the `description` column of `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and is typically used by administrators to explain actions, capture rationale, or add commentary for future reviewers.

It is especially important for events such as `note_added`, manual status adjustments, or escalations that require context beyond the event type alone.

description.description:
Optional textual description that explains the purpose or details of the newly created event.

The description helps admins and risk analysts understand what happened and why when reviewing the dispute timeline. It may contain operational notes, communication summaries, or references to external systems.

When the event type and other metadata fully describe the action, this field can be omitted.

occurred_at.description:
Business timestamp at which the underlying action for this event occurred.

This field maps to the `occurred_at` column in `shopping_mall_dispute_events` and should represent the actual time of the event rather than the request submission time. It allows recording of backdated events or events originating from external systems whose effective time is known.

The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string and is mandatory when creating a dispute event.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvent.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for dispute event records stored in the shopping_mall_dispute_events model.

This type represents the subset of dispute event fields that may be modified after creation, such as descriptive text and, where business policy allows, classification attributes like event_type or status transitions. Immutable identifiers and foreign keys that tie the event to its dispute or actors are not included in this DTO.

The DTO is used by administrative workflows to adjust human-readable notes or to correct event categorization during dispute handling, while preserving the original audit trail of who performed the action and when it occurred in business time.

event_type.description:
Optional updated classification of the dispute event.

Represents the business-level type of the event, such as created, note_added, status_changed, escalated, or evidence_added, depending on configured values. Implementations may restrict which event types can be changed after creation or may disallow changes entirely for certain critical event categories.

When present in an update request, this value should be validated against the platform’s configured dispute event type vocabulary before applying the change.

status_before.description:
Optional correction to the dispute status that applied immediately before this event.

This field mirrors the status of the parent dispute prior to the event and is mainly used for audit readability and analytics. In normal flows it is set at event creation time, but administrators may be allowed to adjust it to fix inconsistencies if permitted by policy.

When supplied as a non-null string, it should align with the status codes used on the shopping_mall_disputes.status column, such as open, under_investigation, resolved, or closed.

status_after.description:
Optional correction to the dispute status that applied immediately after this event.

This field captures the resulting dispute status following the event and is useful for reconstructing the timeline of state transitions. It is typically set when the event is created, especially for status change events.

Any non-null value should use the same status code system as shopping_mall_disputes.status, and updates may be restricted or audited by governance rules to protect the accuracy of the dispute lifecycle history.

description.description:
Updated human-readable description or notes for this dispute event.

This text is used in admin tools and dispute timelines to explain what happened during the event or why a particular action was taken. It may include investigation notes, escalation reasons, or context from external systems.

When set to null, the existing description can be cleared if business rules allow; otherwise, clients should omit the property to leave the current description unchanged.

occurred_at.description:
Optional correction to the business-time timestamp when this event occurred.

The occurred_at field records when the underlying business action actually happened, which may differ from the technical creation time of the record. Administrators may need to adjust this value if an event was registered late or backfilled from an external case management system.

Any non-null value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string. Updates should respect legal hold and audit requirements, and platforms may restrict changes to occurred_at depending on dispute status and policy.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvidence.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying evidence records associated with a specific dispute.

This type is used as the request body for evidence search operations that work against the shopping_mall_dispute_evidences model, scoped to a single dispute identified by its disputeCode path parameter. It allows administrators to express filtering, sorting, and pagination options without repeating the dispute identifier in the body.

The DTO is designed for use in governance, risk, and support consoles where staff need to quickly locate evidences by type, submitter, or time range, while maintaining consistent paging semantics across the platform’s list/search APIs.

page.description:
Page number for paginated evidence search results.

Represents the 1-based index of the result page to retrieve. When omitted, implementations commonly default to the first page. This value is combined with the limit field to determine the offset used when querying shopping_mall_dispute_evidences for the dispute.

Clients should pass positive integers only; very large values may be constrained by the backend to protect performance.

limit.description:
Maximum number of evidence records to return on a single page.

Used together with the page field to control the size of paginated responses from shopping_mall_dispute_evidences. Typical values are bounded by a platform-wide maximum to prevent excessively large responses and to keep dispute tooling responsive.

If not provided, the service may fall back to a sensible default such as 20 or 50 records per page.

sort_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort evidence results within the page.

Common sort targets include created_at to show newest or oldest evidences first, or evidence_type when grouping by kind of artifact is useful. The actual set of allowed values should be validated server-side against supported index definitions on shopping_mall_dispute_evidences.

When null or omitted, the service should apply its default sort ordering, typically descending by created_at.

sort_order.description:
Optional sort direction applied together with sort_by.

Usually constrained to values like asc or desc to indicate ascending or descending order. The backend should normalize and validate the value, defaulting to a safe option such as desc when the property is null or not provided.

This field lets administrators switch between chronological and reverse-chronological views when reviewing dispute evidences.

evidence_type.description:
Optional filter for the type of evidence to include in the results.

Corresponds to the evidence_type column on shopping_mall_dispute_evidences, which may include values such as image, document, message_log, or external_reference depending on the configured taxonomy. When provided, only evidences with the matching type are returned.

If null or omitted, evidences of all types are eligible for inclusion, subject to other filters and access constraints.

submitted_by.description:
Optional filter describing which actor provided the evidence.

This is a logical selector rather than a raw foreign key, typically using values such as customer, seller, admin, or external to map onto the appropriate shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_seller_id, shopping_mall_admin_id, or other linkage fields.

When set, the backend translates the value into appropriate query conditions to restrict results to evidences submitted by the chosen actor category; when null, evidences from all submitter types may be returned.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound of the creation timestamp window for evidence records.

When provided as an ISO 8601 date-time string, only evidences whose created_at value is greater than or equal to this timestamp are eligible to be returned. This is useful for narrowing the search to recent or time-bounded segments of a dispute’s evidence history.

If null or omitted, there is no lower time constraint beyond any global retention or legal hold policies enforced at the database or business layer.

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound of the creation timestamp window for evidence records.

When set, only evidences whose created_at value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are returned. Together with created_from, this enables date-range filtering of evidences for a dispute.

If null or omitted, there is no explicit upper time limit beyond any platform-wide retention or archiving behavior.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvidence.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new dispute evidence record under an existing dispute.

This type is derived from the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model and is used as the request body for operations that attach new evidence artifacts to a `shopping_mall_disputes` row. It exposes only those fields that callers are allowed to set when creating evidence.

Server-managed fields such as the primary key and timestamps are excluded from the request and will be generated automatically. The owning dispute is determined from the path parameter (for example, a `disputeCode` that resolves to a `shopping_mall_dispute_id`), so the foreign key is not supplied directly in the body. Actor attribution fields such as admin, customer, or seller IDs are also not accepted from the client; they are populated by the backend based on the authenticated context to prevent impersonation and maintain audit integrity.

shopping_mall_dispute_event_id.description:
Identifier of the specific dispute event that introduced this evidence, when applicable.

When provided, this value is written to the nullable `shopping_mall_dispute_event_id` column in `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` and ties the new evidence to a particular entry in `shopping_mall_dispute_events`.

If null or omitted, the evidence is associated only with the dispute as a whole rather than a specific timeline event.

evidence_type.description:
Type of evidence being attached to the dispute.

This required field is written to the non-nullable `evidence_type` column in `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` and is expected to classify the evidence, for example as `image`, `document`, `message_log`, or `external_reference`.

Validation and downstream processing rules may depend on this value, so callers should use a controlled vocabulary agreed upon in business and operations policies.

title.description:
Short title or label describing the evidence for use in admin tools.

When provided, this is stored in the nullable `title` column and helps operators quickly identify evidence items in lists or dashboards.

If omitted or null, administrative interfaces may fall back to showing the evidence type or part of the URI as the primary label.

description.description:
Detailed description or notes about what this evidence shows or why it is being attached to the dispute.

This property is persisted to the nullable `description` column and typically contains free-form explanatory text supplied by the actor creating the evidence.

It is especially useful when the underlying artifact is not self-explanatory or when additional context is required for risk, compliance, or legal review.

uri.description:
URI pointing to the stored evidence content in external storage or another system.

This required field is stored in the non-nullable `uri` column and must be a valid URI string that the platform or back-office tools can dereference to access the underlying evidence bytes.

Only a reference is provided here; actual upload of binary content is handled by separate storage or upload services, following the platform’s file management strategy.

checksum.description:
Optional checksum or hash of the evidence content for integrity verification.

If supplied, this value is written to the nullable `checksum` column and can be used by downstream systems to verify that the content referenced by `uri` has not been altered.

Typical values are cryptographic digests such as SHA-256 encoded as hexadecimal or base64 strings, depending on platform conventions.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvidence.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for dispute evidence records stored in the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` table.

This type represents the set of mutable business fields that administrators are allowed to modify on an existing dispute evidence artifact that is already linked to a dispute. It is used as the request body for the `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/disputes/{disputeCode}/evidences/{disputeEvidenceId}` operation and follows a partial-update semantics: only properties that appear in the request body are applied to the underlying record; omitted fields are left unchanged in the database.

Only user-editable, business-facing attributes appear here. Primary keys, foreign keys, and creator-identifying fields are intentionally excluded so that ownership, authorship, and parent dispute relationships remain immutable and are enforced by the backend using path parameters and authentication context. This keeps the DTO aligned with the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model while ensuring a safe and predictable update surface for dispute-handling workflows.

evidence_type.description:
New classification type for this evidence, such as `image`, `document`, `message_log`, or `external_reference`.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `evidence_type` column of the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model. When included in the update payload, the service updates the stored evidence type accordingly; when omitted from the request body, the existing value remains unchanged. Dispute analysts and automated pipelines rely on this type to group, filter, and interpret evidence artifacts in dashboards and workflows.

title.description:
Short human-readable title or label for the evidence item.

This property corresponds to the nullable `title` column on the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` table. When a non-null string is provided, it updates the stored title that is shown in administrative consoles and dispute dashboards, helping analysts quickly identify the purpose of the evidence (for example, "Customer chat transcript" or "Carrier tracking screenshot"). When `null` is supplied, the existing title is cleared. If the field is omitted from the payload, the title stored in the database is left unchanged.

description.description:
Detailed explanation or notes describing what this evidence demonstrates and why it is relevant to the dispute.

This property maps to the nullable `description` column of the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model. Providing a non-null string replaces the existing description with updated narrative context, which is especially important when reviewing complex cases or summarizing external documents. Supplying `null` clears any previously stored description. If this property is omitted from the request body, the existing description value is retained.

uri.description:
URI pointing to the stored evidence content in an external storage service or integrated system.

This field is aligned with the non-nullable `uri` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` table and must contain a valid URI (for example, an HTTPS link to an object in a document repository or evidence store). When present in the update payload, the service layer updates the target location of the evidence content while continuing to enforce the uniqueness constraint `(shopping_mall_dispute_id, uri)` and any legal-hold requirements. When this property is omitted, the existing URI remains unchanged, ensuring that references to evidence content stay stable by default.

Binary evidence data is never sent directly through this DTO. Clients must upload content to a storage system first and then provide the resulting URI here.

checksum.description:
Optional checksum or hash of the evidence content for integrity verification.

This property corresponds to the nullable `checksum` column on the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model. Providing a non-null string (for example, a SHA-256 hash) updates the stored integrity marker and allows governance and risk tooling to detect tampering or unexpected changes to the underlying evidence bytes. Supplying `null` clears any previously stored checksum when business policy permits. If this field is not present in the request body, the stored checksum value is left unchanged.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaConfig.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying case SLA configuration records from `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`.

This type is used as the request body of the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/caseSlaConfigs` operation to express complex search criteria and pagination instructions when listing SLA rules. All fields are optional and may be combined freely: clients can filter on case type, actor role, action type, and activation state, or omit filters entirely to retrieve a broader set of configurations.

When `page` or `limit` are omitted, the backend applies sensible defaults defined by the API contract, such as starting from the first page and using a standard page size. The DTO is not directly bound to the Prisma model via `x-autobe-prisma-schema`; instead, it provides a flexible query interface that is implemented on top of the `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` table and its related policy models.

page.description:
Page index for paginated retrieval of SLA configurations.

This integer selects which page of results to return. The API treats this value according to the platform’s pagination convention (for example, one-based indexing where `1` is the first page). When omitted, the service defaults to the first page. Backends should enforce reasonable upper bounds to prevent excessively deep pagination requests that could degrade performance.

limit.description:
Maximum number of SLA configuration records to return in a single page.

This controls page density for list views and governance dashboards. When omitted, the service uses a default page size defined by the platform (for example, 20 or 50 records per page). Implementations should enforce a safe maximum limit (such as 100 or 200) to avoid large, inefficient result sets while still allowing administrators to adjust density for their workflows.

case_type.description:
Filter by case type that the SLA applies to, such as `cancellation`, `refund`, `dispute`, or other platform-specific case categories.

This value is compared against the `case_type` column of `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. When a non-null string is provided, only SLA configurations whose case type matches the filter are included in the result set. When `null` is supplied or the field is omitted, no filtering is applied on case type and the query can span all supported case types.

actor_role.description:
Filter by actor role whose behavior is constrained by the SLA, for example `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`.

This field is matched against the `actor_role` column of the `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` table. When a non-null value is supplied, only SLA configurations for that actor role are returned. If `null` is provided or the property is left out of the payload, no actor-role filter is applied and SLAs for all roles may be included.

action_type.description:
Filter by the type of action governed by the SLA, such as `initial_response` or `final_decision`.

This filter targets the `action_type` column of `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. A non-null value restricts results to SLA records that apply to the specified action type, enabling administrators to differentiate response-time SLAs from resolution-time SLAs. When `null` is provided or the field is omitted, the query does not constrain results by action type.

is_active.description:
Filter indicating whether only active or inactive SLA configurations should be returned.

This property is evaluated against the `is_active` column of the `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` model. When set to `true`, the response contains only SLA rules that are currently active for new cases. When set to `false`, only inactive or retired SLA configurations are returned. When `null` or absent, the filter is not applied and the result set may include both active and inactive SLA records depending on additional business rules or defaults.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaConfig.description:
Case SLA (Service-Level Agreement) configuration entity for the ShoppingMall platform.

This type models a single SLA rule row stored in the shopping_mall_case_sla_configs Prisma table. Each record defines SLA expectations for a particular combination of case_type, actor_role, and action_type, optionally scoped to a specific business policy version. These configurations are referenced when evaluating cancellations, refunds, disputes, and other support or risk cases, and drive time-based behavior such as response deadlines and resolution windows.

The entity is managed exclusively by administrative and governance tools. Runtime engines that track case progress and record SLA breaches read from this table but never write to it directly. Timestamps reflect when the configuration itself was created or last updated, enabling audit and policy versioning flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SLA configuration record.

This field is the primary key of the shopping_mall_case_sla_configs table and is used by admin APIs and internal services to reference a specific SLA rule. Its value is generated by the database layer and is stable for the lifetime of the record.

case_type.description:
Type of case this SLA applies to, such as cancellation, refund, dispute, or risk-related case.

Downstream processing uses this value to select the appropriate SLA rule when evaluating cases in different domains. The application layer should constrain this value to supported case category codes, even though it is stored as a string in the database.

actor_role.description:
Actor role whose behavior is governed by this SLA configuration, for example customer, seller, or admin.

Engines that monitor SLA compliance use this role to determine which party is responsible for meeting the defined deadlines. UI surfaces for admin users will typically filter and group configurations by actor_role for easier management.

action_type.description:
Action governed by this SLA configuration, such as initial_response, acknowledgement, or final_decision.

This field distinguishes different phases of case handling within the same case_type. For example, a refund request may have separate SLAs for when a seller must first respond and when a final decision must be made.

target_duration_seconds.description:
Target time window in seconds within which the governed action should be completed.

SLA tracking logic uses this value together with the case start timestamp to calculate due dates and to decide when a case is considered to be in breach. The value is typically a positive integer and may be interpreted as seconds, derived from higher-level business inputs such as hours or days.

warning_duration_seconds.description:
Optional warning lead time in seconds before the SLA breach point is reached.

When set, monitoring systems can generate alerts or reminders this many seconds before the target_duration_seconds elapses, allowing operations teams or responsible actors to intervene before a formal SLA violation occurs. When null, no explicit pre-breach warning threshold is configured for this SLA rule.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this SLA configuration is currently active for new cases.

When true, SLA selection logic considers this record when matching rules for incoming or ongoing cases. When false, the configuration is treated as inactive or deprecated and is typically ignored for new evaluations while still retained for historical and audit purposes.

policyVersion.description:
Business policy version associated with this SLA configuration, or null when the SLA is not tied to a specific versioned policy document.

This association replaces the raw shopping_mall_business_policy_version_id foreign key and provides a compact, contextual view of the policy version that defined the SLA. Admin tools and governance dashboards can use this summary to understand which policy version introduced or currently owns the rule without performing separate lookups.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA configuration record was initially created.

This value provides an audit trail for policy changes and allows analytics workloads to reason about when particular SLA expectations came into effect. It is set by the database layer when the row is first inserted.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA configuration record was last updated.
