Whenever administrative tools modify any mutable field of the configuration, this timestamp is refreshed. It is used for change tracking, cache invalidation, and synchronization with external configuration consumers.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaConfig.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new case SLA configuration record in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO is accepted by the administrative creation endpoint that inserts a new row into the shopping_mall_case_sla_configs table. It captures the business-facing inputs required to define an SLA rule, such as the case_type, actor_role, action_type, and the target_duration_seconds used to compute deadlines.

System-managed fields like id, created_at, and updated_at are omitted because they are generated by the persistence layer. Ownership and actor identity are derived from authenticated admin context rather than passed explicitly in this payload.

shopping_mall_business_policy_version_id.description:
Optional business policy version identifier to associate with this SLA configuration.

When supplied, this UUID must reference an existing row in shopping_mall_policy_versions and is used to bind the SLA rule to a specific policy revision. When null or omitted, the SLA may be treated as a global configuration independent of a versioned policy document.

case_type.description:
Case type code identifying the class of cases governed by this SLA, such as cancellation, refund, or dispute.

The application layer should validate this string against the supported set of case categories for the ShoppingMall platform to prevent invalid or unrecognized case types from being configured.

actor_role.description:
Role of the actor whose behavior is constrained by this SLA, for example customer, seller, or admin.

This value determines which party is responsible for meeting the configured time targets. Admin tools typically limit this field to a controlled vocabulary of actor roles defined by the platform.

action_type.description:
Logical action within the case lifecycle that is governed by this SLA, such as initial_response or final_decision.

This field allows multiple SLA rules to exist for the same case_type and actor_role, each covering different steps in the handling process. Validation should ensure that the action_type value conforms to the platform's case action taxonomy.

target_duration_seconds.description:
Target time window in seconds within which the governed action must be completed for this SLA to be considered met.

Administrative UIs often allow configuration in units such as hours or days and convert them to seconds before sending this value. The backend should validate that this integer is positive and within reasonable operational limits.

warning_duration_seconds.description:
Optional pre-breach warning offset in seconds before the target_duration_seconds elapses.

When provided, monitoring systems can emit alerts or notifications this many seconds before the calculated SLA deadline, giving responsible actors a chance to act before a violation occurs. When null or omitted, no explicit warning threshold is configured.

is_active.description:
Flag determining whether the new SLA configuration should be active immediately for new cases.

When true, the rule becomes eligible for selection as soon as it is created. When false, the configuration is stored but not yet applied, allowing administrators to stage or review rules before activation.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaConfig.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing case SLA configuration stored in the shopping_mall_case_sla_configs table.

This type exposes only the mutable business fields of a case SLA configuration so that administrative users can revise SLA thresholds, action types, and activation status without altering system-managed identifiers or audit timestamps. It is used by the admin-facing update endpoint that targets a specific configuration row identified by its path parameter.

All properties are optional to support partial updates; omitted fields are left unchanged by the backend. Validation rules ensure that numeric thresholds remain within acceptable ranges and that uniqueness and consistency constraints defined on the underlying Prisma model are preserved when updates are applied.

case_type.description:
Type of case this SLA applies to, such as cancellation, refund, or dispute.

When present in an update request, this value must continue to align with the allowed case taxonomy used throughout the refunds and disputes domain. Combined with actor_role, action_type, and the optional policy version reference, it participates in a uniqueness constraint on the shopping_mall_case_sla_configs table.

actor_role.description:
Actor role whose behavior is constrained by this SLA, for example customer, seller, or admin.

Updating this field changes which actor is responsible for meeting the specified time targets. The platform uses this role in monitoring and reporting to attribute SLA performance correctly to operational teams or organizational units.

action_type.description:
Action governed by the SLA, such as initial_response or final_decision.

This value describes the business step that must be completed within the configured time window. Changing it reclassifies which part of the workflow the SLA applies to and must remain consistent with back-office and case-management logic that interprets SLA rules.

target_duration_seconds.description:
Target time window in seconds within which the governed action must be completed from its business start time.

Administrators can adjust this threshold to tighten or relax SLA expectations. The backend enforces domain-specific constraints to prevent invalid or negative durations and may require non-zero positive values where appropriate.

warning_duration_seconds.description:
Optional duration in seconds after which a warning should be raised before the SLA breach occurs.

When provided, this value is typically less than target_duration_seconds and is used by monitoring jobs or alerting mechanisms to trigger pre-breach notifications. Setting it to null removes any configured warning offset so that only final breaches are tracked.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this SLA rule is currently active for new cases.

Setting this field to true enables the configuration for future SLA calculations, while setting it to false deactivates it so that new cases no longer use this rule. Deactivation does not remove historical links from existing cases or recorded SLA violations.

shopping_mall_business_policy_version_id.description:
Identifier of the business policy version this SLA config is associated with.

When set, this UUID references a row in shopping_mall_policy_versions and allows governance teams to track which policy version defined the SLA at the time of configuration. Providing null detaches the configuration from a specific policy version, while updates that change this value must respect referential integrity.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaViolation.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying SLA violation records stored in the shopping_mall_case_sla_violations table.

This type encapsulates complex search criteria, including case attributes, actor roles, action types, date ranges, and status-like flags, along with pagination and sorting parameters. It is used by an admin-only PATCH endpoint that returns a paginated list of SLA violation summaries for monitoring dashboards and governance reporting.

All properties are optional so that administrators can combine filters as needed. When a field is omitted, the backend does not filter on that dimension. Pagination defaults and maximum limits are enforced server-side to protect performance when querying large violation datasets.

case_type.description:
Optional filter for the type of case that violated the SLA, such as cancellation, refund, or dispute.

When provided, only violations whose case_type matches the supplied value are included in the result set. This corresponds to the case_type column on the shopping_mall_case_sla_violations table and should mirror the SLA configuration case types for consistent reporting.

actor_role.description:
Optional filter for the actor role responsible for the SLA breach, for example seller or admin.

Use this field to segment SLA violations by accountable party when analyzing operational performance or identifying training and staffing needs across different roles.

action_type.description:
Optional filter for the action type that was governed by the violated SLA, such as initial_response or final_decision.

When set, the search is narrowed to violations associated with a specific step in the case lifecycle. This helps administrators distinguish between early-response issues and delays in final resolutions.

shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id.description:
Optional filter for a specific SLA configuration that was violated.

When this UUID is supplied, only violations linked to the referenced configuration row in shopping_mall_case_sla_configs are returned. This is useful when assessing the impact of a particular SLA rule or when validating new SLA thresholds after deployment.

shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id.description:
Optional filter for violations associated with a particular cancellation request.

If provided, the query restricts results to rows whose shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id matches this value, allowing detailed analysis of SLA performance for a specific cancellation case.

shopping_mall_refund_request_id.description:
Optional filter for violations associated with a specific refund request.

Use this field when investigating SLA adherence for a particular refund case stored in shopping_mall_refund_requests, for example during dispute resolution or compliance reviews.

shopping_mall_dispute_id.description:
Optional filter for violations tied to a given dispute record.

When present, only SLA breaches recorded for the identified dispute in shopping_mall_disputes are returned, supporting case-centric analysis workflows for high-severity conflicts.

breach_duration_seconds_min.description:
Optional lower bound filter for the breach duration in seconds.

When set, only violations whose breach_duration_seconds is greater than or equal to this value are included. This helps teams focus on more severe breaches that exceeded SLAs by a significant margin.

breach_duration_seconds_max.description:
Optional upper bound filter for the breach duration in seconds.

Use this together with breach_duration_seconds_min to define a duration range when segmenting violations by severity. If only this field is provided, the backend filters to violations whose breach_duration_seconds is less than or equal to the specified value.

detected_from.description:
Optional start of the date-time range for when SLA violations were detected.

When supplied, only violations with detected_at greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned, allowing time-windowed analysis such as recent breaches or a specific reporting period.

detected_to.description:
Optional end of the date-time range for when SLA violations were detected.

Combined with detected_from, this field defines an inclusive time window on the detected_at column for slicing reports by calendar periods or campaign windows.

page.description:
Optional 1-based page index for pagination over the result set.

If omitted, the backend uses a sensible default page index (typically 1). When provided, it must be a positive integer and works together with the pageSize field to determine which slice of data is returned.

pageSize.description:
Optional page size indicating the maximum number of violation records to return in a single page.

The server enforces an upper limit to protect performance. When omitted, a default page size is applied. Very large values may be clamped to a configured maximum.

orderBy.description:
Optional field name used to sort the SLA violation results.

Common values include created_at, detected_at, breach_duration_seconds, or other index-backed columns of shopping_mall_case_sla_violations. When absent, the backend applies a default ordering, typically by detected_at in descending order.

orderDirection.description:
Optional sort direction for the specified orderBy field.

Typical values are asc or desc. When not provided, the backend uses its default direction, usually descending for time-based fields so that the most recent or most severe violations appear first.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a refund request in the shopping mall platform.

This type provides a compact, list-optimized representation of a refund case linked to an order and optionally to a specific order payment. It focuses on identifiers, status, high-level monetary information, and timestamps that are critical for dashboards, index views, and embedded references inside other resources.

The summary intentionally omits heavy child collections and detailed status histories, while still exposing enough context for operators and clients to understand who initiated the request, how much money is involved, what order and payment are involved, and where in the lifecycle the refund currently resides.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund request.

This value maps to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_refund_requests` table and is the canonical reference used throughout the platform to identify a specific refund case.

Clients use this identifier in URLs, logs, and cross-system integrations when referencing or tracking a particular refund request instance.

order.description:
Summary information about the order associated with this refund request.

This reference replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key and links to the `shopping_mall_orders` entity through its summary DTO. It provides enough context—such as order code, high-level status, and key monetary figures—for dashboards and list views without requiring additional API calls.

Consumers can still access the order identifier via `order.id` while benefiting from richer context like customer, seller, and basic order metadata in a single response.

orderPayment.description:
Optional summary of the specific logical order payment associated with this refund request.

This reference replaces the nullable `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` foreign key and points to a summarized view of the `shopping_mall_order_payments` entity when the refund is tied to a particular payment record, such as in multi-payment scenarios.

When non-null, clients can use this object to understand payment method, payment status, and core monetary attributes without issuing a separate lookup. When null, the refund is either still general to the order or not bound to a single payment entry.

request_code.description:
Business-visible identifier for the refund request.

This property is mapped from the `request_code` column and is designed for human-oriented communication. It is often shown in emails, support tickets, and customer service UIs so that users and agents can easily reference a refund case.

The combination of `order.id` and `request_code` is unique, ensuring each refund case can be unambiguously identified within the context of a single order.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the refund request.

The value comes from the `status` column and typically follows a controlled set of states such as `requested`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `completed` as defined by the platform's business rules.

Clients and operational tools use this field to drive UI state, filter lists, and determine which actions are available on a given refund case at any point in time.

requested_total_amount.description:
Total monetary amount requested to be refunded by the initiating actor.

This value is stored in the `requested_total_amount` numeric column and represents the sum the requester believes should be returned, expressed in the currency indicated by `currency_code`.

The amount is used for both business decisions and financial reconciliation and is typically derived from the impacted items, shipping, or fees associated with the order.

approved_total_amount.description:
Total monetary amount approved to be refunded after case review.

The field maps to the nullable `approved_total_amount` column and is set when a decision has been reached by automated rules, seller review, or administrative evaluation. It may differ from `requested_total_amount` in partial approval scenarios.

When null, the refund case is usually still under evaluation or has been created but not yet decided, allowing frontends to distinguish between pending and finalized monetary outcomes.

currency_code.description:
Currency code used for the requested and approved refund amounts.

This property reflects the `currency_code` column and generally matches the order currency (for example, `USD` or `KRW`), ensuring monetary values are interpreted consistently across the system.

Clients should render and format `requested_total_amount` and `approved_total_amount` based on this currency code to provide accurate financial information to users.

reason_description.description:
Free-text explanation that provides additional context for the refund request.

The value is stored in the nullable `reason_description` column and supplements the structured primary reason linked via `shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id`. It may contain customer-entered text or internal notes summarizing the case.

Support tools and investigation workflows rely on this field to understand nuanced circumstances, edge conditions, or narrative details that are not fully captured by a reason code alone.

requested_by_actor_type.description:
Actor type that initiated the refund request.

This property corresponds to the `requested_by_actor_type` column and typically holds values such as `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`, indicating who opened the case.

User interfaces and governance tools use this information to adapt tone, permissions, and resolution workflows, as the initiating party can influence both SLA expectations and decision criteria.

requires_return.description:
Flag indicating whether physical goods must be returned to complete this refund request.

The field is backed by the `requires_return` boolean column and encodes whether the refund is contingent on merchandise return, which is critical for warehouse and logistics coordination.

Frontends can use this value to show return instructions to customers, while operations systems use it to trigger return label generation, inbound shipment processing, and inventory reconciliation.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was created in the system.

This value maps to the `requested_at` column and marks the official initiation time of the refund case, often used for SLA calculations and timeline visualizations.

Business reporting, compliance checks, and customer service tools rely on this timestamp to understand when the case entered the workflow and how long it has been pending.

decided_at.description:
Timestamp when a final decision was made for the refund request.

The property corresponds to the nullable `decided_at` column and is populated when the refund transitions into a decision state such as approved or rejected.

This timestamp is important for SLA compliance reporting, dispute resolution tracking, and determining how long review stages take across different refund cohorts.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the financial refund was fully processed and completed.

This field mirrors the nullable `completed_at` column and indicates when funds actually moved, either back to the customer or to an external financial instrument, depending on payment method.

Finance, reconciliation, and accounting subsystems use this timestamp for settlement calculations, ledger posting, and alignment with payment provider reports.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request record was created in the database.

This value is stored in the `created_at` column and may match or be very close to `requested_at`, depending on how the business process records initial events.

It serves as a canonical creation marker for audit trails, internal monitoring, and debugging of any issues related to record ingestion or event ordering.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request record was last updated.

The field is backed by the `updated_at` column and is refreshed whenever mutable attributes change, such as status transitions, approved amounts, or reason text.

Clients and data processing jobs can use this value for cache invalidation, incremental synchronization, and to assess the recency of case data shown in user interfaces.

IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesDashboard.description:
Aggregated dashboard view over refund and dispute activity for administrative and governance users.

This composite DTO does not map to a single Prisma table. Instead it aggregates snapshot metrics from `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` and current case information from `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, `shopping_mall_disputes`, `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`, and related models.

It is designed to power admin console pages that present an at-a-glance overview of refund volume, dispute workload, SLA performance, and resolution times without requiring multiple API calls or client-side aggregation logic.

period.description:
Information about the time window over which the dashboard aggregates are calculated.

The period section allows the UI to present which date range or preset (for example last 7 days or current month) the displayed metrics reference so that operators can interpret trend and volume values correctly.

refundSummary.description:
Aggregated statistics related to refund requests and monetary refunds.

This section summarizes counts, approval and rejection volumes, and basic resolution time metrics derived from snapshot tables like `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` and live refund case data.

disputeSummary.description:
Aggregated statistics related to disputes and their outcomes.

It captures counts of opened and resolved disputes, distribution of resolutions by party, and typical resolution times drawn from snapshot data and current dispute records.

slaSummary.description:
Aggregated view of SLA performance across refund and dispute cases.

This section surfaces counts of SLA breaches and may break them down by case type, actor role, or action type to help admins understand where process or staffing issues are causing missed commitments.

topRefundReasons.description:
List of top recurring refund reasons within the selected period.

Each entry represents a structured reason code and associated counts, helping operations and product teams identify systemic issues that drive refund demand.

recentRefundRequests.description:
A small, recency-ordered sample of refund requests relevant to the selected dashboard period.

This collection is intended for quick navigation from the dashboard to specific cases and should remain limited in size to keep the dashboard payload manageable.

recentDisputes.description:
A small, recency-ordered sample of disputes relevant to the selected dashboard period.

It allows administrators to quickly open high-priority or recently updated disputes directly from the dashboard view.

IShoppingMallDashboardPeriod.description:
Period descriptor for aggregated dashboard metrics.

This type indicates the date range and preset used to compute the statistics returned by the refunds and disputes dashboard. It is primarily a UI convenience structure so that admins can clearly see which window the metrics cover.

Implementations may use either explicit date bounds, a named preset, or both, depending on the dashboard configuration and query capabilities.

preset.description:
Named preset representing the aggregation window.

Common values include `today`, `last_7_days`, `last_30_days`, `this_month`, or other business-specific presets configured by the platform.

start_date.description:
Inclusive calendar date on which the aggregation period starts.

When present, it is typically normalized to midnight in the reporting timezone. It may be null if the dashboard relies solely on a preset without explicit dates.

end_date.description:
Inclusive calendar date on which the aggregation period ends.

When set, it usually corresponds to the most recent date included in the aggregated statistics. It may be null for open-ended or preset-only periods.

IShoppingMallRefundsSummary.description:
Aggregated refund-related metrics for a dashboard period.

This type summarizes core refund KPIs derived from one or more rows of the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot model and, optionally, complementary live data from refund request and payment refund tables.

It is optimized for rendering concise numerical widgets and trend indicators in administrative dashboards.

refund_request_count.description:
Total number of refund requests created within the dashboard period.

The value is sourced from `refund_request_count` in one or more `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` rows corresponding to the selected dates.

approved_refund_request_count.description:
Total number of refund requests approved within the dashboard period.

This figure counts approvals that occurred in the window, regardless of when the underlying requests were created, and mirrors `approved_refund_request_count` from the snapshot model.

rejected_refund_request_count.description:
Total number of refund requests rejected within the dashboard period.

It provides insight into decision patterns and aligns with `rejected_refund_request_count` in the snapshot table.

refunded_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded during the dashboard period in the platform base currency.

This value aggregates the `refunded_amount` field across relevant `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` rows and may combine multiple currencies normalized to the platform base, depending on analytics implementation.

partial_refund_count.description:
Number of refund operations during the dashboard period that were partial relative to the original order or item amount.

The metric helps identify whether refunds are typically full or partial and is taken from `partial_refund_count` in the snapshot model.

full_refund_count.description:
Number of refund operations during the dashboard period that fully refunded the relevant items or orders.

Together with `partial_refund_count`, this field gives a quick overview of how complete or partial typical refunds are.

average_refund_resolution_time_hours.description:
Average time in hours between refund request creation and final decision for cases resolved within the dashboard period.

It mirrors `average_refund_resolution_time_hours` in `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` and is used to monitor operational efficiency and SLA adherence for refund processing.

IShoppingMallDisputesSummary.description:
Aggregated dispute-related metrics for a configurable dashboard period.

This summary is an analytical read model derived from one or more rows of the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot table. It focuses exclusively on dispute activity and outcomes, using precomputed counts and average resolution times to provide a compact KPI view for administrators, risk teams, and operations analysts.

The DTO is typically scoped by a reporting window such as a single calendar day, a week, or a custom date range. For the chosen period, it aggregates how many disputes were opened, how many were resolved, and how final outcomes broke down between customers and sellers. It also exposes a time-based KPI that describes how quickly disputes are resolved, allowing teams to evaluate process efficiency and SLA performance.

In dashboards, these metrics are used together with refund and order statistics to identify systemic issues, capacity constraints, or fraud trends. For example, a rising number of disputes resolved for customers combined with long resolution times can indicate underlying catalog quality problems or slow seller responses that require targeted interventions.

dispute_opened_count.description:
Total number of disputes opened within the configured dashboard period.

This value corresponds to the aggregated `dispute_opened_count` column from the underlying `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot rows that fall into the selected reporting window. It represents the inflow of new dispute cases during that period, regardless of whether those disputes are still open or already resolved.

Analytically, this metric is used as a workload and volume indicator for the dispute-handling function. A spike in this number can highlight product quality issues, seller behavior changes, payment anomalies, or policy changes that cause more customers or sellers to escalate conflicts into formal disputes.

dispute_resolved_count.description:
Total number of disputes that reached a final resolution within the configured dashboard period.

This metric mirrors the aggregated `dispute_resolved_count` field from the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot data. A dispute is counted here when it transitions into a terminal state (for example, resolved in favor of the customer or seller), regardless of the date on which the dispute was originally opened.

The value is primarily used to understand throughput and clearance rate for dispute operations. Comparing `dispute_resolved_count` to `dispute_opened_count` helps teams detect backlogs: sustained periods where opened disputes significantly exceed resolved disputes can indicate staffing shortages, process bottlenecks, or policy friction.

dispute_resolved_for_customer_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the customer within the configured dashboard period.

This metric aligns with the aggregated `dispute_resolved_for_customer_count` column in the snapshot model and counts only those disputes whose final outcome explicitly favors the customer (for example, refund granted, charge reversed, or other customer-beneficial remedy).

Stakeholders use this value to monitor fairness and customer satisfaction from the dispute process. A very low or very high ratio of customer-favorable resolutions, especially relative to historical baselines or seller-favorable outcomes, can indicate biased decision-making, abuse patterns, or the need to re-evaluate policies and escalation rules.

dispute_resolved_for_seller_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the seller within the configured dashboard period.

This metric aggregates the `dispute_resolved_for_seller_count` field from `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` rows in the chosen reporting window. It counts disputes whose terminal outcome confirms the seller’s position, such as cases where claims are rejected due to insufficient evidence or clear policy violations by the customer.

The value is used to understand how often disputes are concluded in a way that supports sellers, which can be important for merchant trust, platform integrity, and fraud mitigation. Analysts often compare this count with customer-favorable resolutions to identify asymmetric patterns across categories, geographies, or seller cohorts.

average_dispute_resolution_time_hours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between dispute creation and final resolution for disputes resolved within the configured dashboard period.

This value is derived from the `average_dispute_resolution_time_hours` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot model. It is typically calculated over the cohort of disputes that reached a terminal state during the reporting window, using the difference between the creation timestamp and the final resolution timestamp.

Operational teams and policy owners rely on this metric as a leading indicator of SLA adherence and process health. Higher values may signal slow evidence collection, manual review bottlenecks, or coordination issues with external parties. Because extreme outliers can influence the average, consumers of this field may also complement it with percentile-based metrics or case-level drill-down views when investigating performance regressions.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaSummary.description:
Aggregated SLA performance metrics for case handling in the refunds and disputes domain.

This DTO summarizes how often configured case-level SLAs (for example, time to initial response or time to final decision) are being breached for cancellations, refunds, and disputes. It is computed from `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`, which stores individual violation records linking a concrete case (such as a cancellation request, refund request, or dispute) to a specific SLA configuration rule.

For a given reporting period, the summary exposes total violation volume as well as a breakdown by case type. This allows administrators and operations teams to quickly identify which case categories are most at risk of missing SLA commitments and to prioritize remediation efforts. It is typically used alongside more granular dashboards that show distributions by actor role, action type, or specific SLA configuration.

By tracking these metrics over time, governance and policy owners can evaluate whether process changes, staffing adjustments, or tighter policies are improving SLA adherence. Persistent high violation counts in any category can motivate updates to SLA definitions, escalation paths, or tooling support for agents who handle these cases.

total_violation_count.description:
Total number of recorded SLA violations across all supported case types within the configured dashboard period.

This count is derived from `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` records whose `detected_at` timestamps fall inside the selected reporting window, regardless of which SLA configuration or case type was involved. Each row typically represents one breached SLA rule for a specific case instance.

At a glance, this value provides a single top-level indicator of SLA health for the refunds and disputes domain. Rising totals over time may indicate that workloads, staffing levels, or process complexity are misaligned with the current SLA targets and that corrective action is required.

cancellation_violation_count.description:
Number of SLA violations associated with cancellation-related cases in the configured dashboard period.

This metric counts SLA violation rows in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` where the underlying case is a cancellation request (for example, via a specific `case_type` value and a non-null cancellation request foreign key). It reflects how often the platform fails to meet commitments such as acknowledging or finalizing cancellation requests within the configured time limits.

Operational and governance teams use this field to monitor whether customers receive timely responses to cancellation requests and whether seller or admin processes are keeping up with expected service levels. Sustained high values can justify adjusting SLA targets, re-prioritizing work queues, or providing stronger automation for cancellation flows.

refund_violation_count.description:
Number of SLA violations associated with refund-related cases in the configured dashboard period.

This metric aggregates SLA violation records where the affected case is a refund request, typically identified by a refund-oriented `case_type` and a non-null refund request foreign key in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`. It includes breaches of rules such as maximum time to initial review, time to customer follow-up, or time to final refund decision.

From a business perspective, this value is closely tied to customer satisfaction and regulatory expectations in some markets. A high or increasing count of refund SLA breaches suggests that customers may be waiting too long for refunds or decisions, and that additional operational capacity, process refinement, or policy updates may be necessary.

dispute_violation_count.description:
Number of SLA violations associated with dispute-related cases in the configured dashboard period.

This metric captures SLA violations for dispute cases (for example, payment disputes or complex order conflicts) detected in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` during the reporting window. It commonly includes breaches of SLAs related to initial acknowledgement, evidence review timelines, or final decision deadlines.

Because dispute handling often has direct implications for customer trust, seller confidence, and in some jurisdictions regulatory compliance, this count is a critical risk indicator. Persistent or growing dispute SLA violations can highlight the need for specialized dispute teams, improved tooling, or revised SLA definitions that more accurately reflect operational realities while still protecting customers and the platform.

IShoppingMallTopRefundReason.description:
Aggregated representation of a top refund reason within a dashboard period.

Each instance of this type corresponds to a structured reason record from the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` Prisma model and the aggregated counts of refund requests that referenced it during the selected analysis period. The DTO is intentionally designed as an analytics projection rather than a full CRUD mirror of the underlying table, so only the most relevant identification and display fields plus aggregated metrics are exposed.

The `label` field is typically derived from the human‑readable name of the refund request reason (for example, from the `name` column of `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` or from its localized presentation layer), while `reason_id` provides the stable UUID identifier of the canonical reason row. The `request_count` value is computed from refund‑related activity (for example, from `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, or snapshot tables) and is not stored directly on the reason entity.

This type is primarily used in administrative dashboards, analytics widgets, and reporting endpoints to highlight the most frequent refund and cancellation drivers across the marketplace. It can be safely combined with other statistics such as refunds‑by‑status or SLA metrics to help operations and governance teams understand trends and root causes.

reason_id.description:
Identifier of the structured refund request reason.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key (`id`) of a row in the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` Prisma model and uniquely identifies which canonical reason is being summarized in this analytics bucket.

code.description:
Business code representing the refund or cancellation reason.

The code is a stable, machine‑friendly key such as `damaged_item` or `not_delivered` that maps directly to the `code` column of `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons`. It is suitable for use in logs, configuration, integration payloads, and programmatic filters where a concise identifier is required.

label.description:
Human‑readable display label for the refund reason used in dashboards and reports.

The label is typically derived from the underlying reason’s display name (for example, the `name` column of `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` or a localized variant) and is intended for direct presentation in UI components. Clients may further localize or format this value according to the active locale and design system conventions.

request_count.description:
Number of refund or cancellation requests within the selected dashboard period that referenced this reason as their primary structured reason.

This value is computed by aggregating refund‑related case data (for example, from `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, or snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`) and is not persisted on the reason row itself. It is commonly used to rank top reasons and to visualize which issues are driving the highest volume of refund activity.

IShoppingMallRefundsByStatusStatistics.description:
Aggregated refund statistics grouped by refund status for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a read-only analytics view built over refund-related Prisma models such as `shopping_mall_payment_refunds`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, and snapshot/aggregate tables like `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. It exposes only summarized counts and monetary totals per refund status and does not map 1:1 to a single Prisma table.

Typical use cases include admin dashboards and monitoring tools that need to understand how many refunds are in each status (for example pending, approved, rejected, completed) and what the total refunded amounts are for each group within a given time window.

statuses.description: List of refund status buckets. Each bucket aggregates statistics for a single refund status, including the number of refund cases and the total refunded amount in that status.

totalRefundCount.description: Total number of refund cases included in this aggregation across all statuses.

totalRefundAmount.description: Total refunded monetary amount across all statuses, expressed in the smallest currency unit used by the underlying payment/refund system (for example cents for USD).

currency.description: Currency code for the monetary amounts in this response, typically a three-letter ISO 4217 currency code such as `USD` or `KRW`. All monetary values in the statistics share this currency.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when these refund statistics were generated. Clients can use this to understand the freshness of the analytics data and for cache validation.

IShoppingMallRefundsByStatusStatistics.I.description:
Single refund status bucket within `IShoppingMallRefundsByStatusStatistics`.

Each bucket aggregates all refund records that share the same business status (for example `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or other domain‑specific states used by the shoppingMall platform). The bucket exposes both the number of refund cases and monetary aggregates for that status to support dashboards and analytic visualizations.

All monetary amounts in this bucket use the same currency as the parent `IShoppingMallRefundsByStatusStatistics` object. Implementations should ensure that the currency is consistent across all buckets in a single response so that totals and averages are meaningful and directly comparable.

status.description:
Refund status represented by this bucket (for example `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or any other business-defined refund state).

The exact set of allowed values is determined by the platform’s refund status model and may be backed by enumerations or configuration tables in the payment and refund domain.

refundCount.description:
Number of refund cases that currently have this status.

This count is typically derived by grouping refund records by their current status over the requested analysis window. It is used in dashboards to understand workload distribution and identify backlogs or bottlenecks in the refund pipeline.

totalRefundAmount.description:
Total refunded monetary amount for all refund cases in this status.

The amount is an aggregated sum (for example, SUM over a Decimal column) expressed in the smallest currency unit used by the payment and refund system, such as cents for USD. The currency matches the `currency` field of the parent `IShoppingMallRefundsByStatusStatistics` object.

averageRefundAmount.description:
Average refunded monetary amount for refunds in this status.

The average is typically computed as `totalRefundAmount / refundCount` using the same currency and units as `totalRefundAmount` and the parent statistics object. When there are no refunds in this status (for example, `refundCount` is 0), this field may be omitted from the response or set to 0 depending on implementation preferences.

IShoppingMallDisputesByStatusStatistics.description:
Aggregated dispute statistics grouped by dispute status for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO provides a read-only analytical view over dispute-related Prisma entities such as `shopping_mall_disputes`, `shopping_mall_dispute_events`, and snapshot/metrics tables like `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. It does not correspond to a single table; instead, it aggregates the number of disputes and related metrics for each dispute status.

Common use cases include risk, governance, and operations dashboards that need to monitor how many disputes are open, under review, resolved, or escalated, as well as the total disputed amount and average age in days for each status group.

statuses.description: List of dispute status buckets. Each bucket aggregates statistics for disputes that share the same current status, including counts and key metrics such as total disputed amount and average age.

totalDisputeCount.description: Total number of disputes included in this aggregation across all statuses.

totalDisputedAmount.description: Total disputed monetary amount across all disputes in this aggregation, expressed in the smallest currency unit used by the payment system (for example cents for USD).

currency.description: Currency code for the monetary amounts in this response, typically a three-letter ISO 4217 currency code such as `USD` or `KRW`. All monetary values in the statistics share this currency.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when these dispute statistics were generated. Clients can use this to understand the freshness of the analytics data and for cache validation.

IShoppingMallDisputesByStatusStatistics..description:
Single dispute status bucket within `IShoppingMallDisputesByStatusStatistics`.

Each bucket aggregates statistics for disputes that currently share the same business status (for example `open`, `under_review`, `resolved`, `escalated`, or other platform-specific statuses). It exposes counts, monetary aggregates, and age-related metrics that are useful for SLA monitoring, backlog analysis, and workload planning.

The required fields (`status`, `disputeCount`, and `totalDisputedAmount`) provide the core identity and scale of the bucket. Optional fields such as `averageDisputedAmount` and `averageAgeDays` may be omitted or set to neutral values when no disputes exist in the bucket or when the underlying analytics layer cannot reliably compute the corresponding averages for the chosen reporting window.

status.description:
Dispute status represented by this bucket (for example `open`, `under_review`, `resolved`, `escalated`, or other platform-specific dispute statuses).

The exact set of allowed values is determined by the dispute status model in the shoppingMall platform and typically aligns with the statuses used in `shopping_mall_disputes` and related workflow tables. This value is intended for display in analytics charts and tables rather than for direct persistence back to the database.

disputeCount.description:
Number of disputes that currently have this status within the reporting scope.

This count reflects the population of disputes included in the analytics query for the specific status bucket. It is commonly used as the denominator for average metrics and as a primary indicator of backlog size or workload for the given status.

totalDisputedAmount.description:
Total monetary amount currently under dispute for all disputes in this status, expressed in the smallest currency unit used by the payment system (for example cents for USD).

The value aggregates the disputed portions of underlying orders or payments that are associated with disputes in this status bucket. When multi-currency scenarios are supported, the analytics layer is expected to normalize values into a platform base currency before populating this field.

averageDisputedAmount.description:
Average disputed monetary amount for disputes in this status, expressed in the smallest currency unit used by the payment system.

Typically computed as `totalDisputedAmount / disputeCount` when `disputeCount` is greater than zero. When there are no disputes in this status for the selected window, the analytics layer may omit this field or set it to a neutral value such as 0, and clients should treat it as optional rather than guaranteed.

averageAgeDays.description:
Average age in days of disputes in this status for the selected reporting window.

Age is usually calculated from the dispute creation timestamp or from the most recent transition into the current status, depending on the business rules of the dispute workflow. When `disputeCount` is zero or when age information is incomplete for the disputes that qualify for this bucket, this field may be omitted, and clients must handle its absence gracefully.

IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesSlaCompli.description:
Aggregated SLA (Service Level Agreement) compliance statistics for refund-, cancellation-, and dispute-related cases in the shoppingMall platform.

This analytical DTO consolidates metrics derived from multiple underlying persistence tables, including SLA configuration records in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, violation records in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`, and daily aggregate snapshots in `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. It is designed purely as a read-only projection for administrative dashboards and operational reports rather than as a direct representation of any single Prisma model.

The root structure groups metrics by logical case type through the `caseTypeStatistics` collection and exposes platform-wide aggregates through the `overallTotals` object. Each per-type entry is represented by `IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesSlaComplianceStatisticsCaseTypeGroup`, and the global aggregate is represented by `IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesSlaComplianceStatisticsOverallTotals`. These nested schemas capture case counts, SLA breach counts, compliance ratios, and timing characteristics such as average first-response and resolution times.

The `generatedAt` timestamp indicates when the analytics snapshot was produced, allowing clients to display data freshness and avoid confusion in dashboards that may be refreshed on different schedules. When the reporting window contains no matching cases, `caseTypeStatistics` may legitimately be an empty array while `overallTotals` conveys zero-volume metrics, ensuring that the response remains structurally stable even for low-activity periods.

caseTypeStatistics.description:
Per-case-type SLA compliance statistics for the refunds and disputes domain.

Each element in this array represents aggregated SLA metrics for a single logical case type, such as cancellation requests, refund requests, or dispute cases. Values are derived by combining configuration data from `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`, violation rows from `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`, and the corresponding case tables (`shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, `shopping_mall_disputes`) over the reporting window.

The array may be empty when the selected reporting period does not contain any matching cases, but it will always be present so that clients can safely iterate without null checks.

overallTotals.description:
Platform-wide SLA compliance totals across all monitored case types in the refunds and disputes domain.

This object summarizes high-level counts and ratios without a `caseType` dimension, combining information from all case families that are covered by `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs`. Typical metrics include the total number of cases evaluated, the number of cases that breached at least one SLA, and the overall SLA compliance rate.

Consumers typically use this object to render a single headline KPI (for example, overall SLA compliance percentage) alongside more detailed per-case-type tiles based on the `caseTypeStatistics` collection.

generatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when these SLA compliance statistics were generated.

The value is expressed as an ISO 8601 UTC `date-time` string and corresponds to the execution time of the analytics job or on-demand query that produced this snapshot. Clients can use this field to display last-updated information in dashboards and to detect when cached data is stale compared to other operational views.

IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesSlaCompli.description:
Aggregated SLA compliance metrics for a single case type, such as cancellations, refunds, or disputes.

Each record in this group corresponds logically to a subset of cases that share the same `case_type` value in configuration and violation tables such as `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` and `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`. The underlying population is typically drawn from one or more transactional case tables such as `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, and `shopping_mall_disputes`, filtered so that only rows matching the given case type are included.

The metrics are computed by an analytics layer over a bounded reporting window (for example, the last day, week, or month). The exact time window, filter criteria, and aggregation rules are defined by the calling API or analytics job and are not encoded directly in this DTO. Client code should treat all values as read‑only analytics derived from historical data rather than as fields that can be written back to a single Prisma model row.

This schema is primarily used for administrative dashboards and SLA monitoring views where multiple case types are listed side by side. It allows operations and governance users to compare workload, breach rates, and handling speed across different categories of cases at a glance.

caseType.description:
Logical case type for the SLA metrics represented by this group.

Typical values correspond to the `case_type` column in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` and `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`, such as `cancellation`, `refund`, or `dispute`. The analytics pipeline uses this value to group cases before computing aggregates.

Client applications should treat this as a business label rather than a closed technical enum. New case types may be introduced over time without changing this schema, so consumers should handle unknown values gracefully and avoid hard‑coding strict switch statements that assume a fixed set.

totalCaseCount.description:
Total number of cases of this type included in the analytics calculation for the selected reporting window.

This value is derived by counting the relevant rows from the underlying case tables, for example `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, or `shopping_mall_disputes`, after all filters such as date range, status, and actor scope are applied.

The count is always a non‑negative integer. When the reporting window contains no cases of this type, this field is set to 0 and the interpretation of ratio fields such as `slaComplianceRate` is determined by the analytics implementation (for example, defaulting to 0 or leaving ratios unchanged from a prior window).

slaBreachCount.description:
Number of cases of this type that breached at least one configured SLA during the reporting window.

Breaches are typically inferred from rows in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` that are associated with the population of cases used to compute `totalCaseCount`. The analytics layer may decide whether multiple violations on the same case are collapsed into a single case‑level breach or counted separately; this DTO exposes the final case‑level count after that decision.

This value is always a non‑negative integer and cannot exceed `totalCaseCount` within the same group. When there are no cases, this field is normally 0.

slaComplianceRate.description:
Fraction of cases of this type that complied with their configured SLAs over the reporting window.

A value of 1 represents 100% compliance (no breaches), and 0 represents 0% compliance (all cases breached). In common implementations this value is computed as `1 - (slaBreachCount / totalCaseCount)` when `totalCaseCount` is greater than zero.

When the reporting window contains no cases of this type, the analytics layer must define how to populate this field (for example, setting it to 0, null in a surrounding union, or carrying forward a historical average). Consumers should treat it as a normalized ratio in the inclusive range [0, 1] and avoid assumptions beyond that documented contract.

averageFirstResponseTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between case creation and the first relevant response action for cases of this type in the reporting window.

This metric is computed from timestamps stored on the underlying case and history tables, such as creation timestamps on refund or cancellation records and first response events or status transitions recorded in tables like `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories` or `shopping_mall_dispute_events`.

The value is always a non‑negative number expressed in hours and may include fractional values for sub‑hour precision. When there are no cases, or when response timestamps are missing for all cases in the window, this value is typically set to 0 or another sentinel as defined by the analytics engine. Client applications should present it as an approximate average response time indicator rather than an exact SLA contract value for any individual case.

averageResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between case creation and final resolution for cases of this type in the reporting window.

Resolution usually corresponds to a terminal status such as `approved`, `rejected`, `resolved`, or `closed` on the case tables, potentially captured through status history tables like `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories` or dispute event logs. Only cases that reach a terminal state within the reporting window are typically included when computing this average.

The value is a non‑negative number expressed in hours and may include fractional values for partial hours. A lower value generally indicates faster end‑to‑end handling of cases, while higher values may point to process bottlenecks or backlog. When no resolvable cases are present in the window, the analytics logic defines how this field is populated (commonly 0 or omitted from charts) and consumers should handle such edge cases explicitly in UI and reporting logic.

IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesSlaCompli.description:
Overall SLA compliance aggregates across all refund‑, cancellation‑, and dispute‑related cases for a given reporting window.

This DTO consolidates the same underlying population used by per‑case‑type groups into a single, platform‑wide set of totals. It draws from the relevant case tables (for example, `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, and `shopping_mall_disputes`) together with SLA configuration and violation records in `shopping_mall_case_sla_configs` and `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations`.

The primary use case is high‑level KPI tiles and summary panels on administrative dashboards, where a single compliance figure and global breach count provide a quick health check of how well the platform is adhering to its case handling SLAs. These values are computed by the analytics layer and are not intended to be written back to any single Prisma model row.

totalCaseCount.description:
Total number of cases across all supported case types that are considered in the SLA analytics for the selected reporting window.

This value is obtained by aggregating counts from all relevant case sources, such as rows in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, and `shopping_mall_disputes`, after applying the same filters and time window used for per‑type metrics.

The count is always a non‑negative integer. When the reporting window is empty (no relevant cases across all types), this field is 0 and downstream consumers should handle ratio metrics like `slaComplianceRate` accordingly.

slaBreachCount.description:
Total number of cases across all supported case types that breached at least one configured SLA in the reporting window.

This value is computed by aggregating case‑level breach information derived from `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` joined with the underlying case universe. Whether multiple violations on a single case are collapsed into one case‑level breach or counted separately is a concern of the analytics layer; the DTO exposes the final case‑level breach count once that decision has been applied.

The count is always a non‑negative integer and, for a given window, cannot exceed `totalCaseCount`. When `totalCaseCount` is 0, this value is typically 0 as well.

slaComplianceRate.description:
Overall SLA compliance rate across all monitored case types for the reporting window.

Conceptually, this is a normalized ratio in the inclusive range [0, 1], where 1 indicates that no cases breached their SLAs and 0 indicates that all cases breached. Implementations commonly compute this as `1 - (slaBreachCount / totalCaseCount)` when `totalCaseCount` is greater than zero.

When there are no cases in the window (that is, `totalCaseCount` equals 0), the analytics engine must decide how to populate this field—for example, defaulting to 0, leaving the metric undefined in a surrounding structure, or using a convention documented with the specific API. Clients should treat this field purely as an aggregate KPI and avoid deriving per‑case guarantees from it.

IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesCaseSearc.description:
Search criteria and pagination options for locating refund-, cancellation-, and dispute-related cases in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used as the request body of the complex search operation `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/refundsAndDisputes/search/cases`. It allows admin users to filter cases that originate from `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_requests`, and `shopping_mall_disputes`, and to narrow down results based on status, creation date, SLA compliance, and related order or actor information.

The structure separates filter conditions from pagination and sorting controls so that clients can construct rich queries while keeping the request body predictable. All filter fields are optional, and combining multiple filters results in intersection semantics (logical AND) unless the service documentation specifies otherwise.

page.description:
One-based index of the result page to retrieve.

If omitted, the service applies a default, typically page 1. This value works together with `limit` to define which slice of the matching case set is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of case summaries to return in a single page.

If omitted, the service applies a default page size and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance. Typical values range from 20 to 100, depending on operational needs.

items.description:
Single case type value used as part of the `caseTypes` filter.

Values align with the logical `case_type` dimension used in SLA and case analytics, for example `cancellation`, `refund`, or `dispute`. The service treats unknown values as invalid or ignores them according to implementation.

caseTypes.description:
List of case types to include in the search results.

If provided, only cases whose logical type is one of the listed values are returned. Leaving this field empty or omitting it means no filtering by case type and the query may return cancellations, refunds, and disputes together.

items.description:
Single case status used as part of the `statuses` filter.

Status values correspond to the current lifecycle state of each case, such as `pending`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `open`, `resolved`, or `closed`. Exact allowed values are defined by business policy and may differ by case type.

statuses.description:
List of case lifecycle statuses to filter by.

Only cases whose current status is one of the listed values are included in the results. Leaving this field empty or omitting it means no status-based filtering, and all statuses are eligible.

items.description:
Single actor type used as part of the `requestedByActorTypes` filter.

Typical values include `customer`, `seller`, and `admin`, mirroring the `requested_by_actor_type` columns on `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` and `shopping_mall_refund_requests`. Additional values may be introduced as the platform evolves.

requestedByActorTypes.description:
List of actor types that initiated the cases to include in the results.

When provided, only cases whose requester type is in this list are returned. This is commonly used to separate customer-initiated cases from seller-initiated or admin-initiated ones.

orderCode.description:
External or business-visible identifier of the order associated with the cases being searched.

This field is used to restrict results to cases linked to a specific order, typically via `shopping_mall_order_id` and the corresponding external order code on `shopping_mall_orders`. When set, it is common for this filter to dominate other filters and narrow results to a single order-related cluster of cases.

customerCode.description:
Business-visible identifier of the customer whose cases should be returned.

This is often a stable external code or login identifier that maps to a record in `shopping_mall_customers`. It allows admins to review all relevant cancellation, refund, and dispute cases for a particular customer.

sellerCode.description:
Business-visible identifier of the seller whose cases should be returned.

This value maps to seller identities in `shopping_mall_sellers` and is useful to review cases where a particular seller is involved, such as refund cases, seller-initiated cancellations, or disputes tied to that seller's orders.

includeOnlySlaBreached.description:
If true, restricts the search results to cases that have at least one recorded SLA violation.

Internally, this filter uses `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` to determine which cases are considered breached. When false or omitted, both compliant and non-compliant cases may be returned depending on other filters.

createdFrom.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range for cases to include.

Cases whose creation timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are eligible for inclusion. The value should be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format, typically in UTC.

createdTo.description:
End of the creation timestamp range for cases to include.

Cases whose creation timestamp is less than or equal to this value are eligible for inclusion. The value should be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format, typically in UTC. When used together with `createdFrom`, the pair defines a closed time interval.

sortBy.description:
Primary sort field to apply when ordering the search results.

Common values include `created_at`, `updated_at`, `status`, and `slaRisk`. The exact allowed values are defined by the search implementation. If omitted, a sensible default such as `created_at` descending is typically applied.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the primary sort field.

The value is usually `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending, matching common ordering semantics. If omitted, the service applies a default direction, often `desc` for time-based fields.

IShoppingMallReview.description:
Detailed review entity representing a single customer-written product review stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table.

This type models the canonical current version of a review including business fields such as rating, optional title and body, visibility and moderation state flags, verified purchase status, incentivized status, and derived helpfulness information.

It also includes belongs-to associations to the authoring customer, the reviewed product, and optionally the specific SKU variant and originating order item, all expressed as `.ISummary` DTOs to provide rich context without creating circular reference chains.

The schema is aligned with the Prisma model for `shopping_mall_reviews` and respects soft deletion semantics through the `deleted_at` field as well as uniqueness and foreign key constraints enforced at the database level. Sensitive internal-only properties such as raw foreign-key identifiers and low-level moderation artifacts are not exposed here; instead, this DTO focuses on customer- and storefront-visible fields that are safe to return in public or customer-authenticated contexts.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review record.

This value corresponds to the primary key in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and is generated by the system when the review is created. It is used in all detail retrieval and update operations as the stable handle for this review.

Clients treat this identifier as an opaque value and must not attempt to infer any business semantics from its structure.

rating.description:
Star rating value assigned by the customer for the reviewed product or SKU.

The rating uses a discrete integer scale such as 1–5 where higher numbers represent more positive evaluations. Business rules enforce that the value falls within the configured bounds, and validation logic will reject values outside the allowed range.

This field is consumed by rating aggregation processes that compute product- and SKU-level averages in tables such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates`.

title.description:
Optional short headline summarizing the review.

When present, the title is a concise sentence or phrase used in list views and detail headers to quickly communicate the main sentiment of the review. It is stored as a nullable string in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and may be omitted or set to null when the customer chooses not to provide a separate title.

Applications typically enforce a reasonable maximum length so that titles remain readable in UI components such as cards and tables.

body.description:
Optional free-form text body containing the detailed review content written by the customer.

The body holds the main textual feedback and may be of substantial length, subject to platform-configured limits for moderation and performance. It can be null or empty when the customer submits a rating-only review without additional comments.

Search, analytics, and moderation subsystems may index or scan this field using GIN-backed full-text capabilities, but those internals are not directly exposed at the API boundary.

visibility_status.description:
Current visibility status of the review in customer-facing and internal contexts.

Typical values include states such as `visible`, `hidden`, `pending_moderation`, or `removed`, though the exact enumeration is defined by business policy. This field is used by query logic to decide which reviews may be returned by public list and detail endpoints and which must be filtered out.

Moderation workflows update this field as decisions are made, and client applications can use it to render badges or state indicators in customer account views and administrative consoles.

moderation_state.description:
High-level moderation state reflecting where this review sits in the moderation lifecycle.

Examples include states such as `unreviewed`, `under_review`, `approved`, or `rejected`, depending on how moderation processes are modeled. This value guides back-office tooling and automated pipelines that triage and resolve reported or risky reviews.

Customer-facing endpoints may expose this field in a limited way (for example, to indicate that a review is pending approval) but should avoid leaking sensitive moderation logic details when not appropriate.

verified_purchase.description:
Flag indicating whether this review is associated with a verified purchase event.

When true, the review has been validated against order history via fields such as `shopping_mall_order_item_id` in the underlying table and meets the platform’s criteria for verified purchase semantics. Many storefront UIs display a special marker for verified reviews.

When false, the review may originate from legacy imports, pre-existing partnerships, or scenarios where a direct linkage to a single order item is not available.

incentivized.description:
Flag indicating whether the review was written under an incentive program.

An incentivized review is one where the customer received some form of reward or compensation, such as coupons, loyalty points, or gifts, in exchange for writing the review. Regulatory requirements and platform policies often require that such reviews be clearly labeled to maintain transparency.

This field does not indicate whether the content is biased; it simply records the presence of an incentive so that UIs and reporting tools can distinguish these reviews from organic ones.

helpfulness_score.description:
Derived integer score representing the net helpfulness of this review.

The score is typically calculated as the difference between the number of helpful votes and unhelpful votes recorded in tables such as `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`. Application logic updates this value as new votes are submitted, and list endpoints use it to sort reviews by perceived usefulness.

Although derived, the score is persisted on the `shopping_mall_reviews` record for efficient querying and should not be directly modified by clients.

customer.description:
Belongs-to association to the customer who authored this review.

This reference summarizes the `shopping_mall_customers` row linked through the internal `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key, providing enough identity and profile context to render the author in review detail views.

Using the `.ISummary` variant prevents circular reference chains while still enabling clients to show key customer information next to each review without separate lookups.

product.description:
Belongs-to association to the product that this review is about.

Internally, this corresponds to the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key on the `shopping_mall_reviews` table, which links to a row in `shopping_mall_products`.

Including this `.ISummary` reference allows review detail endpoints to present the product context—such as name, imagery, and basic identifiers—without requiring clients to call separate product APIs.

sku.description:
Optional belongs-to association to the specific SKU variant that was reviewed, when the review targets a particular variant instead of only the parent product.

This reference is backed by the nullable `shopping_mall_sku_id` foreign key and links to a row in `shopping_mall_skus`. When non-null, it indicates that the customer’s feedback applies to a concrete variant such as a specific size or color.

Representing the relation as `.ISummary` ensures that variant context is available in review detail UIs without introducing circular references or heavy nested compositions.

orderItem.description:
Optional belongs-to association to the originating order item from which this review’s verified purchase semantics are derived.

When present, this reference summarizes the `shopping_mall_order_items` row linked by the nullable `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key and provides order-context information useful in admin tools and order-centric views.

The association is expressed as an `.ISummary` to give sufficient context (such as SKU, quantity, and price) without embedding entire order aggregates or creating circular references back to collections of reviews.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the review was first created.

The value is stored as a non-null datetime in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and represents the moment when the review content was initially persisted. It is used for chronological sorting, eligibility windows, and audit reporting.

Clients treat this timestamp as read-only and typically display it in localized formats appropriate to the end user.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the review was last updated.

This value is changed whenever mutable fields on the review—such as rating, title, or body—are edited by the customer or when system processes alter moderation-related fields. Together with `created_at`, it provides a simple audit trail of the most recent modification time.

Client applications often display this information to indicate that a review has been edited since its original submission.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the review, if it has been logically removed.

When null, the review is considered active from a persistence standpoint, subject to additional visibility rules determined by `visibility_status` and `moderation_state`. When set to a non-null datetime value, the record has been soft-deleted and should be excluded from standard customer-facing queries.

Administrative tools and legal or compliance processes may continue to access soft-deleted reviews for audit, risk, or regulatory purposes, while public APIs treat these reviews as effectively absent.

IShoppingMallReview.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall product review used in list views and as an embedded reference in other entities.

This summary focuses on the core identification, scoring, visibility, moderation, and helpfulness state of a review without carrying the full text body. It is intended for product detail rating sections, review lists, analytics panels, and aggregates where only an overview of each review is required.

The schema is aligned with the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model but deliberately omits raw foreign key identifiers, internal soft-delete flags, and any password- or token-related fields. Instead, it surfaces associated customer, product, and SKU entities as summary objects, enabling consumers to render rich lists without leaking authentication context or sensitive internal governance details.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review in the shopping mall review domain.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_reviews.id` and is used as the primary handle when linking to or fetching detailed information about a specific review. It does not encode any authentication or session information and is safe to expose in public APIs.

rating.description:
Star rating value given by the customer on a discrete integer scale.

The field is backed by `shopping_mall_reviews.rating` and typically uses a 1–5 scale where higher values indicate more positive evaluations. Business rules may enforce minimum and maximum values and may reject ratings outside the configured range.

title.description:
Optional short title summarizing the review.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_reviews.title`. When present it is shown in condensed review listings and highlights the main impression from the customer. When null the UI can fall back to body excerpts or rating-only representations.

visibility_status.description:
Current visibility status of the review in customer-facing contexts.

This field reflects `shopping_mall_reviews.visibility_status` and indicates whether the review is visible, hidden, pending moderation, or removed according to business and moderation rules. It is intentionally exposed only at a coarse-grained level and does not disclose sensitive internal reasons or moderator identities.

moderation_state.description:
High-level moderation state describing the current review moderation lifecycle.

It mirrors `shopping_mall_reviews.moderation_state` and is used by moderation tooling and dashboards to differentiate between newly submitted reviews, flagged content, under-review items, and reviews that have passed moderation checks.
