Only summarized state is exposed here; detailed moderation actions and reports live in separate admin-only DTOs.

verified_purchase.description:
Flag indicating whether the review is considered a verified purchase.

The value is derived from `shopping_mall_reviews.verified_purchase` based on linkage to completed order items and configured eligibility rules. It is commonly surfaced in UI badges so customers can distinguish between reviews from verified buyers and other feedback.

incentivized.description:
Flag indicating whether the review was written under some incentive program.

Backed by `shopping_mall_reviews.incentivized`, this field supports regulatory and transparency requirements by clearly marking reviews created in exchange for coupons, rewards, or other incentives. Client applications should display appropriate disclaimers when this flag is true.

helpfulness_score.description:
Derived integer score representing the net helpfulness of the review.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_reviews.helpfulness_score` and aggregates feedback such as helpful and not-helpful votes. It is used primarily for ranking reviews and enabling users to quickly see which reviews have been most useful to the community, while the underlying vote records remain stored in `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the review was first created.

The value is taken from `shopping_mall_reviews.created_at` and represents the initial submission time of the review. It is used in ordering lists, building timelines, and enforcing time-based review policies such as edit windows.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the review was last updated.

This is mapped from `shopping_mall_reviews.updated_at` and changes when either the author edits the review or system processes such as moderation workflows update visibility or state. It enables clients and auditors to see how recently the review content or its moderation state changed.

customer.description:
Summary of the customer who authored the review.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table. When present, it allows list and analytics views to render customer-facing information such as display name or avatar without issuing extra queries. For legacy or imported reviews where the customer link cannot be resolved, this field may be null.

The nested `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` type is designed to exclude authentication secrets such as password hashes, ensuring that exposing this object does not leak sensitive credential data.

product.description:
Summary of the product being reviewed.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and provides essential product context—such as title and thumbnail—for list and detail views that display reviews. It enables consumers to show which product a review belongs to without re-querying the catalog.

sku.description:
Optional summary of the specific SKU variant being reviewed.

This association replaces the nullable `shopping_mall_sku_id` foreign key from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table. When non-null, it gives precise variant context (for example size or color) in review listings. When null, the review is considered product-level only and variant information is not shown.

IShoppingMallReview.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying product reviews stored in the `shopping_mall_reviews` table.

This type encapsulates all client-specified criteria used when listing or searching review records, including rating and date ranges, visibility or moderation filters, and flags such as verified purchase or incentivized status. It also carries pagination and sorting parameters so that consumers can control how results are segmented and ordered.

The same request shape is reused across multiple review listing endpoints—global, product-scoped, SKU-scoped, and customer-scoped—where contextual constraints such as product or customer identity are provided via path parameters while this body controls additional filters and result formatting.

page.description:
Optional 1-based page index to retrieve when performing a paginated review search.

When provided, this value selects which page of results should be returned according to the requested `limit`. If omitted or null, service implementations may default to the first page or a sensible platform-wide default.

Clients typically start at page 1 and increment this value for subsequent requests when implementing explicit pagination controls.

limit.description:
Optional maximum number of review items to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for list and search operations. If omitted or null, the backend will use a default limit and may enforce an upper bound to protect service performance.

Choosing an appropriate `limit` helps balance between network efficiency and responsiveness of UI components that render reviews.

min_rating.description:
Optional lower bound for the star rating filter.

When set, only reviews whose `rating` is greater than or equal to this value are eligible to be returned. This allows clients to implement filters such as "4 stars and up".

The value must respect the allowed rating scale defined by platform policy, typically matching the integer range enforced on the `rating` column.

max_rating.description:
Optional upper bound for the star rating filter.

When set, only reviews whose `rating` is less than or equal to this value are eligible to be returned. Combined with `min_rating`, this supports rating range filters like "2 to 4 stars".

The backend will validate that `max_rating` is not lower than `min_rating` when both are provided to avoid contradictory criteria.

created_from.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound for the review creation timestamp.

When provided, only reviews with `created_at` greater than or equal to this date-time are included in the result set. This enables clients to restrict searches to recent reviews or specific historical windows.

The timestamp must be expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format and will be interpreted in UTC or the system’s standard time zone.

created_to.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound for the review creation timestamp.

When set, only reviews with `created_at` less than or equal to this date-time are returned. It is typically used together with `created_from` to constrain review searches to a time window.

The backend validates that `created_to` is not earlier than `created_from` when both are present, rejecting contradictory ranges.

visibility_statuses.description:
Optional list of visibility status values that reviews must match to be included.

Providing a non-empty array restricts results to reviews whose `visibility_status` is one of the specified values, such as `visible` or `pending_moderation`. When null or omitted, the server applies its default visibility policy, which commonly includes only user-visible reviews in public contexts.

This filter is especially useful for administrative tools that need to inspect specific subsets of reviews based on their display status.

moderation_states.description:
Optional list of moderation state values to include in the search.

When provided, only reviews whose `moderation_state` is one of the listed values are eligible for inclusion. Administrative and back-office interfaces use this filter to focus on reviews in particular moderation stages, such as `unreviewed` or `under_review`.

In customer-facing scenarios, this field is typically left null so that the service enforces its own default moderation visibility rules.

verified_purchase_only.description:
Optional flag indicating whether only verified purchase reviews should be returned.

If set to true, the query is restricted to reviews where `verified_purchase` is true. If set to false, the filter is explicitly disabled and both verified and non-verified reviews may appear. When null, the service may apply a default strategy or treat the flag as not specified.

This control allows UIs to implement toggles such as "Show only reviews from verified buyers".

incentivized_only.description:
Optional flag to restrict results to incentivized or non-incentivized reviews.

When true, only reviews with `incentivized` set to true are returned. When false, only reviews without incentives may be included. When null, no explicit filter on the incentive flag is applied and the default behavior of the service is used.

This enables analytic or compliance views that focus specifically on reviews written as part of incentive programs.

sort_by.description:
Optional field specifying the primary sort key for the result set.

Supported values include `created_at` for chronological ordering, `rating` for ordering by star score, and `helpfulness_score` for ordering by community-rated usefulness. When null or omitted, the service applies its default sort, which is often `created_at` descending.

The sort key interacts with `sort_direction` to determine whether results are ordered ascending or descending.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction applied to the chosen `sort_by` field.

A value of `asc` requests ascending order, while `desc` requests descending order. When null or absent, the backend will choose a sensible default—commonly `desc` for `created_at` to show the newest reviews first.

Clients should always consider the default behavior when not explicitly specifying a sort direction.

IShoppingMallReview.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for customer-written product reviews in the shopping mall platform.

This type models the client-provided fields required to create a new row in the `shopping_mall_reviews` Prisma model when a customer submits a review for a product, SKU, or order item.
It excludes system-managed identifiers, timestamps, and actor identity fields, which are derived from authentication context and server-side logic.

The DTO is used across multiple creation endpoints scoped by product, SKU, order item, or customer paths.
Path parameters such as productId, skuId, orderItemId, or customerId are never duplicated in this body; they are injected by the backend from the URL and authenticated session when persisting into `shopping_mall_reviews`.

rating.description:
Discrete star rating value given by the customer for the review.

The value is stored in the `rating` column of `shopping_mall_reviews` and must comply with the business-defined rating scale (typically 1–5).
Validation logic should enforce the minimum and maximum bounds before inserting the review row.

title.description:
Optional short title summarizing the review.

When provided, this value is persisted into the `title` column of `shopping_mall_reviews` and is used for quick scanning in review lists.
It may be null when the customer chooses not to specify a headline.

body.description:
Optional free-form text body containing the detailed review content.

This field maps to the `body` column in `shopping_mall_reviews` and can be null when the review is rating-only.
When present, it should respect any maximum length and content policies enforced by the platform.

IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying existing customer product reviews in the shopping mall platform.

This type represents the subset of `shopping_mall_reviews` columns that are allowed to change after initial creation, focusing on customer-authored content fields such as rating, title, and body.
It is used in PUT operations that target an existing review identified by a path parameter like `reviewId`, often additionally scoped by product, SKU, order item, or customer.

Identity, ownership, and governance-related fields such as the review's primary key, foreign keys to customer/product/SKU/order item, and policy-driven visibility or moderation state are never included here and must not be changed via this DTO.
Those aspects are controlled by server-side logic, moderation workflows, and related subsystems.

rating.description:
Updated discrete rating value for the review.

When provided, this new value overwrites the existing `rating` column in `shopping_mall_reviews`, subject to the allowed rating scale.
If omitted, the current rating is left unchanged.

title.description:
Updated short title for the review, or null to clear it.

This property updates the `title` column in `shopping_mall_reviews` when supplied and can be set to null to remove the headline.
If not present in the payload, the existing title remains as-is.

body.description:
Updated detailed review text, or null to clear it.

This field writes into the `body` column of `shopping_mall_reviews` and may be cleared by explicitly sending null when business rules allow.
Omitting the property leaves the current body untouched.

IShoppingMallReviewVersion.description:
Represents a historical snapshot of a customer-written product review in the shopping mall platform.

Each record captures the point-in-time state of a review's core fields such as rating, title, body, visibility status, and moderation state, as well as flags for verified purchase and incentivized status. This allows the platform to reconstruct exactly how a review looked at a specific time, independent of the current review record.

Snapshots are typically created when a customer edits their review or when moderation actions change visibility-critical fields. They are used by administrative tools, compliance workflows, and dispute resolution processes to provide a complete audit trail of review content over time.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this review version snapshot.

This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_review_versions table and uniquely distinguishes each historical version of a review. It is immutable once created and is used to retrieve a specific snapshot record for audit or inspection use cases.

review_id.description:
Identifier of the parent review whose state is captured by this snapshot, expressed in API-friendly naming.

This value corresponds to the underlying `shopping_mall_review_versions.shopping_mall_review_id` column and links the version record back to the main review entity in `shopping_mall_reviews`. It is used to group multiple version snapshots under a single logical review and to scope per‑review history queries and audit timelines.

rating.description:
Rating value of the review at the time this snapshot was created.

The rating preserves the historical score that the customer had assigned when this version became effective. Even if the customer later edits the rating, this value remains unchanged on the snapshot to support accurate reconstruction of the review's evolution.

title.description:
Title text of the review at the time of this snapshot, or null when no title was provided.

This field may differ from the current review title stored on the main `shopping_mall_reviews` record if the customer has edited the review since this snapshot was recorded.

body.description:
Body text of the review at the time this snapshot was captured, or null when no body text was set.

The value is stored to preserve the exact wording originally written by the customer, including any later‑edited or moderated content, for audit and compliance purposes.

visibility_status.description:
Visibility status of the review when this snapshot was created.

This field records whether the review was visible, hidden, pending moderation, or in another platform‑defined state at the time of the version. It enables reconstruction of when a particular review version was publicly accessible.

moderation_state.description:
Moderation state that applied to the review at the time of this snapshot.

The value reflects how the review was classified by moderation workflows (for example, pending, approved, rejected, or escalated). It is used to trace the moderation decision timeline for the underlying review.

verified_purchase.description:
Indicates whether the review was marked as a verified purchase at the time of this snapshot.

This flag preserves the historical verification status so that investigations can determine whether a given version was displayed with a verified‑purchase badge, even if the underlying order or linkage changes later.

incentivized.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether the review was considered incentivized when this snapshot was recorded.

This is used to audit the presence of incentives, promotions, or rewards that may have influenced the review at that point in time, in accordance with marketplace and regulatory guidelines.

snapshot_reason.description:
Optional reason describing why this version snapshot was created, or null if no explicit reason was recorded.

Examples include values like `author_edit`, `moderation_change`, or `system_migration`. This metadata helps auditors understand the triggering event that produced the snapshot.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this snapshot record was created.

The timestamp represents the effective time of the captured state in the `shopping_mall_review_versions` table and is used for ordering version history and constraining time‑based queries.

IShoppingMallReviewVersion.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying historical review version snapshots.

This DTO is used by administrative list and search endpoints over the `shopping_mall_review_versions` table, both for global queries and for per‑review history views. It allows callers to specify filters, sorting, and pagination settings when retrieving review version data for audit and moderation workflows.

Typical usage includes constraining results by parent review, rating ranges, creation time windows, or moderation and visibility states, while also controlling page number and page size for efficient navigation.

page.description:
Page index to retrieve when paginating review version results.

The page index is typically 1‑based and works together with the `limit` parameter to control which slice of the overall result set is returned to the client.

limit.description:
Maximum number of review version records to return per page.

This value is used as the page size in pagination logic. Implementations should enforce sensible maximums to protect the `shopping_mall_review_versions` table from excessively large scans and to keep admin tools responsive.

review_id.description:
Optional filter for restricting results to a single parent review identifier, using API‑level naming.

For the global search endpoint `/shoppingMall/admin/reviewVersions`, this field can be supplied to limit results to versions of a specific review. For the per‑review history endpoint `/shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/versions`, the `reviewId` path parameter provides the constraint and clients MUST NOT duplicate it in this body field; server‑side logic should derive the filter from the path in that case.

min_rating.description:
Optional lower bound for rating values when filtering review versions.

When provided, only versions whose `rating` is greater than or equal to this value are included. This is typically used to focus on higher or lower scoring review histories.

max_rating.description:
Optional upper bound for rating values when filtering review versions.

When provided, only versions whose `rating` is less than or equal to this value are included. Using both `min_rating` and `max_rating` together allows callers to define an inclusive rating range.

visibility_status.description:
Optional filter on the `visibility_status` field of review version snapshots.

When set, only snapshots whose `visibility_status` equals the specified value are returned. This is useful for isolating versions that were visible, hidden, pending, or otherwise categorized by visibility at the time.

moderation_state.description:
Optional filter on the `moderation_state` of review version snapshots.

Use this field to restrict results to versions in a specific moderation workflow state, such as pending, approved, rejected, or escalated, depending on the states defined in the business policy.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp when filtering version snapshots.

When set, only snapshots created at or after this timestamp are included in the result set, allowing time‑window queries such as "versions modified in the last 30 days".

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp when filtering version snapshots.

When set, only snapshots created at or before this timestamp are returned. Combined with `created_from`, this supports filtering review version history to a specific time range.

sort_field.description:
Optional name of the field used for sorting review version results.

When provided, this value indicates which column of the `shopping_mall_review_versions` table should be used as the primary sort key, for example `created_at` or `rating`. If omitted, a sensible default such as `created_at` descending is typically applied.

sort_order.description:
Optional sort direction for ordered review version results.

Common values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the implementation may default to descending `created_at` to show the newest versions first.

IShoppingMallReviewVersion.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a historical review version used for audit listings, timelines, and investigation tools.

Each instance describes one snapshot from the `shopping_mall_review_versions` table, capturing how a review looked at a specific point in time without necessarily exposing the full text body. It focuses on the rating, visibility and moderation state, and key flags that are important when reconstructing moderation or content change history.

This summary is optimized for scenarios where many version records must be displayed or analyzed at once, such as review change timelines or moderation audit reports, while still allowing callers to fetch full detail from a dedicated detail schema when necessary.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this review version snapshot.

This value is the primary key `shopping_mall_review_versions.id` and is used by internal tools and audit features to reference and retrieve a particular snapshot of review state.

review_id.description:
Identifier of the review whose state is captured in this version snapshot, using normalized API naming.

It corresponds to the underlying column `shopping_mall_review_versions.shopping_mall_review_id` and links back to the canonical review record in `shopping_mall_reviews`. This association allows timelines to be grouped per review and enables navigation between current and historical content using a consistent `review_id` field across the review APIs.

rating.description:
Rating value recorded at the time of this snapshot.

This maps to `shopping_mall_review_versions.rating` and preserves the exact score that was in effect when the version was created. It supports investigations into how a review’s rating may have changed over time.

title.description:
Optional title of the review at the time of this snapshot.

The field is backed by `shopping_mall_review_versions.title` and reflects the short summary text as it existed when the snapshot was taken. It may differ from the current title if the customer edited their review.

visibility_status.description:
Visibility status of the review at the time of this snapshot.

This value comes from `shopping_mall_review_versions.visibility_status` and indicates whether, at that specific moment, the review was visible, hidden, pending moderation, or removed. It is essential for reconstructing what customers could see at different times.

moderation_state.description:
Moderation state of the review at the time of this snapshot.

It is aligned with `shopping_mall_review_versions.moderation_state` and captures whether the review was awaiting moderation, flagged, under investigation, or cleared at the moment the snapshot was created. This helps moderation teams understand the progression of a case.

verified_purchase.description:
Flag indicating whether the review was considered a verified purchase in this version.

The value mirrors `shopping_mall_review_versions.verified_purchase` and remains fixed per snapshot even if eligibility logic or associated order data change later, ensuring auditability of historical decisions.

incentivized.description:
Flag indicating whether the review was marked as incentivized at the time of this snapshot.

Backed by `shopping_mall_review_versions.incentivized`, this property preserves historical knowledge of incentive labeling, which is important for regulatory compliance and transparency audits.

snapshot_reason.description:
Optional reason describing why this version snapshot was created.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_review_versions.snapshot_reason` and typically contains values such as `author_edit`, `moderation_change`, or `system_migration`. It gives human‑readable context for the change event represented by the snapshot.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this version snapshot was created.

The value is taken from `shopping_mall_review_versions.created_at` and represents the effective time of the captured state. It is used to order version histories and to align review changes with other system events in investigative workflows.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request schema for querying review report records in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is used by administrative moderation tools to perform filtered, paginated searches over the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table. It encapsulates the primary query dimensions described in the Prisma schema and API specifications, including report status, actor type, reason code, creation date ranges, and pagination/sorting controls.

The request is read-only and does not map directly to a single Prisma model via `x-autobe-prisma-schema` because it represents query parameters rather than a stored record. However, its fields are designed to align with columns in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and related models such as `shopping_mall_reviews` so that implementations can easily translate the criteria into Prisma query predicates.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which page of results to retrieve.

Consumers typically start from page 1. The service layer should enforce sensible upper bounds to prevent excessively deep pagination that could harm performance.

limit.description:
Maximum number of review report summaries to return in a single page.

This value controls the size of the result set and should be constrained by business rules and performance limits (for example, 20–100 items per page).

status.description:
Optional processing status filter for review reports.

The value corresponds to the `status` column in the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table, which represents the current moderation processing state such as `open`, `under_review`, `resolved`, or `dismissed`. When provided, only reports with the specified status are returned.

actor_type.description:
Optional filter for the type of actor who submitted the report.

The value corresponds to the `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table and is used to distinguish between reports submitted by customers, sellers, systems, or other actor categories defined by business rules.

reason_code.description:
Optional filter for the primary reason code associated with the report.

The value maps to the `reason_code` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and is used to focus searches on specific report categories such as `offensive_content`, `spam`, or `conflict_of_interest` as defined in platform policy.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp of review reports to include in the result set.

When provided together with `created_to`, this forms a time range filter over the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports`, enabling moderators to focus on reports created within particular windows.

created_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp of review reports to include in the result set.

Used together with `created_from` to form a bounded time interval filter for querying recent or historical review reports based on their creation time.

sort_field.description:
Name of the primary field used to sort the result set of review reports.

Typical values correspond to sortable columns in `shopping_mall_review_reports`, such as `created_at` or `updated_at`. Implementations should validate this field against an allowed set of sort keys and fall back to a default when absent or invalid.

sort_direction.description:
Direction of sorting applied to the primary sort field when returning review report results.

Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. The service layer should default to descending by creation time when no explicit sort is requested.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.description:
Detailed representation of a single review report as stored in the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table.

Each record corresponds to a complaint or flag raised against a customer product review stored in `shopping_mall_reviews`. The entity captures who reported the review (actor type and opaque reporter reference), the categorized reason, optional free-form description, and the current processing status.

It also records timestamps for creation, last update, and optional soft deletion, allowing governance and moderation tools to track the lifecycle of reports and audit how they were handled over time.

This DTO is used in read operations that expose the full report to administrative or moderation actors and now embeds a summary of the underlying review so that a single API call provides complete contextual information without additional lookups.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review report record.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table and is used in path parameters and internal references to identify a specific report unambiguously.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that submitted the report.

The value comes from the `actor_type` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and indicates whether the report originated from a customer, seller, system, or other actor class defined by business rules. Moderation interfaces use it to interpret the reporter context.

reporter_actor_reference.description:
Opaque reference identifier for the reporter, interpreted according to `actor_type` by the application layer.

This value maps to the `reporter_actor_reference` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports`. It is intentionally not defined as a strict foreign key in the schema so that polymorphic actor references (such as customers, sellers, or systems) can be represented without complex nullable relationships.

reason_code.description:
Categorized reason for the report, such as `offensive_content`, `spam`, or `conflict_of_interest`.

This field corresponds to the `reason_code` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and is used to group reports, drive moderation prioritization, and support analytics on common policy violations.

description.description:
Optional free-form description providing more context about why the review is considered problematic.

This field mirrors the `description` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and typically contains reporter-supplied text elaborating on the selected `reason_code`. It may contain sensitive or offensive language and should therefore be exposed only to trusted moderation interfaces.

status.description:
Processing status of the report, such as `open`, `under_review`, `resolved`, or `dismissed`.

This property reflects the `status` column in the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table and drives moderation workflows and service-level objectives. State transition rules are enforced in the application layer according to business policy.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was created.

This maps directly to the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and is set when the report row is first inserted. It is used for ordering, filtering, and auditing of moderation workloads.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the report record was last updated.

The value corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and is updated whenever mutable fields such as `status` or moderator notes change, enabling chronological tracking of report handling.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the report, if it has been logically removed from active workflows.

This property reflects the nullable `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports`. When set, the report should be excluded from normal moderation queues but retained for audit, compliance, or legal hold requirements.

review.description:
Summary of the customer review that this report targets.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_review_id` foreign key and provides the essential context—such as product, rating, and short content snippet—needed for moderators to understand the subject of the complaint without issuing a separate request to the review detail endpoint.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.ICreate.description:
Create request schema for a new review report stored in the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table.

This DTO is used when a marketplace actor, typically an authenticated customer, files a report against an existing product review from `shopping_mall_reviews`. It captures the target review identifier and the structured and free‑form information describing why the review is considered problematic.

Server logic maps this request into a new row in `shopping_mall_review_reports`, initializing auditing timestamps and default status while deriving reporter identity from the authenticated session rather than trusting client‑supplied actor identifiers.

shopping_mall_review_id.description:
Identifier of the review in `shopping_mall_reviews` that is being reported.

This value is persisted into the `shopping_mall_review_id` foreign key column of `shopping_mall_review_reports` and must reference an existing, report‑eligible review row. The service must validate existence and eligibility of the corresponding review before inserting a new report record.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that is submitting the report, such as `customer`, `seller`, or `system`.

This value is stored in the `actor_type` column of `shopping_mall_review_reports` and is interpreted by higher layers to understand the reporting context. Business rules and moderation tooling may use this field to filter, prioritize, or rate‑limit reports by actor category.

oneOf.description:
Opaque UUID reference that identifies the reporting actor in a way understood by the application layer.

This value is persisted into the `reporter_actor_reference` column of `shopping_mall_review_reports`. It is not modeled as a foreign key so that the component remains agnostic to polymorphic actor tables; instead, the combination of `actor_type` and this identifier is resolved by higher layers.

Null when no stable actor reference should be stored for this report.

This may occur for system‑generated reports or for certain internal flows where the reporter identity is tracked separately from `shopping_mall_review_reports`.

reporter_actor_reference.description:
Opaque reference identifier for the reporter, interpreted together with `actor_type`.

When provided, this UUID allows risk engines and moderation tools to correlate reports from the same logical actor across different reviews, without coupling this component to specific actor tables. The column is nullable in the Prisma model, so this field may be omitted or set to null when no such reference is appropriate.

reason_code.description:
Categorized reason for the report, such as `offensive_content`, `spam`, or `conflict_of_interest`.

This value is written to the `reason_code` column of `shopping_mall_review_reports` and is typically validated against a configured set of allowed codes. Moderation queues and analytics use this code to group and prioritize incoming reports by type of policy concern.

oneOf.description:
Optional free‑form explanation supplied by the reporter giving more context about the complaint.

This text is persisted into the `description` column of `shopping_mall_review_reports`. Clients should respect any maximum length constraints enforced at the API or database layer, and moderation tools may surface this text to reviewers when evaluating the report.

Null when the reporter chooses not to provide any additional free‑form explanation.

In this case only the structured `reason_code` and surrounding context are available for moderation workflows.

description.description:
Optional free‑form description elaborating on why the review is considered problematic.

This field mirrors the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and allows reporters to give natural‑language justification that supplements the structured `reason_code` value.

status.description:
Initial processing status of the report, for example `open`, `under_review`, `resolved`, or `dismissed`.

This value is stored in the `status` column of `shopping_mall_review_reports`. Implementations may choose to default it to an initial value such as `open` when the client omits it, but when provided it must respect the set of supported moderation states and any workflow‑specific transition rules.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.IUpdate.description:
Update request schema for an existing review report stored in the `shopping_mall_review_reports` table.

This DTO is used primarily by administrative and moderation tools to adjust mutable fields on a review report after it has been created. Typical updates include changing the moderation status, refining the reason code, or appending internal notes in the free‑form description field.

Immutable identifiers such as the primary key and the associated review reference are not part of this schema and must never be altered through this DTO. All business rules for allowed status transitions and field combinations must be enforced by the service layer before persisting changes.

actor_type.description:
Updated actor type classification for the reporter, such as `customer`, `seller`, or `system`.

Although actor identity is generally fixed at creation time, administrative workflows may occasionally need to correct mis‑classified actor types. When present in the update payload, this value overwrites the existing `actor_type` column for the report.

oneOf.description:
Replacement opaque UUID reference identifying the reporting actor.

Use this variant when back‑office processes need to correct or attach a reporter reference for an existing report. The combination of `actor_type` and this value remains application‑specific and is not enforced as a foreign key.

Explicitly clear any existing reporter reference associated with this report.

Setting this field to null instructs the service to set the `reporter_actor_reference` column to null, removing any previous linkage to a specific actor identity.

reporter_actor_reference.description:
New or cleared reporter reference for this review report.

This field maps to the nullable `reporter_actor_reference` column in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and allows moderation workflows to maintain or correct the linkage between report records and logical actors over time.

reason_code.description:
Updated classified reason for the report, for example to re‑categorize a complaint from `spam` to `offensive_content`.

When present, this value overwrites the `reason_code` column for the report. Implementations should validate the supplied code against the same catalog used at creation time to maintain consistent classification semantics across the system.

oneOf.description:
Replacement free‑form description providing moderator or reporter notes for this report.

This value is written to the `description` column of `shopping_mall_review_reports` and may contain additional context such as investigation results or policy references. Tooling should respect any maximum length constraints agreed for this column.

Explicitly clear any existing free‑form description associated with this report.

When set to null, the service should set the `description` column to null, removing prior explanatory text while leaving structured fields such as `reason_code` intact.

description.description:
New free‑form text or an explicit clear operation for the report’s descriptive details.

This mirrors the nullable `description` column on `shopping_mall_review_reports` and is often used by moderation staff to document decisions or by tools to remove outdated narrative content.

status.description:
Updated processing status for the review report, such as transitioning from `open` to `under_review`, `resolved`, or `dismissed`.

This field maps to the `status` column of `shopping_mall_review_reports`. The service layer must enforce valid state transitions according to business workflow rules and may require that certain statuses only be set when complementary data, such as resolution notes, is already present.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationAction.description:
Represents a single moderation decision or action applied to a specific customer review within the shoppingMall platform.

Each record corresponds to a row in the `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` table and provides an immutable audit trail entry describing what change was made to a review, why it was made, and who or what performed the action.

This type is used by administrative tooling and governance dashboards when inspecting the full history of moderation applied to reviews, and it always contains enough information to correlate the action back to the underlying review, any triggering report, and the acting admin when applicable.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderation action.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` record and is used to retrieve or reference this specific action from administrative APIs and audit logs.

review.description:
Summary representation of the review that this moderation action targets.

This object replaces the raw `shopping_mall_review_id` foreign key and points to a row in `shopping_mall_reviews`. It provides immediate context in admin tools and dashboards by exposing the core review attributes (such as rating, title, and author) without requiring a separate lookup.

oneOf.description: Null when this moderation action was not triggered by a specific report.

report.description:
Summary of the review report that directly triggered this moderation action, when applicable.

When present, this object replaces the former `shopping_mall_review_report_id` foreign key and references a row in `shopping_mall_review_reports`. It allows governance and moderation tools to trace the chain from a report through to the action that handled it. For proactive or system-driven actions that are not tied to a single report, this property is null.

oneOf.description: Null when the action was performed automatically by a system policy rather than a human administrator.

admin.description:
Summary information about the administrator who performed this moderation action, when the action is manually executed.

This object replaces the previous `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key and references an admin account from `shopping_mall_admins`. It gives audit and governance views concise context about which administrator executed the decision while avoiding exposure of raw IDs alone.

action_type.description:
Type of moderation action that was performed on the review.

Typical examples include values such as `hide_review`, `restore_review`, `edit_visibility`, or `escalate_dispute`. Platform-specific business logic may support additional action types, but all values are stored as opaque strings in the `action_type` column of `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions`.

previous_visibility_status.description:
Moderation-visible visibility status of the review before this action was applied.

This field is populated when the action changes how the review is exposed to customers or sellers and is useful for understanding transitions in visibility over time. It is null when the action does not affect visibility or when no prior status is applicable.

new_visibility_status.description:
Visibility status of the review after this moderation action was applied.

When the action modifies whether or how a review is shown (for example, hiding it from public listings or restoring it), this field records the resulting visibility state. It is null for actions that do not change visibility.

previous_moderation_state.description:
Moderation state of the review before this action was recorded.

Used to capture the prior governance or workflow status (such as `pending_review`, `approved`, or `under_investigation`) so that auditors can reconstruct the evolution of moderation over time. It is null when no previous moderation state is relevant.

new_moderation_state.description:
Moderation state of the review after this action was applied.

This value captures the updated governance or workflow status resulting from the action, enabling downstream systems and dashboards to determine the effective moderation state of the review. It is null when the action does not affect the moderation state.

reason_code.description:
Categorized reason code that explains why this moderation action was taken.

Common examples include values such as `policy_violation`, `legal_request`, and `manual_override`. The platform may manage these codes in dedicated policy or reason tables, but they are stored as simple strings on the moderation action for quick filtering and reporting.

note.description:
Optional free-text note providing additional context or explanation for the moderation decision.

Admins and automated systems can use this field to capture human-readable reasoning, references to internal tickets, or other narrative details helpful for future audits, dispute handling, and policy reviews.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this moderation action was recorded.

The value is written at creation time and never changes thereafter, ensuring that the moderation history for a review can be reconstructed in chronological order for audit and governance purposes.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationAction.ISum.description:
Summary view of a moderation action applied to a shopping mall review.

This DTO is optimized for timelines, activity feeds, and audit summaries that show how a review or associated report has been handled by admins or automated policies. It captures the core identity of the moderation action, its target review, an optional triggering report, and the acting admin in a compact form.

The schema maps to the `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` Prisma model but intentionally includes only the most important scalar fields and reference summaries, keeping it lightweight for paginated retrieval and embedding inside dispute, case, or review detail views.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderation action.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions.id` and uniquely identifies each discrete decision or step taken in the moderation workflow. It is a server-generated UUID and is immutable once created.

review.description:
Summary representation of the review that this moderation action targets.

This object replaces the raw `shopping_mall_review_id` foreign key and links the action to a specific row in `shopping_mall_reviews`. It provides enough information to render the review in lists and timelines without additional lookups.

oneOf.description: Null when the moderation action was not initiated from a specific report.

report.description:
Summary of the review report that triggered this moderation action, when applicable.

When present, this object points to a row in `shopping_mall_review_reports` and lets audit tooling and admin UIs show why the action occurred. When the action is proactive or automated and is not directly linked to a single report, this property is null.

oneOf.description: Null when the moderation action was performed automatically by system policies.

admin.description:
Summary view of the administrator who performed this moderation action, when the decision was made manually.

This object replaces the previous `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key and references an admin account from `shopping_mall_admins`. It is used in moderation timelines and governance dashboards to attribute decisions to specific moderators.

action_type.description:
Type of moderation action performed, such as `hide_review`, `restore_review`, `edit_visibility`, or `escalate_dispute`.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions.action_type` and summarizes the intent and effect of the action. It is the primary label used in audit timelines and operator dashboards to quickly understand what was done to the review.

reason_code.description:
Optional categorized reason for the moderation action, for example `policy_violation`, `legal_request`, or `manual_override`.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions.reason_code` and complements `action_type` by explaining why the action was taken. When not provided, the narrative context can be obtained from the full detail view or internal notes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the moderation action was recorded.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions.created_at` and represents the moment the system persisted the action. It is used for chronological ordering in moderation timelines and for reconstructing the sequence of decisions applied to a review.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationAction.ICre.description:
Create DTO for recording a new review moderation action in the shopping mall platform.

This type represents the business payload that an authenticated admin submits when registering a new moderation decision for a specific review in `shopping_mall_reviews`. It maps to the `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` Prisma model but deliberately excludes system-managed fields such as `id` and `created_at`, as well as actor identity and review foreign keys, which are derived from the request context (path parameters and authenticated admin session).

The DTO focuses on the mutable business aspects of the moderation event: which high-level action was performed, how the review visibility and moderation states should be changed, and why the action was taken. These fields are used to drive downstream effects such as hiding or restoring reviews, updating product rating aggregates, and maintaining a clear audit trail for governance and compliance teams.

Server-side logic will join this DTO with the target review identified by the `reviewId` path parameter and with the acting admin account taken from the admin authentication context. As a result, clients must not attempt to provide raw IDs for `shopping_mall_review_id` or `shopping_mall_admin_id` in this payload.

action_type.description:
Type of moderation action performed for the target review.

This value describes the high-level decision applied to the review content, for example `hide_review`, `restore_review`, `approve_review`, `reject_review`, or `escalate_dispute`. The exact set of supported values is determined by business policy configurations and moderation tooling, and the backend may validate this field against an internal list or an enum derived from policy tables.

The action type drives how the review is treated by the rest of the system, including whether it remains visible in customer-facing listings, whether it is flagged for further investigation, and which follow-up tasks are created for governance teams.

previous_visibility_status.description:
Previous visibility status of the review before this moderation action, when the status is known and relevant.

This field allows the moderation client to explicitly record what the review's effective visibility was at the time of the decision, for example `visible`, `hidden`, `pending`, or `flagged`. Storing this value in the moderation action helps auditors reconstruct how the state of the review evolved over time.

When the visibility status is not being tracked or is not applicable for the specific action type, this field can be omitted or set to null. The backend may cross-check the provided value against the current review state or fill it from canonical review data when omitted.

new_visibility_status.description:
New visibility status that should apply to the review as a consequence of this moderation action, when the action affects visibility.

Typical values might include `visible`, `hidden`, `soft_hidden`, or other policy-defined states used to control whether the review appears in public listings and detail views. This field allows moderation tools to express the intended post-action visibility even when the specific action type is generic.

If the moderation action does not modify visibility, this field can be omitted or set to null, and the backend will leave the current visibility unchanged.

previous_moderation_state.description:
Previous moderation state of the review before this action, when known.

Moderation state captures where the review sits in the moderation workflow, for example `pending_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `under_investigation`, or `locked_by_legal`. Recording the prior moderation state helps governance and risk teams reconstruct the sequence of decisions and verify that state transitions followed policy.

If the prior moderation state is not available at the time of the action or is not relevant for the given decision, this field may be omitted or null.

new_moderation_state.description:
New moderation state that should apply to the review after this action, when the action changes its workflow state.

This value describes the updated moderation lifecycle phase for the review, such as transitioning from `pending_review` to `approved`, from `approved` to `rejected`, or from `under_investigation` to `resolved`. Backend logic uses this field, together with the action type, to drive workflow transitions and enforce policy constraints.

If the moderation action does not alter the workflow state, this property can be omitted or set to null, and the system keeps the current moderation state unchanged.

reason_code.description:
Structured reason code that categorizes why this moderation action was taken.

Typical values may correspond to business policy definitions, such as `policy_violation`, `spam`, `hate_speech`, `legal_request`, `manual_override`, or other platform-specific reasons. Using a code instead of free-form text enables consistent reporting and analytics across large volumes of moderation events.

When the action does not match a predefined reason or when the moderator only provides a free-text note, this field may be omitted or null. In that case, the `note` field should be used to capture detailed context.

note.description:
Optional internal note describing the context, rationale, or additional details for the moderation decision.

This free-form text is intended for internal use by admins, legal, and risk teams. It may include references to policy clauses, links to external evidence, or specific observations about the review content. Notes are stored together with the moderation action and can be used during audits or investigations.

When there is no additional explanation beyond the structured reason code, this field can be omitted or set to null.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationAction.IUpd.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing review moderation action record.

This type represents the subset of fields on `shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions` that administrators are allowed to adjust after an action has been created. It is used together with the `reviewId` and `moderationActionId` path parameters to target a specific moderation action that belongs to a given review.

All properties are optional to support partial updates, and the DTO intentionally excludes immutable system-managed fields such as `id`, `shopping_mall_review_id`, `shopping_mall_review_report_id`, `shopping_mall_admin_id`, and `created_at`. These identifiers and timestamps remain fixed to preserve a reliable audit trail of who created the action and when.

Typical use cases for this DTO include correcting the action type, updating the moderation or visibility states to reflect new decisions, or refining the structured reason code and explanatory note as more information becomes available. The backend should validate that any attempted changes are permissible under the current workflow and legal constraints before applying them.

action_type.description:
Updated moderation action type to reflect a corrected or refined decision.

When supplied, this value replaces the existing `action_type` stored on the moderation action record, subject to business rules that may prohibit changing certain terminal or legally constrained actions. If omitted, the action type remains unchanged.

Typical values mirror those used at creation time, such as `hide_review`, `restore_review`, `approve_review`, or `reject_review`, and should be validated against the platform's allowed list.

previous_visibility_status.description:
Updated previous visibility status snapshot if the original value needs to be corrected for audit accuracy.

In most cases this field is set at creation time and does not change, but in scenarios where an earlier snapshot was inaccurate or incomplete, administrators may adjust it while maintaining a clear rationale in the `note` field. If this property is omitted, the stored value is left as-is.

new_visibility_status.description:
Updated target visibility status for the review if the moderation outcome has been revised.

For example, a review that was previously hidden may be restored to a `visible` state, or vice versa, after appeal or additional investigation. When provided, this value overwrites the existing `new_visibility_status` on the moderation action, and the system must ensure that derived review visibility is updated consistently.

If omitted, the previously stored visibility target remains unchanged.

previous_moderation_state.description:
Corrected snapshot of the moderation state before the action, when the original record needs adjustment.

Administrators may update this field to better reflect the true prior state of the review at the time the action was taken, improving the quality of the moderation timeline for audits and compliance. If left undefined, no change is applied.

new_moderation_state.description:
Updated moderation state that the review should move into as a result of this action.

This property allows admins to revise the intended workflow state, for example moving from `pending_review` to `approved` or `rejected` after new information becomes available. Any change here must be consistent with the platform's moderation workflow rules to avoid invalid state transitions.

If omitted, the existing moderation state associated with this action remains unchanged.

reason_code.description:
Updated structured reason code that categorizes why this moderation action exists.

Use this field to refine the categorization of the action, such as switching from a generic `policy_violation` to a more specific code after detailed review. This supports more accurate reporting and analytics. When omitted, the previous reason code is preserved.

note.description:
Updated internal note providing additional context or corrections to the original explanation for the moderation decision.

Admins can use this field to append new information, clarify the rationale, or correct mistakes in earlier notes. If this property is not included in the request, the existing note text remains untouched.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationAction.IReq.description:
Search and filter parameters for listing moderation actions associated with a specific review.

Instances of this DTO are used by administrative search endpoints that return paginated collections of moderation action summaries, allowing staff to constrain results to specific time ranges, action types, or acting admins.

The `reviewId` path parameter determines which review's moderation history is searched; this request body focuses only on additional filtering, sorting, and pagination hints applied within that scope.

page.description:
Page index used for offset-based pagination when browsing moderation actions.

A value of 1 usually represents the first page of results. When null, the backend may fall back to a default page index, often 1, depending on platform conventions.

limit.description:
Maximum number of moderation action summaries to return in a single page.

This value helps control response size for administrative clients. When null, a sensible default limit configured by the platform is applied.

action_types.description:
Optional list of moderation action types to include in the result set.

When provided, only records whose `action_type` field matches one of the supplied values are returned. This allows admins to focus on specific kinds of actions such as `hide_review` or `escalate_dispute`.

admin_ids.description:
Optional filter restricting results to actions performed by the specified admin accounts.

Each identifier corresponds to a row in `shopping_mall_admins`. When this filter is null, actions from all admins and automated systems are eligible for inclusion.

created_from.description:
Lower bound for the moderation action creation timestamp filter.

When set, only actions with a `created_at` value greater than or equal to this timestamp are included, enabling time-boxed audits and investigations.

created_to.description:
Upper bound for the moderation action creation timestamp filter.

When set, only actions with a `created_at` value less than or equal to this timestamp are included, allowing admins to constrain searches to a closed time window.

reason_codes.description:
Optional list of structured reason codes used to filter moderation actions.

Only actions whose `reason_code` matches one of the supplied values are returned when this filter is present, supporting targeted reporting for specific policy or legal categories.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to note fields or other searchable columns on moderation actions.

This field is commonly used for ad hoc discovery when staff remember fragments of a note, internal ticket identifier, or other textual hint but do not have exact codes or dates.

order_by_created_at_desc.description:
Flag indicating whether results should be ordered by `created_at` in descending order.

When true, newer moderation actions appear first in the result set. When false or null, the backend may apply ascending order or a default ordering strategy defined by the platform.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for querying helpful vote records in the shopping mall review helpful votes domain.

This DTO is used by multiple PATCH-based search endpoints that operate over the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma model, providing a structured JSON body for complex search, filter, sort, and pagination parameters. It allows administrative and customer-facing tools to request pages of helpful vote data without exposing low-level database details directly.

The fields in this request type are purely query parameters and do not map one-to-one to database columns. Instead, they drive how the backend builds queries against shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes, shopping_mall_reviews, and shopping_mall_customers, such as constraining by review, by customer, or by creation time range, while also specifying which page of results to return and how they should be ordered.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve when paginating through helpful vote search results.

The first page is typically represented as 1. Values less than 1 should be treated as invalid by the server and trigger validation errors rather than being silently corrected.

Administrative tools and customer activity screens use this in conjunction with the `limit` field to request specific slices of the overall result set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of helpful vote records to return in a single page of results.

This controls the page size for list and search operations over shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes. Service implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses, even if a client specifies a very high value.

Typical values might range from 10 to 100, depending on the UI requirements and performance characteristics of the deployment.

sortBy.description:
Field or logical key by which the helpful vote results should be sorted.

Common sort keys for helpful vote records include creation time (for newest-first or oldest-first views) and possibly derived metrics such as whether a vote is currently considered active. The exact set of supported values is defined by the backend service and may include options like `created_at` or `updated_at`.

If omitted, the service applies its default ordering, usually newest-first based on creation timestamp.

sortDirection.description:
Direction of sorting to apply when ordering helpful vote results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. When combined with `sortBy`, this lets clients request views such as "newest first" or "oldest first". If not provided, the backend falls back to a sensible default direction for the chosen sort key.

Invalid values should be rejected with a clear validation error so that clients can correct their requests.

reviewId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to helpful votes associated with a specific review.

This value corresponds conceptually to the foreign key `shopping_mall_review_id` in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma model, which references a row in shopping_mall_reviews. When supplied, only votes for the identified review are included in the result set.

Search endpoints that already scope results by a path parameter reviewId typically ignore this field or validate consistency between the path and body values.

customerId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to helpful votes cast by a specific customer.

This value corresponds conceptually to the foreign key `shopping_mall_customer_id` in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma model, which references a row in shopping_mall_customers. When supplied, only helpful vote records created by that customer are returned.

In endpoints that already scope by a customer path parameter, this field is either ignored or validated to match the path-level customer identifier to prevent contradictory filters.

isHelpful.description:
Optional filter indicating whether to return only votes that mark a review as helpful or only votes that mark it as not helpful.

This flag corresponds to the `is_helpful` boolean column on the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes Prisma model. When set to true, only helpful votes are included; when set to false, only non-helpful or negative votes are included.

If omitted, both helpful and non-helpful records are eligible to appear in search results, and ordering is determined by other criteria such as timestamps.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) on the helpful vote creation timestamp when filtering results by time.

This value is compared against the `created_at` column of shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes to include only votes created at or after the specified instant. The timestamp must be provided in an ISO 8601 date-time format such as `2024-01-01T00:00:00Z`.

Used by administrative and analytical tools to focus on recent activity windows or specific historical periods.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) on the helpful vote creation timestamp when filtering results by time.

This value is compared against the `created_at` column of shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes to include only votes created at or before the specified instant. The timestamp must be expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format, for example `2024-01-31T23:59:59Z`.

Combining `createdFrom` and `createdTo` allows clients to request helpful vote activity over a precise date-time range.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.description:
Helpful vote record on a product review created by a customer.

This schema models a single row in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table, which represents the many-to-many relationship between customers and reviews where customers indicate whether a review was helpful. Each instance ties exactly one review to exactly one customer and stores the current helpfulness decision.

The entity is used as business data and as the authoritative source for deriving aggregated helpfulness metrics on reviews. It is referenced by review‑centric, customer‑centric, and generic helpful-vote APIs that need to display or mutate a customer’s helpfulness opinion for a given review.

id.description:
Primary key of the helpful vote entry.

This value uniquely identifies a single helpful vote row in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table and is used by endpoints that address a vote directly via an ID path parameter.

It is generated by the system and is never supplied or modified by clients.

review_id.description:
Identifier of the review that received the helpfulness vote.

This is a foreign key to shopping_mall_reviews.id and scopes the vote to a specific customer‑written product review. It is used to associate this helpful vote with the parent review when deriving helpfulness aggregates or loading review details.

The value is assigned when the vote is created and remains immutable throughout the life of the record.

customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who cast the helpfulness vote.

This foreign key points to shopping_mall_customers.id and establishes ownership of the vote. It is used to enforce that each customer can vote at most once per review and to check authorization when updating or inspecting a customer’s votes.

Although stored in the database, the value is always derived from the authenticated customer context in API operations and must not be accepted directly from untrusted clients.

is_helpful.description:
Flag indicating whether the customer marked the review as helpful.

A value of true means the customer considers the review helpful. A value of false represents a negative or non‑helpful vote, depending on how the business logic interprets non‑helpful states.

Service logic and downstream aggregates use this boolean to compute net helpfulness scores and to drive UI indicators such as helpful vote counts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this helpful vote record was first created.

The value is stored in UTC with full date‑time precision and reflects when the customer initially cast their helpfulness decision for the associated review.

It is managed exclusively by the backend persistence layer and is returned in read APIs for auditing and timeline display.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this helpful vote record was last updated.

The value is stored in UTC with full date‑time precision and is refreshed whenever the customer changes their helpfulness decision, such as toggling from helpful to not helpful.

Clients can use this field to understand the recency of the customer’s latest helpfulness state and to detect concurrent modifications if desired.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a helpful vote record on a product review.

This DTO is used by POST endpoints that register a customer’s helpfulness decision for a specific review by inserting a new row into the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table. It focuses on the business fields required to decide whether the review is helpful while relying on path parameters and authentication context for identifiers.

The DTO must not include system-managed fields such as id, created_at, or updated_at, and it must not accept customer identity directly. Review identity is typically supplied as a path parameter, and customer identity is injected from the authenticated customer session.

is_helpful.description:
Indicates whether the customer considers the target review helpful.

A value of true records a positive helpful vote; a value of false records a negative or non‑helpful decision in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table.

This field is required for vote creation and is the core business input that drives helpfulness aggregates on reviews.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing helpful vote record.

This DTO is used by PUT endpoints that modify a customer’s previously recorded helpfulness decision for a review, targeting an existing row in the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table. Typical usage is toggling the is_helpful flag when a customer changes their mind about whether a review is helpful.

Only mutable business fields are exposed; identifiers and foreign keys are kept immutable and are never accepted from clients. The persistence layer updates the updated_at timestamp automatically whenever this DTO is applied.

is_helpful.description:
Updated helpfulness decision for the target review.

When provided, this value replaces the previous is_helpful state on the underlying shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes record, for example changing from true to false or vice versa.

The field is optional to allow future extension of the DTO, but in typical usage callers supply this flag explicitly whenever they call the update operation.

IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.description:
Product-level rating aggregate snapshot for a single product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This schema represents a denormalized, precomputed view of review metrics derived from the `shopping_mall_reviews` table and related entities. Each record summarizes the current rating state for exactly one product from `shopping_mall_products`, including average rating, total review count, and a per-score distribution.

The data is maintained by background jobs or triggers that react to review and helpful-vote events. It is optimized for read-heavy use cases such as product detail pages and catalog listing cards, where clients need fast access to stable rating summary information without scanning raw reviews.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product rating aggregate row.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` table and is used internally to uniquely distinguish one aggregate snapshot from another. It does not equal the product identifier itself; the product linkage is expressed through `shopping_mall_product_id`.

API consumers typically do not need to use this field directly for navigation, but it can be useful for debugging, logging, or internal tooling that inspects aggregate records.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product whose ratings are aggregated in this record.

This value references `shopping_mall_products.id` and binds the aggregate metrics to a specific product in the catalog. It is the bridge between product entities and their rating summary data.

While clients generally identify the product by the `productId` path parameter, this field allows response consumers to confirm which product the aggregate belongs to or to store the association in caches.

oneOf.description:
Average rating value for the product computed from included reviews.

This value is typically calculated as the mean of all individual rating scores for the product, using the platform's rating scale (for example, 1–5). It may reflect only approved and visible reviews, depending on moderation rules.

The value can include fractional precision (such as 4.3) and is meant for display in rating widgets, sorting, or filtering.

Indicates that no rating have yet been recorded for this product.

When this branch is selected, the product has zero approved reviews and therefore no meaningful average can be computed. Clients should treat this as "no ratings yet" instead of a numeric rating.

average_rating.description:
Average rating value for the product, or null when no reviews exist.

When non-null, this field encodes the current mean rating across all included reviews for the product, using the business-defined rating scale (commonly 1–5). The precision may include decimals to support nuanced display and ordering.

When null, the product has not yet received any eligible reviews and consumers should render a suitable "no ratings" state instead of a numerical value.

rating_count.description:
Total number of reviews that contribute to the aggregate metrics for this product.

This count typically includes only reviews that are currently eligible according to moderation and visibility rules (for example, not soft-deleted or hidden). It is used for display alongside the average rating and for analytics.

Clients can use this value to decide when to show rating widgets, e.g., hiding them when the count is too low to be meaningful.

rating_1_count.description:
Number of included reviews with the lowest rating value (for example, 1-star reviews).

This field supports rating distribution visualizations such as histograms or stacked bars. It reflects how many reviews assigned the minimum rating in the configured scale.

Combined with the other per-score counts, it allows clients to present a detailed breakdown of customer sentiment.

rating_2_count.description:
Number of included reviews with the second rating value on the scale (for example, 2-star reviews).

This field participates in the detailed rating distribution for the product. It is based on reviews that are part of the current aggregate computation and meet visibility and moderation requirements.

Client applications can use it to build rating distribution charts or to power filters such as "show only products with few low ratings".

rating_3_count.description:
Number of included reviews with a mid-range rating value (for example, 3-star reviews).

This count represents neutral or average sentiment and is useful when analyzing the shape of the rating distribution. It can help distinguish products that are polarizing from those that cluster around middle scores.

The value is computed from reviews that are currently considered in the aggregate metrics.

rating_4_count.description:
Number of included reviews with a high rating value (for example, 4-star reviews).

This field indicates how many customers rated the product positively but not at the maximum score. It contributes to understanding the upper portion of the rating distribution and how strongly customers recommend the product.

Display components may combine this with other counts to create cumulative metrics or visual cues such as bar charts.

rating_5_count.description:
Number of included reviews with the highest rating value (for example, 5-star reviews).

This count shows how many customers evaluated the product at the top of the rating scale. It is a key indicator of strong customer satisfaction and is often highlighted in UI components.

Together with the other rating-level counts, it forms a complete distribution that can be used for advanced analytics and presentation.

last_computed_at.description:
