Timestamp at which the rating aggregate metrics were last recomputed for this product.

This value reflects when the aggregate snapshot was last updated in response to changes in underlying review data or scheduled batch recomputations. It helps diagnose staleness and determine whether metrics are recent enough for critical decisions.

Clients may choose to surface or log this timestamp in administrative tools, while typical customer-facing UIs may only use it implicitly for caching or heuristic freshness checks.

IShoppingMallSkuRatingAggregate.description:
SKU-level rating aggregate snapshot for a concrete sellable variant in the shoppingMall catalog.

This schema describes precomputed rating metrics for a single SKU record from `shopping_mall_skus`. It mirrors the fields of the `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` table and summarizes review scores, total review count, and per-score distribution for that specific variant.

The data is populated and refreshed by background processes that aggregate reviews and related events from `shopping_mall_reviews` and associated tables. It is optimized for fast read access to support variant selection views, SKU detail components, and analytical dashboards that require variant-level quality indicators.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU rating aggregate row.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` table and uniquely identifies an aggregate snapshot for a particular SKU. It is distinct from the SKU's own identifier, which is stored in `shopping_mall_sku_id`.

Most external clients do not rely on this identifier directly but it is useful for internal diagnostics, logging, and administration tools.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU whose ratings are aggregated in this record.

This field references `shopping_mall_skus.id` and anchors the aggregate metrics to a specific stock keeping unit. It is the primary linkage between a variant in the product catalog and its rating summary data.

Client code can use this value to verify that the aggregate corresponds to the SKU referenced by the `skuId` path parameter or to cache variant-level rating metrics by SKU identifier.

oneOf.description:
Average rating value for the SKU computed from included reviews.

This value represents the mean of all rating scores associated with this SKU that are eligible under moderation and visibility rules. It may be fractional and is typically based on a 1–5 rating scale or similar.

The field is primarily used for variant-level rating displays, allowing customers to compare different options within the same product.

Indicates that no eligible reviews currently exist for this SKU.

When this branch is selected, the SKU has no qualifying reviews and therefore no numeric average rating. UI components should treat this as a "no ratings yet" state for the variant.

average_rating.description:
Average rating value for the SKU, or null when no eligible reviews exist.

When non-null, the value summarizes the central tendency of customer ratings for this variant and supports ordering, filtering, and visual display. It reflects the current state of approved and visible reviews only.

When null, the absence of eligible reviews prevents any meaningful average from being computed and should be handled as a special display case by clients.

rating_count.description:
Total number of included reviews that contribute to the aggregate metrics for this SKU.

This count measures review volume for the variant and is typically displayed alongside the average rating to provide customers with additional context about how many opinions the score is based on.

Only reviews that meet eligibility criteria (such as not being hidden or removed) are counted here.

rating_1_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with the lowest rating value (for example, 1-star reviews).

This count indicates the volume of strongly negative feedback targeting this variant. It is a component of the detailed rating distribution and is often used in analytics or advanced UI elements such as histogram bars.

The value is derived from the same set of eligible reviews as the other aggregate metrics.

rating_2_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with the second rating value on the scale (for example, 2-star reviews).

This field helps describe the lower-mid portion of the rating distribution. It provides more nuance than a simple average score and allows clients to present a richer picture of customer sentiment.

The count is computed from reviews associated with this SKU that are included in the aggregate process.

rating_3_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with a mid-range rating value (for example, 3-star reviews).

This count represents neutral or mixed feedback for the variant and contributes to understanding how customer opinions are distributed across the scale.

It is particularly useful when distinguishing between variants that are polarizing versus those that cluster around a neutral score.

rating_4_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with a high rating value (for example, 4-star reviews).

This field indicates positive sentiment towards this variant without being at the maximum score. It supports detailed rating charts and can be combined with other counts for cumulative or percentage-based displays.

The count includes only reviews that are currently eligible for aggregation.

rating_5_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with the highest rating value (for example, 5-star reviews).

This count reflects the volume of the strongest positive feedback for the variant and is a key indicator of high customer satisfaction.

Together with the other per-score counts, it forms a complete distribution used in analytics and front-end visualization components.

last_computed_at.description:
Timestamp at which the rating aggregate metrics were last recomputed for this SKU.

This field indicates when the aggregate snapshot was last refreshed based on the underlying reviews and related data. It is useful for monitoring freshness and for internal debugging of the rating pipeline.

Regular recomputation ensures that changes to reviews or eligibility status are eventually reflected in the aggregate values returned by this endpoint.

IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.IReq.description:
Request DTO for searching product-level rating aggregates.

This schema models the filter, sorting, and pagination parameters accepted by the product rating aggregates search endpoint that reads from the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates materialized view.

It allows clients to constrain which products are included in the result set based on rating statistics (average rating, total rating count, per-bucket thresholds) and related catalog dimensions, while also specifying how results should be ordered and paginated for efficient list or dashboard views.

page.description:
Zero-based page index used for offset-based pagination.

Clients typically start with page = 0 for the first page. When combined with the pageSize field, this determines the result window returned from the rating aggregates view.

The value must be greater than or equal to 0. If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of aggregate rows to return in a single page.

This value controls page length for offset-based pagination. It must be greater than or equal to 0, and backend implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

When omitted, the service should apply a sensible default page size.

minAverageRating.description:
Lower bound for the average rating filter.

Only products whose average_rating in shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates is greater than or equal to this value will be included. The value must be non-negative and should follow the platform’s rating scale (for example, 1.0–5.0), although the exact maximum is enforced by business rules rather than this schema.

Useful for showing only well-rated products in discovery flows.

maxAverageRating.description:
Upper bound for the average rating filter.

Only products whose average_rating in shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates is less than or equal to this value will be included. The value must be non-negative and is expected to fall within the platform’s rating scale.

Combined with minAverageRating, this can target a specific rating band.

minRatingCount.description:
Minimum required number of included reviews.

Only products with rating_count greater than or equal to this value will be included. The value must be greater than or equal to 0 so that negative review counts are never accepted.

This filter helps exclude products whose average rating is based on too few reviews.

items.description:
Product identifier value.

Each element corresponds to a shopping_mall_products.id value used to restrict the aggregate query to a specific product set.

productIds.description:
List of product identifiers to include in the search.

When provided, the query will be constrained to aggregates whose shopping_mall_product_id belongs to this set.

oneOf.description:
Field to use for ordering the result set.

Supported values are:
- "averageRating": order by average_rating
- "ratingCount": order by rating_count
- "lastComputedAt": order by last_computed_at

Any other value is rejected by validation to ensure consistent and predictable sorting semantics.

Any other value is rejected by validation to ensure consistent and predictable sorting semantics.

Direction of sorting for the selected sortBy field.

Supported values are:

If omitted, the backend may default to a descending order for rating-based sorts, but only these two values are allowed at the schema level.

Direction of sorting for the selected sortBy field.

Supported values are:

- "desc" for descending order

If omitted, the backend may default to a descending order for rating-based sorts, but only these two values are allowed at the schema level.

IShoppingMallSkuRatingAggregate.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching SKU-level rating aggregates.

This schema defines the structured search, filtering, and pagination options accepted by the SKU rating aggregates search endpoint that reads from the shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates materialized view.

It enables clients to locate specific SKUs based on their rating metrics, filter on review volume or freshness, and combine these filters with catalog constraints such as SKU identifiers or parent product identifiers, while also controlling the sort order and page slicing.

page.description:
Zero-based page index used for offset-based pagination.

Clients normally start with page = 0 for the first batch of SKU aggregate records. Together with pageSize, this determines which window of results is returned.

The value must be greater than or equal to 0. If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of SKU rating aggregate rows to return in the current page.

This value controls page length for offset-based pagination and must be greater than or equal to 0. Backends should enforce a sensible maximum value to prevent excessively large responses and may apply a default when the client does not specify a size.

minAverageRating.description:
Lower bound for the SKU average rating filter.

Only SKUs whose average_rating in shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates is greater than or equal to this value will be included. The value must be non-negative and is expected to fall within the platform’s rating scale (for example, 1.0–5.0).

This filter is useful for highlighting high-quality variants in catalog or seller tools.

maxAverageRating.description:
Upper bound for the SKU average rating filter.

Only SKUs whose average_rating in shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates is less than or equal to this value will be included. The value must be non-negative and should align with the platform’s rating scale.

Used together with minAverageRating to narrow results to a specific rating band.

minRatingCount.description:
Minimum total number of included reviews required for a SKU to be eligible.

Only SKUs with rating_count greater than or equal to this value will be included. The value must be greater than or equal to 0 to prevent invalid negative review counts.

This helps filter out poorly sampled variants whose ratings may not yet be reliable.

items.description:
SKU identifier value.

Each element maps to a shopping_mall_skus.id used to restrict the aggregate query to specific variants.

skuIds.description:
List of SKU identifiers to restrict the search to.

When present, only aggregate rows whose shopping_mall_sku_id appears in this list will be considered.

items.description:
Product identifier value.

Each element corresponds to a shopping_mall_products.id used to limit SKU aggregates to variants of specific products.

productIds.description:
Optional list of parent product identifiers.

When provided, only SKUs belonging to these products (via shopping_mall_skus) will be included in the aggregate search result.

oneOf.description:
Field name that determines the primary sort order of the returned SKU aggregates.

IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.description:
Review eligibility record defining when a customer is allowed to submit a product or SKU review.

This DTO maps directly to the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` Prisma model, which is a subsidiary table linked to customers, order items, products, SKUs, and reviews. Each record represents a single eligibility window derived from order and delivery events and captures whether the customer can currently write a review for a specific purchase.

The type is used in detailed read operations for both customer-facing and admin-facing APIs, allowing clients and internal tools to inspect eligibility status, timing constraints, and the underlying purchase context without modifying the stored data.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review eligibility record.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` model and is generated by the system. It is used to reference this eligibility from review flows and administrative tools and is immutable after creation.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who owns this review eligibility.

This field references `shopping_mall_customers.id` and ties the eligibility to a specific customer account. It is used for scoping queries and enforcing that only the owning customer or authorized internal actors can see this record.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Identifier of the order item that produced this review eligibility.

This field references `shopping_mall_order_items.id` and indicates which purchased line item (SKU within an order) the eligibility is derived from. It is essential for validating that a review corresponds to an actual completed purchase.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that may be reviewed under this eligibility.

This field references `shopping_mall_products.id` and specifies the product concept for which a review can be written. It allows UIs and tools to resolve product-level metadata when presenting review options.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU variant that may be reviewed under this eligibility, when the purchase was for a specific variant.

This field references `shopping_mall_skus.id` when present. It is nullable when the eligibility applies only at the product level without a specific SKU, allowing flexibility between product-wide and variant-specific reviews.

shopping_mall_review_id.description:
Identifier of the review that has consumed this eligibility, if any.

This field references `shopping_mall_reviews.id` when a review has already been created using this eligibility. It remains null while the eligibility is unused, enabling enforcement of one-review-per-eligibility constraints.

status.description:
Current status of the review eligibility.

Typical values include states such as `eligible`, `used`, `expired`, or `revoked`, representing whether the customer can currently submit a review with this record. Business rules in the review and policy domain interpret this status to decide if eligibility may be used in review creation flows.

eligible_from.description:
Timestamp from which the customer is allowed to submit a review based on this eligibility.

This value is usually set when the underlying order item reaches a completion or delivered state. Review creation flows must ensure that the current time is on or after this value before accepting a review that uses this eligibility.

eligible_until.description:
Optional timestamp after which this review eligibility expires and can no longer be used.

When present, this value defines the upper bound of the review window. Once the current time is after `eligible_until`, the eligibility is considered expired and should not be accepted for new reviews. When null, the eligibility does not have a configured expiration timestamp.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the review eligibility record was created.

This field tracks when the eligibility was first generated, typically by order or fulfillment workflows. It is useful for auditing, debugging review flows, and analytical reporting on eligibility creation over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the review eligibility record was last updated.

This value changes whenever the eligibility’s status or other mutable attributes are modified, such as when eligibility is consumed by a review or when policy-driven adjustments are applied.

customer.description:
Summary information about the customer who owns this review eligibility.

This object is a BELONGS-TO association derived from `shopping_mall_customer_id` and provides enough context to render customer-related information in eligibility detail views without an additional API call.

order_item.description:
Summary of the order item that produced this review eligibility.

This BELONGS-TO association is derived from `shopping_mall_order_item_id` and allows clients to understand which specific purchased line item the eligibility refers to when inspecting eligibility details.

product.description:
Summary of the product that may be reviewed under this eligibility.

This BELONGS-TO association is derived from `shopping_mall_product_id` and exposes basic catalog information so that clients can display what product the review would be written for.

sku.description:
Optional summary of the SKU variant that may be reviewed under this eligibility when the purchase was for a specific variant.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_sku_id`. When non-null, it allows clients to show variant-level information (such as size or color) alongside eligibility details without requiring an extra SKU fetch.

review.description:
Optional summary of the review that has consumed this eligibility, when such a review exists.

This BELONGS-TO association is derived from `shopping_mall_review_id` and lets administrative or support tools quickly see the linked review without performing a separate search.

IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for querying review eligibility records.

This DTO is used as the request body for review eligibility search operations, such as customer-scoped or order-item-scoped index endpoints. It allows callers to express flexible filters over customer, product, SKU, order item, status, and eligibility time windows while also controlling pagination and sorting.

The structure follows the platform’s pattern for `.IRequest` types by focusing on query criteria and page metadata rather than representing a database row. All fields are optional so that callers can combine them as needed to support different UI and reporting use cases.

customer_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to eligibilities for a specific customer.

This value should correspond to `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities.shopping_mall_customer_id`. It is typically omitted when the customer is already implied by the path or authentication context and is mainly useful in admin or analytics scenarios.

product_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to eligibilities created for a specific product.

When provided, this value should match `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities.shopping_mall_product_id` and is useful for listing eligibilities related to a particular product in customer or admin tools.

sku_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to eligibilities for a specific SKU variant.

This value should match `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities.shopping_mall_sku_id` when the purchase and eligibility are variant-specific. When omitted or null, results may include both product-level and SKU-level eligibilities.

order_item_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to eligibilities associated with a specific order item.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities.shopping_mall_order_item_id` and is especially useful in order-item-scoped search endpoints and troubleshooting tools.

status.description:
Optional filter on the eligibility status.

Allows callers to request eligibilities in a particular business state, such as `eligible`, `used`, `expired`, or `revoked`, depending on the status values used by the implementation. When omitted or null, eligibilities of all statuses may be returned.

eligible_from_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the `eligible_from` timestamp.

When provided, only eligibilities whose `eligible_from` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This enables searching for eligibility windows that start within a particular time range.

eligible_from_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the `eligible_from` timestamp.

When provided, only eligibilities whose `eligible_from` is less than or equal to this timestamp are included. Combined with `eligible_from_from`, this allows querying for windows created in a bounded period.

eligible_until_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the `eligible_until` timestamp.

This filter is useful when analyzing or listing eligibilities that remain valid beyond a certain date. Eligibilities with null `eligible_until` are typically interpreted separately according to business rules.

eligible_until_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the `eligible_until` timestamp.

When present, this restricts results to eligibilities whose expiration does not exceed the specified timestamp, supporting queries around upcoming or recently expired review windows.

page.description:
Optional page index for paginated results, starting from 1.

When omitted or null, the implementation uses its default page index (commonly the first page). Combined with `limit`, this controls which slice of the overall result set is returned.

limit.description:
Optional maximum number of records to return in a single page.

If omitted or null, the service falls back to its default page size, subject to an internal maximum to protect performance. Clients should choose values that balance UI needs with response size.

sort_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort the result set.

Common values include `eligible_from`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`, depending on which ordering best serves the calling UI or report. When omitted, the service applies its default sort order, typically `created_at` or `eligible_from` descending.

sort_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the result set.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted or null, the implementation’s default sort direction is used, usually `desc` for date-based fields.

IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for review eligibility records in the shopping_mall_review_eligibilities table.

This type is used by administrative and internal back-office workflows to adjust mutable aspects of an existing eligibility record, such as its status or the time window during which a customer is allowed to write a review.

The DTO intentionally excludes immutable identifiers and foreign key columns that bind an eligibility record to a specific customer, order item, product, or SKU. Those identifiers are set when the eligibility is created and must not change during an update operation.

Only fields that can safely change without breaking referential integrity are present here, aligning with governance, policy, and audit expectations for review eligibility management.

status.description:
Current eligibility status value to apply to the record.

Typical business values include states such as eligible, used, expired, or revoked. Implementations should validate the provided value against the allowed status set enforced in domain logic or enums.

Changing this field can immediately affect whether a customer is allowed to create a review for the associated order item and product in higher-level review flows.

oneOf.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp marking the start of the review eligibility window.

When provided, this value controls from which point in time the customer may submit a review based on this eligibility. It is usually aligned with an order item reaching a delivered or completed state.

Updating this value lets administrators correct or backdate eligibility windows when shipment or delivery events were recorded incorrectly.

Null when the existing eligible_from value should remain unchanged.

Use this when no modification to the eligibility window start time is required in the current update operation.

eligible_from.description:
Optional new start timestamp of the eligibility window.

If a non-null value is supplied, the service should update the underlying eligible_from column to the given instant. When omitted entirely from the payload, the field remains unchanged.

Use this field carefully in accordance with review and rating policies so that eligibility windows remain consistent with order and delivery events.

oneOf.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp representing the end of the review eligibility window.

When set, the customer is allowed to submit a review only until this point in time. After this timestamp, the eligibility is considered expired unless policy overrides apply.

Administrators can extend or shorten the window to enforce or correct review policies, especially when shipment or campaign timelines shift.

Null when the eligibility window should no longer have a fixed end time.

Setting this field to null removes any previously configured expiration, allowing business logic to treat the eligibility as open-ended or to rely on other policy-based cutoffs.

eligible_until.description:
Optional new end timestamp of the eligibility window, or null to clear an existing value.

If this property is omitted from the update request, the current eligible_until value stored in the database remains unchanged.

Use this field to enforce or relax time-based constraints on when customers can write reviews, in line with configured business policies.

IShoppingMallReviewRatingDistribution.IR.description:
Request DTO for computing analytic distributions of review ratings based on shopping_mall_reviews and related aggregate tables.

This type captures the filter and segmentation criteria that define which reviews are included in the calculation, such as restricting by product, SKU, seller, category, and time window. It is consumed by analytics endpoints that produce rating distribution statistics instead of raw review rows.

All fields are optional filters; when omitted, the analytics service uses broad defaults, such as considering all visible, non-deleted reviews over the entire dataset. Backoffice dashboards and reporting tools can combine these filters to analyze sentiment patterns for specific catalog slices, campaigns, or periods without affecting underlying review data.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of a specific product whose reviews should be included in the rating distribution calculation.

When provided, the analytics service narrows the computation to reviews associated with this product in shopping_mall_reviews and, if applicable, its aggregate tables. This is useful for product detail dashboards and targeted quality analysis.

Null when no single product restriction is desired.

In this case, the analytics service may use other filters such as category, seller, or time range to determine the review subset.

product_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict analytics to reviews for a single product.

If omitted entirely, reviews for all products that satisfy other filters are considered in the distribution.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of a specific SKU variant whose reviews should be included in the distribution.

When set together with product filters, the analytics service focuses on variant-level sentiment, leveraging sku-specific links in shopping_mall_reviews and sku rating aggregate tables.

Null when analytics should not be limited to a specific SKU.

Use this when analyzing product-level or broader catalog sentiment where SKU granularity is not required.

sku_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict analytics to reviews for a single SKU variant.

If omitted, reviews are aggregated without SKU-level restriction, which is typical for product-level or category-level analysis.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of a seller whose catalog’s reviews should be included in the distribution.

When provided, the analytics service restricts computations to products and SKUs owned by this seller, enabling seller dashboards and performance monitoring views.

Null when analytics should span products from all sellers.

This is appropriate for platform-wide rating distribution views or category-focused analysis that is not tied to a single seller.

seller_id.description:
Optional filter to scope analytics to reviews related to a particular seller’s catalog.

If omitted, reviews across all sellers that meet other filter criteria are included.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of a category whose associated products and SKUs should define the review subset.

The analytics engine uses category-product relationships to collect reviews for products in the specified category, supporting category-level rating dashboards.

Null when no specific category filter is required.

Use this in seller-centric or product-specific analyses where category constraints are not necessary.

category_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict analytics to reviews for products under a given category.

When omitted, all categories are included by default unless constrained by other filters.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the review creation timestamp range in ISO 8601 format.

Only reviews created at or after this time are included when computing rating distributions. This supports time-series comparisons and period-based reporting.

Null when no lower bound on review creation time is required.

In this case, the analytics service considers reviews from the earliest available data up to any specified upper bound.

created_from.description:
Optional start of the review creation time window used for analytics.

If omitted, the analytics engine does not apply a lower bound constraint on review creation timestamps beyond any global defaults.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the review creation timestamp range in ISO 8601 format.

Only reviews created at or before this time are included in the calculation. This enables snapshot analytics up to a specific reporting cutoff date.

Null when no upper bound on review creation time is required.

In this case, all reviews newer than any specified lower bound are considered, up to the most recent available data.

created_until.description:
Optional end of the review creation time window used for analytics.

If omitted, the analytics engine does not apply an upper bound constraint on review creation timestamps beyond any global defaults.

oneOf.description:
Minimum number of reviews that a product, SKU, or grouping must have to be included in certain distribution breakdowns.

This helps avoid skew from very small samples by excluding entities with too few reviews to provide meaningful statistics.

Null when no minimum review count threshold is applied.

In this case, all entities that satisfy other filters are included, even if they have only one review.

min_review_count.description:
Optional threshold for the minimum number of reviews required for an entity to be considered in detailed distribution breakdowns.

When omitted, the analytics service may use its own default or include all entities regardless of review volume.

IShoppingMallReviewRatingDistribution.description:
Aggregated rating distribution analytics for product reviews in the shoppingMall platform.

Represents computed statistics derived from review data in shopping_mall_reviews and precomputed aggregate tables such as shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates and shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates. This DTO does not map directly to a single Prisma model; instead it serves as a read-only analytics view for dashboards and reporting tools.

Used by admin analytics endpoints to understand how customer ratings are distributed across a filtered slice of the catalog, such as by product, SKU, seller, category, or time range.

buckets.description:
List of rating buckets that compose the distribution for the selected scope.

Each bucket typically represents a discrete rating score (for example, 1–5 stars) and carries the absolute review count and relative percentage of all reviews within the current filter.

Buckets are ordered from lowest to highest rating score to simplify charting and visualization.

totalReviewCount.description:
Total number of reviews included in this distribution after applying all filters.

This is the sum of the counts of all buckets. It can be used to enforce minimum review count thresholds on the client side and to display the overall sample size next to rating distribution charts.

averageRating.description:
Overall average rating value for the filtered review set.

This is typically computed as a weighted average across all buckets (for example, on a 1–5 star scale). Clients can use this value directly for numeric displays or combine it with totalReviewCount to show high-level sentiment indicators.

scaleMin.description:
Minimum rating value for the scale used in this distribution.

For standard 5-star systems this is commonly 1. This field is included to support alternative scales (e.g., 0–5 or 1–10) and to allow generic chart components to be configured dynamically.

scaleMax.description:
Maximum rating value for the scale used in this distribution.

For a typical 5-star system this is 5. Including this field allows generic visualizations to adapt to different rating scales without hard-coded assumptions.

IShoppingMallReviewRatingDistributionBuc.description:
Single rating bucket within a review rating distribution.

Represents the statistics for one discrete rating score, such as all reviews that gave 5 stars. Buckets are typically rendered as bars in a histogram or distribution chart.

ratingValue.description:
The discrete rating score represented by this bucket.

For a standard 5-star system this will be an integer between scaleMin and scaleMax (for example, 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5).

reviewCount.description:
Number of reviews that fall into this rating bucket after all filters are applied.

The sum of reviewCount across all buckets will equal the totalReviewCount reported in the parent distribution DTO.

percentage.description:
Percentage of reviews that fall into this rating bucket relative to the totalReviewCount.

Expressed as a value between 0 and 100, where 100 represents all reviews in the current filter. This value can be used directly for charting without recomputing client-side percentages.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessAnalytics..description:
Filter, segmentation, and sorting criteria for computing review helpfulness analytics across the shoppingMall platform.

This request DTO is used by admin analytics endpoints to scope aggregation of helpful vote records from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes combined with review metadata from shopping_mall_reviews and related catalog context. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model and is intended solely for analytic querying.

Callers can restrict the analysis to specific products, SKUs, sellers, categories, or time windows, and control thresholds and sorting options, such as focusing only on reviews with a minimum number of votes or ordering results by helpfulness ratio or total helpful votes.

productIds.description:
Optional list of product identifiers to limit the helpfulness analytics scope.

When provided, only reviews associated with the specified products are considered. This is useful for product-specific dashboards and targeted quality analysis.

skuIds.description:
Optional list of SKU identifiers to further narrow the helpfulness analytics to specific product variants.

If provided, only reviews associated with the given SKUs participate in the aggregation. This allows fine-grained analysis for variants that may have different customer sentiment.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers whose associated reviews should be included in the helpfulness analytics.

This filter supports seller-centric dashboards and performance monitoring by focusing the aggregation on reviews written for products owned by specified sellers.

categoryIds.description:
Optional list of category identifiers to scope analytics to particular sections of the catalog.

Only reviews for products assigned to these categories will be considered, which enables category-level quality and sentiment monitoring.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the review creation timestamp filter.

Only reviews created at or after this instant are included in the helpfulness analytics. If omitted, the analysis is not constrained by a lower time boundary.

toCreatedAt.description:
Inclusive upper bound for the review creation timestamp filter.

Only reviews created at or before this instant are included. If omitted, the analysis is not constrained by an upper time boundary.

minHelpfulVoteCount.description:
Minimum number of helpful votes a review must have to be included in the analytics.

Use this threshold to ignore reviews with very few votes that may not be statistically meaningful when ranking helpfulness.

minTotalVoteCount.description:
Minimum total number of votes (helpful + non-helpful) a review must have to be included in the analytics.

This can be used in combination with minHelpfulVoteCount to filter out reviews with insufficient voting activity.

oneOf.description:
Sorting strategy to apply when ranking analytics results.

Typical values include:
- "helpful_ratio" – order by the ratio of helpful to total votes
- "helpful_count" – order by the absolute number of helpful votes
- "recent_helpful" – prioritize reviews with recent helpful activity.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default ordering for the primary analytics use case.

- "recent_helpful" – prioritize reviews with recent helpful activity.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default ordering for the primary analytics use case.

- "helpful_ratio" – order by the ratio of helpful to total votes
- "helpful_count" – order by the absolute number of helpful votes
- "recent_helpful" – prioritize reviews with recent helpful activity.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default ordering for the primary analytics use case.

Typical values include:

- "helpful_count" – order by the absolute number of helpful votes
- "recent_helpful" – prioritize reviews with recent helpful activity.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default ordering for the primary analytics use case.

oneOf.description:

"asc" orders results in ascending order, while "desc" orders in descending order. If omitted, the backend will select an appropriate default based on the sortBy field (for example, descending for counts and ratios).

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply for the chosen sortBy strategy.

"asc" orders results in ascending order, while "desc" orders in descending order. If omitted, the backend will select an appropriate default based on the sortBy field (for example, descending for counts and ratios).

limit.description:
Maximum number of analytic records or ranked entries to return.

This bounds the result size for ranking-style analytics, such as top N most helpful reviews or products. If omitted, a service-defined default limit is applied, and the backend may also enforce a maximum limit to protect performance.

offset.description:
Number of records to skip from the beginning of the ordered result set.

Used for pagination when exploring large analytics result sets, for example when stepping through multiple pages of ranked reviews or products.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessAnalytics.description:
Aggregated helpfulness analytics for reviews across the shopping mall platform.

This schema represents a computed analytical view derived primarily from the shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes table joined with core review records from shopping_mall_reviews and related product and SKU context. It is used to answer questions such as which reviews are most helpful, which products or SKUs have the highest helpfulness perception, and how helpfulness metrics evolve over time.

The data is designed for admin and analytics dashboards rather than transactional flows. It never exposes individual helpful vote records or personally identifiable information about voters; instead it returns aggregated measures like total helpful votes, not-helpful votes, and helpfulness ratios per review, product, or seller depending on the selected grouping.

summary.description:
High-level summary metrics about review helpfulness across the entire result set.

This object provides top-level KPIs such as total number of distinct reviews included in the computation, total helpful votes, total not-helpful votes, and overall helpfulness ratios. It helps stakeholders quickly understand the overall quality and perceived usefulness of reviews in the selected time window and filter configuration.

byReviews.description:
Per-review helpfulness metrics for individual reviews that match the filter set.

Each entry represents one review with its core identifiers, rating information, aggregated helpfulness metrics, and now direct catalog associations via product, SKU, and seller summary DTOs. These records are suitable for listing top or bottom reviews by helpfulness in administrative dashboards without requiring additional lookups for basic context.

byProducts.description:
Aggregated helpfulness metrics grouped by product.

Each entry represents a single product via its summary DTO and aggregates helpfulness signals across all reviews that belong to that product (and optionally its SKUs) within the current filter set. This can be used to identify products whose review sections are particularly trusted or distrusted by customers.

bySkus.description:
Aggregated helpfulness metrics grouped by SKU variants.

Each entry represents a SKU via its summary DTO and aggregates helpfulness votes across reviews explicitly linked to that SKU via shopping_mall_sku_id. This allows fine-grained variant-level analysis of which SKUs have reviews considered helpful by customers.

bySellers.description:
Aggregated helpfulness metrics grouped by seller.

Each entry aggregates helpfulness signals across reviews associated with products or SKUs owned by a particular seller and exposes the seller as a summary association. This helps evaluate how trustworthy and useful customers perceive review content for each seller’s catalog without requiring extra requests to resolve seller identities.

period.description:
Time period over which the analytics were computed.

This object echoes the effective time window and granularity used when computing the review helpfulness metrics, such as start and end timestamps and optional bucket granularity like day or week.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessAnalytics..description:
Per-review helpfulness metrics used in review helpfulness analytics.

Each record represents one review from shopping_mall_reviews combined with aggregated helpful vote information from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes. It includes identifiers for the review, associated catalog summaries for product, SKU, and seller, the rating score, and computed helpfulness metrics.

This structure is intended for administrative analytics and ranking use cases such as displaying the most helpful or least helpful reviews in dashboards. It avoids embedding full review text but still exposes enough association context to render rich tables without additional API calls.

reviewId.description:
Unique identifier of the review whose helpfulness metrics are being summarized.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_reviews.id in the underlying database and can be used to drill down into full review detail via dedicated review endpoints if needed.

product.description:
Summary information about the product that the review is associated with.

This association replaces the earlier raw productId field and allows analytics consumers to render product context such as name and key merchandising attributes without separate requests.

sku.description:
Optional summary of the SKU variant that the review targets, when applicable.

When the review is at product level only this value is null. When present, it corresponds to a concrete SKU from shopping_mall_skus and enables variant-level analytics views directly from the analytics response.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller that owns the reviewed product or SKU.

This association provides immediate seller context for analytics tables, enabling admins to see which sellers are associated with particularly helpful or unhelpful reviews without performing additional lookups.

rating.description:
Star rating value given by the customer for this review.

This is the integer rating from shopping_mall_reviews.rating, commonly on a 1–5 scale where higher numbers represent more positive evaluations.

totalHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of helpful votes (is_helpful = true) recorded for this review.

This is derived by aggregating rows from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes where shopping_mall_review_id matches this review and is_helpful is true.

totalNotHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of not-helpful votes (is_helpful = false) recorded for this review.

This count is derived from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes for the same review with is_helpful set to false and indicates how often customers have explicitly disagreed with the usefulness of the review.

helpfulnessRatio.description:
Helpfulness ratio for this review, typically computed as totalHelpfulVotes divided by (totalHelpfulVotes + totalNotHelpfulVotes).

This provides a normalized measure between 0 and 1 indicating how helpful other customers perceive this review to be within the context of all helpfulness votes it has received.

lastVoteAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent helpfulness vote recorded for this review.

This reflects the recency of engagement in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes and can be used to prioritize reviews with ongoing activity.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessAnalytics..description:
Aggregated review helpfulness metrics grouped by product.

Each record represents a single product via its summary DTO and summarizes helpfulness signals from reviews attached to that product, regardless of whether they are at product or SKU level. It is intended for use in analytics dashboards that rank products by the perceived usefulness of their review content.

Values are derived from shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes, and may also be correlated with precomputed aggregates in shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates when available.

product.description:
Summary information about the product for which helpfulness metrics are aggregated.

This association replaces the raw productId field and provides enough context (such as product name and key merchandising fields) for analytics consumers to render product-level tables without extra lookups.

totalReviews.description:
Total number of reviews for this product that are included in the current analytics computation.

Only reviews that pass filters such as visibility status, moderation state, and time window are counted here.

totalHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of helpful votes across all eligible reviews for this product.

This value is aggregated from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes records linked to reviews for this product where is_helpful is true.

totalNotHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of not-helpful votes across all eligible reviews for this product.

This is aggregated from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes for reviews linked to this product with is_helpful set to false.

helpfulnessRatio.description:
Overall helpfulness ratio for this product’s reviews, typically computed as totalHelpfulVotes divided by (totalHelpfulVotes + totalNotHelpfulVotes).

This metric indicates how useful customers find the review content related to this product and can be used for ranking and monitoring.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessAnalytics..description:
Aggregated review helpfulness metrics grouped by SKU variant.

Each record represents a single SKU from shopping_mall_skus and aggregates helpfulness signals across reviews that explicitly target that SKU. This allows analytics to distinguish review helpfulness at variant level for products with multiple options.

Metrics are derived from shopping_mall_reviews and shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes and can be used in dashboards that compare variants within or across products.

skuId.description:
Identifier of the SKU whose review helpfulness metrics are aggregated in this record.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_skus.id and is referenced from shopping_mall_reviews.shopping_mall_sku_id.

productId.description:
Identifier of the parent product that owns the SKU.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_products.id and enables grouping or filtering at product level while still viewing SKU-level analytics.

totalReviews.description:
Total number of reviews that target this SKU and are included in the current analytics computation.

Only reviews whose shopping_mall_sku_id matches this SKU and that pass filters such as time window and visibility are counted.

totalHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of helpful votes across all included reviews for this SKU.

This value is aggregated from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes entries for reviews with this skuId where is_helpful is true.

totalNotHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of not-helpful votes across all included reviews for this SKU.

This is aggregated from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes entries where is_helpful is false.

helpfulnessRatio.description:
Overall helpfulness ratio for reviews targeting this SKU, typically computed as totalHelpfulVotes divided by (totalHelpfulVotes + totalNotHelpfulVotes).

This metric indicates how useful customers perceive review content specifically for this variant.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessAnalytics..description:
Aggregated review helpfulness metrics grouped by seller.

Each record represents a seller on the marketplace and aggregates helpfulness-related signals across reviews of products and SKUs owned by that seller. This helps operations and seller success teams understand which sellers provide products whose reviews are perceived as particularly helpful or unhelpful.

Metrics are derived from shopping_mall_reviews joined via products and SKUs to seller ownership, and from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes for helpfulness signals.

sellerId.description:
Identifier of the seller whose review helpfulness metrics are summarized.

This corresponds to the seller entity that owns the products or SKUs whose reviews are included in the aggregation.

totalReviews.description:
Total number of reviews considered in this aggregation for the seller’s catalog within the current filter set.

This count may include reviews across many products and SKUs owned by the seller and filtered by time period, visibility, and moderation state.

totalHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of helpful votes across all reviews included in this aggregation for the seller.

Derived from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes where the underlying review is associated with a product or SKU owned by this seller and is_helpful is true.

totalNotHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of not-helpful votes across all reviews included in this aggregation for the seller.

This is computed from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes where is_helpful is false for reviews linked to the seller’s catalog.

helpfulnessRatio.description:
Overall helpfulness ratio for the seller’s reviews, typically computed as totalHelpfulVotes divided by (totalHelpfulVotes + totalNotHelpfulVotes).

This metric provides a seller-level view of how useful customers find the review content associated with the seller’s products and can be used in internal performance dashboards.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsPeriod.description:
Reusable structure that describes the time window over which analytics metrics are aggregated.

The period contains explicit start and end timestamps and can optionally expose a human‑readable label or bucket key. It does not map to a dedicated database table, but instead represents query parameters and result metadata for analytics computations.

Using a shared period type ensures consistent semantics for time ranges across multiple analytics endpoints and summary DTOs.

start.description:
Inclusive start timestamp of the analytics period.

All events at or after this timestamp are considered for aggregation, subject to additional filters defined by the calling operation.

The value is represented as an ISO 8601 date‑time string with timezone information.

end.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the analytics period.

Events strictly before this moment are included in the aggregation, while events at or after the timestamp fall into subsequent periods.

Represented as an ISO 8601 date‑time string, it allows consumers to display or debug the exact range used for analytics computations.

label.description:
Optional human‑readable label describing the period, such as "2025‑03" or "2025‑03‑01".

This field can be used for chart axis labels, table headings, or simplified user‑facing summaries of the time bucket.

When omitted, clients should derive display labels from the start and end timestamps.

IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.IRequ.description:
Request DTO for computing review volume analytics over the shopping mall marketplace.

This type represents the filter, time range, granularity, and grouping configuration used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/reviews/volume endpoint. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model but drives analytical queries over shopping_mall_reviews and related aggregate tables.

The server uses these parameters to construct SQL aggregations and joins against transactional and aggregate tables, returning normalized analytical metrics instead of raw review rows.

timeRange.description:
Time window over which review volume should be analyzed.

The range is typically applied to review creation timestamps in shopping_mall_reviews, but implementations may also support alternative reference timestamps when documented.

timeGranularity.description:
Requested time bucket granularity for aggregations.

The server uses this to group counts and metrics into daily, weekly, or monthly buckets when time-based grouping is requested.

dimension.description:
Primary grouping dimension for the analytics response.

This controls whether results are broken down by time only, by product, by SKU, by seller, or by other supported dimensions.

ratingFilter.description:
Optional filter restricting reviews to specific rating values or ranges.

When omitted, all rating scores stored in shopping_mall_reviews are included in the aggregation.

moderationFilter.description:
Optional filter restricting reviews by visibility_status and moderation_state.

This allows focusing analytics on visible reviews, pending moderation items, or other moderation subsets.

includeDerivedKpis.description:
Flag indicating whether the server should compute additional derived KPIs.

When true, the response may include metrics such as reviews per order, reviews per active customer, or similar derived indicators based on other aggregates.

IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.description:
Response DTO for review volume analytics across the marketplace.

This type encapsulates aggregated metrics derived from shopping_mall_reviews and related aggregate tables such as shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates and shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates. It is returned by PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/reviews/volume.

The structure focuses on time-bucketed and dimension-bucketed metrics like counts of reviews, distribution of rating scores, and optional derived KPIs. It never exposes raw review content or personally identifiable information and should be safe for use in internal dashboards and reporting tools.

timeRange.description:
Effective time range used for the computation.

This echo of the request parameters allows clients to confirm which window the metrics cover, after any normalization or truncation performed by the server.

timeGranularity.description:
Time granularity actually applied by the server when computing time-bucketed metrics.

In most cases this will match the request, but servers may adjust unsupported granularities to the nearest supported value and report it here.

dimension.description:
Dimension used to group the result lines.

This corresponds to the dimension requested by the client and explains which entity or attribute each analytics line represents.

lines.description:
Collection of aggregated review volume lines.

Each line represents a single bucket in the chosen dimension and time granularity, including counts of reviews, rating distributions, and optional derived KPIs useful for charts and tables.

generatedAt.description:
Timestamp when these analytics were generated.

This helps dashboard consumers understand the recency of the metrics and manage client-side caching or refresh behavior.

IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.ILine.description:
Configuration describing the dimension along which review volume analytics are grouped.

This structure indicates which conceptual key defines each analytics line, such as time-only, product, SKU, seller, or category. It may also describe whether multiple dimensions are combined, for example time by product.

The chosen dimension affects how clients interpret the key fields in IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.ILine and how they render charts and tables in dashboards.

type.description:
High-level type of dimension for review volume breakdown.

Controls whether each analytics line represents a time bucket only, a product, a SKU, a seller, a category, or another supported dimension.

includeTimeBuckets.description:
Indicates whether time bucket grouping is applied in addition to the primary dimension.

When true, lines will typically be grouped by both a time bucket and the chosen entity, allowing time-series charts per product, SKU, or seller.

IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.ILine.description:
Single analytics line representing review volume metrics for a specific bucket.

Each line corresponds to a combination of the chosen dimension and time granularity. For example, a line can represent reviews for a product in a specific day or all reviews created in a given week across the marketplace.

The line contains aggregate measures including total review count, rating distribution, and optional derived KPIs that feed charts, tables, and monitoring widgets in admin or analytics interfaces.

timeBucket.description:
Identifier of the time bucket for this analytics line.

The format is determined by the selected time granularity. For example, daily buckets may use an ISO date string such as 2025-01-15, while monthly buckets may use a year-month representation like 2025-01.

When the active analytics configuration does not include time-based grouping for this line, this field is set to null so that consumers can distinguish purely dimension-based buckets from time-series buckets.

dimensionType.description:
Dimension type for this line.

Echoes the dimension configuration and clarifies which key field should be interpreted as the primary grouping key.

productId.description:
Product identifier when the dimension is product-based.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_products.id and is only populated when the dimension type indicates product or when the server decides to include product context for composite breakdowns.

skuId.description:
SKU identifier when the dimension is SKU-based.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_skus.id and is populated when reviewing volume metrics at variant level.

sellerId.description:
Seller identifier when the dimension groups reviews by seller.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_sellers.id in the broader schema and allows dashboards to show review activity per seller account.

totalReviewCount.description:
Total number of reviews in this bucket.

This is the primary volume metric derived from shopping_mall_reviews and filtered according to the request configuration.

rating1Count.description:
Number of reviews in this bucket with the lowest rating value on the platform scale, for example 1-star reviews.

The exact semantics correspond to the rating scale used in shopping_mall_reviews.rating.

rating2Count.description: Number of reviews in this bucket with the second rating value on the platform scale, for example 2-star reviews.

rating3Count.description: Number of reviews in this bucket with a mid-range rating value, for example 3-star reviews.

rating4Count.description: Number of reviews in this bucket with a high rating value, for example 4-star reviews.

rating5Count.description: Number of reviews in this bucket with the highest rating value, for example 5-star reviews.

averageRating.description:
Average rating value for this bucket.

This is typically computed as a weighted average from the individual ratings stored in shopping_mall_reviews.rating or from precomputed aggregates when available.

reviewsPerOrder.description:
Optional derived KPI indicating reviews per order in this bucket.

This metric is computed by combining review counts with order metrics from other aggregate tables. It may be null when the server or configuration chooses not to compute it.

reviewsPerActiveCustomer.description:
Optional derived KPI indicating reviews per active customer for the bucket.

The exact definition of an active customer is governed by business rules external to this schema. This value may be null when not computed.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationAnalytics.I.description:
Request DTO for computing aggregated review moderation analytics over review-related tables.

All properties in this request object are optional. Clients may send an entirely empty body, in which case the server applies sensible defaults such as a recent time window and unconstrained filters, and returns overall moderation analytics.

When provided, the properties allow admin callers to specify a time range, moderation state filters, reason code filters, seller and product scopes, grouping preferences, and time bucketing when invoking PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/reviews/moderation. The analytics engine uses these settings to build queries against shopping_mall_reviews, shopping_mall_review_reports, shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions, shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes, and shopping_mall_review_eligibilities.

It is purely an analytical query configuration object and does not map to any single Prisma model. Actor identity and authorization are handled separately by the authentication layer and are not represented in this DTO.

from.description:
Start of the time window for which moderation analytics should be calculated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

If omitted, the server may apply a default such as the last 30 days. Values outside the system’s retention window may be clamped silently or cause validation errors depending on business rules.

to.description:
End of the time window for which moderation analytics should be calculated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The interval is typically treated as inclusive of the start and exclusive of the end, but the exact semantics are defined by the analytics implementation. If omitted, the current time may be used as the upper bound.

items.description:
Moderation state filter value.

Typical values reflect the moderation_state column in shopping_mall_reviews and related tables, such as pending, under_review, approved, rejected, escalated, or similar workflow-specific values.

moderationStates.description:
Optional list of moderation states to include in the analytics.

When provided, only reviews or reports whose moderation state is in this list will be considered. When omitted, all moderation states are included.

items.description:
Review report processing status filter value.

Values should align with the status column in shopping_mall_review_reports, such as open, under_review, resolved, or dismissed, depending on configured workflows.

reportStatuses.description:
Optional list of review report processing statuses to include in the analytics.

If present, only reports with the given statuses are aggregated; otherwise, reports in all statuses may contribute to metrics.

items.description:
Reason code filter value.

Values should align with the reason_code column in shopping_mall_review_reports and shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions, for example offensive_content, spam, conflict_of_interest, policy_violation, or custom categories configured by operations.

reasonCodes.description:
Optional filter for specific report or moderation reason codes.

When set, the analytics engine restricts aggregated metrics to reports or actions whose reason_code is one of the specified values, enabling focused analysis on certain problem types.

items.description:
Seller identifier value used when scoping analytics.

Each value corresponds to shopping_mall_sellers.id and allows the caller to limit analytics to reviews that relate to specific sellers.

sellerIds.description:
Optional filter restricting analytics to reviews associated with specific sellers.

Admins may use this field to focus on particular sellers, while some deployments may ignore it or enforce additional scoping rules based on the caller’s permissions.

items.description:
Product identifier value.

Each value should correspond to shopping_mall_products.id, used to limit analytics to reviews for particular products.

productIds.description:
Optional list of product identifiers used to narrow analytics to specific products.

When provided together with sellerIds, the analytics engine typically applies both filters conjunctively, though exact semantics are defined by business rules.

oneOf.description:
Group results by review or report processing status.

This grouping dimension aggregates metrics per status value such as open, under_review, resolved, dismissed, or escalated.

Group results by structured report or moderation reason code.

This dimension aggregates metrics per reason_code, such as offensive_content, spam, or conflict_of_interest.

Group results by moderator or administrative actor.

This dimension aggregates metrics per admin who handled reports or moderation actions.

Group results by seller.

This dimension aggregates metrics per seller account whose catalog received reports or moderation actions.

Group results into time buckets.

This dimension aggregates metrics per time interval as defined by the timeBucket setting.

groupBy.description:
List of grouping dimensions that the client is interested in.

Supported dimension identifiers include:

- status: group by report or moderation status
- reason: group by structured reason_code
- moderator: group by administrative actor handling moderation
- seller: group by seller associated with the reviews
- time: group into time buckets controlled by the timeBucket property

The server uses these hints to populate corresponding breakdown arrays in the IShoppingMallReviewModerationAnalytics response. If omitted, a default set of groupings is applied.

oneOf.description:
Aggregate time-series metrics into hourly buckets.

Use this for high-resolution diagnostics where short-term spikes in moderation activity must be visible.

Aggregate time-series metrics into daily buckets.

This is typically the default for most operational dashboards and reports.

Aggregate time-series metrics into weekly buckets.

Use this for medium-term trend analysis where daily noise can be smoothed out.

Aggregate time-series metrics into monthly buckets.

Use this for long-term trend and planning views over extended periods.

timeBucket.description:
Requested time bucket size for time-series analytics.

Controls how the analytics engine aggregates metrics into the timeSeries array of the response. Common values include:

- hour: for high-resolution diagnostics
- day: for standard operational dashboards
- week: for medium-term trend analysis
- month: for long-term planning and reporting

If omitted, the implementation chooses a sensible default based on the overall time range and platform conventions.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationAnalytics.description:
Aggregated review moderation analytics result for administrator dashboards.

This DTO represents a denormalized analytical view derived from transactional moderation-related tables such as shopping_mall_reviews, shopping_mall_review_reports, shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions, shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes, and shopping_mall_review_eligibilities. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model but combines multiple sources to summarize workload and outcomes in the review moderation lifecycle.

The object is intended for internal governance and operations tooling, exposing counts, time-series metrics, and grouped breakdowns without leaking raw review content or personally identifiable information. It is typically populated by read-only analytics queries behind the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/reviews/moderation endpoint.

timeRange.description:
Echo of the time range that the analytics engine actually used when computing the review moderation metrics.

This field helps consumers verify which period the returned series and aggregates cover, especially when the backend has applied defaults or clamped the requested interval to system limits.

totals.description:
Overall aggregated moderation workload and outcome metrics for the selected time range.

Typical values include counts of reported reviews, open and resolved reports, total moderation actions, and net helpfulness vote statistics over all relevant reviews in scope.

byStatus.description:
Breakdown of moderation metrics grouped by report or review status.

Each entry captures aggregated counts such as number of reports, number of reviews, and average resolution times for a specific status like open, under_review, resolved, or dismissed.

byReason.description:
Breakdown of moderation metrics grouped by report reason code.

This allows admins to see which categories such as offensive_content, spam, or conflict_of_interest are driving moderation workload and whether certain reasons correlate with longer review times or higher escalation rates.

byModerator.description:
Breakdown of moderation metrics grouped by moderator or administrative actor.

Each entry aggregates actions taken and outcomes for a single moderator, enabling performance monitoring, workload balancing, and training needs analysis without exposing underlying personal PII to dashboards that do not require it.

bySeller.description:
Breakdown of moderation metrics grouped by seller.

This helps governance teams identify sellers whose products receive disproportionate numbers of problematic reviews or reports, supporting targeted quality interventions and policy enforcement.

timeSeries.description:
Time-series metrics describing how review moderation workload and outcomes evolve over the requested time range.

Each bucket represents an interval such as day, week, or month and aggregates counts of reports, actions, and resolution events within that interval for trend analysis.

oneOf.description:
Hourly analytics bucket granularity.

Use this value when computing high-resolution time-series metrics over relatively short time windows, such as intra-day moderation or operational diagnostics where hour-by-hour trends are important.

Daily analytics bucket granularity.

This is the most common choice for dashboards and reports, providing a balance between detail and readability when analyzing review moderation activity over days or weeks.

Weekly analytics bucket granularity.

Use this value to smooth out day-to-day noise and observe broader trends in review moderation workload and outcomes across multiple weeks.

Monthly analytics bucket granularity.

Best suited for long-term trend analysis, executive reporting, and capacity planning scenarios where fine-grained daily or hourly fluctuations are less important than overall patterns.

IAnalyticsTimeGranularity.description:
Enumeration of supported time granularities for analytics buckets.

This shared enum-like type is used by multiple analytics request DTOs to specify how time-based aggregations should be grouped, such as hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly buckets. Clients select one of the defined values to control the resolution of returned time-series data and summary statistics.

oneOf.description:
Enumeration of primary dimension types for review volume analytics.

Each value represents a distinct way of grouping reviews when computing volume metrics from shopping_mall_reviews and related tables. Some dimensions may require joining with additional tables such as products, SKUs, or sellers to resolve keys and labels.

Clients use these values when configuring IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.IRequest.dimension to control how charts and tables are organized.

Enumeration of primary dimension types for review volume analytics.

Each value represents a distinct way of grouping reviews when computing volume metrics from shopping_mall_reviews and related tables. Some dimensions may require joining with additional tables such as products, SKUs, or sellers to resolve keys and labels.

Clients use these values when configuring IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.IRequest.dimension to control how charts and tables are organized.

Each value represents a distinct way of grouping reviews when computing volume metrics from shopping_mall_reviews and related tables. Some dimensions may require joining with additional tables such as products, SKUs, or sellers to resolve keys and labels.

Clients use these values when configuring IShoppingMallReviewVolumeAnalytics.IRequest.dimension to control how charts and tables are organized.
