updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was last recalculated or corrected, if applicable.

While many snapshot rows are write‑once, certain pipelines may support recalculation or correction of historical metrics. In such cases this field records the last update time of the snapshot.

Analytics and governance tools can use this timestamp to detect recently corrected data, decide when to invalidate cached aggregates, and support audit requirements for metric revisions.

IShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot..description:
Search and filtering request for querying seller order metrics snapshots from `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots`.

This DTO encapsulates all client‑supplied criteria for analytics queries over the snapshot table, including seller scoping, time range selection, metric‑based filters, sorting preferences, and pagination parameters. It is used exclusively in read‑only search endpoints and never creates or mutates snapshot rows.

Admin and internal analytics tools construct this request body to retrieve pages of snapshot summaries for dashboards, monitoring views, and reporting exports. All filters are optional, allowing broad or highly targeted queries depending on the use case.

items.description:
Identifier of a seller to include in the snapshot search filter.

Each value is expected to match a seller account in `shopping_mall_sellers` and is applied against the `seller_id` column of the snapshot table. When multiple IDs are provided, snapshots for any of the listed sellers are included in the result set.

Admin analytics tools typically populate this array when focusing a dashboard on specific sellers or cohorts of interest.

sellerIds.description:
Optional collection of seller identifiers to filter snapshots by seller.

When provided, the search results will be restricted to snapshot rows whose `seller_id` matches one of the supplied UUIDs. If omitted, snapshots for all sellers that meet other criteria may be returned.

This filter is commonly used in admin consoles and internal reporting to inspect performance for specific sellers or groups of sellers.

snapshotDateFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the snapshot period range to search, expressed as a date-time.

This value is compared against the `snapshot_date` column in `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots` using a greater‑than‑or‑equal condition. It defines the start of the reporting window for which snapshots are returned.

Admins and analysts use this field to restrict analytics to recent periods (for example, the last 30 days) or to a particular historical window for investigations and audits.

snapshotDateTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the snapshot period range to search, expressed as a date-time.

This value is applied as a less‑than‑or‑equal filter on the `snapshot_date` column. Together with `snapshotDateFrom`, it defines the time window of snapshots that will be returned by the query.

It is helpful for constructing fixed reporting ranges such as monthly or weekly windows and for limiting the volume of snapshot rows loaded into dashboards.

timezone.description:
Optional business timezone identifier to filter snapshots by aggregation timezone.

When provided, only snapshot rows whose `timezone` column matches this value will be included. Typical identifiers follow the IANA timezone database, such as `Asia/Seoul`.

This filter is useful in multi‑region platforms where snapshots may be computed in different business timezones and analytics views need to align with a particular regional context.

minGmvAmount.description:
Optional minimum gross merchandise value (GMV) threshold used to filter snapshots.

When set, the query will return only snapshots whose `gmv_amount` is greater than or equal to this value. This helps focus analytics on periods or sellers with meaningful sales volume.

Risk and performance dashboards can use this filter to ignore low‑activity snapshots or to highlight days with significant GMV for further inspection.

maxGmvAmount.description:
Optional maximum gross merchandise value (GMV) threshold used to filter snapshots.

When specified, the query will return only snapshots whose `gmv_amount` is less than or equal to this value. It can be combined with `minGmvAmount` to define a GMV band.

This is commonly used in anomaly detection flows to isolate days with unusually high or low GMV relative to expected ranges for a seller.

minOrdersCancelledCount.description:
Optional minimum threshold for `orders_cancelled_count` when filtering snapshots.

If set, only snapshot rows where the number of cancelled orders or segments is greater than or equal to this value will be included. The filter uses the `orders_cancelled_count` column, which is indexed together with refund counts for efficient querying.

Governance and risk tools can use this filter to quickly surface periods of abnormal cancellation volume that may require investigation.

maxOrdersCancelledCount.description:
Optional maximum threshold for `orders_cancelled_count` when filtering snapshots.

When provided, snapshots with a cancellation count greater than this value are excluded from the result set. Combined with `minOrdersCancelledCount`, this allows analysts to focus on specific cancellation‑rate bands.

It is particularly useful in dashboards that compare sellers or days within a tolerable cancellation range and flag outliers separately.

minOrdersRefundedCount.description:
Optional minimum threshold for `orders_refunded_count` when filtering snapshots.

Snapshots will be included only if the value of `orders_refunded_count` is greater than or equal to this threshold. The filter leverages the indexed combination of cancellation and refund counts for performance.

Risk monitoring and quality assurance teams use this to locate days or sellers with unusually high refund activity indicative of product, logistics, or fraud issues.

maxOrdersRefundedCount.description:
Optional maximum threshold for `orders_refunded_count` when filtering snapshots.

When set, the search will exclude snapshots whose `orders_refunded_count` exceeds this value. Alongside `minOrdersRefundedCount`, it provides a way to model a target band for refund activity.

Analytics applications can use this filter to focus on acceptable ranges and separately highlight extreme refund spikes as anomalies.

sortBy.description:
Sort key indicating which snapshot column to order results by.

Supported values typically include keys that map to indexed columns such as `snapshotDate`, `gmvAmount`, `ordersCancelledCount`, and `ordersRefundedCount`. The concrete mapping to physical columns like `snapshot_date` or `gmv_amount` is handled by the service implementation.

This property, together with `sortDirection`, allows clients to request views ordered by time, sales volume, or risk‑related metrics depending on the analytics scenario.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the result set, usually `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending order.

When combined with `sortBy`, this property allows clients to control whether snapshots are returned from oldest to newest, highest to lowest GMV, or other domain‑specific sort orders.

If omitted, the service should apply a sensible default, commonly descending by `snapshot_date` so that the most recent snapshot appears first in dashboards.

page.description:
1‑based page index indicating which page of results to return.

This parameter works together with `limit` to implement cursor‑less pagination over the filtered snapshot set. A value of `1` typically represents the first page.

Clients should treat this as a user‑facing pagination control in admin consoles and analytics UIs, avoiding extremely large page numbers that would move beyond the meaningful result range.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot records to return in a single page.

The service implementation may enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses. Typical defaults range from 20 to 100 items per page depending on analytics UI requirements.

Pagination parameters like `page` and `limit` allow analytics consumers to navigate through large historical datasets without overloading the client or server.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.I.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating seller performance snapshot records.

This type models the filter, sorting, and pagination parameters that admin analytics tools and risk consoles use when querying the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` snapshot table. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model because it represents query semantics rather than a stored row.

The fields allow callers to constrain which sellers and which time windows are included, along with optional KPI threshold filters and ordering instructions so that dashboards can focus on underperforming or high‑performing sellers.

sellerId.description:
Optional filter for a specific seller identifier.

When provided, only snapshot rows belonging to this seller are considered. This corresponds to the `seller_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` table.

sellerIds.description:
Optional filter for a set of seller identifiers.

When provided, the query restricts results to snapshots whose `seller_id` is included in this list. This is typically used by admin tooling to focus on a curated subset of sellers.

items.description: Identifier of a seller account included in the filter set.

snapshotDateFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the snapshot time window.

Only snapshot rows whose `snapshot_date` is greater than or equal to this value are included. The timestamp should be provided in ISO 8601 date‑time format.

snapshotDateTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the snapshot time window.

Only snapshot rows whose `snapshot_date` is less than or equal to this value are included. The timestamp should be provided in ISO 8601 date‑time format.

timezone.description:
Optional timezone filter used when computing the performance window.

When set, only snapshots whose `timezone` column matches this value are returned. Typical values follow IANA timezone identifiers such as `Asia/Seoul`.

minOrderDefectRate.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `order_defect_rate`.

Only snapshots whose order defect rate is greater than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

maxOrderDefectRate.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `order_defect_rate`.

Only snapshots whose order defect rate is less than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

minRefundRate.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `refund_rate`.

Only snapshots whose refund rate is greater than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

maxRefundRate.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `refund_rate`.

Only snapshots whose refund rate is less than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

minCancellationRate.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `cancellation_rate`.

Only snapshots whose cancellation rate is greater than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

maxCancellationRate.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `cancellation_rate`.

Only snapshots whose cancellation rate is less than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

minLateShipmentRate.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `late_shipment_rate`.

Only snapshots whose late shipment rate is greater than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

maxLateShipmentRate.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `late_shipment_rate`.

Only snapshots whose late shipment rate is less than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

minChargebackRate.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `chargeback_rate`.

Only snapshots whose chargeback rate is greater than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

maxChargebackRate.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `chargeback_rate`.

Only snapshots whose chargeback rate is less than or equal to this value are included. The rate is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

minAverageRating.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `average_rating`.

Only snapshots whose average rating is greater than or equal to this value are included. The rating typically follows a 1–5 scale but is stored as a numeric type in the snapshot table.

maxAverageRating.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `average_rating`.

Only snapshots whose average rating is less than or equal to this value are included. The rating typically follows a 1–5 scale but is stored as a numeric type in the snapshot table.

minRatingCount.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `rating_count`.

Only snapshots whose rating count is greater than or equal to this value are included. This helps analysts focus on metrics backed by sufficient review volume.

maxRatingCount.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `rating_count`.

Only snapshots whose rating count is less than or equal to this value are included. This is mainly useful for quality checks and specialized analytics.

minDisputeOpenCount.description:
Optional lower bound filter on `dispute_open_count`.

Only snapshots whose open dispute count is greater than or equal to this value are included. This is typically used to identify problematic sellers with high numbers of unresolved disputes.

maxDisputeOpenCount.description:
Optional upper bound filter on `dispute_open_count`.

Only snapshots whose open dispute count is less than or equal to this value are included. It can also be used to focus on sellers with consistently low dispute volumes.

tier.description:
Optional filter for a single seller tier classification at the snapshot time.

When provided, only snapshots whose `tier` column matches this value are included. Example tiers include `new`, `standard`, `premium`, and `high_risk`.

tiers.description:
Optional filter for multiple seller tiers.

When provided, only snapshots whose `tier` column is contained in this list are considered. This is useful when segmenting multiple risk or performance bands in a single query.

items.description: Tier value that a snapshot must match to be included when this list is used.

sortBy.description:
Field name used for sorting the snapshot list.

Typical values correspond to key KPI columns such as `snapshot_date`, `order_defect_rate`, `refund_rate`, `cancellation_rate`, `late_shipment_rate`, `chargeback_rate`, `average_rating`, or `dispute_open_count`.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction for the ordered snapshot list.

Accepted values are conventionally `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, implementations may default to descending snapshot date or to a business‑specific default.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

This is a one‑based index indicating which page of results to return. When omitted, the first page is typically assumed.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

Admin tooling and analytics dashboards should enforce an upper bound to keep response sizes manageable while still allowing operators to browse meaningful result sets.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.description:
Detail DTO representing a single seller performance snapshot row from the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` table.

Each instance corresponds to one immutable snapshot of a seller’s performance KPIs computed at a specific point in time. The snapshot aggregates metrics such as order defect rate, refund rate, cancellation rate, late shipment rate, chargeback rate, rating statistics, and dispute counts for the analysis window defined by the snapshot date and timezone.

The data is used by admin back‑office tools, risk engines, and governance dashboards to monitor marketplace health, segment sellers into performance or risk tiers, and trigger case‑management workflows. Records are generated and maintained by internal analytics jobs or reporting pipelines rather than end‑user actions, and API consumers treat this DTO as a read‑only analytical view over time‑series data.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller performance snapshot row.

This value uniquely identifies the snapshot in the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` Prisma model and is stable over the lifetime of the record. It is used by drill‑down APIs and internal tools to retrieve or cross‑reference a specific snapshot instance.

seller.description:
Summary view of the seller associated with this performance snapshot.

This object provides key identity and classification information about the seller—such as identifier, email, status, and high‑level lifecycle state—so that admin analytics tools and dashboards can render meaningful context for the KPIs without issuing additional requests to seller-specific APIs.

snapshot_date.description:
Timestamp or logical date representing when this performance snapshot was computed.

Implementations typically align this field to the end of the analysis window, such as end‑of‑day or end‑of‑week, using ISO 8601 date‑time format. Analytics and reporting tools use this value to build time‑series charts and to compare performance across different periods.

timezone.description:
Timezone context used when computing the snapshot window.

The value reflects the business timezone applied to interpret `snapshot_date` and to define the boundaries of the analysis window, such as `Asia/Seoul`. Consumers should always interpret time‑based aggregations in the context of this timezone to avoid mismatched reporting across regions.

order_defect_rate.description:
Order defect rate for the seller during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

The numerator typically counts orders considered defective according to business rules (for example, orders with severe issues, cancellations after certain stages, or significant service failures), and the denominator counts all relevant orders in the window. Downstream systems should convert this fraction to percentages only for display purposes (for example, 0.12 → 12%).

refund_rate.description:
Refund rate for the seller during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

This metric measures how frequently orders or order items result in refunds relative to the total number of completed or chargeable orders in the window. High refund rates can indicate product quality issues, mis‑set expectations, or operational problems in fulfillment and support.

cancellation_rate.description:
Cancellation rate for the seller during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

The metric reflects the proportion of orders that were canceled before fulfillment out of all relevant orders in the same period. It is commonly used to detect listing accuracy problems, pricing mistakes, or reliability issues in the seller’s internal processes.

late_shipment_rate.description:
Late shipment rate during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

This metric indicates how often shipments were dispatched or delivered later than the expected schedule defined by shipping SLAs. It is computed as the number of late shipments divided by the total number of shipments considered in the window and is a key input to seller performance and customer experience evaluations.

chargeback_rate.description:
Chargeback rate for the seller during the snapshot period, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

The numerator is the count of paid orders that resulted in chargebacks, and the denominator is the total number of paid orders in the analysis window. Elevated chargeback rates are strong risk indicators and may trigger additional review, policy enforcement, or limitations for the seller.

average_rating.description:
Average product rating across the seller’s catalog at the time of snapshot.

The value is typically derived from customer reviews and usually follows a 1–5 scale, but it is stored as a generic numeric value in the snapshot table. Consumers should interpret the value within the configured rating scale and may combine it with `rating_count` to assess statistical reliability.

rating_count.description:
Number of ratings included when computing `average_rating`.

This count indicates how many individual review ratings were aggregated to derive the current average rating. Higher counts generally increase confidence in the average rating, while low counts may signal that the rating is still volatile or not yet representative.

dispute_open_count.description:
Number of disputes that were open for the seller at the time of snapshot computation.

The count reflects active dispute cases (for example, disputes over refunds, chargebacks, or policy violations) that involve the seller when the snapshot was generated. Risk and governance teams use this value to identify sellers with abnormally high levels of unresolved issues.

tier.description:
Optional seller tier classification assigned at this snapshot.

The tier encodes business‑defined performance or risk segments such as `new`, `standard`, `premium`, or `high_risk`. A null value indicates that no tier classification has been applied or that the seller falls outside known segmentation rules for this snapshot.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was created in the database.

This value records when the analytics or reporting pipeline wrote the row, and it may differ slightly from `snapshot_date` depending on computation or ingestion schedules. It is expressed in ISO 8601 date‑time format and is primarily used for operational monitoring and debugging of the analytics pipeline.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was last updated in the database.

Although the table is snapshot‑oriented, certain pipelines may recompute metrics, fix historical data issues, or enrich existing rows. This timestamp allows consumers and operators to understand when a previously generated snapshot was last refreshed or corrected.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionPlan.description:
Seller subscription plan entity for the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents a single subscription plan configuration row from the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans table. Each plan defines commercial terms such as billing period, currency, and recurring price that sellers can subscribe to.

Administrative tools use this type to display full plan information, including system-maintained timestamps and soft-deletion state. Business logic relies on the code field as a stable identifier in configuration, integrations, and reporting.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller subscription plan.

This value is generated by the system and uniquely identifies the plan row in the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans table. Clients receive it in responses but never provide it in create or update requests.

code.description:
Stable business code for the plan, such as BASIC, PRO, or ENTERPRISE.

This value corresponds to the code column with a unique index in shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans. It is used in configuration, integrations, and reporting as a human-readable yet stable identifier for the plan.

name.description:
Human-readable plan name shown to sellers in administrative and seller-facing UIs.

The name is used in lists and detail views to help actors understand which plan they are working with.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of features, benefits, and conditions of the plan.

When present, this text helps admins and sellers understand what the subscription includes beyond the basic name and price. When null, only the name and other metadata describe the plan.

billing_period.description:
Billing period identifier for the plan.

Typical values represent concepts like monthly or yearly, and application logic treats them as an enum-like string. This field determines how often the price_amount is charged.

currency.description:
ISO currency code used for charging the subscription fee.

Common values include currency codes such as USD or KRW. This field must align with the platform's supported currencies and is used together with price_amount when billing sellers.

price_amount.description:
Subscription fee amount per billing period.

This numeric value is expressed in the currency defined by the currency field. Business rules require it to be non-negative and it participates in billing calculations for seller subscriptions.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the plan is currently active and available for new subscriptions.

When true, sellers may newly subscribe to this plan according to other eligibility rules. When false, the plan may be retained for historical subscriptions but not offered to new subscribers.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which the plan becomes effective for new subscriptions.

This field typically marks the start of the validity window for pricing and availability. Business rules expect it to be earlier than or equal to effective_until when that field is set.

effective_until.description:
Optional timestamp after which the plan stops being offered for new subscriptions.

When null, the plan is considered open-ended and remains effective until changed. When set, it defines the end of the plan's configured effectiveness window.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the plan record.

This value is set by the system when the plan is first inserted into shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans and is not intended to be modified afterwards.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the plan record.

The system updates this field whenever mutable attributes of the plan are changed. Clients use it for display and potential concurrency checks.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the plan.

When null, the plan is considered logically present. When set, the plan is treated as deleted or fully retired according to business retention rules, and it should typically be hidden from normal administrative and seller views.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionPlan.IReq.description:
Search and filter request DTO for retrieving a paginated list of seller subscription plans.

This type encapsulates all query conditions, pagination parameters, and sorting options used by the `PATCH /shoppingMall/sellerSubscriptionPlans` endpoint to build a filtered query against the `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` table. It is designed for administrative and internal tools that need to browse and manage the catalog of seller subscription plans.

Typical usage includes combining free-text search over plan names or descriptions with structured filters like plan code, billing period, activation status, price range, and effective date windows, along with standard pagination information for list views.

page.description:
One-based index of the result page to retrieve.

When omitted, implementations typically default to the first page. This parameter is used together with `limit` to determine the offset in the underlying query. It should always be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

This controls the page size for the paginated result set. Implementations may enforce an upper bound regardless of the provided value to protect performance. When omitted, a sensible default such as 20 or 50 records per page is usually applied.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to plan names and descriptions.

This term allows administrators to quickly find plans based on partial matches in the `name` and `description` fields. Implementations may use full-text search indexes, ILIKE queries, or other mechanisms depending on the database configuration. When null, no free-text search filter is applied.

code.description:
Optional exact filter on the plan code.

When provided, only the plan whose `code` matches this value should be returned, effectively acting as a precise lookup within the search API. This is useful when a UI already knows the plan code but still wants to reuse the list endpoint for consistency. When null, no code-specific filter is applied.

name.description:
Optional case-insensitive filter on the plan name.

This filter is typically implemented as a partial match (for example, using a LIKE condition) on the `name` column of the Prisma model. It allows administrators to narrow down results to plans whose display names contain the given text fragment. When null, no name-specific filter is applied.

billing_period.description:
Optional filter on the billing period identifier.

When set, only plans whose `billing_period` column matches this value are included. Common examples are `monthly` and `yearly`, but the exact set of allowed values is governed by business policy. When null, all billing periods are considered.

is_active.description:
Optional filter on the activation status of the plan.

When `true`, the search is restricted to currently active plans, while `false` can be used to find deactivated or legacy plans that are no longer offered for new subscriptions. When null, plans are not filtered by activation status and both active and inactive records may appear.

price_min.description:
Optional lower bound for the plan's price amount.

When provided, only plans with `price_amount` greater than or equal to this value are included in the result. This facilitates searching for plans within a certain pricing band. When null, no minimum price constraint is applied.

price_max.description:
Optional upper bound for the plan's price amount.

When provided, only plans with `price_amount` less than or equal to this value are returned. This parameter is typically used together with `price_min` to specify a price range filter. When null, no maximum price constraint is applied.

effective_from_start.description:
Optional lower bound for the plan's effective_from timestamp.

When set, only plans whose `effective_from` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This is useful for locating plans introduced after a certain date or for focusing on recently added offerings. When null, no lower bound on `effective_from` is enforced.

effective_from_end.description:
Optional upper bound for the plan's effective_from timestamp.

When set, only plans whose `effective_from` is less than or equal to this timestamp are included. Combined with `effective_from_start`, this parameter supports querying plans introduced within a given time window. When null, no upper bound on `effective_from` is enforced.

sort_key.description:
Optional name of the field used for sorting results.

Common values include `code`, `name`, `price_amount`, `effective_from`, or `created_at`. Implementations should validate the supplied value against a whitelist of sortable columns to avoid injection risks. When null, a default ordering (such as by `created_at` descending or `code` ascending) is applied.

sort_order.description:
Optional sort direction for the results list.

Allowed values are typically `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. When null, the default direction is applied in combination with the chosen `sort_key`. Implementations should normalize the value to a safe internal representation before applying it to queries.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionPlan.ICre.description:
Creation payload for registering a new seller subscription plan.

This DTO maps to the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans table and is used by administrative endpoints when defining new subscription plans that sellers can choose from. It supplies all business-managed fields required to describe the plan's commercial terms while leaving identifier and audit fields fully system-managed.

Server-side logic is responsible for generating the primary key id and maintaining created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at timestamps, so those columns are intentionally excluded from this create contract. At creation time the client specifies the business code, name, billing_period, currency, price_amount, is_active flag, and the initial effectiveness window using effective_from and an optional effective_until.

The combination of is_active and the effective_from/effective_until window governs when the plan can be selected for new subscriptions. Even after a plan has been deactivated or passed its effective_until date, existing historical subscriptions may continue to reference it according to business and retention policies.

code.description:
Stable business code for the new plan.

The value must be unique across all existing plans according to the @@unique([code]) constraint in shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans. Typical examples include BASIC, PRO, or ENTERPRISE. This code acts as the primary external identifier in integrations, reporting, and administrative tooling and cannot be changed after creation.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the new subscription plan.

This name is displayed in administrative consoles and potentially seller-facing UIs, giving a concise label for the plan. It can be updated later if naming or branding changes are required.

description.description:
Optional free-form description of the plan's features and benefits.

When provided, this text explains what the plan includes, such as included features, limits, and support tiers. When null, only the name, billing period, currency, and pricing metadata describe the plan.

billing_period.description:
Billing period identifier for the new plan.

Application logic treats this field as an enum-like string representing billing cadence such as monthly or yearly. The value must be one of the platform-supported periods and is used together with price_amount to drive recurring billing behavior.

currency.description:
ISO currency code in which the plan is billed.

The value must correspond to a supported currency like USD or KRW and is used together with price_amount during billing. Changing platform-level currency support or exchange rate behavior does not change values stored in this DTO.

price_amount.description:
Subscription fee amount charged each billing period.

Business validation requires this amount to be non-negative and aligned with the platform's pricing rules for subscription plans. The value is stored in the currency specified by the currency field and participates directly in billing calculations for seller subscriptions.

is_active.description:
Flag specifying whether the new plan is immediately active for new subscriptions.

When true, and when the current time falls within the effective_from and effective_until window, sellers may start subscribing to the plan. When false, the plan is created but not yet available for new sign-ups, although it may still be referenced in administrative tools and future activation workflows.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which the plan becomes effective for new subscriptions.

This value marks the beginning of the plan's effectiveness window for pricing and availability. It must not conflict with the optional effective_until field, and business rules typically require it to be earlier than or equal to effective_until when that value is present.

effective_until.description:
Optional timestamp marking when the plan stops being offered for new subscriptions.

If null, the plan is open-ended and remains potentially available until changed by an admin or governed by a separate deactivation process. If set, the value must be later than effective_from and is used to determine when the plan should no longer be selectable for new subscriptions, even if is_active remains true.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionPlan.IUpd.description:
Update payload for modifying an existing seller subscription plan identified by its business code.

This DTO is used by administrative endpoints that adjust mutable attributes of rows in the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans table. The target plan is selected by its globally unique code in the URL path, so this payload does not include id or code and never changes ownership or primary keys.

All properties are optional to support partial updates. Server-side logic applies only the fields that are present, updates the updated_at timestamp automatically, and enforces business rules regarding billing_period, currency, price_amount, activation status, and effectiveness windows. Fields such as created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at remain strictly system-managed and cannot be altered directly through this DTO.

name.description:
Optional new human-readable name for the plan.

When provided, this value replaces the previous name displayed in administrative and seller-facing UIs. It does not affect pricing or contractual semantics but helps keep catalog labels up to date.

description.description:
Optional updated description of the plan's features and benefits.

Supplying a non-null value replaces the previous description with new explanatory text. Supplying null explicitly clears the description so that only structural fields such as name, billing_period, and currency describe the plan.

billing_period.description:
Optional updated billing period identifier.

When present, this value changes how often the plan is billed, for example switching from monthly to yearly, subject to platform rules about modifying live plans. Implementations should validate that changes do not violate existing contractual expectations for sellers already subscribed to the plan.

currency.description:
Optional updated ISO currency code used for billing.

Changing this field alters the currency in which future charges for the plan are expressed and must follow platform policies about currency transitions. Implementations may restrict such changes when active subscriptions exist.

price_amount.description:
Optional updated subscription fee amount per billing period.

When provided, this value replaces the previous price_amount and must remain non-negative according to business validation rules. Changes to price_amount may be subject to additional governance or notification workflows depending on platform policy.

is_active.description:
Optional flag to activate or deactivate the plan for new subscriptions.

Setting this to true enables new subscriptions when the current time is within the effective_from/effective_until window. Setting it to false prevents new sign-ups while typically leaving historical subscriptions intact. Implementations may enforce additional rules (for example, preventing certain deactivations when specific obligations exist).

effective_from.description:
Optional updated start timestamp for the plan's effectiveness window.

This value, when present, replaces the previous effective_from and must maintain a valid chronological relationship with effective_until if that field is set. Adjusting effective_from can change when the plan first becomes selectable for new subscriptions and should respect historical interpretations of the plan for existing subscribers.

effective_until.description:
Optional updated end timestamp for the plan's effectiveness window.

Providing a non-null value sets or changes the end of the plan's active offering period. Providing null explicitly clears the previous end date, making the plan open-ended again. Implementations should ensure that changes are consistent with governance rules and do not retroactively invalidate historical subscriptions.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscription.description:
Seller subscription entity representing an individual subscription that a seller holds to a specific subscription plan in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` Prisma model and exposes fields required to understand and display the full state of a subscription record, including lifecycle status, time boundaries, pricing amounts, foreign key identifiers, and soft deletion metadata.

In read operations, this type is typically returned by detail endpoints such as `GET /shoppingMall/admin/sellerSubscriptions/{subscriptionId}` for administrative consoles and internal tools that inspect subscription relationships between sellers and plans. It can also be used by background jobs or integration services that need both human-readable plan and seller summaries and the raw foreign key identifiers for efficient joins and data processing.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller subscription record.

This value corresponds to the primary key column `id` of the `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` table and is generated by the system when the subscription is created.

seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who owns this subscription.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable foreign key column `seller_id` in the `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` table and references `shopping_mall_sellers.id`.

It is primarily used by backend services, reporting pipelines, and administrative tools to join subscription records to the underlying seller account, even when a richer `seller` summary object is also present.

seller_subscription_plan_id.description:
Identifier of the subscription plan applied to this seller subscription.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable foreign key column `seller_subscription_plan_id` in the `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` table and references `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans.id`.

It enables backend processes and external integrations to perform joins and analytics keyed by the raw plan identifier while the `plan` summary object provides a human-readable view for UI consumers.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the subscription.

Typical values include business-defined states such as `pending`, `active`, `past_due`, `cancelled`, or `expired`. The allowed set is enforced by application logic rather than a database enum.

started_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription became active for the seller.

This field maps to the non-nullable `started_at` column and is used for billing, entitlement, and analytics calculations.

ended_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription ended or is scheduled to end.

This field is nullable in the database (`ended_at`) and remains null while the subscription is ongoing or open-ended.

next_billing_at.description:
Timestamp of the next expected billing event for this subscription.

This value corresponds to the nullable `next_billing_at` column and is populated when the billing engine has scheduled a future charge.

currency.description:
Currency code in which this subscription is billed.

This string maps to the `currency` column in the Prisma model and typically contains ISO currency codes such as `USD` or `KRW`.

price_amount.description:
Nominal price per billing period for this subscription.

This double-precision field corresponds to the `price_amount` column and is expressed in the subscription currency for the active plan at the time of activation.

discount_amount.description:
Per-period discount amount applied to this subscription, if any.

This field maps to the `discount_amount` column and is zero when no discount is applied for the billing period.

metadata_json.description:
Optional JSON-encoded metadata associated with this subscription instance.

This field corresponds to the nullable `metadata_json` column and can store structured configuration or contextual information that does not warrant separate columns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription record was created.

This value comes from the non-nullable `created_at` column and is used for auditing and chronological reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription record was last updated.

This maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column and is updated whenever mutable fields on the subscription change.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the subscription record.

This nullable `deleted_at` column is set when the subscription is logically removed from normal views while retained for compliance and historical reporting.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller that owns this subscription.

This association transforms the `seller_id` foreign key that points to `shopping_mall_sellers.id` into a rich reference object. It provides enough context to identify and display the seller in administrative and analytical views without requiring an additional API call.

plan.description:
Summary of the subscription plan applied to this seller subscription.

This association replaces the raw `seller_subscription_plan_id` foreign key that references `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans.id` with a summary object. It allows clients to understand which plan governs pricing and entitlements for the subscription while avoiding circular references or over-fetching of full plan details.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscription.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for computing seller subscription analytics over the shoppingMall platform.

This schema encapsulates filter criteria, aggregation dimensions, and pagination controls used when querying analytical metrics derived from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions`, `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans`, and `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`.

It is designed for internal admin and analytics use cases, enabling flexible slicing of subscription behavior without exposing raw subscription rows directly through the API.

date_range.description:
Optional subscription lifecycle date range filter.

When provided, this range is typically applied to subscription activation timestamps such as `started_at` or other lifecycle timestamps depending on the `date_range_type` field.

If omitted, the server may default to a sensible recent window such as the last 30 days.

date_range_type.description:
Type of lifecycle timestamp to which `date_range` should apply.

Typical values include logical categories such as `started_at`, `ended_at`, or `next_billing_at`. The analytics implementation interprets this string to decide which timestamp column to constrain.

When omitted, the server defaults to applying the date range to primary subscription activation timestamps.

items.description: Subscription plan code value corresponding to `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans.code`.

plan_codes.description:
Optional list of seller subscription plan codes to include.

Each entry should correspond to the `code` column in `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans`. When provided, only subscriptions associated with the specified plans are included in analytics.

If empty or omitted, all plans are considered.

items.description: UUID identifier of a seller from `shopping_mall_sellers.id`.

seller_ids.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers to restrict analytics.

Each value references the `id` of a seller in `shopping_mall_sellers`. When provided, only subscriptions owned by these sellers contribute to computed metrics.

If omitted, analytics spans all sellers visible to the admin context.

items.description: Subscription lifecycle status value such as `pending`, `active`, `past_due`, `cancelled`, or `expired`.

statuses.description:
Optional set of subscription lifecycle status filters.

Values should align with the `status` column in `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions`. Only subscriptions whose status is included in this list are considered.

When not specified, subscriptions of all statuses may be included, subject to implementation defaults.

items.description: Analytics grouping dimension key such as `day`, `week`, `month`, `plan`, or `seller`.

group_by.description:
List of dimensions used to group analytics results.

The analytics engine aggregates subscription metrics into buckets determined by these keys, for example grouping by time period, plan, seller, or combinations thereof.

The allowed values and combinations are implementation-specific; unsupported dimensions should result in validation errors.

items.description: Metric identifier such as `new_subscriptions`, `active_subscriptions`, `cancelled_subscriptions`, `churn_rate`, or `mrr`.

metrics.description:
Optional explicit list of metric identifiers to compute.

When provided, the analytics engine restricts computation to the requested metrics, which can reduce processing overhead.

If omitted, a default set of subscription-related metrics is returned.

pagination.description:
Pagination controls for navigating the analytics result set.

This object defines the page index, page size, and optional cursor used by the backend to limit the number of aggregated rows returned per call.

sorts.description:
Optional list of sort directives applied to the aggregated analytics rows.

Each directive specifies a field key, typically a grouping dimension or metric, and a sort direction. When omitted, the server uses a default ordering appropriate for the chosen grouping.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscription.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new seller subscription in the shopping mall platform.

This schema is derived from the shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions Prisma model and includes only the fields that callers are allowed to supply when creating a subscription record. It is used by administrative tooling or internal workflows to connect a seller to a specific subscription plan with an initial pricing configuration.

Server‑managed fields such as the subscription identifier, audit timestamps, and soft‑deletion markers are excluded from this request body, because they are generated and maintained by the backend service logic.

seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who owns this subscription.

This value must reference an existing record in the shopping_mall_sellers table. It determines which seller account the subscription will be attached to and drives subsequent billing, entitlement, and reporting logic for that seller.

seller_subscription_plan_id.description:
Identifier of the subscription plan being applied to the seller.

This must reference a valid plan record in the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans table. The selected plan defines pricing, billing cadence, feature entitlements, and other business rules that will govern the lifecycle of this subscription.

status.description:
Initial status of the seller subscription at creation time.

Typical values include business states such as `pending`, `active`, `past_due`, `cancelled`, or `expired`. The exact set of allowed values is enforced by application logic, and callers must follow the platform’s subscription state transition rules when choosing an initial status.

started_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription becomes effective for the seller.

This field is represented as an ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC. It marks the beginning of the billing and entitlement interval for the selected plan. Implementations may set this to the current time or a future point depending on business rules.

ended_at.description:
Optional timestamp when the subscription ends or is scheduled to end.

When supplied, this value must be an ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC. A null value means that the subscription has no scheduled end yet and is expected to continue until explicitly cancelled or expired by business logic.

next_billing_at.description:
Timestamp of the next expected billing event for this subscription.

This optional field allows callers to set or adjust the anticipated billing schedule according to the selected plan or migration scenarios. When provided, it must be an ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC; when null, the backend may derive the next billing date automatically.

currency.description:
Three‑letter currency code in which this subscription is billed.

This value usually matches the currency configured on the associated subscription plan, but is stored explicitly for historical and reporting accuracy. Typical values follow ISO 4217 codes such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

price_amount.description:
Nominal price per billing period for this subscription, expressed in the specified currency.

This value represents the base amount charged each billing cycle before discounts. It should align with the plan’s standard price or a negotiated rate and is stored as a double‑precision floating‑point number.

discount_amount.description:
Discount amount applied per billing period for this subscription, expressed in the same currency as `price_amount`.

A value of zero means that no discount is applied. Positive values reduce the effective charge per period according to the platform’s billing rules.

metadata_json.description:
Optional JSON‑encoded metadata attached to this subscription instance.

This field can store configuration or contextual information such as rollout flags, migration context, or integration identifiers. The backend does not interpret the structure of this JSON blob directly and treats it as opaque metadata.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscription.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing seller subscription in the shopping mall platform.

This schema is based on the shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions Prisma model and exposes only fields that are allowed to change after the subscription has been created. It is typically used by administrative tools to adjust plan selection, billing configuration, or lifecycle timestamps while preserving immutable identity and audit information.

All properties are optional, allowing callers to perform partial updates. System‑managed fields such as the primary key and audit timestamps remain controlled by the backend and cannot be altered through this DTO.

seller_id.description:
Updated identifier of the seller who owns this subscription.

In most deployments this relation is immutable after creation, but when business rules permit reassignment, this field can be used to move a subscription to a different seller record in the shopping_mall_sellers table.

seller_subscription_plan_id.description:
Updated identifier of the subscription plan applied to this seller subscription.

Changing this value switches the subscription to a different plan in the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans catalog. Implementations must enforce plan compatibility and ensure that billing and entitlements are migrated safely.

status.description:
New status for the seller subscription.

Typical values include business states such as `pending`, `active`, `past_due`, `cancelled`, or `expired`. Application logic validates that the requested transition from the current status to the new status complies with the platform’s subscription state machine.

started_at.description:
Revised effective start timestamp for the subscription.

This ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC may be adjusted in exceptional cases, such as correcting misconfigured start dates or aligning subscriptions with billing cycles. Changes should respect historical billing and entitlement records.

ended_at.description:
Updated end timestamp for the subscription, or null to clear any scheduled end.

When provided, this field specifies when the subscription is considered terminated or scheduled for termination. It must be an ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC if not null, and transitions should follow business rules for cancellations and expirations.

next_billing_at.description:
Updated next billing timestamp for this subscription.

This field can be used to reschedule upcoming billing events in response to plan changes, grace periods, or corrections. It must be an ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC when set, or null when the billing schedule should be recomputed by backend logic.

currency.description:
Updated three‑letter currency code used for billing this subscription.

Changes to this value are rare and must remain consistent with the associated plan and billing configuration. The code normally follows ISO 4217, for example `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

price_amount.description:
Updated nominal price per billing period for this subscription, expressed in the billing currency.

This value can be adjusted to reflect negotiated rates, promotional pricing, or plan changes. It remains a double‑precision numeric field and should be consistent with financial and invoicing rules.

discount_amount.description:
Updated discount amount applied per billing period for this subscription.

Adjusting this value changes the effective charge each cycle relative to `price_amount`. Setting it to zero removes any ongoing discount for the subscription.

metadata_json.description:
Updated JSON‑encoded metadata associated with this subscription instance.

This field can be used to change or clear contextual metadata such as integration keys, rollout flags, or other custom configuration. The backend stores the string as an opaque JSON blob and does not enforce a specific structure.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying seller fee charge records stored in the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` table.

This request type is used by internal admin and finance tools to retrieve a filtered, paginated list of seller fee charges. It exposes rich search criteria aligned with the table's indexed columns and common financial analysis needs, such as searching by seller, fee type, currency, effective date ranges, amount ranges, and platform revenue flag.

The DTO also includes generic pagination and sorting parameters to support back-office list screens and reporting exports, without exposing any internal implementation details of the underlying Prisma model.

page.description:
Page index for pagination.

Represents the 1-based page number to retrieve when listing seller fee charges. Typical admin UIs start at page 1 and increment sequentially as users navigate through results.

Conceptually corresponds to the `current` field in `IPage.IPagination`, and should be a positive integer value. If omitted, the service may default to the first page.

limit.description:
Page size for pagination.

Indicates the maximum number of seller fee charge records to return in a single page. Back-office tools often default this to a moderate value (for example, 20, 50, or 100) to balance usability and performance.

This value aligns with the `limit` field in `IPage.IPagination` and should be a positive integer. If omitted, the service applies a sensible default and may cap the value at an upper limit to protect the system.

sellerId.description:
Filter by seller identifier.

When provided, restricts results to fee charges belonging to a specific seller, identified by the UUID primary key of the seller in the `shopping_mall_sellers` table.

Useful for viewing all fee charges for one seller over a given period.

orderId.description:
Filter by related order identifier.

When set, limits the search to fee charges that are associated with a specific order via the `order_id` foreign key. The value corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.id`.

This is useful for investigating all fee and commission charges attached to a particular order.

paymentRefundId.description:
Filter by related payment refund identifier.

When provided, the query returns only charges attached to a specific refund via the `payment_refund_id` foreign key, which references `shopping_mall_payment_refunds.id`.

This helps back-office workflows analyze fees created by refund operations.

sellerPayoutItemId.description:
Filter by related seller payout item identifier.

Restricts results to fee charges linked to a particular payout item via the `seller_payout_item_id` foreign key, referencing `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.id`.

Useful when reconciling which charges were settled within a specific payout batch item.

items.description:
Single fee type value used to categorize a seller fee charge.

Concrete values are defined by the system as an enum-like set, typically including categories such as `transaction_commission`, `platform_service_fee`, `subscription_fee`, `advertising_fee`, and `adjustment`.

Clients should only send values that are recognized by the business rules for fee categorization.

feeTypes.description:
List of fee type filters.

When provided, the search restricts results to fee charges whose `fee_type` matches any of the given values. The underlying business logic treats the `fee_type` column as an enum-like string.

If omitted, no filter on fee type is applied and all categories are included.

currency.description:
Currency code filter.

When set, limits results to fee charges whose `currency` field equals the specified currency code, such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

This is useful for multi-currency platforms where finance users need to analyze fees per currency.

isPlatformRevenue.description:
Filter by platform revenue flag.

When true, restricts results to charges where `is_platform_revenue` is true, meaning the fee contributes to platform revenue. When false, restricts to pass-through charges owed to third parties.

If omitted, the search does not filter on this flag and returns both platform revenue and non-revenue charges.

effectiveDateFrom.description:
Start of the effective date range filter.

Represents the inclusive lower bound of the business `effective_date` used for revenue recognition and reporting. Only charges with `effective_date` greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned.

Use together with `effectiveDateTo` to narrow results to a specific accounting period.

effectiveDateTo.description:
End of the effective date range filter.

Represents the inclusive upper bound of the `effective_date` field. Only charges with `effective_date` less than or equal to this timestamp are included in the result set.

When combined with `effectiveDateFrom`, this allows finance users to query charges for a specific date range or reporting period.

createdAtFrom.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range filter.

Defines the inclusive lower bound for the `created_at` column, limiting results to fee charges created at or after the given timestamp.

This is often used in operational reporting where the creation time is more relevant than the business effective date.

createdAtTo.description:
End of the creation timestamp range filter.

Defines the inclusive upper bound for the `created_at` column, limiting results to fee charges created at or before this value.

Used together with `createdAtFrom` for time-based operational queries and monitoring.

minAmount.description:
Lower bound of fee amount filter.

When set, limits results to fee charges where the `amount` is greater than or equal to the specified value. The amount is expressed in the same currency as the `currency` field on each record.

Useful for excluding very small fees or focusing on large charges that significantly impact revenue.

maxAmount.description:
Upper bound of fee amount filter.

When set, restricts results to fee charges whose `amount` is less than or equal to the given value. The amount uses the same currency semantics as other fee charge records.

Commonly used in conjunction with `minAmount` to analyze charges within a specific monetary band.

sortBy.description:
Sort key for the result set.

Determines which column is used for ordering the returned seller fee charges. Implementations typically support keys aligned with indexed columns such as `effective_date`, `created_at`, or `amount`.

If omitted, the service applies a sensible default (often `effective_date` or `created_at` in descending order). Supplying an unsupported sort key should result in a validation error or be normalized according to server-side business rules.

sortDirection.description:
Sorting direction for the result set.

Controls whether the list of seller fee charges is sorted in ascending or descending order based on the `sortBy` field. Commonly accepted values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending.

When not provided, the implementation typically defaults to `desc` for date-based sort keys so that the most recent charges appear first in administrative views.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.description:
Seller fee charge entity for the shopping mall marketplace.

This type represents an individual fee or commission charge that the platform applies to a seller, such as transaction commissions, subscription fees, advertising fees, adjustments, or penalties. Each record corresponds to a single charge row in the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` table and is part of the seller’s financial ledger used for reconciliation and payout calculations.

The entity links to a seller and may optionally link to an order, a payment refund, or a payout item for precise traceability of why the fee exists and how it is settled. It also stores monetary information, tax breakdown, effective date for revenue recognition, and soft delete metadata so that historical records remain auditable even when logically removed.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller fee charge.

This is the unique identifier of the row in `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` and is used in path parameters such as `feeChargeId` for update and lookup operations. The value is generated by the system and is immutable once created.

seller.description:
Seller to whom this fee charge applies.

This summary object is resolved from the non-nullable `seller_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` table, which references `shopping_mall_sellers.id`. It provides high-level seller information so that financial and back-office tools can immediately see which seller is being charged without performing additional lookups.

In reconciliation and analytics workflows, this association is used together with seller earnings and payout data to understand the overall financial impact on a particular seller.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the related order that caused this fee charge.

When present, this corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.id` and indicates that the fee is associated with a specific customer order, such as a transaction commission on the order value.

Null when the fee charge is not tied to a specific order.

This is common for subscription fees, advertising packages, or manual adjustments that are not order-based and therefore do not populate the `order_id` foreign key column.

orderId.description:
Optional related order identifier.

This field exposes the order linkage represented by the nullable `order_id` foreign key in the underlying Prisma model. It is nullable so that non–order-based fees can exist while still enabling tight reconciliation for transaction-based fees.

order.description:
Optional summary of the related order that caused this fee charge.

When present, this association is derived from the `order_id` foreign key and the `shopping_mall_orders` table. It provides a lightweight view of the customer order linked via `orderId`, including key business attributes such as order code, state, and monetary context, so that consumers of fee charge data can understand the originating order without issuing additional GET requests.

When null, the fee charge is not tied to a specific order, which is typical for subscription, advertising, or manual adjustment fees that are scoped to a period or account rather than a particular transaction.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the related payment refund record.

When set, this value corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_refunds.id` and indicates that the fee is associated with a particular refund operation, such as refund processing charges or adjustments triggered by a refund.

Null when the fee charge is not directly associated with a payment refund event.

In that case, the `payment_refund_id` foreign key column is left empty in the underlying table.

paymentRefundId.description:
Optional related payment refund identifier.

This field reflects the nullable `payment_refund_id` foreign key in the Prisma model and allows analytics and audit workflows to understand which refund event generated or adjusted this fee charge.

paymentRefund.description:
Optional summary of the payment refund that this fee charge is associated with.

When present, this association is resolved from the `payment_refund_id` foreign key to the `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` table and provides contextual information about the underlying refund, such as refund sequence, status, and high-level amounts.

It is populated when `paymentRefundId` references a valid refund record and remains null when the fee is not tied to a specific refund event.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the payout item that settled this fee charge.

When present, this corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.id` and indicates which payout item included this charge when settling balances with the seller.

Null when the fee has not yet been reconciled into a payout item or when it is tracked independently for reporting.

In that case, the `seller_payout_item_id` foreign key column remains null until a payout batch is created or updated to include this charge.

sellerPayoutItemId.description:
Optional payout item identifier that settled this fee charge.

This field exposes the nullable `seller_payout_item_id` foreign key in the database and is used for reconciliation between individual fee charges and aggregated payout batches.

payoutItem.description:
Optional summary of the seller payout item that settles this fee charge.

When present, this association is resolved from the `seller_payout_item_id` foreign key to the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table and provides a compact view of the payout item that includes this fee. Financial back-office tools and analytics processes use this linkage to navigate from a fee charge to the payout in which it was settled and to reconcile payouts against underlying fees.

It is null when the fee has not yet been assigned to a payout or when reconciliation is handled separately.

feeType.description:
Business category of the fee charge.

This value classifies the nature of the fee, such as `transaction_commission`, `platform_service_fee`, `subscription_fee`, `advertising_fee`, or `adjustment`. The application treats this as an enum-like string backed by the `fee_type` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` table and uses it to drive financial reporting, analytics, and business rules for how the fee should be interpreted.

Downstream systems and analytics pipelines rely on this categorization to group charges for dashboards, statements, and regulatory reports, so consistent usage of defined fee type codes is important.

oneOf.description:
Human-readable description of the fee charge.

Contains explanatory text that describes why this fee was applied, such as invoice numbers, promotion names, manual adjustment reasons, or reconciliation notes. It is intended for use in admin consoles, support tools, and exported statements and is stored in the nullable `description` column.

Null when no additional descriptive text is provided and the fee type alone is sufficient to explain the charge.

In this case the `description` column in the database remains null.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description of the fee.

This mirrors the nullable `description` column in the Prisma model and helps administrators and finance teams understand the business context of the charge beyond its categorical fee type.

currency.description:
Currency code of the fee amount.

This is the ISO-like currency code (for example, `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"`) stored in the `currency` column, indicating the currency in which both `amount` and `tax_amount` are expressed. All monetary calculations and reporting for this fee charge are performed in this currency and must be consistent with related orders, payments, and payouts.

amount.description:
Monetary amount of the fee charge.

Positive values represent charges applied to the seller that reduce the seller’s net earnings or balance. Negative values may be used to represent fee reversals, credits, or adjustments that effectively give value back to the seller. The value is stored as a numeric type in the `amount` column and should be handled with appropriate monetary rounding rules in business logic and reporting.

taxAmount.description:
Tax portion of the fee amount.

This field stores the tax component associated with the fee, expressed in the same currency as `amount` and persisted in the `tax_amount` column. When no tax applies to a particular fee, this value is stored as zero. Tax reporting and compliance processes use this field to determine how much tax is contained in platform revenue or pass-through charges.

isPlatformRevenue.description:
Flag indicating whether the fee contributes to platform revenue.

When true, the fee is treated as income for the platform itself, such as commissions or subscription fees. When false, the fee represents a pass-through amount due to third parties or other entities, meaning it does not contribute to platform revenue even though it is charged to the seller. This distinction, stored in the `is_platform_revenue` column, is crucial for accounting, revenue recognition, and regulatory reporting.

effectiveDate.description:
Business effective date of the fee.

This timestamp, stored in the `effective_date` column, indicates the business date on which the fee is considered effective for revenue recognition, financial reporting, and time-based analytics. It may differ from the technical creation time to align with billing cycles, order completion dates, or accounting periods.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the fee charge record was created.

This is the system-managed creation time for the row in `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`, persisted in the `created_at` column. It is used for audit trails, chronological views, and troubleshooting to understand when the fee was first recorded.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the fee charge record was last updated.

This field tracks the most recent modification to the fee charge, including changes to descriptive metadata or any mutable fields allowed by business rules, and is stored in the `updated_at` column. It supports auditability and helps detect late adjustments or corrections.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the fee was soft deleted.

Indicates the point in time when the fee charge was logically removed from active views, while still remaining in the database for historical, audit, and reconciliation purposes. This value is stored in the nullable `deleted_at` column.

Null when the fee charge is active and has not been soft deleted.

In this case the `deleted_at` column remains null and the record participates in normal queries unless excluded explicitly by filters.

deletedAt.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the fee charge.

This mirrors the nullable `deleted_at` column in the Prisma schema and enables logical deletion strategies where records are hidden from normal queries but remain available for compliance and investigation workflows.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new seller fee charge.

This type defines the input payload accepted by the POST /shoppingMall/admin/sellerFeeCharges endpoint when an administrative or financial workflow records a new fee or commission charge against a seller. It exposes only those fields that are settable at creation time, excluding system-managed attributes such as the primary key, creation timestamps, and soft deletion markers.

The DTO allows callers to specify which seller is being charged, optionally link the fee to an order, payment refund, or payout item, and describe the fee’s business category, monetary amounts, and tax breakdown. It is intended for use by privileged admin or automation processes rather than by sellers themselves, and all referenced identifiers must correspond to existing records to preserve financial integrity.

sellerId.description:
Identifier of the seller to whom this fee charge applies.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges.seller_id and must reference an existing seller in shopping_mall_sellers. It is mandatory because every fee charge must be associated with exactly one seller for reconciliation and payout calculations.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the related order causing the fee.

When provided, this value should reference shopping_mall_orders.id and indicates that the fee is tied to a specific customer order, such as a transaction commission or order-related penalty.

Null when the fee is not tied to an individual order.

This is common for subscription fees, platform service charges, advertising packages, or manual adjustments that refer to a billing period or contractual agreement rather than a specific order.

orderId.description:
Optional order identifier associated with the fee charge.

This mirrors the nullable order_id foreign key and allows transaction-based charges to be tracked alongside the orders that generated them, while still supporting non–order-based fees.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of a related payment refund.

When present, this value should reference shopping_mall_payment_refunds.id and indicates that the fee is associated with a particular refund event, such as a refund processing charge or an adjustment due to a dispute outcome.
Null when there is no specific payment refund linked to this fee charge.

paymentRefundId.description:
Optional payment refund identifier.

Use this to tie the fee charge to a specific refund operation when business rules require explicit tracking of refund-related fees for compliance or analytics.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the payout item that will settle or has settled this fee charge.

When specified, this should reference shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.id and is typically provided when recording adjustments that are known to belong to a specific payout item or when backfilling data for historical reconciliation.
Null when the fee charge has not yet been reconciled into a payout item or when reconciliation occurs later via automated processes.

sellerPayoutItemId.description:
Optional payout item identifier used for reconciliation.

This maps to the seller_payout_item_id foreign key and helps downstream payout processing link individual charges to aggregated payout batches for a seller.

feeType.description:
Business category of the fee being created.

The value must match one of the allowed fee category codes understood by the platform, such as transaction_commission, platform_service_fee, subscription_fee, advertising_fee, or adjustment. It drives how the fee is interpreted for revenue recognition, reporting, and reconciliation, so clients should use consistent, documented codes.

oneOf.description:
Descriptive text explaining the rationale for the fee.

This can contain human-readable notes, such as the invoice or billing cycle reference, a manual adjustment reason, promotion details, or internal comments that help admins and finance teams understand the origin of the charge.
Null when no additional descriptive text is necessary beyond the fee type and related identifiers.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description for the fee.

This value is stored in the description column and is useful for backoffice consoles, account statements, and audit exports where a textual explanation of charges improves transparency.

currency.description:
Currency code in which the fee and tax amounts are expressed.
