Typically this is an ISO 4217–style code (for example, "USD", "EUR", or "KRW"). The chosen currency must be compatible with the seller, the underlying order or payment context, and platform configuration so that subsequent payout and reporting processes can operate correctly.

amount.description:
Monetary amount of the fee charge to apply.

Positive values represent charges that the platform applies to the seller, reducing the seller’s net balance. Negative values may be used for credits or fee reversals. Validation logic should ensure amounts conform to business rules, such as non-negative constraints for certain fee types, and apply appropriate rounding rules.

taxAmount.description:
Tax portion of the fee amount.

This value represents the tax component associated with the fee in the same currency as amount. It should be zero when no tax applies. The combination of amount and taxAmount is used by accounting and compliance processes to calculate tax obligations and revenue figures.

isPlatformRevenue.description:
Flag indicating whether this fee represents platform revenue.

When true, the fee is recognized as revenue for the platform, such as commissions, service fees, or subscription charges. When false, the amount is treated as a pass-through or third-party amount that does not contribute to platform revenue, even though it is charged to the seller.

effectiveDate.description:
Business effective date of the fee.

This timestamp specifies when the fee should be considered effective for reporting and revenue recognition, which may align with order completion dates, billing cycles, or other business events rather than the technical time of request submission.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing seller fee charge.

This type defines the payload accepted by the PUT /shoppingMall/admin/sellerFeeCharges/{feeChargeId} endpoint when administrative workflows need to adjust editable aspects of a previously created fee charge. Typical uses include correcting descriptive information, adjusting fee categorization, or fixing linkage to related records before accounting periods are closed.

All fields in this DTO are optional and represent the subset of properties considered mutable according to business rules. System-managed fields such as the primary key, creation timestamp, and soft deletion timestamp are not exposed. The service implementation is responsible for enforcing additional invariants, such as preventing changes to financial amounts once a charge has been settled in a payout or locked accounting period.

sellerId.description:
Updated identifier of the seller for this fee charge.

This field mirrors the seller_id foreign key and allows reassignment of the fee to a different seller if permitted by business rules. Implementations should carefully restrict or audit changes to this field because reassignment affects financial reconciliation and historical statements.

oneOf.description:
Updated order identifier related to the fee.

When set, this value should reference shopping_mall_orders.id and indicates that the fee is associated with a particular order. It may be used to correct a mis-linked order reference shortly after creation.

Explicitly clears the association to any order.

Setting this field to null removes the link to a specific order, which can be useful when a fee is reclassified as non–order-based.

orderId.description:
Optional updated order identifier association.

This field allows adjusting or clearing the order linkage represented by order_id in the underlying table, subject to validation that the new reference is valid and consistent with business rules.

oneOf.description:
Updated payment refund identifier.

When provided, this should reference shopping_mall_payment_refunds.id and indicates that the fee is associated with a specific refund event.
Explicitly clears the association to any payment refund.

paymentRefundId.description:
Optional updated payment refund identifier.

Use this field to correct or remove the linkage to a payment refund when reconciling refund-related fees.

oneOf.description:
Updated payout item identifier that reconciles this fee.

When set, this value should reference shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.id and indicates which payout item settles or will settle the fee charge.

Explicitly clears the association to any payout item.

This can be used when reversing an erroneous linkage so that reconciliation can be reprocessed correctly.

sellerPayoutItemId.description:
Optional updated payout item association.

This field adjusts the reconciliation link between the fee charge and a payout item, mapping to seller_payout_item_id in the database.

feeType.description:
Updated business category of the fee.

Changing this value reclassifies the fee for reporting and analytics, for example from an adjustment to a transaction_commission. Such changes should be carefully controlled, as they affect revenue categorization and historical reports.

oneOf.description:
Updated descriptive text about the fee.

This can refine or correct the explanation of why the fee exists, such as updating an internal note, adding a reference number, or clarifying a manual adjustment reason.
Explicitly clears the descriptive text for this fee charge.

description.description:
Optional updated human-readable description.

Use this field to modify or remove the textual explanation stored in the description column without altering the financial values themselves.

currency.description:
Updated currency code for the fee amounts.

Changes to currency should be rare and may require additional validation and recalculation of amounts. Implementations should enforce strict rules if allowing currency changes, as they impact reporting and reconciliation.

amount.description:
Updated monetary amount of the fee charge.

Modifying this value changes the charge applied to the seller and therefore must be subject to business rules, such as prohibiting changes after settlement or requiring audit trails for manual corrections.

taxAmount.description:
Updated tax portion of the fee amount.

Adjustments to this value affect tax reporting and may be necessary to correct earlier miscalculations or reflect updated tax treatment.

isPlatformRevenue.description:
Updated flag indicating whether the fee is treated as platform revenue.

Toggling this flag changes how the fee is classified in accounting and analytics and should typically be restricted to trusted administrative workflows.

effectiveDate.description:
Updated business effective date of the fee.

Changing this timestamp affects which reporting period the fee is considered part of and may be necessary to realign fees with the correct accounting or billing period after manual review.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.description:
Seller-facing overview dashboard DTO for the ShoppingMall seller portal.

This type provides a consolidated snapshot of key performance indicators, operational workload, payout summaries, and reputation metrics for the authenticated seller. It is an aggregation DTO that composes data derived from multiple Prisma models including shopping_mall_sellers, shopping_mall_seller_profiles, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_seller_earnings, shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats, shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots, and several rating and review related tables.

The purpose of this schema is to support the main seller dashboard screen with a single, efficient response. It intentionally avoids exposing raw transactional rows and instead surfaces curated numeric indicators and small highlight lists that can be rendered directly in UI widgets. Implementations will typically populate this structure via read-only queries and aggregations, always scoped to the authenticated seller identity.

seller.description:
Basic seller account and profile information used in the dashboard header.

This object contains a curated subset of seller identity and profile data derived from shopping_mall_sellers and shopping_mall_seller_profiles, such as store name, status, and email. It is used to label the dashboard and provide quick visibility into the current seller context.

kpis.description:
Top-level numeric KPIs summarizing commercial performance for the seller.

This section aggregates values such as gross and net merchandise value, order counts by time window, and active catalog statistics. The underlying figures are typically calculated from shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_seller_earnings, and snapshot tables like shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats.

orders.description:
Summary information about current order workload and recent order activity.

This section provides counts of open orders by status, as well as small highlight lists such as the most recent orders. The data is computed from shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, and related status history tables and is always filtered to the authenticated seller.

payouts.description:
Summary of seller earnings, payout eligibility, and recent payouts.

This section aggregates data from shopping_mall_seller_earnings and shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches (and related payout items) to show how much has been earned, what is currently eligible for payout, and which payouts were recently completed.

inventoryAlerts.description:
Inventory-related alerts for the seller, such as low-stock or out-of-stock SKUs.

The alerts are derived from catalog and inventory models like shopping_mall_skus, shopping_mall_seller_warehouses, shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments, and related snapshot tables. They help the seller quickly identify SKUs that require restocking or catalog maintenance.

reviews.description:
Aggregated review and rating information for the seller’s catalog.

This section summarizes the seller’s overall rating, rating distribution, and a highlight list of recent reviews. The data is computed from review-centric tables such as shopping_mall_reviews, shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates, and shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates and is used to monitor customer satisfaction.

performance.description:
Operational performance indicators and risk-related KPIs for the seller.

This section surfaces metrics such as order defect rate, refund rate, late shipment rate, and dispute statistics. Values are typically derived from shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots, shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats, and platform-wide KPI snapshot tables, giving sellers and admins a quick view of operational health and potential risk.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.ISe.description:
Compact seller identity and profile summary used in the dashboard header.

This DTO is built from shopping_mall_sellers and shopping_mall_seller_profiles and is intended for display in the seller dashboard banner. It does not expose sensitive authentication fields such as password hashes, and instead focuses on public or semi-public identity attributes.

The summary is read-only from the perspective of the dashboard endpoint; profile mutations are handled by dedicated profile management APIs.

sellerId.description:
Unique identifier of the seller account.

This value maps to shopping_mall_sellers.id and is used internally when navigating to more detailed seller-specific endpoints. It is exposed here only for client-side routing or linking within the seller portal and not for cross-tenant access.

storeName.description:
Public store name presented to buyers and shown in the seller dashboard header.

This value is derived from shopping_mall_seller_profiles.store_name and represents the primary brand or storefront label for the seller within the marketplace.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the seller account.

Typical values mirror shopping_mall_sellers.status, such as pending_review, active, suspended, or terminated. Clients use this to reflect whether certain features may be restricted or pending approval.

email.description:
Primary business contact email address for the seller.

This value generally reflects shopping_mall_sellers.email and is used for login and communication. It is included in the dashboard summary so that sellers can quickly confirm which account is currently active.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IKp.description:
Top-level KPI summary for the ShoppingMall seller dashboard.

This DTO concentrates key commercial and catalog metrics that are commonly displayed in the first row of dashboard widgets, giving sellers a fast overview of recent performance. The metrics are derived from multiple underlying tables but surfaced as simple numeric values in this schema.

Typical calculations include rolling time-window sales and counts, such as today, the last 7 days, and the last 30 days, as well as catalog counts. Implementations may extend or refine calculations while keeping the public shape of this DTO stable.

totalSalesToday.description:
Total gross merchandise value (GMV) for this seller for the current day.

The value is computed from orders and earnings that relate to the current calendar day in the order currency or platform base currency, depending on implementation. It is intended for quick monitoring of same-day sales performance.

totalSalesLast7Days.description:
Aggregated GMV for this seller over the last 7 full days.

This metric is derived from shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, or shopping_mall_seller_earnings over the past week and helps sellers compare short-term performance trends.

totalSalesLast30Days.description:
Aggregated GMV for this seller over the last 30 full days.

The metric summarizes medium-term sales performance and can be used to understand broader trends beyond the last week.

openOrderCount.description:
Number of currently open orders for this seller across relevant business statuses.

Open orders typically include statuses such as awaiting_payment, payment_confirmed, preparing_shipment, and shipped (but not yet delivered or cancelled). The exact status mapping is controlled by business rules and may be implemented using shopping_mall_orders.current_status.

completedOrderCountLast30Days.description:
Count of orders completed (for example delivered) in the last 30 days for this seller.

This metric indicates fulfillment throughput and recent demand and is usually computed using order status histories or snapshot tables filtered for terminal success states.

activeSkuCount.description:
Number of SKUs currently active and sellable in the seller’s catalog.

This value is derived from catalog tables such as shopping_mall_skus, filtered by visibility and inventory rules. It helps sellers understand the breadth of their active offering at a glance.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IOr.description:
Operational order summary for the ShoppingMall seller dashboard.

This section groups metrics that describe the seller’s current order workload and very recent order activity. It provides counts of orders by critical statuses as well as a compact list of recent orders that can be used for quick drill-down from the dashboard.

Data is populated from shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_items, and related status history tables, and is always scoped to the authenticated seller to preserve tenant isolation.

openOrdersByStatus.description:
List of counts of open orders grouped by business status.

The statuses correspond to shopping_mall_orders.current_status or a mapped set of canonical statuses. This list drives status-specific widgets such as "Awaiting shipment" or "Pending payment".

recentOrders.description:
Small highlight list of the most recent orders visible to the seller.

The list is typically limited to a small fixed number (for example 5–10 orders) to keep the payload light while providing actionable context.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IOr.description:
Aggregated count of seller orders for a specific business status.

This DTO is used in the seller dashboard to render widgets or badges for open orders grouped by status, such as awaiting_payment, payment_confirmed, preparing_shipment, shipped, or delivered.

Values are computed from shopping_mall_orders.current_status and limited to records owned by the authenticated seller.

status.description:
Business status identifier for this bucket of orders.

Typical values mirror shopping_mall_orders.current_status such as awaiting_payment, payment_confirmed, preparing_shipment, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded. Consumers use this to label status-specific widgets.

count.description:
Number of orders for the seller that currently match the given status.

The count is computed from shopping_mall_orders records scoped to the seller and may be further filtered by recent time windows depending on the dashboard design.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IRe.description:
Compact representation of a recent seller order for dashboard display.

This DTO is intentionally small and is used to populate a widget that lists the latest orders for the authenticated seller. It includes only those fields needed to identify and quickly understand the order without loading the full order detail payload.

The values are sourced from shopping_mall_orders and minimal derived calculations over shopping_mall_order_items.

orderId.description:
Unique identifier of the order.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_orders.id and can be used by clients to navigate to a detailed order view using appropriate order detail APIs.

orderCode.description:
Business-facing order code presented to the customer and seller.

This maps to shopping_mall_orders.order_code and is often used as the primary human-readable reference for the order on the seller dashboard.

placedAt.description:
Timestamp when the order was confirmed by the customer.

The value reflects shopping_mall_orders.placed_at and is used to sort and display recent orders in recency order.

currentStatus.description:
Current high-level business status of the order.

This is based on shopping_mall_orders.current_status and indicates whether the order is awaiting payment, being prepared, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.

grandTotalAmount.description:
Total payable amount for the order in the order currency.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_orders.grand_total_amount and includes items, discounts, shipping fees, and applicable taxes.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IPa.description:
Summary of seller earnings and payout status for the ShoppingMall dashboard.

This section aggregates data from financial tables such as shopping_mall_seller_earnings and shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches to show how much the seller has earned, what is currently eligible for payout, and what has already been paid.

The data is read-only from the dashboard perspective and is intended to power simple widgets such as "Pending payouts" and "Last payout".

totalNetEarnings.description:
Total net earnings accrued by the seller over the selected reporting horizon.

This amount aggregates shopping_mall_seller_earnings.net_earning_amount for records owned by the seller and within the reporting window defined by backend business rules (for example year-to-date or lifetime).

pendingPayoutAmount.description:
Total amount of seller earnings that are currently eligible for payout but not yet paid.

This is derived from shopping_mall_seller_earnings rows in an eligible-but-unpaid state and may exclude earnings still within refund or dispute windows.

lastPayoutAmount.description:
Net amount of the most recently completed payout to the seller.

The value reflects data from shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches and associated payout items for this seller, representing the last settled payout transferred to the seller.

lastPayoutDate.description:
Timestamp when the most recent payout to the seller was completed.

This value corresponds to a completion timestamp recorded on shopping_mall_seller_payout_batches or related payout entities and is used for payout history awareness on the dashboard.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IIn.description:
Inventory-focused alert section for the seller dashboard.

This DTO contains compact information about SKUs that require inventory attention, such as low-stock or out-of-stock conditions. The data is computed from catalog and inventory entities including shopping_mall_skus, shopping_mall_seller_warehouses, and shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments.

It is designed to drive alert widgets that prompt the seller to restock or adjust catalog visibility before items become unavailable to buyers.

lowStockSkuCount.description:
Number of SKUs for this seller that are currently considered low-stock.

The threshold for "low-stock" is defined by business rules or configuration and typically depends on remaining quantity and expected sales velocity.

outOfStockSkuCount.description:
Number of SKUs for this seller that are completely out of stock.

Out-of-stock SKUs may be temporarily hidden from catalog views or flagged prominently to encourage replenishment.

items.description: Compact SKU summary for inventory alert highlighting in the seller dashboard.

highlightSkus.description:
Small list of SKUs under inventory alert that should be highlighted to the seller.

The list size is intentionally small to keep the payload light and to emphasize the most urgent SKUs based on thresholds or ranking rules.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IIn.description:
Compact SKU summary used in the seller dashboard inventory alert section.

This type represents SKUs that have crossed low-stock or out-of-stock thresholds and therefore require attention. It includes only those fields necessary for identification and quick decision-making in the dashboard context.

The underlying data is pulled from shopping_mall_skus, seller warehouse inventory tables, and adjustment logs but is presented here as a simple view object.

skuId.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU under alert.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_skus.id and is used for navigation to SKU management pages or detailed inventory views.

skuCode.description:
Business-facing SKU code or external identifier.

This field typically maps to a SKU code or external ID stored on shopping_mall_skus or shopping_mall_sku_external_ids and is included for quick reference.

productName.description:
Name of the product to which this SKU belongs.

The value is a snapshot or denormalized reference to the product name at the time of the alert and helps sellers quickly recognize the item without additional catalog lookups.

currentStockQuantity.description:
Current available stock quantity for this SKU across relevant seller warehouses.

The figure is computed by aggregating inventory levels and subtracting reserved quantities, giving a real-time or near-real-time view of availability.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IRe.description:
Review and rating summary section for the ShoppingMall seller dashboard.

This DTO surfaces key reputation metrics such as average rating, total review count, and distribution by rating score, together with a short list of recent reviews. The data is derived from review and rating tables including shopping_mall_reviews, shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates, and shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates.

The section is intended to give sellers a quick understanding of how customers perceive their products without requiring them to navigate away from the dashboard.

averageRating.description:
Average product rating for the seller’s catalog over the current analysis window.

This value is computed from visible reviews and rating aggregates and generally falls into a bounded scale such as 1.0 to 5.0. It is used to display overall seller reputation.

reviewCount.description:
Total number of published reviews that contribute to the average rating.

The count is useful to distinguish between a well-established rating and a rating based on a small number of reviews.

ratingDistribution.description:
Distribution of review counts by rating score.

This list is used to render charts or histograms that show how many reviews are 1-star, 2-star, and so on, helping sellers evaluate customer sentiment dispersion.

recentReviews.description:
Small list of the most recent reviews impacting the seller’s rating.

The list is limited to a small number of items (for example 3–5 reviews) to keep the payload manageable while still providing actionable context.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IRa.description:
Review count bucket for a specific rating score in the seller dashboard.

This DTO is used to represent the number of reviews that share the same rating value, supporting histogram visualizations on the seller dashboard.

The underlying data is calculated from review and rating aggregate tables tied to products and SKUs owned by the seller.

rating.description:
Rating score for this bucket.

The value typically lies within the configured rating scale (for example integer values between 1 and 5) and is used as the bucket label.

count.description:
Number of reviews that have the given rating score.

This count is derived from shopping_mall_reviews or aggregate tables and is scoped to reviews on products owned by the authenticated seller.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IRe.description:
Compact DTO representing a recent review relevant to the seller.

This type is used in the dashboard to show a small list of the most recent reviews affecting the seller’s rating. It includes only the essential fields needed to understand the review at a glance, while detailed review content remains available through dedicated review APIs.

Data is populated from shopping_mall_reviews and associated product or SKU metadata.

reviewId.description:
Unique identifier of the review.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_reviews.id and can be used to navigate to a detailed review view or moderation tools.

productName.description:
Name of the product that this review is associated with.

The value is typically a snapshot of the product title at review time and helps sellers identify which product received the feedback.

rating.description:
Rating score given by the customer in this review.

The integer is usually within the platform’s rating scale (for example 1–5) and is used as a primary visual indicator of sentiment.

excerpt.description:
Short excerpt of the review content suitable for display in a dashboard list.

Implementations usually truncate the original review text to a safe length while preserving the main message, ensuring the dashboard stays uncluttered.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the review was created.

This value allows the dashboard to sort and label recent reviews, giving context about when the feedback was posted.

IShoppingMallSellerOverviewDashboard.IPe.description:
Operational performance and risk indicator section for the seller dashboard.

This DTO aggregates metrics from analytics and risk-related tables such as shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots, shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats, and refund or dispute statistics tables. It surfaces key ratios that the platform uses to evaluate seller performance and compliance.

The section is mainly informational for the seller but can also be used by admins to communicate performance expectations and thresholds.

orderDefectRate.description:
Order defect rate for the seller over the current analysis window.

The rate is a fraction between 0 and 1 reflecting the proportion of orders with serious issues such as defects, claims, or escalations, based on platform-defined criteria.

refundRate.description:
Refund rate for the seller during the configured analysis period.

This metric is a fraction between 0 and 1 indicating what share of the seller’s orders result in refunds, helping identify potential product quality or expectation issues.

cancellationRate.description:
Cancellation rate for the seller in the analysis period.

The rate is a fraction between 0 and 1 reflecting the share of orders that are cancelled before completion, whether initiated by customers, sellers, or the platform.

lateShipmentRate.description:
Rate of shipments that were dispatched or delivered later than the defined SLA.

This value, between 0 and 1, highlights potential fulfillment or logistics issues and is computed from shipment and SLA tracking data.

disputeOpenCount.description:
Number of currently open disputes involving the seller.

This count is derived from dispute-related tables and shows how many active conflict cases are in progress for the seller.

tier.description:
Optional classification tier assigned to the seller based on performance.

Typical values may include labels such as new, standard, premium, or high_risk, reflecting business rules that classify overall seller health. In some implementations, this may be an empty string when no tier applies.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for seller fee and commission analytics queries in the ShoppingMall platform.

This type is used as the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/seller/analytics/sellerFees endpoint. It allows authenticated sellers to specify time windows, fee categories, and other filters, along with pagination and aggregation preferences, in order to retrieve summarized fee and commission information derived from tables such as shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges and shopping_mall_seller_earnings.

The DTO is read-only from the perspective of business data: it does not create or modify any fee records. Instead, it expresses query parameters that control how existing fee charges and earning rows are grouped, filtered, and paginated. The seller identity is taken from the authenticated context, so no seller ID or account ID fields appear in this schema.

startDate.description:
Inclusive start of the analysis window for fee and commission calculations.

When present, the backend restricts fee and earning records to those whose effective_date or related business date is greater than or equal to this value. If omitted, implementations typically use a default window such as the last 30 days.

endDate.description:
Exclusive end of the analysis window for fee and commission calculations.

When provided, only fee and earning records with effective_date earlier than this timestamp are considered. If omitted, the current time or a default offset from startDate is usually applied.

items.description:
A specific fee_type value to include in the analytics query.

Values correspond to shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges.fee_type, such as transaction_commission, platform_service_fee, subscription_fee, advertising_fee, or adjustment. The backend treats the list as an inclusion filter; when empty or omitted, all fee types are considered.

feeTypes.description:
Optional list of fee categories to include in the analysis.

If provided, the analytics engine restricts calculations to fee charges whose fee_type matches one of the specified values. If omitted, all available fee types for the seller are considered.

minAmount.description:
Optional minimum absolute fee amount used as a filter.

When present, only fee or commission records whose absolute amount is greater than or equal to this threshold are included in the aggregation. This can be used to ignore trivial fees in analytical views.

maxAmount.description:
Optional maximum absolute fee amount used as a filter.

When provided, fee or commission records whose absolute amount exceeds this value may be excluded from the analysis, which is useful for focusing on typical fees and excluding extreme adjustments.

groupBy.description:
Primary aggregation dimension for the fee analytics query.

Common values include day (aggregate by calendar date), fee_type (aggregate per fee category), and order (aggregate per order). The backend must validate the supplied value against allowed grouping modes and default to a sensible option when absent.

page.description:
Page index for paginated analytical results.

This is a 1-based page number used together with pageSize to control which slice of the aggregated results is returned. When omitted, implementations typically default to the first page.

pageSize.description:
Number of aggregated records to return per page.

This controls the size of the data array in the paginated response IPageIShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.ISummary. Backend implementations should enforce sensible upper bounds to protect performance.

sortBy.description:
Field name used for sorting aggregated analytics rows.

Common options include totalAmount, totalCount, or a date field depending on the chosen groupBy. The backend should validate the requested sortBy against a whitelist of supported sort keys.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the aggregated result set.

Allowed values typically include asc for ascending and desc for descending order. If omitted, implementations usually default to descending order for monetary totals or descending chronological order for date-based groupings.

IAnalyticsDateRange.description:
Generic analytics date range model used by multiple analytics request DTOs.

This type expresses a closed or half-open time interval by specifying inclusive start and end timestamps. Analytics queries use this range to bound the time window for fact records such as subscriptions or inventory adjustments.

When either `from` or `to` is omitted, the analytics engine infers an open-ended bound according to product defaults, for example infinite past or present time.

from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the analytics time window.

Represents the earliest timestamp (in ISO 8601 date-time format) that should be considered when selecting underlying fact rows.

If omitted, the backend may apply a default minimum such as a fixed platform start date or relative interval (e.g., 90 days ago).

to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the analytics time window.

Represents the latest timestamp (in ISO 8601 date-time format) that should be included when filtering underlying fact rows.

If omitted, the backend typically interprets this as "up to now" at query execution time.

IAnalyticsPagination.description:
Generic pagination configuration used by analytics request DTOs.

This model defines how analytics endpoints limit the number of aggregated rows returned per call and how clients request specific pages of results.

It supports both classic page/size pagination and cursor-based continuation via an opaque cursor string, enabling scalable traversal of large result sets.

page.description:
1-based page index used for classic offset pagination.

When both `page` and `size` are provided and `cursor` is not set, the analytics engine computes an offset from `(page - 1) * size` and returns the requested slice.

If omitted in favor of `cursor`, the backend switches to cursor-based pagination semantics.

size.description:
Maximum number of analytics rows to return in a single page.

This value should remain within server-enforced limits to prevent excessively large responses. Typical limits range between 50 and 1000 rows depending on environment.

When omitted, the backend applies a default page size.

cursor.description:
Opaque continuation token representing the current position within the analytics result set.

When provided, the analytics engine ignores `page` and uses the cursor to fetch the next page of results. Callers should treat the token as an implementation detail and not attempt to parse or construct it manually.

IAnalyticsSort.description:
Sort directive for analytics result sets.

Each instance describes the logical field used for sorting and the direction in which the field should be ordered. The field typically corresponds to a grouping dimension key (such as period or seller) or a particular metric (such as net quantity change).

Multiple directives can be combined in an ordered list to define compound ordering conditions, where earlier entries have higher precedence than later ones.

field.description:
Logical analytics field key to sort by.

This may reference a grouping dimension, such as `period`, `plan`, `seller`, `warehouse`, or `reason`, or a metric such as `new_subscriptions`, `net_quantity_change`, or `event_count`.

If the field name is not recognized by the analytics engine for the current query, the request should be rejected with a validation error.

direction.description:
Sort direction for the given field.

Supported directions typically include `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. The analytics layer must treat values case-sensitively or normalize them according to implementation rules.

When omitted, the backend may default to ascending order per field.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.description:
Administrative role definition entity for the shopping mall RBAC system.

This type maps directly to the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model and represents a single administrative role record that can be assigned to one or more admin accounts. Each role defines a stable machine-readable code, a human-readable name, and optional descriptive metadata explaining the role’s scope and responsibilities within the platform’s governance model.

The role entity also carries system-level flags and lifecycle timestamps, including whether the role is system-protected, when it was created, when it was last updated, and an optional soft-deletion timestamp. These fields are important for auditing, compliance, and safe evolution of the RBAC configuration over time.

id.description:
Primary key identifier of the administrative role record.

This value is generated by the database layer when a new record is created and uniquely identifies the role across the entire platform. It is used internally for joins and references but is also safe to expose in API responses for debugging, tooling, or administrative UIs.

code.description:
Stable, unique machine-oriented code for the role.

This value corresponds to the `code` column of the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table and is constrained to be globally unique. Typical examples include values such as `"super_admin"`, `"operations_admin"`, or `"risk_reviewer"`.

Application logic and configuration use this field as a stable identifier when attaching permissions, building policy rules, or performing RBAC checks, so it should remain immutable after creation.

name.description:
Human-readable display name for the administrative role.

This value is shown in administrative UIs, audit tools, and configuration dashboards to help operators understand which role they are working with. It should be concise but descriptive enough to differentiate it from other roles with similar purposes.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of the role’s purpose and scope.

This field mirrors the nullable `description` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` schema. It can be used to document which kinds of administrators should receive this role, what permissions it implies, and any risk or governance considerations.

When null, no additional descriptive text has been provided for this role.

is_system.description:
System-protected role indicator.

This boolean flag corresponds to the non-nullable `is_system` column and indicates whether the role is reserved for system-level or platform-internal use.

When `true`, the role is typically not editable or deletable via standard admin tools, and only platform-level migrations or governance processes should modify it. When `false`, higher-privileged admins may be allowed to change or remove the role, subject to business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this role was created.

This non-nullable field records the exact moment the role record was first inserted into the database, using an ISO 8601 date-time representation. It is used for auditing, historical reporting, and governance workflows that depend on the age of RBAC configurations.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this role was last updated.

This non-nullable field is automatically updated whenever mutable fields on the role record change. It supports audit trails, change tracking, and tooling that needs to identify stale configuration that may require review.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the role record.

This nullable field is set when the role has been logically removed from active use but must remain in the database for historical or compliance reasons. When non-null, the role should no longer be assignable to new admin accounts, and application logic should treat it as inactive.

When null, the role is considered active or at least not soft-deleted from a data lifecycle perspective.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for listing administrative roles.

This DTO is used by the `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/adminRoles` endpoint as the request body type. It encapsulates filter conditions, pagination controls, and sort options for searching the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table in a structured way.

Admin consoles and other governance tools send instances of this type to retrieve a paginated list of roles that match specific codes, names, system flags, and creation or update date ranges, while also controlling result size and ordering.

page.description:
One-based index of the page of results to retrieve.

This value controls which slice of the overall result set should be returned by the admin-role listing endpoint. Page numbering starts at 1, and values less than 1 should be rejected by validation.

If omitted, the implementation should apply a sensible default such as `1` to return the first page of results.

limit.description:
Maximum number of admin role records to return in a single page.

This property is used together with `page` to implement server-side pagination for role listings. It should be subject to an upper bound in the service layer to prevent excessively large result sets.

Typical values might range from 10 to 100 depending on UI requirements and performance characteristics.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to role code or name.

When provided, this string can be used to perform partial matching against the `code` and `name` columns of the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table. This allows operators to quickly locate roles by entering a fragment of their identifier or label.

When null or omitted, no free-text search filter is applied and roles are selected solely by other filter fields.

code.description:
Exact match filter for the admin role code.

This property corresponds to the unique `code` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` model. When set, the search should restrict results to the role whose code exactly matches this value.

It is particularly useful when tooling already knows the precise code and wants to fetch only that role through the list endpoint instead of using the dedicated detail endpoint.

name.description:
Optional filter on the human-readable role name.

This field can be used for exact or partial matching on the `name` column of the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table, depending on the implementation. It enables operators to narrow results when they know part or all of the displayed role name.

When null or omitted, this filter does not constrain the result set.

is_system.description:
Filter flag for system-protected roles.

When set to `true`, the search should return only roles where the underlying `is_system` column is true, helping operators focus on system-protected RBAC definitions. When set to `false`, only non-system roles should be returned.

When null or omitted, both system and non-system roles may be included in the results based on other filters.

created_from.description:
Lower bound for the role creation timestamp filter.

This property represents the earliest `created_at` value (inclusive) that a role must have to be included in the search results. It allows UIs to implement date-range filtering on the time when roles were created.

When null or omitted, no lower bound on creation time is applied.

created_to.description:
Upper bound for the role creation timestamp filter.

This field specifies the latest `created_at` value (inclusive) that a role may have for it to appear in the search results. Together with `created_from`, it forms a date range filter on role creation time.

When null or omitted, no upper bound on creation time is enforced.

order_by.description:
Sort key for ordering admin role search results.

Typical values include column names such as `code`, `name`, or `created_at`, which the service layer maps to corresponding Prisma orderBy expressions for the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table.

When null or omitted, a default sort order such as `created_at DESC` or `code ASC` should be applied, as defined by business requirements.

order_direction.description:
Direction for sorting admin role results.

Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order, which are interpreted by the underlying query when combined with `order_by`. The field is optional to allow the server to apply default ordering when not specified.

Validation should restrict this property to allowed tokens and treat null as a signal to use default sort direction.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new administrative role definition in the shopping mall RBAC system.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model and contains all business-level fields that an authorized admin must provide when defining a new role, such as the unique role code, display name, and optional descriptive text. It intentionally omits system-managed fields like the primary key and timestamps, which are populated by the backend or database.

Create operations using this type are typically restricted to high-privilege admin actors because new roles directly affect platform governance and access control. The values supplied here must respect uniqueness constraints on the `code` column and adhere to any length or validation rules enforced at the database or application layer.

code.description:
Stable, globally unique machine-oriented code for the administrative role.

This corresponds to the non-nullable and uniquely indexed `code` column of the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table. Examples include values such as `"super_admin"`, `"operations_admin"`, or `"risk_reviewer"`.

Once created, this code is treated as an immutable business identifier and is used throughout RBAC configuration, permission checks, and governance tooling.

name.description:
Human-readable display name for the administrative role.

This field is required when creating a role and is used in administrative UIs and audit logs to clearly describe the role’s purpose. It should be concise but descriptive enough for operators to distinguish it from other roles.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of the role’s scope, responsibilities, and intended audience.

This field maps to the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. When provided, it should explain how and when the role should be used, any associated risk level, and any special governance considerations.

When omitted or set to null, the role will not carry additional free-form documentation beyond its code and name.

is_system.description:
Indicates whether the created role is a system-protected role.

This value populates the non-nullable `is_system` column. When set to `true`, the role is generally reserved for platform-level or internal use and may be locked against modification or deletion by regular admins. When `false`, higher-privilege admins may be able to manage the role more freely, subject to business rules.

API consumers should typically create non-system roles (`false`) for normal operational use and leave system roles to be defined by controlled deployment or migration processes.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.IUpdate.description:
Request payload for updating an existing administrative role definition identified by its unique role code.

This DTO is mapped to the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model, whose key columns include `id`, `code`, `name`, `description`, `is_system`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`. Among these, only the human-facing and configuration-oriented fields `name`, `description`, and `is_system` are exposed as mutable through this update type.

Immutable fields such as the primary key `id`, the business role code `code`, and the lifecycle timestamps `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally excluded from the DTO. The target record is instead selected via the `{adminRoleCode}` path parameter of the operation, and the backend is responsible for maintaining timestamp fields and identifiers.

All properties in this type are optional so that callers can perform partial updates. When a property is omitted from the payload, the existing value in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` row is preserved. When a property is present, the backend applies validation based on the underlying Prisma schema (for example, string length limits or uniqueness constraints) and then updates only those fields. Business rules should ensure that updates respect uniqueness constraints and do not violate governance policies around system-protected roles.

name.description:
New human-readable display name for the administrative role.

When provided, this value replaces the current `name` stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table. It should remain descriptive and unambiguous so that administrators can clearly recognize the role’s purpose in UIs and audit trails.

If this property is omitted from the request body, the existing `name` value in the database is left unchanged.

description.description:
Updated descriptive text for the role’s purpose and scope.

If a non-null string is provided, it overwrites the existing `description` value in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` with the new documentation. This allows governance and risk teams to clarify the intended usage, permissions, and audience for the role.

If explicitly set to null, any existing description will be cleared, and the corresponding database column will be set to `NULL`. When omitted, the current description remains unchanged, preserving the existing explanation for the role.

is_system.description:
Updated system-protected flag for the role.

When present, this flag updates the `is_system` column of the target `shopping_mall_admin_roles` record. Changing this from `false` to `true` or vice versa can have significant governance implications, so the service layer should enforce appropriate permissions and validations before applying the change.

If omitted, the system flag remains as currently stored, and the platform continues to treat the role according to its existing `is_system` setting.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.IReques.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating admin role assignment records.

This schema models the rich search criteria used by administrative tools to query `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`, which link admin accounts (`shopping_mall_admins`) to admin roles (`shopping_mall_admin_roles`). Its fields act as filters and pagination controls rather than a 1:1 representation of a single database row.

Although it carries `x-autobe-prisma-schema: "shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments"` to indicate the primary table being queried, this type does not correspond to a concrete entity instance. Instead, it drives Prisma `where` and `orderBy` clauses over key columns such as `shopping_mall_admin_id`, the role reference (`shopping_mall_admin_role_id`, typically resolved via `role_code`), `granted_by_admin_id`, `created_at`, and `deleted_at`. It is used by search endpoints such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/adminRoleAssignments` and `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}/assignments` to retrieve pages of `IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.ISummary` records for governance dashboards and audit views.

page.description:
Zero-based page index to retrieve when paginating through admin role assignment records.

Clients use this together with `limit` to navigate through large result sets. A value of `0` refers to the first page, and negative values are not allowed. When omitted by higher-level abstractions, the backend may apply a sensible default such as `0` to start at the beginning of the result set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of admin role assignment summaries to return in a single page.

Used in conjunction with `page` to implement offset-based pagination over `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`. The backend should enforce an upper bound (for example, 50 or 100 records per page) to protect performance even if a larger value is supplied by the client. Values less than `1` are rejected so that each page, when available, returns at least one record.

admin_id.description:
Filter assigning admin account by its primary key in `shopping_mall_admins.id`.

When supplied, the search will only return assignment records whose `shopping_mall_admin_id` equals this value, effectively listing all roles currently or historically associated with a specific admin account.

role_code.description:
Optional filter on the business role code from `shopping_mall_admin_roles.code`.

When this field is provided in addition to or instead of a path parameter, the backend resolves the corresponding role or roles and constrains the search to assignments linked to those roles. This is primarily used by the global index endpoint `/shoppingMall/admin/adminRoleAssignments` where the role context is not fixed in the URL.

granted_by_admin_id.description:
Filter assigning admin records by the admin who granted the role.

Maps logically to the `granted_by_admin_id` column on `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`. When specified, only assignments created by the given admin are included, supporting governance views such as "roles granted by a particular operator".

created_from.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range filter for assignment records.

Only assignments whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this instant are included in results. The timestamp must be supplied in ISO 8601 `date-time` format with timezone information, and it is typically used together with `created_to` to bound the search window.

created_to.description:
End of the creation timestamp range filter for assignment records.

Only assignments whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this instant are included in results. The timestamp must be supplied in ISO 8601 `date-time` format with timezone information and should be greater than or equal to `created_from` when both are provided, so that the time window is well-defined.

include_deleted.description:
Flag indicating whether logically deleted (revoked) admin role assignments should be included in search results.

When `false` or omitted, the backend typically excludes rows with a non-null `deleted_at` value to show only current assignments. When `true`, both active and logically deleted assignments are eligible to appear, supporting historical audit and governance use cases where revoked assignments must remain visible.

sort_by.description:
Field name used to sort assignment results within each page.

Typical supported values include `"created_at"` or `"updated_at"` so that records can be ordered by recency. The backend validates this value against an internal allowlist of sortable fields and will reject unsupported values rather than silently ignoring them. When omitted, the service usually defaults to sorting by `created_at` in descending order so that the newest assignments appear first.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordered assignment results.

Accepts only `"asc"` for ascending order or `"desc"` for descending order applied to the chosen `sort_by` field. When omitted, most implementations default to `"desc"` to show the most recent assignments first. Any other value is considered invalid and should result in a validation error rather than falling back to a default.

Sort direction for ordered assignment results.

Accepts only `"asc"` for ascending order or `"desc"` for descending order applied to the chosen `sort_by` field. When omitted, most implementations default to `"desc"` to show the most recent assignments first. Any other value is considered invalid and should result in a validation error rather than falling back to a default.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for ordered assignment results.

Accepts only `"asc"` for ascending order or `"desc"` for descending order applied to the chosen `sort_by` field. When omitted, most implementations default to `"desc"` to show the most recent assignments first. Any other value is considered invalid and should result in a validation error rather than falling back to a default.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new admin role assignment.

This schema represents the mutable fields required to insert a new record into `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`, which links an admin account from `shopping_mall_admins` to a role from `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. It is used by administrative tooling to grant roles to admins under the context of a specific role identified by its business `code` in the request path.

System‑managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally omitted because they are generated and maintained by the backend. The role itself is identified by the `{adminRoleCode}` path parameter of endpoints like `POST /shoppingMall/admin/adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}/assignments`, so this DTO does not contain a role id or code field. It focuses solely on specifying the target admin and optional governance metadata such as human‑readable reasons for the assignment.

admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin account that will receive the role assignment.

At the database level this value is mapped directly into the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key column, which points to `shopping_mall_admins.id`. Together with the role resolved from the `{adminRoleCode}` path parameter (used to populate `shopping_mall_admin_role_id`), it uniquely identifies the admin–role pair for the new assignment.

The backend must validate that the referenced admin exists and is eligible for role assignment before creating the record, and should enforce any governance rules that restrict which admins may receive which roles.

reason.description:
Optional human‑readable justification or comment describing why this role is being granted to the admin.

Conceptually maps to the nullable `reason` column on `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`. Governance and risk teams use this note to understand the context behind permission changes during audits and reviews. When omitted or left empty, the assignment is still valid, but downstream audit tooling may have less context for explaining the change.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.description:
Admin role assignment entity linking an administrator account to a specific administrative role within the shoppingMall platform.

This model represents the many-to-many join between shopping_mall_admins and shopping_mall_admin_roles and captures when and why a given role was granted to a particular admin. Each record is a security-sensitive RBAC configuration artifact and is typically created and managed only by privileged administrative tooling.

The entity also carries lifecycle metadata such as creation, update, and optional soft-deletion timestamps to support auditability and governance analysis over time. In this base DTO, relationships to the admin and role are intentionally modeled as raw foreign key identifiers that mirror the underlying Prisma model exactly; higher-level association views that embed admin or role summary objects should be provided by separate summary or invert DTOs layered on top of this core representation, rather than by extending this schema directly.

id.description:
Primary identifier of the admin role assignment record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments table and is generated by the system when a new assignment is created. Clients receive this identifier in responses and use it in path parameters for read or update operations.

The identifier is immutable for the lifetime of the record and is used as the stable reference in audit logs and cross-entity relations.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin account that receives the role assignment.

This value maps directly to shopping_mall_admins.id and indicates which administrator user is being granted the role represented by this assignment. It is part of the logical many-to-many relationship between admins and roles.

The raw foreign key is intentionally exposed in this base DTO for low-level correlation and bulk tooling; UI layers that require human-readable admin information can resolve this identifier to an appropriate admin summary DTO.

shopping_mall_admin_role_id.description:
Identifier of the administrative role granted to the admin by this assignment.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_admin_roles.id and, together with shopping_mall_admin_id, uniquely identifies the role membership for the admin according to the unique index defined on the assignments table.

The raw foreign key is preserved to match the Prisma schema exactly; higher-level clients can join this identifier to an admin role summary view when they need to display role code, name, or permission groupings alongside the assignment.

reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation for why this role was granted to the admin.

This field stores free-form text that can describe the business justification, ticket reference, or approval context behind the assignment. It is nullable so that automated or legacy assignments can omit a reason when none is provided.

Governance and audit tools can display this field to help reviewers understand the rationale behind the admin's permissions and to support compliance reviews.

granted_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who granted this role assignment, when applicable.

When a human administrator explicitly grants the role, this field should contain the shopping_mall_admins.id of the granting admin, allowing later correlation with activity logs and approvals. For system-generated or migrated assignments where a clear granting actor does not exist, this field may be null.

This value is treated as historical metadata and is not typically changed after creation. It supports auditability and helps detect self-escalation or unauthorized changes when combined with other security event data.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin role assignment record was created.

The value is stored as a DateTime in the shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments table and reflects the moment the assignment became effective from a data perspective. It is managed exclusively by the backend and is never supplied or modified by clients.

Audit and reporting features use this timestamp to reconstruct the timeline of permission changes and to evaluate compliance with governance policies over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin role assignment record was last updated.

This field is automatically maintained by the backend whenever mutable fields such as reason or policy-related attributes are changed. It allows operators to distinguish newly created assignments from those that have been modified since initial grant.

The value is read-only from the client perspective and is important for troubleshooting and audit trails where the evolution of an assignment must be understood.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when this assignment was revoked or logically removed.

When null, the assignment is considered active and should be taken into account by RBAC evaluation logic. When populated, the record is treated as logically deleted or revoked, allowing historical analysis while excluding the assignment from current permission calculations.

Business rules, administrative UIs, and reporting modules can use this field to separate active assignments from historical ones and to trace when permission changes occurred.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields for updating an existing admin role assignment in the shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments table.

This DTO is used by administrative tooling to modify assignment metadata, such as the justification reason or the granting admin reference, without altering immutable identifiers or core foreign keys. It aligns with the Prisma model while excluding fields that should not be changed after creation, such as the primary key and the admin and role identifiers.

All properties are optional so that clients can submit partial updates. System-managed timestamps like created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are not directly writable by clients; instead, they are maintained by the backend as part of the update workflow or separate revocation processes.

reason.description:
Updated human-readable explanation for why this role is or was granted to the admin.

Clients can use this field to correct or refine the business justification, add references to tickets, or document policy changes. Passing null explicitly can clear an existing reason when business rules permit such removal.

If omitted from the update payload, the current value stored in the database remains unchanged.

granted_by_admin_id.description:
Updated identifier of the admin who is considered to have granted this assignment.

This field may be changed when responsibility or attribution needs to be corrected, for example after reassigning ownership of an approval or adjusting migrated data. A null value can be used to indicate that the granting actor is unknown or system-generated.

When this property is omitted in the request, the existing granting admin reference is preserved.

IShoppingMallAdminPermission.description:
Full administrative permission entity as stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_permissions` table.

Instances of this schema represent individual RBAC permissions that can be attached to roles or evaluated directly by authorization logic. Each permission has a globally unique machine‑oriented code, human‑readable metadata, and lifecycle timestamps.

This DTO is typically returned from creation and read operations, and may be embedded into other admin‑facing responses when showing role configurations or policy details.

id.description:
Primary key of the admin permission record.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.id` and uniquely identifies the permission row in the database.

It is generated by the system on creation and must not be supplied or changed by clients.

code.description:
Stable, globally unique machine-oriented code for the permission.

This field is persisted as `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.code` and is used by RBAC evaluation, configuration, and policy mapping.

Once in use, the code should remain stable to avoid breaking existing role configurations and policy references.

name.description:
Human‑readable display name of the permission.

Stored in `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.name`, this value is shown in admin UIs wherever permissions are listed or assigned.

It can be updated for clarity without affecting underlying authorization checks, which depend on the `code` field.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of the permission’s purpose and behavior.

Backed by `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.description`, it documents what actions the permission authorizes, any constraints, and potential risks.

Admin tools can surface this text to help operators choose appropriate permissions for roles and to support governance documentation.

category.description:
Optional high‑level grouping or module name for the permission.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.category` and is used to cluster related permissions in administrative interfaces.

Common examples include `users`, `orders`, `catalog`, `risk`, and `configuration`, but the exact taxonomy is platform‑specific.

is_system.description:
Indicates whether this permission is system‑defined and protected from arbitrary removal.

This field reflects `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.is_system`. System permissions are typically seeded or managed by deployment scripts and cannot be deleted or substantially altered by standard administrator workflows.

Client UIs may use this flag to disable destructive actions or highlight critical permissions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this permission record was created.

The value is stored in `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.created_at` and represents the moment the permission was first inserted into the database.

It is system‑managed and useful for audit views and change history displays.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this permission record was last updated.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.updated_at` and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields such as `name`, `description`, or `category` change.

It allows administrators to track recency of modifications and to reason about configuration drift over time.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the permission was logically removed.

Backed by `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.deleted_at`, this field is null when the permission is active and set when it has been retired or logically deleted.

Soft‑deleted permissions are typically excluded from selection lists but may still be referenced in historical audit data or legacy role definitions.

IShoppingMallAdminPermission.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for querying administrative permissions from the `shopping_mall_admin_permissions` table.

Encapsulates complex search criteria, pagination parameters, and sorting options used by the PATCH `/shoppingMall/admin/adminPermissions` operation. Admin console UIs use this DTO to filter permissions by code, name, category, system flag, and lifecycle timestamps, as well as to control whether logically deleted permissions are included. Pagination and ordering fields enable efficient browsing of large permission catalogs.

IShoppingMallAdminPermission.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for defining a new administrative permission in the shoppingMall RBAC system.

This schema maps to the writable business fields of the `shopping_mall_admin_permissions` Prisma model that an admin must supply when registering a new permission. It excludes all system-managed identifiers and timestamps while enforcing that the permission code and name are provided and valid.

The DTO is used exclusively by high-privilege administrative tools to extend the permission catalog. It must be validated carefully to ensure that permission codes remain globally unique and human‑readable metadata is well formed.

code.description:
Stable, globally unique machine-oriented permission code.

This value is persisted into `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.code` and is used by RBAC evaluation logic, configuration files, and policy definitions. Typical values follow a dot‑separated namespace such as `users.manage`, `orders.refund.approve`, or `catalog.products.block`.

The code must remain stable once deployed because it can be referenced by business policies and configuration. Client implementations should treat the code as case‑sensitive and avoid whitespace or special characters outside of dots and ASCII letters/numbers/underscores.

name.description:
Human‑readable display name for the permission.

This field is stored in `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.name` and is shown in admin consoles and configuration UIs when assigning permissions to roles or describing permission sets.

The name should be concise but descriptive enough for administrators to understand the governed action without reading the full description.

description.description:
Optional long‑form description that explains what the permission allows and any important constraints or warnings.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.description`. It can describe side effects, risk level, or specific modules that are impacted when the permission is granted.

When omitted or null, consuming UIs may fall back to the code and name for explanation.

category.description:
Optional logical category or module grouping for the permission.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.category` and is typically used to cluster permissions in the UI (for example, `users`, `orders`, `catalog`, `risk`, or `configuration`).

When provided, it helps administrators navigate large permission catalogs and filter by functional area.

is_system.description:
Flag indicating whether the permission is system‑defined and protected from arbitrary modification.

This maps to `shopping_mall_admin_permissions.is_system`. When true, the permission is considered critical to the platform’s baseline security posture and should not be deleted or substantially altered by normal admin users.

If omitted, the backend may default this flag according to its own rules, typically treating created permissions as non‑system unless a specific workflow promotes them.

IShoppingMallAdminAuditLog.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying administrative audit logs stored in `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs`.

This schema models the complex, read‑only search criteria used by admin‑only endpoints that expose the platform’s append‑only audit trail. It allows callers to constrain results by actor, entity, action type, time range, and free‑text fields while also specifying pagination settings.

The DTO does not map directly to a single Prisma model via `x-autobe-prisma-schema` because it represents query parameters rather than a persisted row. It is used exclusively in PATCH search endpoints that return paginated `IShoppingMallAdminAuditLog.ISummary` results.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Optional filter for the admin who performed the action.

When provided, only audit log entries whose `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.shopping_mall_admin_id` matches this identifier are returned. This is useful when investigating actions taken by a specific administrator account.

If null or omitted, no filtering by acting admin is applied.

action_type.description:
Optional filter for a specific machine‑readable admin action type.

This field should match values stored in `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.action_type`, such as `USER_STATUS_CHANGE`, `SELLER_APPROVAL`, or `PRODUCT_BLOCK`.

When set, the search is constrained to audit events of the given action category; when null or omitted, all action types are included.

entity_type.description:
Optional filter for the type of business entity affected by the admin action.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.entity_type` and can contain values such as `customer`, `seller`, `product`, `order`, `refund_request`, or `dispute`.

Providing this filter narrows the search to a particular domain area; leaving it null or omitted allows all entity types.

entity_id.description:
Optional filter for a specific target entity identifier.

This value should match `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.entity_id` when present, allowing investigators to retrieve the full history of admin actions performed on a single resource, such as a particular order or customer.

When null or not supplied, no direct filtering by entity identifier is applied.

request_id.description:
Optional correlation identifier for the request or session in which actions occurred.

This maps conceptually to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.request_id` and can be used to gather all audit events related to the same incoming request or workflow execution.

If omitted or null, the search will not restrict results by request correlation.

ip.description:
Optional filter for the remote IP address associated with the admin action.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.ip`, which stores a best‑effort textual representation of the source IP where the action originated.

Providing this value allows operators to investigate actions coming from specific network locations; leaving it null or absent disables this filter.

user_agent.description:
Optional filter for the user agent string or client identifier used when performing the action.

This aligns with `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.user_agent` and can distinguish between different admin consoles, automated tools, or browsers.

Typically used in specialized investigations; when null or omitted, no user‑agent‑based filtering is applied.

message.description:
Optional free‑text search term applied to the human‑readable summary message.

This roughly corresponds to the `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.message` column and is often backed by a text or GIN index for efficient searching.

Providing a short keyword or phrase allows administrators to locate audit entries based on their descriptive content, while null or omitted values skip message‑based filtering.

from_created_at.description:
Optional lower bound for the `created_at` timestamp of audit log entries.

When set, only entries whose `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.created_at` value is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included in the result set.

If null or omitted, no lower time bound is enforced.

to_created_at.description:
Optional upper bound for the `created_at` timestamp of audit log entries.

When present, only entries whose `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.created_at` value is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned.

If null or omitted, no upper time bound is applied, and recent entries remain eligible.

page.description:
Optional 1‑based page index controlling which slice of the result set is returned.

When omitted or null, the backend typically defaults this to the first page. Combined with `limit`, this property allows administrators to navigate through large audit histories page by page.

Implementations should enforce sensible maximum page sizes and handle out‑of‑range page values gracefully.

limit.description:
Optional maximum number of records to return in a single page.

If provided, this limits the number of `IShoppingMallAdminAuditLog.ISummary` entries returned by the search operation. When null or missing, the backend should apply a default page size and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

Client applications should use this together with `page` to implement efficient, bounded pagination over the immutable audit log data.

IShoppingMallAdminAuditLog.description:
Admin audit log entry recorded in the shopping mall platform.

This type represents a single immutable audit trail record stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs` table. Each entry captures one administrative or system-level action, including who performed it, what entity was affected, when it occurred, and optional serialized snapshots of the entity state before and after the action.

Records are append-only and are used for compliance, forensic analysis, and governance reporting. They are typically queried by time range, acting admin, entity type, action type, or target entity identifiers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin audit log entry.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs` table and is generated by the system when the audit event is recorded.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the admin who performed the action when the event is directly associated with a specific administrator account.
