This field references `shopping_mall_admins.id` and is nullable to support system-initiated events, batch jobs, or external integrations where no human admin is directly responsible.
Null when the event was not triggered by a specific admin account, such as for system-level actions or background processes.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Reference to the admin account that performed the action, when applicable.

The value is a foreign key to `shopping_mall_admins.id` and may be null for system-generated or anonymous events.

action_type.description:
Machine-readable code indicating the category of action that was performed.

Typical examples include values such as `USER_STATUS_CHANGE`, `SELLER_APPROVAL`, `PRODUCT_BLOCK`, or other business-defined action identifiers. Consumers use this field to group, filter, and analyze audit events by category.

entity_type.description:
Type of the business entity that was affected by the administrative action.

Examples include `customer`, `seller`, `product`, `order`, `refund_request`, or `dispute`. This field allows auditors to focus on a specific domain when reviewing the audit trail.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the target entity as stored in its corresponding domain table.

This value is typically a UUID that matches the primary key or business ID of the affected entity.
Null when the action does not target a single concrete entity record, such as global configuration changes or system-wide operations.

entity_id.description:
Identifier of the target domain entity when the action is associated with a specific record.

The value may be null for actions that conceptually apply to a broad scope or to no single entity.

oneOf.description:
Human-friendly identifier for the target entity captured at the time of the event.

Examples include customer email addresses, seller names, or order codes that help auditors quickly recognize the affected record without needing to perform a separate lookup.
Null when no stable or meaningful display identifier was available at the time of logging.

entity_display.description:
Human-readable display value that helps auditors recognize the target entity.

This field complements `entity_id` by preserving a convenient label for the affected record, even if the underlying entity later changes or is removed from primary views.

oneOf.description:
Correlation identifier for the request or session in which the action occurred.

This ID can be used to group multiple audit log entries that were produced as part of a single HTTP request, workflow, or background job.
Null when no explicit request or correlation identifier was available at the time of logging.

request_id.description:
Optional correlation or request identifier used to link multiple audit events belonging to the same logical operation.

This value is useful for tracing complex workflows that generate several audit records.

oneOf.description:
Best-effort textual representation of the remote IP address from which the action originated.

The stored value is generally an IPv4 or IPv6 string but the format is not strictly validated to avoid dropping edge-case representations or proxy-provided values.
Null when IP information could not be determined or is not applicable to the action source.

ip.description:
Remote IP address string captured when the audited action was performed.

This field helps security and compliance teams identify the network origin of administrative operations, subject to the quality of upstream proxies and logging infrastructure.

oneOf.description:
User agent string or descriptive label for the client used to perform the action.

For web-based admin consoles this typically contains the browser user agent, while for automated or system calls it may be a short descriptive identifier for the integration or service.
Null when no user agent or client descriptor was available.

user_agent.description:
Client user agent or client descriptor associated with the audited action.

This information supports forensic analysis by indicating what kind of software or integration performed the operation.

oneOf.description:
Short human-readable summary of the action suitable for list views and quick inspection.

The message often describes what was changed or why the action occurred in a concise form and may include important identifiers or status values.
Null when no human-readable summary was recorded, for example in purely programmatic events.

message.description:
Human-oriented summary describing the nature of the administrative action.

This field is used in dashboards and audit views to give reviewers an immediate understanding of the event without reading serialized payloads.

oneOf.description:
Serialized representation of selected entity fields before the change took place.

The content is stored as an opaque text payload (often JSON) and is meant for audit and forensic use only, not for programmatic reconstruction of the entity.
Null when the action did not capture a pre-change snapshot or when the event type did not modify entity state.

before_snapshot.description:
Optional serialized snapshot of relevant entity data before the action was applied.

This value allows auditors to compare the prior state of an entity with the state after the change when investigating configuration or data modifications.

oneOf.description:
Serialized representation of selected entity fields after the change took place.

The payload is generally stored as JSON or another text-based format and is intended for inspection in compliance tools, not as a full canonical projection.
Null when the action did not capture a post-change snapshot or the event type is not state-changing.

after_snapshot.description:
Optional serialized snapshot of the entity state after the administrative action.

Together with `before_snapshot`, this field helps reviewers understand exactly what data was altered by a given operation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this audit log entry was recorded.

This value is set by the system at insertion time in the `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs` table and never changes afterwards, providing an immutable chronology of administrative events.

IShoppingMallLegalHold.IRequest.description:
Search request parameters for querying legal hold records from the shopping mall platform.

This DTO models complex, body-based search criteria used by administrative and governance tools when calling PATCH-based search endpoints over `shopping_mall_legal_holds`. It encapsulates filters for fields such as legal hold code, status, creation and release timestamps, and identifiers of the admins who created or released the hold.

The request also carries pagination and sorting options so that clients can efficiently browse large result sets in list or dashboard views. All properties are optional; omitted filters are simply ignored by the search implementation. This type does not map directly to a single Prisma model and therefore does not include an `x-autobe-prisma-schema` marker.

items.description:
Legal hold code value used as a stable external reference.

Each element in this array corresponds to the `code` column of the `shopping_mall_legal_holds` table and allows callers to restrict the search to one or more specific legal holds.

codes.description:
Optional list of legal hold codes to match in the search.

When provided, the search engine should restrict results to legal holds whose `code` field is contained in this list. If omitted or empty, no code-based filtering is applied.

items.description:
Single legal hold status value such as `active`, `released`, or other business-defined states.

These values correspond to the `status` column of the `shopping_mall_legal_holds` table and are used to filter holds by lifecycle phase.

statuses.description:
Optional list of legal hold status values to include in the result set.

Typical statuses include values like `active`, `released`, or other platform-specific lifecycle states. When this array is present, only holds whose `status` is in the given list should be returned.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound of the creation timestamp range used for filtering legal holds.

Only records whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this timestamp should be considered when this property is provided.
Null when no lower bound on the creation timestamp is required.

created_from.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound on the `created_at` timestamp of legal holds to be returned.

Use this field to restrict search results to holds created on or after a given point in time. If omitted, no minimum creation time filter is applied.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound of the creation timestamp range used for filtering legal holds.

Only records whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this timestamp should be returned when this property is provided.
Null when no upper bound on the creation timestamp is required.

created_to.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound on the `created_at` timestamp of legal holds to be returned.

Use this field together with `created_from` to filter holds created within a specific time interval. If omitted, no maximum creation time filter is applied.

items.description:
Identifier of an admin who may have created a legal hold.

Each value corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.created_by_admin_id` and is used as a filter criterion when searching by creator.

created_by_admin_ids.description:
Optional list of admin identifiers who created the legal holds.

When present, the search should be restricted to records whose `created_by_admin_id` is contained in this list. If omitted, holds created by any admin may be returned.

items.description:
Identifier of an admin who may have released a legal hold.

Each value corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_by_admin_id` and is used to find holds associated with a particular releasing admin.

released_by_admin_ids.description:
Optional list of admin identifiers who released the legal holds.

When provided, results should be limited to legal holds whose `released_by_admin_id` is in this list. If the values are empty or the property is omitted, this filter is not applied.

oneOf.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether only active or only non-active legal holds should be returned.

When set to true, the search should return only holds that are currently effective. When set to false, it should return only holds that are no longer active, such as those with a release timestamp.
Null when the caller does not want to filter by active or inactive status.

is_active.description:
Optional flag to restrict the result set based on whether legal holds are currently active.

Values of true or false indicate filtering by active or inactive holds respectively. If this property is omitted or null, both active and inactive holds may be returned depending on other criteria.

items.description:
External reference identifier such as a legal case number or ticket ID.

Each value corresponds to the `external_reference` column in `shopping_mall_legal_holds` and is used to correlate holds with external systems or processes.

external_references.description:
Optional list of external reference identifiers to match when searching legal holds.

This can be used to find all holds associated with specific external case or ticket identifiers, enabling integration with legal or compliance tooling.

oneOf.description:
The 1-based page index to retrieve from the filtered result set.

If provided, this controls which slice of the paginated results is returned. The default is typically page 1 when the property is omitted.
Null when the default page index (usually 1) should be used.

page.description:
Optional 1-based page number for pagination over legal hold search results.

When omitted or null, the implementation defaults to returning the first page of results.

oneOf.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

The value should respect platform-wide upper bounds to prevent excessively large responses from being requested by clients.
Null when the system should apply a default page size.

limit.description:
Optional page size limit controlling how many legal hold summaries are returned.

If omitted or null, the implementation should use a reasonable default such as 20 or 50 records per page, while still enforcing a global maximum allowed page size.

oneOf.description:
Field name that determines the primary sort key of the result set.

Typical values include `created_at`, `released_at`, or `status`, depending on which columns are indexed and supported by the search implementation.
Null when the system should apply a default sort ordering, usually by newest creation time first.

order_by.description:
Optional sort field name indicating how legal hold results should be ordered.

When not provided, the default ordering is typically by `created_at` descending so that the most recently created holds appear first.

oneOf.description:
Explicit direction for the sort ordering.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order when combined with the `order_by` property.

Explicit direction for the sort ordering.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order when combined with the `order_by` property.
Null when the search should use the default direction associated with the chosen `order_by` field, typically descending for timestamps.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the result ordering when `order_by` is used.

Allowed values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending. If omitted or null, the implementation uses a sensible default such as descending by creation time.

IShoppingMallLegalHold.description:
Represents a single legal hold configuration within the ShoppingMall platform.

A legal hold prevents deletion or modification of data associated with specific business entities for compliance, investigation, or litigation purposes. Each record corresponds directly to a row in the `shopping_mall_legal_holds` Prisma model and is uniquely identified by its primary key and stable business `code`.

Legal holds are created and managed by administrative users with governance or compliance responsibilities. They are associated with one or more target entities through `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` records, which define the exact scope of data that must be preserved. Lifecycle fields such as `status`, `effective_from`, `released_at`, and `deleted_at` describe when a hold becomes effective, whether it is currently active, and when it has been released or soft-deleted.

Client applications use this DTO in read operations to display full details about a legal hold, including descriptive fields, scope notes, and linkage to creating and releasing admins via both identifier fields and associated admin summaries. Downstream subsystems such as deletion schedulers, export modules, and risk or dispute workflows evaluate this representation to determine whether operations on protected data are permitted.

id.description:
Unique primary key of the legal hold record.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.id` and is generated by the database. It is used internally by the platform as a stable, opaque identifier for low-level operations and relations.

Client applications generally prefer to reference the hold by its business `code`, but this identifier is still exposed in responses for debugging and deep integration scenarios.

code.description:
Stable business identifier code for the legal hold.

The `code` is a human-readable, globally unique identifier that maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.code`. Governance and compliance administrators use this value when referring to a specific legal hold in user interfaces, documentation, and external correspondence.

API operations such as `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/legalHolds/{legalHoldCode}` resolve legal holds using this value instead of the internal UUID `id`.

title.description:
Short, human-readable title describing the legal hold.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.title` and typically contains a brief case name, subject line, or summary label. It helps administrators quickly recognize the purpose of the hold when browsing lists or dashboards.

Titles should be concise but descriptive enough to distinguish similar holds created for different matters or time periods.

description.description:
Optional detailed explanation of the legal hold.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.description` and may contain narrative text explaining the legal basis, context, and scope of the hold. It is commonly used by compliance teams to capture background information and references to external documentation.

When null, only the concise `title` and `scope_description` fields are available to describe the hold at a high level.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the legal hold.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.status` and represents business-defined states such as "active", "released", or other platform-specific codes. The exact set of allowed values is enforced by application logic and possibly by database constraints or check rules.

Client applications and downstream services use this field to determine whether the hold is currently in force, has been released, or is otherwise inactive for new enforcement decisions.

scope_description.description:
Optional business description of the scope of the legal hold.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.scope_description` and is used to summarize which kinds of entities, accounts, or time periods are covered by the hold. Typical examples include references to specific customers, sellers, orders, or disputes and the temporal boundaries of preservation.

When provided, this text complements the structured targets in `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` and helps readers understand the hold’s intended coverage at a glance.

external_reference.description:
Optional external reference identifier associated with the legal hold.

This maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.external_reference` and usually stores a case number, ticket ID, or reference from an external legal, compliance, or ticketing system. It allows cross-referencing between the ShoppingMall platform and external tools used by legal and risk teams.

When null, the legal hold is managed solely within the ShoppingMall environment without an explicit external reference.

effective_from.description:
Optional timestamp from which the legal hold is considered effective.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.effective_from`. When set, it indicates the point in time after which the platform must treat affected entities as protected by the hold. If null, the hold is generally treated as effective from its creation time or from a default business rule.

Consumers should use this field, together with `status`, to interpret whether a hold should currently prevent data deletion or modification.

released_at.description:
Timestamp marking the official release of the legal hold, if any.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_at`. When non-null, it records the date and time at which the hold was formally concluded or deactivated according to business processes. After this point, new operations that were previously blocked may become allowed, subject to other policies.

A null value indicates that the hold has not yet been released and may still be in effect depending on its `status` and other flags.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the legal hold record.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.created_at` and is automatically set when the record is inserted. It is used for auditing, ordering, and reporting on when specific holds were established.

Client applications typically treat this field as read-only and display it in administrative views or audit logs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the legal hold record.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.updated_at` and changes whenever mutable attributes of the legal hold are modified through administrative operations. It supports audit timelines and helps detect the freshness of displayed information.

The value is managed by the application or database layer and should not be altered directly by clients.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the legal hold.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.deleted_at`. When set, the legal hold is considered logically deleted from an operational standpoint and should not be used for new enforcement decisions. However, the record remains in the database for historical and audit purposes.

A null value indicates that the legal hold is not soft-deleted and remains part of the active dataset, subject to its `status` and business rules.

created_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who created the legal hold.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.created_by_admin_id` and references a row in `shopping_mall_admins.id`. It allows the platform to track which administrative actor established the hold for accountability and audit purposes.

The value is populated by the backend based on the authenticated admin context and is exposed in responses for traceability.

released_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who formally released the legal hold, if any.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_by_admin_id` and references `shopping_mall_admins.id`. When non-null, it records which administrative actor performed the release action, supporting compliance audits and governance reviews.

When null, the hold has either not been released or has been released in a way that does not associate the action with a specific admin account.

created_by_admin.description:
Summary information for the administrator who created this legal hold.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_legal_holds.created_by_admin_id` and references the corresponding administrator in `shopping_mall_admins`. It provides human-readable context such as admin name or handle for governance UIs without requiring additional lookups.

The summary shape follows the standard `.ISummary` pattern for admin entities to avoid deep circular references while still providing sufficient contextual information.

released_by_admin.description:
Summary information for the administrator who released this legal hold, if any.

When present, this association is resolved from `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_by_admin_id` and points to the corresponding administrator in `shopping_mall_admins`. It allows dashboards and audit views to display who concluded the hold without extra API calls.

When null, either the legal hold has not yet been released or the release action is not associated with a specific admin record.

IShoppingMallLegalHold.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new legal hold in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_legal_holds` Prisma model and is used by administrative and governance actors when calling `POST /shoppingMall/admin/legalHolds` to establish a new hold that constrains data deletion and modification.

Only business-configurable fields such as the legal hold code, title, descriptive reasoning, scope description, and external reference are accepted. System-managed fields like `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and actor identity fields for the creating admin are not accepted from the client and are populated by the backend.

Validation should ensure that the `code` value is unique, required textual fields are present, and that any optional lifecycle fields are logically consistent before inserting the new row.

code.description:
Stable business identifier or reference code for the new legal hold.

This value will be stored in `shopping_mall_legal_holds.code` and must be globally unique across all legal holds. Governance and compliance users will reference holds by this code in admin UIs and external documentation.

The backend must enforce uniqueness at the database level and should reject attempts to create a new hold with a code that already exists.

title.description:
Short human-readable title for the legal hold.

The value is written into `shopping_mall_legal_holds.title` and is intended to briefly describe the subject or purpose of the hold, such as an investigation name or regulatory request summary.

This field is required so that admin lists and detail pages always have a clear label to display to human operators.

description.description:
Optional detailed explanation of the reason and context for the legal hold.

When provided, this value is stored in `shopping_mall_legal_holds.description` and may include legal context, links to policy references, or detailed scoping notes.

Clients may pass null or omit the field if only the short title is known at creation time, and more detailed notes can be added later through the update endpoint.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status of the legal hold.

The value is persisted into `shopping_mall_legal_holds.status` and determines how the hold is treated immediately after creation, for example `active` for newly enacted holds or another platform-defined state according to policy.

The backend should validate that the provided status string is one of the supported values and enforce any business rules around which statuses are allowed at creation time.

scope_description.description:
Optional human-readable description of the scope of the legal hold.

This content is saved in `shopping_mall_legal_holds.scope_description` and can document which entities, time ranges, or subsystems are affected by the hold in business terms.

The field is intended for human readers; automated enforcement should rely on structured target records in related tables rather than parsing this text.

external_reference.description:
Optional external case or ticket identifier related to the legal hold.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.external_reference` and is typically used to store IDs from external legal, compliance, or issue-tracking systems.

Providing this field is recommended when there is a corresponding external case so that future reviewers can quickly correlate internal holds with outside records.

effective_from.description:
Optional datetime from which the legal hold becomes effective.

If supplied, this value will be written to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.effective_from`. It allows administrators to define holds that take effect at a specific point in time, such as the start of an investigation or the date of a regulatory request.

When null or omitted, the hold is typically treated as effective from the service’s creation timestamp (`created_at`). The backend should validate that the effective-from time is not later than any future business constraints defined by platform policy.

IShoppingMallLegalHold.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating mutable fields of a legal hold in the ShoppingMall platform.

This type is used as the request body for administrative update operations such as `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/legalHolds/{legalHoldCode}`. It exposes only those columns from the `shopping_mall_legal_holds` Prisma model that are intended to be changed after creation, and all properties are optional so that callers can send partial updates.

Typical uses include adjusting the descriptive text, updating the scope description, changing the lifecycle `status`, or setting or updating date fields such as `effective_from` and `released_at`. Server-side logic interprets omitted properties as "no change" and applies validation rules to ensure that the resulting state remains compliant with legal and business requirements. Identity and audit fields such as `id`, `code`, `created_by_admin_id`, and timestamp metadata are never accepted from the client and are therefore excluded from this DTO.

title.description:
New short title for the legal hold.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `shopping_mall_legal_holds.title`. It should remain a concise and recognizable label that helps administrators identify the hold in lists and dashboards.

If omitted, the current title is preserved.

description.description:
Updated detailed explanation of the legal hold.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.description`. Sending a non-null string replaces the previous description with new narrative text describing the legal context or scope. Sending null explicitly clears the existing description.

If the property is omitted from the payload, the current description remains unchanged.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status for the legal hold.

When supplied, this field updates `shopping_mall_legal_holds.status` to a new business-defined value, such as transitioning from an initial state to "active" or marking the hold as "released". Application-level validation enforces allowed transitions and may reject invalid state changes.

If this property is not included in the request, the legal hold’s status is left unchanged.

scope_description.description:
Revised business description of the hold’s scope.

This value updates `shopping_mall_legal_holds.scope_description`. A non-null string replaces the existing scope summary, while null explicitly clears it. The scope description helps readers understand which entities or periods are covered by the hold.

When omitted, the current scope description is preserved.

external_reference.description:
Updated external reference identifier associated with the legal hold.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.external_reference`. A non-null value replaces the existing external case or ticket identifier, while null clears any previously stored reference.

If the field is not included in the request, the existing external reference remains unchanged.

effective_from.description:
New effective-from timestamp for the legal hold.

When provided, this value updates `shopping_mall_legal_holds.effective_from`, changing the point in time from which the hold is considered effective. A null value explicitly clears a previously set timestamp, reverting to implicit business rules based on creation time or other defaults.

If omitted, the current `effective_from` value is left unchanged.

released_at.description:
Updated release timestamp for the legal hold.

Supplying a non-null value updates `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_at` to mark the exact time at which the hold was officially released. Providing null clears an existing release timestamp, which should only be done under strict governance rules.

If this property is not present in the payload, the existing `released_at` value is preserved.

IShoppingMallLegalHoldTarget.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a single legal hold target associated with a legal hold in the shopping mall governance subsystem.

This DTO is intended for use in paginated list responses and embedded contexts, where clients need to understand which entities are under legal hold without loading every descriptive detail. It captures the core identification and classification fields required to render search results, dashboards, and overviews.

The summary focuses on the target entity itself rather than the full legal hold configuration, which is addressed by the parent resource identified by `legalHoldCode` in the API path. Administrative and governance tools can use this summary to quickly scan which customers, sellers, orders, disputes, or other records are preserved under a given legal hold.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the legal hold target record.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` table and is used by detail endpoints and administrative tooling to retrieve or update a specific target.

In list or search contexts, it allows clients to construct links to target-detail views or to drive follow-up actions on a particular preserved entity.

target_type.description:
Type of the business entity affected by the legal hold.

Common values include domain labels such as `customer`, `seller`, `order`, `dispute`, or `review`. This classification enables governance, compliance, and risk tooling to understand which subsystem and table the associated `target_id` belongs to.

The value space and semantics are governed by business rules and service-layer validation rather than enforced directly in the schema, but it is always required for a valid target record.

target_id.description:
Identifier of the targeted entity in its owning domain table.

This field stores the canonical identifier (typically the primary key) for the business record that is subject to the legal hold. Combined with `target_type` and the parent legal hold, it uniquely identifies which entity must be preserved.

User interfaces can surface this value for debugging or deep-link construction, or rely on `target_display` for more human-friendly presentation where appropriate.

target_display.description:
Optional human-friendly display label for the target entity.

Typical examples include a customer email address, seller display name, or order number captured at the time the target was attached to the legal hold. This snapshot improves usability when scanning lists of targets in administrative consoles.

When null, clients may either show only the raw `target_type` and `target_id` or perform on-demand lookups against the underlying domain entity if such live enrichment is desired and permitted.

note.description:
Optional note describing why this particular entity was attached to the legal hold.

The note is captured at the time the target row is created in the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` table and can be used to record legal, investigative, or operational context for the preservation decision.

In list and search responses, this field gives administrators immediate insight into the rationale for including the target without requiring them to open a separate detail view or consult external documentation. When no additional commentary was provided at attachment time, this field may be empty and callers should treat the absence of a note as expected rather than exceptional.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this target was attached to the legal hold.

The value is recorded when the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` row is created and does not change afterward, providing an immutable audit trail of when preservation obligations began for this entity.

List views can use this field for sorting and filtering, for example to group or highlight recently attached targets under long-running legal holds.

IShoppingMallLegalHoldTarget.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating legal hold targets associated with a specific legal hold.

This type is used as the request body for administrative listing operations such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/legalHolds/{legalHoldCode}/targets`. It contains filtering, sorting, and pagination parameters that control how rows from the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` Prisma model are selected and ordered.

Common usage patterns include narrowing results to specific target types, filtering by underlying entity identifiers, and constraining results to targets created within particular time windows. When combined with the `legalHoldCode` path parameter, this DTO allows governance and compliance administrators to efficiently inspect the scope of a legal hold without loading all targets at once.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve from the target list.

If provided, this value requests a specific page of results, where 1 indicates the first page. When omitted, server implementations typically default to the first page or a configured starting index.

Values less than 1 should be treated as invalid by server-side logic and may result in a validation error.

limit.description:
Maximum number of target records to return per page.

This field controls the page size for the query, allowing clients to balance result granularity against response payload size. If omitted, the server applies a sensible default and may enforce a maximum to protect performance.

Very large requested limits may be capped by server-side configuration even when accepted syntactically.

target_type.description:
Optional filter on the type of entity under hold.

When set, this value restricts results to targets whose `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets.target_type` matches the supplied code, such as "customer", "seller", "order", or "dispute". This allows administrators to focus on particular categories of preserved entities.

If null or omitted, the query includes targets of all types associated with the specified legal hold.

target_id.description:
Optional filter on the underlying entity identifier.

Providing a non-null UUID restricts results to targets whose `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets.target_id` matches the given value. This is useful when an administrator needs to confirm whether a specific entity is covered by the legal hold.

If null or omitted, no direct filter on `target_id` is applied, and results are instead constrained by other criteria or by the parent `legalHoldCode` path parameter.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the creation timestamp window for targets.

When supplied, this value filters results to targets whose `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets.created_at` is greater than or equal to the specified instant. It enables time-based slicing, such as focusing on recently added targets.

If null or omitted, no explicit lower time bound is applied beyond any defaults imposed by server logic.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the creation timestamp window for targets.

Setting this value filters results to targets whose `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets.created_at` is less than or equal to the specified instant. Combined with `created_from`, it defines a closed time range for target inclusion.

If null or omitted, no explicit upper time bound is applied, and all targets up to the present may be included subject to other filters.

order_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort the result set.

Typical values correspond to columns in `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets`, such as "created_at" or "target_type". The exact list of allowed values is enforced by server-side validation to prevent arbitrary or unsafe order clauses.

When null or not provided, the server applies a default sort, usually descending by `created_at` so that the most recently added targets appear first.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction for the ordered results.

Common values include "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending order. The combination of `order_by` and `order_direction` determines how `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` rows are sorted before pagination is applied.

If null or omitted, the server uses a default direction that typically aligns with the default `order_by` field.

IShoppingMallLegalHoldTarget.description:
Represents a single legal hold target record within the shopping mall governance and compliance subsystem.

Each legal hold target links a specific business entity, such as a customer, seller, order, dispute, review, or other domain object, to an existing legal hold registered in the `shopping_mall_legal_holds` table. Legal hold targets are append-only records that describe which concrete entities must be preserved for investigations, regulatory inquiries, or litigation.

This entity is designed for internal administrative and governance tooling. It is not exposed to regular marketplace users. The record captures the target type, its identifier in the corresponding domain table, an optional human-readable display label, and optional notes describing why the entity has been placed under legal hold. Timestamps provide auditability for when the target was attached to the legal hold.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the legal hold target record.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` table and is generated by the system when a new target is created.

Clients receive this identifier in read operations but never provide or modify it directly.

shopping_mall_legal_hold_id.description:
Identifier of the parent legal hold in the `shopping_mall_legal_holds` table.

This foreign key ties the target to a specific legal hold configuration that describes the overall case, scope, and lifecycle of the hold.

In external APIs that use business-level codes (for example, `legalHoldCode`), this identifier is resolved by the backend and is not supplied by clients.

target_type.description:
Type of the business entity affected by the legal hold.

Typical values include domain labels such as `customer`, `seller`, `order`, `dispute`, or `review`. These values allow governance tools to understand which subsystem and table the `target_id` belongs to.

The exact set of allowed values is governed by business rules and validation logic in the service layer rather than enforced at the database level.

target_id.description:
Identifier of the targeted entity in its owning domain table.

This field stores the primary key or canonical identifier for the business entity that is subject to the legal hold. The combination of `shopping_mall_legal_hold_id`, `target_type`, and `target_id` is unique to prevent duplicate targets for the same entity and hold.

Application logic is responsible for ensuring that the referenced entity actually exists and that the pairing of `target_type` and `target_id` is semantically correct.

target_display.description:
Optional human-friendly display identifier for the target entity.

Examples include an email address for a customer, a seller name, or an order number captured at the time the target is linked. This value improves usability for legal and compliance staff when reviewing legal hold scopes.

When null, user interfaces may fall back to resolving a live label from the underlying domain entity if that is still available.

note.description:
Optional note describing why this particular entity was included in the legal hold.

Notes can capture case-specific reasoning, references to legal instructions, or additional internal context that is not stored in the main legal hold record.

When null, no additional explanation was recorded at the time the target was attached.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this target was attached to the legal hold.

This datetime is recorded when the row is created in the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` table and never changes afterward.

It provides an auditable timeline for when the platform started preserving data for this specific entity under the associated legal hold.

IShoppingMallLegalHoldTarget.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new legal hold target under an existing legal hold.

This DTO is used by administrative or governance APIs such as `POST /shoppingMall/admin/legalHolds/{legalHoldCode}/targets` to register which concrete business entity is being placed under legal hold.

The server derives the `shopping_mall_legal_hold_id` foreign key from the `legalHoldCode` path parameter of the parent legal hold. Clients provide only the type and identifier of the target entity, along with optional user-friendly display and notes that help legal and compliance teams understand the scope and purpose of the hold.

target_type.description:
Type of the business entity being attached to the legal hold.

Typical values include labels such as `customer`, `seller`, `order`, `dispute`, or `review`. The application validates and interprets these values to locate and preserve data in the appropriate domain tables.

This value is required and must follow the platform’s configured set of target type identifiers.

target_id.description:
Identifier of the target entity in its own domain table.

This value is used together with `target_type` and the parent legal hold derived from the path to enforce the uniqueness constraint on legal hold targets and to locate the affected records.

The backend may validate that the referenced entity exists or is otherwise a valid subject for legal hold at creation time.

target_display.description:
Optional human-friendly label for the target entity at the moment it is registered.

Examples include a customer email address, seller display name, or business order number. Capturing this snapshot allows legal and compliance staff to recognize the target even if underlying records later change or are partially anonymized.

If omitted or set to null, the system may rely on live lookups to present contextual labels in administrative tools.

note.description:
Optional note explaining why this entity is being placed under legal hold.

Notes can capture legal instructions, references to external case identifiers, or internal governance commentary that is specific to this target.

When null, no additional explanation is recorded beyond what exists on the parent legal hold.

IShoppingMallLegalHoldTarget.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for an existing legal hold target connected to a specific legal hold.

This type represents the subset of `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` fields that are allowed to change after a target has been created. It is used by administrative governance tools when correcting or enriching metadata about which concrete business entities are under a legal hold.

Linkage fields such as the primary key, the foreign key to the parent legal hold, and the polymorphic subject identifiers remain immutable and are not part of this DTO. Only descriptive and explanatory fields can be patched through this structure, preserving referential integrity and the original scope of the legal hold.

note.description:
Optional free-form note describing why this particular entity was attached to the legal hold, or providing additional explanatory context.

This field updates the `note` column on `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets`. It may contain internal comments for legal or compliance teams and can be changed over time as investigations evolve.

target_display.description:
Optional human-friendly display identifier for the target entity, such as an email address for a customer, a seller name, or an order number captured at the time the target was linked to the legal hold.

This field updates the `target_display` column on `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets`. It is purely descriptive metadata used by legal and compliance staff to more easily recognize the subject of the hold and does not change the underlying linkage fields or the scope of the legal hold itself. When set to null, any previously stored display label is cleared while the target remains attached to the legal hold.

IShoppingMallRiskCase.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying risk cases stored in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`.

This type is used by administrative and risk-operations interfaces to express complex search criteria, pagination, and sorting options when retrieving lists of risk cases. It does not map directly to a Prisma model, but its fields are designed around the indexed columns and business attributes of the `shopping_mall_risk_cases` table.

All properties are optional filters or controls. When a property is omitted, that dimension is not constrained. Implementations typically combine the provided filters to build a WHERE clause against `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, constrained by platform-wide limits on result size.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated result sets.

When omitted, implementations typically default this to 1. Combined with `limit`, it determines the offset when querying `shopping_mall_risk_cases` for list views.

limit.description:
Maximum number of risk case records to return per page.

Backend implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses. When omitted, the system applies a sensible default page size for administrative risk-case listings.

status.description:
Optional filter on the current lifecycle status of a risk case.

This value is matched against the `status` column in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, whose description mentions values such as `open`, `under_review`, or `closed`. When provided, only risk cases with the given status are returned.

severity.description:
Optional filter on the severity classification of risk cases.

This corresponds to the `severity` column of `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, which conceptually contains business-level categories such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. When set, only cases with the specified severity will be included in the results.

caseCode.description:
Optional exact filter on the stable case code or reference identifier.

When provided, the search narrows results to risk cases whose `case_code` column exactly matches this value, making it suitable for direct navigation when the case code is already known.

primarySubjectType.description:
Optional filter on the type of primary subject associated with the risk case.

This maps to the `primary_subject_type` column of `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, whose description references categories such as `customer`, `seller`, `order`, or `payment`. When provided, only cases whose primary subject matches the given type are returned.

primarySubjectId.description:
Optional filter on the UUID identifier of the primary subject associated with the case.

This corresponds to the `primary_subject_id` column in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`. When set together with `primarySubjectType`, it can narrow results to risk cases associated with a specific entity in its own domain table.

ownerAdminId.description:
Optional filter on the admin currently responsible for the risk case.

This matches the `owner_admin_id` foreign key in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, allowing queues to show cases owned by a particular administrator or analyst.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the case creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only risk cases whose `created_at` column is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are returned, allowing time-range based queries.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the case creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only risk cases whose `created_at` column is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are returned, supporting time-window searches in combination with `createdFrom`.

sortBy.description:
Optional sort field name applied to the risk case list.

Typical values align with indexed columns on `shopping_mall_risk_cases`, such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, `severity`, or `status`. When omitted, the backend applies its default ordering, commonly newest cases first.

sortOrder.description:
Optional sort direction for the chosen sort field.

Expected values are conceptual directions such as `asc` or `desc`. When absent, implementations typically default to descending order on the default sort field.

IShoppingMallRiskCase.description:
Detailed representation of a single risk or fraud case managed within the ShoppingMall platform.

This type is backed directly by the `shopping_mall_risk_cases` Prisma model and exposes the core business attributes of a case including its business code, classification, lifecycle status, and key timestamps. It is primarily used in administrator-facing UIs and governance tools where risk and fraud teams investigate suspicious behavior.

The DTO includes only fields that are actually present on the Prisma model and follows the same naming and nullability rules. It does not expose any authentication or credential data and is safe to return to authorized admin actors who are permitted to manage risk cases.

Relations to admin accounts (creator, owner, and closing admin) are presented as summary association objects rather than raw UUIDs, providing richer context for UI rendering without requiring additional lookup calls.

id.description:
Primary key identifier of the risk case record.

This value is generated by the database and uniquely identifies the risk case row in the `shopping_mall_risk_cases` table.

It is used for internal joins and correlations but is generally not exposed in URLs, which instead use the stable `case_code` business identifier.

case_code.description:
Stable business code or reference identifier for the risk case.

This value corresponds to the `case_code` column which has a unique index on the `shopping_mall_risk_cases` model. It is the human-readable identifier that appears in admin consoles, ticketing tools, and external references.

API operations such as `GET /shoppingMall/admin/riskCases/{riskCaseCode}` and `PUT /shoppingMall/admin/riskCases/{riskCaseCode}` use this code in the path as `riskCaseCode`.

title.description:
Short summary title describing the risk case.

The title should concisely capture the main suspicion or subject of the case, such as the primary pattern of abuse, suspicious account, or anomalous financial behavior.

This field is intended for use in list views, dashboards, and notifications where a quick textual label is required.

description.description:
Optional detailed narrative of the risk scenario and initial findings.

This field maps to the nullable `description` column and may include investigation context, rule hits, analyst notes at creation time, or other free-form commentary.

Clients should treat `null` as "no additional description provided" and avoid assuming any default text.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the risk case.

The exact set of allowed values (for example, `open`, `under_review`, `closed`) is governed by business rules and database constraints on the `status` column of `shopping_mall_risk_cases`.

Admin applications use this status to drive workflows, queues, and SLA tracking for the case.

severity.description:
Business-level severity classification for the risk case.

Typical values might include `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical` depending on the risk policy definition for the marketplace. This field is stored in the `severity` column and is required.

Severity is used by governance and risk teams to prioritize cases and to drive alerting or escalation workflows.

primary_subject_type.description:
Type of the primary subject associated with the case.

Examples can include `customer`, `seller`, `order`, or `payment`, but the authoritative list of valid values is defined by the business rules and any enum-like constraints on the `primary_subject_type` column.

When `null`, the case is considered systemic or not tied to a single primary subject entity.

primary_subject_id.description:
Identifier of the primary subject entity in its own domain table.

This field corresponds to the nullable `primary_subject_id` column and allows linking the case to a concrete object such as a customer account, seller account, order, or payment.

When `null`, the case either has no specific subject or is handled via other linkage tables.

primary_subject_display.description:
Human-readable display identifier for the primary subject.

Typical values include an email address, seller name, or order number, providing quick recognition of the subject in UIs and reports.

This string is derived or captured at case creation time and stored in the `primary_subject_display` column for convenience.

sla_due_at.description:
Service-level agreement due timestamp for handling the case.

If populated, this datetime indicates when the case should be addressed or resolved according to risk and governance SLAs and comes from the `sla_due_at` column.

When `null`, either no explicit SLA applies or the SLA schedule has not yet been computed for this case.

closed_at.description:
Timestamp when the case reached a closed or terminal state.

The value is stored in the nullable `closed_at` column and is set when the status transitions into a business-defined terminal state such as `closed`.

Consumers can use this field in analytics and auditing to measure case resolution times and SLA conformance.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the risk case was created.

This field maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column and records when the case record was first inserted into the database.

It is used for ordering, reporting, and lifecycle analytics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the risk case was last updated.

This value comes from the non-nullable `updated_at` column and is refreshed whenever mutable fields on the case are changed.

It supports audit trails, last-change indicators in UIs, and concurrency checks if required.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the risk case.

When set in the `deleted_at` column, the case is considered logically deleted or archived and typically excluded from active work queues.

The record remains persisted for historical analysis, compliance, and auditing even after deletion from active views.

created_by_admin.description:
Summary of the admin who created the risk case.

This association replaces the raw `created_by_admin_id` foreign key and provides immediate access to key identifying information for the creator, such as their id, display name, and contact details as defined by `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary`.

Returning a summary object instead of a bare UUID allows admin-facing UIs to render meaningful context (for example, "created by Alice Smith") without issuing an additional lookup call.

owner_admin.description:
Summary of the admin currently responsible for managing the case.

This association replaces the nullable `owner_admin_id` foreign key and represents the primary owner or assignee of the risk case in current workflows.

When `null`, the case is considered unassigned or handled by a shared queue. When non-null, the embedded admin summary provides enough context to render ownership information directly in list and detail views.

closed_by_admin.description:
Summary of the admin who closed the risk case, when applicable.

This association replaces the nullable `closed_by_admin_id` foreign key and identifies the administrative actor who performed the final resolution or closure action.

When `null`, the case has not yet been closed or the closer has not been recorded. When populated, the summary object enables UIs and reports to show who made the closing decision without requiring a separate admin lookup.

IShoppingMallRiskCase.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new risk or fraud case in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO mirrors the writable subset of the `shopping_mall_risk_cases` Prisma model at creation time. It allows privileged admin actors to open a new case with a business code, classification fields, and optional primary subject linkage.

Server-side logic is responsible for populating system-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and any admin identity fields like `created_by_admin_id`. Clients must not attempt to provide those values in the request body.

case_code.description:
Stable business code or reference identifier to assign to the new risk case.

This field maps to the required `case_code` column and must be unique across all risk cases according to the unique index defined on the Prisma model.

It is the identifier that will be used in path parameters such as `riskCaseCode` for subsequent retrieval and update operations.

title.description:
Short summary title describing the new risk case.

The title should briefly convey the primary suspicion, affected subject, or pattern that triggered the case creation.

It is stored in the non-nullable `title` column and will appear in admin dashboards and lists.

description.description:
Optional detailed description or initial narrative for the case.

This text maps to the nullable `description` column and can include background context, triggering rule information, or notes from the admin opening the case.

When omitted or `null`, it indicates that no additional narrative was provided at creation time.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status to assign to the case.

The value must comply with the allowed status set defined by business rules and database constraints on the `status` column (for example, an initial status of `open` or `under_review`).

This status controls how the case appears in risk operations queues and workflows immediately after creation.

severity.description:
Initial severity classification for the case.

This required value maps to the `severity` column and should reflect the business impact of the risk scenario at the time of creation (for example, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`).

Severity is typically used to drive prioritization, alerting, and escalation logic in governance tools.

primary_subject_type.description:
Type of the primary subject associated with the case at creation.

Examples include `customer`, `seller`, `order`, or `payment`. The exact semantics are controlled by business logic and any constraints on the `primary_subject_type` column.

If the case is not tied to a single subject, this field can be omitted or set to `null`.

primary_subject_id.description:
Identifier of the primary subject entity that the case targets.

This value corresponds to the nullable `primary_subject_id` column and should reference the primary key of the associated domain entity such as a customer, seller, order, or payment.

When omitted or `null`, the case is considered either systemic or not yet linked to a specific subject record.

primary_subject_display.description:
Human-readable display identifier for the primary subject at the time of case creation.

Typical values are email addresses, seller names, or order numbers that help admins quickly recognize the subject without additional lookups.

This value is stored in the nullable `primary_subject_display` column and is optional in the creation payload.

sla_due_at.description:
Optional SLA due timestamp to assign when opening the case.

If provided, this datetime is written to the `sla_due_at` column and indicates when the case should be handled or resolved according to configured service-level agreements.

If omitted or `null`, the SLA may be computed or updated later by background jobs or risk workflows.

IShoppingMallRiskCase.IUpdate.description:
Update request DTO for modifying an existing risk case stored in the shopping_mall_risk_cases table.

This type represents the set of fields that are allowed to change during the lifecycle of a risk case, such as its status, severity, ownership, and descriptive metadata. It is used by administrative and risk-operations workflows when they transition cases between states, reassign ownership among admins, or refine the textual description and primary subject information.

Only mutable, business-facing columns from the shopping_mall_risk_cases Prisma model are exposed. Immutable identifiers and system-managed timestamps are excluded, and ownership fields that depend on the current authenticated admin are treated carefully according to security rules. All properties are optional to support partial updates, while server-side validation enforces any business rules such as valid status transitions or required fields when closing a case.

title.description:
Short human-readable title summarizing the risk case.

The title describes the main suspicion, pattern, or subject of the investigation in a concise way for use in dashboards and work queues. Examples include phrases like "Abnormal refund pattern for seller X" or "Multiple failed payment attempts from same IP".

Updates to this field are typically performed by admins when they gain more clarity about the nature of the case. Validation should ensure that the title remains within acceptable length limits and avoids empty or purely whitespace content.

description.description:
Detailed narrative description of the risk scenario or investigation notes.

This field maps to the nullable description column on shopping_mall_risk_cases and can contain extended text describing context, findings, and hypotheses. Admins may update it as the investigation progresses, for example to record communication summaries, data analysis, or rationale for status changes.

Setting this field to null clears the stored description, while providing a non-empty string replaces the previous content. Implementations may apply additional length or content validation based on business policy.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the risk case.

This value represents the business-level state machine for risk cases, such as "open", "under_review", or "closed" as documented in the Prisma schema comments and governance rules. Admins use this field to drive workflows and SLA tracking.

Server-side logic must enforce valid status transitions according to configured policies. For example, the system may prohibit reopening a case after it reaches certain terminal states, or require specific fields to be set before moving to "closed". Clients should send only recognized status values; otherwise the request must be rejected with a clear validation error.

severity.description:
Business severity classification of the risk case.

Severity captures the relative importance or urgency of the case, typically using values such as "low", "medium", "high", or "critical" based on platform risk policy. Adjusting severity helps prioritize work queues and reporting, and may influence SLA deadlines.

Admin users can update this field when new information changes the perceived impact of the case. Implementations should validate that any provided severity value matches allowed categories and may combine it with status and SLA rules for additional checks.

primary_subject_type.description:
Type of the primary subject associated with this risk case.

Typical values described in the Prisma schema include markers such as "customer", "seller", "order", or "payment" to indicate whether the case primarily concerns an actor, an order, or a specific financial transaction. This classification supports filtering, reporting, and routing to specialized teams.

Admins may update this field when they re-scope the investigation or refine their understanding of what entity is central to the case. Providing null clears the subject type, while a non-null string should match the controlled vocabulary established by risk operations.

primary_subject_id.description:
Identifier of the primary subject entity in its own domain table.

This field corresponds to the nullable primary_subject_id column on shopping_mall_risk_cases and usually stores a UUID referencing a customer, seller, order, payment, or other domain entity. It allows direct linkage from the risk case to the row that is most strongly implicated.

When updating this property, admins can point the case to a different subject if the investigation reveals that a different entity is central, or set it to null if the case is systemic rather than tied to a single record. The server should validate that any provided UUID has the correct format and, if necessary, that the referenced entity exists.

primary_subject_display.description:
Human-readable reference for the primary subject of the case.

Examples include an email address, seller name, order number, or other display identifier that is convenient for admins to recognize without looking up internal UUIDs. This field mirrors the primary_subject_display column and is often used in dashboards and exports.

Updates to this field typically accompany changes to primary_subject_type or primary_subject_id, or reflect improved normalization of display values. Sending null clears the display value, while a non-null string should remain concise and suitable for UI presentation.

sla_due_at.description:
Datetime by which the risk case should be handled according to SLA.

This property maps to the nullable sla_due_at column and indicates the deadline for completing analysis or taking action on the case, derived from SLA configuration in tables such as shopping_mall_case_sla_configs. Adjusting it allows admins or automated processes to re-evaluate or extend the due date when business circumstances change.

Clients may set this field to a future ISO 8601 timestamp string, or to null when clearing previously assigned SLA information. Server logic should ensure that any provided datetime value is well-formed and compatible with internal time zone and SLA handling rules.

closed_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the case reached a closed or terminal state.

Although many systems prefer to set closed_at automatically when status transitions into a terminal value, this field is exposed in the update DTO to allow migration or correction scenarios where historical closure times must be adjusted. In most normal workflows, server-side logic may ignore client-supplied values and manage this column itself.

When accepted, the value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string or null to clear an accidentally set closure time. Business rules often require that closed_at is non-null when status is closed and null when the case is still active.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the risk case, used for archival and audit purposes.

The deleted_at column determines whether a case is considered active in work queues or hidden but preserved for historical review. While many implementations reserve this field for internal use, it is available in the update DTO for systems that allow privileged admins to deliberately soft-delete or restore cases.

Providing a non-null ISO 8601 timestamp marks the case as soft-deleted at that time, while sending null clears the deletion marker and restores the case to active visibility according to business rules. Access to this capability should be tightly controlled and audited.

owner_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin currently responsible for the risk case.

This property updates the owner_admin_id foreign key, which assigns primary ownership of the case to a specific admin user from the shopping_mall_admins table. Reassigning ownership helps route work between team members and queues.

Because this field targets another admin, not the calling actor themselves, it is permissible to accept it in the request body. The server should validate that any provided UUID refers to an existing admin and may apply additional rules such as limiting ownership to certain roles or teams. Setting this field to null clears ownership, placing the case into an unassigned state.

closed_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who closed the case, when applicable.

The closed_by_admin_id column records which administrative user executed the closure action. In most workflows this should be set automatically from the authenticated admin context at the moment the case transitions to a terminal status.

This field is included in the update DTO primarily to support data correction or migration scenarios. If the implementation chooses to honor client-supplied values, it must validate that the UUID corresponds to an existing admin and apply appropriate authorization checks. Providing null clears the recorded closer, which may be useful when reopening or correcting records.

IShoppingMallRiskCaseEvent.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for retrieving risk case events from the shopping_mall_risk_case_events table.

This type encapsulates pagination, sorting, and filter criteria for listing timeline events associated with a particular risk case. It is used in administrative dashboards and risk investigation tools to navigate event histories efficiently, especially when a case accumulates many status changes, notes, and automated rule triggers.

The DTO focuses on generic query dimensions independent of the underlying primary and foreign keys, since the parent risk case is identified by a separate path parameter and the API implementation resolves it to internal IDs. Filtering by event type, date ranges, or admin actor allows risk teams to quickly locate relevant parts of the timeline without over-fetching data.

page.description:
One-based page index indicating which slice of the event timeline to return.

A value of 1 refers to the first page of results, 2 to the next, and so on. This parameter works in combination with the limit field to support offset-style pagination over the shopping_mall_risk_case_events records for the given risk case.

If omitted, the server may default to the first page. Negative values are invalid and should be rejected by validation logic.

limit.description:
Maximum number of events to return in a single page of results.

This parameter controls the page size for the event list and helps bound response payload size for long timelines. Implementations should enforce an upper bound according to platform performance guidelines, such as capping the value at 100 or 200 items.

If not provided, the server should apply a sensible default page size. Values less than or equal to zero are invalid and must trigger a validation error.

event_type.description:
Optional filter by machine-readable event type value.

The event_type field corresponds to the event_type column on shopping_mall_risk_case_events and distinguishes different kinds of timeline entries, such as "created", "status_changed", "note_added", or "rule_triggered". Supplying a value here restricts the result set to events of that specific type.

When null or omitted, the API returns events of all types. Implementations may support both single-value filters and richer patterns by mapping this property into an internal query builder, but values that do not match recognized event types should either produce an empty result set or a validation error based on business policy.

from_created_at.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for filtering events by their creation timestamp.

When specified, only events whose created_at value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are included in the result set. This allows admins to focus on a particular time window within the overall case timeline, such as recent activity or activity during a specific investigation period.

Providing null or omitting this field disables the lower bound filter. The server must ensure that any provided timestamp is correctly parsed and interpreted in the system's time zone strategy.

to_created_at.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for filtering events by their creation timestamp.

When supplied, only events whose created_at value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are returned. This filter is typically used together with from_created_at to carve out a time range of interest in the event history.

Setting this field to null or leaving it out disables the upper bound filter. The server should validate that any provided value is a valid date-time string and, when used with from_created_at, optionally enforce that it is not earlier than the lower bound.

admin_id.description:
Optional filter limiting results to events associated with a specific admin.

This parameter corresponds conceptually to the shopping_mall_admin_id foreign key on shopping_mall_risk_case_events and allows clients to view only those events that were performed by, or attributed to, a given admin user. It is useful for audit scenarios such as "show me everything admin X did on this case".

When provided, it must be a well-formed UUID string representing an admin identity; null or omission disables the filter. The implementation may choose whether to enforce that the referenced admin actually exists before executing the query.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction for ordering events by their creation time.

Typical values are "asc" for chronological order and "desc" for reverse-chronological order from newest to oldest. If omitted or null, the server may default to descending order so that the most recent activity appears first in dashboard views.

The implementation should validate that any non-null string provided matches one of the supported directions and reject unsupported values with a clear error message.

IShoppingMallRiskCaseEvent.description:
Risk case event entity representing a single timeline entry for a governance or fraud risk case.

This type is backed by the Prisma model `shopping_mall_risk_case_events`, which stores append-only events that describe the lifecycle of a high-level risk case in `shopping_mall_risk_cases`. Each record captures what happened, when it happened, which admin (if any) triggered it, and optional links to other domain entities such as orders, payments, or disputes.

Risk case events are used by internal governance, risk, and compliance tools to reconstruct the full history of a case and to support auditing, reporting, and decision review. Records are immutable from a business perspective and are always read in chronological order per case.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the risk case event.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_risk_case_events` table and is generated by the system when the event is recorded. It is globally unique across all risk case events and is used in path parameters and internal references.

Clients should treat this identifier as an opaque value and must not attempt to infer meaning from it.

shopping_mall_risk_case_id.description:
Identifier of the risk case this event belongs to.

This field links the event record to its parent risk case in the `shopping_mall_risk_cases` table. It is used internally for joins and filtering when querying the full timeline of a risk case.

In higher-level APIs, this linkage is usually represented by the risk case business code in the URL path rather than exposing this raw UUID to clients.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable type of the risk case event.

Typical values include codes such as `created`, `status_changed`, `note_added`, `rule_triggered`, or other business-defined tokens representing distinct event categories. Implementations usually enforce this field using an internal enumeration or constrained string set.

Client applications use this type to choose appropriate icons, labels, and grouping logic when rendering risk case timelines.

from_status.description:
Previous status of the associated risk case when this event represents a status transition.

For non-status-change events (for example, free-form notes or rule evaluation logs), this field is null. When set, it contains the status code of the risk case immediately before the change, such as `open`, `under_review`, or `closed`.

Back-office tools use this value together with `to_status` to display human-friendly status transition messages in the event timeline.

to_status.description:
New status of the associated risk case when this event represents a status transition.

For events that do not change status, this field is null. When provided, it contains the status code of the risk case after the transition, for example `open`, `under_review`, or `closed`.

Analysts can use this field to quickly identify when a case reached terminal states or escalated to higher severity levels.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description or note explaining what happened in this event.

This text is typically authored by an admin or risk analyst when adding manual notes, but it may also be generated by automated systems to explain rule results, threshold breaches, or integration callbacks.

The content may contain references to policies, internal ticket numbers, or short explanations that help future reviewers understand why the event was recorded.

related_entity_type.description:
Optional type of another domain entity associated with this risk case event.
