Common examples include values such as `order`, `payment`, `refund`, or `dispute`, indicating that the event is specifically tied to a record in the corresponding domain table.

Together with `related_entity_id`, this field enables back-office tools to deep-link from a risk case event to the underlying transactional or account entity that triggered the event.

related_entity_id.description:
Identifier of the related entity referenced by this event, when applicable.

When `related_entity_type` is set, this field holds the primary key of the referenced record in its own domain table, such as an order ID or payment ID. When there is no specific related entity, this field is null.

Consumers should interpret this value together with `related_entity_type` to avoid misrouting links across different domains.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this risk case event was recorded.

The value is stored as a precise UTC date-time in the `shopping_mall_risk_case_events.created_at` column and never changes after insertion. It defines the chronological order of events within a risk case.

User interfaces typically use this timestamp to sort events and to display localized date and time information in risk case timelines.

admin.description:
Admin actor who triggered this risk case event, when the event originates from a human administrator or an admin-owned automation.

When non-null, this object is a summary view of the corresponding administrator account from the `shopping_mall_admins` table, exposed through `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary`. It provides enough context—such as identity and display information—for governance and risk-operations tools to attribute actions in the event timeline without requiring additional API calls.

If the event was generated automatically by system logic or an external risk engine without a specific admin owner, this field is null. In all cases, the underlying foreign key is managed by the backend and is not required or accepted from client requests.

IShoppingMallRiskCaseEvent.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new risk case event under a specific risk case.

This DTO is derived from the `shopping_mall_risk_case_events` Prisma model and is used in POST operations scoped by a parent risk case code in the URL path. It captures the event-specific attributes that risk operators or internal systems provide when appending an entry to a case timeline.

Parent-identifying fields such as the risk case ID are supplied via the path parameter and not included here, and system-managed fields like the event ID and creation timestamp are generated by the backend.

This type is intended for use by administrative or risk-operations clients only and is not exposed to end users such as customers or sellers.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable type of the new risk case event to be recorded.

Clients must provide a value that corresponds to the platform’s configured event type vocabulary, such as `created`, `status_changed`, `note_added`, or `rule_triggered`. The backend will validate this value against allowed codes according to business policy.

This field is required because it categorizes the event for later filtering, analytics, and user interface rendering.

from_status.description:
Previous status of the risk case when creating a status-change event.

When the new event represents a transition between two case statuses, this field should contain the status code in effect before the change. For non-status events or when the previous status is not being explicitly tracked, clients can omit this value or send null.

Back-office logic may use this value to validate that the requested transition is allowed from the current state of the risk case.

to_status.description:
New status of the risk case when the event represents a status update.

If the event changes the case status, this field should hold the resulting status code such as `under_review`, `closed`, or `escalated`. For events that do not involve a status change, this field may be omitted or set to null.

The service layer can use this value to drive updates to the parent risk case record and to enforce lifecycle and SLA rules.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description or note explaining the event being created.

Risk analysts or automated systems can use this field to provide additional context, such as the rationale for a decision, an explanation of rule outcomes, or links to external case tracking systems.

When present, this text appears in risk case timelines and audit views and should be written with sufficient clarity to support future reviews.

related_entity_type.description:
Optional type discriminator for an external entity related to this new event.

Examples include `order`, `payment`, `refund`, or `dispute`, indicating that the event is specifically associated with a record in that domain. When not applicable, this field may be omitted or set to null.

Together with `related_entity_id`, this helps investigation tools surface quick navigation links to the underlying transaction or account.

related_entity_id.description:
Identifier of the related entity in its own domain table, when the event is tied to a specific record.

Clients should provide a UUID that corresponds to the primary key of the entity indicated by `related_entity_type`, such as an order ID or payment ID. When there is no particular related entity, this value can be null.

The backend does not typically enforce referential integrity at this level but may perform best-effort validations in some implementations.

IShoppingMallPolicyOverride.description:
Policy override entity representing explicit exceptions to default business policies in the shopping mall platform.

Each record links a base policy version to a specific subject (such as a seller, category, product, or global scope) and defines an override value, status, and effective window. Governance, risk, and compliance workflows use these overrides to adjust how refunds, commissions, reviews, SLAs, and other business rules are applied.

The model is administered exclusively by platform admins and is audited through separate admin audit log mechanisms. It is soft-deletable to preserve history for legal and analytical purposes while preventing further use in active decision-making flows.

This DTO not only exposes the raw FK identifiers used for filtering and joins, but also embeds summary views of the related policy version and administrative actors, enabling atomic read operations in governance UIs.

id.description:
Primary key for the policy override record.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes a single override row in the shopping_mall_policy_overrides table. It is generated by the system at creation time and is used as the stable reference in administrative APIs and internal services.

shopping_mall_policy_version_id.description:
Identifier of the base policy version being overridden.

This field references shopping_mall_policy_versions.id and determines which concrete version of a logical business policy the override is scoped against. Service logic uses this link to understand the default rules being modified when evaluating behavior for the target subject.

policyVersion.description:
Summary of the policy version being overridden.

Embedding this summary provides governance and risk users with immediate visibility into the underlying policy version (for example, version code, domain, and effective dates) without requiring an additional API call.

The summary is derived from the `shopping_mall_policy_versions` row referenced by `shopping_mall_policy_version_id`.

created_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who created this policy override.

This value references shopping_mall_admins.id and records which administrative actor initiated the override. It is used for audit trails, accountability, and governance analysis but is not intended to be modified after initial creation.

createdByAdmin.description:
Summary of the administrator who created this policy override.

This embedded summary allows interfaces to show who originally introduced the override, including key identity and role information, without performing a separate admin lookup.

It reflects the `shopping_mall_admins` record referenced by `created_by_admin_id`.

approved_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who approved this override, if approval is required.

When present, this field references shopping_mall_admins.id for the administrator who formally approved the override according to governance workflows. It remains null when approval is not required or has not yet occurred.

approvedByAdmin.description:
Summary of the administrator who approved this override, when approvals are part of the governance workflow.

Including this summary lets users immediately see which admin granted approval for the exception, providing transparency in oversight and review screens.

The value is null when `approved_by_admin_id` is null or when approval has not yet occurred.

subject_type.description:
Type of subject to which the override applies, such as "seller", "category", "product", or "global".

Service-level logic interprets this string to determine how subject_id and subject_display should be resolved and how the override participates in policy evaluation. The allowed values are governed by business requirements and may include additional subject types for accounts, orders, or campaigns.

subject_id.description:
Identifier of the specific subject entity when applicable.

For subject types that target a concrete entity (for example a seller, customer, category, product, or specific order), this field stores the UUID or primary key of that subject. It may be null for global overrides that are not bound to a single entity instance.

subject_display.description:
Human-friendly representation of the subject, such as a seller name or category path.

The value is stored for quick reference in administrative tools so that governance users can understand what the override targets without additional joins. Typical examples include seller display names, category breadcrumbs, or short textual labels for campaigns.

override_code.description:
Code or key that identifies which aspect of the policy is being overridden.

Examples include business-level identifiers for refund windows, commission rates, review rules, SLA thresholds, or risk scoring parameters. Application logic uses this code in combination with the base policy version to determine the exact rule segment being replaced or refined.

override_value.description:
Business-level value used in place of the default policy configuration.

The value is stored as text to support a wide range of override formats such as numeric thresholds, percentage rates, JSON-encoded fragments, or enumerated mode values. Interpretation and validation of this value is handled by policy-specific application logic that understands the corresponding override_code.

reason.description:
Optional explanation of why this override exists.

Typical content includes the business justification, links or identifiers for risk or legal cases, and free-form notes that help governance teams understand the context. When null, no explicit justification was recorded at creation time.

status.description:
Current status of the override, such as "pending", "active", or "expired".

Business workflows use this status to control whether the override participates in policy evaluation and to drive approval, review, or retirement processes. Implementations commonly constrain this to a finite set of values enforced at the application level.

effective_from.description:
Datetime from which the override should start applying.

When set, this timestamp defines the lower bound of the period in which the override is considered during policy evaluation. A null value indicates that the override becomes effective immediately upon creation or activation according to business rules.

effective_until.description:
Datetime after which the override should no longer apply.

When present, this timestamp defines the upper bound for the override's applicability window. Policy engines ignore the override for evaluations occurring after this point. A null value represents an indefinite override that must be manually revised or retired.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the policy override was created.

This value is set by the system when the row is inserted into shopping_mall_policy_overrides and remains immutable thereafter. It is used in administrative views, audit trails, and time-based reporting of governance activities.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the policy override was last updated.

The system updates this value whenever mutable fields on the override change. It supports audit use cases, conflict detection, and tooling that needs to track recent configuration changes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the policy override.

When set, the override is considered inactive and should not be used in active policy evaluation, but the row remains stored for historical analysis and legal audit. A null value indicates that the override is logically present and may still affect system behavior subject to its status and effective window.

IShoppingMallPolicyOverride.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for listing policy override records in administrative contexts.

This DTO is used as the request body for PATCH-based index operations that retrieve paginated lists of policy override summaries from the `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` table.

It allows administrators and governance tools to specify filters such as subject type, subject identifier, status, and effective periods, together with pagination and sorting controls, so that they can efficiently locate relevant overrides across the marketplace.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve in the paginated result set.

This value is typically 1-based and works together with `limit` to determine the offset when querying policy override records.

If omitted, the implementation may default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of policy override records to return in a single page.

Administrators can use this field to control list density in grid views while the backend enforces an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

If not specified, the service applies a sensible default that balances usability and performance.

status.description:
Optional filter for the lifecycle status of policy overrides, such as `pending`, `active`, or `expired`.

When provided, the search operation returns only overrides whose `status` matches the given value, enabling governance teams to focus on currently active or pending entries.

If null or omitted, overrides of any status may be included, depending on other filters and soft deletion behavior.

subject_type.description:
Optional filter for the subject type to which overrides apply, for example `seller`, `customer`, `product`, `order`, or `global`.

By specifying this field, administrators can narrow search results to overrides targeting a particular domain, such as seller-related exceptions or order-level risk adjustments.

If left null, overrides for all subject types are eligible for inclusion in the result set.

subject_id.description:
Optional filter for the specific subject identifier.

When provided, only overrides whose `subject_id` matches the given UUID are returned, which is useful for inspecting all exceptions that affect a particular seller, customer, order, or product.

If null, the search is not constrained to a single subject and may return overrides across many entities.

override_code.description:
Optional filter for the override code indicating which policy dimension is being overridden.

Typical examples include tokens like `refund_window`, `commission_rate`, or `sla_threshold`, and filtering by this value helps administrators find all overrides affecting the same business rule.

If omitted or null, overrides for any code are considered.

effective_from_from.description:
Lower bound for the effective-from date filter.

When specified, only overrides whose `effective_from` is greater than or equal to this timestamp—or whose effective period logically overlaps this lower bound—are included.

This helps governance staff focus on overrides that became active after a particular point in time.

effective_from_to.description:
Upper bound for the effective-from date filter.

Used together with `effective_from_from`, this field limits results to overrides that became effective on or before the given timestamp, supporting time-window based investigations.

If null, no explicit upper limit is imposed on the effective-from date.

effective_until_from.description:
Lower bound for the effective-until date filter.

This field allows administrators to search for overrides whose configured end dates fall after or at the specified timestamp, which is useful when reviewing overrides that are expiring or recently expired.

If null, the search does not enforce a lower constraint on `effective_until`.

effective_until_to.description:
Upper bound for the effective-until date filter.

When set, only overrides whose `effective_until` is less than or equal to this timestamp—or that logically intersect this upper limit—are considered in the result set.

If null, there is no explicit upper bound on the effective-until date in the applied filters.

created_from.description:
Lower bound for filtering overrides by creation timestamp.

Overrides whose `created_at` is greater than or equal to this value are eligible for inclusion, allowing governance teams to focus on overrides created after a certain date.

If null, there is no minimum creation time constraint.

created_to.description:
Upper bound for filtering overrides by creation timestamp.

Only overrides with `created_at` less than or equal to this timestamp are returned, which is helpful for retrospective reviews over a fixed historical period.

If null, the search does not enforce an upper limit on creation time.

IShoppingMallPolicyOverride.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a policy override configuration within the shopping mall governance system.

This DTO is tailored for lightweight list responses, admin dashboards, and embedded references where only the key identification, subject scoping, associated base policy version, and high-level lifecycle status of an override are needed.

It maps directly to the `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` Prisma model for scalar fields and exposes the related business policy version as a summary association, while omitting low-level foreign key wiring details that are not required for summary views.

In addition to the nested policy version summary, this type also surfaces the underlying foreign key identifier so that administrative tools and reporting pipelines can filter, join, and trace overrides efficiently without always deserializing nested objects.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the policy override.

This maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` table and is used to reference the override in detail views, links, and subsequent administrative actions.

shopping_mall_policy_version_id.description:
Identifier of the underlying policy version that this override is based on.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_policy_version_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` Prisma model and references `shopping_mall_policy_versions.id`. It allows admin and analytics clients to filter, aggregate, and join overrides by the exact policy version without relying solely on nested objects.

Although the richer `policyVersion` association is typically used for display and context, this raw foreign key is essential for efficient querying, reporting, and cross-service integration where only identifiers are exchanged.

policyVersion.description:
Summary of the base policy version that this override is derived from.

This association replaces the raw foreign key in many read scenarios and allows admin tools to navigate from an override back to the underlying policy version document and its high-level rule definition without additional API calls.

The data is derived from the `shopping_mall_policy_versions` row referenced by `shopping_mall_policy_version_id` and typically includes identifying information such as version code, title, lifecycle status, and effective dates.

subject_type.description:
Type of subject to which the policy override applies.

Typical values include categories such as `seller`, `category`, `product`, or `global`, and determine which domain the override should be evaluated against when computing effective policy decisions. Governance workflows and risk engines use this field to route the override to the correct evaluation pipeline.

subject_id.description:
Identifier of the specific subject entity when the override targets a concrete object.

This value points to the domain entity (for example, a seller or category) associated with the override. It is null for global overrides that apply platform-wide or to an entire subject type without a single concrete instance.

Consumers can use this field to trace which concrete account, product, or category is impacted by the override when subject_type denotes an entity-level target.

subject_display.description:
Human-friendly representation of the subject governed by this override.

Examples include a seller name, a category path, or a product title, and the field is intended to simplify scanability in admin consoles and audit reports without requiring a join to the underlying domain table at read time.

Because this value is denormalized and informational, it should not be used as the only key for programmatic joins or decisions; instead, combine it with `subject_id` and `subject_type` when needed.

override_code.description:
Code or key identifying the specific aspect of the policy that is being overridden.

Business logic uses this code to decide which configuration knob or rule the override should replace, such as refund windows, commission rates, score thresholds, or SLA targets. The combination of `subject_type`, `subject_id`, and `override_code` uniquely identifies which rule segment is impacted for a given subject.

override_value.description:
Business-level value to apply in place of the default policy configuration.

The value is stored as text to allow flexible interpretation by application logic; typical interpretations include numbers, durations, percentages, or enumerated flags that are resolved based on the associated `override_code`. Policy evaluation engines must validate and cast this value to the appropriate type at runtime based on the policy definition.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the policy override.

Examples include values such as `pending`, `active`, or `expired`, and they control whether the override should be considered when evaluating effective policy at runtime. Administrative workflows and dashboards rely on this field to track approval state, scheduling, and retirement of overrides.

effective_from.description:
Datetime from which this override should be considered active, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When null, the override is effective immediately from creation once its status allows it. When set, evaluation engines must compare the current time against this boundary before applying the override so that future-dated overrides do not accidentally influence current decisions.

effective_until.description:
Datetime after which this override should no longer be applied, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

A null value indicates that the override has no scheduled end and remains valid until explicitly changed or removed. When set, the override is treated as inactive after this timestamp for policy evaluation purposes and should typically appear in dashboards as expired or past-due for review.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the policy override was created, stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This is used primarily for audit, ordering in admin list views, and investigation of configuration history. It reflects when the override row was first persisted in the `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the policy override record was last modified, stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

The value allows clients and auditors to understand when the latest change to the override occurred and can be used for optimistic concurrency control, configuration drift detection, and change history analysis.

IShoppingMallPolicyOverride.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new policy override in the shopping_mall_policy_overrides table.

Administrative governance and risk tools use this DTO to define explicit exceptions to default business policies for a specific subject, such as a seller, category, product, or global scope. The payload captures which policy version is being overridden, the subject identity and display information, the override code and value, the intended status at creation, and the optional effectiveness window and justification.

Server-managed fields such as the primary key, creator admin id, timestamps, and soft deletion flag are not accepted from the client and are populated automatically by the service layer based on the authenticated admin and database behavior.

shopping_mall_policy_version_id.description:
Identifier of the base policy version being overridden.

The client must supply the UUID of an existing row in shopping_mall_policy_versions that represents the concrete version of a business policy whose behavior will be modified for the selected subject. The service validates that this policy version exists and is eligible for overrides before creating the record.

subject_type.description:
Type of subject to which the override applies, such as "seller", "category", "product", or "global".

The subject type determines how subject_id and subject_display will be interpreted by policy evaluation logic. Business agreements define which subject types are valid and how they map to underlying entities like accounts, catalog records, or campaigns.

subject_id.description:
Identifier of the specific subject entity when applicable.

For subject types that represent a concrete entity instance (such as a particular seller, category, product, customer, or order), this field carries the UUID or primary key for that entity. For global or non-instance-specific overrides, this field may be null.

subject_display.description:
Human-friendly representation of the subject, such as a seller name or category path.

Providing this string improves the usability of admin consoles and governance dashboards by avoiding extra joins when listing overrides. Typical values include seller display names, category breadcrumbs, or campaign labels.

override_code.description:
Code or key that identifies which aspect of the policy is being overridden.

Clients must use business-defined codes that correspond to the rule segment being changed, such as refund window identifiers, commission rule keys, review policy codes, or SLA threshold names. The service may validate the override_code against the selected policy version to prevent incompatible overrides.

override_value.description:
Business-level value that will be used in place of the default policy configuration.

The value is stored as text so it can represent numeric thresholds, percentages, JSON fragments, or enumerated modes depending on the referenced policy and override_code. Validation of the format and semantics is performed by policy-specific logic in the service layer.

reason.description:
Optional explanation of why this override is being created.

Administrators can include justification text, references to risk or legal cases, or other contextual notes that support later audits and reviews. When omitted or null, no explicit reason is stored beyond what can be inferred from related records.

status.description:
Initial status of the policy override, such as "pending" or "active".

The chosen status controls whether the override is immediately effective or awaits additional approval steps. The platform may restrict allowed values to a predefined set like "pending", "active", or "inactive" and enforce transitions through governance workflows.

effective_from.description:
Datetime from which the override should begin to apply.

Providing a value allows administrators to schedule overrides to take effect at a future point, for example to align with campaign start dates. When null, the override is considered effective immediately upon activation according to its status and business rules.

effective_until.description:
Datetime after which the override should stop applying.

This field is used to schedule automatic expiry of the override, supporting temporary campaigns or time-bounded risk adjustments. A null value indicates an open-ended override that remains active until explicitly updated or retired.

IShoppingMallPolicyOverride.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing policy override in the shopping_mall_policy_overrides table.

This DTO carries only fields that are allowed to change after creation, such as subject metadata, override configuration, reason text, status, and effective window. Immutable values like the primary key and creator admin information come from the existing row and the request context rather than from this payload.

Administrative clients use this schema together with the policyOverrideId path parameter to refine or retire overrides as business conditions change. All properties are optional so that callers can submit partial updates containing only the fields they intend to modify.

shopping_mall_policy_version_id.description:
Identifier of the base policy version being overridden.

When supplied, this value updates the policy version reference to a different row in shopping_mall_policy_versions, allowing the override to track a new default rule set. The service must validate that the referenced version exists and is compatible with the existing override configuration.

approved_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who approved this override, if approval is required.

Administrators or automated workflows may set this field when an override moves from a pending state to an approved or active state, or clear it if approval is revoked. The value should correspond to shopping_mall_admins.id.

subject_type.description:
Type of subject to which the override applies, such as "seller", "category", "product", or "global".

While typically stable, this field can be updated in exceptional cases where the override is re-scoped to a different subject classification. Business rules should constrain such changes to avoid creating inconsistent or ambiguous overrides.

subject_id.description:
Identifier of the specific subject entity when applicable.

Updating this field changes which concrete entity the override targets, for example switching from one seller or category to another. Implementations must ensure that the new subject is compatible with the subject_type and policy version.

subject_display.description:
Human-friendly representation of the subject, such as a seller name or category path.

Administrators may revise this value to keep display text aligned with current naming or structure. Changes here affect only how overrides appear in administrative tooling and do not alter policy logic.

override_code.description:
Code or key that identifies which aspect of the policy is being overridden.

Updating the code effectively retargets the override to a different rule segment within the associated policy. Governance processes should ensure that such changes are reviewed carefully, as they may significantly alter system behavior.

override_value.description:
Business-level value that will be used in place of the default policy configuration.

Admins or automated controls can adjust this value as circumstances change, such as tightening risk thresholds or changing commission percentages. The service validates the new value according to the semantics of the selected policy and override_code.

reason.description:
Optional explanation or updated justification for the override.

This field can be used to add new context, reference evolving risk or legal cases, or clear outdated notes. Maintaining accurate reasons helps support audits and governance reviews over the lifecycle of the override.

status.description:
Updated status of the policy override, such as "pending", "active", or "expired".

Status changes drive the operational lifecycle of the override and control whether it is considered during policy evaluation. Typical transitions include moving from pending to active upon approval or to expired when the override is retired.

effective_from.description:
Updated datetime from which the override should begin to apply.

Changing this value allows administrators to reschedule the start point of an override, either delaying effect or moving it earlier subject to business constraints. Setting it to null indicates that the override should be effective immediately upon activation.

effective_until.description:
Updated datetime after which the override should stop applying.

Administrators can extend, shorten, or remove an override's expiry based on evolving requirements. A null value removes any automatic end date so that retirement must occur through future updates.

IShoppingMallAdminNotification.description:
Administrator notification entity representing tasks, alerts, and operational messages directed to admin users within the shopping mall governance and operations domain.

Each record corresponds to a single notification row in the `shopping_mall_admin_notifications` table and is used to surface governance, risk, dispute, SLA, and configuration events to administrators. It holds assignment to a specific admin, classification fields such as type, status, and priority, as well as polymorphic linkage to risk cases, legal holds, and other related entities.

This DTO is used as the full-detail response type for read operations like `GET /shoppingMall/admin/adminNotifications/{adminNotificationId}` and after create/update operations. It intentionally exposes only business-meaningful, non-sensitive fields that exist on the underlying Prisma model.

id.description:
Primary key for the admin notification record.

This value uniquely identifies a notification in the `shopping_mall_admin_notifications` table and is used as the path parameter `adminNotificationId` in detail and update APIs.

It is generated by the database and is immutable after creation.

admin.description:
Administrator who should see or act on this notification.

This is a transformed belongs-to association derived from the `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_admins`.

The summary provides enough context (such as admin identity and display name) for governance UIs without requiring additional API calls.

relatedRiskCase.description:
Optional risk case context associated with this notification.

When present, this object summarizes the related `shopping_mall_risk_cases` row that originated or is linked to the notification, enabling quick navigation from the notification to the risk case.

It is `null` when the notification is not tied to a specific risk case.

relatedLegalHold.description:
Optional legal hold context associated with this notification.

When present, this object summarizes the related `shopping_mall_legal_holds` record, allowing administrators to understand and navigate to the legal hold that prompted the notification.

It is `null` when no legal hold is associated with the notification.

type.description:
Machine-readable type of the notification.

Typical values include codes such as `seller_approval_needed`, `refund_escalation`, `risk_sla_violation`, or other category-like identifiers.

These codes are used by backend logic and admin consoles to group, filter, and display notifications consistently.

title.description:
Short human-readable title summarizing the notification content.

This field is optimized for use in list views, inbox-style dashboards, and notification headers.

It should be concise but descriptive enough for admins to understand the nature of the alert at a glance.

body.description:
Optional detailed body text providing extended context, instructions, or additional information for the admin.

When present, this may contain multi-line, localized explanatory content describing the underlying event, required actions, or links to further documentation.

It is `null` for minimal notifications that rely solely on the title or for systems that attach external content instead of storing it inline.

status.description:
Current status of the notification from the admin perspective.

Common examples include `unread`, `read`, `archived`, or similar lifecycle values representing whether the notification has been reviewed or dismissed.

Business rules may constrain the valid status transitions; this DTO simply exposes the string stored in the database.

priority.description:
Optional business-level priority indicator for the notification.

Typical values can include `low`, `normal`, or `high`, enabling admin dashboards to sort or highlight important items.

When `null`, the notification is treated as having the default priority semantics for its type.

entity_type.description:
Optional polymorphic entity type associated with the notification.

Examples include values such as `seller`, `order`, `dispute`, or `risk_case`, indicating the domain object that the notification refers to.

The combination of `entity_type` and `entity_id` allows clients to construct deep links into the appropriate admin views.

entity_id.description:
Identifier of the associated business entity referenced by this notification.

When set together with `entity_type`, this field allows navigation to a specific record, such as an order, dispute, or account.

It is stored as a UUID and is `null` for notifications not tied to a particular entity.

entity_display.description:
Human-friendly label for the associated entity.

Typical values include an order number, case code, or seller name and are stored for quick reference in list and detail views.

This value is optional and may be `null` when not explicitly stored at creation time.

read_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin first marked or viewed this notification as read.

A `null` value indicates that the notification is currently considered unread.

The timestamp uses ISO 8601 `date-time` format in UTC and is managed by business logic invoked when admins open or acknowledge notifications.

archived_at.description:
Timestamp when the notification was archived or explicitly dismissed.

When populated, this signals that the notification should be hidden from standard active queues and only shown in archival or history views.

The value is `null` for notifications that are still active or have not been archived.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the notification record was created.

This marks the moment the underlying governance, risk, or operational event produced the notification in the system.

The value is stored in ISO 8601 `date-time` format in UTC and is set by the database or service layer at insert time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the notification was last updated.

Typical updates include changes to status, priority, or assignment-related fields.

The timestamp is maintained by the system and uses ISO 8601 `date-time` format in UTC.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the notification.

When non-null, the notification is excluded from normal list views but retained in the database for audit and compliance purposes.

The value is `null` for active records that have not been soft-deleted.

IShoppingMallAdminNotification.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying admin notifications in a flexible, body-based PATCH search API.

This DTO is used by operations such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/adminNotifications` and `PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/adminSearch/adminNotifications` to express complex criteria that would be cumbersome as query parameters.

It combines filtering, sorting, and pagination information so that admin consoles can construct rich inbox-style queries against the `shopping_mall_admin_notifications` table.

page.description:
Page index for paginated notification search results.

The first page is 1, and subsequent pages increment by 1. Combined with `limit`, this determines which slice of the ordered notifications is returned.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default such as page 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of notification summaries to return in a single page.

This controls page size for list views in admin consoles and should be capped by the server to a safe upper bound to avoid overly expensive queries.

When not provided, an implementation-specific default page size is applied.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Optional filter restricting results to notifications assigned to a specific admin.

When set, only notifications whose `shopping_mall_admin_id` matches this UUID are considered. This is typically the current authenticated admin.

If `null` or omitted, the backend may infer the admin from authentication context or return notifications based on broader role-level rules.

types.description:
Optional list of notification type codes to include in the result set.

Each item corresponds to values stored in the `type` column of `shopping_mall_admin_notifications`, such as `seller_approval_needed`, `refund_escalation`, or other domain-specific identifiers.

When provided, only notifications whose type is in this list are matched.

statuses.description:
Optional list of statuses to filter notifications by.

Common examples are `unread`, `read`, and `archived`, matching the `status` column in the underlying table.

Filtering by multiple statuses in a single request allows admins to build views such as "open and unread" notifications.

priorities.description:
Optional list of priority values to filter notifications on.

Values typically align with the `priority` column, for example `high`, `normal`, or `low`, and enable admins to focus on critical tasks.

Only notifications whose priority is in this list are included when the filter is present.

entity_type.description:
Optional filter for the polymorphic entity type associated with notifications.

Examples include `seller`, `order`, `dispute`, or `risk_case`, matching the `entity_type` column in the table.

When provided, only notifications linked to the specified entity type are returned, allowing focused views such as "order-related" alerts.

entity_id.description:
Optional filter for a specific entity identifier referenced by notifications.

When set together with or without `entity_type`, this restricts results to notifications whose `entity_id` equals the given UUID, such as all notifications associated with a particular order or case.

It is typically used by back-office tools to drill down into notifications around a single business record.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to human-readable fields such as title or body.

Implementations may use full-text indexes (for example, on the `title` column) to efficiently search notifications for matching keywords.

When omitted or `null`, no full-text filter is applied.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound for filtering notifications by creation timestamp.

Only notifications with `created_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 `date-time` value are returned when the filter is specified.

Useful for building time-windowed views, such as "notifications from the last 7 days".

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound for filtering notifications by creation timestamp.

When provided, only notifications with `created_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 `date-time` value are included.

Combined with `created_from`, this supports date-range filtering over the notification history.

order_by.description:
Optional field name to sort notifications by.

Common values include `created_at`, `priority`, or `status`, allowing admin dashboards to control the ordering of results.

If omitted or `null`, the backend should default to a sensible ordering, typically `created_at` descending to show the newest notifications first.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for ordered results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order and are applied in conjunction with `order_by`.

When not specified, the backend usually defaults to descending order to surface most recent or highest-priority notifications first.

IShoppingMallAdminNotification.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for administrator notifications stored in the shopping_mall_admin_notifications table.

This schema is used by privileged backend services and admin-facing tools to enqueue new notifications or tasks targeted at specific admin users. It captures all business-controllable fields that define the meaning and routing of a notification while excluding system-managed identifiers and audit timestamps.

The DTO focuses on describing who should receive the notification, what type of event or category it represents, its textual content, and optional polymorphic references to related governance entities such as risk cases or legal holds. It also exposes fields to control priority and classification so that admin consoles can sort and filter notifications effectively.

Creation time, update time, and soft-delete timestamps are managed by the database layer and therefore are not accepted in this request schema. The authenticated admin context comes from the caller's session and is validated by the authorization layer, but the target admin of the notification is explicitly identified by shopping_mall_admin_id in this DTO.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who should see or act on this notification.

This field maps directly to shopping_mall_admin_notifications.shopping_mall_admin_id and must reference an existing row in shopping_mall_admins. It determines the ownership and visibility of the notification in admin dashboards.

The value is a UUID string and is required so that the platform can route the notification to the correct administrative user.

related_risk_case_id.description:
Optional reference to a related risk case for quick navigation from the admin notification.

When provided, this value must contain the UUID of an existing record in shopping_mall_risk_cases. It allows governance and risk teams to click through from the notification to the underlying risk case that triggered it.

Set to null or omit this field when the notification is not tied to a specific risk case.

related_legal_hold_id.description:
Optional reference to a related legal hold associated with this notification.

When present, the value is the UUID of a row in shopping_mall_legal_holds, enabling direct navigation from the notification to the legal hold context. This is typically used for compliance and data preservation workflows.

Set to null or omit this field if the notification is unrelated to legal hold activity.

type.description:
Machine-readable type of the notification such as "seller_approval_needed", "refund_escalation", or "risk_sla_violation".

This value allows backend services and admin UIs to categorize notifications, apply specialized rendering, and trigger automation rules. It should be stable and controlled by the platform, not free-form user input.

Typical values follow a lower_snake_case or lowerCamelCase convention agreed across governance and operations teams.

title.description:
Short human-readable title summarizing the notification content.

The title is displayed prominently in admin notification lists and detail views to help administrators quickly understand the purpose of the notification.

It should be concise yet descriptive, typically limited to a single sentence or phrase.

body.description:
Optional detailed body text providing context, instructions, or additional information for the admin.

Use this field to explain what action is required, provide background on the underlying case, or describe the impact of the event that generated the notification.

When not needed, this field may be null or omitted, leaving the title and type to convey the primary meaning.

status.description:
Initial status of the notification from the admin perspective, such as "unread", "read", or "archived".

This field determines how the notification appears in admin dashboards at creation time, for example whether it is counted as a new unread item or already marked as processed.

Business logic should validate that the provided status value matches an allowed set of states configured for admin notifications.

priority.description:
Optional business-level priority indicator such as "low", "normal", or "high".

Priority values help admin consoles sort and highlight notifications that require urgent attention, such as critical risk alerts or SLA breaches.

When omitted or null, the system may default to a standard priority level defined by the platform configuration.

entity_type.description:
Optional polymorphic entity type associated with the notification, for example "seller", "order", "dispute", or "risk_case".

Combined with entity_id and entity_display, this field enables deep linking from the notification to arbitrary domain entities without hard-coding relationships for every model.

Set to null or omit this field if the notification is purely informational and not bound to a specific entity type.

entity_id.description:
Identifier of the associated entity referenced by this notification.

When entity_type is provided, this UUID should identify a specific record within that domain, allowing the admin console to navigate directly to the related resource.

If the notification is not tied to a single entity, this field may be null or omitted.

entity_display.description:
Human-friendly label for the associated entity such as a name, code, or concise descriptor.

This value is stored redundantly to support quick display in notification lists without needing to resolve the entity on every request, improving performance and resilience.

Typical examples include an order number, seller display name, or risk case code; it may be null if no meaningful label is available.

read_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when the notification should initially be considered read.

In most cases, new notifications are created as unread and this field is left null, letting the system fill it when an admin views or marks the item as read.

For migration or backfill scenarios, a value may be supplied to align imported notifications with existing read state history.

archived_at.description:
Optional timestamp marking when the notification was archived or dismissed.

Normally this field is controlled by administrative actions after creation time and remains null for active notifications.

It can be set during creation only for special backfill or migration cases where historical archive state must be preserved.

IShoppingMallAdminNotification.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for administrator notifications in the shopping_mall_admin_notifications table.

This schema represents the set of mutable fields that admins or internal services may change on an existing notification record. It is used by update operations that adjust presentation state, content, and routing metadata without altering system-managed identifiers or audit timestamps.

Typical use cases include marking a notification as read or archived, changing its priority, updating descriptive text, or modifying links to related entities such as risk cases or legal holds. All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates, supplying only the fields that need to change.

The schema deliberately excludes immutable columns such as the primary key and creation timestamp, as well as the hard deletion marker, to preserve data integrity and auditability.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who should see or act on this notification.

Updating this field effectively reassigns the notification to a different admin account, which may be permitted in workflows where tasks are handed off between administrators.

When provided, the value must be a valid UUID referencing an existing shopping_mall_admins record; when null, the assignment may be cleared depending on business rules.

related_risk_case_id.description:
Optional reference to a related risk case for quick navigation from the notification.

Updates to this field can attach or detach the notification from a risk case maintained in shopping_mall_risk_cases, enabling governance teams to keep relationships in sync as cases evolve.

Set to null to remove an existing risk case association when it is no longer relevant.

related_legal_hold_id.description:
Optional reference to a related legal hold record.

Modifying this field allows administrators to link or unlink the notification from an entry in shopping_mall_legal_holds, supporting legal workflows that require tracking which notifications correspond to preserved data.

Use null to clear the association if the legal hold relationship should be removed.

type.description:
Machine-readable type of the notification, such as "seller_approval_needed" or "risk_sla_violation".

Changing this value should be done cautiously, as it impacts how the notification is categorized and may influence automation rules in governance tooling.

When set to null, business logic may either disallow the change or treat it as a reset to a default type, depending on platform rules.

title.description:
Short human-readable title summarizing the notification content.

Admins or automated processes may update the title to reflect new context or to clarify the required action as a case progresses.

Setting this field to null may be interpreted as clearing the title, although many UIs expect a non-empty title and may enforce additional validation.

body.description:
Detailed body text providing context, instructions, or additional information for the admin.

This field can be updated to reflect new information, extended guidance, or resolution details linked to the underlying governance event.

Supplying null clears the existing body text when it is no longer necessary or should be hidden.

status.description:
Current status of the notification from the admin perspective, such as "unread", "read", or "archived".

Status transitions implement the core lifecycle of admin notifications, controlling how items appear in queues, badge counts, and dashboards.

Business rules should validate that requested status changes are allowed, especially for terminal states that may not be reversible.

priority.description:
Business-level priority indicator for the notification, for example "low", "normal", or "high".

Updating the priority allows admins or automation to escalate or de-escalate items based on evolving risk, customer impact, or SLA considerations.

Providing null may clear an explicit priority and revert to a default behavior configured elsewhere in the system.

entity_type.description:
Polymorphic entity type associated with the notification such as "seller", "order", or "dispute".

Changes to this field adjust how the notification is interpreted and which domain object it points to when entity_id is set.

Setting it to null disassociates the notification from a specific entity type while leaving other content intact.

entity_id.description:
Identifier of the associated entity that the notification refers to.

When updated alongside entity_type, this field redirects the notification's deep link in admin UIs to a different domain object, such as another order, seller, or risk case.

A null value removes the direct entity linkage, making the notification informational without a specific target record.

entity_display.description:
Human-friendly label for the associated entity such as an order number, seller name, or risk case code.

This denormalized field can be refreshed when the underlying entity's display name changes, keeping notification listings accurate without additional lookups.

Supplying null clears the label when it is no longer applicable or should not be shown.

read_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin first marked or viewed this notification as read.

Update operations may set this to the current time when an admin reads the notification, or clear it (set to null) if the system supports reverting to an unread state under specific conditions.

Values must be valid ISO 8601 date-time strings in UTC or a consistent platform time zone.

archived_at.description:
Timestamp when the notification was archived or explicitly dismissed by an admin.

Setting this field allows workflows to move notifications out of active queues and into historical views while preserving full audit history.

A null value represents an active, non-archived notification that is still visible in normal admin dashboards.

IShoppingMallAdminGovernanceOverview.description:
Aggregated governance overview dashboard for shoppingMall administrators.

Represents a read-only, computed DTO that consolidates key governance, compliance, and operational health metrics for the shoppingMall platform. It is primarily derived from multiple snapshot and primary Prisma models, including platform KPI snapshots, order and revenue statistics, refund and dispute statistics, legal hold records, and admin audit logs.

The structure is optimized for admin console dashboards, providing high-level KPIs, recent trend snippets, and governance indicators in a single payload without exposing raw transactional data.

platformKpis.description: High-level platform KPIs summarizing marketplace health over a recent reporting window, typically derived from shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.

orderStats.description: Aggregated order volume and revenue statistics over recent days, computed from shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.

refundAndDisputeStats.description: Aggregated refund and dispute metrics over a recent period, derived from shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.

legalHoldStats.description: Summary of active legal holds and targeted entities, based on shopping_mall_legal_holds and shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets.

adminActivityStats.description: Recent administrative activity indicators and counts based on shopping_mall_admins, shopping_mall_admin_roles, shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments, and shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this governance overview snapshot was generated on the server side, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

IShoppingMallPlatformKpisSummary.description:
High-level platform KPI snapshot segment for the admin governance overview.

This DTO represents a compact view of key marketplace-wide metrics such as active customers and sellers, gross merchandise volume (GMV), and order counts over a specific reporting window. It is designed to power top-of-page KPI tiles and summary sections in administrative dashboards.

The values surfaced here are typically derived from precomputed snapshot tables (for example, `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`) and related analytical aggregates. Implementations may compute the metrics in near real-time or batch them periodically, but the API consumer can treat this object as a read-only summary of the current or requested platform health window.

Client applications should use `periodStart` and `periodEnd` to label charts and KPI tiles, and treat all metric fields as scoped strictly to that window. When building trend views or comparing multiple windows, multiple instances of this DTO can be fetched or stored over time.

periodStart.description:
Inclusive start timestamp of the reporting window for which these platform KPIs were calculated.

The timestamp MUST be expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (for example, `2025-11-17T00:00:00Z`). Implementations commonly use UTC for consistency across regions, but a well-defined platform reporting timezone may also be used as long as it is documented consistently.

All KPI metrics in this object should be interpreted as covering events that occur on or after this timestamp.

periodEnd.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the reporting window for which these platform KPIs were calculated.

The timestamp MUST be expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format and is treated as an upper bound that is not included in the interval (that is, `[periodStart, periodEnd)`). Most implementations will align this with day boundaries or standard reporting cutoffs.

Consumers can safely assume that events with timestamps greater than or equal to `periodEnd` are not included in the aggregated metrics reported by this DTO.

activeCustomerCount.description:
Number of active customers within the reporting window.

"Active" is defined by business rules, typically customers that have shown meaningful activity such as logging in, creating or updating carts, placing orders, or performing other tracked interactions. The precise definition should remain consistent across all analytics that expose this value.

This metric is useful for understanding recent engagement breadth on the customer side of the marketplace during the specified time range.

activeSellerCount.description:
Number of active sellers within the reporting window.

Active sellers are those who have exhibited meaningful operational activity, such as updating inventory, publishing or modifying products, accepting or fulfilling orders, or meeting other seller-activity thresholds defined by the business.

This metric helps administrators assess the health and participation level of the supply side of the marketplace over the same reporting window used for customer KPIs.

orderCount.description:
Total number of confirmed customer orders created in the reporting window.

Only orders that have reached a business-defined "confirmed" or equivalent state should be counted here. Draft carts, failed checkouts, or fully cancelled attempts that never became valid orders are typically excluded from this count.

This value is frequently used as a baseline volume indicator for sales activity during the specified time range.

grossMerchandiseVolume.description:
Total gross merchandise volume (GMV) for the reporting window, expressed in the platform’s base currency.

GMV typically represents the sum of item-level or order-level amounts before platform commissions, fees, and external payment charges. Discounts, promotions, and taxes may be included or excluded based on the platform’s chosen GMV definition, but the behavior must be consistent across all analytics endpoints.

This value is intended for high-level revenue and sales health monitoring and should not be used as a replacement for detailed financial accounting reports.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency used for GMV and other monetary KPIs reported in this object.

Most shoppingMall deployments will use a single platform base currency (for example, `"USD"` or `"KRW"`) for all aggregated KPIs, even if individual orders span multiple currencies internally. If multi-currency support is implemented, values in this DTO should reflect a normalized reporting currency and be clearly documented.

Clients should treat this code as the authoritative currency label when displaying monetary values from this summary.

IShoppingMallOrderStatsSummary.description:
Aggregated order volume and revenue statistics segment for the admin governance overview.

This DTO provides a compact summary of total order counts and revenue over a primary reporting window, such as "today", the last 24 hours, or a configurable custom period. It is typically used to feed high-level tiles and summary panels in administrative dashboards.

In addition to the headline totals, the DTO may optionally include a short time series of daily statistics through `recentDailyStats`. This allows client applications to render lightweight sparkline charts or trend indicators without making separate analytics queries.

Underlying data is usually derived from snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats` or equivalent analytical materializations, rather than from raw transactional tables on every request.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of customer orders in the primary reporting window.

Only orders that meet the platform’s definition of a valid, confirmed order should be included. Canceled or rejected orders may or may not be counted depending on the chosen business rule, but that rule must be applied consistently for all usages of this DTO.

This value is intended for quick at-a-glance understanding of recent order volume and may be complemented by the per-day breakdown in `recentDailyStats` when provided.

totalRevenue.description:
Total order revenue accumulated in the primary reporting window, denominated in the platform’s base currency.

This figure typically represents the sum of order-level payable amounts or a similar high-level revenue definition, and may differ from GMV if the platform distinguishes between gross merchandise volume and recognized revenue.

The exact composition of this metric (for example, tax inclusion, discount handling, and fee treatment) should match the platform’s standard revenue analytics semantics and remain consistent across dashboard views.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency used for `totalRevenue` and any revenue values implied by this summary.

Most platforms will use a single base reporting currency for this DTO. If the underlying orders are multi-currency, the amounts exposed here should already be normalized into this reporting currency using a consistent conversion policy.

Client applications should display this code alongside monetary figures to avoid ambiguity when dashboards are used across different locales.

recentDailyStats.description:
Optional short time-series of daily order statistics used for trend visualization.

Each element is a single-day aggregate represented by `IShoppingMallOrderDailyStatPoint` and is typically ordered from the oldest date to the most recent date. The length of the series is intentionally kept small (for example, the last 7–30 days) to keep responses lightweight for dashboard usage.

This array may be omitted entirely when the client does not request trend data or when the backend is configured to return only headline metrics. When present, clients should treat it as complementary context for `totalOrders` and `totalRevenue`, not as an exact reconciliation source for those totals.

IShoppingMallOrderDailyStatPoint.description:
Single daily data point for order statistics used in governance and analytics dashboards.

This DTO represents an aggregated snapshot of order activity for one calendar date. It is commonly sourced from precomputed tables such as `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats` or other daily snapshot mechanisms, ensuring efficient retrieval for time-series charts.

Instances of this type are typically consumed as part of small time-series collections (for example, within `recentDailyStats` of `IShoppingMallOrderStatsSummary`) to show short-term trends in order volume and revenue.

date.description:
Calendar date that this aggregated data point represents.

The value MUST be expressed in ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` format. The date is interpreted in the platform’s reporting timezone, which may be UTC or a specific business timezone.

All orders contributing to `orderCount` and `revenue` for this point should fall within this reporting date according to the chosen cutoff rules.

orderCount.description:
Total number of customer orders associated with the given reporting date.

Only orders that satisfy the platform’s definition of a valid, counted order for daily statistics should be included. This typically excludes drafts and failed checkouts and may optionally exclude certain cancelled or test orders based on configuration.

This value is primarily used for charting daily volume trends and for quick comparisons across consecutive dates.

revenue.description:
Total order revenue associated with the given reporting date, expressed in the platform’s base reporting currency.

The metric should follow the same revenue definition that is used across other order analytics (for example, whether taxes, discounts, and fees are included). When used in conjunction with other analytics DTOs, this consistency ensures that charts and summary totals align.

Client applications typically use this value to render revenue trend lines or bar charts over a sequence of dates.

IShoppingMallRefundAndDisputeStatsSummar.description:
Aggregated refund and dispute metrics segment for the admin governance overview.

Derived from shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats and related analytical sources, providing high-level insight into refund and dispute activity over the current reporting period and, optionally, recent trends.

totalRefundCount.description: Total number of refund operations executed in the primary reporting window.

totalRefundAmount.description: Total amount refunded during the primary reporting window, in the platform's base currency.

totalDisputeCount.description: Total number of disputes opened in the primary reporting window.

refundRate.description: Refund rate expressed as a ratio or percentage of refunds relative to total orders in the reporting window, as defined by business rules. For example, 0.05 may represent a 5% refund rate.

disputeRate.description: Dispute rate expressed as a ratio or percentage of disputes relative to total orders in the reporting window.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency used for monetary refund values.

IShoppingMallLegalHoldStatsSummary.description:
Aggregated legal hold statistics segment for the admin governance overview dashboard.

This DTO provides high-level counts that describe how many legal holds are currently active, how many have been recently closed, and how many distinct entities are presently affected by at least one legal hold.

The values are derived from governance and compliance tables such as `shopping_mall_legal_holds` and `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets`, and are intended for at-a-glance monitoring by operations, legal, and compliance teams rather than for low-level record inspection.

activeLegalHoldCount.description:
Total number of legal holds that are currently active at the time this statistics snapshot is generated.

The value represents a non-negative integer count of open legal holds that still prevent deletion or alteration of the associated data for compliance, investigation, or regulatory reasons.

recentlyClosedLegalHoldCount.description:
Number of legal holds that moved to a closed or resolved state within the primary reporting window (for example, today or the last 24 hours).

This metric helps governance and legal teams understand closure throughput and whether the backlog of legal holds is trending up or down over the chosen analysis period.

affectedEntityCount.description:
Total number of distinct entities (such as customers, sellers, admins, orders, or other domain objects) that are currently under at least one active legal hold.

The value is typically computed by aggregating and de-duplicating records from `shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets` and provides a quick indication of how broadly legal holds are impacting the platform at the snapshot time.

IShoppingMallAdminActivityStatsSummary.description:
Aggregated administrator activity statistics segment for the admin governance overview dashboard.

This DTO summarizes how many administrator accounts exist, how many are recently active, and how much administrative activity has been recorded in the audit logs over a defined reporting window.

The values are conceptually derived from administrator and governance tables such as `shopping_mall_admins`, `shopping_mall_admin_roles`, `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`, and `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs`, and are used to monitor governance workload, security-relevant actions, and capacity planning for the admin team.

totalAdminCount.description:
Total number of administrator accounts that exist in the platform at the time this statistics snapshot is produced.

This non-negative integer includes both currently active and inactive admins and typically changes slowly as new administrators are onboarded or removed.

activeAdminCount.description:
Number of administrator accounts that have been active within a defined recent-activity window, such as the last few hours or the current day.

Activity is usually determined from authentication events or audit log entries and is used to understand how many admins are concurrently participating in operational and governance tasks.

recentAuditEventCount.description:
Total number of administrator audit log events recorded within the primary reporting window (for example, today or the last 24 hours).

This metric reflects the overall volume of administrative actions captured in `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs` and provides a coarse measure of governance workload and configuration change frequency.

highSeverityAuditEventCount.description:
Number of audit log events within the reporting window that are categorized as high severity or critical.

These events typically correspond to sensitive operations such as role changes, policy overrides, or security-related actions, and the count helps governance and security teams quickly assess whether unusual or risk-heavy activity has occurred during the analysis period.

IShoppingMallAdminRiskOverview.description:
Aggregated risk overview dashboard for shoppingMall administrative and risk management users.

This DTO is a read-only, computed snapshot that consolidates the most important fraud and risk posture indicators into a single response for governance and risk teams. It does not map to a single Prisma table; instead, it composes metrics from risk case headers, risk case events, risk rules, policy overrides, refund and dispute statistics, and daily behavioral snapshots for customers and sellers.

Each top-level segment represents a focused analytical view over a subset of the risk domain:
- `riskCaseStats` summarizes the current and recent state of risk or fraud cases stored in `shopping_mall_risk_cases` and their timelines in `shopping_mall_risk_case_events`.
- `riskRuleStats` surfaces configuration-level indicators about risk rules and policy overrides defined in `shopping_mall_risk_rules` and `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`.
- `refundAndDisputeRiskStats` highlights abnormal refund, dispute, and chargeback activity derived from `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` and related payment/dispute analytics.
- `actorAnomalyStats` provides high-level anomaly counts for customers and sellers, based on behavioral snapshots in `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` and `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`.
- `campaignRiskStats` (when present) adds campaign-related risk signals computed from `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` and platform-level KPI snapshots.

The `generatedAt` field marks the exact moment the dashboard snapshot was produced on the server, allowing clients to reason about data freshness and caching. All segment DTOs referenced here are aggregates that can be computed repeatedly from underlying risk and analytics tables without exposing raw transactional detail, making this DTO suitable for admin consoles and monitoring dashboards.

riskCaseStats.description: Summary of open and recently closed risk cases, broken down by status or severity, derived from `shopping_mall_risk_cases` and `shopping_mall_risk_case_events`. This segment focuses on how many risk cases exist, how severe they are, and how quickly they are being resolved within the current reporting window.

riskRuleStats.description: Indicators about configured risk rules and policy overrides, based on `shopping_mall_risk_rules` and `shopping_mall_policy_overrides`. This segment helps administrators understand how many rules are active or disabled and how often default policy behavior is overridden in production.

refundAndDisputeRiskStats.description: Risk-oriented view of refund, dispute, and chargeback activity derived from `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` and related payment/dispute analytics tables. It highlights abnormal rates or spikes that can indicate emerging fraud patterns or systemic issues in order handling.

actorAnomalyStats.description: High-level anomaly indicators for customers and sellers computed from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` and `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`. This segment surfaces how many actors are currently flagged as anomalous or high-risk and how many have transitioned into that state in the most recent analysis window.

campaignRiskStats.description: Optional metrics summarizing campaign-related risk signals and anomalous behavior, derived from `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` and platform KPI snapshots. This segment is typically populated when marketing or pricing campaigns are active and campaign-level analytics are enabled; it may be omitted in environments where campaigns or campaign analytics are not configured.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this risk overview snapshot was generated on the server side, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). Consumers can use this value to assess data freshness, align the snapshot with other time-based analytics, and control client-side caching or auto-refresh behavior.

IShoppingMallRiskCaseStatsSummary.description:
Risk case statistics segment for the admin risk overview.

Provides aggregated counts and breakdowns of risk cases, such as open vs. closed and severity levels, based on shopping_mall_risk_cases and shopping_mall_risk_case_events.

openCaseCount.description: Total number of currently open risk cases across the platform.

recentlyClosedCaseCount.description: Number of risk cases closed within the primary reporting window (for example, the last 24 hours).

highSeverityOpenCaseCount.description: Number of currently open risk cases that are classified as high severity according to risk case configuration.

mediumSeverityOpenCaseCount.description: Number of currently open risk cases classified as medium severity.

lowSeverityOpenCaseCount.description: Number of currently open risk cases classified as low severity.

IShoppingMallRiskRuleStatsSummary.description:
Indicators about risk rules and policy overrides for the admin risk overview.

This summary DTO provides a compact view of how the risk engine is configured at a given point in time. It reports how many rules exist in total, how many are active in production, how many are disabled, and how many explicit policy overrides are in effect.

The metrics are derived from configuration entities such as the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` and `shopping_mall_policy_overrides` tables. They help risk and governance teams understand whether the rule set is sufficiently rich, whether there are many dormant or experimental rules, and how heavily the platform depends on ad‑hoc overrides.
