Only snapshot rows whose `stats_date` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. The value should represent the start of the reporting window, usually normalized to midnight UTC for consistency with how snapshots are generated.

statsDateTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound for the stats_date range filter.

Only snapshot rows whose `stats_date` is less than or equal to this timestamp are included. Combined with `statsDateFrom`, this allows callers to search for customer daily stats over a specific reporting period such as a day, week, or month.

minOrderCount.description:
Minimum order_count threshold filter.

When specified, only snapshot rows where `order_count` is greater than or equal to this value are returned. This helps focus analytics on days with a minimum level of ordering activity.

maxOrderCount.description:
Maximum order_count threshold filter.

When specified, only snapshot rows where `order_count` is less than or equal to this value are returned. This can be combined with `minOrderCount` to define a closed interval for order volume.

minGmvAmount.description:
Minimum GMV amount threshold filter.

This filter applies to the `gmv_amount` metric (gross merchandise value) stored in the `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` snapshot table. Only rows whose `gmv_amount` is greater than or equal to this value are included. This is useful for identifying high-value customer-days based on gross merchandise value.

maxGmvAmount.description:
Maximum GMV amount threshold filter.

This filter applies to the `gmv_amount` metric (gross merchandise value) stored in the `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` snapshot table. Only rows whose `gmv_amount` is less than or equal to this value are returned. Combined with `minGmvAmount`, it supports range queries over GMV distributions.

minNmvaAmount.description:
Minimum NMV amount threshold filter.

This filter applies to the `nmv_amount` metric (net merchandise value) stored in the `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` snapshot table. Despite the historical `Nmva` spelling in the property name, it is explicitly intended to filter the `nmv_amount` field. Only rows whose `nmv_amount` is greater than or equal to this value are included, allowing analytics to focus on days with a minimum realized net revenue after refunds and cancellations.

maxNmvaAmount.description:
Maximum NMV amount threshold filter.

This filter applies to the `nmv_amount` metric (net merchandise value) from the `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` snapshot table. Although the property name contains `Nmva` for historical reasons, it is conceptually the upper-bound counterpart to `minNmvaAmount` for the `nmv_amount` field. Only rows whose `nmv_amount` is less than or equal to this value are included. Together with `minNmvaAmount`, this supports range filtering over net revenue per customer-day.

isNewCustomer.description:
Filter flag for acquisition-day snapshots.

When true, only snapshot rows where `is_new_customer` is true are included, so that the result set is restricted to the days on which customers were first acquired. When false, only non-acquisition days are returned. When omitted, no filter on acquisition status is applied.

hasRepeatOrders.description:
Filter flag for repeat-purchaser snapshots.

When true, only snapshot rows where `has_repeat_orders` is true are included, representing customers that have made at least two lifetime orders by that day. When false, only customers without repeat orders are returned. When omitted, no filter on repeat order status is applied.

page.description:
1-based index of the page of results to retrieve.

If omitted, implementations typically default to the first page. Combined with `limit`, this controls which slice of the overall result set is returned for large analytics queries.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot rows to return in a single page.

Clients should provide a sensible page size (for example, 20–100 rows) depending on UI needs. Implementations may enforce an upper bound to protect performance and prevent excessively large responses.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort the result set.

Common sort fields include `stats_date`, `gmv_amount`, `nmv_amount`, and `order_count`. Implementations should validate this value against an allowlist of sortable fields to avoid invalid or insecure sort expressions.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction applied to the field specified by `sortBy`.

Allowed values are typically `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the default is usually descending order by `stats_date`, so that the most recent days appear first in analytics dashboards.

IShoppingMallCustomerDailyStat.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a customer’s daily activity and value metrics on the shopping mall platform.

This summary DTO is intended for analytics dashboards, growth and retention monitoring tools, and background reporting systems that analyze customer behavior over time. It surfaces the most important KPIs from the `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` snapshot while staying compact enough for list and trend visualizations.

Use this type whenever you need per-customer, per-day statistics such as order volume, monetary contribution, engagement signals, and lifecycle markers (new versus repeat customers).

id.description:
Unique identifier of this customer daily stats snapshot row.

This UUID is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` table and uniquely identifies a single customer-date combination in the analytics store.

customer.description:
Summary view of the customer whose metrics are captured in this snapshot row.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key and provides inline context such as customer code, display name, and status for analytics dashboards and list views.

Consumers can still access the underlying customer identifier via `customer.id` while avoiding additional lookups for basic customer information.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which the customer metrics are calculated.

The analytics pipeline normalizes the time component to midnight UTC so that each snapshot represents a single calendar day. This field is suitable for grouping by date, building retention cohorts, and plotting customer-level time series.

order_count.description:
Number of orders created by this customer on this date.

Each order placed by the customer that is recorded on the stats date contributes to this count, regardless of whether it later completes payment or is cancelled.

paid_order_count.description:
Number of the customer’s orders that reached a paid state on this date.

This metric enables payment conversion analysis for the customer segment, and can differ from `order_count` when some orders remain unpaid or fail payment.

gmv_amount.description:
Total gross merchandise value of orders created by this customer on this date, expressed in the platform’s base currency.

GMV does not account for cancellations or refunds and therefore represents the top-line value of the customer’s purchase intent for the stats date.

nmv_amount.description:
Net merchandise value for this customer on this date after applying refunds or cancellations, expressed in the platform’s base currency.

This metric is derived from GMV minus cancelled and refunded amounts and more accurately reflects the realized merchandise value contributed by the customer.

refund_amount.description:
Total amount refunded to this customer on this date, in the platform’s base currency.

Refunds may relate to orders placed on different days; the metric is keyed solely by the date on which refund operations were executed. It is used for churn and dissatisfaction analysis as well as financial reconciliation.

cart_add_count.description:
Number of add-to-cart actions performed by this customer on this date.

This engagement metric captures interest and browsing behavior even when orders are not placed. Growth and product teams typically use it to understand funnel behavior and intent levels.

wishlist_add_count.description:
Number of wishlist-add actions performed by this customer on this date.

Wishlist additions reflect long-term interest and are useful for remarketing, campaign targeting, and understanding product affinity beyond immediate purchases.

session_count.description:
Number of authenticated sessions started by this customer on this date.

A session represents a period of authenticated interaction with the platform. This metric helps analyze activity frequency, stickiness, and engagement patterns over time.

is_new_customer.description:
Flag indicating whether the stats date is considered the customer’s acquisition date.

The analytics logic typically treats either the registration date or the date of the first order as the acquisition date. When this flag is true, downstream analytics can classify the customer as newly acquired for the stats date.

has_repeat_orders.description:
Flag indicating whether the customer has placed more than one order over their lifetime as of the end of this date.

This boolean is used to distinguish repeat customers from one-time purchasers and is central to retention and lifecycle analyses.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this customer daily stats snapshot row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

This marks when the metrics for the given customer and date were initially computed and stored. It helps operators understand data freshness and processing lag.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this customer daily stats snapshot row was last recomputed or corrected.

Backfills or corrections performed by analytics or ETL jobs update this timestamp, enabling consumers to track when historical metrics have been revised.

IShoppingMallCampaignMetric.description:
Analytics snapshot entity representing aggregated performance metrics for a single marketing or pricing campaign on a given calendar date.

Each row in this table corresponds to one campaign code and one stats_date combination and stores precomputed KPIs such as order counts, GMV and NMV amounts, and discount funding splits between platform and sellers. Records are generated and maintained by offline or near-real-time analytics pipelines, not by direct user input.

This DTO is used in read operations that expose detailed campaign metric snapshots to admin-facing analytics dashboards and reporting tools. It is strictly read-only from the API perspective and is never mutated directly by business workflows.

id.description:
Primary key for the campaign metrics snapshot row.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes a single snapshot record in the shopping_mall_campaign_metrics table, combining the campaign_code and stats_date pair plus any internal sequencing the analytics pipeline uses.

Clients can safely treat this as an opaque UUID that is stable over the lifetime of the snapshot record and use it as the lookup key in detail endpoints.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these campaign metrics are calculated.

Although only the date component is semantically meaningful, the value is stored as a full timestamp and SHOULD be normalized to midnight UTC by the analytics pipeline.

Consumers typically use this field to group or filter campaign metrics by day when constructing time-series charts or daily performance reports.

campaign_code.description:
Business identifier of the campaign associated with this metrics snapshot.

This value usually corresponds to a voucher code, campaign ID, or promotion key that is used by pricing and promotion engines when applying discounts.

Admin and analytics tools use campaign_code to join this snapshot to higher-level campaign configuration records and to filter metrics for specific campaigns.

order_count.description:
Number of orders on this stats_date that were affected by this campaign.

This count includes all orders where the campaign conditions were met and the campaign was recorded as contributing to the order, regardless of subsequent payment success or failure.

Use this together with paid_order_count to understand drop-off between campaign-attributed orders and actually paid orders.

paid_order_count.description:
Number of campaign-attributed orders on this stats_date that successfully reached a paid state.

Only orders that are considered financially completed according to the platform's payment lifecycle are counted here.

Comparing paid_order_count with order_count provides a measure of payment completion rate for the campaign on this date.

gmv_amount.description:
Gross merchandise value attributable to this campaign on this stats_date, before refunds.

GMV is represented in the platform base currency and typically reflects the sum of item-level or order-level amounts before any cancellations or refunds are applied.

Analytics users rely on this field to evaluate the absolute revenue scale driven by the campaign without considering post-purchase adjustments.

nmv_amount.description:
Net merchandise value attributable to this campaign on this stats_date after refunds or cancellations.

NMV is calculated by subtracting refunded or cancelled amounts from GMV, still expressed in the platform base currency.

This value provides a more realistic view of economic impact than GMV by accounting for returned or cancelled orders that reduce realized revenue.

discount_total_amount.description:
Total discount amount granted under this campaign on this stats_date.

This metric aggregates the absolute monetary value of all discounts the campaign applied to eligible orders, without distinguishing who funded the discount.

It is useful for understanding the total promotion cost associated with the campaign and evaluating ROI when compared against incremental NMV or other KPIs.

platform_funded_discount_amount.description:
Portion of discount_total_amount that is funded by the platform for this campaign on this stats_date.

This amount reflects how much promotional cost is borne directly by the marketplace or platform operator, as opposed to individual sellers.

Finance and marketing teams use this field to assess platform-level marketing spend and to reconcile with budget allocations or accruals.

seller_funded_discount_amount.description:
Portion of discount_total_amount that is funded by sellers for this campaign on this stats_date.

This value represents the aggregate monetary contribution of sellers toward discounts given under the campaign, often according to predefined funding rules or split ratios.

It allows the platform to analyze how promotion costs are shared and to design funding models that are sustainable for both the platform and participating sellers.

new_customer_order_count.description:
Number of paid orders under this campaign on this stats_date created by customers classified as new.

"New" is determined according to campaign attribution rules, for example customers with no prior paid orders or customers whose first order occurs within the campaign period.

This metric is especially important for acquisition-focused campaigns where success is measured by the ability to attract new customers rather than re-orders.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this campaign metrics snapshot row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

The value represents when the metrics were initially computed or ingested into the shopping_mall_campaign_metrics table.

Operations teams may use this to monitor pipeline freshness and to detect delayed or missing metric generation for specific dates or campaigns.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this campaign metrics snapshot row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

Updates may occur if late-arriving events, retroactive corrections, or pipeline fixes require the metrics to be recalculated for a given date and campaign.

Consumers should consider that earlier API responses might not reflect updated values until this timestamp changes, and may choose to refresh cached analytics views when updates are detected.

IShoppingMallCampaignMetric.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO used to retrieve paginated lists of campaign analytics metrics from the shopping_mall_campaign_metrics snapshot table.

Clients send this DTO in the body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/analytics/campaignMetrics operation to express complex search criteria, including campaign codes, date ranges, KPI thresholds, sorting preferences, and pagination controls.

The structure is designed for admin and analytics dashboards that require flexible exploration of campaign performance data while keeping the endpoint read-only and analytics focused.

page.description:
1-based index of the page of results to retrieve.

This controls which slice of the matching campaign metrics will be returned in the paginated response.

If omitted, the server should default to the first page, but clients are encouraged to send explicit values for clarity.

limit.description:
Maximum number of campaign metric summary records to return in a single page.

This value allows clients to tune the density of list views in analytics dashboards while preventing excessively large result sets.

Servers may impose an upper bound regardless of the requested value to protect performance and resource usage.

items.description:
Campaign business identifier to filter metrics by.

Each entry represents a campaign_code value as stored in the shopping_mall_campaign_metrics table.

When multiple codes are provided, the server should match any of them (logical OR) when selecting snapshot rows.

campaign_codes.description:
Optional list of campaign codes used to restrict the search to specific campaigns.

This filter is useful when analysts want to focus on a subset of campaigns, such as those associated with a particular marketing initiative or experiment.

When omitted or empty, metrics for all campaigns are eligible for inclusion subject to other filters.

oneOf.description:
Start of the stats_date filter range in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Although only the date component is semantically relevant, the server will typically normalize or interpret the value to include all snapshots on or after the given calendar date.

Use this together with date_to to restrict the search to a specific reporting window.

Indicates that no explicit lower bound on stats_date is applied.

When null, the server may use its own defaults, such as limiting the search to a recent time window for performance reasons, or it may allow the full historical range depending on system configuration.

Clients should set an explicit date_from when they need deterministic and repeatable filtering behavior.

date_from.description:
Lower inclusive boundary for the stats_date of campaign metrics to include in the search.

Specifying this field restricts results to snapshots whose stats_date is greater than or equal to the given value, usually interpreted at calendar-day granularity.

If omitted or null, no explicit lower date bound is enforced beyond any system-wide defaults.

oneOf.description:
End of the stats_date filter range in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The server typically interprets this as an inclusive upper bound, returning snapshots with stats_date less than or equal to the specified calendar date.

Combined with date_from, this allows clients to query metrics for custom date ranges such as weeks, months, or campaign periods.

Indicates that no explicit upper bound on stats_date is applied.

When null, the server may default to including only metrics up to the current date or may allow the full available history depending on system configuration.

Analytics UIs should send explicit bounds to avoid unintentionally large result sets.

date_to.description:
Upper inclusive boundary for the stats_date of campaign metrics to include in the search.

Specifying this filter constrains results so that only snapshots whose stats_date is less than or equal to the given value are returned.

If omitted or null, no explicit upper date bound is applied other than any global safety limits enforced by the implementation.

oneOf.description:
Minimum GMV threshold used to restrict campaign metrics by scale of gross merchandise value.

Snapshots whose gmv_amount is greater than or equal to this value in platform base currency will be eligible for inclusion.

This is useful for focusing analysis on campaigns that exceed a certain revenue contribution level.

Indicates that no explicit minimum GMV filter is applied.

When null, snapshot rows are not excluded based on gmv_amount alone, though other filters may still limit the result set.

Clients may omit or set this to null when they want to see all campaigns regardless of GMV magnitude.

min_gmv_amount.description:
Optional lower bound filter applied to the gmv_amount metric.

Use this when analysts want to exclude very low-volume or test campaigns from dashboard views, focusing instead on campaigns that reach meaningful revenue levels.

If omitted or null, GMV-based filtering is not applied.

oneOf.description:
Minimum number of new-customer paid orders required for a snapshot to be included in results.

Snapshots with new_customer_order_count greater than or equal to this value will match the filter.

This is valuable for acquisition-focused reporting where campaigns are evaluated based on their ability to bring in new customers.

Indicates that no explicit minimum new customer order count filter is applied.

When null, snapshots are not filtered on new_customer_order_count, and campaigns with zero or low acquisition may still be present in the results.

Clients can omit this field when they do not need acquisition-specific filtering.

min_new_customer_order_count.description:
Optional lower bound filter applied to the new_customer_order_count metric.

When set, this encourages the query to return only snapshots where the campaign generated at least the specified number of new-customer orders during the stats_date.

If omitted or null, no acquisition-based threshold is enforced.

oneOf.description:
Field name used to sort the resulting campaign metric summaries.

Typical values include stats_date, gmv_amount, nmv_amount, order_count, or new_customer_order_count, subject to the implementation's supported sort keys.

If an unsupported value is provided, the server should return a validation error to help the client correct the request.

Indicates that the server should apply its default sort order.

Common defaults include sorting by stats_date in descending order or by gmv_amount to highlight top-performing campaigns first.

Clients may omit or set this to null when comfortable with the system-defined default ordering.

sort_by.description:
Optional name of the field to use for sorting campaign metric summaries in the response.

This allows analytics UIs to present metrics ordered by recency, revenue, or other business-relevant dimensions.

If omitted or null, the implementation chooses a sensible default sort, often stats_date descending.

oneOf.description:
Direction in which to sort the results, either ascending or descending.

Common allowed values are "asc" and "desc", though the exact accepted literals are defined by the implementation.

When combined with sort_by, this controls whether, for example, the newest or oldest stats_date appears first.

Indicates that the server should use its default sort direction for the selected sort_by field.

Typically this is descending for date and amount fields so that the most recent or largest values appear at the top of the result list.

Clients can omit or set this to null when they do not need to override the default.

sort_direction.description:
Optional direction for sorting campaign metric summaries.

Together with sort_by, this provides fine-grained control over how analytics results are ordered in list views.

If omitted or null, the server applies a default direction appropriate for the chosen sort key.

IShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot.description:
Platform-level KPI snapshot entity for the shopping mall marketplace.

Each record represents an aggregated set of business KPIs over a specific reporting period, such as a day, week, month, or custom time window. The row stores metrics like GMV, NMV, platform revenue, order counts, active customer and seller counts, refund and chargeback statistics, and average order value.

Snapshots are generated and updated by background analytics pipelines, not by direct user interaction. They are used to power executive dashboards, operational monitoring views, and historical trend analyses, allowing admins to quickly understand marketplace health without executing heavy real-time aggregation queries.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this KPI snapshot record in the `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots` table.

The primary key is generated by the analytics pipeline when a new snapshot row is inserted. It is used as the stable reference for detail retrieval APIs and for internal joins to other analytics structures when needed.

period_type.description:
Type of reporting period this KPI snapshot covers, such as "day", "week", "month", or "custom".

The value determines how `period_start` and `period_end` should be interpreted and how snapshots are grouped in dashboards. Business logic and UI components typically use this field to filter or segment KPI data by aggregation granularity.

period_start.description:
Inclusive start timestamp of the reporting period summarized by this snapshot.

All contributing events (orders, payments, refunds, disputes and so on) are counted from this timestamp onward. It is expressed in a normalized time zone (for example UTC) according to platform-wide analytics conventions.

period_end.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the reporting period summarized by this snapshot.

No contributing events occur at or after this timestamp for the purposes of this row. Combined with `period_start`, it defines the exact window over which KPIs like order counts and GMV were computed.

gmv_amount.description:
Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) accumulated during the reporting period, in the platform's base currency.

GMV represents the total value of orders before refunds, cancellations, discounts, or chargebacks are applied. It is a primary measure of overall transaction volume flowing through the marketplace.

nmv_amount.description:
Net Merchandise Value (NMV) for the reporting period, in the platform's base currency.

NMV is typically derived from GMV by subtracting the monetary impact of refunds, cancellations, and other negative adjustments. It reflects realized merchandise value after post-order corrections.

platform_revenue_amount.description:
Total platform revenue recognized during the reporting period, expressed in the platform's base currency.

This amount usually includes commissions, platform-owned fees, subscription charges, advertising fees, and other revenue streams, net of any applied adjustments or revenue-related refunds.

take_rate.description:
Platform take rate for the reporting period.

The take rate is generally computed as `platform_revenue_amount / gmv_amount`. It is used by business stakeholders to understand the effective monetization level of the marketplace for the given time window.

order_count.description:
Number of successfully created orders within the reporting period.

This count includes all orders that reached the initial created state, regardless of later payment success or failure, and serves as a volume indicator for customer purchasing activity.

paid_order_count.description:
Number of orders that reached a paid or completed payment state during the reporting period.

This metric is often used to compute conversion ratios and to differentiate between simple order creation and successful payment capture.

active_customer_count.description:
Number of active customers during the reporting period based on configured activity rules.

Typical definitions include customers who created at least one session, placed an order, or performed other meaningful interactions on the platform. The precise criteria are governed by analytics business rules outside this entity.

new_customer_count.description:
Number of newly registered customer accounts during the reporting period.

This metric is used to track customer acquisition performance and growth, often segmented by marketing channel or campaign in higher-level analyses.

active_seller_count.description:
Number of active sellers during the reporting period according to seller activity rules.

Activity commonly includes having at least one paid order, updating product listings, or performing other defined interactions. This KPI helps measure marketplace supply-side engagement.

refund_request_count.description:
Total number of refund requests opened within the reporting period.

It reflects customer dissatisfaction and operational friction levels, and provides an input into refund rate calculations and support workload planning.

approved_refund_count.description:
Number of refund requests that were approved during the reporting period.

This count is used along with refund amounts to gauge effective refund volume, policy application, and potential revenue leakage.

refunded_amount.description:
Total refunded amount paid out during the reporting period, in the platform's base currency.

This includes amounts refunded to customers for all approved refund requests whose financial impact was realized within the snapshot window.

chargeback_count.description:
Number of chargeback cases recorded in the reporting period.

Chargebacks typically represent disputes initiated by payment providers or card issuers and are a strong signal for potential fraud or severe customer dissatisfaction.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total value of chargebacks recorded during the reporting period, in the platform's base currency.

The sum is used by risk and finance teams to quantify the monetary impact of chargebacks across the marketplace for the given window.

average_order_value.description:
Average order value (AOV) for the reporting period, calculated according to platform analytics rules.

A common definition is GMV divided by `paid_order_count`, but the exact formula can vary. AOV is widely used as a high-level indicator of purchasing behavior and pricing strategy effectiveness.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this KPI snapshot row was initially created by the analytics pipeline.

It records when the snapshot was first materialized and inserted into the database, which may be later than the reporting period end depending on batch processing and scheduling.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this KPI snapshot row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

Subsequent analytics jobs may update an existing snapshot to account for late-arriving events or corrections; this timestamp allows consumers to detect when KPI values were most recently refreshed.

IShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot.IReques.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying platform KPI snapshot records from `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`.

This DTO is used by admin-facing analytics APIs to express complex query parameters in the request body, including period type filters, time windows, pagination options, and sort preferences. It supports retrieving daily, weekly, monthly, or custom KPI snapshots over specified date ranges.

All fields are optional to allow flexible combinations of filters. Service-layer validation can enforce additional business rules, such as requiring at least one time-bound constraint for certain operations or restricting the size of requested windows for performance reasons.

items.description:
One of the supported period types stored in `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.period_type`, such as "day", "week", "month", or "custom".

Clients should only send values understood by the analytics pipeline. Unknown values should be rejected by server-side validation to avoid ambiguous filtering.

periodTypes.description:
Optional list of period types to include in the search.

When provided, only snapshots whose `period_type` matches one of the specified values are returned. If omitted, snapshots of all period types are eligible for selection.

periodStartFrom.description:
Lower bound for the `period_start` field of KPI snapshots to include in the result set.

When specified together with `periodStartTo`, it defines the start of a time window over which platform KPIs are analyzed. Snapshots whose `period_start` is earlier than this value are excluded.

periodStartTo.description:
Upper bound for the `period_start` field of KPI snapshots to include in the result set.

Typically used together with `periodStartFrom` to restrict the time window. Snapshots whose `period_start` is greater than this value are excluded. Exact inclusiveness or exclusiveness can be defined in service logic but should be consistent across analytics endpoints.

periodEndFrom.description:
Lower bound for the `period_end` field of KPI snapshots to include in the search.

This filter is useful when the reporting window is defined primarily by the snapshot completion time, for example when listing all snapshots that ended within a certain date range.

periodEndTo.description:
Upper bound for the `period_end` field of KPI snapshots to include in the search.

Used in combination with `periodEndFrom` to define a filter on the end of the snapshot period. This allows analytics clients to retrieve historical KPI windows that completed before or within a specified date.

minGmvAmount.description:
Optional lower bound for the GMV amount of snapshots to include.

When provided, only snapshots whose `gmv_amount` is greater than or equal to this value are returned. This can be used to focus on periods with significant transaction volume.

maxGmvAmount.description:
Optional upper bound for the GMV amount of snapshots to include.

When provided, only snapshots whose `gmv_amount` is less than or equal to this value are returned. This allows administrators to detect anomalously low volume periods or perform what-if analyses.

page.description:
Page index for paginated search results, starting from 1.

If omitted, the service usually defaults to the first page. The combination of `page` and `limit` controls which slice of the ordered result set is returned to the client.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot records to return in a single page.

Service implementations may enforce an upper bound to protect the system from excessively large result sets. When omitted, a reasonable default page size is typically applied.

orderBy.description:
Field name used to sort KPI snapshots in the result set.

Common options include `period_start`, `period_end`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`. The service should validate the value against an allow-list of sortable columns and reject unsupported keys.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the field specified in `orderBy`.

Typical values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. When omitted, the service usually defaults to descending order on the primary time field, for example most recent snapshots first.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodStat.description:
Detailed payment method statistics snapshot entity representing precomputed, daily aggregated metrics per payment method.

Each record is stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` Prisma model and corresponds to a single payment method and a single calendar date. Metrics are produced by back-office analytics pipelines that aggregate raw payment events, refunds, and chargebacks into stable snapshot rows.

This DTO exposes all core numeric counters and monetary amounts required for analytics dashboards, finance reporting, and operational monitoring of payment method performance. It is strictly read-only from the API perspective; creation and updates are handled by internal batch jobs or streaming consumers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment method statistics snapshot row.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.id` and is generated by the analytics or ETL pipeline when inserting snapshot data.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these payment method metrics are calculated.

The time component is typically normalized to midnight UTC for consistency with reporting pipelines and date-based filters. This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.stats_date`.

payment_method_code.description:
Stable business code identifying the payment method.

Typical values include generic method families such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or provider-specific identifiers. This field allows analytics and dashboards to group and filter statistics even when a direct foreign-key link is absent. Maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_method_code`.

paymentMethod.description:
Associated payment method configuration for this statistics snapshot.

This summary object represents the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` row referenced by this snapshot and provides key display attributes (such as name, provider, and activation state) required by admin analytics dashboards.

By exposing the belongs-to relation as `paymentMethod: IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary`, the API allows clients to render complete payment method context for the snapshot without additional lookup calls, while still using `payment_method_code` for analytical grouping and filters.

payment_attempt_count.description:
Total number of payment attempts initiated using this payment method on the given stats date.

This counter maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_attempt_count` and includes both successful and failed attempts where the payment flow was started.

payment_success_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that completed successfully for this payment method on the given stats date.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_success_count` and represents transactions that reached a final paid or captured state.

payment_failure_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that definitively failed or were declined for this payment method on the given stats date.

This counter maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_failure_count` and excludes temporary pending states that later succeeded or expired.

payment_expired_count.description:
Number of payment attempts using this method that expired without a final success or failure outcome within the allowed time window.

This metric maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_expired_count` and typically corresponds to pending invoices or redirect-based payments that timed out.

paid_gmv_amount.description:
Total GMV (gross merchandise value) associated with successful payments using this method on the given stats date.

This amount is stored in `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.paid_gmv_amount` and is expressed in the platform's base currency. It reflects the sum of authorized and captured amounts that are considered successfully paid.

refunded_amount.description:
Total amount refunded against payments that used this method on the given stats date.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.refunded_amount` and includes both full and partial refunds, expressed in the platform base currency.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total amount of chargebacks related to this payment method on the given stats date.

This metric is stored as `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.chargeback_amount` and represents disputed or reversed amounts that have been charged back by issuers or acquirers.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment method statistics row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.created_at` and records the initial insertion time of the snapshot.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment method statistics row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.updated_at` and is updated whenever downstream analytics jobs recalculate or fix the metrics for this date and payment method.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodStat.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating payment method statistics stored in `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats`.

This type is used by analytics and admin endpoints to filter snapshot rows by date range, payment method identity, and payment method code while controlling pagination and basic sorting. It does not map directly to a Prisma model because it represents query parameters rather than a persisted entity.

The combination of temporal filters and method-identifying fields allows dashboards to slice and aggregate precomputed payment performance metrics without performing heavy, real-time aggregations on transactional tables.

fromDate.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the stats date range filter.

When provided, only statistics rows with `stats_date` greater than or equal to this value are included in the result set. If omitted, the query may default to a platform-defined reporting window such as the last 7 or 30 days.

toDate.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the stats date range filter.

When provided, only statistics rows with `stats_date` less than or equal to this value are included. If omitted, the query may default to the current date or a platform-defined maximum window.

items.description:
Unique identifier of a configured payment method whose statistics should be included in the query.

Each value corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_methods.id` and is used to filter `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.shopping_mall_payment_method_id` when the foreign key is present.

paymentMethodIds.description:
Optional list of payment method identifiers to restrict the search scope.

When provided, only snapshot rows whose `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` matches one of the listed IDs are returned.

items.description:
Stable business code identifying a payment method to include in the search.

Values typically match `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_method_code`, such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or provider-specific keys.

paymentMethodCodes.description:
Optional list of payment method business codes for filtering statistics.

When present, only rows whose `payment_method_code` matches one of these codes are considered, allowing analytics users to query across methods even when a direct foreign key is absent.

minPaidGmvAmount.description:
Optional lower bound for `paid_gmv_amount` used as a filter.

When specified, only snapshot rows whose total paid GMV is greater than or equal to this value are included. This is useful for focusing on high-volume payment methods.

maxFailureRate.description:
Optional upper bound on the failure rate used to filter statistics rows.

Implementations typically compute the failure rate as `payment_failure_count / NULLIF(payment_attempt_count, 0)` and retain only rows whose computed rate is less than or equal to this threshold. This helps identify well-performing methods when scanning large datasets.

page.description:
1-based index of the result page to retrieve.

If omitted, implementations typically default to the first page. This value is multiplied with `limit` to determine the offset when querying `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats`.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot rows to return in a single page.

If omitted, the backend should apply a safe default and may enforce an upper bound to protect system performance when scanning the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` table.

orderBy.description:
Name of the field used for sorting snapshot rows.

Common values include `stats_date`, `payment_attempt_count`, `payment_success_count`, or `paid_gmv_amount`. Implementations should validate this value against an allowlist to avoid exposing arbitrary ordering logic.

orderDirection.description:
Sorting direction applied together with `orderBy`.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. Implementations should normalize and validate the value against an allowlist rather than trusting arbitrary strings.

IShoppingMallShippingPerformanceStat.description:
Daily aggregated shipping and delivery performance metrics snapshot record for the shopping mall platform.

This type represents a single row from the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` snapshot table, which stores precomputed KPIs about shipping and delivery behavior. Each row is tied to a specific calendar date and a particular shipping method code, and optionally to a concrete shipping method configuration record.

Operations and analytics dashboards use this entity to inspect detailed operational performance, such as how many shipments were created, shipped, delivered, failed, or returned, and how quickly fulfillment and transit processes are executed for a given method.

The data in this entity is read-only from the API perspective and is populated exclusively by background analytics or ETL pipelines that aggregate raw shipment and tracking events. Clients use this type to render detail views and drill-down panels in admin and operations consoles.

id.description:
Primary key for the shipping performance stats snapshot row.

This identifier uniquely represents a single aggregated statistics record in the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` table. It is generated by the analytics pipeline and used by APIs as the stable reference for fetching a specific snapshot.

Clients should treat this value as an opaque UUID and must not attempt to infer any semantics from it.

shopping_mall_shipping_method_id.description:
Optional identifier of the shipping method configuration record.

When present, this UUID links the snapshot row to a concrete configuration in the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` table. This allows analytics tools to correlate performance metrics back to the exact shipping method definition used at the time of aggregation.

When null, the row represents an aggregate over shipments that are not associated with a specific shipping method record, such as legacy or external methods that are only identified by business code.

shipping_method.description:
Optional summary of the shipping method configuration associated with this snapshot row.

When present, this object provides a convenient, human-readable view of the shipping method (for example, display name, business code, and status) corresponding to `shopping_mall_shipping_method_id` and `shipping_method_code`. It allows admin and analytics dashboards to render method details without issuing additional lookups to shipping method endpoints.

When null, the snapshot either aggregates over shipments that are not bound to a concrete `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` record, or the related configuration record is not currently available. In such cases, consumers should fall back to `shipping_method_code` for coarse-grained identification.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these shipping performance metrics are calculated.

Although this field represents a calendar date, it is stored as a timestamp. The time component SHOULD be normalized to midnight UTC so that all rows for a given day share the same canonical value.

Dashboards typically group and filter by this value to visualize shipping performance trends over time.

shipping_method_code.description:
Business code identifying the shipping method or carrier/service combination used for aggregation.

This code distinguishes different shipping strategies such as "standard", "express", or carrier-specific services. It is the primary business-facing grouping key that operations staff recognize when interpreting performance charts.

Multiple snapshot rows may share the same code across different dates, allowing analysis of how a particular method performs over time.

shipment_created_count.description:
Number of shipments created on this date using this shipping method.

This count reflects how many shipment records entered the system (for example, when an order was allocated to a shipping method) during the aggregation date.

It is a fundamental volume metric that, in combination with other fields, helps estimate operational load for the method.

shipment_shipped_count.description:
Number of shipments that transitioned to a shipped state on this date using this method.

A shipment is considered "shipped" when it is handed over to the carrier or otherwise leaves the warehouse. This count helps track fulfillment throughput and the capacity of the warehouse and carrier handoff process.

Comparing this value with `shipment_created_count` can highlight backlog or processing delays.

shipment_delivered_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as delivered on this date using this method.

Delivery is typically recorded when a carrier event or confirmation indicates that the package has reached the customer. This metric is a key indicator of successful completions within the shipping pipeline.

It is frequently used for service-level monitoring and can be combined with time-based metrics to understand overall delivery performance.

shipment_delivery_failed_count.description:
Number of shipments that entered a delivery failed state on this date using this method.

Failures may be caused by incorrect addresses, recipient unavailability, carrier issues, or other exceptional conditions. This count highlights stability and quality issues in last-mile delivery.

High values may indicate problems with address quality, carrier performance, or fraud patterns that require operational intervention.

shipment_returned_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as returned to sender on this date using this method.

Returns are shipments that successfully left the warehouse but ultimately came back, often due to failed delivery, refused acceptance, or customer-initiated returns. This metric reflects reverse logistics workload for the given method.

Operations teams use this information to understand the cost and operational impact of returns across different shipping methods.

median_fulfillment_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from order payment confirmation to shipment handover for this shipping method on this date.

This metric measures how long it typically takes the fulfillment pipeline to pick, pack, and hand over orders to the shipping carrier after payment confirmation. Using the median makes the value robust against a small number of extreme outliers.

Lower values generally indicate efficient warehouse operations, whereas higher values may be a sign of staffing issues, batching strategies, or process bottlenecks.

median_transit_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from shipment handover to delivery confirmation for shipments using this method delivered on this date.

This metric captures carrier transit performance and last-mile delivery efficiency. It is calculated over those shipments that were delivered during the aggregation date.

Operations teams and vendor managers can use this value to benchmark carriers and shipping methods across regions and time periods.

on_time_delivery_rate.description:
Proportion of shipments delivered on or before their expected delivery time threshold for this method on this date.

The value is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1, where 1 represents 100% of deliveries being on time. The underlying expected delivery time may be defined by business policy or carrier SLA.

Low on-time delivery rates often trigger investigations, SLA reviews, or operational mitigations such as switching carriers or adjusting promised delivery windows.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping performance stats row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

This field indicates when the aggregation job wrote the initial version of the snapshot. It is useful for debugging analytics pipelines and confirming that data is fresh.

In most cases, this timestamp will be close to the scheduled execution time of the batch job that generates the statistics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping performance stats row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

Some analytics processes may recalculate historical statistics to incorporate late-arriving events or to fix earlier issues. When that happens, this field is updated to reflect the time of the latest correction.

Consumers that require the most up-to-date metrics can use this timestamp to verify that the snapshot has been processed by the latest pipeline version.

IShoppingMallShippingPerformanceStat.IRe.description:
Search and filtering request for shipping performance statistics snapshot records.

This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH `/shoppingMall/admin/analytics/shippingPerformanceStats` endpoint. It allows administrative and operational clients to specify complex filters, sorting preferences, and pagination options when querying the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` table.

Because this operation is read-only and analytics-oriented, the fields in this type are purely query parameters; no database records are created or modified using this DTO. It is designed to express typical analytics use cases such as constraining by date range, selecting specific shipping methods, and focusing on rows with poor KPIs.

dateFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the stats_date range filter.

When provided, only snapshot rows whose `stats_date` is greater than or equal to this value are included in the result set. The value should be expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format, and callers are encouraged to normalize to midnight UTC for daily buckets.

If null, no lower bound on the aggregation date is applied.

dateTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the stats_date range filter.

When provided, only snapshot rows whose `stats_date` is less than or equal to this value are included in the result set. The value should be expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format, typically representing the end of a reporting window.

If null, no upper bound on the aggregation date is applied.

shippingMethodCodes.description:
Optional list of shipping method business codes to include in the query.

When this array is non-empty, the query is restricted to snapshot rows whose `shipping_method_code` matches one of the provided values. This is commonly used to focus on particular methods such as "standard", "express", or carrier-specific services.

If the array is omitted or empty, no filter is applied on `shipping_method_code` and all methods are considered.

minOnTimeDeliveryRate.description:
Optional lower bound for the on-time delivery rate filter.

When set, only snapshot rows whose `on_time_delivery_rate` is greater than or equal to this value are returned. The expected range is from 0 to 1, where 1 means 100% of shipments were delivered on time.

If null, no minimum threshold is enforced for on-time delivery rate.

maxOnTimeDeliveryRate.description:
Optional upper bound for the on-time delivery rate filter.

When set, only snapshot rows whose `on_time_delivery_rate` is less than or equal to this value are returned. This is typically used to highlight poorly performing methods or periods by selecting rows with low rates.

If null, no maximum threshold is enforced for on-time delivery rate.

minMedianTransitTimeHours.description:
Optional lower bound for the median transit time filter, expressed in hours.

When provided, only snapshot rows whose `median_transit_time_hours` is greater than or equal to this value are included. This can be used to detect carriers or methods that are consistently slower than expected.

If null, no minimum filter is applied for median transit time.

maxMedianTransitTimeHours.description:
Optional upper bound for the median transit time filter, expressed in hours.

When provided, only snapshot rows whose `median_transit_time_hours` is less than or equal to this value are included. This is commonly used to focus on fast methods or to constrain a performance range.

If null, no maximum filter is applied for median transit time.

sortBy.description:
Primary sort key to apply when ordering the snapshot rows in the result set.

Typical values include `"stats_date"` for chronological ordering, `"on_time_delivery_rate"` for ranking methods by reliability, and `"median_transit_time_hours"` for ordering by speed. The concrete implementation should validate and map this field to safe, whitelisted columns on the snapshot table.

If omitted, the default sort is usually descending by `stats_date` so that the most recent data appears first.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the `sortBy` field.

The value `"asc"` sorts from lowest to highest (for example, oldest to newest date, or worst to best KPI), while `"desc"` sorts from highest to lowest. The combination of `sortBy` and `sortDirection` gives clients full control over how analytics tables are ordered.

If omitted, implementations typically default to `"desc"` when sorting by date or KPI metrics so that the most recent or most severe values are prioritized.

Sort direction applied to the `sortBy` field.

The value `"asc"` sorts from lowest to highest (for example, oldest to newest date, or worst to best KPI), while `"desc"` sorts from highest to lowest. The combination of `sortBy` and `sortDirection` gives clients full control over how analytics tables are ordered.

If omitted, implementations typically default to `"desc"` when sorting by date or KPI metrics so that the most recent or most severe values are prioritized.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the `sortBy` field.

The value `"asc"` sorts from lowest to highest (for example, oldest to newest date, or worst to best KPI), while `"desc"` sorts from highest to lowest. The combination of `sortBy` and `sortDirection` gives clients full control over how analytics tables are ordered.

If omitted, implementations typically default to `"desc"` when sorting by date or KPI metrics so that the most recent or most severe values are prioritized.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results, starting from 1.

This field, in combination with `limit`, controls offset-based pagination for the snapshot query. Clients move forward or backward through the result set by adjusting the page number.

If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot rows to return in a single page of results.

This value protects the system from overly broad queries that could fetch an excessive number of rows in a single response. Typical values are between 20 and 200, depending on UI needs.

If omitted, the implementation should fall back to a sensible default such as 50.

IShoppingMallRefundAndDisputeStat.IReque.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for querying refund and dispute analytics snapshots from the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot table.

This request type is used by the admin analytics endpoint to express complex search criteria, including date ranges, segmentation dimensions (such as seller or marketplace scope), metric thresholds, and pagination/sorting options. It is read-only and does not modify any data. All fields are optional filters; when omitted, the backend should apply sensible defaults (for example, a default date range or ordering).

dateFrom.description: Inclusive start of the snapshot date range to search over, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string (UTC). When omitted, the backend may default to a recent historical window such as the last 7 or 30 days.

dateTo.description: Inclusive end of the snapshot date range to search over, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string (UTC). When omitted, the backend may default to the current day or another implementation-defined boundary.

sellerId.description: Optional filter for restricting statistics to snapshots associated with a specific seller or seller segment, when the snapshot table is dimensioned by seller. This should be the seller's unique identifier when supported by the underlying schema.

paymentMethodCode.description: Optional filter narrowing statistics to snapshots associated with a particular payment method or payment method grouping. The exact semantics depend on how payment methods are represented in the snapshot schema (for example, a code or key).

disputeCategory.description: Optional filter for narrowing results to a specific dispute or refund category, if the snapshot model records category-level dimensions. Useful for focusing on chargebacks, customer-initiated disputes, service-level issues, or other policy-defined buckets.

minRefundRate.description: Optional lower bound filter on refund rate (for example, refunds as a ratio of total orders in the snapshot). When provided, only snapshots whose refund rate is greater than or equal to this value should be returned.

maxRefundRate.description: Optional upper bound filter on refund rate. When provided, only snapshots whose refund rate is less than or equal to this value should be returned.

minDisputeRate.description: Optional lower bound filter on dispute rate (for example, disputes as a ratio of relevant orders or payments). When provided, only snapshots with dispute rate greater than or equal to this value should be included.

maxDisputeRate.description: Optional upper bound filter on dispute rate. When provided, only snapshots with dispute rate less than or equal to this value should be included.

page.description: 1-based page index for paginated results. If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of snapshot summaries to return in a single page. The backend may enforce an upper bound regardless of the value provided here to prevent excessively large responses.

orderBy.description: Field name to order the snapshot results by. Common values include `snapshotDate` or key metric fields such as total refunds or dispute rate. The exact allowed values are determined by the implementation and underlying schema.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for the `orderBy` field: `asc` for ascending order, `desc` for descending order.
Sort direction for the `orderBy` field: `asc` for ascending order, `desc` for descending order.

orderDirection.description: Sort direction for the `orderBy` field: `asc` for ascending order, `desc` for descending order.

IShoppingMallRefundAndDisputeStat.description:
Detailed DTO representing a single row from the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot table.

Each snapshot row captures daily aggregated statistics for refund and dispute activity across the entire shopping mall platform for a specific calendar date. The underlying Prisma model stores non-nullable counts, monetary totals, and average resolution times, providing a stable analytical backbone for risk, operations, and finance reporting.

This DTO is used primarily by administrative analytics dashboards, reporting jobs, and internal monitoring tools whenever a complete, low-level view of one snapshot record is required—for example, when drilling down from a list of snapshots or when exporting daily operational metrics for offline analysis. Records are generated and updated by internal batch or streaming aggregation pipelines; they are not created or modified via public write APIs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund and dispute statistics snapshot record.

This value maps directly to the primary key column `id` on the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` Prisma model and is generated by the analytics or ETL pipeline when inserting or recomputing snapshot rows. Clients use this identifier when requesting a specific snapshot record through detail analytics APIs.

statsDate.description:
Calendar date for which these refund and dispute metrics are calculated, stored as a `DateTime` in the `stats_date` column of the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` table.

Although the column is typed as a full timestamp, business logic normalizes the value to represent the start of the day (for example, midnight in a reference time zone). All aggregated counts and amounts in this record correspond to this date window.

refundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests created on this snapshot date.

This field maps to the non-nullable `refund_request_count` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` Prisma model and reflects how many distinct refund cases were opened during the day, regardless of their eventual outcome.

approvedRefundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests that were approved on this snapshot date, regardless of when the requests were originally created.

This value maps to `approved_refund_request_count` in the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` table and is used to track operational workload and approval behavior for the day.

rejectedRefundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests that were rejected on this snapshot date.

This count maps to the `rejected_refund_request_count` column and provides visibility into how many refund cases received a negative decision during the day, regardless of their creation date.

refundedAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded on this snapshot date across all refund operations, expressed in the platform base currency.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `refunded_amount` column of the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` Prisma model and aggregates completed refunds executed during the day, independent of when the underlying orders were placed.

partialRefundCount.description:
Number of refund operations on this snapshot date that were partial relative to the original order or item amount.

This value maps to the `partial_refund_count` column and helps distinguish partial adjustments from full refunds when analyzing refund patterns and customer experience.

fullRefundCount.description:
Number of refund operations on this snapshot date that fully refunded the relevant items or entire orders.

This count maps to the `full_refund_count` column and is commonly compared against partial refunds to understand severity and cost of refund activity.

disputeOpenedCount.description:
Number of dispute cases that were opened on this snapshot date for any reason, including payment disputes, fulfillment conflicts, or policy violations.

This field maps to the non-nullable `dispute_opened_count` column of the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` Prisma model and reflects new dispute inflow for the day.

disputeResolvedCount.description:
Number of dispute cases that reached a resolved or closed state on this snapshot date, regardless of when they were initially opened.

This value maps to the `dispute_resolved_count` column and captures total dispute outflow (closures) for the day, without distinguishing outcome direction.

disputeResolvedForCustomerCount.description:
Number of dispute cases that were resolved in favor of the customer on this snapshot date.

This field maps to `dispute_resolved_for_customer_count` and is used to monitor how many resolved disputes resulted in customer-favored outcomes in the daily window.

disputeResolvedForSellerCount.description:
Number of dispute cases that were resolved in favor of the seller on this snapshot date.

This value maps to the `dispute_resolved_for_seller_count` column and complements the customer-favored count to analyze win/loss distribution for disputes.

averageRefundResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between refund request creation and final decision (approved or rejected) for refund cases resolved on this snapshot date.

This metric maps to the `average_refund_resolution_time_hours` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` Prisma model and provides a key SLA indicator for refund handling efficiency.

averageDisputeResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between dispute creation and resolution for disputes that were resolved on this snapshot date.

This field maps to the `average_dispute_resolution_time_hours` column and is used as a core SLA and operational efficiency metric for dispute handling in the marketplace.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this refund and dispute stats snapshot row was first created by the analytics or ETL pipeline.

This property maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` table and typically represents the time when the initial aggregation job wrote the row.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this refund and dispute stats snapshot row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

This field maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column and is updated whenever the underlying aggregation logic reprocesses historical data for data quality fixes, late-arriving events, or model changes.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.description:
Administrative overview dashboard DTO for the shoppingMall platform.

This type aggregates key performance indicators from multiple snapshot and operational statistics tables, including `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`, `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`, `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats`, `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`, and `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`.

It is optimized for admin UI dashboard rendering and surfaces today-level metrics, recent platform KPIs, payment performance, shipping performance, and refund/dispute activity in a single response structure. It does not correspond to a single Prisma model but composes values derived from several analytics pipelines and snapshot models.

todayOrderStats.description: Headline order and revenue statistics for the current business day derived from `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats`. This block summarizes order counts, GMV, NMV, and related top-level KPIs used in the dashboard header.

todaySellerStats.description: Aggregated seller activity metrics for the current day, including active sellers, earnings, and dispute outcomes. Values are derived from `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` and related analytics snapshots.

todayCustomerStats.description: Aggregated customer activity metrics for the current day, such as active customers, new customers, session counts, and engagement actions. Values are derived from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` and related analytics processes.

currentPlatformKpis.description: Platform-level KPI snapshot representing the most recent reporting period (for example, today, yesterday, or the last completed day). Values mirror those in `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots` but are exposed in a dashboard-friendly DTO.

paymentMethodStats.description: Collection of per-payment-method statistics for the current day, derived from `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats`. This allows the dashboard to visualize payment success ratios and failure patterns by method.

shippingPerformanceStats.description: Collection of per-shipping-method performance statistics for the current day, based on `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats`. It supports dashboard widgets that display shipment volumes and SLA adherence by carrier or service type.

refundAndDisputeStats.description: Aggregated refund and dispute activity metrics for the current day, derived from `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. It summarizes refund volumes, dispute outcomes, and resolution times.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.ITod.description:
Top-level order and revenue statistics for the current business day.

Values in this DTO are derived from the `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats` snapshot row corresponding to today's `stats_date`. They represent aggregate platform-wide order activity and revenue numbers that appear at the top of the administrative dashboard.

The fields mirror key columns from the snapshot model, such as order counts, GMV, NMV, and refund-related amounts, and provide admins with an immediate at-a-glance view of daily trading performance.

statsDate.description: Calendar date for which these statistics are calculated, normally the current day. The time component is typically normalized to midnight UTC in the underlying snapshot table.

orderCount.description: Total number of successfully created orders on this date, regardless of payment outcome. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.order_count`.

paidOrderCount.description: Number of orders that reached a paid state on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.paid_order_count`.

cancelledOrderCount.description: Number of orders that were cancelled on this date, including both customer-initiated and system-initiated cancellations. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.cancelled_order_count`.

refundedOrderCount.description: Number of orders that had at least one refund completed on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.refunded_order_count`.

gmvAmount.description: Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) for orders associated with this date, before refunds and cancellations, expressed in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.gmv_amount`.

nmvAmount.description: Net Merchandise Value (NMV) for this date after subtracting refunded or cancelled amounts, expressed in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.nmv_amount`.

itemCount.description: Total number of order line items across all orders created on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.item_count`.

uniqueCustomerCount.description: Number of distinct customers who placed at least one order on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.unique_customer_count`.

uniqueSellerCount.description: Number of distinct sellers who had at least one item included in orders created on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.unique_seller_count`.

averageOrderValue.description: Average order value (AOV) for this date, typically calculated as GMV divided by `paid_order_count`. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.average_order_value`.

refundAmount.description: Total amount refunded on this date across all orders, expressed in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.refund_amount`.

chargebackAmount.description: Total value of chargebacks recorded on this date, expressed in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.chargeback_amount`.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.ITod.description:
Aggregated seller-centric metrics for the current business day.

This DTO does **not** represent a single row from the `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` table. Instead, for a given `statsDate` it aggregates data across all snapshot rows stored in that table, typically one row per seller. Each field in this schema is derived from concrete numeric columns in `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` using well-defined aggregation functions such as `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`, `SUM(...)`, or weighted averages.

The purpose of this type is to provide a compact seller-focused section on the administrative overview dashboard. It exposes only the most important KPIs needed for a high-level view of seller performance and risk, such as the number of active sellers, aggregated GMV/NMV, platform commission, net seller earnings, dispute volumes, and the overall average rating across sellers.

The `x-autobe-prisma-schema` annotation links this dashboard DTO to the `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` model as its analytical data source, documenting where implementations should read from when computing these aggregates. Implementations are expected to issue aggregate queries over that table rather than map these properties directly to a single snapshot row.

statsDate.description:
Calendar date for which these seller metrics are calculated, typically the current business day.

In the underlying `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` table this corresponds to the `stats_date` column. All other metrics in this DTO must be computed by aggregating rows whose `stats_date` equals this value, usually treating the time component as normalized (for example, midnight UTC).

activeSellerCount.description:
Number of distinct sellers that are considered active on this date.

This value is usually computed as `COUNT(DISTINCT shopping_mall_seller_id)` over rows in `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` for the specified `statsDate`, optionally constrained by business rules such as requiring at least one order, shipment, or earnings event. It represents the population of sellers that contributed measurable activity in the selected period.

gmvAmount.description:
Total Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) attributable to all sellers on this date, before commissions, refunds, and cancellations, expressed in the platform base currency.

Implementations normally compute this as the sum of the `gmv_amount` column across all `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` rows whose `stats_date` equals `statsDate`. It provides a seller-centric view of top-line sales volume for the day.

nmvAmount.description:
Total Net Merchandise Value (NMV) attributable to all sellers on this date after refunds, cancellations, and similar negative adjustments, expressed in the platform base currency.

This is typically calculated as the sum of the `nmv_amount` column across all rows in `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` for the given `statsDate`. It indicates the realized merchandise value that remains after accounting for reversals and adjustments at the seller level.

commissionAmount.description:
Total platform commission charged to sellers on this date, expressed in the platform base currency.

A typical implementation sums the `commission_amount` column from every `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` row with the matching `stats_date`. This KPI helps administrators understand platform revenue attributable to seller transactions for the day.

sellerEarningsAmount.description:
Total net earnings owed to sellers on this date after commissions, seller-funded discounts, and other adjustments, expressed in the platform base currency.

This value is generally computed by summing the `seller_earnings_amount` column across all `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` rows for the selected `statsDate`. It describes how much value accrued to sellers and is often reviewed alongside `commissionAmount` to understand value sharing between the platform and its sellers.

disputeOpenedCount.description:
Number of dispute cases involving sellers that were opened on this date.

Implementations normally compute this by summing the `dispute_opened_count` column from `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` rows with the specified `statsDate`. An elevated value can indicate growing friction or dissatisfaction that may require operational or policy intervention.

disputeLostCount.description:
Number of disputes involving sellers that were resolved against the seller (for example, customer-favored or platform-favored outcomes) on this date.

This value is typically the sum of the `dispute_lost_count` column across `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` rows for the chosen `statsDate`. It highlights the volume of adverse dispute outcomes for sellers and can be used as an input to risk, compliance, or seller quality monitoring processes.

averageRating.description:
Marketplace-wide snapshot of the average product rating associated with sellers on this date.
