This metric should be computed as a weighted average of per-seller ratings recorded in `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats`, for example by combining `average_rating` with the corresponding `rating_review_count` so that sellers with many reviews influence the metric more than those with only a few. It serves as a high-level indicator of catalog quality and customer satisfaction from the seller perspective on the selected day.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.ITod.description:
Aggregated customer-centric activity metrics for the current business day.

This DTO provides a high-level view of how customers interacted with the marketplace today, including order volumes, revenue contribution, refunds received, and engagement actions such as add-to-cart or wishlist events. Values are derived from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` snapshot rows aggregated across customers.

Admins use this information to understand daily acquisition, retention, and engagement trends without inspecting individual customer records.

statsDate.description: Calendar date for which these customer metrics are calculated, typically the current day. The time component is usually normalized to midnight UTC in the underlying snapshot model.

activeCustomerCount.description: Number of customers that had at least one qualifying activity on this date, such as a session, cart action, or order. Derived from counting non-passive rows in `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`.

newCustomerCount.description: Number of customers whose acquisition date falls on this day, based on `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.is_new_customer` flags. This is a key acquisition KPI.

orderCount.description: Total number of orders created by customers on this date, aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.order_count`.

paidOrderCount.description: Total number of orders from customers that reached a paid state on this date, aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.paid_order_count`.

gmvAmount.description: Total GMV associated with customer orders created on this date, in the platform base currency. Aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.gmv_amount`.

nmvAmount.description: Total NMV for this date after refunds and cancellations, aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.nmv_amount`.

refundAmount.description: Total amount refunded to customers on this date, aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.refund_amount`.

cartAddCount.description: Total number of add-to-cart actions performed by customers on this date, aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.cart_add_count`.

wishlistAddCount.description: Total number of wishlist-add actions performed by customers on this date, aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.wishlist_add_count`.

sessionCount.description: Total number of authenticated sessions started by customers on this date, aggregated from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats.session_count`.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.IPla.description:
Platform-level KPI snapshot for the current or most recent reporting period.

This DTO exposes core key performance indicators from `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots` for use in the admin overview dashboard. It is typically sourced from the latest snapshot row matching the platform’s reporting cadence (for example, today, yesterday, week-to-date, or month-to-date).

The fields cover GMV, NMV, platform revenue, take rate, active and new customer counts, active seller counts, refund and chargeback activity, and other KPIs that are central to understanding marketplace health.

periodType.description: Type of reporting period this KPI snapshot represents, such as "day", "week", "month", or "custom". Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.period_type`.

periodStart.description: Inclusive start timestamp of the reporting period covered by this snapshot. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.period_start`.

periodEnd.description: Exclusive end timestamp of the reporting period covered by this snapshot. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.period_end`.

gmvAmount.description: Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) for the reporting period before refunds and cancellations, in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.gmv_amount`.

nmvAmount.description: Net Merchandise Value (NMV) for the reporting period after refunds and cancellations, in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.nmv_amount`.

platformRevenueAmount.description: Total platform revenue recognized during the reporting period, including commissions, fees, subscriptions, and advertising revenue, net of adjustments. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.platform_revenue_amount`.

takeRate.description: Platform take rate for the reporting period, typically calculated as `platform_revenue_amount / gmv_amount`. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.take_rate`.

orderCount.description: Number of successfully created orders within the reporting period. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.order_count`.

paidOrderCount.description: Number of orders that reached a paid state within the reporting period. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.paid_order_count`.

activeCustomerCount.description: Number of active customers during the reporting period based on configured activity criteria. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.active_customer_count`.

newCustomerCount.description: Number of newly registered customers during the reporting period. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.new_customer_count`.

activeSellerCount.description: Number of active sellers during the reporting period based on seller activity rules. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.active_seller_count`.

refundRequestCount.description: Number of refund requests created during the reporting period. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.refund_request_count`.

approvedRefundCount.description: Number of refund requests approved during the reporting period. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.approved_refund_count`.

refundedAmount.description: Total amount refunded during the reporting period, in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.refunded_amount`.

chargebackCount.description: Number of chargebacks recorded during the reporting period. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.chargeback_count`.

chargebackAmount.description: Total value of chargebacks recorded during the reporting period, in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.chargeback_amount`.

averageOrderValue.description: Average order value (AOV) for the reporting period, usually computed as GMV divided by `paid_order_count`. Mirrors `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots.average_order_value`.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.IPay.description:
Per-payment-method statistics for a single calendar date.

This DTO represents a row of aggregated payment metrics from `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` and is used in the admin overview dashboard to display payment success ratios, failures, and volumes broken down by payment method.

The platform typically fetches the stats row for today (or the current reporting day) per payment method and displays them in charts or tables that help admins understand payment performance across methods and providers.

statsDate.description: Calendar date for which these payment method metrics are calculated. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.stats_date` and is usually normalized to midnight UTC in the snapshot table.

paymentMethodCode.description: Stable business code identifying the payment method (for example "card", "bank_transfer", or provider-specific code). Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_method_code`.

paymentAttemptCount.description: Number of payment attempts initiated using this payment method on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_attempt_count`.

paymentSuccessCount.description: Number of payment attempts that completed successfully (paid) using this method on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_success_count`.

paymentFailureCount.description: Number of payment attempts that definitively failed or were declined using this method on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_failure_count`.

paymentExpiredCount.description: Number of payment attempts using this method that expired without a final success or failure outcome by timeout rules on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_expired_count`.

paidGmvAmount.description: GMV associated with successful payments using this method on this date, in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.paid_gmv_amount`.

refundedAmount.description: Total amount refunded for payments that used this method on this date, in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.refunded_amount`.

chargebackAmount.description: Total amount of chargebacks related to this payment method on this date, in the platform base currency. Mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.chargeback_amount`.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.IShi.description:
Per-shipping-method shipping and delivery performance statistics for a single calendar date.

This DTO mirrors a row from `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` and is surfaced on the admin overview dashboard to help operations teams monitor fulfillment speed, on-time delivery rates, and shipping failures per method or carrier.

The platform typically aggregates stats for the current day and visualizes them in charts or tables that highlight problematic shipping methods or carriers.

statsDate.description: Calendar date for which these shipping performance metrics are calculated. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.stats_date` and is usually normalized to midnight UTC in the snapshot table.

shippingMethodCode.description: Business code identifying the shipping method or carrier/service combination used for aggregation, such as "standard" or "express". Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipping_method_code`.

shipmentCreatedCount.description: Number of shipments created on this date using this shipping method. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_created_count`.

shipmentShippedCount.description: Number of shipments that transitioned to a shipped state on this date using this method. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_shipped_count`.

shipmentDeliveredCount.description: Number of shipments that were marked as delivered on this date using this method. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_delivered_count`.

shipmentDeliveryFailedCount.description: Number of shipments that entered a delivery failed state on this date using this method. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_delivery_failed_count`.

shipmentReturnedCount.description: Number of shipments that were marked as returned to sender on this date using this method. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.shipment_returned_count`.

medianFulfillmentTimeHours.description: Median time in hours from order payment confirmation to shipment handover for shipments associated with this method on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.median_fulfillment_time_hours`.

medianTransitTimeHours.description: Median time in hours from shipment handover to delivery confirmation for shipments using this method delivered on this date. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.median_transit_time_hours`.

onTimeDeliveryRate.description: Proportion of shipments delivered on or before their expected delivery time threshold for this method on this date, represented as a value between 0 and 1. Mirrors `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats.on_time_delivery_rate`.

IShoppingMallAdminOverviewDashboard.IRef.description:
Aggregated refund and dispute activity metrics for a single calendar date in the shoppingMall platform.

Each instance of this DTO represents one row from the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot table, keyed by a business calendar date rather than an arbitrary event timestamp. The underlying Prisma model stores metrics such as refund request volumes, approved and rejected counts, refunded amounts, dispute openings, dispute resolutions, and average resolution times for the given date.

The fields exposed here focus on business-facing metrics that risk, operations, and finance teams use to understand after‑sales workload, customer experience, and risk exposure. Internal ETL pipeline timestamps such as `created_at` and `updated_at` exist on the Prisma model but are intentionally not exposed through this DTO, because they are implementation details of the statistics pipeline rather than part of the reporting contract.

statsDate.description:
Calendar date for which these refund and dispute metrics are calculated, serialized as an ISO 8601 date string in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

In the underlying `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` table this corresponds to the `stats_date` column, which is typically normalized to midnight UTC internally. API consumers should treat this value as a pure date bucket key rather than a precise event timestamp.

refundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests created on this date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.refund_request_count` and includes all refund requests whose creation timestamp falls on the `stats_date` bucket, regardless of when they are later resolved.

approvedRefundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests approved on this date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.approved_refund_request_count` and counts approvals whose decision timestamp falls on the `stats_date` bucket, even if the original request was created on a different day.

rejectedRefundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests rejected on this date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.rejected_refund_request_count` and counts rejections whose decision timestamp falls on the `stats_date` bucket.

refundedAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded on this date, in the platform base currency.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.refunded_amount` and typically aggregates completed payment refunds recorded on the `stats_date` bucket. Implementations should document the exact currency (for example, platform base currency such as KRW or USD) at the system level.

partialRefundCount.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that were partial relative to the original order or item amount.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.partial_refund_count` and helps quantify how often only part of an order is refunded instead of a full reversal.

fullRefundCount.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that fully refunded the relevant line items or orders.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.full_refund_count` and complements `partialRefundCount` for analyzing refund patterns and customer satisfaction.

disputeOpenedCount.description:
Number of disputes created on this date for any reason, including payment disputes, fulfillment conflicts, or policy violations.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_opened_count` and reflects the volume of new dispute cases entering the pipeline on the `stats_date` bucket.

disputeResolvedCount.description:
Number of disputes resolved on this date, regardless of when they were originally opened.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_resolved_count` and measures dispute processing throughput for the `stats_date` bucket.

disputeResolvedForCustomerCount.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the customer on this date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_resolved_for_customer_count` and is useful for understanding customer‑sided outcomes and potential goodwill impact.

disputeResolvedForSellerCount.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the seller on this date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_resolved_for_seller_count` and is useful for analyzing seller‑sided outcomes and risk distribution across participants.

averageRefundResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between refund request creation and final decision (approved or rejected) for refund cases resolved on this date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.average_refund_resolution_time_hours` and helps evaluate refund handling SLAs and operational efficiency for the `stats_date` bucket.

averageDisputeResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between dispute creation and resolution for disputes resolved on this date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.average_dispute_resolution_time_hours` and provides a high‑level indicator of dispute lifecycle duration and SLA adherence for the `stats_date` bucket.

IShoppingMallSalesByDayStatistics.description:
Aggregated daily sales statistics over a requested reporting window for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is a computed analytical view that does not correspond to a single Prisma model. Instead, it represents the result of grouping transactional data from orders, order items, payments, and refunds by calendar day and computing metrics such as order counts, GMV, NMV, and average order value.

The type contains the effective date range applied to the query, the time zone normalization used to bucket events into days, and an array of per-day metric rows that the admin dashboard or reporting UI can use to render charts and tables.

startDate.description: Inclusive start date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD). This reflects the normalized date used when aggregating the underlying transactional data.

endDate.description: Inclusive end date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD). This reflects the normalized date used for the last bucket in the aggregation.

timezone.description: IANA time zone identifier (for example, "Asia/Seoul" or "UTC") that determines how order timestamps are bucketed into calendar days. If omitted in the request, a platform default is used but the effective value is always returned here.

days.description: Collection of per-day sales statistics rows for each calendar date included in the reporting window. Each element represents aggregated order and revenue metrics for a single normalized day.

IShoppingMallSalesByDayStatistics.IDay.description:
Aggregated sales metrics for a single calendar date in the platform’s reporting time zone.

Each instance of this DTO corresponds to one bucket in the `IShoppingMallSalesByDayStatistics.days` array and summarizes core KPIs such as order volume, paid order counts, GMV, NMV, cancellations, refunds, and average order value for that specific date.

The structure is intentionally compact so that a time series of these rows can be efficiently rendered in charts and tables on an admin reporting or analytics screen.

statsDate.description: Calendar date (in the reporting time zone) to which these metrics apply. This is the grouping key used when aggregating transactional data into daily buckets.

orderCount.description: Total number of orders created on this date, regardless of payment outcome.

paidOrderCount.description: Number of orders that reached a paid state on this date.

cancelledOrderCount.description: Number of orders that were cancelled on this date, including both customer-initiated and system-initiated cancellations.

refundedOrderCount.description: Number of orders that had at least one refund completed on this date.

gmvAmount.description: Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) for orders associated with this date before refunds and cancellations, expressed in the platform base currency.

nmvAmount.description: Net Merchandise Value (NMV) for this date after subtracting refunded or cancelled amounts, expressed in the platform base currency.

averageOrderValue.description: Average order value (AOV) for this date, typically computed as GMV divided by `paid_order_count`. Implementations may zero-handle or omit the ratio when there are no paid orders.

refundAmount.description: Total monetary amount refunded on this date, in the platform base currency.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceByDayStati.description:
Aggregated daily performance statistics for one or more sellers on the shoppingMall platform over a requested reporting window.

This analytical DTO composes per-seller, per-day metric rows along with metadata about the query period. It is derived from snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` and related transactional tables (orders, order items, payments, earnings), but it does not mirror any single Prisma model row.

The structure is optimized for administrative dashboards and monitoring tools. It exposes a curated set of metrics that summarize marketplace activity for each seller on each calendar date, together with high-level totals for the entire result set.

Use this type strictly as a computed reporting view. All metrics are pre-aggregated server-side for the requested date range and seller filters, and consumers must not assume a one-to-one correspondence between these properties and underlying database columns.

startDate.description:
Inclusive start date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD) that was effectively used for this statistics computation after applying defaults and validation.

If the caller omitted an explicit start date, this value reflects the default chosen by the implementation (for example, 30 days before the effective end date).

endDate.description:
Inclusive end date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD) that was effectively used for this statistics computation.

When the caller does not specify an end date, this value typically resolves to the business current date in the selected reporting time zone.

timezone.description:
IANA time zone identifier (for example, `Asia/Seoul` or `UTC`) that was applied when bucketing timestamps into calendar days for this statistics result.

All daily metrics in the `rows` collection are grouped according to this time zone, which means that date boundaries and local midnight are interpreted relative to this value rather than raw UTC timestamps.

sellerFilter.description:
Optional filter information describing which sellers were included in this statistics query.

When the client restricts the analysis to a specific seller or a small subset of sellers, this object echoes those constraints so that dashboards and reports can clearly communicate the scope of the metrics being visualized.

rows.description:
Time-series of seller performance metrics. Each row represents the aggregated metrics for a single seller on a single calendar date within the requested window.

The row objects are analytical views built from snapshot tables and transactional data. They expose curated KPIs such as order counts, item counts, gross merchandise value, net earnings, commissions, and refund-related indicators, rather than raw database columns.

summary.description:
Optional summary aggregates computed over all returned rows.

This summary combines the row-level metrics into high-level totals and averages for the entire result set, such as total number of sellers, overall GMV, total net earnings, and derived ratios like average refund rate or average order value for the analyzed period.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceByDayStati.description:
Single-row representation of a seller’s daily performance metrics in the shoppingMall platform.

Each instance corresponds to one seller on one calendar date. The fields summarize activity by combining data from snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_seller_daily_stats` and transactional sources including orders, order items, payments, refunds, and commissions.

This DTO is a curated analytical view rather than a direct projection of any single Prisma model. Property names and aggregations are chosen to be intuitive for dashboards and reports, focusing on key KPIs such as order volume, gross merchandise value, net earnings, commissions, and refund or cancellation activity.

date.description:
Calendar date (in the applied reporting time zone) for which these performance metrics were computed, expressed in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

All other numeric fields in this row represent aggregates restricted to this `(seller, date)` combination.

sellerId.description:
Identifier of the seller whose metrics are represented in this row.

This value corresponds to the seller’s primary key in the `shopping_mall_sellers` table and is used as the primary grouping key when computing daily seller metrics.

seller.description:
Summary representation of the seller associated with this performance row.

The summary object provides lightweight identification and status information about the seller (such as email, lifecycle status, and creation timestamp) so that analytics consumers can render context directly alongside the metrics without issuing additional lookup requests.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of customer orders that contained at least one item belonging to this seller on this date.

This count typically includes all relevant order statuses that participate in GMV calculations, and may be derived from order and order-item level records associated with the seller.

totalOrderItems.description:
Total number of order line items associated with this seller across all orders on this date.

This metric provides finer-grained insight into sales volume than `totalOrders` by counting individual items rather than orders.

grossMerchandiseValue.description:
Gross merchandise value (GMV) for this seller on this date, before commissions, fees, and refunds.

GMV is usually computed as the sum of merchandise line item amounts for completed or otherwise included order statuses, expressed in the platform base currency. It serves as a primary indicator of sales volume for the seller.

netEarnings.description:
Net earnings for this seller on this date after applying platform commissions, fees, and completed refunds.

This value represents the amount effectively owed to the seller for the day’s activity and is typically aligned with entries in seller earnings or settlement subsystems, expressed in the platform base currency.

commissionAmount.description:
Total amount of platform commissions and fees charged to this seller on this date across all relevant order items and payments.

This metric helps governance and finance teams understand the platform’s revenue contribution from the seller for the given date and is recorded in the platform base currency.

refundCount.description:
Number of refund operations or refunded order items associated with this seller on this date.

The exact counting strategy (per refund request, per payment refund, or per refunded line item) is defined by the analytics pipeline, but, in all cases, this value represents how frequently refunds occurred for the seller during the day.

refundAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded to customers for this seller’s orders on this date.

This amount is aggregated from payment-level or line-level refund records, expressed in the platform base currency, and provides visibility into revenue reversals for the seller.

cancellationCount.description:
Number of cancelled orders or order items associated with this seller on this date.

The analytics pipeline determines whether cancellations are counted at order or line level, but the metric always reflects the volume of customer- or platform-initiated cancellations that impacted this seller’s orders on the given date.

refundRate.description:
Refund rate for this seller on this date.

Common computations include the ratio of `refundCount` to `totalOrders`, or `refundAmount` to `grossMerchandiseValue`. The exact formula is defined by the analytics implementation and should be documented in operational runbooks. Consumers should treat this as a dimensionless ratio between 0 and 1 or a percentage depending on presentation.

averageOrderValue.description:
Average order value (AOV) for this seller on this date.

This metric is typically computed as `grossMerchandiseValue` divided by `totalOrders` for orders that meet inclusion criteria. When there are no qualifying orders, the analytics pipeline may emit 0 or omit the value depending on configuration.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceByDayStati.description:
Aggregate summary of seller performance statistics over the entire requested period and seller scope.

This object is computed from the collection of `IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceByDayStatistics.IRow` entries in the response rather than directly from any single database table. It consolidates row-level metrics into high-level totals and averages that are convenient for dashboard headers and at-a-glance reporting.

Use this DTO to display marketplace-wide or filter-scoped KPIs such as total GMV, total net earnings, total refunds, and derived ratios for the time window represented by the parent statistics object.

totalSellers.description:
Number of distinct sellers included in the statistics result.

This count is derived from the unique `sellerId` values present in the `rows` collection and indicates how many sellers contributed data to the aggregated metrics.

totalDays.description:
Number of distinct calendar dates covered by the statistics result.

This value corresponds to the number of unique `date` values present across all seller performance rows in the result set.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of orders across all sellers and days in the result set.

This is the sum of `totalOrders` over all rows and is useful for understanding the overall volume of orders during the analyzed period.

totalOrderItems.description:
Total number of order line items across all sellers and days in the result set.

This is the sum of `totalOrderItems` over all rows and reflects the total item-level sales volume for the selected time window and seller cohort.

totalGrossMerchandiseValue.description:
Sum of gross merchandise value (GMV) across all sellers and days in the result set.

This aggregate is computed by summing `grossMerchandiseValue` from each row and represents the total merchandise value before commissions, fees, and refunds, expressed in the platform base currency.

totalNetEarnings.description:
Sum of net earnings across all sellers and days in the result set.

This aggregate is computed by summing `netEarnings` from each row and represents the total amount owed to sellers after commissions, fees, and refunds for the analyzed period, expressed in the platform base currency.

totalCommissionAmount.description:
Sum of commissions and fees charged to all sellers across all days in the result set.

This metric is typically computed by summing `commissionAmount` over all rows and provides a view of platform revenue derived from seller activity during the analyzed period.

totalRefundAmount.description:
Sum of all refunded amounts across all sellers and days in the result set.

This value is computed by summing `refundAmount` over all rows and indicates the total volume of revenue that was reversed via refunds for the analyzed period, expressed in the platform base currency.

averageRefundRate.description:
Average refund rate across all rows in the result set.

Typical implementations compute this metric as the arithmetic mean of the per-row `refundRate` values, or compute a global ratio based on total refunds and total orders. Consumers should treat this as a dimensionless ratio or percentage depending on how it is presented in the UI.

averageOrderValue.description:
Average order value across the result set.

This metric is commonly computed as `totalGrossMerchandiseValue` divided by `totalOrders` when `totalOrders` is greater than zero. It provides a high-level view of order size for the analyzed period and selected seller cohort.

IShoppingMallCustomerActivityDailyStatis.description:
Time-series statistics describing daily customer activity on the shoppingMall platform over a requested period.

This analytical DTO is built from snapshot-oriented models such as shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats and shopping_mall_order_daily_stats and is intended for administrative analytics and monitoring. It exposes per-day aggregates covering new customer registrations, active customers, order activity, and monetary totals, without revealing any personally identifiable information about individual customers.

Unlike raw Prisma snapshot rows, this DTO represents a higher-level analytical view that groups and aggregates multiple underlying records into a time-series structure. It includes the effective reporting window, the timezone used for date bucketing, a collection of daily metric rows, and an optional overall summary that can be displayed in dashboards and analytics UIs.

startDate.description:
Inclusive start date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD) that was effectively used for this customer activity statistics computation.

Clients should treat this value as the canonical lower bound of the time range represented by the returned rows, even if the original request omitted a start date or specified a broader range that was internally constrained by the system.

endDate.description:
Inclusive end date of the reporting window in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD) that was effectively used for this customer activity statistics computation.

This value represents the canonical upper bound of the time range for which customer activity metrics were aggregated, ensuring that consumers can accurately label charts and tables without needing to re-derive the effective range from the raw request.

timezone.description:
IANA time zone identifier (for example, Asia/Seoul or UTC) that was applied when grouping underlying events and snapshots into calendar days.

The analytics pipeline uses this timezone when converting raw timestamps into calendar dates for bucketed metrics. All date values returned in the `rows` collection are interpreted relative to this timezone, so consumers must use the same timezone when aligning the metrics with other reports or visualizations.

rows.description:
Time-series of daily customer activity metrics. Each row represents aggregated customer behavior for a single calendar date within the requested window.

Rows are typically ordered by date in ascending order so they can be directly rendered in charts and tables. Each row combines metrics derived from snapshot models such as shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats and shopping_mall_order_daily_stats and may include both direct counts (orders, active customers) and derived indicators (ratios, average order value).

summary.description:
Optional summary aggregates computed across all daily rows in the series, useful for dashboards and reporting headers.

When present, the summary provides precomputed totals and averages over the full reporting window, allowing clients to display headline KPIs such as total GMV, total active customers, and average daily orders without recomputing them from the `rows` collection.

IShoppingMallCustomerActivityDailyStatis.description:
Single-day snapshot of customer activity metrics on the shoppingMall platform.

Each instance corresponds to one calendar date and aggregates counts and monetary totals such as new registrations, active customers, orders placed, and gross merchandise value generated by those orders. Metrics are typically derived from snapshot tables like shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats and shopping_mall_order_daily_stats, which are populated by offline or near-real-time analytics jobs.

Some fields represent direct counts (for example, number of orders or cart additions), while others are derived indicators such as ratios and average order value. Together they provide a compact view of how engaged the customer base was on that date and how effectively activity translated into paid orders and revenue.

date.description:
Calendar date for which these customer activity metrics were computed, expressed in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD).

The date is defined in the timezone returned by the enclosing IShoppingMallCustomerActivityDailyStatistics response. All counts and monetary values in this row aggregate behavior that occurred within this calendar day in that timezone.

newRegisteredCustomers.description:
Number of customers who completed registration on this date.

This metric helps distinguish acquisition effects from pure engagement. It typically counts new rows created in the shopping_mall_customers table during the snapshot window corresponding to this calendar date.

activeCustomers.description:
Number of customers who were considered active on this date, typically defined as having performed at least one meaningful action such as placing an order, adding items to cart, or interacting with key site features.

The precise definition of "active" is derived from the analytics pipeline and may involve combining multiple event sources and snapshot tables. This value is used for engagement, retention, and conversion-rate calculations.

orderingCustomers.description:
Number of distinct customers who placed at least one order on this date.

This metric focuses specifically on customers who generated order activity, and is often compared against `activeCustomers` to understand conversion from engagement to purchasing behavior.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of customer orders placed on this date.

This count usually corresponds to the number of order headers created in the shopping_mall_orders table whose creation timestamp falls within the snapshot window for this calendar date.

totalOrderItems.description:
Total number of order line items across all customer orders placed on this date.

This metric helps analyze basket size and product mix, and is often used with GMV and customer counts to derive additional KPIs such as average items per order.

grossMerchandiseValue.description:
Gross merchandise value (GMV) generated by customer orders on this date, before refunds and adjustments.

GMV is typically expressed in the platform base currency and computed as the sum of merchandise amounts on all qualifying orders for the day. It excludes taxes, shipping, and fees when the business definition of GMV requires that separation.

averageOrderValue.description:
Average order value (AOV) for customer orders on this date.

AOV is usually computed as grossMerchandiseValue divided by totalOrders when totalOrders is greater than zero. When there are no orders, this field may be omitted or set according to the analytics pipeline’s null-handling policy.

activeCustomerRatio.description:
Ratio of active customers to the total eligible customer base for this date, when available.

This engagement indicator is typically computed as activeCustomers divided by the size of the eligible customer cohort (for example, all registered customers that are not soft-deleted). Implementations may choose to omit this field if the denominator cannot be reliably determined for a given day.

orderingCustomerRatio.description:
Ratio of ordering customers to active customers for this date.

This metric reflects the percentage of engaged customers who actually placed an order on the day in question, and is often used as a conversion-rate KPI in dashboards and analytics reports.

netMerchandiseValue.description:
Net merchandise value (NMV) generated by customer orders on this date after applying refunds and cancellations.

This metric typically corresponds to the net merchandise amount stored in snapshot tables such as shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats (for example, the nmv_amount column). It helps differentiate between gross sales volume and the value that ultimately remains after post-order adjustments.

refundAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded to customers on this date, expressed in the platform base currency.

This value aggregates all refund activity whose effective date falls within the snapshot window for this calendar date, and generally corresponds to fields such as refund_amount in the underlying analytics snapshot tables.

cartAddCount.description:
Number of add-to-cart actions performed by customers on this date.

This metric is typically derived from aggregated cart event data and aligned with the `cart_add_count` field in daily snapshot models such as shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats. It is used to understand upper-funnel engagement and how frequently customers initiate purchase intent.

wishlistAddCount.description:
Number of wishlist-add actions performed by customers on this date.

The metric corresponds conceptually to a field such as `wishlist_add_count` in the daily customer snapshot schema and is useful for tracking interest and intent that may not immediately convert into orders.

sessionCount.description:
Number of authenticated customer sessions started on this date.

This count usually aggregates session creations from tables such as shopping_mall_customer_sessions and is aligned with the `session_count` snapshot column in shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats. It is often used as a denominator for engagement ratios and funnel analyses.

isNewCustomer.description:
Flag indicating whether this date is considered the acquisition date for the customer cohort represented by this row, from the perspective of the analytics pipeline.

In many implementations this flag mirrors the semantics of an `is_new_customer` snapshot field, which marks the first date on which a customer is treated as acquired for analytics tracking purposes. It can be used to distinguish acquisition cohorts from purely returning activity, depending on how the analytics aggregation groups customers into rows.

hasRepeatOrders.description:
Flag indicating whether the customers represented in this daily snapshot have placed more than one order over their lifetime as of the end of this date.

This metric is conceptually aligned with a `has_repeat_orders` snapshot field and helps identify cohorts that have demonstrated repeat purchase behavior. It is useful for retention and lifecycle analyses when combined with other metrics in the row.

IShoppingMallCustomerActivityDailyStatis.description:
Aggregate summary of customer activity metrics over the entire requested period.

This summary DTO is derived from many per-customer, per-day snapshot rows in the `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` table rather than from a single database record. Each field aggregates or derives metrics across all relevant snapshot rows within the selected reporting window, allowing dashboards to present high-level KPIs without exposing raw per-day or per-customer data directly.

The structure is strictly read-only and is intended for analytics, monitoring, and executive reporting scenarios. It is typically returned alongside a time-series of `IShoppingMallCustomerActivityDailyStatistics.IRow` entries so that clients can correlate per-day trends with overall period-level headline numbers computed from the same underlying snapshot source.

totalDays.description:
Number of distinct calendar dates covered by the statistics result.

This value usually corresponds to the count of business dates within the requested reporting range for which the analytics pipeline produced `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` rows. It is used as the denominator when computing average per-day metrics in this summary.

If the requested period includes days for which no snapshot data exists (for example, before system launch), those dates may or may not be reflected here depending on the implementation; clients should treat this as the effective number of days represented by the returned data.

totalNewRegisteredCustomers.description:
Total number of customers who registered during the reporting window.

This aggregate is typically computed by counting distinct customers whose snapshot rows within the period indicate a "new" status according to business rules (for example, first registration date or first order date). It provides a period-level view of acquisition volume derived from `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`.

Operators can compare this value to active and ordering customer counts to understand acquisition effectiveness and early engagement behavior over the same window.

totalActiveCustomers.description:
Total count of active-customer instances across all days in the reporting window.

In most implementations, this value is obtained by summing, for each `stats_date`, the number of customers classified as "active" in `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`. Because the same customer can be active on multiple days, this total usually counts repeat activity and may exceed the number of unique customers.

It helps quantify engagement intensity across the period and is often analyzed alongside average active customers per day and ordering-customer metrics.

totalOrderingCustomers.description:
Total count of ordering-customer instances across all days in the reporting window.

This metric is generally derived by summing, for each `stats_date`, the number of customers who placed at least one order as captured in `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`. Like `totalActiveCustomers`, a customer may contribute to this count on multiple days if they place orders on multiple dates.

Comparing this aggregate to total active customers provides insight into how effectively the platform converts active users into buyers over the reporting window.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of orders placed by customers during the reporting window.

This value is computed from underlying order data and represented in the customer-daily statistics snapshots, then aggregated across all days in the selected period. It reflects gross order volume before separating out payment status, cancellations, or refunds.

Business stakeholders often use this metric in combination with GMV, NMV, and order-item counts to reason about marketplace throughput and conversion performance over time.

totalOrderItems.description:
Total number of order line items across all orders placed during the reporting window.

This aggregate is typically derived by summing item-level counts from order and order-item domain tables that feed into `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats`. It measures the total quantity of discrete line items sold, not just order headers.

Analysts frequently combine this metric with total orders and GMV to assess average basket size, product mix, and purchasing behavior during the period.

totalGrossMerchandiseValue.description:
Sum of gross merchandise value (GMV) across all days in the reporting window.

This figure is the aggregate of per-day GMV values ultimately derived from transactional data and surfaced via `shopping_mall_customer_daily_stats` or related snapshot tables. It is expressed in the platform’s base currency and does not account for refunds, cancellations, or other negative adjustments.

Dashboards commonly present this metric as the primary revenue-like headline for the selected period and compare it with net merchandise value and refund volumes obtained from complementary analytics endpoints.

averageDailyActiveCustomers.description:
Average number of active customers per day over the reporting window.

This metric is typically calculated as `totalActiveCustomers / totalDays` when `totalDays` is greater than zero. Implementations may choose how to round or format the resulting value for display.

It normalizes engagement intensity across periods of different lengths so that operators can compare day-to-day activity levels between time ranges without manually adjusting for duration.

averageDailyOrderingCustomers.description:
Average number of ordering customers per day over the reporting window.

This value is usually computed as `totalOrderingCustomers / totalDays` when at least one day is present in the summary. It describes the typical number of customers who place orders on a given day within the selected period.

When analyzed together with average daily active customers and order counts, it provides a compact view of how frequently active users convert into buyers throughout the reporting window.

averageDailyOrders.description:
Average number of orders per day over the reporting window.

The analytics pipeline generally computes this as `totalOrders / totalDays` for non-empty periods. It reflects the typical daily order volume for the chosen range and is useful for comparing operational load and sales performance between different reporting windows.

Stakeholders can use this metric alongside average daily GMV to understand both volume and value dimensions of daily order activity.

averageDailyGrossMerchandiseValue.description:
Average gross merchandise value (GMV) per day over the reporting window.

This metric is commonly calculated as `totalGrossMerchandiseValue / totalDays` when `totalDays` is greater than zero. It expresses the average daily GMV in the platform’s base currency, smoothing out day-to-day fluctuations across the reporting range.

Comparing this value between different periods helps identify growth trends, seasonal effects, or anomalies in daily revenue-like performance while controlling for differences in the number of days included in each period.

IShoppingMallCampaignPerformanceDailySta.description:
Daily campaign performance statistics time series for shoppingMall marketing and pricing campaigns.

This schema represents the response structure returned by the administrative campaign performance analytics endpoint that aggregates and normalizes metrics from snapshot tables such as `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` and potentially `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots`. It focuses on providing a compact, dashboard-friendly representation of campaign KPIs over time rather than exposing raw transactional or event-level data.

The structure is read-only from the API consumer’s perspective. Data is populated by background analytics pipelines that compute daily aggregates per campaign and store them in snapshot tables. The API simply projects those aggregates into a normalized, strongly typed DTO for use in admin reporting UIs, BI integrations, and operational monitoring tools.

items.description:
List of per-campaign daily performance series.

Each element in this array represents the complete time series of metrics for a single logical campaign (for example, a voucher, promotion, or marketing initiative) over the requested date range. The series is built from snapshot rows in tables such as `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`, grouped by campaign code and ordered by business date.

Client applications typically iterate over this array to render multiple lines in charts, one per campaign, or to build tabular campaign comparison reports.

IShoppingMallCampaignPerformanceDailySer.description:
Time-series performance metrics for a single shoppingMall marketing or pricing campaign.

This schema groups together all daily KPI points for one campaign over a specified date range. It is constructed primarily from rows in the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` snapshot table, optionally enriched with additional platform-level KPIs when needed. Each series is identified by a campaign code and may include human-readable labels used by dashboards.

The series is strictly analytical and read-only. It does not allow direct modification of underlying campaign configuration or snapshot rows. Instead, it provides a structure that admin UIs and reporting tools can use to display campaign trends such as impressions, clicks, conversions, GMV, and derived effectiveness ratios like CTR and conversion rate.

campaignCode.description:
Business identifier of the campaign.

This value corresponds to the `campaign_code` column in the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` snapshot table. It uniquely identifies the marketing, pricing, or voucher campaign whose performance is being analyzed.

Client applications use this code to correlate analytics data with campaign configuration entities and to display or filter specific campaigns in dashboards.

campaignName.description:
Human-readable name or label of the campaign for display purposes.

This field is not persisted directly in the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` snapshot table. Instead, it is typically joined or derived from campaign configuration tables or external marketing configuration services.

Dashboards use this value as the primary display label when rendering charts and tables so administrators do not have to rely on opaque campaign codes.

periodStart.description:
Inclusive start calendar date of the period covered by the series, using ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

This date corresponds to the earliest `stats_date` from `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` included in `points`. It is validated so that all points in the series fall on or after this date.

Admin dashboards use this field to clearly indicate the time window used when generating the campaign performance chart or report.

periodEnd.description:
Inclusive end calendar date of the period covered by the series, using ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

This date corresponds to the latest `stats_date` from `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` included in `points`. All daily points in the series must have a business date less than or equal to this value.

Together with `periodStart`, this allows clients to verify alignment between requested filters and actual data returned by the analytics pipeline.

points.description:
Ordered daily KPI points for this campaign within the requested period.

Each point corresponds to a single row in the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` snapshot table for the campaign’s code and a particular `stats_date`. The array is typically sorted by `statsDate` ascending so that clients can render continuous time-series charts easily.

Missing calendar dates within the period may be omitted or represented with zero values depending on the analytics pipeline; clients should be prepared to gracefully handle gaps or sparse series.

IShoppingMallCampaignPerformanceDailyPoi.description:
Single-day campaign performance metrics for a specific marketing or pricing campaign.

This schema provides a normalized view of one row from the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` snapshot table. It exposes daily counts and monetary values that quantify how a campaign performed on that date, including order volume, GMV, NMV, discount funding split, and new customer acquisition.

All fields are read-only from the API’s perspective. The underlying snapshot rows are maintained by analytics or ETL processes that recompute metrics periodically. API consumers must not attempt to infer or modify business rules based on this structure; instead they should treat it as a reporting-only representation.

statsDate.description:
Business date for which the campaign metrics are calculated, in ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

This value is derived from the `stats_date` column in the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` table, which is expected to be normalized to midnight UTC for consistency. It represents the calendar day used for grouping and aggregating metrics.

Clients commonly use this field as the x-axis dimension when plotting campaign performance charts and when aligning campaign data with other daily KPI series.

orderCount.description:
Number of orders on this date that were affected by the campaign.

This corresponds to the `order_count` column in `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`. It includes all orders where the campaign’s code was applied during pricing or checkout, regardless of payment outcome.

The count helps marketing and operations teams understand how much order volume the campaign drove relative to baseline activity and other campaigns.

paidOrderCount.description:
Number of campaign-affected orders on this date that reached a paid state.

Mapped from the `paid_order_count` column in `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`, this count reflects successful conversions where payment was completed. Orders that were cancelled, expired, or otherwise not paid are excluded.

This metric is often used together with `orderCount` and platform-level traffic metrics to compute campaign conversion performance and revenue quality.

gmvAmount.description:
Gross merchandise value attributable to this campaign on this date.

This value is derived from the `gmv_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` table and represents the total value of goods sold before refunds and cancellations, in the platform’s base currency.

It is a key input for marketing and finance reporting, enabling comparison of campaign-driven sales volume across time and between different campaigns.

nmvAmount.description:
Net merchandise value attributable to this campaign on this date.

This field is mapped from the `nmv_amount` column in `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`. It reflects GMV after accounting for refunds, cancellations, or other adjustments, again expressed in the platform’s base currency.

Comparing `nmvAmount` to `gmvAmount` helps operators understand the true retained value of campaign-driven orders after post-order events.

discountTotalAmount.description:
Total discount amount granted under this campaign on this date.

This value corresponds to `discount_total_amount` in `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`. It aggregates all discount impact applied due to the campaign, regardless of whether the platform or sellers funded the discount.

Analytics users often compare this to `nmvAmount` and `platformFundedDiscountAmount` to evaluate cost efficiency and ROAS (return on ad spend) for different campaigns.

platformFundedDiscountAmount.description:
Portion of the total discount amount funded by the platform.

Sourced from the `platform_funded_discount_amount` column in `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`, this value indicates how much of the discount budget was borne by the marketplace itself for this campaign and date.

It is used by finance and marketing teams to track promotional cost allocation and to calculate platform-side profitability of campaigns.

sellerFundedDiscountAmount.description:
Portion of the total discount amount funded by sellers.

This field maps to `seller_funded_discount_amount` in `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`. It represents the share of campaign discount costs that participating sellers agreed to bear.

Combined with `platformFundedDiscountAmount`, it enables transparent reporting of discount cost splits and supports reconciliation with seller earnings and invoices.

newCustomerOrderCount.description:
Number of paid orders under this campaign created by customers classified as new.

Based on the `new_customer_order_count` column in `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics`, this metric counts orders where the underlying customer satisfies the platform’s new-customer attribution rules (for example, first order within a given look-back window).

It is an important KPI for acquisition-focused campaigns and is often used to compute cost per new customer alongside marketing spend metrics.

IShoppingMallRefundAndDisputeStats.ISumm.description:
Summary view of daily refund and dispute statistics for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used as the element type in the response body of the administrative endpoint that exposes `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` rows over a given date range. Each instance represents a single calendar day’s aggregated metrics for refund and dispute activity, derived from operational tables such as refund requests, payment refunds, and disputes.

The schema is read-only and purely analytical. It allows admin and operations dashboards to render time-series charts and tabular reports without exposing raw case details or personally identifiable information. All numeric values are pre-aggregated by backend analytics jobs that populate the underlying snapshot table.

statsDate.description:
Business date for which refund and dispute metrics are calculated, in ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

This field is derived from the `stats_date` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot table. Time is normalized to midnight UTC in the underlying model so that each row clearly corresponds to a single calendar day.

Clients typically use this value as the x-axis dimension for time-series graphs and to align refund and dispute data with other daily KPIs, such as order volume or platform revenue.

refundRequestCount.description:
Total number of refund requests created on this date.

Mapped from the `refund_request_count` column in `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`, this value counts all newly opened refund cases regardless of their eventual outcome.

Operations and risk teams use this metric to monitor the inflow of new refund workload and to identify abnormal spikes in refund activity that may indicate product issues or potential abuse.

approvedRefundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests approved on this date.

This corresponds to the `approved_refund_request_count` column. It counts refund cases for which a positive decision was made on the given date, independent of when the request was originally opened.

Comparing this metric to `refundRequestCount` helps teams understand processing throughput and approval ratios over time.

rejectedRefundRequestCount.description:
Number of refund requests rejected on this date.

Derived from the `rejected_refund_request_count` column in the snapshot table, this figure captures how many refund cases received a negative decision on the business date.

Together with `approvedRefundRequestCount`, this value is used to calculate decision ratios and to monitor changes in refund policy enforcement or dispute resolution behavior.

refundedAmount.description:
Total refunded monetary amount on this date, expressed in the platform’s base currency.

This metric maps to the `refunded_amount` column in `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. It aggregates all payment refund operations that were completed on the date, regardless of when the underlying orders or refund requests were created.

Finance and risk teams rely on this figure to track the platform’s daily refund exposure and to reconcile it with payment provider reports and accounting systems.

partialRefundCount.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that were partial relative to the original charge.

Sourced from the `partial_refund_count` column, this count reflects cases where only a portion of the order or item value was refunded, as opposed to a full refund.

This metric is useful for understanding the complexity of customer service interactions and for identifying patterns such as frequent partial refunds on specific products or sellers.

fullRefundCount.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that fully refunded the relevant order or item.

This aligns with the `full_refund_count` column in the snapshot table. It counts refund events where the refund amount matches the full eligible amount for the affected order or line items.

Comparing `fullRefundCount` to `partialRefundCount` helps stakeholders understand whether refunds are primarily complete cancellations or targeted adjustments.

disputeOpenedCount.description:
Number of disputes created on this date for any reason.

Mapped from the `dispute_opened_count` column, this value counts newly opened disputes across all dispute types (for example, payment disputes, delivery conflicts, or policy violations).

Risk and operations teams use this metric to monitor the inflow of high-severity cases that may require manual investigation or cross-team collaboration.

disputeResolvedCount.description:
Number of disputes resolved on this date, regardless of when they were opened.

This value corresponds to the `dispute_resolved_count` column in `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. It tracks the throughput of dispute resolution workflows.

Comparing this count to `disputeOpenedCount` over time helps assess whether the backlog of open disputes is growing, shrinking, or remaining stable.

disputeResolvedForCustomerCount.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the customer on this date.

Derived from the `dispute_resolved_for_customer_count` column, this metric indicates how many resolved cases had customer-favorable outcomes, such as full refunds or corrective actions against sellers.

It is useful for monitoring customer satisfaction trends and for ensuring that platform policies are being applied consistently and fairly.

disputeResolvedForSellerCount.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the seller on this date.

This field maps to the `dispute_resolved_for_seller_count` column in the snapshot table. It counts cases where the seller’s position was upheld, such as disputes where the platform determined that service levels were met and no refund was warranted.

Analysts often review this metric alongside `disputeResolvedForCustomerCount` to evaluate balance in dispute decisions and to detect potential biases or policy issues.

averageRefundResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between refund request creation and final decision for refunds resolved on this date.

This value is taken from the `average_refund_resolution_time_hours` column in `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats`. It is computed over all refund cases whose final decision (approved or rejected) occurred on the business date.

Service teams use this KPI to assess operational efficiency, measure adherence to refund SLAs, and identify trends that may warrant process improvements or staffing adjustments.

averageDisputeResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between dispute creation and resolution for disputes resolved on this date.

Mapped from the `average_dispute_resolution_time_hours` column, this metric aggregates the resolution time for all disputes closed on the business date.

It is a key indicator for compliance with dispute SLAs and for understanding how quickly serious issues are being addressed. Significant increases may signal capacity constraints, process bottlenecks, or particularly complex cases.

IShoppingMallRegion.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall region used in list responses, dropdowns, and reference contexts.

This DTO exposes only the key identification and display fields required to represent a region in lightweight scenarios, while also surfacing its associated country as a summary object instead of a raw foreign key.

It maps directly to the `shopping_mall_regions` Prisma model but omits internal lifecycle management fields that are not needed for basic selection and display. The association to `shopping_mall_countries` is represented by the `country` summary object rather than by exposing the `shopping_mall_country_id` UUID column directly.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the region.

This value maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_regions` table and is used as the stable technical identifier when referencing a region from other entities or APIs.

It is suitable for use in internal references, administrative tools, and any API operations that require a region identifier.

code.description:
Business-level code for the region within its country.

The value is unique per country and may represent ISO subdivision codes or internal business identifiers. It is used in administrative tools, configuration screens, and sometimes in deep links or import/export processes.

Client applications typically use this code along with the associated `country` to constrain region choices and to maintain stable business references across environments.

name_en.description:
Region name in English used as the default human-readable label.

Client applications normally display this value in selection UIs such as address forms, shipping destination pickers, configuration pages, and geographic analytics dashboards.

In multilingual deployments, this value acts as a fallback label when a fully localized region name is not available.

region_type.description:
Optional semantic classification of the region, such as `state`, `province`, `city`, or a custom business-defined type.

This field can be used for reporting, analytics, or grouping regions in the user interface. Typical values might align with ISO subdivision types or internal taxonomy names.

When `null`, the region does not carry a specific classified type and is treated as a generic region in listings and filters.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this region is currently enabled for use across shopping mall features.

When `true`, the region can be used in shipping, risk segmentation, pricing, and address validation flows. When `false`, the region is effectively disabled for new operations but may still appear in historical data views and analytics.

Administrative tools and configuration UIs typically filter out inactive regions from default selection lists while still allowing operators to view and manage them.

sort_order.description:
Display ordering value within the country.

Lower values are positioned earlier when listing regions for selection, allowing administrators to control the default ordering of regions in UI components such as dropdowns and picker dialogs.

This field is also useful for building custom navigation trees or prioritized region lists in analytics and operational dashboards.

country.description:
Associated country that this region belongs to, represented as a lightweight summary object.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_country_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_regions` Prisma model, which links to a row in `shopping_mall_countries`.

Using `IShoppingMallCountry.ISummary` here provides enough context for display (for example, country name and code) without requiring clients to issue an additional API call to resolve the region's country for typical list and selection scenarios.

IShoppingMallRegionShippingPolicy.ISumma.description:
Summary representation of a region-specific shipping policy used in admin lists, configuration overviews, and lightweight references.

This DTO exposes the identifying fields and core constraint flags that describe how shipping behaves for a region without including the full historical or operational detail.

It maps to the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` Prisma model and is intended for read-only summary contexts. Create and update operations should use dedicated DTOs that focus on input constraints.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the region shipping policy.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table and is used as the stable handle when referencing or editing a specific policy record.

shopping_mall_region_id.description:
Identifier of the region this shipping policy applies to.

The value maps to the `shopping_mall_region_id` foreign key column and links the policy to a specific `shopping_mall_regions` record. Client applications use this to tie policy summaries back to the region context.

region.description:
Lightweight summary of the region this shipping policy belongs to.

Provides essential contextual information such as region code and name so that admin UIs and configuration overviews can display which geographic region the policy targets without issuing an additional region lookup.

policy_name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping policy for the region.

This name is primarily used in administrative tools and configuration user interfaces to help operators recognize and manage different regional shipping policy variants.

shipping_method_group.description:
Optional identifier of a shipping method group or profile preferred for this region.

The value can associate the policy with predefined carrier or service-level profiles defined elsewhere in the system. When null, no specific group preference is configured and the default platform behavior applies.

min_order_amount.description:
Minimum order total required for this policy to allow shipping to the region.

When set, orders whose monetary total falls below this threshold should be blocked or prevented from selecting shipping options governed by this policy. When null, there is no minimum order amount constraint at the policy level.

max_order_amount.description:
Maximum order total for which this policy is applicable.

This can be used to route high-value orders through different workflows or policy variants. When null, there is no upper bound on the order total for which this policy can be applied.

allows_cod.description:
Flag indicating whether cash-on-delivery (COD) or pay-on-delivery payments are allowed under this policy.

Checkout and payment flows must honor this flag when presenting payment options to customers whose shipping address falls within the associated region.

is_shipping_allowed.description:
Flag that determines whether the platform allows any shipping to the associated region under this policy.

When `false`, checkout flows for addresses mapped to this region must prevent shipping and surface an appropriate message to the user that shipping is not available.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes for operators that describe special conditions, exceptions, or reasoning behind this region shipping policy.

This text is stored in the `notes` column of the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table and can include internal guidance such as carrier limitations, regulatory constraints, or temporary business decisions. When null, no additional explanation has been recorded for this policy.

effective_from.description:
Optional start timestamp from which this policy becomes effective.

If provided, the platform should only consider the policy valid for shipments or checkouts occurring at or after this time. When null, the policy is treated as effective from system initialization or the moment it was created, subject to other business rules.

effective_until.description:
Optional end timestamp after which this policy is no longer considered active.

If populated, any shipments or checkouts evaluated after this timestamp should ignore the policy and consider more recent or fallback configurations. When null, the policy has no predefined expiry and remains valid until explicitly changed or soft-deleted.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this region shipping policy record was created.

This value comes from the non-nullable `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table and is stored in ISO 8601 date-time format. It is primarily used for auditing, troubleshooting configuration changes, and understanding when a particular shipping rule first became available.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this region shipping policy record was last updated.

The value reflects the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_region_shipping_policies` table and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields such as thresholds, flags, or notes are modified. Clients and admin tools can use it to detect stale configurations, support optimistic concurrency, or trigger cache invalidation.

IShoppingMallCategoryLocalization.ISumma.description:
Summary DTO for localized shopping mall category information.

Represents a lightweight view of a category’s localized metadata for a specific locale in the shopping mall catalog. Used primarily in list responses, nested references, and read operations where only essential localization fields are required rather than the full localization entity.

This summary typically accompanies category structures when rendering localized navigation trees, search results, or filter menus, without exposing internal or non-essential fields.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category localization record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` table and uniquely distinguishes each localization entry for a category and locale pair.

locale.description:
Locale code associated with this localization entry.

Typically follows IETF BCP 47 language tag format such as `en-US`, `ko-KR`, or `ja-JP`. It determines which language and regional formatting this localization applies to and is used by the storefront when selecting appropriate translations for a user.

name.description:
Localized display name of the category for the given locale.

This value is stored in the `name` column of `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is used as the primary label when rendering category navigation menus, search filters, and product listing breadcrumbs in the target language.

description.description:
Optional localized description that explains the category in the specified language.

The value corresponds to the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations`. It can contain marketing copy or explanatory text for category landing pages, SEO content blocks, or contextual help. When null, no localized description has been provided and the storefront may fall back to a default language or omit the extended description.

seo_title.description:
Optional localized SEO title for the category.

This field maps to the `seo_title` column in the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` table and is typically used as the HTML `<title>` content or equivalent metadata when rendering localized category pages. When null, the system may derive a title from the localized name or other defaults.

seo_description.description:
Optional localized SEO description for the category.

The value is stored in the `seo_description` column of `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is intended for use in meta description tags and search engine snippets. It should provide a concise, human-readable summary of the category in the target language. When null, the storefront may omit the description or fall back to another language or generic text.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this category localization record was created.

This non-nullable field mirrors the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_category_localizations` Prisma model and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string. It is primarily used for auditing, debugging content rollout, and understanding when localized content became available.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this category localization record was last updated.

The value is taken from the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_category_localizations` and is updated whenever any localized field such as `name`, `description`, `seo_title`, or `seo_description` changes. Consumers may use it for cache invalidation, synchronization with external content systems, or display of "last updated" information.

category.description:
Summary of the base category that this localization belongs to.

This field provides essential identity and display information for the underlying category, such as its slug, English name, and status, without requiring clients to fetch the full category separately. It allows navigation and management UIs to show both the localized label and the category’s structural context in a single response.

IShoppingMallPolicyVersion.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single policy version within the shopping mall business policy framework.
