This summary focuses on the identifying and lifecycle fields needed to list or embed policy versions in other resources, without exposing the full Markdown body or large parameter payloads.

It is typically returned in list endpoints, selection dialogs, or as a referenced object when explaining which policy version governed a particular decision or case.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the policy version.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_policy_versions` table and is used to reference this version from other entities such as cases, overrides, or audit logs.

version_code.description:
Business-facing version code for this policy version.

Examples include short semantic identifiers such as `v1`, `v2`, or date-based codes like `2024-01`. It is unique per business policy and is used by operators when referring to a specific version in discussions and documentation.

title.description:
Short human-readable title summarizing the intent of this policy version.

The title is shown in administrative UIs, configuration tools, and audit screens where operators need to quickly recognize which version is being referenced.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the policy version.

Typical values include labels such as `draft`, `active`, or `retired`. Only versions in an active status should be applied to new decisions, while draft or retired versions remain in history for audit and analysis.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this policy version becomes applicable, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When null, the version is considered applicable immediately once it enters an active status. This field is used when determining which version was in force at a given point in time.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which this policy version is no longer applicable, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When null, there is no scheduled expiry and the version remains valid until it is explicitly retired or superseded. Consumers can use this field to determine whether the version is currently within its effective window.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this policy version record was created.

This value is stored in the `created_at` column and participates in audit and timeline views, allowing operators to see when a particular version first entered the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this policy version record was last updated.

This field is useful for understanding configuration change recency and for troubleshooting situations where rule behavior changed after an update.

policy.description:
Logical business policy that this concrete version belongs to.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_business_policy_id` and provides a business-friendly summary of the parent policy so that clients can understand which policy is being versioned without performing an additional lookup.

IShoppingMallRiskRule.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a risk rule used by the shopping mall risk engine.

This DTO exposes the identifying, scoping, and lifecycle metadata necessary to list, search, and embed risk rules in other responses, without including the full expression payload or complete configuration details.

It is commonly used in admin risk configuration screens, risk case timelines, and audit views to indicate which rules were active or triggered for a given evaluation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the risk rule.

This primary key comes from the `shopping_mall_risk_rules` table and is used as a stable reference from risk cases, events, and audit records.

rule_code.description:
Stable business identifier for the risk rule.

Example values include `high_refund_rate`, `multiple_failed_logins`, or `suspicious_address_mismatch`. This code is used by risk systems, configuration tools, and reporting to reference the rule in a human-friendly yet stable way.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the risk rule.

The name is displayed in administrative consoles, dashboards, and configuration UIs so that risk analysts and operators can quickly recognize what the rule does.

scope.description:
Scope in which this risk rule operates.

Typical scopes include values such as `account`, `order`, `payment`, `seller`, or `session`. The scope determines the kind of entity this rule is evaluated against and helps segment rules by functional area.

severity.description:
Business severity of this risk rule.

Example values include `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. Severity influences alerting, escalation policies, and how aggressively downstream systems respond to rule hits.

is_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether this risk rule is currently enabled for evaluation.

Enabled rules are considered by the risk engine during scoring and detection, while disabled rules are preserved for history and potential future reactivation but are ignored in runtime evaluations.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this risk rule becomes effective, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When null, the rule is considered effective immediately on creation or enablement. This field is used when reconstructing which rules were in effect at the time a specific risk decision was made.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which this risk rule is no longer considered during evaluation, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When null, the rule has no scheduled expiry and continues to apply until it is explicitly disabled or logically retired.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this risk rule was created.

This value supports audit trails and helps risk teams understand when a rule first became available in the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this risk rule was last updated.

Changes to expression parameters, naming, or configuration will update this field, giving operators visibility into recent configuration activity.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall customer authentication session.

This DTO is used to represent existing sessions in list responses, dashboards, and audit-oriented views where only high-level context is required. It includes connection metadata, lifecycle timestamps, and a summarized view of the owning customer account for quick inspection.

The schema maps directly to the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` Prisma model and is designed for administrative and security monitoring use cases, exposing only non-sensitive fields and a minimal customer summary reference.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer session.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table and uniquely distinguishes each authenticated session instance for auditing and monitoring purposes.

customer.description:
Summary of the customer account that owns this authenticated session.

This object is derived from the `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` model and resolves to a lightweight `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` representation. It allows administrators and security tools to see who owns the session without performing an additional customer lookup.

ip.description:
IP address observed when the session was created.

The value is taken from the `ip` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table and captures the remote client IP at login time for audit, security analytics and risk evaluation.

href.description:
Full URL (href) that the customer used when establishing the session.

This value mirrors the `href` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` model and provides page-level context such as which entry point or UI flow was used during login.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL at the time the session was created.

The underlying column is `referrer` in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table and is commonly used for marketing attribution, security investigation and anomaly detection.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created after successful authentication.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` model and represents the precise moment the login flow completed successfully.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the session was explicitly terminated or naturally expired.

When present, this reflects the `expired_at` column in `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` and indicates that the session is no longer considered active.

Indicates that the session is still considered active and has not yet recorded an expiry time.

Active sessions keep `expired_at` as null until logout, timeout, or cleanup processes mark a concrete end.

expired_at.description:
Nullable timestamp representing when the session stopped being active.

A non-null value indicates logout, expiry, or forced invalidation. A null value indicates that the session is still active according to business rules and cleanup policies.

IShoppingMallCustomerAddress.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a customer-managed shipping address in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is designed for list and reference scenarios, such as rendering the customer's address book or selecting a shipping destination during checkout, where only the most important identifying and display fields are required.

It preserves the core address components from the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` Prisma model and enriches them with associated country and region summary objects so that UIs can render localized labels without issuing additional lookup requests.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer address record.

This value maps directly to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table and is used as the stable reference when updating or deleting an address.

It is generated by the system and is always present for persisted address records.

recipient_name.description:
Name of the person or entity receiving deliveries at this address.

The value corresponds to the `recipient_name` column in `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` and is typically shown prominently in address book and checkout UIs.

It should reflect the contact name that the carrier will see on the shipping label.

line1.description:
First address line for the shipping destination.

This field maps to the `line1` column and typically contains the street name, house or building number, and other primary location details.

Clients should ensure this line is complete and unambiguous enough for the local postal system or carrier.

line2.description:
Optional second address line providing additional location detail.

This property corresponds to the nullable `line2` column in `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` and is often used for apartment numbers, suites, building names, or additional routing instructions.

When not needed, the value is null rather than an empty string to clearly distinguish absence of data.

city.description:
City or locality component of the address.

The value comes from the `city` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table and is displayed in address summaries and shipping labels.

It should represent the municipality or locality recognized by the destination country’s postal system.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code associated with this address.

This field maps to the `postal_code` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` model and is required for most shipping destinations.

Format validation is typically country-specific and may be enforced by client applications or server-side business rules.

phone_number.description:
Optional phone number for contacting the recipient about deliveries.

This property mirrors the nullable `phone_number` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table and can be used by carriers or customer support in case of delivery issues.

When absent, the value is null; when present, it should follow a normalized format appropriate for the supported region, such as E.164.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this address is the customer’s preferred default shipping address.

The value is taken from the `is_default` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table and is typically true for at most one active address per customer.

Client applications can use this marker to pre-select the address during checkout or to highlight it in address book views.

country.description:
Summary of the country in which this address resides.

This association is derived from the non-nullable `shopping_mall_country_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` model and resolves to a lightweight `IShoppingMallCountry.ISummary` representation.

It is intended to provide localized country labels and codes directly in address summary responses so that UIs do not need to perform separate lookups.

region.description:
Optional summary of the region or state associated with this address.

This association is based on the nullable `shopping_mall_region_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table. When present, it resolves to `IShoppingMallRegion.ISummary` to expose human-readable region names and codes.

When the address does not belong to a specific region or the region concept is not applicable for the country, this property is null.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the address record was first created.

This property directly reflects the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table and records the creation time in UTC.

It is useful for audit displays, sorting address lists by recency, or diagnosing when an address entered the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the address record was last updated.

The value corresponds to the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` model and is automatically maintained by the backend whenever the address changes.

Consumers may use this to detect stale data, show last-edited information to the user, or implement optimistic concurrency where appropriate.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the address, or null when the address is active.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_addresses` table and indicates when the address was logically removed.

Active addresses have a null value, while non-null timestamps allow the system to preserve historical references without showing the address in normal customer-facing lists.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrator authentication session on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is intended for list views and monitoring tools that need to show recent or active sessions for admin accounts without exposing sensitive authentication material such as tokens or secrets.

It closely follows the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` Prisma model while selecting only the columns that are meaningful and safe to expose in a summary context, such as the owning admin, network origin, and lifecycle timestamps of the session. It also transforms the owning admin relation into a semantic `admin` summary reference instead of exposing the raw foreign key.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin session.

This value corresponds to the `id` primary key column in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table and uniquely distinguishes each authentication session established by admin users.

It can be used by administrative tools to reference, inspect, or terminate a specific session when such capabilities are implemented.

admin.description:
Summary information about the administrator who owns this session.

This field represents the BELONGS-TO relation previously exposed as the `shopping_mall_admin_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table.

By providing an `IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary` object instead of a raw UUID, client applications can render session lists with human-friendly admin context (such as name or email) in a single call, without needing a separate lookup for the admin record.

ip.description:
IP address from which the admin initiated the session.

The value is stored in the `ip` column of the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table and captures the network origin at login time, which is useful for audit, anomaly detection, and security investigations.

Client UI components typically display this field in security and session management screens to help operators verify whether access patterns look legitimate.

href.description:
Full URL that was accessed when the session was created.

This property is backed by the `href` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table and records the complete location the admin was visiting at the time of authentication, including path and query string.

It is valuable in troubleshooting, as it provides context about the entry point used to establish the session and can assist in reconstructing navigation flows when investigating issues.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL present when the admin logged in and the session was established.

It is stored in the `referrer` column of the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table and indicates the previous page or external site that led to the login, helping with security analysis and traffic source attribution.

This value is especially useful in risk analysis tools and internal dashboards that monitor how admins access the platform.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session was created after successful authentication.

It maps directly to the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table and marks the point in time the session became valid.

Monitoring and audit interfaces commonly use this field to sort sessions chronologically and to compute session lifetimes.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session ended or expired, or null if the session is still considered active.

This property is backed by the nullable `expired_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_sessions` table and is populated when the platform explicitly terminates the session or when it naturally expires based on policy.

Security and governance tools can rely on this field to distinguish currently active sessions from historical ones and to detect unusually long-lived sessions.

IShoppingMallGuestuserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a guest user session in the shoppingMall platform aligned directly to the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` Prisma model.

Each instance corresponds to a single row in the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table and captures when and how a guest identity interacted with the platform during a particular browsing session. The summary exposes connection context such as IP address and entry URLs as well as lifecycle timestamps for creation and optional expiration.

This schema intentionally includes only fields that are physically present in the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` model. Richer projections that embed guest user details or cross-reference other entities are defined in separate DTOs that are not directly bound to this Prisma model.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user session.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table and is stored in its `id` column. It is used by administrative tools and backend services to reference, audit, or correlate this session with related guest activity.

Clients should treat this identifier as opaque and use it strictly for lookups, diagnostics, and correlation.

ip.description:
IP address observed for the guest session when it was created.

The value is stored in the `ip` column of the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table and typically represents the client IP address as interpreted by the platform, potentially influenced by load balancers or reverse proxies.

Security, risk, and analytics subsystems can use this property to detect suspicious access patterns, perform geo-based segmentation, and support forensic investigations.

href.description:
URL that initiated the guest session from the platform perspective.

This field is persisted in the `href` column of the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table and usually contains the full URL of the first page where the session became recognizable, such as a landing page or product detail view.

Product and analytics teams can leverage this value to analyze entry funnels, understand which pages are responsible for session creation, and debug user journeys for anonymous visitors.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL recorded at the time the guest session started.

The value is stored in the `referrer` column of the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table and generally represents the previous page or external website that directed the visitor to the platform when the session was first created.

Marketing and risk analysis tools can use this property to attribute traffic sources, evaluate the quality and safety of referrers, and identify campaigns or channels that drive guest activity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest session record was created.

This property maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table. It indicates the exact moment when the platform persisted the session for the associated guest identity based on the first qualifying interaction.

The value is an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and is commonly used to order sessions chronologically, filter by time range, and compute session-based metrics such as daily active sessions.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest session expired, was terminated, or otherwise closed.

This field corresponds to the nullable `expired_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guestuser_sessions` table. When `expired_at` is `null`, the session is considered active or at least not explicitly closed from the system perspective. When populated, it contains an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC representing the moment when the session reached its inactivity timeout, was revoked, or was closed by the authentication subsystem.

This property allows operators and analytics systems to distinguish between ongoing and completed sessions, estimate session durations, and implement cleanup or archival processes for stale session data.

IShoppingMallAccountRiskFlag.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an account risk flag within the shopping mall platform.

This summary DTO is optimized for list views, dashboards, and embedding inside other entities where only the key identifying and business-critical attributes of a risk flag are required.

It exposes the risk flag identity, classification, severity, activation status, and core lifecycle timestamps, without including any polymorphic ownership linkage rows.

Use this type when you need to quickly evaluate or display risk posture across many accounts without loading full linkage details per actor.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the account risk flag.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.id` and is a UUID primary key used to join with linkage tables and for audit trails.

Use this value whenever you need to reference or fetch the detailed risk flag record.

actor_type.description:
Logical actor type that this risk flag targets, such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `guestuser`.

This directly maps to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.actor_type` and is used for filtering and aggregations across different actor populations.

Client applications should treat this as a machine-readable classification string and avoid hard-coding assumptions beyond documented actor types.

code.description:
Machine-oriented risk flag code, for example `HIGH_REFUND_RATE` or `SUSPICIOUS_LOGIN_PATTERN`.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.code` and is used by risk engines, rule evaluators, and reporting systems.

UI surfaces can also display this value as a compact identifier next to localized human-readable labels.

severity.description:
Business severity level of this risk, such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical` depending on policy configuration.

This maps to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.severity` and determines how aggressively automated systems or admins should react to the flag.

Client applications may use this field to choose visual emphasis or sorting order in dashboards.

active.description:
Indicates whether this risk flag is currently active.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.active`. When `true`, the flag should be considered during risk evaluation and decision-making; when `false`, the flag has been cleared, expired, or superseded.

Use this property when filtering for currently effective risk flags versus historical ones.

expires_at.description:
Optional timestamp when this risk flag automatically stops being considered active.

This directly maps to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.expires_at`. When present, systems should treat the flag as time-bounded and ignore it after this point.

Clients should handle `null` to represent flags with no scheduled automatic expiry.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the risk flag record.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.created_at` and is stored in UTC using an ISO 8601 date-time representation.

It is primarily used in audit trails, chronological listings, and to understand when the risk condition was first detected.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the risk flag record.

This maps to `shopping_mall_account_risk_flags.updated_at` and reflects when any part of the risk flag definition was last modified, such as severity changes or reason updates.

Use this value when sorting by recency of changes or for cache invalidation strategies.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a security-related event associated with an actor in the shopping mall platform.

This summary DTO is used by index and search endpoints that return paginated lists of actor security events for administrative monitoring, investigations, and dashboards. It exposes only the key scalar fields required to scan and filter event history efficiently, without including large metadata payloads.

Clients can use the `id` from this summary to retrieve the full `IShoppingMallActorSecurityEvent` detail representation when deeper forensic or compliance analysis is required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the security event.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` table and is used to fetch the full detail record or correlate with linkage tables that attach the event to concrete actors.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that this security event concerns.

Typical values include `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, and `guestuser`. It enables administrators to quickly understand which actor family is affected and to apply actor-type specific filters in list views and analytics queries.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable code describing the category of security event.

Examples include `LOGIN_FAILED`, `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`, `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED`, or `SESSION_REVOKED`. List screens and dashboards use this field to group, sort, and identify patterns across large numbers of events.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the security event was recorded.

This value represents the creation time of the row in the `shopping_mall_actor_security_events` table and is commonly used for chronological sorting, time-range filtering, and retention policy evaluation in administrative UIs.

ip.description:
Optional IP address associated with the security event.

When present, this string captures the remote address from which the action originated and provides quick context for detecting suspicious geolocation or repeated failures. It is nullable when the IP is not known, not collected, or not applicable to the event type.

user_agent.description:
Optional HTTP user agent string captured for the event.

In summary views this field offers a compact glimpse into the device or client used during the event, supporting simple pattern checks (for example, mobile versus desktop, or specific automation signatures) without requiring access to the full detail payload.

IShoppingMallActorSearch.ISummary.description:

displayName.description:
Primary display name of the actor shown in search results.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a product in the shopping mall catalog for list and search results.

Represents a lightweight projection of the core product attributes along with key classification and rating aggregates required to render product grids, carousels, and search results, without including full description or deep SKU/variant details.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product in the shopping mall catalog.

This value is stable across all SKUs and localized representations of the same logical product concept.

name.description:
Primary name of the product as displayed in catalog lists and search results.

This is typically the default or locale-resolved title that customers see when browsing.

thumbnailUrl.description:
URL of the primary thumbnail image representing this product in list views.

The image is expected to be pre-uploaded to a CDN or object storage and accessible via HTTPS. May be omitted when a product does not yet have any images configured.

minPrice.description:
Lowest current sellable price among all active SKUs for this product, expressed in the platform's default currency.

Used for price badges such as "from $X" in product lists.

maxPrice.description:
Highest current sellable price among all active SKUs for this product, expressed in the platform's default currency.

When equal to minPrice the product is effectively single-priced across its variants.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency of minPrice and maxPrice values (for example, "USD" or "KRW").

primaryCategoryName.description:
Human-readable name of the primary category to which this product belongs.

This is a denormalized value used to show category chips or breadcrumbs in list views without requiring additional category lookups.

ratingAverage.description:
Average rating score for the product calculated from approved customer reviews.

Typically represented on a 1–5 scale. May be omitted when the product has no reviews yet.

ratingCount.description:
Total number of approved reviews that contribute to the ratingAverage for this product.

Used for displaying review counts in list views and for sorting by popularity.

isVisible.description:
Indicates whether the product is currently visible in the public catalog for the calling context.

A false value means the product is hidden due to visibility rules, policy blocks, or availability constraints.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an additional product image used in product galleries.

This summary DTO is designed for list and embedding contexts where only lightweight image information is required rather than the full product and catalog hierarchy. It exposes the core identity, ordering, and presentation metadata of a product image without including heavy relational payloads.

The schema maps directly onto the shopping_mall_product_images Prisma model but intentionally omits soft‑delete internals and full parent product details to keep responses compact and safe for public exposure.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product image.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_product_images.id and is used to distinguish individual image records in read operations, logs, and internal references.

Clients typically do not need to manipulate this value directly but may use it when referring back to a specific image in UI state or audit flows.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that owns this image.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_product_images.shopping_mall_product_id at the database level and links the image record to its parent product entity.

In this summary DTO it is exposed as a concise, API‑friendly `product_id` field and kept as a scalar UUID to avoid circular references and heavy expansions, while still allowing administrative and analytical callers to correlate images with products.

image_uri.description:
Absolute or fully qualified URI pointing to the image or media resource.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_product_images.image_uri and should reference a CDN or object storage location that is directly accessible by clients. The URI must be valid according to standard URI syntax and is the primary field used by frontends to render product gallery images.

alt_text.description:
Optional human‑readable alternative text describing the image for accessibility.

This field maps to shopping_mall_product_images.alt_text and is intended for screen readers and situations where the image cannot be displayed. When null, no explicit alternative text has been provided for this particular image.

display_order.description:
Ordering index used to control the sequence of images within a product gallery.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_product_images.display_order and participates in a uniqueness constraint together with the owning product. Lower values generally appear earlier in galleries, but exact ordering is determined by client logic using this numeric value.

IShoppingMallProductLocalization.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of localized product content for a specific locale.

This DTO is optimized for list and embedding scenarios where a compact view of localized product text is needed, such as catalog listings or search results. It exposes the key identifying and display fields without loading the full product hierarchy or heavy related data.

The schema maps directly to the shopping_mall_product_localizations Prisma model and is structured so that clients can quickly select appropriate locale content while keeping payloads small and efficient.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product localization row.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_product_localizations.id and uniquely distinguishes each localized text bundle for a product and locale pair.

Most clients rely on the combination of `product_id` and `locale` for selection and may use this identifier primarily for internal tracking and debugging.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that this localization belongs to.

This field maps to shopping_mall_product_localizations.shopping_mall_product_id at the database level and links localized text back to the core product entity stored in shopping_mall_products.

In this summary DTO it is exposed as a compact `product_id` to keep the API surface clean and to avoid embedding the full product object, which would be unnecessary and could introduce circular references in list or search result contexts.

locale.description:
IETF language tag representing the locale of this localization, such as "en-US" or "ko-KR".

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_product_localizations.locale and participates in a uniqueness constraint together with product_id. Clients use this tag to select the appropriate localized content matching the user’s language and region settings.

title.description:
Localized product title for this locale.

This field maps to shopping_mall_product_localizations.title and is typically used as the primary display name of the product in localized catalog listings, detail pages, and search result summaries.

summary.description:
Localized short summary description suitable for listing views.

This corresponds to shopping_mall_product_localizations.summary and provides a concise, locale‑specific explanation of the product intended for grid and list UIs where space is limited.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall product category used in list responses, dropdowns, and lightweight references.

This summary focuses on identifiers, default English naming, hierarchy hints, status, and display-order information so that clients can render navigation and selection UIs without loading the full category entity.

It is derived from the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and intentionally excludes large text fields and internal audit details that are not necessary for list or reference contexts.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category.

This is the primary key of the underlying `shopping_mall_categories` record and is used to reference the category in APIs, foreign keys, and internal links.

slug.description:
URL-friendly slug identifying the category within its parent scope.

The slug is unique among siblings and is typically used to build SEO-friendly URLs, navigation paths, and integration keys for the category.

name_en.description:
Default English name of the category.

This value is used as the primary display label in UIs when no locale-specific label is applied or when English is the desired locale.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the category.

Typical values include `active`, `hidden`, and `deprecated`, and client applications can use this field to decide whether to show the category in navigation, selection controls, or administrative tools.

is_leaf.description:
Indicates whether the category is currently treated as a leaf node in the hierarchy.

Leaf categories are usually eligible targets for product assignments and are often treated differently in navigation or validation logic compared to non-leaf categories.

sort_order.description:
Numeric ordering value used to determine the relative display order of this category among its siblings.

Lower values are displayed earlier in lists or navigation menus, enabling administrators to control category ordering without relying solely on alphabetical sorting.

IShoppingMallProductAttributeValue.ISumm.description:
Summary representation of an allowed product attribute value in the shopping mall catalog.

Each record corresponds to a single permissible value for a product-specific attribute, such as a particular color or size option. The summary view focuses on identifiers and display-related fields that are frequently used to build selection UIs and variant pickers.

This type is intended for lightweight listing and embedding within product and SKU-related responses, avoiding heavy relational detail while preserving ordering and localization-relevant information.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product attribute value.

This value maps directly to shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.id and serves as the stable primary key for the attribute value. It is used as the join target from SKU attribute binding tables and for administrative management operations.

Client applications should treat this as an opaque identifier and should not assume any semantic structure.

value.description:
Canonical representation of the attribute value.

This property is sourced from shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.value and encodes the normalized data value for the option, such as "RED", "XL", or another system-friendly form. It is used internally for uniqueness enforcement and programmatic comparisons.

Consumers may use this field for machine-level logic or to construct stable keys, while preferring display_value for end-user presentation.

display_value.description:
Human-readable display text for the attribute value.

This value comes from shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_value and is optimized for direct presentation in user interfaces, such as dropdowns, swatches, or filter chips. It may reflect localized or stylistically adjusted text compared to the canonical value.

UI components should generally prefer this field when showing attribute values to end users.

display_order.description:
Ordering hint for this value within its attribute.

The value corresponds to shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.display_order and determines how the option should be sorted relative to other values of the same attribute. Lower numbers typically appear earlier in selection lists.

This ordering is important for consistent variant presentation, such as listing sizes in a logical progression or colors in a curated sequence.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the attribute value record.

This field maps to shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.created_at and captures when the value was first defined for the associated product attribute. It is useful for audit trails and chronological reporting.

In many UI scenarios this timestamp is not surfaced directly, but it remains important for data governance and back-office tooling.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the attribute value record.

The property reflects shopping_mall_product_attribute_values.updated_at and is updated whenever the canonical or display characteristics of the value change, such as renaming or reordering.

Client systems can use this value to drive incremental synchronization logic or to detect when cached attribute configurations have become stale.

id.description:
Primary key of the SKU-attribute-value link in summary form.

This UUID uniquely identifies a single association between a SKU and a specific product attribute value within the shopping mall catalog. It corresponds directly to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.id` and is used to reference this junction row in list and inspection contexts.

Clients typically use this identifier when drilling down into a single association or when invoking update and delete operations on the link.

shopping_mall_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU that owns this attribute value association.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_sku_id` and references the primary key of a `shopping_mall_skus` record. It indicates which concrete SKU variant this association belongs to.

In summary views, this is kept as a raw UUID to avoid circular references while still allowing clients to correlate link rows back to their owning SKU when needed.

shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id.description:
Identifier of the product attribute value linked to the SKU.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.shopping_mall_product_attribute_value_id` and references a row in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`. It specifies which allowed attribute value (for example, a concrete color or size) is applied to the SKU through this association.

In summary responses, clients can aggregate or filter link rows by this identifier and retrieve full attribute value details from dedicated product attribute endpoints.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU-attribute-value association row was created.

The value reflects `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.created_at` and captures the moment the link between the SKU and the product attribute value was first established. It is useful for audit trails, catalog configuration history views, and debugging variant setup flows.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU-attribute-value association row was last updated.

This value mirrors `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.updated_at` and is automatically maintained whenever the junction record is modified. In list views, it helps operators identify recently changed associations that may require review or synchronization.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this SKU-attribute-value association, if any.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values.deleted_at`. When `null`, the association is considered active. When set to a date-time value, it indicates that the link has been logically removed while still retained for historical, analytical, or audit purposes.

Summary lists may choose to exclude rows with a non-null `deleted_at`, or present them with distinct visual status depending on the use case.

IShoppingMallSkuAttributeValue.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a SKU–attribute-value link used for list and search responses.

This schema represents a lightweight projection of the `shopping_mall_sku_attribute_values` junction table, which binds concrete SKUs in `shopping_mall_skus` to allowed product attribute values defined in `shopping_mall_product_attribute_values`.

It includes the primary key, foreign key identifiers to the owning SKU and attribute value, and audit timestamps, allowing clients to efficiently inspect and filter association rows in list and search APIs without loading full, deeply nested catalog structures.

IShoppingMallSkuExternalId.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an external identifier associated with a single SKU in the shopping mall catalog.

This DTO is designed for list and embedding scenarios where integrations or operations tooling need to understand which external systems reference a SKU without loading the full entity. It focuses on the core identifying fields and timestamps that are important for monitoring and auditing.

The summary intentionally omits any composition children or heavy navigation properties so it can be safely used in paginated responses or nested inside other DTOs without causing payload bloat.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU external identifier record.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids.id` and is generated by the system when the external mapping is created. It is immutable for the lifetime of the record and is used as the primary key in all internal references.

Clients can safely treat this as an opaque identifier and must not attempt to infer meaning from its value.

system_code.description:
Machine-readable code of the external system that owns this identifier.

Typical examples include codes for warehouse management systems, enterprise resource planning tools, third‑party marketplaces, or barcode registries. The value corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids.system_code` and participates in unique constraints combined with the external identifier or the SKU.

Client applications use this field to distinguish between different integration channels when displaying or managing external IDs.

external_id.description:
Identifier value used by the external system for this SKU.

This string maps to `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids.external_id` and contains the raw identifier issued by the external system, such as a remote SKU code, barcode value, or partner catalog key.

The `(system_code, external_id)` pair is unique and can be used to look up the corresponding SKU mapping during synchronization or reconciliation flows.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this external identifier record was created.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids.created_at` and is recorded in UTC. It allows operators to understand when the integration mapping was first established.

The field is immutable after creation and can be leveraged for chronological sorting or historical analysis.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this external identifier record was last updated.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_sku_external_ids.updated_at` and is automatically maintained by the system whenever the external identifier mapping changes, for example if the external system code or identifier string is corrected.

Clients can use this field to detect stale mappings or to order records by most recently synchronized.

IShoppingMallCatalogVisibilityRule.ISumm.description:
Lightweight summary view of a catalog visibility rule.

This summary type is designed for list views, quick inspection screens, and embedded references where only the key identification, scoping, and high-level behavior of a visibility rule are required instead of the full entity.

It corresponds to the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` Prisma model but intentionally omits large or rarely-used fields while still allowing operators and admins to understand which catalog entity is affected, for which actors or regions, and whether the rule is currently active.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the catalog visibility rule.

This field maps to the primary key column `id` in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and uniquely distinguishes one visibility rule from another in the platform.

rule_type.description:
Type of the visibility rule, such as `hide`, `show_only_to_registered`, or `region_restricted`.

This value comes from the `rule_type` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and is used by the catalog engine to determine how the rule should be applied when evaluating product or SKU visibility.

actor_type.description:
Optional actor type this visibility rule targets.

When present, it corresponds to the `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and typically contains values such as `guestUser`, `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`, indicating which user group is affected by the rule. When null, the rule applies regardless of actor type.

region_code.description:
Optional region or market code that scopes this visibility rule.

This mirrors the `region_code` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and is used when the rule is specific to a geographic or logical region. When null, the rule is not restricted to a particular region.

enabled.description:
Indicates whether this visibility rule is currently active.

This maps to the `enabled` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and is evaluated by the catalog layer to decide if the rule should be considered when calculating visibility. Disabled rules remain stored for audit or future reactivation but are ignored at runtime.

seller.description:
Seller that this visibility rule is scoped to, if the rule is seller-specific.

This association replaces the low-level `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and provides a summary view of the affected seller using `IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary`. When null, the rule is not restricted to a single seller and may apply at a broader catalog scope.

product.description:
Product that this visibility rule targets when the rule is product-specific.

This association replaces the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key and exposes a lightweight summary of the product via `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary`, allowing clients to understand the impacted catalog item without issuing separate product queries.

sku.description:
SKU that this visibility rule targets when the rule is SKU-specific.

This association replaces the `shopping_mall_sku_id` foreign key and provides a summary of the concrete variant using `IShoppingMallSku.ISummary`, which is especially useful when a rule applies only to a particular SKU rather than the entire product.

starts_at.description:
Optional timestamp from which this visibility rule becomes effective.

This property mirrors the `starts_at` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table. When set, catalog engines should only apply the rule at or after this point in time. When null, the rule is considered effective immediately upon creation or enablement.

ends_at.description:
Optional timestamp after which this visibility rule no longer applies.

It corresponds to the `ends_at` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table. When populated, the rule is treated as expired strictly after this moment. When null, the rule has no scheduled end time and remains active until disabled or deleted.

reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation describing the purpose or background of this visibility rule.

This directly reflects the `reason` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and is typically used in governance, audit, and admin UI screens to document why the rule was introduced or what scenario it is intended to address.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this visibility rule record was created.

This field maps to the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and is used for chronological sorting, audit trails, and determining how long the rule has been in effect.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this visibility rule record was last updated.

It comes from the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_visibility_rules` table and indicates the most recent modification time, which is useful for audit history and cache invalidation strategies.

IShoppingMallCatalogSearchIndexEntry.ISu.description:
Summary view of a catalog search index entry stored in the shoppingMall search subsystem.

This DTO is optimized for administrative and operational list views that need to inspect the state of the full-text search index for products and SKUs without loading unnecessary internal details, such as all raw denormalized text.

It corresponds to the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` Prisma model and focuses on fields that help understand which catalog entity is indexed, for which locale, and how strongly it will be ranked in search results.

In addition to the core index columns, the summary exposes lightweight projections of the associated product and SKU through `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary` and `IShoppingMallSku.ISummary`. These projections allow tools and operators to immediately see which catalog entities are represented by a given index entry without performing extra lookups.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the catalog search index entry.

This property maps to the `id` primary key column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` table and uniquely identifies one denormalized search record for a product or SKU.

Administrative tools use this value to retrieve, inspect, and potentially rebuild or remove specific index entries when performing diagnostics or maintenance operations.

locale.description:
Locale code for which this search index entry was generated, such as `en-US` or `ko-KR`.

It corresponds to the `locale` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` table and is used to scope search queries and ranking logic to the correct language and regional context.

Multiple index entries may exist for the same product or SKU across different locales, enabling localized search experiences while keeping each locale-specific representation independent in the index.

search_text.description:
Concatenated and normalized search text used for full-text search.

This field mirrors the `search_text` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` table and typically contains combined content such as product titles, summaries, tags, and attribute labels that are preprocessed for efficient search indexing.

The value is optimized for machine consumption and ranking rather than direct display to end users, and may include normalization such as case folding, tokenization, and removal of stop words depending on the indexing strategy.

boost_score.description:
Precomputed numeric boost score that influences search ranking.

This property comes from the `boost_score` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` table and is used by the search engine to prioritize entries based on factors such as popularity, manual merchandising boosts, recency, or other business-defined heuristics.

Higher scores generally correspond to stronger promotion in search results, and administrative tools can use this value to audit how ranking signals are being applied to specific catalog entries.

product.description:
Product whose content is represented by this search index entry, when the entry is product-scoped.

This replaces the lower-level `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key and provides a summary representation of the associated product using `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary`, so that administrators and tools can immediately see which product an index row belongs to.

Exactly one of `product` or `sku` is typically populated depending on whether the index entry was built at the product level or at the SKU/variant level.

sku.description:
SKU whose content is represented by this search index entry, when the entry is SKU-scoped.

This association replaces the `shopping_mall_sku_id` foreign key and exposes a summary representation of the concrete SKU via `IShoppingMallSku.ISummary`, which is particularly useful when indexing variant-specific search text such as size or color labels.

Diagnostic tools can use this summary to quickly confirm that the correct variant-level data has been indexed for the SKU in question.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this search index entry was created or last fully rebuilt.

It is sourced from the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` table and is useful for diagnosing index freshness, monitoring rebuild processes, and ordering entries by creation time in diagnostic tools.

Operations teams may rely on this field to verify that recent catalog changes have been propagated into the search index within expected SLAs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the metadata of this search index entry was last updated.

This property reflects the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_catalog_search_index_entries` table and is typically adjusted when administrative metadata or boost configuration changes, even if the underlying `search_text` stays the same.

Comparing `created_at` and `updated_at` can help distinguish between full rebuilds and incremental adjustments to ranking or indexing metadata.

IShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a cart line item for high-level cart and validation listings.

This DTO exposes the primary identifiers, pricing snapshot fields, and key lifecycle and validation timestamps needed to understand which SKU was placed in the cart, in what quantity, and how recently it was validated. It intentionally omits child collections, full SKU details, and deep history so that it remains compact and suitable for list responses.

Data originates from the `shopping_mall_cart_items` table, which stores quantities, unit prices, currencies, validation hints, and soft-deletion metadata for each SKU attached to a cart. The summary is typically embedded within other DTOs such as validation summaries or cart summaries, enabling quick context without additional network round trips.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart item.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_cart_items.id` and is generated by the database. It uniquely identifies the specific line item within the cart for analytics, debugging, and drill-down operations.

cart_id.description:
Identifier of the cart that owns this item.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_cart_items.shopping_mall_cart_id` and links the item back to a cart header stored in `shopping_mall_carts`. The field is provided as a raw identifier in the summary to support correlation and routing without embedding a full cart object.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU associated with this cart item.

The value maps to `shopping_mall_cart_items.shopping_mall_sku_id` and points to a SKU record in `shopping_mall_skus`. It allows downstream APIs, administrative tools, or reporting processes to look up product and inventory context for the line item when necessary.

quantity.description:
Requested quantity of the SKU in this cart item.

This comes from the `shopping_mall_cart_items.quantity` column and must be a positive integer. It represents the quantity last confirmed for the line item and is subject to revalidation against inventory constraints and purchase limits as the cart evolves.

unit_price.description:
Snapshot unit price of the SKU in the cart currency.

The value is sourced from `shopping_mall_cart_items.unit_price` and reflects the price of a single unit at the time it was last recalculated. It remains stored as part of the cart item to support consistent order creation and auditing even if catalog prices later change.

currency_code.description:
ISO currency code applied to the unit price of this cart item.

This value originates from `shopping_mall_cart_items.currency_code` and should match the currency configured on the owning cart in `shopping_mall_carts.currency_code`. It is typically a three-letter ISO 4217 code and is used for display, rounding, and downstream financial processing.

last_validation_status.description:
Result of the most recent lightweight validation performed on this cart item.

The field is backed by `shopping_mall_cart_items.last_validation_status` and contains compact codes such as `ok`, `out_of_stock`, or `price_changed`. It enables quick checks when rendering cart summaries and helps decide whether more detailed validation history needs to be fetched.

When null, either the item has not yet been validated or the status was intentionally cleared as part of a business workflow.

last_validation_at.description:
Timestamp when the `last_validation_status` field was last updated.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_cart_items.last_validation_at` and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. Together with `last_validation_status`, it allows clients and administrative tools to understand how fresh the validation result is relative to recent catalog, price, or inventory changes.

added_at.description:
Business event timestamp representing when the item was first added to the cart.

This property is populated from `shopping_mall_cart_items.added_at` and uses ISO 8601 date-time format. It can differ from `created_at` if the system distinguishes between the logical time the customer added the item and the time the row was persisted to the database.

Analytics and UX flows can use this field to calculate cart aging, identify stale items, and understand when a customer first expressed interest in a SKU.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart item record was created in the database.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_cart_items.created_at` and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. It is primarily useful for operational auditing, troubleshooting, and understanding data lifecycle events at the persistence layer.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the cart item record was last modified.

The value is backed by `shopping_mall_cart_items.updated_at` and uses ISO 8601 date-time format. It changes whenever mutable aspects of the cart item—such as quantity, pricing snapshot, or validation status—are updated, and therefore acts as a simple change indicator for synchronization and caching strategies.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp used to logically remove the cart item from active use while preserving history.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_cart_items.deleted_at` and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format when present. When non-null, the item should generally be excluded from active cart calculations while remaining available for analytics, auditing, and reconciliation processes.

IShoppingMallCartItemValidation.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single validation record for a shopping cart item.

This DTO is used in list responses and embedded contexts where only high-level information about a validation attempt is required, not the full historical payload. It focuses on identifiers, core classification fields, and timestamps that allow clients to understand when and how a cart item was validated.

The underlying persistence is provided by the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations` table, which stores detailed audit entries for validations triggered during cart interactions such as add-to-cart, cart view, and checkout. This summary variant intentionally omits large text fields and non-essential numeric detail so that lists remain lightweight while still supporting debugging, analytics correlation, and drill-down navigation to detail resources.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart item validation record.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations.id` and is generated by the database. Clients use this identifier when referencing a specific validation entry in logs, support tools, or detail views. It is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

cartItem.description:
Owning cart item whose state was evaluated during this validation.

This reference provides lightweight context about the item that was checked, such as the SKU and quantity, without requiring clients to issue an additional lookup. Internally it maps to the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations.shopping_mall_cart_item_id` foreign key that joins to `shopping_mall_cart_items.id`. The summary projection of the cart item MUST follow the `.ISummary` DTO rules and must not contain its own child collections.

validation_type.description:
Business type of validation that was executed for the cart item.

The value reflects the interaction or lifecycle event that triggered the validation, such as `add_to_cart`, `cart_view`, or `checkout`. It comes from the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations.validation_type` column and is used in analytics and diagnostics to group and filter validation records by scenario.

API consumers should treat this as an opaque but stable business code string and avoid hard-coding assumptions about the full list of possible values.

status.description:
Outcome classification of the validation attempt.

This value is derived from the `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations.status` field and typically expresses states like `success`, `error`, or `adjusted` depending on how the validation completed. It allows client applications and reporting tools to quickly determine whether the corresponding cart item remains valid, was rejected, or required correction.

Combined with timestamps and validation type, the status enables high-level analysis of cart friction and error patterns without inspecting full underlying rule logic.

message.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of the validation result.

The content comes from `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations.message` and is intended for logging, support tooling, or, when appropriate, customer-facing error messaging. It may describe reasons such as stock unavailability, pricing changes, or policy violations.

When null, either no additional description was recorded for this validation or the message is not relevant in the current presentation context.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of this validation record.

This value mirrors `shopping_mall_cart_item_validations.created_at` and indicates when the validation was executed and stored. It is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format and is immutable once written.

Clients commonly use this timestamp to order validation records chronologically, filter validation history over a time range, and correlate cart validation events with other operational logs or customer interactions.

IShoppingMallCartMergeEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a guest-to-customer or cart-to-cart merge operation.

This DTO captures the key identifiers, actor classifications, and aggregate counts that describe a merge event where items from one cart were combined into another. It is designed for use in audit logs, customer service tooling, and analytics dashboards where high-level insight into cart merge behavior is needed without loading every detailed field.

Underlying data is stored in the `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events` table, which records the actors involved, their carts, outcome counts, and contextual reason text. The summary representation exposes only the most relevant attributes to make list views efficient while preserving the ability to correlate with customers, guest users, and carts through their identifiers.

In addition to scalar identifiers, this summary also exposes lightweight `.ISummary` association views for the source and target actors and carts, allowing clients to render meaningful context in a single call without traversing additional endpoints.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart merge event.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.id` and is generated by the database. It is used as the primary key when retrieving or referencing a specific merge audit record.

source_actor_type.description:
Type of the source actor for the merge.

The value is read from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.source_actor_type` and typically contains codes such as `guestuser` to indicate which actor model the source identifiers refer to. It allows clients and operational tools to interpret which foreign keys are expected to be populated on the event.

target_actor_type.description:
Type of the target actor for the merge.

This string comes from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.target_actor_type` and commonly identifies the actor that received the merged cart, such as `customer`. It complements `source_actor_type` and helps reporting tools categorize merge patterns.

source_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the source cart whose items were merged.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.source_shopping_mall_cart_id`. When present, it references the cart from which items were taken during the merge operation. When null, the merge may have involved only actor-level consolidation without a specific persisted cart source.

target_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the target cart that received merged items.

The value is derived from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.target_shopping_mall_cart_id` and references a cart in `shopping_mall_carts` that represents the final, consolidated cart after the merge. A null value indicates edge cases where the merge did not result in a concrete target cart record, though such cases are expected to be rare.

source_guestuser_id.description:
Identifier of the source guest user, when applicable.

This reflects `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id` and is populated when the merge originates from a guest user identity. It supports auditing and analytics around guest behavior and how effectively guest carts are preserved at login.

The field is nullable because not all merge events involve a guest user.

target_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the target customer who received merged cart contents.

The value is mapped from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.target_shopping_mall_customer_id` and points to a record in `shopping_mall_customers`. It is typically present when a guest cart is merged into a logged-in customer's cart, but may be null for other merge strategies.

merged_item_count.description:
Number of cart items successfully merged from the source cart into the target cart.

This integer is taken from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.merged_item_count` and provides a quick measure of merge effectiveness. It can be used in analytics to evaluate how much value is preserved when users authenticate or when carts are consolidated.

dropped_item_count.description:
Number of source cart items that could not be merged.

The value comes from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.dropped_item_count` and counts items that were skipped during the merge due to validation failures such as discontinued SKUs, policy violations, or other conflicts. A high dropped count can indicate friction in the merge flow and may warrant investigation.

reason.description:
Optional descriptive reason or strategy label for the merge.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.reason` and can describe the business rule set or campaign that governed the merge behavior, or provide ad-hoc operator notes. When null, no additional textual reason was recorded for the event.

sourceGuestuser.description:
Lightweight summary of the source guest user identity when the merge originated from a guest session.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.source_shopping_mall_guestuser_id` and the corresponding `shopping_mall_guestusers` record. It gives audit and analytics consumers immediate access to basic guest context—such as when the guest was created or last active—without requiring a separate lookup.

When the event did not involve a guest user, this field is omitted or null depending on the serialization rules of the platform.

targetCustomer.description:
Lightweight summary of the target customer account that received the merged cart contents.

This association is based on `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.target_shopping_mall_customer_id` and the related `shopping_mall_customers` row. It allows dashboards and support tools to show who ultimately owns the consolidated cart, while still keeping the response compact through a `.ISummary` projection.

The field is omitted or null when the merge did not resolve into a concrete customer account.

sourceCart.description:
Summary representation of the source cart that contributed items to this merge event.

The data is linked via `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.source_shopping_mall_cart_id` to a row in `shopping_mall_carts`. Including a `.ISummary` view enables clients to understand the size and basic properties of the original cart without issuing separate cart queries.

When no concrete source cart record exists for the merge scenario, this association is omitted or null depending on the platform’s serialization semantics.

targetCart.description:
Summary representation of the target cart that absorbed items from the source cart.

This association is resolved through `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.target_shopping_mall_cart_id` to a row in `shopping_mall_carts`. It provides a concise view of the cart that the user continues with after the merge, suitable for list views and audit screens.

If the merge did not result in a persistent target cart, this field is omitted or null according to the platform’s serialization rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the merge event record was created.

The value is sourced from `shopping_mall_cart_merge_events.created_at` and records when the merge occurred. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string and is used to order merge records chronologically, define reporting windows, and correlate merges with authentication or order-placement events.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an item contained in a customer wishlist.

This DTO is intended for use in wishlist item listings, search results, and embedded contexts where only primary identification, ordering, and high‑level product context are necessary, rather than the full relational graph.

It is derived from the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` Prisma model and focuses on fields that describe which product or SKU is saved, its position, and its lifecycle timestamps, while exposing product and SKU associations as summary objects instead of raw foreign keys.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist item.

This value corresponds to the primary key in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table and is used when updating, reordering, or removing individual items.

Clients treat this as an opaque identifier and do not infer meaning from its structure.

product.description:
Summary of the product that the customer saved in the wishlist.

This replaces the raw `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key from the underlying table and references the `shopping_mall_products` row through a rich summary view.

Clients can use this object to render product title, thumbnail, and key merchandising attributes in wishlist lists without issuing additional product detail requests.

sku.description:
Optional summary of the specific SKU variant saved to the wishlist.

When present, this corresponds to the `shopping_mall_sku_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table and provides variant‑level details such as size or color via `IShoppingMallSku.ISummary`.

When null, the wishlist item represents the general product without a pre‑selected variant, and selection may occur later during cart or checkout flows.

position.description:
Relative ordering position of the item within the wishlist.

Lower values are displayed earlier in the list, supporting a stable and controllable customer-defined ordering.

This field is typically updated when items are added, removed, or reordered via drag-and-drop or similar UI interactions.

added_at.description:
Timestamp when the item was added to the wishlist.

This reflects the moment the customer first saved the product or SKU into the wishlist and is distinct from the general record creation timestamp when necessary.

It is useful for sorting items by recency and for analytics on customer interest over time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist item record was created in the database.

Typically this matches `added_at`, but it can differ when items are migrated, imported, or reconstructed during data maintenance.

It is primarily used for auditing and low-level diagnostics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist item was last updated.

Changes such as position reordering, associated SKU adjustments, or soft deletion toggles update this value.

Clients and services can use it to determine whether cached wishlist item representations are stale.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the wishlist item.

When null, the item is active and appears in normal wishlist displays.

When set, the item is logically removed from customer views but retained for historical analysis, recovery workflows, or compliance reporting.

IShoppingMallWishlistMergeEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing a wishlist merge audit event in the shopping mall platform.

This type is designed for read-only list and overview views where consumers need to understand that a guest or customer wishlist merge occurred, when it happened, and at a high level how many items were merged or dropped.

It maps directly to the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` Prisma model but intentionally exposes only non-sensitive, business-facing fields suitable for summaries, without navigation properties to related entities. Detailed relations to customers, guest users, and wishlists are expected to be resolved through dedicated APIs using the stored identifiers when required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist merge event.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_wishlist_merge_events` table and is used to uniquely reference this audit record across the platform.

source_actor_type.description:
Type of the source actor whose wishlist was merged.

Typical values are domain-specific strings such as `"guestuser"`, indicating that the origin of the wishlist was a guest user session. This field helps interpret which of the optional source actor identifiers are expected to be populated.

target_actor_type.description:
Type of the target actor who received the merged wishlist items.

In standard flows this is typically `"customer"`, indicating that the merge moved items into a registered customer account. This value determines which target actor foreign key is semantically meaningful for this record.

merged_item_count.description:
Number of wishlist items successfully merged from the source wishlist into the target wishlist.

This count reflects items that satisfied visibility, duplication, and policy rules and therefore became part of the final target wishlist state.

dropped_item_count.description:
Number of wishlist items that could not be merged from the source wishlist into the target wishlist.

Items are counted here when they are skipped due to product unavailability, catalog visibility rules, duplication prevention, or other business policies active during the merge operation.

reason.description:
Optional free-form textual reason describing the merge context.

Typical values include the name of the merge policy, conflict resolution notes, or debugging information that explains why certain items were merged or dropped. When no additional context is captured, this field is null.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist merge event was recorded.
