The value is stored in the database at the time the merge was processed and is used for chronological sorting, auditing, and time-based analysis of wishlist merge behaviors.

IShoppingMallOrderPriceSnapshot.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for an order price snapshot in the shopping mall domain.

This type provides a compact view of a single monetary snapshot for an order, focusing on the decomposed price components and high‑level metadata that are most relevant for list views and embedded displays.

It intentionally omits heavy relational navigation and internal foreign key identifiers, while preserving enough structure for audit, reporting, and customer‑facing history screens where the parent order is already implied by the surrounding context or endpoint path.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the price snapshot.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.id` and is generated by the system when the snapshot row is created.

item_subtotal_amount.description:
Sum of item‑level subtotals before any discounts for this order at the time of the snapshot.

Mapped from `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.item_subtotal_amount`. This includes the raw extended prices of all items in the order, prior to applying line or order level discounts.

item_discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied at the line level across all items for this snapshot.

Backed by `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.item_discount_amount`. This can include both seller‑funded and platform‑funded discounts that are applied directly to individual line items.

order_discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied at the order level for this snapshot.

This property reflects `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.order_discount_amount` and usually represents coupons, campaigns, or other promotions that are calculated on the overall order rather than per line item.

shipping_fee_amount.description:
Total shipping fee amount charged to the customer in this snapshot.

Comes from `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.shipping_fee_amount`. This value can be zero when free shipping promotions apply or when the shipping cost is absorbed by the platform or seller.

payment_surcharge_amount.description:
Total payment method surcharge charged to the customer for this snapshot, if any.

Mapped from `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.payment_surcharge_amount`. Depending on business configuration, this may represent platform‑owned fees or pass‑through charges imposed by payment providers.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount calculated for the order at the time of this snapshot.

Derived from `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.tax_amount`. In tax‑exempt jurisdictions or for certain orders, this value can legitimately be zero.

grand_total_amount.description:
Grand total amount to be charged to the customer for this snapshot.

Represents `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.grand_total_amount`. Conceptually this is computed as the item subtotal minus all discounts plus shipping fees, payment surcharges, and taxes, and is the main payable amount used for downstream payment logic.

is_final.description:
Indicates whether this snapshot represents the final confirmed monetary state for the order.

Backed by `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.is_final`. Business logic typically treats the latest snapshot with `is_final = true` as authoritative for financial reporting and reconciliation.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the snapshot row.

Mapped from `shopping_mall_order_price_snapshots.created_at`. This records when the snapshot was persisted and is useful for chronological sorting and historical analysis within an order’s lifecycle.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single order status history entry for use in list and timeline responses.

This DTO is designed for lightweight listing of status changes associated with an order, such as in order detail timelines or admin history overviews. It focuses on the business-relevant fields that describe how the order status evolved over time without exposing internal foreign key identifiers or persistence metadata.

Use this type in paginated responses and embedded collections where clients need to render a concise chronological view of an order’s lifecycle, while the full `IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory` DTO remains available for internal or drill-down use cases when a complete record projection is required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this order status history entry.

This value can be used to request or update a specific history record through detail-oriented administrative APIs or drill-down views when supported by the application.

from_status.description:
Previous order status value before this transition.

This field is null when this history entry represents the initial status assigned to the order, or when the previous status was not recorded. When present, it helps users understand how the order state changed at this point in the timeline.

to_status.description:
New order status value applied by this history entry.

Typical values mirror those used in `shopping_mall_orders.current_status` (for example, `PENDING`, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`, or `DELIVERED`). It represents the effective status of the order immediately after this transition occurred.

reason_code.description:
Optional machine-readable reason code that explains why this status change happened.

When populated, it carries structured identifiers such as `payment_confirmed`, `customer_cancelled`, or `system_timeout`, which can be used by client applications for grouping, filtering, and localized label rendering.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp at which this status change took effect from a business perspective.

This value is used to construct chronological timelines of order activity and may differ from the persistence time if entries are backfilled or corrected later. Clients should treat it as the canonical moment when the status transition happened in the order lifecycle.

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shipping method used in the shopping mall platform.

This type is optimized for list views, references inside other DTOs, and lightweight embeddings where only identification and key display fields are required.

It is derived from the `shopping_mall_shipping_methods` Prisma model and intentionally omits verbose descriptive content that is more appropriate for detail views while still providing enough information to understand which method is being referenced.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipping method record.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipping_methods.id` and is used as the primary key when referencing this shipping method from other entities such as shipments and configuration records.

Clients use this identifier for internal linking or caching but typically do not expose it directly to end users.

method_code.description:
Machine-readable shipping method code used internally.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_shipping_methods.method_code` and is unique across all shipping methods.

Typical examples include logical identifiers such as `"standard"`, `"express"`, or carrier-specific codes. Client applications should treat this field as a stable key suitable for business rules, feature flags, or localization lookups.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping method.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipping_methods.display_name` and is the primary label shown to customers and sellers when selecting or viewing a shipping option.

UI layers should prefer this property over `method_code` when rendering method names in dropdowns, order summaries, and shipment details.

IShoppingMallShipment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shipment generated from a customer order.

This DTO is designed for list endpoints and embedded references inside order and seller views where a compact representation of shipment state is sufficient.

It is based on the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma model and exposes key identifiers, high-level status information, and tracking metadata while omitting heavy relational graphs such as shipment items and detailed event timelines.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment record.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipments.id` and is the primary reference used by backend services when loading or updating shipment information.

Client applications use this identifier for navigation to shipment detail views and for constructing API requests that target a specific shipment.

shipment_code.description:
Business-facing shipment code used in customer and seller communication.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_code` and is unique per shipment. It is often derived from the order code with an additional sequence or generated from a dedicated sequence range.

UI layers should display this value prominently in shipment lists, order detail pages, and support tools so that humans can reference shipments without needing to know the internal UUID.

shipping_status.description:
Current shipping status of this shipment.

The value is stored in `shopping_mall_shipments.shipping_status` and represents coarse-grained states in the shipment lifecycle such as `"pending"`, `"preparing"`, `"ready_for_pickup"`, `"shipped"`, `"in_transit"`, `"out_for_delivery"`, `"delivered"`, `"delivery_failed"`, `"returned"`, or `"cancelled"`.

Clients can use this field to determine which actions are available to sellers and customers and to render status badges, progress indicators, or filtering controls.

carrier_name.description:
Name of the carrier responsible for this shipment, when assigned.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipments.carrier_name` and is nullable because some shipments may not yet be allocated to a carrier or may use a generic shipping method without a named carrier.

Typical values include branded logistics providers or internal logistics labels. When `null`, clients should treat the shipment as not yet assigned or rely on the shipping method name for user-visible context.

tracking_number.description:
Carrier-provided tracking identifier for this shipment.

This maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.tracking_number` and is nullable when tracking is not yet available or not supported for the shipping method.

When non-null, this value can be used to build deep links to carrier tracking pages, to power tracking widgets, or to synchronize with external logistics integrations.

expected_ship_date.description:
Expected date-time when the shipment is planned to leave the seller or warehouse.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipments.expected_ship_date` and is optional because not all shipments have a precise planned dispatch time.

Clients may use this field to communicate estimated dispatch windows, highlight delays, or support SLA dashboards for operations teams.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment was actually marked as shipped or first entered the carrier network.

The value originates from `shopping_mall_shipments.shipped_at` and is null for shipments that have not yet been dispatched.

This field is useful for tracking outbound performance, calculating transit durations, and displaying chronological shipment histories in compact list views.

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when the shipment was confirmed delivered to the customer.

It maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.delivered_at` and is null until delivery has been confirmed or if the shipment never reached the delivered state.

Applications may use this field for customer experience features like delivery confirmation banners, feedback prompts, or delivery performance analytics.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the shipment record.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipments.created_at` and records when the shipment header was first inserted, usually during order fulfillment planning.

It is frequently used as a sort key in shipment lists and operational dashboards to show newest or oldest shipments first.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the shipment record.

The value is stored in `shopping_mall_shipments.updated_at` and reflects the last time any high-level shipment data changed, such as status updates or tracking information.

Clients can rely on this field to detect stale cache entries, trigger UI refreshes, or support polling and synchronization mechanisms.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a payment method configuration for listing and selection flows.

This type represents a lightweight projection of the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` model that is suitable for presenting available payment options at checkout, as well as for administrative overviews.

It includes identifiers, human-readable labels, status, and core configuration attributes that influence eligibility and display, while leaving detailed configuration and audit history to the full payment method DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment method configuration.

This value maps directly to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` table and is used internally for referencing and updating the configuration.

In most customer-facing contexts this field is not exposed directly but underpins selection and reconciliation logic.

code.description:
Business identifier code of the payment method, such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or other platform-specific identifiers.

This code is stable over time and is used in configuration, logging, and references from other tables like order payments and statistics.

It is unique across the platform, making it suitable for technical integrations and feature toggling.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name of the payment method, shown in checkout and administration UIs.

Typical examples are `Credit Card`, `Bank Transfer`, or localized labels appropriate for the region.

Frontends rely on this field to present a concise and understandable label to end users when choosing how to pay.

provider_type.description:
High-level category or gateway family for this payment method, such as `card_processor`, `bank_gateway`, `wallet`, or `cod`.

This classification enables grouping, analytics, and provider-specific feature handling in business logic and operational reporting.

It comes directly from the `provider_type` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` table.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the payment method, for example `active` or `disabled`.

Checkout flows and admin consoles consult this value to determine whether the method can be offered to customers, and to distinguish deprecated or temporarily unavailable methods.

The status is maintained in the underlying `shopping_mall_payment_methods.status` column and participates in operational filters and dashboards.

allowed_currencies.description:
Optional serialized representation of the order currencies allowed for this payment method.

Typical values are comma-separated ISO 4217 currency codes such as `USD,KRW` when the method is restricted to specific currencies, or null to indicate no explicit currency constraint.

Search, configuration, and analytics views may surface this field to help operators understand coverage of each payment method.

allowed_countries.description:
Optional serialized representation of the countries or regions in which this payment method may be used.

Values commonly contain comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, or are null when the method is globally available without geographical restriction.

This information is useful for administrative listings and for debugging why a method is not visible for a given customer.

min_amount.description:
Optional minimum payable amount for orders using this payment method, expressed in the order currency.

When present it enforces that orders below this threshold cannot select the method, and UIs may use it to display eligibility hints.

A null value indicates that there is no lower bound enforced by this configuration.

max_amount.description:
Optional maximum payable amount for orders using this payment method, expressed in the order currency.

When present it acts as an upper bound for eligibility at checkout, often driven by risk policies or provider constraints.

A null value means there is no configured upper limit on transaction size for this method.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment method configuration record was created.

This is primarily used in administrative overviews and analytics to understand configuration lifecycle and to audit when a method was first introduced to the platform.

It corresponds directly to the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods`.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment method configuration record was last updated.

Operators use this field to identify recently changed payment methods, for example after risk policy updates, provider migrations, or label changes.

The value matches the `updated_at` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` table.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodSurcharge.ISum.description:
Summary view of a payment method surcharge configuration for the shopping mall platform.

This summary DTO represents a single surcharge rule that is attached to a particular payment method and optionally scoped by region, currency, or order amount range. It is used in list screens and embedded contexts where only the key financial and scoping attributes of the surcharge are required, without exposing internal implementation details.

Applications use this summary type to show which additional customer-facing or platform-owned fees may apply when a given payment method is selected. It supports quick inspection of fee ranges and refund behavior while keeping payload size small and focusing on the most important decision-making attributes.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment method surcharge configuration.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_surcharges.id` and is a server-generated UUID. It is used to reference this particular surcharge record when performing read operations or administrative updates.

payment_method.description:
Payment method configuration that this surcharge rule belongs to.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` and provides immediate context about the payment method, including its code, display name, provider type, and status.

Clients can rely on this summary to present which method the surcharge applies to without performing additional lookups.

scope_code.description:
Optional business scope identifier that narrows where this surcharge rule applies.

Scope codes can represent logical segments such as region codes, sales channels, or customer segments. When null, the rule is considered globally applicable for its parent payment method unless further constrained by other fields.

currency_code.description:
Optional ISO 4217 currency code for which this surcharge configuration applies.

When populated, the surcharge is evaluated only for payments denominated in this specific currency. When null, the rule may apply regardless of currency, subject to other matching criteria such as scope and amount range.

min_order_amount.description:
Lower bound of the order amount range for which this surcharge is valid.

If set, only payments whose payable amount is greater than or equal to this value are eligible for this rule. When null, there is no explicit minimum bound on the order amount.

max_order_amount.description:
Upper bound of the order amount range for which this surcharge is valid.

If set, only payments whose payable amount is less than or equal to this value are eligible for this rule. When null, there is no explicit maximum bound on the order amount, and the rule can apply to arbitrarily large payments.

fixed_fee_amount.description:
Optional fixed fee amount that is added when this payment method is used and the rule applies.

This value is denominated in the surcharge's `currency_code` when it is set, or in the payment's currency when `currency_code` is null. When null, no fixed fee component is contributed by this rule.

percentage_fee_rate.description:
Optional percentage fee rate applied to the payable amount when the rule matches.

Typical values are expressed as human-readable percentages, such as `2.9` for a 2.9% fee. When null, no percentage-based fee component is applied and only the fixed component, if defined, contributes to the surcharge.

is_platform_revenue.description:
Flag indicating whether the surcharge amount is treated as platform-owned revenue.

When true, the calculated fee is considered revenue for the shopping mall platform and may be recorded as part of internal earnings. When false, the fee is treated as a pass-through cost that belongs to an external party, such as a payment gateway or carrier, and should not be counted as platform revenue.

refundable_policy.description:
Optional textual policy describing how this surcharge behaves during refunds.

Typical values describe whether the surcharge is fully refundable, non-refundable, or partially refundable under certain conditions. The exact semantics are determined by business policy, and clients usually render this for human operators rather than parsing it programmatically.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this surcharge rule was created.

This field reflects the creation moment of the configuration row in the database and is useful for auditing, sorting, and historical analysis in administrative UIs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this surcharge rule was last updated.

Each change to the surcharge configuration updates this value, allowing clients to detect recent modifications and implement optimistic concurrency or cache invalidation strategies if needed.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a logical payment associated with a customer order in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO exposes key financial and lifecycle attributes for a single order payment, including order linkage, customer association, payment method, monetary amounts, and high-level business status. It is designed for use in list views, dashboards, and embedded contexts where a compact yet informative overview of payments is required.

Consumers of this type can quickly understand how much should be paid, how much has been captured or refunded, and what the current business status of the payment is, without loading all auxiliary details or unbounded related entities such as attempts or detailed status histories.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the logical order payment.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_order_payments.id` and is a server-generated UUID. It identifies the payment record across the platform for tracing, auditing, and linking related events such as attempts, refunds, or chargebacks.

order.description:
Parent order associated with this logical payment.

This is a transformed association for the underlying foreign key `shopping_mall_order_payments.shopping_mall_order_id`. It provides a compact summary of the customer-facing order header so clients can understand which order this payment relates to without issuing additional order lookup calls.

customer.description:
Customer who owns the order and therefore this payment.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_order_payments.shopping_mall_customer_id`. It exposes a lightweight summary of the customer for administrative and analytical views while avoiding exposure of low-level actor IDs in the summary response.

payment_method.description:
Configured payment method used for this payment from the platform perspective.

This field is the object-valued counterpart of the database foreign key `shopping_mall_order_payments.shopping_mall_payment_method_id`. It allows clients to understand which payment option was used (for example, card processor, bank transfer, or wallet) without a secondary lookup.

payment_sequence.description:
Sequence number of this payment within its parent order.

The first payment for an order typically uses sequence 1, with additional records created for partial, split, or retry payments. This sequence enables deterministic ordering and differentiation of multiple payments associated with the same order.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the monetary amounts of this payment.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_order_payments.currency_code` and ensures that payable, captured, refunded, and chargeback amounts are interpreted in the correct currency context for reporting and reconciliation.

payable_amount.description:
Total amount that is expected to be paid for this payment in the specified currency.

This amount typically includes line items, taxes, and customer-facing fees that belong to this payment. It originates from order pricing logic and may be used to determine whether the payment is fully satisfied by captured funds.

captured_amount.description:
Total amount that has actually been captured or confirmed as paid so far.

This field aggregates successful capture events or equivalent confirmations from the payment provider. When equal to `payable_amount` the payment is fully paid; when lower, the payment is partially paid or still pending additional capture operations.

refunded_amount.description:
Total amount that has been refunded against this payment across all completed refund operations.

This value is used together with `captured_amount` to assess net revenue and to determine if the payment is fully or partially refunded from a business perspective.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total amount that has been chargebacked for this payment across all chargeback cases.

Chargeback amounts represent funds that have been reversed by external parties such as card schemes or banks. This field helps risk, finance, and operations teams monitor exposure and loss associated with a specific payment.

business_status.description:
High-level business status of the payment lifecycle.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, `chargeback`, or `cancelled`. The exact vocabulary is defined by business policy and drives downstream behavior such as shipment eligibility or refund handling.

provider_status_code.description:
Optional provider-specific status code summarizing the last known state from the payment gateway.

This field mirrors the most recent status communicated by the external payment provider, such as an internal code or textual indicator. It is primarily used for operational debugging and reconciliation rather than customer-facing messaging.

provider_reference.description:
Optional reference identifier from the payment provider at the payment level.

Common examples include payment intent identifiers, transaction IDs, or authorization references. These values enable cross-system tracing between the shopping mall platform and external payment systems during investigations and reconciliation.

metadata.description:
Optional serialized metadata associated with this payment.

This field corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_payments.metadata` column and typically stores structured JSON or other encoded data describing provider-specific details, internal diagnostic information, or integration context. It can be null when no additional metadata is recorded for the payment or when such metadata is stored in external systems.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment record was created in the system.

This value is typically aligned with the moment the order initiated a payment request and serves as the starting point for payment lifecycle metrics and SLA calculations.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment record was last updated.

Any change to monetary amounts, business status, or provider metadata triggers an update to this field, enabling clients to detect recent changes and synchronize local caches or analytical snapshots.

IShoppingMallOrderPaymentAttempt.ISummar.description:
Lightweight summary view of a single payment attempt performed for an order payment.

This summary is intended for list views, audit drill-downs, and embedding inside other payment-related DTOs where only the key identifying and diagnostic fields are required, rather than the full raw payload.

It focuses on core business attributes such as amount, status, associated logical payment, and provider reference, and omits verbose debug fields that are not generally needed in high-frequency responses.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment attempt.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts` table and is used to reference this attempt from logs, admin tools, or debugging utilities.

order_payment.description:
Parent logical order payment that this attempt belongs to.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts.shopping_mall_order_payment_id`. It groups multiple technical attempts under the same business-level payment and provides enough context for list and drill-down views without extra lookups.

payment_method.description:
Payment method that was actually used in this attempt.

This association is the object-level representation of the `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts.shopping_mall_payment_method_id` foreign key. It allows operators and tools to see which configured payment method was used on this attempt, including cases where it differs from the initial configuration on the logical payment.

attempt_sequence.description:
Sequence number of this attempt within the parent logical payment.

Numbering starts from `1` and increases monotonically per `order_payment`. It enables chronological ordering of retries or multiple technical attempts for the same payment in logs and UI displays.

status.description:
Current business status of this payment attempt.

Typical values include labels such as `"pending"`, `"success"`, `"failed"`, `"error"`, or `"expired"`. Exact vocabulary is governed by payment integration rules and may be refined over time.

amount.description:
Monetary amount that this attempt tried to authorize or capture.

The value is denominated in the currency configured on the parent order payment and should match or be consistent with the logical payment amount.

oneOf.description:
Non-null provider reference string such as a gateway transaction id or intent id.

This is supplied by the external payment provider and is commonly required for reconciliation, support investigation, or dispute handling.
Null when the payment provider did not return any stable reference for this attempt or when it could not be captured due to a hard failure.

provider_reference.description:
Reference identifier assigned by the external payment provider for this attempt.

When present it usually contains transaction ids, intents, or similar provider-side handles that are essential for reconciliation and support analysis.

oneOf.description:
Non-null failure or error code string returned by the payment provider or internal risk engine.

This can encode reasons such as `"card_declined"`, `"insufficient_funds"`, or integration-specific error codes.
Null when the attempt has not failed, or when no structured failure code was reported for the error condition.

failure_code.description:
Structured failure or error code associated with this attempt when it did not succeed.

When populated, this field is primarily used for operations, risk analysis, and fine-grained monitoring dashboards.

oneOf.description:
Non-null human-readable message explaining the failure.

This may be a normalized platform message or a message proxied from the payment provider and is intended for internal support staff, not necessarily for direct end-user display.
Null when the attempt is successful or when no explanatory message was available from the provider.

failure_message.description:
Human-readable explanation describing why the attempt failed or errored.

The content is optimized for internal investigation and audit rather than being a fully localized customer-facing message.

raw_response.description:
Optional serialized raw response payload returned by the payment provider for this attempt.

This field corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_payment_attempts.raw_response` column and typically contains JSON or other encoded data used for debugging, reconciliation, and audit purposes. It may be null when the raw payload is not stored due to privacy, storage, or configuration constraints.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment attempt record was created.

The value is stored as a precise DateTime in the database and marks when the platform first persisted information about this attempt.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment attempt record was last updated.

In typical implementations this changes when the attempt status or diagnostic information is modified, providing a quick indicator for the freshest state.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a payment-level refund within the shopping mall platform.

This summary type is optimized for list views, overviews on order or payment detail pages, and embeddings inside other DTOs where full refund composition is not required. It exposes the key identifying and financial fields of a refund record without loading subsidiary refund item rows.

Use this schema whenever you need to display or transmit high-level refund information such as status, requested and approved amounts, and linkage to the parent payment and admin actor, while keeping payloads small and avoiding deep nesting.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment refund.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_refunds` table and is used to reference a specific refund operation across the system, including in logs, admin tools, and related entities.

Clients should treat this value as an opaque UUID and never attempt to infer semantics from its structure.

orderPayment.description:
Logical order payment that this refund is applied to.

Instead of exposing only the raw `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` foreign key, this association provides a lightweight summary of the parent payment so that list and detail views can show core payment context without extra round trips.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who approved or executed the refund, when applicable.

This field references `shopping_mall_admins.id` and is nullable because not all refunds are necessarily driven by an admin actor (some may be automated or system-triggered). When present, it indicates which administrator made the refund decision.

Use this field in internal tools or audit UIs to correlate refunds with responsible administrators; for public customer-facing APIs this field is typically hidden or ignored.

refund_sequence.description:
Sequence number of this refund for the given payment, starting from 1.

For any given logical order payment, this value uniquely orders multiple refund operations over time. It allows the platform to distinguish first, second, and subsequent refunds against the same payment.

Clients may use this to display a human-friendly incremental sequence like "Refund #1" or "Refund #2" within the context of a single payment.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for this refund.

This matches the currency in which the refund was denominated and usually equals the parent payment currency. Examples include "USD", "EUR", or "KRW".

Use this together with the amount fields when presenting values to users or when integrating with external accounting and reporting systems.

requested_amount.description:
Amount initially requested to be refunded at the business level.

This value reflects the requested refund amount before any policy checks, approvals, or external provider limitations are applied. It is useful for understanding the customer's or seller's original intent.

In some workflows this may differ from the final approved or actually refunded amounts due to partial approvals or technical constraints.

approved_amount.description:
Amount that was approved for refund based on policy and decision.

This field captures the outcome of internal review, business rules, and risk checks. It represents the maximum amount that the platform has agreed to refund for this refund case.

Comparing `approved_amount` with `requested_amount` helps identify partial approvals and may be used in dispute analytics or operational dashboards.

refunded_amount.description:
Amount that the payment provider confirms has actually been refunded to the customer.

This is the authoritative financial value that has been processed by the payment gateway or acquirer. It may be lower than the approved amount in rare cases where provider-side limitations or failures occur.

Use this field for financial reconciliation, ledger postings, and customer-facing communication about what has actually been returned to their payment instrument.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of this refund.

Typical values include states such as "pending", "approved", "rejected", "completed", or "failed". The exact allowed values are governed by business policy and the implementation of the payment and refund engine.

Client applications should treat this value as an opaque status string for display and filtering, and should not attempt to implement business rules based on specific literal values without central coordination.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code describing why the refund was requested or processed.

This field is intended to align with a catalog of business-level refund reasons, such as product defects, late delivery, or customer remorse. When non-null, the code enables analytics, policy enforcement, and operational reporting.

When null, either no structured reason was supplied or the case is handled using free-text explanation only.

reason_message.description:
Optional free-text explanation of the refund reason.

This message stores a human-readable description capturing the context or narrative around the refund, suitable for internal audit, dispute handling, or customer support review.

Consumers should not rely on this field for programmatic decisions; it is primarily for display and manual investigation.

provider_reference.description:
Optional external refund transaction reference from the payment provider.

Examples include gateway-specific refund IDs, PSP transaction codes, or acquirer reference numbers. When present, this field is critical for reconciliation between the shopping mall platform and external payment systems.

It may also be exposed in internal support tools to allow fast cross-checking with provider dashboards.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund record was created.

The value is stored as an absolute UTC timestamp and reflects when the refund case was first registered in the platform, regardless of later status changes.

Use this for chronological sorting, time-based analytics, and audit trails of refund activity.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund record was last updated.

This value changes whenever the refund record is modified, including status transitions, amount corrections, or metadata updates. It provides a quick way to detect recent changes.

In conjunction with `created_at`, it helps identify long-running refunds and supports monitoring SLAs on refund processing times.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefundItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a line-level refund item that contributes to a payment refund.

Each refund item summary represents how much of a specific order item was refunded within a particular refund operation. It is optimized for list and detail views where high-level per-line information is needed without loading all related entities.

Use this type in responses that need to show per-SKU or per-line refund quantities and monetary values, such as refund detail screens or seller and customer overviews, while delegating full order and refund context to other DTOs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund item record.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items` table and uniquely identifies a single per-line refund breakdown within the system.

It is used when referencing or inspecting a specific refund item in internal tools or diagnostic APIs.

shopping_mall_payment_refund_id.description:
Identifier of the parent payment refund that this item belongs to.

This field points to `shopping_mall_payment_refunds.id` and groups one or more line-level refund items under a single refund transaction.

Client applications can use this to correlate refund items with the refund header and to reconstruct the full refund composition when necessary.

shopping_mall_order_item_id.description:
Identifier of the order item whose charge is being refunded.

The value references `shopping_mall_order_items.id` and identifies the specific SKU or order line for which quantity and monetary amounts are being reversed.

It is essential for seller analytics, SKU-level reporting, and reconciliation of refunds against original sales lines.

refunded_quantity.description:
Quantity of the original order item that was refunded in this line.

This value supports fractional quantities if the platform allows partial units, enabling scenarios such as weight-based products or partially consumed services.

Use this together with the original ordered quantity and unit of measure to understand the degree of reversal for the order item.

unit_price_amount.description:
Unit price amount used as the basis for this refund line, expressed in the same currency as the parent refund.

Typically this matches the effective per-unit charge of the associated order item at the time of purchase, including discounts and adjustments applied at checkout.

It is useful for validating the correctness of refund calculations and for generating financial reports that reconcile revenue and refunds at the unit level.

line_refund_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded for this order item line within this refund operation.

This represents the extended refund amount corresponding to `refunded_quantity * unit_price_amount`, possibly adjusted by additional per-line discounts or rounding rules.

Aggregation of `line_refund_amount` across items belonging to the same refund can be compared with the header-level `refunded_amount` for validation and analytics.

reason_code.description:
Optional item-level structured reason code for this refund line.

Example values may include codes such as "damaged", "wrong_item", or "customer_remorse", aligned with the platform's refund reason catalog. When set, it enables more granular analytics of refund causes at the SKU or line level.

When null, the line either inherits its reason context from the parent refund or relies solely on free-text descriptions elsewhere in the system.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund item record was created.

The value is stored as an absolute UTC timestamp and indicates when this particular line-level breakdown was first persisted, typically around the time the parent refund was registered.

It is used in audit trails and time-based reporting for refund activity per item.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund item record was last updated.

This timestamp advances whenever fields on the refund item change, such as quantity corrections, amount adjustments, or reason code updates.

In conjunction with `created_at`, it supports tracing the evolution of refund details for compliance, dispute resolution, and operational monitoring.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a payment chargeback case in the shopping mall platform.

This summary focuses on the key identifiers, monetary figures, high-level status information, and now also includes contextual summaries for the parent payment and optionally the overseeing admin. It is intended for list views, dashboards, and other lightweight contexts where full detail is unnecessary.

BELONGS-TO relations are expressed as `.ISummary` association objects to provide sufficient context without exposing low-level foreign key columns or risking circular reference graphs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the chargeback record.

This UUID is the primary key of the chargeback row and is used to correlate the chargeback with internal risk tooling, dispute workflows, and reporting systems.

orderPayment.description:
Summary of the logical order payment associated with this chargeback.

This replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` foreign key and gives list consumers immediate visibility into which order payment is being disputed, without requiring additional API calls.

oneOf.description: Null when no overseeing admin is currently assigned to this chargeback.

admin.description:
Optional summary of the admin responsible for this chargeback case.

Provides lightweight context about who is currently overseeing investigations or manual decisions for the dispute. Null when the case has no explicit admin owner or is handled automatically.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code of the disputed amount.

This code usually matches the currency of the underlying order payment and is used to ensure consistent reporting and reconciliation across multi-currency environments.

disputed_amount.description:
Amount that has been disputed by the issuer or payment provider.

This value reflects the total monetary exposure under dispute for the related payment transaction and is expressed in the currency indicated by `currency_code`.

chargeback_amount.description:
Amount that has actually been withdrawn from the platform due to this chargeback.

In some cases, the chargeback amount may be lower than the initially disputed amount depending on partial resolutions, reversals, or arbitration outcomes.

reason_code.description:
Provider- or scheme-defined reason code for this chargeback.

This field typically contains network-specific codes (for example card scheme reason codes) that explain why the dispute was raised, which is important for analytics and process optimization. It is null when no standardized reason code is available.

status.description:
Business status of the chargeback case.

Examples include values such as "open", "won", "lost", or "writing_off". The status summarizes where the chargeback stands in the dispute lifecycle from the platform's perspective.

stage.description:
Optional lifecycle stage of the chargeback as defined by the payment network or provider.

Typical examples include stages like "first_presentment", "pre_arbitration", or "arbitration". This field helps finance and operations teams understand how far the case has progressed in external dispute workflows.

provider_reference.description:
External chargeback reference identifier assigned by the payment provider, card scheme, or bank.

This reference is used when communicating with acquirers or payment processors and allows reconciliation between the platform's records and external dispute management tools.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the chargeback record was created in the platform.

This value is used for chronological sorting, SLA tracking, and historical analysis of dispute intake volumes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the chargeback record was last updated.

The platform updates this field whenever the status, stage, financial amounts, or administrative assignments of the chargeback change, enabling auditability of case evolution.

IShoppingMallSellerEarning.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a seller earning line item derived from orders and payments.

This summary exposes the core financial components that determine a seller's net earnings, together with key relational context and lifecycle status used for payout eligibility and analytics.

It is optimized for list views, reporting feeds, and payout batch previews where full order and payment details are not required but high-level earning composition and associations must be visible.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller earning record.

This UUID is the primary key of the earning row and is used to join with payout items, reporting pipelines, and reconciliation tools.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller who owns this earning.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and provides human-readable seller context for list and analytics views without requiring additional lookups.

order.description:
Summary of the customer order from which this earning originates.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key and allows consumers to understand the purchase context of the earning while keeping the summary lightweight.

oneOf.description: Null when the earning is not tied to a specific logical order payment.

orderPayment.description:
Summary of the logical order payment associated with this earning, when relevant.

When present, this replaces the `shopping_mall_order_payment_id` foreign key and helps consumers reason about payout eligibility and payment lifecycle in the same response.

orderItemId.description:
Identifier of the specific order item that generated this earning, when applicable.

This scalar reference is retained to support fine-grained correlation with a single order item without embedding full order-item structures in the summary.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code of this earning record.

All monetary fields in this summary are expressed in the same currency, which matches the underlying order or payment context.

gross_amount.description:
Gross merchandise amount associated with this earning before commissions and platform-funded promotions.

This represents the full value of the underlying sale used for GMV calculations and high-level revenue analytics.

seller_discount_amount.description:
Amount of discount funded directly by the seller for this earning.

This value reduces the seller's gross earnings and is important for understanding the impact of seller-funded promotions on net income.

platform_discount_amount.description:
Amount of discount funded by the platform for this earning.

This field captures the cost of platform-funded promotions or campaigns that reduce customer prices without reducing seller gross earnings.

commission_amount.description:
Commission amount charged by the platform for this earning.

This is the main revenue component for the platform derived from the underlying sale and is deducted from the gross amount when calculating net earnings.

other_fee_amount.description:
Additional fee amount that affects the seller's net earnings.

Examples include per-order fixed fees, subscription-related fees tied to transactions, or manual adjustments that are not modeled as commissions.

net_earning_amount.description:
Net amount owed to the seller after all commissions, fees, and seller-funded discounts are applied.

This is the primary figure used for payout calculations and for reporting the seller's revenue for the corresponding order or item.

earning_type.description:
Type of earning represented by this record.

Typical values include categories such as "order_item", "shipping", or "manual_adjustment" that describe the business origin of the earning and support detailed revenue breakdowns.

business_status.description:
Lifecycle status of this earning from the payout perspective.

Common statuses include "pending", "eligible", "paid_out", or "reversed" and determine whether the earning should be included in payout batches or reported as settled.

eligible_at.description:
Timestamp at which this earning became eligible for payout.

This field is typically set after conditions such as refund windows, chargeback risk periods, or fulfillment confirmations are satisfied. It is null while the earning is still pending.

reversed_at.description:
Timestamp when this earning was reversed, if applicable.

Earnings are reversed when refunds, chargebacks, disputes, or corrective adjustments negate previously recognized earnings. The field remains null for earnings that have not been reversed.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this earning record was created.

Commonly aligned with order placement or payment confirmation events and used for chronological reporting and reconciliation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this earning record was last updated.

The platform updates this value whenever financial amounts or lifecycle status change, ensuring an auditable history of earning transformations.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an individual seller payout item belonging to a payout batch.

Each summary represents a single link between a seller earning and the payout batch in which it is settled. It exposes identifiers, core monetary information, lifecycle status, and key timestamps required for payout detail views, reconciliation tools, and seller statements.

The summary replaces raw foreign keys with association summaries so that clients can navigate from payout items to their parent batch and underlying earning without issuing extra API calls.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payout item.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table and is used to reference this payout record when drilling down into details or attaching reconciliation and audit events.

payoutBatch.description:
Summary of the payout batch that this payout item belongs to.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_payout_batch_id` foreign key and provides the batch context (such as batch code, execution date, and currency) directly in payout item lists.

earning.description:
Summary of the seller earning that is being paid out in this batch item.

This replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_earning_id` foreign key and lets clients see what underlying earning is being settled, including net amounts and associated order context.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code of the payout amount for this item.

It normally matches the currency of the parent payout batch and the associated seller earning, ensuring consistent interpretation of monetary values across the payout pipeline.

payout_amount.description:
Net amount being paid out for the associated seller earning in this payout item.

This usually equals the net earning amount but can differ when partial payouts or prior adjustments have been applied, making it critical for reconciliation of earning-to-payout flows.

status.description:
Business status of this payout item.

Typical values include `pending`, `included`, `paid`, or `reversed`. Applications should enforce valid states and transitions in domain logic and use this property to filter payout items or drive UI badges and workflow actions.

paid_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout item was confirmed as paid to the seller, if applicable.

When present, this marks the time at which the payout was successfully executed by a bank or payment provider. When the item has not yet been paid or payment is not confirmed, this field is null.

reversed_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout item was reversed due to adjustments, chargebacks, or corrections.

If a previously paid payout item must be compensated or cancelled, this field captures when the reversal event occurred. It is null when no reversal has been applied.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the payout item record.

This reflects when the item was first generated and associated with a payout batch, and is commonly used for auditing and ordering in payout detail views.

updated_at.description:
Last updated timestamp of the payout item record.

This is updated whenever the payout item status, monetary values, or timestamps change, supporting synchronization, caching, and investigative reporting scenarios.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodAnalytics.ISum.description:
Summary view of payment method performance analytics for reporting and dashboard use.

This DTO aggregates key daily metrics for a single payment method, combining configuration data from the payment method master table with numeric statistics from the payment method statistics snapshot table.

It is optimized for list and chart views where operators or analysts review success rates, failure patterns, and monetization performance per payment rail.

payment_method_code.description:
Business identifier of the payment method being summarized.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_methods.code` and uniquely identifies the logical payment method such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or provider-specific codes.

Client applications use this code to correlate analytics rows with payment method configuration records and labels.

payment_method_display_name.description:
Human-readable name of the payment method used for display in analytics UIs.

Typically derived from `shopping_mall_payment_methods.display_name`, for example "Credit Card" or "Bank Transfer".

This value helps operators quickly recognize the payment method without relying solely on technical codes.

provider_type.description:
High-level provider type or gateway family for this payment method.

Values mirror `shopping_mall_payment_methods.provider_type`, such as `card_processor`, `bank_gateway`, `wallet`, or `cod`.

Analytics tools can group methods by provider type to understand performance across similar rails.

status.description:
Current business lifecycle status of the payment method.

This usually reflects `shopping_mall_payment_methods.status`, for example `active` or `disabled`, and indicates whether the method is currently selectable at checkout.

Consumers can use this to filter analytics to only active methods or to compare historical results for disabled methods.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which the aggregated metrics are calculated.

This maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.stats_date`, which is typically normalized to midnight UTC for consistency.

Dashboards often use this field as the X-axis key when rendering time series charts per payment method.

payment_attempt_count.description:
Number of payment attempts initiated using this payment method on the given stats date.

This equals `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_attempt_count` and includes all attempts regardless of eventual outcome.

It is the primary volume metric and the denominator for success, failure, and expiry rates.

payment_success_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that completed successfully (paid) for this method on the stats date.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_success_count` and directly contributes to revenue recognition.

Combined with attempts, it allows consumers to compute success ratios per method.

payment_failure_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that definitively failed or were declined for this method on the stats date.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_failure_count`.

Operators monitor this metric to detect degradation of provider quality or configuration issues.

payment_expired_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that expired without reaching a success or failure outcome on the stats date.

This equals `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_expired_count` and typically represents timeouts or abandoned flows.

High expiry counts can indicate UX problems or provider latency issues.

paid_gmv_amount.description:
GMV amount associated with successful payments for this method on the stats date, in platform base currency.

This maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.paid_gmv_amount` and represents the revenue volume processed through the method.

Finance and operations teams use this metric to understand the financial importance of each method.

refunded_amount.description:
Total amount refunded for payments that used this method on the stats date, in platform base currency.

This is taken from `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.refunded_amount` and aggregates all refunds associated with the method.

It provides insight into the quality of orders processed via the method and potential customer dissatisfaction.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total chargeback amount related to this payment method on the stats date, in platform base currency.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.chargeback_amount` and reflects the financial risk or loss associated with disputes and fraudulent transactions.

Risk and finance teams track this metric closely when assessing method-level risk exposure.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of an order cancellation request for list views and compact overviews.

This DTO combines key header information from `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` with light-weight order and actor context so that customer support agents, sellers, or admins can quickly scan and filter cancellation queues.

It is intentionally optimized for performance and readability, exposing identifiers, status, scope, and timestamps while omitting heavy child collections such as per-item breakdowns or full order payloads.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cancellation request.

This is the primary key `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id` and is used as the stable technical identifier when drilling down into a detailed cancellation view or performing actions on the request.

request_code.description:
Business-visible identifier for the cancellation request.

It corresponds to `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.request_code` and is typically shown in customer and seller communication, audit exports, and support tools.

The combination of `shopping_mall_order_id` and this code is unique, allowing easy reference within the scope of a single order.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the cancellation request.

It reflects `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.status` and usually takes values such as `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `expired` depending on the business workflow.

Queues and dashboards use this field for filtering and for driving the next available actions.

scope_type.description:
Scope of the cancellation being requested.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.scope_type` and distinguishes between full-order cancellations and partial-item cancellations.

Frontends can use this to label the request clearly, for example "Full order" vs "Partial items".

reason_code.description:
Structured reason code selected for the cancellation, when provided.

It directly mirrors `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.reason_code` and typically contains normalized values such as `change_of_mind` or `ordered_by_mistake`.

Null indicates that the requester either skipped a structured reason or only provided free-text explanation.

requested_by_actor_type.description:
Actor type that initiated the cancellation request.

This is `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.requested_by_actor_type` and can contain values like `customer`, `seller`, or `admin` according to governance rules.

Support and analytics tools use this field to segment cancellation behavior by actor group.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was created.

This is mapped from `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.requested_at` and marks the start of the SLA measurement period.

Support dashboards and SLA monitoring tools rely on this timestamp when calculating time-to-decision and backlog age.

decided_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request reached a terminal decision such as approved or rejected.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.decided_at` and is null while the request is still pending or in progress.

SLA and operational reports use this to measure processing times and to identify overdue requests.

order.description:
Summary of the order referenced by this cancellation request.

Represents the BELONGS-TO association from `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_order_id` to the `shopping_mall_orders` table, transformed into a lightweight order summary.

Includes enough information (such as order code, customer, monetary totals, and status) for list views and dashboards to render context without issuing additional order detail queries per cancellation row.

customer.description:
Customer who requested the cancellation when the actor type is `customer`.

Derived from the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_customer_id` and exposed as a lightweight customer summary instead of a raw UUID.

Null when the request was initiated by a different actor type such as seller or admin.

seller.description:
Seller who requested the cancellation when the actor type is `seller`.

Derived from the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_seller_id` and exposed as a lightweight seller summary instead of a raw UUID.

Null when the request originates from a different actor type such as customer or admin.

admin.description:
Administrator who created or submitted the cancellation request when the actor type is `admin`.

Derived from the optional foreign key `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.shopping_mall_admin_id` and exposed as a lightweight admin summary instead of a raw UUID.

Null when the cancellation request was submitted directly by customers or sellers without an intermediary admin actor.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequestItem.ISu.description:
Summary DTO for a single cancellation request line item in the shopping mall domain.

This type represents a concise, read-optimized view of an individual cancellation line associated with a higher-level cancellation request. It is intended for list views, overviews on cancellation request detail screens, and embedded summaries where full relational depth is not required.

The summary exposes identifying information, the linked order item and parent cancellation request as lightweight summary objects, the quantity being cancelled, and key audit timestamps so that clients can quickly understand what portion of an order is affected by this cancellation line without loading the full entity graph or chasing raw foreign key identifiers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cancellation request item.

This value maps directly to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items` table and is used to uniquely reference a specific item-level cancellation line within the platform.

Clients use this identifier when they need to reference or discuss a particular cancellation line in logs, audit tools, or internal dashboards.

cancellationRequest.description:
Summary of the parent cancellation request that owns this line item.

This object corresponds to the `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id` foreign key column that links the line back to its header record in `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests`.

Including the parent cancellation request summary here allows clients to render basic header context—such as high-level status, who initiated the request, and when—without making an additional API call or dealing with raw UUID values.

orderItem.description:
Summary of the underlying order item affected by this cancellation line.

This is the transformed representation of the `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key targeting `shopping_mall_order_items`, and it identifies which concrete purchased SKU and order line are impacted by the cancellation.

By providing an order item summary instead of just an ID, UIs can immediately show product name, SKU, and pricing information in cancellation line lists without performing additional lookups.

requested_quantity.description:
Quantity of the order item that the requester wants to cancel.

The value comes from the `requested_quantity` column and expresses how many units of the referenced order item are being requested for cancellation.

This number is always non-negative in valid business flows and is interpreted in the same unit as the original order item quantity, allowing partial cancellations of multi-quantity lines.

reason_description.description:
Optional free-text explanation specific to this item-level cancellation.

This field is backed by the nullable `reason_description` column and is used when an item requires more granular explanation than the header-level reason stored on the parent cancellation request.

When present, the text can be displayed to support agents and back-office tools to better understand special conditions or edge cases for this particular item line.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request item record was created.

The value mirrors the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_items` table and captures when the line first entered the system.

It is primarily used for audit trails, time-based reporting, and troubleshooting scenarios where agents need to know the exact creation moment of each item-level cancellation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request item record was last updated.

This corresponds to the `updated_at` column and is refreshed whenever mutable attributes of the item record change according to business rules.

The field allows clients and operational tools to understand recency of changes, supporting cache invalidation decisions and giving support staff insight into the lifecycle of the item record.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single refund request line item within a shopping mall order.

This type is optimized for list and embedding scenarios where only key financial and linkage information about the refund line is required, not the full relational graph.

It corresponds to the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` table but intentionally exposes its header, order item, payment refund item, and reason relationships as lightweight `.ISummary` objects instead of raw foreign key identifiers, making it more readable and directly usable in higher-level DTOs and UI layers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund request item.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_items` record and is used to reference this specific refund line in APIs and internal processes.

refundRequest.description:
Summary of the parent refund request that owns this line item.

This object represents the header entity referenced by the `shopping_mall_refund_request_id` foreign key and groups together all lines that belong to the same refund case.

Including this summary allows list and detail views of refund items to show high-level case information without requiring an extra fetch by ID.

orderItem.description:
Optional summary of the associated order item when the refund targets a specific purchased SKU.

When non-null, this is the transformed representation of the `shopping_mall_order_item_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_order_items` and tells which concrete order line is being refunded.

When null, the refund line is amount-based only or relates to a payment-level component, and there is no single order item to associate.

paymentRefundItem.description:
Optional summary of the underlying payment refund item that realizes this refund line at the payment provider level.

When present, this corresponds to the `shopping_mall_payment_refund_item_id` foreign key and links business-level refund semantics to a specific row in `shopping_mall_payment_refund_items`.

This summary is useful for reconciliation tools and payment operations dashboards that need to correlate refund request lines with gateway-level refund executions.

reason.description:
Optional structured reason associated with this refund line.

When non-null, this is the transformed representation of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_reason_id` foreign key pointing to a `shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons` record and may differ from the primary reason stored on the refund request header.

Providing the reason as a `.ISummary` object enables UIs and reports to display user-friendly labels and categories for the line-level reason without additional lookups.

requested_quantity.description:
Quantity of the item that the requester asked to be refunded on this line.

When null, the line is amount-based rather than quantity-based. When non-null, it typically corresponds to a subset of the original ordered quantity and shares the same unit as the order item quantity.

This field is useful for partial quantity refunds where only part of an order line is being refunded.

approved_quantity.description:
Quantity that has been approved for refund by the reviewing actor.

This may be less than the `requested_quantity` when only a partial quantity refund is authorized, or null when the refund is purely amount-based without explicit quantity semantics.

Consumers can compare requested and approved quantities to understand partial approvals at a glance.

requested_amount.description:
Monetary amount requested to be refunded for this line item, expressed in the order currency.

This amount should match or be derived from the value of the related order item or payment component, before any approvals or adjustments are applied.

It is a required field because each refund line must specify the requested monetary impact even when quantity is null.

approved_amount.description:
Monetary amount approved to be refunded for this line item after review, expressed in the order currency.

When null, the approval decision has not yet been finalized for this line or uses an implicit rule based on other data. When non-null, it represents the authoritative approved amount for settlement and reconciliation.

Comparing requested and approved amounts provides insight into partial approvals and adjustments made during the review process.

currency_code.description:
Currency code for the requested and approved amounts on this refund line.

This typically matches the currency of the parent order (for example, `USD` or `KRW`) and is used to ensure correct financial reporting, aggregation, and reconciliation in multi-currency environments.

The code should follow standard ISO 4217 currency codes as defined in the underlying Prisma schema and business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request item record was created.

Used for audit, ordering, and analytics, this value represents when the line first entered the system, usually close to the creation time of the parent refund request.

It supports chronological sorting, time-based reporting, and incident investigation workflows.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund request item record was last updated.

This reflects the most recent modification of the line, such as changes to approved amounts, quantities, or linkage fields, and is useful for tracking the lifecycle and operational handling of the refund item.

Analytics and monitoring tools can use this value to measure processing times and detect stale or long-pending refund items.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestStatusHistory..description:
Summary view of a single status transition in the lifecycle of a shopping mall refund request.

This type is designed for list and timeline presentations where the full relational graph is not required, but key information about when and how the status changed must be visible.

It corresponds to the `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories` table and exposes the principal audit fields that describe each transition event, without exposing raw foreign key identifiers to related entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund request status history entry.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_refund_request_status_histories` table and is used to reference this specific transition record in audit and troubleshooting tools.

from_status.description:
Previous status of the refund request before this transition.

Null is typically used for the first transition when the refund request is created and there is no prior status to record.

to_status.description:
New status of the refund request after this transition.

This value represents the target lifecycle state (for example, requested, under_review, approved, rejected, or completed) and is the primary status indicator for this history row.

changed_by_actor_type.description:
Actor type that caused the status change, such as `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `system`.

This field is useful for analytics, governance, and filtering timelines by who performed specific actions during the refund process.

reason_description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation describing why this status change occurred.

This can contain notes from admins or system-generated messages summarizing the trigger condition or decision rationale for the transition.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change took effect from a business perspective.

This is the primary temporal marker used to order the lifecycle events of a refund request in user-facing timelines and audit views.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this status history record was inserted into the database.

In most cases this closely matches `occurred_at`, but it may differ for backfilled or asynchronously processed events.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this status history record was last updated.

Updates are rare as the table is conceptually append-only, but this field supports corrections and metadata adjustments while preserving auditability.

IShoppingMallRefundRequestReason.ISummar.description:
Summary view of a refund or cancellation request reason used in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO provides a lightweight representation suitable for listing and selection UIs, focusing on the stable business identifier, human readable name, and applicability flags without exposing full configuration details.

It is derived directly from the shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons table and preserves only the fields that are essential for client-side decision making and analytics-friendly filters.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund request reason.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_refund_request_reasons record and is used to reference the reason in refund and cancellation request APIs.

Clients should treat this identifier as an opaque UUID that is stable over time.

code.description:
Unique machine-friendly code representing the refund or cancellation reason.

The code is used by both backend services and reporting pipelines to categorize refund and cancellation cases in a stable way, for example damaged_item or change_of_mind.

Business rules and policy engines typically reference this field rather than the localized name.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the refund or cancellation reason.

This value is intended for display in management tools and user interfaces, usually after localization is applied on the client or at the API edge.

The name should clearly communicate when this reason should be selected in the context of a refund or cancellation request.

applies_to_cancellation.description:
Indicates whether this reason is valid for order or order-item cancellation requests.

When true, cancellation flows may present this reason in their reason pickers, and analytics for cancellations can group by this flag.

When false, the reason must not be offered in cancellation-specific user interfaces.

applies_to_refund.description:
