Indicates whether this reason is valid for refund requests.

When true, refund flows and refund request forms may present this reason as an option for customers, sellers, or admins.

When false, the reason must be excluded from refund-specific reason selectors.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating if this reason is currently allowed for new refund or cancellation requests.

Active reasons can be selected in new cases while inactive reasons are preserved only for historical requests and analytics.

Client applications should typically filter on this flag when populating selectable lists of reasons.

IShoppingMallDisputeParty.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a party participating in a platform-level dispute.

This summary DTO is optimized for list views and nested embeddings where only key identification and role information about each party are required, rather than the full dispute party record.

It is built directly from the `shopping_mall_dispute_parties` Prisma model and intentionally excludes relational collections or large text fields, focusing instead on fields that describe who the party is and how they participate in the dispute.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute party record.

This value matches the primary key of the corresponding `shopping_mall_dispute_parties` row and is used to reference this party in detailed APIs or when correlating audit data.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that this party represents in the dispute.

Typical values include `customer`, `seller`, `admin`, or `external`. This field determines which of the actor foreign keys (customer, seller, admin) is populated in the underlying Prisma model and is essential for interpreting this party within the dispute context.

role.description:
Role of this party in the dispute process.

Examples include `complainant`, `respondent`, `witness`, or `observer`. Business workflows, permissions, and UI labels for the party are typically derived from this role value.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name shown in admin and operations tooling for this dispute party.

For internal actors, this is generally derived from the corresponding customer, seller, or admin profile. For external parties, it may be manually entered. This field can be null when a name is not available or not required.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a single event in the lifecycle of a dispute.

This DTO is designed for compact timeline or activity list views where only core event classification, status change information, timestamps, and minimal parent dispute context are required, rather than the full event record.

It is mapped directly from the `shopping_mall_dispute_events` Prisma model and intentionally omits long-form descriptions or relational collections, focusing instead on the information needed to quickly understand what happened, when it happened, and which dispute it belongs to.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute event.

This value matches the primary key of the corresponding `shopping_mall_dispute_events` row and is used to reference this event in detailed dispute timelines or audit trails.

event_type.description:
Categorization of the event within the dispute workflow.

Typical values include `created`, `note_added`, `status_changed`, `escalated`, `evidence_added`, or `external_update`. Client applications use this field to choose appropriate icons, labels, or rendering logic for each event in timelines.

status_before.description:
Dispute status immediately before this event occurred.

This field is populated when the event involves a status transition, such as moving from `open` to `under_investigation`. It is null for event types that do not modify status, such as simple notes or evidence additions.

status_after.description:
Dispute status immediately after this event occurred.

For status-changing events, this value records the resulting lifecycle state of the dispute. For events that do not change status, this field is null.

occurred_at.description:
Business timestamp when the event occurred.

This represents the point in time when the underlying action actually happened (for example, when an admin made a decision or when a user submitted information), and is used for ordering events in dispute timelines and for SLA analysis.

dispute.description:
Parent dispute that this event belongs to, represented as a lightweight summary.

This replaces the raw `shopping_mall_dispute_id` foreign key in the summary DTO so that consumers can immediately understand which dispute the event is associated with, without performing an additional lookup.

The summary form avoids circular references and keeps the payload compact while still providing sufficient context for timelines, search results, and administrative overviews.

IShoppingMallDisputeEvidence.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single dispute evidence item attached to a dispute within the shopping mall platform.

This summary type is optimized for list and contextual views inside dispute timelines and case dashboards, where operators need to quickly understand what kind of evidence exists without loading full domain graphs.

It exposes key identifying fields, core classification metadata, lightweight dispute linkage, and minimal temporal information, while avoiding heavy or deeply nested relations. Use this schema when embedding evidence information inside other DTOs or paginated collections.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute evidence record.

This value directly corresponds to the `id` primary key column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` Prisma model.

It is a stable UUID assigned at creation time and never changes for the lifetime of the evidence record.

shopping_mall_dispute_id.description:
Identifier of the dispute that this evidence supports.

This field maps to the `shopping_mall_dispute_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences`, which references the primary key of the `shopping_mall_disputes` model.

Use this value to correlate evidence items with their parent dispute when building dispute-centric views or performing joins on the dispute identifier.

shopping_mall_dispute_event_id.description:
Optional identifier of the specific dispute event that introduced this evidence.

When present, this value points to the `shopping_mall_dispute_event_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences`, referencing `shopping_mall_dispute_events`. It allows UIs and back-office tools to anchor the evidence to a particular step in the dispute timeline.

When null, the evidence is associated only at the dispute level and not to a specific event instance.

evidence_type.description:
Type classification of the evidence, such as `image`, `document`, `message_log`, or `external_reference`.

This field maps to the non-nullable `evidence_type` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` and is used for filtering, grouping, and rendering different viewers in admin consoles.

Client implementations should treat this as an opaque string constrained by business configuration, rather than attempting to infer behavior solely from free-form values.

title.description:
Optional short title or label that describes this evidence in operator tools.

This property reflects the nullable `title` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences`. When set, it should provide a concise summary that helps admins and agents quickly recognize the evidence item.

When null, UIs are expected to fall back to generic labels derived from the evidence type or URI.

uri.description:
URI pointing to the stored evidence content in external storage or another system.

This property maps to the non-nullable `uri` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences`. It is typically a fully-qualified URL into an object storage service, document system, or integrator endpoint.

The evidence DTO always exposes only metadata and the URI; actual binary content is retrieved via the referenced system rather than through this API directly.

checksum.description:
Optional checksum or hash of the evidence content used for integrity verification.

This property corresponds to the nullable `checksum` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences`. When present, it can hold hashes such as SHA-256 in hex string form and is intended for audit, forensics, or tamper detection flows.

When null, no integrity hash has been recorded for this particular evidence item.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this dispute evidence record was created.

This value maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences` and is stored in a timezone-normalized ISO 8601 format.

It is primarily used for chronological sorting, filtering, and time-based analytics over dispute evidence activity.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this dispute evidence record was last updated.

This property reflects the non-nullable `updated_at` column on `shopping_mall_dispute_evidences`. It is automatically updated when mutable metadata such as title or description is changed.

Consumers can rely on this value to implement optimistic concurrency checks or to detect when a local cache of evidence metadata is stale.

dispute.description:
Summary of the dispute that this evidence belongs to.

This association is a lightweight view over the parent dispute and can be populated when evidence summaries are loaded in contexts where dispute information is already joined or cached.

Including this field allows list and dashboard views to show basic dispute attributes alongside each evidence record without requiring additional network calls.

dispute_event.description:
Summary of the dispute event that introduced this evidence, when applicable.

This association references the corresponding `shopping_mall_dispute_events` row and can be used to display the timeline context for each evidence item in event-centric views.

When null, the evidence is not tied to a specific event and should be treated as dispute-level context instead.

IShoppingMallCaseSlaViolation.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single SLA violation record for shopping mall case handling.

This summary DTO represents a compact projection of the `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` table, focusing on the essential identifiers, classification fields, timing information, and the violated SLA configuration required for list views and dashboards.

It is intended for use in aggregated lists of SLA breaches, monitoring screens, and analytics drill-down entry points, where full relational expansion to the underlying cancellation, refund, or dispute cases is not required but direct access to the violated SLA rule is important.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SLA violation record.

This corresponds to the primary key `id` column in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` and is used to reference a specific breach when navigating to detail views or performing audit queries.

case_type.description:
Type of the underlying case that violated the SLA, such as cancellation, refund, or dispute.

This mirrors the `case_type` column in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` and is used to distinguish which case domain (cancellations, refunds, or disputes) produced this SLA breach for reporting and filtering.

actor_role.description:
Actor role responsible for satisfying the breached SLA, for example seller or admin.

This corresponds to the `actor_role` column and allows operations and governance teams to see which actor group was accountable for the missed service-level commitment.

action_type.description:
Action for which the SLA was defined and subsequently breached, such as `initial_response` or `final_decision`.

This maps to the `action_type` field and clarifies which specific process milestone exceeded the configured target time.

breach_duration_seconds.description:
Number of seconds by which the SLA target was exceeded.

This corresponds to `breach_duration_seconds` and quantifies how late the responsible actor was relative to the SLA configuration, enabling severity classification and ranking of breaches.

detected_at.description:
Timestamp when the system detected that this SLA violation occurred.

This maps to the `detected_at` column and represents when monitoring logic first recognized the breach, which may be later than the exact point when the target time was crossed.

slaConfig.description:
Summary of the SLA configuration that was violated.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id` foreign key and provides immediate context about the breached rule, such as case_type, actor_role, action_type, and configured thresholds. Admin dashboards and monitoring tools can use this summary directly without issuing additional queries to resolve the associated SLA configuration.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA violation record was first created in the database.

This is the `created_at` field in `shopping_mall_case_sla_violations` and is used for audit trails and temporal analysis of when violation records were inserted.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SLA violation record was last updated.

This maps to the `updated_at` column and is typically modified if additional metadata or corrections are applied to the violation record by background jobs or maintenance processes.

IShoppingMallRefundsAndDisputesCaseSumma.description:
Summary of refund and dispute activity for a specific calendar date across the shopping mall platform.

This DTO provides a compact, read-optimized projection of the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` snapshot table, exposing core counters and timing aggregates relevant for operational reporting and monitoring.

It is typically used in analytics dashboards, daily KPI reports, and timeline visualizations where each instance represents metrics for one day, optionally filtered by date range or combined with other platform KPIs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund and dispute stats snapshot row.

This corresponds to the `id` primary key in `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` and is mainly used for internal referencing and audit of the aggregated record.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these refund and dispute metrics are calculated.

This maps to the `stats_date` column and SHOULD be normalized to midnight UTC for each business day, serving as the primary temporal dimension for grouping and charting.

refund_request_count.description:
Total number of refund requests created on this date.

This corresponds to `refund_request_count` and counts all new refund cases regardless of their eventual approval or rejection outcome.

approved_refund_request_count.description:
Number of refund requests that reached an approved state on this date.

This field maps to `approved_refund_request_count` and includes approvals for cases that may have been opened on earlier dates, focusing on decision timing rather than creation time.

rejected_refund_request_count.description:
Number of refund requests that were rejected on this date.

This corresponds to the `rejected_refund_request_count` column and captures how many refund cases received a negative decision during the given day, independent of when they were originally created.

refunded_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded on this date in the platform's base currency.

This maps to `refunded_amount` and aggregates the value of completed payment refunds, enabling financial teams to track refund exposure and cash outflow related to after-sales operations.

partial_refund_count.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that were partial relative to the original order or item amount.

This field corresponds to `partial_refund_count` and is used to distinguish partial remediation actions from full order or line-item refunds for risk and customer experience analysis.

full_refund_count.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that fully refunded the relevant order or items.

This maps to `full_refund_count` and helps measure the share of complete reversals versus partial adjustments in the refund workload.

dispute_opened_count.description:
Number of new disputes created on this date for any reason.

This corresponds to `dispute_opened_count` and includes disputes arising from payment issues, fulfillment conflicts, policy violations, or other high-severity cases.

dispute_resolved_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved on this date, regardless of when they were originally opened.

This field represents the `dispute_resolved_count` column and reflects throughput of dispute resolution activities within the day.

dispute_resolved_for_customer_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the customer on this date.

This maps to `dispute_resolved_for_customer_count` and is a key metric for customer-centric decision bias and satisfaction analysis.

dispute_resolved_for_seller_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the seller on this date.

This corresponds to `dispute_resolved_for_seller_count` and indicates how often dispute outcomes support seller positions, useful for fairness and risk calibration monitoring.

average_refund_resolution_time_hours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between refund request creation and final decision for refunds resolved on this date.

This maps to `average_refund_resolution_time_hours` and serves as a core SLA and efficiency indicator for refund processing performance.

average_dispute_resolution_time_hours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between dispute creation and resolution for disputes resolved on this date.

This corresponds to `average_dispute_resolution_time_hours` and is used by operations and risk teams to evaluate dispute handling speed relative to target service levels.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this stats row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

This maps to `created_at` and is typically set when the aggregation job first computes metrics for the given `stats_date`.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this stats snapshot was last recomputed or corrected.

This corresponds to `updated_at` and may be updated if late-arriving events or corrections cause the analytics pipeline to recalculate metrics for the same stats date.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single review report in the shopping mall review system.

This DTO is designed for list and overview screens where moderators or admins need a compact representation of reports submitted against customer product reviews. It focuses on identity, linkage to the underlying review, key classification fields, and high‑level processing status without exposing the full report lifecycle history.

The schema is mapped directly to the `shopping_mall_review_reports` Prisma model but intentionally omits large or rarely used fields so that it can be efficiently returned in paginated result sets and embedded inside other entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review report.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_review_reports.id` and uniquely distinguishes each report row created when an actor flags a review as problematic. It is a server‑generated UUID and is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

shopping_mall_review_id.description:
Identifier of the review that has been reported as problematic.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_review_reports.shopping_mall_review_id` and links the report to a row in `shopping_mall_reviews`. It allows moderation tooling, analytics pipelines, and linking logic to reference the underlying review record directly using its primary key when needed.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that submitted the report, such as `customer`, `seller`, or `system`.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_review_reports.actor_type` and is used by higher‑level application logic to interpret the `reporter_actor_reference` identifier. Typical values distinguish organic customer complaints from seller‑initiated or automated policy‑driven reports, which can affect prioritization and handling workflows.

reason_code.description:
Categorized reason for the report, for example `offensive_content`, `spam`, `conflict_of_interest`, or `other`.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_review_reports.reason_code` and is used to group and prioritize moderation queues. Downstream analytics can aggregate reports by reason to identify emerging abuse patterns or problematic product segments.

status.description:
Processing status of the review report, such as `open`, `under_review`, `resolved`, or `dismissed`.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_review_reports.status` and indicates the current moderation workflow state. It is used by operational dashboards to route work, measure backlog, and enforce service‑level expectations for report handling.

review.description:
Summary of the underlying customer review that has been reported as problematic.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_review_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_reviews` and is projected as `IShoppingMallReview.ISummary` to expose key review attributes (such as rating, headline, and product or SKU context) without requiring additional API calls.

Moderation and analytics UIs can use this object to render the core review content inline within report lists while still relying on `shopping_mall_review_id` for precise linking and drill‑down operations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was created.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_review_reports.created_at` and records the moment the platform accepted the report from the actor. It is commonly used for sorting, SLA calculation, and time‑based filtering in moderation tools.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the report record was last updated.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_review_reports.updated_at` and is modified whenever mutable attributes like `status`, `reason_code`, or descriptive details are changed by moderators or system processes. It helps operators understand how recently a report has been touched.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulVote.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single helpful vote on a shopping mall product review backed by the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` Prisma model.

This DTO is used in list, search, and analytics responses to represent that a specific customer has cast a helpfulness vote on a particular review. It exposes only non-sensitive columns from the underlying table so that client applications and internal dashboards can reason about voting behavior without loading the full review or customer entities.

The summary aligns one-to-one with the non-nullable columns of the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` model, including audit timestamps. It is intended as a read-only projection: creation and mutation of helpful votes should use dedicated request DTOs that derive actor identity from authentication context rather than trusting arbitrary identifiers from clients.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the helpful vote record.

This value maps to the primary key `id` column in the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` table. It is generated by the system when the vote is first created and remains stable for the lifetime of the record, allowing deterministic references from logs, analytics pipelines, and administrative tools.

shopping_mall_review_id.description:
Identifier of the review that this helpful vote refers to.

The value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_review_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` model and points to `shopping_mall_reviews.id`. Use this field to group or aggregate votes by review when computing helpfulness metrics or when building review detail views that embed vote information.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who cast this helpful vote.

This field maps directly to the `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key column in `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`, referencing `shopping_mall_customers.id`. In write flows the authenticated customer identity is typically derived from the authorization context, but in this summary response it is exposed as an ID so that internal tools and analytics jobs can attribute votes to specific customers when needed.

is_helpful.description:
Flag indicating whether the customer marked the review as helpful.

When `true`, the vote contributes positively to the review's perceived helpfulness; when `false`, it represents a negative or non-helpful decision. Both positive and negative votes are stored so that net helpfulness and more nuanced distributions can be computed in the reviews and rating analytics domain.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the helpful vote record was first created.

The value comes from the non-nullable `created_at` column on `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes` and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It is typically used for chronological sorting, time-window filtering, and reconstruction of historical voting patterns.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this helpful vote record.

This field mirrors the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes`. It is updated whenever the vote changes, for example when a customer flips from helpful to not helpful. Analytics and audit tools can compare `created_at` and `updated_at` to detect changes over time or to reason about when a vote last contributed to aggregate metrics.

IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.ISum.description:
Summary view of precomputed rating aggregates for a single product based on the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` Prisma model.

This DTO exposes denormalized statistics such as average rating, total review counts, and per-score breakdowns that are optimized for fast reads from product detail pages, category listings, and analytics dashboards. The underlying data is derived from `shopping_mall_reviews` and related entities and is maintained by background jobs or trigger-based processes rather than direct user writes.

Consumers should treat this object as a materialized aggregate snapshot rather than the source of truth for individual reviews. It is designed for read-only scenarios, giving clients enough information to render rating widgets, filter and sort products by rating, and analyze rating distributions over time without querying the underlying review tables directly.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this product rating aggregate row.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` column in the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` table. It is primarily used by internal systems, analytics pipelines, and administrative tooling to reference and manage specific aggregate snapshots.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product whose rating metrics are summarized by this record.

The field maps to the `shopping_mall_product_id` column in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and references `shopping_mall_products.id`. Each product normally has at most one active aggregate row, allowing quick joins from catalog queries to the latest rating statistics.

average_rating.description:
Average rating score for the product computed from all included reviews.

This value is derived from customer reviews stored in `shopping_mall_reviews` and follows the business-defined rating scale, for example from 1.0 to 5.0 with one or two decimal places of precision. The field is nullable in the underlying Prisma model and will be omitted or set to null when no eligible reviews exist for the product, signalling that the product has not yet been rated.

rating_count.description:
Total number of reviews that contribute to the aggregate metrics for this product.

The count comes from the non-nullable `rating_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. Only reviews that satisfy business eligibility and visibility rules (for example, not soft-deleted or fully suppressed by moderation) are included, ensuring that public-facing metrics accurately reflect the reviews customers can see.

rating_1_count.description:
Number of included reviews that carry the lowest rating value on the configured scale, typically 1-star reviews.

This field maps to the non-nullable `rating_1_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. It allows clients and analytics tools to understand how many strongly negative reviews exist for the product.

rating_2_count.description:
Number of included reviews with the second rating value on the scale, typically 2-star reviews.

The value comes from the `rating_2_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and helps characterize mildly negative or below-average customer sentiment for the product.

rating_3_count.description:
Number of included reviews with a mid-range rating value, typically 3-star reviews.

This value is stored in the `rating_3_count` column of `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and is useful when visualizing neutral or mixed sentiment about the product.

rating_4_count.description:
Number of included reviews with a high rating value, typically 4-star reviews.

The value corresponds to the `rating_4_count` column in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. It is commonly used when presenting positive sentiment distributions in rating charts or dashboards.

rating_5_count.description:
Number of included reviews with the highest rating value on the scale, typically 5-star reviews.

This count is persisted in the `rating_5_count` column of `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. A high 5-star count combined with a strong average rating usually indicates that the product is performing very well from a customer satisfaction perspective.

last_computed_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the aggregate metrics were last recalculated for this product.

The value is taken from the non-nullable `last_computed_at` column in the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` table and is represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Clients can use this timestamp to understand data freshness, implement cache invalidation policies, or display messages when rating information may be slightly out of date due to batch recomputation intervals.

IShoppingMallSkuRatingAggregate.ISummary.description:
Summary view of precomputed rating aggregates for a single SKU.

This DTO exposes the key rating metrics derived from customer reviews for a specific SKU variant, allowing clients to quickly display rating information without recomputing aggregates at query time.

It is backed by the `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` materialized table and therefore reflects data that is periodically recomputed by background processes rather than updated directly via business workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU rating aggregate record.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates` table and is used internally to track and reference the aggregate row.

It is system-generated and immutable from the client perspective.

sku.description:
SKU whose rating metrics are represented by this aggregate.

This association points to the concrete sellable variant (SKU) in the catalog and follows the standard `.ISummary` pattern for belongs-to relations.

Clients can use this object to render SKU context (name, code, etc.) alongside rating aggregates without issuing additional SKU detail queries.

average_rating.description:
Average rating value for the SKU computed from customer reviews.

When there are one or more reviews associated with this SKU, this field contains the aggregated average rating value, typically on a fixed-point scale such as 1–5.

When the SKU has not yet received any reviews, this field is `null` to indicate the absence of rating data rather than a numeric value of zero.

rating_count.description:
Total number of included reviews that contribute to the rating metrics for this SKU.

This count reflects all reviews that are considered valid and included in the aggregate, after applying any business rules such as moderation or eligibility filters.

Clients can use this value to show how many customers have rated the SKU, which is often displayed alongside the average rating.

rating_1_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with the lowest rating score, for example one-star ratings.

This value helps analytics and UI components display distributions of ratings so users can understand how many customers gave the minimum possible score.

It is derived exclusively from the set of reviews that are currently considered valid for aggregation.

rating_2_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with the second-lowest rating score, typically two-star ratings.

Together with the other per-score counts, this enables display of rating histograms or breakdown charts on product detail pages.

The value always represents a non-negative integer computed from eligible reviews.

rating_3_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with a mid-range rating score, typically three-star ratings.

Mid-range scores often indicate neutral or mixed experiences, and this count helps merchants and customers understand the balance of sentiment.

The value is maintained by background aggregation processes using underlying review data.

rating_4_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with a high rating score, typically four-star ratings.

This count contributes to the rating distribution visualization and can be used to understand how many customers were satisfied but not maximally enthusiastic.

It is always a non-negative integer derived from the set of accepted reviews for the SKU.

rating_5_count.description:
Number of included reviews for this SKU with the highest rating score, typically five-star ratings.

This value indicates how many customers rated the SKU with top marks and is frequently used to highlight positive sentiment in UI components such as rating bars or histograms.

The count is computed from review records and kept in sync by aggregation logic rather than direct client writes.

last_computed_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the aggregate metrics were last recomputed for this SKU.

This value lets clients and operators understand the freshness of the rating statistics, which may lag behind real-time review submissions depending on aggregation schedules.

The timestamp is always managed by backend processes and should be treated as read-only from API consumers.

IShoppingMallReviewEligibility.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a review eligibility record that describes when and for which purchase a customer may write a review.

This DTO represents the essential business information about a customer’s eligibility to submit a product or SKU review, without exposing lower-level operational details or raw foreign key columns.

It is backed by the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` table and is typically used when checking or listing which items a customer can still review.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review eligibility record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_review_eligibilities` table and uniquely identifies a single eligibility instance.

It is system-generated and immutable from the perspective of API clients.

customer.description:
Customer who owns this eligibility to write a review.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_customer_id` column in the response layer and exposes a lightweight `.ISummary` view of the customer.

Clients can use it to render customer context when needed, particularly in administrative or analytical views of review eligibility.

product.description:
Product that may be reviewed under this eligibility.

This association replaces the underlying `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key and provides a `.ISummary` representation of the catalog product.

The product link is always present even when the purchase was not tied to a more granular SKU variant.

sku.description:
SKU variant that may be reviewed under this eligibility when the purchase is tied to a specific SKU.

When present, this association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_sku_id` foreign key and gives callers a `.ISummary` view of the concrete variant.

When `null`, the eligibility applies at the product level only, and the review is expected to be associated with the product without SKU granularity.

review.description:
Review that has consumed this eligibility, if a review has already been created.

When set, this association replaces the underlying `shopping_mall_review_id` column and exposes a summary of the actual review that used this eligibility.

When `null`, the eligibility is either still available or has expired/been revoked without producing a review, depending on the `status` value.

status.description:
Current eligibility status code that controls whether the customer can currently create a review.

Typical business values include states such as `eligible`, `used`, `expired`, or `revoked`, expressing whether a review can still be created from this record.

Clients should treat this as an opaque business status string and rely on documented state transitions rather than inferring semantics from the literal value alone.

eligible_from.description:
Timestamp from which the customer is allowed to submit a review based on this eligibility.

This is usually set when the associated order item reaches a delivered or completed state, marking the beginning of the review window.

Before this point in time clients should not offer the ability to create a review for the linked purchase.

eligible_until.description:
Optional timestamp after which this eligibility expires and can no longer be used to create a new review.

If present, the value marks the end of the allowed review window and clients should prevent review creation when the current time is beyond this point.

When `null`, no fixed expiry is configured at the eligibility record level and the effective window may be governed by higher-level policy rules instead.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the review eligibility record was created.

This is typically around the time when the order item reached a qualifying state for review, such as completion or delivery.

The value is managed solely by backend processes and is provided for audit trails, reporting, and time-based filtering.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the review eligibility record was most recently updated.

Updates can occur when status changes (for example from `eligible` to `used` or `expired`) or when related fields such as the consumed review reference are modified.

This field is useful for synchronization, troubleshooting, and identifying recently changed eligibility records.

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustmentReason.I.description:
Minimal inventory adjustment reason summary.

Represents the standardized business reason behind an inventory adjustment in a compact form suitable for list views and analytics.

The summary focuses on the code and primary label so operators can immediately understand the high‑level purpose of each adjustment without inspecting the full reason configuration record.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the inventory adjustment reason.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons.id` and is the canonical key for this reason definition.

code.description:
Business code of the inventory adjustment reason.

Used in configuration, reporting, and integrations to identify the reason category, such as `CORRECTION`, `DAMAGE`, or `AUDIT`.

name.description:
Human‑readable name of the inventory adjustment reason.

Displayed in admin tools, dashboards, and exported reports so users can quickly understand why an adjustment was performed.

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustment.ISummar.description:
Summary view of inventory adjustment analytics for a seller across SKUs and warehouses.

This DTO aggregates adjustment events from the underlying inventory adjustment tables to provide a compact view suitable for dashboards and list responses. It exposes only pre‑computed, read‑only metrics and does not map directly 1:1 to any single Prisma model.

The summary is typically used in seller and admin analytics UIs to quickly understand how inventory levels are being changed over a given time window, which directions dominate (increase vs decrease), and which SKUs or warehouses contribute most to stock volatility.

seller.description:
Seller for whom these inventory adjustment analytics are calculated.

This is a summary representation of the seller identity, derived from the core seller account model. It provides enough context to identify the seller in analytics dashboards without exposing sensitive authentication fields.

The seller reference allows consumers to correlate analytics with other seller‑centric reports and management tools.

period.description:
Time period over which the inventory adjustment metrics are aggregated.

The period encapsulates a concrete start and end timestamp, and may also include a human‑readable label such as a day, week, or month bucket. Analytics UIs can use this structure to align charts and tables with a consistent temporal window.

Using an explicit period object avoids ambiguities about the time range of the metrics and makes it easy to reuse the same pattern across different analytics summaries.

totalAdjustmentCount.description:
Total number of inventory adjustment events included in this summary period.

This count represents how many discrete adjustment records were processed for the given seller during the time range. It is useful to understand how frequently manual or system‑driven changes are made to stock.

A higher count may indicate operational volatility, frequent corrections, or high throughput of inbound and outbound movements that are not purely order‑driven.

totalIncreaseQuantity.description:
Sum of all positive quantity changes (increases) applied during the period for this seller.

This metric aggregates `quantity_delta` values from adjustment events that represent stock increases, such as inbound shipments, corrections that add stock, or returns processed back into inventory.

It is commonly used together with totalDecreaseQuantity to understand net movement and to validate reconciliation reports between physical and system counts.

totalDecreaseQuantity.description:
Sum of all negative quantity changes (decreases) applied during the period for this seller.

This metric aggregates the absolute quantity from adjustment events that reduce stock, including damage, shrinkage, write‑offs, and manual corrections that lower available units.

Comparing this value to totalIncreaseQuantity and netQuantityChange helps identify potential loss drivers and quality problems in the seller’s operations.

netQuantityChange.description:
Net quantity change for the seller during the period, computed as totalIncreaseQuantity minus totalDecreaseQuantity.

A positive value indicates that inventory levels have grown overall, while a negative value indicates that more stock was removed than added. A value close to zero suggests that increases and decreases roughly balanced out.

This metric is central for high‑level reconciliation and can be used as a quick health indicator for inventory stability.

distinctSkuCount.description:
Number of distinct SKUs that had at least one inventory adjustment during the period.

This count reflects how broadly inventory adjustments are distributed across the seller’s catalog. A high distinct SKU count indicates that many products are being corrected or tuned.

It is particularly useful to scope detailed drill‑down reports and to prioritize which SKUs may require stricter operational controls.

distinctWarehouseCount.description:
Number of distinct warehouses with at least one inventory adjustment for this seller during the period.

This metric shows how geographically or operationally distributed the adjustments are. For multi‑warehouse sellers, it helps identify which locations are most active or problematic.

Operations and risk teams can use this value to decide where to focus audits or training efforts.

topReasons.description:
Top inventory adjustment reasons ranked by their contribution to overall activity in the period.

Each element captures aggregated statistics for a single standardized reason code, such as damage, shrinkage, or inbound_receipt. Including this array allows dashboards to highlight which business reasons drive most inventory changes.

The list is typically limited to the most impactful reasons to keep the payload compact while still providing actionable insight.

topSkus.description:
Top SKUs ranked by adjustment activity for this seller within the period.

Entries summarize how much each SKU’s stock was increased or decreased across all warehouses, enabling quick identification of products with unstable inventory levels.

Analytics consumers can use this information to drill into SKU‑level history, investigate root causes, or adjust safety stock configurations.

topWarehouses.description:
Top warehouses ranked by adjustment volume for this seller during the period.

Each summary aggregates adjustment metrics per warehouse, helping to identify locations that require attention due to frequent corrections or high shrinkage.

This information is especially useful for multi‑warehouse sellers and for admins monitoring platform‑wide operational health.

IShoppingMallSellerOrderMetricsSnapshot..description:
Summary DTO representing a single time-series snapshot of seller order-related metrics.

This type provides a compact view of aggregated KPIs for one seller over a specific snapshot period such as a day, aligned with a particular business timezone.

It is optimized for dashboards, monitoring views, and reporting APIs, exposing counts and monetary totals together with lightweight seller context without expanding underlying transactional details from orders, items, refunds, or chargebacks.

The schema maps directly to the `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots` Prisma model and preserves the same field semantics used by the metrics computation process.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller order metrics snapshot row.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.id` and serves as the technical primary key.

It is mainly used for internal referencing, debugging, and deduplication of snapshot records.

seller.description:
Seller whose performance metrics are captured in this snapshot.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `seller_id` from the underlying snapshot table and points to a lightweight seller summary representation.

Including this summary object in the list view allows dashboards and list endpoints to render seller context (for example, seller name or code) alongside metrics without performing additional lookups.

snapshot_date.description:
Date or date-time boundary that defines the logical period for this snapshot.

The value reflects the point in time representing the summarized period, typically the start of the business day for which metrics were aggregated.

It is taken directly from `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.snapshot_date` and is used together with `timezone` to interpret day boundaries correctly.

timezone.description:
Business timezone identifier used when aggregating metrics for this snapshot.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.timezone` and typically contains values like `Asia/Seoul`.

It ensures that daily and periodic metrics respect the seller’s or platform’s configured time boundaries instead of raw UTC day splits.

orders_placed_count.description:
Number of orders that entered a placed or confirmed state for the seller within the snapshot period.

This count is derived from order headers and associated seller segments that became active during the period, aligning with the business definition of "placed" or "confirmed".

It maps to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.orders_placed_count` and is often used as a top-of-funnel indicator in performance dashboards.

orders_paid_count.description:
Number of orders that reached a paid state for the seller within the snapshot period.

The value is computed based on order payment state transitions and indicates how many seller-related orders successfully completed payment.

It reflects `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.orders_paid_count` and is commonly used to track conversion from placed to paid orders.

orders_cancelled_count.description:
Number of orders or order segments that were cancelled for the seller during the snapshot period.

This includes cancellations for any reason at either full order or partial line-item level, aggregated into a single integer.

The field is taken from `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.orders_cancelled_count` and is useful for monitoring operational risk and customer experience issues.

orders_refunded_count.description:
Number of orders or segments that had approved refunds impacting the seller in the snapshot period.

This count reflects the volume of refund activity, not the monetary amount, and is derived from refund-related transactional tables.

It corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.orders_refunded_count` and is often used along with refund amounts to understand post-purchase risk.

gmv_amount.description:
Gross merchandise value for the seller’s orders within the snapshot period.

The amount is calculated before cancellations and refunds, representing the raw total of order item values attributable to the seller.

It maps to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.gmv_amount` and is commonly used as a top-line revenue proxy in analytics.

nmv_amount.description:
Net merchandise value for the snapshot period after accounting for cancellations and refunds.

This metric starts from GMV and subtracts appropriate cancellation and refund impacts, reflecting the seller’s effective sales volume.

It corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.nmv_amount` and is a core KPI for financial and performance reporting.

shipping_fee_amount.description:
Total shipping fee amount charged to customers and associated with the seller’s items during the snapshot period.

The value aggregates shipping-related charges from relevant transactional sources.

It is taken from `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.shipping_fee_amount` and allows analysis of shipping revenue alongside merchandise value.

refund_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded to customers for this seller’s items within the snapshot period.

The figure aggregates approved refund amounts from refund operations and related breakdown tables.

It maps directly to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.refund_amount` and is a key input to margin and risk analyses.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total chargeback amount associated with this seller in the snapshot period.

This metric aggregates monetary values of chargebacks initiated by payment providers or card networks and linked to the seller’s transactions.

It corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.chargeback_amount` and is used in risk, compliance, and financial reconciliation reporting.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was first created by the metrics computation process.

The value comes from `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.created_at` and indicates when the snapshot became available for reporting.

It is useful for debugging batch jobs and validating that metric computation is running on schedule.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was last recalculated or corrected.

This field reflects `shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots.updated_at` and changes if a recomputation job adjusts the metrics due to late-arriving data or corrections.

Clients can use this timestamp to detect when cached values may need to be refreshed.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot.I.description:
Summary view of a seller performance snapshot in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents a lightweight, list‑optimized projection of the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` entity, focusing on key KPIs, timestamps, and a compact seller summary. It is intended for use in paginated lists, dashboards, and analytic overviews where many snapshot rows must be rendered efficiently.

Consumers typically use this summary to scan for high‑risk or high‑performing sellers, sort by important metrics such as refund or chargeback rates, and then navigate to the full detail representation `IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSnapshot` when deeper investigation is required. The summary keeps bandwidth usage low while still conveying all essential signals for monitoring and governance workflows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller performance snapshot.

This is the primary key of the underlying `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots` record and uniquely distinguishes this snapshot from all other snapshots in the system. It is used by detail APIs and internal tools to retrieve the full snapshot document when needed.

seller.description:
Summary view of the seller whose performance metrics are included in this snapshot.

Embedding the seller summary allows list and dashboard views to show seller identity and basic account state alongside KPIs without issuing additional API calls. Typical fields include seller id, email, lifecycle status, and key timestamps relevant for operational monitoring.

snapshot_date.description:
Logical date or date-time when the performance metrics were computed for this snapshot.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.snapshot_date` and indicates the boundary or reference point of the analysis window that produced the KPIs. It is expressed in ISO 8601 date‑time format and is used for ordering snapshots chronologically and building time‑series charts.

timezone.description:
Timezone context used for computing the performance window of this snapshot.

The value maps to `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.timezone` and typically contains IANA timezone identifiers such as `Asia/Seoul`. Consumers should interpret `snapshot_date` and any time‑based grouping in the context of this timezone to avoid ambiguity across regions and reporting tools.

order_defect_rate.description:
Order defect rate during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

The value mirrors `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.order_defect_rate` and captures the ratio of defective orders (according to platform business rules) to all relevant orders in the same period. Higher values indicate a greater incidence of problematic orders and may trigger further review or automated risk actions.

refund_rate.description:
Refund rate for the seller in the snapshot period, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.refund_rate` and measures how frequently orders or order items lead to refunds relative to the total number of eligible orders. It is commonly used in dashboards to identify sellers with unusually high refund behavior.

cancellation_rate.description:
Cancellation rate for the seller in the snapshot period, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

The metric reflects `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.cancellation_rate` and indicates how often orders are canceled before fulfillment relative to all relevant orders. Elevated cancellation rates can highlight catalog accuracy problems, pricing issues, or operational instability.

late_shipment_rate.description:
Late shipment rate computed for the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.late_shipment_rate` and measures the proportion of shipments that violated expected shipping SLAs, such as dispatch or delivery deadlines. It is a key signal for customer experience and logistics performance monitoring.

chargeback_rate.description:
Chargeback rate observed in the snapshot period, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

The value is taken from `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.chargeback_rate` and represents the ratio of orders that resulted in chargebacks to the total number of paid orders considered. High chargeback rates are strong fraud or risk indicators and often require governance attention.

average_rating.description:
Average product rating for the seller at this snapshot point.

This metric mirrors `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.average_rating` and is derived from customer reviews associated with the seller’s catalog. It usually follows a 1–5 scale, and should be interpreted together with `rating_count` to understand how robust the rating is statistically.

rating_count.description:
Number of individual ratings used to compute `average_rating`.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.rating_count` and indicates the sample size of reviews considered. Larger counts generally increase confidence in the average rating, while smaller counts highlight that the rating may still be volatile.

dispute_open_count.description:
Number of open disputes involving the seller at the snapshot time.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.dispute_open_count` and shows how many active dispute cases were associated with the seller when the snapshot was taken. Dashboards and risk consoles use this signal to prioritize follow‑up and case management actions.

tier.description:
Optional seller tier classification derived at the snapshot time.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.tier` and may contain values such as `new`, `standard`, `premium`, or `high_risk`, depending on configured business rules. A null value indicates that the seller has not been assigned a tier or that tiering was not applicable for this row.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the snapshot row was created in the database.

This value is taken from `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.created_at` and records when the analytics or reporting pipeline originally persisted the snapshot. It is useful for operational monitoring and for debugging data ingestion or recomputation processes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the snapshot row was last updated in the database.

This field mirrors `shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots.updated_at` and changes if metrics are recomputed, corrected, or enriched. Consumers can use it to detect refreshed data and to understand the recency of the KPIs for this snapshot row.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionPlan.ISum.description:
Summary DTO for a seller subscription plan offered on the shopping mall platform.

This type is used when embedding plan information inside other resources, such as seller subscription summaries, and in plan list views where detailed configuration is not required.

It exposes key identifying, pricing, and lifecycle fields from the underlying `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` model while omitting heavier configuration payloads and soft‑deletion details that are primarily relevant to deep configuration or compliance views.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the subscription plan.

This corresponds to the `id` primary key in `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` and is used for referencing and internal linking.

Client code can rely on this value when requesting detailed plan information or changing a seller’s subscription to another plan.

code.description:
Stable business code for the plan, such as `BASIC`, `STANDARD`, or `PREMIUM`.

This directly maps to the `code` column which is unique and used in configuration, integrations, and reporting.

Because it is stable over time, clients can safely persist this value for feature toggles or analytics without depending on numeric identifiers.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the plan.

The value is taken from the `name` column and is intended for display in seller portals and administrative consoles.

It should be localized or mapped to localized labels when building multi-language user interfaces.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of the features and benefits included in this plan.

This corresponds to the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` and can contain marketing copy or configuration notes that help sellers and admins understand the plan.

Client applications may show this text in plan detail views or tooltips, but list screens can safely treat it as optional and omit it when null.

billing_period.description:
Billing period identifier for the plan, for example `monthly` or `yearly`.

This is stored in the `billing_period` column and is treated as an application-level enum describing how often billing recurs.

Client applications may use this field to show subscription cadence and to group or filter plans by payment frequency.

currency.description:
ISO currency code in which the plan is billed.

This reflects the `currency` column and defines the currency for `price_amount` values for all subscriptions on this plan.

Typical examples include `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`, and clients should format monetary values accordingly.

price_amount.description:
Subscription fee amount per billing period for this plan.

This maps to the `price_amount` column and represents the base list price before any per-seller discounts are applied.

It is expressed in the plan’s currency and is typically rendered as a fixed-point monetary value in UIs.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the plan is currently active and available for new subscriptions.

This is taken from the `is_active` column. When false, the plan may still be associated with historical or continuing subscriptions but should not be presented as a selectable option to new sellers.

Admin tooling often uses this field to manage the lifecycle of subscription offerings without deleting historical records.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which the plan becomes effective for new subscriptions and pricing calculations.

This property reflects the non-nullable `effective_from` column in `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` and marks the moment when the plan configuration is considered active for business logic.

List and analytics views can use this value to filter or sort plans by introduction date, and to interpret historical subscription pricing in the context of when a plan first became available.

effective_until.description:
Timestamp after which the plan is no longer offered for new subscriptions, or null if the plan is open-ended.

This property corresponds to the nullable `effective_until` column in `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans`. When non-null, it marks the sunset point for selling this plan to new or upgrading sellers while leaving existing subscriptions unaffected according to business rules.

Client applications and reporting tools can use this field to hide sunset plans from standard selection UIs, while still preserving them for historical views and legacy subscriptions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription plan record was created.

This value comes from the non-nullable `created_at` column and represents when the plan definition was first inserted into the system.

It is useful for auditing, time-based analysis, and for administrative list screens that need to surface newly introduced plans near the top of the list.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the subscription plan record was last updated.

This property mirrors the non-nullable `updated_at` column and changes whenever the plan metadata is edited, for example when renaming the plan, adjusting pricing, or toggling activation flags.

Admin consoles and integration clients can use this field to detect recently modified plans, implement cache invalidation strategies, or display "last updated" information in configuration views.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscription.ISummary.description:
Summary analytics view of seller subscription activity, revenue, and discounts over a reporting period.

This DTO aggregates data primarily from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` together with their associated plans in `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` for a single seller or seller cohort.

It is designed for use in dashboards and admin tools where stakeholders need to understand subscription adoption, churn, and subscription‑based revenue without inspecting individual subscription rows.

seller.description:
Seller for whom subscription analytics are summarized.

For cohort or global analytics this field may be omitted or replaced by a synthetic summary record, but for single‑seller views it should contain the seller’s identity and profile context.

Using the summary variant avoids deep nesting and prevents circular references into other seller aggregates.

currency.description:
Currency code used for monetary aggregations in this summary.

The value is typically derived from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions.currency` and `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans.currency`, and should be an ISO 4217 code such as `USD` or `KRW`.

All monetary fields in this DTO, including recurring price and discount aggregates, are calculated in this currency.

period_start.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the reporting period over which subscription events and billing amounts are aggregated.

This timestamp is usually compared against `started_at`, `ended_at`, and `next_billing_at` fields in `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions`.

It enables clients to clearly label and audit which time window a particular analytics snapshot covers.

period_end.description:
Exclusive upper bound of the reporting period for subscription analytics.

The backend filters subscription events so that only those whose effective timestamps fall within `(period_start, period_end]` are considered in counts and monetary totals.

Using an exclusive upper bound supports back‑to‑back period queries without overlap.

total_active_subscriptions.description:
Number of subscriptions that were in an active status at the end of the reporting period.

This count is typically derived from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` rows whose `status` represents an active state (for example `active` or `past_due`) and where `deleted_at` is null.

It is a key KPI for tracking adoption of subscription‑based seller services.

total_new_subscriptions.description:
Total number of subscriptions that started within the reporting period.

The backend counts `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` rows whose `started_at` timestamps fall inside the reporting window.

This metric measures new subscription acquisition during the period.

total_cancelled_subscriptions.description:
Total number of subscriptions that transitioned into a terminal cancelled or expired state during the reporting period.

The backend typically counts `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` rows for which `ended_at` falls inside the reporting window and `status` matches a set of final states.

This metric is used to derive churn rates for seller subscription products.

total_recurring_price_amount.description:
Aggregate nominal recurring price amount for all relevant subscriptions during the reporting period, expressed in `currency`.

This is generally calculated from the `price_amount` field on `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions`, multiplied by the number of billing periods or billing events that occur in the window.

It reflects the gross recurring subscription price before discounts.

total_discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied to seller subscriptions during the reporting period, expressed in `currency`.

The backend computes this using the `discount_amount` field on `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` together with billing frequency, capturing both promotional and negotiated discounts.

This metric allows product and finance teams to gauge the cost of incentives and discounting strategies.

total_net_subscription_revenue_amount.description:
Net subscription revenue amount for the reporting period, expressed in `currency`.

This value is typically calculated as `total_recurring_price_amount - total_discount_amount`, optionally adjusted for refunds or proration rules.

It serves as the primary KPI for revenue generated from seller subscription plans.

status_breakdowns.description:
Breakdown of subscription counts and revenue contribution by current subscription status.

Each element groups together `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` rows that share the same `status` (for example `active`, `pending`, `past_due`, `cancelled`, or `expired`) within the reporting period filters.

Use this structure to render tables or charts that show how subscriptions are distributed and which states contribute most to subscription revenue.

plan_breakdowns.description:
Breakdown of subscription counts and revenue contribution by subscription plan.

Each element aggregates metrics for a specific plan from `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans`, including plan code, name, and the number of active or new subscriptions in the period.

This structure allows business stakeholders to compare the performance of different plans and to identify which tiers or offerings drive the most revenue.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeCharge.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a fee or commission charge applied to a seller account.

This DTO is optimized for list pages, statements, and reconciliation dashboards where many charge rows must be displayed efficiently with essential context.

It exposes identifiers, the fee type, descriptive text, monetary amounts, and effective date information from the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` model while omitting heavy relational objects and audit metadata.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the fee charge record.

This corresponds to the `id` primary key on `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` and is used when retrieving detailed charge information or linking to audit trails.

It primarily serves as an internal reference key rather than a user-facing value.

feeType.description:
Business category of the fee, such as `transaction_commission`, `platform_service_fee`, `subscription_fee`, `advertising_fee`, or `adjustment`.

This value maps directly to the `fee_type` column and is treated as an enum by business logic for classification, reporting, and filtering.

Clients can display localized labels based on this code and may group or color-code rows by fee category.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description explaining the origin or context of the fee.

This mirrors the nullable `description` column and may contain text such as order identifiers, campaign names, or admin notes.

When null, client applications should fall back to the fee type name or other structured context fields for display.

currency.description:
Currency code in which the fee amount is expressed.

The value comes from the `currency` column and determines the monetary unit for both `amount` and `taxAmount`.

Typical values are ISO currency codes such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW` that client applications use to format monetary values.

amount.description:
Fee amount applied to the seller, expressed in the given currency.

This reflects the `amount` column. Positive values represent charges that reduce the seller’s net earnings, while negative values may represent credits, fee reversals, or adjustments.

In financial statements, this field is usually shown as a signed monetary value with appropriate formatting.

taxAmount.description:
Tax portion associated with this fee, expressed in the same currency as `amount`.

This corresponds to the `tax_amount` column and is zero when no tax applies to the fee.

Reporting and invoice generation workflows can aggregate this field to compute total tax charged over a period.

isPlatformRevenue.description:
Indicates whether this fee contributes to platform revenue.

This maps to the `is_platform_revenue` column. When true, the fee amount is treated as revenue for the marketplace operator, and when false, the fee is a pass-through amount owed to third parties.

Analytics and financial reporting use this flag to separate platform margin from amounts collected on behalf of others.

effectiveDate.description:
Business-effective date and time for the fee charge.

This mirrors the `effective_date` column and is used as the primary date for reporting, revenue recognition, and time-based filtering.

While it may align with `created_at`, it is explicitly modeled to capture the business perspective of when the fee should be considered active.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.ISummary.description:
Summary analytics view of fee and commission charges applied to a single seller over a reporting period.

This DTO aggregates raw fee charge records from the `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` model into high‑level metrics that can be rendered in seller or admin dashboards without exposing individual charge rows.

It is intentionally read‑only and does not correspond directly to a single database row. Instead, it groups charges by business dimensions such as fee type and effective date range, while preserving currency context for correct financial interpretation.

Use this type in response payloads where the caller needs an at‑a‑glance overview of how much has been charged to the seller, how much of that is platform revenue, and what the net impact is for the selected time window.

seller.description:
Seller for whom the fee analytics are being summarized.

This object provides the high‑level identity and profile context of the seller so that the analytics response can be rendered without an additional lookup.

Use the summary variant to avoid deep nesting and to prevent circular references with other seller‑related aggregates.

currency.description:
Currency code in which all aggregated monetary fields of this summary are expressed.

The value must match the currency codes stored in `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges.currency` and is typically an ISO 4217 currency code such as `USD` or `KRW`.

All total and breakdown amounts below are calculated in this single currency context for consistency within a single summary object.

period_start.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the reporting period for which fee charges have been aggregated.

This timestamp is typically derived from the `effective_date` column on `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` and marks the first business date included in the calculation.

Clients can use this to label charts and to confirm which window of time is represented in the summary.

period_end.description:
Exclusive upper bound of the reporting period for which fee charges have been aggregated.

This timestamp typically corresponds to the logical end of the requested reporting range and is compared against the `effective_date` of fee charge records.

The `(period_start, period_end]` interval semantics should be applied consistently by the backend so clients can request adjacent periods without overlaps or gaps.

total_fee_amount.description:
Total absolute fee amount charged to the seller during the reporting period, expressed in the selected `currency`.

This value is the sum of `amount` across all `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` rows in the period, with positive amounts representing charges to the seller and negative amounts representing fee reversals or credits.

Use this metric to understand the overall monetary impact of all fee types combined.

total_tax_amount.description:
Total tax portion associated with seller fee charges in the reporting period, expressed in the same `currency`.

This is derived from summing the `tax_amount` column on `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` over the filtered set of rows.

It helps finance and tax reporting processes understand how much of the fee burden is attributable to tax obligations versus core platform fees.

total_platform_revenue_amount.description:
Total amount of fee charges that contribute to platform revenue for the selected seller and reporting period.

This amount is computed by summing `amount` for records where `is_platform_revenue` is true in `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`, using the same currency as the summary.

Business teams can use this field to track revenue performance by seller segment without exposing individual fee rows.

total_non_revenue_pass_through_amount.description:
Total amount of fee charges that are classified as non‑revenue pass‑through amounts during the reporting period.

This value sums `amount` for records where `is_platform_revenue` is false, such as third‑party handling charges collected on behalf of logistics providers.

Separating this from revenue fees supports accurate financial reporting and helps sellers reconcile why total charges may exceed platform revenue figures.

fee_type_breakdowns.description:
Per‑fee‑type breakdown of fee and tax amounts within the reporting period.

Each element groups together all fee charge records sharing a common `fee_type` value from `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges`, allowing clients to render stacked charts or detailed tables by fee category.

This structure gives sellers fine‑grained insight into which kinds of fees (for example transaction commissions or subscription fees) dominate their total charges.

daily_trends.description:
Time‑series breakdown of fee and tax amounts per business day within the reporting period.

The backend typically groups fee charge records by the date component of `effective_date` to build this series, enabling chart visualizations such as line graphs or bar charts for day‑over‑day trend analysis.

Clients can use this array to plot how fee charges and platform revenue evolve through the selected window, including the impact of campaigns, seasonality, or policy changes.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalyticsFeeTypeBr.description:
Aggregated view of fee and tax amounts for a single fee type within a seller fee analytics summary.

This DTO groups together all `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` rows for a seller that share the same `fee_type` during the selected period, capturing both charge and tax amounts in the common reporting currency.

It is used as an element inside `IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.ISummary.fee_type_breakdowns` to support detailed analysis by business fee category such as transaction commissions, platform service fees, subscription fees, advertising fees, or adjustments.

fee_type.description:
Business category of the fee that this breakdown row represents.

Values correspond directly to the `fee_type` column on `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` and may include categories like `transaction_commission`, `platform_service_fee`, `subscription_fee`, `advertising_fee`, or `adjustment`.

Clients should treat this as an opaque string enum driven by backend configuration and should not attempt to localize values without a separate mapping.

total_fee_amount.description:
Total fee amount for this fee type within the reporting period, expressed in the parent summary `currency`.

This value is calculated by summing the `amount` column across all fee charge records matching this `fee_type` and time window.

Positive values represent net charges to the seller, while negative values indicate net reversals or credits for this fee category.

total_tax_amount.description:
