Total tax portion for this fee type within the reporting period, expressed in the parent summary `currency`.

The backend computes this by summing `tax_amount` for all matching `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` rows.

This helps finance and compliance functions understand the tax contribution of each fee category separately.

platform_revenue_amount.description:
Total amount among this fee type that is recognized as platform revenue in the reporting period.

This typically sums `amount` for records of the given `fee_type` where `is_platform_revenue` is true.

It allows business stakeholders to understand which fee categories are the primary sources of revenue for the platform.

non_revenue_pass_through_amount.description:
Total amount among this fee type that is classified as pass‑through (non‑revenue) for the platform in the reporting period.

This amount is usually the portion of `amount` where `is_platform_revenue` is false, such as third‑party shipping or handling fees.

Separating this helps both sellers and finance teams reconcile gross charges versus platform revenue across fee categories.

IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalyticsDailyTren.description:
Daily trend line item for seller fee analytics, capturing aggregated fee and tax amounts for a single business date.

This DTO aggregates `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` records by the date portion of their `effective_date` for a specific seller and currency.

It is used as an element in `IShoppingMallSellerFeeAnalytics.ISummary.daily_trends` to support plotting day‑over‑day fee movements in dashboards and reports.

business_date.description:
Business date for which the fee and tax amounts have been aggregated.

This is typically derived from the date component of `effective_date` on `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` after applying the requested time zone normalization.

Each trend element in a summary should have a unique `business_date` within the reporting period.

total_fee_amount.description:
Total fee amount charged to the seller on this `business_date`, expressed in the parent summary `currency`.

The backend calculates this as the sum of `amount` across all fee charge records whose `effective_date` falls on this date.

This metric is suitable for plotting as a line or bar in time‑series visualizations.

total_tax_amount.description:
Total tax portion associated with seller fees on this `business_date`, expressed in the parent summary `currency`.

This is computed by summing `tax_amount` for all matching fee charge records.

It can be used to analyze the tax component of fee flows over time.

platform_revenue_amount.description:
Total amount of fee charges on this `business_date` that are recognized as platform revenue.

This aggregates `amount` from `shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges` for rows where `is_platform_revenue` is true and whose `effective_date` corresponds to `business_date`.

It enables granular revenue trend analysis at the daily level.

non_revenue_pass_through_amount.description:
Total amount of fee charges on this `business_date` that are classified as pass‑through (non‑revenue) for the platform.

This aggregates `amount` from rows where `is_platform_revenue` is false.

It helps separate third‑party cost flows from platform revenue when examining daily fee trends.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.description:
Aggregated subscription analytics for a single subscription status within a seller subscription analytics summary.

This DTO groups seller subscriptions from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` that share the same `status` value over the selected reporting period.

It is used inside `IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.ISummary.status_breakdowns` to provide a detailed view of how different states contribute to subscription volume and revenue.

status.description:
Subscription status represented by this breakdown row.

Values mirror those stored in `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions.status` and may include `pending`, `active`, `past_due`, `cancelled`, or `expired`.

Clients should treat this as an opaque string enum, using a separate mapping layer for localization or display names.

subscription_count.description:
Number of subscriptions currently or historically in this status within the reporting period, depending on the applied filters.

This may count subscriptions whose `status` equals this value at the end of the period or subscriptions that transitioned into this status during the window, based on the analytics query definition.

It is used to assess prevalence and flow between subscription lifecycle states.

recurring_price_amount.description:
Aggregate nominal recurring price amount associated with subscriptions in this status during the reporting period, expressed in the parent summary `currency`.

Typically derived from `price_amount` in `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions`, multiplied by the number of billing periods while the subscription is in this state.

This value helps distinguish revenue potential between active and non‑active statuses.

discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount granted to subscriptions in this status over the reporting period.

Based on `discount_amount` from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions`, this figure can reveal where discounts are concentrated across the lifecycle, such as during acquisition (`pending`) or retention (`past_due`).

Product and finance teams can use this metric to tune discount strategies per status segment.

net_revenue_amount.description:
Net subscription revenue amount for this status segment in the reporting period, expressed in the parent summary `currency`.

This is typically `recurring_price_amount - discount_amount`, optionally adjusted to account for refunds, prorations, or write‑offs specific to this status.

It enables analysis of which subscription states actually contribute to realized subscription revenue.

IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.description:
Aggregated subscription analytics for a single seller subscription plan within a subscription analytics summary.

This DTO combines metadata from `shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans` with aggregated counts and revenue metrics from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` that reference that plan.

It is used inside `IShoppingMallSellerSubscriptionAnalytics.ISummary.plan_breakdowns` to help compare plan‑level adoption, churn, and revenue performance.

plan.description:
Summary information about the subscription plan to which this breakdown row refers.

The embedded summary exposes stable identifiers such as plan code and user‑facing labels so that analytics UIs can show plan names without extra lookups.

Only the summary projection is included to keep the analytics response payload compact and avoid deep plan configuration nesting.

subscription_count.description:
Number of subscriptions linked to this plan that are included in the analytics time window.

Depending on the query semantics, this may count active subscriptions at period end, new subscriptions that started in the window, or all subscriptions that existed at any time during the period.

It is a primary indicator of adoption for the corresponding plan.

active_subscription_count.description:
Number of subscriptions for this plan that are in an active status at the end of the reporting period.

This count is typically derived from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` rows referencing this plan where `status` is considered active and `deleted_at` is null.

It is useful for understanding current revenue‑generating footprint per plan.

recurring_price_amount.description:
Aggregate nominal recurring price amount for all subscriptions on this plan during the reporting period, expressed in the analytics `currency`.

This metric is generally based on `price_amount` from `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` multiplied by billing occurrences falling in the window.

It contributes to the parent summary’s `total_recurring_price_amount` when summed across all plan breakdown rows.

discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount granted to subscriptions on this plan within the reporting period, expressed in the analytics `currency`.

It is derived from `discount_amount` on `shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions` and may include promotional, negotiated, or retention discounts.

Business teams can use this value to understand the effective discount rate and margin impact for each plan tier.

net_revenue_amount.description:
Net subscription revenue amount for this plan in the reporting period, expressed in the analytics `currency`.

It is typically computed as `recurring_price_amount - discount_amount`, optionally adjusting for refunds or prorations attributed to this plan.

When summed across all plan breakdown rows, this metric should align with the parent summary’s `total_net_subscription_revenue_amount` within rounding tolerances.

IShoppingMallInventoryAdjustmentReasonAn.description:
Summary metrics for a single standardized inventory adjustment reason within a larger analytics result.

The record aggregates how often a given reason code was used and how much stock it added or removed during a specific period. It is designed to be embedded inside higher‑level analytics DTOs rather than used as a standalone entity.

This summary helps sellers and admins understand which operational reasons, such as damage, shrinkage, or inbound receipts, contribute most to inventory movement.

reason.description:
Reference to the standardized inventory adjustment reason that this summary describes.

The reason summary exposes the business code and display name used across the platform while hiding internal management flags.

Linking to a reason summary allows UI layers to render consistent labels and tooltips alongside the aggregated metrics.

adjustmentCount.description:
Number of adjustment events that used this reason within the aggregation period.

This count indicates how frequently the reason is applied and serves as the primary frequency measure for ranking reasons in dashboards.

Sudden spikes in this count can highlight emerging operational problems or changes in business processes.

totalIncreaseQuantity.description:
Total quantity added to stock for all adjustment events using this reason in the period.

Only adjustments classified as increasing inventory are included in this sum. Typical examples include inbound shipments, corrections that add stock, or positive reconciliation differences.

Comparing this metric across reasons helps explain where additional stock originates.

totalDecreaseQuantity.description:
Total quantity removed from stock for all adjustment events using this reason in the period.

This metric focuses on adjustments that reduce inventory, such as damage, shrinkage, expiry, or corrective write‑offs.

Large decrease volumes for a particular reason may signal quality issues, process gaps, or fraud risk that require attention.

netQuantityChange.description:
Net quantity change for this reason, calculated as totalIncreaseQuantity minus totalDecreaseQuantity.

A positive value indicates that, on balance, this reason increased available stock, while a negative value indicates net removal.

The net metric enables quick interpretation of whether the reason primarily contributes to gains or losses in inventory.

IShoppingMallSkuInventoryAdjustmentAnaly.description:
Aggregated inventory adjustment analytics for a single SKU within a seller’s catalog over a given period.

This DTO condenses event‑level data into per‑SKU metrics, making it suitable for ranking SKUs by volatility or operational attention required. It does not map directly to a standalone Prisma table but is a computed projection.

The summary is typically embedded within seller‑level analytics responses and used to power drill‑down reports and SKU health indicators.

sku.description:
Summary reference to the SKU whose inventory adjustments are being analyzed.

The SKU summary includes key identification and catalog attributes necessary to display the product variant in analytics UIs without loading full product details.

Linking via a summary keeps payloads small while still providing enough context for users to understand which variant is affected.

adjustmentCount.description:
Total number of inventory adjustments recorded for this SKU within the aggregation period.

A higher count indicates more frequent manual or system‑initiated changes, which can highlight catalog items with unstable stock.

Merchants and admins can use this metric to prioritize which SKUs need process improvements or configuration changes.

totalIncreaseQuantity.description:
Total quantity increased for this SKU across all warehouses during the period.

Includes events such as inbound receipts, positive corrections, and returns to stock that are associated with the SKU.

The value helps explain how much supply entered the system for this specific variant.

totalDecreaseQuantity.description:
Total quantity decreased for this SKU across all warehouses during the period.

This includes damage, shrinkage, write‑offs, and other negative adjustments tied to the SKU.

High negative volumes, especially relative to sales, may indicate quality problems, theft, or mis‑configured processes.

netQuantityChange.description:
Net quantity change for the SKU during the period, calculated as totalIncreaseQuantity minus totalDecreaseQuantity.

Positive values signify net additions to stock, while negative values show net removals.

This metric is an important input when reconciling on‑hand quantities and explaining stock level changes over time.

IShoppingMallWarehouseInventoryAdjustmen.description:
Aggregated inventory adjustment metrics for a single seller warehouse over a specified period.

This DTO condenses adjustment data to the warehouse level, enabling dashboards and reports to rank locations by activity, volatility, or potential issues.

It is typically included inside seller‑centric analytics responses when multi‑warehouse operations are in use.

warehouse.description:
Summary reference to the seller warehouse whose inventory adjustments are being analyzed.

The warehouse summary provides enough metadata to identify the location in UIs, including code and name, without loading full address and configuration details.

Embedding the summary keeps analytics payloads compact while still supporting navigation to detailed warehouse pages.

adjustmentCount.description:
Number of inventory adjustment events recorded for this warehouse in the aggregation period.

This metric reflects how frequently staff or systems are modifying stock counts at the location.

High counts may indicate operational churn, frequent corrections, or high throughput of non‑order movements.

totalIncreaseQuantity.description:
Total quantity added to inventory at this warehouse during the period via adjustment events.

Includes positive corrections, inbound receipts, and other reasons that increase on‑hand stock at the location.

It helps explain how much new stock arrived or was reconciled into the warehouse.

totalDecreaseQuantity.description:
Total quantity removed from inventory at this warehouse during the period via adjustments.

Covers shrinkage, damage, write‑offs, and other negative adjustments that lower the available quantity.

Significant negative volumes may indicate process issues, local fraud risks, or environmental problems affecting goods.

netQuantityChange.description:
Net quantity change at this warehouse for the period, computed as totalIncreaseQuantity minus totalDecreaseQuantity.

Positive net values show that the warehouse ended with more stock than it started with due to adjustments, while negative values show net removal.

This is a key indicator when reconciling physical counts with system records and when reviewing warehouse‑level performance.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for an administrative role used by the shoppingMall platform’s RBAC system.

This representation is optimized for list views, selectors, and references inside other admin and governance entities. It captures the key identification and classification attributes while omitting deep configuration and audit metadata.

The summary enables management tools to display role catalogs, link admins to their assigned roles, and reason about which roles are system‑protected without transferring unnecessary detail.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin role.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the role record and is used when assigning roles to admin accounts and in audit logs.

Clients should treat it as an opaque identifier used solely for referencing the role in administrative operations.

code.description:
Stable, unique code for the role, for example "super_admin" or "operations_admin".

The code is machine‑oriented and is used in configuration, policy definitions, and sometimes in logs to refer to the role.

It should remain stable over time to preserve consistency of historical records and external integrations.

name.description:
Human‑readable display name for the administrative role.

This is the label shown in admin consoles, assignment dialogs, and reports so that operators can understand the purpose of each role.

Localized variants of the name can be layered on top of this base value at the presentation layer if needed.

isSystem.description:
Indicates whether this administrative role is system‑protected.

System roles are typically seeded by the platform and cannot be freely edited or deleted by ordinary admins to prevent accidental loss of critical access paths.

Management UIs and automation scripts can use this flag to enforce stricter modification rules and to visually distinguish built‑in roles from custom ones.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the role was created.

This value is useful when auditing RBAC configuration changes over time and when correlating role introductions with shifts in operational behavior.

The timestamp is represented as an ISO 8601 date‑time string with timezone information.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.ISummar.description:
Lightweight summary view of an admin role assignment within the shoppingMall platform.

This summary is intended for list views, audit overviews, and embedded references where only key identification, role context, and temporal information are required, without full assignment reasoning or deep relational expansion.

It reflects the underlying shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments Prisma model but exposes only the most relevant, non-sensitive fields for administrative UI and reporting scenarios.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin role assignment record.

This value corresponds directly to shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.id and is used to reference or inspect a specific assignment in detail views or audit tools.

admin.description:
Summary information of the admin account who holds this role assignment.

This object provides minimal identification and display fields for the assigned admin, instead of exposing the raw shopping_mall_admin_id foreign key, to make list views and logs more readable.

role.description:
Summary information of the administrative role granted to the admin.

This replaces the raw shopping_mall_admin_role_id foreign key and provides human-friendly role context such as code and name when rendering lists or audit trails.

granted_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who granted this role assignment.

This field mirrors shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.granted_by_admin_id and is kept as an ID-only reference because the granting admin is typically inspected only in deeper audit flows rather than in every summary list.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this role assignment was created.

The value is copied from shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.created_at and is used to understand when the role became effective for the admin, especially in audit and compliance views.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this role assignment record was last updated.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.updated_at and changes whenever assignment-related fields such as the associated role or justification are modified. It is useful for audit timelines, troubleshooting recent configuration changes, and determining the freshness of RBAC data in caches or replicated systems.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when this role assignment was revoked, if ever.

When null, the assignment is still considered active. When set, it reflects shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.deleted_at and is useful in historical role timeline inspections.

IShoppingMallAdminPermission.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a fine-grained administrative permission in the shoppingMall platform.

This summary is designed for use in permission catalogs, role configuration UIs, and audit reports where only the identifying code, human-readable label, and basic classification of the permission are required.

It maps directly to the shopping_mall_admin_permissions Prisma model while omitting metadata that is not essential for list and reference scenarios.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin permission record.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_admin_permissions.id and is primarily used internally or when referencing a specific permission in configuration or audit tools.

code.description:
Stable, unique machine-oriented code of the permission.

This field mirrors shopping_mall_admin_permissions.code and is the primary programmatic identifier used by RBAC evaluation and configuration (for example, "user.manage" or "seller.suspend").

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the permission.

The value reflects shopping_mall_admin_permissions.name and is intended for admin-facing configuration screens, reports, and documentation listings.

category.description:
Optional high-level category or module grouping for this permission.

When present, this field corresponds to shopping_mall_admin_permissions.category and is used to organize permissions in the UI (for example, "users", "orders", or "catalog"). When null, the permission is uncategorized.

is_system.description:
Flag indicating whether this permission is system-defined and protected from arbitrary modification.

This mirrors shopping_mall_admin_permissions.is_system and helps distinguish core platform permissions from custom or configurable ones in administrative tools.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this permission definition was created.

This value is taken from the shopping_mall_admin_permissions.created_at column and is used to understand when the permission was first introduced into the system. It supports governance reporting, troubleshooting rollout timelines, and reasoning about which roles could have referenced the permission at a given point in time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this permission definition was last modified.

The value corresponds to shopping_mall_admin_permissions.updated_at and changes whenever mutable attributes of the permission, such as name, description, or category, are adjusted. It is important for audit trails, synchronization processes, and detecting stale permission metadata in downstream services.

IShoppingMallAdminAuditLog.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an admin audit log entry in the shopping mall governance domain.

This summary type is optimized for list views, dashboards, and search results where many audit entries are displayed together and only the most important identifying fields are required.

It surfaces the core identifiers, actor information, target entity hints, and temporal context needed for admins to quickly scan and filter audit activity without loading full serialized snapshots.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin audit log entry.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.id` and is used as the stable reference when navigating to a detailed audit view or linking from other governance tools.

In list views it is typically not displayed to human users but is essential for API interactions and deep-linking.

action_type.description:
Machine-readable code representing the type of administrative action that was performed.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.action_type` and may contain codes such as `USER_STATUS_CHANGE`, `SELLER_APPROVAL`, or `PRODUCT_BLOCK` depending on business configuration.

Client applications use this field to categorize and filter audit entries and to drive localized, human-readable labels in the UI.

entity_type.description:
High-level classification of the business entity affected by the admin action.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.entity_type` and typically includes values like `customer`, `seller`, `product`, `order`, `refund_request`, or `dispute` according to governance rules.

It allows audit views to be filtered or grouped by domain, and combined with `entity_id` and `entity_display` provides quick context about the target of the action.

entity_id.description:
Identifier of the target business entity as stored in its own domain table, when available.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.entity_id` and is nullable for actions that do not target a single concrete record, such as configuration changes or platform-wide updates.

When present, API consumers may use this value to cross-link into the corresponding domain resource (for example, an order or customer detail page).

entity_display.description:
Human-friendly identifier or label for the target entity captured at the time of the admin action.

This property comes from `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.entity_display` and may contain values such as a customer email address, seller name, product title, or order code.

It is primarily used in list and search views to help admins understand which real-world object was affected without resolving additional references.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin account that performed the action when the event was human-initiated.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.shopping_mall_admin_id` and is nullable for system-triggered events or automated jobs that do not have a specific human actor.

Clients may use this value for filtering and joining, while the `admin` association provides the immediate contextual details needed in governance UIs.

admin.description:
Summary representation of the administrator who performed the action when it is human-initiated.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.shopping_mall_admin_id` and resolved against `shopping_mall_admins`. It exposes the minimal identity information (for example, name and email) required to understand who executed the change.

In audit log lists and dashboards, this field allows admins to see at a glance which administrator was responsible for an action without issuing additional API calls to fetch admin details.

ip.description:
Best-effort textual representation of the remote IP address from which the admin action was initiated.

This value is taken from `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.ip` and may be an IPv4 or IPv6 literal as recorded by the platform at the time of the request.

It is used in security investigations and anomaly detection to correlate admin activity with network locations or risk indicators.

message.description:
Short human-readable summary describing the admin action.

The value corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.message` and is intended for display in audit tables and filters so that admins can quickly understand the nature of the change.

While the exact phrasing is implementation-specific, it should remain concise and descriptive enough to be understood without loading full before/after snapshots.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this audit log entry was recorded in the system.

This field maps directly to `shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs.created_at` and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Audit list views typically sort by this field in descending order so that the most recent administrative actions appear first for review and monitoring.

IShoppingMallLegalHold.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a legal hold record for governance and compliance dashboards.

This summary type exposes the primary identifiers, status, and key temporal markers needed by admins and legal teams to scan, filter, and report on active or historical legal holds without loading the full detail for every record.

It focuses on fields that describe who created the hold, its current lifecycle state, when it was created or released, and how it should be referenced in external correspondence.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the legal hold record.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.id` and serves as the stable reference used when navigating to detail views, exporting for compliance archives, or integrating with external case management systems.

In most user interfaces it is kept internal while human-friendly codes and titles are shown instead.

code.description:
Stable business identifier or reference code assigned to the legal hold.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.code`, which is unique across all holds and is suitable for inclusion in external correspondence, legal documents, or internal tickets.

Admins and legal staff frequently search and filter holds using this code, making it a key display field in list views and reports.

title.description:
Short human-readable title describing the subject or purpose of the legal hold.

The value is taken from `shopping_mall_legal_holds.title` and should summarize the underlying case, investigation, or legal matter in a concise way.

In dashboards and tables this field is typically the primary label shown to users alongside the code and status.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the legal hold.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.status` and typically includes business-defined values such as `active`, `released`, or other states aligned with the organization’s legal hold policy.

Filtering and reporting on legal holds relies heavily on this field to distinguish currently effective holds from historical or superseded ones.

created_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who created the legal hold.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.created_by_admin_id` and references an entry in `shopping_mall_admins.id`.

It is used for governance reporting and audit trails to attribute responsibility for creating holds, while the `created_by_admin` association provides the immediate identity details needed in dashboards and case lists.

created_by_admin.description:
Summary representation of the administrator who created the legal hold.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_legal_holds.created_by_admin_id` and exposes the minimal identity information (for example, name and email) required for governance and compliance views.

In dashboards and search results, this field enables quick attribution of responsibility without additional API calls to fetch admin account details.

released_by_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the admin who formally released the legal hold, when applicable.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_by_admin_id` and is null for holds that are still active or have not yet been explicitly released.

Compliance and audit tooling use this field to determine which administrator authorized release and to support review of release decisions.

released_by_admin.description:
Summary representation of the administrator who released the legal hold, when a release has occurred.

This association is resolved from `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_by_admin_id` and remains null for active holds that have not been released.

Governance dashboards use this field to surface who authorized the release without requiring separate admin lookups.

effective_from.description:
Datetime from which the legal hold is considered effective according to business rules.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.effective_from` and may be null, in which case the hold is treated as effective from its creation time.

Reporting tools and legal review processes often use this field to determine which data and time periods are covered by the hold when evaluating retention obligations.

released_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the legal hold was officially released, if it has been released.

The value is taken from `shopping_mall_legal_holds.released_at` and is null for holds that remain active.

This field is important for demonstrating the duration of a hold and for calculating exposure windows in regulatory audits.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the legal hold record was originally created.

This maps directly to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.created_at` and is stored in ISO 8601 date-time format.

List views and compliance exports frequently sort or filter by creation date to understand the temporal distribution of legal holds across the platform.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the legal hold record.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_legal_holds.updated_at` and changes whenever status, descriptive fields, or admin references are modified.

It is useful for monitoring recent activity on holds and understanding when they were last reviewed or adjusted.

IShoppingMallRiskCase.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a risk or fraud case managed by governance and risk teams.

This DTO is designed for list screens, dashboards, and embedded references where a compact but informative representation of a risk case is required. It surfaces key identifiers, lifecycle status, severity, and primary subject context without loading full case narratives or timelines.

It maps directly to shopping_mall_risk_cases and is typically used as the item type in paginated risk case searches and in references from related admin tools such as legal holds, policy overrides, or admin notifications.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the risk case.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_risk_cases.id and uniquely identifies a single risk investigation or case record within the platform.

Use this identifier when navigating to detailed case views or linking from other governance objects.

case_code.description:
Stable code or reference identifier for the risk case, such as an internal case number.

This mirrors shopping_mall_risk_cases.case_code and is used in reporting, cross-system references, and operator communications.

The code is unique and is often more user-friendly than the raw UUID id for human workflows.

title.description:
Short summary title describing the risk case.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_risk_cases.title and should briefly capture the main suspicion, subject, or scenario being investigated.

It is commonly displayed in risk case lists, dashboards, and notification messages.

status.description:
Current status of the risk case, such as "open", "under_review", or "closed".

This mirrors shopping_mall_risk_cases.status and drives workflow behavior and SLA tracking in the risk management process.

Client applications should treat this as a business code and derive presentation labels from configuration rather than hard-coding assumptions.

severity.description:
Business-level severity classification for the case, such as "low", "medium", "high", or "critical".

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_risk_cases.severity and is used to prioritize handling, routing, and escalation.

UI components often use this value to apply visual emphasis or grouping in dashboards and work queues.

primary_subject_type.description:
Type of the primary subject of the risk case, for example "customer", "seller", "order", or "payment".

This field maps to shopping_mall_risk_cases.primary_subject_type and helps categorize the focus of the investigation for filtering and reporting.

It may be null when the case is systemic or not tied to a single primary subject.

primary_subject_id.description:
Identifier of the primary subject entity in its own domain table.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_risk_cases.primary_subject_id and, together with primary_subject_type, allows direct linking to the affected entity where appropriate.

It is nullable to support cases that do not reference a single specific subject.

primary_subject_display.description:
Human-readable identifier for the primary subject such as an email address, seller name, or order number.

This mirrors shopping_mall_risk_cases.primary_subject_display and is captured so that operators can quickly understand the subject without resolving IDs.

When null, UI components may display a generic placeholder or derive context from other fields.

sla_due_at.description:
Datetime by which the case should be handled according to SLA, if applicable.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_risk_cases.sla_due_at and is used to drive risk operations prioritization and SLA violation detection.

It may be null when no explicit SLA applies to the case type.

closed_at.description:
Timestamp when the risk case reached a terminal or closed status.

This mirrors shopping_mall_risk_cases.closed_at and is important for audit, reporting, and SLA compliance analysis.

It is null while the case is still open or under review.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the risk case was created.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_risk_cases.created_at and indicates when the investigation was first registered in the system.

It is commonly used in sorting, filtering, and aging analysis of cases.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the risk case was last updated.

This mirrors shopping_mall_risk_cases.updated_at and tracks the most recent modification to the case record, including status changes or metadata updates.

It is useful for identifying stale cases or monitoring ongoing activity.

IShoppingMallRiskCaseEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single risk case event in the shopping mall governance and risk system.

This summary DTO is designed for list views, timeline widgets, and embedded contexts where a concise representation of risk activity is required without the full event payload. It focuses on the core identifying fields, event classification, and minimal relational context.

The schema is mapped directly to the `shopping_mall_risk_case_events` Prisma model and exposes only non-sensitive, business-relevant fields suitable for read operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the risk case event.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_risk_case_events` table and is used to reference or drill down into a specific event when a full detail view is required.

risk_case_id.description:
Identifier of the risk case that this event belongs to.

This value matches `shopping_mall_risk_cases.id` and allows clients to correlate timeline events with their parent risk case entity in list and detail views.

The DTO intentionally uses the domain-oriented name `risk_case_id` instead of the raw database column name to avoid leaking table naming conventions into the API surface.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable type of the risk event.

Typical values include markers such as `created`, `status_changed`, `note_added`, or `rule_triggered`, and are used by clients to choose appropriate labels and icons in the case timeline UI.

from_status.description:
Previous status of the associated risk case when this event represents a status change.

When the event is not a status change, or when the case has no meaningful previous status, this field is null. When present, it reflects the value of the case `status` prior to the transition represented by this event.

to_status.description:
New status of the associated risk case when this event represents a status change.

For non-status-change events this value is null. When set, it matches the updated `status` of the parent risk case after the transition at the time this event was recorded.

related_entity_type.description:
Optional type of a related entity referenced by this event.

Examples include entity types such as order, payment, dispute, or other domain objects that were directly involved in, or triggered, the event. When there is no specific related entity, this field is null.

related_entity_id.description:
Identifier of the related domain entity when `related_entity_type` is set.

This value can be used by clients or backend services to navigate to the underlying order, payment, or other domain object associated with this risk event. It is null when the event is not tied to an external entity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this risk case event was recorded.

The value is stored as a precise UTC datetime in the `shopping_mall_risk_case_events` table and is used to sort and render the case timeline in chronological order.

IShoppingMallAdminNotification.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an admin notification item in the shopping mall governance system.

This summary DTO is optimized for list views and lightweight dashboard widgets where administrators need to quickly scan notifications without loading full bodies or heavy related collections.

It exposes the primary identifiers, basic categorization, status, priority, key timestamps, and an associated admin summary while omitting large text bodies or composition collections that are not required for list rendering.

The schema maps directly to the `shopping_mall_admin_notifications` Prisma model but includes only a carefully selected subset of its columns plus a transformed admin association for performance and clarity in summary responses.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin notification record.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.id` and is used by clients to reference or navigate to the detailed notification view or follow-up actions.

It is a server-generated UUID that remains stable for the lifetime of the notification, including when it is marked read or archived.

admin.description:
Summary information about the administrator to whom this notification is addressed.

This association is derived from `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.shopping_mall_admin_id` and exposes the target admin as a domain concept rather than a raw foreign key.

Clients can use the embedded admin summary to display who is responsible for the notification (for example, name or handle) and to navigate to admin-level views without performing additional lookup calls.

type.description:
Machine-readable type key describing the category of this notification.

Examples include values such as `seller_approval_needed`, `refund_escalation`, or `risk_sla_violation`, matching the business taxonomy defined for admin work queues.

API consumers should treat this as a stable programmatic discriminator for grouping, filtering and iconography rather than a human-facing label.

title.description:
Short title summarizing the notification content for list and badge displays.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.title` and is designed to be concise so that it fits within common list row or toast notification layouts.

Clients typically render this as the primary text for the notification entry without additional truncation logic, assuming the backend enforces reasonable length limits.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the notification from the admin perspective.

Typical values include `unread`, `read`, and `archived`, reflecting whether the admin has seen the item and whether it should appear in active queues.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.status` and is the primary attribute for filtering by inbox, processed items or archived history.

priority.description:
Business-level priority indicator for the notification.

Common values are `low`, `normal`, or `high`, and may be extended as the platform evolves to reflect additional severity or urgency levels.

It maps to `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.priority` and can be used by UI clients to highlight high-risk or time-sensitive items with distinct styling.

entity_type.description:
Optional polymorphic type name of the entity associated with this notification.

For example, values such as `seller`, `order`, `dispute`, or `risk_case` may appear depending on which part of the system triggered the notification.

This mirrors the `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.entity_type` column and allows generic clients to infer how to route deep links without hard-coding model-specific logic.

entity_id.description:
Identifier of the associated business entity, when present, used for deep linking.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.entity_id` and typically stores a UUID for the related record such as an order, seller, or risk case.

It is nullable to support purely informational notifications that are not bound to a specific entity; in those cases the value will be `null`.

entity_display.description:
Human-friendly label for the associated entity stored for quick reference.

This mirrors `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.entity_display` and might contain values such as a seller name, order number, or case code that are safe to surface in list rows.

It is nullable and may be omitted when the platform cannot safely or efficiently denormalize a display string for a particular notification type.

read_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin first marked or viewed this notification as read.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.read_at` and follows the ISO 8601 `date-time` format in UTC.

It is `null` while the notification remains unread, enabling clients to distinguish between unread and read states without relying solely on the `status` field.

archived_at.description:
Timestamp when the notification was archived or explicitly dismissed from active views.

The field corresponds to `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.archived_at` and uses an ISO 8601 `date-time` representation in UTC.

A `null` value indicates that the notification is still considered active and may appear in the admin's inbox or work queue, while a non-null value indicates archival for audit history or low-priority retention.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the notification record.

This field is taken directly from `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.created_at` and records when the system first generated the notification.

Clients commonly use it for sorting notifications by recency and for displaying relative times such as "5 minutes ago" in list views.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this notification record.

The value mirrors `shopping_mall_admin_notifications.updated_at` and is updated when mutable aspects such as status, priority or linked entities change.

In summary responses it allows consumers to detect when a notification has been modified since they last retrieved data without loading the full detail payload.

IShoppingMallOrderDailyStat.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing daily aggregated order and revenue statistics for the marketplace.

Each instance corresponds to a single row of the `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats` snapshot table and captures key metrics such as order counts, customer and seller participation, GMV, NMV and refund-related amounts.

This summary form is intended for analytics dashboards, reports, and monitoring views where the full set of snapshot fields is useful but no nested relations are required.

It is optimized for read-only analytical use: values are computed by batch jobs or pipelines and should be treated as immutable aggregates for the given calendar date.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the daily stats snapshot row.

This value directly maps to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.id` and is primarily used as a technical key for referencing the row in APIs.

Although the business grain is the `stats_date`, exposing the `id` allows clients to use stable identifiers when caching or linking to specific aggregates.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these statistics are calculated.

The value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.stats_date` and is expected to be normalized to midnight UTC, representing the entire business day.

Clients should treat the date component as the primary partitioning key when querying or charting time series, while ignoring the time-of-day component beyond its normalization semantics.

order_count.description:
Total number of successfully created orders on this date.

This maps to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.order_count` and includes all orders regardless of payment status or subsequent cancellation.

It is often used to understand gross order creation volume and to compare order funnel throughput across days.

paid_order_count.description:
Number of orders that reached a paid state on this date.

The value aligns with `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.paid_order_count` and typically counts orders whose payment authorization or capture succeeded.

Comparing this metric with `order_count` and `cancelled_order_count` helps business stakeholders understand payment conversion and drop-off patterns.

cancelled_order_count.description:
Number of orders that were cancelled on this date.

This field originates from `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.cancelled_order_count` and includes both customer-initiated and system-initiated cancellations.

It is a key indicator for operational issues or customer experience problems when monitored as a ratio of total orders or paid orders.

refunded_order_count.description:
Number of orders that had at least one refund completed on this date.

The value maps to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.refunded_order_count` and counts distinct orders rather than individual refund events.

It is used by finance and risk teams to monitor refund incidence and to correlate with other quality or fraud indicators.

gmv_amount.description:
Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) for orders associated with this date.

This metric corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.gmv_amount` and represents the total order value before refunds and cancellations, expressed in the platform base currency.

Business stakeholders typically use GMV as a headline growth KPI, often plotted together with NMV to understand the impact of cancellations and refunds.

nmv_amount.description:
Net Merchandise Value (NMV) for this date after accounting for cancellations and refunds.

The value mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.nmv_amount` and is also denominated in the platform base currency.

NMV provides a closer approximation of realized marketplace revenue and is frequently monitored alongside GMV to detect anomalies in refund or cancellation behavior.

item_count.description:
Total number of order line items across all orders created on this date.

This aggregates `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.item_count` and reflects basket size and product-level volume.

When divided by `order_count` it can be used to approximate average items per order, which is an important merchandising and cross-sell metric.

unique_customer_count.description:
Number of distinct customers who placed at least one order on this date.

The value maps to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.unique_customer_count` and counts unique customer identities rather than total orders.

It is a key input for understanding active customer base trends, daily purchasing cohorts, and retention dynamics.

unique_seller_count.description:
Number of distinct sellers who had at least one item included in orders created on this date.

This field mirrors `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.unique_seller_count` and captures marketplace breadth from the supply side.

Tracking this metric over time helps evaluate seller engagement, concentration risk, and the effectiveness of seller acquisition programs.

average_order_value.description:
Average order value (AOV) for this date.

The metric corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.average_order_value` and is typically derived as GMV divided by `paid_order_count` or another business-approved denominator.

It offers a concise indicator of customer basket value and is commonly used by marketing and merchandising teams to assess pricing and cross-sell strategies.

refund_amount.description:
Total amount refunded on this date across all orders.

This value is taken from `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.refund_amount` and represents the sum of refund transactions, expressed in the platform base currency.

Monitoring refund amounts relative to GMV and NMV is essential for quality assurance, fraud detection, and financial planning.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total value of chargebacks recorded on this date.

The field maps to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.chargeback_amount` and aggregates the financial impact of chargeback events in the base currency.

Chargeback levels are a critical risk and compliance KPI that card networks and payment providers often monitor closely, so surfacing this value in daily summaries is essential for governance.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

It corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.created_at` and indicates when the initial aggregation job produced the metrics for the given `stats_date`.

Clients may use it to distinguish between preliminary and finalized computations or to troubleshoot delayed pipeline runs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot row was last recomputed or corrected.

This field reflects `shopping_mall_order_daily_stats.updated_at` and is updated whenever the analytics process reruns for the same `stats_date`, for example to incorporate late-arriving events or corrections.

Consumers who cache or export metrics can use this timestamp to detect when previously retrieved aggregates might need to be refreshed.

IShoppingMallCampaignMetric.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of campaign performance metrics for a specific marketing or pricing campaign on a particular date.

This summary DTO is optimized for list views, dashboards, and report tables where many campaign rows are displayed together, and only key figures are needed instead of the full underlying analytics record.

Each instance represents one snapshot row from the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` table, preserving the business meaning of the original Prisma model while reducing the field set to the most important KPIs for monitoring campaign effectiveness.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this campaign metrics snapshot row.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_campaign_metrics` table and is used to uniquely reference a specific metrics record when navigating to detail views or exporting data.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these campaign metrics were calculated in the analytics pipeline.

Although only the date portion is logically significant, the value is stored as a `datetime` and typically normalized to midnight UTC to maintain consistency across reporting processes and queries.

campaign_code.description:
Business identifier of the campaign for which metrics were aggregated on `stats_date`.

This value usually corresponds to a voucher code, campaign ID, or other promotion key defined in the business configuration layer. It is part of a unique constraint with `stats_date` in the underlying Prisma model.

order_count.description:
Total number of orders on `stats_date` that were affected by this campaign.

This count includes both paid and unpaid orders where the campaign logic was applied during pricing or promotion calculation.

paid_order_count.description:
Number of campaign-affected orders on `stats_date` that reached a paid state.

This metric helps distinguish overall campaign reach from orders that successfully converted into completed payments.

gmv_amount.description:
Gross merchandise value (GMV) attributable to this campaign on `stats_date` before refunds and cancellations.

The value is recorded in the platform base currency and reflects the full merchandise value influenced by this campaign regardless of who funded any discounts.

nmv_amount.description:
Net merchandise value (NMV) attributable to this campaign on `stats_date` after applying refunds or cancellations.

This figure is calculated in the platform base currency and is useful for understanding campaign performance after post-order adjustments.

discount_total_amount.description:
Total discount amount granted under this campaign on `stats_date`.

This amount includes every discount applied when the campaign was active, without differentiating between platform-funded and seller-funded portions.

platform_funded_discount_amount.description:
Subset of `discount_total_amount` representing the discount value funded directly by the platform on `stats_date`.

This metric is necessary for internal cost analysis, as it expresses how much the platform invested in subsidizing this campaign.

seller_funded_discount_amount.description:
Subset of `discount_total_amount` representing the discount value funded by sellers on `stats_date`.

It is used to evaluate the seller contribution to campaign incentives and for sharing the cost of promotions between the marketplace and participating sellers.

new_customer_order_count.description:
Number of paid orders under this campaign on `stats_date` created by customers categorized as "new" according to campaign attribution rules.

This metric is a key indicator for acquisition performance, showing how effectively the campaign drives first-time purchases and onboarding of new customers.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this campaign metrics row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

It reflects when the metrics for the corresponding `stats_date` and `campaign_code` were initially materialized, which is useful for auditing and pipeline monitoring.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this campaign metrics row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

This field is updated whenever the analytics job reprocesses data for the same `stats_date` and `campaign_code`, for example after late-arriving events, data corrections, or backfill operations.

IShoppingMallPlatformKpiSnapshot.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a platform-level KPI snapshot over a defined reporting period.

This DTO is tailored for dashboards, timeline charts, and list views where multiple KPI points are shown together. It surfaces the most important marketplace health indicators from the `shopping_mall_platform_kpi_snapshots` table without exposing every possible analytical field in full detail.

Each instance corresponds to a single row in the KPI snapshot table, covering a period identified by `period_type`, `period_start`, and `period_end`, and provides GMV, NMV, revenue, take rate, order counts, participant activity, and refund and chargeback statistics.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this platform KPI snapshot row.

This primary key is used to reference a specific snapshot for detailed inspection, export, or correlation with other reporting artifacts.

period_type.description:
Type of reporting period covered by this KPI snapshot.

Typical values include logical periods such as "day", "week", "month", or business-specific labels like "custom". The combination of `period_type`, `period_start`, and `period_end` is unique and defines how the time window should be interpreted in reporting tools.

period_start.description:
Inclusive start timestamp of the reporting period that this KPI snapshot summarizes.

All events and transactions counted in this snapshot occur at or after this timestamp, forming the lower bound of the time window for the aggregated metrics.

period_end.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the reporting period that this KPI snapshot summarizes.

All events and transactions included in this snapshot occur before this timestamp, forming the upper bound of the time window used for aggregations.

gmv_amount.description:
Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) aggregated over the reporting period before refunds and cancellations.

The value is expressed in the platform base currency and serves as a top-of-funnel indicator of transaction volume and demand during the snapshot window.

nmv_amount.description:
Net Merchandise Value (NMV) for the reporting period after applying refunds and cancellations.

This metric is calculated in the platform base currency and provides a corrected view of actual merchandise value retained by the marketplace over the time window.

platform_revenue_amount.description:
Total platform revenue recognized during the reporting period.

This includes commissions, platform-owned fees, subscriptions, advertising fees, and other revenue streams, net of adjustments, all calculated in the platform base currency.

take_rate.description:
Platform take rate for the reporting period, typically computed as `platform_revenue_amount` divided by `gmv_amount`.

This ratio is a key business KPI indicating the efficiency of the business model and the share of GMV captured as revenue by the marketplace.

order_count.description:
Number of successfully created orders within the reporting period.

This metric counts all order headers that reached a created state, regardless of subsequent payment or fulfillment status, and is useful for tracking demand and conversion from cart to order.

paid_order_count.description:
Number of orders that reached a paid state within the reporting period.

This measure is more conservative than `order_count` and reflects orders that successfully completed payment, which is crucial for revenue and cash-flow analysis.

active_customer_count.description:
Number of active customers during the reporting period according to configured activity criteria.

Activity criteria typically include conditions such as at least one session, order, or other interaction, and this count is used to track customer engagement and retention trends.

new_customer_count.description:
Number of newly registered customers during the reporting period.

This is a core acquisition metric, highlighting how many fresh customer accounts joined the marketplace within the defined time window.

active_seller_count.description:
Number of active sellers during the reporting period based on seller activity rules.

Activity is usually defined via paid orders or similar thresholds, and this metric helps evaluate the vibrancy of the seller ecosystem on the platform.

refund_request_count.description:
Total number of refund requests created during the reporting period.

This metric tracks how often customers, sellers, or admins initiated refunds, serving as an early indicator of potential quality or satisfaction issues.

approved_refund_count.description:
Number of refund requests approved during the reporting period.

Combined with `refund_request_count`, this value is used to derive approval ratios and to monitor how many cases result in actual refunds.

refunded_amount.description:
Total monetary value refunded during the reporting period in the platform base currency.

This amount covers all approved refund operations and is essential for understanding the net impact of refunds on NMV and platform revenue.

chargeback_count.description:
Number of chargeback cases recorded during the reporting period.

Chargebacks typically arise from disputes raised with payment providers and are a key risk and fraud indicator in the payment lifecycle.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total value of chargebacks recorded during the reporting period, expressed in the platform base currency.

This metric quantifies the financial impact of chargebacks and is used alongside `chargeback_count` for risk and payment performance analysis.

average_order_value.description:
Average order value (AOV) for the reporting period.

This metric is usually computed as GMV divided by `paid_order_count` and provides insight into purchasing behavior and the effectiveness of merchandising and pricing strategies.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this platform KPI snapshot row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

It indicates when the aggregation job first materialized the metrics for the associated period, which is important for operational monitoring and debugging of reporting jobs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this platform KPI snapshot row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

This value changes when the system reprocesses or backfills data for the same period, allowing consumers to detect late updates or revisions to historical KPI figures.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodStat.ISummary.description:
Summary view of daily payment method performance statistics for the shopping mall platform.

This summary DTO represents a compact projection of the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` snapshot model that is optimized for list views, dashboards, and lightweight analytics queries rather than full detailed inspection.

Each instance aggregates payment activity for a specific payment method and calendar date, enabling monitoring of success rates, failure patterns, and monetary impact per method without transferring the full underlying snapshot row.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this payment method stats snapshot row.

The value corresponds to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` model and is represented as a UUID string.

It is primarily used for internal reference, troubleshooting and direct navigation to detailed views of a specific stats record.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these payment method metrics were calculated.

The value corresponds to the `stats_date` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` model and is typically normalized to midnight UTC for consistency across the analytics pipeline.

Clients should treat the date component as the business date of aggregation rather than a specific event timestamp.

payment_method_code.description:
Stable business code that identifies the payment method represented by this summary row.

This field comes from the `payment_method_code` column in `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` and may contain values like `card`, `bank_transfer`, or more provider-specific identifiers.

It is used as the primary grouping and filtering key when building dashboards and reports per payment method.

payment_attempt_count.description:
Total number of payment attempts initiated using this method on the given stats date.

The value maps to `payment_attempt_count` in the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` table and counts all attempts regardless of final outcome.

It is commonly used together with success and failure counts to derive success rates and to understand volume distribution across payment methods.

payment_success_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that completed successfully (paid) using this method on the stats date.

This is sourced from the `payment_success_count` column and represents attempts that reached a terminal successful state.

It is useful for computing conversion rates, revenue contribution, and for comparing the effectiveness of different payment methods.

payment_failure_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that definitively failed or were declined using this method on the stats date.

The value is stored in `payment_failure_count` in the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` model and includes cases where the payment provider or issuer rejected the attempt.

High failure counts may indicate integration issues, risk policies, or card issuer behavior that requires further investigation.

payment_expired_count.description:
Number of payment attempts using this method that expired without a final success or failure outcome on the stats date.

This corresponds to the `payment_expired_count` column and typically includes attempts that timed out due to user abandonment or provider time limits.

Operations teams use this metric to identify friction in payment flows and to optimize retry or reminder strategies.

paid_gmv_amount.description:
Gross merchandise value (GMV) processed successfully via this payment method on the stats date, expressed in the platform base currency.

The value comes from `paid_gmv_amount` in the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` table and aggregates the monetary amount of successfully paid orders.

It is a key metric for understanding revenue distribution by payment method and for financial reconciliation dashboards.

refunded_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded for payments that used this method on the stats date, in the platform base currency.

This maps to the `refunded_amount` column and includes both partial and full refunds that were processed for payments associated with this payment method.

It helps finance, operations, and risk teams assess the refund burden and post-transaction risk profile of different methods.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total amount of chargebacks related to this payment method on the stats date, represented in the platform base currency.

The value is stored in the `chargeback_amount` column and typically reflects disputed card transactions or similar chargeback flows handled by acquirers.

Monitoring this metric per payment method is important for fraud management, cost control, and negotiating terms with payment providers.

IShoppingMallShippingPerformanceStat.ISu.description:
Summary view of daily shipping and delivery performance metrics for the shopping mall platform.

This DTO provides a concise projection of the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` snapshot model focused on key operational KPIs that are suitable for dashboards, list endpoints, and lightweight analytics.

Each instance aggregates shipment activity for a specific shipping method code and calendar date, enabling teams to monitor fulfillment speed, on-time delivery performance, and failure patterns without transferring the entire snapshot record.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this shipping performance stats snapshot row.

The value corresponds to the primary key `id` on the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` model and is represented as a UUID string.

It is useful for internal linking, drill-down navigation, and troubleshooting specific stats rows in back-office tooling.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these shipping performance metrics were calculated.

The value reflects the `stats_date` column on `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` and is typically normalized to midnight UTC for consistency in analytics.

Clients should interpret the date component as the business aggregation date rather than a specific shipment event timestamp.

shipping_method_code.description:
Business code that identifies the shipping method or carrier/service combination associated with this summary row.

This property is sourced from `shipping_method_code` in the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` table and may represent values such as `standard`, `express`, or specific carrier service identifiers.

It is the primary key used for grouping and filtering metrics by shipping configuration in dashboards and monitoring views.

shipment_created_count.description:
Number of shipments created on the stats date using this shipping method.

This value maps to `shipment_created_count` in the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` model and counts newly created shipment records, regardless of their later lifecycle outcomes.

It is typically used to understand overall shipping volume and to correlate with order creation and fulfillment capacity.

shipment_shipped_count.description:
Number of shipments that transitioned into a shipped state on the stats date for this method.

The value corresponds to `shipment_shipped_count` in the shipping performance stats table and represents shipments that have been handed over to the carrier or moved out of the warehouse.

Comparing shipped counts against created counts helps operations teams evaluate fulfillment throughput and potential backlog.

shipment_delivered_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as delivered on the stats date using this shipping method.

This property is backed by the `shipment_delivered_count` column and captures successful delivery confirmations recorded in tracking events.

It is a core indicator of actual delivery volume and is used alongside delivery failure and return metrics to assess service quality.

shipment_delivery_failed_count.description:
Number of shipments that entered a delivery failed state on the stats date for this method.

The value originates from `shipment_delivery_failed_count` and includes shipments that could not be delivered successfully due to address issues, recipient unavailability, or carrier failures.

Monitoring this metric over time helps logistics and support teams identify problem patterns and improve delivery reliability.

shipment_returned_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as returned to sender on the stats date for this method.

This maps to `shipment_returned_count` in the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` model and represents shipments that completed a return-to-sender flow after dispatch.

High return counts may indicate address quality issues, customer refusal rates, or misconfigured shipping promises that require investigation.

median_fulfillment_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from order payment confirmation to shipment handover for shipments associated with this method on the stats date.

The value is computed into the `median_fulfillment_time_hours` column and summarizes the central tendency of fulfillment cycle durations for the given date and method.

It is used by operations and warehouse teams to monitor and optimize internal picking, packing, and handover efficiency.

median_transit_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from shipment handover to delivery confirmation for shipments using this method delivered on the stats date.

This property corresponds to `median_transit_time_hours` in the `shopping_mall_shipping_performance_stats` table and summarizes typical transit time experienced by customers.

Logistics and carrier management teams rely on this metric to evaluate carrier performance, SLA adherence, and the impact of route or service changes.

on_time_delivery_rate.description:
Proportion of shipments delivered on or before their expected delivery threshold for this shipping method on the stats date, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

The value is stored in `on_time_delivery_rate` on the shipping performance stats model and is generally calculated as on-time deliveries divided by total delivered shipments.

It is a key KPI for service quality monitoring, SLA management, and customer satisfaction analysis.

IShoppingMallRefundAndDisputeStat.ISumma.description:
Summary view of daily refund and dispute statistics for the shopping mall analytics domain.

This summary DTO represents a single aggregated snapshot row from the `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats` table, focused on the key metrics that business, operations, and risk stakeholders typically monitor on dashboards and list views.

It is optimized for read-only reporting scenarios and omits internal implementation details while preserving all important numeric indicators from the underlying Prisma model.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this refund and dispute statistics snapshot row.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.id` and is generated by the analytics pipeline or database layer. It is used as a stable primary key when referencing or caching this summary record.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these refund and dispute metrics are calculated.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.stats_date`. Although modeled as a full datetime for compatibility, the time component SHOULD be normalized to midnight UTC so that each row represents exactly one calendar day.

refund_request_count.description:
Total number of refund requests that were created on this reporting date.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.refund_request_count` and counts newly opened refund cases, regardless of when they are ultimately resolved.

approved_refund_request_count.description:
Number of refund requests that reached an approved decision on this date.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.approved_refund_request_count` and includes approvals for requests that may have been opened on earlier dates.

rejected_refund_request_count.description:
Number of refund requests that were rejected on this date.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.rejected_refund_request_count` and includes all requests for which a final rejection decision was recorded during the reporting day.

refunded_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded on this date in the platform base currency.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.refunded_amount` and aggregates completed payment refund operations, not just approvals, to reflect real financial impact.

partial_refund_count.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that were partial relative to the original item or order amount.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.partial_refund_count` and helps distinguish partial compensation scenarios from full refunds.

full_refund_count.description:
Number of refund operations on this date that fully refunded the related items or orders.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.full_refund_count` and indicates how many cases resulted in a complete reimbursement outcome.

dispute_opened_count.description:
Number of disputes created on this reporting date.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_opened_count` and includes all high-severity conflicts that were newly opened, regardless of their eventual resolution.

dispute_resolved_count.description:
Number of disputes that were resolved on this date.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_resolved_count` and counts all disputes that transitioned into a terminal resolution state during the reporting day.

dispute_resolved_for_customer_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the customer on this date.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_resolved_for_customer_count` and indicates how many dispute outcomes benefitted the customer side from a decision-making perspective.

dispute_resolved_for_seller_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved in favor of the seller on this date.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.dispute_resolved_for_seller_count` and tracks dispute outcomes where the seller position was upheld.

average_refund_resolution_time_hours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between refund request creation and final decision (approved or rejected) for cases resolved on this date.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.average_refund_resolution_time_hours` and provides an operational KPI for refund handling speed.

average_dispute_resolution_time_hours.description:
Average elapsed time in hours between dispute creation and resolution for disputes resolved on this date.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.average_dispute_resolution_time_hours` and serves as a key KPI for dispute lifecycle efficiency and SLA adherence.
