created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund and dispute statistics row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.created_at` and is generally set once when the snapshot is initially generated.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund and dispute statistics row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_and_dispute_stats.updated_at` and is updated whenever the underlying aggregation is recalculated or backfilled.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethodPerformanceByD.description:
Daily performance metrics for a single payment method on the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents an aggregated analytics snapshot built from the `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats` table and is intended for reporting endpoints that display payment behavior and health over time, broken down by payment method.

It exposes key volume, success, and loss indicators that operations, finance, and risk teams monitor when evaluating payment provider quality and user payment behavior.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this payment method statistics snapshot row.

This property maps directly to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.id` and acts as the primary key for referencing and caching the aggregated record.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these payment method metrics are calculated.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.stats_date`. The time component SHOULD be normalized to midnight UTC so that each row clearly represents a single calendar day of activity.

payment_method_code.description:
Stable business code identifying the payment method to which these metrics belong.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_method_code` and typically holds values such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or provider-specific identifiers as configured in payment settings.

payment_attempt_count.description:
Number of payment attempts initiated using this payment method on the reporting date.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_attempt_count` and includes all attempts regardless of final success, failure, or expiry.

payment_success_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that completed successfully using this payment method on the reporting date.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_success_count` and is used together with attempt count to derive success rate KPIs.

payment_failure_count.description:
Number of payment attempts that definitively failed or were declined using this payment method on the reporting date.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_failure_count` and covers hard failures and explicit declines, excluding mere expirations.

payment_expired_count.description:
Number of payment attempts using this payment method that expired without a final success or failure outcome by the configured timeout rules on the reporting date.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.payment_expired_count` and helps track abandoned, timed-out, or incomplete payment flows.

paid_gmv_amount.description:
Gross merchandise value (GMV) associated with successful payments using this method on the reporting date, in the platform base currency.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.paid_gmv_amount` and is a primary indicator of revenue volume driven by this payment instrument.

refunded_amount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded for payments that used this payment method on the reporting date, in the platform base currency.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.refunded_amount` and measures the volume of post-payment reversals associated with the method.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total monetary amount of chargebacks related to this payment method on the reporting date, in the platform base currency.

This maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.chargeback_amount` and serves as a key risk and loss metric when evaluating the payment instrument.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment method statistics row was first created by the analytics pipeline.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.created_at` and is populated when the snapshot is initially generated.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment method statistics row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_payment_method_stats.updated_at` and is updated whenever the underlying aggregates are recalculated or backfilled.

IShoppingMallShippingPerformanceByDay.description:
Daily aggregated shipping and delivery performance metrics per shipping method.

This type represents a denormalized metrics row computed by analytics pipelines from underlying shipment and tracking data. Each instance captures counts and time-based KPIs for a single calendar date and a specific shipping method code, or aggregate method grouping, within the shopping mall platform.

These statistics are used by operations, logistics, and business intelligence stakeholders to monitor fulfillment quality, detect degradation in carrier performance, and support capacity planning and SLA monitoring.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this shipping performance snapshot row.

This UUID is generated by the analytics pipeline when inserting or recomputing the stats row. It is used as the primary key reference when debugging or correlating this row with internal processing logs.

stats_date.description:
Calendar date for which these shipping performance metrics are calculated.

The time component SHOULD be normalized to midnight UTC for consistency across the analytics pipeline. Consumers should treat this as a date bucket representing all shipment activity that occurred on that day rather than a precise timestamp of any single event.

shipping_method_code.description:
Business code identifying the shipping method or carrier/service combination used for aggregation.

This value can represent concrete carrier products (for example, `CJ-EXPRESS`, `FEDEX-GROUND`) or logical groupings (for example, `standard`, `express`). It is the primary semantic key for grouping and comparing shipping performance across days.

shipment_created_count.description:
Number of shipments that were created on this date using this shipping method.

This count increments when new shipment records are instantiated from orders or fulfillment actions. It is useful to understand daily shipment volume and to compare against shipped and delivered counts for the same period.

shipment_shipped_count.description:
Number of shipments that transitioned into a shipped state on this date for this method.

This metric measures how many shipments were handed over to the carrier or otherwise marked as shipped in the fulfillment workflow. It can diverge from `shipment_created_count` depending on handling delays and backlogs.

shipment_delivered_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as delivered on this date for this shipping method.

This metric is based on delivery confirmation events and is used to derive fulfillment and transit performance statistics, such as total throughput and delivery success rates.

shipment_delivery_failed_count.description:
Number of shipments that entered a delivery failed state on this date for this method.

Delivery failures include events such as address issues, recipient unavailable, or carrier-specific failure codes that prevent successful delivery. High values can indicate carrier problems, data quality issues, or fraud-related patterns.

shipment_returned_count.description:
Number of shipments that were marked as returned to sender on this date for this shipping method.

Return events usually follow delivery failures, customer refusals, or logistics routing problems. Operations teams can use this metric to track reverse logistics load and quality problems per carrier or shipping product.

median_fulfillment_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from order payment confirmation to shipment handover for shipments in this bucket.

The fulfillment time measures how quickly the seller or warehouse operations convert paid orders into outbound shipments. This value is computed as a median across all relevant shipments on the date, which reduces sensitivity to extreme outliers and provides a robust central tendency indicator.

median_transit_time_hours.description:
Median time in hours from shipment handover to delivery confirmation for shipments using this method delivered on this date.

Transit time captures carrier performance between pickup and final delivery. As a median value, it summarizes the typical customer experience while ignoring a small number of unusually slow or fast deliveries that would skew an average.

on_time_delivery_rate.description:
Proportion of shipments delivered on or before their expected delivery deadline, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

This rate is calculated for the specified date and shipping method based on configured SLA thresholds or carrier promises. A value of `1` indicates that all deliveries met the on-time criteria, while `0` means none of the deliveries satisfied the SLA.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping performance stats row was initially created by the analytics pipeline.

This value is managed solely by the backend aggregation process and is not editable through API requests. It allows operators to understand when the snapshot was first generated.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipping performance stats row was last recomputed or corrected by the analytics pipeline.

Recomputation can happen when late events arrive, corrections are applied, or the aggregation logic changes. Consumers can use this field to detect stale or recently refreshed statistics.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessAnalytics..description:
High-level summary metrics about review helpfulness across the entire result set.

This summary object captures top-level KPIs such as the total number of reviews considered, the total counts of helpful and not-helpful votes, and an overall helpfulness ratio. It is designed for use in admin dashboards and analytics tiles to give a quick sense of how useful customers perceive review content within the selected filters and time window.

Although derived from the same underlying tables as the detailed buckets, this type is intentionally compact and does not expose per-review or per-entity breakdowns, focusing instead on aggregate signals.

totalReviews.description:
Total number of distinct reviews included in the helpfulness analytics for the current filter set.

This count corresponds to review rows aggregated from shopping_mall_reviews that have at least one helpfulness-related signal in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes or that otherwise match the query criteria.

totalHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of helpful votes (is_helpful = true) across all reviews in the analytics result set.

This is computed by summing the number of helpful vote records in shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes that match the current filters and time window.

totalNotHelpfulVotes.description:
Total number of not-helpful votes (is_helpful = false) across all reviews in the analytics result set.

This count is derived from shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes and complements totalHelpfulVotes for understanding net sentiment about review usefulness.

overallHelpfulnessRatio.description:
Overall helpfulness ratio across the result set, typically computed as totalHelpfulVotes divided by (totalHelpfulVotes + totalNotHelpfulVotes).

This metric provides a coarse signal about whether reviews in the filtered scope are generally perceived as helpful by customers.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceByDayStati.description:
Filter context describing which sellers were included when computing seller performance by day statistics.

This object echoes back the seller-scoping information supplied by the caller (for example, a specific seller identifier) so that consumers can clearly understand and display the scope of the analytics window represented by the response.

sellerId.description: Identifier of a specific seller whose performance was explicitly requested. When present, all metric rows in the response belong to this seller; when absent, the response may include multiple sellers according to the applied filters and platform defaults.

IPageIShoppingMallPaymentStatusHistory.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusHistory.IReque.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating payment status history rows for a specific logical order payment.

This type is used as the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/payments/{orderPaymentId}/statusHistories endpoint. It encapsulates filtering, sorting, and pagination options that are applied when reading from the shopping_mall_payment_status_histories table in conjunction with the parent shopping_mall_order_payments record.

Clients use this contract to narrow results by time range, status codes, and other criteria, and to control page size and sort ordering when inspecting the lifecycle of a payment.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which page of results to return.

This value works together with the pageSize field to select a window over the ordered result set of shopping_mall_payment_status_histories rows for the given order payment. When omitted, the backend may assume page 1 as a default.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of history rows to include in a single page of results.

This value controls the size of the data array in the IPageIShoppingMallOrderPaymentStatusHistory response. Implementations typically enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets for a single request.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the created_at timestamp filter.

When provided, only history rows whose created_at is greater than or equal to this value will be included. When null or omitted, there is no lower time bound and the query may consider all past rows for the scoped order payment.

toCreatedAt.description:
Exclusive upper bound for the created_at timestamp filter.

When provided, only history rows whose created_at is strictly less than this value will be included. When null or omitted, there is no upper time bound and the query may consider all rows up to the current time.

items.description:
A business status value recorded in shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.new_business_status, such as "pending", "paid", "partially_refunded", "refunded", "chargeback", or other configured codes.

Filtering by this value allows callers to focus on specific types of lifecycle transitions when reviewing payment history for a given logical payment.

businessStatuses.description:
Optional filter limiting results to history rows whose new_business_status field is one of the provided values.

When this array is provided and non-empty, only rows with matching new_business_status values are returned. When omitted or empty, the query does not restrict histories by business_status.

items.description:
A provider-specific status code value recorded in shopping_mall_payment_status_histories.new_provider_status_code.

These codes represent gateway or processor states and can be used to focus on particular external outcomes, such as authorization failures or capture confirmations.

providerStatusCodes.description:
Optional filter restricting results to rows whose new_provider_status_code is one of the provided values.

When specified, the query only returns histories with matching provider codes; when omitted or empty, no filtering by provider_status_code is applied.

sortBy.description:
Field to sort the payment status history rows by.

Typical values include "created_at" for chronological ordering. Additional sortable fields may be supported by the implementation, but created_at is the canonical choice for reviewing the timeline of a payment.

sortDirection.description:
Direction in which results should be ordered relative to the sortBy field.

Conventional values include "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. For example, using sortBy = "created_at" and sortDirection = "desc" yields newest-first ordering of status history records.
